8497 – al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatādah regarding His saying: "allā taʿūlū," he said: incline.

8498 – It was related to me from ʿAmmār, saying: Ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ: "dhālika adnā allā taʿūlū," he says: that you not incline.

8499 – Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn related to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal related to us, saying: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: "dhālika adnā allā taʿūlū," he says: incline.

8500 – al-Muthannā related to me, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us, saying: Muʿāwiyah ibn Ṣāliḥ related to us, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah, from Ibn ʿAbbās regarding His saying: "adnā allā taʿūlū," he means: that you not incline.

8501 – Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to us, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās: "dhālika adnā allā taʿūlū," he says: that is closer that you not incline.

8502 – Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Ḥuṣayn informed us, from Abū Mālik regarding His saying: "dhālika adnā allā taʿūlū," he said: that you not act unjustly.

8503 – al-Muthannā related to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn related to us, and ʿĀrim Abū al-Nuʿmān, both saying: Hushaym related to us, from Ḥuṣayn, from Abū Mālik, the same.

8504 – Ibn Wakīʿ related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Yūnus, from Abū Isḥāq, from Mujāhid: "dhālika adnā allā taʿūlū," he said: incline. [[Report 8504: In the manuscript and the printed edition: "ʿan Ibn Isḥāq, ʿan Mujāhid," which is an obvious error; the correct reading is "ʿan Abī Isḥāq," namely Abū Isḥāq al-Subaʿī, and his narration from Mujāhid in this commentary has passed hundreds of times.]]

8505 – Yūnus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "dhālika adnā allā taʿūlū," that is less for your expenditure: one is less than two, three and four; and your slave-girl is an easier expense than a free woman; "allā taʿūlū," easier for you regarding dependents. [[In the manuscript: "ahwan ʿalayka fī al-qitāl" (easier for you in fighting), and the correct reading is that of the printed edition.]]

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 4, Verse 4:

**The discussion of the words of God: ﴿And give the women their dowries as a gift﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: Give the women their bridal gifts (mahr) as an obligatory gift [[In the manuscript, it reads "عليه واجبة" ("upon him, obligatory"), and a "ط" has been placed over "عليه" to indicate an error. The correct reading is what appears in the printed edition.]] and a binding duty.

* *

It is said of it: "Fulan gave (nahala) Fulan such-and-such, so he gives him a gift (nihla) and a bestowal (nuhl)," as follows:

8506 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurai' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding his words: "And give the women their dowries as a gift (nihlah)," he said: an obligation.

8507 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih informed me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding his words: "And give the women their dowries as a gift," he meant by "nihlah" the mahr.

8508 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding his words: "And give the women their dowries as a gift," he said: a specified obligation.

8509 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Ibn Zayd say, regarding his words: "And give the women their dowries as a gift," he said: "Nihlah" in the speech of the Arabs means the obligatory. He means: he does not marry her except with something obligatory for her, a dowry (sadaqah) that he names for her as obligatory. It is not befitting for anyone, after the Prophet ﷺ, to marry a woman except with an obligatory dowry, and it is not befitting that the naming of the dowry be a lie without right.

* *

Others said: Rather, by his words: "And give the women their dowries as a gift," he meant the guardians of the women, because they used to take their dowries.

Those who said this:

8510 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Sayyar, from Abu Salih, who said: When a man married off his unmarried woman (ayyim), he would take her dowry without her. So God, blessed and exalted, forbade them from that, and the verse was revealed: "And give the women their dowries as a gift."

* *

Others said: Rather, this was from the guardians of women, that a man would give his sister to another man on condition that the other give him his sister, with no substantial mahr between them. So they were forbidden from this.

[[This is the "shighar" (exchange-marriage) of those marrying without a mahr, except the marriage of a woman under their guardianship or an unmarried woman. This was part of the marriage practice of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era), and the Messenger of God ﷺ forbade it.]]

Those who said this:

8511 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, who said: A man from Hadramawt claimed that people would give this man his sister and take the man's sister, and they would not take a substantial mahr. So God, blessed and exalted, said: "And give the women their dowries as a gift."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most preferable of the interpretations we have mentioned concerning this is the interpretation we have stated. This is because God, blessed and exalted, began the mention of this verse with an address to those who marry women, forbade them from wronging them and oppressing them, and informed them of the way to be saved from wronging them. There is no indication in the verse that the address has been turned away from them to others. Since this is the case, it is known that those who were addressed with: "Then marry what seems good to you of women, two, three, or four," are the same ones addressed with: "And give the women their dowries," and the meaning is: Give those women you have married their dowries as a gift. This is because He said at the beginning of [the verse] [[In the manuscript, the mention of "الآية" (the verse), which I have placed between brackets, is omitted. In the printed edition it reads "في الأول" (in the first), but the context requires the addition as I have recorded it.]]: "Then marry what seems good to you of women," and He did not say: "So marry them off" (i.e., give them to be married by guardians). Thus His words "And give the women their dowries" are directed to the meaning that it refers to the husbands of women and not to the guardians of women.

This is a command from God to the husbands of women who have been consummated with and for whom a dowry was specified, that they give them their dowries, excluding women divorced before consummation for whom no dowry was specified in the marriage contract.

* *

The discussion of the words of God: ﴿But if they give you willingly some of it, then consume it with satisfaction and ease﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, He, may His praise be exalted, means: If, O men, your wives give you some of their dowries, their souls being content with that, then consume it with satisfaction and ease, as follows:

8512 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufadhdhal narrated to us, saying: Imarah narrated to us, from Ikrimah: "But if they give you willingly some of it," he said: the mahr.

8513 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Harami ibn Imarah narrated to me, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Imarah, from Ikrimah, [from Imarah] regarding His words, may God bless and exalt Him: "But if they give you willingly some of it," he said: the sadaqat (dowries). [[The narration 8513: "Harami ibn Imarah ibn Abi Hafsah al-Ataki," Abu Rawh, who narrated from Shu'bah. Ahmad said: "Truthful, but there was heedlessness in him," as mentioned in al-Tahdhib. The "Imarah" who narrated from Ikrimah is the father of this "Harami ibn Imarah," namely "Imarah ibn Abi Hafsah al-Ataki," a trustworthy narrator, also mentioned in al-Tahdhib.

As for the phrase "Ikrimah, from Imarah," I do not know of anyone from whom Ikrimah narrated who was named "Imarah." I think it is an error by the copyist: either he repeated "Imarah," or the correct reading is "from Ibn Abbas," and he mistakenly wrote "from Imarah." That is why I have placed it in brackets.]]

8514 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Al-Hammani narrated to me, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Salim, from Sa'id: "But if they give you willingly some of it," he said: the husbands.

8515 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Ubaydah, who said: Ibrahim said to me: "You have eaten from the wholesome and easy!" I said: What is that? He said: Your wife gave you some of her dowry.

8516 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: A man entered upon Alqamah while he was eating from food before him, from something his wife had given him from her dowry or something else. Alqamah said to him: Come near and eat from the wholesome and easy!

8517 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: "But if they give you willingly some of it, then consume it with satisfaction and ease," he says: If it is without harm or deception, then it is wholesome and easy, as God, may His praise be exalted, said.

8518 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij: "But if they give you willingly some of it," he said: the dowry; "then consume it with satisfaction and ease."

8519 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Ibn Zayd say, regarding His words: "But if they give you willingly some of it," after you have made it obligatory for them and given it to them as a gift, "then consume it with satisfaction and ease." [[In the printed edition: "I heard Ibn Zayd say regarding His words: But if they give you willingly some of it, then consume it with satisfaction and ease," which is an incomplete statement that mentions only the text of the verse. I have kept the reading of the manuscript, although the copyist may have omitted "فكلوه" (then consume it), which I have restored.]]

8520 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, from his father, who said: A man from Hadramawt claimed that people would feel sinful about asking one of them back regarding something he had given to his wife. So God, blessed and exalted, said: "But if they give you willingly some of it, then consume it with satisfaction and ease." [[In the printed edition: "that one of them might return," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

8521 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "But if they give you willingly some of it, then consume it with satisfaction and ease," he says: what their souls are content with, without reluctance or humiliation. [[In the manuscript: "in other than dhikrih," and the correct reading is what appears in the printed edition.]] God has permitted you to consume that with satisfaction and ease.

* *

Others said: Rather, by this statement He meant the guardians of the women, and it was said to them: If the souls of the women whose marriage bonds are with you are content to give their dowries willingly, then consume it with satisfaction and ease.

Those who said this:

8522 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Sayyar narrated to us, from Abu Salih, regarding His words: "But if they give you willingly some of it," he said: When a man married off his daughter, he would make for her dowry and take it. He said: So this verse was revealed concerning the guardians: "But if they give you willingly some of it, then consume it with satisfaction and ease."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two interpretations is the one we have stated, namely that the verse is addressed to the husbands. This is because the opening of the verse begins with mention of them, and His words "But if they give you willingly some of it" fall within its context.

* *

If someone says: How is it said: "But if they give you willingly some of it," when you know that the meaning of the statement is: If their souls are content with you [receiving] something? And how is "nafs" (soul) made singular when the meaning is for all of them? This is because He, may His remembrance be exalted, said: "And give the women their dowries as a gift."

It is said: As for transferring the action of the souls to the owners of the souls, this is widespread in the speech of the Arabs. From their well-known speech: "I was constricted by this matter, an arm's length (dhira'an) and a cubit (dhar'an)," and "my eye was cooled by this matter (qarrat bihi 'aynan)," and the meaning is: my cubit was constricted by it, and my eye was cooled by it, as the poet said: [[He is al-Qatami.]]

When the strong, muscular stallion (al-tayyaz) — we say: "To you, to you!" — he was constricted by her, the arm (dhira'an).

[[Diwan: 44; Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 256; al-Lisan (t-y-z), then vol. 20: 319. I have previously cited it in 1: 446, note 6, so refer to it. It is from his poem in which he praised Zafar ibn al-Harith, and this verse describes his she-camel, which he cared for well until she grew strong, fat, and full of energy. Before it: "When she grew fat upon her, as you plaster the palace with mud (al-siyya')."

"I ordered the men to take her, while we thought she could not be controlled."

"Al-siyya'" is mud, and "al-fadan" is a palace. The speech is reversed; its original form is: as the palace is plastered with mud, so it became smooth. He describes her fatness until she was full and strong, like a lofty castle. "Al-tayyaz" is the one with abundant, thick, and strong flesh. His words "ilayka, ilayka" mean: take her. He says to him: Take her and control her, but he was not able to manage her, and he was constricted by her "dhira'an." Ibn Barri has rejected the interpretation of "ilayka ilayka" as meaning "take her in order to ride her and tame her," and said: "There is a difficulty in this, because Sibawayh and all the Basrans held that 'ilayka' means 'withdraw,' and that it does not take a direct object. According to what they explained in the verse, it implies that it is transitive, because they made it mean 'take her.'" Abu Amr al-Shaybani narrated it as "ladayka ladayka" instead of "ilayka ilayka." He said: This is more like the speech of the Arabs and the view of the grammarians, because "ladayka" means "with you," and "'indaka" (with you) in the imperative is transitive.

In my view, the explanation of the commentators regarding "ilayka" is sound and good, and Ibn Barri's reasoning has been corrected; he was not correct in what he corrected.]] Then the attribute of "dhira'" (arm) was transferred to "the owner of the arm," and then "dhira'" was brought out as an explanation of the location of the verb.

Likewise, "nafs" is singular in His words: "But if they give you willingly some of it, a nafs," since "nafs" explains the location of the subject.

[["Al-tafsir" and "al-mufassar" (explanation and what is explained): the tamyiz (specification) and the mumayyaz, the terminology of the Kufans. See what has preceded in the index of terms. See also the statement of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 256.]]

* *

As for the singular "nafs" in place of the plural "nufus" (souls), it is because he meant "the desire" (al-hawa), and "al-hawa" can be a collective, as the poet said: [[He is Alqamah ibn Abdah (Alqamah al-Fahl).]]

In it are the carcasses of the exhausted, as for their bones, they are white, and as for their skins, they are a glossy residue (salib).

[[Diwan: 27; Sharh al-Mufaddaliyyat: 777; Sibawayh 1: 107; it will also appear in the Tafsir 17: 10 (Bulaq), from his poem about al-Harith ibn Jabalah ibn Abi Shamir al-Ghassani, when he captured his brother Sha's, and Alqamah traveled to him seeking his release. His words "in it are the carcasses of the exhausted": the pronoun refers to "al-'ulub" in the previous verse, which are traces of the road in the hard ground. "Al-hasra" are those who are exhausted, whose companions leave them and they die. "Al-salib" is the grease that flows from their skins once a period of time has passed since their death, while they are under the sun and its heat. He says: They died, and time passed over them, so their bones turned white, and their skin wasted away, so nothing of it remained on the surface of the road except the traces of the grease that flowed from their skins. The context is: "As for their skin, there is no skin, only the glossy residue alone."

The evidence in the verse is "jildaha" (her skin), when he intended "juludaha" (their skins).]]

As the other said: [[He is al-Musayyab ibn Zayd Manat al-Ghanawi.]]

In your throats is a bone, and we have been choked by it.

[[Sibawayh 1: 107; Sharh al-Mufaddaliyyat: 778; al-Lisan (sh-j-a). Before it: "Do not deny the killing, for we have been taken captive."

He mentions a people who captured some of his people. His people came and killed some of them, and he said to them: Do not deny our killing of you, since captivity has befallen us. If we have killed some of you until killing has become like a bone in your throats, lodged in their passage, then in our throats too there is a choking that has lodged: your capture of those of us you have taken. He says: This is in exchange for that.

The evidence is his words "in your throats" (fi halqikum), when he intended "throats" (hulukikum).]]

* *

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: It is permissible in "nafs" in this context to use both the plural and the singular: "fa-in tibna lakum 'an shay'in minhu nafsan" and "anfusan," and "daqtu bihi dhira'an" and "dhar'an" and "adhru'an," because it is related to you and to the one about whom you speak, so the singular was used instead of the plural for this reason, and it was not thought that it does not have the meaning of a plural, because before it there is a plural.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct position on this, in our view, is that "nafs" occupies the position of nouns that come in the singular form, conveying its meaning when mentioned in the singular, and that it has the meaning of the plural in reference to all of them.

* *

As for His words "hanien" (wholesome), it is derived from: "I smeared the camel with tar (qatran)," when it had mange and was treated with it, as the poet said: [[He is Durayd ibn al-Simmah.]]

Disheveled, his good qualities appear, placing the tar where the mange is.

[[Al-Shi'r wa al-Shu'ara' 302; al-Aghani 10: 22; al-Lisan (n-q-b); and others. From his verses which he composed when he passed by al-Khansa' bint Amr ibn al-Sharid, who was smearing a camel of hers with tar. She had become disheveled until she finished with it, then she removed her clothes and bathed, while Durayd was watching her and she was not aware of him, and he was pleased with her. He then turned back to his camp, saying:

Greet Tumadir, and stop, my companions; stand, for your standing is enough for me.

O Khunas, my heart has been lost for you, and a sickness of love has struck it.

I have not seen nor heard of anything like today, the one with the mangy she-camels.

Disheveled ... ... ... ... ... ... ...

Exhausted, the tar was sprinkled on him, like the sprinkling of perfume on a striped garment.

So ask them about me, O Khunas, when the matter grips everyone: what is my matter?

Then he proposed to her to her father, and she rejected him. He satirized her, claiming that she had rejected him because he was an old man. It was said to al-Khansa': Will you not respond to him? She said: I will not combine rejecting him with satirizing him. "Al-naqb" is (with the n vowelled with a damma and the q sukun) and "al-naqab" (damma then fatha) is the plural of "naqbah," the first sign of mange when it appears.]]

* *

So the meaning of His words "then consume it with satisfaction and ease" is: consume it as a healing cure.

* *

It is said of it: "Hana'ani al-ta'am wa mari'ani" (the food was wholesome and easy for me), meaning it became for me a remedy and a healing cure. "Hani'ani wa mari'ani" with the kasra is also possible, but rare. Those who say this word say: "yahna'uni wa yamra'uni." Those who say "hana'ani" say: "yahni'uni wa yamri'uni." When they use the singular, they say: "qad amra'ani hadha al-ta'am imra'an." It is also said: "hana'tu al-qawm" when I provided for them, and some Arabs have been heard to say: "Hanian was only named Hanian so that he would be wholesome," meaning: so that he would provide for and suffice.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 5 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And do not give the foolish your property which Allah has made for you a means of support, but provide for them from it and clothe them﴾ [[The printed edition and the manuscript contained the verse only up to "qiyaman." However, Abu Ja'far's tafsir included the rest of the verse, "wa-arzuquhum fiha wa-iksuhum," as will come on p. 571, so I completed it.]]

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters differed concerning "the foolish" (al-sufaha') whom Allah, mighty and majestic is He, forbade His servants to give their property to. [[For the discussion of "al-safah" (foolishness) and "al-sufaha'" (the foolish), see what has passed: 1/293-295; 3/90, 129; 6/57-60.]]

Some said: They are women and children.

Mention of those who said this:

8523 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from 'Abd al-Karim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The orphans and the women.

8524 - al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan regarding His words: "And do not give the foolish your property," he said: Do not give to the young children and the women.

8525 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurai' related to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: The woman and the boy.

8526 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn related to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Shurayk, from Abu Hamza, from al-Hasan, who said: The women and the children, and the women are the most foolish of the foolish.

8527 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan regarding His words: "And do not give the foolish your property," he said: "The foolish" are your foolish son and your foolish wife. And it has been mentioned that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Fear Allah regarding the two weak ones: the orphan and the woman."

8528 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Hammani related to us, saying: Humayd related to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman al-Ru'asi, from al-Suddi = he said: he returns it to 'Abd Allah = he said: The women and the children.

8529 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "And do not give the foolish your property." As for "the foolish," they are the child and the woman.

8530 - It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "And do not give the foolish your property," meaning: a man's children and his wife, and she is the most foolish of the foolish.

8531 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib related to me, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "And do not give the foolish your property," he said: "The foolish" are the children, and the women are the most foolish of the foolish, so they become masters over you.

8532 - Ahmad ibn Hazim al-Ghifari related to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Salama ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak, who said: Your children and your women.

8533 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Hammani related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Salama, from al-Dahhak, who said: The women and the children.

8534 - Ahmad ibn Hazim related to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Humayd al-A'raj, from Mujahid: "And do not give the foolish your property," he said: The women and the children.

8535 - Ahmad related to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ghaniyya related to us, from al-Hakam: "And do not give the foolish your property," he said: The women and the children. [[Report 8535: "Abu Nu'aym" is al-Fadl ibn Dukayn; his biography has passed under nos. 2554 and 3035. "Ibn Abi Ghaniyya" (with a fatha on the ghayn, a kasra on the nun, and a shadda on the ya) is 'Abd al-Malik ibn Humayd ibn Abi Ghaniyya al-Khuza'i, who related from his father, Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani, and al-Hakam ibn 'Utayba. Al-Thawri related from him, and he was among his contemporaries, as did Waki', Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida, 'Imara ibn Bishr, Abu Nu'aym, and others. He is trustworthy (thiqa). In the printed edition it read "Ibn Abi 'Anbasa," but in the manuscript the copyist did not write it well so that it looked like "Ibn Abi 'Aniya"; the correct reading is what has been given. And "al-Hakam" is al-Hakam ibn 'Utayba al-Kindi, which has passed many times, under no. 3297.]]

8536 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada regarding His words: "And do not give the foolish your property which Allah has made for you a means of support," the command of Allah regarding this property is that it be stored and its keeping be done well, and it should not be possessed by a foolish woman or a foolish boy.

8537 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Hammani related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Isma'il, from Abu Malik, who said: The women and the children.

8538 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And do not give the foolish your property," he said: your wife and your sons; and he said: "The foolish" are the boys, and the women are the most foolish of the foolish.

* *

Others said: Rather, "the foolish" are specifically the children.

Mention of those who said this:

8539 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Shurayk, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His words: "And do not give the foolish your property," he said: They are the orphans.

8540 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: my father related to me, from Shurayk, from Salim, from Sa'id, who said: "The foolish" are the orphans.

8541 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Yunus informed us, from al-Hasan regarding His words: "And do not give the foolish your property," he says: do not grant the children (la tanhalu al-sighar).

* *

Others said: Rather, He means by this: the foolish among a man's children.

Mention of those who said this:

8542 - Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Malik regarding His words: "And do not give the foolish your property," he said: Do not give your foolish child your property, lest he corrupt it, which is your support after Allah, exalted is He.

8543 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to us, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And do not give the foolish your property," he says: Do not empower the foolish one from your children = so Ibn 'Abbas used to say: That was revealed concerning the foolish, and the orphans have no part in it. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "wa-laysu al-yatama" (and they are not the orphans), which is a poor construction, and I fear it may be a copyist's error.]]

8544 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'ba related to us, from Firas, from al-Sha'bi, from Abu Burda, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari that he said: Three people call upon Allah and He does not answer them: a man whose wife has bad character and he does not divorce her; a man who gave his wealth to a foolish person when Allah has said: "And do not give the foolish your property"; and a man who had a debt owed to him by another man and did not have it witnessed. [[Report 8544: al-Hakim cited it in al-Mustadrak 2:203 through the route of Abu al-Muthanna Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari, from his father, from Shu'ba, raised (marfu') to the Prophet, and said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs, but they did not record it, because the companions of Shu'ba stopped this hadith at Abu Musa (i.e., made it mawquf). They only agreed on the chain of Shu'ba's hadith with this isnad: 'Three people will be given their reward twice,' and both of them agreed on recording it." Al-Dhahabi said: "They did not record it, because the majority related it from Shu'ba as mawquf, and Mu'adh ibn Mu'adh raised it from him."]]

8545 - Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Ibn Zayd: "And do not give the foolish your property," the verse, he said: Do not give the foolish one from your children a head (ra's) or a garden, nor anything that is yours, a means of support from your property.

* *

Others said: Rather, "the foolish" in this place are specifically the women, to the exclusion of others.

Mention of those who said this:

8546 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from his father, who said: A Hadrami claimed that a man deliberately gave his property to his wife, and she placed it in other than the right, so Allah, blessed and exalted, said: "And do not give the foolish your property."

8547 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Humayd, from Mujahid: "And do not give the foolish your property," he said: The women.

8548 - Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Thawri, from Humayd, from Qays, from Mujahid regarding His words: "And do not give the foolish your property," he said: They are the women.

8549 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: "And do not give the foolish your property which Allah has made for you a means of support," he said: He forbade men to give women their property, and they are foolish whether they are wives, mothers, or daughters.

8550 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

8551 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Hisham related to us, from al-Hasan, who said: The woman.

8552 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, who said: The women are among the most foolish of the foolish.

8553 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Abu 'Awana, from 'Asim, from Mawraq, who said: A woman passed by 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, having an appearance and an outfit, so Ibn 'Umar said to her: "And do not give the foolish your property which Allah has made for you a means of support."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement concerning the interpretation of this, in our view, is that Allah, mighty and majestic is He, made general by His words: "And do not give the foolish your property," and did not specify one foolish person over another. So it is not permissible for anyone to give his property to a foolish person, whether he be a small child or a grown man, male or female.

And "the foolish" whom it is not permitted for his guardian to give his property is the one who deserves restriction (hajr) because of his squandering of his property, his corruption and causing corruption, and his poor management of that.

And we said what we said, that the intended meaning of His words "And do not give the foolish" is the one we have described and no other, because Allah, mighty and majestic is He, said in the verse that follows: "And test the orphans until they reach marriageable age; then if you perceive in them rushd (sound judgment), deliver to them their property," so He commanded the guardians of orphans to deliver their property to them when they reached marriageable age and sound judgment was perceived in them. And "the orphans" may include males and females, so He did not specify the command to deliver their property to males over females, nor to females over males.

Since that is so, it is known that those whose guardians were commanded to deliver their property to them, and for whom it was permitted for the Muslims to deal and transact with them, are other than those whose guardians were commanded to withhold their property from them, and for whom it was forbidden for the Muslims to lend to them or transact with them.

Since that is so, it is clear that "the foolish" whom Allah forbade the believers to give their property to are those who deserve restriction and merit that their property be placed under a guardian, and they are those whose description we gave earlier; and that whoever is other than this is not foolish, because restriction is not deserved by one who has reached maturity and whose rushd is perceived.

* *

As for the statement of those who said: "He meant by the foolish the women specifically," they have made the language other than its proper form. For the Arabs hardly form the pattern "fa'il" into "fu'ala'" except for the plural of males, or of males and females together. As for when they intend the plural of females only, with no males among them, they form it into "fa'a'il" and "fa'ilat," such as "gharība" (strange, feminine), whose plurals are "gharā'ib" and "gharībāt"; but "al-Ghurabā'" is the plural of "gharīb" (masculine). [[This argument is from sound reflection on Arabic grammar and the meanings of its patterns. What Abu Ja'far rejected, namely making the language other than its proper form and loading Arabic with what it cannot bear in its patterns and structure, and interpreting the Book of Allah specifically by forced extraction and boldness toward the language, seems in our time to have become the rule upon which every innovator in religion builds his corruption by his own opinion, and every seeker of fame among people through what he says about the religion of his Lord, which was entrusted to him, from those to whom His Book was sent down, to teach and guide them. They have opposed the path of knowledge and strayed from the ways of guidance.]]

* *

The interpreters differed concerning the interpretation of His words: "your property which Allah has made for you a means of support, and provide for them from it and clothe them."

Some said: He means by this: do not give the foolish, from among the women and the children = according to what we have mentioned of the difference of those whose statements we have related before = O you of sound judgment, your property which you possess, lest you empower them over it so they corrupt and waste it; but provide for them from it yourselves, if they are among those whose maintenance is incumbent upon you, and clothe them, and speak to them a fair word.

We have mentioned the reports from a group of those who said this, among them: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatada, and the Hadrami; and we will mention the statements of the others whose statements were not mentioned before.

8554 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "And do not give the foolish your property which Allah has made for you a means of support, and provide for them from it," he says: Do not give your wife and your son your property, lest they become the ones who take charge over you; feed them from your property and clothe them.

8555 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And do not give the foolish your property which Allah has made for you a means of support, and provide for them from it and clothe them, and speak to them a fair word," he says: Do not empower the foolish one from your children over your property, and command him to provide for him from it and clothe him.

8556 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And do not give the foolish your property," he said: Do not give the foolish one from your property anything that is yours.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "And do not give the foolish their property," but it was attributed to the guardians, because they are its managers and administrators.

* *

Mention of those who said this:

8557 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak related to us, from Shurayk, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His words: "And do not give the foolish your property," [it is the property of the orphan that is in your keeping; he says: do not give it to him, and spend on him from it until he reaches maturity. And He attributed it to the guardians, saying "your property," because they are its managers and administrators]. [[Report 8557: What is between the brackets is an addition not found in the printed edition or the manuscript; I added it from al-Baghawi's tafsir (in the margin of Ibn Kathir) 2:349. It is closer to al-Tabari's wording in presenting this view. Al-Baghawi attributed this view which I quoted to Sa'id ibn Jubayr and 'Ikrima, and I judge that it dropped from the copyist of al-Tabari's tafsir. It appears that al-Suyuti also saw a copy of al-Tabari's tafsir in which this omission occurred, so he neglected Sa'id ibn Jubayr's statement that al-Baghawi quoted, and quoted from Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim from Sa'id ibn Jubayr the following text:
"From Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His words: (And do not give the foolish), he said: the orphans - (your property), he said: their property, in the same manner as His words: (And do not kill yourselves)."
And it is clear that the text of al-Baghawi is closer to what Abu Ja'far mentioned than the text of al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:120, so I have adopted it. And I hope nothing has dropped from Abu Ja'far's following words.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It may be that "your property" in His words, "And do not give the foolish your property," includes the property of those who are forbidden from giving it to them, and the property of "the foolish." Because His words "your property" are not specified to exclude some properties over others. And the Arabs do not prohibit addressing a people with an address, so that the speech comes out partly as report about them and partly about absent ones; as when they say: "You ate, O so-and-so, your property wrongfully," addressing one person with the address of the plural, meaning: you and your companions or your people ate your property. Likewise His words: "And do not give the foolish," mean: do not give, O people, your foolish ones your property, part of which is yours and part of which is theirs, lest they waste it.

Since that is so, and since Allah, exalted be His remembrance, made general the prohibition on giving the foolish all the property, and did not specify any part of it over another, it was clear from that that the meaning of His words "which Allah has made for you a means of support" is only "which Allah has made for you and for them a means of support," but the foolish were included in the mention of those addressed by His words "for you."

* *

As for His words, "which Allah has made for you a means of support": "qiyaman," "qiyaman" and "qiwaman" have one meaning. Originally "al-qiyam" is "al-qiwam," but because the "qaf" before the "waw" was kasra, the "waw" was changed into "ya'" because of the kasra before it, as it is said: "sumtu siyaman" (I fasted a fast), and "sultu siyalan" (I fought a fight), [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "halat hiyalan" with a ha', and the correct reading seems to be what has been given.]] and it is said from it: "Fulan qawwam ahl baytihi" and "qiyam ahl baytihi" (So-and-so is the manager of his household).

* *

The readers differed in reading this.

Some of them read: ﴿allati ja'ala Allahu lakum qiyaman﴾ with a kasra on the "qaf" and a fatha on the "ya'" without an "alif."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 5 (part 2 of 2):

Others read it: "qiyaman" (as a means of support), with an alif.

* *

Muhammad said: [[This is the second time that "Qal Muhammad" ("Muhammad said") has been written, meaning Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari, Abu Ja'far, in place of "Qal Abu Ja'far." See 519, note 1, above.]] The reading we choose is "qiyaman" with the alif, because it is the well-known reading in the recitation of the cities of Islam (qira'at, the canonical readings of the Qur'an), although the other reading is not wrong or corrupt. We have chosen what we have chosen for this reason: when the readings differ in wording but agree in meaning, the one we prefer is the one that is more evident and more widely known among the reciters of the cities of Islam.

* *

The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil, those who interpret the Qur'an) said things similar to what we have said concerning the interpretation of His words, "qiyaman." Those who said this are mentioned:

8558: Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Malik: "Your property which Allah has made for you a means of support (qiyaman)," which is your support after Allah. [[The report 8558 is an abridgement of the report preceding it, numbered 8542.]]

8559: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Your property which Allah has made for you a means of support (qiyaman)." Property is the means by which people stand, the support of their livelihood. He says: Be yourself the guardian of your family, and do not give your wife [and your son] your property, lest they become the ones who stand over you. [[The report 8559 is an abridgement of the report numbered 8554. The words in brackets are from it; without them the pronouns do not hold together. In the manuscript and the printed edition it reads "kunta anta" ("you were you"), but the correct form is "kun anta" ("be you"), as I have written it.]]

8560: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: "Do not give the foolish your property which Allah has made for you a means of support (qiyaman)." Allah the Glorious says: Do not turn to your property, which Allah has bestowed on you and made a means of livelihood for you, and give it to your wife or your sons, and then look at what is in their hands. Rather, keep your property and manage it, and be yourself the one who spends on them for their clothing, their provision, and their maintenance. He said: And His words "qiyaman" mean: your support in your livelihoods.

8561: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan concerning His words "qiyaman," he said: the standing of your life.

8562: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Sharud narrated to us, from Mujahid, that he read "allati ja'ala Allahu lakum qiyaman" with the alif, saying: the standing of your life. [[In this report, "Ishaq" is Ishaq ibn al-Day'if, or Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Day'if al-Bahili, and he is trustworthy (thiqah). He is listed in al-Tahdhib. As for "Bakr ibn Sharud," al-Bukhari mentioned him in al-Kabir (2/1/90) and said: "A San'ani. Ibn Ma'in said: I saw him; he is not trustworthy." Ibn Abi Hatim, in al-Jarh wa-al-Ta'dil (1/1/338), mentioned him as "Bakr ibn Abd Allah ibn Sharus, also called Ibn Sharud, al-San'ani," and said: "He narrated from Ma'mar. Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn al-Day'if narrated from him. I heard my father say: he is weak in hadith." As for the Hafiz Ibn Hajar, he mentioned him in Lisan al-Mizan (2:52–54), narrated from Ibn Ma'in that he said: "A liar, of no account," and dealt with his case fully. As for "Mujahid," he is Mujahid ibn Jabr, the famous Successor (tabi'i) and imam. In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "from Ibn Mujahid," and the addition of "Ibn" is an error beyond doubt. The copyist apparently took him to be "Ibn Mujahid" the reciter, the master of the craft, the first to fix the seven readings, who was of a later birth. He was born in 245 AH; this is "Abu Bakr ibn Mujahid," that is, Ahmad ibn Musa ibn al-Abbas ibn Mujahid al-Tamimi.]]

8563: Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: "Your property which Allah has made for you a means of support (qiyaman)": Do not give the foolish among your children anything; it is for you, the one who manages your property. [[Report 8563: see the report numbered 8545 above. Their wording differs while their chains of narration agree.]]

* *

As for His words, "wa-arzuquhum fiha wa-iksuhum" (and provide for them from it and clothe them), the exegetes differed in its interpretation.

As for those who said that Allah, mighty and majestic, meant by His words, "Do not give the foolish your property," the property of the guardians of the foolish, and not the property of the foolish themselves [[The words in brackets, "amwal" (property of), I have inferred from the context and set down for clarity. This is probably correct.]], they said: "The meaning of that is: provide for your foolish ones, O people, from among your wives and children, from your property, their food and what they cannot do without of their maintenance and clothing."

We have mentioned some of those who said this earlier, and we will mention those who were not mentioned among their sayers.

8564: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: They were ordered to provide for their foolish ones, of their wives, their mothers, and their daughters, from their property.

8565: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

8566: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn Abbas said concerning His words, "wa-arzuquhum": he said, he means: spend on them.

8567: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "wa-arzuquhum fiha wa-iksuhum": he means: feed them from your property and clothe them.

* *

As for those who said: "He meant by His words, 'Do not give the foolish your property,' the property of the foolish, that their guardians should not give it to them," they said: "The meaning of His words, 'wa-arzuquhum fiha wa-iksuhum,' is: provide for your foolish ones from their property, O guardians of the property of the foolish, their food and what they cannot do without of their maintenance and clothing." This has already been mentioned. [[See the report numbered 8557.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for what we consider correct in His words, "Do not give the foolish your property," in terms of interpretation, we have already mentioned it, and we have given proof for what we said, which suffices without repeating it.

* *

The interpretation of His words, "wa-arzuquhum fiha wa-iksuhum," according to the interpretation we have given of His words, "Do not give the foolish your property," is: spend on your foolish ones among your children and wives, whose maintenance is obligatory upon you, with food and clothing from your property, and do not empower them over your property so that they destroy it; and [spend] on your foolish ones from among them, those whose maintenance is not obligatory upon you, and from others whose affairs you manage, from their property, for what they cannot do without of their sustenance in their food, drink, and clothing. [[See the explanation of "al-rizq" (provision) above in 4:274, 5:44, 6:311, and of "al-kiswah" (clothing) above in 5:44, 5:480.]] This is because that is the obligation of the ruling according to the saying of all the authorities (al-hujjah), with no disagreement among them about it, together with the evident indication of the revelation for what we have said.

* *

The discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿And speak to them a fair word﴾ (5)

Abu Ja'far said: The exegetes differed in the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: The meaning of that is: promise them a pleasing promise of kindness and support.

Those who said this are mentioned:

8568: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And speak to them a fair word." He said: They were ordered to say to them a fair word of kindness and support, meaning the women, who in his view are the foolish ones.

8569: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid: "And speak to them a fair word." He said: a promise that you make them.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: pray for them.

Those who said this are mentioned:

8570: Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: "And speak to them a fair word": If he is not your child, nor one whom you are obliged to maintain, then say to them a fair word; say to them: "May Allah grant us and you well-being," and "May Allah bless you."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings is what Ibn Juraij said: that the meaning of His words, "And speak to them a fair word," is: say, O company of the guardians of the foolish, a fair word to the foolish: "If you become righteous and mature, we will hand over your property to you, and leave it between you and yourselves; so fear Allah regarding your souls and your property," and what is similar to that of speech which contains exhortation to obey Allah and warning against disobeying Him. [[See the explanation of "al-ma'ruf" (the fair, the known) above in 3:371, 4:547, 5:7, 5:44, 5:76, 5:93, 5:137, 7:91, 7:105, 7:130, and of "qawl ma'ruf" (a fair word) above in 5:520.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 6 (part 1 of 3):

The explanation of His, may His remembrance be exalted, words: ﴿And test the orphans until, when they reach marriageable age﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His, may His remembrance be exalted, words "and test the orphans," He means: test the minds of your orphans in their understanding, and their righteousness in their religion, and their ability to manage their wealth, as:

8571 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah and al-Hasan, concerning His words "and test the orphans," they both said: He says: test the orphans.

8572 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: As for "test the orphans," examine their minds.

8573 - Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, saying: ʿIsa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words "and test the orphans," he said: their minds.

8574 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words "and test the orphans," he said: test them.

8575 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words "and test the orphans until, when they reach marriageable age," he said: Test him in his opinion and in his mind, how he is. When it is known that sound judgment has been perceived from him, his wealth is handed over to him. He said: And that is after puberty.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have already shown earlier that the meaning of "ibtila'" (testing) is examination, which is sufficient so that it need not be repeated. [[See the explanation of "ibtila'" above: 2:49 / 3:7, 220 / 5:339 / 7:297, 325, 454.]]

* *

As for His words "when they reach marriageable age," He means: when they reach puberty (al-hulm), as:

8576 - Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from ʿIsa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words "until, when they reach marriageable age," until they have had wet dreams.

8577 - ʿAli ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "until when they reach marriageable age," he said: at the time of puberty.

8578 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words "until when they reach marriageable age," he said: puberty.

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿And if you perceive in them sound judgment﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "and if you perceive in them sound judgment," means: if you find them and know them, as:

8579 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "and if you perceive in them sound judgment," he said: you know of them.

* *

It is said: "I perceived goodness and righteousness from so-and-so" (with the alif elongated) [[In the printed edition: "I perceived goodness from so-and-so, and it was read with the alif lengthened"; the reading of "wabarran" was not rendered correctly in the manuscript, which corrupted the sense badly.]] means "inasan", and "I was familiar with him, I am familiar with him, a familiarity" (with the alif shortened), when he became familiar with him.

* *

It is also reported that in the reading of ʿAbd Allah it is: ﴿fa-in ahsaytum minhum rushdan﴾, [[In al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:257: "fa-in ahstum" with a single, unvowelled sin; in some copies, as in Tabari's tafsir, but in the manuscript it is written in both places as "ahsistum" with two sins, which is an error; the correct form is that of the printed edition and al-Farra's Ma'ani.]] meaning: "ahsastum," that is, you found.

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of "rushd" (sound judgment) mentioned by God in this verse. [[See the explanation of "rushd" above: 3:482 / 5:416.]]

Some of them said: The meaning of "rushd" in this place is reason and righteousness in religion.

Those who said that:

8580 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "and if you perceive in them sound judgment," intellect and righteousness.

8581 - Bishr ibn Muʿadh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah: "and if you perceive in them sound judgment," he says: righteousness in their minds and religion.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: righteousness in their religion and proper management of their wealth.

Those who said that:

8582 - Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Mubarak, from al-Hasan, who said: sound judgment in religion, righteousness, and preservation of wealth.

8583 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah narrated to me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "and if you perceive in them sound judgment," in their condition, and the proper management of their wealth.

* *

Others said: Rather, that is intellect alone.

Those who said that:

8584 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: We do not hand over to the orphan his wealth even if he takes hold of his beard, [[His words "takes hold of his beard" mean: grey hair has taken hold of his beard; see the following report: 8586.]] even if he is an old man, until his sound judgment, meaning intellect, is perceived in him.

8585 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, from Mujahid: "perceived in them sound judgment," he said: intellect.

8586 - Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Shubrumah informed us, from al-Shaʿbi, who said: I heard him say: A man may take hold of his beard while his sound judgment has not yet reached maturity. [[The report 8586: "Abu Shubrumah" is the kunya of "Ibn Shubrumah," the judge, jurist and mufti ʿAbd Allah ibn Shubrumah ibn Hassan al-Dabbi. He was chaste, resolute, intelligent, a jurist, resembling the ascetics, trustworthy in hadith, a poet, of good character, and generous. Thus they described him, may God have mercy on him.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, it is righteousness and knowledge of what sets it right.

Those who said that:

8587 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "and if you perceive in them sound judgment," he said: righteousness and knowledge of what sets it right.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most preferable of these sayings to me regarding the meaning of "rushd" in this place is intellect and the proper management of wealth [[See the previous commentary, p. 576, note 1, on the sources for the explanation of "rushd."]], because of the consensus of all that if he is like this, he is not among those who deserve to be restrained concerning his wealth and to have what is in his hand taken from him, even if he is impious in his religion. And since this is a consensus of all, the same ruling applies when he reaches maturity while his wealth is in the hands of his father's guardian, or in the hands of a ruler who has been appointed over his wealth during his childhood: it is obligatory upon them to hand over his wealth to him, if he is sane, mature, and manages his wealth well, not wasteful, for the reason by which he deserves to be placed in charge of the wealth in his hand is the same reason by which he deserves to have his hand barred from the wealth in the hand of a guardian [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "in the hand of a walī"; the correct reading omits this hā', for it corrupts the sentence; had it been read "in the hand of his walī," it would have been sound.]], for there is no difference between them.

In their consensus that it is not permissible to take possession of what is in his hand when his mind is sound and what is in his hand is well managed, there is clear evidence that it is not permissible to prevent his hand from what is his in such a state, even if it was previously in the hand of another; there is no difference between them. Whoever distinguishes between them, the argument is reversed against him, and he is asked for the difference between them from a principle or an analogy, and he will not state a position on one of them without being compelled to the same on the other.

Since what we have described is a consensus of all [[In the printed edition: "if what we have described," the correct reading is from the manuscript.]], it is clear that the "rushd" by which an orphan, when he reaches maturity and sound judgment is perceived in him, deserves to have his wealth handed over to him, is what we have said: soundness of mind and proper management of his wealth.

* *

The explanation of His, may His praise be exalted, words: ﴿So hand over to them their wealth, and do not consume it extravagantly﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means the guardians of the orphans' wealth. God says to them: when your orphans reach puberty and you perceive in them intellect and proper management of their wealth, then hand over their wealth to them, and do not withhold it from them.

* *

As for His words "do not consume it extravagantly," He means: by other than what God has permitted you, [[In the printed edition: "what God has permitted you" in the plural; I have kept the manuscript. See the explanation of "consuming wealth" above: 3:548–551 / 7:528.]] as:

8588 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah and al-Hasan: "and do not consume it extravagantly," he says: do not be extravagant in it.

8589 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "and do not consume it extravagantly," he said: he is extravagant in eating.

The root of "israf" is exceeding the permitted limit to what is not permitted. It may be in excess, and it may be in deficiency. However, when it is in excess, the usage is "asraf yusrif israfan." When it is in deficiency, the expression is "saraf yasraf sarafan," as it is said: "I passed by you and sarafтukum," meaning: I forgot you and missed you, as the poet said: [[It is Jarir.]]

They gave Hunaydah, driven by eight (camels)... there is no reproach nor *saraf* in their giving.

[[Diwan: 389; Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shuʿara: 359; al-Ishtiqaq: 241; Lisan (h-n-d) (s-r-f), and others; it will come in the tafsir 8:46 / 30:159 (Bulaq), from his qasida in which he praised Yazid ibn ʿAbd al-Malik and satirised the family of al-Muhallab, saying to Yazid before it: "I hope for bounties, for God has favoured you... before you my soul met destruction..."; "Whoever among us, when our needs descend, is like the one with whom there is honour and kindness..."; "How often have I alighted with you as a guest, and you cover me with the extra blanket, and the extra is a fine thing to be wrapped in..." Hunaydah is the name for every hundred camels, not declined, nor taking the definite article, nor pluralised, and has no singular of its own kind. Hind is similar in meaning, and a woman was named after it, I believe, when a hundred camels were driven as her bridal gift, out of her nobility and honour and the desire of husbands for her due to her rank. His words "eight" mean eight slaves who attend to her affairs.]]

He means by his words "and no saraf" that there is no error in it; the meaning is that they hit the right places of giving and do not miss them.

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿And [do not consume it] in haste, lest they grow up﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His, may His remembrance be exalted, words "wa-bidaran," is meant "and hastening." It is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "I hastened this matter, a hastening and bidaran."

* *

He means by this, may His remembrance be exalted, the guardians of the orphans' wealth. He says to them: do not consume their wealth extravagantly, meaning what God has permitted you to consume, nor hastening on your part to their reaching maturity and perceiving sound judgment in them, out of fear that they will reach it and it will become binding upon you to hand it over to them, as:

8590 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words "extravagantly and in haste": he means consuming the orphan's wealth in haste before he reaches maturity, so that he is barred from his wealth.

8591 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatadah and al-Hasan: "and do not consume it extravagantly and in haste," he says: do not be extravagant in it, and do not hasten it. [[In the printed edition: "and do not hasten" without the final hā'; I have kept the manuscript.]]

8592 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "and in haste," in haste that they grow up and take their wealth.

8593 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words "extravagantly and in haste," he said: this is for the guardian of the orphan, that he consumes it; they made it lawful for him to eat with him when he finds nothing, he puts his hand with him, then he delays, saying: "I will not hand over his wealth to him," and you desire to eat it, because if you do not hand it to him you have a share in it, and if you hand it to him you have no share in it. [[This sentence in the manuscript was in corrupt, undotted writing, and is faulty. The printed edition corrected it and wrote: "this is for the guardian of the orphan specifically, and it was made lawful for him," and erred in what it read and what it wrote. Then it wrote "fa-yadhhabu bi-wajhihi" in place of "yu'akhkhiruhu," which is also an error. Then it added "in" in the phrase "because you did not hand it to him," making it "because if you do not hand it to him," which is correct, but I preferred "idha."]]

* *

The position of "an" in His words "an yakbarū" is in the accusative governed by "al-mubadarah" (hastening), because the meaning of the statement is: do not consume it by hastening their growing up. [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:257.]]

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿And whoever is rich, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His remembrance be exalted, "and whoever is rich," from among the guardians over the orphans' wealth, let him abstain with his own wealth from consuming it, without extravagance and without hastening that they grow up, by what God has permitted him to consume it, as:

8594 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, and Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words "and whoever is rich, let him abstain," he said: by his richness from his wealth, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "li-ghanahu ʿan maalihi" (for his richness from his wealth); the correct reading has the bā'.]] until he is independent of the orphan's wealth.

8595 - And with the same chain: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, concerning His words "and whoever is rich, let him abstain," by his richness.

8596 - Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Layth, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words "and whoever is rich, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable," he said: from his own wealth; and whoever among them is poor, in need of it, let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Then the people of interpretation differed concerning the "reasonable" (al-ma'ruf) by which God, may His praise be exalted, permitted the guardians of their wealth to consume it, when they were in poverty and need of it. [[See the explanation of "al-ma'ruf" above, p. 573, note 2, and the sources cited there.]]

Some of them said: That is lending: he borrows from the wealth and then repays it.

Those who said that:

8597 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Sufyan and Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Harithah ibn Mudarrib, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, said: I have placed the wealth of God, may He be exalted, in my hands in the position of the orphan's wealth: if I become rich, I abstain; if I become poor, I eat in accordance with what is reasonable; and when I become well-off, I repay. [[Report 8597: "Harithah ibn Mudarrib al-Kufi," who narrated from ʿUmar and ʿAli, and from whom Abu Ishaq al-Sabiʿi narrated. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/87, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/255. In the manuscript and printed edition it was "Harithah ibn Musarrif," which is an error and a misreading.]]

8598 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿAtiyyah narrated to us, from Zuhayr, from al-ʿAla' ibn al-Musayyib, from Hammad, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words "and whoever is poor, let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable," he said: it is lending.

8599 - Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir narrated to us, saying: I heard Yunus, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from ʿUbaydah al-Salmani, that he said concerning this verse: "and whoever is rich, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable," he said: the one who spends from the orphan's wealth, it becomes a loan upon him.

8600 - Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, saying: Salamah ibn ʿAlqamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: I asked ʿUbaydah about His words "and whoever is rich, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable," he said: it is only a loan; do you not see that He says: "And when you hand over to them their wealth, then have witnesses over them"? He said: I thought he said it by his own opinion.

8601 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Hisham informed us, from Muhammad, from ʿUbaydah, concerning His words "and whoever is poor, let him eat in accordance with what is reasonable," and it is a loan upon him.

٨٦٠٢ - Yaqub told me, saying: Hushaym told us, from Salama ibn Alqama, from Ibn Sirin, from Ubayda, regarding His saying: ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat in reasonableness﴾. He said: "Al-ma'ruf" is the loan. Do you not see His saying: ﴿So when you hand over to them their property, then call witnesses against them﴾? [[The report: 8602 - "Salama ibn Alqama al-Tamimi," who narrated from Muhammad ibn Sirin. Trustworthy. Biographed in al-Tahdhib (Tahdhib al-Tahdhib). In the manuscript and the printed edition it reads "Salama from Alqama," which is an error; see the earlier chain no. 8600, which has it correctly.]]

٨٦٠٣ - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told me, saying: Abd al-Razzaq told us, saying: Mu'ammar informed us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, from Ubayda, the same as the report of Hisham. [[He means no. 8601.]]

٨٦٠٤ - Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih told me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat in reasonableness﴾: he meant the loan.

٨٦٠٥ - Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And whoever is rich, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat in reasonableness﴾: He says: If he is rich, it is not lawful for him to eat anything of the orphan's property. And if he is poor, let him borrow from it; then when he finds means, let him give back what he borrowed. That is his eating in reasonableness.

٨٦٠٦ - Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Idris told us, saying: I heard my father mention, from Hammad, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: He eats as a loan in reasonableness. [[The report: 8606 - "Ibn Idris" is "Abdullah ibn Idris ibn Yazid ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi," the teacher of Abu Kurayb, who has passed several times. In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "Abu Idris," which is an error. His father is "Idris ibn Yazid ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Awdi," who narrated from his father, Abu Ishaq al-Sab'i, Simak ibn Harb, and others. Biographed in al-Tahdhib. The manuscript reads "I heard Abu Bakr," and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.]]

٨٦٠٧ - Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Hajjaj informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: It is the loan. Whatever of it he takes, he repays when he becomes well-off. He means His saying: ﴿And whoever is rich, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat in reasonableness﴾.

٨٦٠٨ - Yaqub told me, saying: Ibn Ulayya told us, from Hisham al-Dastawa'i, who said: Hammad told us, saying: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about this verse: ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat in reasonableness﴾. He said: If he takes from his property an amount sufficient for his sustenance as a loan, then if he becomes well-off afterward, he repays it. And if death comes to him while he has not become well-off, he seeks the orphan's pardon for it. And if the orphan is a minor, he seeks pardon from his guardian. [[In the manuscript: "halalahu min waliyyihi" (he pardoned him from his guardian), and perhaps it is "halallahu minhu waliyyuhu" (his guardian pardoned him from it). What is in the printed edition fits the context.]]

٨٦٠٩ - Hamid ibn Mas'ada told us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Shu'ba told us, from Hammad, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: Let him eat as a loan. [[In the manuscript: "fa-la ya'kul qardan" (so let him not eat as a loan), which is an error; the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.]]

٨٦١٠ - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'ba told us, from Hammad, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat in reasonableness﴾, he said: It is the loan.

٨٦١١ - Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Hakkam told us, from Amr ibn Abi Qays, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from al-Sha'bi: ﴿And whoever is rich, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat in reasonableness﴾. He said: He does not eat it except when he is compelled to it, as one is compelled to eat carrion. If he eats any of it, he repays it.

٨٦١٢ - Hamid ibn Mas'ada told us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Shu'ba told us, from Abdullah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: ﴿Let him eat in reasonableness﴾. He said: As a loan.

٨٦١٣ - Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'ba told us, from Abdullah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

٨٦١٤ - Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Let him eat in reasonableness﴾. He said: A loan (salaf) from the property of his orphan.

٨٦١٥ - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, and from Hammad, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: ﴿Let him eat in reasonableness﴾. Both said: It is the loan. Al-Thawri said: al-Hakam also said it. Do you not see that He said: ﴿So when you hand over to them their property, then call witnesses against them﴾?

٨٦١٦ - Yaqub told me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Hajjaj told us, from Mujahid, who said: It is the loan. Whatever of it he takes, he repays when he becomes well-off. He means: ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat in reasonableness﴾.

٨٦١٧ - Ibn Waki' told us, saying: My father told us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliya: ﴿Let him eat in reasonableness﴾. He said: It is the loan. Do you not see His saying: ﴿So when you hand over to them their property﴾?

٨٦١٨ - Ibn Waki' told us, saying: My father told us, from Sufyan, from Asim, from Abu Wa'il, who said: A loan.

٨٦١٩ - Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mansur, from al-Hakam, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: If the guardian has need or becomes poor and finds nothing, he eats from the orphan's property and records it. If he becomes well-off, he repays it. If he does not become well-off until death approaches him, he calls the orphan and seeks his pardon for what he ate.

٨٦٢٠ - Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Ibn Ulayya told us, saying: Ibn Abi Najih informed us, from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat in reasonableness﴾, from the orphan's property, without extravagance, and with no obligation to repay what he ate from it.

* *

The proponents of this view differed regarding the meaning of "eating that in reasonableness." Some of them said: That he eats of the food with the tips of his fingers, and does not wear it (i.e., does not dress in it or take it for clothing).

Those who said that:

٨٦٢١ - Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Abu Ahmad told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from al-Suddi, who said: Someone informed me that he heard Ibn Abbas say: ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat in reasonableness﴾. He said: With the tips of his fingers.

٨٦٢٢ - Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ubayd Allah al-Ashja'i told us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from one who heard Ibn Abbas say, and then he mentioned the same. [[The report: 8622 - "Ubayd Allah al-Ashja'i" is "Ubayd Allah ibn Ubayd al-Rahman al-Ashja'i." Ibn Ma'in said: "No one in Kufa knew Sufyan al-Thawri better than al-Ashja'i." He is trustworthy and reliable. Biographed in al-Tahdhib. In the printed edition it reads "Abdullah al-Ashja'i," which is an error.]]

٨٦٢٣ - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: ﴿And whoever is rich, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat in reasonableness﴾. He says: "Whoever is rich" - whoever is in charge of the orphan's property - let him abstain from eating it; "and whoever is poor" - whoever is in charge of the orphan's property - let him eat with him using his fingers, not extravagantly, and not wearing it. [[In the printed edition: "fa-liyasta'if 'an malihi" (let him abstain from his property), and I have restored the correct reading from the manuscript.]]

٨٦٢٤ - Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Harami ibn Umara told us, saying: Shu'ba told us, from Umara, from Ikrima, regarding the orphan's property: Your hand is with their hands, and do not make a cap out of it.

٨٦٢٥ - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Uyayna informed us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ata and Ikrima, who both said: You place your hand with his hand.

* *

Others said: Rather, "reasonableness" in that means that he eats what satisfies his hunger and wears what covers his nakedness.

Those who said that:

٨٦٢٦ - Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Mughira informed us, from Ibrahim, who said: Indeed reasonableness is not wearing linen or fine garments, but rather what stills hunger and covers nakedness.

٨٦٢٧ - Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, who said: It used to be said: Reasonableness is not wearing linen and fine garments, but reasonableness is what stills hunger and covers nakedness.

٨٦٢٨ - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim, the same.

٨٦٢٩ - Ali ibn Sahl told us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim told us, saying: Abu Ma'bad told us, who said: Makhul was asked about the guardian of the orphan: what is his eating in reasonableness if he is poor? He said: His hand with his hand. It was said to him: And the clothing? He said: He wears from his own garments. As for taking from his property something for himself, no.
