٨٦٣٠ - Abu Kurayb told us, saying: al-Ashja'i told us, from Sufyan, from Mughira, from Ibrahim regarding His saying: ﴿Let him eat in reasonableness﴾, who said: What stills hunger and covers nakedness. Indeed, it is not the clothing of linen and fine garments. [[The report: 8630 - "al-Ashja'i" is "Ubayd Allah ibn Ubayd al-Rahman al-Ashja'i," who was mentioned shortly before in the note on report no. 8622.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, that "reasonableness" is eating its dates and drinking its milk (risl) of the livestock, in return for his tending to it. As for gold and silver, he has no right to take any of them except by way of a loan.

Those who said that:

٨٦٣١ - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Mu'ammar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said: I have orphans' property in my care? He was seeking his permission to take some of it. Ibn Abbas said: Are you not seeking its strayed animal? [[The Arabic: "baghā al-ḍāllah" means he searched for and sought it.]] He said: Yes! He said: Are you not smearing its mange-stricken camels with tar? He said: Yes! He said: Are you not plastering its troughs? He said: Yes! He said: Are you not bringing the water to them on their day of watering? [[The Arabic: "farrata" means he went ahead of the camels to the water, prepared the ropes and buckets for them, filled the troughs and drew water for them. "Yawm al-warid" (with a kasra on the ra') is their day when they come to the water. In the printed edition it reads "yawm wurudiha," which is also correct in meaning, but the manuscript reading is the purest.]] He said: Yes! He said: Then take from their milk. He meant: from their milk.

٨٦٣٢ - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: A Bedouin came to Ibn Abbas and said: I have orphans in my care, and they have camels, and I have camels, and I lend out my camels and lend the use of a camel for riding, so what is lawful for me from their milk? He said: If you seek its strayed animal, and smear its mange-stricken camels, and plaster its troughs, and draw water for them, then drink without harming the offspring and without over-milking. [[Note: The two reports: 8631 and 8632. Malik narrated it in the Muwatta' through the chain "Yahya ibn Sa'id, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad," like the second report here, with some variation in wording. Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas narrated it in al-Nasikh wal-Mansukh (p. 93). al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (1:122) to Malik, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Nahhas in his Nasikh.]]

٨٦٣٣ - Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abd al-Wahhab told us, saying: Dawud told us, from Abu al-Aliya regarding this verse: ﴿And whoever is rich, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat in reasonableness﴾, who said: From the surplus of the milk and the date. [[In the printed edition: "wal-thamara" with a thā' (the third letter), and I have kept what is in the manuscript here. It will come in later reports in the manuscript with a thā', but its correct form is with a tā'; see my argument for that in report no. 8636.]]

٨٦٣٤ - Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Abd al-A'la told us, saying: Dawud told us, from Abu al-Aliya regarding the guardian of the orphan's property, who said: He eats from the milk of the livestock and from the dates, due to his tending to it, and he does not eat from the property itself. And he said: Do you not see that He said: ﴿So when you hand over to them their property﴾?

٨٦٣٥ - Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Idris told us, saying: I heard Dawud, from Rufay' Abu al-Aliya, who said: The guardian of the orphan was granted leave to take from the milk and eat from the dates, but as for gold and silver, they must be returned. Then he recited: ﴿So when you hand over to them their property﴾. Do you not see that He said: "There must be a handing over"? [[The report: 8635 - "Rufay' ibn Mihran al-Riyahi." "Abu al-Aliya" has passed in nos. 44, 184, and other places. In the manuscript and the printed edition here it reads "Rufay' from Abu al-Aliya," with the addition of "from" (an), which is a plain error.]]

٨٦٣٦ - Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Awf informed us, from al-Hasan, that he said: Indeed their property at that time was the palm trees and livestock, and so He granted them leave, when one of them was in need, to take from the milk. [[In the printed edition: "adkhal al-nakhl wal-mashiya" (introducing the palm trees and livestock); in the manuscript: "adhal," and I could not find meaning in any of these readings after trying most of the possible corrections. Eventually I came to lean toward the view that the correct reading is what I have given, and it seems the copyist saw the "dhal" of "dhalika" (that), joined to its alif, and took it for a "ha'," and he wrote the final "kaf" as a "lam." What I have given is the very sense of the context, God willing.]]

٨٦٣٧ - Yaqub told me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Salim informed us, from al-Sha'bi regarding His saying: ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat in reasonableness﴾, who said: If he is poor, he eats from the dates, and drinks from the milk, and takes from the milk of the livestock. [[In the printed edition: "min al-thamar" with a thā', and I have kept what is in the manuscript. See the earlier note p. 589, no. 6.]]

٨٦٣٨ - Bishr ibn Mu'adh told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada: ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat in reasonableness﴾. It was mentioned to us that the paternal uncle of Thabit ibn Rifa'a, while Thabit at that time was an orphan in his care, from the Ansar, came to the Prophet of God (ﷺ) and said: O Prophet of God, my nephew is an orphan in my care, so what is lawful for me from his property? He said: Eat in reasonableness, without protecting your property with his property, and do not take from his property a large amount. [["Wafara malahu wafran": he gathered it until it multiplied and became abundant. He means: to accumulate wealth for himself and gather it from the property of his orphan.] And the orphan would have a garden of palm trees, ["al-ha'it" is a garden of palm trees; if it has a wall, it is ha'it (walled), but if it is not enclosed, it is "dahiya" (open)], so his guardian would tend to its upkeep and irrigation, and eat from its dates; or he would have livestock, and his guardian would tend to their upkeep, or take charge of their treatment and expenses, and eat from their fleece, their sick animals, and their milk. [[Al-jizaz and al-jizaza (with a damma on the jim), and al-jizz (with two fathas), and al-juzza (with a kasra on the jim and a shadda on the zay); its plural is juzz (with a kasra then a fatha): it is what is shorn from the wool of a sheep or other animals. The reading in Lisan al-Arab and al-Faʾiq of al-Zamakhshari is "juzzaha," the plural of "juzza." "Al-awarid" is the plural of "ariḍa," which is a sheep or camel struck by a calamity, a break, or a disease, so they slaughter it. From their sayings: "The Banu so-and-so eat only the awarid," meaning they do not slaughter camels except for one afflicted by a disease. "Al-rasl" is milk.]] As for the necks of the property and the roots of the property, [["Raqab al-mal" means livestock, and "usul al-mal" means palm trees.] he has no right to consume them. [[Report 8638: The scholar Ibn Hajar mentioned it in al-Isaba, in the biography of "Thabit ibn Rifa'a," and did not attribute it to Ibn Jarir. He attributed it to Ibn Manda and Ibn Fathun, through the chain of Abd al-Wahhab, from Sa'id, from Qatada, and said: "This is mursal (a report with a missing companion), its narrators are trustworthy."]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 6 (part 3 of 3):

8639: It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say, concerning His words ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat according to what is reasonable﴾: "That means riding the animal and making use of the servant." If he takes a loan (qard) from his property while being wealthy, then he must repay it, and he may not eat anything from his property.

* *

Others said: He may eat from all of the property, if he is in charge of it, and even if it consumes the property, and there is no repayment obligation upon him.

Those who said this:

8640: Abu Kurayb related to us, who said: Isma'il ibn Subayh related to us, from Abu Uways, from Yahya ibn Sa'id and Rabi'ah together, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, who said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) was asked what is appropriate for the guardian of an orphan. He said: "If he is wealthy, let him abstain. If he is poor, let him eat according to what is reasonable."
[Report 8640: Isma'il ibn Subayh al-Yashkuri has passed under no. 2996. Abu Uways is 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Uways ibn Malik ibn Abi 'Amir al-Asbahi, the paternal cousin of Malik and his brother-in-law through his sister. Ibn Ma'in said: "Truthful, but not a proof." Abu Hatim said: "His narrations are written down but not relied upon, and he is not strong." He is biographied in al-Tahdhib. In the printed edition it read "from Abu Idris," which is an error; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]

8641: Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Yahya ibn Ayyub informed us, from Muhammad ibn 'Ajlan, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father: that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab used to say: "What is lawful for the guardian of an orphan is lawful for the ruler: 'Whoever is wealthy, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat according to what is reasonable.'"

8642: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, who said: Hushaym related to us, who said: al-Fadl ibn 'Atiyyah informed us, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, concerning His words ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat according to what is reasonable﴾, he said: "If he is in need, let him eat according to what is reasonable. If he becomes well-off after that, there is no repayment obligation upon him."

8643: Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, who said: al-Husayn ibn Waqid related to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from 'Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, who both said: "Allah, blessed and exalted, mentioned the property of orphans and said: ﴿And whoever is wealthy, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat according to what is reasonable﴾." And what is reasonable in this is that he fears Allah regarding his orphan.

8644: Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Hakkam related to us, from 'Amr, from Mansur, from Ibrahim (al-Nakha'i): that he did not see any repayment obligation upon the guardian of an orphan if he ate while in need.

8645: Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Jarir related to us, from Mansur, from Mughirah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, concerning ﴿let him eat according to what is reasonable﴾, regarding the executor (wasi), he said: "There is no repayment obligation upon him."

8646: Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, who said: Shu'bah related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim that he said regarding this verse ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat according to what is reasonable﴾: "If the guardian of the orphan works with it, he may eat according to what is reasonable."

8647: Bishr ibn Muhammad related to us, who said: Yazid ibn Zuray' related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan used to say: "If he is in need, he may eat from the property according to what is reasonable, as a provision (tu'mah) from Allah for him."
[Ta'mah (with a vowel on the first letter and a sukun on the second): provision and sustenance. It is said: "The ruler assigned such-and-such a district to so-and-so as a ta'mah," meaning a source of food from which he eats, just as he eats from his earnings.]

8648: al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from al-Hasan al-Basri, who said: A man said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "I have an orphan in my care. Shall I strike him?" He said: "Would you strike your own child?" He said: "May I take from his property?" He said: "According to what is reasonable, without accumulating wealth, and without protecting your wealth with his wealth."
[Ta'ththul mal (accumulating property): to take the root of property, to gather it, establish it, and store it.]

8649: al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: al-Thawri informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from al-Zubayr ibn Musa, from al-Hasan al-Basri, the same.
[Report 8649: al-Zubayr ibn Musa ibn Mayna al-Makki narrated from Jabir, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Amr ibn Dinar, 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Aziz and others. Ibn Jurayj, al-Thawri and Ibn Abi Najih narrated from him. He is biographied in al-Tahdhib. I fear that the correct reading is: "al-Thawri and Ibn Abi Najih informed us."]

8650: Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'Ata', that he said: "He places his hand with theirs and eats with them, in proportion to his service and his work."

8651: al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, from 'A'ishah, who said: "The guardian of an orphan, if he is in need, eats according to what is reasonable, because he takes care of his property."

8652: Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, and I asked him about the words of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿And whoever is wealthy, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat according to what is reasonable﴾. He said: "If he becomes wealthy, he refrains. If he is poor, he eats according to what is reasonable." He said: "He eats with his hand along with them, because of his guardianship over their property and his preservation of it. He eats from what they eat from. If he becomes wealthy, he refrains from it and eats nothing from it."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views is the view of the one who said: the "reasonable" (ma'ruf) that Allah, blessed and exalted, means in His words ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat according to what is reasonable﴾ is the eating of an orphan's property when there is necessity and need for it, by way of borrowing from it (qard). As for any other way, it is not permissible for him to eat it.

That is because all agree that the guardian of an orphan does not own the property of his ward except for the duty of looking after its welfare. Since there is a consensus among them that he is not its owner, and since it is not permissible for anyone to consume the property of another, whether the owner is an orphan or a mature, sound-minded adult, and since if he transgresses and consumes it by eating or otherwise, he must compensate its owner, by consensus of all, and since the guardian of an orphan is in the same position as anyone else in that he does not own his ward's property, his ruling regarding what he must repay if he eats from it is the same as anyone else's. He differs in that he may borrow from it when in need, just as others may borrow against him when they are in need of what they borrow, if he is responsible for what serves its welfare.

* *

There is no sense in the view of the one who said: "The 'reasonable' meant in this place is the guardian of the orphan eating from the orphan's property because of his care of it, as a compensation for his work and effort." That is because the guardian of an orphan may hire himself out to the orphan for managing his affairs when the orphan is in need of that, for a known wage, just as one may hire other workers for him, and just as one may buy for him someone who assists him, [In the printed edition it reads "and just as one may buy for him from his share," which has no sense; in the manuscript it is unclear, and I read it as I have recorded it, meaning he buys him a slave to assist him], whether the guardian is wealthy or poor.

Since this is so, and since Allah, mentioned, has indicated by His words ﴿And whoever is wealthy, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat according to what is reasonable﴾ that permission to eat an orphan's property was granted to those guardians in a state of poverty and need, and since the state in which guardians may hire themselves out to orphans, given the orphans' need for workers, is not restricted to a state of wealth or a state of poverty, it is known that the meaning for which permission was granted to them regarding their orphans' property in every state is not the meaning for which permission was granted in one state and not another.

As for the one who rejects what we have said, from among those who claim that the guardian of an orphan may eat his ward's property when in need of it, not by way of loan, and who takes as evidence this verse: It is said to him: "Is there consensus that what you say is the interpretation of His words ﴿And whoever is poor, let him eat according to what is reasonable﴾?"

If he says: "No!"

It is said to him: "Then what is your proof that this is its interpretation, when you know that he does not own his ward's property?"

If he says: "Because Allah permitted him to eat it!"

It is said to him: "Did He permit him to eat it absolutely, or on condition?" [In the manuscript it reads "permitted him to eat it absolutely on condition, on condition," which is a scribal error; the correct reading is that of the printed edition.]

If he says: "On a condition, which is that he eats it according to what is reasonable."

It is said to him: "And what is that 'reasonable'? You know that those who said so among the Companions, the Successors, and those after them among the later generations said that it is eating it as a loan (qard) and as an advance (salaf)?"

It is also said to them, in addition: "Consider the ones placed under guardianship over their property, the insane and the feeble-minded. Do the guardians of their property have the right to eat from their property when they are in need of it, not by way of loan nor as compensation for their management of it, just as you said this about orphans' property, permitting it for them? If they say: 'That is permitted for them,' they have departed from the position of all the authorities."

And if they say: "That is not permitted for them."

It is said to them: "Then what is the difference between their property and the orphans' property, when the ruling regarding their guardians is the same: they are guardians of the property of others? Thus they will not say anything about one of them without being bound to say the same about the other." [In the printed edition and manuscript it reads "they will not say anything about one of them," which is an error; the correct reading is what I have recorded.]

They are likewise asked about the one placed under restriction (mahjur 'alayh): is it permissible for the one who manages his property to eat from his property when he is in need of it? This is like our question to them about the property of the insane and the feeble-minded.

* *

The discussion on the interpretation of His words, mighty and majestic: ﴿Then when you hand over to them their property, call witnesses against them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: And when you hand over, O guardians of orphans' property, to the orphans their property, "then call witnesses against them," meaning: call witnesses against the orphans that they have received it from you and that you handed it over to them, as:

8653: Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, who said: My father related to me, who said: My paternal uncle related to me, who said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words ﴿Then when you hand over to them their property, call witnesses against them﴾, he said: "When an orphan's property is handed to him, let it be handed over to him in the presence of witnesses, as Allah, exalted, has commanded."

* *

The discussion on the interpretation of His words: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner﴾ (6)

Abu Ja'far said: May His praise be exalted, means: And Allah is sufficient as a guardian, apart from the witnesses whom the guardian of the orphan calls upon when handing over his ward's property to him, as:

8654: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, who said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Reckoner﴾, he said: "As a witness."

* *

It is said from this: "al-Dhi 'indi qad ahsabani" (what I have is enough for me), meaning: sufficed me. And it has been heard from the Arabs: "La-uhsibanna-kum min al-aswadayn" (I will certainly make you have enough of the two blacks), meaning: of water and dates. [It was said in explaining this word: "That is, I will certainly provide abundantly for you," which carries the sense of sufficiency.] "Al-muhsib" among men: one of high lineage. "Al-muhsab": one who is sufficed. [See the interpretation of "hasbahu" in what has passed, 4:244 / 7:405.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 7:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and the relatives leave, and for women there is a share of what the parents and the relatives leave, whether it is little or much, a share ordained.﴾ (7)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His remembrance be exalted, He means: for the males among the sons of a deceased man there is a portion of his inheritance, and for the females among them there is a portion of it, from what he leaves behind, little or much, a portion ordained [[See the explanation of "al-fard" (obligation, prescribed share) above, 4:121 / 5:120.]], obligatory and known, fixed (muwaqqata). [[Muwaqqata: determined and defined. Its origin is from "al-waqt" (time), then its use was extended to everything that is limited. From it is the hadith of Ali, may Allah be pleased with him: "For the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not fix anything for it," meaning he did not prescribe a specific measure of lashes for drinking wine. From this, the grammarians took their term for a proper noun that specifies its referent absolutely and without restriction, such as "Zayd," which is: "a defined (muwaqqata) definite noun." See the explanation of this in 1:181, footnote 1.]]

* *

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed because the people of the Jahiliyya used to bequeath to males only, not to females, as:

8655 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, who said: "They did not bequeath to women, so this was revealed: 'And for women there is a share of what the parents and the relatives leave.'"

8656 - Al-Qasim told us, saying: Al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrima, who said: It was revealed concerning Umm Kahla and the daughter of Kahla, and Tha'laba and Aws ibn Suwayd, and they were of the Ansar. One of them was her husband and the other was the paternal uncle of her son. She said: "O Messenger of Allah, my husband died and left me and his daughter, and we were not given an inheritance!" The paternal uncle of her son said: "O Messenger of Allah, she does not ride a horse, nor carry a burden, nor strike an enemy; she is earned for and does not earn!" So this was revealed: "For men there is a share of what the parents and the relatives leave, and for women there is a share of what the parents and the relatives leave, whether it is little or much, a share ordained." [[The narration 8656: Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar cited it in al-Isaba in the biography of "Umm Kajja," and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:122, attributing it to Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim. Al-Hafiz mentioned the narration of al-Tabari and said in it: "It was revealed concerning Umm Kajja, and the daughter of Umm Kajja, and Tha'laba, and Aws ibn Thabit," which contradicts the text of al-Tabari at this point, regarding "Umm Kajja" and "Aws ibn Thabit," as you see. In the printed edition it read "Umm Kahha" and "bint Kahha" with the unmarked ha', and the correct form is with a damma on the kaf and a shadda on the jim with a fatha, as Al-Hafiz vocalised it in al-Isaba. As for al-Suyuti, he said: "It was revealed concerning Umm Kulthum and the daughter of Umm Kahla, or Umm Kahha," also with the unmarked ha', which is an error. As for "Umm Kahla," as it appears in the manuscript and as I have recorded it, al-Hafiz also said in al-Isaba: "As for the woman, there is no disagreement that she is Umm Kajja (with a damma on the kaf and shadda on the jim), except what Abu Musa related from al-Mustaghfiri, that he said of her: Umm Kahla (with a sukun on the unmarked letter followed by lam), and except what preceded, that she is the daughter of Kajja, as in the two narrations of Ibn Jurayj. It is possible that her kunya matched the name of her father, and it is derived from the narration of Ibn Jurayj that she is Umm Kulthum."

This seems to negate that the narration of al-Tabari reads "Umm Kahla," but the manuscript has established it clearly in both places, so I found no way to omit or change it, given this narration that al-Hafiz related from al-Mustaghfiri, and its confirmation also in the text of al-Suyuti, as he transmitted from al-Tabari, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn al-Mundhir.

The mention of Umm Kajja will come in narration no. 8725, where she is the wife of Abd al-Rahman, brother of Hassan ibn Thabit; see the commentary on that narration there.

As for "Aws ibn Suwayd," as you have seen, al-Hafiz mentioned it as attributed to Ibn Jarir as "Aws ibn Thabit," but what is established in the sources of tafsir and what is transmitted from him is "Aws ibn Suwayd." Al-Hafiz gave biographies of Aws ibn Thabit al-Ansari and Aws ibn Suwayd, and of Tha'laba ibn Thabit al-Ansari and Tha'laba ibn Suwayd, and mentioned the disagreement over their names in this very story. I have left the text of al-Tabari as it is, and suffice it to note the disagreement mentioned by al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar; whoever wishes may consult it fully there and in its other sources.

* *

As for His saying: "la tahmil kallan": meaning, she does not take charge of dependents and striving for them. "And the kall" means the dependents, who need someone to carry them and provide for them, such as the orphan and others.

As for His saying: "wa la tunka'a 'aduwwan": it is said from it: "nakaytu al-'aduwwa anka' (with a kasra on the kaf) nakaya," when one inflicts harm upon them, kills them, and inflicts many wounds. It is also said: "wa naka'tu al-'aduwwa" with a hamza, with the same meaning. In the printed edition it read "wa la tunka'" with a hamza, and I have recorded what is in the manuscript, and both are correct.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Narrated to me Yunus, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "For men there is a share of what the parents and the relatives leave": He said: In the Jahiliyya women were not inherited from by the fathers, and the elder would inherit while the young would not inherit even if male. So Allah, blessed and exalted, said: "For men there is a share of what the parents and the relatives leave," up to His saying: "a share ordained." [[In the printed edition: "la yarthina" differing from the manuscript, which I have recorded.]]

Abu Ja'far said: The accusative of His saying "nasiban mafrudan," which is an attribute of an indefinite noun, is because it comes in the manner of a verbal noun (masdar), like the speaker's saying: "laka 'alayya haqqun wajiban" ("you have a right upon me, binding"). Had the phrase in place of "nasiban mafrudan" been a proper noun, its accusative would not be permissible. One does not say "laka 'indi haqqun dirhaman," so His saying "nasiban mafrudan" is like His saying: "nasiban fariḍatan" and "fardan," just as one says "'indi dirhamun hibatan maqbudatan." [[See the meanings of the Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:257, as his wording is.]]

* *

The seventh part of the Tafsir of al-Tabari is complete.

Followed by the eighth part, and its beginning:

**The exegetes differed concerning the ruling of this verse: is it definitive (muhkam) or abrogated (mansukh)?**

Abu Ja'far said: The exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil, "the people of interpretation") differed concerning the ruling of this verse. Is it muhkam or mansukh?

Some of them said: It is muhkam.

Mention of those who said that:

8658: Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Sufyan, from al-Shaybani, from Ikrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "It is muhkam, and it is not mansukh," meaning His saying: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship, and the orphans, and the needy﴾ (the verse).

8659: Abu Kurayb told us, saying: al-Ashja'i told us, from Sufyan, from al-Shaybani, from Ikrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, the like of it. [[Report 8659: This report is missing from the printed edition, and it has been confused with the one that follows it.]]

8660: Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Sufyan, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim and al-Sha'bi, who both said: "It is muhkam." [[Report 8660: In the printed edition it read: "Abu Kurayb told us, saying: al-Ashja'i told us, from Sufyan..." The word "al-Ashja'i" was placed in the chain of the earlier report that had been dropped, in place of "Ibn Yaman." I have restored it to the correct form from the manuscript.]]

8661: Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "It is obligatory (wajib): what the hearts of the heirs' people are pleased with."

8662: Abu Kurayb told us, saying: al-Ashja'i told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship, and the orphans, and the needy﴾. He said: "It is obligatory upon the heirs, what their souls are pleased with."

8663: Abu Kurayb told us, saying: al-Ashja'i told us, from Sufyan, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim and al-Sha'bi, who both said: "It is muhkam, not mansukh."

8664: Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Yahya ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, from Sufyan. And al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, both from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "It is obligatory upon the heirs, what their souls are pleased with."

8665: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Abu Bishr informed us, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, that he was asked about His saying: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship, and the orphans, and the needy, then provide for them from it and speak to them a kind word﴾. Saʿid said: "People are careless about this verse." He said: "They are two guardians: one of them inherits, and the other does not inherit. The one who inherits is the one commanded to provide for them," he said, "to give them," he said, "and the one who does not inherit is the one commanded to speak to them a kind word. And it is muhkam, not mansukh."

8666: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim, with something similar to that, and he said: "It is muhkam, not mansukh."

8667: Bishr ibn Muʿadh told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saʿid told us, from Mutarrif, from al-Hasan, who said: "It is established (thabitah), but people were stingy and miserly."

8668: al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Mansur and al-Hasan informed us, both saying: "It is muhkam, not mansukh."

8669: al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: ʿAbbad ibn al-ʿAwwam told us, from al-Hajjaj, from al-Hakam, from Miqsam, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: "It remains in force, and is acted upon."

8670: Muhammad ibn ʿAmr told me, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, from ʿIsa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship, and the orphans, and the needy, then provide for them from it﴾: "What the souls are pleased with is a definite, obligatory right."

8671: al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Abu Sufyan told us, from Maʿmar, from al-Hasan and al-Zuhri, who both said concerning His saying: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship, and the orphans, and the needy, then provide for them from it﴾: "It is muhkam."

8672: al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Mansur informed us, from Qatadah, from Yahya ibn Yaʿmar, who said: "Three verses are muhkam and Medinan, and people have abandoned them: this verse; and the verse of seeking permission (al-istidhan): ﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess ask your permission﴾ [Surah al-Nur: 58]; and this verse: ﴿O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female﴾ [Surah al-Hujurat: 13]."

8673: Bishr ibn Muʿadh told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saʿid told us, from Qatadah, who said: "al-Hasan used to say: it is established."

* *

Others said: It is mansukh.

Mention of those who said that:

8674: Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, both saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi told us, from Saʿid, from Qatadah, from Saʿid, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship, and the orphans, and the needy﴾: "This verse was a division before the inheritance shares. When God sent down the inheritances to their rightful people, the bequest was made for the relatives who are present at the division and do not inherit."

8675: Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, saying: Qurrah ibn Khalid told us, from Qatadah, who said: "I asked Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab about this verse: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship, and the orphans, and the needy﴾, and he said: 'It is mansukh.'"

8676: Bishr told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saʿid told us, from Qatadah, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "This was before the obligatory shares and the division of inheritance. When the obligatory shares and the inheritances came, it was abrogated."

8677: Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, who said: "The verse of inheritance abrogated it."

8678: Abu Kurayb told us, saying: al-Ashja'i told us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, the like of it.

8679: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told us, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told us, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship, and the orphans﴾, the verse, up to His saying: "a kind word." That was before the shares were sent down. Then God, blessed and exalted, sent down the shares after that, and gave every person of right his right. So charity was assigned to what the deceased named.

8680: al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, who said: "The inheritances abrogated it."

* *

Others said: "It is muhkam and not mansukh; but the meaning of that is: ﴿And when the division is attended﴾, meaning by it the division of the dead man's property by his bequest to those to whom he bequeathed it." They said: He was commanded to make his bequest from his property to those whom God, exalted, named in this verse.

Mention of those who said that:

8681: Saʿid ibn Yahya al-Umawi told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad: that ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman divided his father's inheritance while ʿA'ishah was alive, and he left no one in the house without giving to him, and he recited this verse: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship, and the orphans, and the needy, then provide for them from it﴾. al-Qasim said: "I mentioned that to Ibn ʿAbbas, and he said: 'He did not hit the mark. This is only a bequest,'" meaning the deceased, "that he should bequeath to his relatives." [[Report 8681: "Saʿid ibn Yahya ibn Saʿid al-Umawi," whose biography has passed under number 2225 and in other places. In the printed edition it read "Yahya ibn Saʿid al-Umawi," transposed; the correct form is from the manuscript. "ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman" is "ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq," who was the nephew of Umm Salamah, the wife of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).]]

8682: al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Ibn Abi Mulaykah informed me: that al-Qasim ibn Muhammad informed him, that ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr divided (an inheritance), and he mentioned something similar.

8684: ʿImran ibn Musa al-Saffar told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Warith ibn Saʿid told us, saying: Dawud told us, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, concerning His saying: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship, and the orphans, and the needy﴾, he said: "He was commanded to bequeath a third of his property to his relatives." [[Report 8683: "ʿImran ibn Musa al-Saffar," whose biography has passed under number 2154, but he is described in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim as "al-Qazzaz." This is a difference that should be specified.]]

8684: Ibn al-Mubarak told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿla told us, saying: Dawud told us, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, who said: "That is only when making the bequest, from one third of the property."

8685: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhab told us, saying: Dawud told us, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship, and the orphans, and the needy, then provide for them from it﴾, he said: "It is the bequest from people."

8686: Yunus told us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship, and the orphans, and the needy﴾: "The division is the bequest. When a man made a bequest, they would say: 'So-and-so is dividing his property.' Then He said: ﴿provide for them from it﴾, meaning: bequeath to them. He says to the one who bequeaths: ﴿and speak to them a kind word﴾. If you do not bequeath to them, then say to them something good."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these statements is the statement of the one who said: "This verse is muhkam, not mansukh, and it is only meant as a bequest to the near kin of the testator; and by the orphans and the needy is meant that a kind word be said to them."

We have said that this is more correct than others, because of what we have shown in more than one place in this book and elsewhere [[See what has passed: 2:471, 472, 482, 534, 535 / 3:385, 563 / 4:582 / 5:414 / 6:54, 118.]] that it is not permissible for any of the rulings of God, blessed and exalted, which He established in His Book or explained through the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ), to be described as abrogating another ruling, or as abrogated by another ruling, unless the two rulings, of which one is declared abrogating and the other abrogated, negate each other, so that it is impossible for the two rulings to apply at the same time in any way; and even if it were permissible, it would be turned away from naskh (abrogation). [[In the printed edition and the manuscript it read "mansukh li-hukm" with a lam; the correct form is with a ba'.]] Or you must say that one of them is abrogating and the other abrogated, by a proof that must be accepted.

Since that is so, as we have shown in more than one place, and since His saying, exalted be His mention: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship, and the orphans, and the needy, then provide for them from it﴾, may bear the meaning: "When the division of a man's property by his bequest is attended by his relatives, the orphans, and the needy, then provide for them from it," meaning: "then bequeath to your relatives who do not inherit from you, and say to the orphans and the needy a kind word," just as He said in another place: ﴿Prescribed for you, when death approaches one of you, if he leaves wealth, is a bequest to the parents and the near relatives in a reasonable manner, a duty upon the righteous﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 180], and it is not abrogated by the verse of inheritance, [[The context: "Since that is so, as we have shown in more than one place ... it is not permissible for anyone..." What lies between them is connection and explanation.]] no one may take it to be abrogated by the verse of inheritance, since there is no indication that it is abrogated by it from the Book or from an established sunnah, and it bears the interpretation we have explained. Since that is so, the meaning of His saying: "when the division is attended," is the division of the testator's property by bequest; "by those of kinship, and the orphans, and the needy, then provide for them from it" means: "so divide for them from it by bequest," i.e., "bequeath to the near kin from your wealth," ﴿and speak to them﴾, meaning the others, who are the orphans and the needy, ﴿a kind word﴾, meaning: that good be invoked for them, [[See the explanation of "a kind word" above in 7:572, 573, note 2, and then 582, note 1, and the references there.]] as Ibn ʿAbbas said and all those whose statements we have mentioned before.

* *

As for those who said: "The verse is abrogated by the verse of inheritance," and those who said: "It is muhkam, and what is commanded is the heirs of the deceased," they directed His saying: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship, and the orphans, and the needy, then provide for them from it﴾ to mean: "give them from it," ﴿and speak to them a kind word﴾. We have mentioned some of those who said that, and we will mention the rest of those who said it whom we have not mentioned:

8687: al-Muthanna told me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih told us, saying: Muʿawiyah ibn Salih told me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship, and the orphans, and the needy﴾: God, mighty is His praise, commanded the believers, at the division of their inheritances, to join their kin and their orphans from the bequest, if he bequeathed; and if there was no bequest, he would deliver to them from their inheritance.

8688: Muhammad ibn Saʿd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship﴾, the verse, meaning: at the division of the inheritance.

8689: al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah: that his father gave him from the inheritance of al-Musʿab, when he divided his property.

8690: al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: ʿAwf informed us, from Ibn Sirin, who said: "They used to give them a small portion (yarduskhun) at the division." [[Radkhahu min malihi radikhah: he gave him a gift of property that was near or small.]]

8691: Bishr ibn Muʿadh told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saʿid told us, from Mutarr, from al-Hasan, from Hittan: that Abu Musa commanded that they be given, when the division of the inheritance is attended, the relatives, the orphans, the needy, and the poor neighbours.

8692: Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Yahya ibn Saʿid and Ibn Abi ʿAdi, and Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, from Shuʿbah, from Qatadah, from Yunus ibn Jubayr, from Hittan ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Raqashi, who said: "Abu Musa divided (an inheritance) by this verse: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship, and the orphans, and the needy﴾."

8693: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Muhammad and Yahya ibn Saʿid told us, from Shuʿbah, from Qatadah, from Yunus ibn Jubayr, from Hittan, from Abu Musa, concerning this verse: ﴿And when the division is attended﴾, the verse, who said: "Abu Musa ruled by it."

8694: Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Jarir told us, from Mughirah, from al-ʿAla' ibn Badr, concerning the inheritance when it is divided, who said: "They used to give from it the chest (al-tabut) and the thing whose division would be embarrassing." [[The word "al-tabut" here, and what it refers to, is unclear to me.]]

8695: Ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿla told us, saying: Dawud told us, from al-Hasan and Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who both used to say: "That is at the division of the inheritance."

8696: Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Sufyan, from ʿAsim, from Abu al-ʿAliyah and al-Hasan, who both said: "They give a small portion and say a kind word," concerning this verse: ﴿And when the division is attended﴾.

* *

Then those who said: "This verse is muhkam, and the division for the near kin, the orphans, and the needy is obligatory upon the heirs; if some of the heirs are minors and the inheritance is divided upon them, their guardian is responsible for them," differed.

Some of them said: The guardian of their property may not divide any of the property or the bequest from it, because he does not own any of the property; rather, he says to them a kind word. They said: The one God commanded to say a kind word to them is the guardian of the orphan's property when he divides the orphan's property between him and the orphan's co-sharers, unless the guardian of the property is one of the heirs, in which case he gives them from his share, and gives them from the shares of those whose command over the property is permitted. They said: As for the minor's property, the one to whom the property is entrusted may not give them anything from it.

Mention of those who said that:

8697: Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from al-Suddi, from Abu Saʿid, who said: "I asked Saʿid ibn Jubayr about this verse: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship, and the orphans, and the needy, then provide for them from it﴾, and he said: 'If the deceased bequeathed something to them, their bequest is carried out for them; and if the heirs are adults, they give them a small portion; and if they are minors, their guardian says: "I do not own this property, and it is not mine; it belongs to the minors." That is His saying: ﴿and speak to them a kind word﴾.'"

8698: Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar told us, saying: Shuʿbah told us, from Abu Bishr, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, concerning this verse: ﴿And when the division is attended by those of kinship, and the orphans, and the needy, then provide for them from it and speak to them a kind word﴾, he said: "They are two guardians: a guardian who inherits, and a guardian who does not inherit. As for the one who inherits, he gives; and as for the one who does not inherit, say to him a kind word."

٨٦٩٩ - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to me, from al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who both used to say: "That is at the time of dividing the inheritance. If the inheritance belongs to one who has reached maturity, he may clothe from it and feed the poor and the needy. But if the inheritance belongs to young orphans, the guardian says: 'Indeed, they are young orphans,' and says to them a kind word." [[The narration: ٨٦٩٩. In the printed edition it reads "Ibn Dawud narrated to us," which is an error caused by the manuscript. It was first written "haddathana," then "thana" was struck through and "thani" was written in its place, so the reader took it as "Ibn" and wrote what he wrote. "Dawud" is Dawud ibn Abi Hind, whose biography has already passed earlier: 1608, and in other places.]]

٨٧٠٠ - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-Suddi, from Abu Sa'd, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "If they are adults, they are given a small portion (ruḍkh); and if they are minors, they make an apology to them." [[The narration: ٨٧٠٠. In the printed edition: "from Abu Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr," but I have kept what is in the manuscript. "Abu Sa'd" is Abu Sa'd al-Arhabi al-Kufi, the reciter of the Azd. It is also said "Abu Sa'id," from whom Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Suddi al-Kabir narrated; he is described in al-Tahdhib.]]

٨٧٠١ - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasa, from Sulayman al-Shaybani, from Ikrima, regarding ﴿And when the division is attended by relatives﴾: he said, Ibn 'Abbas used to say: "If one is in charge of anything of that, he gives a small portion to the relatives of the deceased. And if he does not do so, he makes an apology to them and says to them a kind word."

٨٧٠٢ - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And when the division is attended by relatives, orphans and the needy, then provide for them from it and speak to them a kind word﴾: "This is of three kinds. As for one, he bequeaths to them a bequest, [[In the printed edition: "As for the first, he bequeaths to them...," as if he thought the wording of the report was an error, so he altered it to match his words afterwards: "As for the second." What is in the manuscript is very correct, and there is no reason to change it.]] so they attend and take their bequest. As for the second, they attend and divide, if they are men, and it is proper for them to give to them. As for the third, the heirs are minors, so their guardian stands up when dividing among them and says to those who attended: 'Your right is a right, and your kinship is a kinship. Had I a share in the inheritance I would have given to you, but they are young; when they grow up they will know your right.' This is the kind word." [[The narration: ٨٧٠٢. In the manuscript and the printed edition: "Ahmad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us," which is an error; the correct form is "Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us." His biography has already passed under number 7120, and its chain has been repeated hundreds of times correctly, the closest being number 8654.]]

٨٧٠٣ - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from a man, from Sa'id, that he said, regarding ﴿And when the division is attended by relatives, orphans and the needy, then provide for them from it and speak to them a kind word﴾: "If the heir is present at the division, and there is a vessel or a thing that cannot be divided, then he should give them a small portion. And if the inheritance belongs to orphans, then he should say to them a kind word."

* *

Others said: "That is obligatory regarding the property of minors and adults, for the relatives, orphans and the needy. If the heirs are adults, they themselves undertake giving them that at the division; and if they are minors, their guardian of property undertakes giving that on their behalf."
Those who said that:
٨٧٠٤ - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Yunus, regarding His saying: ﴿And when the division is attended by relatives, orphans and the needy, then provide for them from it﴾: he related from Muhammad, from 'Ubayda, that he was in charge of a bequest, so he ordered a sheep to be slaughtered and prepared food, because of this verse, and said: "Were it not for this verse, this would have been from my own property." He said: "And al-Hasan said: It was not abrogated. They used to attend and be given a thing, or a worn garment." He said: Yunus said: "Muhammad ibn Sirin was in charge of a bequest, or he said, of orphans, so he ordered a sheep to be slaughtered and prepared food, as 'Ubayda had done."

٨٧٠٥ - Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Hassan informed us, from Muhammad: that 'Ubayda divided the inheritance of orphans, so he ordered a sheep to be bought from their property, and food to be prepared, and said: "Were it not for this verse, I would have loved for it to be from my own property." Then he recited this verse: ﴿And when the division is attended by relatives, orphans and the needy, then provide for them from it﴾, to the end of the verse.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It seems that those who held the view we have mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and those who said, "A small portion is given at the division of inheritance to the relatives, orphans and the needy," interpreted His saying ﴿then provide for them from it﴾ as: give them from it. And it seems that those who went along with what 'Ubayda and Ibn Sirin said interpreted His saying ﴿then provide for them from it﴾ as: feed them from it.

* *

They differed concerning the interpretation of His saying ﴿and speak to them a kind word﴾.
Some of them said: It is a command from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, to the guardians of orphans, that they should say to their relatives, to the orphans and to the needy who attend their division of the property of which they are in charge, shared between them and their co-heirs in it, that they should make an apology to them, in the manner we have mentioned previously regarding apology, as:
٨٧٠٦ - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Bishr narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding ﴿and speak to them a kind word﴾: "It is the one who does not inherit; he is commanded to say to them a kind word. He says: 'This property belongs to absent people, or to young orphans, and you have a right in it, but we do not possess the power to give you anything from it.' This is the kind word."

* *

Others said: Rather, the one commanded to speak the kind word, which Allah, may His majesty be exalted, ordered to be said to them, is the man who makes a bequest from his property. The "kind word" is supplication for them for provision and wealth, and similar words of goodness. We have already mentioned those who said this earlier. [[In the printed edition, after his words "earlier," it adds "with what is sufficient without repeating it," as if he was comfortable with how often Abu Ja'far repeated such a sentence. But this phrase is not in the manuscript, and the discussion here does not need it.]]

**The meaning of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them. So let them keep their duty to God and speak words of appropriate justice.﴾ (9)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed over the meaning of this. Some of them said: "And let them fear" means: let those who attend a testator who makes a bequest from his wealth fear. Their concern should be that he not order his wealth to be distributed as a bequest to someone who is not his heir. Rather, they should order him to preserve his wealth for his children, just as if they themselves were the testator, who would be glad for someone attending him to urge him to protect his wealth for his children and not leave them dependent on others, weak and unable to manage or find a livelihood.

[[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "وصية به", and the correct reading is what I have adopted.]] [[See the discussion of "al-khashya" (fear, awe) above, 1:559-560, 2:239, 243, note 3. Then see "al-dhurriyya" (offspring) above, 3:19, 73; 5:543; 6:327, 361-362. Then the interpretation of "al-du'afa'" and "al-dhi'af" (the weak), 5:543, 551, and the following report no. 8708.]]

**Mention of those who said this:**

**8707** – Ali ibn Dawud told me: Abdullah ibn Salih told us: Mu'awiya ibn Salih told me, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his words: "And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them," to the end of the verse. This refers to a man whom death attends, and someone hears him make a bequest that harms his heirs. So God, glorified is He, commands whoever hears him to keep his duty to God, and He guides and directs him to what is right, and to look after his heirs as he would wish to be treated regarding his heirs if he feared they would be left in destitution.

**8708** – Ali told us: Abdullah ibn Salih told us: Mu'awiya told me, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talha, on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding his words: "And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them." He means: the one whom death attends, and it is said to him, "Give charity from your wealth, free slaves, and give from it in the way of God." They were forbidden to command him to do that. That is, whoever among you attends a sick man at the time of death, let him not command him to spend his wealth on freeing slaves, charity, or in the way of God. Rather, let him command him to state his wealth and what debts he owes, and to make a bequest from his wealth to his relatives who do not inherit, and to bequeath to them a fifth or a quarter. He says: Would not one of you dislike, when he dies and has weak children, meaning young ones, to leave them with no wealth so that they become dependent on people? So you should not command him to do what you would not be content with for yourselves or your children, but say what is right in this matter.

**8709** – Bishr ibn Mu'adh told us: Yazid told us: Sa'id told us, on the authority of Qatada regarding his words: "And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring," he said: Whoever attends a dying man should command him to justice and goodness, and forbid him from injustice and oppression in his bequest, and let him fear for his dependants what he would fear for them if death came upon him.

**8710** – al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: Ma'mar told us, on the authority of Qatada regarding his words: "And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring." He said: When you attend the bequest of a dead man, command him with what you would command yourself regarding that by which you draw near to God, and fear in this matter what you would fear for weak ones (ḍa'afa) if you left them behind after you. [[In the printed edition: "على ضعفتك" with an added kaf, but what is in the manuscript is entirely correct; by "ḍa'fa" he means: young children.]] He says: So keep your duty to God and speak appropriate words, if he deviates.

**8711** – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us: Asbat told us, on the authority of al-Suddi: "And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them; so let them keep their duty to God and speak appropriate words." This refers to a man whom death attends, and people attend him at the time of the bequest. It is not right for them to say to him, "Bequeath all your wealth and prepare for yourself, for God will provide for your dependants." Nor should they let him bequeath all his wealth. Rather, he says to those present: "And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them." That is: just as one of you fears for his dependants if he dies and leaves them young and weak with nothing, fearing their destitution after him, so let him fear for the dependants of his Muslim brother, and say to him the appropriate words. [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "أن يتركهم صغارًا ..." which does not make sense, so I have preferred "إذ يتركهم" and it would also be correct to read "إن تركهم صغارًا".]]

**8713** – al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His words: "And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring." **8714** – Yahya ibn Abi Talib told me: Yazid told us: Juwaybir told us, on the authority of al-Dahhak regarding His words: "And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring," to the end of the verse. **8715** – Muhammad ibn Amr told me: Abu Asim told us: Isa told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid regarding His words: "And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them," to the end of the verse. He said: This refers to one who distributes wealth at the time of division, and those present say, "You have given too little, give more to so-and-so." So God, exalted is He, says: "And let those fear who, if they left behind them," so let those people fear, and let them say regarding them what each of them would like said about his own child, with justice: if he gives too much, "Preserve something for your child."

\* \*

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "And let those fear who attend the testator while he makes his bequest," those "who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them destitution because of their weakness and youth," should forbid him from making a bequest to his relatives, and should command him to hold on to his wealth and keep it safe for his children. Had they been relatives of the testator, they would have been glad for him to bequeath to them.

**Mention of those who said this:**

He said: But it is the man whom death attends, and whoever attends him says to him, "Keep your duty to God, and hold on to your wealth, for no one has more right to your wealth than your child." And if the one making the bequest had relatives among them, they would have wished him to bequeath to them. [[The report 8716: "Miqsam," who is "Miqsam ibn Bajra." **8717** – al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us: Abd al-Razzaq told us: al-Thawri told us, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said: Miqsam said: They are the ones who say, "Keep your duty to God and hold on to your wealth." And if he had relatives among them, they would have wished him to bequeath to them.

So let him keep his duty to God, and command him to bequeath, even if he is the heir, or something similar. [[In the manuscript: "فليق الله هو قلت أمره بالوصية", which is not an understandable statement, and I have not found the correct meaning, so I have left what is in the printed edition as it is, though I consider the whole sentence unsatisfactory in both the manuscript and the printed edition, and I fear some part of it may have dropped out.]]

\* \*

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is a command from God to the guardians of orphans to care for them with goodness regarding their persons and their wealth, not to consume their wealth extravagantly or hastily before they grow up, and to treat them as they would like the guardians of their young children after them to treat them with goodness, if they were the ones who died and left their children as young orphans.

**Mention of those who said this:**

**8719** – Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me: my father told me: my paternal uncle told me: my father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them." He means by that the man who dies and has young, weak children, whom he fears will be left in poverty and destitution, and who fears that after him those who take charge of them will not treat them well. He says: So if someone takes charge of children like his own, weak orphans, let him treat them well, and not consume their wealth extravagantly or hastily for fear that they will grow up; let him keep his duty to God and speak appropriate words.

\* \*

Others said: The meaning of that is: "And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them; so let them keep their duty to God and speak appropriate words," God will spare them the matter of their descendants after them.

**Mention of those who said this:**

**8720** – Ibrahim ibn Atiyya ibn Ruday' ibn Atiyya told us: my paternal uncle Muhammad ibn Ruday' told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of al-Saybani, who said: We were in Constantinople during the days of Maslama ibn Abd al-Malik, and among us were Ibn Muhayriz, Ibn al-Daylami, and Hani' ibn Kulthum, who said: We began discussing what would happen at the end of time. He said: I was distressed by what I had heard. He said: I said to Ibn al-Daylami: O Abu Bishr, I wish I would never have a child! Shall I not direct you to a matter which, if you reach it, God will save you from it, and if you leave your children after you, God will protect them on your account? He said: I said: Yes! He said: Then he recited at that moment this verse: "And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them; so let them keep their duty to God and speak appropriate words." I have found none for "Muhammad ibn Ruday'," but he is mentioned in the biography of his father in al-Tahdhib as one whose son Muhammad narrated from him. He was a reliable Successor, one of the best of Muslims.

As for "Ibn al-Daylami," he is "Abdullah ibn Fayruz al-Daylami," Abu Bishr, also said Abu Bisr with a plain sin, who lived in Bayt al-Maqdis, narrated from a group of Companions, and al-Saybani narrated from him. He is a reliable Successor, biographed in al-Tahdhib.

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct interpretation of the verse is the view of those who said: its meaning is: "And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them destitution, if they had distributed their wealth during their lifetime, or divided it as a bequest from them to the close relatives, the orphans, and the needy, and kept their wealth for their children, out of fear of destitution for them after them, along with their weakness and inability to meet their needs. So let them command those who attend the one making the bequest to his close relatives, and to orphans and the needy and others, to bequeath from his wealth justly, and let them keep their duty to God and speak appropriate words, which is to make him know what God has permitted him regarding bequests, and what He has chosen for those who make bequests among the people of faith in God, His Book, and His Sunnah." [[In the printed edition: "وما اختاره المؤمنون ..." is an attempt at correcting what was in the manuscript, which read "وما اختاره المؤمنين ..." The context requires "للموصين" as I have adopted it, and the two are close in corruption.]]

\* \*

We only said that the interpretation of the verse is more correct than other interpretations because of what we have already mentioned earlier [[See what passed: 12 and what follows.]], that the meaning of His words: "And when the division is attended by close relatives, orphans, and the needy, then give them a bequest," is according to the evidence we have indicated.

\* \*

If that is the interpretation of His words: "And when the division is attended by close relatives, orphans, and the needy," to the end of the verse, then it is necessary that His words, may His remembrance be exalted, "And let those fear who, if they left behind them," be a disciplining from Him of His servants regarding the matter of bequest, in what He permitted them, since it follows the verse before it concerning the rule of bequest, and its most evident meaning is what we have said. So connecting its ruling to the ruling before it is more correct, given the similarity of their meanings, than directing its ruling to something else that is not comparable to it.

\* \*

Regarding the meaning of what we have said in the interpretation of His words, "and speak appropriate words," those whose statements we mentioned at the beginning of the interpretation of this verse said the same, and Ibn Zayd used to say this.

**8721** – Yunus told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them; so let them keep their duty to God and speak appropriate words." He said: Let him speak appropriate words, mentioning this poor man and benefiting him, and not wrong this orphan, the heir of the one who pays, nor harm him, for he is a child who cannot defend himself. So care for him as you would care for your child if they were young.

\* \*

"Al-sadid" in speech means justice and correctness.

The Interpretation of His Words: "Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly – they only consume fire into their bellies. And they will burn in a blaze" (4:10)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His majesty be praised, "Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly," He means: without right. "They only consume fire into their bellies," [meaning] on the Day of Resurrection, for their consuming the property of orphans unjustly in the world, the fire of Hell. "And they will burn" by their consuming "in a blaze."

Ibn Jarir's note: In the manuscript and the printed edition: "He means by that..." but the context requires what I have established.

Ibn Jarir's note: In the manuscript: "wa-inna Jahannam" (and indeed Hell), which is very corrupt; what is in the printed edition is close to the correct reading.

As for the narrations, Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) cites the following:

8722 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly, they only consume fire into their bellies," he said: When a man stands up consuming the property of an orphan unjustly, he will be raised on the Day of Resurrection with a flame of fire coming out of his mouth, his ears, his nose and his eyes, and whoever sees him will recognize him as one who consumed the property of an orphan.

Editor's note: In the printed edition: "ya'kul mal al-yatim" with a yā', while in the manuscript it is unpointed; the correct reading is with a bā' (ta'kul... ) as shown.

8723 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Abu Harun al-Abdi informed me, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) narrated to us about the night he was taken on the Night Journey, saying: "I looked, and behold, there were people who had lips like the lips of camels, and an angel had been assigned to them who would seize their lips, then place in their mouths a rock of fire which would come out of their lower parts. I said: O Jibril, who are these? He said: These are those who consume the property of orphans unjustly; they only consume fire into their bellies."

Note on the report: Abu Harun al-Abdi is 'Imarah ibn Juwayn. He narrated from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Ibn Umar. He is weak, and some said he was a liar. Al-Daraqutni said: "Yatalawwan (wavering), a Khariji and a Shi'i." Ibn Hibban said: "He used to narrate from Abu Sa'id what was not from his narrations; it is not permitted to write his hadith except as a matter of wonder." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.

The report is also transmitted by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 2:360, and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:124, attributing it to Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim.

8724 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "Indeed, those who consume the property of orphans unjustly, they only consume fire into their bellies and they will burn in a blaze," he said: My father said: This applies to the people of polytheism, when they did not give inheritance to them (the orphans) and consumed their property.

* *

As for His words, "And they will burn in a blaze" (wa-sayaslawna sa'iran): it is derived from "al-salā" and "al-sallā," which is being exposed to fire, that is, warming oneself by it, as al-Farazdaq said:

"Kalb al-hayy fought over the fire of its people, to lie down in it, and the warmth (al-sala) is surrounding it."

Note: In Lisan al-Arab under "ṣ-l-w," attributed to Imru' al-Qays, which is an error to be corrected. The verse is from a poem describing cold and drought days, praising his people. Its opening reads: "When the horizons of the sky grew dusty and the red, shivering wind uncovered the tents of the people..." The commentators explain: "Kalb" is the dog of the tribe; "al-sala" is the fire; "mutakannaf" means they have gathered around it and sat around it. Its meaning: whoever comes to us finds plenty and generosity in this year of drought.

And as al-Ajjaj said:

"And the hearth-stones (al-sāliyāt) are for the fire, burning."

Note: In the printed edition it read "wa-sāliyān," which is an error; the correct reading is from the manuscript and the diwan. "Al-sāliyāt" means the three stones on which pots are placed; "al-sala" is the fuel.

Then this was used for anyone who personally engages in any matter, whether war, fighting, dispute, or otherwise, as the poet said: [Al-Harith ibn Abbad al-Bakri]

"I was not among its (the war's) protectors, God knows, and today I am burning with its heat."

Note: Al-Fakhir of al-Mufaddal ibn Salama, and al-Khizanah; this is among his famous verses about the War of al-Basus. He had withdrawn from it, then plunged into it when he sent his son Bujayr to Muhalhil, who was killed by Muhalhil.

In the printed edition it read "li-harriha," a misreading of the manuscript.

So he made what one suffers from the severity of war and the harm of fighting, the same as suffering the harm and heat of fire.

* *

The readers differed regarding the recitation of this.

The majority of the readers of Medina and Iraq recited "wa-sayaslawna sa'iran" with a fatha on the yā', according to the interpretation we have stated. (Ibn Jarir's note: printed edition reads "qulna" without the hā'; I have kept the manuscript.)

* *

Some Meccan and some Kufan readers recited "wa-sayuslawna" with a ḍamma on the yā', meaning: they will be burned, from the saying "a roasted sheep" (shah maslīyah), meaning roasted.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The fatha is more correct than the ḍamma, because all the readers agree on the fatha of the yā' in His words, "None will burn in it except the most wretched" (92:15), and because of His words, "except one who is burning in Hellfire" (37:163), indicating that the fatha is preferable.

As for "sa'ir": it is the intensity of the heat of Hell. From it is said "istaʿarat al-harb" (the war blazed) when it intensified. It is originally "mas'ur," then it was changed to "sa'ir," as they said "kaff khadib" (a dyed hand) and "liḥya dahin" (an oiled beard), when originally it was "makhdub" (dyed) and changed to the form "fa'il."

Note: In the printed edition "qīla" without "kamā," the correct text is from the manuscript, but the scribe erred in writing it; the first editor deleted it.

* *

So the meaning of the speech is: "And they will burn in a fire that is kindled, that is, set ablaze, its heat intense."

And we said that this is so because Allah, may His majesty be praised, said, "And when Hellfire is kindled" (81:12), describing it as kindled.

Then He, may His majesty be praised, informed that the devourers of orphans' property will burn in it while it is as such. Thus "sa'ir" in this place is an attribute of Hellfire, as we have described.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 11 (part 1 of 3):

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Allah enjoins you concerning your children: for the male, the like of the portion of two females﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, "Allah enjoins you," exalted is His praise, He means: Allah charges you [[See the explanation of "awsa" (enjoin) in what has preceded, 3:94, 405.]] concerning your children, "for the male the like of the portion of two females." He says: Your Lord charges you that when one of you dies and leaves behind children, male and female, then his inheritance belongs to his sons and daughters together, and the male among them receives the like of the portion of two females, when he has no heir other than them. This applies equally to his young children and his adult children, and to his daughters, in that all of that is shared among them, the male receiving the like of the portion of two females.

The word "mithl" (like) is in the nominative as an attribute (ṣifah) [[The "ṣifah" here refers to the prepositional phrase, namely the "lam" in His words "lil-dhakar" (for the male).]], and it is not in the accusative governed by "yuwṣīkum Allāh" (Allah enjoins you), because "wasiyyah" (enjoining) in this context means charging and informing, which has the sense of saying, and "saying" does not take as its object the nouns that are reported. [[The "wuqū'" (taking an object) means transitivity to the direct object, as mentioned in 4:293, note 1, and in the indexes of technical terms.]] It is as if it were said: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to you: Concerning your children, for the male among them is the like of the portion of two females.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Prophet ﷺ as an explanation from Allah of the obligatory ruling concerning the inheritance of one who dies and leaves heirs, as He has made clear. This is because the people of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) used not to allot any share of a dead man's estate to any of his heirs after him who did not face the enemy or fight in wars, including his young children, and including the women among them. They would restrict this to the fighting men to the exclusion of the offspring. So Allah, exalted is His praise, informed that what the deceased leaves is to be divided among those whom He named and for whom He prescribed an inheritance in this verse and at the end of this surah. He said, concerning the young children of the deceased, his adult children, and his daughters: they have the inheritance of their father, when he has no heir other than them, "for the male the like of the portion of two females."

Mention of those who said this:

8725 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Allah enjoins you concerning your children: for the male the like of the portion of two females." The people of the Jahiliyyah used not to bequeath to the girls or the young boys; a man would inherit from his offspring only one who was able to fight. Then 'Abd al-Rahman, the brother of the poet Hassan, died, leaving a wife called Umm Kujjah, and five sisters. The heirs came to take his property, so Umm Kujjah complained of this to the Prophet ﷺ, and Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed this verse: "And if they are women above two, then for them is two-thirds of what he left, and if there is one, then for her is half" ... Then He said concerning Umm Kujjah: "And for them is the quarter of what you leave if you have no child, but if you have a child, then for them is the eighth." [[The report 8725: concerning "Umm Kujjah", see what has preceded in the note on report 8656, and her account there. In the printed edition and manuscript it reads "Umm Kuhhah" with a ḥāʾ. As for "'Abd al-Rahman the brother of the poet Hassan", he refers to Hassan ibn Thabit ibn al-Mundhir ibn Haram al-Ansari, the poet of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned him in al-Isabah, and cited the report of al-Suddi, then said, "I say: I have not seen it from anyone else, and the genealogists did not mention for Hassan a brother named 'Abd al-Rahman."]]

8726 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Allah enjoins you concerning your children: for the male the like of the portion of two females."
