That was because when the obligations which Allah imposed regarding the male child, the female child, and the parents were revealed, the people, or some of them, disliked them and said: "The woman is given a quarter or an eighth, and the daughter is given a half, and the young boy is given (a share), yet none of these fights the people or gains booty!! Be silent about this matter, perhaps the Messenger of Allah ﷺ will forget it, or we will say to him and he will change it." Some of them said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall we give the girl half of what her father left, though she does not ride a horse nor fight the people, and give the boy an inheritance though he is of no use?!" They used to do this in the Jahiliyyah, not giving inheritance except to one who fought, giving it to the oldest, then the next oldest. [[In the printed edition: "wa-yu'tūnahu al-akbar" with an extra waw that has no place; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, this was revealed because the property used to belong to the children before its revelation, and the bequest was for the parents; so Allah, blessed and exalted, abrogated that by this verse.

Mention of those who said this:

8727 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid or 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: "Allah enjoins you concerning your children." He said: The property belonged to the child, and the bequest was for the parents and the relatives; then Allah abrogated from that what He willed, making for the male the like of the portion of two females, and making for the two parents, each one of them, a sixth with the child, and for the husband a half or a quarter, and for the wife a quarter or an eighth. [[Report 8727: al-Bukhari narrated it through Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas. (al-Fath 8:184, 12:19).]]

8728 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Allah enjoins you concerning your children: for the male the like of the portion of two females." He said: Ibn 'Abbas used to say: The property belonged (to the children), and the bequest was for the parents and relatives; then Allah, blessed and exalted, abrogated from that what He willed, making for the male the like of the portion of two females. Then he mentioned something similar.

8729 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

It is narrated from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah that:

* *

8730 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated this to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, who said: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon me while I was ill, so he performed ablution and sprinkled on me from his water; I regained consciousness and said: "O Messenger of Allah, only kalalah inherits from me, so how is the inheritance?" Then the verse of the inheritance was revealed. [[Hadith 8730: al-Bukhari narrated it (Fath 1:261), through Shu'bah, with this chain. What follows this is the narration of Ibn Jurayj, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir. Likewise al-Bukhari narrated it (8:182) through Ibn Jurayj, and al-Bukhari also narrated it (10:98 and 12:2) through Sufyan, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir. Ibn Kathir mentioned it (2:362) from the narration of al-Bukhari through Ibn Jurayj, then said, "Thus Muslim and al-Nasa'i narrated it from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Muhammad al-A'war, from Ibn Jurayj, with this; and all of them narrated it from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir." Al-Suyuti mentioned it (2:124-125) and added its attribution to 'Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan.]]

8731 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj who said: Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir narrated to me, from Jabir who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him) visited me while I was in the Banu Salamah, walking, and they found me unable to think clearly. So he asked for water, performed ablution, then sprinkled on me; I regained consciousness and said: "O Messenger of Allah, how shall I deal with my property?" Then "Allah enjoins you concerning your children: for the male the like of the portion of two females" was revealed. ... [[Hadith 8731: it is a repetition of the hadith before it, as we have pointed out. In the printed edition: "fa-da'a bi-wudu'in fa-tawaḍḍa'a"; in the manuscript: "fa-da'a fa-tawaḍḍa'a"; and in al-Bukhari through this route: "fa-da'a bi-ma'". The likeliest is that Tabari's text had "bi-ma'", and a copyist inadvertently dropped the word "bi-ma'", the final letters of "da'a" being confused with "bima" since they often omit the hamzah.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And if they are women above two, then for them is two-thirds of what he left﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, "And if they are," meaning: if the ones left behind are "women above two," and by "women" he means the daughters of the deceased, "above two," he says: more than two in number, "then for them is two-thirds of what he left," he says: then for his daughters are two-thirds of what he left behind of his inheritance, to the exclusion of the rest of his heirs, if the deceased left no male child with them. The scholars of Arabic grammar differed regarding the meaning of His words "if they are women."

Some of the grammarians of Basra said in line with what we have said: "If the ones left behind are women." This is also the view of some grammarians of Kufa.

Others among them said: Rather, the meaning is: "If the children are women," and he said: Allah mentioned the children, saying, "Allah enjoins you concerning your children," then divided the bequest, saying, "If they are women," and if the children were [women, and if the children were one] as a rendering by him of "the children."

Abu Ja'far said: The first view I have reported from those Basran scholars is more correct in my opinion. Because His words "wa-in kunna" (if they are), had it referred to "the children," would have been "wa-in kanu" (if they are, masculine), since "al-awlad" (the children) comprises males and females. And when that is so, one says "kanu," not "kunna."

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And if she is alone, then for her is half; and for his parents, to each one of them is a sixth of what he left, if he has a child﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, "And if she is," [and if she is] the one left behind is a single daughter [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "wa-in kanat al-matrukah ibnatan wahidah", which does not stand, so I added what is between the brackets, following the context of his explanation of its sisters.]] "then for her is half," he says: for that single one is half of what the deceased left of his inheritance, if there is with her no other child of the deceased, male or female.

* *

If someone says: This is the prescribed share of a single woman and of more than two women; where is the prescribed share of two?

It is said: Their prescribed share is by the transmitted Sunnah, the transmission of inheritance in which doubt is not permitted. [[He apparently means by this the hadith of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah concerning the death of Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ giving his two daughters two-thirds (al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi 6:229), which Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah narrated through several routes; and the report of Zayd ibn Thabit: "If a man and a woman leave a daughter, then for her is half, and if they are two or more, then for them is two-thirds..." narrated by al-Bukhari (al-Fath 12:8). Yet it is strange that Abu Ja'far leaves out the wording of the reports as his proof at this point; I fear that some of the early copyists dropped part of his book, or that he intended to cite the reports and then forgot them, and the later copies remained lacking the evidence of his argument. This is the first time Abu Ja'far departs from his method in compiling this tafsir.]]

* *

As for His words, "and for his parents," he means: and for the two parents of the deceased, "to each one of them is a sixth" of his estate and what he left behind of his property, the mother and father being equal in this, neither of them receiving more than a sixth, "if he has a child," whether the child is male or female, single or many.

* *

If someone says: If this is the interpretation, then it would follow that the father should not receive more than a sixth of the inheritance from his dead child when there is a single daughter. Saying this would contradict what the Community (ummah) is unanimously agreed upon, in their assigning the remainder of the deceased's estate, after the daughter has taken her share, entirely to the father!

It is said: The matter is not as you supposed. Rather, each of the deceased's two parents has a sixth of his estate with his child, whether the child is male or female, single or many, as a fixed obligation from Allah for him. Then what is added beyond that from the remainder of the half with the single daughter, when there is no one other than her and the deceased's other parent, is added to them secondly by reason of the nearness of the deceased's agnatic kin to him [[In the printed edition: "fa-in zīda 'ala dhalika min baqiyat al-nisf", and I have kept what was in the manuscript, which is the better reading.]], since the rule regarding whatever the shares of the prescribed portions leave is that it belongs to the nearest male agnates of the deceased, by the ruling of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [[This refers to what the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated with their chain to Ibn 'Abbas from the Prophet ﷺ who said, "Give the prescribed shares to their people; then what remains belongs to the nearest male" (al-Fath 2:8, 9 / al-Sunan al-Kubra 6:234). It is also narrated as "li-adna rajul," meaning the nearest man of the agnates. This too is a strange omission by Abu Ja'far of the proof from hadith, as is his habit in all that preceded; see p. 36, note 1. It seems he was abridging at this point and omitted his proof, because he must have fully documented it in its place in his other books.]], and the father is the nearest agnate of his son and the most entitled to him, when the dead son has no son.

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And if he has no child and his parents inherit from him, then for his mother is a third﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, exalted is His praise, "If he has no child," if the deceased has no "child," male or female, "and his parents inherit from him," to the exclusion of any other child or heir, "then for his mother is a third," he says: then for his mother is a third of his entire estate and what he left behind after him.

* *

If someone says: Then who has the other two-thirds?

It is said to him: The father.

If he says: By what? [[In the printed edition: "fa-in qala qa'il: bi-madha?" with the extra word "qa'il", which is clearly an addition; the correct reading is as in the manuscript.]] I say: By being the nearest of the deceased's kin to him. [[In the manuscript: "bi-annahu aqrab walad al-mayyit ilayhi", which is an error by the copyist; the correct reading is from the printed edition.]] For this reason he omitted mentioning who has the remaining two-thirds, since he had already made clear, by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, to His servants [[See the earlier note, p. 37, note 3.]] that for every deceased person, his nearest agnate is the most entitled to his inheritance, after the holders of prescribed shares have received their shares of the inheritance.

This reason is the one for which the mother was assigned what was assigned to her, when the deceased left no heir other than his two parents, because the mother is not an agnate in any circumstance for the deceased. So Allah, exalted is His praise, made clear to His servants what He prescribed for her from the inheritance of her dead child, and omitted mention of who has the remaining two-thirds with her, since He had already informed them, in the general course of His explanation, who has the remaining portions of the property after the people of the shares have taken their shares and prescribed portions; and that explanation was sufficient for them, without repeating the ruling with each person to whom He assigns a right in the inheritance of a dead person and whose share He names. [[In the printed edition: "wa-kana bayanuhu dhalika mu'inan lahum 'ala takrir hukmihi", which is a plain error and a bad construction; in the manuscript: "mughnian lahum 'an takrir hukmihi", which is the correct reading I have adopted.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿And if he has brothers, then for his mother is a sixth﴾

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says: What is the meaning for which He mentioned the ruling on the two parents together with the siblings, and left out mention of their ruling with a single brother?

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 11 (part 2 of 3):

Qultu [[The word "qultu" ("I say") is not in the manuscript, but the context requires it, so the editor was right to include it in the text.]] The difference in their ruling between a group of siblings and a single sibling. In God's making clear to His servants their ruling regarding what they inherit from their deceased child together with his siblings, there is sufficiency and adequacy, so that there is no need to say that their ruling regarding what they inherited from him remains unchanged from what it was for them when the deceased had no brother and no heir other than them. This is because it was known to them that everyone who is entitled to a right by God's decree, that right which his Lord, may He be exalted, has decreed for him does not pass from what He decreed for him to another, except by God transferring it from him to whomever He transfers it to among His creation. So in His decree, may He be exalted in remembrance, concerning the mother, what He decreed was, when the deceased child had no heir other than her and his father, and no brother = [[In the printed edition: "... and other than his father, the clear evidence is manifest ..." This is something Abu Ja'far would never write. In the manuscript: "and other than his father, the evident indication ...", and the correct reading is "and no brother" conjoined to his saying "when her deceased child has no heir ...". His saying "the clear evidence" is the subject of "kana" (was) in his saying "and it was in His decree, may He be exalted in remembrance ..."]] the clear evidence for creation that this prescribed share, which is a third of her deceased child's property [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "is a third of her deceased child's property", without the "wa" (and), and the correct reading includes it, otherwise the sentence is disrupted.]] is a right owed to her, until that prescribed share is changed by the one who prescribed it for her. When He, may He be exalted in remembrance, changed what He had prescribed for her in this respect with a group of siblings, and left it unchanged with a single brother, it became known by this that her share remains unchanged from what was prescribed for her, except in the state in which the one whose obedience is binding on the servants changed it, and not in other states.
* *
Then the interpreters of the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about the number of siblings whom God, may He be exalted in remembrance, meant by His saying: "If he has siblings."
A group of the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ and the Successors who followed them in excellence, and the scholars of the Muslims after them in every era said: God, may He be exalted, meant by His saying: "If he has siblings, then for his mother is a sixth," two or more, whether they were two females or more females, or two males or more males, or one male and one female. Many of those who said this argued that this was stated by the community (ummah) on the explanation of God, may He be exalted, through the tongue of His Messenger ﷺ, and that the community of his Prophet transmitted it by widespread transmission (mustafid), which removes any excuse for its arrival and removes doubt from the hearts of creatures regarding its narration. [[This too is a place where there is something in the soul about it, for Abu Ja'far omitted the sequence of his evidence from the reports, as he did in the two previous places. See p. 36 note 1, and p. 37 note 3. Then see al-Bayhaqi's al-Sunan al-Kubra 6: 227, 228.]]
* *
It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he used to say: Rather, God, may He be exalted, meant by His saying: "If he has siblings," a group whose minimum is three. He used to deny that God, may He be exalted, would block the mother from her third together with the father by fewer than three siblings. So he would say, regarding a case of two parents and two siblings: the mother has a third, and what remains is for the father, just as the people of knowledge said regarding two parents and one brother.
Mention of the report from him to this effect:
8732 - My teacher Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Hakam told me, saying: Ibn Abi Fudayk told us, saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'b told me, from Shu'ba, the mawla (client) of Ibn Abbas, from Ibn Abbas: that he entered upon Uthman, may God be pleased with him, and said: Why do two brothers reduce the mother to a sixth, when God only said: "If he has siblings," and two brothers in the language of your people and the speech of your people are not siblings? Then Uthman, may God have mercy on him, said: Can I overturn a matter that existed before me, which the people have inherited and which has gone on in the cities? [[The report 8732: it was cited by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 6: 227 through the chain: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Shababa, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Shu'ba, mawla of Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Kathir quoted it in his tafsir 2: 367. Ibn Kathir commented on it, saying: "There is doubt about the soundness of this report, for this Shu'ba was criticized by Malik ibn Anas. Had this been sound from Ibn Abbas, his special companions would have adopted it, but what is transmitted from them is the opposite. Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad has narrated from Kharija ibn Zayd, from his father, that he said: 'The two brothers are called siblings,' and I have devoted a separate treatise to this question."
As for "Shu'ayb, the mawla of Ibn Abbas," he is Shu'ayb ibn Dinar al-Hashimi, who is other than the Kufan. Ibn Hibban said of him: "He narrated from Ibn Abbas what has no basis, to the point that he seems to be another Ibn Abbas." See the disagreement of the scholars regarding him in al-Tahdhib, and most of them abandoned using him as evidence. He is biographized in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/2: 244, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1: 367.]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The correct position in this matter, in my view, is that what is meant by His saying: "If he has siblings" is two or more of the deceased's siblings, according to what the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ said, and not what Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said, because the community inherited the transmission of the soundness of what they said on this matter from authoritative evidence, and because they rejected what Ibn Abbas said on it. [[This too is a place where Abu Ja'far should have set out his evidence, or referred to an earlier evidence, but he did not do so. See the previous note, p. 40 note 1, and the reference to the earlier places there.]]
* *
If someone says: How is it said of two brothers "siblings" (ikhwa), when you know that "two brothers" (al-akhawan) in the speech of the Arabs has a pattern that does not resemble the pattern of "siblings" in their speech?! [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "And you know that al-akhawan in the speech of the Arabs has a pattern ...", which is corrupt, and the correct reading is "that li-al-akhawayn" (for the two brothers), as I have written it with the added "lam".]]
It is said: Although that is so, it is part of the nature of the two statements to be joined together when their meanings are close, even if they differ in some aspects. Since this is so, and since it was widespread and common in their speech and used in their discourse: "I struck the heads of Abdullah and Amr, and I hurt their backs," and this was more widespread in their speech than saying "I hurt their two backs (zahrayhima)," even though it has been said: "I hurt their two backs (zahrayhima)," [[In the printed edition: "zahrahuma" in place of "zahrayhima", which is an error, because it is not evidence in this place. The evidence is what came in the manuscript as I have written it, in the dual form.]] just as al-Farazdaq said:
By what is in our two hearts of longing and passion, and the one with the broken, love-struck heart is healed.
Yet that wording, though it has been said, is less eloquent than: "By what is in our hearts (afida)," just as God, may He be exalted, said: "If you two turn in repentance to God, your hearts have indeed inclined" [Surah al-Tahrim: 4].
So since what you described = of bringing out everything that was in a human as singular when another one from another human is joined to the single one, so that they become two from two, with a plural expression, is more eloquent in their speech and more well-known in their discourse [[In the printed edition: "the plural expression is more eloquent in their speech", and the correct reading is what I have written from the manuscript. His saying "more eloquent" is the predicate of his saying "since what you described".]] = and since "the two brothers" are two persons, each one different from the other, from two separate selves, their two meanings resemble the meaning of what was in a human of organs that is single with no second [[In the printed edition: "their meaning resembles", in the singular, and the correct reading from the manuscript is the dual. His saying "and the two brothers" is conjoined to his saying "since what you described", meaning: "and since the two brothers ...". The sentence's structure: "and the two brothers were two persons ... their two meanings resembled the meaning of what was in a human of organs singular."]] so the dual of the two organs you described was brought out in its dual form [[In the printed edition: "so their two testicles (anthayayhima) were brought out in the form of the singular 'testicle' (unthā al-ʿudwayn)", which is a sentence without meaning, and the correct reading is from the manuscript, for the discussion concerns "the two" and "the plural", not "the female" and "the male".]], so "siblings" is said with the meaning of "the two brothers," just as "backs" (zuhur) is said with the meaning of "the two backs," and "mouths" (afwah) with the meaning of "two mouths," and "hearts" (qulub) with the meaning of "two hearts."
* *
Some grammarians have said: "Siblings" (ikhwa) is only said because the minimum of the plural is two. That is because two things were joined together, and they became together after being two separate singulars, so they were made plural, so that it would be known that two is a plural.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: Although this is so in meaning, it is not a cause that indicates the permissibility of bringing out the dual through a pattern and form other than the pattern and form of three or more, which has already been used in the speech of the Arabs widely and commonly on their tongues. For whoever says, "Your two brothers stood up," there is no doubt that he knows that each of the "two brothers" is a single unit, joined together with another, so that they became together after having been separate. However, even though this is so, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "after being separate, the title of the matter, even though this is so," which is an odious sentence with no meaning. The copyist hurried, as you have seen and known, and wrote "however the matter," "the title of the matter," so the sentence became corrupt, and this misled the first publisher in his understanding of the meanings.]] the Arabs do not permit in their speech that one says, "Your two brothers did (plural) stand up," so that the verb "stood up" (qamu), which is a plural form referring to the group, is used to refer to "the two brothers" who are in the dual form. This is because everything that has been used in their speech, known to them by a pattern and form, if someone changes what they have known about it, they reject it. [[In the printed edition: "because for everything that has been used in their speech there is a known pattern and form among them, and if someone changes what they know about them, he rejects it," in place of what was in the manuscript, which was a transposition that made "a pattern" into "patterns," moved it from its place, and changed the whole sentence as you have seen. What caused this is that the copyist wrote "because for everything that has been used" and the correct reading is "because everything that has been used," as I have written it.
As for "nakiruhu" (they rejected it), he made it "ankaruhu" (they denied it), and both are correct, except that it was incumbent on him to keep what is in the manuscript. It is said: "He rejected the thing, rejection and rejection (nakr, on the pattern of sami'a)." God, may He be exalted, said in Surah Hud, 70: {When he saw their hands not reaching toward it, he disliked them and felt a fear of them} [Hud: 70].]] Likewise, "the two brothers," even when they are in the dual, one of them joined to his companion, have a pattern in speech and a form that is other than the pattern and form of three or more of them. It is not permissible to change one into the other except with a understood meaning. Since this is so, no saying is more correct than what we said before.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: If someone says: Why is the mother reduced from her third when the siblings of the deceased become two or more with her?
It is said: The scholars differed about this.
Some of them said: The mother is reduced from that, but not the father, because the maintenance of the siblings is upon the father, not upon their mother.
Mention of those who said this:
8733 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh told us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurai' told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: "If he has no child and his parents inherit from him, then for his mother is a third. If he has siblings, then for his mother is a sixth." They harm the mother, and they do not inherit, and one brother does not block her from the third, but more than that does. The people of knowledge used to hold that they only blocked their mother from the third because their father is responsible for their marriage and their maintenance, not their mother. [[The report 8733: Ibn Kathir cited it in his tafsir 2: 367, 368, and said, "This is a good statement," and al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 126.]]
* *
Others said: Rather, the mother is reduced by a sixth, and she is limited to one sixth, as an aid to the deceased's siblings with the sixth that they blocked their mother from.
Mention of those who said this:
8734 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The sixth that the siblings blocked the mother from, they only blocked their mother from it so that it would be theirs and not their mother's.
* *
It has been narrated from Ibn Abbas a view contrary to this, and it is what follows:
8735 - Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Uyayna informed us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The kalala (one who leaves neither child nor parent) is the one who has no child and no parent.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The most correct position on this matter is to say: God, may He be exalted in remembrance, prescribed for the mother with siblings a sixth, for what He knows better about the benefit of His creation = and it is possible that this was for what He imposed on fathers for their children = and it is possible that this was for something else. This is not among what He obliged us to know, rather we were only commanded to act upon what we know.
* *
As for what is narrated from Tawus from Ibn Abbas, it is a statement contrary to what the community holds. This is because there is no disagreement among all of them that a deceased brother has no inheritance alongside his father. Their consensus against it is sufficient as evidence of its falsity.
* *
On the interpretation of God's words, may He be exalted: "After a bequest he makes or a debt" [Surah al-Nisa: 11].

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "after any bequest he may have bequeathed or a debt" (min ba'di wasiyyatin yusi biha aw dayn), Allah, exalted is His mention, means that the portion which Allah, blessed and exalted, has apportioned to the children of the deceased, males and females, and to his parents from his estate after his death, He apportions to them as He has apportioned in this verse, after the settlement of the debt of the deceased who died owing it from his estate, and after the execution of his bequest in its proper place (fi babiha) after the settlement of all his debt. [[So it is in the printed edition, "fi babiha", while in the manuscript it is undotted, and it is an unusual word here, which I do not think was current on the tongues of the people at that time with this meaning; if I were given the choice I would choose "fi ahliha" (among its people), but I have left it as it is for fear that my opinion may be mere conjecture.]] Thus Allah, exalted is His mention, did not assign to any of the heirs of the deceased, nor to anyone to whom a bequest was made, anything except after the settlement of his debt from the whole of his estate, even if it encompasses all of that. Then, after the settlement of his debt, He made the recipients of bequests partners of his heirs in what remains, for what was bequeathed to them, so long as it does not exceed one third of it. If it exceeds one third, He placed the choice in permitting what exceeds the third, or returning it to his heirs: if they wish they may permit the excess over one third, and if they wish they may reject it. As for what is up to the third, it is binding upon them.

All of what we have said on this is the consensus of the community (ummah). And a report has been transmitted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to this effect, namely what:

8736 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun related to us, saying: Sufyan informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith al-A'war, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "You recite this verse: 'after any bequest he may have bequeathed or a debt', and indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ decided the debt before the bequest." [[In the printed edition: "anna rasul Allah" without the waw; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

8737 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun related to us, saying: Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'ida related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), from the Prophet ﷺ, with the like of it.

8738 - Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath related to us, saying: Ash'ath related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from Ali, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the like of it. [[The reports 8736, 8737, 8738: a weak hadith, because of the weakness of "al-Harith al-A'war", who is al-Harith ibn Abd Allah al-A'war al-Hamdani, who is very weak; al-Sha'bi and others said: "He was a liar." The discussion of him has passed at no. 174 in what my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad wrote, and in al-Musnad no. 565.
All three of its chains revolve around "al-Harith al-A'war", and Ahmad related it in his Musnad, nos. 595, 1091, 1221, in full; al-Bayhaqi recorded it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 6:267; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 4:336; Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 2:368, where he said, "Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah and the authors of the exegeses related it"; and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:126, attributing it to Abu Shaybah, Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan. Al-Shafi'i related it in al-Umm 4:29, abridged as al-Tabari related it; al-Shafi'i said: "A report has been transmitted from the Prophet ﷺ regarding giving precedence to the debt over the bequest, a hadith which the people of hadith do not affirm the like of." He then cited the hadith from Sufyan from Abu Ishaq.
Al-Bayhaqi said: "The reluctance of the people of hadith to affirm this is because al-Harith al-A'war alone transmitted it from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), and al-Harith is not to be relied upon, since the memorizers have criticized him." As for al-Hakim, he mentioned a similar defect in al-Harith al-A'war and said: "For this reason al-Shaykhan did not record it, but this legal opinion has been authenticated from Zayd ibn Thabit," and then he cited Zayd ibn Thabit's opinion with its chain.
Ibn Kathir said: "Then al-Tirmidhi said: We do not know it except from the hadith of al-Harith al-A'war, and some scholars have spoken about him." I (Ibn Kathir, the speaker) say: "But he was a memorizer of the inheritance laws, careful about them and about calculation."]]

8739 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Harun ibn al-Mughira related to us, from Ibn Mujahid, from his father, regarding "after any bequest he may have bequeathed or a debt": he said, one begins with the debt before the bequest.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed in reading this. The majority of the reciters of Madina and Iraq read it: ﴿yūṣī bihā aw dayn﴾ (active).

* *

Some of the reciters of Makka, Syria and Kufa read it: ﴿yūṣā bihā﴾ (passive), in the sense of the unnamed agent.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings is the reading of the one who reads it: ﴿min baʿdi waṣiyyatin yūṣī bihā aw dayn﴾ in the sense of the named agent, because the whole verse is a report about one whose agent has been named. Do you not see that He says: "And for his parents, to each one of them is a sixth of what he leaves if he has a child"? Likewise, what is more appropriate with His words "he bequeaths with it or a debt" is that it be a report about one whose agent has been named, because the meaning of the speech is: "And for his parents, to each one of them is a sixth of what he leaves if he has a child, after a bequest he bequeathes or a debt, it is settled on his behalf."

* *

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Your fathers and your sons, you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, exalted is His mention, "your fathers and your sons", He means those concerning whom Allah has enjoined you, regarding the division of the inheritance of your deceased among them, as He has named and explained to you in this verse: your fathers and your sons [[The context of this phrase: "these are those concerning whom Allah has enjoined you ... your fathers and your sons", intending the grammatical analysis of "your fathers and your sons", that it is the predicate of an omitted subject. No one among the exegetes has pointed to this analysis. Rather, al-Qurtubi said in his tafsir: "It is in the nominative by being the subject, and the predicate is implied; its estimate is: they are the ones divided among, and they are the ones given." Al-Alusi said in his tafsir: "The address is to the heirs, 'your fathers' is the subject, 'your sons' is conjoined to it, and 'you do not know' with what is in its scope is its predicate." Likewise al-Ukbari said in I'rab al-Qur'an 1:94. The best saying is what Abu Ja'far said in the context of this verse.]] — "you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit", he says: give them their rights from the inheritance of your deceased, which I have enjoined you to give them, for you do not know which of them is nearer and more beneficial to you in the speedy affairs of your worldly life and the deferred affairs of your next life.

* *

The people of interpretation differed regarding His words: "you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit."

Some of them said: By this is meant which of them is nearer to you in benefit in the Hereafter.

Those who said that:

8740 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "Your fathers and your sons, you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit", he says: the most obedient to Allah among the fathers and sons, the highest of you in rank on the Day of Resurrection, because Allah, glorified is He, intercedes for the believers on behalf of one another.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit in this world.

Those who said that:

8741 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "which of them is nearer to you in benefit", in this world.

8742 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

8743 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi regarding His words: "you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit", some of them said: in benefit of the Hereafter, and some of them said: in benefit of this world.

* *

Others said regarding that what we have said.

Those who said that:

8744 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit", he said: which of them is better for you in religion and the world: the parent or the child who inherit from you, no one else having entered upon you, He prescribed for them the inheritances, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "fard lahum" (fardi), which is a distortion and a scribal error by the copyist, and has no meaning; the correct reading is what I have set down.]] He did not bring others who would share with them in your wealth.

* *

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿a duty from Allah; indeed Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ (11)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, exalted is His mention, "a duty from Allah" and "if he has brothers, then for his mother is a sixth", a duty, he says: determined portions, specified and defined by Allah for them. [[His words "muwaqqata", i.e., limited and determined by a limit; the explanation of this word has passed earlier, vol. 7:597, note 3, and the references there, and in the glossary of terms.
Then see the explanation of "al-fard" and "al-fari-da" previously at 4:121 / 5:120 / 7:597.]]

* *

The words "fariḍatan" are in the accusative as a verbal noun from His words: "Allah enjoins you regarding your children: for the male, the like of the portion of two females" — "a duty" — so "a duty" is removed from the meaning of the speech, since its meaning is what I have described.

It is also permissible that its accusative be on the basis of an emphatic circumstance from His words: "if he has brothers, then for his mother is a sixth" — "a duty", so that "al-fariḍa" is in the accusative as an emphatic circumstance of His words: "if he has brothers, then for his mother is a sixth", just as you say: "It is a gift to you, and it is a charity from me to you." [[See what has passed at 7:599.]]

* *

As for His words, "indeed Allah is ever Knowing and Wise", He, exalted is His mention, means: indeed Allah has never ceased to be possessed of knowledge of what benefits His creation, O people, so follow what He commands you, and He will set your affairs right for you. "Wise": he says, He has never ceased to be possessed of wisdom in His management, and He is so in what He apportions to some of you from the inheritance of others, and in what He decides among you of rulings, no flaw or error entering His judgment, for it is the judgment of one from whom the places of benefit, in the beginning and in the end, are not hidden.

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿And for you is half of what your wives leave, if they have no child. But if they have a child, then for you is a quarter of what they leave, after any bequest they make or debt.﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: Thereby He, may His praise be exalted, means: "And for you," O people, "is half of what your wives leave" after their death, of wealth and inheritance, "if they have no child," on the day death comes to them, "neither male nor female." "But if they have a child," meaning: if your wives have a male or female child on the day death comes to them, "then for you is a quarter of what they leave," of wealth and inheritance, as an inheritance for you from them, "after any bequest they make or debt," meaning: that is for you as an inheritance from them, from what remains of their estates and wealth, after the settlement of their debts which they owed, and after the execution of their lawful bequests, if they made any.

* *

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿And for them is a quarter of what you leave, if you have no child. But if you have a child, then for them is an eighth of what you leave, after any bequest you make or debt.﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, "And for them is a quarter of what you leave if you have no child," meaning: and for your wives, O people, is a quarter of what you leave after your death, of wealth and inheritance, if death comes to one of you and he has no child, male or female. "But if you have a child," meaning: if death comes to one of you and he has a child, male or female, whether one child or several, "then for them is an eighth of what you leave," meaning: then for your wives at that time, from your wealth and estate which you leave behind after your death, is an eighth, after the settlement of your debts which you owed when death came to you, and after the execution of your lawful bequests which you make.

* *

It was said, "after a bequest you make or a debt," placing the mention of the bequest before the mention of the debt, because the meaning of the statement is: what I have prescribed for those of you whom I have prescribed in these verses is only theirs after the removal of whichever of these two is in the property of the deceased among you, whether a bequest or a debt. Therefore it is the same whether the mention of the bequest comes before the mention of the debt or the mention of the debt comes before the bequest, because the meaning does not intend that both things, "the debt and the bequest," be removed from his property, so that mentioning the debt first would be more appropriate than mentioning the bequest.

* *

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿And if a man leaves an inheritance as kalala (one with neither ascendant nor descendant heirs), or a woman﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "And if a man or a woman leaves an inheritance as kalala."

Then the reciters differed regarding the recitation of this.

* *

The majority of the reciters of the Muslim community recited it: ﴿And if a man leaves an inheritance as kalala﴾, meaning: and if a man is inherited from by one whose lineage encircles him (i.e., collateral relatives).

* *

Here "kalala," according to this reading, is a verbal noun from their saying: "the lineage encircled him (takallalahu al-nasab) with encircling (takullulan) and kalala," meaning: lineage enveloped him.

* *

Some of them recited it: ﴿And if a man leaves an inheritance as kalala﴾, meaning: and if a man bequeaths to one who encircles him, meaning: one who surrounds him by lineage, such as a brother or a sister.

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning "kalala."

Some of them said: it is what is other than the father and the child.

Those who said this:

8745 - Al-Walid ibn Shuja' al-Sakuni narrated to us, saying: ʿAlī ibn Mushir told me, from ʿĀṣim, from al-Shaʿbī, who said: Abu Bakr (may Allah have mercy on him) said: "I have formed an opinion regarding the kalala. If it is correct, it is from Allah alone, without partner; and if it is an error, it is from me and from Satan, and Allah is free of it" — that kalala is other than the child and the father. When ʿUmar (may Allah have mercy on him) became caliph, he said: "I am truly ashamed before Allah, blessed and exalted, to oppose Abu Bakr in an opinion he held."

[Footnote: Report 8745 — Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan 6:223-224, and Ibn Kathir and al-Baghawi 2:370, and al-Durr al-Manthur 2:250, attributing it also to ʿAbd al-Razzaq, Saʿīd ibn Mansūr, Ibn Abi Shayba, and Ibn al-Mundhir. In al-Durr and al-Bayhaqi: "When ʿUmar was stabbed," and in Ibn Kathir: "When ʿUmar took office," and one of al-Bayhaqi's narrations and al-Baghawi's narration, like al-Tabari's: "When he became caliph." In the printed edition: "and Abu Bakr (may Allah be pleased with him)," and likewise for "ʿUmar"; I have retained what is in the manuscript in this place and what follows, and I did not draw attention to it in what follows. In the manuscript and printed edition: "fa-minnī wal-Shayṭān" without "min," and the correct version is from Tafsir Ibn Kathir and al-Baghawi in its margin 2:370, and al-Durr al-Manthur 2:250.]

8746 - Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal informed us, saying: al-Shaʿbī narrated to us: that Abu Bakr (may Allah have mercy on him) said concerning the kalala: "I say about it according to my opinion; if it is correct, it is from Allah: it is what is other than the child and the father." He said: When ʿUmar (may Allah have mercy on him) came to power, he said: "I am truly ashamed before Allah to oppose Abu Bakr."

8747 - [Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā] narrated to us, saying: Sufyān informed us, from ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal, from al-Shaʿbī: that Abu Bakr and ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "The kalala is one who has neither child nor father."

[Footnote: Report 8747 — Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā al-Ṣadafī al-Miṣrī, the teacher of al-Tabari, from whom Abu Ja'far narrated a great deal in his tafsir and in his other books, and it has passed as number 1679. In the printed edition it was "Abu Bishr ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā," and there is no narrator with this name among the transmitters, especially not among al-Tabari's teachers. In the manuscript: "Abu Bishr ʿAbd al-Aʿlā," and this also is unknown. In my view it is most likely a scribal corruption and distortion, and the correct form is "Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā," the teacher of al-Tabari, so I have written it that way between brackets.]

8748 - Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: My father told me, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥudayr, from al-Sumayṭ, who said: ʿUmar was a man who was left-handed-ambidextrous [Arabic: ayṣar], so he went out one day, gesturing with his hand like this, turning it around, except that he said: "A time came upon me when I did not know what the kalala is. Indeed, the kalala is what is other than the child and the father."

[Footnote: Report 8748 — Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 6:224 through Muḥammad ibn Naṣr, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, from Ḥammād, from ʿImrān ibn Ḥudayr, from al-Sumayṭ ibn ʿUmayr, with a different and abbreviated wording. Al-Suyuti abbreviated it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:250-251 and did not attribute it to anyone other than Ibn Abi Shayba. "ʿImrān ibn Ḥudayr al-Sadūsī" — his biography has passed earlier as number 2634. As for "al-Sumayṭ," he is Sumayṭ ibn ʿUmayr al-Sadūsī, and it is said Sumayṭ ibn Samīr, and it is said Sumayṭ ibn ʿAmr; he is mentioned in al-Tahdhib and in al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/2/204, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/317. Regarding the phrase "ʿUmar was a man who was ayṣar": the attested description of ʿUmar is that he was aʿsar yasar (both with fatḥa), meaning he worked with both hands; this is what they call al-adbaṭ, whose left hand is as strong as his right in work. If he works with the left hand only, he is aʿsar; and if a man is aʿsar but not yasar, his right hand is weaker than his left. Here he apparently meant by "ayṣar" that he worked with his left hand, which is unusual among the lexicographers. The phrase "aʿsar ayṣar" also occurs as a description of ʿUmar. Abu ʿUbayd al-Qāsim ibn Sallām said: "It is thus narrated in the hadith, but the correct form in Arabic usage is aʿsar yasar." Ibn al-Sikkīt said: "Do not say aʿsar ayṣar." However, this is how the report appears in the copy of Abu Ja'far's tafsir available to us, so I do not know whether its copyist erred or this was indeed his narration. I have not found the report in full elsewhere. The word "yaqūlu" in "yaqūlu bi-yadihi hākadhā" means: he moves it, indicating or gesturing with it. "Qawl" in Arabic usage is used in many senses, among them indicating, moving, and gesturing.]

8749 - Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Jābir, from ʿĀmir, from Abu Bakr, who said: "The kalala is what is other than the child and the father."

8750 - Yunus told me, saying: Sufyān informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The kalala is one who has neither child nor father."

8751 - Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Ibn Jurayj narrate, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The kalala is one who has neither child nor father."

8752 - Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: Muʾammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from al-Ḥasan ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥanafiyya, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The kalala is what is other than the child and the father."

[Footnote: Reports 8750, 8751, 8752 — three chains. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan 6:225 through two routes: through Abu Saʿid al-Aʿrābī, from Saʿdān ibn Naṣr, from Sufyān; and through Muḥammad ibn Naṣr, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ṣabbāḥ, from Sufyān, in a longer form.]

8753 - Ibn Bashshār and Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, both saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abu Isḥāq, from Sulaym ibn ʿAbd, from Ibn ʿAbbās, with the same.

[Footnote: Report 8753, and then reports 8754, 8756, 8757, 8758, 8759 — various routes for the report of Sulaym ibn ʿAbd al-Sulamī from Ibn ʿAbbās, which will also be narrated as number 8768. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 2:224 through another route, through Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā, from Hushaym, from Zakariyyā ibn Abi Zāʾida, from Abu Isḥāq. He pointed to number 8753 and 8754 as the route of Isrāʾīl from Abu Isḥāq. "Sulaym ibn ʿAbd al-Sulamī," also called "Sulaym ibn ʿAbd Allāh," a Kufan. He is in al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/2/127, Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/212, and Taʿjīl al-Manfaʿa: 163. Al-Bukhari and Abu Hatim said: "He narrated from Ḥudhayfa; Abu Isḥāq al-Sabīʿī narrated from him," and the hafiz added in Taʿjīl al-Manfaʿa "only." He said: "Ibn Ḥibbān declared him trustworthy and said: He witnessed the expedition of Ṭabaristān." Al-ʿIjlī said: "Kufan, trustworthy. They were three brothers: Sulaym ibn ʿAbd, ʿUmāra ibn ʿAbd, and Zayd ibn ʿAbd — trustworthy, Sulamīs, Kufans." This report of al-Tabari and al-Bayhaqi's chain has also informed us that he narrated from others among the Companions besides Ḥudhayfa; he narrated from Ibn ʿAbbās as well, as you hear.]

8754 - Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Abu Isḥāq, from Sulaym ibn ʿAbd al-Sulamī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "The kalala is what is other than the child and the father."

8755 - al-Muthannā told me, saying: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Muʿāwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ told me, from ʿAlī ibn Abi Ṭalḥa, from Ibn ʿAbbās, his saying: "And if a man leaves an inheritance as kalala, or a woman," he said: "The kalala is one who leaves neither child nor father."

8756 - Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd al-Muḥāribī told me, saying: Abu al-Aḥwaṣ narrated to us, from Abu Isḥāq, from Sulaym ibn ʿAbd, who said: "I did not see them except that they agreed that whoever dies leaving neither child nor father is a kalala."

8757 - Tamīm ibn al-Muntaṣir narrated to us, saying: Isḥāq ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, from Sharīk, from Abu Isḥāq, from Sulaym ibn ʿAbd, who said: "I did not see them except that they agreed that the kalala is one who has neither child nor father."

8758 - Ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Abu Isḥāq, from Sulaym ibn ʿAbd, who said: "The kalala is what is other than the child and the father."

8759 - Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, from Ashʿath, from Abu Isḥāq, from Sulaym ibn ʿAbd, who said: "I found them saying: if a man leaves neither child nor father, he is inherited from as a kalala."

8760 - Bishr ibn Muʿādh narrated to us, saying: Yazīd ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, concerning His words: "And if a man leaves an inheritance as kalala, or a woman": the kalala is one who has neither child nor father, neither father nor grandfather, nor son nor daughter. These are the brothers from the mother.

8761 - Muḥammad ibn al-Muthannā told me, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, from Shuʿba, from al-Ḥakam, who said concerning the kalala: "It is what is other than the child and the father."

8762 - Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "The kalala is everyone whose inheritance is not received by a father or a child, and everyone who has neither child nor father is inherited from as a kalala, men and women among them."

8763 - al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda, al-Zuhrī and Abu Isḥāq, who said: "The kalala is one who has neither child nor father."

8764 - Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Muḥammad narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhrī, Qatāda and Abu Isḥāq, the same.

* *

Others said: "The kalala is what is other than the child," and this is a statement from Ibn ʿAbbās, and it is the report we mentioned earlier through the narration of Ṭāwūs from him: [Footnote: this is report number 8734, previously mentioned] that he gave the brothers from the mother a sixth alongside the parents.

* *

Others said: the kalala is what is other than the father.

Those who said this:

8765 - Ibn al-Muthannā told me, saying: Sahl ibn Yūsuf narrated to us, from Shuʿba, who said: I asked al-Ḥakam about the kalala, and he said: "It is what is other than the father."

* *

The grammarians differed regarding the governing element of "kalala" (what makes it accusative).

Some of the Basran grammarians said: If you wish, you may put "kalala" in the accusative as the predicate of "kāna," and make "yūrathu" a description of "the man." And if you wish, you may make "kāna" independent of a predicate, like "waqaʿa" (it happened), and make the accusative of "kalala" a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl), meaning: one who is inherited from as a kalala, [Footnote: in the printed edition: "yūrathu kalala," and in the manuscript it may resemble "mūrath," and that is better, so I have written it, because it is more deserving of that position] just as one says: "He is struck standing."

* *

Others said: his saying "kalala" is the predicate of "kāna"; the inherited person is not the kalala, rather the heir is the kalala.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: the correct view in this matter, in my opinion, is that "kalala" is in the accusative by way of exception from His saying "yūrathu," and the predicate of "kāna" is "yūrathu." And although "kalala" is accusative by exception from "yūrathu," it is not accusative as a circumstantial accusative, but as a verbal noun in the sense of the statement. Because the meaning of the statement is: "And if a man is inherited from by one whose lineage encircles him, as kalala" — then the mention of "whose lineage encircles him" was dropped, being sufficiently indicated by His saying "yūrathu."

* *

The scholars differed regarding what is named "kalala."

Some of them said: "kalala" is the inherited person, that is, the deceased himself, who is named thus when he is inherited from by someone other than his parent and child. [Footnote: in the printed edition: "sammā bi-dhālika" (he was named thereby), and in the manuscript: "sammā," without dots, and the correct reading is what I have given.]

Those who said this:

8766 - Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, concerning His saying about the kalala [Footnote: in the printed edition: "qawlahum fī al-kalala" (their saying about the kalala), and I have retained the manuscript reading, which is correct], who said: "It is the one who leaves neither parent nor child."

8767 - Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, from Sulaymān al-Aḥwal, from Ṭāwūs, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "I was the last of the people to meet ʿUmar (may Allah have mercy on him)" [Footnote: in the printed edition: "may Allah be pleased with him," and I have retained the manuscript reading], "and I heard him say: 'The saying is what I said.'" [Footnote: in the printed edition: "fa-sami'tuhu yaqūlu mā qult" — omitting "al-qawl" — and in the manuscript: "fa-sami'tuhu yaqūlu yaqūlu mā qult," which is a hasty error of the copyist and a distortion; the correct version is what I have given from al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi.] I said: "And what did you say?" He said: "The kalala is one who has no child."

[Footnote: Report 8767 — "Sulaymān al-Aḥwal" is Sulaymān ibn Abi Muslim al-Makkī al-Aḥwal, maternal uncle of Ibn Abi Najīḥ. He is trustworthy, and the Six Books narrate from him. This report was narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 2:225 through Saʿdān ibn Naṣr, from Sufyān (meaning Ibn ʿUyayna), from Sulaymān al-Aḥwal. Al-Bayhaqi commented on his narration: "So it is in this narration; but what we have narrated from ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās regarding the explanation of the kalala is more consistent with the indications of the Book and the Sunna than this narration, and more fitting to be sound, due to this narration standing alone and the multiplicity of narrations from them to the contrary." Ibn Kathir also pointed to it in his tafsir 2:371, saying: "There is a report from Ibn ʿAbbās that contradicts that, namely that it is one who has no child; the sound report from him is the first, and perhaps the narrator did not grasp what he intended."]

This is further, Abu Ja'far also responded to it with the well-known report from Ibn 'Abbas, citing the account of Sulaym ibn 'Abd al-Sulami from Ibn 'Abbas, which has preceded at nos. 8753 to 8759, by another route. He considered this sufficient as a reply to this view, which Tawus alone transmitted from Ibn 'Abbas.]]

8768. Ibn Wakic related to us, saying: My father and Yahya ibn Adam related to us, from Israil, from Abu Ishaq, from Sulaym ibn 'Abd, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The *kalalah* is one who has neither child nor parent. [[The report: 8768. There are two isnads for it. One is "Ibn Wakic from his father," which has preceded at 8754. The other is "Ibn Wakic from Yahya ibn Adam," an isnad which he did not mention among the isnads of this report in what has preceded at nos. 8753–8759. In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "Sulayman ibn 'Abd," which is an error; it is rather "Sulaym ibn 'Abd al-Sulami," as in the isnads of this report above.]]

Others said: The *kalalah* are the heirs who inherit from the deceased, when they are siblings, male or female, or others, if they are not a child or a parent, according to what we have mentioned of their disagreement on this.

* *

Others said: Rather, the *kalalah* is both the deceased and the living.

Mention of who said this:

8769. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: The *kalalah* is the deceased who has neither child nor parent, or the living; they are all *kalalah*. This one inherits through *kalalah*, and this one is inherited from through *kalalah*. [[In the manuscript: "this one inherits through kalalah, and this one inherits through kalalah," which is an error by the copyist; the correct reading is that of the printed edition.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter, in my opinion, is what these said, namely that the *kalalah* are those who inherit from the deceased, other than his child and parent. This is because of the soundness of the report we have mentioned from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, that he said: "I said, O Messenger of God, only *kalalah* inherit from me, so how about the inheritance?" [[This is the report which preceded at no. 8730.]] And with it:

8770. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Ibn 'Awn, from 'Amr ibn Sa'id, who said: We were with Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman in the slave market. He said: Then he rose from us and returned, and said: "This is the last of three from the Banu Sa'd who related this report to me. They said: Sa'd fell gravely ill in Mecca. He said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) came to visit him. He said: 'O Messenger of God, I have much wealth, and I have no heir except a *kalalah*. Shall I bequeath all my wealth?' He said: 'No.'" [[The report: 8770. "'Amr ibn Sa'id al-Qurashi," who transmitted from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Sha'bi, and Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Himyari. Transmitting from him were Ayyub, Yunus, Ibn 'Awn, and others. And "Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Himyari," from whom the six compilers transmitted. He transmitted from Abu Bakrah, Ibn 'Umar, Abu Hurayrah, Ibn 'Abbas, and three from the descendants of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas (who are those mentioned in this report), and others. Ibn Sa'd said: "He was trustworthy, and he had hadiths." Both are biographied in the Tahdhib.

The report of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas concerning the bequest, and his saying, "I bequeath a *kalalah*," was transmitted by Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat 3/1/103, and Ahmad in his Musnad 4:60. Both: 'Affan ibn Muslim, from Wuhayb, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym, from 'Amr ibn al-Qari, from his father, from his grandfather 'Amr ibn al-Qari.

Ibn 'Abd al-Barr transmitted it in al-Isti'ab: 444, and Ibn al-Athir in Usd al-Ghabah 4:119, and said: "Three of them transmitted it," meaning Ibn Mandah, Abu Nu'aym, and Ibn 'Abd al-Barr.]]

8771. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Suwayd related to us, from al-'Ala' ibn Ziyad, who said: An old man came to 'Umar, may God be pleased with him, and said: "I am an old man, and I have no heir except a *kalalah* of Bedouins whose lineage is distant [[His saying "mutaraakhin nasabuhum" means: their lineage is far off, from the expression "taraakha fulan 'anni," meaning he was distant from me. The lexicographers did not cite a witness for it, and this is its witness.]]. Shall I bequeath a third of my wealth?" He said: "No."

* *

These reports have thus confirmed the soundness of what we have said regarding the meaning of *kalalah*, and that they are the heirs of the deceased, other than his parent and child.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And if he has a brother or a sister, then for each one of them is a sixth. But if they are more than that, they are sharers in the third﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted: "And he has a brother or a sister," meaning that for the man who is inherited from as a *kalalah*, there is a brother or a sister, that is, a brother or sister from his mother, as:

8772. Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ya'la ibn 'Ata', from al-Qasim, from Sa'd, that he used to read: "And if a man is inherited from as a *kalalah* or a woman, and he has a brother or a sister." Sa'd said: "From his mother."

8773. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Ya'la ibn 'Ata', who said: I heard al-Qasim ibn Rabi'ah say: I read to Sa'd: "And if a man is inherited from as a *kalalah* or a woman, and he has a brother or a sister." Sa'd said: "From his mother."

8774. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Ya'la ibn 'Ata', from al-Qasim ibn Rabi'ah ibn Qanif [[In the printed edition: "al-Qasim ibn Rabi'ah from Fatik," which is a plain error. In the manuscript it is as I have recorded it, except that the copyist miswrote and misdotted it, and the editors changed it. See the following note.]], who said: I read to Sa'd, and he mentioned something similar.

8775. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Hushaym informed us, saying: Ya'la ibn 'Ata' informed us, from al-Qasim ibn Rabi'ah, who said: I heard Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas recite: "And if a man is inherited from as a *kalalah*, and he has a brother or a sister from his mother." [[The reports: 8772–8775. "al-Qasim ibn Rabi'ah" is "al-Qasim ibn Rabi'ah ibn Qanif al-Thaqafi," attributed to his grandfather, so he is "al-Qasim ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Rabi'ah ibn Qanif al-Thaqafi." He is trustworthy, and none transmitted from him except "Ya'la ibn 'Ata' al-'Amiri." His biography and isnad have preceded at nos. 1755–1757.

This report from Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas was transmitted by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 6:223, and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:126, and he added its attribution to Sa'id ibn Mansur, 'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Darimi, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim.]]

8776. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: "And he has a brother or a sister." These brothers from the mother: if there is one, he has a sixth; and if they are more than that, they are sharers in the third, the male and the female being equal in it. [[A number was omitted from the numbering: 8777.]]

8778. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadhdhal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "And if a man is inherited from as a *kalalah*, or a woman, and he has a brother or a sister." These are the brothers from the mother; they are sharers in the third, equally the male and the female.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for His saying: "Then for each one of them is a sixth," when a brother alone or a sister alone is present, and there is no other brother or sister from the mother besides him or her, then he or she has a sixth of the inheritance of the brother from the mother. If there is a brother and a sister, or two brothers with no third with them from the same mother, or two sisters likewise, or a brother and a sister with no one else from the same mother besides them, then for each of them there is a sixth of the inheritance of their brother from the mother. "But if they are more than that," meaning: if the brothers and sisters from the mother of the deceased who is inherited from as a *kalalah* are more than two, "then they are sharers in the third," that is: the third which I prescribed for the two of them, if there is no other from their mother as an inheritance for them from their deceased brother who is inherited from as a *kalalah*, is shared among them, if they are more than two, however many their number, with no male preferred over a female in this, but it is among them equally.

* *

If someone says: How is it said, "And he has a brother or a sister," and not "For them is a brother or a sister," when before that it was mentioned, "a man or a woman," so it was said: "And if a man is inherited from as a *kalalah*, or a woman"? The answer: It is among the customs of the Arabs that when they put two names before the report, joining one to the other with "or," and then bring the report, they sometimes attribute the report to both of them, and sometimes to one of them. When they attribute it to one of them, it is the same to them whichever of the two names they mentioned it is attributed to. So you say: "Whoever has a boy or a girl, let him treat him well," meaning: let him treat the boy well; and "let him treat her well," meaning: let him treat the girl well; and "let him treat them both well." [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:257–258.]]

* *

As for His saying: "Then for each one of them is a sixth," when the mention of the brother and the sister has come earlier with one joined to the other, and the indication that what is meant by the sense of the speech is one of them in His saying: "And he has a brother or a sister," this is permitted because the meaning of the speech is: "Then for each one of the ones mentioned is a sixth." [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "wa-li-kull wahid" with a waw, but the context requires what I have recorded.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿After a bequest that is made or a debt, without causing harm. An ordinance from God. And God is Knowing, Forbearing﴾ (12)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted: "After a bequest which he makes," meaning: this which I have prescribed for the brother of the deceased who is inherited from as a *kalalah*, and his sister, or his brothers and sisters, from his inheritance and estate, is for them only after the payment of the deceased's debt which was upon him on the day the event of death befell him, from his estate, and after the execution of his permitted bequests which he made during his life to whomever he bequeathed to after his death, as:

8779. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: "After a bequest which he makes, or a debt," and the debt is the most deserving thing to be begun with from all the wealth, so it is paid from the trust of the deceased; then the bequest; then the heirs divide their inheritance.

* *

As for His saying: "without causing harm," He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: after a bequest he makes, without harming his heirs in their inheritance from him, as:

8780. Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His saying: "without causing harm," he said: In the inheritance of his family.

8781. al-Qasim related to me, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid concerning His saying: "without causing harm." He said: In the inheritance of his family.

8782. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: "without causing harm, an ordinance from God." God, blessed and exalted, disliked harm in life and at death, and forbade it, and made it unlawful, so harm is not permissible in life or at death.

8783. Nasr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Azdi related to me, saying: 'Ubaydah ibn Humayd related to us; and Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us; all of them from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this verse: "without causing harm, an ordinance from God, and God is Knowing, Forbearing." He said: Harm in a bequest is among the major sins. [[The report: 8783. "Nasr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Azdi" was biographied at nos. 423, 875, 2859. Here, as there, both the manuscript and the printed edition read "al-Awdi" with a waw, which is an error. "'Ubaydah ibn Humayd ibn Suhayb al-Taymi" was mentioned at no. 2781. See also the note at the end of these reports, nos. 8787 and 8788.]]

8784. Ibn Abi al-Shawarib related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayi' related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Harm in a bequest is among the major sins.

8785. Humayd ibn Mas'adah related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufadhdhal related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it.

8786. Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Injustice (*hayf*) in a bequest is among the major sins.

8787. Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi and 'Abd al-A'la related to us, both saying: Dawud related to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Harm and injustice in a bequest are among the major sins. [[Report 8787 and what precedes it: the report of Ibn 'Abbas. Abu Ja'far transmitted it with five isnads, halting at him. It will come in the next one as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet). It was transmitted by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 6:271 by way of Sa'id ibn Mansur, from Hushaym, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, and he said: "This is the sound one, halting at Ibn 'Abbas. Likewise Ibn 'Uyaynah and others transmitted it from Dawud as halting. It was transmitted by another route as marfu', but its raising is weak," which points to the following report transmitted by al-Tabari.

Ibn Kathir also cited it in his Tafsir 2:372–373, saying: "al-Nasa'i transmitted it in his Sunan, from 'Ali ibn Hujr, from 'Ali ibn Musharhar, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, halting... Likewise Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted it from Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, from 'A'idh ibn Habib, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind. Ibn Jarir transmitted it from a group of memorizers, from Dawud, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, halting." Then he said: "Ibn Jarir said: The sound one is the halting." What Ibn Kathir attributed to Ibn Jarir I did not find in his Tafsir in its usual place for this passage, so I do not know whether something fell out of the book, or whether Ibn Kathir found it elsewhere in Abu Ja'far's works, or whether Ibn Kathir was hasty and erred.

Now, in these reports in the manuscript and the printed edition, it reads "al-hayf fi al-wasiyyah" (injustice in the bequest). In the Sunan al-Kubra it reads "al-janf," which has the same meaning, and which agrees with what is in the verse of bequest in Surat al-Baqarah 2:182: "Then whoever fears from a testator an injustice (*janfan*) or a sin."]]

8788. Musa ibn Sahl al-Ramli related to me, saying: Ishaq ibn Ibrahim Abu al-Nadr related to us, saying: 'Umar ibn al-Mughirah related to us, saying: Dawud ibn Abi Hind related to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Harm in a bequest is among the major sins." [[The report: 8788. "Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Yazid," Abu al-Nadr al-Dimashqi al-Faradisi, client of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz. Al-Bukhari transmitted from him, and sometimes attributed him to his grandfather Yazid. He is trustworthy, and is biographied in the Tahdhib.

As for "'Umar ibn al-Mughirah," Abu Hafs, he is from Basra, and went to al-Massisah. He transmitted from Dawud ibn Abi Hind and al-Jald ibn Ayyub, and Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid and Hisham ibn 'Ammar transmitted from him. Ibn Abi Hatim said: "I asked my father about him, and he said: A shaykh." And he said: "Abu al-Nadr al-Dimashqi al-Faradisi, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, transmitted from him." And al-Bukhari said: "'Umar ibn al-Mughirah, munkar al-hadith, unknown." And 'Ali ibn al-Madini said: "He is unknown; I do not know him." He is biographied in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/136 and Lisan al-Mizan 4:332.

In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "'Amr ibn al-Mughirah," and what I have recorded is correct.

This report was transmitted by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 6:271 by way of 'Abd Allah ibn Yusuf al-Tinnisi, from him. Ibn Kathir cited it in his Tafsir 2:372 and attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim, from his father, from Abu al-Nadr al-Dimashqi, from 'Umar ibn al-Mughirah.

The Hafiz said in the biography of "Ishaq ibn Ibrahim" in the Tahdhib 1:220: "al-Azdi related it to him in al-Du'afa', a hadith from 'Umar ibn al-Mughirah, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, raised: 'Harm in a bequest is among the major sins.' Al-Azdi said: 'What is preserved is from the words of Ibn 'Abbas; he does not raise it.' I say (the speaker is the Hafiz Ibn Hajar): 'Umar is very weak, so the blame for it falls on him, and it was transmitted by al-Thawri and others from Dawud as halting.'"]]

8789. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Abu 'Amr al-Taymi informed us, from Abu al-Duha, who said: I entered with Masruq upon a sick man, and he was making a bequest. Masruq said to him: "Be just, and do not go astray." [[The report: 8789. "Abu 'Amr al-Taymi," I did not know who he is, and I fear that he is "Abu al-Mu'tamir al-Taymi," who is "Sulayman ibn Tarkhan al-Taymi."]]

* *

"Ghayra mudarr" (not causing harm) is put in the accusative as an exception from His saying: "bi-ha yuusa" (by which he bequeaths).

* *

As for His saying: "wasiyyatan" (an ordinance), its accusative is from His saying: "God enjoins you concerning your children: for the male is the equal of the portion of two females," and the rest of what He enjoined concerning the two; then He said: "an ordinance from God," as an infinitive from His saying: "yusikum" (He enjoins you). ["The infinitive" means the absolute object.]

* *

Some of the grammarians said: That is accusative from His saying: "then for each one of them is a sixth," as in "an ordinance from God," and he said: It is like your saying: "For you are two dirhams as provision to your family." [[This is the view of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:258.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What we have said is more correct, because God, exalted is His mention, opened the mention of the division of inheritances in these two verses with His saying: "God enjoins you" (﴿يُوصِيكُمُ اللَّهُ﴾), then concluded that with His saying: "an ordinance from God" (﴿وَصِيَّةً مِّنَ اللَّهِ﴾), informing that all of that is an ordinance from Him to His servants. So the accusative of His saying "ordinance" as a verbal noun (maṣdar) from His saying "enjoins you" is more correct than its accusative as a specification (tafsir, i.e. tamyiz, as we have mentioned several times, the last of which was at 6:586, note 1) from His saying: "then for each one of them is a sixth" (﴿فَلِكُلِّ وَاحِدٍ مِّنْهُمَا السُّدُسُ﴾), for the reason we have mentioned.

* *
