By His saying, exalted is His mention: "an ordinance from God" (﴿وَصِيَّةً مِّنَ اللَّهِ﴾), He means a binding charge from God to you concerning what is due to you of the inheritance of whoever among you dies, [see the explanation of "wasiyyah" (ordinance) earlier, p. 30, note 2, and the references there] "and God is All-Knowing" (﴿وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ﴾), meaning: God possesses knowledge of the interests of His creatures and their harms, and of who deserves to be given from the relatives and kin of whoever among you dies from his inheritance, and who is to be deprived of that, and the extent of what each one who deserves it is entitled to as a share, and other matters concerning His servants and their interests, "Most Forbearing" (﴿حَلِيمٌ﴾), meaning: possessor of forbearance toward His creatures, and possessor of patience in not hastening to punish them for one another's wrongdoing, [see the explanation of "ʿalīm" and "ḥalīm" under their roots in the language indexes earlier] in giving them inheritance—to the people of strength and vigour among the sons of the deceased, and the people of wealth and might among them—rather than to the people of weakness and incapacity among his young children and his daughters.

**The interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿These are the limits of Allah. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger – He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein eternally. And that is the great attainment.﴾ (4:13)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The people of ta'wil (interpretation) differed regarding the interpretation of His words, "These are the limits of Allah." Some of them said: It means, "These are the conditions of Allah." [[See the explanation of "al-hudud" (limits) above, 3:546-547; 4:564-565, 583-585, 599. In this place there is an elaboration not previously given like it, and it is an elaboration of extreme excellence and precision.]]

Mention of those who said that:

8790 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufadhdhal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, on the authority of al-Suddi: "These are the limits of Allah" – he says: "the conditions of Allah."

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "These are the obedience of Allah."

Mention of those who said that:

8791 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to us, on the authority of Ali ibn Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "These are the limits of Allah" – meaning: "the obedience of Allah," meaning the inheritance shares which Allah has specified.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "These are the sunnah (way) of Allah and His command."

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: "These are the obligations of Allah."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions regarding the truth is what we are explaining, namely that the "hadd" (limit) of everything is that which separates it from other things. For this reason the boundaries of a house and the boundaries of lands are called "hudud," because they separate what is bounded by them from other things. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "li-fusulihā bayna mā ḥudda bihā wa-bayna ghayrihi" (for its separations between what is bounded by them and other than it), as if "al-fusul" were the verbal noun of "fasala bayna al-shay'ayn yafsilu." But the lexicographers did not make the verbal noun for this meaning that; they said its verbal noun is "al-fasl." As for "al-fusul," it is the verbal noun of "fasala fulan min 'indi" when he departed. What the lexicographers said is the pure truth.

I hold that the copyist omitted something from the text, and that the original wording of al-Tabari was: "And for this reason the boundaries of a house and the boundaries of lands were called hudud – and they are its separations (fusuluhā), for their separation ..." and "al-fusul" here, as will come in his wording later, is the plural of "fasl" (with a fatha and sukun), which is like "al-hadd," meaning the barrier between two things.]]

Likewise His words, "These are the limits of Allah," mean: this division which your Lord has apportioned for you, and the obligatory shares which He has imposed for your living from your dead in this verse, according to what He imposed and explained in these two verses. "The limits of Allah" means: the separations between the obedience of Allah and His disobedience in your division of the inheritances of your dead, as Ibn Abbas said. [[That is, in the report numbered 8791.]] He omitted "obedience of Allah" [[Thus in the manuscript and the printed edition: "ṭā'at Allāh" (obedience of Allah). What was omitted was "ṭā'a" (obedience) alone; so I would prefer the wording to be: "He omitted – obedience – and the meaning by that is ..."]], and the meaning of that is: the limits of the obedience of Allah, relying on the addressees' knowledge of the meaning of the speech from its mention. The evidence for the correctness of what we have said regarding that is His words, "And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger," and the verse after it: "And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger." [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "al-āyah allatī ba'dahā" (the verse that follows it) without the conjunction "wa" (and), which is a corruption; the correct reading is to include it. This is a clear proof in explaining the meaning of "the limits of Allah." May Allah have mercy on Abu Ja'far and reward him with good for his book.]]

* *

So the interpretation of the verse is: This division which your Lord has apportioned among you, O people, concerning the inheritances of your dead, consists of separations by which He has distinguished for you between His obedience and His disobedience, and limits for you at which you should stop and not transgress them, so that He may know from among you the people of His obedience from the people of His disobedience, [[In the printed edition: "wa-faṣala minkum ahla ṭā'atihi min ahli ma'ṣiyatihi" – the editor did not read well what was in the manuscript and changed it. In the manuscript it was: "li-salam minkum ahla ṭā'atihi" as if they were the heads of "sīn," and the correct reading is what I have set down.]] in what He commanded you concerning the division of the inheritances of your dead among yourselves, and in what He forbade you from them.

Then He, may His praise be exalted, informed of what He has prepared for each group among them, and He said regarding the group of the people of His obedience in that: "And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger" – in acting upon what He commanded him, and stopping at what He set as limits for him in the division of inheritances and other matters, and avoiding what He forbade him in that and other matters – "He will admit him to gardens beneath which rivers flow."

* *

So His words, "He will admit him to gardens," mean: orchards beneath whose trees and plantings rivers flow – "abiding therein," means: remaining therein forever, never dying nor perishing therein, nor being removed from them – "And that is the great attainment."

It means: Allah's admitting them into the gardens He described, with what He described of that, is "the great attainment," meaning the great success. [[See the explanation of "al-fawz" (attainment) above: 7:452, 472. And His word "al-falah" (with a fatha on the fa' and the lam together). And "al-falh" and "al-falah": success, deliverance, and remaining in bliss and good.]]

* *

The people of ta'wil said things in line with what we have said regarding that.

Mention of those who said that:

8792 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Juraij, on the authority of Mujahid: "These are the limits of Allah. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger He will admit him..." to the end of the verse – he said: "concerning the matter of the inheritances mentioned before."

8793 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah regarding His words: "These are the limits of Allah," which He set for His creation and His obligations among them regarding the inheritance and the division – so stop at them and do not transgress them to other than them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 14:

The explanation of His words: ﴿And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits – He will admit him to a Fire, wherein he will abide forever, and for him is a humiliating punishment.﴾ (4:14)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be majestic, He means: "And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger" in acting upon what they commanded him concerning the division of inheritances, as they commanded him to divide them among them, and other of Allah's obligations, opposing their command by what they forbade him, "and transgresses His limits" – that is, goes beyond the boundaries of His obedience, which He, exalted is He, made as a dividing line between it and disobedience to Him [[See the explanation of "limits" above, p. 68, and the note: 3.]] – to what He forbade him of dividing the estates of their deceased among their heirs, and other of His limits [[In the printed edition: "among his heirs" in the singular; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] – "He will admit him to a Fire, wherein he will abide forever," meaning: remaining in it eternally, never dying and never coming out of it, "and for him is a humiliating punishment," meaning: for him is a punishment that abases, and whoever is punished with it is disgraced by it. [[See the explanation of "humiliating" above, 2:347, 348 / 7:423. Note: 1.]]

* *

Those of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said regarding its interpretation.

Mention of those who said that:

8794 – Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: "And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger and transgresses His limits," the verse, concerning the inheritances mentioned before. Ibn Juraij said: "And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger," he said: from those who commit sins for which Allah punishes.

* *

If someone says: Is one who disobeys Allah and His Messenger in the division of inheritances eternally abiding in the Fire? It is said: Yes, if he combines with his disobedience in that a doubt that Allah has obligated upon him what He obligated upon His servants in these two verses, or he knows that and opposes Allah and His Messenger in their command – following what Ibn Abbas related of the statement of the one who said, when the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted is He, was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male, what is equal to the share of two females﴾ up to the completion of the two verses: "Shall one inherit who does not ride a horse, nor fight the enemy, nor acquire booty, half the property or all of the property?" [[He means the report of Ibn Abbas that preceded as no. 8726, and he related its meaning, not its wording.]] – deeming it objectionable that Allah's division of what He divided for the young children of the deceased, his women, and his daughters... [[The phrase "one who opposed the division of Allah" is the continuation of his earlier words: "he opposes Allah and His Messenger in their command..." and what lies between them is a separation I placed between the two lines.]] – one who opposed the division of Allah of what He allotted from the inheritance of the heirs among them, as He allotted it in His Book, and opposed His ruling in that and the ruling of His Messenger, deeming their ruling objectionable, as those whose matter Ibn Abbas mentioned objected, from among the hypocrites who were among the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, concerning whom this verse was revealed and those like them [[The full context of these passages: "Yes, if he combines with his disobedience in that a doubt ... or he knows that and opposes Allah and His Messenger in their command ... one who opposed the division of Allah of what He allotted from the inheritance of the heirs ... then he is among the people of eternal abiding in the Fire."]] – then he is among the people of eternal abiding in the Fire, because by deeming Allah's ruling in that objectionable, he becomes a disbeliever in Allah and leaves the religion of Islam.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 15 (part 1 of 2):

On the interpretation of His words, exalted is His praise: ﴿And those of your women who commit lewdness (al-fahishah), call against them four witnesses from among you. And if they testify, then confine them to the houses until death takes them or Allah ordains for them a way (sabil).﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, exalted is His praise, "And those of your women who commit lewdness," he means: the women who commit fornication (al-zina), that is, who commit adultery,[[His statement in his tafsir, "yata'tina bil-zina" (come to it with fornication), with the insertion of the preposition bi- contrary to what is in the verse, its meaning will become clear to you at p. 81 and footnote 1; and that the reading of Abdullah is "wallati ya'tina bil-fahishah," with bi-.]] "from among your women," and they are chaste women with husbands or without husbands; "then call against them four [witnesses] from among you," meaning: call four men from among your men as witnesses against them regarding what they have committed of lewdness, meaning from among the Muslims; "and if they testify" against them, "then confine them to the houses," meaning: imprison them in the houses,[[See the explanation of "al-imsak" (confinement) earlier, vol. 4, p. 546.]] "until death takes them," meaning: until they die; "or Allah ordains for them a way," meaning: or Allah appoints for them an outlet and a path to deliverance from what they have committed of lewdness.[[See the explanation of "al-sabil" (way) earlier: vol. 7, p. 490, Bulaq edition, footnote 2, and the references there.]]

* *

Those of the people of interpretation said the same as what we have said on this.
Those who said that:

8795 - Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i Muhammad ibn Yazid narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "And those of your women who commit lewdness, call against them four from among you. And if they testify, then confine them to the houses," he ordered their imprisonment in the houses until they die. "Or Allah ordains for them a way," he said: the prescribed punishment (al-hadd).[[The report 8795: Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i, Muhammad ibn Yazid, his biography has passed under no. 2739 and elsewhere. In the printed edition it read "Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i 'an Muhammad ibn Yazid," with the added "an," which is a clear error; the correct reading is in the manuscript.]]

8796 - Harithani Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: "And those of your women who commit lewdness," he said: fornication. He had ordered their imprisonment when four witnesses testify against them, until they die. "Or Allah ordains for them a way," and the way is the prescribed punishment.

8797 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: "And those of your women who commit lewdness," through "Or Allah ordains for them a way." A woman who committed fornication was confined in the house until she died. Then Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed after that: ﴿The fornicatress and the fornicator, flog each one of them a hundred lashes﴾ [Surah al-Nur: 2]. If they are both muhsan (married and chaste), they are stoned. This is their way which Allah has ordained for them.

8798 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "Or Allah ordains for them a way," so Allah has ordained for them: it is flogging and stoning.

8799 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "And those of your women who commit lewdness," until: "Or Allah ordains for them a way." This was before the prescribed punishments: both of them were harmed by speech, and the woman was confined. Then Allah ordained for them a way: the way for those who were muhsan was a hundred lashes then stoning with stones, and the way for those who were not muhsan was a hundred lashes and exile for a year.

8800 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah and Abdullah ibn Kathir said: "al-fahishah" is "al-zina," and "al-sabil" is the prescribed punishment (al-hadd): stoning and flogging.[[In the printed edition: "and al-sabil the stoning and flogging," omitting "al-hadd"; I have restored it from the manuscript.]]

8801 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And those of your women who commit lewdness, call against them four from among you," through "Or Allah ordains for them a way." These are the ones who have married and become muhsan. When a woman committed fornication, she was confined in the house, and her husband took her dowry, and it was his. That is His words: ﴿O you who believe, it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will, nor to restrain them that you may take away part of what you have given them, unless they commit a clear lewdness﴾ — the fornication. [[In the printed and manuscript texts: "That is His words: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take from what you have given them anything, unless they commit a clear lewdness﴾, and I suppose this is a slip by the copyist rather than by Abu Ja'far, since the passage he quoted derives from another verse in Surah al-Baqarah 229: ﴿And it is not lawful for you to take from what you have given them anything, unless they both fear that they will not keep the limits of Allah﴾.
It is strange regarding al-Suyuti: he took it out in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 129, attributed it to Ibn Jarir alone, and cited it as it is in the manuscript and printed edition, and did not pause at this verse merged from another verse!! So I have established the text of the verse which was the subject of his citation. Moreover, the editor omitted the word "al-zina" after "a clear lewdness," and I have restored it from the manuscript and al-Durr al-Manthur.]] (And consort with them in kindness) [Surah al-Nisa': 19], until the prescribed punishments came and abrogated it. She was flogged and stoned, and her dowry was inherited, and "the way" was flogging.

8802 - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say regarding His words: "Or Allah ordains for them a way," he said: the prescribed punishment (al-hadd). The prescribed punishment abrogated this verse.

8803 - Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Khusayf, from Mujahid: "Or Allah ordains for them a way," he said: a hundred lashes, for the male and female fornicator.

8804 - al-Rifa'i narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: the flogging.

8805 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Hattan ibn Abdullah al-Raqashi, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, that the Prophet ﷺ, when revelation descended upon him, lowered his head, and his companions lowered their heads; when it was lifted from him, he raised his head and said: "Allah has ordained for them a way: the thayyib (previously married) with the thayyib, and the bikr (virgin) with the bikr. As for the thayyib, they are flogged and then stoned; and as for the bikr, they are flogged and then exiled for a year."[[The hadith 8805: Al-Tabari narrates this hadith here through five chains: 8805–8807, 8810, 8811. All are sound and connected except the last, as will come, God willing.
Muslim narrated it (2: 33) from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, the teacher of al-Tabari here, through this chain. He and others narrated it through other chains, to which we will point.
Hattan ibn Abdullah al-Raqashi al-Basri: a trustworthy, reliable Successor, who was a reciter of the Qur'an. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/1/109, Ibn Sa'd 7/1/93, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/303-304, and Tabaqat al-Qurra' 1:253.]]

8806 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Hattan ibn Abdullah, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "Take from me, Allah has ordained for them a way: the thayyib with the thayyib, a hundred lashes and stoning with stones; and the bikr with the bikr, a hundred lashes and exile for a year."[[The hadith 8806: Sa'id is Ibn Abi 'Arubah.
The phrase [from al-Hasan] between Qatadah and Hattan has dropped out of the chain here, in both the manuscript and printed editions; this is an error by the copyists. The hadith was narrated by Muslim (2: 33) from Ibn Bashshar, the teacher of al-Tabari here, and from Ibn al-Muthanna, both from Abd al-A'la, through this chain, correctly. Hence we have restored what the copyists omitted.
Moreover, all the reports we have seen that say "from Qatadah" contain this addition, including the chain after this one, and the chain 8810.
Likewise Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 5: 318 (Halabi) from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Sa'id, from Qatadah.
Likewise Abu Dawud narrated it: 4415, by way of Yahya, from Sa'id.
Likewise al-Bayhaqi narrated it, 8: 210, by way of Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata', from Sa'id.
Likewise Ahmad narrated it, 5: 317, by way of Hammad, from Qatadah and Humayd, both from al-Hasan.]]

8807 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Hattan ibn Abdullah, brother of the Banu Raqash, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, when revelation descended upon him, was distressed by it and his face darkened,[[In the manuscript it read "karaba li-tilka," and the correct reading is from the narrations of the hadith; the printed edition earlier corrected it. "Karraba" in the passive form from "karabahu al-amr yakrubuhu" means it grieved him and weighed heavily upon him. "Tarabbada wajhuhu" means his color changed to dust-colored. And his saying afterward, "sura 'anhu," in the passive, means it was relieved from him, its distress lifted, from the saying "sarā al-thawb" when one removes it, and the doubling is for emphasis.]] and Allah revealed to him one day, and he met that. When it was lifted from him, he said: "Take from me, Allah has ordained for them a way: the thayyib with the thayyib, a hundred lashes then stoning with stones, and the bikr with the bikr, a hundred lashes then exile for a year."[[The report 8807: see the note on the hadith 8805.]]

8808 - Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And those of your women who commit lewdness, call against them four from among you. And if they testify, then confine them to the houses until death takes them or Allah ordains for them a way," he said: He says: do not marry them until death takes them, and He did not remove them from Islam. Then this was abrogated, and the way was made that Allah would ordain for them a way.[[In the printed edition it read: "then this was abrogated and the way which he mentioned was made that He would ordain..." adding "which he mentioned," and there is no good in adding it; what is in the manuscript, as I have given, is correct to some extent if "ja'ala" is read in the passive, so I left it that way, lest it be fully correct, though I am now in doubt about it.]] He said: So a way was made for her if she committed fornication while muhsanah: she was stoned and expelled, and the way for the bikr was made a hundred lashes.

8809 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "until death takes them or Allah ordains for them a way," he said: the flogging and the stoning.[[In the printed edition: "Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Juwaybir informed us," dropping "Yazid" from the chain; it is in the manuscript, and this is a recurring chain in the tafsir.]]

8810 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Hattan ibn Abdullah al-Raqashi, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Take from me, Allah has ordained for them a way: the thayyib with the thayyib and the bikr with the bikr; the thayyib is flogged and stoned, and the bikr is flogged and exiled."[[The hadith 8810: [Ibn] al-Muthanna is Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, the teacher of al-Tabari. The word [ibn] was dropped in the printed edition by mistake; it is present in the manuscript.
"Muhammad ibn Ja'far" is Ghundar, the companion of Shu'bah. The printed edition read "Muhammad ibn Abi Ja'far," which is an obvious error; the correct form is in the manuscript.
The hadith by this route was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 5: 320, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah.
Likewise Muslim narrated it, 2: 33, from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, the teacher of al-Tabari here, and from Ibn Bashshar, both from Shu'bah.
Ahmad also narrated it, 5: 320, from Yahya, from Hajjaj, from Shu'bah. al-Tahawi narrated it in Sharh Ma'ani al-Athar 2: 79, by way of Asad ibn Musa, from Shu'bah. Likewise Hammad ibn Salamah narrated it from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Hattan, from Ubadah, in al-Darimi's Sunan 2: 181.
Most of the narrators who related this hadith from al-Hasan al-Basri said it was "from al-Hasan, from Hattan al-Raqashi, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit." Few of them did not mention "from Hattan" in the chain, as we will mention in the chain following this one.
The apparent view is that al-Hasan heard it from Hattan, from Ubadah, and so he used to narrate it; and that at some times he would narrate it as mursal from Ubadah, without mentioning "from Hattan."
Among those who narrated it from him connected, with "Hattan" in the chain: al-Mubarak ibn Fudalah, in al-Tayalisi's Musnad: 584.
And Mansur ibn Zadhan, in Ahmad's al-Musnad 5: 313, Sunan al-Darimi 2: 181, Sahih Muslim 2: 33, Sunan Abi Dawud: 4416, al-Tirmidhi 2: 242, al-Muntaqa of Ibn al-Jarud, pp. 371-372, al-Tahawi 2: 79, Ibn al-Nahhas in al-Nasikh wal-Mansukh, p. 97, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 8: 221-222.
Al-Hasan did not alone narrate it from Hattan; Yunus ibn Jubayr also narrated it. Ibn Majah narrated it, 2550, by way of Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Yunus ibn Jubayr, from Hattan ibn Abdullah, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit. Thus Qatadah had two teachers for it: al-Hasan and Yunus.]]

8811 - Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to us, from his father, from his grandfather, from al-A'mash, from Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Basri, from al-Hasan, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: We were sitting with the Prophet ﷺ when his face reddened, as he did when revelation descended upon him, and he was seized as in a swoon, from the weight of it. When he recovered he said: "Take from me, Allah has ordained for them a way: the bikran (virgins) are flogged and exiled for a year, and the thayyiban (previously married) are flogged and stoned."[[The hadith 8811: This is the fifth chain, the interrupted one, as we pointed out in the first chain: 8805.
Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi, teacher of al-Tabari: his biography passed under no. 84 in the first volume.
Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Basri: his biography passed under no. 5417.
He narrated this hadith "from al-Hasan, from Ubadah," interrupted, because al-Hasan al-Basri did not hear from Ubadah. Isma'il was not alone in narrating it from al-Hasan in interrupted form; others followed him in that, which shows that al-Hasan sometimes connected the hadith through Hattan and sometimes narrated it as mursal from Ubadah.
al-Shafi'i narrated it in al-Risalah: 378, 636 with our commentary, and in Ikhtilaf al-Hadith (margin of al-Umm 7: 252), from Abd al-Wahhab, who is Ibn Abd al-Majid al-Thaqafi, "from Yunus ibn Ubayd, from al-Hasan, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit." Then he said in al-Risalah: 379, "A trustworthy man of knowledge informed us, from Yunus ibn Ubayd, from al-Hasan, from Hattan al-Raqashi, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit." And he said in Ikhtilaf al-Hadith, after narrating from Abd al-Wahhab: "The trustworthy man narrated to me that al-Hasan used to insert between him and Ubadah: Hattan al-Raqashi. I do not know whether Abd al-Wahhab inserted it between them, so it dropped from my book when I transferred it from the original, or not? The original, on the day I wrote this book, was absent from me."
He mentioned it in al-Umm 6: 119, as an unattributed citation, firmly with the addition, saying: "Then al-Hasan narrated, from Hattan al-Raqashi, from Ubadah." So I do not know whether he was certain that Abd al-Wahhab "inserted it between them" afterward, or whether he meant the narration of what the "trustworthy man" told him. I did not find the narration of "Yunus ibn Ubayd" elsewhere, so that I could be certain which of these it was.
It was also narrated, interrupted: "Jarir ibn Hazim, from al-Hasan, from Ubadah," in al-Tayalisi 584, Ahmad's al-Musnad 5: 327 (Halabi), and al-Bayhaqi's al-Sunan 8: 210.
Likewise it was narrated, interrupted: "Humayd, from al-Hasan, from Ubadah," in Ahmad's al-Musnad 5: 317 (Halabi). The hadith is sound in any case, and the connection of the interrupted narrations to the connected ones has become clear.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it, 2: 375, from some narrations of Ahmad, al-Tayalisi, Muslim, and the authors of the Sunan.
al-Suyuti mentioned it, 2: 129, and added its attribution to Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Hibban.]]
* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the interpretations of His saying ﴿or Allah ordains for them a way﴾ is the view of those who say that the way Allah, mighty and majestic is He, ordained for the married (thayyib) free persons (muhsanin) is stoning with stones, and for the virgins (bikr) is a hundred lashes and a year of exile. This is because of the soundness of the report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he stoned and did not flog; and because of the consensus of the authoritative community (al-hujjah), whose transmitted consensus cannot be subject to error, forgetfulness, or lying; and because of the soundness of the report from him that he judged in the case of virgins for a hundred lashes and a year of exile. In what is soundly reported from him, that he did not flog those who were stoned among the adulterers in his time, there is a clear proof of the weakness of the report that was transmitted from al-Hasan, [[In the printed edition: "على وهي الخبر" (ʿalā wahy al-khabar). I have kept what is in the manuscript, as you will see later. I had corrected it in volume 4, p. 18, making the phrase "لوهي أسانيدها، وأنها مع وهي أسانيدها" (its chains being weak), the verbal noun of "wahā al-shayʾ yahī wahyan" (the thing became weak). I then did the same in the same volume, p. 155, and in the footnote 1 I said that I feared this was from the copyist of the tafsir, not from Abu Ja'far. I also cited al-Mutarrizi's statement in al-Mughrib that the jurists' "wahāʾ" is an error and not to be relied upon. Then I did the same in volume 4 itself, p. 361, footnote 3, and likewise in volume 6, p. 85, footnote 2. However, I now see that I should keep what is in the manuscript, for two reasons. First, it recurs many times, which makes the claim of a copyist's error untenable. Second, I have come across parts of Abu Ja'far al-Tabari's book Tahdhib al-Athar, two fragments in two different ancient hands, and I found in them that he writes "wahāʾ" and not "wahā," so I judged that Abu Ja'far himself wrote it this way, even though al-Mutarrizi says it is an error and not to be relied upon.]] from Hittan, from Ubadah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: The way for the married thayyib is flogging and stoning.

* *

It has been mentioned that this verse, in the recitation of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud), reads: ﴿And those of your women who commit lewdness﴾. The Arabs say: "I came to a great matter" (atayta amran ʿaẓīman), and "I came with a great matter" (bi-amrin ʿaẓīm), and "I spoke an ugly speech" (takallamtu bi-kalāmin qabīḥ), and "an ugly speech" (kalāman qabīḥan) [with the object given directly, and with the preposition bi-]. [[See Maʿani al-Quran by al-Farra', 1:258.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 16:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And the two of you who commit it among you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "And the two of you who commit it among you," He means the man and the woman who commit it. He says: they commit the abomination (fahisha). The "ha'" (her) and the "alif" (the dual) in His saying "yatiyanha" ("commit it") refer to the "abomination" (fahisha) in His saying: "And those of your women who commit abomination." The meaning is: "And the two of you among you who commit the abomination, then harm them."

* *

Then the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning who is meant by His saying: "And the two of you who commit it among you, then harm them."

Some of them said: They are the two virgins (bikran) who have not been married (lam yuhsina), and they are other than those referred to in the verse before it. They said: His saying "And those of your women who commit abomination" refers to the previously married women (thayyibat) who are chaste through husbands; and His saying "And the two of you who commit it among you" means the virgin unmarried pair.

Those who said this:

8812 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, who said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: He mentioned the young women and young men who had not married, and said: "And the two of you who commit it among you, then harm them."

8813 - Yunus related to us, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying "And the two of you who commit it among you": the two virgins, then harm them. [[In the printed edition: "al-bikran" in the nominative, as if the editor disapproved of what was in the manuscript as I have recorded it, and that is the correct reading.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, by His saying "And the two of you who commit it among you," is meant the two men who commit fornication.

Those who said this:

8814 - Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i related to us, who said: Yahya related to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid: "And the two of you who commit it among you, then harm them," he said: the two men who do the act, who are not named (la yukna).

8815 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying "And the two of you who commit it among you": the two fornicators.

* *

Others said: Rather, it means the man and the woman, except that it is not specifically intended as a virgin rather than a previously married person.

Those who said this:

8816 - Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i related to us, who said: Yahya related to us, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata': "And the two of you who commit it among you, then harm them," he said: the man and the woman.

8817 - Muhammad ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from 'Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, who both said: "And those of your women who commit abomination" up to His saying "or God makes a way for them" — he mentioned the man after the woman, then joined them both together, saying: "And the two of you who commit it among you, then harm them. But if they repent and amend, then turn away from them. Indeed God is ever Relenting, Merciful."

8818 - al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: 'Ata' and 'Abdullah ibn Kathir said, concerning His saying "And the two of you who commit it among you": this is for the man and the woman together.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions regarding the interpretation of His saying "And the two of you who commit it among you" is the view of the one who said: "It refers to the unmarried virgins when they commit fornication, and they are one man and one woman," because if what was intended by it were to clarify the ruling concerning male fornicators, just as what was intended by His saying "And those of your women who commit abomination" was to clarify the ruling concerning female fornicators, it would have been said: "And those who commit it among you, then harm them," or it would have been said: "And he who commits it among you," just as it was said of the previous one: "And those of your women who commit abomination." Then their mention would have been brought out in the plural for all of them, and it would not have said: "And the two of you who commit abomination."

This is how the Arabs act when they wish to clarify a threat upon an act, or a promise for it: they bring out the names of its doers by mentioning the plural or the singular, because the singular indicates its kind, and they do not bring them out by mentioning two. So they say: "Those who do such-and-such, for them is such-and-such," and "He who does such-and-such, for him is such-and-such," and they do not say: "The two who do such-and-such, for them both is such-and-such," unless it is an act that can only occur between two different persons, like fornication, which occurs only between a male fornicator and a female fornicator. When that is so, the dual is used, meaning the doer and the one acted upon. But that the dual be mentioned while meaning two persons in an act each of whom could be alone in it, or in an act in which they would not be partners, is something not known in their speech.

Since this is so, the corruption of the view of the one who said, "By His saying 'And the two of you who commit it among you' is meant the two men," is clear, and the soundness of the view of the one who said that it means the man and the woman is clear. [[His saying "and the soundness of the view of the one who said" is coordinated with his saying "the corruption of the view of the one who said," in the nominative.]]

Since this is so, it is known that they are other than those whose ruling was previously explained in His saying "And those of your women who commit abomination," because these are two, and those are a group.

Since this is so, it is known that confinement was a punishment for the previously married women until they die, before God makes a way for them, because it is more severe as punishment than the harm, which is reproach and rebuke or abuse and disgrace, just as the way made for them, which is stoning, is more severe than the way made for the virgins, which is flogging a hundred lashes and exile for a year.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then harm them. But if they repent and amend, then turn away from them. Indeed God is ever Relenting, Merciful﴾ (16)

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning the "harm" (adha) which God, may He be remembered, made a punishment for those who commit the abomination, before He makes a way for them.

Some of them said: That harm is harm by speech and tongue, such as reproach and rebuke for what they committed of the abomination.

Those who said this:

8819 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, who said: Yazid related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: "Then harm them," he said: both of them were harmed by speech.

8820 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, who said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "Then harm them. But if they repent and amend, then turn away from them." He said: when the young woman and the young man committed fornication, they were rebuked and disgraced until they stopped that.

* *

Others said: That harm was harm by the tongue, except that it was abuse.

Those who said this:

8821 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to us, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Then harm them," meaning: abuse.

* *

Others said: Rather, that harm was by tongue and hand.

Those who said this:

8822 - al-Muthanna related to me, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, who said: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: "And the two of you who commit it among you, then harm them." He said: when the man committed fornication he was harmed with disgrace and struck with sandals.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the views on this, to be said, is that God, may He be remembered, had commanded the believers to harm the two fornicators mentioned, when they committed that and were of the people of Islam. "Harm" (adha) may apply to any displeasure that befalls a person, from an evil word by the tongue or from an action. [[In the printed edition: "qad yaqa bi-kull makruh," and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript; the meaning of "yaqa'" here is: comes, or is placed, or is applied in usage.]] [[See the explanation of "adha" in what has preceded: 4: 374 / 7: 455.]] The verse does not clarify which of these the believers were commanded at that time, nor was it reported from the Messenger of God ﷺ by a single transmission or a group transmission that would establish the proof. The people of interpretation differ on this, and it is possible that it was harm by tongue or by hand, and it is possible that it was harm by both. [[In the printed edition: "and it is possible that it was harm by the tongue and hand, and it is possible that it was harm by one of them." The manuscript reads "harm by both," and I have preferred this as correct, and made the first "harm by tongue or hand" in place of the conjunction with waw.]] There is no benefit in knowing by which of these it was, in religion or worldly life, nor is there harm in not knowing it, since God, may His praise be exalted, has abrogated that from His legislation by what He made obligatory upon His servants regarding them and regarding those women before them. As for what He made obligatory upon them regarding the two, it is what He made obligatory in Surat al-Nur (24:2): ﴿The adulteress and the adulterer, flog each one of them a hundred lashes﴾. As for what He made obligatory regarding the women before them, it is the stoning which the Messenger of God ﷺ judged concerning them. The people of interpretation all agree that God, may He be remembered, has made a way for the people of fornication, male and female, through the prescribed penalties by which He judged concerning them. [[In the printed edition: "the people of interpretation all agreed" and the text is as recorded.]]

* *

A group of the people of interpretation said: God, glory be to Him, abrogated by His saying "The adulteress and the adulterer, flog each one of them a hundred lashes" (Surat al-Nur: 2) His saying "And the two of you who commit it among you, then harm them."

Those who said this:

8823 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And the two of you who commit it among you, then harm them," he said: all of that was abrogated by the verse in "al-Nur" with the prescribed hadd (fixed punishment).

8824 - Abu Hisham related to us, who said: Yahya related to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid: "And the two of you who commit it among you, then harm them," the verse, he said: this was abrogated by the verse in "Surat al-Nur" with the prescribed hadd.

8825 - Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Abu Tumaylah related to us, who said: al-Husayn ibn Waqid related to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from 'Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, who both said concerning His saying "And the two of you who commit it among you, then harm them," the verse: it was abrogated by the verse of flogging, when He said: (The adulteress and the adulterer, flog each one of them a hundred lashes).

8826 - al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Abu Salih related to us, who said: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: "And the two of you who commit it among you, then harm them." Then God revealed after this: ﴿The adulteress and the adulterer, flog each one of them a hundred lashes﴾, and if they were married, they were stoned in the Sunnah of the Messenger of God ﷺ.

8827 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, who said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "And those of your women who commit abomination," the verse: the hudud came and abrogated it.

8828 - Related to me by al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say: this verse abrogated the hadd. [[The report 8828: in the printed edition "'Ubayd ibn Sulayman," and the correct reading is from the manuscript; in the manuscript there is another error, written "'Utbah ibn Sulayman," which is an error. This chain recurs in the tafsir.]]

8829 - al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Abu Sufyan related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "Then confine them in the houses" the verse, he said: the hudud abrogated it, and His saying "And the two of you who commit it among you" was abrogated by the hudud. [[The report 8829: "Abu Sufyan al-Mu'ammari" is Muhammad ibn Humayd al-Yashkuri, mentioned earlier under no. 1787, and this chain has appeared much before: 526, 1200, 1253, 1516, 1699.]]

8830 - Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying "And the two of you who commit it among you, then harm them," the verse: then this was abrogated, and the way for her was made: if she committed fornication while married, she was stoned and expelled, and the way for the male was made a hundred lashes.

8831 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying "Then confine them in the houses until death takes them": he said: it was abrogated by the hudud.

* *

As for His saying: "But if they repent and amend, then turn away from them," He, may He be exalted, means: if the two repent of the abomination they committed, and return to obedience to God between them, "and amend" means: and amend their religion by returning in repentance from their fornication and acting in what pleases God; "then turn away from them" means: then pardon them, and withhold from them the harm with which I had commanded you to harm them as punishment for what they committed of the abomination, and do not harm them after their repentance. [[See the explanation of "al-i'rad" (turning away) in what has preceded: 2: 298, 299.]]

* *

As for His saying: "Indeed God is ever Relenting, Merciful," He means: God has always been returning to His servants with what they love when they return to what He loves of them, of obedience to Him [[See the explanation of "kana" in this sense in what has preceded: 8: 51 / note 1 / and the explanation of "tawba" in what has preceded in lexical references.]] "Merciful" to them, meaning: possessing mercy and compassion.

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil in ignorance﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, exalted is His praise, "Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil in ignorance," He means that repentance is not incumbent upon Allah for any of His creatures except those among the believers who do evil in ignorance, "then they repent soon." He says: Allah does not turn back for any of His creatures toward what He loves of pardon and forgiveness of the sins they committed in the past, except for those who commit their sins out of ignorance on their part while they are believers in their Lord, then they return to obedience to Allah and repent to Him, in accordance with what Allah has commanded them: remorse for it, seeking forgiveness, and not returning to its like, before the coming of death upon them.

That is the "soon" (al-qarib) which Allah, mentioned in His praise, referred to when He said, "then they repent soon." [[See the explanation of "soon" below, p. 93.]]

* *

Those who engaged in interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said regarding the interpretation of this. However, they differed regarding the meaning of His words, "in ignorance" (bi-jahala).

Some of them said, in agreement with what we have said, and held that his doing evil is the "ignorance" which is meant.

Those who said this:

8832 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Aliyah, that he used to narrate that the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say: every sin that a servant commits is in ignorance.

8833 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words, "for those who do evil in ignorance," he said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gathered and were of the view that everything disobeyed through it is "ignorance," whether it was deliberate or otherwise.

8834 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words, "for those who do evil in ignorance," he said: Everyone who disobeys his Lord is ignorant until he desists from his disobedience.

8835 – al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words, "Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil in ignorance," he said: Everyone who acts in disobedience to Allah, that is from him in ignorance until he turns back from it.

8836 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil in ignorance," as long as he continues to disobey Allah, he is ignorant.

8837 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl ibn Ghazwan narrated to us, from Abu al-Nadr, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil in ignorance," he said: Whoever does evil is ignorant; it is from his ignorance that he does evil.

8838 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid, who said: Whoever disobeys Allah is ignorant until he desists from his disobedience. Ibn Juraij said: And 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir informed me, from Mujahid, who said: Every doer of disobedience is ignorant at the time he does it. Ibn Juraij said: And 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said to me something similar.

8839 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding Allah's words, "Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil in ignorance, then they repent soon," he said: "Ignorance" is that every person who does any of the acts of disobedience to Allah is ignorant forever until he desists from them. And he recited: ﴿Do you know what you did to Joseph and his brother when you were ignorant?﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 89], and he recited: ﴿And if You do not turn away from me their plot, I might incline toward them and be among the ignorant﴾ [Surah Yusuf: 33]. He said: Whoever disobeys Allah is ignorant until he desists from his disobedience.

* *

Others said: the meaning of His words, "for those who do evil in ignorance," is that they do that deliberately, intending it.

Those who said this:

8840 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Mujahid: "do evil in ignorance," he said: The ignorance is deliberateness.

8841 – Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid, the same.

8842 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil in ignorance," he said: The ignorance is deliberateness.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil in this world.

Those who said this:

8843 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from 'Ikrimah regarding His words, "Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil in ignorance," he said: The whole world is ignorance.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions regarding the interpretation of the verse is the view of the one who said: its interpretation is: Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil, and their doing evil is the ignorance in which they were ignorant, whether they were deliberately engaging in sin, or ignorant of what Allah has prepared for its people. [[See above, 2:183, his explanation of "the ignorant" as: the foolish.]]

This is because it is not found in the speech of the Arabs to call one who deliberately does a thing "ignorant of it," unless it is meant that he is ignorant of the measure of its benefit and harm, so it is said: "he is ignorant of it," in the sense that he does not know the extent of its benefit and harm. [[Perhaps the correct reading is "bi-mablagh naf'ihi wa darrihi" (by the extent of its benefit and harm), which the copyist garbled.]] But if he knows the measure of its benefit and harm, and intends it, then it is not permissible, because of his intending it, to say: "he is ignorant of it" [[In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads: "then it is not permissible, because of not intending it, to say: he is ignorant of it," which is certainly not consistent with what precedes or what follows it. The copyist's error here is also beyond doubt. I think his pen slipped and he wrote "min ghayr" (without) in place of "min ajl" (because of) as I have restored it, or it was "min jara' qasdihi ilayhi" (as a result of intending it), and he misread "min jara'" and wrote "min ghayr," which is a very close misreading, of which you have seen something far worse.]] because "the ignorant of a thing" is one who does not know it or recognize it at the time he approaches it, or [one who] knows it but whose doing is compared to the doer, since the error of what he did is like the ignorant one who undertakes a matter while being ignorant of it, and so misses the point of success in it, so it is said: "he is indeed ignorant of it," even if he knows it, because of his committing an act that only those ignorant of it would commit.

Likewise, the meaning of His words, "they do evil in ignorance," is said of them: "they do evil in ignorance," even if they commit it knowing the extent of Allah's punishment upon its people, intending to commit it, while knowing that it is forbidden to them. This is because their doing that was among the acts that none would commit except one who is ignorant of the greatness of Allah's punishment upon its people in the hasty life of this world and the deferred life of the Hereafter. So it is said of one who commits it while knowing it: "he committed it in ignorance," meaning that he did the act of those ignorant of it, not that he was ignorant.

* *

Some of the people of Arabic grammar claimed that its meaning is: they were ignorant of the full reality of the punishment in it, so they did not know it as the knowing person knows, even though they knew it to be a sin, and therefore it is said, "they do evil in ignorance." [[The speaker of this is al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, 1:259.]]

Abu Ja'far said: If the matter were as the speaker of this view says, then there would have to be no repentance for one who knows the full reality of what is in it. This is because He, exalted is His praise, said, "Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil in ignorance, then they repent soon," excluding others. So it is necessary for the holder of this view that there be no repentance [[The word "repentance" is the subject of "there be not" in His words: "that there be not for the knowing one..."]] for the knowing one who did evil knowing the full reality of what is in it, and then repented soon. And that contradicts what is established from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: that every repentant one, Allah may turn to him [[These two reports were transmitted by Abu Ja'far without a chain, and it seems he mentioned their meaning rather than their wording. The first seems to be: "Every sin, Allah may forgive it, except one who dies as a polytheist or kills a believer deliberately," which al-Suyuti recorded in al-Jami' al-Saghir, attributing it to Abu Dawud, from the hadith of Abu al-Darda', and to Ahmad, al-Nasa'i and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak, from the hadith of Mu'awiyah.
As for the second, it seems to be his saying ﷺ: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, extends His hand at night so that the one who sinned by day may repent, and extends His hand by day so that the one who sinned by night may repent, until the sun rises from its west," recorded by Muslim, 17:76, from the hadith of Abu Musa.]] and the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Except for one who repents and believes and does righteous deeds﴾ [Surah al-Furqan: 70] would be contradicted.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿then they repent soon﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of "soon" (al-qarib) in this place.

Some of them said: the meaning of that is: then they repent in their health, before their illness and before their death.

Those who said this:

8844 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "then they repent soon," and "soon" before death is while he is still in health.

8845 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Abu al-Nadr, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas: "then they repent soon," he said: in life and in health.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: then they repent before witnessing the Angel of Death.

Those who said this:

8846 – al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "then they repent soon," and "soon" is the period between now and when he looks at the Angel of Death.

8847 – Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard 'Imran ibn Hudayr say: Abu Mijlaz said: A man remains in repentance until he sees the angels.

8848 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ma'shar, from Muhammad ibn Qays, who said: "Soon" is what is before a sign from the signs of Allah the Exalted descends upon him and death descends upon him. [[The report 8848: Muhammad ibn Qays al-Madani, the judge of 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz. Ibn Sa'd said: "He narrated much hadith and was learned." Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat. He has one hadith in Muslim, from Abu Sarmah, from Abu Hurayrah. He is the one from whom Abu Ma'shar narrates. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

8849 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "Repentance is only incumbent upon Allah for those who do evil in ignorance, then they repent soon," and his repentance is for what is between him and when he sees the Angel of Death. So if he repents when he sees the Angel of Death, it is not for him.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: then they repent before death.

Those who said this:

8850 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from a man, from al-Dahhak, "then they repent soon," he said: Everything before death is "soon."

8851 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from al-Hakam ibn Aban, from 'Ikrimah: "then they repent soon," he said: The whole world is "soon."

8852 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "then they repent soon," before death.

8853 – Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from Abu Qilabah, who said: It was mentioned to us that when Iblis was cursed and granted respite, he said: "By Your might, I will not leave the heart of the son of Adam as long as the spirit is in him." Then the Blessed and Exalted said: "By My might, I will not prevent him from repentance as long as the spirit is in him."

8854 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: 'Imran narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: We were with Anas ibn Malik, and Abu Qilabah was there, and Abu Qilabah narrated, saying: Indeed Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, when He cursed Iblis, Iblis asked Him for respite, so He said: "By Your might, I will not leave the heart of the son of Adam!" Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, said: "By My might, I will not prevent him from repentance as long as the spirit is in him."

8855 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah, who said: Indeed Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, when He cursed Iblis, Iblis asked Him for respite, so He granted him respite until the Day of Judgment, and he said: "By Your might, I will not leave the heart of the son of Adam as long as the spirit is in him!" He said: "By My might, I will not withhold repentance from him as long as the spirit is in him."

8856 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: 'Awf narrated to us, from al-Hasan, who said: It reached me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Iblis saw Adam hollow, he said: 'By Your might, I will not leave from his inside as long as the spirit is in him!' Then Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, said: 'By My might, I will not come between him and repentance as long as the spirit is in him.'" [[The reports 8853–8856 are mursal (broken-chain) reports. Ibn Kathir referred to them in his tafsir, 2:380, then said: "This has been transmitted in a marfu' hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, through 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr and Abu al-Haytham al-'Itwari, both from Abu Sa'id, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: 'Iblis said: O Lord, by Your might and Your majesty, I will not cease to mislead them as long as their spirits are in their bodies!' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: 'By My might and My majesty, I will not cease to forgive them as long as they seek forgiveness from Me.'"]]

8857 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Qatadah, from al-'Ala' ibn Ziyad, from Abu Ayyub Bushayr ibn Ka'b: that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he has not begun the death rattle." [[The report 8857: "Bushayr ibn Ka'b ibn Abi al-Humayri, Abu Ayyub al-'Adawi." A well-known trustworthy narrator who transmitted from Abu al-Darda', Abu Dharr, and Abu Hurayrah. "Bushayr" is a diminutive.
This is another mursal hadith, which Imam Ahmad recorded in his Musnad, 6610, 6408, as marfu' from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit ibn Thawban, from his father, from Makhul, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, from Ibn 'Umar, and it is a sahih hadith. It was also transmitted by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, and al-Tirmidhi said: "hasan gharib." See its takhrij in the commentary on the Musnad of my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad.
"Al-gharghara": that one places drink in his mouth and moves it to the far end of the throat, then does not swallow it. They likened the fluttering of the spirit before its departure to the gargling of the sick person. This is a remarkable expression in one word for the state of one who witnessed it, which testifies that the Arabs were people of eloquence, and that their language is the most capable of depicting the subtle and the difficult in a single word.]]

8858 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, and then he mentioned the like. [[The report 8858: This is a munqati' (disconnected) hadith, since 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit died in the year 34 AH, and Qatadah was born in the year 61 AH. See the commentary on the preceding report.]]

8859 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from 'Awf, from al-Hasan, who said: It reached me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, accepts the repentance of the servant as long as he has not begun the death rattle." [[The report 8859: See the commentary on report 8857.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions, regarding this matter, is the view of the one who said: its interpretation is, "Then they repent before their death," in the state in which they understand the command and prohibition of Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, and before they are overcome in their selves and their minds, and before the time when they are occupied with the agony of the death-rattle (al-hashrajah) and the distress of the final gasp (al-gharghara), so that they neither recognize Allah's command and prohibition nor comprehend repentance. For repentance is not repentance except from one who feels regret for what has passed from him, and resolves to abandon returning to it, [[In the printed edition: "except from one who feels regret for what has passed from him, and resolves in it to abandon returning to it," altered from what was in the manuscript, because he saw its distortion; the manuscript read: "except from one who feels regret for what has passed from him, and recognizes in it the abandonment of returning to it." The first clause is sound and I have kept it; the second is a corruption whose correct reading is what I have adopted.]] and he comprehends regret and chooses to abandon returning to it. As for one who is preoccupied with the distress of death and overwhelmed by the grief of the death-rattle, I do not suppose he is anything but overcome in his regret for his sins. This is why the one who said, "Repentance is accepted as long as the servant has not reached the final gasp," [[His saying "This is why the one who said" indicates that Abu Ja'far, when he related the three mursal hadiths numbered 8857–8859, did not have what was authentically traced back to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.]] said so. So if a person in that state comprehends with the understanding of one who is sound, and grasps with the perception of an intelligent, discerning person, and then makes a fresh turning back from his sins, and a return from his straying from his Lord to His obedience, he will, God willing, be among those who enter into the promise of Allah, which He made to those who turn back to Him from their wrongdoing soon, in His saying: "Repentance with Allah is only for those who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon." [Qur'an 4:17]
* *
The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So those - Allah will turn to them in forgiveness, and ever is Allah Knowing and Wise﴾ [4:17]
Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "So those" (fa-ulaika), meaning: these who do evil in ignorance and then repent soon, "Allah will turn to them" (yatubu Allahu 'alayhim), in contrast to one who does not repent until his mind is overcome and the death-rattle of his dying overwhelms him, so that he says, while not understanding what he says, "Indeed I have repented now," deceiving his Lord and being hypocritical in his religion.
* *
The meaning of His saying "Allah will turn to them" is: He will grant them the turning back to His obedience, and accept from them their return to Him and the repentance they have made from their sins. [[See the entry on "tawbah" and "taba" in the linguistic indices of earlier volumes.]]
* *
As for His saying "and ever is Allah Knowing and Wise," it means: Allah, may His praise be exalted, has never ceased [[See the meaning of "kana" above, shortly before: 88 note 2, and the references there.]] to be "Knowing" (alim) of people among His servants who turn back to Him in obedience after turning away from Him, and who come back to Him after having turned their backs, and of other matters of His creation, and "Wise" (hakim) in His accepting the repentance of those of them who repent from their disobedience, and in other aspects of His management and decree; no defect enters His actions, and no error or slip mingles with them. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "lā yakhlituhu," but one says "khalaṭa al-shay' bi al-shay'" (mixed one thing with another), and this is not its place; the correct reading is what I have adopted. See also the entries on "alim" and "hakim" in the linguistic indices of earlier volumes.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 18:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be mighty, He means: "And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds," from among the people who persist in disobedience to God, "until, when death approaches one of them," meaning: when one of them is in the death rattle and sees the angels of his Lord coming toward him to seize his soul, and he has been overcome in himself and has been prevented from understanding, being occupied by the distress of his death rattle and his gasping, "he says, 'Indeed, I have repented now.'" Meaning: there is no repentance for this one with God, may He be blessed and exalted, because he said what he said not in a state of repentance, as:

8860 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Ya'la ibn Nu'man, who said: One who heard Ibn Umar say informed me: "Repentance is open as long as it has not reached the throat (sawq)." Then Ibn Umar recited: "And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, 'Indeed, I have repented now.'" Then he said: "And is the approach (hudur) anything other than the sawq?" [[The narration 8860: Ya'la ibn Nu'man is a Kufan, trustworthy. Listed in al-Kabir 4/2/418, Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/304, and Ta'jil al-Manfa'a: 457. He narrated from Ikrimah and Bilal ibn Abi al-Darda'. Narrated from him al-Ala' ibn al-Musayyab, al-Thawri, and al-Zuhri.

This report was cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:131, and he also attributed it to Abd al-Razzaq, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi.

"Saq al-mayyit yasuq" and "saqa bi-nafsihi," "saqa nafsahu," "sawqan wa-siyaqan wa-suwuqan," and "hadartu fulanan fi al-sawq, wa fi al-siyaq al-mawt": that is the death rattle at the approach of death.]]

8861 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: "And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, 'Indeed, I have repented now'": When death has become manifest in him, God does not accept repentance from him.

8862 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Abu al-Nadr, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas: "And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, 'Indeed, I have repented now'": there is no repentance for this one with God.

8863 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, saying: I heard Ibrahim ibn Maymun narrating, from a man of the Banu al-Harith, who said: a man among us narrated to us, from Abd Allah ibn Amr that he said: "Whoever repents a year before his death, it is accepted from him," until he mentioned a month, until he mentioned an hour, until he mentioned a fuwaq. He said: A man said: "How can this be, when God, may He be exalted, says: 'And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, "Indeed, I have repented now"'?" Abd Allah said: "I will tell you what I heard from the Messenger of God ﷺ." [[The narration 8863: Imam Ahmad cited it in his Musnad, no. 6920, and Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi: 301. My brother al-Sayyid Ahmad said in the commentary on the Musnad: "Its chain is weak, because of the ambiguity of the man from the Banu al-Harith, whose narrator is a Successor (tabi'i)," and he has fully discussed its takhrij there.

His words "until he mentioned a fuwaq" mean: the fuwaq of a she-camel. This is among the expressions they use for a short, brief time. The root of "fuwaq" (with a damma on the fa' and a fatha on the waw) is the interval between two milkings: when you open your hand, close it, and then release it during milking.]]

8864 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, from Ibrahim, who said: It used to be said: "Repentance is open as long as he has not been seized by the throat (kazm)." [["Al-kazm" (with two fathas), its plural "kizam" (with a kasra on the kaf) and "akzam," is the passage of breath at the throat. He means: at the departure of his soul and the cessation of his breath. From it comes the saying "kazama ghaydahu," meaning he suppressed and restrained it, and "rajul kazum," meaning one who is very secretive about what stirs within himself.

In the manuscript it read "ma akhadha bi-kazamih," which is a scribal error, and Ibn al-Athir narrated it, and al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:131, attributing it to Ibn Jarir and Ibn al-Mundhir, with the wording adopted by the editor of the first printed edition, which is the pure correctness, God willing.]]

* *

The interpreters differed regarding who is meant by His words: "And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, 'Indeed, I have repented now.'"

Some of them said: It refers to the hypocrites.

Those who said that:

8865 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "Repentance is only incumbent upon God for those who do evil in ignorance, then repent soon after" [Q. 4:17]. He said: The first was revealed concerning the believers, and the middle was revealed concerning the hypocrites, meaning: "And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds," and the last concerning the disbelievers, meaning: "Nor for those who die while they are disbelievers."

* *

Others said: Rather, it refers to the people of Islam.

Those who said that:

8866 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sufyan, who said: It has reached us concerning this verse: "And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, 'Indeed, I have repented now'," that they are the Muslims. Do you not see that He said: "Nor for those who die while they are disbelievers"?

* *

Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed concerning the people of faith, but it was abrogated.

Those who said that:

8867 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words: "And repentance is not for those who do evil deeds until, when death approaches one of them, he says, 'Indeed, I have repented now.' Nor for those who die while they are disbelievers." Then God, may He be blessed and exalted, revealed after that: ﴿Indeed, God does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [Q. 4:48, 116], so God forbade forgiveness for one who dies while a disbeliever, and deferred the people of monotheism to His will, and did not make them despair of forgiveness. [[The narration 8867: al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:131, and attributed it also to Abu Dawud in his Nasikh, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings in my view is what al-Thawri mentioned, that it reached him that it refers to Islam. [[Meaning the report no. 8866 above.]] That is because the hypocrites are disbelievers, and if it were meant to refer to the people of hypocrisy, His words "Nor for those who die while they are disbelievers" would have no understandable meaning, since they and those before them would have the same meaning: that all of them are disbelievers. There is no basis for differentiating their rulings, and the meaning for which repentance is rendered impossible for them [applies to them all alike]. And in God's distinguishing between their names and attributes, by naming one category "disbelievers" and describing the other category as "people of evil deeds" without calling them disbelievers, is evidence that their meanings differ. And in the soundness of this being so is the soundness of what we have said and the falsehood of what contradicts it. [[In the manuscript, after the words "understandable meaning," there is the text: "because if they were those before them in one meaning, that all of them are disbelievers. There is no basis for differentiating their rulings, and the meaning for which it became invalid that there be repentance of one," which is an extremely disordered phrasing. However, the copyist lightly struck through the lam of "li-annahum," so it became clear to me that what follows it is "idh kanu al-ladhina qablahum," and the waw was dropped by the copyist who was inattentive in writing it. He also erred by omitting "lahum," which I placed between the brackets. Thus the sentence became sound as I have written it.

As for the editor of the first printed edition, he greatly mishandled it, rendering the sentence thus: "because if they and those before them had one meaning: that all of them are disbelievers, then there is no basis for differentiating any of them in the meaning for which it became invalid that there be an accepted repentance of one." He failed to notice what the copyist struck through in "li-annahum," added to "kanu al-ladhina qablahum," making it "kanu hum wa-al-ladhina qablahum."
