Then he changed "wa-la wajh" to "fa-la wajh," changed "ahkamahum" to "ahadin minhum," then changed "wa-al-ma'na" to "fi al-ma'na," and added "maqbulah" from his own in the end of the sentence, corrupting the sentence with yet another corruption. May God have mercy on Abu Ja'far, and forgive the copyist of his book, and praise be to God who guided to the correct.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Nor for those who die while they are disbelievers; those, We have prepared for them a painful punishment﴾ (18).

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be mighty, He means: "Nor is repentance for those who die while they are disbelievers," so the place of "those" is in the genitive, because it is conjoined to His words "for those who do evil deeds." "Those, We have prepared for them a painful punishment," meaning: these are the ones who die while they are disbelievers, "We have prepared for them a painful punishment," because they are furthest from repentance, owing to their dying in disbelief. [[This is also another corruption by the editor of the first printed edition, who did not read the manuscript well, since it was undotted, so he turned this sentence around in a way that destroyed its meaning and eradicated the meaning Abu Ja'far intended, writing: "because they are farthest from repentance is their being in disbelief," taking "lamawnahum" as the copyist wrote it to be "kawnahum," and so he tampered with the speech in a way no scholar would accept. See the text of the passage in the report that follows.]] As in:

8868 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Abu al-Nadr, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas: "Nor for those who die while they are disbelievers": those are farthest from repentance.

* *

The scholars of the Arabic language differed concerning the meaning of "a'tadna lahum" (We have prepared for them).

Some of the Basran grammarians said: The meaning of "a'tadna" is "af'alna," from "al-'atad" (readiness). He said: its meaning is "a'addna" (We have readied).

* *

Some of the Kufan grammarians said: "a'addna" and "a'tadna" have the same meaning.

* *

So the meaning of His words "a'tadna lahum" is: We have readied for them "a painful punishment," meaning: painful, afflicting.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 19 (part 1 of 3):

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Blessed and exalted is He, by His saying [[The words between the brackets are an addition required by the context of his speech.]] "O you who have believed," means: O you who have affirmed Allah and His Messenger, ﴿it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force﴾, meaning: it is not lawful for you to inherit the marriage of the women of your relatives and fathers by force. [[See the explanation of "al-karh" (force) above, 4:297-298 / 6:565.]]

* *

If someone says: How did they used to inherit them? And what is the reason for forbidding their inheritance? For you know that women are inheritable just as men are inheritable!

It is said: That is not the meaning of inheriting them when they die and leave property. Rather, it is that in the Jahiliyyah, when a woman's husband died, his son or relative had more right to her than others, and she was (in his power) herself: if he wished, he married her; and if he wished, he prevented her ('adl) from others and did not marry her off until she died. So Allah, exalted is He, forbade this to His servants, and prohibited them from marrying the wives of their fathers, and forbade them from preventing them (i.e., 'adl) from marriage.

* *

And the people of interpretation said the same as what we have said about this.
Mention of those who said that:

8869 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Asbat ibn Muhammad narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, meaning: al-Shaybani, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: "O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force, nor to prevent them that you may take back part of what you have given them," he said: When a man died, his guardians had more right to his wife: if some of them wished, he married her; and if they wished, they married her off; and if they wished, they did not marry her off. And they had more right to her than her own family. So this verse was revealed concerning that. [[The report: 8869. "Abu Ishaq al-Shaybani" is Sulayman ibn Abi Sulayman; his biography has passed under nos. 1307, 3003, 3023. This report was recorded by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (Fath 8:184), al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 7:138, and Abu Dawud in his Sunan 2:310 no. 2089. al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:131, adding its attribution to Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Abi Hatim. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar has fully discussed it in al-Fath; see also Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:381-382.]]

8870 - And Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to me, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf, from his father, who said: When Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat died, his son wished to marry his wife, and this was (customary) for them in the Jahiliyyah. So Allah revealed: "It is not lawful for you to inherit women by force." [[The report: 8870. "Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi" is the teacher of al-Tabari; he is narrated from under the name "Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Habib" in al-Tarikh, and his full lineage is "Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Nayzak ibn Habib"; his biography has passed under no. 3833. "Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih al-Azdi al-Ataki" was a Rafidi (a Shi'i partisan), and he used to visit Ahmad ibn Hanbal, who would draw near to him and honour him. It was said to him about this, and he said: "Glory be to God! A man who loves a people from the People of the House of the Prophet ﷺ!" And he is trustworthy (thiqah). Yahya ibn Ma'in said: "A man from the people of Kufa is coming to you, called Abd al-Rahman ibn Salih; he is trustworthy, truthful, a Shi'i; for him to fall from the sky is more beloved to him than to lie in half a letter." Ibn Adi said: "He is well known among the Kufans; he was not mentioned for weakness in narration nor accused of it, except that he was extreme in what he held of Shi'ism." He is translated in al-Tahdhib. "Yahya ibn Sa'id" is al-Ansari, whose biography has passed under nos. 2154, 3395, 5074. "Muhammad ibn Abi Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf" narrated from his father, whose name was "As'ad," and from Aban ibn Uthman. Yahya ibn Sa'id, Ibn Ishaq and Malik narrated from him. He is trustworthy. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar, in his biography of him, pointed to this report, that al-Nasa'i narrated it; apparently it is in al-Sunan al-Kubra. "Abu Umamah ibn Sahl ibn Hunayf al-Ansari," whose name is "As'ad ibn Sahl...," was born in the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ two years before his death, as it is narrated. Ibn Sa'd said: "Trustworthy, abundant in narrations." This report was recorded by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:132, adding its attribution to al-Nasa'i and Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Kathir recorded it attributed to Ibn Mardawayh with the same wording, 2:382.]]

* *

8871 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from al-Husayn ibn Waqid, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, who both said regarding His saying: "It is not lawful for you to inherit women by force, nor to prevent them that you may take back part of what you have given them, except that they commit a clear immorality," that a man used to inherit the wife of his close relative and then prevent her until she died or returned to him her dowry. So Allah "ahkam" (restrained) him from that, meaning: Allah forbade you from that. [[The report: 8871. Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan 1:311 no. 2090, through Ali ibn Husayn ibn Waqid from his father, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas. Also al-Durr al-Manthur 2:131. His words "ahkam Allah 'ala dhalika" will be explained afterwards; its root is from "hakamtu al-faras wa ahkamtuhu," meaning when I bridled and restrained the horse; and "hakama al-rajul wa ahkamahu" means he prevented him from what he wanted. In the manuscript it reads "fa-ahkam 'an dhalika," and the first printed edition adopted the text of Abu Dawud and al-Durr al-Manthur.]]

8872 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Mijlaz regarding His saying: "O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force," he said: The Ansar used to do that. When a man's intimate (hamim) died, his intimate inherited his wife, so he had more right to her than the guardian of her own self. [["Al-hamim" is the relative whom you love and who loves you, and whose affair concerns you.]]

8873 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Ata al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force," the verse, he said: When a man's father or intimate died, he had more right to his wife: if he wished, he kept her, or he detained her until she ransomed herself from him with her dowry, or she died and he took her property. Ibn Juraij said: Ata ibn Abi Rabah informed me that the people of the Jahiliyyah, when a man died and left a wife, his family would detain her for the young boy among them, so the verse was revealed: "It is not lawful for you to inherit women by force," the verse. Ibn Juraij said: Mujahid said: When a man's father died, he had more right to his wife; he married her if he wished, if she was not his son's mother, or he married her to whomever he wished, his brother or his brother's son. Ibn Juraij said: Ikrimah said: It was revealed concerning Kabishah bint Ma'n ibn Asim, from the Aws, whom Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat left as a widow. His son inclined over her, so she came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Prophet of Allah, neither am I inheriting my husband, nor am I left to be married off!" So this verse was revealed. [[The report: 8873 is the account of Kabishah bint Ma'n. Ibn al-Athir recorded it in Usd al-Ghabah 5:538, attributing it to Abu Musa; al-Suyuti recorded it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:132, adding its attribution to Ibn al-Mundhir. Regarding his words "jana 'alayha" (inclined over her): it means he spread his wing or his protection over her and leaned over her, meaning that he leaned over her to keep people away from her. Report no. 8877 below contains a good explanation of the meaning of this word, namely the saying of al-Suddi: "If the heir of the deceased is first, and throws his garment over her, then he has more right to her, that he may marry her," so this act, i.e., throwing a garment over the woman, is what Ikrimah used the expression "jana 'alayha" for. I have not found in the lexicons anyone who recorded this good metaphor, and it deserves to be recorded there explained. So record it there if you wish. See also the throwing of a garment over a woman in the following reports nos. 8878, 8880, 8881, 8882.]]

8874 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force," he said: When a man died, his eldest son had more right to his wife: he married her if he wished, if she was not his mother, or he married her to whomever he wished, his brother or his brother's son.

8875 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Amr ibn Dinar, the same as the saying of Mujahid.

8876 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, saying: I heard Amr ibn Dinar say the like of that.

8877 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "It is not lawful for you to inherit women by force": In the Jahiliyyah, a man's father or brother or son would die, and when he died and left his wife, if the heir of the deceased was first and threw his garment over her, he had more right to her, to marry her with the dowry of the other, or to marry her and take her dowry. But if she got ahead of him and went to her family, they had more right to her person.

8878 - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman al-Bahili [[In the printed edition: "Ubayd ibn Sulayman," which is an error; the correct form is from the manuscript, and it has passed several times in this chain in the tafsir.]] informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: "It is not lawful for you to inherit women by force": In Medina, when a man's intimate died and left a wife, the man would throw his garment over her and inherit her marriage, and he had more right to her. And this was marriage among them. If he wished, he kept her until she ransomed herself from him. And this was in polytheism.

8879 - Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "It is not lawful for you to inherit women by force," he said: Inheritance was among the people of Yathrib, here in Medina. A man would die and his son would inherit his father's wife as he inherits his mother; she could not refuse. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "la yastati' an yamna'" (she is not able to prevent), which is an error by the copyist that does not make the sentence sound; the correct reading is as given.]] If he wished to take her, he took her, as his father used to take her; and if he disliked her, he separated from her; and if he was a child, she was held for him until he grew up. If he wished, he had intercourse with her; and if he wished, he separated from her. That is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: "It is not lawful for you to inherit women by force."

8880 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force." That was because men of Medina, when a man's intimate died, would throw his garment over his wife, and he inherited her marriage; no one else married her but him, and he held her with him until she ransomed herself from him with a ransom. So Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: "O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force."

8881 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ali ibn Badhimah, from Muqsim, who said: In the Jahiliyyah, when a woman's husband died, a man came and threw his garment over her, and he had more right to her than anyone. He said: So this verse was revealed: "It is not lawful for you to inherit women by force."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: So the interpretation of the verse according to this interpretation is: O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit your fathers' and relatives' marriage to their women by force. The mention of "fathers," "relatives," and "marriage" was dropped, and the address was directed to the prohibition of inheriting women, relying on the addressees' knowledge of the meaning of the speech, since its meaning was understood by them.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: It is not lawful for you, O people, to inherit their estates (tarikat) from women by force. He said: It was only said in that way because they used to detain their women, who were unwilling to be detained, until they died, and then they would inherit their wealth.

Mention of those who said that:

8882 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women by force," he said: When a man died and left a slave-girl, his intimate would throw his garment over her and prevent her from people. If she was beautiful, he married her; and if she was ugly, he detained her until she died and then he inherited her. [[In the printed edition: "If she was ugly he detained her..."; in the manuscript: "dhamima"; the correct reading is as given. "Al-damima" means the ugly one.]]

8883 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri regarding His saying: "It is not lawful for you to inherit women by force," he said: It was revealed concerning some men of the Ansar, who, when a man among them died, his guardian was the most entitled to his wife, so he would hold her until she died and then inherit her. So this was revealed concerning them.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the two interpretations of the verse is the saying we mentioned from the one who said: its meaning is: "It is not lawful for you to inherit the women of your relatives," [[In the printed edition: "an tarithu al-nisa' karhan aqaribakum," which is utterly corrupt; it mishandled the error that was in the manuscript, which read: "an tarithu al-nisa' aqaribakum," a slip of the pen by the copyist; the correct form is as given.]] because Allah, may His praise be glorified, has explained the inheritances of those entitled to inheritance; that belongs to its people, whether the deceased from whom they inherit that was a man or a woman was pleased with their inheriting him or disliked it.

[[In the manuscript: "fa-dhalika li-ahlihi nahwahu wirathatuhum iyyahu al-mawrutha dhalika 'anhu min al-rijal aw al-nisa' aw radiya". The first editor found the word "nahwahu" obscure and found no meaning for it, so he wrote the sentence: "fa-dhalika li-ahlihi nahwa wirathatuhum iyyahu al-mawrutha dhalika 'anhu min al-rijal aw al-nisa'. Fa-qad 'ulima bi-dhalika..." making "nahwahu" "nahwa" without the ha', and deleting "aw radiya" so the sentence would seem to work, but it became meaningless! The correct reading is that "nahwahu" should be read as "karhahu" (his disliking), so the sentence works as in the manuscript without deletion. The first printed edition did great harm to this noble book by the way it was altered, as you have seen in thousands of my notes, and as you will see. May God forgive us and him.]]

It is thus known by this that He, may His praise be glorified, did not forbid His servants to inherit women in what He made for them as an inheritance from them, [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "an yarithu al-nisa' ma ja'alahu lahum mirathan"; the context requires "fima" as I have recorded it.]] and that He only forbade that they be inherited by force, meaning the prohibition of inheriting their marriage, when their deceased whom they inherited had been the one who held authority over them in marriage, just as a man holds the usufruct of what he rents of houses, lands, and all his property's benefits. [[In the manuscript: "wa sa'ir malahu nafi'", and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition; his saying "ma lahu manafi'" means: and the rest of the things that have benefits which their owner benefits from.]]

So Allah, may His praise be glorified, made clear to His servants that what a man among them owns of his wife's womb [[The printed edition has "zawjatihi" (his wife), but I have recorded what is in the manuscript. "Al-bud'" (with a damma on the ba' and a sukun on the dad) is the woman's private part; it is said to be intercourse, and it is said to be the marriage contract. All are close, and the first is the closest, and the rest branch from it.]] is a meaning different from the meaning of what one of them owns of the usufructs of other property that may be rented. For the owner of his wife's womb, if he dies, what he owned of his wife by marriage does not pass to his heirs after him, as the things he owned by purchase, gift, or rent pass to them after his death by their inheriting it from him. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "bi-mirathihi dhalika anhu" in the singular; the correct form is the plural, as I have recorded it.]]

* *

As for His saying, exalted is He: "nor prevent them that you may take back part of what you have given them," the people of interpretation differed about its interpretation.

Some of them said: Its interpretation: "nor prevent them," that is: nor detain, O company of heirs of the men who have died, their wives from marrying the men they wish to marry, so that they may die, "and thus you take back part of what you have given them," that is: so that you take from their wealth when they die what your deceased whom you inherited had given them from their dowries.

Among those who said this were a group whom we have already mentioned some of, including Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan al-Basri, and Ikrimah. [[See the reports nos. 8871, 8873, 8877, and those following.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: nor prevent your women, O people, detaining them out of harm, when you have no need of them, so that you harm them that they may ransom themselves from you with what you have given them of their dowries.

Mention of those who said that:

٨٨٨٤ - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words ﴿and do not restrain them﴾, he said: "Do not oppress them." ﴿So that you may take away part of what you have given them﴾, meaning: a man has a wife whom he dislikes being married to, and she has a dower owed to her by him, so he harms her so that she will ransom herself (from him).

٨٨٨٥ - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿and do not restrain them﴾, he said: "It is not lawful for you to hold back your wife out of harm until she ransoms herself from you." He said: Ma'mar also informed us, saying: Sammak ibn al-Fadl informed me, from Ibn al-Baylamani, who said: "These two verses were revealed: one of them concerning the matter of the Jahiliyya (the pre-Islamic period), and the other concerning the matter of Islam."
[[The report 8885: "Sammak ibn al-Fadl al-San'ani" is trustworthy. Al-Thawri said: "Hardly any of his narrations is dropped, due to its soundness." "Ma'mar" is Ma'mar ibn Rashid, who narrates from him. "Ibn al-Baylamani" is Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Baylamani, a freedman of Umar. Trustworthy. His biography has passed under numbers 4946 and 4947.]]

٨٨٨٦ - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ma'mar, who said: Sammak ibn al-Fadl informed us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Baylamani, regarding His words ﴿It is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will, nor to restrain them﴾, he said: "These two verses were revealed: one of them in the Jahiliyya, and the other concerning Islam." Abdullah (i.e., Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak) said: "It is not lawful for you to inherit women in the Jahiliyya, nor to restrain them in Islam."
[[The report 8886: "Abdullah" means Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak. In the printed edition it read: "and the other in Islam," omitting "matter" (amr). The copyist of the manuscript also wrote it that way, but added "matter" in the margin, and so I have included it.]]

٨٨٨٧ - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Salim, from Sa'id, regarding "and do not restrain them," he said: "Do not confine them."

٨٨٨٨ - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿and do not restrain them that you may take away part of what you have given them﴾: as for "restrain them," he says: "Harm them so that they will ransom themselves from you."

٨٨٨٩ - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿and do not restrain them﴾: "Restraint (al-adl) is that a man dislikes his wife and harms her until she ransoms herself from him." God, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿And how could you take it back when you have been intimate with one another?﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 21].
[[In the printed edition: "Ubayd ibn Salman," which is an error that is very frequent in the previous printed edition; the correct form is from the manuscript, and it is a recurring chain in the tafsir.]]

* *

Others said: What is meant by the prohibition against restraining women in this verse is their guardians (awliya').
Those who said this:

٨٨٩٠ - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words ﴿and do not restrain them that you may take away part of what you have given them, unless they marry their husbands﴾, (it is) like the restraint in Surat al-Baqara.
[[See the explanation of the verse no. 232, in vol. 5, pp. 17–27. In the manuscript it read: "like the restraint in Surah," omitting "al-Baqara."]]

٨٨٩١ - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

Others said: Rather, the one prohibited from this is the husband of a woman after he has separated from her. They said: That was an action of the Jahiliyya, so they were forbidden from it in Islam.
Those who said this:

٨٨٩٢ - Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Restraint (al-adl) was practised among the Quraysh in Mecca: a man would marry a noblewoman, but perhaps she would not agree with him, so he would divorce her on condition that she not marry anyone except with his permission. He would bring witnesses and have this written down against her and witnessed. Then, when a suitor proposed to her, if she gave him (the suitor) what she gave him and pleased him, he would permit her; otherwise he would restrain her. He said: So this is the saying of God: ﴿and do not restrain them that you may take away part of what you have given them﴾, the verse.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: We have already explained in what has passed the meaning of "restraint" (al-adl) and its origin, with evidence from the indications of such proofs. [[See what has passed in vol. 5, pp. 24–25, and what precedes those reports.]]

The most correct of these sayings we have mentioned, in the interpretation of His words ﴿and do not restrain them that you may take away part of what you have given them﴾, is the saying of one who said: God, mighty is His praise, forbade a woman's husband from constraining her and harming her, while he dislikes her company and loves her separation, so that she would ransom herself from him with part of what he gave her of the dowry.

We only said that this is more correct, because there is no way for anyone to restrain a woman except one of two men: either her husband, by constraining her and confining her to himself while he dislikes her, harming her thereby, so that he takes back from her what he gave her by her ransoming herself from him in this way; or her guardian, to whom it falls to marry her off.

If there is no way to restrain her by anyone other than these two, and the guardian is known to be someone who has not given her anything (such that it could be said that if he restrained her from marriage, "he restrained her so that he would take back part of what he gave her"), then it is known that the one whom God, blessed and exalted, meant by His prohibition against restraining her is her husband, who has the way to restrain her out of harm so that she ransoms herself from him.

And if that is established, and it is known that God, may His remembrance be exalted, did not make a way for anyone over his wife after he has separated from her and she has become separated from him, so that he would have a way to restrain her in order that she ransom herself from his restraint of her, whether she has committed a gross immorality or not, [[The phrase "God, mighty is His praise" is joined to the phrase "and it is known."]] and God, mighty is His praise, had permitted husbands to restrain them when they commit a manifest immorality until they ransom themselves from him, [[The phrase "it is clear by that..." is the answer to "when" in the phrase "and when that is established."]] it was clear by that that the interpretation of Ibn Zayd was in error, and the interpretation of the one who said: "The prohibition against restraint in this verse means the guardians of unmarried women," [[The phrase "and the soundness of what we have said about it" is in the nominative, joined to "error" in the phrase "it was clear by that the error of the interpretation."]] and the soundness of what we have said about it.

* *

[The phrase]: ﴿and do not restrain them﴾, [[I added what is between the brackets, following Abu Ja'far's method in explaining all the previous verses.]] is in the accusative position, as a conjunction with His words ﴿that you inherit women against their will﴾. Its meaning: it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will, nor to restrain them. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "and do not restrain them," with "that" omitted, which is an error, as shown by his later words: "And so it is in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud." The recitation (qira'a) of Ibn Mas'ud is: ﴿nor that you restrain them﴾. See also al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 259.]]

And so it is in what is reported in the reading (harf) of Ibn Mas'ud.

If it were said: it is in the jussive position by way of prohibition, it would not be an error. [[See also al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 259.]]

* *

The discussion on His words: ﴿except that they commit a manifest immorality﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be mighty, He means: It is not lawful for you, O believers, to restrain your women out of harm from you, while you dislike their company and they are obedient to you, so that you may take away part of what you have given them of their dowries ﴿except that they commit a manifest immorality﴾; then it is lawful for you at that time to harm them so that they will ransom themselves from you. [[In the manuscript after "that they will ransom themselves from you" there is: "and do not restrain them that you may take away part of what you have given them," which is a repetition that the first editor wisely removed.]]

Then the interpreters differed regarding the meaning of "immorality" (fahisha) that God, mighty is His praise, mentioned in this place. [[See the explanation of "fahisha" and "fahsha'" previously, p. 73, note 3, and the sources there.]]

Some of them said: Its meaning is adultery (zina). They said: If a man's wife commits adultery, it becomes lawful for him to restrain her and harm her so that she ransoms herself from him with what he gave her of her dowry.
Those who said this:

٨٨٩٣ - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Ashath informed us, from al-Hasan, regarding a virgin who commits fornication: he said: She is to be flogged a hundred times, exiled for a year, and what she took from him is returned to her husband. And he interpreted this verse: ﴿and do not restrain them that you may take away part of what you have given them, except that they commit a manifest immorality﴾.

٨٨٩٤ - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ata al-Khurasani, regarding a man whose wife commits an immorality: he takes back what he gave her and expels her. Then the hudud (prescribed punishments) abrogated that (naskh).

٨٨٩٥ - Ahmad ibn Mani' narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, who said: If a man sees an immorality from his wife, [[In the manuscript: "if a man sees his wife an immorality," and the correct form is that of the printed edition.]] then there is no harm if he harms her and presses her until she seeks khul' (divorce by her ransom) from him.

٨٨٩٦ - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed me, from Ayyub, from Abu Qilaba, regarding a man who discovers an immorality from his wife: he mentioned something similar.

٨٨٩٧ - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿except that they commit a manifest immorality﴾: it is adultery. So if they do that, take their dowries.

٨٨٩٨ - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abd al-Karim informed me that he heard al-Hasan al-Basri (regarding) ﴿except that they commit an immorality﴾, he said: It is adultery. He said: I also heard al-Hasan and Abu al-Sha'tha' say: If she does that, it becomes lawful for her husband to be the one who asks her for khul', so that she ransoms herself. [[In the manuscript: "tafdi salha," which is unclear; the correct reading, in my judgment, is "nafsaha" (herself). As for the printed edition, it omitted the word entirely and made the verb "li-tafdi" (so that she ransoms).]]

* *

Others said: "The manifest immorality" in this place is nushuz (disobedience/ill-treatment of the husband by the wife).
Those who said this:

٨٨٩٩ - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿except that they commit a manifest immorality﴾, which is hatred and nushuz. So if she does that, then it is lawful for him to take a ransom from her.

٨٩٠٠ - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, saying: Anbasa narrated to us, from Ali ibn Badhima, from Miqsam, regarding His words: ﴿and do not restrain them that you may take away part of what you have given them, except that they commit an immorality﴾, in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud. He said: If she disobeys you and harms you, then it is lawful for you to take what she took from you.
[[The report 8900 passed under number 4828, and see the commentary there. In the manuscript: "then it is lawful for you what she took from you," and above "منك" there is a mark of error, and the first editor of the printed edition corrected it from al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 132; it passed in the earlier chain in the correct form. Here it read: "if she restrained and harmed you," and its correct form is from the earlier chain, as I showed there.]]

٨٩٠١ - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mutarrif ibn Tarif, from Khalid, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim: ﴿except that they commit a manifest immorality﴾, he said: The immorality here is nushuz. So if she is disobedient, it becomes lawful for him to take her khul' from her.
[[The report 8901: "Mutarrif ibn Tarif al-Harithi," who narrated from al-Sha'bi and Abu Ishaq al-Subay'i, and others; trustworthy. His biography is in al-Tahdhib. "And Khalid" is Khalid ibn Abi Nawf al-Sijistani, who narrates from Ibn Abbas in mursal form, and narrated from Ata ibn Abi Rabah and al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim. He is trustworthy. His biography is in al-Tahdhib.]]

٨٩٠٢ - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words ﴿except that they commit a manifest immorality﴾, he said: It is nushuz.

٨٩٠٣ - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ata ibn Abi Rabah said regarding ﴿except that they commit a manifest immorality﴾: if they do, then if you wish, keep them, and if you wish, release them.

٨٩٠٤ - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: [[In the printed edition: "Ubayd ibn Salman," which is an error that is very frequent in the printed edition; its correct form is from the manuscript, and it is a recurring chain in the tafsir, so I will not point out its correction again after this time.]] I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say regarding His words ﴿except that they commit a manifest immorality﴾: He said: Our Lord, blessed and exalted, acted justly in the judgment, then returned to the women and said: ﴿except that they commit a manifest immorality﴾; and "immorality" is disobedience and nushuz. So if that comes from her side, then God commanded him to strike her and commanded him to abandon her (hajr). If she does not give up disobedience and nushuz, then there is no blame on him after that for taking a ransom from her.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most fitting of what has been said regarding the interpretation of His words ﴿except that they commit a manifest immorality﴾ is that it refers to every "immorality": whether foul speech against her husband, [[In the printed edition: "badha'a" (foul speech), and I have kept what is in the manuscript; "al-badha'" and "al-bad'a" are the same.]] and harm to him, and adultery with her private part. That is because God, mighty is His praise, by His words ﴿except that they commit a manifest immorality﴾, encompassed every immorality that is clearly evident and apparent. [[In the printed edition: "manifest, apparent," which is the wording of the verse; in the manuscript, which is poorly written, I found it better to read "mutabayyina" (clearly evident), so I have kept it that way.]] So every husband of a woman who commits an immorality from among the immoralities, which is adultery or nushuz, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "fa-li-kull zawj imra'a" (so for every husband of a woman), and the context requires "fa-li-kull," as shown by his later words "then he has the right to restrain her."]] then he has the right to restrain her in accordance with what God has explained in His Book, and to constrain her until she ransoms herself from him, by whatever meanings of immorality she has committed, [[In the manuscript: "bi-anna ma'ani fawahish atat" which is a corruption; in the printed edition: "bi-ayyi ma'ani fawahish atat," which is correct, but he overlooked making "fawahish" into "al-fawahish" so that the Arabic of the statement would be sound.]] after it has become manifest and clearly evident, [[The phrase "according to the apparent meaning of God's Book" is connected to the word stated above: "so for every husband of a woman ... then he has the right to restrain her ... according to the apparent meaning of God's Book," and so the context goes.]] according to the apparent meaning of God's Book, blessed and exalted, and the soundness of the report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), like what was narrated:

٨٩٠٥ - Yunus ibn Sulayman al-Basri narrated to me, saying: Hatim ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from his father, from Jabir, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Fear God regarding women, for you have taken them by the trust of God, and made their private parts lawful by the word of God. And you have the right over them that they do not let anyone you dislike onto your bedding. If they do that, then strike them with a light blow, and they have a right over you to their provision and clothing according to what is customary."
[[The hadith 8905: "Yunus ibn Sulayman al-Basri," the teacher of al-Tabari: his name is thus established in this place. I did not find among al-Tabari's teachers anyone named thus, nor did I find that among all the narrators in the sources available to me. The more likely, in my view, indeed I nearly am certain, is that it is a corruption of "Yusuf ibn Salman." Al-Tabari narrated two pieces of this hadith from him with this chain: 2003 and 2365. It is the hadith of Jabir, the long one, concerning the Hajj. This hadith is a part of the hadith of Jabir ibn Abdullah, concerning the description of the Farewell Pilgrimage. We have shown its takhrij (sourcing) in 2003. This piece was mentioned by al-Suyuti, 2: 132, attributed to al-Tabari alone! He—may Allah have mercy on him—missed that it is a piece of the long hadith.]]

٨٩٠٦ - Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Zayd ibn al-Hubab narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Ubayda al-Rabadhi narrated to us, saying: Sadaqa ibn Yasar narrated to me, from Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "O people, women are with you as 'awan (captives). You have taken them by the trust of God, and made their private parts lawful by the word of God. You have a right over them, and they have a right over you. Among your rights over them is that they do not let anyone onto your bedding, nor disobey you in what is good. If they do that, then they have their provision and clothing according to what is customary."
[[The hadith 8906: Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi, the teacher of al-Tabari; his biography passed at 174. This chain is very weak, because of "Musa ibn Ubayda al-Rabadhi," as we showed at 1875 and 1876. The hadith was mentioned by al-Suyuti, 2: 132, and he did not attribute it to anyone other than al-Tabari. I have not found it elsewhere. Its meaning is established and sound, by the soundness of the hadith of Jabir just before it here. It is also established from the hadith of Amr ibn al-Ahwas al-Jushami, raised to the Prophet. It was transmitted by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, and al-Tirmidhi said: "A hasan sahih hadith," as in al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib 3: 73. It is also established from the hadith of Abu Hurra al-Raqashi from his paternal uncle, raised to the Prophet. Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 5: 72–73 (Halabi edition).
"'Awan" is the plural of "ani'a," meaning a captive. He says: they are with you in the position of prisoners. The Prophet of God spoke truly: he guided to the truth and clarified it, and he was kind and merciful to the believers. And "al-'aniya" is from "'ana al-rajul ya'nu 'anwan wa 'ana'" when a man humbles himself to you and becomes a captive; so he is "'ani."]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 19 (part 3 of 3):

= So the Prophet (ﷺ) informed that among the husband's rights over the wife is that she should not let anyone else lie on his bed, and that she should not disobey him in what is reasonable (ma'ruf). What is owed to her in provision and clothing is incumbent upon him, but this is obligatory on him only when she has rendered to him what is due from her, by refraining from letting another lie on his bed and from disobeying him in what is reasonable.

It is known that the meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying, "Among your rights over them is that they should not let anyone else lie on your beds," is only that they should not allow anyone other than you to have access to themselves. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "أن لا يمكن أنفسهن من أحد سواكم." In the manuscript, "لا" is written above the sin of "أنفسهن," as if he was about to correct the word and then overlooked it. The correct context requires the sentence to be as I have recorded it, and the copyist simply erred.]]

If what we have related on this matter is sound from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), then it is clear that when a woman lets her own self lie with another man and allows him to have intercourse with her instead of her husband, her husband has the same right to withhold clothing and provision from her, within what is reasonable, as he has to withhold them when she disobeys him in what is reasonable. Since this is his right, it is known that by withholding from her what he has the right to withhold, he is not depriving her of a right owed to her by him. Since this is so, it is clear that if she ransoms herself from her husband at that point, and the husband takes back from her what he gave her, he has not taken it through prohibited restraint (adl), but has taken what he took from her through a restraint that is permitted to him. Since this is so, it is clear that he falls under God's exception, blessed and exalted is He, by His saying: "And do not restrain them to take away part of what you have given them, unless they commit a clear immorality." Since this is established, it is clear that the view of those who say that "unless they commit a clear immorality" is abrogated (mansukh) by the prescribed penalties (hudud) is false [[See what has preceded, no. 8894.]], because the prescribed penalty is a right of God, exalted is His praise, upon the one who commits the immorality, which is fornication (zina). As for restraining the wife so that she ransoms herself from her husband with what he gave her or part of it, it is a right of the husband, just as his restraining her and constricting her life when she rebels against him, so that she ransoms herself from him, is a right of his. The ruling of one does not nullify the ruling of the other.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the verse is: "It is not lawful for you, O you who believe, to restrain your wives, constricting them and withholding from them their provision and clothing in what is reasonable, in order to take away part of the bridal gifts (sadaqat) you have given them, unless they commit a clear and manifest immorality, be it fornication, or abuse toward you and opposition to you in what is due to you from them. Then it becomes lawful for you at that time to restrain them and constrict them so that you may take back part of the dowry you gave them, if they ransom themselves from you with it."

* *

The readers (qurra') differed in their recitation of His saying: "mubayyina" (manifest).
Some of them read it as "mubayyanatin," with a fatha on the "ya," meaning that it has been made clear to you, announced and displayed.
Others read it as "mubayyinatin," with a kasra on the "ya," meaning that it is manifest and clear to people as an immorality.

* *

These are two widely transmitted recitations among the readers of the lands of Islam. Whichever of them the reader recites, he is correct in his recitation, because when the immorality is displayed by its perpetrator, it is manifest and clear. And when it becomes manifest, it becomes manifest through the perpetrator's displaying it. So it is not manifest and clear unless it has been made clear, and it is not made clear unless it is making clear. Therefore I judge both recitations, whichever the reader uses, to be correct.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And consort with them in kindness﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, "And consort with them in kindness," blessed and exalted is He means: Deal well with your wives, O men, and keep company with them "in kindness," meaning in accordance with what I have commanded you regarding companionship. That consists of either keeping them by rendering the rights which God, exalted is His praise, has made obligatory for them upon you, or releasing them from you with goodness. As:

8907 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, concerning "And consort with them in kindness," he said: "And mix with them."

* *

= Thus Muhammad ibn al-Husayn said, but it is in fact "khalliqu-hunna" (consort with them), from "al-'ushra," which is companionship. [[This distinction between "khaliqu-hunna" and "khalitu-hunna," and this correction by Abu Ja'far, reflect good discernment of the divergence of meanings and their proper rendering in conveying the senses of the language, especially in explaining its words.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿But if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and God makes in it much good﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, exalted is His remembrance, He means: Do not restrain your wives in order to take away part of what you have given them, without any impropriety or rebellion on their part; rather, consort with them in kindness even if you dislike them. Perhaps you will dislike them and yet keep them, and God will then place in your keeping them despite your dislike of them, much good: a child that He provides you through them, or your affection for them after your dislike of them. As:

8908 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "But if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing and God makes in it much good," he said: "Perhaps God will place much good in the dislike."

8909 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

8910 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to me, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: "And God makes in it much good," he said: "The child."

* *

8911 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And God makes in it much good." The abundant good is that he (the husband) should feel affection for her, so that the man is provided with her child, and God places in her child much good.

The "ha'" (pronoun) in His saying, "And God makes in it much good," according to the view of Mujahid which we have mentioned, refers back to the verbal noun of "tukrahu" (you dislike), as if the meaning of the statement in his view is: "But if you dislike them, perhaps you dislike a thing, and God places in its dislike much good." [[In the manuscript and printed edition, this clause is written exactly like the verse: "ويجعل الله فيه خيرًا كثيرًا." This is not right. Rather, the context requires that it be "في كرهه" ("in its dislike"), because it is an explanation of the meaning of his statement that the "ha'" in "fihi" refers to the verbal noun of "tukrahu."]]

If the interpretation of the statement were: "Perhaps you dislike a thing, and God places in that thing which you dislike much good," it would also be permissible and sound.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And if you wish to exchange one spouse for another, and you have given one of them a great amount of wealth, do not take back anything from it﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His saying, may His majesty be exalted, "And if you wish to exchange one spouse for another," he means: and if you, O believers, wish to marry a woman in place of a woman you have, whom you divorce [[See the explanation of "al-istibdal" (exchange) above, 2:130, 494 / 7:527.]] — "and you have given one of them," meaning: and you have already given her whom you wish to divorce from the dowry [[See the explanation of "al-itha'" (giving) in the indices of vocabulary, above.]] — "a great amount of wealth (qintar)."

* *

And "qintar" means a large amount of wealth. We have already mentioned above the disagreement of the people of interpretation regarding its measure, and the view we hold to be correct on that matter. [[See the explanation of "qintar" above, 6:244–250.]]

* *

"Then do not take anything from it," meaning: do not harm them when you wish to divorce them, so that they ransom themselves from you with what you have given them, as:

8912 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying, "And if you wish to exchange one spouse for another": the divorce of one woman in place of another, so it is not lawful for him to take anything from the property of the divorced woman, even if it is great.

8913 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Would you take it by slander and manifest sin?﴾ (20)

Abu Ja'far said: By His exalted saying, "Would you take it," he means: would you take back what you gave them of their dowries, "by slander," meaning: by injustice, without right, "and manifest sin," meaning: and a sin whose manifest nature makes clear that whoever takes it from them by taking it is an oppressor.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 21:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿How could you take it back when you have had intimacy with one another?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "How could you take it back" – He, may His praise be exalted, means: In what manner would you take back from your wives what you have given them as their dowries (ṣadāqāt), when you desire to divorce them and to exchange them for other wives as spouses? "When you have had intimacy with one another" – that is, when you have come together and touched one another.

* *

This statement, although its form is that of a question, carries the sense of censure and severity, just as a man says to another: "How could you do such-and-such, when I am not pleased with it?" – meaning a threat and a warning. [[In the printed edition: "al-tahdid" (threat); I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

* *

As for "al-ifḍā'" (intimacy) toward a thing, it is reaching it by direct contact with it, as the poet said: [[I do not know who the poet is.]]

[Their sinews] wore out with a wear that reached every ... (kutba), its thread showing from within after it had been visible without.

[[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "bali afḍā ilā kutbatin ... bada sayruhā min bāṭinin ba'da ẓāhir", with a blank space in the original between the words. I have added what is between the brackets by reasoned estimation so that the verse is metrically sound. "Al-kutba" (with a damma and then a sukun) is the tightly bound stitch which joins the two sides of the leather strip on a waterskin, a leather bucket, or a water-carrier. It is said: "kataba al-qirba", meaning he stitched the waterskin with two strips. This is a verse describing leather buckets or water-skins whose stitching has worn out severely, so that water dripped from them and they were no longer fit to carry water.]]

He means by this that corruption and wear reached the stitches. What is meant by "ifḍā'" in this place is sexual intercourse in the vagina.

* *

Thus the meaning of the statement, given that this is its meaning, is: How could you take back what you have given them, when you have had intimacy with one another through intercourse?

* *

Several of the people of interpretation have said in agreement with what we have said:

Those who said this:

8914 – Abd al-Ḥamīd ibn Bayān al-Qannād told me, saying: Isḥāq narrated to us, from Sufyān, from ʿĀṣim, from Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "al-ifḍā'" is direct contact, but God is generous and speaks euphemistically of what He wills.

8915 – Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Bakr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "al-ifḍā'" is intercourse, but God uses euphemism.

8916 – Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from ʿĀṣim, from Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muzanī, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: "al-ifḍā'" is intercourse.

8917 – Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr told me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, saying: ʿĪsā narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: "and you have had intimacy with one another," he said: sexual relations with women.

8918 – al-Muthannā told me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, the same.

8919 – Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī: "How could you take it back when you have had intimacy with one another," meaning copulation.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And they have taken from you a firm covenant﴾

Abu Ja'far said: That is: the pledge you gave them on your own selves, from the covenant and acknowledgement you made regarding what you acknowledged on your own selves, namely keeping them in kindness or releasing them with goodness. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "mā wathaqta bihi lahunna" – the shift of pronouns here is an error; the correct form is "wathaqtum", as I have given.]]

* *

It was the custom in the marriage contracts of the Muslims in earlier times, as has reached us, that the groom be told: "By God, [you must] keep her in kindness or release her with goodness!"

8920 – Bishr ibn Muʿādh narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda, regarding His words: "And they have taken from you a firm covenant." The firm covenant which He took from men for women is: keeping in kindness or releasing with goodness. And it was in the contracts of the Muslims at their marriages: "By God, you must keep her in kindness or release her with goodness." [[In the printed edition: "ʿahd al-Muslimīn"; I have kept the manuscript reading.]]

* *

The people of interpretation differed about the "covenant" (mīthāq) which God, may His praise be exalted, meant by His words: "And they have taken from you a firm covenant."

Some of them said: It is keeping in kindness or releasing with goodness.

Those who said this:

8921 – Yaʿqūb ibn Ibrāhīm told me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk regarding His words: "And they have taken from you a firm covenant," he said: keeping in kindness or releasing with goodness.

8922 – al-Muthannā told me, saying: ʿAmr ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, the same.

8923 – al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Maʿmar informed us, from Qatāda regarding His words: "And they have taken from you a firm covenant," he said: It is what God, blessed and exalted, took for women from men: keeping in kindness or releasing with goodness. He said: And that used to be taken at the conclusion of the marriage contract.

8924 – Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī: As for "And they have taken from you a firm covenant," it is that when a man marries a woman, her guardian says: "We have married her to you under the trust of God, on the condition that you keep her in kindness or release her with goodness."

8925 – ʿAmr ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to us, saying: Saʿīd narrated to us, from Qatāda regarding His words: "And they have taken from you a firm covenant," he said: "The firm covenant" which God took for women: keeping in kindness or releasing with goodness, and it was at the bond of the Muslims at their marriage: "By the oath of God upon you, you must keep her in kindness or release her with goodness."

8926 – ʿAmr ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, saying: Abū Qutayba narrated to us, saying: Abū Bakr al-Hudhalī narrated to us, from al-Ḥasan and Muḥammad ibn Sīrīn regarding His words: "And they have taken from you a firm covenant," he said: keeping in kindness or releasing with goodness.

* *

Others said: It is the words of marriage by which one makes lawful the private parts.

Those who said this:

8927 – Muḥammad ibn ʿAmr told me, saying: Abū ʿĀṣim narrated to us, from ʿĪsā, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: "And they have taken from you a firm covenant," he said: the words of marriage by which they made their private parts lawful.

8928 – al-Muthannā told me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, the same.

8929 – Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Abū Hāshim al-Makkī, from Mujāhid regarding His words: "And they have taken from you a firm covenant," he said: his saying: "I have married [nakaḥtu]." [[Report 8929: "Abū Hāshim al-Makkī" is Ismāʿīl ibn Kathīr, the companion of Mujāhid. Ibn Saʿd said: "Trustworthy, narrates much." Sufyān al-Thawrī, Ibn Jurayj, Musʿar ibn Kidām and others narrated from him. His biography is in al-Tahdhīb.]]

8930 – Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Ḥakkām narrated to us, saying: ʿAnbasa narrated to us, from Muḥammad ibn Kaʿb al-Qurazī: "And they have taken from you a firm covenant," he said: it is their saying: "You have taken possession of the marriage."

8931 – al-Muthannā told me, saying: Abū Nuʿaym narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Sālim al-Aftas, from Mujāhid: "And they have taken from you a firm covenant," he said: the words of marriage.

8932 – Yūnus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And they have taken from you a firm covenant," he said: the covenant is marriage.

8933 – ʿAmr ibn ʿAlī narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, saying: Sālim al-Aftas told me, from Mujāhid: "And they have taken from you a firm covenant," he said: the words of marriage, his saying: "I have married."

* *

Others said: Rather, it refers to the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "You have taken them under the trust of God, and made their private parts lawful by the word of God." [[See the two earlier reports, nos. 8905 and 8906.]]

Those who said this:

8934 – Ibn Wakīʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isrāʾīl, from Jābir and ʿIkrima: "And they have taken from you a firm covenant," the two said: You have taken them under the trust of God, and made their private parts lawful by the word of God.

8935 – al-Muthannā told me, saying: Isḥāq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abī Jaʿfar narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ: "And they have taken from you a firm covenant," and the firm covenant: you have taken them under the trust of God, and made their private parts lawful by the word of God.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most probable of these opinions in interpreting this is the view of the one who said: The covenant meant in this verse is the pledge taken for the woman from her husband at the conclusion of the marriage contract, to keep her in kindness or release her with goodness, which the man acknowledged. This is because God, may His praise be exalted, thereby enjoined men regarding their wives.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "mīthāq" earlier, in a manner sufficient to dispense with repeating it in this place. [[See what has preceded: 1:414 / 2:156, 157, 288 / 6:550.]]

* *

The scholars differed regarding the ruling of this verse: is it muḥkam (definitive) or mansūkh (abrogated)?

Some of them said: It is muḥkam, and it is not permissible for a man to take any of what he gave her when he wishes to divorce her, unless she is the one who wants the divorce.

* *

Others said: It is muḥkam; it is not permissible for him to take any of what he gave her in any circumstance, whether she is the one desiring the divorce or he is. Among those reported to have held this view is Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Muzanī.

8936 – Mujāhid ibn Mūsā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Ṣamad narrated to us, saying: ʿUqba ibn Abī al-Ṣahbāʾ narrated to us, who said: I asked Bakr about the woman who has obtained khul', whether he may take anything from her. He said: No. "And they have taken from you a firm covenant." [[This report was mentioned earlier as no. 4877, where it reads "ʿUqba ibn Abī al-Muhannā", see the note there; the sources are cited there. Abū Jaʿfar added another chain for this report from ʿUqba ibn Abī al-Ṣahbāʾ, from Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muzanī, in that place, and this is one of the indications of Abū Jaʿfar's abridgement of this tafsir.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, it is abrogated, abrogated by His words: ﴿It is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of God﴾ [Sūrat al-Baqara: 229].

Those who said this:

8937 – Yūnus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And if you desire to exchange a wife in place of another wife," up to His words: "And they have taken from you a firm covenant," he said: Then He later granted leniency, saying: ﴿It is not lawful for you to take anything of what you have given them, unless both fear that they will not keep within the limits of God. And if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of God, there is no blame upon them concerning that by which she ransoms herself﴾ [Sūrat al-Baqara: 229]. He said: So this abrogated that.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the opinions regarding this is the view of the one who said: "It is muḥkam and not abrogated," and it is not permissible for a man to take anything of what he gave her, when he wishes to divorce her without any nushūz on her part, nor any immorality committed by her.

That is because the abrogating ruling is that which negates its contrary among the rulings, as we have explained in our other books. [[See what has preceded, what he said in this book regarding "naskh": 3:385, 635 / 4:582 / 6:54, 118.]] His words: "And if you desire to exchange a wife in place of another wife" do not negate the ruling of His words: ﴿And if you fear that they will not keep within the limits of God, there is no blame upon them concerning that by which she ransoms herself﴾ [Sūrat al-Baqara: 229]. This is because what God prohibited for the man by His words: "And if you desire to exchange a wife in place of another wife, and you have given one of them a heap of gold, do not take anything from it," is taking back what he gave her when he is the one who desires to divorce her. As for what He permitted him to take from her by His words: ﴿there is no blame upon them concerning that by which she ransoms herself﴾, it is when she is the one desiring the divorce and he dislikes it, for some of the meanings we have mentioned elsewhere. [[See what has preceded: 4:549–585, and his discussion of abrogation regarding the two verses on pp. 579–583 of the same volume.]]

There is no negation of the ruling of one of the two verses in the ruling of the other.

Given that this is so, it is not permissible to rule that one of them is abrogating and the other abrogated, except by a proof that must be accepted.

As for what Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Muzanī said – that the husband of a woman who obtained khul' has no right to take back what he gave for her separation, when she is the one seeking separation and he is the one who dislikes it – it is not correct, because of the authentic report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that he ordered Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās to take back what he had given his wife as dowry and to separate from her, when she asked for separation from him, and the nushūz was on her part. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "in ṭalabat firāqahu" (if she asked for his separation); the correct reading is "idh" (when), as I have given.]] [[See the reports and traditions earlier, nos. 4807–4811, and the commentary upon them, which is the report of Thābit ibn Qays ibn Shammās.]]

**The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He: "And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women, except what has already passed. Indeed, it was an abomination and hateful, and an evil way." (22)**

Abu Ja'far said: It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning people who would take the wives of their fathers. Islam came while they were still doing so. Allah, blessed and exalted, forbade them to remain married to these women, and He pardoned them for what they had done of that in their Jahiliyyah (the time of ignorance before Islam) and their polytheism, not holding them accountable for it, provided they feared Allah in their Islam and obeyed Him in it.

**Mention of the reports transmitted about this:**

8940. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraj, from 'Ikrimah, regarding His words: "And do not marry those whom your fathers married of women, except what has already passed," he said: It was revealed concerning Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat, who married Umm 'Ubayd bint Sakhr, [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "bint Damrah," and the correct form from the references where the report is takhrij'd is as given. [[The report 8940: Ibn al-Athir related this report in the biography of Umm 'Ubayd bint Sakhr, then referred to it in the biographies of its people, and attributed the transmission of the report to Abu Musa Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr ibn Abi 'Isa al-Isfahani, in his supplement to Ibn Mandah. This matter requires lengthy investigation, as you see. I have confined myself to this indication of it. Umm 'Ubayd is: (Umm 'Ubayd bint Sakhr ibn Malik ibn 'Amr ibn 'Aziz). "Al-Jarwal" is a stone that fills a man's palm, so it seems his father named him Jarwal and named his brother Sakhr, in accordance with the custom of the Arabs in this. Also the Ansar frequently have "Sakhr" in their genealogies, and I did not find anyone among them named "Damrah," so I preferred what I have established. However, Ibn Kathir transmitted this report in his tafsir (2:388), and in it is "Umm 'Ubayd Allah bint Damrah," but reliance on Ibn Kathir's transmission in such a matter is not sound.
