As for the meaning of His saying "what is beyond that": it means what is other than these women whom He has forbidden to you, "that you seek with your wealth" — he says: that you seek and desire with your wealth, [[See the interpretation of "ibtaghā" in what has passed at 3:508, 4:163, 6:196, 564, 570, 7:53.]] either by buying with it, or by marriage with a known bridal gift, as His majesty and praise said: ﴿and they disbelieve in what is beyond it﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 91], meaning: in what is other than it and what is besides it. [[See the interpretation of "wara'" in what has passed at 2:348, 349, and the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:60, 261.]]

* *

As for the position of "an" in His saying "that you seek with your wealth," it is in the nominative, as an explanation of "ma" in His saying "And lawful for you is what is beyond that" in the recitation of one who recites "wa-uhilla" with the alif of "uhilla" vowelled with a damma, and in the accusative accordingly in the recitation of one who recites it "wa-ahalla" with the alif opened.

It may be that the accusative is possible in both recitations, in the sense of: "And lawful for you is what is beyond that, so that you may seek." When the preposition "lam" was dropped, it joined the verb before it and became accusative. [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:261.]] It may also be that it is in the genitive position with this meaning, [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "fa-hadha al-ma'na", which is an extremely corrupt error.]] since the "lam" in this position is known to be needed for the sentence.

* *

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying: ﴿chaste, not fornicating﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted in remembrance, "chaste" (muhsinin) he means: chaste (a'affa') by your seeking what is beyond what He forbade you of the women with your wealth [[See the interpretation of "ihsan" in what has passed just above: 165, 166.]] — "not fornicating", he says: not committing illicit sexual relations, as:

9025 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His saying: "chaste," he said: marrying; "not fornicating," he said: committing adultery with every adulteress.

9026 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "chaste": marrying; "not fornicating": fornication is adultery.

9027 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "chaste, not fornicating," he says: chaste, not adulterers.

* *

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying: ﴿So whatever you enjoy from them, give them their wages as an obligation﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters differed regarding the interpretation of His words: "So whatever you have enjoyed of them", ﴿فما استمتعتم به منهن﴾.

Some of them said: its meaning is: "So whatever you have had of them" (i.e., you have had intercourse with them), meaning: from the women, "then give them their wages as an obligation" (i.e., their dowries), a fixed obligation. [See the explanation of "istimta'" (enjoyment) under "m-t-'", "ita'" (giving) under "a-t-y", and "fard" (obligation) under "f-r-d" in the language indexes in the preceding volumes.]

Those who said this:

9028 - Al-Muthanna related to me, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, who said: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "So whatever you have enjoyed of them, give them their wages as an obligation", he said: If one of you marries a woman and then consummates the marriage once, her entire dowry becomes due. "Istimta'" is marriage, as in His words: ﴿And give the women their dowries graciously﴾ [Surah an-Nisa': 4].

9029 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan regarding His words: "So whatever you have enjoyed of them", he said: it is marriage.

9030 - Al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, who said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "So whatever you have enjoyed of them", (it means) marriage.

9031 - Al-Qasim related to us, who said: al-Husayn related to us, who said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding His words: "So whatever you have enjoyed of them", he said: he intended marriage.

9032 - Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "So whatever you have enjoyed of them, give them their wages as an obligation", the verse, he said: This is marriage, and there is nothing in the Qur'an but marriage. When you take her and enjoy her, give her her wage, the dowry. If she remits any of it to you, it is wholesome for you. Allah obligated her to observe the waiting period and assigned her inheritance. He said: "Istimta'" here is marriage, when he has consummated with her.

* * *

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: whatever you have enjoyed of them with a wage, the enjoyment of pleasure, not by a marriage in the absolute sense, in the manner of the marriage that takes place with a guardian, witnesses and a dowry.

Those who said this:

9033 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, who said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "So whatever you have enjoyed of them for a specified term, give them their wages as an obligation, and there is no blame upon you in what you mutually agree after the obligation", [His words "for a specified term" are, in this report from al-Suddi, part of the verse's context; see the following reports 9035–9043, and see al-Tabari's rejection of this reading at the end of the explanation of the verse.] This is the mut'a: a man marries a woman on condition of a specified term, with two witnesses, with permission from her guardian; when the term ends, he has no claim over her and she is free from him, and she must observe the waiting period for what is in her womb, and there is no inheritance between them; neither inherits from the other.

9034 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, who said: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "So whatever you have enjoyed of them", he said: meaning the marriage of mut'a.

9035 - Abu Kurayb related to us, who said: Yahya ibn 'Isa related to us, who said: Nasir ibn Abi al-Ash'ath related to us, who said: Ibn Habib ibn Abi Thabit related to me, from his father, who said: Ibn 'Abbas gave me a codex (mushaf) and said: This is according to the reading of Ubayy. [Abu Kurayb said: In the manuscript and the printed edition it reads "Abu Bakr" instead of "Abu Kurayb", which is an error by the copyist, as you see.] Yahya said: I saw the codex with Nasir, and in it: "So whatever you have enjoyed of them for a specified term". [The report 9035: Yahya ibn 'Isa al-Ramli, the teacher of Abu Kurayb, whose biography has passed as no. 6317, then 7418. Nasir ibn Abi al-Ash'ath, also called Ibn al-Ash'ath al-'Aradi al-Asadi, narrated from Abu Ishaq al-Sab'i and others. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. As for "Ibn Habib ibn Abi Thabit", I could not establish which of them he is; they are 'Abd Allah ibn Habib, 'Ubayd Allah ibn Habib and 'Abd al-Salam ibn Habib, whom al-Daraqutni mentioned, saying: "The sons of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, all of them trustworthy." In the printed edition "ibn" was dropped, reading "Habib ibn Abi Thabit", while it is present in the manuscript. His father is Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who narrated from Ibn 'Abbas; his biography passed shortly before, no. 9012.]

9036 - Humayd ibn Mas'ada related to us, who said: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, who said: Dawud related to us, from Abu Nadra, who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about the mut'a of women. He said: Do you not read Surat an-Nisa'? I said: Yes! He said: Do you not read in it: "So whatever you have enjoyed of them for a specified term"? I said: No! If I had read it thus, I would not have asked you! He said: Then it is thus.

9037 - Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, who said: 'Abd al-A'la related to me, who said: Dawud related to me, from Abu Nadra, who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about the mut'a, and he mentioned similar.

9038 - Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, who said: Shu'ba related to us, from Abu Salama, from Abu Nadra, who said: I recited this verse to Ibn 'Abbas: "So whatever you have enjoyed of them". Ibn 'Abbas said: "For a specified term". I said: I do not recite it thus! He said: By Allah, Allah sent it down thus! Three times.

9039 - Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, who said: Abu Dawud related to us, who said: Shu'ba related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Umayr: that Ibn 'Abbas recited: "So whatever you have enjoyed of them for a specified term".

9040 - Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, who said: Ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, from Shu'ba = and Khallad ibn Aslam related to us, who said: al-Nadr informed us, who said: Shu'ba informed us = from Abu Ishaq, from Ibn 'Abbas, similarly.

9041 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, who said: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, who said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, who said: In the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "So whatever you have enjoyed of them for a specified term".

9042 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, who said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, who said: Shu'ba related to us, from al-Hakam, who said: I asked him about this verse: "And the married women, except what your right hands possess", up to this point: "So whatever you have enjoyed of them", is it abrogated? He said: No. al-Hakam said: 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, said: Had 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, not forbidden mut'a, none would have committed fornication except a wretched person.

9043 - Al-Muthanna related to me, who said: Abu Nu'aym related to us, who said: 'Isa ibn 'Umar al-Qari al-Asadi related to us, from 'Amr ibn Murra: that he heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr reciting: "So whatever you have enjoyed of them for a specified term, give them their wages."

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two interpretations is the interpretation of the one who interpreted it as: "So whatever you have married of them and had intercourse with, give them their wages" — because of the established proof of Allah's prohibition of mut'a with women outside the valid marriage or valid ownership, upon the tongue of His Messenger ﷺ.

9044 - Ibn WakI' related to us, who said: My father related to us, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz, who said: al-Rabi' ibn Sabra al-Juhani related to me, from his father: that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Enjoy (istimta') these women." And "istimta'" among us at that time meant marriage. [The hadith 9044: al-Tabari, may Allah have mercy on him, or his teacher Sufyan ibn WakI' abbreviated the wording of the hadith, which gave a meaning other than what its complete context indicates. Ibn WakI', al-Tabari's teacher, is Sufyan ibn WakI', who is weak, as we explained earlier: 142. The hadith was related by Imam Ahmad in the Musnad in full: 15415 (vol. 3, p. 405–406, Halabi), and there is a great difference between Ahmad and Ibn WakI'. He related it from WakI', with this chain, and in it: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: Enjoy these women. He said: And 'istimta'' among us at that time meant marriage. He said: We presented that to the women, and they refused except that we set a term between us and them. He said: We mentioned that to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: Do it" — then he mentioned the account of his enjoying a woman for ten days, and that he spent the night with her: "Then in the morning I went out toward the mosque, and there was the Messenger of Allah ﷺ between the door and the Hijr, addressing the people, saying: O people, I had permitted you the enjoyment of these women. Beware, Allah, blessed and exalted, has forbidden that until the Day of Resurrection" — to the end of the hadith.

Al-Bayhaqi related it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 7: 203, similarly, through Abu Nu'aym, from 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz.

Ahmad related the hadith of Sabra ibn Ma'bad on the prohibition of mut'a, in full and abridged, through many routes (3: 404–405).

Similarly Muslim related it, 1: 395–396, in full and abridged.

The story of Sabra ibn Ma'bad occurred either during the Hajj of Farewell or during the conquest of Mecca, according to differing reports from him on this. al-Hafiz said in Fath al-Bari 9: 147: "The report from him that it was at the conquest is more sound and more widely known." In any case, the prohibition in it is the final abrogating ruling, and al-Hafiz elaborated fully on the explanation of abrogation, 9: 143–151.

See also al-Muhalla 9: 519–520, and al-Bayhaqi's al-Sunan al-Kubra 7: 200–207.]

* * *

We have already shown that mut'a outside valid marriage is forbidden, in another place in our books, with what suffices so that it need not be repeated here.

* * *

As for what is reported from Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Ibn 'Abbas regarding their recitation: "So whatever you have enjoyed of them for a specified term", it is a reading contrary to what the codices of the Muslims contain. It is not permissible for anyone to add to the Book of Allah, the Exalted, something that has not come with a decisive report that excuses one from whom opposing it is not permitted.

* * *

The discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿And there is no blame upon you in what you mutually agree after the obligation. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾ (24)

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters differed regarding the interpretation of that.

Some of them said: the meaning is: there is no sin upon you, O husbands, if hardship befalls you after you have fixed for your wives their wages as an obligation, in what you mutually agree of remission and release, after the obligation previously set by you for them, which you had fixed.

Those who said this:

9045 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to us, who said: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman related to us, from his father, who said: A man from Hadramawt claimed that men used to fix the dowry, and then one of them might be struck by hardship, so Allah said: "And there is no blame upon you in what you mutually agree after the obligation."

Others said: the meaning is: there is no blame upon you, O people, in what you and the women with whom you enjoyed a specified term mutually agree, when the term you set between you and them for separation has ended, that they may extend the term for you, and you increase the wage and the obligation, [In the manuscript: "that they may extend the term for you, and you increase the wage", and what is in the printed edition is the better of the two wordings.] before they have purified their wombs.

Those who said this:

9046 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, who said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "And there is no blame upon you in what you mutually agree after the obligation": if he wished to please her after the first obligation, meaning the wage he gave for his enjoyment of her, before the term between them ended, and said: "I enjoy you again for such and such," and she increased before her womb was purified, then the period ends. This is His words: "in what you mutually agree after the obligation."

Others said: the meaning is: there is no blame upon you, O people, in what you and your women mutually agree after you have given them their wages for your enjoyment of them, of staying or parting.

Those who said this:

9047 - Al-Muthanna related to us, who said: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, who said: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "And there is no blame upon you in what you mutually agree after the obligation", and mutual agreement: that he pays her dowry and then gives her the choice.

* * *

Others said: rather, the meaning is: there is no blame upon you in what your women remit to you of their dowries after the obligation.

Those who said this:

9048 - Yunus related to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And there is no blame upon you in what you mutually agree after the obligation": if she remits any of it to you, it is wholesome for you.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings is the saying of the one who said: the meaning is: there is no blame upon you, O people, in what you and your women mutually agree after giving them their wages for the marriage that took place between you and them, of remitting what was due to them from you, or releasing, or deferring and waiving. This is similar to His words, exalted is His praise: ﴿And give the women their dowries graciously; but if they give you of it willingly, then consume it with satisfaction and ease﴾ [Surah an-Nisa': 4].

As for what al-Suddi said, it is a saying without meaning, because it contradicts the permission of intercourse with a woman without marriage or ownership by right hand.

* * *

As for His words: "Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing and Wise", it means: Indeed, Allah is ever possessed of knowledge of what sets right your affairs, O people, in your marriages and other matters, and the affairs of all His creation; "Wise" in what He arranges for you and for them, and in what He commands and forbids you, no flaw or error entering His wisdom. [See the explanation of "Knowing" (alim) and "Wise" (hakim) in the language indexes above.]

**On the interpretation of His words, ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford (ṭawl) to marry free believing women﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Ṭabarī) said: The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wīl) differed over the meaning of *al-ṭawl* (ṭawl, "means" or "capacity") mentioned by God in this verse.

Some of them said: It means bounty, wealth, and abundance.

Those who said this include:

9049. Muḥammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abū 'Āṣim narrated to us, from 'Īsā, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His words, ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford ṭawl﴾, he said: *al-ghinā* (wealth).

9050. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, the same.

9051. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Mu'āwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to me, from 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn 'Abbās, concerning His words, ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford ṭawl﴾, he said: Whoever does not have *sa'a* (ample means).

9052. Bishr ibn Mu'ādh narrated to us, saying: Yazīd narrated to us, saying: Sa'īd narrated to us, from Qatāda, concerning His words, ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford ṭawl﴾, he said: Whoever among you is not able to have *si'a* (ample means).

9053. al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abū Bishr narrated to us, from Sa'īd ibn Jubayr, concerning His words, ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford ṭawl﴾, he said: *al-ṭawl* is *al-ghinā*.

9054. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Ḥibbān ibn Mūsā narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubārak informed us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Abū Bishr, from Sa'īd ibn Jubayr, concerning His words, ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford ṭawl﴾, he said: *al-ṭawl* is *al-si'a* (ample means).
[[Note on the text: In the printed edition it reads "Ḥadatha Ibn al-Muthannā" with the added word "ibn", which is absent in the manuscript; the manuscript reading is correct, and the narration of "al-Muthannā" from "Ḥibbān ibn Mūsā" occurs in hundreds of places, such as 4498, 4528, 4548, and what will come shortly, nos. 9059, 9061.]]

9055. Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, concerning ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford ṭawl﴾: as for His words *ṭawl*, it is ample wealth.

9056. Yūnus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words, ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford ṭawl﴾, the verse, he said: *ṭawl* means he does not find what he can marry a free woman with.

* *

Others said: The meaning of *al-ṭawl* in this place is *al-hawā* (desire).

Those who said this include:

9057. Yūnus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: 'Abd al-Jabbār ibn 'Umar narrated to me, from Rabī'a, that he said concerning His words, ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford ṭawl﴾, he said: *al-ṭawl* is *al-hawā*. He said: One marries a slave woman if his desire is for her.
[[Note: "'Abd al-Jabbār ibn 'Umar al-Ayli" has had his biography given under no. 4068. The printed edition had "'Abd al-Jabbār ibn 'Amr," which is an error.]]

9058. Yūnus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: Rabī'a would soften this somewhat. He used to say: If one fears for himself, if he loves her (i.e., the slave woman), even though he is able to marry someone other than her, then I think he should marry her.

9059. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Ḥibbān ibn Mūsā narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubārak informed us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Salama informed us, from Abū al-Zubayr, from Jābir, that he was asked about a free man marrying a slave woman. He said: If he has *ṭawl*, then no. It was said: What if love for the slave woman falls into his heart? He said: If he fears *al-'anat* (sin/hardship), then let him marry her.

9060. Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from 'Ubayda, from al-Sha'bī, who said: A free man should not marry a slave woman, unless he does not find (the means) — and Ibrāhīm used to say: There is no harm in it.

9061. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Ḥibbān ibn Mūsā narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubārak informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: I heard 'Aṭā' say: We do not dislike that a man of means today marries a slave woman, if he fears that he will be wretched because of her.
[[In the printed edition: "an yasʿā bihā" (that he will strive for her); this is what the manuscript reads, and the correct reading is what is given. He means by this what passed in the earlier reports, "if he fears al-'anat."]]

* *

Abū Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions regarding this is the opinion of the one who said: The meaning of *al-ṭawl* in this place is ample means and wealth, because of the consensus of all that God, blessed and exalted, did not forbid any of the things — except marrying slave women for one who has the means to marry a free woman — and then permitted what He had forbidden in such matters when desire overcame the one forbidden, for the satisfaction of pleasure.
[[The first editor found the meaning of this sentence and the one after it problematic. The meaning is: God did not forbid something and then permit it because desire overpowered or for the sake of pleasure. Rather, He permitted the forbidden out of necessity, where the one compelled fears for his own destruction. Since this is a consensus of all regarding everything He forbade, marrying slave women is similar, and cannot be permitted for the sake of overpowering desire.]]
Since that is a consensus of all regarding what is other than marrying slave women for one who has the means, the same applies to the prohibition: marrying slave women for one who has the means is not made lawful for him because desire for her has overcome him, because that, while he is able to marry a free woman, is for the satisfaction of pleasure and lust, and is not a situation of necessity that is lifted by a dispensation,
[[In the printed edition: "not a situation of necessity that repels his dispensation," which is not correct wording. In the manuscript: "tarfa'u bi-rukhsa" (lifted by a dispensation) without dots; the correct reading is what is given here.]]
like carrion for one compelled who fears the destruction of his own soul, so that he may eat it in order to preserve his life, and similar forbidden things for which God has granted dispensation to His servants in a state of necessity and fear of destruction for themselves, though those things remain forbidden to them in other circumstances.
[[The phrase "mā ḥurrima ʿalayhim minhā" is the object of "rakhkhasa Allāh li-ʿibādihi" (God granted dispensation to His servants).]]
God, blessed and exalted, has not granted a servant dispensation in what is forbidden for the satisfaction of pleasure. And in the consensus of all that if a man is overcome by desire for a woman, whether free or slave, she is not lawful to him except by marriage or purchase as God has permitted, there is what clarifies the corruption of the view of those who said: "The meaning of *al-ṭawl* in this place is desire," and permitted the one with means to marry a free woman to marry slave women.

* *

Thus the interpretation of the verse, since the matter is as we have described, is: And whoever among you does not find sufficient means of wealth to marry free women, then let him marry from what your right hands possess.

* *

The root of *al-ṭawl* is *al-ifḍāl* (bestowal, favor). It is said from it: "ṭāla ʿalayhi yaṭūlu ṭawlan," meaning in bestowal; and "ṭāla yaṭūlu ṭūlan," in the sense of length, which is the opposite of shortness.

* *

**On the interpretation of His words, ﴿to marry believing chaste women, and from what your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾**

Abū Ja'far said: He means by this: And whoever among you, O people, cannot afford *ṭawl* — meaning among the free — ﴿to marry chaste women﴾, who are free women, ﴿believing﴾, who have affirmed the oneness of God and what the Messenger of God ﷺ brought of truth.

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wīl) said the same concerning *al-muḥṣanāt* (chaste women) as we have said.

Those who said this include:

9062. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Mu'āwiya ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to me, from 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭalḥa, from Ibn 'Abbās, concerning His words, ﴿to marry chaste women﴾, he said: to marry free women, so let him marry from the slave women of the believers.

9063. Muḥammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abū 'Āṣim narrated to us, from 'Īsā, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, concerning His words, ﴿to marry believing chaste women, and from what your right hands possess﴾, he said: *al-muḥṣanāt* are the free women; so let him marry the believing slave woman.

9064. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: Abū Ḥudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, the same.

9065. Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī: As for *fatayātikum* (your young women), they are your slave women.

9066. al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, saying: Abū Bishr informed us, from Sa'īd ibn Jubayr, concerning ﴿to marry believing chaste women, and from what your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾, he said: As for one who does not find what he can marry a free woman with, he marries the slave woman.
[[In the printed edition: "fa-yatazawwaju al-amata" (so he marries the slave woman); the manuscript reading is what is given.]]

9067. Yūnus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words, ﴿to marry believing chaste women, and from what your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾, he said: He does not find what he can marry a free woman with, so he marries this slave woman, and he preserves his chastity through her, and her family bears her expenses for him. God did not permit that to anyone, except one who does not find what he can marry a free woman with and spend on her, and it is not lawful to him until he fears *al-ʿanat* (sin).
[[In the printed edition: "... except for one who does not find what he can marry a free woman with and spend on her." The manuscript reading is what is given here; it is the correct and good one.]]

9068. al-Muthannā narrated to us, saying: Ḥibbān ibn Mūsā narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubārak informed us, saying: Sufyān informed us, from Hishām al-Dastawā'ī, from 'Āmir al-Aḥwal, from al-Ḥasan: that the Messenger of God ﷺ forbade a slave woman to be married while a free woman is married (to the man), and forbade a free woman to be married while a slave woman is married (to him); and whoever finds *ṭawl* for a free woman, let him not marry a slave woman.

* *

Abū Ja'far said: The readers (qurrā') differed in reciting this. A group of the readers of Kufa and Mecca recited ﴿an yankiḥa al-muḥṣanāt﴾ with a kasra on the *ṣād*, along with all similar instances in the Qur'an, except His words, ﴿and the chaste women from among women, except what your right hands possess﴾ [Sūrat al-Nisā': 24], where they put a fatḥa on its *ṣād*, and they interpreted it to mean that they are chaste by their husbands, and that their husbands made them chaste. As for the rest of the Qur'an, they interpreted the kasra on its *ṣād* to mean that the women made themselves chaste through chastity.

* *

The readers of Medina and Iraq generally recited all of that with a fatḥa, in the sense that some of them were made chaste by their husbands, and some were made chaste by their freedom or their Islam.

* *

Some of the early readers recited all of it with a kasra, in the sense that they were chaste and made themselves chaste. This reading, meaning with kasra throughout, is reported from 'Alqama, with differences in the narrations from him.
[[Abū Ja'far did not refer, in the interpretation of Sūrat al-Nisā' 24 above, to this reading, nor did he mention this difference in the recitation of *al-muḥṣanāt*. This is among the evidences of his condensing the tafsīr, as I have pointed out many times.]]

* *

Abū Ja'far said: Our correct view on this is that they are two widely transmitted readings among the readers of the regions, and with the agreement of their meaning. Whichever one the reader recites, he is correct, except in the first word [of Sūrat al-Nisā' 24], which is His words, ﴿and the chaste women from among women, except what your right hands possess﴾. I do not permit the kasra on its *ṣād*, because the readers of the regions agree on its fatḥa. [[All of this was not mentioned in the interpretation of the first verse of al-Nisā'; the explanation of the meaning of *al-iḥṣān* has passed shortly before: 165, 166.]] If the reading with its kasra were as widely transmitted as its fatḥa, it would be correct to recite it that way too, because of the varied uses of *al-iḥṣān* in the meanings we have explained. So its meaning if read with a kasra would be: the chaste women among women are forbidden to you, except what your right hands possess, in the sense that they made themselves chaste through chastity. [[All of this was not mentioned in the interpretation of the first verse of al-Nisā'; the explanation of the meaning of *al-iḥṣān* has passed shortly before: 165, 166.]]

* *

As for *al-fatayāt* (young women), they are the plural of *fatāh*, which means young women. Then every female slave who is of an age or young is called *fatāh*, and a male slave is called *fatā*.

* *

Then the scholars differed concerning marrying non-believing slave women, and whether God meant by His words, ﴿from your believing young women﴾, the prohibition of all those other than believers among them, or whether that is a divine instruction (ta'dīb) for the believers.

Some of them said: That is from God, exalted is He, as an indication of the prohibition of marrying slave women of polytheists.

Those who said this include:

9069. Muḥammad ibn Bashshār narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Raḥmān narrated to us, saying: Sufyān informed us, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿from your believing young women﴾, he said: It is not fitting for one to marry a Christian slave woman.

9070. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyān, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid: ﴿from your believing young women﴾, he said: It is not fitting for a free Muslim to marry a slave woman from the People of the Book.

9071. 'Alī ibn Sahl narrated to us, saying: al-Walīd ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: I heard Abū 'Amr, Sa'īd ibn 'Abd al-'Azīz, Mālik ibn Anas, and Abū Bakr ibn 'Abd Allāh ibn Abī Maryam say: It is not lawful for a free Muslim man or a Muslim slave, a Christian slave woman, because God says, ﴿from your believing young women﴾, meaning in marriage.
[[Report 9071: al-Walīd ibn Muslim al-Dimashqī, whose biography has passed under nos. 2184, 6611. "Abū 'Amr" is al-Awza'ī; in the printed edition and manuscript it read "Abū 'Amr Sa'īd," as if it were one person, or "Abū 'Amr" and "Sa'īd," and the correct reading is what is given. Sa'īd ibn 'Abd al-'Azīz al-Tanūkhī, Abū Muḥammad, whose biography has passed under no. 8966. As for Abū Bakr ibn 'Abd Allāh ibn Abī Maryam al-Ghassānī, he was among the devout and diligent worshippers and narrated many hadith but was weak. Abū Ḥātim said: "Weak in hadith; thieves attacked him and took his goods, and he became confused." He died in the year 156. In Tahdhīb al-Tahdhīb there is an error in the year of his death, written as "the year 256," and the correct year is 156. Ibn Sa'd has also given his biography in his Ṭabaqāt, 7/2/170, in the fifth edition, among the people of Syria, in which is also "Sa'īd ibn 'Abd al-'Azīz al-Tanūkhī." In the printed edition and manuscript it stood as "Mālik ibn 'Abd Allāh ibn Abī Maryam," and there is no narrator by that name; the correct reading is what is given. Abū Bakr ibn Abī Maryam is one from whom al-Walīd ibn Muslim narrated, as he narrated from all those mentioned before him.]]

* *

Others said: That is from God as guidance and recommendation, not as prohibition. Among those who said this were a group of the people of Iraq.

Those who said this include:

9072. Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Jarīr narrated to us, from Manṣūr, from Mughīra, who said: Abū Maysara said: As for the People of the Book, they are in the position of free women.

* *

= Among them is Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions, [[The phrase "Among them is Abū Ḥanīfa and his companions" is joined to the earlier statement before the report: "a group of the people of Iraq said that..."]] and they argued for their position with God's words: ﴿Lawful for you are the good things, and the food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you, and your food is lawful for them; and the chaste women from among the believers and the chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you, when you have given them their bridal payments﴾ [Sūrat al-Mā'ida: 5]. They said: God has made lawful the chaste women of the People of the Book in general, so no one may specify from among them a slave woman or a free woman. They said: The meaning of His words, ﴿believing young women﴾, is non-idolatrous, meaning not from the worshippers of idols.

* *

Abū Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions on this is the opinion of the one who said: It is an indication of the prohibition of marrying slave women of the People of the Book, for they are not made lawful except by ownership of the right hand. That is because God, mighty is His praise, made the marriage of slave women lawful under conditions, so whoever does not combine the conditions by which He named them, it is not permissible for a Muslim to marry them.
[[In the printed edition: "the conditions by which He named them", while the manuscript reads "the conditions by which He named them" with the correct form given here, which is good.]]

* *

If someone says: Does not the verse in *al-Mā'ida* indicate their permissibility for marriage?

It is said: As for the one in *al-Mā'ida*, it has made clear that its ruling applies to a particular group of their chaste women, and that what is meant by it is their free women and not their slave women, which is indicated by His words, ﴿from your believing young women﴾. Neither of the two verses dismisses the ruling of the other; rather, each of them explains the ruling of the other. One of the two would only dismiss the ruling of the other if it were impossible for both rulings to stand together as correct. [[In the printed edition and manuscript here: "ḥukmahā," in the singular; the correct reading is the dual, as given.]] It is not permissible to rule that one of them dismisses the other unless by a proof accepted from a report or analogy, and there is no report or analogy for that. The verse can bear what we have said: the chaste women from among the free women of those who were given the Scripture before you, apart from their slave women.

* *

**On the interpretation of His words, ﴿And God knows best your faith; you are of one another﴾**

Abū Ja'far said: This is from what is postponed in its wording but whose meaning is preposed (*al-mu'akhkhar alladhī ma'nāhu al-taqdīm*).

* *

Its interpretation: "And whoever of you cannot afford the means to marry free believing women, then [let him marry] from those whom your right hands possess of your believing slave-girls" (﴿فَمِمَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ مِنْ فَتَيَاتِكُمُ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾), so let some of you marry from others. The meaning is: let this man marry the slave-girl of that man.
* *
"Some of you" (al-ba'ḍ, بعض) is in the nominative case by way of the sense of the statement. Its meaning, since His saying "from what your right hands possess" carries the sense of "let him marry from what your right hands possess," then "some of you" is taken back to that meaning and is therefore in the nominative.
* *
Then He, mighty is His praise, said: ﴿وَاللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ بِإِيمَانِكُمْ﴾ ("And God knows best your faith"). [[In the manuscript the verse is completed here with "some of you from others", and the first editor was right to omit this addition here, because the context of the exegesis is that His saying "And God knows best your faith" comes before His saying "some of you from others".]] That is: God knows best the faith of whoever among you believes in God and His Messenger and in what he brought from God, and affirms all of that. [[The context: "And God knows best ... among you."]]
* *
He says: let whoever of you cannot afford the means to marry a free woman marry a believing slave-girl of yours. Let this needy man, who cannot afford the means to marry a free woman, marry from this wealthy man his believing slave-girl who has shown her faith and made it manifest. Leave their inner states to God, for knowledge of that belongs to God, not to you, and God knows best your inner states and theirs.
* *
On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿فَانْكِحُوهُنَّ بِإِذْنِ أَهْلِهِنَّ وَآتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ بِالْمَعْرُوفِ﴾ ("So marry them with the permission of their people, and give them their bridal payments justly").
Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, mighty is His praise, "so marry them" (فانكحوهن), He means: marry them [[See the explanation of "nikah" (marriage) above, 7: 574.]]. By "with the permission of their people" (بإذن أهلهن) He means: with the permission of their guardians, and with their command to you to marry them and their consent [[See the explanation of "idhn" (permission) above, 2: 449, 450 / 4: 286, 371 / 5: 352, 355, 395 / 7: 288, 377.]]. By His saying "and give them their bridal payments" (وآتوهن أجورهن) He means: give them their dowries [[See the explanation of "itā'" (giving) above in the index of language, and the explanation of "ujūr" (payments) above shortly before: 175.]], as:
9073 - Yunus told us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding "and give them their bridal payments": it is the dowry.
* *
By His saying "justly" (بالمعروف) He means: according to what you agree upon, of what God has made lawful for you and permitted you, that you make it as dowries for them [[See the explanation of "al-ma'rūf" (what is customary/just) above: 121, note 1, and the sources there.]].
* *
On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿مُحْصَنَاتٍ غَيْرَ مُسَافِحَاتٍ وَلا مُتَّخِذَاتِ أَخْدَانٍ﴾ ("chaste women, not fornicating openly, nor taking secret lovers").
Abu Ja'far said: By His saying "muhsanāt" (محصنات) He means: chaste [[See the explanation of "muhsanāt" above shortly before: 151, 168, 185.]]; "not fornicating openly" means not committing unlawful sexual acts (mezāwīn) [[See the explanation of "al-sifāḥ" (open fornication) above shortly before: 174.]]; "nor taking secret lovers" means: nor taking friends for illicit relations.
* *
It is mentioned that this was said in this way, [[In the printed edition: "And it has been mentioned..." with the added "qad"; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] because the prostitutes in the pre-Islamic period among the Arabs were those who openly committed adultery, and "those who take secret lovers" (المتخذات الأخدان) were women who confined themselves to a single lover and a close companion, for fornication with him in secret rather than publicly declaring it.
Those who said this:
9074 - Al-Muthanna told us, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "chaste, not fornicating openly, nor taking secret lovers": he means, marry them as chaste women, not prostitutes in secret or openly; "nor taking secret lovers" means: friends.
9075 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying "not fornicating openly": "those who fornicate openly" are those who openly commit adultery; "nor taking secret lovers": those who have one lover. He said: The people of the pre-Islamic period used to forbid what was apparent of adultery and permit what was hidden, saying: "As for what is apparent of it, it is baseness; as for what is hidden, there is no harm in it." So God, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿وَلا تَقْرَبُوا الْفَوَاحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ﴾ ("And do not approach indecencies, whether apparent or concealed," Surah al-An'am: 51).
9076 - Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Mu'tamir told us, saying: I heard Dawud narrate, from Amir, who said: Adultery is of two kinds: one commits adultery with a secret lover and does not commit it with anyone else; and the woman is "sawman" [[In the printed edition: "and the woman is a shu'm (ill omen)", which is a statement with no meaning here. In the manuscript it is "sawman", without dots, which is correct. "Sawm" means an offer; it is said: "an offer was made to me in a sawm manner," meaning the offer was made to me without exaggeration, as water is offered to camels, which drink once after another. It is used as a metaphor for one who offers you what you are not in need of, like a man who knows that you have stopped at his house as a guest and he offers you hospitality. From it is "al-sawm," the offering of goods for sale. This has the meaning of what will come in the report No. 9080: "the prostitute who hires herself out to whoever offers her." This word is not explained in the dictionaries, so I have recorded it there.]] Then he recited: ﴿مُحْصَنَاتٍ غَيْرَ مُسَافِحَاتٍ وَلا مُتَّخِذَاتِ أَخْدَانٍ﴾.
9077 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: As for "muhsanāt," they are the chaste; so let him marry the slave-girl with the permission of her people, as a chaste woman. "Muhsanāt" means the chaste; "not fornicating" means: "fornicating" means openly committing adultery; "nor taking a friend" means a companion.
9078 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying "nor taking secret lovers": a man takes a mistress, and a woman takes a lover.
9079 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.
9080 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatada regarding: "chaste, not fornicating openly, nor taking secret lovers": "fornicating" is the prostitute who hires herself out to whoever offers her. "One who has a lover" is one who has a single lover. So God forbade them to marry either of them.
9081 - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman told us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say regarding His saying: "chaste, not fornicating openly, nor taking secret lovers": as for "muhsanāt," they are free women, meaning: marry a free woman. As for "fornicating," they are those who openly fornicate without a bridal payment [[In the printed edition: "those who openly make it known" (al-mu'lanāt), and in the manuscript: "the one who openly makes it known." I considered that the correct version is what I have recorded.]]. As for "taking secret lovers," it is the woman who has a single lover whom she keeps hidden. [[Al-mustasirra: the one who hides herself, from "al-sirr" (secrecy).]] God forbade that.
9082 - Al-Qasim told us, saying: Al-Husayn told us, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Isma'il ibn Salim informed us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: Adultery has two ugly aspects, one of which is more vile than the other. As for the more vile of them: it is "al-musafiḥa," who commits fornication with whoever comes to her. As for the other: it is the one who has a secret lover (dhāt al-khidn).
9083 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "chaste, not fornicating openly, nor taking secret lovers": he said: "al-musāfiḥ" is the one who meets a woman and commits adultery with her, then he leaves and she leaves. "Al-mukhādin" is the one who remains with her in disobedience to God and she remains with him; that is "al-akhdān" (secret lovers).
* *
On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿فَإِذَا أُحْصِنَّ﴾ ("When they are chaste").
Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed regarding the reading of this.
Some of them read it: ﴿فَإِذَا أُحْصِنَّ﴾ with an opening "alif", meaning: when they embrace Islam, so they become protected from forbidden unlawful intercourse by Islam.
* *
Others read it: ﴿فَإِذَا أُحْصِنَّ﴾, meaning: when they marry, so they become protected from unlawful intercourse by husbands.
Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this, in my opinion, is that both are well-known, widely transmitted readings in the cities of Islam, so whichever of them the reader recites is correct in his recitation.
* *
If someone supposes that what we have said on this is impermissible, since the two are different in meaning, and that a reading in two ways is only permitted for what the meanings agree upon, then he has been heedless. [[His saying "he has been heedless" is the answer to the condition in "if someone supposes." "Aghfala" is an intransitive verb, meaning he fell into heedlessness. See the explanation of a similar usage above: 1: 151, note 1 / 5: 52, note 4 = then: 160, note 1.]]
That is because the two meanings, though they differ, do not exclude one another, for God has obligated the free woman who is a Muslim and the one who is not a Muslim, by the tongue of His Messenger ﷺ, the prescribed punishment (ḥadd).
9084 - He ﷺ said: "If the slave-girl of one of you commits adultery, let him flog her, according to the Book of God, and let him not reproach her. Then if she does it again, let him flog her, according to the Book of God, and let him not reproach her. Then if she does it again, let him flog her, according to the Book of God, and let him not reproach her. Then if she commits adultery a fourth time, let him flog her, according to the Book of God, and sell her even for a rope of hair." [[Report 9084: a sound hadith, transmitted without a chain, and it seems to be from the Musnad of Abu Hurayra. Al-Bukhari transmitted it in other wording (al-Fath 4: 350 / 12: 143-147), and Muslim 12: 211, and Ahmad in his Musnad No. 7389, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 8: 242-244, through several chains.
His saying "the Book of God" is in the accusative. In a narration of al-Nasa'i it is "with the Book of God."
His saying ﷺ "and let him not reproach her" means: he should not shame her for adultery, nor rebuke her for what she did, nor blame her harshly. This is the courtesy of the Prophet of God ﷺ toward his community: that they should not shame one who has committed a sin for what he committed, that they should show him kindness and turn away from reminding him of the immorality, lest his soul be filled with grief, anger and hatred toward people. But you see the people of our time who overpower everyone who commits a crime, so that the press is filled with abuse and innuendo and ugly descriptions for everyone who commits a crime, as if one of them had taken a pledge from the remaining days of his life that he would never be entangled in sin or crime. Who knows, perhaps the one with the longest tongue in that is the one most concealing of what is worse than the crime the offender committed.]]
9085 - And he ﷺ said: "Establish the prescribed punishments upon what your right hands possess." [[Report 9085: Ahmad transmitted it in his Musnad, Nos. 736, 1137, 1142, 1230, and al-Bayhaqi, al-Sunan al-Kubra 8: 243. See its takhrij in the Tafsir of Ibn Kathir 2: 406.]]
* *
So he did not specify from them a married woman or one who is not married. Therefore the prescribed punishments are obligatory upon the masters of the slave-women to carry out upon them, if they commit adultery, according to the Book of God and the command of the Messenger of God ﷺ.
* *
If someone says: What do you say about what has been related to you:
9086 - Ibn Bashshar said: Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Malik ibn Anas told us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah, from Abu Hurayra and Zayd ibn Khalid: that the Prophet ﷺ was asked about a slave-girl who commits adultery and is not chaste. He said: Flog her; if she commits adultery, flog her; if she commits adultery, flog her; if she commits adultery, [he said in the third or fourth time] sell her even for a rope. "Al-ḍafīr" (rope) is hair.
9087 - Abu Kurayb told us, saying: Ibn Uyayna told us, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah, from Abu Hurayra and Zayd ibn Khalid: that the Messenger of God ﷺ was asked, and he mentioned something similar. [[Reports 9086 and 9087: the first chain was transmitted by Malik in al-Muwatta, p. 826-827, with slight differences in wording, and at its end he said: "al-ḍafīr, the rope", and both have the same meaning. Al-Bukhari (al-Fath 4: 350 / 12: 143-145) and Muslim 12: 212-213 transmitted it through several chains.]]
* *
This shows that the prescribed punishment which must be carried out by the Sunnah of the Messenger of God ﷺ on slave-women is what was before their being chaste. As for what is obligatory upon them by the Book, is it after their being chaste?
It is said to him: We have already explained that one meaning of "iḥṣān" (chastity/protection) is Islam, and the other meaning is marriage, and that "iḥṣān" is a word that encompasses various meanings. [[See what preceded shortly before, pp. 151-196.]] There is no clarification in the report of those who related from the Prophet ﷺ that he was asked "about a slave-woman who commits adultery before she is made chaste" that the one he was asked about is the one who commits adultery before marriage, so that this would be proof for one who argues that the "iḥṣān" which the Prophet ﷺ prescribed as the punishment of slave-women for adultery is Islam and not marriage, nor that it is marriage and not Islam.
Since there is no clarification in this, the correct view is that every enslaved woman who commits adultery is obligated to have the prescribed punishment carried out upon her by her master, whether she is married or unmarried, according to the apparent meaning of the Book of God and what is established in the Sunnah of the Messenger of God ﷺ, except for those whom it is necessary to accept as exempted from the obligation of the prescribed punishment.
Since this is the case, the soundness of what we have chosen as the reading in His saying "fa-idhā uḥṣina" is established.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: If someone supposes that in the saying of God, mighty is His mention: ﴿وَمَنْ لَمْ يَسْتَطِعْ مِنْكُمْ طَوْلًا أَنْ يَنْكِحَ الْمُحْصَنَاتِ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ فَمِمَّا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ مِنْ فَتَيَاتِكُمُ الْمُؤْمِنَاتِ﴾ there is an indication that His saying "fa-idhā uḥṣina" means "they married," since its mention came after describing them as believers by His saying "from your believing slave-girls" [[The word "wa-ḥasiba" (and he supposed) is conjoined to "fa-in ẓanna ẓānn" (if someone supposes).]], and he supposed that this does not allow any meaning other than marriage, along with the previous description of them as believers, then he has supposed wrongly. [[His saying "then he has supposed wrongly" is the answer to the condition in "if someone supposes."]]
That is because it is not impossible in speech that the meaning of that is: "And whoever of you cannot afford the means to marry chaste believing women, then [marry] from what your right hands possess of your believing slave-girls," and when they have believed, "if they commit a flagrant act, then upon them is half the punishment of chaste women," so the statement would be a new announcement of what is obligatory upon them of the prescribed punishment if they commit a flagrant act after their faith, [[In the printed edition: "then the statement is an explanation of what is obligatory upon them of the prescribed punishment," which differs from the manuscript through poor editing; the correct version is what I have recorded from the manuscript. Moreover, the words "statement" (khabar) and "beginning" (mubtada') are not used in the grammatical sense established among grammarians, but rather God's announcement, and that it is a beginning not connected to what came before.]] after the explanation of what it is not permissible for believers to marry from them and of whom it is permissible for them to marry from among them.
Since that is not impossible in speech, it is not permissible for anyone to direct its meaning to marriage rather than Islam, on account of the previous description of them as believers by God.
* *
However, what we choose for the one who reads ﴿مُحْصَنَاتٍ غَيْرَ مُسَافِحَاتٍ﴾ with an opening "ṣād" (muḥṣanāt) in this place, is to read ﴿فَإِذَا أُحْصِنَّ فَإِنْ أَتَيْنَ بِفَاحِشَةٍ﴾ with a "ḍamma" on the "alif" (uḥṣinna).
And for the one who reads "muḥṣināt" with a kasra on the "ṣād" in it, let him read ﴿فَإِذَا أُحْصِنَّ﴾ with an opening "alif" (fatḥa), so that the reader's recitation is consistent in one meaning and one context, because "muḥṣanāt" is close to "fa-idhā uḥṣina." If one differs from that, it would not be a grammatical error, but the justification for the reading is what I have described.
* *
The people of interpretation have differed on its interpretation, just as the readers have differed on its reading. Some of them said: the meaning of His saying "fa-idhā uḥṣina" is: when they embrace Islam.
Those who said this:
9088 - Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Bazi' related to me, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaḍḍal told us, from Sa'id, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ibrahim, that Ibn Mas'ud said: her embracing Islam is her chastity. [[Report 9088: "Sa'id" is Sa'id ibn Abi Arouba. "Abu Ma'shar" is Ziyad ibn Kulayb. In the printed edition and the manuscript it was "Sa'id ibn Abi Ma'shar," which is a clear error.]]
9089 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Jarir ibn Hazim informed me that Sulayman ibn Mihran told him, from Ibrahim ibn Yazid, from Hammam ibn al-Harith: that al-Nu'man ibn Abd Allah ibn Muqarrin asked Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud and said: My slave-girl committed adultery? He said: Flog her fifty lashes. He said: But she is not chaste! Ibn Mas'ud said: Her chastity is her embracing Islam.
9090 - Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim: that al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin asked Ibn Mas'ud about a slave-girl who committed adultery and had no husband, and he said: Her embracing Islam is her chastity. [[Reports 9089 and 9090: In the first chain, "Ibrahim ibn Yazid" is Ibrahim al-Nakha'i. "Hammam ibn al-Harith al-Nakha'i" is trustworthy; he was among the worshippers and would not sleep except sitting. He narrated from Ibn Mas'ud.
In the first chain it is mentioned: "al-Nu'man ibn Abd Allah ibn Muqarrin," thus in both the manuscript and the printed edition; I have not found this name mentioned in the books, and in the report that follows it is "al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin." There has been disagreement about "al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin": it is said "al-Nu'man ibn Amr ibn Muqarrin," and it is said they are two men. This is detailed in the books of biographies, and none of them mentioned "al-Nu'man ibn Abd Allah ibn Muqarrin."]]

This is a Tabari text with an incomplete start. Let me translate it.

Moreover, al-Bayhaqi narrated this report in al-Sunan al-Kubra (8:243), and he added to the difficulty by transmitting it from the hadith of Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, from Hammam ibn al-Harith, from Amr ibn Sharahil, that Ma'qil ibn Muqarrin came to Abdullah ibn Mas'ud = and I was not able to be certain of anything in this confusion.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This interpretation accords with the reading of one who read ﴿فَإِذَا أُحْصِنَّ﴾ with a damma on the alif, and with the interpretation of one who read ﴿فَإِذَا أُحْصِنَّ﴾ with a fatha on it. We have already explained the correct position in this matter, both in speech and in reading.

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿فَإِنْ أَتَيْنَ بِفَاحِشَةٍ فَعَلَيْهِنَّ نِصْفُ مَا عَلَى الْمُحْصَنَاتِ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "fa-in atayna bi-fahishah," the Exalted means: if your slave-girls, who are your female slaves, after they became chaste by Islam, or were made chaste by marriage, [[See the explanation of "committed the fahishah" in what has preceded: 73, 81.]] "bi-fahishah," which is fornication [[See the explanation of "al-fahishah" in what has preceded: 3:303 / 5:571 / 7:218 / 8:73, 115, 116.]] "then upon them is half of what is upon the chaste women of punishment": meaning, upon them is half of the hadd that is upon free women, if they commit fornication before becoming chaste through husbands.

* *

The "punishment" which Allah, blessed and exalted, mentions in this place is the hadd, and that half which Allah made a punishment for slave-women who commit fahishah when they are chaste: fifty lashes, and exile for six months, which is half a year. For the obligation upon a free woman, if she commits fahishah before becoming chaste through a husband, is a hundred lashes and a year's exile. So half of that is fifty lashes and half a year's exile. This is what Allah made a punishment for chaste slave-women when they commit fahishah, as:

9108 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: "Then upon them is half of what is upon the chaste women of punishment"........... [[Report 9108: this report is incomplete in the manuscript and the printed edition, though he presented it as if it were not incomplete, so these dots were placed to indicate the gap. I did not find it elsewhere.]]

9109 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "Fa-in atayna bi-fahishatin fa-alayhinna nisfu ma ala al-muhsanati mina al-adhab," fifty lashes, and no exile nor stoning.

* *

If someone says: how is it said "then upon them is half of what is upon the chaste women of punishment"? Can flogging be upon someone?

It is said: the meaning of that is: what is binding on their bodies is that they be flogged half of what is binding on the bodies of chaste women, just as it is said "upon me is a day's prayer," meaning: it is binding on me to pray a day's prayer, [[In the manuscript: "lazim ila an usalli," and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.]] and "upon me is the Hajj and fasting," similarly. And likewise "upon him is the hadd," meaning: it is binding on him that his person be made available for the hadd to be carried out on him.

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿ذَلِكَ لِمَنْ خَشِيَ الْعَنَتَ مِنْكُمْ﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "dhalika," the Exalted means: this which I have permitted, O people, from marrying your believing slave-girls, for the one among you who cannot afford the means to marry believing free women: I have permitted it for one who fears ihnat among you, to the exclusion of others who do not fear ihnat.

* *

The people of interpretation differed on this point.

Some said: it is fornication.

Those who said this:

9111 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from al-Awwam, from one who narrated to him, from Ibn Abbas that he said: "The one who marries a slave-girl hardly refrains from fornication, except a little." [[Report 9111: Sahib al-Lisan mentioned this report under (zahlaf) and (zalhaf), and said regarding "izlahaf" that it is inverted from "izhalaf" on the pattern of "iqshaarr," and both are read with the zay sukun, the lam and ha' fathah, and the shaddah on the fa'. His saying "izlahaf" means: withdrew and kept away, a little. The rest of the report in al-Lisan: "for Allah, mighty and majestic, says: and that you be patient is better for you." See the following report no. 9114.]]

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: the punishment which causes him ihnat, which is the hadd.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct position regarding His words "Dhalika li-man khashiya al-ʿanata minkum" is: that is for one among you who fears harm to his religion and his body.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This is because "al-ʿanat" is that which harms a man. It is said from it: "Fulan has been harmed (ʿanita), so he is harmed (yaʿnatu), an ʿanat," when he encounters what harms him in religion or worldly affairs. From it is the saying of Allah, blessed and exalted: ﴿وَدُّوا مَا عَنِتُّمْ﴾ [Surah Al ʿImran: 118]. And it is said: "Fulan has caused me ʿanat, so he causes me ʿanat," when he inflicts harm upon me. It has also been said: "al-ʿanat" means destruction.

* *

= Those who directed the interpretation of this to fornication said: fornication is harm to religion, and it is of the ʿanat.
= Those who directed it to sin said: all sins are harm to religion, and they are of the ʿanat.
= Those who directed it to the punishment which causes ʿanat to the body, which is the hadd, said: the hadd is harm upon the body of the one punished in his worldly life, and it is of the ʿanat.

Allah has encompassed in His words "li-man khashiya al-ʿanata minkum" all the meanings of ʿanat. Fornication gathers all of that, because it requires punishment upon its doer in this world, by which his body suffers ʿanat, and he acquires by it sin and harm in his religion and his worldly life. The people of interpretation, who are its people, agreed that this is its meaning. So although in itself it is pleasure and the fulfilment of desire, by its leading to ʿanat, it is attributed to it and described by it, if it is a cause of ʿanat. [[In the printed edition: "an kana lil-ʿanat", which is correct, but I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿وَأَنْ تَصْبِرُوا خَيْرٌ لَكُمْ وَاللَّهُ غَفُورٌ رَحِيمٌ (٢٥)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this the Exalted means: "wa-an tasbiru," O people, from marrying slave-girls, "khayrun lakum." "Wallahu ghafur," toward you for marrying slave-girls, that you marry them in what He has made lawful and permitted you, and for what has passed from you in that, if you set right your affairs between yourselves and Allah, "rahim" toward you, since He permitted you to marry them when in need and lacking the means to marry free women.

* *

In accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation said.

Those who said this:

9121 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Abu Bishr informed us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Wa-an tasbiru khayrun lakum," he said: from marrying slave-girls.

9122 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: I heard Layth, from Mujahid: "Wa-an tasbiru khayrun lakum," he said: from marrying slave-girls.

9123 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Wa-an tasbiru khayrun lakum," he said: that you be patient and do not marry a slave-girl so that your children become enslaved, and that is better for you.

9124 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Wa-an tasbiru khayrun lakum," he said: that you be patient from marrying slave-girls is better for you, and it is lawful.

9125 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "Wa-an tasbiru khayrun lakum," he said: that you be patient from marrying them = meaning marrying slave-girls = is better for you.

9126 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hibban ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Fudayl ibn Marzuq informed us, from Atiyyah regarding His words: "Wa-an tasbiru khayrun lakum," he said: that you be patient from marrying slave-girls is better for you.

9127 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hibban narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Ibn Tawus informed us, from his father: "Wa-an tasbiru khayrun lakum," he said: that you be patient from marrying a slave-girl is better for you.

9128 - Ali ibn Dawud narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: "Wa-an tasbiru khayrun lakum," he said: that you be patient from the slave-girl is better for you.

* *

The "an" in His words "wa-an tasbiru" is in the nominative position as the predicate "khayrun," meaning: and patience from marrying slave-girls is better for you.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 26:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Allah desires to make clear to you and to guide you to the traditions (sunan) of those before you, and to turn to you in forgiveness. And Allah is Knowing, Wise.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, "Allah desires to make clear to you," may His praise be exalted, He means: His lawful and His unlawful. "And to guide you to the traditions (sunan) of those before you," means: and to set you right [[See the explanation of "guidance" (al-huda) in the earlier indexes of language.]] "to the traditions of those before you," meaning: the ways of those before you among the people of faith in Allah and His prophets, and their methods regarding what He forbade you of marrying mothers, daughters, sisters, and all the rest that He forbade you in the two verses in which He clarified what was forbidden of women. [[See the explanation of "sunnah" in what has passed, 7:230, 231, and see Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubaydah, 1:124.]] "And to turn to you," means: Allah desires to bring you back to His obedience in that, from what you were upon of His disobedience in your doing that before Islam, and before He revealed what He revealed to His Prophet of that. "To you," so that He may overlook for you, through your repentance, what has passed from you of that ugly conduct before your turning back and repentance. "And Allah is Knowing," means: Allah possesses knowledge of what benefits His servants in their religion and their worldly affairs and other matters, and of what they do and leave undone of what He has made lawful or unlawful for them, preserving all of that for them. "Wise," means: in His management of them, in His disposing of them in what He has disposed them to. [[See the explanation of the remaining words of the verse in what has passed, in the indexes of language.]]

* *

The scholars of Arabic differed regarding the meaning of His saying, "Allah desires to make clear to you."

Some of them said: The meaning of that is: Allah desires this for the sake of making clear to you. They said: That is like His saying: ﴿And I have been commanded to be just among you﴾ [Surah al-Shura: 15], with a kasra on the "lam," because its meaning is: I have been commanded with this for the sake of that.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: Allah desires that He make clear to you and guide you to the traditions of those before you. They said: It is a habit of the Arabs to interchange "kay," "lam of kay," and "an," and to place each of them in the position of the others with "aradtu" and "amartu." They say: "Amartuka an tadhhaba, and li-tadhhaba" ("I commanded you that you go" and "I wanted you to go"), and "aradtu an tadhhaba, and li-tadhhaba" ("I desired that you go" and "I desired that you go"), as Allah, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And we have been commanded to submit to the Lord of the worlds﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 71], and He said in another place: ﴿Say: Indeed I have been commanded that I be the first to submit﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 14]. [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "wa-umirtu an akuna," which is a copyist's error; I have restored the wording of the recitation.]] And as He said: ﴿They desire to extinguish the light of Allah﴾ [Surah al-Saff: 8], then He said in another place: ﴿They desire to extinguish﴾ [Surah al-Tawbah: 32]. They gave as their reasoning for using "an" with "amartu" and "aradtu" the sense of "kay," and for directing "kay" with that to the sense of "an," that "aradtu" and "amartu" require the future, and that no past verb may be used with them. One does not say "amartuka an qumta" or "aradtu an qumta." They said: Since "an" may occur with the past in other than "aradtu" and "amartu," they reinforced for it the meaning of the future with what no past verb can ever accompany, namely "kay" and the "lam" that has the meaning of "kay." They said: Likewise the Arabs sometimes combine them in a single particle, and one of them said in the plural: [[Its speaker is not known.]]

Aradta li-kaymā an tatīra bi-qirbatī ... fa-tatrukahā shannan bi-baydā'a balqa'i

[[Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:262; al-Insaf 242; al-Khizanah 3:585; al-'Ayni (margin of al-Khizanah) 4:405; and others. As the author of al-Khizanah said: "This verse is rarely absent from any grammatical book."

"Shann": a worn-out waterskin; "bayda'": a deadly wilderness; "balqa'": a barren land with nothing in it. He means: you only intended by that my destruction and loss in a deadly desert.]] So he combined them, because their meanings agree and their wordings differ, as another said: [[Attributed to al-'Ajjaj and to Ru'bah, and not in his diwan; see the following note.]]

Qad yaksibu al-mala al-hidanu al-jafi ... bi-ghayri la 'asfin wa-la istiraf

[[Diwan al-'Ajjaj 40, 82; Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:262; al-Insaf 242; al-Lisan (s-r-f) ('-s-f) (h-d-n), and the following verse, which is the one reported in the poetry of al-'Ajjaj: "Qala alladhi jama'ta li sawafiya ... min ghayri la 'asfin wa-la istiraf."

It is from a poem in which he reproaches his son Ru'bah, and Ru'bah replied with a poem in his diwan, p. 99. It is evident that this is the cause of the confusion in attributing this poetry, and the correct attribution is to al-'Ajjaj, because it fits the meaning of his reproach to his son when he grew old and trembled, and thought his son coveted his wealth and hoped for his death. He ended his poem with: "Laysa kadhakum walada al-ashraf ... a'ajalani al-mawt wa-lam yukafi"; "Sawfa yujazika malikun wafin ... bi-l-akhdhi in jazaka aw yu'afi."

"Al-hidan": the coward, or the heavy, sluggish sleeper who does not rise early for his needs. "'Asafa ya'sifu" and "i'tasafa": sought, earned and contrived. "Al-'asf": earning and contriving. "Sarrafa al-rajul fi amri, fa-tasarrafa wa-stasrafa": he contrived in seeking gain.]]

So he combined "ghayr" and "la," for emphasis of negation. They said: It is permissible to make "an" stand in place of "kay," and "kay" in place of "an," only in positions where the governing particle is not accompanied by a past verb or by a non-future verb. But where it is accompanied by a past verb or a non-future verb, that is not permissible. It is not permitted in their view to say "zanantu li-yaqum," nor "azunnu li-yaqum," meaning "azunnu an yaqum," because "an" which enters with the verb of thinking (zann) may occur with a past verb, one says "azunnu an qad qama Zayd," and with a future verb, and with nouns. [[Their examples in al-Farra' 1:263 read: "and with the future, so you say: azunnu an sayaqumu Zayd; and with nouns, so you say: azunnu annaka qa'im."

What has passed is an abridgment of al-Farra's discussion in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:261-263.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the two opinions in my view is the opinion of the one who said: the "lam" in His saying, "Allah desires to make clear to you," has the meaning of "an": Allah desires that He make clear to you, for the reason I mentioned from the one who said that it is so.

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted is He and Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And Allah desires to accept your repentance, but those who follow their desires desire that you deviate into a great deviation﴾ [4:27]

Abu Ja'far said: Its meaning, exalted is His remembrance: "And Allah desires to turn back to you in obedience to Him and to return to Him, so that He may pardon for you what has passed of your sins and overlook for you what was from you in your jahiliyyah (the period of ignorance before Islam), from your considering lawful what is unlawful for you, such as marrying the wives of your fathers and your sons, and other things you used to consider lawful and commit, which it was not permissible for you to commit, of the disobediences to Allah." ﴿But those who follow their desires﴾ means: those who seek the pleasures of this world and the desires of their own souls therein. ﴿Desire that you deviate﴾ means: deviate from the command of Allah, blessed and exalted is He, so that you act unjustly by committing what He has forbidden you and engaging in His disobediences. ﴿A great deviation﴾ means: a severe injustice and turning away from Him.

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning those whom Allah described as "those who follow their desires."

Some of them said: They are the fornicators.

Mention of those who said this:

9129 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, "and those who follow their desires," he said: fornication. "That you deviate a great deviation": he said: they desire that you commit fornication.

9130 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Huthayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And those who follow their desires desire that you deviate a great deviation": that you become like them, fornicating as they fornicate.

9131 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "And those who follow their desires," he said: fornication. "That you deviate a great deviation," he said: that the people of Islam fornicate as they fornicate. He said: it is like His words: ﴿They wish that you would compromise, so they would compromise﴾ [68:9].

9132 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Warqa', from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And those who follow their desires," he said: fornication. "That you deviate," he said: that you fornicate.

* *

Others said: Rather, they are the Jews and the Christians.

Mention of those who said this:

9133 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And those who follow their desires," he said: they are the Jews and the Christians. "That you deviate a great deviation."

* *

Others said: Rather, they are the Jews specifically, and their desire from the Muslims was to follow their desires regarding marriage with paternal sisters. That is because they considered it lawful to marry them. So Allah, blessed and exalted is He, said to the believers: "And those who desire that those who make lawful marriage with paternal sisters should deviate you from the truth, so that you would make it lawful as they made it lawful."

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: everyone who follows a desire in his religion for other than what has been permitted to him.

Mention of those who said this:

9134 - Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Ibn Zayd say regarding His words, "And those who follow their desires," the verse: He said: those of falsehood and those who follow desires in their religion desire that you deviate in your religion a great deviation, that you follow their religious matters and abandon the command of Allah and the command of your religion.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings concerning this, in terms of truth, is the saying of the one who said: The meaning of that is: "And those who follow the desires of their own souls, from the people of falsehood, seekers of fornication and marriage with paternal sisters, and other things Allah has forbidden, desire that you deviate" from the truth, [[The manuscript and the printed edition read: "that you deviate a great deviation from the truth ...", but I have deduced from its mention at the end of the paragraph, "a great deviation," that the phrase "a great deviation" here is a slip of the copyist, the remainder of the verse having run on his tongue and he recorded it; and if that were correct, this latter would have no place at the end of the paragraph.]] and from what Allah has permitted you in it, so that you swerve from His obedience to His disobedience, and become like them in following the desires of your souls in what Allah has forbidden, and abandon His obedience: "a great deviation."

We said that this is more correct because Allah, mighty and majestic is He, by His words, "And those who follow their desires," generalized, describing them as following their blameworthy desires of their souls, and encompassing them with this description without describing them as following some blameworthy desires. Since that is so, the most appropriate meanings of the verse are those indicated by its apparent sense, not its hidden sense for which there is no evidence from a source or analogy. Since that is so, the Jews, the Christians, the fornicators, and every follower of falsehood fall within "those who follow their desires," because everyone who follows what Allah has forbidden him is following the desire of his own soul. Since this is the more appropriate interpretation of the verse, the correctness of what we have chosen as the interpretation of it is established.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Allah desires to lighten [the burden] for you, and man was created weak﴾ (4:28).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His saying, "Allah desires to lighten [the burden] for you," He, great is His praise, means: Allah desires to make things easy for you, [see the explanation of "lightening" (al-takhfif) in what has preceded, 6:577], by permitting you to marry believing slave-women when you are unable to afford marrying free women.
