It was said: "And what are the major sins?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah, disobedience to parents, and fleeing on the day of battle."

[[Hadith 9224: Ibn Abi al-Sarri, Muhammad ibn al-Mutawakkil ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, the hafiz of Asqalan: trustworthy; Ibn Ma'in and others declared him trustworthy. He died in 238. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/105, and Tadhkirat al-Huffaz 2: 53-54.
Yahya ibn Sa'id: he is al-'Attar al-Ansari al-Himsi; his biography has passed (5753). In the printed edition, in its place, it reads "Muhammad ibn Sa'd," which is a definite distortion. What we have set is what is in the manuscript, though the word "Yahya" in it is not entirely clear. It was possible here that the name was "Bahir ibn Sa'd," because he narrated this hadith, as will come. But I did not find mention of Bahir ibn Sa'd among the shaykhs of Ibn Abi al-Sarri, whom the huffaz al-Mizzi listed in Tahdhib al-Kamal, as is his custom. However, he mentions among his shaykhs "Yahya ibn Sa'id al-'Attar."
Khalid ibn Ma'dan al-Kala'i: has passed (2070).
Abu Ruhm, with a damma on the ra' and a sukun on the ha': Ahzab ibn Usayd al-Suma'i: an early, trustworthy Successor. Some have counted him among the Companions; the more probable view is the first.
The hadith was transmitted by Ahmad in al-Musnad 5: 413 (Halabi), from al-Muqri', from Haywah ibn Shurayh: "Baqiyyah narrated to us, Bahir ibn Sa'd told me, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan..." — and so on.
Then he transmitted it 5: 413-414, from Zakariyya ibn 'Adi, who said: Baqiyyah informed us, from Bahir, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan..."
Baqiyyah is Ibn al-Walid. He is trustworthy; some who spoke of him said he practised tadlis, but he explicitly stated hearing in the first isnad in Ahmad, so the suspicion of tadlis is removed.
"Bahir ibn Sa'd al-Himsi" is trustworthy; Ahmad, Ibn Sa'd, and others declared him trustworthy. "Bahir" has a fatha on the b, a kasra on the h, and ends in ra'. His father "Sa'd" has a fatha on the s and a sukun on the 'ayn. It is firmly established in the correct form in al-Mizzi's Tahdhib al-Kamal (manuscript microfilm), al-Bukhari's al-Kabir 1/2/137-138, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/412, al-Dhahabi's al-Mushtabih, the Musnad, and elsewhere. It is written "Sa'id" in Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, al-Taqrib, and al-Khulasah, which is an error beyond doubt.
Ibn Kathir narrated the hadith 2: 417-418, from the second version of the Musnad. In it "Yahya ibn Sa'id" appears in place of "Bahir ibn Sa'd"! This is a copyist's or printer's error. He then attributed it also to al-Nasa'i.
al-Suyuti mentions it 2: 146, adding attribution to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Hibban, and al-Hakim, who "authenticated it."
Another isnad will come after this, from a different route.]]

9225 - 'Abbas ibn Abi Talib told me, saying: Sa'd ibn 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Ja'far, from Ibn Abi al-Zinad, from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from 'Abdullah ibn Sulayman al-Aghar, from his father Abu 'Abdullah Sulayman al-Aghar, who said: Abu Ayyub Khalid ibn Ayyub al-Ansari, a man of 'Aqabah and Badr, said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no servant who worships Allah, associating nothing with Him, establishes the prayer, pays the zakat, fasts Ramadan, and avoids the major sins, but he enters Paradise." They asked him: "What are the major sins?" He said: "Associating partners with Allah, fleeing from the battle, and killing a soul."

[[Hadith 9225: This is another isnad, by another route, for the previous hadith.
'Abbas ibn Abi Talib: his biography has passed (880). Sa'd ibn 'Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja'far al-Ansari: his biography has passed (3959), and we there favoured his trustworthiness. The printed edition (and manuscript) reads "Sa'd ibn 'Abd al-Hamid 'an Ja'far," which is an error; I have placed "'an" in place of "ibn."
As for his saying "'an Ibn Abi Ja'far": this is what is established here. If it is correct it would be "'Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far al-Razi," whose biography has passed (7030). But I incline to think that it is an addition to the isnad from confusion by the copyists, for "Sa'd ibn 'Abd al-Hamid" is known for narrating from Ibn Abi al-Zinad.
Ibn Abi al-Zinad is "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Zinad." His biography has passed (1694).
"'Abdullah ibn Sulayman al-Aghar": it is established here as "'Abdullah" with a takbir. He is trustworthy and narrates from his father. But I incline to think the correct form is "'Ubaydullah," with a diminutive. For they did not mention a narration of Musa ibn 'Uqbah from "'Abdullah." He is known only for narrating from his brother "'Ubaydullah."
"'Ubaydullah ibn Sulayman al-Aghar": a well-known trustworthy narrator, from whom Malik, Musa ibn 'Uqbah, and others narrate.
His father "Sulayman al-Aghar, Abu 'Abdullah al-Madani": a well-known trustworthy Successor, from whom the Jama'ah narrated.
The hadith has already been takhrij'd. As for this route, from the narration of Sulayman al-Aghar from Abu Ayyub, I have not found it outside this place.]]

9226 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: 'Abbad ibn 'Abbad narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah: that some men from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) mentioned the major sins while he was reclining, and they said: "Associating partners with Allah, consuming the property of orphans, fleeing from the battle, slandering chaste women, disobedience to parents, false speech, misappropriation of booty, sorcery, and consuming usury." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Then where do you place: ﴿Indeed, those who sell the covenant of Allah and their oaths for a small price...﴾?" up to the end of the verse [Surah Al 'Imran: 77].

[[Hadith 9226: This is a weak, collapsed isnad.
Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr al-Dimashqi: very weak. He narrated from al-Qasim from Abu Umamah a fabricated (mawdu') copy, as we explained earlier (1939).
Ibn Kathir cited the hadith 2: 423 from this place. al-Suyuti mentions it 2: 147 and did not attribute it to anyone other than al-Tabari. He said it is "with a good isnad"! In this he is mistaken. It is merely a weak isnad with no standing whatever.]]

9227 - 'Ubaydullah ibn Muhammad al-Firyabi narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Mu'awiyah, from Abu 'Amr al-Shaybani, from 'Abdullah, who said: I asked the Prophet (ﷺ): "What are the major sins?" He said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you, and that you kill your child lest he eat with you, or that you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to us: ﴿And those who do not call upon another god with Allah, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit adultery﴾ [Surah al-Furqan: 68].

[[Hadith 9227: 'Ubaydullah ibn Muhammad al-Firyabi, the shaykh of al-Tabari: his biography has passed at no. 17, and it will come, p. 254, l. 3, that al-Tabari considers him to have erred in this hadith. He means an error in meaning! But we do not agree with him in that. For the meaning of this hadith and the following one is one; it is merely a difference in wording.
"Sufyan": this is Ibn 'Uyaynah.
See the isnad that follows this one.]]

9228 - 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri narrated this hadith to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah al-Nakha'i — and he was in charge of the prison — heard it from Abu 'Amr, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Which deed is the worst?" He said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He created you, and that you kill your child lest he eat with you, or that you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." And he recited to me: ﴿And those who do not call upon another god with Allah﴾ [...]

[[Hadith 9228: 'Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Miswar ibn Makhramah al-Zuhri, shaykh of al-Tabari: trustworthy. Biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/163.
Abu Mu'awiyah al-Nakha'i, in this isnad and the preceding one: he is 'Amr ibn 'Abdullah ibn Wahb. He is trustworthy; Ibn Ma'in and others declared him so. Biographed in al-Tahdhib, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/1/243-244.
Abu 'Amr al-Shaybani: he is Sa'd ibn Iyas, the great Successor. His biography has passed (5524).
The hadith will come in al-Tabari, at the commentary on verse 71 of Surah al-Furqan (19: 26, Bulaq), from 'Ubaydullah ibn Muhammad al-Firyabi, from Sufyan, with this isnad, and then he transmitted it there by other isnads.
It was transmitted by Ahmad in al-Musnad, from the narration of Abu Wa'il Shaqiq ibn Salamah, from 'Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas'ud, many times with several isnads: 3612, 4102, 4131-4134, 4411, 4423.
Likewise al-Bukhari transmitted it many times, among them 8: 124, 12: 101-103, and 13: 413 (Fath).
Likewise Muslim transmitted it 1: 36-37.
In some of their narrations there is an addition, "'Amr ibn Shurahbil," in the isnad between Abu Wa'il and Ibn Mas'ud. The apparent view to me is that Abu Wa'il heard it from Ibn Mas'ud, and from 'Amr ibn Shurahbil from Ibn Mas'ud, and so he narrated it in both forms. This would be an addition within a connected chain. The hafiz explained this matter at length at 12: 101-103.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it 6: 194-195, from one of the narrations of the Musnad, and one of al-Tabari's narrations to come.
al-Suyuti mentioned it 5: 77, adding attribution to al-Firyabi, 'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of what has been said in interpreting "al-kaba'ir" is what the report transmitted from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) establishes as sound, rather than what others have said, even though each speaker among those whose sayings we have mentioned strove and exerted himself, and his saying has a path to soundness. So the major sins are: associating partners with Allah, disobedience to parents, killing a soul whose killing is forbidden, false speech — and false testimony may enter under "false speech" — slandering chaste women, the perjurious oath, and sorcery — and killing a soul whose killing is forbidden includes a man killing his child lest he feed with him — and fleeing from the battle, and adultery with the wife of a neighbour.

Since this is so, every report transmitted from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning the major sins is sound, and some of it confirms the rest. For what is transmitted from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said, "They are seven," its meaning then is "They are seven" in detail. And the meaning of his saying in the report transmitted from him, "They are associating partners with Allah, killing a soul, disobedience to parents, and false speech," is in summary, since his saying "and false speech" may bear various meanings, and "false speech" may encompass all of them.

As for the report of Ibn Mas'ud which al-Firyabi narrated to me as I mentioned, it is in my view an error from 'Ubaydullah ibn Muhammad, because the widely attested sound reports from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet (ﷺ), [[In the printed edition: "from the sound routes," and I do not know why it changed what was in the manuscript!!]] in the manner of the narration which al-Zuhri transmitted from Ibn 'Uyaynah. None of them said in his narration from Ibn Mas'ud that "the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about the major sins." So their transmission of what they transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud from the Prophet (ﷺ) is more worthy of soundness than al-Firyabi's transmission.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: So whoever avoids the major sins, which Allah has promised that avoiding them will expiate what lies beyond them of his misdeeds, and will admit him to a noble abode, and performs the obligations which Allah has imposed upon him, finds Allah fulfilling His promise to him and steadfast in keeping it. [[In the printed edition: "and steadfast in keeping it with perseverance," altering what was in the manuscript, which read "and steadfast in keeping it with perseverance" unpointed; this reading is correct, God willing.]]

* *

As for His saying, "We will expiate from you your misdeeds," He means by it: We will expiate from you, O believers, by your avoidance of the major sins of what your Lord has forbidden you, your minor misdeeds [[See the explanation of "expiation" above: 7: 482, 490 = and the explanation of "misdeeds" above 2: 281-283 / 7: 482, 490.]] — meaning: your minor sins, as:

9229 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told me, saying: Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "We will expiate from you your misdeeds," the minor ones. [[Report 9229: In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads "Muhammad ibn al-Hasan," and the correct form is what is established here; it is a looping isnad in the tafsir, the nearest of which is 9133.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 31 (part 4 of 4):

9230 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Aliyyah narrated to us, from Ibn Awn, from al-Hasan: Some people met Abd Allah ibn Amr in Egypt and said: "We see things in the Book of God that He commanded to be acted upon, yet they are not acted upon. [[In the manuscript: "amr an yu'mal bi-ha la na'mal bi-ha" with the nun in the second verb. What appears in the printed edition and in Ibn Kathir is correct, because they came complaining about their governor in Egypt, as is clear from the end of the report.]] So we wished to meet the Commander of the Faithful about this." So he came, and they came with him. Umar met him and said: "When did you arrive?" He said: "Such-and-such time ago." He said: "Did you come with permission?" He said: "I do not know how he replied." Then [the man] said: "O Commander of the Faithful, some people met me in Egypt and said: 'We see things in the Book of God, blessed and exalted, that He commanded to be acted upon, yet they are not acted upon,' and they wished that you would meet them about this." He said: "Gather them for me." He said: "I gathered them for him." Ibn Awn said: "I think he said: in a courtyard [bahw]. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "fi nahr" (in a river), and the correct reading is from Ibn Kathir's tafsir. "Al-bahw" is the house-front before the houses, and every open space or cleared area is called "bahw" by the Arabs.]]" Then he took the one nearest to them by the hand and said: "I adjure you by God and by the right of Islam upon you: Have you recited the whole Qur'an?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Have you counted it in your mind [ahsaytahu fi nafsika]? [[Ahsa al-shay' means to encompass and preserve it. The meaning is: have you fulfilled every command in it, preserved it, and kept tight control of acting upon it? From this is God's saying, "He knew that you would not be able to count it, so He turned to you in forgiveness" [Qur'an 73:20], i.e., you would not be able to perform it.]]" He said: "God forbid, no!" He said: "Had he said 'yes,' he would have overcome him [lakhasamahu]. [["Khasamtu al-rajul fa-khasamtuhu": I disputed with the man and defeated him with argument.]]" He said: "Then have you counted it with your sight? Have you counted it with your speech? Have you counted it with your footsteps? [[Al-athar is the trace left on the earth by the weight of one's steps upon it, and here it means striving on the earth, as in God's saying, "We record what they have sent forward and their traces" [Qur'an 36:12], i.e., their steps wherever they strove on the earth.]]" He continued with them until he reached the last of them, then said: "May Umar's mother be bereaved! Do you burden him to make the people stand upon the Book of God? Our Lord has known that we would commit sins." He said: And he recited: "If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you to a noble entrance" [Qur'an 4:31]. Then he said: "Did the people of Medina know [or he said: did anyone know] of your coming?" They said: "No!" He said: "Had they known, I would have made an example of you." [[Report 9230: Ibn Kathir cited it in his tafsir 2:423-424, and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:145. Ibn Kathir said: "Its chain is sound and its text is good, although al-Hasan's narration from Umar contains a break in transmission; yet such a report is well known, and its fame suffices." Al-Suyuti said: "Ibn Jarir narrated it with a good chain."
As for his saying "I would have made an example of you," it means: I would have inflicted upon you punishment that would serve as a lesson to others among the people. That is because they came complaining about their governor in Egypt, and they were overly strict and did not facilitate, and they wished that the people be made to walk by what they themselves could not bear in terms of encompassing all the works of Islam and what God had commanded them. This is among the great trials. They did not intend the outward matters of Islam and its rulings, but only some of what God had disciplined His creation with. Umar was too exalted to be lax in the rulings of Islam. I have said this and explained it out of fear that a proponent of the authorities and tyranny might use it as evidence for permitting the abandonment of God's rulings and their non-implementation, as is the practice of the tyrants and oppressors among the rulers of our time.]]

9231 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn Aliyyah narrated to us, saying: Ziyad ibn Mikhraq narrated to us, from Mu'awiya ibn Qurra, who said: We came to Anas ibn Malik, and among what he related to us he said: "We have not seen anything like what has reached us from our Lord. Then we did not go out to Him from every family and property! [[The word "thumma" is absent from the manuscript; I have left it out because it is in al-Durr al-Manthur and Ibn Kathir's tafsir.]]" Then he was silent for a moment, then said: "By God, our Lord has imposed upon us something easier than that! He has overlooked for us what is less than the major sins! So what do we have to do with them?" Then he recited: "If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden..." the verse. [[Report 9231: Ibn Kathir 2:425; al-Durr al-Manthur 2:145, and he also attributed it to Ibn Abi Shayba and Abd ibn Humayd.]]

9232 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: "If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden..." the verse: God only promised forgiveness to those who avoid the major sins. It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: "Avoid the major sins, aim for what is right [sadiduu], and rejoice [abshiru]."

9233 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from a man, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Concerning five verses from Surat al-Nisa', I would prefer them over the whole world:" "If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds" [Qur'an 4:31]; and His saying: "Indeed, God does not wrong [anyone] an atom's weight, and if it is a good deed He doubles it" [Qur'an 4:40]; and His saying: "Indeed, God does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills" [Qur'an 4:48, 4:116]; and His saying: "And whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness of God will find God Forgiving and Merciful" [Qur'an 4:110]; and His saying: "And those who believe in God and His messengers and do not discriminate between any of them—those, He will give them their rewards, and God is ever Forgiving and Merciful" [Qur'an 4:152]. [[Report 9233: al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:145, and also attributed it to Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Salam, Sa'id ibn Mansur in his Fada'il, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, and al-Bayhaqi in Shu'ab al-Iman.]]

9234 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Nadr narrated to me, from Salih al-Murri, from Qatada, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Eight verses were revealed in Surat al-Nisa', which are better for this Community than what the sun rises upon and sets upon. The first of them: 'God wants to make clear to you and guide you to the ways of those before you and to turn to you in forgiveness, and God is Knowing and Wise' [Qur'an 4:26]; the second: 'And God wants to turn to you in forgiveness, but those who follow their desires want you to deviate with a great deviation' [Qur'an 4:27]; the third: 'God wants to lighten for you, for man was created weak' [Qur'an 4:28]," = then he mentioned the same as Ibn Mas'ud's statement, and added in it: then he went on explaining it at the end of the verse: "And God is ever Forgiving and Merciful to those who commit evil deeds." [[Report 9234: "Abu al-Nadr" is apparently Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Yazid al-Dimashqi al-Faradisi, one of the teachers of al-Bukhari and Abu Zur'a. He met him but did not write from him. Born in 141 AH, died in 227 AH, trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, and he appeared previously under no. 8788.
"Salih al-Murri" is Salih ibn Bashir ibn Wada' al-Murri, the storyteller. He narrated from al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Qatada, and others. He was a righteous man, but he narrated unusual reports which the imams criticized him for. He is abandoned in narration [matruk al-hadith]. He died in 172 or 176 AH. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and in al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/2/274.]]

As for His saying "and admit you to a noble entrance" [mudkhalan kariman], the readers differed in its recitation. The common reading of the people of Medina and some of the Kufans is: "wa-nudkhilkum mudkhalan karimā" with a fatha on the mim, and likewise what is in al-Hajj: "la-yudkhilannahum mudkhalan yarḍawnahu" [Qur'an 22:59]. So the meaning of "wa-nudkhilkum mudkhalan" is that they enter a noble entrance. It may be possible, according to the view of those who read this reading, that "al-madkhal" means the place and location, because the Arabs sometimes open the mim in such words with this meaning, as the rajiz [rhymed poet] said: [[I do not know his name.]]
"bi-maṣbaḥi al-ḥamdi wa-ḥaythu numsī" [[Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:264; Lisan al-Arab (ṣabaḥa).]]
Some of them recited to me from the Arabs by hearing: [[He is Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt.]]
"al-ḥamdu lillāhi mamsānā wa-muṣbaḥanā... bi-l-khayri ṣabbaḥanā rabbī wa-massānā" [[His Diwan: 62; Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:264; al-Khizana 1:120; Lisan al-Arab (msy). This is the opening of this poem.]]
And another recited to me besides him:
"al-ḥamdu lillāhi mumsānā wa-muṣbaḥanā"
because it is from "asbaha" and "amsa". The Arabs do likewise with the verb whose form is built on four radicals: they put a ḍamma on its mim in such a case, so they say: "daḥraja'tuhu, adḥrijuhu, mudaḥrajan, fa-huwa mudaḥraj" [[In the manuscript: "daḥraja'tuhu fa-huwa mudaḥraj", with a gap of several words between, so the printed edition added "mudaḥrajan", and I added "adḥrijuhu" because the context that follows requires mentioning it.]] Then they treat what comes in the pattern "af'ala yuf'ilu" in the same way. [[In the printed edition: "fa'ala yaf'alu," and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] Because "yuf'il", from "yudkhil", although it is of four radicals, its origin is "yu'af'il", "yu'adkhil" and "yu'akhrij", so it is a parallel of "yudaḥrij".
* *
The common reading of the Kufans and Basrans was "mudkhalan" with a ḍamma on the mim, meaning: "wa-nudkhilkum idkhalan karimān" [and We will cause you to enter a noble entry].
* *
Abu Ja'far [al-Tabari] said: The more correct of the two readings is the reading of the one who recited "wa-nudkhilkum mudkhalan karimā" with a ḍamma on the mim, for the reason we have described, that the verb whose form is built on four radicals in "fa'ala" [[By his saying "fa'ala" here in both places, he means the past-tense verb, not the morphological pattern.]] has its verbal noun in "mufʿal". And that "adkhala" and "daḥraja" have "fa'ala" as their form of four radicals. [[By his saying "fa'ala" here he means the past-tense verb, not the morphological pattern.]] So "al-mudkhal" as a verbal noun is more fitting than "mad'khal", although that is more eloquent in the speech of the Arabs regarding the verbal nouns of what comes in "af'ala", as one says: "He stayed in a place and so the stay pleased him," when the meaning is residence = and "he stood in his place, so he is in a wide station [maqam]," as His exalted praise said: "Indeed, the God-fearing will be in a secure station" [Qur'an 44:51], from "qama yaqumu". If "residence" were meant, it would be recited "inna al-muttaqina fi muqamin amin," as it was recited: "And say, 'My Lord, cause me to enter a sound entrance [mudkhala sidq] and cause me to exit a sound exit [makhraja sidq]'" [Qur'an 17:80], meaning "entering" and "exiting." No one has transmitted to us that anyone recited "madkhala sidq" or "makhraja sidq" with a fatha on the mim.
* *
As for "the noble entrance," it means: the good and fine, honored by the negation of calamities and afflictions from it, and by the removal of worries and sorrows and the entry of turbidity into the life of one who enters it. Therefore God called it "noble," as:

9235 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And admit you to a noble entrance," he said: "The noble [karim]" is the goodness in Paradise. [[Report 9235: In the printed edition: "Muhammad ibn al-Hasan," which is an error. See the note on the previous report no. 9229.]]

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you excel over others﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, He, mighty is His praise, means: do not desire what Allah has favoured some of you with over others. [[See the explanation of "tamanni" (wishing) above, 2:366.]]

It has been mentioned that this was revealed concerning women who wished for the positions of men, and that they should have what men have. So Allah forbade His servants from vain wishes and commanded them to ask Him for His bounty, since such wishes bring their possessors envy and transgression without right. [[But this is a subject of speech and desire, in which the people of this age have persisted, and they have confused its understanding to a degree from which there is no escape except through sincerity of intention, a correct understanding of the nature of this human being, a distinction between what are vain wishes with no basis in necessity, and an exit from the bondage of imitating the dominant nations, and a liberation from the captivity of the corrupt society that convulses nations today with great convulsion. But the people of our religion, may Allah guide them and set their affairs right, have been drawn into the path of error, and have confused what is reform of what has corrupted their affairs through resolve, reason and wisdom with what is corruption in the form of reform. The people have exaggerated, and the callers from among those with grudges, who have stood up on the press of their age, have multiplied, until tongues became confused, minds were disordered, and many people slipped after these callers, so that we now find among the people of knowledge, those who attribute themselves to religion, one who says in this a statement from which every person of religion disassociates himself. There is a difference between a nation reviving its men and women with a sound life, free from blights, defects and ignorance, and a nation dropping every barrier between men and women, so that the whole matter becomes a matter of vain wishes that bring their possessors envy and transgression without right, as Abu Ja'far said, may Allah have mercy on him and reward him. O Allah, guide us to the even path, in a time when tongues have betrayed their minds! Let those who oppose the command of Allah, and His decree concerning them, beware lest a calamity strike them that takes away what remains of their traces on this earth, as it took away those before them.]]

Hadith reports supporting what we have mentioned:

9236: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Umm Salamah said: "O Messenger of Allah, are we not given a share of inheritance, and are we not allowed to fight in the way of Allah so that we may be killed?" Then this was revealed: "And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you excel over others." [[Hadith 9236: Sufyan in this chain may be al-Thawri or Ibn 'Uyaynah. Mu'ammal narrates from both, and both narrated this hadith: al-Thawri in the narration after this one, 9237, and Ibn 'Uyaynah in narration 9241. The takhrij (tracing of the hadith through the sources) will come under 9241.]]

9237: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Hisham narrated to us, from Sufyan al-Thawri, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Umm Salamah said: "O Messenger of Allah, the men fight and we do not fight, and we only have half of the inheritance!" Then this was revealed: "And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you excel over others. For men there is a share of what they have earned, and for women there is a share of what they have earned," and this was revealed: ﴿Indeed, the Muslim men and the Muslim women﴾ [Surah al-Ahzab: 35].

9238: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you excel over others." He said: A man should not wish, saying: "Would that I had the wealth of so-and-so and his family!" So Allah, glorified is He, forbade that, but let him ask Allah for His bounty.

9239: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you excel over others." He said: It is the saying of women: "Would that we were men, so that we could fight and attain what men attain!" [[In the printed edition: "laytana rijal" with the nominative, which is the common reading. In the manuscript, it is written "rijalan" and vocalised with the pen, so I have recorded it as it stands in the manuscript. "Layta" (would that) puts the noun in the accusative and the predicate in the nominative, but some grammarians put both nouns in the accusative, and they cited the verse: "Yā layta ayyāma al-ṣabā rawāji'ā" (Would that the days of youth would return). Some grammarians related that some Arabs use "layta" in the sense of "wajadtu", making it transitive to two objects and treating it like verbs, so one says "layta Zaydan shākhiṣan" (Would that I found Zayd standing). The narration with the accusative for the predicate is correct, as you see, and there is no reason to change it. This should not be attributed to a scribal error, since it appears that Abu Ja'far brought the following report, in which is "laytana rijal", to draw attention to this narration with the accusative. See p. 264, footnote 1.]]

9240: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you excel over others": it is the saying of women wishing: "Would that we were men so that we could fight!" Then he mentioned the like of the hadith of Muhammad ibn Amr.

9241: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: Umm Salamah said: "O Messenger of Allah, do the men fight and we do not fight, while we only have half of the inheritance?" Then this was revealed: "And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you excel over others." [[Hadith 9241: It is in the Tafsir of Abd al-Razzaq, p. 41 (photographed manuscript), with this chain. It was earlier narrated with two other chains: 9236, 9237. It was also narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 6:322 (Halabi edition), from Sufyan, who is Ibn 'Uyaynah, with this chain. It was narrated by al-Tirmidhi 4:88, from Ibn Abi Umar, from Sufyan, and in it: "from Mujahid, from Umm Salamah, that she said: The men fight..." etc. It was narrated by al-Hakim 2:305-306, by way of Qabisah ibn Uqbah, from Sufyan, who is al-Thawri, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "from Umm Salamah, that she said..." It was narrated by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 110, by way of Qutaybah, from Ibn 'Uyaynah, like the narration of Abd al-Razzaq here, and Ahmad in al-Musnad. The wording of the narration from Mujahid thus differs. In some of them: "from Mujahid, who said: Umm Salamah said." In others: "from Mujahid, from Umm Salamah, that she said." The first wording apparently implies an interruption (irsal) in the chain, since its meaning is that Mujahid relates on his own authority what Umm Salamah said to the Prophet (ﷺ), so it would be a mursal report (one in which a Successor reports directly from a Companion), because he did not witness it. The second wording apparently implies continuity, since its meaning is that Mujahid mentions this as a report from Umm Salamah. Then they also differed in its connection without evidence. Al-Tirmidhi said, after narrating "from Mujahid, from Umm Salamah": "This is a mursal hadith. Some of them narrated it from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, as a mursal report: that Umm Salamah said such and such." Al-Hakim said, after narrating "from Mujahid, from Umm Salamah": "This is a hadith meeting the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), if Mujahid heard from Umm Salamah." Al-Dhahabi agreed with his authentication and ignored its critique, not mentioning it. In my view, from what appears to me of the context and indications, the two narrations have one meaning, and the difference is only in wording from the transmitters' paraphrasing. All of them mean "Mujahid from Umm Salamah." Both wordings are established in the narration of Ibn 'Uyaynah. Likewise both are established in the narration of al-Thawri, here at 9237, and in the narration of al-Hakim. Ibn Kathir 2:428 quoted from Ibn Abi Hatim that he said: "Yahya al-Qattan and Waki' ibn al-Jarrah narrated from al-Thawri, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Umm Salamah, who said: I said: O Messenger of Allah..." As for al-Tirmidhi's ruling in his narration by way of Ibn 'Uyaynah that it is a mursal hadith, he asserted it without evidence. Mujahid certainly met Umm Salamah and lived in her time, for he was born in the year 21 AH, and Umm Salamah died after the year 60 AH, according to certainty. Contemporaneity (mu'asarah) from a trustworthy narrator implies continuity, unless the narrator is a mudallis (one who conceals defects in the chain, tadlis). No one claimed that Mujahid was a mudallis, except a statement by al-Qutb al-Halabi in his commentary on al-Bukhari, which al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) reported in Tahdhib 10:44, then commented on it, saying: "I have not seen anyone attribute tadlis to him." Al-Hafiz also said in Fath 6:194, in response to one who claimed that Mujahid did not hear from Abd Allah ibn Amr: "But the hearing of Mujahid from Amr ibn Abd Allah is established, and he is not a mudallis." Thus the continuity and soundness of the hadith are established for us. Praise be to Allah. Ibn Kathir 2:428 mentioned the hadith from the narration of al-Musnad, then referred to the narrations of al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, Ibn Jarir and al-Hakim. Al-Suyuti 2:149 mentioned it and added its attribution to Abd ibn Humayd, Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir.]]

9242: Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from a shaykh from the people of Mecca, regarding His words: "And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you excel over others." He said: The women used to say: "Would that we were men, so that we could struggle as men struggle, and fight in the way of Allah!" Then Allah said: "And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you excel over others."

9243: Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, who said: You wish for the wealth of so-and-so and the wealth of so-and-so! And what do you know? Perhaps his ruin lies in that wealth!

9244: Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Ikrimah and Mujahid, that they both said: It was revealed concerning Umm Salamah, daughter of Abu Umayyah ibn al-Mughirah. [[Report 9244: Ibn Kathir 2:429, and al-Durr al-Manthur 2:149, which attributed it to no one other than Ibn Jarir.]]

9245: And with this chain, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Ata', who said: It is the person who says: "I wish I had the wealth of so-and-so!" He said: "And ask Allah for His bounty," and the saying of women: "Would that we were men, so that we could fight and attain what men attain!" [[In the printed edition: "laytana rijal fanaghzu", in the common reading, but I have recorded what is in the manuscript and have not changed it, and it is correct according to the grammarians. They say that among the dialects of the Arabs is that "anna" (or "laytana") puts both the noun and the predicate in the accusative. This was said by Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam, al-Farra', Ibn al-Sayyid and Ibn al-Tarawah. They cited the verse of the poet: "Idha iltaffa jinhu al-layli, fa-l-ta'ti, wa-l-takun / khutaka khafifan, inna hurrasana asda" (When the wing of night enfolds, then come, and let your steps be light, for indeed our guards are lions). See the previous footnote, p. 261, footnote 2.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: let none of you wish for what Allah has given some over others of the stations of excellence.

Mention of who said that:

9246: Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding His words: "And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you excel over others." The men said: "We want to have double the reward of women, as we have double the share in the arrows, so we want to have two rewards." The women said: "We want to have a reward like the reward of men, for we cannot fight, and if fighting were prescribed for us, we would fight!" Then Allah the Exalted revealed the verse, and said to them: Ask Allah for His bounty; He will provide you with deeds, and it is better for you.

9247: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, who said: You were forbidden from vain wishes, and were directed to what is better than it: "And ask Allah for His bounty."

9248: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Arim narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub, who said: When Muhammad heard a man wishing for worldly things, he would say: Allah has forbidden you from this: "And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you excel over others," and has directed you to what is better than it: "And ask Allah for His bounty."

Abu Ja'far said: The sense of the statement according to this interpretation is: And do not wish, O men and women, for that by which Allah has favoured some of you over others, of the stations of excellence and degrees of goodness. Let each of you be content with what Allah has apportioned to him as a share, but ask Allah for His bounty.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿For men there is a share of what they have earned, and for women there is a share of what they have earned﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of this. [[Note: "ahl al-ta'wil" refers to the exegetes.]]

Some of them said: The meaning of that is: for men there is a share of what they have earned, of reward for obedience and punishment for disobedience, "and for women there is a share" of that, like that.

Mention of who said that:

9249: Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you excel over others. For men there is a share of what they have earned, and for women there is a share of what they have earned": The people of the Jahiliyyah did not give women any inheritance, nor a boy any, but they would give the inheritance to whoever earned a living and provided and defended. [[Ihtaraf li-'ayalihi, and harrafa li-'ayalihi: he strove for them in earning and seeking sustenance.]] When a woman was given her share and a boy his share, and he (the father) gave the male a share like the share of two females, the women said: "If only our shares in inheritance were like the shares of men!" And the men said: "We hope to be favoured over women in the Hereafter with our good deeds, as we are favoured over them in inheritance!" So Allah revealed: "For men there is a share of what they have earned, and for women there is a share of what they have earned," meaning: a woman is rewarded for her good deed tenfold, as a man is rewarded. Allah the Exalted said: "And ask Allah for His bounty." [[In the printed edition and the manuscript and al-Durr al-Manthur 2:149: "lahaqa" (joined/attached), and the lam in the manuscript is slanted. I saw that "lahaqa" here has no meaning, and I had not previously found it in speech with a meaning like this, so I made an effort at reading and judged it to be "najaza" (accomplished). One says "najaza hajatahu" when he fulfilled and hastened it, as if he said: when he hastened to give the woman her share and fulfilled it.]]

9250: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad narrated to us, saying: Abu Layla narrated to me, who said: I heard Abu Huraiz say: When it was revealed: "The share of the male is like the share of two females," the women said: Likewise, they have two shares of sins, as they have two shares of inheritance! So Allah revealed: "For men there is a share of what they have earned, and for women there is a share of what they have earned," meaning the sins, "and ask Allah, O women, for His bounty." [[Report 9250: For "Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad," see what has preceded from him under nos. 3109, 4077, 6691, 8431, and al-Muthanna's narration from him. "Abu Layla" is Abd Allah ibn Maysarah al-Kufi, kunyah Abu Ishaq, whose biography has preceded under no. 6920. "Abu Huraiz" is Abd Allah ibn al-Husayn al-Azdi, judge of Sijistan. Ibn Hibban said in al-Thiqat: "Truthful." Ibn Abi Adi said: "Most of what he narrates, no one follows him in it." Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam said: "He was a man of analogy (qiyas), and there is nothing in hadith." His biography is in al-Tahdhib. In the printed edition it read "Abu Jarir," which is an error; the manuscript is unpointed.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: for men there is a share of what they have earned from the inheritance of their deceased, and for women there is a share of them.

Mention of who said that:

9251: Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "For men there is a share of what they have earned, and for women there is a share of what they have earned," meaning: what the parents and the near relatives leave; he says: the male has the like of the share of two females.

9252: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Ikrimah or other, regarding His words: "For men there is a share of what they have earned, and for women there is a share of what they have earned." He said: In inheritance; they did not give women inheritance.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most preferable of the two views regarding the interpretation of the verse is the view of the one who said: its meaning is: for men there is a share of the reward and punishment of Allah, of what they have earned, that is, what they did of good or evil, and for women there is a share of what they have earned of that, as for men.

We only said that this is more preferable for the interpretation of the verse than the view of those who said: "Its interpretation is: for men there is a share of inheritance, and for women there is a share of it," because Allah the Exalted informed that for each group of men and women there is a share of what they earned. Inheritance is not something the heir earned; rather it is wealth that Allah bequeathed from his deceased without earning. "Kasb" (earning) is only work, and "al-mukhtarif" is the one who works for a living. [[See the explanation of "kasb" and "iktisab" above: 2:273-274; 3:100-101, 128-129; 4:449; 6:131, 295; 7:327, 364.]] It is not permissible that the meaning of the verse, since Allah said: "For men there is a share of what they have earned, and for women there is a share of what they have earned," be: for men there is a share of what they inherited, and for women there is a share of what they inherited. For if that were so, it would say: "For men there is a share of what they did not earn, and for women there is a share of what they did not earn"!!

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And ask Allah for His bounty﴾

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 32 (part 2 of 2):

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His majesty be exalted, He means: "Ask Allah for His aid and His success in acting in ways that please Him, through obedience to Him, so that He is pleased with you." Thus His bounty (fadl) in this place is His success and His help, as [see the explanation of "al-fadl" in what has passed before: 2:344 / 5:164, 571 / 6:516 / 7:299, 414.]

9253 - Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Nufayli narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Sa'id, regarding "And ask Allah for His bounty," he said: "It is worship, not a matter of this world."

9254 - Muhammad ibn Muslim narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to me, saying: Musa narrated to us, from Layth, who said regarding "His bounty": "It is worship, not a matter of this world." [The two reports: 9253 and 9254. "Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Razi" is the well-known Ibn Warah, whose full name is "Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Uthman ibn Abdullah," the hafiz, who was one of the trustworthy and precise narrators. They said: Ibn Muslim was a remarkable figure. Abu Zur'a al-Razi would not rise for anyone, and would not seat anyone in his place except Ibn Warah. Ibn Warah had a strong sense of self-importance and pride. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/79, and Tarikh Baghdad 3:256.
And "Abu Ja'far al-Nufayli" is "Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Nufayl al-Qudha'i," from whom the imams narrated. He was a hafiz, and Imam Ahmad, when he saw him, would venerate him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]

9255 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid regarding His saying "And ask Allah for His bounty," he said: "It is not the goods of this world."

9256 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding "And ask Allah for His bounty," [He] provides you with deeds, and that is better for you.

9257 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from a man whom he did not name, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Ask Allah for His bounty, for He loves to be asked, and among the best of worship is waiting for relief." [The report: 9257 - "Hakim ibn Jubayr al-Asadi," they have spoken about him. Ahmad said: "weak in narration, confused." Abu Hatim said: "weak in narration, rejected in narration, holds an unpraised opinion, we ask Allah for safety, extreme in Shi'ism."
This report was narrated by al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Supplications (Kitab al-Da'awat), no. 514, through: Bishr ibn Mu'adh al-Aqadi, from Hammad ibn Waqid, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. Then al-Tirmidhi said: "Thus Hammad ibn Waqid narrated this hadith, and Hammad ibn Waqid is not a hafiz. Abu Nu'aym narrated this hadith from Isra'il, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from a man, from the Prophet ﷺ, and Abu Nu'aym's hadith is more likely to be sound." Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir 2:430, quoting what al-Tirmidhi said: "Likewise Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the hadith of Waki' from Isra'il. Then he narrated it from the hadith of Qays ibn al-Rabi', from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Ask Allah for His bounty, for Allah loves to be asked, and the most beloved of Allah's servants to Him is the one who awaits relief.'"]

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever, of all things, Knowing﴾ (32)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His majesty be exalted, He means: Indeed Allah is aware of what benefits His servants, in what He has apportioned to them of good, and in His elevating some of them above others in religion and in the world, and in other than that of His decrees and judgments concerning them. "Knowing" means: possessing knowledge. So do not wish for what He has decreed for you, but rather obey Him, submit to His command, be content with His decree, and ask Him for His bounty.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And for every one We have made heirs of what the parents and close relatives leave﴾

By His saying, may His majesty be exalted, "And for every one We have made heirs," meaning: for each of you, O people, "We have made heirs," i.e., inheritors from the sons of his paternal uncle, his brothers, and the rest of his agnates other than them.

* *

The Arabs call a cousin "mawla," and from it is the saying of the poet: [I do not know who said it.]
"And a mawla around whom we shot arrows, while he was a corrupter (mudghil) with our honor, and the wounding (al-mundiyat) were swift (sarru')." [I have not found this verse anywhere, and it is in the manuscript as: "bi-a'wadina wal-mumdiyat saru'" (with our compensations and the ... ). "Rajul mudghil" means one with treachery who corrupts among people. "Al-mundiyat" means the disgracing things. I am still in great doubt about "bi-a'radina" and "sarru'," so I have left the verse as it is until I find it or find a sound way to read it. His saying "ramayna hawlahu" means we fought on his behalf, defended him, and shot at those around him who were shooting at him.]

Meaning by this: and a cousin around whom we shot arrows. From it is the saying of al-Fadl ibn al-Abbas:
"Gently, sons of our paternal uncle, gently, our mawali; do not reveal to us what was buried."
[Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu Ubayda 1:125; al-Kamil 2:279; al-Mu'talif wal-Mukhtalif; Mu'jam al-shu'ara' pp. 35, 310; al-Hamasa 1:121; al-Sadaqa wal-sadiq p. 139; al-Lisan (w-l-y), and others. Their version: "Do not stir up between us what was buried."
This is the better of the two versions and more fitting to the sense of the poetry; in al-Lisan there is another version that does not hold.]

And the people of interpretation have said in accordance with what we have said regarding this.

Those who said this:

9258 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, saying: Idris narrated to us, saying: Talha ibn Musarrif narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying "And for every one We have made heirs," he said: "Heirs."

9259 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas: "And for every one We have made heirs of what the parents and close relatives leave," he said: "The mawali are the 'asaba, meaning: the heirs."

9260 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid regarding His saying "And for every one We have made heirs," he said: "The mawali are the 'asaba."

9261 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, His saying "And for every one We have made heirs," he said: "They are the guardians (awliya')."

9262 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "And for every one We have made heirs," he says: "'Asaba."

9263 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada regarding His saying "And for every one We have made heirs," he said: "The mawali: the guardians of the father, or the brother, [or] the son of the brother, or others of the 'asaba."

9264 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And for every one We have made heirs," as for "mawali," they are the people of inheritance.

9265 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying "And for every one We have made heirs," he said: "The mawali are the 'asaba. They were in the Jahiliyya the mawali, but when the non-Arabs (al-'ajam) entered among the Arabs, they did not find a name for them, so Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿If you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your mawali﴾ [Surat al-Ahzab: 5], and they were named 'al-mawali.'" He said: "And the 'mawla' today is of two kinds: a mawla who inherits and is inherited from, and these are the relatives by blood (dhawu al-arham); and a mawla who is inherited from but does not inherit, and these are the 'ataqa (freed slaves)." [It is said: "He is a mawla 'ataqa," meaning one who was freed from bondage; "al-'ataqa" (with fatha on the 'ayn) is a verbal noun like "al-'itq" (with kasra and sukun) and "'ataq" (with fatha on the 'ayn). His saying "fa-ha'ula' al-'ataqa" means: these are the mawali of manumission; if "mawali" has dropped from the copyist's text, then it is a verbal noun used as a description, meaning these are the freed persons.] He said: "Do you not see the saying of Zakariyya: ﴿And indeed I fear the mawali after me﴾ [Surat Maryam: 5]? So the mawali here are the heirs."

* *

By His saying "of what the parents and close relatives leave," He means: of what his father and his relatives leave of inheritance.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The meaning of the speech is: For each of you, O people, We have appointed agnates who inherit by it from what his father and his relatives leave of their inheritance.

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿And those whom your oaths have bound [to alliance], give them their share﴾**

[[The manuscript and the printed edition do not mention "give them their share" (فآتوهم نصيبهم) at this point or after it, so I have inserted it in its place, because he explains it afterwards at this point.]]

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The reciters differed in their reading of this.

Some of them read: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ عَقَدَتْ أَيْمَانُكُمْ﴾ ("and those whose oaths you have tied"), meaning: "and those with whom your oaths have tied the alliance between you and them." This is the reading of the majority of the Kufan reciters.

* *

Others read it: ﴿والذين عاقدت أيمانكم﴾ ("and those with whom your oaths have made a contract"), meaning: "and those with whom your oaths and their oaths have made the alliance between you and them."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What we hold regarding this is that they are two well-known readings, widely transmitted among the reciters of the cities of the Muslims, with one meaning.

* *

As for the indication in His words "your oaths" that it refers to the oaths of both the contracting parties and of those bound by the alliance, there is no need to rely on the reading of "tied" (عقدت) or "made a contract" (عاقدت) for this. Those who read "made a contract" said that a contract of alliance can only be made by two parties, and that we must have an indication in the wording that this is so. They overlooked the place where "your oaths" indicates that the meaning is your oaths and the oaths of those bound, and that the tying is merely an attribute of the oaths, not of those who make the alliance. Some of them even claimed that when it is read "your oaths have tied," the sentence needs a suppressed particle to complete it [[In the printed edition: "a relative pronoun (ضمير صلة) in the sentence," which is a confusion with no meaning. I have restored what is in the manuscript. His phrase "a pronoun" means "a suppressed element" (إضمار), and something similar has passed before (1:427, note 1; 2:107, note 1). As for his phrase "an attribute" (صفة), it has been noted several times that "الصفة" here is the preposition, and "حروف الصفات" are the prepositions (see 6:329, note 6, and the references there). The meaning is: a suppressed preposition.

As for his phrase "to complete the sentence" (تقى الكلام), this expression is obscure in its meaning, and it is in the manuscript as I have given it. Perhaps he meant that the preposition connected with "tied" protects the sentence from corruption of meaning. This may be from the old phrasing of the scholars, though I cannot verify it, and above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing.]] so that the sentence would mean: "and those for whom your oaths have been tied," forgetting the aspect we have mentioned, namely that the oaths refer to the oaths of both parties.

* *

As for "your oaths have made a contract," it means: the oaths of these people have made a contract with the oaths of those people, the alliance.

The two are close in meaning, although the reading of the one who reads "tied your oaths" without the alif is more correct in meaning than the reading of the one who reads "made a contract," because of the sufficient indication in the attribute of the oaths as "tied," [[In the printed edition: "from the indication upon the meaning in the attribute of the oaths by the tying," which is meaningless. In the manuscript it reads "the indicating (المعنية)," and what is beyond doubt is that "على" ("upon") has been added in this phrase, and that the correct reading is "المغنية" ("sufficient"). See the following note.]] that they are the oaths of both parties, which is sufficient from indication of that by other means. [[The prepositions in this sentence have become entangled, and I wished to smooth its structure. He says: "because of the sufficient indication in the attribute of the oaths by the tying ... from indication of that by other means." So "from the indication" is connected to "sufficient." The meaning is that the attribute of the oaths as tied is an indication that they are the oaths of both parties, and this indication is sufficient so that no other indication is needed for that meaning.]]

* *

As for the meaning of His words "tied your oaths," it means: joined, strengthened and confirmed. "Your oaths" means your pledges, by which each of you pledged to the others ["each of you" in manuscript and printed edition: "pledged to one another"; the context requires "each of you," as I have given it] = "give them their share."

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of "share" (نصيب), which Allah commanded the parties to the alliance to give to one another in Islam. [[See the explanation of "share" above: 4:206 / 6:288.]]

Some of them said: It is his share of the inheritance, because in the pre-Islamic period they used to inherit from one another. In Islam Allah made it obligatory, through that alliance, for some of them to inherit from others, and in Islam the same kind of inheritance as they had in the pre-Islamic period. Then this was abrogated by what was prescribed of the obligatory shares for those with kinship ties and blood relations.

Those who said this:

9266 - Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Waqid, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah and al-Hasan al-Basri, regarding His words: "And those with whom your oaths have made a contract, give them their share; indeed Allah is ever a witness over all things" [[Recitations "made a contract" (عاقدت) and "tied" (عقدت) will come in the following reports. I have left them as they are in the manuscript and printed edition. If they differ, I have kept what is in the manuscript, without indicating this by my own action.]] He said: A man would make an alliance with a man with whom there was no kinship, and one of them would inherit from the other. Then Allah abrogated that in "al-Anfal," saying: ﴿وَأُولُو الأرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَى بِبَعْضٍ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَيْءٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾ ("And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah; indeed Allah is Knowing of all things") [Surah al-Anfal: 75]. [[I have included the full verse from the manuscript.]]

9267 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding Allah's words: "And those with whom your oaths have made a contract," he said: A man would make a contract with a man and inherit from him. Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, made a contract with a freedman (mawla) and inherited from him.

9268 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "And those with whom your oaths have made a contract, give them their share." He said: A man would make a contract with a man, that whichever of them died, the other would inherit from him. Then Allah revealed: ﴿وَأُولُو الأرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَى بِبَعْضٍ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُهَاجِرِينَ إِلا أَنْ تَفْعَلُوا إِلَى أَوْلِيَائِكُمْ مَعْرُوفًا﴾ ("And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah than the believers and the emigrants, except that you do to your allies a kindness") [Surah al-Ahzab: 6]. He says: "except that they bequeath to their allies, those with whom they made the contract, a bequest, which is permissible for them from a third of the deceased's estate." That is the "kindness" (ma'ruf).

9269 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "And those with whom your oaths have made a contract, give them their share; indeed Allah is ever a witness over all things." A man would make a contract with a man in the pre-Islamic period, saying: "My blood is your blood, my ruin is your ruin, you inherit from me and I inherit from you, you seek vengeance for me and I seek vengeance for you." [[Their saying "my blood is your blood" means: if a person kills me, you seek vengeance for my blood as you seek the blood of your kinsman and brother. "Al-hadm" (with the consonant dal either unvowelled or vowelled) : if the dal is unvowelled, it means: whoever demolishes my honour and dignity has demolished it from you, or: whoever wastes my blood has wasted yours, or: whatever I have forgiven of the blood, you must forgive it. As for "al-hadm" with a fatha on the dal: its origin is "the thing that has collapsed," and it is close in meaning to the first; it is also said it means "the grave," i.e., "be buried where I am buried." They mean: neither of us will leave the other in life or death.

Their saying "you seek vengeance through me and I seek it through you" means: you seek retribution for me if some harm befalls me, and I do likewise for you. The "bi" here means "cause," i.e., because of me and as a result of what has befallen me. All these expressions are a binding of the covenant, a firm contract obliging the two men to help one another in good and in evil, so that neither leaves the other in trial and affliction.]] Then he (the heir) was given a sixth of the whole estate in Islam, and afterwards the heirs divided their inheritance. Then this was later abrogated in "Surah al-Anfal," where Allah said: ﴿وَأُولُو الأرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَى بِبَعْضٍ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ﴾ ("And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another in the Book of Allah") [Surah al-Anfal: 6].

9270 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: "And those with whom your oaths have made a contract," he said: In the pre-Islamic period a man would make a contract with a man, saying: "You inherit from me and I inherit from you, you seek vengeance for me and I seek vengeance for you." [[See the preceding note.]] When Islam came, some of them remained, and they were commanded to give them their share of the inheritance, which was a sixth. Then this was abrogated by inheritance, when He said: ﴿وَأُولُو الأرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَى بِبَعْضٍ﴾ ("And those of blood relationship are more entitled to one another").

9271 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammam ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: I heard Qatadah say, regarding His words: "And those with whom your oaths have made a contract, give them their share": that was because a man in the pre-Islamic period would make a contract with a man, saying: "My ruin is your ruin and my blood is your blood, you inherit from me and I inherit from you, you seek vengeance for me and I seek vengeance for you." [[See the preceding note.]] So he was given a sixth of the whole estate, and then the heirs divided their inheritance. Later this was abrogated in "al-Anfal," where He said: ﴿وَأُولُو الأرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَى بِبَعْضٍ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ﴾, and the inheritances became for those with blood relationship.

9272 - Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Ikrimah, who said: This was an alliance in the pre-Islamic period, where a man would say to a man: "You inherit from me and I inherit from you, you help me and I help you, you pay the blood-money (aql) for me and I pay it for you." [["Al-aql" (with fatha then sukun): the blood-money (diyah). "Aqala al-qatil aqlan" means he paid his blood-money. "Aqala 'anhu" means he paid his crime on his behalf, which is when he is obliged to pay blood-money and another pays it for him.]]

9273 - Narrated to me on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: [[In the printed edition: "Ubayd ibn Salman," which is an error that occurred often in this printing; I have pointed it out several times, and the correct form is from the manuscript. It is a chain that recurs throughout the tafsir, and I will correct it from today and will not refer to it again.]] I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: "And those with whom your oaths have made a contract": a man would follow a man and make a contract with him: "If I die, you will have the same as what some of my children inherit!" And this was abrogated.

9274 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "And for each We have made heirs of what the parents and the close relatives leave, and those with whom your oaths have made a contract, give them their share." In the pre-Islamic period a man would take another man as an attached follower, so when a man died, his family and relatives received the inheritance, and his attached follower was left with nothing. Then Allah revealed: "And those with whom your oaths have made a contract, give them their share," and so he would be given from the inheritance. Then Allah revealed afterwards: ﴿وَأُولُو الأرْحَامِ بَعْضُهُمْ أَوْلَى بِبَعْضٍ فِي كِتَابِ اللَّهِ﴾.

* *

Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed concerning those whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made brothers among the Emigrants and the Helpers, so some of them inherited from others through that brotherhood. Then Allah abrogated that by the obligatory shares and by His words: "And for each We have made heirs of what the parents and the close relatives leave."

Those who said this:

9275 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, saying: Idris ibn Yazid narrated to us, saying: Talhah ibn Musarrif narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "And those with whom your oaths have made a contract, give them their share." He said: When the Emigrants came to Medina, the Emigrant would inherit from the Helper rather than his blood relatives, because of the brotherhood that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had established between them. Then when this verse was revealed: "And for each We have made heirs," it abrogated it. [[Report 9275: al-Bukhari recorded it in his Sahih (al-Fath 8:186) in full, and al-Tabari divided it, narrating part of it here and the rest under number 9277. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: "Idris is Ibn Yazid al-Awdi (with fatha on the alif and sukun on the waw), father of Abdullah ibn Idris the Kufan jurist; he is trustworthy according to them, and he has nothing in al-Bukhari except this hadith. In al-Tabari's narration from Abu Kurayb, from Abu Usamah: 'Idris ibn Yazid narrated to us,' appears." There is an omission in al-Bukhari's narration, in which "give them their share" dropped out, although the phrase "from the support" is connected to "give them their share," not to "made a contract," and this is the proper construction. Al-Hafiz added it in al-Fath from this narration of al-Tabari.]]

9276 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And those with whom your oaths have made a contract," those whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ bound by contract: "give them their share," when no blood relative comes between them. He said: And this does not occur today; it was only among a group whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made brothers, and that ended. This applies to no one except the Prophet ﷺ, who made brothers between the Emigrants and the Helpers; today no one is made brother with anyone.

* *

Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed concerning the people of the alliance by oath, but they were commanded to give one another their portions of support, counsel, and the like, excluding inheritance.

Those who said this:

9277 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, saying: Idris al-Awdi narrated to us, saying: Talhah ibn Musarrif narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: "And those with whom your oaths have tied [the alliance], give them their share," of support, counsel and "al-rifadah," and he bequeaths to them, though the inheritance has gone. [[Report 9277: this is the completion of the preceding report 9275, which has already been commented on. In the manuscript it read: "and the inheritance" with a blank space between them, which the printed edition completed correctly from al-Bukhari's narration. In al-Bukhari there is an addition: "and the inheritance has gone, and he bequeaths to him."

"Al-rifadah" (with kasra on the ra): help by way of gift and kindness. From it comes the "rifadah" which the Quraysh used to share in the pre-Islamic period, each person contributing money according to his means, and they would gather a great sum of money during the season, with which they would buy camels, food and raisins for the pilgrims, and they would continue feeding people until the days of the pilgrimage ended. The "rifadah" and the "siqayah" (provision of water) belonged to the Banu Hashim.]]

9278 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: "And those with whom your oaths have tied." He said: There was an alliance in the pre-Islamic period [["Kana" here is complete, with no subject or predicate.]] and in Islam they were commanded to give them their share of the blood-money, the counsel and the support, but no inheritance.

9279 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid that he said regarding this verse: "And those with whom your oaths have made a contract, give them their share," of aid, support and alliance.

9280 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Mansur, from Mujahid regarding Allah's words: "And those with whom your oaths have made a contract," he said: This was an alliance in the pre-Islamic period, and when Islam came, they were commanded to give them their share of support, loyalty and counsel, but no inheritance.

9281 - Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Ibn Juraij said: "And those with whom your oaths have made a contract," Abdullah ibn Kathir informed me that he heard Mujahid say: it is the alliance, "your oaths have tied." He said: "give them their share": the support.

9282 - Zakariyya ibn Yahya narrated to me, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Ibn Juraij said: Ata' informed me, saying: It is the alliance. He said: "give them their share": the blood-money and the support.

9283 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding Allah's words: "And those with whom your oaths have made a contract," he said: They have their share of support, "al-rifadah" and blood-money. [[Report 9283: in the printed edition: "Muhammad ibn Muhammad ibn Amr," which is a plain error; the correct form is from the manuscript. Nevertheless, it is a chain that recurs frequently throughout the tafsir; the nearest instance is 9239.

See the explanation of "al-aql" and "al-rifadah" in the notes shortly above.]]

9284 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly.

9285 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Sharik narrated to us, from Salim, from Sa'id: "And those with whom your oaths have made a contract," he said: They are the allies.

9286 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Abbad ibn al-Awwam narrated to us, from Khusayf, from Ikrimah, the same.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 33 (part 2 of 3):

9287 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And to those with whom your oaths have been contracted, give them their share﴾. As for "your oaths have been contracted" (ʿaqadat aymanukum), it refers to the alliance (al-ḥilf). A man in the Jahiliyyah would arrive among a people and they would form an alliance with him that he was one of them, supporting him with themselves. [["āsāhu bi-nafsihi wa-wāsāhu bi-nafsihi" means he made him an equal to himself (uswah lahu), i.e., a likeness to him. From this comes al-muwasah (mutual support), which is sharing and partnership in livelihood and sustenance.] If they had a right or a fight, he was like them; and if he had a right or needed help, they would abandon him. When Islam came, they asked about him, but God refused except to strengthen it. The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Islam has not increased the allies except in strength."
* *
Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed concerning those who used to adopt the sons of others in the Jahiliyyah; in Islam they were commanded to make a bequest to them at death. [[In the printed edition: "fa-umiru bi-l-Islam" ("they were commanded by Islam"), which is corrupt; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]
Mention of those who said this:
9288 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: al-Layth narrated to me, from ʿUqayl, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab narrated to me that God said: ﴿And for every one We have made heirs of what the parents and close relatives leave, and those with whom your oaths have been contracted, give them their share﴾. Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: This verse was revealed only concerning those who used to adopt men who were not their sons and would bequeath to them. God revealed concerning them, and made a share for them in the bequest, and returned the inheritance to the mawali (blood-relations) in the case of kinship and agnatic kin. [[In the printed edition: "fi dhawi al-rahm," which is correct; what I have recorded from the manuscript is also correct.] God refused inheritance for the adopted claimants from those who claimed and adopted them, but God made for them a share in the bequest.
* *
Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct interpretation of His words "and those with whom your oaths have been contracted" is the view of those who said: "those with whom your oaths have been contracted by alliance, and they are the allies (al-ḥulafāʾ)." This is because it is known to all people of knowledge of the days and reports of the Arabs that the contracting of an alliance among them occurred through oaths, covenants and pacts, in the manner of the narration we have mentioned.
Since God, may His praise be exalted, described only those whose oaths had contracted what they had bound between themselves, and not those who had not contracted a bond between them by oaths [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "dūna man lam yaʿqid ʿaqd mā baynahum aymānuhum", and the correct reading is what I have recorded. Then his later words: "and the brotherhood of the Prophet ..." are coordinated with his words: "since God ..."]] = and the brotherhood the Prophet ﷺ established between those he made brothers among the Muhajirun and the Ansar was not by their oaths, and likewise adoption = [[His words "it was known" are the answer to "since God ..." and what is coordinated with it.]] it was known that the correct view on this matter is the view of the one who said "it is the alliance," and not other than it, for the reason we have described.
* *
As for His words "give them their share", the more correct of the two interpretations is that upon which all are agreed concerning its established ruling: that is, the giving by the people of the alliance which existed in the Jahiliyyah, not in Islam, to one another of their portions of support, counsel and opinion, but not inheritance. This is due to the soundness of the report from the Messenger of God ﷺ that he said: "There is no alliance in Islam; and whatever alliance was in the Jahiliyyah, Islam has only increased it in strength."

9289 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us this, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Shurayk, from Simak, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, from the Messenger of God ﷺ. [[Hadith 9289: its isnad is sound.
It was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad, 2911, 3046, by way of Shurayk, with this isnad, abridged, without his saying "there is no alliance in Islam." This addition is established in it through the narration of Abu Yaʿla. Al-Haythami mentioned it in Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid 8: 173, in full, and said: "Abu Yaʿla and Ahmad narrated it abridged. Their men are the men of the Sahih."
Ibn Kathir mentioned it 2: 431-432, from this place in al-Tabari.
Al-Suyuti mentioned it 2: 151, abridged as in the Musnad's narration. He was very brief in its takhrij, as he attributed it only to ʿAbd ibn Humayd.]]
