9290 - And Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Musʿab ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, from Isra'il ibn Yunus, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, mawla of the family of Talhah, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "There is no alliance in Islam, and every alliance that was in the Jahiliyyah, Islam has only increased in strength." And it would not please me that I had red camels, and that I had annulled the alliance that was in the Dar al-Nadwah. [[Hadith 9290: This is another isnad, from another route, for the hadith of Ibn ʿAbbas, with a longer wording than the preceding.
Its isnad is sound.
Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿUbayd, mawla of the family of Talhah: trustworthy (thiqah); Ibn Maʿin and others declared him trustworthy. Biographied in al-Tahdhib; also al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 1/1/146, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/318.
The addition here, "and it would not please me that I had red camels," was mentioned by al-Haythami in Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid as a separate hadith, 8: 172, and he said: "Al-Tabarani narrated it, and in it is Marzuq ibn al-Marzuban, whom I do not know, and the rest of its men are the men of the Sahih."
The isnad of al-Tabarani is not before me, so that I could speak on it. But the isnad of al-Tabari here is free of that man, so the hadith is sound by this route.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it 2: 432, from this place, and added nothing.
For "red camels" (ḥumr al-naʿam), see its explanation above at no. 9185.]]

9291 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from his father, from Shuʿbah ibn al-Tawam al-Dabbi: that Qays ibn ʿAsim asked the Prophet ﷺ about the alliance, and he said: "There is no alliance in Islam, but hold fast to the alliance of the Jahiliyyah."

9292 - Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mughirah informed us, from his father, from Shuʿbah ibn al-Tawam, from Qays ibn ʿAsim: that he asked the Prophet ﷺ about the alliance; he said: "Whatever alliance was in the Jahiliyyah, hold fast to it, and there is no alliance in Islam." [[Hadiths 9291 and 9292: Mughirah is Ibn Miqsam al-Dabbi, already passed at 3349. His father, "Miqsam al-Dabbi": biographied briefly in al-Taʿjil, p. 409, and that Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat. He is a Tabiʿi, who narrated from al-Nuʿman ibn Bashir. Al-Bukhari treated him in al-Kabir 4/2/33, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/414-415. Neither of them mentioned any criticism of him.
Shuʿbah ibn al-Tawam al-Dabbi, also said "al-Tamimi": a trustworthy Tabiʿi. Biographied in al-Taʿjil, pp. 177-178, al-Isabah 3: 230, al-Kabir 2/2/244, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/368.
The hadith was narrated by al-Tayalisi, 1084, from Jarir ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid, from Mughirah, i.e., with the first of the two isnads here.
Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 5: 61 (Halabi), from Hushaym, from Mughirah, i.e., with the second.
Ibn Kathir transmitted it 2: 432 from the second, then pointed to Ahmad's narration, then transmitted it again, p. 433, from the Musnad's narration.
Al-Haythami mentioned it in Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid 8: 172, and said: "Ahmad narrated it." Then he added nothing!
Ibn Abi Hatim alluded to it in the biography of "Shuʿbah ibn al-Tawam," saying: "He narrated from Qays ibn ʿAsim, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said: There is no alliance in Islam."]]

9293 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Waki' narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi ʿAbd Allah, from Ibn Judʿan, from his grandmother, from Umm Salamah: that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "There is no alliance in Islam, and whatever alliance was in the Jahiliyyah, Islam has only increased in strength." [[Hadith 9293: Dawud ibn Abi ʿAbd Allah, mawla of Banu Hashim: trustworthy; Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat, as in al-Tahdhib. Ibn Abi Hatim biographied him 1/2/417, and mentioned no criticism of him.
Ibn Judʿan: the one known by this name among the people of this field is "ʿAli ibn Zayd ibn Judʿan." Al-Tirmidhi narrated 4: 25, with this isnad, "Abu Kurayb ..." — the hadith "the counsellor is trustworthy."
The Hafiz Ibn ʿAsakir, in his book al-Atraf, thought that he was "ʿAli ibn Zayd." Al-Hafiz al-Mizzi reproached him in Tahdhib al-Kamal, pp. 817-818 (photographed manuscript), saying: "That is an error from him. The correct is: his grandfather ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Judʿan" — meaning, because of his saying in the isnad: "from Ibn Judʿan, from his grandmother."
In Tahdhib al-Kamal and Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, in the biography of Dawud, and in the biography of "ʿAbd al-Rahman" (3: 191, and 6: 267 of Tahdhib al-Tahdhib), it is stated that al-Bukhari narrated in al-Adab al-Mufrad the hadith "the counsellor is trustworthy" by way of Dawud "from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad" — this one. And that this is the evidence that what is meant by "Ibn Judʿan" is "ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad." What I saw in al-Adab al-Mufrad (p. 29) with this isnad is a lengthy hadith, but it does not contain the words "the counsellor is trustworthy." So it appears that they mean the original hadith. But the narration of al-Bukhari is what revealed the correct name of "Ibn Judʿan."
The grandmother of this Ibn Judʿan is unknown; her name is not known. In my view her unknown status does no harm. The more likely, in my opinion, is that she was a Companion, because ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad is a Tabiʿi who narrated from ʿAʾishah and from Ibn ʿUmar. So his grandmother is nearly certain to a knowledgeable person to be a Companion, or at least a mukhadram. Women in those eras were not known for fabricating reports. Therefore al-Dhahabi said in al-Mizan (3: 395): "A section on unknown women. I do not know of any woman who was accused, nor one whom they abandoned." His words here, "from his grandmother," in the printed edition are "from whoever narrated to him" — which is a distortion. And in the printed edition of Ibn Kathir 2: 432, when he transmitted this hadith from al-Tabari: "from Ibn Judʿan, narrated to him" — which is also a distortion. Its correct form, as we have recorded, is "from his grandmother." It is confirmed in the correct form in the Azhar manuscript of Ibn Kathir's tafsir (2: 273, photographed copy in my possession).
The hadith was mentioned by al-Haythami in Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid 8: 173, and he said: "Abu Yaʿla and al-Tabarani narrated it. In it is the grandmother of Ibn Abi Mulaykah, whom I do not know. The rest of its men are trustworthy."
And "the grandmother of Ibn Abi Mulaykah" is "the grandmother of Ibn Judʿan," because Ibn Judʿan here is "ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn Judʿan." He is the nephew of "ʿAli ibn Zayd ibn Judʿan," and they were attributed to their great-grandfather. For "ʿAli ibn Zayd" is "ʿAli ibn Zayd ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah Zuhayr ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Judʿan." What became famous among the hadith scholars as "Ibn Abi Mulaykah" is "ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah Zuhayr..." And he is the paternal cousin of "ʿAli ibn Zayd."]]

9294 - Humayd ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, saying: Husayn al-Mu'allim narrated to us = and Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Husayn al-Mu'allim narrated to us = and Hatim ibn Bakr al-Dabbi narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, from Husayn al-Mu'allim = he said: My father narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, from his father, from his grandfather: that the Messenger of God ﷺ said in his sermon on the day of the conquest of Makkah: "Fulfil the alliance, for Islam only increases it in strength, and do not create a new alliance in Islam." [[Hadith 9294: Hatim ibn Bakr al-Dabbi, teacher of al-Tabari: thus his father's name is confirmed here as "Bakr." It passed at 3222 with the diminutive "Bukayr." There I explained that it is confirmed in al-Taqrib and al-Tahdhib as "Bakr," and in al-Khulasah as "Bukayr." So this difference has occurred in two places in al-Tabari. Then I returned to the photographed manuscript copy of Tahdhib al-Kamal, p. 214, and it became clear that its copyist dropped the word "Bakr" and recorded "Hatim ibn Ghaylan," attributed to his grandfather. This is certainly an error by the copyist, because he recorded it before the biography of "Hatim ibn Huraith." If the original were "Hatim ibn Ghaylan," it would have been placed later in its position in the letter ghayn among the fathers of those named "Hatim," so it would be after "Hatim ibn al-ʿAla'." So the problem with the name of his father remains as it is?
This hadith al-Tabari narrated here, abridged, with three isnads: from "Humayd ibn Mas'adah, from Husayn al-Mu'allim." Then from "Mujahid ibn Musa, from Yazid ibn Harun, from Husayn al-Mu'allim." Then from "Hatim ibn Bakr al-Dabbi, from ʿAbd al-Aʿla, from Husayn al-Mu'allim." Then Husayn al-Mu'allim says: "My father narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb."
There are two problems in these isnads:
The first: Humayd ibn Mas'adah died in the year 244, so it is impossible that he narrated from Husayn al-Mu'allim and said, as here, "Husayn al-Mu'allim narrated to us." For Husayn died in the year 145, so between their deaths are 99 years!! The more likely view to me is that the copyists dropped a shaykh between Humayd and Husayn.
The second: "Husayn al-Mu'allim" is "Husayn ibn Dhakwan." He narrates from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb directly. Had this been alone, there would be a possibility that he also narrates from him through his father. But the problem is that "Dhakwan," the father of Husayn al-Mu'allim, has no mention in the registers of men with any narration, and no one mentioned that his son narrated from him. So I also favour that his saying here, "My father narrated to us," is an erroneous addition by the copyists.
What supports that the addition of "my father narrated to us" is a confusion by the copyists is that Ibn Kathir, when he referred to this isnad at 2: 432, said: "Then he (i.e., al-Tabari) narrated it from the hadith of Husayn al-Mu'allim and ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, with it." So he mentioned that Husayn narrated it from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb. He did not mention "from Husayn, from his father."
As for the hadith itself, its meaning will come, from the narration of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb: 9297, 9298, and from the narration of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith, from ʿAmr: 9299. Its takhrij will be given there, God willing.]]

9295 - Abu Kurayb and ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Saffar narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Zakariya ibn Abi Zaʾidah narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, from his father, from Jubayr ibn Mut'im: that the Prophet ﷺ said: "There is no alliance in Islam; and whatever alliance was in the Jahiliyyah, Islam has only increased it in strength." [[Hadith 9295: Zakariya ibn Abi Zaʾidah al-Hamdani al-Wadaʿi: a well-known trustworthy narrator, among the shaykhs of Shuʿbah and al-Thawri. The Jama'ah narrated from him.
Sa'd ibn Ibrahim ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, judge of Madinah: trustworthy, of many narrations, and he is firm, without doubt. The Jama'ah narrated from him.
His father "Ibrahim ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman": a trustworthy Tabiʿi, of the great Tabiʿun. Biographied in al-Tahdhib; also al-Kabir 1/1/295, Ibn Saʿd 5: 39-40, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/111.
"Jubayr ibn Mut'im": a well-known Companion, of Quraysh, of Banu Nawfal. He came to Madinah for the ransom of the captives of Badr. Then he embraced Islam afterwards.
The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad: 16832, vol. 4 p. 83 (Halabi), by way of Zakariya, that is Ibn Abi Zaʾidah, with this isnad.
Likewise Muslim narrated it, 2: 270, and al-Bayhaqi 6: 262, both by way of Zakariya.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it 2: 432-433, from the narration of the Musnad. Then he pointed out that Muslim, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir and al-Nasa'i narrated it.]]

9296 - Humayd ibn Mas'adah and Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, both saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq narrated to us = and Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq = from al-Zuhri, from Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, from his father, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, that the Messenger of God ﷺ said: "I witnessed the alliance of the Mutayyibun, and I was a boy with my paternal uncles, and it would not please me that I had red camels and that I should break it." — Yaʿqub added in his narration from Ibn ʿUlayyah: He said: al-Zuhri said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Islam has not come upon an alliance except that it increased it in strength." He said: "And there is no alliance in Islam." He said: "And the Messenger of God ﷺ united Quraysh and the Ansar." [[Hadith 9296: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal ibn Lahiq al-Basri: trustworthy, one of the shaykhs of Ahmad, Ishaq and Ibn al-Madini. The Jama'ah narrated from him. Biographied in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 1/2/84, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/366.
This hadith was narrated by al-Tabari by two isnads by way of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq.
That is "ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq ibn ʿAbd Allah al-ʿAmiri." He is trustworthy; Ibn Maʿin and others declared him trustworthy, and Muslim narrated from him. Biographied in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 1/1/52, Ibn Saʿd 5: 151-152, and Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/218.
The hadith was narrated by Ahmad, 16055, from Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, with this isnad.
Then he narrated its first part: 16076, from Isma'il, that is Ibn ʿUlayyah, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq.
Likewise al-Bukhari narrated its first part in al-Adab al-Mufrad, p. 83, by way of Ibn ʿUlayyah. An error in printing occurred there, which is corrected from this place.
This hadith is, in reality, two hadiths:
The first: a connected hadith, from the hadith of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf.
The second: a mursal hadith. It is al-Zuhri's saying: "The Messenger of God ﷺ said..." — to its end.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 33 (part 3 of 3):

I have explained this matter at length in the Musnad: 1655.]]

9297. Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered Makkah in the year of the Conquest, he stood up to address the people and said: "O people, any alliance (hilf) that existed in the Jahiliyya (the Age of Ignorance), Islam has only strengthened it. But there is no alliance in Islam."

9298. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ), a similar report.

9299. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn Makhlad narrated to us, saying: Sulayman ibn Bilal narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith narrated to us, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, from the Prophet (ﷺ), a similar report. [[The reports 9297 to 9299 are three chains (asanid, sing. isnad) for a single hadith. It has already passed in a similar form: 9294.
Yazid, in the first chain: he is Yazid ibn Harun.
Abd al-Rahman, in the third chain: he is Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Abd Allah ibn Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah.
The hadith is also transmitted by Ahmad in the Musnad, within a lengthy hadith: 6692, from Yazid ibn Harun, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq. We have indicated many of its chains there, and in the Istidrak: 2832.
Al-Bukhari transmitted it in al-Adab al-Mufrad, pp. 83-84, in abridged form as here, from Khalid ibn Makhlad, with the last chain mentioned here.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it, vol. 2, p. 432, citing the report 9298 here. Then he pointed to the two reports 9294 and 9299.]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: Since what we have mentioned from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is sound, and since a verse whose ruling is disputed, as to whether it is abrogated (mansukh) or not abrogated, [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "mansukh hiya" (it is abrogated), which is an error; the correct reading is what has been adopted.]] cannot be judged to be abrogated, given the disagreement of those who differ over it, and since there is a sound basis for upholding its ruling and denying that it is abrogated, [[The sense of the sentence is: "it is not permissible to judge it abrogated ... except by a proof that must be accepted," and what lies between them is a qualifying clause interposed between the two parts of the statement.]] except by a proof that must be accepted, due to what we have shown in various places in our books, the evidence for the soundness of this view [[See his discussion in: "al-Nasikh wa'l-Mansukh" (Abrogating and Abrogated) above: 131, note 1, and the references there.]] = [[His words "then it is necessary..." are the answer to his earlier words: "Since what we have mentioned from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) is sound."]] then it is necessary that the sound view regarding the interpretation of His words, "And those whom your oaths have bound, give them their share," is what we have mentioned as the interpretation: that His words "whom your oaths have bound" refer to alliance, and His words "give them their share" refer to support, aid, counsel and opinion, as the Messenger of God (ﷺ) commanded in the reports we have cited from him = [[The context: "then it is necessary that the sound view ... is what we have mentioned as the interpretation ... and not the view of the one who said: 'The meaning of His words, give them their share, is inheritance,' and that this was a ruling later abrogated by His words, 'And those related by blood are nearer to one another in the Book of God,' and not any view other than the one we have stated in its interpretation."]] and not the view of those who say: "The meaning of His words, 'give them their share,' is inheritance, and that this was a ruling which was then abrogated by His words, 'And those related by blood are nearer to one another in the Book of God,'" and not any view other than the one we have stated concerning its interpretation. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "dun ma siwa al-qawl" without the conjunctive wa; the correct reading includes the conjunction "wa," coordinating with his earlier words: "not the view of those who say."]]
And since what we have said on this is correct, it is necessary that the verse be decisive (muhkama), not abrogated. [[Ibn Kathir found this passage of al-Tabari's words problematic, so he quoted it and then said: "There is something to examine here, for among oaths some were for support and aid, and some were for inheritance, as many of the early authorities have related, and as Ibn Abbas said: 'The Emigrant (muhajir) used to inherit from the Helper (ansari) to the exclusion of his kin and blood relations, until that was abrogated.' So how can he say that this verse is decisive and not abrogated? And God knows best."
What Ibn Kathir found surprising has in fact been explained by al-Tabari, who built his whole method upon it in every abrogating and abrogated (nasikh and mansukh) matter. He repeated it many times in his tafsir, and here he restated it when mentioning the abrogating and abrogated, saying: if the verse's ruling is disputed, whether it is abrogated or not, and those who differ over its ruling disagree, and there is a sound basis for denying abrogation from it and affirming that it is decisive, then no one may judge that its ruling is abrogated, except by a proof that must be accepted. Abu Ja'far has repeatedly made clear that the proof which must be accepted is: the apparent meaning of the Qur'an, and the sound report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ). As for the interpretation of Ibn Abbas or of other imams, it is not a proof for establishing abrogation in a verse, since it interprets the verse as decisive on a sound basis.
So it is strange of Ibn Kathir to marvel at Abu Ja'far's interpretation and exposition. Had he been fair, he would have refuted al-Tabari's argument in his discussion of abrogating and abrogated, rather than objecting to him and marvelling at him with an argument that is itself refuted according to al-Tabari, who expounded its refutation repeatedly in this book and in his other books, as he said. May God have mercy on Abu Ja'far, and forgive Ibn Kathir.]]
* *
The discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, God is ever, over all things, a witness﴾
Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: give those whom your oaths have bound their share of support, counsel and opinion, for God is a witness to what you do of such things and to your other deeds, watching over all of it and guarding it, until He recompenses all of you for all of it with its recompense: for the one among you who does good and follows My command and obedience, with good; and for the one among you who does evil and opposes My command and My prohibition, with evil. The meaning of His words "a witness (shahid)" is one who bears witness to that. [[See the explanation of "al-shahid" (the witness) above: 1: 376-378 / 3: 97, 145 / 6: 60, 75 / 7: 243.]]

**The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿Men are the protectors and maintainers of women, because Allah has made some of them to excel others, and because they spend of their property﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His majesty be praised, [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "by that, may His majesty be praised," but the context requires what has been adopted here.]] "Men are the protectors and maintainers of women," means: men are those who stand over their wives, disciplining them and restraining them from what is obligatory upon them toward Allah and toward themselves. "Because Allah has made some of them to excel others" means: because of what Allah has made men to excel their wives in: their giving them dowries, their spending their property on them, and their providing for their needs. That is Allah's favouring of them over the women, and for this reason they became maintainers over them, with their command enforced over them in those matters of theirs that Allah has placed in their hands.

* *

Those who engaged in ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

9300 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "Men are the protectors and maintainers of women," meaning: they are commanders over them. It is incumbent upon her to obey him in what Allah has commanded her of obedience to Him, and her obedience is that she be good to his family and guard his property. And He favoured him over her by his expenditure and his effort.

9301 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "Men are the protectors and maintainers of women because Allah has made some of them to excel others," he said: The man is a maintainer over the woman; he commands her to obey Allah. If she refuses, he has the right to strike her with a non-severe blow, and he has over her the superiority of his expenditure and his effort.

9302 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi regarding "Men are the protectors and maintainers of women": he said: They take hold of their hands and discipline them. [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "and they discipline them," which is an error by the copyist. In the margin of the manuscript is the letter "ṭ," indicating an error, or it was as such in the original from which he copied, also an error.]]

9303 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Hibban ibn Musa related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: I heard Sufyan say regarding "because Allah has made some of them to excel others": by Allah's making men to excel women.

* *

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a man who slapped his wife, so the matter was brought before the Prophet (ﷺ), and he ruled in her favour for retaliation.

The report regarding that:

9304 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, who said: al-Hasan related to us: that a man slapped his wife, so she came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he wanted to have retaliation against him for her. Then Allah revealed: "Men are the protectors and maintainers of women because Allah has made some of them to excel others, and because they spend of their property." So the Prophet (ﷺ) summoned him and recited it to him, and said: "You intended a matter, and Allah intended other than it."

9305 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada regarding His words: "Men are the protectors and maintainers of women because Allah has made some of them to excel others and because they spend of their property," he mentioned to us that a man slapped his wife, so she came to the Prophet (ﷺ), then he mentioned something similar.

9306 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada regarding His words: "Men are the protectors and maintainers of women," he said: A man struck his wife, so she came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he wanted to have retaliation from him for her. Then Allah revealed: "Men are the protectors and maintainers of women."

9307 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Jarir ibn Hazim, from al-Hasan: that a man from the Ansar slapped his wife, so she came seeking retaliation, and the Prophet (ﷺ) made retaliation between them. Then there was revealed: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you﴾ [Surah Ta-Ha: 114], and there was revealed: "Men are the protectors and maintainers of women because Allah has made some of them to excel others." [["Surah Ta-Ha" is unanimously a Meccan surah, so al-Hasan's saying that it was revealed concerning the Ansari woman, which took place in Madina, is undoubtedly a matter open to question.]]

9308 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: A man struck his wife, so the Prophet (ﷺ) wanted retaliation. While they were in that state, the verse was revealed.

9309 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: as for "Men are the protectors and maintainers of women": a man from the Ansar had a dispute with his wife, and he struck her, so her family set out and mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he informed them: "Men are the protectors and maintainers of women," to the end of the verse.

* *

al-Zuhri used to say: There is no retaliation between a man and his wife in matters short of death.

9310 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: I heard al-Zuhri say: If a man wounds his wife in the head or injures her, there is no qawad (retaliation) against him in that, but he must pay the 'aql (blood-money), unless he transgresses against her and kills her, in which case he is killed for her. [["Al-qawad": retaliation. "Al-'aql": the blood-money and what is similar to it.
Moreover, it is sufficient for a Muslim man to preserve from the authentic hadith of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and what al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated: "Does one of you strike his wife and then lie with her at the end of the day?" and what Ibn Majah narrated: "The best of you are the best to their women."]]

* *

As for His words: "and because they spend of their property," it means: and because of the dowries they gave them and the maintenance they spent on them, as follows:

9311 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: He favoured him over her by his expenditure and his effort.

9312 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Abu Zuhayr related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, the like of it.

9313 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Hibban ibn Musa related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: I heard Sufyan say: "and because they spend of their property": because of the dowries they gave.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: So the meaning of the statement is: Men are the protectors and maintainers of their women, by Allah's favouring them over them, and by their spending on them from their property.

* *

The "ma" in His words "because Allah has made some to excel" and in His words "and because they spent" is in the sense of a verbal noun (masdar).

* *

The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿So righteous women are obedient, guarding in secret what Allah has guarded﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His majesty be praised, "righteous women," he means those upright in religion, doers of good, [[See the explanation of "al-salih" (righteous) earlier: 3:91 / 6:380 / 7:130.]] as follows:

9314 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Hibban ibn Musa related to us, saying: 'Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak related to us, saying: I heard Sufyan say: "righteous women," they act with goodness.

* *

As for His words "qanitat" (obedient), it means: obedient to Allah and to their husbands, as follows:

9315 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "qanitat," he said: obedient.

9316 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "qanitat," he said: obedient.

9317 - Al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it. [[The report 9317: I have added this report from the manuscript, and the printed edition omitted it. It was rightly omitted, since it repeats what precedes it without meaning. But I have kept it here, lest the copyist's eye have passed over, and he wrote the isnad again as it is, so that there might be a difference in the isnad that his eye missed.]]

9318 - 'Ali ibn Dawud related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas: "qanitat," obedient.

9319 - Al-Hasan ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: "qanitat," that is: obedient to Allah and to their husbands.

9320 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada who said: "obedient."

9321 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "al-qanitat," the obedient.

9322 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Hibban ibn Musa related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: I heard Sufyan say regarding His words "qanitat," he said: obedient to their husbands.

We have already explained the meaning of "al-qunut" earlier, that it is obedience, and we have shown the correctness of that from evidences sufficient to dispense with repeating it. [[See what has passed: 2:538, 539 / 5:228–237 / 6:264, 401.]]

* *

As for His words "guarding in secret," it means: guarding themselves in the absence of their husbands from them, in their private parts and their husbands' property, and what is obligatory upon them of Allah's right in that and other matters, as follows:

9323 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada: "guarding in secret," he says: guarding what Allah has entrusted them with of His right, and guarding the unseen of their husbands.

9324 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "guarding in secret what Allah has guarded," he says: she guards her husband's property and her private part for him until he returns, as Allah has commanded her.

9325 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj who said: I asked 'Ata' about His words "guarding in secret," he said: guarding for the husband.

9326 - Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida related to me, saying: Hajjaj related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: I asked 'Ata' about "guarding in secret," and he said: guarding for the husbands.

9327 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Hibban ibn Musa related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: I heard Sufyan say: "guarding in secret," guarding for their husbands what is absent of their affairs.

9328 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Abu Ma'shar related to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi related to us, from Abu Hurayra who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The best of women is the woman who, when you look at her, pleases you; when you command her, she obeys you; and when you are absent from her, she guards you in herself and your property." He said: Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited: "Men are the protectors and maintainers of women," to the end of the verse. [[Report 9328: In the printed and manuscript editions: "Sa'id from Abu Sa'id al-Maqburi," which is an evident error, as will become clear to you from its takhrij (sourcing). Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it in his Musnad: 306, from the hadith of Abu Ma'shar, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi. Ibn Kathir mentioned in his tafsir 2:436 that Ibn Abi Hatim "narrated it from Yunus ibn Habib, from Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Dhi'b, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, the same." If that is so, then Ibn Abi Hatim erred in his narration from Abu Dawud; what is established in his Musnad is that it is from his hadith from Abu Ma'shar, and perhaps this is a mistake, for the reports immediately preceding it were narrated by Abu Dawud through the route of Ibn Abi Dhi'b from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi.
This report al-Suyuti attributed in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:151 to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan. What I found in al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim 2:161, through the route of Ibn 'Ajlan, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayra, with its meaning but not this wording, abridged, and he said: "Sahih according to the condition of Muslim, though they did not narrate it." I did not know its place in the Sunan of al-Bayhaqi.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This report from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) indicates the correctness of what we have said in interpreting this, and that its meaning is: righteous in their religion, obedient to their husbands, guarding them in their persons and their property.

* *

As for His words "what Allah has guarded," the readers differed regarding its recitation.

The majority of readers in all the regions of Islam recited: ﴿bima hafiza Allah﴾ with the subject "Allah" in the nominative, meaning: by Allah's guarding of them, since He made them so, as follows:

9329 - Zakariyya ibn Yahya ibn Abi Za'ida related to me, saying: Hajjaj related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: I asked 'Ata' about His words "what Allah has guarded," he said: He says: Allah has guarded them.

9330 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Hibban ibn Musa related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: I heard Sufyan say regarding His words "what Allah has guarded," he said: by Allah's guarding of her, that He made her so.

* *

Abu Ja'far Yazid ibn al-Qa'qa' al-Madani recited that: ﴿bima hafiza Allah﴾ [["Abu Ja'far: Yazid ibn al-Qa'qa' al-Madani al-Makhzumi," a freedman of 'Abdullah ibn 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'a al-Makhzumi, one of the ten readers, a famous Successor of great standing. He was brought to Umm Salama, mother of the believers, when he was young, and she wiped his head and prayed for blessing for him, and he prayed behind Ibn 'Umar. He was the leading authority of the people of Madina in recitation, and was called "al-Qari'" (the reciter). Ibn Ma'in said: "He was trustworthy, few in hadith." Tabaqat al-Qurra' 2:382–384.]] meaning: by their guarding Allah in His obedience and in the discharge of His right, by what He commanded them of guarding the unseen of their husbands, like a man saying to another: "You did not guard Allah in such and such," meaning: you did not watch over Him nor fear Him. [[In the manuscript: "you did not watch over him nor fear him," and in the printed edition: "you did not watch over him nor take note of him." The correct reading of the manuscript is what has been adopted, with the addition of "ma" before "raqabtahu," and his saying "wa la khiftahu" (nor did you fear him) is from fear.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in this matter is what the recitation of the Muslims has brought, in a manner that cuts off the excuse of whoever it reaches and establishes his proof against him, apart from what Abu Ja'far alone reported, which deviates from them. That recitation raises the subject "Allah," blessed and exalted: ﴿bima hafiza Allah﴾, along with the soundness of that in Arabic and the speech of the Arabs; and its raising to the accusative is ugly in Arabic, as it departs from the known usage of Arab speech.

That is because the Arabs do not omit the agent with the verbal nouns, since when the agent is omitted with them there is no known doer for the verb.

* *

Within the speech there is an omitted element, which the apparent meaning of the speech makes unnecessary to mention, and its meaning is: "So righteous women are obedient, guarding in secret by what Allah has guarded; so be good to them and set things right."

* *

Likewise it is so in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud.

9331 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad related to us, saying: 'Isa al-A'mash related to us, from Talha ibn Musarrif who said: In the recitation of 'Abdullah: ﴿So righteous women are obedient, guarding in secret, by what Allah has guarded; so be good to them, and those whose disobedience you fear﴾.

9332 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿So righteous women are obedient, guarding in secret by what Allah has guarded﴾, so be good to them.

9333 - 'Ali ibn Dawud related to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "So righteous women are obedient, guarding in secret by what Allah has guarded," so set things right with them.

9334 - 'Ali ibn Dawud related to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "So righteous women are obedient, guarding in secret by what Allah has guarded," meaning: when they are like this, then set things right with them.

* *

The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿And those whose disobedience you fear, admonish them﴾ [[The words "admonish them" are not mentioned in the manuscript or the printed edition, although he explained them afterward, and did not treat them separately from this place.]]

The people of ta'wil differed regarding the meaning of His words: "and those whose disobedience you fear."

Some of them said: its meaning is: "and those whose disobedience you know." The turning of "fear" in this place to "knowledge," in the view of these people, is like the turning of "zann" (supposition) to "knowledge," because the two meanings are close, since "zann" is doubt, and "fear" is connected with hope, and both are acts of a person's heart [[See the explanation of "fear" earlier: 3:550, 551.]], as the poet said: [[He is Abu Mahjan al-Thaqafi.]]

"Do not bury me in the wilderness, for I fear, when I die, that I will not taste it."

[[This verse has been cited and its takhrij given earlier at 3:551, and I add here: Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:146, 265, with a slight difference in the transmission; and I had forgotten there to refer it to this place, so I attach it in its place there.]]

Its meaning: "for I know," and as the other poet said: [[He is Abu al-Ghawl al-Tahawi.]]

"A speech came to me from Nusayb, saying it, and I did not fear, O Salam, that you would blame me."

[[Its takhrij and explanation have been given earlier at 3:550, and I add here Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:146, 265. In the printed edition here it was "annaka 'aibi," which is a corrupt error; in the manuscript it is unpointed.]]

Meaning: "and I did not suppose."

* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 34 (part 2 of 6):

A group of the people of ta'wil (interpretation) said: The meaning of "fear" (al-khawf) in this context is the fear that is the opposite of "hope" (al-raja'). They said: The meaning of that is: when you see from them what you fear will be nushuz (defiance) toward you, such as looking at what it is not proper for them to look at, and entering and leaving, and you suspect them regarding their affairs, then admonish them and forsake them. Among those who said this was Muhammad ibn Ka'b. [[The report of Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi will come, under no. 9342.]]
* *
As for His saying "nushuzahunna" (their defiance), it means: their exalting themselves over their husbands, their raising themselves above their marital beds through disobedience on their part, and opposing them in what it is incumbent upon them to obey them in, out of hatred and aversion toward them.
* *
The root of "nushuz" is elevation (irtifa'). From it comes the saying of an elevated place on the ground: "nashz" and "nashaz". [[See the explanation of "nushuz" and "nashz" in what has passed, 5: 475, 476.]]
"Fa-'izuhunna" (then admonish them): he says: remind them of God, and warn them of His threat, regarding their committing what God has forbidden to them of disobedience to their husbands in what He has made obligatory upon them to obey them in. [[See the explanation of "wa'z" (admonition) in what has passed, 2: 180, 181 / 6: 14 / 7: 233.]]
* *
The people of ta'wil have said in agreement with what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that "nushuz" is hatred and disobedience to the husband:
9335 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "wa-allati takhafuna nushuzahunna" (and those from whom you fear defiance): he said: their hatred.
9336 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying "wa-allati takhafuna nushuzahunna": she whose disobedience you fear. He said: "nushuz" is her disobedience and opposition.
9337 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying "wa-allati takhafuna nushuzahunna": that woman defies, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "qila al-mar'a tanshuz" (it is said the woman defies), which is extremely corrupt wording; the correct reading is from al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 154, 155, and al-Sunan al-Kubra 7: 303.]] and makes light of her husband's right and does not obey his command. [[The report 9337: al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan 7: 303, through the route of Uthman ibn Sa'id, from Abdullah ibn Salih, similar to it at length; al-Tabari will narrate part of it under no. 9339 and then no. 9356.]]
9338 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Rawh narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, saying: 'Ata' said: "nushuz" is that she loves to be separated from him, and the man likewise.
* *
Mention of the transmission from those who said as we have said regarding His saying "fa-'izuhunna".
9339 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas: "fa-'izuhunna", meaning: admonish them with the Book of God. He said: God commanded that if she defies, he should admonish her and remind her of God, and magnify his right over her. [[The report 9339: Sunan al-Bayhaqi 3: 303; see the commentary on report 9337.]]
9340 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "wa-allati takhafuna nushuzahunna fa-'izuhunna", he said: when a woman defies her husband's bed, he says to her: "Fear God and return to your bed!" If she obeys him, then he has no path over her.
9341 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan who said: If a woman defies her husband, let him admonish her with his tongue. That is, he commands her to fear God and obey Him.
9342 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ubayda, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi who said: If the man sees a lightness in her gaze, [[In the printed edition: "idha ra'a al-rajul taqsiraha fi haqqihi" (when the man sees her neglecting his right), with a note saying: "In some copies: idha ra'a al-rajul khiffatan fi basariha, wa fi mudkhalaha wa mukhrajaha" (when the man sees lightness in her gaze, and in her entering and leaving). What is in some copies is what is in our manuscript, with "fi" before "wa fi mudkhalaha" removed; this is the pure correct reading, and what is in the printed edition is without doubt a corrupt alteration by a copyist. Abu Ja'far mentioned this just before, p. 299, line 5: "If you see from them what you fear they will defy, of looking at what it is not proper for them to look at," and attributed it to Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi; this is the meaning of "khiffa fi basariha" (lightness in her gaze), i.e., she casts her eye toward other men.]] and her entering and leaving. He said: he says to her with his tongue: "I have seen from you such and such, so desist!" If she makes amends, then he has no path over her. If she refuses, he forsakes her bed. [[The report 9342: its end will come under no. 9364. The words "wa mudkhalaha wa mukhrajaha" are in the accusative, coordinated with "khiffa", and are the object of "ra'a". "A'tabat" is from your saying "a'tabani fulan", when he abandons what you were displeased with on his account and returns to what pleases you, after his anger at you over it.]]
9343 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hibban ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, saying: Shibl informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying "fa-'izuhunna": he said: when a woman defies her husband's bed, he says to her: "Fear God and return!"
9344 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Israil, from Jabir, from 'Ata' regarding "fa-'izuhunna": he said: with speech.
9345 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj regarding His saying "fa-'izuhunna": he said: with tongues.
9346 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Amr ibn Abi Qays, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding "fa-'izuhunna": he said: admonish them with the tongue. [[The report 9346: "Amr ibn Abi Qays al-Razi", whose biography has passed under no. 8611.]]
* *
On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And forsake them in the beds﴾
Abu Ja'far said: The people of ta'wil differed regarding the interpretation of that.
Some of them said: The meaning of that is: admonish them regarding their defiance toward you, O husbands; then if they refuse to return to the truth in that and to what is owed to you by them, forsake them by abstaining from intercourse with them when you lie with them.
Mention of those who said that:
9347 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying "fa-'izuhunna wa-hjuruhunna fi al-madaji'": he means: admonish them; if they obey you, then well; otherwise forsake them.
9348 - Muhammad ibn Mas'ad narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "wa-hjuruhunna fi al-madaji'", meaning by forsaking: that the man and his wife are on one bed, and he does not have intercourse with her.
9349 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: al-hajr is the forsaking of intercourse.
9350 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: as for "takhafuna nushuzahunna", his husband should admonish her, and if she does not accept, he should forsake her in the bed. That is, he lies beside her, turns his back to her, and has intercourse with her without speaking to her. [[The phrase "hakadha fi kitabi" (thus it is in my book) is from the words of Abu Ja'far al-Tabari; this is extreme precision and entire trustworthiness, together with fear of corrupting the meaning in several ways; yet he recorded it as he found it in his book, fearing that he might have meant that forsaking is forsaking speech alone and not forsaking intercourse, though the stronger view is otherwise; otherwise he would have appended it to the following statement and mentioned it with the reports that have that meaning there.]]
9351 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding His saying "wa-hjuruhunna fi al-madaji'": he said: he lies with her, forsakes her speech, and turns his back to her.

Abu Ja'far said: The word "al-hajr" has no meaning in the speech of the Arabs except in one of three aspects.
The first: "a man forsook another man's speech and talk," meaning he abandoned and left it. From it one says: "hajara fulan ahlahu yahjuruha hajran wa-hijranan" (so-and-so forsook his wife).
The second: excessive speech with repetition in the manner of the speech of one who mocks, one says: "hajara fulan fi kalamihi yahjuru hajran," when he raves and drags out the word, "wa-ma zalat tilka hijjiraahu wa-ihjiraahu" (and that remained his habit), and from it is the saying of Dhu al-Rumma:
He shot and missed, while destinies are dominant,
so they scattered, and woe and war were his habit.
The third: "hajara al-ba'ir" (the camel was tied), when its owner tied it with the "hijar", which is a rope tied at its flanks and its foreleg. From it is the saying of Imru' al-Qays:
She saw a chasm at the edge of the ghabit, and nearly cut that hijar.
As for the speech in which there is harshness and harm, it is "al-ihjar", and from it one says: "ahjara fulan fi mantiqihi" (so-and-so spoke obscenely) when he says "al-hujr", which is foul speech: "yuhjiru ihjaran wa-hujran."
* *

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 34 (part 3 of 6):

Since "al-hajr" (هَجْر, pronounced with a fatha on the ha and a sukun on the jim) in speech can only mean one of the three meanings [[Meaning: "al-hajr" with a fatha on the ha and a sukun on the jim.]], and since the woman whose nushuz (nushuz: a wife's open defiance or disobedience toward her husband) is feared is only admonished by her husband so that she will return to obedience to him in what is required of her, namely that she come to him when he calls her to his bed, then it is impermissible that his admonition should be for that purpose until the woman returns to the command of God and to the obedience of her husband in this matter, and then the husband be commanded to forsake her in the very matter for which he admonished her.

Since this is so, the view of those who said, "The meaning of His words, 'and forsake them in the beds, and forsake their intercourse,'" is invalid.

Or, since this meaning is invalid, it could mean: "and forsake their speech, on account of their forsaking your beds." This also has no intelligible basis. For God, may He be remembered, has informed through the tongue of His Prophet ﷺ that it is not lawful for a Muslim to forsake his brother for more than three days [[This is from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, narrated by al-Bukhari (al-Fath 10:413): "From Anas ibn Malik: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: 'Do not hate one another, do not envy one another, do not turn away from one another, and be servants of God as brothers. It is not lawful for a Muslim man to forsake his brother for more than three days.'"

And the hadith of Abu Ayyub al-Ansari: "It is not lawful for a man to forsake his brother for more than three days; when they meet, one turns away and the other turns away, and the best of them is the one who begins with the greeting of peace" (al-Fath 10:413).]]. Moreover, even if that were lawful, forsaking her in speech would have no intelligible meaning. For if she has turned away from him and is defiant toward him, then part of her gladness is that he not speak to her, not see her, and she not see him. So how is a man commanded, in a state where his wife hates him and turns away from him, to abandon what would give her gladness by abandoning her intercourse and conversation and speaking with her? [[In the printed edition: "mujadhabatuha" (her pulling away); I chose to read it as I have given, since it is undotted in the manuscript.]] Yet he is commanded to strike her so that she will desist from what she is doing in abandoning his obedience when he calls her to his bed, and from other things that require her obedience. [[This argument is very good when one considers only one form of nushuz and one cause, which is what Abu Ja'far mentioned. But nushuz has many forms, and its causes differ. This verse is a general instruction that the Muslim man acts upon when he needs it, whether he fears nushuz or knows it and its causes. You will see that Abu Ja'far dropped all the other views in order to lead to his own interpretation, and we will mention Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi's response to it in a note that will come at the end of Abu Ja'far's discussion.]]

Or, since these two interpretations are corrupt, its meaning is: "and forsake them in your speech to them," meaning: repeat your words to them when you speak to them, in a harsh manner. [[The repetition of "yakun" here in this context is good Arabic.]] If this is its meaning, then there is no basis for governing the pronoun of the defiant women's names, i.e., the "ha" and "nun" in His words "wa-hjuruhunna" (and forsake them) by the verb. For if that meaning is intended, the verb would not be transitive. One says, "Fulan forsook (hajara) in his speech," but one does not say, "Fulan forsook Fulan."

Since all these meanings contain the defects we have mentioned, the most correct of the views concerning this is that His words "wa-hjuruhunna" be directed toward the meaning of tying with a halter (hijar), in accordance with what we have mentioned from the Arab saying about a camel when its owner ties it with a rope, as we have described: "He halted it (hajarahu), so he halts it (yahjuruhu) with hajr."

* *

If that is its meaning, then the interpretation of the statement is: "As for those whose nushuz you fear, admonish them concerning their nushuz against you. If they heed the admonition, then there is no way for you against them. And if they refuse to return from their nushuz, then secure them with a rope in their beds," meaning: in their dwellings and houses, where they lie down and where they lie with their husbands, as:

9372 - Abbas ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, from Shibl, who said: I heard Abu Qaza'a relate, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Hakim ibn Mu'awiya, from his father: that he came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "What is the right of the wife of one of us over him?" He said: "Feed her, clothe her, do not strike the face, do not disfigure her, and do not forsake her except in the house." [[Hadith 9372: Abbas ibn Abi Talib is "Abbas ibn Ja'far ibn Abdullah"; his biography has passed at 880. Shibl is Ibn Abbad al-Makki, the reciter, who has passed at 280.

Abu Qaza'a (with a fatha on the qaf, zay, and ayn) is Suwayd ibn Juhayr ibn Bayan; his biography has passed at 8281 and 8283.

His words here, "yuhaddithu 'an Amr ibn Dinar" (he relates from Amr ibn Dinar): in my view the likely reading is that the "an" (from) is a scribal error of addition, and the correct reading is "yuhaddithu Amr ibn Dinar" (he relates to Amr ibn Dinar), meaning that Shibl ibn Abbad heard the hadith from Abu Qaza'a while Abu Qaza'a was relating it to Amr ibn Dinar. For the hadith is known from Abu Qaza'a from Hakim ibn Mu'awiya directly, with no intermediary. Abu Qaza'a and Amr ibn Dinar belong to the same generation, so one may relate from the other. But what actually occurred here, in my view, is that the hadith is from Abu Qaza'a directly from Hakim.

Then I became certain that what I had inferred is correct. This hadith is a portion of a longer hadith narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 4:446-447 (Halabi edition), from Abdullah ibn al-Harith, and from Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr, both from Shibl ibn Abbad, who said: "I heard Abu Qaza'a relate to Amr ibn Dinar, relating from Hakim ibn Mu'awiya al-Bahzi..." to the end. The printed edition of the Musnad has "yuhaddithu 'an Amr ibn Dinar" with an added "an," as in the copy of al-Tabari here. But the Riyad manuscript of the Musnad (vol. 3, p. 1074) confirms the correct reading I have mentioned, with the word "an" omitted. This is the correct reading, God willing.

Hakim ibn Mu'awiya ibn Haydah al-Qushayri: his biography and that of his father has passed at 873.

The full takhrij (sourcing) of this hadith will come in the third narration: 9374.]]

9373 - al-Hasan ibn Arafa narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Shu'ba ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Qaza'a, from Hakim ibn Mu'awiya, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ, similarly. [[Hadith 9373: al-Hasan ibn Arafa al-Abdi al-Baghdadi, the teacher of al-Tabari, is trustworthy. He is in the Tahdhib, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/31-32, and Tarikh Baghdad 7:394-396. He died in 257 AH, having passed 110 years.

The hadith was narrated by Ahmad 4:447 (Halabi), from Yazid ibn Harun, from Shu'ba, with this chain.]]

9374 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hibban ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, saying: Bahz ibn Hakim informed us, from his grandfather, who said: "I said: 'O Messenger of God, our women, what of them may we approach, and what may we leave?' He said: 'Your tilth. So go to your tilth however you wish, except that you do not strike the face, do not disfigure, do not forsake except in the house. Feed when you eat, clothe when you clothe yourself. How can it be, when some of you have gone in to others?'" except for what is lawful upon them. [[Hadith 9374: Hibban (with a kasra on the ha) ibn Musa ibn Sawwar al-Sulami is trustworthy, one of the teachers of al-Bukhari and Muslim. He is in the Tahdhib, al-Kabir 2/1/84, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/271.

This hadith is a longer repetition of the two hadiths before it. It has also come with sound chains more extensively than this. It was related from Hakim ibn Mu'awiya by his two sons, Bahz and Sa'id, and others. Ahmad related it in al-Musnad, in both longer and shorter forms, 4:446, 447, many times, and 5:3, 5 (Halabi).

Abu Dawud related it: 2142-2144.

Ibn Majah related it: 1850, by way of Yazid ibn Harun, like the narration before this one.

al-Bayhaqi related it 7:295, 305, in longer and shorter forms. al-Mundhiri said, in Tahdhib al-Sunan 2057: "The imams differed about relying on this copy, some relied on it, and some refused. al-Tirmidhi extracted part of it and authenticated it." He means the copy of "Bahz ibn Hakim from his father from his grandfather." The truth is that it is sound if the chain to Bahz is sound. Ibn Kathir mentioned it, 2:437, in abbreviated form without a chain, and attributed it to the Sunan and the Musnad.

His words "illa bima halla 'alayha" (except for what is lawful upon her): in the Musnad (5:5) it reads "illa bima halla 'alayhinna" (except for what is lawful upon them), meaning: except for the striking that God has made lawful for you when you fear their nushuz. This is what God specified in this noble verse: "And those [wives] from whom you fear nushuz, admonish them, forsake them in the beds, and strike them." And one does not exceed in this the limit God has permitted: "And if they obey you, then seek no way against them" (4:34).]]

Scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said similarly to what we have said about its interpretation.

Mention of those who said that:

9375 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from al-Hasan, who said: "If a woman shows nushuz toward her husband, let him admonish her with his tongue. If she accepts, that is well. Otherwise, let him strike her with a striking that is not severe. If she returns, that is well. Otherwise, it becomes lawful for him to take from her and let her go."

9376 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His words, "and forsake them in the beds and strike them," he said: He does that with her, and strikes her until she obeys him in the beds. When she obeys him in the bed, he has no way against her when he lies with her.

9377 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hibban narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Bishr informed us, that he heard Ikrimah say concerning His words, "and forsake them in the beds and strike them," a striking that is not severe, he said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said: "Strike them when they disobey you in what is right, a striking that is not severe." [[Report 9377: The report that Ikrimah related, which al-Tabari relies on later, is a mursal report (one where a Successor skips the companion in the chain). al-Suyuti extracted it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:155, and attributed it to no one other than Ibn Jarir.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: All of those whose views we have mentioned did not assign to "forsaking" any meaning other than striking, and they did not assign forsaking (hajr) to be a condition among the conditions in which the struck woman is when she is struck, [[He means by his words, "since it is a condition among the conditions...," that the struck woman is only struck because she has forsaken her husband's bed. So forsaking is one of the states she is in when she is struck.]] together with the indication of the report that Ikrimah related from the Prophet ﷺ, that he commanded striking them when they disobey their husbands in what is right, without his commanding the husbands to forsake them, [[The context is: "and they did not assign forsaking... for the reason we described." The reason why they did not assign forsaking is separated from it by the phrase.]] for the reason we have described.

Abu Ja'far said: If someone supposes that what we have said about the interpretation of the report from the Prophet ﷺ that Ikrimah related is not as we have said, and that it is correct that the Prophet ﷺ's leaving off commanding a man to forsake his wife when she disobeys him in what is right, and commanding him to strike her before forsaking, would be evidence for the correctness of what we have said, that the meaning of "hajr" is what we have explained, then it would follow that there is no purpose in God's command to her husband to admonish her when she shows nushuz, since there is no mention of admonition in Ikrimah's report from the Prophet ﷺ.

= [[His words "for the matter in that regard..." are the answer to his statement at the start of the previous paragraph, "If someone supposes," and this second part is made a separate paragraph because it is like an answer, and so that the meanings of the speech are not confused.]] The matter in this is contrary to what he supposed. For the Prophet ﷺ's words, "when they disobey you in what is right," are clear evidence that he did not permit the man to strike his wife except after admonishing her about her nushuz. For she cannot be disobedient to him unless an order or admonition in what is right, according to what God has commanded, has previously come from him to her. [[Al-Tabari's interpretation at this point of the meaning of "hajr," that it is binding with a halter, and the securing of them with a rope in their dwellings and houses where they lie down and lie with their husbands, is an extremely strange interpretation, one in which he stood apart from every interpretation the earlier scholars gave. Later scholars have criticized it, and among the best of those who said something about it is Abu Bakr ibn al-Arabi in his book Ahkam al-Qur'an 1:175. He said: "What a slip from a scholar of the Qur'an and the Sunnah!! I am truly surprised at this: what emboldened him to this interpretation, without wanting to state plainly that he took it from it, is a strange hadith that Ibn Wahb related from Malik: that Asma bint Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, the wife of al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam..." Then he mentioned the story of al-Zubayr striking Asma and her co-wife, and that he tied the hair of one to the other, and Asma's complaint to Abu Bakr, and Abu Bakr's advice to her to be patient, because al-Zubayr was a righteous man, and perhaps he would be her husband in Paradise = Then Ibn al-Arabi said: "So he saw binding and tying, given the possible sense of the word, together with al-Zubayr's act, and so he went forward with this interpretation on that basis. How strange it is that, despite his mastery of the sciences and of the Arabic language, the correct statement was far from him, and he swerved from sound reasoning!!"

Abu Bakr's extraction of al-Tabari's intention, when he mentioned the report that emboldened him to this interpretation, does not please me. Had al-Tabari intended it, he would have mentioned it as is his custom. But I suspect that Abu Ja'far became entangled in this interpretation because of the reasons he advanced after his discussion of the meaning of "hajr," and that if the speech had been "fa-hjuruhunna fi al-madaji" (so forsake them in the beds) without God having said before it "fa-'izuhunna" (so admonish them), Abu Ja'far would not have needed this interpretation. Thus what led him to this interpretation is the sequence of the two statements, "admonish them" and "forsake them in the beds." Furthermore, he also found no way to combine the meaning of "nushuz" with the meaning of "hajr," as I said on page 308, note 4. A full discussion of this belongs in another place.]]

* *

The discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿And strike them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Admonish them, O men, concerning their nushuz. If they refuse to return to what is incumbent upon them toward you, then secure them with a rope in their dwellings, and strike them so that they return to what is obligatory upon them of obedience to God in what they owe you of your rights.

* *

The people of interpretation said: The manner of striking which God permitted to a husband of a defiant wife is the striking that is not severe (ghayr al-mubarrih).

Mention of those who said that:

9378 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "And strike them," he said: a striking that is not severe.

9379 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Abu Hamza informed us, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the same.

9380 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughira, from al-Sha'bi, who said: The striking is not severe. [[In the printed edition: "ghayr al-mubarrih" (with the definite article); I have adopted the reading of the manuscript.]]

9381 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hibban ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, saying: Shurayk informed us, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: "And strike them," he said: a striking that is not severe.

9382 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas: "And forsake them in the beds and strike them," he said: You forsake her in the bed. If she comes back, well; otherwise God has permitted you to strike her with a striking that is not severe, and not to break any bone of hers. If she comes back, well; otherwise, the ransom (fidya) from her becomes lawful for you.

9383 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan and Qatada, concerning His words, "and strike them," he said: a striking that is not severe.

9384 - And with the same chain: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: I said to Ata: "And strike them?" He said: a striking that is not severe.

9385 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "And forsake them in the beds and strike them," he said: You forsake her in the bed. If she refuses you, then strike her with a striking that is not severe, meaning: not disfiguring.

9386 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Uyayna narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata, who said: I said to Ibn Abbas: "What is the striking that is not severe?" He said: The siwak (tooth-stick) and the like, with which he strikes her.

9387 - Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us, saying: Ibn Uyayna narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata, who said: I said to Ibn Abbas: "What is the striking that is not severe?" He said: With the siwak and the like.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 34 (part 4 of 6):

9388 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Hibban ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said in his sermon: "a beating that does not leave a mark" (ḍarban ghayra mubarrih). He said: [It is] the miswak and the like. [[Meaning his sermon (ﷺ) during the Farewell Pilgrimage, and this has passed under no. 8905, so refer to the takhrij there.]]

9389 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not forsake women except in the bed, and beat them a beating that does not leave a mark" = he means: one that does not leave an effect.

9390 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Israil, from Jabir, from Ata: "And beat them," he said: a beating that does not leave a mark.

9391 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Hibban narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Yahya ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Ikrimah, the like of it.

9392 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And beat them," he said: If she responds to the forsaking, [then well]; otherwise he beats her a beating that does not leave a mark.

9393 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Musa ibn Ubaydah, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b, who said: Forsake her bed as long as you see that she will desist. ["Tanza'" means: she gives up her disobedience (nushuz) and abandons it.] If she does not desist, he beats her a beating that does not leave a mark.

9394 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan: "And beat them," he said: a beating that does not leave a mark.

9395 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Hibban narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id informed us, from a man, from al-Hasan, who said: a beating that does not leave a mark, one that leaves no effect.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Then if they obey you, do not seek a way against them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: If your women, O people, whose rebellion you fear, obey you when you admonish them, then do not forsake them in the beds. But if they do not obey you, then forsake them in the beds and beat them. If they then return to obedience to you at that point and turn back to what is obligatory upon them, then do not seek a path to harming them or to what they dislike, and do not seek a way to what is not lawful for you of their bodies and their property through pretexts. That is, one of you says to one of them, while she is obedient to him: "You do not love me, and you hate me," and so he beats her for that or harms her. So God, exalted be He, said to the men: "If they obey you," meaning: despite their hatred for you, then do not wrong them, and do not burden them with your love, for that is not in their hands, so that you beat them or harm them over it.

* *

The meaning of His saying: "then do not seek" (fa-la tabghu) means: do not search for or pursue, from the saying of the speaker: "baghaytu al-dalla" (I sought the lost animal), when you seek it [[See the explanation of "bagha" above, 3: 508 / 4: 163 / 6: 196, 564, 570 / 7: 53.]], and from it is the poet's saying describing death: [[He is Suhaym, slave of the Banu al-Hasḥas.]]

"It sought you, and you did not seek it, until you found it, as if you had promised it a rendezvous yesterday"
[[The line has passed, with its takhrij and explanation, above: 4: 163 / 7: 53.]]
Meaning: your seeking, and what you seek.

* *

And in accordance with what we have said on this, the people of interpretation have said.

Those who said that:

9396 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning His saying: "Then if they obey you, do not seek a way against them": he said: If she obeys you, do not burden her with pretexts.

9397 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Ubayd Allah, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn Abbas, who said: If she obeys him, he has no way against her when he lies with her.

9398 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, concerning His saying: "do not seek a way against them", he said: the pretexts.

9399 - And he said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri said, concerning His saying: "Then if they obey you": he said: If she comes to the bed while she hates him.

9400 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ya'la narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: If he does this, he does not oblige her to love him, for her heart is not in her hands.

9401 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: If she obeys him and lies with him, then God says: "Then if they obey you, do not seek a way against them."

9402 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "Then if they obey you, do not seek a way against them", he says: If she obeys you, do not seek to burden her with pretexts.

* *

On the interpretation of His exalted saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Exalted, Grand﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He says: Indeed, God is high above everything, so do not seek, O people, against your wives — if they obey you in what God has obligated them to you of right — a way to the exaltation of your hands over their hands, for God is higher than you and than everything, above you [[In the printed edition: "Indeed God is higher than you and than everything, and higher than you over them", while in the manuscript: "... , above them, you over them", and the editor wished to correct it and corrupted it; the correct reading is "above you, you over them", and his saying "above you" follows from the context of "indeed God is higher than you and than everything above you".]] and greater than you and than everything, and you are in His hand and grasp, so fear God lest you wrong them and seek a way against them. And they are obedient to you, so your Lord, who is higher than you and than everything, and greater than you and than everything, will take their part against you.

[[See the explanation of "al-'Ali" above: 5: 405.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And if you fear a breach between them, then send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family; if they both desire reconciliation, God will bring about harmony between them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted: "And if you fear a breach between them", meaning: if you know, O people [[See the explanation of "fear" in the sense of "know" above, p. 298, note 2, and the references there.]], "a breach between them", and that is the opposing of each of them to the other, which is one's doing what grieves the other of matters. As for the woman's part, it is rebellion and her abandoning the discharge of God's right upon her, which God obligated her to her husband. As for the husband's part, it is his abandoning keeping her in kindness or releasing her with goodness.

* *

And "al-shiqaq" is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "shaqqa fulanun fulanan" (so-and-so opposed so-and-so) = when each of them does to the other what grieves him of matters, so "he opposes him in opposition and breach (shiqaq)", and that may be enmity, [[See the explanation of "al-shiqaq" above: 3: 115, 116, 336.]] as:

9403 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His saying: "And if you fear a breach between them", he said: If he beats her and she refuses to return and opposes him = he means: she is hostile to him.

* *

"Al-shiqaq" is attributed to "al-bayn" because "al-bayn" may be a noun, as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, your bond has been severed﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 94], in the reading of one who read it so. [[This reading is with "baynakum" in the nominative, meaning: your connection that connected between you.]]

* *

As for His saying: "then send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family", the people of interpretation differed regarding those addressed by this verse: who is the one commanded to send the two arbiters?

Some of them said: The one commanded to do that is the ruler to whom the matter is referred.

Those who said that:

9404 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Ayyub narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: that he said concerning the woman who seeks khul': he admonishes her; if she desists, [well]; otherwise he forsakes her. If she desists, [well]; otherwise he beats her. If she desists, [well]; otherwise the matter is referred to the ruler, who sends an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from hers. The arbiter from her family says: "Let him do such-and-such to her," and the arbiter from his family says: "Let her do such-and-such to him." Whichever of them is the wrongdoer, the ruler restrains him and takes what is above his hands; and if she is rebellious, he orders her to seek khul'.

9405 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak: "And if you fear a breach between them, then send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family", he said: Rather, that is up to the ruler.

* *

Others said: Rather, the one commanded to do that is the husband and the wife.
