Those who said that:

9406 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And if you fear a breach between them, then send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family": if he beats her and she returns, then he has no way against her. But if she refuses to return and opposes him, then he sends an arbiter from his family, and she sends an arbiter from her family.

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed concerning what the two arbiters are sent for, what the two arbiters are permitted to judge between them, and how they are sent between them.

Some of them said: The spouses send them by delegating to them the task of looking into matters between them. The two have no right to act in their affair except what they have each delegated to them, or what each of them has delegated from what is in his or her hands, so they act by what the one delegating them from the man and the woman delegated them to, in what it is permissible to delegate them in, or the delegation of whoever among them was delegated in that.

Those who said that:

9407 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, from Ubaydah, who said: A man and his wife, between whom there was a breach, came to Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), with each of them a crowd of people. Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family. Then he said to the two arbiters: Do you know what is upon you? Upon you, if you see that you should unite them, that you unite them; and if you see that you should separate them, that you separate them. The woman said: I am content with the Book of God, with what is upon me in it and what is mine. The man said: As for separation, no. Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said: You have lied, by God; you will not turn back until you acknowledge what she has acknowledged. [[The report: 9407 - Al-Shafi'i narrated it in al-Umm 5: 177 through the route of Abd al-Wahhab ibn Abd al-Majid al-Thaqafi, from Ayyub ibn Abi Tamimah, the same exactly. Al-Bayhaqi also recorded it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 7: 305, 306. Al-Shafi'i said: "The hadith of Ali is established according to us."]]

9408 - Muhammad ibn Mujahid ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Hassan and Abd Allah ibn Awn narrated to us, from Muhammad: that a man and his wife came to Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), and with each of them was a crowd of people. Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) commanded them to send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family, to examine. When the two arbiters drew near to him, Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said to them: Do you know what is yours? For you, if you see that you should separate, you have separated; and if you see that you should unite, you have united. Hisham said in his narration: Then the woman said: I am content with the Book of God, for me and against me. The man said: As for separation, no! Ali said: You have lied, by God, until you are content with what she was content with. Ibn Awn said in his narration: You have lied, by God; you will not leave until you are content with what she was content with. [[The two reports: 9408, 9409 - Al-Bayhaqi recorded it in al-Sunan 7: 306, abridged.]]

9409 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mansur and Hisham informed us, from Ibn Sirin, from Ubaydah, who said: I witnessed Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), and he mentioned the like of it. [[The two reports: 9408, 9409 - Al-Bayhaqi recorded it in al-Sunan 7: 306, abridged.]]

9410 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: If he forsakes her in the bed and beats her, and she refuses to return and opposes him, then he sends an arbiter from his family and she sends an arbiter from her family. The woman says to her arbiter: "I have entrusted my affair to you; if you order me to return, I will return, and if you separate, we are separated," and she informs him of her matter, if she wants maintenance or dislikes something of the things, and orders him to remove that from her and return; or she informs him that she does not want divorce. And the man sends an arbiter from his family, entrusting him with his affair, and informs him of what he wants: whether he wants her or does not want to divorce her. If he wants her, he gives her what she asked and increases her maintenance; otherwise he says to him: "Take for me from her what she owes me, and divorce her." He entrusts him with his affair, and if he wills he divorces, and if he wills he keeps her. Then the two arbiters meet, and each informs the other of what he wants for his companion, and each strives to bring about what he wants for his companion. If the two arbiters agree upon something, it is permissible, whether they divorce or keep. That is the saying of God: "then send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family; if they both desire reconciliation, God will bring about harmony between them." If the woman sends an arbiter and the man refuses to send one, then he does not approach her until he sends an arbiter.

* *

Others said: The one who sends the two arbiters is the ruler, except that he only sends them so that they may know the wrongdoer from the wronged among them, to compel each of them to what is due to each from the other, not to separate them.

Those who said that:

9411 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan = and this is the saying of Qatadah = that the two of them said: The two arbiters are only sent to reconcile and to bear witness against the wrongdoer for his wrong. As for separation, it is not in their hands, and they are not given that authority; i.e., "And if you fear a breach between them, then send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family."

9412 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: "And if you fear a breach between them, then send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family", the verse: the two arbiters are only sent to reconcile. If they are unable to reconcile, they bear witness against the wrongdoer for his wrong, and separation is not in their hands, nor are they given that authority.

9413 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Qays ibn Sa'd, who said: And I asked about the two arbiters, [[In the printed edition: "I asked about the two arbiters", and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is correct; it is apparently part of a report, not the opening of one; see note 3.]] He said: Send an arbiter from his family and an arbiter from her family; whatever the two arbiters judge is permissible. God, blessed and exalted, says: "If they both desire reconciliation, God will bring about harmony between them." He said: The arbiter of the man retires with the husband, and the arbiter of the woman with the wife, and each says to his companion: "Be truthful with me about what is in your soul." When each of them is truthful with his companion, the two arbiters meet, and each takes a covenant from his companion: "You shall be truthful with me about what your companion told you, and I shall be truthful with you about what my companion told me." That is the time when they desired reconciliation, and God brings about harmony between them. When they have done that, each of them becomes aware of what his companion confided to him, and they then know the wrongdoer and the rebellious one among them, and they come to him and judge against him. If the woman is the one, they say: "You are the wrongdoer, the disobedient; he shall not maintain you until you return to the truth and obey God in it." If the man is the wrongdoer, they say: "You are the wrongdoer, the harmful one; you shall not enter a house for her until you maintain her and return to truth and justice." If he refuses that, she is the wrongdoer and disobedient, and he takes from her what is hers, and it is lawful and good for him. And if he is the wrongdoer who harms her and injures her, he divorces her, and nothing of her property becomes lawful for him. If he keeps her, he keeps her in what God commanded, and maintains her and treats her well.

[[The report: 9413 - "Qays ibn Sa'd al-Makki," client of Nafi' ibn Alqamah, narrated from Tawus, Ata, Mujahid, and Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Trustworthy. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

This chain of narration appeared in the printed edition as: "He said: Shabl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Qays ibn Sa'd." The manuscript was similar, except that above "Shabl" was written "lā" and above "Mujahid" was written "ilā," which are the scribes' signs for omitting what lies between them, so they did not need to strike it through with a pen. The editor did not know their conventions for writing and omissions, so he included what should have been omitted. As you can see, "Qays ibn Sa'd" narrates from Mujahid, but Mujahid is not one of his narrators. This report seems to be one that Qays ibn Sa'd asked Mujahid or Ata', as occurred in some of the earlier chains, whose places are no longer known to me today.]]

9414 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Mūsā ibn ʿUbaydah, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who said: ʿAlī ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him) used to send two arbitrators, one from the husband's family and one from the wife's family. The arbitrator from the wife's family would say: "O so-and-so, what do you resent about your wife?" He would say: "I resent such-and-such from her." He said: Then he would say: "Do you see, if she turns from what you dislike to what you love, will you be mindful of Allah concerning her and treat her well according to what is due from you regarding her maintenance and clothing?" If he said "Yes," the arbitrator from his family would say: "O so-and-so, what do you resent about your husband, so-and-so?" She would say the same. If she said "Yes," he would bring them together. He said: ʿAlī (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The two arbitrators, by them Allah brings together and by them He separates.

9415 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Al-Hasan said: The two arbitrators judge concerning reconciliation, and they do not judge concerning separation.

9416 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, his statement regarding "And those whose rebellion you fear, admonish them," and she is the woman who rebels against her husband. So her husband may divorce her by khul' (divorce at the wife's request) when the two arbitrators order that, and this is after she says to her husband: "By Allah, I will not fulfill any oath for you, and I will admit (people) into your house without your permission!" And the ruler says: "We do not permit you to take a khul'," until the woman says to her husband: "By Allah, I will not bathe for you from impurity, nor will I perform prayer for you!" At that point the ruler says: "Let the woman divorce by khul'!"

9417 - Yūnus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, "And those whose rebellion you fear, admonish them": He said: She admonishes her, and if she refuses and prevails, then he abandons her in her bed. If she overcomes this too, he strikes her. If she overcomes this too, an arbitrator from his family and an arbitrator from her family are sent. If she overcomes this too and wants something else, then my father said, or: my father used to say [[In the printed edition: "Then my father said," and in the manuscript: "Then my father said, and my father used to say." The correct reading is what is in the manuscript, except his statement "and my father used to say," whose correct form is "or: my father used to say." The speaker of this sentence is ʿAbd Allah ibn Zayd Aslam, and his father is Zayd ibn Aslam.]] = the two arbitrators have no power over separation. If they see injustice on the part of the husband, they say: "You, so-and-so, are an oppressor, so depart!" If he refuses, they refer the matter to the ruler. The arbitrators have no authority over separation.

* *

Others said: Rather, the ruler is the one who sends the two arbitrators, on the basis that their judgment binds the spouses in both reconciliation and separation.

Mention of those who said this:

9418 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from ʿAlī ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, his statement regarding "And if you fear a breach between them, send an arbitrator from his family and an arbitrator from her family": This man and woman, when the relationship between them deteriorates, Allah the Glorified commands that they send a righteous man from the man's family and a like him from the woman's family, and the two of them look at which of them is the wrongdoer. If the man is the wrongdoer, they keep his wife away from him and confine him to paying maintenance ["To confine someone to something" means to hold him to it and compel him to it by force and coercion. In a hadith: "You must confine him to the truth, confining him," meaning by compulsion and overpowering. It derives from "qasr," and the sin was replaced by a ṣād, and the two interchange in much speech.]]. If the woman is the wrongdoer, they confine her to her husband and deny her maintenance. If the two of them agree to separate or to reconcile, their decision is valid. If they see fit to reconcile, and one spouse is pleased while the other dislikes it, and then one of them dies, the one who was pleased inherits from the one who disliked it, but the one who disliked does not inherit from the one who was pleased. This is His statement: "If they both desire reconciliation, Allah will bring about harmony between them." He said: They are the two arbitrators. "Allah will bring about harmony between them."

9419 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Rawh narrated to us, saying: ʿAwf narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, that the arbitrator from her family and the arbitrator from his family separate and reconcile if they see that: "So send an arbitrator from his family and an arbitrator from her family."

9420 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, who said: I asked Sa'id ibn Jubayr about the two arbitrators, and he said: "I was not born at that time!" [[Sa'id ibn Jubayr, when ʿAmr ibn Murrah asked him about "the two arbitrators," went to the meaning that he referred to the arbitrators in the matter of ʿAlī and Mu'awiyah (may Allah be pleased with them), and their meeting at Dumat al-Jandal in the year 37 AH. Therefore he said: "I was not born at that time," because Sa'id ibn Jubayr (may Allah have mercy on him) was killed by al-Hajjaj in the year 95 AH, at the age of forty-nine, so it seems he was born in the year 46 AH, after the arbitration. It is also reported that when Sa'id ibn Jubayr was summoned to be executed, he called his son, and the son began to weep. He said: "What makes you weep? What is your father's remaining life after fifty-seven years?" So by this narration he was born around the year 38 AH, which is also after the arbitration of the two arbitrators.]] I said: "I only mean the arbitrators of the breach." He said: They approach the one who came with the dispute ["In the printed edition: 'the one who came with harm,' which failed to read the manuscript correctly, since it is undotted. It is from 'tadāra'u,' dropping its hamzah: 'the two men disputed,' meaning they quarreled and one opposed the other. In a saying of some wise men: 'Do not learn knowledge for three things, and do not abandon it for three: do not learn it for contention, nor for argument, nor for boasting, nor abandon it out of disinterest, nor out of contentment with ignorance, nor out of shame at acting upon it.' By his statement 'tadārī' here he meant quarreling and mutual accusation. See the following report, number 9428.]] from his side. If he does, well; otherwise, they approach the other. If he does, well; otherwise, they arbitrate. Whatever they decide is valid.

9421 - ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid informed us, from Isma'il, from ʿAmir, regarding His statement, "So send an arbitrator from his family and an arbitrator from her family," he said: Whatever the two arbitrators decide is valid.

9422 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Dawud, from Ibrahim, who said: Whatever they decide is valid. If they separate the two with three divorces or two divorces, it is valid. If they separate with one divorce, it is valid. If they judge against him with compensation from his wealth in this manner [[In the printed edition: "in this manner from his wealth," which in the manuscript is undotted and has no meaning here. I judged that its correct form is "compensation" (bi-jaza'), because the following report says: "or they divorce her for a consideration" (ʿalā ju'l), and "al-ju'l" (with a dammah and then a sukun) is the wealth given for something, whether as a wage or otherwise. "Al-jazā'" is a replacement, as if he gives her something in exchange for what she suffered from his wrongdoing, and as a punishment for the wrongdoer.]], it is valid. If they reconcile, it is valid. If they remit something, it is valid.

9423 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Hibban narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, regarding His statement, "And if you fear a breach between them, send an arbitrator from his family and an arbitrator from her family," he said: Whatever the two arbitrators do is binding on them both. If they divorce three times, it is binding on them both. If they divorce once, and they divorce her for a consideration, it is valid [[See the earlier note.]], and whatever they do is valid.

9424 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, who said: If the two arbitrators wish to separate, they separate; and if they wish to reconcile, they reconcile.

9425 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to me, from Husayn, from al-Sha'bi: A woman rebelled against her husband, and they brought their dispute before Shurayh. Shurayh said: "Send an arbitrator from his family and an arbitrator from her family." The two arbitrators examined their situation and decided to separate them. The man disliked that, so Shurayh said: "Then what were they doing today?" and he upheld their decision. [[Report 9425: recorded by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra, 7:306.]]

9426 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Tawus, from Ikrimah ibn Khalid, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: Myself and Mu'awiyah were sent as two arbitrators. Ma'mar said: It reached me that ʿUthman (may Allah be pleased with him) sent them, and said to them: If you see fit to reconcile, then reconcile; and if you see fit to separate, then separate. [[Report 9426: recorded by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra, 7:306.]]

9427 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Rawh ibn ʿUbadah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Mulaykah narrated to me: That ʿAqil ibn Abi Talib married Fatimah bint ʿUtbah, and there was some disagreement between them. She came to ʿUthman and told him about it, so he sent for Ibn ʿAbbās and Mu'awiyah. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I will certainly separate them!" Mu'awiyah said: "I would not separate two elders of the Banu ʿAbd Manaf!" They went to them, and by then they had reconciled. [[Report 9427: al-Shafi'i narrated it in al-Umm 5:177-178 through Muslim ibn Khalid, from Ibn Jurayj, and al-Bayhaqi recorded it in al-Sunan 7:306.]]

9428 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, regarding His statement, "And if you fear a breach between them, send an arbitrator from his family and an arbitrator from her family": They are to be just witnesses over them. This is when the man and woman quarrel and dispute before the ruler, and he appoints two arbitrators over them, one from the man's family and one from the woman's family, who are to be trustworthy over both of them, and they examine which of them is responsible for the corruption. If it comes from the woman, she is compelled to obey her husband, and he is commanded to fear Allah, treat her well, and provide for her according to what Allah has given him, "retaining her with kindness or releasing her with goodness." If the wrongdoing is from the man, he is commanded to be kind to her, and if he does not, it is said to him: "Give her her right and release her." It is only the ruler who handles that between them. [[See the explanation of "tadārā" earlier, p. 326, note 2.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions regarding His statement, "So send an arbitrator from his family and an arbitrator from her family," is that Allah addressed the Muslims with this, and commanded them to send the two arbitrators when a breach is feared between the spouses, to examine their matter, and He did not specify the command for some of them over others.

All agree that sending the two arbitrators in this matter is not for anyone other than the spouses and the ruler who governs the affairs of the Muslims, or whoever he appoints in his place for this.

They differed about the spouses and the ruler: who is the one commanded to send them, the spouses or the ruler? [[In the manuscript: "the spouses or the ruler," which is an obvious error.]] There is no indication in the verse showing that this command is specific to one of the spouses, and nothing has been reported from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about it, and the community differs on it.

Since the matter is as we have described, the most correct of these opinions is that what all agree is specified from the verse is specified. Since that is so, it is necessary that the spouses and the ruler both be included in the ruling of the verse and the command "So send an arbitrator from his family and an arbitrator from her family." Since there is disagreement between them as to whether they are the ones addressed by this command or not, and the apparent meaning of the verse encompasses them both, then what must be said, since what we have described is correct, is that if the spouses each send an arbitrator on his behalf to examine their matter, and each of them has sent his arbitrator in this regard with full authority over what is due to him from the other and what is due from him to the other [[In the printed edition: "each one of them has a power over his companion from the one he sent in this matter, and his companion has power over him," which is wholly unsound. In the manuscript: "each of them, the one he sent in this matter, has a claim over his companion, and his companion has a claim over him." It is evident that "the one he sent" means "he has sent," and as for "in this matter, has a claim," I judged that its correct form is "in this matter, what is his" (fī dhālika lamā lah), meaning he has sent him with full authority over his whole affair, over everything he has against his companion and his companion has against him. I was reassured in this by the following part of this discussion.]], then his appointing of him in this regard is valid and binding for and against him.

If he appoints him for only part and not for the whole, then what the arbitrator does, within what his companion appointed him for, is valid and binding according to what he was appointed for. That is, one of them appoints him for what is his, not for what is due from him.

If neither of the spouses appoints the arbitrator for what is his and what is due from him, [[In the printed edition: "or one of the spouses does not appoint," in place of the manuscript: "and if he does not appoint," which is a faulty alteration, as it corrupts the sentence and adds confusion upon confusion.]] or for what is his or for what is due from him,
except the two arbitrators together, [[In the printed edition: "then the two arbitrators have no ...," in place of the printed text: "except the two arbitrators," and it added more confusion to the text.]] [it is not permitted] except what the two of them agree upon, not what one of them does alone. [[What is between the brackets is very clearly omitted by the copyist, or something similar in meaning. With this the sentence is made sound, which required an effort we could have done without, had the copyist written it correctly.]]

And if neither of them appointed the arbitrators for anything, but they were sent only to examine the matter between them, to know which of them is the wrongdoer and which the wronged, [[In the printed edition, the phrase "between them" is omitted.]] so they could testify about them before the ruler if they need their testimony, then it is not permitted for them to introduce anything between them other than that, such as divorce, or taking property, or anything else, and nothing of that is binding on the spouses or on either of them. [[In the manuscript: "lam yalzam" without the waw, and the printed text is correct.]]

* *

If someone says: What is the meaning of "arbitrators," given that the matter is as you have described?
It is said: There has been disagreement about that.

Some said: The meaning of "al-hakam" (the arbitrator) is the just judgment, as al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim said in the report we mentioned, which:

9429 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated it to us, from Yazid, from Juwaybir, from him: "No, you two are judges who judge between them" =

* *

= in the manner we explained from his statement. [[His statement, "in the manner we explained from his statement," is from al-Tabari's own words, commenting on the rest of his earlier discussion. He meant by it al-Dahhak's statement he mentioned just above, number 9428. If this context were left without breaks, no one could understand it except those who persevere through hardships.]]

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is that they are the two judges, who judge between them what the spouses have delegated to them.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Whichever of the two meanings is correct, neither of them, nor either one of them, has the authority to judge between the spouses by separation, or by taking property, except with the consent of the one judged against, and except what is binding as a right of one spouse over the other by Allah's judgment, which is what is binding on the husband toward his wife, namely maintenance and retaining her with kindness, if he is the one who wrongs her.

As for anything else, that is not for them, nor for anyone other than them, neither the ruler nor anyone else. For if the husband is the wrongdoer toward the wife, the imam has a way to compel him to what is due to her as a right. And if the wife is the wrongdoer, rebelling against her husband, then Allah has permitted him to take ransom from her and has placed the power of divorcing her in his hand, as we explained in "Surat al-Baqarah." [[See what has passed, 4:549-583.]]

Since the matter is so, it is not permitted for anyone to separate a man and a woman without the husband's consent, nor to take property from the woman without her consent by her giving it, except by a proof that must be accepted, from a source or by analogy.

And if the ruler (al-sultan) sends the two arbitrators (al-hakamayn), it is not permissible for them to rule between the spouses by separation (tafriqa) unless the husband has delegated that authority to them, [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "wa la yajuz lahuma" with a waw, but the correct reading is with a fa'.]] nor for them to rule by taking property from the woman unless the woman consents. What proves this is what we have already explained earlier concerning the action of ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, in this regard, and the scholars who held his view. [[See the earlier reports, numbers 9407–9409.]] Rather, they may reconcile the spouses and investigate which of them is the wrongdoer and which the wronged, so that they may testify against the wrongdoer if the wronged party needs their testimony.

And we said, "They have no authority to separate," for the reason we mentioned just above. The ruler sends the two arbitrators, when he does send them, only when the spouses bring their dispute before him, each complaining of the other, and it is unclear to him which of them is in the right and which in the wrong. For if it is not unclear to him who is in the right and who is in the wrong, there is no reason for him to send arbitrators in a matter whose ruling is already known.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 35:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿If they both desire reconciliation, God will bring about harmony between them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "If they both desire reconciliation," He means: if the two arbiters (al-hakamān) desire reconciliation between the man and the woman, that is, between the spouses about whose discord one is afraid, then "God will bring about harmony" between the two arbiters, so that they agree on reconciling between them. This is the case when each of them is truthful in what he reaches concerning the matter of the spouses, the one who was sent to examine the affair of the spouses.

* *

Those of the exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil) also said something similar to what we have said about this.

Mention of those who said that:

9430 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yahya related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Hashim, from Mujahid, regarding His saying, "If they both desire reconciliation," he said: Indeed, it is not the man and the woman, but rather the two arbiters.

9431 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from 'Amr, from 'Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "If they both desire reconciliation, God will bring about harmony between them," he said: They are the two arbiters. "If they both desire reconciliation, God will bring about harmony between them."

9432 - Al-Muthanna related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiya related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "If they both desire reconciliation, God will bring about harmony between them," and that refers to the two arbiters, and likewise every reconciler whom God guides to the truth and what is right.

9433 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "If they both desire reconciliation, God will bring about harmony between them," meaning by that the two arbiters.

9434 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "If they both desire reconciliation," he said: If the two arbiters desire reconciliation, they will reconcile.

9435 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Abu Hashim, from Mujahid: "If they both desire reconciliation, God will bring about harmony between them," God brings about harmony between the two arbiters.

9436 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib related to me, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Juwaybir related to us, from al-Dahhak regarding His saying: "If they both desire reconciliation," he said: They are the two arbiters, when they give sincere counsel to both the woman and the man.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, God is ever Knowing and Acquainted﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He means, may His praise be exalted: "Indeed, God is Knowing" of what the two arbiters intend of reconciliation between the spouses and other than that, "Acquainted" with that and with other than that of their affairs and the affairs of others. Nothing of it is hidden from Him, and He preserves them, until He recompenses each of them with his recompense: with good for good, and with pardon or punishment for evil.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, may His remembrance be exalted: ﴿Worship God and associate nothing with Him, and be good to parents and to near relatives and orphans and the needy﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Humble yourselves to God through obedience, submit to Him in it, single Him out in lordship, and sincerely direct to Him submission and humility by adhering to His command and refraining from His prohibition. Do not make for Him, in lordship and worship, a partner whom you honor as you honor Him.

"And to parents good treatment," he says: and He commands you to good treatment of parents, meaning kindness toward them. And for this reason "good treatment" is in the accusative, because it is a command from Him, may His praise be exalted, to keep to good treatment of parents, in the form of an urging (al-igra').

* *

Some of them said: its meaning is "and show kindness to parents," and it is close in meaning to what we have said.

* *

As for His saying "and to near relatives," He means: and He also commands regarding near relatives, namely those related to one of us through his father or his mother, whose kinship is close to him by blood from either side, with good treatment through maintaining kinship ties.

* *

As for His saying "and orphans," they are the plural of "orphan" (yatim), who is a child whose father has died and perished.

* *

"And the needy," the plural of "miskin," who is one whom the humiliation of poverty and need has overtaken, so he becomes wretched because of it.

* *

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: Be mindful of these people with kindness toward them, show compassion to them, and hold fast to My charge concerning good treatment of them.

**The explanation of His words: ﴿And the neighbour who is near of kin﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: The people of ta'wil (interpretation, tafsir) differed over the meaning of this. Some of them said: its meaning is, "And the neighbour who is a relative and kin to you."

Those who said this:

9437 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "And the neighbour who is near of kin," meaning: the one between you and whom there is kinship.

9438 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "And the neighbour who is near of kin," meaning: the one who is a close relative (dhu al-rahm).

9439 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada and Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "And the neighbour who is near of kin," he said: "Your neighbour who is your relative."

9440 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Ikrima and Mujahid regarding His words: "And the neighbour who is near of kin," the two of them said: "Kinship."

9441 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "And the neighbour who is near of kin," he said: "Your neighbour with whom there is kinship between you and him."

9442 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And the neighbour who is near of kin," your neighbour who is a relative.

9443 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "And the neighbour who is near of kin," if he has a neighbour who is a kinsman, then he has two rights: the right of kinship and the right of neighbourhood.

9444 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And the neighbour who is near of kin," he said: "The neighbour who is near of kin is your relative."

* * *

Others said: Rather, it is the neighbour of your relative.

Those who said this:

9445 - Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Layth, from Maymun ibn Mihran regarding His words: "And the neighbour who is near of kin," he said: "A man who seeks your favour through the neighbourhood of your relative."

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: This view is contrary to what is known from the speech of the Arabs. The one described as "near of kin" in His words, "And the neighbour who is near of kin," is "the neighbour," not anyone else. So the speaker of this view made him the neighbour of a near relative. Had the meaning been as Maymun ibn Mihran said, it would have been said, "And the neighbour of the near of kin," and not "And the neighbour who is near of kin." Then, when "the neighbour" is attached to "near of kin," the command would be to show goodness to the neighbour who is a relative [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "the command between the neighbour who is a relative," which is meaningless; it is a scribal and textual error, and the correct reading is what I have given.]], and not to the neighbour who is not a relative. As for "the neighbour" with the definite article, it is not permissible for "near of kin" to be other than an adjective of "the neighbour." Since that is so, the command from God in His words, "And the neighbour who is near of kin," is to show goodness to the neighbour who is a kinsman, not to a neighbour who is not a relative. And what Maymun ibn Mihran said on this is clearly wrong. [[Here too the printed edition and manuscript read: "between the neighbour who is near of kin," which is an error and a misreading, as I have already noted.]]

* * *

Others said: The meaning is: "And the neighbour who is near to you through Islam."

Those who said this:

9446 - Muhammad ibn Umara al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Nawf al-Shami: "And the neighbour who is near of kin," the Muslim. [[The report 9446: "Nawf al-Shami" is Nawf ibn Fudala al-Himyari al-Bakali, whose biography has passed under no. 3965 and will come again under no. 9456.]]

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: This too has no meaning. The interpretation of the Book of God, blessed and exalted is He, is not permissible to be turned except toward the most common usage of the Arabs in whose tongue the Qur'an was revealed, the usage known among them, and not toward the most unusual usage which they do not recognise, unless there is a proof to the contrary which must be accepted. Since that is so, and it is known that the familiar usage of the Arabs when it is said, "So-and-so is a relative (dhu qaraba)," means only that he is close in kinship to him, and not closeness through religion, then turning it to kinship by blood is more fitting than turning it to closeness through religion.

* * *

The explanation of His words: ﴿And the distant neighbour﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of ta'wil differed over the meaning of this. Some of them said: its meaning is, "And the distant neighbour who has no kinship between you and him."

Those who said this:

9447 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas: "And the distant neighbour," the one between whom and you there is no kinship.

9448 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "And the distant neighbour," meaning: a neighbour from a foreign people.

9449 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "And the distant neighbour," the one between whom there is no kinship, and he is a neighbour, so he has the right of neighbourhood.

9450 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And the distant neighbour," the stranger neighbour who is from the people.

9451 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada and Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And the distant neighbour," your neighbour from other people.

9452 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And the distant neighbour," your neighbour with whom there is no kinship between you and him, distant in lineage, yet he is a neighbour.

9453 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Ikrima and Mujahid regarding His words: "And the distant neighbour," he said: "The one who is at the side."

9454 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "And the distant neighbour," the one between you and whom there is no blood tie or kinship. [[In the printed edition: "...wajh wa-la qaraba," which has no meaning; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]

9455 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak: "And the distant neighbour," he said: "From other people."

* * *

Others said: It is the polytheist neighbour.

Those who said this:

9456 - Muhammad ibn Umara al-Asadi narrated to me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Nawf al-Shami: "And the distant neighbour," he said: "The Jew and the Christian." [[Report 9456: "Ubayd Allah ibn Musa ibn Abi al-Mukhtar al-Absi," whose biography has passed under no. 5796. He narrates from Sufyan al-Thawri and from Shaybān ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Tamimi. In this chain the printed edition has "Shaybān, from Abu Ishaq," and the manuscript also has it, but the word "Shaybān" is written very poorly, as though the copyist were unsure of it. In the chain above at no. 9446 "Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq" is very clear in the manuscript, so I have preferred it and adopted it here. See the commentary on report 9446.]]

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two views is the view of the one who said: "The meaning of al-junub (the distant) in this place is the stranger, the distant one, whether Muslim or polytheist, Jew or Christian," because of what we have already shown, that "the near-of-kin neighbour" is the neighbour who is a relative by blood. It is necessary that "the neighbour of distance" be the distant neighbour, so that this is an injunction covering all kinds of neighbours, near and far.

* * *

Furthermore, al-junub in the speech of the Arabs means "distant," as the poet A'sha Bani Qays said:

I came to Harith as a visitor from a distance,
but Harith was stingy with my gifts.

He means by "from a distance" (an janaba): from afar and as a stranger. From this it is said: "So-and-so kept away from so-and-so (ijtanaba fulanan)," when he kept far from him, and "tajannabahu," and "jannabahu khayrahu," when he withheld his good from him. [[In the printed edition: "wa-tajannabahu khayrahu," with "wa-jannabahu" dropped between the two phrases, which spoils the context; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] From this the one in a state of ritual impurity is called junub, because he withdraws from prayer until he washes.

So the meaning is: "And the neighbour who keeps away from kinship."

* * *

The explanation of His exalted words: ﴿And the companion at the side﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of ta'wil differed over what is meant by this.

Some of them said: It is the companion of a man on a journey.

Those who said this:

9457 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas: "And the companion at the side," the fellow traveller.

9458 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya and Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, the two of them saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Bukayr, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr say: "And the companion at the side," the fellow traveller. [[Report 9458: "Abu Bukayr al-Taymi," the muezzin of Taym, whose name is "Marzuq." He narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrima, and Mujahid, and from him narrated Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, Isra'il, Sufyan al-Thawri, and Shurayk. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.
In the printed edition it reads "Abu Bakr," which is an error; the correct reading is as I have given from the manuscript. It will come in the correct form in nos. 9467 and 9468.]]

9459 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada and Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "And the companion at the side," your companion on the journey.

9460 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "And the companion at the side," who is the fellow traveller.

9461 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And the companion at the side," the fellow traveller, whose lodging is your lodging, whose food is your food, and whose journey is your journey.

9462 - Sufyan narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, from Ikrima and Mujahid: "And the companion at the side," the two of them said: the fellow traveller.

9463 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Al-Hammani narrated to us, saying: Shurayk narrated to us, from Jabir, from Amir, from Ali and Abdullah, the two of them said: "The companion at the side" is the righteous fellow.

9464 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Sulaym informed me, from Mujahid, who said: "The companion at the side," your fellow traveller, who comes to you with his hand in yours.

9465 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, by reading to Ibn Jurayj, who said: Sulaym informed us that he heard Mujahid say: "And the companion at the side," and he mentioned the like of it.

9466 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And the companion on the journey," the companion on the journey.

9467 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Dukayn narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Bukayr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "And the companion at the side," the righteous fellow.

9468 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Al-Thawri informed us, from Abu Bukayr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the like of it.

9469 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding His words: "And the companion at the side," he said: the fellow traveller.

9470 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, the like of it.

* * *

Others said: Rather, it is the man's wife who is with him at his side.

Those who said this:

9471 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Amir, or al-Qasim, from Ali and Abdullah, may God be pleased with them both, regarding "And the companion at the side," the two of them said: "It is the wife." [[The words "may God be pleased with them both" are an addition from the manuscript.]]

9472 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from some of his companions, from Jabir, from Ali and Abdullah, the like of it.

9473 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "And the companion at the side," meaning: the one who is with you in your dwelling.

9474 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Hilal, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, that he said regarding this verse: "And the companion at the side," he said: "It is the wife."

9475 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Ibrahim: "And the companion at the side," he said: "The wife."

9476 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Al-Thawri said, Abu al-Haytham said, from Ibrahim: "It is the wife."

9477 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Ibrahim, the like of it.

9478 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Suqa, from Abu al-Haytham, from Ibrahim, the like of it.

9479 - Amr ibn Bayдhaq narrated to me, saying: Marwan ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Suqa, from Abu al-Haytham, from Ibrahim, the like of it. [[Report 9479: "Amr ibn Bayḏaq" (with the dotted dhal), so written in the manuscript, a teacher of al-Tabari whose biography I have not found. He narrates from him in the book Tarikh al-Sahaba wa-al-Tabi'in, appended to the History, p. 86, where he is written "Amr ibn Bayḍaq" with the undotted dal. The first is probably the more correct.]]

* * *

Others said: It is the one who clings to you and accompanies you, hoping for your benefit.

Those who said this:

9480 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "The companion at the side," the one who keeps close. He also said: your companion who accompanies you.

9481 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "And the companion at the side," the one who cleaves to you, who is at your side, and who stays at your side hoping for your good and your benefit.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in the interpretation of this, in my opinion, is that the meaning of "the companion at the side" is the companion who is beside, as one says: "So-and-so is at the side of so-and-so, and beside him." It comes from the saying, "Fulan janaba fulanan, fa-huwa yajnubuhu janban," when he was at his side. [[This passage is a piece of lexical explanation, rarely found in a book of lexicography.]] From this comes "janab al-khayl," when he leads some of the horses beside others. It may include the fellow traveller, the wife, and the one who attaches himself to a man and keeps close to him hoping for his benefit, because all of them are at the side of the one with whom they are, and near to him. God, exalted is He, has enjoined all of them, since the right of the companion is binding upon the one he accompanies, and...

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 36 (part 2 of 2):**

9482 - Sahl ibn Musa al-Razi related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Fudayk related to us, from so-and-so ibn Abd Allah, from a trustworthy person in his presence: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was with a man from among his companions, and they were on two riding animals. The Prophet (ﷺ) dismounted and entered a thicket of tamarisk, [["al-Ghaydah" is a place where water gathers and overflows, so that trees grow there and become dense. The plural is "ghiyad." "al-Tarfa'" is a tree of the thorny (ida') kind. Its foliage is like that of the athl tree, but it has no usable wood. It only sends out smooth, straight stalks into the sky. Camels sometimes eat it as a sour-tasting fodder when they find no other.]] and he cut two green shoots, one crooked and the other straight. [[In the printed edition it reads "fasilayn" with a fa, which has no meaning. In the manuscript it reads "fasilayn" unpointed. In al-Durr al-Manthur it reads "fasalayn," which also has no meaning. "al-Qasil" with a qaf is what is cut (iqtasala, i.e., taken off) from the crop while still green. From this comes "al-qasil," the green fodder given to animals. One says "qasala al-dabbah," meaning he fed the animal qasil.]] He then went out with them, giving his companion the straight one and taking the crooked one for himself. The man said: "O Messenger of Allah, may my father and mother be ransom for you, you have more right to the straight one than I do!" He said: "No, O so-and-so. Every companion who accompanies a companion is answerable for his companionship, even for an hour of a day. [[The report: 9482. "Sahl ibn Musa al-Razi," see what I wrote about him under no. 4319, and before it no. 180. As for "Ibn Abi Fudayk," he is Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Muslim ibn Abi Fudayk, whose biography has already passed under no. 4319. This report is weak as a mursal (a report in which the link to the Prophet's source is missing), because of the unknown identity of those from whom Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated. I have not found it except in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:159, where it is attributed to no one other than Ibn Jarir.]]

9483 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Haywah, who said: Sharahbil ibn Shurayk related to me, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The best of companions with Allah, may He be blessed and exalted, is the one who is best to his companion. And the best of neighbors with Allah is the one who is best to his neighbor." [[The report: 9483. Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad, no. 6566, through the route of Abd Allah ibn Yazid, from Haywah and Ibn Lahi'ah, with the same wording. Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 4:164, and al-Tirmidhi 3:129, through the route of Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, like the version of al-Tabari. My brother al-Sayyid Ahmad said: "Its isnad is sound." "Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli" is Abd Allah ibn Yazid al-Ma'afiri, whose biography has passed under no. 6657.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Since "al-sahib bil-janb" (the companion at the side) can carry the meaning we have mentioned, [[In the printed edition: "And if the companion at the side has the meaning we have mentioned." It omitted "muhtamalan" (carrying the meaning), because in the manuscript it was written as "muttasilan" (connected), with confused writing, so the reader did not read it well and deleted it, even though the sentence cannot stand without it. As for what appears in the printed edition and the manuscript, namely "wa in kana" (and if it were), it is a plain error that breaks the sentence. Its correct form is what I have written: "fa-idh kana" (since it is).]] it includes everyone who joins a man in companionship during a journey, [[In the printed edition: "who accompanies him on a journey," which is a clear error that disrupts the flow of the speech. In the manuscript it is unpointed, and the correct reading is what I have written.]] or in marriage, or in attachment to him and connection with him, [[The phrase "and Allah did not" is joined to "since the companion."]] and Allah, may His praise be exalted, did not single out any of them from what the apparent meaning of the revelation admits. [[The phrase "therefore the correct view" is the answer to "since the companion ... therefore the correct view is to say."]] So the correct view is to say: all of them are meant by that, and Allah has enjoined kindness to each of them. [[In the printed edition: "wa-bikullihim" (and to all of them). The reader did not read the manuscript well. The correct form is what I have written.]]

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿and the wayfarer﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed about its meaning. Some of them said: "ibn al-sabil" (the wayfarer) is the traveler who passes through on his way.

Those who said this:

9484 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, and from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "and the wayfarer" is the one who passes by you while he is a traveler.

9484 (a) - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ma'mar, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid and Qatadah, the same.

9485 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His saying: "and the wayfarer." He said: He is the one who passes by you, even if he was originally wealthy.

* *

Others said: He is the guest.

Those who said this:

9486 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shabl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His saying: "and the wayfarer," he said: The guest, who has a right during travel and at home.

9487 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: "and the wayfarer," who is the guest.

9488 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn related to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak: "and the wayfarer," he said: The guest.

9489 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, the same.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter is that "ibn al-sabil" is the one who is on the road. "al-Sabil" is the road, and "ibn" here means its companion, the one who walks on it. [[See the explanation of "ibn al-sabil" above, 3:345-347 / 4:295. And the explanation of "al-sabil" at 2:497, and the other indexes of language.]] So he has a right over the one who passes by him in need and cut off from his people, provided his journey is not in disobedience to Allah: that he should help him if he needs assistance, host him if he needs hospitality, and carry him if he needs a mount. ["al-Himlan" (with a damma on the ha and a sukun on the mim) is what one is carried upon of animals.]

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿and what your right hands possess﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: those whom you own from among your slaves. He attributed "possession" (malk) to "the right hands" (yamin), as one says: "your mouth spoke" (takallama fawka), "your foot walked" (mashat rijluk), "your hand struck" (batashat yaduk), meaning: you spoke, you walked, you struck. However, what is described as belonging to each limb is attributed to it because that is what, in common usage among people, is done by it and not by the rest of the body's members. So the intended meaning of the speech was known by describing that limb with what it is described with. [[In the printed edition: "ma wusifat bihi" in both places, but the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] Likewise His saying: "what your right hands possess," because the slaves of one of us are under his hands. He only feeds what our right hands give, clothes what we clothe, [[In the printed edition: "wa-nukassi ma yakswuh," which is an error; the correct reading is from the manuscript. The verbs in this sentence to its end are unpointed in the manuscript, and the editor of the printed edition placed the dots on them badly, which broke their meaning. It was: "... nut'imu ... nukassi ... wa-nasrifuhu," and the correct form is what I have written.]] and directs them to whatever he likes to direct them with those [hands]. So their ownership is attributed to "the right hands" for that reason.

* *

The people of interpretation have said what we have said on this matter.

Those who said this:

9490 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shabl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "and what your right hands possess," of what Allah has entrusted to you. All of this Allah has enjoined.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Mujahid, in his saying "All of this Allah has enjoined," means: the parents, the near kin, the orphans, the needy, the neighbor who is near, the neighbor who is distant, the companion at the side, and the wayfarer. Our Lord, majestic in His glory, has enjoined all of these upon His servants as kindness toward them, and He commanded His creatures to preserve His command concerning them. So it is incumbent upon His servants to preserve the command of Allah concerning them, and then to preserve the command of His Messenger (ﷺ).

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is self-deluded and boastful﴾ (36)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "Indeed, Allah does not love one who is self-deluded," He means: Indeed, Allah does not love the one who has arrogance (khuyala').

"al-Mukhtal" is the "mufta'al" form, from your saying: "khala al-rajul, fa-huwa yakhulu khawlan wa-khalan" (the man became self-deluded, and so he is self-deluded). [[This is one of the two aspects of the speech. The other is "khala yakhalu khaylan wa-khalan," with a ya, and some preferred it because it derives from "al-khuyala'" (arrogance).]] From it is the saying of the poet: [[He is Anas ibn Musahiq al-Abdi, a man from Abd al-Qays.]]

If you were our lord, you would lead us; but if you were a fool, then go and act as you wish with your vanity.

[[Hamasah of Abu Tammam 1:133; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu Ubaydah 1:127; al-Lisan (khayl). Before the verse: "Let my friend Rashid know, of old, and my full brother, when he is connected: that the flour makes the noble man agitated, and that the mighty, when he is harmed, is humiliated; and that prudence is that you turn away from the chests of spears toward another tribe besides us." In the verse "fakhul," you may read it with a damma on the kha or a fatha on it, meaning: go and be self-deluded as the vanity wills for you.]]

And from it is the saying of al-Ajjaj:

And self-delusion is a garment of the ignorant.

[[The age has in it heedlessness for the heedless, and a man wears it out as a wrap wears out, the turning of nights and the changing of conditions. In the printed edition it read "thiyab al-jamal" (the garments of beauty), which is a distortion; the correct reading is in the manuscript.]]

As for "al-fakhur" (boastful), it is the one who boasts over the servants of Allah with what Allah has bestowed upon him of His blessings and spread for him of His bounty, and does not praise Him for what came to him of His favor, but is self-deluded and arrogant because of it, and haughty over others because of it. As:

9491 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shabl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Indeed, Allah does not love one who is self-deluded," he said: arrogant. "boastful," he said: He counts what he has been given, while he does not thank Allah.

9492 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Kathir related to us, from Abd Allah ibn Wahid Abi Raja' al-Haruwi, who said: You will not find one who mistreats his possessions (sayyi' al-malakah) except that you find him self-deluded and boastful. [["al-Malakah" (with a fatha on the mim and the lam) and (with a kasra on the mim and a sukun on the lam) refer to one who mistreats when he owns something, so he becomes domineering and arrogant. In the hadith: "The one who mistreats his possessions will not enter Paradise." It is one who mistreats his slaves or whatever falls under his authority.]] And he recited: "and what your right hands possess; indeed, Allah does not love one who is self-deluded and boastful." And you will not find a disobedient son (aqq) except that you find him a tyrant and wretched. And he recited: ﴿and dutiful to my mother, and He has not made me a tyrant, wretched﴾ [Surah Maryam: 32].

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿Those who are niggardly and enjoin niggardliness upon people and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His mention be exalted, He means: Indeed Allah does not love the arrogant boaster, the one who is niggardly and enjoins niggardliness upon people.

"Those who" (alladhina) may be in the nominative position, as a response to what is in His words "boastful" (fakhuran), in the sense of a pronoun referring back to it [[In the printed edition: "min dhamm" (from blame), which has no meaning whatsoever. The correct reading is from the manuscript: the intended word is "dhikr" (mention), meaning the pronoun. Abu Hayyan rejected this view in his tafsir 3:247 and did not attribute it to al-Tabari.]], and it may be in the accusative position as a qualifier of "man" (whoever).

In the speech of the Arabs, "bukhl" (niggardliness) is a man withholding from his petitioner what he has, while having an excess beyond it [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "min fadl 'anhu" (from excess of it); the correct text seems to be what is established here. This definition of "bukhl" is rarely found in lexicographical works.]], as related:

9493 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ibn Tawus, from his father, concerning His words: "Those who are niggardly and enjoin niggardliness upon people." He said: Bukhl is that a person is niggardly with what is in his hands, while shuhh is that he is greedy for what is in the hands of people. He said: He loves that what is in the hands of people should be his, by lawful and unlawful means, and he is never content.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words: "and enjoin niggardliness upon people."

* *

The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it: "bi-l-bakhal" with a fatha on the "ba" and the "kha".

The majority of the readers of Medina and some of the Basrans recited it with a damma on the "ba": "bi-l-bukhl".

Abu Ja'far said: Both are eloquent dialects with one meaning; they are two well-known readings that do not differ in meaning, so whichever of them the reciter reads, he is correct in his recitation.

* *

It has been said that by His words: "Those who are niggardly and enjoin niggardliness upon people," Allah, may His mention be exalted, meant those among the Jews who concealed the name and description of Muhammad ﷺ and did not make it clear to the people, although they found it written in their Torah and Gospel.

Mention of those who said that:

9494 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, from al-Hadrami: "Those who are niggardly and enjoin niggardliness upon people and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty." He said: They are the Jews; they were niggardly with the knowledge they possessed and concealed it.

9495 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning Allah's words: "Those who are niggardly and enjoin niggardliness upon people," up to His words: "And Allah is ever Knowing of them," that between these is about the Jews.

9496 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

9497 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, concerning His words: "Those who are niggardly and enjoin niggardliness upon people," and they are the enemies of Allah, the People of the Book, who were niggardly with the right of Allah upon them, and concealed Islam and Muhammad ﷺ, while they find him written in their Torah and Gospel.

9498 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: As for "those who are niggardly and enjoin niggardliness upon people," they are the Jews; "and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty," the name of Muhammad ﷺ. As for "are niggardly and enjoin niggardliness upon people," they are niggardly with the name of Muhammad ﷺ, and some of them enjoin others to conceal it.

9499 - Muhammad ibn Muslim al-Razi narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi narrated to me, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from 'Arim, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His words: "Those who are niggardly and enjoin niggardliness upon people," he said: This is about knowledge; there is nothing of worldly matters in it.

9500 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: "Those who are niggardly and enjoin niggardliness upon people," he said: These are Jews. He recited: "and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty," and said: They are niggardly with what Allah has given them of provision, and they conceal what Allah has given them of the Books; when they are asked about a thing and what Allah has revealed, they conceal it. And he recited: ﴿Or do they have a share in the kingdom? Then they would not give the people even a speck﴾ [Surah an-Nisa: 53], concerning their niggardliness.

9501 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salama narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, from 'Ikrima or from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Kardam ibn Zayd, ally of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, and Usama ibn Habib, and Nafi' ibn Abi Nafi', and Bahri ibn 'Amr, and Huyayy ibn Akhtab, and Rifa'a ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut, used to come to men of the Ansar, = and they used to mix with them, giving them sincere advice = from among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and say to them: Do not spend your wealth, for we fear for you poverty in its loss; and do not hasten in spending, for you do not know what will happen! So Allah revealed concerning them: "Those who are niggardly and enjoin niggardliness upon people and conceal what Allah has given them of His bounty," that is: of prophethood [[In Ibn Hisham: "that is: of the Torah", which is the better of the two narrations, if this here is not a scribal error. But I feared it might have some sense, so I left it.]], in which is the confirmation of what Muhammad ﷺ brought: "And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment," up to His words: "And Allah is ever Knowing of them." [[The report 9501: narrated by Ibn Hisham from Ibn Ishaq in his Sirah 2:208, 209, and it follows the reports whose last was 8338 earlier.

As for "Kardam ibn Zayd", in Ibn Hisham's Sirah it is "Kardam ibn Qays", who is mentioned in Ibn Hisham's Sirah 2:160 as also an ally of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, from Banu al-Nadir. As for "Kardam ibn Zayd" in al-Tabari's narration from Ibn Ishaq, Ibn Hisham mentions him in his Sirah 2:162 and counts him among Banu Qurayza. Moreover, those mentioned in this report from the Jews are attributed in Ibn Hisham's Sirah as follows: "Kardam ibn Qays" and "Huyayy ibn Akhtab" from Banu al-Nadir; "Kardam ibn Zayd", Usama ibn Habib, and Nafi' ibn Abi Nafi', from Banu Qurayza; Bahri ibn 'Amr, and Rifa'a ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut, from Banu Qaynuqa'.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse according to the first interpretation is: Indeed Allah does not love those possessing pride and boasting, who are niggardly in making clear what Allah commanded them to make clear to the people, concerning the name, attributes and description of Muhammad ﷺ which He sent down in His Books upon His prophets, while they knew it = and who enjoin upon the people who know that, like their knowledge, the concealing of what Allah commanded them to make clear to him, and conceal the knowledge and recognition of that from whom Allah forbade them to conceal it.

* *

As for the interpretation of Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn Zayd: "Indeed Allah does not love whoever is arrogant and boastful," those who are niggardly toward the people with the excess of what Allah has provided them of their wealth; then the rest of their interpretation and the interpretation of others is the same.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the sayings concerning this is what was said by those who said: Allah described these people whose description He gave in this verse with niggardliness, by informing [of the truth] to whoever was ignorant of the matter of Muhammad ﷺ, that it is true, and that Muhammad ﷺ is a sent prophet, and other truth which Allah, may His mention be exalted, had made clear in what He revealed to His prophets from His Books. These people were niggardly in making it clear to the people, and they enjoined whoever was in their state, in knowing it, to conceal it from whoever was ignorant of it, and not to make it clear to the people.

We only said this view is more correct as an interpretation of the verse, because Allah, may His mention be exalted, described them as enjoining people to niggardliness, and it has not reached us concerning any nation that they enjoined people to niggardliness as a religion or as a moral trait; rather, they see that as ugly and blame its doer; [[In the printed edition: "wa yudhimm fa'iluhu" with a ya, which is an error in reading the manuscript, since it is undotted, and this error led the printer to change what was in the manuscript when the meanings of the speech became confused, as you will see.]] and they praise—even if they adopt niggardliness and practise it themselves—generosity and liberality, [[In the printed edition: "wa la yamtadih ... fa-l-sakha', ta'udduhu ...", which, having misread the previous word, changed what was in the manuscript entirely: it added "la" to "wa yamtadih", made "bi-l-sakha'" into "fa-l-sakha'", and made "wa ta'udduhu" into "ta'udduhu" by removing the waw. He wanted the phrase to be straightened, but it became corrupted altogether without any qualification or condition!!

Moreover, the context of the sentence: "rather they see that as ugly and blame its doer, and praise ... with generosity and liberality, and count it among noble deeds," and he brought in the phrase "even if they adopt niggardliness and practise it themselves" as a parenthetical insertion.]] and count it among noble deeds and urge it. For this reason we said: Their niggardliness which Allah described them with was only niggardliness with the knowledge which Allah had given them, so they were niggardly in making it clear to the people and concealed it, not niggardliness with wealth = unless the meaning of that is: those who are niggardly with their wealth, which they spend in the rights of Allah and His ways, and enjoin the people among the people of Islam to abandon spending in that. Then their niggardliness with their wealth, and their enjoining the people to niggardliness, would be in this sense [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "fa-hadha al-ma'na", and the correct text is what is established here; its context: "then their niggardliness with their wealth ... in this sense ..."]] — according to what we have mentioned from the narration from Ibn 'Abbas — and then there would be a comprehensible aspect to describing them with niggardliness and enjoining it.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment (37)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He means by this, may His mention be exalted: "And We have prepared," and made ready for those who deny the blessing of Allah which He bestowed upon them, from the knowledge of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, who disbelieve in him after knowing him, who conceal his description and attributes from the people whom Allah commanded them to make them clear to: "a humiliating punishment," meaning: the degrading punishment for whoever is punished by remaining in it forever, [[See the explanation of "al-muhin" earlier: 2:347, 348 / 7:423 / 8:72.]] a provision for him in the Hereafter, which he will find when he comes before his Lord, for what he earlier did of denying the obligation of Allah which He imposed upon him. [[In the printed edition: "wa akhdhuhu bi-ma salafa ..." and the correct text is what is in the manuscript, for the beginning of this sentence is "when he comes before his Lord, he finds ...", which is the explanation of "al-ʿatad" (provision).]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 38:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And those who spend their wealth to be seen by people, and do not believe in God or in the Last Day﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: We have prepared a humiliating punishment for the disbelievers in God among the Jews, whose description God has given, ﴿and those who spend their wealth to be seen by people.﴾

* *

"Those" (alladhina) is in the genitive position, in apposition to "the disbelievers" (al-kafirin).

* *

As for His words, "to be seen by people" (ri'a' al-nas), it means: spending it for show (muraa'at) before people, not for obedience to God or in His way, but in the way of Satan [[See the explanation of "ri'a'" above, vol. 5, pp. 521–522.]]. "And they do not believe in God or in the Last Day" means: they do not affirm the oneness of God, nor the return to Him on the Day of Resurrection [[In the printed edition: "and the promise" (al-mi'ad).]], in which the recompense for deeds is given, as something that will occur. [[His words "as something that will occur": the context is "they do not affirm the return... that it will occur."]]

* *

Mujahid has said that this describes the Jews, but it is more fitting as a description of the hypocrites (ahl al-nifaq), who were people of polytheism who displayed Islam out of dissimulation (taqiyyah) before the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the people of faith, while remaining steadfast in their disbelief. It is more fitting for them than for the Jews, because the Jews affirmed the oneness of God and believed in resurrection and the return. Their disbelief was only in denying the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ). [[The context: "it describes the people of hypocrisy... more fitting than the description of the Jews." The correction of the earlier text stands. As for the editor of the printed edition, seeing that the sentence was not sound, he wrote "more fitting for them than the description of the Jews," which made the sentence even more corrupt.]]

* *

Furthermore, God's separation between the description of those who do not believe in God or in the Last Day and the description of the other group mentioned in the preceding verse, whom He described and informed that they have a humiliating punishment, by the conjunction "and" (waw) separating them [[The context: "in God's separation... by the separating 'and' between them, is a sign that..."]] indicates that they are two descriptions of two kinds of people with differing meanings, even though all of them are people of disbelief in God. Had both descriptions been of one kind of people, it would have been said, "And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment, those who spend their wealth to be seen by people," but He separated them with "and" for the reason we have described. [[In the printed edition: "and although they all are..." which is a plain error; the correct reading is from the manuscript, where the word is undotted.]]

* *
