If someone supposes that the insertion of "and" is not objectionable when one description follows another for a single described subject in Arabic speech, then that is so, but the more eloquent usage in Arabic, when a second description different from the first is intended, is to omit the "and." When a different description is intended for the second, the "and" is inserted. [[In the printed edition: "inserts the and," and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] Directing the words of God to the most eloquent and well-known usage of those whose language the Book was revealed in is more fitting for us than directing it to the more unusual of their speech.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And whoever has Satan as a companion, then evil is the companion﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Whoever has Satan as a close friend and companion, who acts by obeying him, follows his command, and abandons God's command concerning spending his wealth for show before people, not for His obedience, and denies the oneness of God and resurrection after death, ﴿then evil is the companion,﴾ meaning: evil is Satan as a companion.

* *

The word "companion" (qarin) is in the accusative because "evil" (sa'a) contains a reference to Satan, as His praise says: ﴿Evil is it as an exchange for the wrongdoers﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 50]. The Arabs do the same with "sa'a" and its counterparts [[See what has preceded on "sa'a," vol. 8, p. 138, note 8; the Meanings of the Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 267–269; and the Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu Ubaydah 1: 127.]]. Among this is the saying of Adi ibn Zayd:

Do not ask about the man, but look at his companion,
for the companion is guided by the one he accompanies. [[His Diwan, among the poets of pre-Islamic times, p. 466; Majmu'at al-Ma'ani, p. 14; and many others. I have recorded the verse as Abu Ja'far narrated it and as it appears in the manuscript. As for the editor of the printed edition, he altered it and recorded the version he followed:
"Do not ask about the man, but ask about his companion,
for every companion is guided by the one he accompanies."
This is an undoubted mishandling.]]

He means by "companion" (qarin): the friend and the comrade.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 39–40 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And what would it have harmed them had they believed in God and the Last Day and spent of what God has provided for them? God is ever Knowing of them.﴾ (39)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: What harm would it be upon these people who spend their wealth to be seen by people, and do not believe in God or the Last Day, ﴿had they believed in God and the Last Day﴾, had they affirmed that God is One with no partner, sincerely devoted monotheism to Him, been certain of the resurrection after death, and affirmed that God will recompense them for their deeds on the Day of Resurrection; ﴿and spent of what God has provided for them﴾, meaning: and paid the zakat of their wealth which God provided them and gave them, willingly, and not spent it to be seen by people, seeking mention and pride among the people of disbelief in God, and false praise among people; ﴿and God was﴾, regarding those whom He described, that they spend their wealth to be seen by people in hypocrisy, while they are deniers of God and the Last Day; ﴿Knowing﴾, meaning: possessing knowledge of them and their deeds, [[In the manuscript: "dhu 'ilm" in the nominative case, and there is no harm in it.]] and of what they intend and desire by spending the wealth they spend, and that they desire by it showing off, reputation and praise among people. He preserves their deeds for them, nothing of them is hidden from Him, until He recompenses them for them with their reward when they return to Him.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Indeed, God does not wrong [even] the weight of an atom. And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.﴾ (40)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "And what would it have harmed them had they believed in God and the Last Day and spent of what God has provided for them?" Indeed God does not diminish for anyone of His creation who spends in His cause from what He has provided him, any of the reward of his spending in this world, nor of its recompense on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿The weight of an atom﴾, meaning: what would weigh it and be according to its heaviness in weight; but He recompenses him for it and rewards him for it, as:

9502 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: that he recited, "Indeed, God does not wrong [even] the weight of an atom. And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it," and said: "That my good deeds exceed my evil deeds by the weight of an atom is dearer to me than the world and all that is in it." [[Forgiveness, O God! The publisher of this printed edition commits countless errors in distorting the text, and alters it without basis in understanding or trustworthiness. He did not read the manuscript well as it was written, so he made what was in it meaningless and wrote in its place: "That my good deeds exceed what weighs an atom is dearer to me than the world and all that is in it." I do not know, how much he would have been better off without such a reprehensible act!]]

9503 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Some of the people of knowledge used to say: That my good deeds exceed my evil deeds by the weight of an atom is dearer to me than that the entire world be mine.

* *

As for the "atom" (dharrah), it is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said about it, as:

9504 - Ishaq ibn Wahb al-Wasiti narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Shabib ibn Bishr narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "the weight of an atom," he said: the head of a red ant. [[The report: 9504 - "Ishaq ibn Wahb ibn Ziyad al-'Allaf," Abu Ya'qub al-Wasiti. Al-Bukhari, Ibn Majah, Abu Zur'ah and Abu Hatim narrated from him. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.
And "Abu 'Asim" is: al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad. Has passed several times.
And "Shayb ibn Bishr" narrated from Anas and 'Ikrimah, reliable but weak in narration, makes many errors. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

* *

= Abu Ja'far said: Ishaq ibn Wahb said to me: Yazid ibn Harun said: They claim that this red atom has no weight. [[In the printed edition: "this red worm," which is a pure error; in the manuscript: "these red worms," which is a distortion.]]

* *

With something similar to what we have said regarding this, reports have been authenticated from the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

9505 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: 'Imran narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: Indeed God does not wrong a believer a good deed, for which he is given provision in this world, and is recompensed for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is fed by it in this world, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, he will have no good deed. [[The report: 9505 - Abu Dawud: this is al-Tayalisi.
"'Imran": is Ibn Dawar al-Qattan.
The hadith is in Musnad al-Tayalisi: 2011, with this chain.
Ahmad in his Musnad narrated it through Hammam, from Qatadah: 12264, 12291, 14063 (vol. 3 pp. 123, 125, 283, Halabi edition).
Likewise Muslim 2: 344-345 narrated it through Hammam, then narrated it through other routes.
Ibn Kathir 2: 450 mentioned it from the narration of al-Tayalisi.
al-Suyuti 2: 163 mentioned it and attributed it to these.]]

It was narrated to us by Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi, saying: Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam informed us, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar: By Him in whose hand is my soul, none of you is more insistent in demanding a right which he sees as his due from the believers regarding their brothers when they see that they have been saved from the Fire, saying: "Our Lord, our brothers, who used to pray with us, fast with us, perform Hajj with us, and fight with us, have been seized by the Fire!" God says to them: "Go, and whomever you recognize by his form, bring him out!" And He forbids their forms to the Fire, so they find a man whom the Fire has seized up to the middle of his shins, and up to his knees, and up to his waist; so they bring out many people from it. Then they return and speak, and He says: "Go, and whomever you find in his heart the weight of a qirat of good, bring him out!" So they bring out many people from it. Then they return and speak, and He keeps saying that to them until He says: "Go, and whomever you find in his heart the weight of an atom, bring him out!" = Abu Sa'id, whenever he narrated this hadith, would say: If you do not believe, then recite: "Indeed, God does not wrong [even] the weight of an atom. And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward." = They will say: "Our Lord, we have left in it no good."
[[The report: 9506 - Ja'far ibn 'Awn ibn 'Amr ibn Huraith, al-Makhzumi al-Kufi: reliable. The compilers all narrated from him.
The hadith is part of a long hadith on intercession. The imams narrated it in the collections by many routes, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri:
Al-Tayalisi narrated it: 2179, from Kharijah ibn Mus'ab, from Zayd.
Ahmad in his Musnad narrated it: 11144 (3: 16-17, Halabi), through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Zayd.
He also narrated it: 11922 (3: 94-95, Halabi), through Ma'mar, from Zayd.
Muslim 1: 66-67 narrated it through Hafs ibn Maysarah, from Zayd.
Then he narrated it, without mentioning its wording, through Ja'far ibn 'Awn, from Hisham ibn Sa'd. This is the route narrated by al-Tabari here.
The reference to al-Bukhari's narration will come in the following hadith.]]

9507 - And Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: My father and Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to me, from al-Layth, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Hilal, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), with something similar. [[The report: 9507 - "al-Layth": is Ibn Sa'd. Khalid ibn Yazid: is al-Jumahi al-Misri. "Ibn Abi Hilal": is Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal al-Misri.
The hadith repeats the preceding one.
Al-Bukhari 13: 358-361 (Fath) narrated it through al-Layth ibn Sa'd with this chain. Ibn Kathir 2: 449 mentioned a portion of it and attributed it to the two Sahihs.]]

* *

Others said regarding this, with what:

9508 - It was narrated to me by al-Muthanna, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Sadaqah ibn Abi Sahl narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amr narrated to us, from Zadhan, who said: I came to Ibn Mas'ud and he said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will gather the first and the last, then a caller from God will call out: "Whoever was seeking a wrong, let him come to his right and take it!" He said: By God, a man will be pleased that a right is due to him from his father, or his child, or his wife, so he takes it from him, even if he is young. [[In the printed edition: "then by God the child is pleased," and in the manuscript: "then by God the one who ... ," and the correct reading of it is "the man" as I have established from the references mentioned below. "Dhaba li 'ala fulan min al-haqq kadha, yadhubu," meaning it was established and became due to him.]] = And the proof of that is in the Book of God, blessed and exalted: ﴿So when the Horn is blown, there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask one another.﴾ [Surah al-Mu'minun: 101] = Then it will be said to him: "Go to these people and give them their rights" = meaning: give them their rights = He will say: "O Lord, from where, when the world has gone?" God will say to His angels: "O My angels, look into his righteous deeds and give them from them!" If there remains the weight of an atom of good, the angels will say, while He knows better than them: "Our Lord, we have given each person with a right his right, and there remains for him the weight of an atom of good." He will say to the angels: "Multiply it for My servant, and make him enter Paradise by the bounty of My mercy." = And the proof of that in the Book of God: "Indeed, God does not wrong [even] the weight of an atom. And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward," meaning: Paradise, He gives it. If his good deeds run out and his evil deeds remain, the angels will say, while He knows better: "Our God, his good deeds have run out and his evil deeds remain, and many claimants remain!" God will say: "Add to it from their burdens, and write for him a document to the Fire." [[In the printed edition: "place upon it from their burdens," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript. See the following report.]] Sadaqah said: Or a sakk (writ) to Hell; Sadaqah doubted which of the two he said. [[The report: 9508 - Sadaqah ibn Abi Sahl: biographed in al-Ta'jil, p. 185-186. And al-Kabir 2/2/298, no. 2891, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/434-435, no. 1907. They mention no criticism of him, so he is reliable.
His teacher "Abu 'Amr": I do not know who he is, as this kunya is common.
"Zadhan": is al-Kindi the blind. He is a well-known reliable Successor.
See the chain following this one.]]

9509 - And I was told from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd, from Harun ibn 'Antarah, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib who said: I heard Zadhan say: 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: The male and female servant will be taken by the hand on the Day of Resurrection, and a caller will call out over the heads of the first and last: "This is so-and-so son of so-and-so; whoever has a right, let him come to his right," so the woman is pleased that a right is due to her from her father, or from her son, or from her brother, or from her husband, [[See the explanation of "yadhubu" above, p. 363, note 1.]] then Ibn Mas'ud recited: ﴿So there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask one another.﴾ [Surah al-Mu'minun: 101]. God, blessed and exalted, will forgive from his right whatever He wills, and will not forgive anything of the rights of people. He will stand before people and say: "Give to people their rights!" He will say: "Lord, the world has gone, from where shall I give them their rights?" He says: "Take from his righteous deeds, and give each person with a right his right, according to the measure of his injustice." If he was a friend of God, then there remains for him the weight of an atom of excess, He multiplies it for him until He admits him to Paradise by it = Then he recited to us: "Indeed, God does not wrong [even] the weight of an atom" = And if he was a wretched servant, the angel will say: "Lord, his good deeds have run out, and many claimants remain!" He will say: "Take from their evil deeds and add them to his evil deeds, then write for him a writ to the Fire." [[The report: 9509 - It is a repetition of the preceding one in its meaning. But al-Tabari begins it with the vague form "I was told from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd," so this chain is lost by that vagueness.
Ibn Kathir 2: 449-450 transmitted it from Ibn Abi Hatim: "Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Harun ibn 'Antarah...," so the weakness at the start of the chain is removed.
Harun ibn 'Antarah: his authentication and biography were passed at: 405.
'Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kindi, also called al-Shaybani, al-Kufi: a well-known reliable narrator. Al-A'mash and al-Thawri narrated from him, and Muslim narrated from him.
This chain, according to Ibn Abi Hatim, is a sound chain.
The report is a statement (mawquf) of Ibn Mas'ud. But I consider it to have the ruling of the marfu'. For what Ibn Mas'ud mentioned is not something known through opinion, and Ibn Mas'ud would not say this on his own; and he is not one who narrates from the People of the Book or accepts Isra'iliyyat.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it, as we have said, then said: "Some of this report has a witness in the authentic hadith." Al-Suyuti narrated it 2: 163 and added its attribution to 'Abd ibn Humayd.
"Al-sakk": the writ. And his saying "sakku" is a verb from "al-sakk," meaning: write for him a writ. This verb is not mentioned in the lexicon books, and this is its witness.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: So the interpretation of the verse according to this interpretation of 'Abd Allah is: Indeed God does not wrong a servant to whom is due the weight of an atom from another servant of His in his return and on the day of meeting Him, or more than that, so that He leaves it upon him and does not take it for the wronged from his wrongdoer; rather He takes it from him for him, and takes from every wrongdoer for every wronged person his due against him. ["Al-tab'ah" (with a fatha on the ta') and "al-tiba'ah" (with a kasra on the ta'): what you have pursued against your companion of injustice or a right you have over him.]
﴿And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it﴾, meaning: and if a good deed is found for him, He multiplies it, in the sense that its reward and its recompense are multiplied for him. ﴿And gives from Himself a great reward﴾, meaning: and gives him from Himself a great reward. "The great reward" is Paradise, according to what 'Abd Allah said.

* *

Both interpretations have a clear meaning, namely the interpretation that Ibn Mas'ud gave and the one that Qatadah gave. We have chosen the first interpretation for its agreement with the report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), together with the indication of the apparent meaning of the revelation regarding its soundness, since it is in the context of the verse before it, in which God urges spending in His obedience and censures spending in obedience to Satan. Then He connected that with what He promised the hypocrites in His obedience, by His saying: "Indeed God does not wrong [even] the weight of an atom, and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward."

The readers differed concerning His saying: "And if it is a good deed" (wa-in taku hasanatan). The majority of the readers of Iraq recited it: ﴿وَإِنْ تَكُ حَسَنَةً﴾ with the accusative "hasanatan," meaning: and if the weight of the atom is a good deed, He multiplies it.

* *

The majority of the readers of Medina recited it: ﴿وَإِنْ تَكُ حَسَنَةٌ﴾ with the nominative "hasanatun," meaning: and if a good deed is found, as I have mentioned from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud's interpretation of that.

As for His saying "yudā'ifuhā" (He multiplies it), it came with an "alif" and He did not say "yudha'╼ifuhā" (He doubles it), because it is intended, according to the saying of some of the people of the Arabic language: [[Meaning Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 127, whose text is: "yudā'ifuhā" = manifold multiplications, and "yudha''ifuhā" = two-fold.]] He multiplies it in many multiples; and if it were intended in His saying [[Meaning: in the saying of Abu 'Ubaydah.]] "yudha''ifu dhālika di'fayn" (He doubles that twofold), it would have been said "yudha''ifuhā" with the doubled letter.

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed about those whom God promised by this verse what He promised them in it.

Some of them said: They are all the people of faith in God and in Muhammad (ﷺ). And they argued for that with what:

9510 - Al-Fadl ibn al-Sabah narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Mubarak ibn Fudalah, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi who said: I met Abu Hurayrah and said to him: It has reached me that you say: Indeed the good deed is multiplied a thousand thousand good deeds! He said: And what amazes you about that? By God, I heard him — meaning the Prophet (ﷺ) — say: Indeed God multiplies the good deed two thousand thousand good deeds! [[The report: 9510 - Narrated in the Musnad of Ahmad: 7932, from Yazid ibn Harun, with this chain.
It is a sound hadith. We have discussed its takhrij in full in the Musnad.
Ibn Kathir 2: 451 mentioned it from the Musnad narration, then transmitted it from Ibn Abi Hatim by two chains.
He mentioned it again from Ibn Abi Hatim's narration, at the commentary on verse 38 of Surah al-Tawbah (vol. 4 pp. 168-169).
Al-Suyuti 2: 163 mentioned it and very briefly cited its takhrij, not attributing it to anyone other than al-Tabari. He mentioned something similar before it and attributed it to Ibn Abi Shaybah only.]]

Others said: Rather, that refers specifically to the Emigrants (muhajirun), to the exclusion of the people of the desert and the Bedouins. And they argued for that with what:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 39–40 (part 2 of 2):

٩٥١١ - Muhammad ibn Harun Abu Nashit narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated to us, from ʿAtiyya al-ʿAwfi, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmayr, who said: This verse was revealed concerning the Bedouin Arabs: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed, he will have ten times the like of it﴾ [Surah al-Anʿam: 60]. He said: A man said: "What is for the Emigrants (al-Muhajirun)?" He said: "Something greater than that: ʿAllah does not wrong an atom's weight, and if it is a good deed He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward," and when Allah says of something that it is "great," it is great.

[Note on the hadith No. 9511: The isnad of this report is weak, because of ʿAtiyya al-ʿAwfi. We have already explained his weakness earlier: 305.
As for al-Tabari's teacher, "Muhammad ibn Harun ibn Ibrahim al-Rabaʿi": he is trustworthy (thiqa). He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.
Ibn Kathir transmitted the hadith, 2: 450, from the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim, through the route of Fudayl ibn Marzuq, with this isnad. He did not mention anything in its takhrij or its ʿilla.
And al-Suyuti mentioned it, 2: 162–163, and added its attribution to Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani.]

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two opinions regarding this matter is the view of the one who said: "This verse refers to the Emigrants, not the Bedouin Arabs." That is because it is not permissible that there be in the reports of Allah or the reports of His Messenger ﷺ anything that contradicts another part of them. Since the promise of Allah that whoever of His believing servants brings a good deed will receive ten times its like as reward, and that He will multiply it for whoever of them brings a good deed, is true, and since the two reports we have mentioned from him ﷺ are both sound, it is not permissible except that one of them is general (mujmal) and the other explained (mufassar), since his ﷺ reports confirm one another. Given that this is so, it is correct that the report of Abu Hurayra means that a good deed is multiplied for the believing Emigrants two thousand thousand times, and for the Bedouin believers among them ten times its like, in accordance with what Ibn ʿUmar narrated from the Prophet ﷺ; and that His saying: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed, he will have ten times the like of it﴾ means: whoever of the believing Bedouins brings a good deed, he will have ten times its like; and whoever of their Emigrants brings a good deed, it will be multiplied for him, and Allah will give him from Himself — meaning, will give him from His own — "a great reward," meaning: a great recompense (ʿiwad) for his good deed, and that great recompense is Paradise, as:

٩٥١٢ - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Sadaqa ibn Abi Sahl narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAmr narrated to us, from Zadhan, from Ibn Masʿud: "and gives from Himself a great reward," i.e., Paradise, which He gives.
[Note on the report No. 9512: This is from the earlier report No. 9508.]

٩٥١٣ - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ʿAbbad ibn Abi Salih informed me, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, regarding his saying: "and gives from Himself a great reward," he said: The great reward is Paradise.
[Note on the report No. 9513: "ʿAbbad ibn Abi Salih Dhakwan, al-Sammān" is "ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Salih." Al-Bukhari said in al-Saghir: "munkar al-hadith" (weak in narration). Ibn Maʿin said: "thiqa," and al-Saji said: "thiqa, except that he narrated from his father what was not corroborated." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]

٩٥١٤ - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "and gives from Himself a great reward," he said: "a great reward" is Paradise.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 39–40 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And what would it have harmed them had they believed in God and the Last Day and spent of what God has provided for them? God is ever Knowing of them.﴾ (39)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: What harm would it be upon these people who spend their wealth to be seen by people, and do not believe in God or the Last Day, ﴿had they believed in God and the Last Day﴾, had they affirmed that God is One with no partner, sincerely devoted monotheism to Him, been certain of the resurrection after death, and affirmed that God will recompense them for their deeds on the Day of Resurrection; ﴿and spent of what God has provided for them﴾, meaning: and paid the zakat of their wealth which God provided them and gave them, willingly, and not spent it to be seen by people, seeking mention and pride among the people of disbelief in God, and false praise among people; ﴿and God was﴾, regarding those whom He described, that they spend their wealth to be seen by people in hypocrisy, while they are deniers of God and the Last Day; ﴿Knowing﴾, meaning: possessing knowledge of them and their deeds, [[In the manuscript: "dhu 'ilm" in the nominative case, and there is no harm in it.]] and of what they intend and desire by spending the wealth they spend, and that they desire by it showing off, reputation and praise among people. He preserves their deeds for them, nothing of them is hidden from Him, until He recompenses them for them with their reward when they return to Him.

* *

The interpretation of His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Indeed, God does not wrong [even] the weight of an atom. And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward.﴾ (40)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "And what would it have harmed them had they believed in God and the Last Day and spent of what God has provided for them?" Indeed God does not diminish for anyone of His creation who spends in His cause from what He has provided him, any of the reward of his spending in this world, nor of its recompense on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿The weight of an atom﴾, meaning: what would weigh it and be according to its heaviness in weight; but He recompenses him for it and rewards him for it, as:

9502 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: that he recited, "Indeed, God does not wrong [even] the weight of an atom. And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it," and said: "That my good deeds exceed my evil deeds by the weight of an atom is dearer to me than the world and all that is in it." [[Forgiveness, O God! The publisher of this printed edition commits countless errors in distorting the text, and alters it without basis in understanding or trustworthiness. He did not read the manuscript well as it was written, so he made what was in it meaningless and wrote in its place: "That my good deeds exceed what weighs an atom is dearer to me than the world and all that is in it." I do not know, how much he would have been better off without such a reprehensible act!]]

9503 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: Some of the people of knowledge used to say: That my good deeds exceed my evil deeds by the weight of an atom is dearer to me than that the entire world be mine.

* *

As for the "atom" (dharrah), it is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said about it, as:

9504 - Ishaq ibn Wahb al-Wasiti narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Shabib ibn Bishr narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "the weight of an atom," he said: the head of a red ant. [[The report: 9504 - "Ishaq ibn Wahb ibn Ziyad al-'Allaf," Abu Ya'qub al-Wasiti. Al-Bukhari, Ibn Majah, Abu Zur'ah and Abu Hatim narrated from him. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.
And "Abu 'Asim" is: al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad. Has passed several times.
And "Shayb ibn Bishr" narrated from Anas and 'Ikrimah, reliable but weak in narration, makes many errors. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

* *

= Abu Ja'far said: Ishaq ibn Wahb said to me: Yazid ibn Harun said: They claim that this red atom has no weight. [[In the printed edition: "this red worm," which is a pure error; in the manuscript: "these red worms," which is a distortion.]]

* *

With something similar to what we have said regarding this, reports have been authenticated from the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

9505 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, both saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: 'Imran narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas: that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: Indeed God does not wrong a believer a good deed, for which he is given provision in this world, and is recompensed for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is fed by it in this world, and when the Day of Resurrection comes, he will have no good deed. [[The report: 9505 - Abu Dawud: this is al-Tayalisi.
"'Imran": is Ibn Dawar al-Qattan.
The hadith is in Musnad al-Tayalisi: 2011, with this chain.
Ahmad in his Musnad narrated it through Hammam, from Qatadah: 12264, 12291, 14063 (vol. 3 pp. 123, 125, 283, Halabi edition).
Likewise Muslim 2: 344-345 narrated it through Hammam, then narrated it through other routes.
Ibn Kathir 2: 450 mentioned it from the narration of al-Tayalisi.
al-Suyuti 2: 163 mentioned it and attributed it to these.]]

It was narrated to us by Musa ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi, saying: Ja'far ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Zayd ibn Aslam informed us, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar: By Him in whose hand is my soul, none of you is more insistent in demanding a right which he sees as his due from the believers regarding their brothers when they see that they have been saved from the Fire, saying: "Our Lord, our brothers, who used to pray with us, fast with us, perform Hajj with us, and fight with us, have been seized by the Fire!" God says to them: "Go, and whomever you recognize by his form, bring him out!" And He forbids their forms to the Fire, so they find a man whom the Fire has seized up to the middle of his shins, and up to his knees, and up to his waist; so they bring out many people from it. Then they return and speak, and He says: "Go, and whomever you find in his heart the weight of a qirat of good, bring him out!" So they bring out many people from it. Then they return and speak, and He keeps saying that to them until He says: "Go, and whomever you find in his heart the weight of an atom, bring him out!" = Abu Sa'id, whenever he narrated this hadith, would say: If you do not believe, then recite: "Indeed, God does not wrong [even] the weight of an atom. And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward." = They will say: "Our Lord, we have left in it no good."
[[The report: 9506 - Ja'far ibn 'Awn ibn 'Amr ibn Huraith, al-Makhzumi al-Kufi: reliable. The compilers all narrated from him.
The hadith is part of a long hadith on intercession. The imams narrated it in the collections by many routes, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri:
Al-Tayalisi narrated it: 2179, from Kharijah ibn Mus'ab, from Zayd.
Ahmad in his Musnad narrated it: 11144 (3: 16-17, Halabi), through 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Zayd.
He also narrated it: 11922 (3: 94-95, Halabi), through Ma'mar, from Zayd.
Muslim 1: 66-67 narrated it through Hafs ibn Maysarah, from Zayd.
Then he narrated it, without mentioning its wording, through Ja'far ibn 'Awn, from Hisham ibn Sa'd. This is the route narrated by al-Tabari here.
The reference to al-Bukhari's narration will come in the following hadith.]]

9507 - And Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: My father and Shu'ayb ibn al-Layth narrated to me, from al-Layth, from Khalid ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Hilal, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), with something similar. [[The report: 9507 - "al-Layth": is Ibn Sa'd. Khalid ibn Yazid: is al-Jumahi al-Misri. "Ibn Abi Hilal": is Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal al-Misri.
The hadith repeats the preceding one.
Al-Bukhari 13: 358-361 (Fath) narrated it through al-Layth ibn Sa'd with this chain. Ibn Kathir 2: 449 mentioned a portion of it and attributed it to the two Sahihs.]]

* *

Others said regarding this, with what:

9508 - It was narrated to me by al-Muthanna, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Sadaqah ibn Abi Sahl narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amr narrated to us, from Zadhan, who said: I came to Ibn Mas'ud and he said: When the Day of Resurrection comes, God will gather the first and the last, then a caller from God will call out: "Whoever was seeking a wrong, let him come to his right and take it!" He said: By God, a man will be pleased that a right is due to him from his father, or his child, or his wife, so he takes it from him, even if he is young. [[In the printed edition: "then by God the child is pleased," and in the manuscript: "then by God the one who ... ," and the correct reading of it is "the man" as I have established from the references mentioned below. "Dhaba li 'ala fulan min al-haqq kadha, yadhubu," meaning it was established and became due to him.]] = And the proof of that is in the Book of God, blessed and exalted: ﴿So when the Horn is blown, there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask one another.﴾ [Surah al-Mu'minun: 101] = Then it will be said to him: "Go to these people and give them their rights" = meaning: give them their rights = He will say: "O Lord, from where, when the world has gone?" God will say to His angels: "O My angels, look into his righteous deeds and give them from them!" If there remains the weight of an atom of good, the angels will say, while He knows better than them: "Our Lord, we have given each person with a right his right, and there remains for him the weight of an atom of good." He will say to the angels: "Multiply it for My servant, and make him enter Paradise by the bounty of My mercy." = And the proof of that in the Book of God: "Indeed, God does not wrong [even] the weight of an atom. And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward," meaning: Paradise, He gives it. If his good deeds run out and his evil deeds remain, the angels will say, while He knows better: "Our God, his good deeds have run out and his evil deeds remain, and many claimants remain!" God will say: "Add to it from their burdens, and write for him a document to the Fire." [[In the printed edition: "place upon it from their burdens," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript. See the following report.]] Sadaqah said: Or a sakk (writ) to Hell; Sadaqah doubted which of the two he said. [[The report: 9508 - Sadaqah ibn Abi Sahl: biographed in al-Ta'jil, p. 185-186. And al-Kabir 2/2/298, no. 2891, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/434-435, no. 1907. They mention no criticism of him, so he is reliable.
His teacher "Abu 'Amr": I do not know who he is, as this kunya is common.
"Zadhan": is al-Kindi the blind. He is a well-known reliable Successor.
See the chain following this one.]]

9509 - And I was told from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd, from Harun ibn 'Antarah, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib who said: I heard Zadhan say: 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud said: The male and female servant will be taken by the hand on the Day of Resurrection, and a caller will call out over the heads of the first and last: "This is so-and-so son of so-and-so; whoever has a right, let him come to his right," so the woman is pleased that a right is due to her from her father, or from her son, or from her brother, or from her husband, [[See the explanation of "yadhubu" above, p. 363, note 1.]] then Ibn Mas'ud recited: ﴿So there will be no kinship among them that Day, nor will they ask one another.﴾ [Surah al-Mu'minun: 101]. God, blessed and exalted, will forgive from his right whatever He wills, and will not forgive anything of the rights of people. He will stand before people and say: "Give to people their rights!" He will say: "Lord, the world has gone, from where shall I give them their rights?" He says: "Take from his righteous deeds, and give each person with a right his right, according to the measure of his injustice." If he was a friend of God, then there remains for him the weight of an atom of excess, He multiplies it for him until He admits him to Paradise by it = Then he recited to us: "Indeed, God does not wrong [even] the weight of an atom" = And if he was a wretched servant, the angel will say: "Lord, his good deeds have run out, and many claimants remain!" He will say: "Take from their evil deeds and add them to his evil deeds, then write for him a writ to the Fire." [[The report: 9509 - It is a repetition of the preceding one in its meaning. But al-Tabari begins it with the vague form "I was told from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd," so this chain is lost by that vagueness.
Ibn Kathir 2: 449-450 transmitted it from Ibn Abi Hatim: "Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, 'Isa ibn Yunus narrated to us, from Harun ibn 'Antarah...," so the weakness at the start of the chain is removed.
Harun ibn 'Antarah: his authentication and biography were passed at: 405.
'Abd Allah ibn al-Sa'ib al-Kindi, also called al-Shaybani, al-Kufi: a well-known reliable narrator. Al-A'mash and al-Thawri narrated from him, and Muslim narrated from him.
This chain, according to Ibn Abi Hatim, is a sound chain.
The report is a statement (mawquf) of Ibn Mas'ud. But I consider it to have the ruling of the marfu'. For what Ibn Mas'ud mentioned is not something known through opinion, and Ibn Mas'ud would not say this on his own; and he is not one who narrates from the People of the Book or accepts Isra'iliyyat.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it, as we have said, then said: "Some of this report has a witness in the authentic hadith." Al-Suyuti narrated it 2: 163 and added its attribution to 'Abd ibn Humayd.
"Al-sakk": the writ. And his saying "sakku" is a verb from "al-sakk," meaning: write for him a writ. This verb is not mentioned in the lexicon books, and this is its witness.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: So the interpretation of the verse according to this interpretation of 'Abd Allah is: Indeed God does not wrong a servant to whom is due the weight of an atom from another servant of His in his return and on the day of meeting Him, or more than that, so that He leaves it upon him and does not take it for the wronged from his wrongdoer; rather He takes it from him for him, and takes from every wrongdoer for every wronged person his due against him. ["Al-tab'ah" (with a fatha on the ta') and "al-tiba'ah" (with a kasra on the ta'): what you have pursued against your companion of injustice or a right you have over him.]
﴿And if it is a good deed, He multiplies it﴾, meaning: and if a good deed is found for him, He multiplies it, in the sense that its reward and its recompense are multiplied for him. ﴿And gives from Himself a great reward﴾, meaning: and gives him from Himself a great reward. "The great reward" is Paradise, according to what 'Abd Allah said.

* *

Both interpretations have a clear meaning, namely the interpretation that Ibn Mas'ud gave and the one that Qatadah gave. We have chosen the first interpretation for its agreement with the report from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), together with the indication of the apparent meaning of the revelation regarding its soundness, since it is in the context of the verse before it, in which God urges spending in His obedience and censures spending in obedience to Satan. Then He connected that with what He promised the hypocrites in His obedience, by His saying: "Indeed God does not wrong [even] the weight of an atom, and if it is a good deed, He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward."

The readers differed concerning His saying: "And if it is a good deed" (wa-in taku hasanatan). The majority of the readers of Iraq recited it: ﴿وَإِنْ تَكُ حَسَنَةً﴾ with the accusative "hasanatan," meaning: and if the weight of the atom is a good deed, He multiplies it.

* *

The majority of the readers of Medina recited it: ﴿وَإِنْ تَكُ حَسَنَةٌ﴾ with the nominative "hasanatun," meaning: and if a good deed is found, as I have mentioned from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud's interpretation of that.

As for His saying "yudā'ifuhā" (He multiplies it), it came with an "alif" and He did not say "yudha'╼ifuhā" (He doubles it), because it is intended, according to the saying of some of the people of the Arabic language: [[Meaning Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 127, whose text is: "yudā'ifuhā" = manifold multiplications, and "yudha''ifuhā" = two-fold.]] He multiplies it in many multiples; and if it were intended in His saying [[Meaning: in the saying of Abu 'Ubaydah.]] "yudha''ifu dhālika di'fayn" (He doubles that twofold), it would have been said "yudha''ifuhā" with the doubled letter.

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed about those whom God promised by this verse what He promised them in it.

Some of them said: They are all the people of faith in God and in Muhammad (ﷺ). And they argued for that with what:

9510 - Al-Fadl ibn al-Sabah narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Mubarak ibn Fudalah, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi who said: I met Abu Hurayrah and said to him: It has reached me that you say: Indeed the good deed is multiplied a thousand thousand good deeds! He said: And what amazes you about that? By God, I heard him — meaning the Prophet (ﷺ) — say: Indeed God multiplies the good deed two thousand thousand good deeds! [[The report: 9510 - Narrated in the Musnad of Ahmad: 7932, from Yazid ibn Harun, with this chain.
It is a sound hadith. We have discussed its takhrij in full in the Musnad.
Ibn Kathir 2: 451 mentioned it from the Musnad narration, then transmitted it from Ibn Abi Hatim by two chains.
He mentioned it again from Ibn Abi Hatim's narration, at the commentary on verse 38 of Surah al-Tawbah (vol. 4 pp. 168-169).
Al-Suyuti 2: 163 mentioned it and very briefly cited its takhrij, not attributing it to anyone other than al-Tabari. He mentioned something similar before it and attributed it to Ibn Abi Shaybah only.]]

Others said: Rather, that refers specifically to the Emigrants (muhajirun), to the exclusion of the people of the desert and the Bedouins. And they argued for that with what:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 39–40 (part 2 of 2):

٩٥١١ - Muhammad ibn Harun Abu Nashit narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, saying: Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated to us, from ʿAtiyya al-ʿAwfi, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmayr, who said: This verse was revealed concerning the Bedouin Arabs: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed, he will have ten times the like of it﴾ [Surah al-Anʿam: 60]. He said: A man said: "What is for the Emigrants (al-Muhajirun)?" He said: "Something greater than that: ʿAllah does not wrong an atom's weight, and if it is a good deed He multiplies it and gives from Himself a great reward," and when Allah says of something that it is "great," it is great.

[Note on the hadith No. 9511: The isnad of this report is weak, because of ʿAtiyya al-ʿAwfi. We have already explained his weakness earlier: 305.
As for al-Tabari's teacher, "Muhammad ibn Harun ibn Ibrahim al-Rabaʿi": he is trustworthy (thiqa). He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.
Ibn Kathir transmitted the hadith, 2: 450, from the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim, through the route of Fudayl ibn Marzuq, with this isnad. He did not mention anything in its takhrij or its ʿilla.
And al-Suyuti mentioned it, 2: 162–163, and added its attribution to Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani.]

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The more correct of the two opinions regarding this matter is the view of the one who said: "This verse refers to the Emigrants, not the Bedouin Arabs." That is because it is not permissible that there be in the reports of Allah or the reports of His Messenger ﷺ anything that contradicts another part of them. Since the promise of Allah that whoever of His believing servants brings a good deed will receive ten times its like as reward, and that He will multiply it for whoever of them brings a good deed, is true, and since the two reports we have mentioned from him ﷺ are both sound, it is not permissible except that one of them is general (mujmal) and the other explained (mufassar), since his ﷺ reports confirm one another. Given that this is so, it is correct that the report of Abu Hurayra means that a good deed is multiplied for the believing Emigrants two thousand thousand times, and for the Bedouin believers among them ten times its like, in accordance with what Ibn ʿUmar narrated from the Prophet ﷺ; and that His saying: ﴿Whoever brings a good deed, he will have ten times the like of it﴾ means: whoever of the believing Bedouins brings a good deed, he will have ten times its like; and whoever of their Emigrants brings a good deed, it will be multiplied for him, and Allah will give him from Himself — meaning, will give him from His own — "a great reward," meaning: a great recompense (ʿiwad) for his good deed, and that great recompense is Paradise, as:

٩٥١٢ - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Sadaqa ibn Abi Sahl narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿAmr narrated to us, from Zadhan, from Ibn Masʿud: "and gives from Himself a great reward," i.e., Paradise, which He gives.
[Note on the report No. 9512: This is from the earlier report No. 9508.]

٩٥١٣ - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: ʿAbbad ibn Abi Salih informed me, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, regarding his saying: "and gives from Himself a great reward," he said: The great reward is Paradise.
[Note on the report No. 9513: "ʿAbbad ibn Abi Salih Dhakwan, al-Sammān" is "ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Salih." Al-Bukhari said in al-Saghir: "munkar al-hadith" (weak in narration). Ibn Maʿin said: "thiqa," and al-Saji said: "thiqa, except that he narrated from his father what was not corroborated." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]

٩٥١٤ - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "and gives from Himself a great reward," he said: "a great reward" is Paradise.

Abu Ja'far said: Its meaning, exalted is His praise, is: Indeed, Allah does not wrong His servants by the weight of an atom, so how will it be with them ﴿when We bring from every nation a witness﴾, meaning, one who will testify against it concerning its deeds, and concerning whether it affirmed or denied its messengers, ﴿and We bring you, Muhammad, as a witness against these﴾, meaning, against your nation, ﴿a witness﴾. He says: a witness, as follows:[[See the explanation of "al-shahid" (the witness) above: 1:376-378 / 3:97, 145 / 6:60, 75 / ...]]

9515 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, concerning ﴿How then, when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these﴾: He said: The prophets will come on the Day of Resurrection. Some of them will have with them from their people one, or two, or ten, and fewer or more than that, until the people of Lut (ﷺ) are brought, of whom only his two daughters believed with him. It will be said to them: "Did you convey what you were sent with?" They will say: "Yes." It will be said: "Who will bear witness?" They will say: "The nation of Muhammad (ﷺ)!" It will be said to them: "Bear witness, for the messengers have entrusted a testimony to you.[[In the printed edition: "Do you bear witness that the messengers..." I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]] So by what do you bear witness?" They will say: "Our Lord, we bear witness that they have conveyed, just as they bore witness in this world to the conveying." It will be said: "Who will testify to that?" They will say: "Muhammad (ﷺ)." Muhammad (peace be upon him) will be summoned, and he will testify that his nation has affirmed, and that the messengers have conveyed. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation, that you may be witnesses over the people, and the Messenger may be a witness over you﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:143].

9516 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said concerning His saying: ﴿How then, when We bring from every nation a witness﴾: He said: "Its messenger, who will testify against it that he conveyed to them what Allah sent him with to them." ﴿And We bring you as a witness against these﴾: He said: "When the Prophet (ﷺ) passed by them, his eyes would overflow with tears."

9517 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan narrated to us, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah, concerning His saying: ﴿And a witness and a witnessed﴾ [al-Buruj 85:3], he said: "The witness is Muhammad, and the witnessed is the Day of Congregation (Friday). That is His saying: 'How then, when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these.'"

9518 - Abdullah ibn Muhammad al-Zuhri narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from Ja'far ibn Amr ibn Huraith, from his father, from Abdullah: "How then, when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these," he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: ﴿When You caused me to die, You were the Watcher over them, and You are Witness over all things﴾.[[The hadith, no. 9518. Sufyan is Ibn Uyaynah.

Al-Mas'udi here is Ma'n ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, and he is trustworthy (thiqah). The Two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated from him. Al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir 4/1/390, and Ibn Abi Hatim in 4/1/277.

"Ja'far ibn Amr ibn Huraith al-Makhzumi": trustworthy. Al-Bukhari included him in 1/2/193, and Ibn Abi Hatim in 1/1/484.

His father, "Amr ibn Huraith": a Companion (sahabi).

This hadith, although its chain is sound, I have not found except through al-Tabari's narration. Ibn Kathir did not attribute it to anyone else (2:453), and likewise al-Suyuti (2:164).

See the hadith that follows it.

The verse is an embedding (tadmin) of the verse of Surah al-Ma'idah, 117.]]

9519 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Wazir narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from al-Mas'udi, from al-Qasim: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Ibn Mas'ud: "Recite to me." He said: "Shall I recite to you, when it was revealed to you?" He said: "I love to hear it from someone other than myself." So Ibn Mas'ud recited Surah al-Nisa until he reached: ﴿How then, when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you as a witness against these﴾. He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) was moved to tears, and Ibn Mas'ud stopped. Al-Mas'udi said: Ja'far ibn Amr ibn Huraith narrated to me, from his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "A witness over them for as long as I am among them. But when You cause me to die, You were the Watcher over them, and You are a witness over all things."[[The hadith, no. 9519. Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Wazir, whose name Abu al-Wazir is Umar, is Ibn Mutarrif al-Makki, a client of the Banu Hashim. He is trustworthy; Muhammad ibn Bashshar and others declared him trustworthy. He is included in al-Tahdhib, in al-Kabir 1/1/333, and in Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/114-115.

In reality this hadith consists of two hadiths:

The first: the narration of al-Mas'udi (Ma'n ibn Abd al-Rahman) from al-Qasim. The apparent identity of this al-Qasim is his brother, al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Mas'ud. He is a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i). However, he did not live to narrate from his grandfather Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, and he is not stated here to have narrated "from Ibn Mas'ud," so that it would be a broken chain (munqati'). Thus it is a mursal hadith.

But this first of the two hadiths is established and sound through connected chains. Al-Bukhari narrated it in 9:81 (Fath), through al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Ubaydah, from Abdullah. Likewise Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad: 3606 and 4118, through al-A'mash, with the same chain. Ahmad also narrated it in 3550, from the narration of Abu Hayyan al-Ashja'i, from Ibn Mas'ud, and in 3551, through Abu Razin, from Ibn Mas'ud.

Ibn Kathir quoted it in Fada'il al-Qur'an, p. 77, from al-Bukhari, then said: "The group (al-jama'ah) narrated it, except Ibn Majah, through several routes from al-A'mash, and it has routes whose full exposition would be lengthy."

He also quoted it in his tafsir, 2:452-453, from al-Bukhari as well, then said: "It has been narrated through multiple routes from Ibn Mas'ud, so it is definitively established. Ahmad narrated it through Abu Hayyan and Abu Razin, from him."

Al-Suyuti quoted it in 2:163, and added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il.

The second: the narration of al-Mas'udi, from Ja'far ibn Amr ibn Huraith, from his father. This repeats the previous hadith, no. 9518, but here it is given as a hadith from Amr ibn Huraith, without mention of his narrating from Ibn Mas'ud. It is therefore a mursal of a Companion (mursal sahabi). It is sound in every case.

Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 3:319, through Ja'far ibn Awn, from al-Mas'udi, from Ja'far ibn Amr ibn Huraith, from his father, in extended form, with the story of Ibn Mas'ud reciting these verses to the Prophet (ﷺ). In it is the text found here: "a witness over them for as long as I am among them..." So the origin of the hadith is sound and established. For this reason al-Hakim said: "This hadith has a sound chain, but the two Shaykhs did not record it." Al-Dhahabi agreed with him.

Al-Suyuti quoted al-Hakim's narration, somewhat abridged, at 2:163, and did not attribute it to anyone else.]]

The commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾ (4:42).

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His praise be mentioned, means by this: On the Day when We bring forth from every nation a witness, and We bring you, O Muhammad, as a witness over your nation, ﴿those who disbelieved will wish﴾, that is, those who denied the Oneness of Allah and disobeyed His Messenger will long, ﴿that the earth were leveled over them﴾. [[See the explanation of "wadd" (wishing/loving) earlier: 2:470 / 5:542.]]

* *

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of this.

The common reciters of the people of the Hijaz, Mecca and Medina recited it: ﴿law tusawwa bihimu al-ardu﴾ with the sin doubled (tashdid) and the waw, and with the ta' vowelled with a fatha, meaning: "if the earth would level itself over them" (latatasawwa), then the second ta' was assimilated into the sin, the intended meaning being that they wish they would become dust, so that they and the earth would be equal.

Others recited it: ﴿law tusawwa bihimu al-ardu﴾ with the ta' vowelled with a fatha and the sin without doubling (takhfif). This is the common recitation of the reciters of Kufa, with the first meaning, except that they dropped the doubling of the sin, arguing that the Arabs scarcely combine two doublings in a single letter.

Others recited it: ﴿law tusawwa bihimu al-ardu﴾, meaning: "if Allah and the earth made them equal", so that they become dust like it, by His making them so, as He does to those beasts whom it is mentioned He will do this to.

Abu Ja'far said: All these recitations are close in meaning, and whichever of them the reader recites is correct, because whoever among them wishes to be dust on that Day wishes to be so by Allah's creating him so; and whoever wishes that Allah had made him so, has wished to be dust. Nevertheless, the recitation most preferable to me is: ﴿law tusawwa bihimu al-ardu﴾ with the ta' vowelled with a fatha and the sin unduplicated, out of dislike of combining two doublings in one letter, and to harmonize the meaning between this and His saying: ﴿And the disbeliever will say: "Would that I were dust!"﴾ (78:40). Allah informed about them that they wish they were dust, and He did not report that they said, "Would that I were dust!" Likewise His saying, "if the earth were leveled over them," so that they themselves would be leveled. This is more preferable to me, so that it accords with the meaning He reported about them in His saying, "Would that I were dust!"

As for His saying: ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾, the people of interpretation have explained it to mean: ﴿and their limbs will not conceal from Allah any statement, even though their mouths deny it.﴾

Those who said this:

9520 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, saying: Amr related to us, from Mutarrif, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said: "I heard Allah say: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾ (6:23), and in another verse He said: ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah any statement.﴾" Ibn Abbas said: As for His saying, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists," when they saw that none would enter Paradise except the people of Islam, they said, "Come, let us deny!" So they said, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists!" Then Allah sealed their mouths, and their hands and feet spoke, so they will not conceal from Allah any statement.

9521 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from a man, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr who said: A man came to Ibn Abbas and said: "Things are confusing to me in the Qur'an?" He said: "What is it? Do you doubt the Qur'an?" He said: "Not doubt, but difference!" He said: "Then state what differs for you." He said: "I hear Allah say: ﴿Then their trial will be only that they said, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists'﴾ (6:23), and He said, "and they will not conceal from Allah any statement," yet they concealed!" Ibn Abbas said: As for His saying, "Then their trial will be only that they said, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists'," when they see on the Day of Resurrection that Allah forgives the people of Islam and forgives sins, but does not forgive polytheism, and no sin is too great for Him to forgive, the polytheists denied and said, "By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists," hoping He would forgive them. So He sealed their mouths, and their hands and feet spoke of what they used to do. At that: ﴿Those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah any statement.﴾

9522 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Zubayr related to us, from al-Dahhak: that Nafi' ibn al-Azraq came to Ibn Abbas and said: "O Ibn Abbas, the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah any statement﴾, and His saying: ﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾?" Ibn Abbas said to him: "I think you got up from among your companions and said, 'Ibn Abbas has thrown at me the ambiguous verses of the Qur'an.' When you return to them, inform them that Allah will gather the people on the Day of Resurrection in one open plain [[al-baqi': an open, spacious area of land, in which there may be some trees.]], and the polytheists will say, 'Allah does not accept anything from anyone except from those who affirm His Oneness!' So they will say, 'Come, let us lie!' [[In the printed edition: "come, let us deny" (tajhad), differing from the manuscript; I have adopted what is in the manuscript. The printed reading has no clear meaning to me, while the manuscript's reading is correct, though lexicographers have been brief in establishing this sense. Here "naqul" derives from "qawl" and is meant as lying or insinuation, which I have encountered repeatedly in the books of biography, among them in Ibn Hisham's Sira, vol. 3, p. 58, in the report of the killing of Ka'b al-Ashraf, where Muhammad ibn Maslama said to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "O Messenger of Allah, we must say [something]!" The Messenger of Allah said: "Say what you wish, for you are free from blame in that." This is similar in meaning to lying.]] Then He will ask them, and they will say, 'By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists.' He said: Then their mouths will be sealed, and their limbs will be questioned, so their limbs will testify against them that they were polytheists. At that point they will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah any statement."

9523 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my uncle related to me, saying: my father related to us, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they will not conceal from Allah any statement," meaning: that the earth be leveled with the mountains and the earth, over them. [[In the printed edition: "that the earth be leveled with the mountains over them," omitting the second "the earth"; the correct text is that of the manuscript.]]

So the interpretation of the verse according to this statement attributed to Ibn Abbas is: On that Day those who disbelieved and disobeyed the Messenger will wish that the earth were leveled over them, and they would not have concealed from Allah any statement [[In the printed edition: "and they will not conceal from Allah any statement," which is a gross error; the correct text is that of the manuscript.]] — as if they wished that they were leveled with the earth, and that they had not concealed from Allah any statement.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: On that Day they will not conceal from Allah any statement, and they will wish that the earth were leveled over them. Not a single word of their speech is concealed from Allah, since He, may His remembrance be exalted, knows all their speech and their affairs; so if they conceal it with their tongues by denying it, nothing of it is hidden from Him. [[In the printed edition: "if they conceal it with their tongues," which is also a gross error; the correct text is that of the manuscript.]]

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His majesty be exalted, "O you who have believed," He means: O you who have affirmed God and His Messenger. "Do not approach prayer," do not pray. "While you are intoxicated," *sukara* (سكارى), which is the plural of *sakran* (سكران, intoxicated). "Until you know what you are saying," in your prayer, so that you distinguish what God has commanded you to recite in it, or what He has urged you to say in it, from what He has forbidden you and warned you against.

* *

Then the exegetes (*ahl al-ta'wil*) differed concerning the *sukr* (سكر, intoxication) that God meant by His words: "Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated."

Some of them said: He meant intoxication from drink.

Those who said this:

9524. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, from 'Ali: that he, 'Abd al-Rahman, and another man drank wine, and 'Abd al-Rahman led them in prayer and recited: ﴿Say: O disbelievers﴾, and he confused its words, so this was revealed: "Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated."

9525. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from 'Abd Allah ibn Habib: that 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf prepared food and drink, and invited a group of the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ. They ate and drank until they became drunk. They put 'Ali forward to lead them in the Maghrib prayer, and he recited: "Say: O disbelievers, I do not worship what you worship, and you are not worshippers of what I worship, and I am not a worshipper of what you have worshipped, nor are you worshippers of what I worship. For you is your religion, and for me is my religion." So God, blessed and exalted, revealed this verse: "O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying."

9526. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated," before wine was prohibited. Then God said: "O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated," the verse.

9527. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Abu Razin concerning His words: "O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated." He said: This was revealed while they were drinking wine. He said: And this was before the prohibition of wine was revealed.

9528. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Abu Razin, who said: They used to drink after the verse in "al-Baqarah" was revealed,[[That is the verse of Surat al-Baqarah 2:219: "They ask you about wine and gambling."]] and after the one in "al-Nisa'," and when the one in "al-Ma'idah" was revealed, they abandoned it.[[That is the verses of Surat al-Ma'idah 5:90–91: "O you who have believed, indeed wine, gambling, stone altars, and divining arrows are an abomination from the work of Satan, so avoid it."]]

9529. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His words: "And you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying," he said: They were forbidden to pray while they were intoxicated, then the prohibition of wine abrogated it (*naskh*, abrogation).

9530. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

9531. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah concerning His words: "Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated," he said: They used to avoid intoxication at the times of the prayers, then it was abrogated by the prohibition of wine.

9532. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Abu Wa'il, Abu Razin and Ibrahim concerning His words: "O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated," and "They ask you about wine and gambling. Say: In them is great sin and benefits for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit" [Surat al-Baqarah: 219], and His words: "You take from it intoxicant and good provision" [Surat al-Nahl: 67]. They said: This was before the prohibition of wine was revealed.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "Do not approach prayer while you are drunk from sleep."

Those who said this:

9533. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Nabit, from al-Dahhak: "Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated." He said: It is not for one who approaches it to be a drunkard from drink; rather, by it is meant the intoxication of sleep.[[In the printed edition: "He said: the intoxication of sleep," omitting what lies between. In the manuscript: "for one who approaches it intoxicated; by it is meant the intoxication of sleep," with a blank space in the speech, and the letter "ṭ" was placed in the margin of the manuscript to mean an error. I have made the effort to read it as I have established it.]]

9534. Ahmad ibn Hazim al-Ghifari narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from al-Dahhak: "O you who have believed, do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated," he said: By it is not meant the intoxication of wine; rather, by it is meant the intoxication of sleep.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions regarding the interpretation of the verse is the interpretation of those who said: This is a prohibition from God to the believers against approaching prayer while they are intoxicated from drink, before wine was prohibited, because of the widely transmitted reports from the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ that this is so, a prohibition from God; and that this verse was revealed concerning those whom I mentioned it was revealed concerning.

* *

If someone says to us: How can that be its meaning, when the intoxicated person in a state of loss of his reason is like the insane person in a state of loss of his reason, and you are one who considers the imposition of religious obligation on the insane impossible, since they lack understanding of what they are commanded and forbidden?

It is said to him: If the intoxicated person were in the same position as the insane person, it would not be permissible to command or forbid him. But the intoxicated person is one who understands what he does and what he leaves undone, except that the drink has weighed down his tongue and the parts of his body and numbed them, until he is unable to perform his recitation in his prayer and its obligatory limits upon him in it, without losing his reason. So he is aware and understanding of what he has been commanded and forbidden, but is unable to perform some of it due to the numbness of his body from the drink. As for one who has reached a point where he does not understand what he does or leaves undone, that one has moved from intoxication to madness and the condition of the insane, and it is not that one who was addressed by His words: "Do not approach prayer," because that one is insane; rather, the intoxicated person was addressed, and the intoxicated person is as we have described his condition.

* *

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿nor one who is in a state of janabah, except passing through, until you have bathed﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: The exegetes differed in the interpretation of this. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: "Do not approach prayer while you are intoxicated until you know what you are saying," and "nor approach it in a state of *janabah* (جنب, ritual impurity requiring a full bath), except passing through," meaning: except that you are passing along a road, i.e., travelling, "until you have bathed."[[See the explanation of "al-junub" earlier, p. 340.]]

Those who said this:

9535. Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, both saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu Mijlaz, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His words: "nor one in a state of janabah except passing through," he said: The traveller. Ibn al-Muthanna said: "on a journey."

9536. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, his words: "nor one in a state of janabah except passing through," he says: Do not approach prayer while you are in a state of janabah if you find water; but if you do not find water, I have permitted you to perform tayammum (تيمم, dry ablution) with the earth.

9537. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Minhal, from 'Abbad ibn 'Abd Allah, or from Zirr, from 'Ali, may God be pleased with him: "nor one in a state of janabah except passing through," he said: Except that you are travellers and do not find water, then perform tayammum.[[In the printed and manuscript editions: "then you do not find water," and the correct reading is what I have established.]][[Report 9537: "'Abbad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Asadi." He narrated from 'Ali, and al-Minhal ibn 'Amr narrated from him. Al-Bukhari said: "There is something to examine in him." Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy (*al-thiqat*), and Ahmad spoke about him. His biography is in al-Tahdhib. See the following report, no. 9540.]]

9538. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr concerning His words: "nor one in a state of janabah except passing through," he said: The traveller.

9539. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu Mijlaz, from Ibn 'Abbas, the same.

9540. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Harun ibn al-Mughirah narrated to us, from 'Anbasah, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Minhal ibn 'Amr, from 'Abbad ibn 'Abd Allah, from 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, who said: It was revealed concerning travel: "nor one in a state of janabah except passing through," and "passing through" (*'abir al-sabil*) is the traveller who, if he does not find water, performs tayammum.

9541. Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Harun narrated to us, from Ibn Mujahid, from his father: "nor one in a state of janabah except passing through," he said: The traveller, if he does not find water, then he performs tayammum, then he enters and prays. [[In the printed edition: "then he performs tayammum and prays," omitting "then he enters," as if he did not know what was meant by it and so omitted it; this is a bad and ugly action. His words "then he enters" mean: the mosque.]]

9542. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His words: "nor one in a state of janabah except passing through," he said: It is the man who is on a journey, and janabah afflicts him, so he performs tayammum and prays.

9543. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "nor one in a state of janabah except passing through," he said: Travellers who do not find water, so they perform tayammum with clean earth, since they did not find water to bathe with. [[In the printed edition: "until they find water and bathe," and in the manuscript: "li yajidu al-ma'a fa-yaghtasilu" [with an error]; the correct reading is what I have established.]]

9544. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid concerning His words: "nor one in a state of janabah except passing through," he said: Travellers who do not find water.

9545. Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Mis'ar, from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim concerning His words: "nor one in a state of janabah except passing through," he said: Except that they are travellers, and they do not find water, so they perform tayammum.[[In the printed edition: "so they do not find water and perform tayammum," and I have established what is in the manuscript, except "fa-lam yajidu" [they did not find], since it had "fa-la yajidu" [they do not find] in it.]]

9546. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Mansur, from al-Hakam: "nor one in a state of janabah except passing through," he said: The traveller whom janabah afflicts, and he does not find water, so he performs tayammum.

9547. 9550. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir, who said: We used to hear that it was on a journey.

9551. Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: "nor one in a state of janabah except passing through," he said: It is the traveller who does not find water, so he must perform tayammum and pray; he performs tayammum and prays. He said: My father used to say this.

* *

Others said the meaning of that is: Do not approach the place of prayer (*al-musalla*) while you are intoxicated, until you know what you are saying, and do not approach it in a state of janabah until you have bathed, except passing through it, meaning: except passing through it in order to leave it.

The proponents of this view said: The word "prayer" (*al-salah*) was put in the place of "the place of prayer" (*al-musalla*) and "the mosque," since the prayer of the Muslims in their mosques in those days was such that they did not stay away from gathering (*al-tajmi'*) in them. So the prohibition against approaching prayer sufficed as a mention of the mosques and the place of prayer in which they pray.[[In the printed edition: "al-tajma' fiha" [gathering in it]; "al-tajmi'" means: attending congregational prayer, or establishing congregational prayer.]]
