**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 43 (part 2 of 7):**

9567 - Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Al-Layth told me, saying: Yazid ibn Abi Habib told me, concerning the words of God: "Nor [approach prayer] in a state of janabah (major ritual impurity), except while passing through [the mosque]." That men of the Ansar had their doors opening onto the mosque, and they would become junub with no water at hand. They would want water but would find no way to pass except through the mosque. So God, blessed and exalted, revealed: "Nor [approach prayer] in a state of janabah, except while passing through."

9568 - Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Shu'bah, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, concerning "nor in a state of janabah, except while passing through." He said: One does not cross through the mosque, except if he finds no other path.

9569 - Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Harun told us, from Ibn Mujahid, from his father: The junub does not pass through the mosque, taking it as a path.

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The more correct of the two views in interpreting this is the interpretation of those who understood it as: "Nor in a state of janabah, except those passing through a path in it." This is because He had already explained the ruling for the traveller who lacks water while junub, in His words: ﴿And if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself, or you have touched women, and you find no water, then seek clean earth﴾. Thus it was known from this that His words "nor in a state of janabah, except while passing through, until you wash" — had they referred to the traveller, would have had no meaningful purpose in the repetition of it in His words "and if you are ill or on a journey", since its ruling had already been mentioned before that.

* *

Since this is so, the interpretation of the verse is: O you who believe, do not approach the mosques for prayer while you are intoxicated, until you know what you are saying, nor approach them also in a state of janabah until you wash, except while passing through.

* *

"Ibn al-sabil" (the passer-by): the one who crosses through a place in passing and traversal. It is said of it: "I crossed this road, so I cross it crossing (ʿabran) and crossing (ʿubūran)." From this comes the saying: "So-and-so crossed the river," when he traversed it and passed over. From it is also said of a camel strong for journeys: "She is ʿubr asfār and ʿabr asfār" [[In the printed edition the second "ʿabr asfār" was omitted, as if it were thought to be a repetition. Rather, he meant one with a ḍamma on the ʿayn and a sukūn on the bāʾ, and the other with a fatḥa on the ʿayn and a sukūn on the bāʾ; and there is a third with a kasra on the ʿayn and a sukūn on the bāʾ.]] for her strength on journeys.

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, majestic is His praise, "And if you are ill," he means from a wound or smallpox while you are junub, as:

9570 - Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih told us, saying: Abu al-Munabbih al-Fadl ibn Sulaym told us [[The narration 9570: "Abu al-Munabbih al-Fadl ibn Sulaym," I did not find him; I only found "al-Fadl ibn Sulaym al-ʿAbdi." He narrated from al-Qasim ibn Khalid, and Muslim ibn Ibrahim narrated from him. He is biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 3/2/63.]], from al-Dahhak, from Ibn Mas'ud, his words: "And if you are ill or on a journey," he said: The ill one for whom tayammum has been permitted is the one with a broken bone and the wounded one. If janabah afflicts the one with the broken bone, he washes; and the wounded one does not loosen his wound except with a wound about which there is no fear. [[In the printed edition, the phrase "and he does not loosen his splints" was omitted, as if its meaning was unknown!! It is more well-known than that!]] [[In the manuscript: "and the wound does not loosen its wound", and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.]]

9571 - Tamim ibn al-Muntasir told us, saying: Ishaq ibn Yusuf al-Azraq told us, from Sharik, from Isma'il al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, who said concerning this verse: "And if you are ill or on a journey," he said: It is for the ill one who has a wound about which he fears if he washes, so he does not wash. So he is permitted tayammum.

9572 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "And if you are ill," and "the illness" is the wound. The wound about which there is fear from the water, if it harms its owner, he performs tayammum with clean earth.

9573 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi told us, from Said, from Qatadah, from ʿAzrah, from Said ibn Jubayr, concerning His words: "And if you are ill," he said: If he has wounds or sores, he performs tayammum. [[Narration 9573: "ʿAzrah ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Khuzaʿi," passed as no. 2752, 2753. In the printed edition it was "ʿUrwah," and the correct one is from the manuscript, though it is undotted.]]

9574 - Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Hakkam told us, from ʿAmr, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: "And if you are ill," he said: From sores that occur on the forearms.

9575 - Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Harun told us, from ʿAmr, from Mansur, from Ibrahim: "And if you are ill," he said: Sores on the forearms.

9576 - Ibn Humayd told us, saying: Harun told us, from ʿAmr, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak who said: The one with a wound about which fear is held, performs tayammum. Then he recited: "And if you are ill or on a journey."

9577 - Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And if you are ill," and "the illness" is when a man is afflicted with a wound, a sore, or smallpox [[In the printed edition: "or sores or smallpox," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]], and he fears for himself from the cold of the water and its harm, so he performs tayammum with the dust, as the traveller who finds no water performs it.

9578 - Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Muʿadh ibn Hisham told us, saying: My father told me, from Qatadah, from ʿAsim — meaning al-Ahwal — from al-Shaʿbi: that he was asked about [the words]: the one afflicted with smallpox, does janabah afflict him? He said: The horsemen of this verse have departed. [[Thus in the manuscript: "concerning his words: the one afflicted with smallpox…" I have placed it between brackets, because I am in doubt about it. As for his words "the horsemen of this verse have departed," its meaning has been unclear to me, and I have perhaps inclined to think that he meant that the verse was revealed concerning the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ from the Ansar whose doors were in the mosque, who would become junub with no water at hand, so they would want water and find no passage except in the mosque, as passed in the narration no. 9567. So his words "the horsemen of this verse have departed" refer to that portion of the verse "nor [approach in a state of janabah] except while passing through," and that they are the Ansar among the companions of the Messenger of God, whose doors were in the mosque, and they have passed away; none of them remains today. This is the utmost of my effort, and above every possessor of knowledge is one more knowing.]]

* *

And others said concerning this, what follows:

9579 - Yunus told me this, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His words: "And if you are ill or on a journey, and you find no water, then perform tayammum." He said: The ill one who finds no one to bring him water, and is not able to obtain it, and has no servant or helper; so if he cannot reach the water, and has no one with him to bring it, nor can he move toward it, he performs tayammum and prays when the prayer time comes. He said: All of this is the saying of my father [[i.e., of Zayd ibn Aslam, Ibn Zayd's father]], if he is not able to reach the water and has no one to bring it, he does not abandon the prayer, and he is more excused than the traveller.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse, then, is: And if you are wounded, or have sores on you, or a broken bone, or an illness with which you cannot wash from janabah, while you are residents and not travellers, then perform tayammum with clean earth.

* *

As for His words "or on a journey," it means: or if you are travellers and you are healthy and junub, then perform tayammum with earth.

* *

Likewise is the interpretation of His words "or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself": it says, or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself, having fulfilled his need, and he is a healthy traveller, then let him also perform tayammum with earth.

* *

And "al-ghaʾit" (the place of relieving oneself): what is wide of the valleys and slopes down. It was used as a metonym for a person's relieving himself, because the Arabs used to choose to relieve themselves in the open lowlands, and this became so common among them that it prevailed over them. So it was said of everyone who relieved himself in the lowlands, wherever he relieved himself on the ground: "muta-ghawwit" and "so-and-so came from al-ghaʾit," meaning he had relieved himself where one relieves oneself in the open lands. [[See the explanation of "al-ghaʾit" in what has passed: 5/354.]]

* *

It is related from Mujahid that he said of "al-ghaʾit": the valley.

9580 - Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself," he said: al-ghaʾit, the valley.

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿or you have touched women﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, majestic is His praise, is meant: or you have come into contact with women with your hands.

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed concerning the "touching" (al-lams) which God meant by His words "or you have touched women."

Some of them said: By that He meant sexual intercourse.

9610 - Ibn Wakiʿ told us, saying: My father told us, from Sufyan, from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, from Abu ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allah who said: The kiss is from touching.

9611 - Abu al-Sa'ib told us, saying: Abu Muʿawiyah told us = and Ibn Wakiʿ told us, saying: Ibn Fudayl told us = from al-Aʿmash, from Ibrahim, from Abu ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud who said: The kiss is from touching, and in it is wudu.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 43 (part 3 of 7):

9612 - Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, from Shurayk, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Abu Ubayda, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, the like of it.

9613 - Ahmad ibn Abdah al-Dabbi narrated to us, saying: Salim ibn Akhdar informed us, saying: Ibn Awn informed us, from Muhammad, who said: I asked Ubayda about His saying: ﴿or you have touched women﴾. He said: He pointed with his hand thus. [Salim related it] and Abu Abd Allah showed it to us, closing his fingers. [[The report 9613: Salim ibn Akhdar al-Basri. He narrated from Ibn Awn. Ibn Sa'd said: "He was the most constant of them in attending Ibn Awn, and he was trustworthy." Biographed in al-Tahdhib. "Abu Abd Allah" is Ahmad ibn Abdah al-Dabbi, who passed as no. 5502.]]

9614 - Yaqub and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Salamah ibn Alqamah, from Muhammad, who said: I asked Ubayda about His saying: ﴿or you have touched women﴾. He said, with his hand, and I understood what he meant, so I did not ask him. [[His saying "with his hand" means he gestured and pointed. His saying "I understood what he meant" means I grasped it and comprehended it. It is said: "tabana al-shay yatbanu tabanan" and "tabana lahu," meaning he understood it. A "tabin" man is one who is shrewd, skilled and knowledgeable in everything. In the printed edition it reads "I supposed what he meant," which is worthless. It is in the manuscript, poorly pointed. The correct reading is what I have established, and it will come in report 9616: "until I knew what he intended," so it is knowledge, not supposition, as you see; likewise report 9626.]]

9615 - Yaqub narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ibn Awn, who said: They mentioned in the presence of Muhammad touching the private part, and I think they mentioned what Ibn Umar said about that. Muhammad said: I said to Ubayda about His saying: ﴿or you have touched women﴾, and he said with his hand. Ibn Awn said: with his hand, as if he were grasping something and gripping it. [[The word "qal" in this report, in both places, means gesturing and indicating, as I stated in the earlier note.]]

9616 - Yaqub narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Khalid informed us, from Muhammad, who said: Ubayda said: "The touching is with the hand."

9616m - Yaqub said: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, from Hisham, from Muhammad, who said: I asked Ubayda about this verse: ﴿or you have touched women﴾, and he said with his hand, and closed his fingers, until I knew what he intended.

9617 - Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Umar informed me, from Nafi', that Ibn Umar used to perform ablution because of a woman's kiss, and considered ablution required because of it, and would say: it is among the "lims" (touching). [["Lamas" (with a kasra on the lam) is the verbal noun of "lamasahu, mulamasatan wa lamasan."]]

9618 - Abd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid informed us, from Isma'il, from Amir, who said: Mulamasah is what is less than intercourse.

9619 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: Muhill ibn Muhriz narrated to us, from Ibrahim, who said: Touching out of desire nullifies ablution. [[Report 9619: Muhill ibn Muhriz al-Dabbi al-Kufi al-A'war. He narrated from Abu Wa'il, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and al-Sha'bi. Al-Bukhari placed him among the weak narrators, and Ibn Abi Hatim said: "I heard my father say: he is to be shifted from there." Yahya al-Qattan said: "He was middling, not of that standing." He is trustworthy. Biographed in al-Tahdhib. "Muhill" is vowelled with a damma on the mim, a kasra on the ha, and the lam doubled.]]

9620 - Yaqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam and Hammad, that both said: Lams is what is less than intercourse.

9621 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Ata', who said: Mulamasah is what is less than intercourse.

9622 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Hafs narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from al-Sha'bi, from the companions of Abdullah, from Abdullah, who said: Mulamasah is what is less than intercourse.

9623 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Bayan, from Amir, from Abdullah, who said: Mulamasah is what is less than intercourse.

9624 - He said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from Abdullah, the like of it.

9624m - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Sufyan, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, from Abdullah, the like of it.

9625 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ibrahim, who said: Abdullah said: Mulamasah is what is less than intercourse. Then he recited: ﴿or you have touched women, and you find no water﴾.

9626 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Hisham, from Ibn Sirin, who said: I asked Ubayda about: ﴿or you have touched women﴾, and he gestured thus with his hand, so I understood what he meant.

9627 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from his father, and Hasan ibn Salih, from Mansur, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, from Abu Ubayda, who said: Kissing is of touching.

9628 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Zuhayr, from Khusayf, from Abu Ubayda: Kissing and the touching [[His saying "wal-shay'," is thus in the printed edition; in the manuscript it reads "al-sy" undotted, and I fear its correct form is "wal-mass".]].

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions regarding this is the view of the one who said: "God meant by His saying ﴿or you have touched women﴾ intercourse, and not other meanings of touching," because of the soundness of the report from the Messenger of God ﷺ, that he kissed some of his wives and then prayed without performing ablution.

9629 - Ismail ibn Musa al-Sudi narrated to me this, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash informed us, from al-A'mash, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Urwah, from A'ishah, who said: The Prophet ﷺ would perform ablution, then kiss, then pray without performing ablution. [[The two reports 9629-9630: "Urwah" in these two chains is Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, the nephew of A'ishah, with certainty, contrary to whoever claimed he is "Urwah al-Muzani," on account of a word said by al-Thawri: "Habib did not narrate to us except from Urwah al-Muzani!" Even if he did not narrate it from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, another narrated from him. The hadith was related by Ahmad in al-Musnad 6: 210 (Halabi), from Wakī' — with the second chain here — and in it explicitly "from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr." Likewise the explicit statement that it is "Urwah ibn al-Zubayr" came in the narration of Ibn Majah: 502, from the route of Wakī'. Every doubt and difficulty is thereby removed. Al-Thawri's remark was related by Abu Dawud in his Sunan, after the hadith: 180, in the passive form: "it was narrated from al-Thawri." Then he himself refuted it, saying: "Hamzah al-Zayyat narrated from Habib, from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from A'ishah, a sound hadith." The hadith was also related by Abu Dawud: 179, and al-Tirmidhi: 86 (with our commentary) — both from Wakī' with it. In them it reads "from Urwah" only, as here. Scholars have extended discussion on the defect of this hadith, while others disagreed and affirmed its soundness "from Urwah ibn al-Zubayr." This is correct. We have elaborated on it in our commentary on al-Tirmidhi 1: 133-142, and established its soundness, and the preference for the view that "mulamasah" in this verse is intercourse, and that a woman's touch does not nullify ablution. We saw no need to repeat that and prolong it here. See al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi, and Ibn al-Turkmani's refutation of it 1: 123-127, and Ibn Kathir 2: 465-466.]]

9630 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Wakī' narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Urwah, from A'ishah: that the Prophet ﷺ kissed some of his wives, then went out to prayer without performing ablution. I said: Is she anyone other than you? So she laughed. [[The same note applies to the two reports 9629-9630, as above.]]

9631 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Hajjaj, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from Zaynab al-Sahmiyyah, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he used to kiss and then pray without performing ablution. [[Report 9631: Hajjaj is Ibn Artah. Zaynab al-Sahmiyyah is the daughter of Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As, so she is the paternal aunt of Amr ibn Shu'ayb. Ibn Hibban mentioned her among the trustworthy, and al-Daraqutni claimed she was unknown! The hadith in this narration is mursal, because Zaynab al-Sahmiyyah is a Successor, not a Companion. It was narrated in al-Musnad as connected, 6: 62 (Halabi), from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, from Hajjaj, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from Zaynab al-Sahmiyyah, from A'ishah, so the interruption is removed. Likewise Ibn Majah narrated it: 503, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, connected. Some hadith critics gave it a defect: that Hajjaj ibn Artah is a mudallis, and he narrated it here with "from Amr ibn Shu'ayb," without explicit statement of hearing.]]

9632 - Abu Zayd Umar ibn Shabbah narrated to us, saying: Shihab ibn Abbad narrated to us, saying: Mandal narrated to us, from Layth, from Ata', from A'ishah; and from Abu Rawq, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from A'ishah, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ would touch me with a kiss after ablution, and then would not renew his ablution. [[Report 9632: Al-Tabari narrates this hadith here through two routes. He narrates it from Umar ibn Shabbah, from Shihab ibn Abbad, from Mandal. Then Mandal narrates it from Layth, from Ata', from A'ishah, and Mandal also narrates it from Abu Rawq, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from A'ishah. Umar ibn Shabbah Abu Zayd: his biography passed at 6310. Shihab ibn Abbad al-Abdi al-Kufi Abu Umar: trustworthy, among the teachers of al-Bukhari and Muslim. Ibn Adi said: "He was among the best of people." Biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/2/236, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/363. His name appears distorted in the manuscript and printed edition as "Suhad ibn Abbad"! No narrator bears this name. Another distortion appears in Ibn Kathir 2: 466 as "Hisham ibn Abbad"! quoted from this place of al-Tabari, and it is correct in the Azhari manuscript of Ibn Kathir's tafsir (2: 301, photographed copy in my possession). Mandal, with a fatha on the mim and dal with a silent nun between them: he is Ibn Ali al-Anzi, with a fatha on the nun, the Kufan. He is disputed between authentication and weakening; in my view the preponderant opinion is that his hadith is good. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir 4/2/73, Ibn Sa'd 6: 265, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/434-435. Layth is Ibn Abi Sulaym. Ata' is Ibn Abi Rabah. Abu Rawq is Atiyyah ibn al-Harith al-Hamdani, whose authentication passed at 137. The first route, "Ata' from A'ishah," was also narrated by al-Bazzar in his Musnad, from the route of Muhammad ibn Musa ibn A'yan, from his father, from Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from Ata', from A'ishah. Ibn al-Turkmani cited it in al-Jawhar al-Naqi 1: 125 (with al-Sunan al-Kubra), and al-Zayla'i in Nasb al-Rayah 1: 74 (Egyptian edition). This is a sound chain without defect. It was also narrated by al-Daraqutni, p. 50, from the route of Ubayd Allah ibn Amr, from Abd al-Karim, from Ata', from A'ishah. This too is a sound chain. However, al-Daraqutni tried to give it a defect that is not damaging: he mentioned that al-Thawri narrated it from Abd al-Karim, from Ata' only, as Ata's own words, and said: "and this is the correct one"! This is a feeble defect. The connecting and raising are additions from a trustworthy narrator, so both are accepted. Note: in al-Jawhar al-Naqi, this hadith reads "from Abd al-Karim, from A'ishah," without "from Ata'." This is an undoubted printing error, shown by al-Zayla'i's citation and by the rest of the text in al-Jawhar, which indicates "from Ata', from A'ishah" with certainty. The second route, from Ibrahim al-Taymi from A'ishah, was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 6: 210 (Halabi), from Wakī', from Sufyan — al-Thawri — from Abu Rawq, with the same. Likewise Abu Dawud: 178, al-Nasa'i 1: 39, al-Daraqutni p. 50-51, and al-Bayhaqi 1: 126-127, all from the route of al-Thawri, from Abu Rawq. Abu Dawud said: "It is mursal; Ibrahim al-Taymi did not hear anything from A'ishah." Al-Nasa'i said: "There is no hadith in this chapter better than this hadith, though it is mursal." Al-Tirmidhi alluded to it, 1: 138 (with our commentary), and said: "This too is not sound. We do not know that Ibrahim al-Taymi heard from A'ishah." This hadith has also been narrated as connected, from the narration of Ibrahim al-Taymi, from his father, from A'ishah, which I explained in detail in the commentary on al-Tirmidhi. There is another sound chain from A'ishah: al-Daraqutni narrated it, p. 49, from the route of Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Mansur, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from A'ishah. Al-Zayla'i and Ibn al-Turkmani also quoted it from him. Al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 1: 247, and said: "al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat. In it is Sa'id ibn Bashir: Shu'bah and others deemed him trustworthy, and Yahya and a group weakened him." The tawthiq of "Sa'id ibn Bashir" I preferred at 5439.]]

9633 - Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Yazid ibn Sinan narrated to me, from Abd al-Rahman al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Umm Salamah: that the Messenger of God ﷺ would kiss her while fasting, and then would not break his fast, nor renew ablution. [[Report 9633: This hadith is not in any of the six books. I did not find it in the Musnad of Ahmad either. Ibn Kathir 2: 466 quoted it from al-Tabari without attributing it to anyone else. Al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 1: 247, and said: "al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat. In it is Yazid ibn Sinan al-Rahawi: Ahmad, Yahya and Ibn al-Madini weakened him, while al-Bukhari and Abu Hatim deemed him trustworthy, and Marwan ibn Mu'awiyah affirmed him. The rest of its narrators are trustworthy." Yazid here is disputed, as al-Haythami said. The preponderant view in my judgment is his tawthiq. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib; al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir 4/2/337 without mentioning any criticism, did not mention him among the weak, and Ibn Abi Hatim biographed him 4/2/266.]]

= In the soundness of the report we mentioned from the Messenger of God ﷺ lies clear evidence that "touching" in this place means touching for intercourse, not all meanings of touching, as the poet said:

"And they walk with us in whispers... If the bird speaks truly, we shall touch (lamisa)."

[[Previously cited at 4: 126, note 1.]]

He means by it: "we shall touch (lamasan)." [[His saying "lamasan" means mulamasah. It seems he made "lamis" a verbal noun from "lams," like "masis" from "mass." This is a strange view that I did not find with anyone else. Rather, most say: "Lamis: a woman's name," and the meaning of "imra'ah lamis" is a woman soft to the touch.]]

* *

It was mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a group of the companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ who were afflicted with janabah, and among them were wounded men. [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "wa-hum jirah," and "jarih" has its plural "jarha," not "jirah," and I found no one who states this, or an irregular form by analogy. I judged that the copyist wrote "wa-hum" in place of "wa-fihim," so I established it thus.]]

9634 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Muhammad ibn Jabir, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, concerning the sick person who cannot perform ghusl from janabah, or the menstruating woman, who said: Tayammum suffices them. He said: The companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ suffered a wound that spread among them, [[In the printed edition: "wa-nal ashab rasul Allah ...," in place of "wa-qal: asaba ashab rasul Allah," as if he misread the manuscript.]] then they were afflicted with janabah, so they complained of this to the Prophet ﷺ, and there was revealed: ﴿And if you are sick, or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving himself﴾, the whole verse.

* *

Others said: It was revealed concerning a group of the companions of the Prophet ﷺ whom the water failed, and they did not find it on a journey of theirs.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 43 (part 4 of 7):

Mention of those who said this:

9635 - Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard ʿUbaydullah ibn ʿUmar, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from ʿAʾisha, that she said: "I was on a journey with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, until when we were at Dhat al-Jaysh, my necklace was lost. [["ḍalla al-shayʾ": if it was lost.]] So I informed the Prophet ﷺ of that, and he ordered that it be searched for, and it was searched for but not found. The Prophet ﷺ made his camel kneel, and the people made their camels kneel, and they spent that night there. The people said: ʿAʾisha has detained the Prophet ﷺ!" She said: "Abu Bakr came to me while the head of the Prophet ﷺ was in my lap, and he was sleeping. He began to jab me and pinch me and say: 'For the sake of your necklace you have detained the Prophet ﷺ!' She said: 'I did not move, lest the Prophet ﷺ wake up, and he had hurt me, and I did not know what to do!' When he saw that I did not answer him, he went away. [[It is said: "aḥāra ʿalayhi jawābahu" and "aḥāra lahu jawāban", meaning he replied to him, and "mā aḥāra bi-kalima" and "mā aḥāra ilayya jawāban", meaning he did not return an answer. Her words "lā uḥīru ilayhi" mean: I did not answer him nor complete (speech) to him.
In the printed edition it was: "lā ujīru" with a jīm, which is an error. The correct reading is what is established from the manuscript.]] When the Prophet ﷺ woke up and wished to pray, and found no water," she said, "Allah the Exalted revealed the verse of tayammum." She said: "Ibn Hudayr said: 'This is not the first of your blessings, O family of Abu Bakr!'" [[Hadith 9635 - ʿUbaydullah ibn ʿUmar: he is al-ʿUmari, one of the seven jurists.
The apparent character of this hadith is irsal (a broken chain), because here it is from the narration of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim from ʿAʾisha, and ʿAbd al-Rahman did not live to hear from his paternal aunt ʿAʾisha.
A similar version will come: 9641, from the narration of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from ʿAʾisha, connected. We will cite it there, God willing.]]

9636 - Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Abi Mulayka: that the Prophet ﷺ was on a journey, and ʿAʾisha lost a necklace of hers, so he ordered the people to dismount. They dismounted, and they had no water with them. Abu Bakr came to ʿAʾisha and said to her: "You have troubled the people!" = Ayyub said, gesturing with his hand, describing that he pinched her [[His words "qāla biyadihi" mean he gestured and pointed, as was mentioned many times before.]] = He said: "And the verse of tayammum was revealed, and the necklace was found in the kneeling place of the camel. The people said: 'We have never seen a woman greater in blessing than her!'" [[Hadith 9636 - This also is mursal, because Ibn Abi Mulayka related the story without mentioning who told him. He was a Successor (tabiʿi).
A similar meaning will come: 9639, from the narration of Ibn Abi Mulayka from Dhakwan, ʿAʾisha's chamberlain.
It will also come: 9642, from the narration of Ibn Abi Mulayka, about the story of Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿAʾisha, without the intermediary Dhakwan.]]

9637 - Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah al-Hilali narrated to me, saying: ʿImran ibn Muhammad al-Haddad narrated to me, saying: al-Rabiʿ ibn Badr narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from a man of ours, from Bal-ʿArj, [["Bal-ʿArj" means Banu al-Aʿraj, as they say "Bal-ʿanbar" for "Banu al-ʿAnbar"; its proper form would be "Bal-Aʿraj" (with fatha on the bāʾ, sukun on the lām, and fatha on the hamza), but it was softened, the hamza was dropped and its vowel placed on the lām, so it became fatha on the bāʾ and lām with a sukun on the ʿayn. "Banu al-Aʿraj" are: Banu al-Aʿraj ibn Kaʿb ibn Saʿd ibn Zayd Manat ibn Tamim. The name "al-Aʿraj" is al-Harith, whose leg was cut off, as Abu ʿUbayda mentioned in al-Naqaʾid: 1025.]] who is called al-Aslaʿ, he said: "I used to serve the Prophet ﷺ and saddle (his mount) for him. He said to me one night: 'O Aslaʿ, get up and saddle for me.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, I am in a state of janabah!' He was silent for a while, then he called me, and Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him with the verse of al-saʿid, and described to us two strikes." [[Hadith 9637 - Muhammad ibn ʿAbdullah al-Hilali - the teacher of al-Tabari - has passed in: 1275, 6180.
ʿImran ibn Muhammad al-Haddad: I have not found a biography of him nor mention of him in any of the references.
al-Rabiʿ ibn Badr ibn ʿAmr ibn Jarad al-Saʿdi al-Aʿraji, whose laqab is "ʿUlayla": weak, with agreed-upon weakness.
His father "Badr", and his grandfather "ʿAmr ibn Jarad": there is obscurity in both. Only al-Rabiʿ ibn Badr narrated from them, and he is weak, as we have said.
The hadith was narrated by al-Tabari right after this, through ʿAmr ibn Khalid, from al-Rabiʿ, with the same wording approximately.
Ibn Saʿd narrated it in al-Tabaqat 7/1/45, in the biography of "al-Aslaʿ", from Muslim ibn Ibrahim, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Badr. The heading of the biography there is given as "Maymun ibn Sanbadh al-Aslaʿ". This is a confusion by the printer, for "Maymun ibn Sanbadh" is other than "al-Aslaʿ"; rather, it is an independent heading without a biography, as frequently occurs in Ibn Saʿd, and then "al-Aslaʿ" is the heading of another biography.
al-Daraqutni narrated it, p. 66, and al-Tahawi in Maʿani al-Athar 1: 67-68, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 1: 208 - all from the route of al-Rabiʿ ibn Badr. al-Bayhaqi said: "al-Rabiʿ ibn Badr is weak, but he is not alone in it."
al-Zayla'i related it in Nasb al-Raya 1: 153, and quoted al-Bayhaqi's statement, and criticized it, saying that this is not sufficient for proof unless the other route and its grade are known. Likewise Ibn al-Turkumani criticized it in al-Jawhar al-Naqi.
The other route which al-Bayhaqi indicated - Ibn Kathir related it, 2: 472-473, from the narration of Ibn Mardawayh, through al-ʿAbbas ibn Abi Sariya, "al-Haytham ibn Ruzayq al-Maliki narrated to me, from Banu Malik ibn Kaʿb ibn Saʿd, and he lived one hundred and seventeen years, from his father, from al-Aslaʿ ibn Shurayk..." - then he mentioned the hadith, similarly.
"al-ʿAbbas ibn Abi Sariya": I did not know who he is, and I did not find a biography of him.
"al-Haytham ibn Ruzayq": Ibn Abi Hatim included his biography 4/2/83-84, and mentioned no criticism of him, and he pointed to this narration. He has a brief biography in Lisan al-Mizan 6: 206, and it does not mention that he narrates from his father. "Ruzayq" with the ra' placed first, as in al-Mushtabih, p. 221, and the Azhari manuscript of Ibn Kathir 2: 307. It was garbled in the references we refer to.
His father "Ruzayq": Ibn Abi Hatim included his biography 1/2/504 (in the chapter of the ra').
al-Tabarani also narrated it in al-Kabir, through this route. al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma al-Zawa'id 1: 261-262, and said: "In it is al-Haytham ibn Ruzayq. Some of them said: his hadith is not followed."
al-Haythami also mentioned the narration of al-Rabiʿ ibn Badr, in two wordings, 1: 262, and attributed them to al-Tabarani in al-Kabir, and noted the weakness of al-Rabiʿ in both.
Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned these narrations in al-Isaba 1: 34-35, in the biography of "al-Aslaʿ". It contains many benefits.]]

9638 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: ʿAmr ibn Khalid narrated to us, saying: al-Rabiʿ ibn Badr narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from a man of ours called al-Aslaʿ, he said: "I used to serve the Prophet ﷺ" = and he mentioned the like of it, except that he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was silent for a little while [[His words "shayʾan" mean a little, and it was explained in this report as "sāʿa" (an hour). I have already explained this with its evidences, and that it is one of the rare words of the language that the lexicons overlooked, in 6: 448, footnote 2.]] = or he said: "for an hour" - the doubt is from ʿAmr - =" He said: "Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him with the verse of al-sa'id, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Get up, O Aslaʿ, and perform tayammum.' He said: 'So I performed tayammum, then I saddled for him.' He said: 'We travelled until we passed by water, and he said: "O Aslaʿ, rub this on your skin" = or: "Amissu" = He said: "He showed me the tayammum, as his father had shown him: one strike for the face, and one strike for the two hands and the elbows." [[In the printed edition: "ilā al-mirfaqayn" (up to the elbows); I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

9639 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Bughayl narrated to us, saying: Zuhayr ibn Muʿawiya narrated to us, saying: ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUthman ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, saying: ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUbaydullah ibn Abi Mulayka narrated to me: that Dhakwan Abu ʿAmr, the chamberlain of ʿAʾisha, narrated to him: that Ibn ʿAbbas entered upon her during her illness and said: "Rejoice! You were the most beloved of the wives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not love except good. Your necklace fell on the night of al-Abwa'. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ kept searching for it until morning came while he was at the lodging. The people awoke with no water with them, so Allah revealed: 'Perform tayammum with clean earth' (4:43), and that was because of you, and Allah did not permit this nation the concession (of tayammum)..." [[Hadith 9639 - Hafs ibn Bughayl al-Hamdani al-Marhabi al-Kufi: he is biographied in al-Tahdhib, and in Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/170, and no criticism is mentioned of him, so he is trustworthy. "Bughayl": with a dammah on the unpointed bā' and a fatha on the ghayn. In the printed edition it was "Nufayl", which is a corruption. In the manuscript it is unpointed.
ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUbaydullah ibn Abi Mulayka: he is the well-known Successor. His biography has passed in: 6605. In the printed edition it was "ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUbaydullah ʿan Ibn Abi Mulayka", making two narrators, which is a plain error, for there is no one named "ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUbayd" among the teachers of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUthman ibn Khuthaym, nor among the students of Ibn Abi Mulayka, by the complete survey in Tahdhib al-Kamal (photographed manuscript). Ibn Khuthaym narrates directly from Ibn Abi Mulayka.
Then this very hadith is known from his narration from him, as will come.
Dhakwan Abu ʿAmr al-Madani, chamberlain and client of ʿAʾisha: a trustworthy Successor. He is biographied in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/1/238, Ibn Saʿd 5: 218, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/451.
The hadith is a portion of a long hadith, narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad: 2496, from Muʿawiya ibn ʿAmr, from Zaʾida, from Ibn Khuthaym, from Ibn Abi Mulayka, from Dhakwan.
Then he also narrated it: 3262, with a similar meaning, from ʿAbd al-Razzaq, from Maʿmar, from Ibn Khuthaym.
It will come in abridged form, similar, through the route of Ibn ʿUyayna: 9642.
The seeking of permission by Ibn ʿAbbas to enter upon ʿAʾisha was when she was dying. Therefore Ibn ʿAbbas said to her at that time: "Rejoice, there is nothing between you and meeting Muhammad ﷺ and the beloved except that the soul leaves the body." May Allah be pleased with her and make her pleased.
His words "wa-mā adhina Allāh li-hādhihi al-umma mina al-rukhṣa" (and Allah did not permit this nation the concession) - this is the correct established reading in the printed edition, and it agrees with the narration of al-Musnad 2496. It is supported by what is in the other narration from it: 3262: "So that was a concession for people in general because of you." In the manuscript here it was "li-hādhihi al-āya" (this verse), which is an error with no meaning.]]

9640 - Sufyan ibn Waki narrated to us, saying: Ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Hisham, from his father, from ʿAʾisha: that she borrowed a necklace from Asma, and it was lost, [[His words "halakat", meaning it was cut off, lost, and went astray.]] so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent men to search for it, and they found it. The prayer time came upon them while they had no water, so they prayed without ablution. They complained of that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah revealed the verse of tayammum. Usayd ibn Hudayr said to ʿAʾisha: "May Allah reward you with good; by Allah, no matter did befall you that you disliked, except that Allah made for you and for the Muslims good in it!" [[Hadith 9640 - Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 6: 57 (Halabi), from Ibn Numayr with this chain.
Likewise al-Bukhari narrated it, 1: 373 (Fath), through Ibn Numayr.
Muslim 1: 109-110, Abu Dawud: 317, Ibn Majah: 568, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra 1: 214 narrated it through several routes, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, similarly.
Ibn Kathir quoted it, 2: 471, from the narration of al-Musnad.
See the hadith following this one.]]

9641 - Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: my paternal uncle ʿAbdullah ibn Wahb narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn al-Harith informed me: that ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim narrated to him, from his father, from ʿAʾisha, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ: that she said: "A necklace of mine fell at al-Bayda', and we were entering Madina, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ made (his camel) kneel and dismounted. While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asleep in my lap, my father came and struck me a blow, then said: 'You have detained the people!' Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ awoke and the dawn prayer time came, and water was sought but not found, and the verse was revealed: 'O you who believe, when you rise to prayer...' (5:6), the verse." Usayd ibn Hudayr said: "May Allah bless the people through you, O family of Abu Bakr! You are nothing but a blessing!" [[Hadith 9641 - Its meaning has passed with a broken chain: 9635, from the narration of ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim from ʿAʾisha. This one, however, is connected, narrated by ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim from his father from ʿAʾisha.
Malik narrated it in al-Muwatta', pp. 53-54, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from ʿAʾisha.
Likewise Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 6: 179 (Halabi), al-Bukhari 1: 365-368 (Fath), Muslim 1: 109, and al-Nasai 1: 59, all through the route of Malik.
Ibn Kathir quoted it, 2: 471-472, from the narration of al-Bukhari.]]

9642 - al-Husayn ibn Shabib narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, saying: ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUthman ibn Khuthaym narrated to us, from ʿAbdullah ibn Abi Mulayka, who said: "Ibn ʿAbbas entered upon ʿAʾisha and said: 'You were the greatest of the Muslims in blessing for the Muslims! Your necklace fell at al-Abwa', so Allah revealed concerning you the verse of tayammum!'" [[Hadith 9642 - al-Husayn ibn Shabib ibn Rashid ibn Mutar, Abu ʿAli al-Muʾaddib, the teacher of al-Tabari: Ibn Abi Hatim gave a brief biography of him, 1/2/18, and al-Khatib included him in Tarikh Baghdad 7: 328, and al-Hafiz in Lisan al-Mizan 2: 213-214. Ibn ʿAdi said: "He narrated from the trustworthy with falsehoods, and connected hadiths which are mursal." al-Daraqutni said: "He is considered, but not strong."
This hadith from this shaykh certainly contains an error, and perhaps it is from his confusion! For he narrates it from Ibn ʿUyayna, from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUthman ibn Khuthaym directly, with explicit statement of hearing. This in itself is possible, since Ibn ʿUyayna did hear from Ibn Khuthaym. But this very hadith is not so:
Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad: 1905, longer than here, from Sufyan, who is Ibn ʿUyayna: "from Maʿmar, from ʿAbdullah ibn ʿUthman ibn Khuthaym." He thus established the intermediary between Ibn ʿUyayna and Ibn Khuthaym. We do not find it acceptable to weigh Imam Ahmad against this shaykh, al-Husayn ibn Shabib.
It was narrated, similarly, by al-Bukhari 8: 371-372, and Ibn Saʿd in al-Tabaqat 8: 51, both through ʿUmar ibn Saʿid ibn Abi Husayn, from Ibn Abi Mulayka.
In these three narrations, as in al-Tabari's narration here, it is from Ibn Abi Mulayka's own account of the story, without mentioning that Dhakwan, the chamberlain of ʿAʾisha, informed him of it, as passed in narration 9639.
My preferred view is that these narrations are mursal, and that Ibn Abi Mulayka did not witness ʿAʾisha's dying and Ibn ʿAbbas's entry upon her, and that he heard that from her client Dhakwan. But al-Hafiz in al-Fath attempted to strain to suppose that he did witness it. That is a far-fetched strain.]]

* *

The reciters differed regarding the reading of His words: "aw lamastum al-nisa'".
The majority of the reciters of Madina and some of the Basrans and Kufans read: ﴿aw lāmastum﴾, meaning: or you have touched your women and they have touched you.
* *
The majority of the reciters of Kufa read: ﴿aw lamastum al-nisa'﴾, meaning: or you, O men, have touched your women. These are two readings close in meaning, for a man is not a toucher (lāmis) of his wife unless she is also a toucher of him. So "al-lams" in this indicates the sense of "al-limas," and "al-limas" indicates the sense of "al-lams," each of the two being the other's partner. So whichever of the two readings the reciter reads, he is correct, because their meanings agree.
* *
The explanation of His words: ﴿fa-lam tajidū māʾan fa-tayammamū ṣaʿīdan ṭayyiban﴾
Abu Jaʿfar said: By His words, may His praise be majestic: "fa-lam tajidū māʾ" (and you find no water), "aw lamastum al-nisa'" (or you have touched women), so you sought water to purify yourselves with, but did not find it, neither for a price nor without a price. "Fa-tayammamū" says: then intend (ta'ammadū).
* *
= It is "tafaʿʿalū" from the saying of the speaker: "tayammamtu kadhā" = if I aimed at it and intended it, "fa-anā ataymammuhu" (then I intend it). It may be said from it: "yammamahu fulān fa-huwa yuyammiḥu" (so-and-so intended it, and he intends it), and "ammamtuhu ana" and "amamtuhu" (lightened), and "tayammamtu wa-ta'ammamtu," and no "yamamtu" (lightened) is heard for it. [[Rather, al-Lihyani related that, saying: "amu, wa-yamu."]] Among it is the verse of al-A'sha of Banu Tha'laba:
You intended Qays, and how many a land lay between him and you, of a desert of the wilderness of one with a rough gait. [[The verse, its explanation and its takhrij, were mentioned earlier in 5: 558.]]
By his words "tayammamt" (you intended), he meant: you aimed for and purposed. [[See the explanation of "tayammum" previously, 5: 558, 559.]]
* *
It has been mentioned that in the reading of ʿAbdullah it is: "fa-ummū ṣaʿīdan" (then aim for clean earth).
* *
And in accordance with what we have said regarding this, the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.
Mention of those who said this:

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 43 (part 5 of 7):**

9643 - Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: Abdan related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: I heard Sufyan say concerning His words: ﴿So perform tayammum with clean earth﴾, he said: "Seek out and intend clean earth." [[Report 9643: "Abdullah ibn Muhammad" is "Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Yazid, Abu Muhammad al-Hanafi," and "Abdan" is "Abdullah ibn Uthman ibn Jabalah ibn Abi Rawwad al-Azdi." Their biographies have passed under no. 5000, and this same chain has passed under nos. 5009, 6198, 6200. See the following chains: 9648, 9676.]]

* *

As for "al-sa'id" (clean earth, or earth surface), the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning it.

Some of them said: It is smooth ground on which there is no vegetation or planting.

Those who said this:

9644 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurai' related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿clean earth﴾: "That which has no tree or vegetation on it."

* *

Others said: Rather, it is level ground.

Those who said this:

9645 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "Al-sa'id" is level ground.

* *

Others said: Rather, "al-sa'id" is dust.

Those who said this:

9646 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir related to us, saying: Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i related to us, saying: "Al-sa'id" is dust. [[Report 9646: "al-Hakam ibn Bashir ibn Salman" has passed under nos. 1497 and 6171. In the printed edition and the manuscript it read "al-Hakam ibn Bashr," which is an error. "Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i" has passed under nos. 886 and 6171.]]

* *

Others said: "Al-sa'id" is the surface of the earth.

* *

Others said: Rather, it is the surface of the earth which is dusty.

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The most correct of these views is the saying of the one who said: "It is the surface of the earth, free of vegetation, planting and buildings, and level." Among the evidence for this is the verse of Dhu al-Rummah:

*As if he, in the forenoon, strikes the sa'id with it,*
*A stinging insect (dabbabah) at the base of the skull, a snout (khurtum).*

[[From his Diwan, p. 571, from his famous well-constructed ode. The line is among his verses describing a female gazelle who left her young child among trees; when the forenoon sun rose and fatigue overcame her, she dropped onto the ground as though she were a drunkard overcome by sleep. "Dabbabah" means that it crawls through the joints of the one who drinks it, i.e., wine. In the printed edition it read "wa ma bihi," which is an error. "Khurtum" describes wine that quickly intoxicates, taking hold of its drinker until he raises his snout (his nose) from the intensity of drunkenness and its dominance.]]

That is, he strikes it against the surface of the earth.

* *

As for His words "clean" (tayyiban), it means: pure from filth and impurities. [[See the explanation of "tayyib" earlier: 3:301 / 5:555 / 7:424.]]

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of His words "clean."

Some of them said: Lawful (halal).

Those who said this:

9647 - Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: Abd al-Razzaq related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: I heard Sufyan say concerning His words ﴿clean earth﴾: "Some of them said: lawful."

* *

Some of them said something else:

9648 - Abdullah related to me, saying: Abdan related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, by reading (qira'ah), who said: I said to Ata': "So perform tayammum with clean earth." He said: "Clean is what is around you." [[In the printed edition: "al-tayyib ma hawlaka" (the clean is what is around you), and it was the same in the manuscript, except that the alif and lam were struck through.]] I said: "A place that is bare (jard), not sandy (batih)," [[Regarding "jard" (with a fatha and then a sukun): this is open ground with no vegetation in it, and it seems he meant that it once had vegetation, but winter and drought stripped it bare. "Bathh," on the pattern of "farah," is sand in the sandy plain; "al-abtah" is also the same, and it is ground whose dust is smooth and soft, with fine pebbles in it. In the printed edition it read "ghayr abtah," but I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] Will it suffice me?" He said: "Yes." [[Report 9648: See the note on the preceding chain no. 9643.]]

* *

The meaning of the speech: If you do not find water, O people, and you are sick, or on a journey, or one of you comes from the privy, or you have touched women, and you wish to pray, then ﴿perform tayammum﴾, that is: intend the pure surface of the earth, ﴿and wipe your faces and your hands﴾.

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And wipe your faces and your hands﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, He, the Mighty and Majestic, means: wipe with it (from it) your faces and your hands. But He omitted mentioning "from it" (minhu), relying on the context to indicate it.

* *

"Wiping with it for the face" means that the one performing tayammum (mutayammim) strikes the clean earth with his hands, or what takes its place, and wipes his face with the dust that clings to them. If much dust clings to them, and he blows or shakes it off his hands, that is permissible. If no dust clings to his hands, though he struck the earth with both hands or one of them and then wiped his face with them or it, that suffices him, by the consensus (ijma') of all the proofs (al-hujjah), that if the one performing tayammum strikes the earth with his hands, and that earth is sand, and nothing clings to his hands from it, and he performs tayammum with it, this is sufficient for him; no one whose dissent is considered (ya'tadd) dissents from this. [[In the printed edition it read "an ya'tadd bi-khilafih" (that dissent of his is counted), which differs from the manuscript and is close to correct. "Yu'tadd khilafan" means "is counted as dissent." "Khilafan" is a verbal noun used as an adjective, on the pattern of "adl," and the meaning is: one whose dissent is counted as dissent.]] Since this was a consensus among them, it is known that what is intended by striking the earth with the hands is the contact of the hands with the earth, in the sense in which God commanded contact with it with them, not taking dust from it.

* *

As for "wiping with the hands," the people of interpretation differed concerning the limit to which God commanded the hands to be wiped.

Some of them said: The limit is the palms up to the wrists (zanad), and the one performing tayammum is not required to wipe what lies beyond that of the forearms.

Those who said this:

9649 - Abu al-Sa'ib Salm ibn Janadah related to me, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik, who said: "Ammar performed tayammum, striking his hands once on the dust, then wiped his hands one over the other, then wiped his face, then struck his hands again, and he began to twist one hand over the other, and he did not wipe the forearm." [[Report 9649: al-Bayhaqi related it with other wording in al-Sunan al-Kubra 1:210. See the following report, no. 9651.]]

9650 - Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, from Ibn Abi Khalid, who said: "I saw al-Sha'bi describe tayammum to us: he struck his hands on the earth once, then shook them off and wiped his face, then struck again, and he began to twist his palms, one over the other. He did not mention that he wiped the forearm."

9651 - Hannad related to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik, who said: "Ammar ibn Yasir placed his palms in the dust, then raised them and blew on them, then wiped his face and his palms." Then he said: "This is how tayammum is."

9652 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Abu Tumaylah related to us, saying: Salam, mawla of Hafs, related to us, saying: I heard Ikrimah say: "Tayammum is two strikes: a strike for the face, and a strike for the two palms."

9653 - Ali ibn Sahl related to us, saying: al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, from al-Awza'i, from Sa'id and Ibn Jabir, that Makhul used to say: "Tayammum is one strike for the face and the two palms up to the carpal joint (kuka')." Makhul interpreted the Qur'an in this regard: ﴿So wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 6], and His saying regarding tayammum: "wipe with your faces and your hands," and He did not make an exception in it as He made an exception in ablution, "up to the elbows." Makhul said: God said ﴿And as for the thief, male or female, cut off their hands﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 38], and the hand of the thief is cut at the joint of the carpus.

9654 - Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Hakam related to me, saying: Bishr ibn Bakr al-Tinisi related to us, from Ibn Jabir, that he saw Makhul performing tayammum, striking his hands on the clean earth, then wiping his face and palms with one stroke.

9655 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us, from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "Tayammum is a strike for the face and the two palms."

* *

The narration that the one who held this view relied upon is what follows:

9656 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Abdah and Muhammad ibn Bishr related to us, from Ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, from his father, from Ammar ibn Yasir: that he asked the Messenger of God ﷺ about tayammum, and he said: "Once, for the palms and the face." [[In the printed edition: "ala al-wajh" (for the face), but the correct reading is in the manuscript.] And in the hadith of Ibn Bashshar: that Ammar asked the Prophet ﷺ about tayammum. [[Hadith 9656: Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, mawla of Khuza'ah, is a reliable Successor (tabi'i). The Jama'ah (compilers of the six books) narrated from him. His father, Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, had companionship (suhbah), and he met the Prophet ﷺ and was with him.

This hadith was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 4:263 (Halabi), from Affan, from Aban, from Qatadah, from Izrah, from Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman, with this chain, similar in wording.

He added "from Izrah" in the chain between Qatadah and Sa'id.

Izrah is Ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Zurarah al-Khuza'i. His biography has passed under nos. 2752 and 2753.

Likewise Ibn al-Jarud narrated it in al-Muntaqa, p. 67, by way of Affan, from Aban.

Likewise Abu Dawud (no. 327) and al-Tirmidhi (no. 144, with our commentary) narrated it, both by way of Yazid ibn Zurai', from Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah, from Qatadah, from Izrah, with the same wording.

al-Tirmidhi said: "The hadith of Ammar is a hadith that is hasan sahih (good and sound). It has been narrated from Ammar by more than one route."

Likewise al-Bayhaqi narrated it (1:210), by way of Abd al-Wahhab ibn Ata', from Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah.

Then al-Bayhaqi said: "Likewise a group narrated it from Ibn Abi Arubah. Isa ibn Yunus narrated it from Ibn Abi Arubah without mention of Izrah in its chain. Likewise Aban ibn Yazid al-Attar narrated it from Qatadah, and there was disagreement on him regarding the mention of Izrah in its chain."

al-Darimi narrated it (1:190) from Affan, who is the shaykh from whom Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated, from Aban ibn Yazid al-Attar, from Qatadah, from Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman, without the mention of Izrah in the chain.

Is this one of the disagreements over Aban that al-Bayhaqi pointed to? Perhaps. But I consider it unlikely, because this occurs in the printed edition of al-Darimi, which is full of errors and distortions and cannot be relied upon. The mention of "from Izrah" is established in an old, sound manuscript in the Dar al-Kutub, from the book of al-Darimi. So that is the principal reference in this matter, given that the shaykh of al-Darimi is the shaykh of Ahmad. And he narrated it from him with the addition of "from Izrah," as we mentioned just above.

In any case, the chain is sound, because Qatadah also narrates directly from Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza. But those who added "Izrah" to the chain are more numerous and more retentive than those who did not mention it. And if both chains are sound, then perhaps it is an addition within the connected chains (al-muttasil min al-asanid).

However, the text of the hadith here is distorted: "once with the palms upon the face"! This has no meaning. Its correct form in the manuscript is: "once for the face and the palms." This agrees with the meaning of the hadith in the other transmissions. The wording of al-Musnad is also: "a strike for the face and the palms."

Ibn Kathir mentioned the hadith (2:469), from the narration of al-Musnad. In it (in both the manuscript and the printed edition) "Urwah" occurs instead of "Izrah." This is a distortion by the copyists.]]

9657 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ubayd ibn Sa'id al-Qurashi related to us, from Shu'bah, from al-Hakam, from Ibn Abza, who said: "A man came to Umar and said: 'I have become junub (in a state of major impurity) and I have not found water!' Umar said: 'Do not pray.' Ammar said to him: 'Do you not remember that we were on a journey in the time of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and you and I became junub? As for you, you did not pray. As for me, I rolled in the dust and prayed. I came to the Messenger of God ﷺ and mentioned that to him, and he said: "It would have been sufficient for you," and he struck his palms on the earth, blew on them, and wiped his face and palms once?'" [["Tamaakka fi al-turab" means he rolled himself in it.]] [[Hadith 9657: Ubayd ibn Sa'id ibn Aban ibn Sa'id ibn al-As, al-Qurashi al-Umawi, is reliable; Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in and others declared him reliable. He is the brother of "Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Hafiz."

al-Hakam is Ibn Utaybah al-Kindi.

Ibn Abza is Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman, whose biography appears in the hadith before this one.

On the apparent chain here, the hadith would be discontinuous (munqati'), for it would be a narration by Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza of the incident in the time of Umar, and he did not certainly witness that, since he was among the younger Successors. He narrates this only from his father.

I do not know whether this narration reached al-Tabari in this form, or whether it is a confusion by the copyists.

As for the hadith itself, it is sound by this route:

Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 4:265 (Halabi), from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah, from al-Hakam, from Dharr (he is Ibn Abd Allah al-Murhabi al-Hamdani), from Ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, from his father: "that a man came to Umar..." etc.

Likewise al-Tayalisi narrated it from Shu'bah, similarly (no. 638).

Likewise al-Bukhari narrated it (1:375-377), with several chains through Shu'bah.

Likewise Muslim (1:110), Abu Dawud (nos. 324-326), al-Nasa'i (1:59-60, and 60-61), Ibn Majah (no. 569), and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (1:209-210) narrated it, with chains, all by way of Shu'bah, similarly.

In all these chains it is narrated from Sa'id, from his father. As for the addition of "Dharr ibn Abd Allah al-Murhabi" in the chain between al-Hakam and Sa'id: al-Bukhari and Muslim, the two Shaykhs, established al-Hakam's explicit statement that he heard it from "Ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abza, from his father, like the hadith of Dharr." So he heard it from Sa'id through an intermediary, and then he heard it from him directly.

Two other hadiths of Ammar concerning tayammum will follow: 9670, 9672.]] They said: God commanded in tayammum the wiping of the face and the two hands. So whatever of the face and hands is wiped in tayammum suffices, unless something prevents that which must be accepted, whether from a textual basis or from analogy (qiyas).

* *

Others said: The limit of the wiping which God commanded in tayammum is that one wipes the entire face and the two hands up to the elbows.

Those who said this:

9658 - Imran ibn Musa al-Qazzaz related to us, saying: Abd al-Warith ibn Sa'id related to us, saying: Ayyub related to us, from Nafi', that Ibn Umar performed tayammum at Mirbad al-Na'am. [["Al-mirbad" (with a kasra and sukun) is the place where camels and sheep are confined. "Mirbad al-Na'am" is in Medina.] He struck once and wiped his face, and he struck once and wiped his hands up to the elbows.

9659 - Ibn Abd al-A'la related to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir related to us, saying: I heard Ubayd Allah, from Nafi', from Abd Allah, that he said: "Tayammum is two wipings: a man strikes the earth with his hands and wipes his face with them, then strikes with them again and wipes his hands up to the elbows." [[In the manuscript: "then he wipes with them again," and the correct reading is in the printed edition.]]

9660 - Ibn al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Yahya ibn Ubayd Allah related to us, saying: Nafi' informed me, from Ibn Umar regarding tayammum, he said: "One strike for the face, and one strike for the palms up to the elbows."

9661 - Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib related to us, both saying: Ibn Idris related to us, from Ubayd Allah, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: "He used to say, regarding the wiping in tayammum: up to the elbows." [[Reports 9658-9661: See what al-Bayhaqi narrated in his Sunan 1:207 from the report of Ibn Umar.]]

9662 - Humayd ibn Mas'adah related to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufadhdhal related to us, saying: Ibn Awn related to us, saying: "I asked al-Hasan about tayammum, and he struck his hands on the earth, wiped his face with them, and struck his hands and wiped his two forearms, their outer and inner surfaces."

9663 - Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab related to us, saying: Dawud related to us, from Amir, that he said concerning this verse: ﴿So wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows, and wipe your heads and your feet up to the ankles﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 6], and he said concerning this verse: ﴿So wipe with your faces and your hands from it﴾ [Surah al-Ma'idah: 6]. [[This verse is from Surah al-Ma'idah, and in it is "minhu" (from it). As for the verse of Surah al-Nisa' that we are dealing with, it does not contain "minhu," but "minhu" is established in the manuscript, so I have returned it to the verse of al-Ma'idah.]] He said: "He commanded that one wipe in tayammum what he commanded to be washed in ablution, and he abrogated what he commanded to be wiped in ablution: the head and the feet."

9664 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah related to us = and Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Adi related to me = all from Dawud, from al-Sha'bi, concerning tayammum, he said: "A strike for the face, and for the two hands up to the elbows." [[In the printed edition: "wa darbah li-l-yadayn" (and a strike for the two hands). It added "darbah" (strike); I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

9665 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "Tayammum was commanded, in the same way that washing was commanded."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 43 (part 6 of 7):

9666 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Ayyub, who said: I asked Salim ibn 'Abd Allah about tayammum (dry ablution). He struck the earth once with his hands and wiped his face with them, then struck the earth again with his hands and wiped his hands up to the elbows.

9667 - Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Habib ibn al-Shahid also informed us, from al-Hasan, that he was asked about tayammum and said: One strike with which he wipes his face, then another strike with which he wipes his hands up to the elbows.

* *

The reasoning of those who held this view is that tayammum is a substitute (badal) for wudu' (ablution), and the one performing tayammum must bring the dust to the same extent on his face and hands as he would be required to bring the water in wudu'. They relied on the report:

9668 - Musa ibn Sahl al-Ramli narrated this to me, saying: Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated to us, saying: Kharijah ibn Mus'ab narrated to us, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ata', from Musa ibn 'Uqbah, from al-A'raj, from Abu Juhaym, who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) urinating. I greeted him, but he did not return the greeting. When he had finished, he went to a wall, struck it with his hands and wiped his face with them, then struck the wall with his hands and wiped his hands up to the elbows, and then returned my greeting.

[[Hadith 9668 - Nu'aym ibn Hammad ibn Mu'awiyah al-Khuza'i al-Farid: a trustworthy (thiqah) narrator, one of the teachers of al-Bukhari; some have criticised him in ways that do not undermine his reliability. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/2/100, Ibn Sa'd 7/2/205-206, Ibn Abi Hatim 4/1/463-464, and Tarikh Baghdad 13: 306-314.
Kharijah ibn Mus'ab ibn Kharijah al-Khurasani: heavily disputed. Most scholars weaken him. The fairest statement about him is that of al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 1: 499, who said: "Kharijah was criticised only for narrating from unknown narrators; when he narrates from reliable and precise narrators, his narration is accepted."
'Abd Allah ibn 'Ata': if he is not al-Ta'i al-Makki, then I do not know who he is, and I fear he is one of the unknown narrators from whom Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrates.
Al-A'raj: he is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz, the well-known reliable Successor (tabi'i). I have not seen any narration of his from Abu Juhaym, and I do not think he met him. He narrates this hadith from "'Umayr, mawla of Ibn 'Abbas," from Abu Juhaym, as will come.
I do not know whether this was dropped from the copies of al-Tabari, or whether it is like this in this narration. If so, the error is from Nu'aym ibn Hammad or from his teacher 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ata'!
Ibn Kathir has transmitted it, 2: 468-469, as it stands here. If it is a copying error, it is an old one.
Abu Juhaym (diminutive) ibn al-Harith ibn al-Simmah al-Ansari: a known Companion (sahabi).
The hadith is authentic in its origin, but not with this chain of al-Tabari, which can barely stand!
Al-Bukhari narrated it 1: 374-375 (Fath): "Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us, saying: al-Layth [i.e. Ibn Sa'd] narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Rabi'ah, from al-A'raj, who said: I heard 'Umayr, mawla of Ibn 'Abbas, say: I and 'Abd Allah ibn Yasar, mawla of Maymunah, wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), came and entered upon Abu Juhaym ibn al-Harith ibn al-Simmah al-Ansari. Abu Juhaym said: The Prophet (ﷺ) came from the direction of Bir Jamal, and a man greeted him, but the Prophet (ﷺ) did not return the greeting until he faced the wall, and wiped his face and hands, and then returned the greeting."
This is the sound narration. As for the addition here, "up to the elbows," it is a weak addition in its chain, as you see. The Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) pointed to two other narrations containing "wiped his face and forearms," and weakened them because of the weakness of their narrators, and said: "The established wording in the hadith of Abu Juhaym is 'his hands,' not 'his forearms'."
See also al-Bayhaqi's al-Sunan al-Kubra 1: 205.
Abu Dawud (329) and al-Nasa'i (1: 59) also narrated it, both through al-Layth ibn Sa'd, with the same wording.
Muslim also mentioned it in his Sahih 1: 110-111 as a suspended narration (mu'allaq), saying: "al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated..." etc. It appears that he was not confident of it, and errors occurred in two places: "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yasar" instead of "'Abd Allah ibn Yasar," and "Abu Jahm" with a single diminutive, instead of "Abu Juhaym." Al-Hafiz explicitly stated his error in both places in al-Fath.
Ahmad also narrated it in al-Musnad (17614; vol. 4 p. 169, Halabi edition), from Hasan ibn Musa, from Ibn Lahi'ah: "narrated to us from al-Rahman al-A'raj," then the hadith, like al-Bukhari's narration.
Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar made a serious error in this narration, in al-Isabah 7: 35, in the biography of Abu Juhaym, saying: "Ibn Lahi'ah narrated it from 'Abd Allah ibn Yasar, from Abu Juhaym! Ahmad narrated it." But Ahmad's narration is not as he stated. Rather, it is like the narrations of al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i, which he mentioned earlier.]]

Others said: The limit to which Allah commanded that the dust be brought in tayammum is the armpits (al-aba'it).

Those who said this:

9669 - Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Barqi narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn Abi Salamah al-Tannisi narrated to me, from al-Awza'i, from al-Zuhri, who said: Tayammum is up to the armpits.

The reasoning of those who said this: Allah commanded the wiping of the hand in tayammum, just as He commanded the wiping of the face. They agreed that one must wipe the entire face, so likewise one must wipe the entire hand, and from the tip of the palm to the armpit is "hand." They relied on the report:

9670 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Sayfi ibn Rabi'i narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu al-Yaqzan, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when a necklace of 'A'ishah was lost (halaka al-'iqd, meaning it was broken off and gone). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stayed until dawn broke. Abu Bakr became angry with 'A'ishah, and then the concession was revealed: wiping with the clean earth (al-sa'id). Abu Bakr came in and said to her: "You are blessed! A concession has come down concerning you!" Then we struck with our hands: one strike for our faces, and one strike with our hands up to the shoulders and armpits.

[[Hadith 9670 - Sayfi ibn Rabi'i al-Ansari: mentioned by Ibn Hibban in al-Thiqat. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. Ibn Abi Hatim biographed him at 2/1/448, and narrated from his father, who said: "Sound in hadith; I see no harm in his narration." His biography appears in two entries with two numbers in the printed Ibn Abi Hatim, following one of its manuscripts; the respected editor erred in preferring it over the other manuscript, which had one entry.
Abu al-Yaqzan: he is 'Ammar ibn Yasir, and this is his kunya.
The hadith was narrated by al-Tayalisi in his Musnad (637), from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, with this chain, in full.
Likewise al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 1: 208, through al-Tayalisi.
Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 4: 320 (Halabi), from Hajjaj, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, with this chain.
Ibn Majah narrated it (565), through al-Layth ibn Sa'd, from al-Zuhri, with this chain.
The hadith in this form, with this chain, is mursal (disconnected), because 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utbah ibn Mas'ud did not meet 'Ammar ibn Yasir, and his narration from him is mursal.
It is established, however, that 'Ubayd Allah heard it from his father, from 'Ammar, and heard it from Ibn 'Abbas, from 'Ammar. So its chain is connected through these two routes:
Al-Bayhaqi said, after narrating it: "Likewise it was narrated by Ma'mar ibn Rashid, Yunus ibn Yazid al-Ayli, al-Layth ibn Sa'd, the nephew of al-Zuhri, and Ja'far ibn Burqan, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utbah, from 'Ammar."
Then he narrated it, in similar form, through Malik, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utbah, "that he informed him, from his father, from 'Ammar ibn Yasir."
Abu Dawud said, after the hadith (320) that we will mention below: "Malik said: from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from his father, from 'Ammar. Likewise Abu Uways narrated it from al-Zuhri."
Ibn Majah narrated it (566) through Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, from 'Amr, that is Ibn Dinar, from al-Zuhri: "from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from his father, from 'Ammar ibn Yasir," in abridged form.
As for the narration of 'Ubayd Allah from Ibn 'Abbas: Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 4: 263-264, through Salih, that is Ibn Kaysan, from al-Zuhri: "'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to me, from Ibn 'Abbas, from 'Ammar ibn Yasir," then he mentioned it in full.
Likewise al-Bayhaqi narrated it 1: 208-209, through Ahmad in al-Musnad.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it 2: 472, from the narration of al-Musnad.
Likewise Abu Dawud (320) and al-Nasa'i (1: 60) both narrated it through Salih, from al-Zuhri, with it, mentioning Ibn 'Abbas in the chain.
Al-Tayalisi said, after the hadith (637) that we mentioned just above: "Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated this hadith, from al-Zuhri, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from 'Ammar."
Likewise Abu Dawud in his Sunan, and al-Bayhaqi, after narrating it through Salih, stated explicitly that Ibn Ishaq narrated it from al-Zuhri, mentioning "from Ibn 'Abbas."
In any case: the hadith is sound. We do not regard this as confusion (idtirab); rather these are multiple established routes, none of which is a defect for the others.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The correct position on this matter is that the limit which the one performing tayammum must not fall short of in wiping his hands with dust is: the two palms, up to the two wrist-bones (al-zundayn), because all agree that falling short of this is not permissible. Beyond that, he has a choice: if he wishes, he may extend his wiping to the elbows, and if he wishes, to the armpits. The reason why we made him free to choose beyond the two palms is that Allah did not set for wiping the hands with dust in tayammum a limit below which it is not permissible to fall short. So whatever part of his hands the one performing tayammum wipes suffices him, except what there is consensus upon, or what proof has established that falling short of it does not suffice. All agree that falling short of the two palms does not suffice, so this was made clear by the Sunnah, and whatever lies beyond it is disputed. Since it is disputed, and the one wiping with his two palms is included in the general scope of the verse, he has fulfilled what was obligatory of that duty.

* *

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the junub (one in a state of major impurity): is he among those included in the concession of tayammum when he does not find water, or not?

A group of the interpreters from among the Companions, the Successors, and those after them, including the later generations, said: The ruling for the junub regarding what is required of him in tayammum when he does not find water is the same as the ruling for one who comes from the toilet (ghā'it) and every other person who has had a minor impurity (muhdith), for whom tayammum has been made a purifier for his prayer. They mentioned the view of some who interpreted Allah's words "or you have touched women," or "you have had intercourse with them," and we have left out mention of the rest because of the number of those who said this.

* *

Those who held this view argued that the junub may perform tayammum when he does not find water on his journey, by the consensus of the authority (al-hujjah) on this, transmitted from its Prophet (ﷺ), which removes the excuse and dispels doubt.

* *

Some of the earlier scholars said: Nothing suffices the junub except bathing (ghusl) with water, and he may not pray with tayammum, for tayammum does not purify him. They said: Tayammum was only made a concession for other than the junub. They interpreted Allah's words "and not [approaching prayer while] in a state of major impurity, except as travellers" [accordingly]. They said: Allah has forbidden the junub from approaching the musalla (prayer place) of the Muslims, except passing through it, until he bathes, and did not grant him the concession of tayammum.

They said: The interpretation of His words "or you have touched women," is: touching them with the hand, excluding the private parts and excluding intercourse.

They said: So we do not find that Allah granted the junub a concession in tayammum; rather He commanded him to wash, and not to approach prayer except as one who has bathed. They said: Tayammum does not purify him for his prayer.

Those who said this:

9671 - Abu Kurayb and Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to us, both saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Shaqiq, who said: I was with 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud and Abu Musa al-Ash'ari. Abu Musa said: "O Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, what do you think of a man who became junub and did not find water for a month: does he perform tayammum?" 'Abd Allah said: "He does not perform tayammum, even if he does not find water for a month." Abu Musa said: "Then how do you deal with this verse in Surat al-Ma'idah: ﴿So seek clean earth﴾?" 'Abd Allah said: "If they were given this concession, they would soon, when the water became cold for them, perform tayammum with the earth!" Abu Musa said to him: "You only disliked this for that reason!" He said: "Yes!" Abu Musa said: "Did you not hear 'Ammar's words to 'Umar: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me on an errand, and I became junub and did not find water, so I rolled in the earth as an animal rolls. I mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said: It suffices you to do this,' and he struck his palms once, wiped his face with them, and wiped his palms"?" 'Abd Allah said: "Did you not see that 'Umar was not satisfied by 'Ammar's statement?"

[[Hadith 9671 - Abu al-Sa'ib: he is Salm ibn Janadah, whose biography has passed at 48. Shaqiq: he is Ibn Salamah, Abu Wa'il al-Asadi, the great Successor who met both the time of the Prophet and that of the Companions (mukhadram).
The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 4: 264-265 (Halabi), from Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash with this chain.
Likewise al-Bukhari narrated it 1: 386 (Fath), Muslim 1: 110, Abu Dawud (321), and al-Nasa'i 1: 61, all through Abu Mu'awiyah from al-A'mash.
Ahmad also narrated it, 4: 265, through 'Abd al-Wahid, that is Ibn Ziyad al-'Abdi, from al-A'mash, with it, in similar form.
Ibn Kathir transmitted this narration from al-Musnad, 2: 269.
Likewise Muslim narrated it 1: 110, through 'Abd al-Wahid.
Al-Bayhaqi narrated it 1: 211, through Ya'la ibn 'Ubayd, from al-A'mash.
