Then he said: "al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it through several routes from al-A'mash. al-Bukhari pointed to the narration of Ya'la ibn 'Ubayd, who was the most precise of them in relating the hadith's wording." The indication of al-Bukhari is in 1: 387, following the narration of Abu Mu'awiyah.]]

9672 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salamah, from Abu Malik, and from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, who said: We were with 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah have mercy on him, when a man came to him and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, we remain for a month or two months without finding water!" 'Umar said: "As for me, if I did not find water, I would not pray until I found water." 'Ammar ibn Yasir said: "Do you remember, O Commander of the Faithful, when we were at such-and-such a place, while we were grazing the camels, and you know that we became junub?" He said: "Yes!" "As for me, I rolled in the dust, and we came to the Prophet (ﷺ)," and he said: "It would have sufficed you to do this: he struck the earth with his palms, then blew into them, then wiped his face and part of his forearms." 'Umar said: "Fear Allah, O 'Ammar!" 'Ammar said: "O Commander of the Faithful, if you wish, I will not mention it!" He said: "No, but we will entrust you with what you have taken upon yourself."

[[Hadith 9672 - 'Abd al-Rahman: he is Ibn Mahdi.
Sufyan: he is al-Thawri.
Salamah: he is Ibn Kuhayl; his biography has passed at 439 and 2435.
Abu Malik: he is Ghazwan al-Ghifari, a known Successor, who has passed many times.
'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza: reliable. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/94, and he is the brother of "Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-Rahman," biographed at 9656, 9657.
In al-Tabari's text here, a certain copyist's error occurred: it dropped, both in the manuscript and in the print, [from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza]. So the apparent chain becomes that 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman was the one who was with 'Umar and related the story! This never happened, because 'Abd Allah did not reach that, and he has no narration except from his father. The context here does not allow this to be a difference of narration.
Moreover, what definitively confirms this is that al-Nasa'i narrated this hadith (1: 60), from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, the teacher of al-Tabari here, with this same chain, and in it: [from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza], which we have added here.
Likewise Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad 4: 319 (Halabi), from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi, the teacher's teacher of al-Tabari here, with this chain. In it is this addition. But there is a printing error in the printed Musnad, "from Abu Thabit" instead of "from Abu Malik," and we corrected it from the manuscript of the Musnad that we have.
So the hadith is narrated by Salamah ibn Kuhayl from two teachers, namely Abu Malik and 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, both from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abza.
Al-Bayhaqi (1: 209-210) indicated narrations from Salamah ibn Kuhayl concerning this hadith, which he took to be confusion (idtirab) on Salamah's part, but it appears that they are differences of narration among those who narrated from him.
His words in the body of the hadith, "He said: Yes. As for me, I rolled..." - this is also the established wording in the narration of al-Nasa'i. In the Egyptian print, it reads "As for me" without the fa' (then). This is a sound construction, given the assumption that "he said" is omitted after his words "Yes." Because it is evident that his words "As for me" are the words of 'Ammar ibn Yasir, not the words of 'Umar. Similar things are common. The wording of the Musnad at this point reads: "He said: Yes, he said: Indeed I rolled in the dust."]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 43 (part 7 of 7):

9673 - Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from al-Hakam, who said: I heard Ibrahim (al-Nakha'i) in the shop of Muslim al-A'war, and I said: "What do you say if he does not find water and he is junub?" He said: "He does not pray." [[The report 9673: "Muslim al-A'war" is Muslim ibn Kaysan al-Dabbi, weak, whom the scholars have spoken about, but he has no bearing on this report. "Ibrahim" is al-Nakha'i.]]
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter is that the junub is among those whom God commanded to perform tayammum if he does not find water, and (commanded) the prayer, by His saying: "Or if you have touched women, and you find no water, then perform tayammum with clean earth." We have already explained there that the meaning of "touching" (mulamasah) in this context is sexual intercourse, by transmission of a proof against which error is impermissible in what it transmits, on which there is consensus, and against which there is neither forgetfulness nor collusion nor conspiracy ("tasha'ur", meaning pretentious learning and collusion; this word has passed at 6:127, note 2, and 155, note 1; in the printed edition it was "tadafur", which the editor changed because he did not understand it), that the ruling for the junub in this matter is the ruling for everyone who has incurred a state requiring purification, so that he is obliged to purify himself for his prayer, together with what has been related on this matter from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in reports, some of which we have mentioned and many of which we have omitted, being content with what we have mentioned of them over what we have not mentioned, and out of our dislike of lengthening the book by exhausting all of them.
* *
The people of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of His saying: "But if you find no water, then perform tayammum," and whether that is a command from God to perform tayammum whenever one is obliged to seek water, or whether it is a command from Him to perform tayammum whenever one is obliged to seek water while being in a state of minor impurity which would require wudu' with water had he found water. [[In the printed edition the wording is "hal dhalika amr" without the waw; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]
Some of them said: That is a command from God to perform tayammum whenever the obligation of seeking water falls upon one, after seeking, whether he is in a state of impurity or not.
Mention of those who said this:
9674 - Ya'qub related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, from al-Hajjaj, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from Ali (may God be pleased with him), that he used to say: Tayammum is for every prayer.
9675 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Hushaym informed us, saying: al-Hajjaj informed us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from Ali, the like of it.
9676 - Abdullah ibn Muhammad related to me, saying: Abdan al-Marwazi related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Abd al-Warith informed us, saying: Amir al-Ahwal informed us, from Nafi', that he related to him from Ibn Umar the like of that. [[Report 9676: see the note on report 9643.]]
9677 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, saying: Mujalid informed us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: One prays with tayammum only one prayer.
9678 - al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, who said: He performs tayammum for every prayer, interpreting this verse: "and you find no water."
9679 - He said: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: al-Firyabi related to us, from al-Awza'i, from Yahya ibn Sa'id and Abd al-Karim ibn Rabi'ah ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman, who said: Tayammum is for every prayer. [[Report 9679: "Yahya ibn Sa'id ibn Qays al-Ansari", the judge, who related from Anas. "Abd al-Karim ibn Abi al-Makhariq", the jurist, who related from Anas. "Rabi'ah ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman al-Taymi", who is Rabi'ah al-Ra'y, the authority on legal opinion in Medina. In the printed and manuscript texts it reads "Abd al-Karim ibn Rabi'ah ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman", which is an error and does not fit the context either.]]
9680 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abu Dawud related to us, saying: Imran al-Qattan related to us, from Qatadah, from al-Nakha'i, who said: He performs tayammum for every prayer.
* *
Others said: Rather, that is a command from God to perform tayammum after seeking water for the one who is obliged to seek it, if he is in a state of minor impurity. As for one who has not incurred impurity after his purification with earth, and the obligation of seeking water falls upon him, he is not required to renew his tayammum, and he may pray with his first tayammum.
Mention of those who said this:
9681 - Humayd ibn Mas'adah related to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Habib related to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: Tayammum is in the position of wudu'.
9682 - Isma'il ibn Musa al-Sudi related to us, saying: Umar ibn Shakir related to us, from al-Hasan, who said: The one performing tayammum prays with his tayammum so long as he does not incur impurity; if he finds water, then let him perform wudu'. [[Report 9682: "Umar ibn Shakir al-Basri", who related from Anas things that are denounced (munakir). Isma'il ibn Musa al-Sudi al-Fazari related from him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]
9683 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: Hisham informed us, from al-Hasan, who said: A man would pray all the prayers with one ablution so long as he did not incur impurity. Likewise with tayammum.
9684 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: Hisham informed us, from al-Hasan, who said: A man would pray all the prayers with one ablution.
9685 - Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abu Dawud related to us, saying: my father related to us, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, who said: One prays the prayers with tayammum so long as one does not incur impurity.
9686 - Humayd ibn Mas'adah related to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Habib related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', who said: Tayammum is in the position of wudu'.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two views in our opinion is the view of the one who said: "The one praying performs tayammum for every prayer for which he is obliged to seek water for purification," because God, may His praise be majestic, commanded everyone who rises to prayer to purify himself with water, and if he does not find water, then tayammum. Then the Sunnah of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) excluded from the one rising to prayer those who had already risen to it with wudu' with water. [[The phrase "sunnatu rasul Allah" is nominative, being the subject of "akhraja ... sunnatu rasul Allah".]] Unless he has incurred a state that nullifies his purity, in which case the obligation of wudu' falls away from him by the Sunnah. As for one rising to prayer who had already risen to it with tayammum for a previous prayer, the obligation of tayammum for him remains binding by the apparent sense of the revelation, after his seeking water when he is unable to find it.
* *
Concerning the interpretation of His saying: "Indeed God is ever Pardoning, Forgiving" (4:43)
Abu Ja'far said: He means by this, may His praise be majestic: God has always been "Pardoning" of the sins of His servants, and His leaving punishment for many of them so long as they do not associate anything with Him, just as He pardoned you, O believers, for your rising to prayer, which He made obligatory upon you, in your mosques while you were intoxicated. "Forgiving" means: He has always covered over their sins by His not hastening punishment upon them for their sins, just as He covered over for you, O believers, by not hastening upon you for your prayers in your mosques while intoxicated. He says: so do not return to the like of it, lest you incur, by returning to what I have forbidden you from, a severe punishment ("munakkilah"). [["Munakkilah" (with the mim vowelled with damma, the nun with fatha, and the kaf doubled and kasra-vowelled) comes from tankil, which is the infliction of a severe punishment such that one who sees it is deterred and warned. Had it been read "munkilah" (with fatha on the mim, sukun on the nun, and fatha on the lam), it would also be correct, and similar is "al-mankal", which also means the punishment.]]
* *
Concerning the interpretation of His saying: "Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture" (4:44)
Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of His saying, may His praise be majestic: "Have you not seen those who..." Some people said: its meaning is: Have you not been informed?
* *
Others said: its meaning is: Have you not known?
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter is: "Have you not seen with your heart, O Muhammad, with knowledge, those who were given a portion." That is because "information" and "knowledge" do not make it sight, but it is seeing of the heart by knowledge. So it is as we have said. [[In the manuscript: "bi-ilmika" (by your knowledge), which is an error; the correct reading is what is printed.]]
* *
As for the interpretation of His saying: "those who were given a portion of the Scripture," it means: those who were given a share of the Book of God and who have learned it.
It is mentioned that God meant by this a group of the Jews who were around the emigration place of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).
Mention of those who said this:
9687 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah concerning His saying: "Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, who buy error and want you to lose the way?" They are the enemies of God, the Jews, who bought error.
9688 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrimah: "Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture," to His saying: "they distort words from their places," he said: It was revealed concerning Rifa'ah ibn Zayd ibn al-Sa'ib, the Jew. [[Thus it reads in the manuscript also, "Rifa'ah ibn Zayd ibn al-Sa'ib"; but you will see that in the following report it is "...ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut". Jewish names are problematic, so I could not be certain of their error. Perhaps "al-Sa'ib" is his grandfather's name and his epithet was "al-Tabut".]]
9689 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, who said: [[In the printed and manuscript texts it reads "from Abu Ishaq", which is a gross error.]] Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, related to me, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or Ikrimah related to me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Rifa'ah ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut was among their great men, that is, among the great men of the Jews. When he spoke to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he twisted his tongue and said: "Ra'ina sam'aka, O Muhammad, until we make you understand!" Then he attacked Islam and defamed it, so God revealed: "Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, who buy error," to His saying: "so they do not believe except a few." [[Report 9689: Ibn Hisham's Sirah 2:209, and it is a continuation of the earlier report numbered 9501.]]
9690 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salamah related to us, from Ibn Ishaq, [[In the printed edition alone: "from Abu Ishaq", while the manuscript is correct here.]] with his chain, from Ibn Abbas, the like of it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verses 44–45:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿They purchase error and wish that you would lose the way﴾ (44) ﴿But Allah is most knowing of your enemies. And sufficient is Allah as an ally, and sufficient is Allah as a helper﴾ (45).

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, "They purchase error," may He be exalted in praise, He means the Jews who were given a portion of the Book: they choose error, which is taking a path other than the truth and treading a way other than the right course and the correct direction, while knowing the intended path and the method of truth. [[See the explanation of "purchase" (ishtira') above: 1:312–315 / 2:340–342, 455 / 3:328 / 6:527 = and the explanation of "error" (dalala): 1:195, 313 / 2:495, 496 / 6:66, 500, 584 / 7:369.]] God only meant by describing them as purchasing error: their persistence in denying Muhammad (ﷺ), their abandoning of belief in him, while they know that the true way is belief in him and affirming him, by what they have found of his description in their books that are in their possession.

* *

As for His words, "and wish that you would lose the way," He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: these Jews whom He described as having been given a portion of the Book wish that you, O company of the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ) who affirm him, would go astray from the straight path and the road of truth, so that you would deny Muhammad and become misguided like them.

This is a warning from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, to His believing servants that they should not seek sincere counsel from any of the enemies of Islam regarding any matter of their religion, nor listen to anything of their slander against the truth.

* *

Then Allah, exalted in praise, informed of the enmity of these Jews, whom He forbade the believers from seeking counsel from in their religion, so He said: ﴿But Allah is most knowing of your enemies﴾. He, may His remembrance be exalted, means: Allah knows better than you the enmity of these Jews toward you, O believers. He says: so submit to My obedience regarding what I have forbidden you, namely seeking their counsel in your religion, [[In the manuscript: "mimma nahaytukum 'anhu" and in the printed edition: "amma nahaytukum 'anhu"; the correct reading is what I have recorded.]] for I know what they harbor toward you of deceit, enmity and envy, and that they only seek to harm you and wish that you would stray from the path of truth and perish.

* *

As for His words, "And sufficient is Allah as an ally, and sufficient is Allah as a helper," He says: so in Allah, O believers, place your trust, rely upon Him, and turn to Him alone, not to other than Him, and He will suffice you in your concerns and help you against your enemies. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as an ally﴾: He says, and Allah, your Lord, is sufficient and enough for you as an ally who takes charge of you and your affairs by guarding you and protecting you from your enemies provoking you away from your religion or preventing you from following your Prophet. [[See the explanation of "wali" (ally) above: 2:489, 564 / 5:424 / 6:142, 313, 497.]]

﴿And sufficient is Allah as a helper﴾: He says, and Allah is sufficient for you as a helper against your enemies and the enemies of your religion, and against whoever seeks to harm you and to bend your religion crooked. [[See the explanation of "nasir" (helper) above: 2:489, 564 / 5:581 / 6:443, 449.]]
