He says: so submit to My obedience regarding what I have forbidden you, namely seeking their counsel in your religion, [[In the manuscript: "mimma nahaytukum 'anhu" and in the printed edition: "amma nahaytukum 'anhu"; the correct reading is what I have recorded.]] for I know what they harbor toward you of deceit, enmity and envy, and that they only seek to harm you and wish that you would stray from the path of truth and perish.

* *

As for His words, "And sufficient is Allah as an ally, and sufficient is Allah as a helper," He says: so in Allah, O believers, place your trust, rely upon Him, and turn to Him alone, not to other than Him, and He will suffice you in your concerns and help you against your enemies. ﴿And sufficient is Allah as an ally﴾: He says, and Allah, your Lord, is sufficient and enough for you as an ally who takes charge of you and your affairs by guarding you and protecting you from your enemies provoking you away from your religion or preventing you from following your Prophet. [[See the explanation of "wali" (ally) above: 2:489, 564 / 5:424 / 6:142, 313, 497.]]

﴿And sufficient is Allah as a helper﴾: He says, and Allah is sufficient for you as a helper against your enemies and the enemies of your religion, and against whoever seeks to harm you and to bend your religion crooked. [[See the explanation of "nasir" (helper) above: 2:489, 564 / 5:581 / 6:443, 449.]]

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿Among those who are Jews are those who distort words from their [proper] places﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: Regarding the words of His, glorified is His praise, "Among those who are Jews are those who distort words," there are two possible interpretations.

The first: its meaning is, "Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture?" = "Among those who are Jews are those who distort words." In this case, "Among those who are Jews" is a relative clause modifying "those who." Most of the grammarians of Arabic from Kufa held this view and construed His words "Among those who are Jews are those who distort" in this way. [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 271.]]

* *

The other: its meaning is "Among those who are Jews are some who distort words from their places," so that "man" (some who) is omitted from the sentence, being sufficiently indicated by "Among those who are Jews." This is because if "min" (among) were mentioned in the sentence, it would be a part of "man," so the indication of "min" was relied upon instead. The Arabs say, "Among us is one who says that, and among us is one who does not say it," meaning, "Among us is one who says that, and among us is one who does not say it." So "man" is omitted, the indication of "min" being sufficient for it, as Dhu al-Rummah said:

*So they remained, and among them was one whose tears were flowing ahead of him, and another turning the tear of his eye with trickles.* [[From his Diwan, p. 485. Before it: "I wept over Mayy when I recognized her, and I stirred up love until the people wept on my account." With a variant reading: "So they remained, and among them was one whose tears overcame him, and another turning the tear of the eye with trickles. And is the flow of the eye returning what has passed of longing, or bringing you near me, O Mayy, from my people?" In the printed edition it read "yudhri" (scatters), which is an error and a change by the printer; in the manuscript it is "yuthni" (turns back), as in the Diwan. His words "yuthni dam'at al-'ayn" mean "turns back the flow of the eye," that is, it stops its flow. "Bil-hamal" is connected to "dam'a." Here "dam'a" is used as a verbal noun of "dama'at 'aynuhu dam'an, wa-dam'anan, wa-dumu'an" (his eye shed tears). He himself formed "dam'a" on the pattern of "rahma" among the verbal nouns, and likewise in the variant "'abra," both are verbal nouns, though the lexicons do not record them. He says: "and another turns back the running of the eye's tears, making them flow sparsely," meaning, were it not for that, his tears would have flowed in abundance.]]

That is, "And among them is one whose tears..." As Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿There is none of us but has a known position﴾ [Surah as-Saffat: 164]. Most of the grammarians of Arabic from Basra held this meaning as the interpretation of His words "Among those who are Jews are those who distort words." However, they said the implied element in that is "people" (qawm), as if its meaning for them were: "Among those who are Jews are a people who distort words." They cite as a parallel the words of al-Nabigha:

*As if you were one of the camels of Banu Uqaysh, rattled behind its hind legs with a skin bag.* [[Its takhrij was mentioned previously, 1: 179, note 2. I had forgotten to return it to this place, so I have included it here.]]

That is, "as if you were a camel of the camels of Uqaysh."

As for the grammarians of Kufa, they deny that the implied element with "min" can be anything other than "man" (one who) or something similar. [[See al-Farra's discussion in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 271.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The view that is more correct in my judgment regarding this is the view of the one who said: His words "Among those who are Jews" are a relative clause modifying "those who were given a portion of the Scripture," because both reports and both descriptions concern one category of people, namely the Jews whose description Allah gave in His words "Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Scripture?" The interpretation of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) has come in accordance with this, so there is no need in the speech, since the matter is so, for anything to be omitted from it.

* *

As for the interpretation of His words "they distort words from their places," it means that they change their meanings and alter them from their true interpretation.

* *

"Al-kalim" is the plural of "kalima" (word).

* *

Mujahid used to say: By "al-kalim" is meant the Torah.

9691 – He told me, Muhammad ibn 'Amr, who said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words "they distort words from their places": it is the Jews' altering of the Torah.

9692 – He told me, al-Muthanna, who said: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, who said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

* *

As for His words "from their places," it means: from their locations and the aspects that are their true aspects.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿and they say, "We hear and we disobey"﴾

Allah, glorified is His praise, means by this: among those who are Jews are those who say, "We hear, O Muhammad, your statement, and we disobey your command," as:

9693 – Ibn Humayd told us, who said: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasa, from Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid regarding His words "We hear and we disobey," he said: The Jews said, "We hear what you say, but we will not obey you."

9694 – He told me, Muhammad ibn 'Amr, who said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

9695 – He told me, al-Muthanna, who said: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, who said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

9696 – He told me, Yunus, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words "We hear and we disobey": they said, "We have heard, but we will not obey you."

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿and "Hear, without being made to hear"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from Allah, glorified is His praise, about the Jews who were around the emigration place (muhajar) of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in his time: that they used to curse the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and harm him with abusive speech, saying to him, "Hear from us without being made to hear," like the speaker's saying to a man he is cursing, "Hear, may Allah not make you hear," as:

9697 – He told me, Yunus, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words "and hear without being made to hear": He said, this is the statement of the People of the Book, the Jews, like the way a person says, "Hear, may you not hear," as harm to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and insult and mockery of him.

9698 – It was narrated to me from al-Minjab, who said: Bishr ibn 'Imara narrated to us, from Abu Rawq, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding "and hear without being made to hear": he said, they say to you, "Hear, may you not hear."

It has been narrated from Mujahid and al-Hasan that they both interpreted this as meaning: "Hear, [what you say] being unacceptable from you."

= Had that been its meaning, it would have said "hear, without being heard" (ghayra masmu'). But its meaning is: "hear, you will not hear." Allah, exalted is His remembrance, said "twisting with their tongues and attacking the religion," so He described them as distorting speech with their tongues and attacking the religion by reviling the Prophet (ﷺ).

* *

As for the view I reported from Mujahid, "hear without being made to hear," that is, "unaccepted is what you say," it is as follows:

9699 – al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "and hear without being made to hear," he said: "without being listened to." Ibn Jurayj said, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza, from Mujahid: "and hear without being made to hear," unacceptable is what you say.

9700 – He told me, al-Muthanna, who said: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, who said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

9701 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan regarding His words "and hear without being made to hear," he said: like when you say, "Hear, [what you say] being unlistened to from you."

9702 – And Musa ibn Harun narrated to us, who said: 'Amr narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Some people among them used to say "and hear without being made to hear," like your saying, "Hear, not humbled."  [[In the printed edition: "ghayra sagh" (not sagh), and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿and "Ra'ina" distorting with their tongues and attacking the religion﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "Ra'ina" is meant: "Ra'ina sam'aka" (attend to us with your hearing), understand from us and make us understand. We have explained the interpretation of this in Surat al-Baqara with its evidence, enough to avoid repeating it. [[See what preceded, 2: 459–467.]]

* *

Then Allah, glorified is His praise, informed about them that they say this to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "distorting with their tongues," that is, moving their tongues with it, by twisting its meaning toward the disliked of its two meanings, [[See the explanation of "al-layy" and "layy bil-alsina" previously, 6: 535–537.]] and making light of the rights of the Prophet (ﷺ), and attacking the religion, as:

9703 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya told me, who said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, who said: Qatada said: The Jews used to say to the Prophet (ﷺ), "Ra'ina sam'aka!" mocking by this. So the Jews were ugly in [using this word]; it was said "ra'ina sam'aka" = "distorting with their tongues," and al-layy is moving their tongues with it = "and attacking the religion."  [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "fa-kana fi al-yahud qabiha fa-qala," which is not at all coherent; its unquestionable correct form is what I have written. See that it is an ugly word of the Jews in 2: 460.]]

9704 – It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words "Ra'ina, distorting with their tongues": a man of the polytheists would say "Arina sam'aka!" twisting his tongue with it, meaning he distorts its meaning.

9705 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to us, who said: My father told me, who said: My paternal uncle told me, who said: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "Among those who are Jews are those who distort words from their places," through "and attacking the religion," for they used to mock and twist their tongues against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and attack the religion.

9706 – Yunus told me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said: "And Ra'ina, distorting with their tongues and attacking the religion." He said: "Ra'ina" is their attack on the religion, and their twisting with their tongues is to nullify and deny it. He said: "al-Ra'in" is the faulty word.  [[See the discussion of "al-ra'in" previously, 2: 465–466.]]

9707 – It was narrated to me from al-Minjab, who said: Bishr narrated to us, who said: Abu Rawq narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words "distorting with their tongues," he said: distortion by lying.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And if they had said, "We hear and we obey, and hear and look at us," it would have been better for them and more upright﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, glorified is His praise, means by this: If these Jews, whose description Allah gave, had said to the Prophet of Allah, "We hear your statement, O Muhammad, and we obey your command, and we accept what you have brought us from Allah, and hear from us, and look at us, that is, wait for us to understand from you what you say to us," "it would have been better for them and more upright," that is, it would have been better for them with Allah, "and more upright," that is, more just and more correct in speech.

* *

It derives from "al-istiqama" (uprightness) from Allah's words ﴿and more upright in speech﴾ [Surat al-Muzzammil: 6], meaning: "more correct in speech," as:

9708 – Yunus told me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words "If they had said, 'We hear and we obey, and hear and look at us,' it would have been better for them": he said: They say, "Hear from us, for we have heard and obeyed, and look at us, so do not hasten against us."

9709 – al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Abu Tumayla narrated to us, from Abu Hamza, from Jabir, from 'Ikrima and Mujahid regarding His words "and look at us": he said, "Hear from us."

9710 – al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, "and look at us": he said, "Make us understand."

9711 – He told me, Muhammad ibn 'Amr, who said: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, who said: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, "and look at us": he said, "Make us understand."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: What Mujahid and 'Ikrima said, in directing the meaning of "and look at us" to "hear from us," and Mujahid's directing it to "make us understand," is something we do not recognize in the speech of the Arabs, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "ma la na'rifu" without fa'; but I added it, because it is more deeply rooted in Arabic and more appropriate to the context.]] unless he meant by his direction to "make us understand" = "wait for us, so we may understand what you say" = or "wait for us until you hear from us," so that would be an understood meaning, though not an interpretation of the word or an explanation of it. [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "ghayr ta'wil al-kalima," and the correct one is what I have written.]] We do not recognize "unzurna" (look at us) in the speech of the Arabs except with the meaning "wait for us" and "look toward us." As for "unzurna" meaning "wait for us," there is the saying of al-Hutay'a:

*And I have awaited you, if only your milk-camel, one day, would come to me with its milking and its soothing.* [[From his Diwan, p. 52, and al-Kamil 1: 351. This is an unquestionable error in the reading of the verse; I have left it as it is, because it shows Abu Ja'far's haste sometimes in writing his commentary, and evidence of his memorization of poetry. Had it not been so, he would not have confused it so badly, since this qasida is the one in which he satirized al-Zibriqan ibn Badr and praised Baghid ibn 'Amir, and for which al-Zibriqan complained of him to 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, who imprisoned him. He says to al-Zibriqan when he became angry because he was hosted by Baghid: "The fault of Baghid was not, may you have no father, in a wretch who came driving the last of the people. I have milked you, if only your milk-camel would come to me one day with its milking and its soothing. I praised you deliberately to guide you, so that there might be for you a rope of wooden ..." Then follows the line of evidence that Abu Ja'far should have mentioned here, as he mentioned previously in the explanation of "unzurna" from Surat al-Baqara, 2: 467–468, and I explained it there. Had I not wished to preserve Abu Ja'far's state in his book, I would have dropped the verse mentioned in the text and put this verse: "And I have looked at you, [waiting] like the dwellers of the rain-carrying clouds, for the fifth [day of watering], whose guarding and waiting for it lasted long." The saying "Laqad miritukum" (I have milked you) derives from "marayt al-naqa yamriha maran," meaning when one strokes her udder to make her yield milk. "Al-darra" is a single flow of milk, and "al-masḥ" is stroking the udder for milking. "Al-Ibsas" is the herdsman's call, which he makes to his she-camel during milking so she calms down and her milking becomes easy. He says: I have been gentle with you, extracting your best with soft praise and gentle words, but I did not obtain any good, and you did not give any. In the manuscript it was "yajī'u bihi," which is an error.]]

As for "unzurna" meaning "look toward us," there is the saying of 'Abd Allah ibn Qays al-Ruqayyat:

*Apparent in beauty and loveliness, they look, as the gazelles look at the arak tree.* [[From his Diwan, p. 171, from his qasida in which he boasted of Quraysh and praised Mus'ab ibn al-Zubayr, and mentioned the women of 'Abd Shams ibn 'Abd Manaf, saying: "And graceful ones like statues, of 'Abshamiyyat, upon them is radiance and modesty; they do not sell their garments in the season of the people, when the women circle around the garments." "Apparent in beauty and nobility..." The rest of the line is damaged in the text. "Al-sarw" is nobility and generosity of lineage. This is the better of the two versions. His saying "as the gazelles look at the arak tree" is a fine simile, and an exact observation of the link between nobility and high rank, and what a man has of character, bearing and appearance. He means that they raise their necks, as gazelles stretch toward the arak tree to reach it. That is more evident of the beauty of their necks and their movement. The neck here is a sign of creation that no discerning person misses.]] meaning "as the gazelles look at the arak."  [[See the interpretation of a similar word from the Qur'anic verse "and say, 'unzurna'," 2: 467–469.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿But Allah has cursed them for their disbelief, so they believe not, except a few﴾ (46)

Abu Ja'far said: By this is meant: But Allah, blessed and exalted, humiliated these Jews whose description is given in this verse, and removed them and distanced them from right guidance and following the truth [[See the explanation of "al-la'na" (curse) previously, 2: 328 / 3: 254, 261 / 6: 577.]] "for their disbelief," that is, for their denial of the prophethood of His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and of what came to them from their Lord of guidance and clear signs. "So they believe not, except a few," that is, they do not affirm Muhammad (ﷺ) and what came to them from their Lord, nor do they acknowledge his prophethood, "except a few," that is, they do not affirm the truth that you brought them, O Muhammad, except a little faith, as:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 46 (part 2 of 2):

9712 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿So they do not believe, except a few﴾, he said: "They do not believe, except a few."

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: We have already explained the reasoning behind this in Surah al-Baqarah. [[That is, the commentary on the words of Allah Most High: ﴿So few of them believe﴾, 2:329-331.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 47:

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿O you who were given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their backs﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, "O you who were given the Scripture," He, may His praise be exalted, means the Jews of the Children of Israel who were around the place of emigration of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). God said to them: O you to whom the Scripture was sent down and who were given knowledge of it. "Believe" means: affirm what We have sent down to Muhammad of the Criterion (al-Furqan), "confirming what is with you," meaning: verifying what is with you of the Torah which We sent down to Moses son of Imran, "before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their backs."

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: "Its obliterating" (tamsuhā) means: erasing its traces until it becomes like the nape of the neck.

Others said: The meaning is that We obliterate their eyes and make them blind, but the report came by mentioning the "face," and what is meant is their sight. "And turn them back on their backs" means: We make their sight to be from behind their napes.

Those who said this:

9713 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to us, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "O you who were given the Scripture, believe" up to His saying "before We obliterate faces." Its obliterating is that they be blinded. "And turn them back on their backs" means: that We make their faces to be from behind their napes, so they walk backwards, and We give one of them two eyes in his nape.

9714 - Abu al-'Aliya Isma'il ibn al-Haytham al-'Abdi related to me, saying: Abu Qutayba related to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from 'Ata' al-'Awfi regarding His saying: "before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their backs," he said: We make them in their napes, so it walks on its heels backwards. [[The report 9714: "Abu al-'Aliya Isma'il ibn al-Haytham al-'Abdi" – we have not found him; see what has preceded, nos. 9365, 9366. And "Abu Qutayba" is Salm ibn Qutayba, whose biography has passed under nos. 1899, 1924, 9365.]]

9715 - Muhammad ibn 'Umara al-Asadi related to me, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa related to us, saying: Fudayl ibn Marzuq related to us, from 'Ata', similarly – except that he said: its obliterating: that He returns it upon its napes.

9716 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada: "and turn them back on their backs," he said: We turn their faces toward their backs.

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that [[In the printed edition, "bal" ("rather") is omitted.]] is: before We blind a people from the truth, "and turn them back on their backs," into misguidance and disbelief.

Those who said this:

9717 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "that We obliterate faces and turn them back on their backs": We turn them away from the path, from the truth, "and turn them back on their backs," he said: into misguidance.

9718 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Huthayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "that We obliterate faces" from the path of truth, "and turn them back on their backs," into misguidance.

9719 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us by reading, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid, the same.

9720 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: al-Hasan: "We obliterate faces," he says: We obliterate them from the truth, "and turn them back on their backs," upon their misguidance.

9721 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "O you who were given the Scripture" up to His saying "as We cursed the People of the Sabbath," he said: It was revealed concerning Malik ibn al-Sayyif and Rifa'a ibn Zayd ibn al-Tabut, of the Banu Qaynuqa'. As for "that We obliterate faces and turn them back on their backs," he says: We blind them from the truth and return them as disbelievers.

9722 - I was told by al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, saying: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: "before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their backs," meaning: that We turn them back from guidance and insight, and so He has turned them back on their backs, and they disbelieved in Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he brought.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: before We erase their traces from their faces, which they have, and their direction in which they are, "and turn them back on their backs," from the place from which they came at the beginning, from Syria. [[In the printed edition: "bad'an min al-Sham" ("starting from Syria"); the manuscript has "bady'an," and both are correct. "Badiyyan" means at the beginning of their affair. The explanation of "al-wujuh" here is: the directions.]]

Those who said this:

9723 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their backs," he said: My father used to say: to Syria.

* *

Others said: The meaning of: "before We obliterate faces," is: then We erase their traces and level them, "and turn them back on their backs," by making the faces the place of hair growth, as the faces of apes are places of hair growth, because the hair of the sons of Adam is on the backs of their faces. They said: When hair grows on their faces, He has turned them back on their backs, by making them like napes and the backs of faces. [[This is al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 272.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings in interpretation is the saying of the one who said: the meaning of His saying "before We obliterate faces" is: before We obliterate their sight and erase their traces, making them level like napes, "and turn them back on their backs," meaning: We make their sight on their backs; by this He means: We make the faces on the backs of faces, so the meaning is: We turn faces into napes and napes into faces, so they walk backwards, as Ibn 'Abbas, 'Ata' and those who said this said.

* *

We only said that this is more correct because God, may His praise be exalted, addressed with this verse the Jews whose description He gave in His saying: "Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Scripture, who buy misguidance?" Then He warned them, may His praise be exalted, by His saying: "O you who were given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their backs" – the verse – with His might, His dominance, and the hastening of His punishment upon them, [[The context: "then He warned them ... with His might and dominance ..."]] if they did not believe in what He commanded them to believe in. And there is no doubt that they, when He commanded them to believe, were then disbelievers.

* *

Since that is so, the corruption of the saying of the one who said: the interpretation of that is: that We blind them from the truth and return them into misguidance, is evident. For what is the sense of returning one who is already in misguidance into it? Rather, one is returned into a thing only if he was outside it. As for one who is within it, there is no sense in saying "We return him into it."

* *

Since that is so, and since it is correct that God threatened those mentioned in this verse with returning their faces upon their backs, the corruption of the interpretation of the one who said: the meaning is: He threatens them with returning them into their misguidance, is clear.

* *

As for those who said: the meaning is: before We make the faces places of hair growth like the appearance of the faces of apes, this is a saying opposed to the saying of the people of interpretation. And its departure from the saying of the people of knowledge among the Companions and the Successors and those after them among the later generations is sufficient evidence of its error.

* *

As for the saying of the one who said: its meaning is: before We obliterate their faces in which they are, and return them to Syria from their dwellings in the Hijaz and Najd, this – although it has some basis – is far from what the apparent sense of the revelation indicates. [[In the printed edition: "kama yadullu 'alayhi" ("as it indicates"); the manuscript has "kama yadullu 'ala", which contains two errors. The correct reading is what has been given.]] That is because the known meaning of "wujuh" (faces) in the speech of the Arabs is the opposite of "aqfa'" (napes), and the Book of God is directed in its interpretation toward the predominant usage of the speech of those in whose tongue it was revealed, until it indicates that something else than that is meant by the faces, which must be accepted.

* *

As for "tamus" (obliteration), it is effacement and obliteration in levelness. From it one says: "tamasat a'lam al-tariq tatmisu tumusan" when the signposts of the road are effaced and become worn, sunk and level with the ground, as Ka'b ibn Zuhayr said:

From every sweating, bristling-necked one, when her flank sweats, [its] flank is a road with obliterated signposts, unknown.

Meaning: "tamis al-a'lam," effaced of signposts, their markers buried. And from this is said of the blind man whose eyelids' slit has been effaced and his eyes obliterated: "a blind man, mutmas (obliterated), and tamsi," as God, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿And if We willed, We would obliterate their eyes﴾ [Surah Ya-Sin: 66].

* *

Abu Ja'far said: "al-Ghurr" is the slit that is between the two eyelids. [[In the printed edition: "al-'arasiq alladhi bayn al-khafayn" ("the 'arasiq between the two palms"); the first editor added a note to it with great confusion, which others copied from him!! As for the manuscript, which the editor did not read well, it had: "al-'ara-l-siq alladhi bayn al-khifayn," all unpointed; its correct reading is what has been given. The origin of this is that "al-ghurr" (with a fatha on the ghayn and shadda on the ra') is the crack in the earth. "Al-ghurr" also: the fold that occurs in cloth, and the creases in skin, and it is the folds of the skin; and from it comes the saying: "fold the cloth along its ghurr," meaning along its fold. This word appeared in Abu Ja'far's tafsir 23: 17, 18 misspelled with a zay: "And obliteration of the eye is that there is not between the two eyelids (ghuz), and that is the slit between the two eyelids." And see Ibn Ishaq's commentary in his Sira 2: 210: "The one with obliterated eye: the one who has no slit between his eyelids."

Thus the correctness of our reading and its soundness become clear from this, and the confusion of one who does not know how to confuse, let alone to be correct!!]]

* *

If someone says: If the matter is as you have described the interpretation of the verse, did what He threatened them with occur?

It is said: It did not occur, because a group of them believed, among them: 'Abd Allah ibn Salam, Tha'laba ibn Sa'ya, Asad ibn Sa'ya, [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "Asad ibn Sa'ya"; in Ibn Ishaq: "Usayd ibn Sa'ya" (with a fatha on the alif and a kasra on the sin). The difference in his name and his father's name is great.]] Asad ibn 'Ubayd, Mukhayriq, [[I have not found "Mukhayriq" in any other place than this; in the other books and in his biography it is "Mukhayriq." The differences in the names of the Children of Israel are great. So I left it as it is here, because it is thus confirmed in the manuscript.]] and a group other than them; so He averted (the punishment) from them by their faith.

And of what shows that this verse was revealed concerning the Jews whose description we have mentioned is what follows:

9724 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr related to us – and Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Salama related to us – both from Ibn Ishaq, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, related to me, saying: Sa'id ibn Jubayr or 'Ikrima related to me, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) spoke to leaders of the rabbis of the Jews, among them 'Abd Allah ibn Suriya and Ka'b ibn Asad, and said to them: O assembly of Jews, fear God and submit! By God, you know that what I have brought you is the truth! They said: We do not know that, O Muhammad! And they denied what they knew, and persisted in disbelief. So God revealed concerning them: "O you who were given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their backs" – the verse. [[In the manuscript: "the one which He ruled is true"; in the margin of the copy, in an old hand: "The correct: 'I was sent'"; the one who wrote this was mistaken; the correct is what is in the printed edition, and it is the text of Ibn Hisham's Sira.]] [[Report 9724: Sira of Ibn Hisham 2: 209, following the earlier report: 9689, 9690.]]

9725 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, from 'Isa ibn al-Mughira, who said: We discussed at the house of Ibrahim the Islam of Ka'b, [[That is, "Ka'b al-Ahbar."]] and he said: Ka'b embraced Islam in the time of 'Umar. He came, intending Bayt al-Maqdis, and passed by Medina, and 'Umar came out to him and said: O Ka'b, embrace Islam! He said: Do you not read in your Book: ﴿The likeness of those who were charged with the Torah, then did not carry it, is like the donkey carrying books﴾ [Surah al-Jumu'a: 5]? And I have carried the Torah! He said: So he left him. Then he went out until he reached Homs. He said: He heard a man of its people, sorrowful, saying: "O you who were given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their backs" – the verse. Ka'b said: O Lord, I have believed! O Lord, I have submitted! For fear that the verse would strike him. Then he returned and came to his family in Yemen, and then brought them, as Muslims.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Or We curse them as We cursed the People of the Sabbath, and God's command is ever carried out﴾ (4:47)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "Or We curse them," He means: or We curse you, and disgrace you, and make you apes, "as We cursed the People of the Sabbath," meaning: as We disgraced those among your forefathers who transgressed on the Sabbath. [[See the explanation of "the curse" above, p. 439, note 2, and the references there.]] This was said in the form of address in His saying: "believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you," as He said: ﴿until, when you are in the ship and they sail with them with a good wind, and they rejoice in it﴾ [Surah Yunus: 22]. [[See what has preceded 1: 154 / 3: 304, 305 / 6: 238, 464, and many other places earlier.]]

It may also be that its meaning is: "before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their backs," or We curse the people of the faces. The "ha' and mim" in His saying "Or We curse them" then refers to the people of the faces, since the speech contains an indication of that.

Those of the people of interpretation said things similar to what we have said regarding this.

Those who said that:

9726 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada regarding His saying: "O you who were given the Scripture" up to His saying "or We curse them as We cursed the People of the Sabbath": that is, We transform them into apes.

9727 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan: "Or We curse them as We cursed the People of the Sabbath," he says: or We make them apes.

9728 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "Or We curse them as We cursed the People of the Sabbath," or We make them apes.

9729 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "Or We curse them as We cursed the People of the Sabbath," he said: They are all Jews; We curse these as We cursed those of the People of the Sabbath whom We cursed. [[See the report on "the People of the Sabbath" above 2: 166–175.]]

* *

As for His saying, "and God's command is ever carried out," it means: and all that God commanded to be would be, existent and created, and nothing is impossible for Him to create of what He wills to create. And "the command" (al-amr) in this place is the thing commanded; it is called "God's command" because it came from His command and by His command.

The meaning is: and what God commanded was carried out.

The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with; but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His mention be exalted, He means: "O you who were given the Scripture, believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you" = Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with. That is, Allah does not forgive association with Him (shirk) and disbelief (kufr), and He forgives what is less than that, which is other than shirk, for whomever He wills among the people of sins and transgressions.

* *

Since that is the meaning of the speech, His words "that He be associated with" (an yushraka bihi) are in a place of accusative (naṣb) by the governing of "yaghfiru" (forgive) upon them [["al-waqū'" (the governing) transfers the verb to an object, as has passed many times.]] = or, if you wish, by the omission of the preposition that would have put them in the genitive had it been present. The meaning may be directed to: Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, on the interpretation of the conditional, as if it were said: Allah does not forgive a sin accompanied by association, or resulting from association. [[In the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' (1:272): "with association, nor from association", and the correct reading in the tafsir is as given.]]

According to this interpretation, it is possible that "an" (that) is in a place of genitive, in the view of some of the grammarians. [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' (1:272), for this is his opinion.]]

* *

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning people who doubted about the matter of the polytheists when the verse was revealed: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed, Allah forgives all sins; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [Surah al-Zumar: 53].

The report regarding this:

9730 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: Mujabbar related to me, from Abdullah ibn Umar, that he said: When the verse "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves" was revealed, a man stood up and said: "And shirk, O Prophet of Allah?" The Prophet ﷺ disliked that and said: "Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills, and whoever associates others with Allah has indeed fabricated a tremendous sin." [[Hadith 9730 - Ibn Abi Ja'far: he is Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far al-Razi, whose biography and that of his father have passed at 7030.

Al-Rabi': he is Ibn Anas al-Bakri, whose biography has passed at 5480.

Mujabbar (with a damma on the mim, a fatha on the jim, and a doubled, fathah-vowelled ba', in the pattern of "Muhammad"): he is the nephew of Abdullah ibn Umar. "Mujabbar" is his epithet; his name is "Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asghar ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab". Al-Mus'ab mentioned him in Nasab Quraysh, p. 356; Ibn Hazm in Jamharat al-Ansab, p. 146; and al-Dhahabi in al-Mushtabih, p. 462. He is biographed in al-Ta'jil, pp. 392-393, and he is also mentioned there in the biography of his son "Abd al-Rahman," pp. 256-257.

He has a narration in the Musnad (1402), from Uthman and Talhah. I think it is a disconnected narration, for his generation is too young to have met them.

He is mentioned in the Muwatta', p. 397: "Malik, from Nafi', from Abdullah ibn Umar: that he met a man from his family called Mujabbar, who had performed the ifadah and had not shaved or trimmed, being ignorant of that; so Abdullah commanded him to return, and to shave or trim, then return to the House and perform the ifadah."

I have found no other biography of him. He is a Successor (tabi'i) whose person is known and who was not described with any defect, so at least his hadith is to be considered good (hasan).

Ibn Kathir narrated the hadith at 2:481 from this place, then said: "Ibn Mardawayh narrated it through several chains from Ibn Umar."

Al-Suyuti mentioned it at 1:169 and attributed it also to Ibn Abi Hatim.

It will come after this with a weak chain, because of the ambiguity of al-Tabari's shaykh.

9731 - It was narrated to me from Ammar, who said: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', concerning His words: "Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills," he said: Mujabbar informed me, from Abdullah ibn Umar, that he said: When this verse was revealed, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves," a man stood up and said: "And shirk, O Prophet of Allah?" The Prophet disliked that and said: "Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills."

9732 - Muhammad ibn Khalaf al-Asqalani related to me, saying: Adam related to us, saying: al-Haytham ibn Jammaz related to us, saying: Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani related to us, from Ibn Umar, who said: We, the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, had no doubt about the killer of a soul, the eater of an orphan's wealth, the false witness, and the one who severs the ties of kinship, until this verse was revealed: "Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills," and then we refrained from testifying. [[Hadith 9732 - Adam: he is Ibn Abi Iyas al-Asqalani, whose biography has passed at 187. Al-Haytham ibn Jammaz al-Bakka, al-Hanafi al-Basri al-Qadi: weak; weakened by Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in, al-Nasa'i and others. He is biographed in Lisan al-Mizan 6:204-205, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/2/216, Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/81, and al-Du'afa' of al-Nasa'i, p. 30.

"Jammaz" (with a fatha on the jim, a doubled mim, and a final zay) appears in the manuscript and printed edition as "Hammad," which is a scribal error. Likewise it appears misspelled in al-Tahdhib 11:100, in the biography of "al-Haytham ibn Abi al-Haytham."

Bakr ibn Abdullah al-Muzani: a known, trustworthy Successor, from whom the whole group narrated.

The hadith is mentioned by al-Suyuti at 2:169, attributed also to Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bazzar.

Its meaning is established from Ibn Umar through other narrations:

In al-Durr al-Manthur 2:169: "Ibn al-Darris, Abu Ya'la, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Adi narrated with a sound chain, from Ibn Umar, who said: We used to refrain from seeking forgiveness for the people of major sins until we heard from our Prophet ﷺ: (Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills), and he said: I have stored up my supplication as my intercession for the people of major sins from my community. So we refrained from much of what was in our hearts, then we spoke afterward and hoped." al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7:5 and said: "Abu Ya'la narrated it, and its men are the men of the Sahih, except Harb ibn Surayj, who is trustworthy."

In Majma' al-Zawa'id 10:210-211: "From Ibn Umar, who said: We used to refrain from seeking forgiveness for the people of major sins, until we heard our Prophet ﷺ say: (Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with, and He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills), and he said: My intercession has been delayed for the people of major sins on the Day of Resurrection. Al-Bazzar narrated it, and its chain is good." It is similar to the preceding.

Also in it, at 10:193, are narrations with this meaning from Ibn Umar.

Moreover, in the manuscript it read: "we had no doubt about the believer, and the eater of an orphan's wealth": there is a blank between them, and above "the believer" there is a letter "ta'," which indicates that the copy from which it was transcribed was not clear, so we have established what came in the other narrations.

And this verse has made clear that every possessor of a major sin is within the will of Allah: if He wills, He pardons him, and if He wills, He punishes him for it, so long as the sin is not the major sin of associating partners with Allah.

* *

The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah, he has indeed fabricated a tremendous sin﴾ (4:48)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His mention be exalted, He means: "And whoever associates others with Allah" in worshipping other than Him from among His creation, "then he has indeed fabricated a tremendous sin," meaning: he has indeed invented a tremendous sin. [[See the explanation of "iftara" (fabricated) above, 6:292.] And He, may His mention be exalted, called him "a fabricator" because he spoke falsehood and lies by his denial of the Oneness of Allah, and by his affirmation that Allah has a partner from His creation, and a consort or a son. So the one who says that is a fabricator. Likewise, every liar is a fabricator in his lie, one who invents it.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 49:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Have you not seen those who justify themselves? Rather, God justifies whom He wills﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His majesty be exalted, He means: Have you not seen, Muhammad, with your heart [see the explanation of "Have you not seen" earlier, ref. 426, note 5, and the references there], those who justify themselves from among the Jews, declaring themselves innocent of sins and purifying them? [See the explanation of "tazkiyah" (purification, self-justification) earlier, ref. 369, note 2, and the references there.]

* *

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning by which the Jews used to justify themselves.

Some of them said: Their self-justification was their saying, "We are the sons of God and His beloved."

Those who said this:

9733 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "Have you not seen those who justify themselves? Rather, God justifies whom He wills, and they will not be wronged even the bit of a date-thread." They are the enemies of God, the Jews, who justified themselves with a matter they had not attained, and said, "We are the sons of God and His beloved," and said, "We have no sins."

9734 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan regarding His saying: "Have you not seen those who justify themselves," he said: They are the Jews and the Christians, who said, "We are the sons of God and His beloved," and said, "None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians."

9735 - And al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Tamilah narrated to us, from Ubayd ibn Sulayman, from al-Dahhak, who said: The Jews said, "We have no sins except like the sins of our children on the day they are born! If they have sins, then we have sins! For we are just like them!" God, may His remembrance be exalted, said: ﴿Look how they invent lies against God, and sufficient is that as a manifest sin.﴾

9736 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "Have you not seen those who justify themselves," he said: The People of the Book said, "None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians," and said, "We are the sons of God and His beloved," and said, "We are upon that which God loves." So the Blessed and Exalted said: "Have you not seen those who justify themselves? Rather, God justifies whom He wills," when they claimed that they would enter Paradise, and that they were the sons of God and His beloved and the people of His obedience.

9737 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Have you not seen those who justify themselves? Rather, God justifies whom He wills, and they will not be wronged even the bit of a date-thread," was revealed concerning the Jews, who said, "We teach our children the Torah while they are young, so they have no sins, and our sins are like the sins of our children; whatever we do by day is expiated for us by night."

* *

Others said: Rather, their self-justification was their placing their children forward to lead them in prayer, claiming that they had no sins.

Those who said this:

9738 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "Those who justify themselves," he said: The Jews, who used to put their children forward in prayer, having them lead them, claiming that they had no sins. That is the self-justification.

9739 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

9740 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from al-A'raj, from Mujahid, who said: They used to put the children in front of them in supplication and prayer, having them lead them, and claiming that they had no sins; that is self-justification. Ibn Jurayj said: They are the Jews and the Christians.

9741 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Husayn, from Abu Malik regarding His saying: "Have you not seen those who justify themselves," he said: It was revealed concerning the Jews, who used to put their children forward, saying, "They have no sins."

9742 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Abu Makin, from Ikrimah regarding His saying: "Have you not seen those who justify themselves," he said: The People of the Book used to put forward the boys who had not reached puberty to pray with them, saying, "They have no sins!" So God revealed: "Have you not seen those who justify themselves," the verse. [Report 9742: "Abu Makin" is Nuh ibn Rabi'ah al-Ansari, their mawla. His biography is in al-Tahdhib.]

* *

Others said: Rather, their self-justification was their saying, "Our children will intercede for us and purify us."

Those who said this:

9743 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "Have you not seen those who justify themselves." That was because the Jews said, "Our children have died, and they are a means of nearness for us to God, and they will intercede and purify us!" So God said to Muhammad: "Have you not seen those who justify themselves," up to "and they will not be wronged even the bit of a date-thread."

* *

Others said: Rather, that was from them: a self-justification by some of them of others.

Those who said this:

9744 - Yahya ibn Ibrahim al-Mas'udi narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, from his father, from al-A'mash, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: Abd Allah said: "A man goes out in the morning with his religion, then returns with nothing of it! He meets a man who owns neither benefit nor harm for him, and says, 'By God, you are such-and-such and such-and-such,' and perhaps he returns without having obtained anything of his need, and he has angered God against himself." Then he recited: "Have you not seen those who justify themselves," the verse. [Report 9744: Yahya ibn Ibrahim ibn Abi Ubaydah al-Mas'udi, whose biography was given earlier under no. 5379. Qays ibn Muslim al-Jadali al-Adwani narrated from Tariq ibn Shihab, and was narrated from by al-A'mash, Sufyan al-Thawri and others. Ahmad said: "Trustworthy in hadith, he was a Murji'i." Ahmad also said, quoting Sufyan: "They say: he has not raised his head to the sky for such-and-such a time, out of glorification of God." Tariq ibn Shihab al-Ahmasi: all four (authors of the Sunan) narrated from him. Tariq saw the Prophet (ﷺ), narrated from him as a mursal report, and narrated from the four rightly guided caliphs, Bilal, Hudhayfah, and Khalid ibn al-Walid.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions is the view of those who said: the meaning of "the self-justification of the people" whom God described as justifying themselves is that they described themselves as having no sins or faults, and that they are sons and beloveds of God, as God reported that they used to say. This is because that is the most evident of its meanings, since God reported that they only justified themselves and not others.

* *

As for those who said the meaning is "their placing children forward for prayer," that is an interpretation whose soundness cannot be known except by a conclusive report that necessitates knowledge.

* *

As for His saying, may His majesty be exalted, "Rather, God justifies whom He wills": it is a refutation from God of the Jews and Christians who justify themselves, declaring themselves free of sins. God says to them: The matter is not as you claim, that you have no sins or faults and that you are innocent of what God dislikes; rather, you are people of slander and lying against God. The one who is justified is not the one who justifies himself, but the one whom God justifies. God justifies whom He wills of His creation, purifying him and declaring him free of sins, by granting him success to avoid what He dislikes of disobedience, and to what He is pleased with of obedience.

* *

We only said that this is so because of His saying, may His majesty be exalted: "Look how they invent lies against God," and He reported that they invent lies against God by their claim that they are the sons of God and His beloved, and that God has purified them of sins.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿and they will not be wronged the bit of a date-thread (fatil)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His majesty be exalted, He means: God does not wrong these people whom He reported as justifying themselves, nor any other of His creatures, by depriving them, in leaving their self-justification unrewarded, or in the justification of those whom He justifies among His creatures, of any part of their rights, nor does He place anything in other than its proper place. Rather, He justifies whom He wills of His creatures, granting him success, and forsakes whom He wills of the people of disobedience. All of that is for Him and in His hand, and in all of that He wrongs no one, whether justified by Him or not, even by the bit of a date-thread.

* *

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of "fatil."

Some of them said: It is the filth that comes out from between the two fingers and the palms when one of them is rubbed against the other.

Those who said this:

9745 - Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar [said: Muhammad ibn al-Salt narrated to us] narrated to me, saying: Abu Kudaynah narrated to us, from Qabus, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Fatil is what comes out from between your two fingers. [Report 9745: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar ibn Zurayq al-Khayyat, mentioned earlier at no. 5994; likewise the biography of Muhammad ibn al-Salt, and of Abu Kudaynah: Yahya ibn al-Muhallab. The chain appears to be defective, as I judge: the mention of Muhammad ibn al-Salt has dropped out, as in 5994 and 7964, and as the same chain appears later at 9799; also Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar did not meet Abu Kudaynah. Qabus is Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan al-Janbi, who narrated from his father Husayn ibn Jundub. He is weak and not to be relied upon, as Ibn Sa'd said. Ibn Hibban said: "He had poor memory, and transmitted from his father what has no basis." His father Husayn ibn Jundub al-Janbi, Abu Zabyan, narrated from Umar, Ali, Ibn Mas'ud, Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar and others among the Companions and Successors, and he is trustworthy. Biography in al-Tahdhib.]

9746 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Anbasah, from Abu Ishaq al-Hamdani, from al-Taymi, who said: I asked Ibn Abbas about His saying, "and they will not be wronged the bit of a date-thread," and he said: What you twist between your two fingers.

9747 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Dirham Abu al-Ala', who said: I heard Abu al-Aliyah from Ibn Abbas: "and they will not be wronged the bit of a date-thread," he said: The fatil is what comes out from between the two fingers of a man. [Report 9747: Yazid ibn Dirham Abu al-Ala' al-Ajami, brother of Muhammad ibn Dirham, narrated from Anas ibn Malik and al-Hasan; here he also narrates from Abu al-Aliyah, which they did not mention. Narrated from by Waki' and Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith. al-Fallas said: "Trustworthy"; Ibn Ma'in said: "He is nothing." Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy and said: "He errs much." Biography in Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/260 and Lisan al-Mizan 6:286. See the next report 9811 and its commentary. In the printed edition it read "Zayd ibn Dirham", the correct reading being from the manuscript.]

9748 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "and they will not be wronged the bit of a date-thread." Fatil is that you rub your two fingers, and whatever comes out between them is that.

9749 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Abu Malik regarding His saying: "and they will not be wronged the bit of a date-thread," he said: The fatil is the dirt that comes out from between the palms.

9750 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: The fatil is what you twist with your two hands, and dirt comes out.

9751 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "and they will not be wronged the bit of a date-thread," he said: What you rub in your hands so that it comes out between them.

* *

Others say: It is what is in the inside of the date-stone.

Those who said this:

9752 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "fatilan," he said: What is in the inside of the date-stone.

9753 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Talhah ibn Amr, from Ata', who said: The fatil is what is in the inside of the date-stone.

9754 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Talhah ibn Amr narrated to me that he heard Ata' ibn Abi Rabah say, and he mentioned the like.

9755 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Abd Allah ibn Kathir informed me that he heard Mujahid say: The fatil is what is in the split of the date-stone.

9756 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: The fatil is in the date-kernel.

9757 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His saying: "and they will not be wronged the bit of a date-thread," he said: The fatil is what is in the split of the date-stone.

9758 - It was reported from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say: The fatil is the split of the date-stone.

9759 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: The fatil is what is in the inside of the date-stone.

9760 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, who said: The fatil is what is in the split of the date-stone.

9761 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "and they will not be wronged the bit of a date-thread," the thread of the date-stone.

9762 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Amir narrated to us, saying: Qurrah narrated to us, from Atiyyah, who said: The fatil is what is in the inside of the date-stone. [Report 9762: Abu Amir is Abu Amir al-Aqadi, Abd al-Malik ibn Amr, whose biography was given earlier under no. 4143. Qurrah is Qurrah ibn Khalid al-Sadusi, who narrated from Abu Raja' al-Utaridi, Ibn Sirin and al-Hasan; narrated from by Shu'bah, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi and others. Biography in al-Tahdhib. Atiyyah is Atiyyah ibn Sa'd ibn Janadah al-Awfi; biography at no. 305.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The root of "fatil" is "maftul" (twisted), transformed from the pattern "maf'ul" to "fa'il," as it is said "sari'" and "dahin" from "masru'" and "madhun."

Since this is so, and since God, may His majesty be exalted, intended by His saying "and they will not be wronged the bit of a date-thread" a report that He does not wrong His servants even the least of things, which has no weight, how much less what has weight; and since the filth that comes out from between a man's two fingers, or between his palms when one twists one against the other, is like what is in the split and inside of the date-stone, and the like of such twisted things that have no weight and no value: it is necessary that all of that enter the meaning of "fatil," unless some part of it is excluded by what must be accepted, as indicated by the apparent sense of the revelation.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 50:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Look how they invent lies against Allah, and sufficient is that as a manifest sin﴾ (4:50).

Abu Ja'far said: Exalted is His praise, by this He means: Look, O Muhammad, at how these people who purify themselves, from among the People of the Book, those who say, "We are the sons of Allah and His beloved," and that none will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians, those who claim that they have no sins, invent falsehood and lies in speech, fabricating it against Allah. ﴿And sufficient is that﴾ means: their saying that falsehood and lies about Allah is sufficient for them as ﴿a manifest sin﴾, meaning that it makes their lying clear to those who hear it, and makes plain to them that they are liars and wicked sinners. [[See the interpretation of the words of this verse in the earlier linguistic indexes.]] As related:

9763 - Al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿Have you not seen those who purify themselves﴾, he said: They are the Jews and the Christians. ﴿Look how they invent lies against Allah﴾ [[See the interpretation of "Have you not seen" earlier, at 452, footnote 1, and the references there; and the interpretation of "al-nasib" earlier, at 427, footnote 3, and the references there.]]

**The exegesis of His words: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book, who believe in jibt and taghut﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: Almighty God means by this: Have you not seen with your heart, O Muhammad, those who were given a share of the Book of God and learned it, "who believe in jibt and taghut." That is, they affirm the truth of jibt and taghut and disbelieve in God, while they know that believing in them is disbelief and affirming them is polytheism.

* * *

Then the people of ta'wil (interpretation, i.e., the exegetes) differed over the meaning of "jibt" and "taghut."

Some of them said: They are two idols that the polytheists worshipped besides God.

Those who said this include:

9764. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, saying: Ayyub informed me, from Ikrimah, that he said: "Jibt" and "taghut" are two idols.

* * *

Others said: "Jibt" means the idols, and "taghut" means the interpreters of the idols. [[By his words "the interpreters of the idols" he means the soothsayers, who speak through the tongues of the idols, as though they say to people in their own language what those idols say with their tongues.]]

Those who said this include:

9765. Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: "Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book, who believe in jibt and taghut": "Jibt" is the idols, and "taghut" is those who stand before the idols and express falsehood on their behalf in order to mislead people.

* * *

It was claimed by some men that "jibt" is the soothsayer (kahin), and "taghut" is a man from the Jews called Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, who was the chief of the Jews.

* * *

Others said: "Jibt" is sorcery, and "taghut" is the Satan.

Those who said this include:

9766. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Adi told us, from Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from Hassan ibn Fa'id, who said: Umar, may God have mercy on him, said: "Jibt" is sorcery, and "taghut" is the Satan. [[The report 9766: Hassan ibn Fa'id al-Absi, mentioned under no. 5834. In the printed edition of this report and the following one it appeared as "Hassan ibn Qa'id al-Anasi." This isnad passed under no. 5835.]]

9767. Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: My father told us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Hassan ibn Fa'id al-Absi, from Umar, the like of it. [[Report 9767: passed under no. 5834.]]

9768. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim told me, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Abd al-Malik informed us, from one who narrated to him, from Mujahid, who said: "Jibt" is sorcery, and "taghut" is the Satan.

9769. Ya'qub told me, saying: Hushaym informed us, saying: Zakariyya informed us, from al-Sha'bi, who said: "Jibt" is sorcery, and "taghut" is the Satan.

9770. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words "who believe in jibt and taghut," who said: "Jibt" is sorcery, and "taghut" is the Satan in the form of a human being to whom they refer their disputes, and he is the one who controls their affair.

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view concerning the interpretation of "who believe in jibt and taghut" is to say: They affirm the truth of two objects of worship besides God, worship them besides God, and take them as two gods.

That is because "jibt" and "taghut" are names for anything that is venerated by worship besides God, or by obedience, or by submission to it, whatever that venerated thing may be: a stone, a human being, or a satan. Since this is so, and the idols which the people of ignorance (jahiliyyah) worshipped were venerated by worship besides God, they were indeed "jibt" and "taghut." Likewise the satans whom the disbelievers obeyed in disobedience to God; likewise the sorcerer and the soothsayer, whose words concerning the people of polytheism were accepted. Likewise Huyayy ibn Akhtab and Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, because they were obeyed among the people of their religion, the Jews, in disobedience to God and in disbelief in Him and in His Messenger; so they were a "jibt" and a "taghut."

I have already explained the root from which "taghut" was derived, sufficiently so that it need not be repeated here. [[See above, 5:419, and the remaining reports concerning "taghut" from no. 5834 to 5845.]]

**The exegesis of His words: ﴿And they say to those who disbelieved, "These are better guided in the way than those who believed"﴾ (4:51)**

Abu Ja'far said: Almighty God means by this: And they say to those who denied the oneness of God and the prophethood of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): "These," that is, those whom God described as disbelievers, "are better guided," that is, more upright and more just, "than those who believed," that is, than those who affirmed the truth of God and His Messenger and acknowledged what their prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) brought them, "in the way," that is, in the path.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: This is only an example. The meaning of the statement is: God described those among the People of the Book who were given a share of the Scripture, the Jews, as those who venerated other than God by worship and submitted to Him in obedience, in their disbelief in God and His Messenger and their disobedience to them, and that they said that the people of disbelief in God were more entitled to the truth than the people of belief in Him, and that the religion of those who denied God and His Messenger was more just and more correct than the religion of those who affirmed God and His Messenger. It was mentioned that this was a description of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, and that he was the one who said it. [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "and that they said" with the conjunction waw; the waw is joined to the alif in the manuscript, and the correct reading is what I have given. The phrase "that" depends on the statement "God described ..."]]

[[In the printed edition: "the best of the people of Medina"; in the manuscript: "hibr," though it is unpointed in many places. Lisan al-Arab, under the root ṣ-n-b, has "khayr," and under the root b-t-r has "hibr." Abu Jaʿfar said: The most correct of the opinions regarding this is the statement of the one who said: It is a report from Allah, may His praise be exalted, about a group of the People of the Book from the Jews. It is permissible that the group were those whom Ibn ʿAbbas named in the report narrated by Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad from ʿIkrimah or Saʿid, or that it was Huyayy and another with him, either Kaʿb or someone else.

**The meaning of His words, "Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, and whoever Allah curses, you will not find for him a helper" (﴿أُولَئِكَ الَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ وَمَنْ يَلْعَنِ اللَّهُ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُ نَصِيرًا﴾ 4:52)**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words "Those" (﴿أُولَئِكَ﴾), He, may His praise be exalted, means these people whose description He gave, that they were given a share of the Scripture and they believe in al-jibt and al-taghut. They are "the ones whom Allah has cursed (﴿الَّذِينَ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾)," meaning: Allah has disgraced them and removed them far from His mercy, because of their belief in al-jibt and al-taghut, and their disbelief in Allah and His Messenger, out of obstinacy toward Allah and His Messenger, and because of their saying to those who disbelieved, "These are better guided than those who believed in the way" (﴿هَؤُلَاءِ أَهْدَى مِنَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا سَبِيلًا﴾). "And whoever Allah curses (﴿وَمَنْ يَلْعَنِ اللَّهُ﴾)," meaning: whoever Allah disgraces and so removes far from His mercy, "then you will not find for him a helper (﴿فَلَنْ تَجِدَ لَهُ نَصِيرًا﴾)," meaning: you will not find for him, O Muhammad, any helper who will support him against the punishment of Allah and His curse which will befall him, so as to ward that off from him.

As this is related:

So Allah revealed: "Those are the ones whom Allah has cursed, and whoever Allah curses, you will not find for him a helper."

[[See the explanation of "al-la'nah" (curse) above, p. 439, note 2, and the references there; and the explanation of "al-nasir" (helper) above, p. 430, note 2, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 53:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Or do they have a share of the dominion? Then they would not give the people even a speck (naqir).﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "Or do they have a share of the dominion" — "or do they have a portion (hazz) of the dominion" — He means: they have no portion of the dominion. [See the explanation of "al-nasib" (share) in what preceded: 460, footnote 2, and the references there.] As related:

9797 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: God said: "Or do they have a share of the dominion," he said: So they have no share of the dominion, [they do not give the people a speck] = "then they would not give the people a speck." [In the printed edition the whole phrase "they do not give the people a speck" is omitted, and it is in fact a disjointed sentence, so I have restored it as it is between brackets.] And if they had a share and portion of the dominion, they would not then give the people a speck, out of their stinginess.
