9808 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, who said: "The naqir" is in the date-stones.

9809 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Abdullah ibn Kathir informed me: that he heard Mujahid say: "The naqir" is the naqir of the date-stone that is in its middle.

9810 - It was related to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say: "The naqir" is the naqir of the date-stone that is in the middle of the date-stone.

* *

Others said: the meaning is: a man flicking a thing with the tips of his fingers.

Those who said this:

9811 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Dirham Abu al-Ala', who said: I heard Abu al-Aliyah: Ibn Abbas placed the tip of the thumb on the back of the index finger, then raised them and said: This is the naqir. [Report 9811: Yazid ibn Dirham Abu al-Ala' appeared as no. 9747 in this same chain, and I commented on him there. In the printed edition here also it was "Zayd ibn Dirham," and I showed the error there. As for the manuscript here, it read: "from Ibn Dar ibn Dirham," poorly written, with the two rā's joined and unpointed.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings is that it should be said: God described this group of the People of the Book with stinginess in a small thing of no worth, even though they were kings and people of power over things of great standing. Since this is so, what is more appropriate for the meaning of "naqir" is that it be the smallest of what is called a naqr. And if that is the more appropriate, then the pit that is on the back of the date-stone is among the smallest of the naqr, and whatever resembles it of the naqr may be included in that. His saying "lā yu'tūna al-nās" (they do not give the people) is in the nominative and is not put in the accusative after "idhan," and the rule of "idhan" is that it puts the future verbs in the accusative when the speech begins with them, because of the "fa" that accompanies it. And its rule, when some conjunctive particle enters upon it, is that it may be directed toward beginning with it once, and toward transferring it to something else another time. This place is one where the "fa" is intended to transfer from "idhan" to what follows it, and the meaning of the speech is: "Or do they have a share, so they do not give the people a speck then." [The discussion of "idhan" has been fully treated by al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:273-274.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 54:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His majesty be exalted, "Or do they envy the people," he means: Or do these people who were given a portion of the Book, namely the Jews, envy [others], as:

9812 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the word of Allah, "Or do they envy the people," he said: "The Jews."

9813 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

9814 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, the same.

* *

As for His words "the people," the scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning whom Allah meant by it.

Some of them said: Allah meant by that Muhammad (ﷺ) specifically.

Those who said this:

9815 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Amr narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Khalid, from Ikrima, regarding His words, "Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty," he said: "The people" in this place means the Prophet (ﷺ) specifically.

9816 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to me, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty," meaning Muhammad (ﷺ).

9817 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, the same.

9818 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty," he said: "The people" means Muhammad (ﷺ).

9819 - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say, and he mentioned something similar.

* *

Others said: Rather, Allah meant by it the Arabs.

Those who said this:

9820 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty," "Those are the Jews; they envied this tribe of the Arabs for what Allah had given them of His bounty."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views is to say: Allah rebuked the Jews whose description He gave in these verses, when they said to the polytheists, worshippers of idols, that they were better guided than Muhammad and his companions in the way, while knowing that in what they said they were liars: "Do you envy Muhammad and his companions for what Allah has given them of His bounty?" [[In the printed edition: "Or do they envy," and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]

* *

We said that this is more correct because what precedes His words "Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty" passed with the censure of the Jewish speakers who said of those who disbelieved: "These are better guided than those who believed in the way." So attaching His words "Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty" to their censure for that, and to the praise of the believers about whom that was said, is more fitting and more correct, so long as no evidence indicates that its meaning has turned away from that meaning.

* *

The scholars of interpretation differed concerning the interpretation of "the bounty" (al-fadl) which Allah informed that He gave to those He mentioned in His words "Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty." [[See the explanation of "al-fadl" earlier in the language indexes.]] Some of them said: That "bounty" is prophethood.

Those who said this:

9821 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty," they envied this tribe of the Arabs for what Allah had given them of His bounty. Allah sent a prophet from among them, and they envied them for that.

9822 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: "For what Allah has given them of His bounty," he said: prophethood.

Others said: Rather, that "bounty" which Allah mentioned that He gave them is His permitting for His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) what He permitted of women, so that he might marry as many as he wished without limit. They said: And what is meant by "the people" is Muhammad (ﷺ), as I mentioned before.

Those who said this:

9823 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty," to the end of the verse. That was because the People of the Book said: "Muhammad claims that he was given what he was given out of humility, and he has nine wives; his only concern is marriage! What kingship is greater than this!" So Allah said: "Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty."

9824 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty," meaning Muhammad, that he may marry whatever women he wishes.

9825 - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: "Or do they envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty," that the Jews said: "What is the matter with Muhammad? He was given prophethood as he claims, yet he is hungry and naked, and his only concern is marrying women?" So they envied him for marrying wives, and Allah made lawful for Muhammad that he marry from among them whatever he wished to marry. [[Report 9825: In the manuscript and the printed edition, "It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say," the chain as I have set it down dropped out. It is a chain that recurs in the tafsir, the nearest of which is no. 9819.

I have already noted that this statement of the Jews was taken up after them by those harboring rancor against Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, and they continue to spread it in their books, and their followers among the misguided people who worship their masters among the orientalists of our time have clung to it.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the two interpretations is the statement of Qatada and Ibn Jurayj that we mentioned before: that the meaning of "the bounty" in this place is the prophethood by which Allah favored Muhammad and honored the Arabs, since He gave it to a man from among them rather than others. This is because the apparent meaning of this verse indicates that it is praise of the Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions, may Allah have mercy upon them, [[In the printed edition: "may Allah be pleased with them," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript; I have done this many times without noting it in some places.]] as we have already explained. Marriage and the marrying of women, though it is among the bounty of Allah, may His majesty be exalted, which He gave to His servants, is not a praise or commendation of them.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿For We had already given the family of Abraham the Book and wisdom, and We gave them a great kingdom﴾ (54)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His majesty be exalted, He means: Or do these Jews, whose description He gave in these verses, envy the people for what Allah has given them of His bounty, because they are not of them? How then do they not envy the family of Abraham? For We had given them the Book. By His words "For We had already given the family of Abraham," he means: We had given the family of Abraham, that is, his household and followers in his religion [[See the explanation of "family" (al) earlier: 2:37 / 3:222, note 1 / 6:326.]], "the Book," meaning the Book of Allah which He revealed to them, such as the scrolls of Abraham and Moses and the Psalms, and all the other books that He gave them.

* *

As for "wisdom," it is what was revealed to them that was not a written book. "And We gave them a great kingdom."

* *

The scholars of interpretation differed concerning the meaning of "the great kingdom" that Allah intended in this verse. [[See the explanation of "kingdom" (al-mulk) earlier: 1:148–150 / 2:488 / 5:312, 314, 371 / 6:299, 300.]]

Some of them said: It is prophethood.

Those who said this:

9826 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the word of Allah, "Or do they envy the people," he said: "The Jews." "For what Allah has given them of His bounty; for We had already given the family of Abraham the Book," and they are not of them, "and wisdom, and We gave them a great kingdom," he said: "Prophethood."

9827 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same, except that he said: "kingdom" is prophethood.

* *

Others said: Rather, that is the permitting of women. They said: What Allah meant by that is: Or do they envy Muhammad for what Allah made lawful for him of women? Allah had made lawful for Dawud and Sulayman and other prophets the like of what He made lawful for him of them. So why did they not envy those, while envying Muhammad, peace be upon him?

Those who said this:

9828 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "For We had already given the family of Abraham," Sulayman and Dawud, "the wisdom," meaning prophethood, "and We gave them a great kingdom," over women. What is the matter then that this was made lawful for those, who were prophets, that Dawud should marry ninety-nine women and Sulayman a hundred, and it is not lawful for Muhammad to marry as they married?

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of His words "and We gave them a great kingdom" is what was given to Sulayman son of Dawud.

Those who said this:

9829 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "And We gave them a great kingdom," meaning the kingdom of Sulayman.

* *

Others said: Rather, they were supported with the angels.

Those who said this:

9830 - Ahmad ibn Hazim al-Ghifari narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from Hammam ibn al-Harith: "And We gave them a great kingdom," he said: They were supported with the angels and the hosts.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these interpretations for the verse, namely His words "and We gave them a great kingdom," is the statement reported from Ibn Abbas that he said: "Meaning the kingdom of Sulayman." This is because that is what is well known in the speech of the Arabs, rather than the view that it is the kingdom of prophethood, or the view of those who said it is the permitting of women and dominion over them. This is because the speech of Allah, addressed to the Arabs, may not be directed except toward the well-known meanings of words as used among them, unless some evidence comes or a proof is established that it is otherwise, in which case submission to it is obligatory.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 55:

The interpretation of the words of the Mighty and Majestic One: ﴿Among them are those who believed in it, and among them are those who turned away from it. And Hell is sufficient as a blazing fire.﴾ (4:55)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Among those who were given the Book, [He means] of the Jews of the Children of Israel, to whom He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿Believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their hinds﴾ — "Among them are those who believed in it," meaning: those who affirmed what We sent down to Muhammad ﷺ, confirming what was with them. "And among them are those who turned away from it," meaning: among them are those who turned away from affirming it. [See the explanation of "ṣadd" (turning away) in what has passed: 4:300 / 7:53.] As:

9831 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Among them are those who believed in it," he said: [meaning] in what was sent down to Muhammad, from the Jews. "And among them are those who turned away from it."

9832 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This verse indicates that those who turned away from what Allah sent down to Muhammad ﷺ, from the Jews of the Children of Israel who were around the place of emigration of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, had only the threat of Allah lifted from them, which He threatened them with in His saying: ﴿Believe in what We have sent down, confirming what is with you, before We obliterate faces and turn them back on their hinds, or curse them as We cursed the people of the Sabbath; and the command of Allah is ever executed﴾ in this world, [This is the preceding verse of "Surat an-Nisa" numbered 47.] and their punishment was delayed until the Day of Resurrection, because of the faith of those among them who believed; and the threat from Allah to them of hastening punishment in this world was only upon all of them remaining in disbelief in what was sent down to His prophet Muhammad ﷺ. So when some of them believed, they were released from the threat that had been made against them in the immediate world, and the punishment of those who persisted in denial was delayed until the Hereafter, so He said to them: "Hell is sufficient for you as a blazing fire." [See what has passed on p. 445, line 4 and following.]

* *

By His saying, "And Hell is sufficient as a blazing fire," He means: sufficient for you, O deniers of what I sent down to Muhammad, My prophet and My messenger, is Hell as a blazing fire, meaning: the fire of Hell, kindled against you, that is, set alight upon you.

* *

It has been said: "Sa'ir" (blazing fire) is originally "mas'ur" (kindled), from "su'ira, yus'ar, fa-hiya mas'ura," as Allah said: ﴿And when Hellfire is kindled﴾ [Surat at-Takwir: 12]. But it has been converted into the form "fa'il," as it is said: "kaff khadib" (a dyed hand) and "lihya dahin" (an oiled beard), meaning: dyed and oiled. And "as-sa'ir" is fuel. [See the explanation of "as-sa'ir" in what has passed: 30.]

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying (Exalted is He): ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our verses — We will surely drive them into a Fire. Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins, so that they may taste the punishment.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a warning from Allah, mighty is His praise, to those who persisted in denying what Allah sent down to Muhammad ﷺ — among the Jews of the Children of Israel and others, and among all the rest of the disbelievers — and in denying His Messenger. Allah says to them: Indeed, those who denied what I sent down to My Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, of My verses — meaning: the verses of My revelation, the inspiration of His Book, which are its proofs and evidences for the truthfulness of Muhammad ﷺ — and did not believe in them, from the Jews of the Children of Israel and others among all the people of disbelief in it: ﴿We will surely drive them into a Fire﴾, meaning: We will surely roast them in a Fire in which they will be burned (yuṣallūna), i.e., they will be roasted in it [[See the explanation of "al-iṣlāʾ" (roasting/burning) previously: 27–29, 231.]]. ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through﴾, meaning: every time their skins are scorched by it and burned. ﴿We will replace them with other skins﴾, meaning: other than the skins that had been roasted and scorched.

As related:

9833 – Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Jarīr related to us, from al-A'mash, from Thuwayr, from Ibn ʿUmar: "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins," he said: When their skins are burned, We will replace them with white skins like sheets of paper. [[The report 9833: "Thuwayr" is Thuwayr ibn Abī Fākhitah Saʿīd ibn ʿAlāqah al-Hāshimī; his biography has passed under nos. 3212, 5414. In the printed edition: "Nuwayr," while in the manuscript it is undotted. In the printed edition: "jildan bayḍāʾ" (white skin), which is an error; the correct reading is in the manuscript. "al-qarāṭīs" is the plural of "qirṭās," the white sheet on which one writes.]]

9834 – Bishr ibn Muʿādh related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, regarding His saying: "Indeed, those who disbelieved in Our verses — We will surely drive them into a Fire; every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins," he said: Every time their skins are burned, We will replace them with other skins.

9835 – Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Isḥāq related to us, saying: Ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ regarding His saying: "Every time their skins are roasted through," he said: We have heard that it is written in the earlier Book: the skin of one of them is forty cubits thick, [[In the printed edition: "anna jilda..."; I have kept the manuscript reading. He means by this the thickness of the skin, as will come in no. 9837.]] and his tooth is seventy cubits, and his belly, if a mountain were placed in it, would contain it. [[In the printed edition: "lawasaʿahu"; I have kept the manuscript reading.]] So when the Fire consumes their skins, they will be given other skins in their place.

9836 – Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Naṣr related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubārak informed us, saying: It reached me from al-Ḥasan: "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins," he said: We will roast them seventy thousand times a day.

9837 – Al-Qāsim related to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn related to us, saying: Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥaddād related to us, from Hishām ibn Ḥassān, from al-Ḥasan regarding His saying: "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins," he said: The Fire roasts seventy thousand skins every day. He said: The thickness of the skin of the disbeliever is forty cubits — and Allah knows best by which cubit! [[The report 9837: "Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥaddād" is ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Wāṣil al-Sadūsī; his biography has passed under no. 8284. "Hishām ibn Ḥassān al-Qurdūsī" has passed under no. 2827.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone asks: What is the meaning of His saying (mighty is His praise): "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins"? And is it permissible that they be replaced with skins other than the skins they had in this world, and then be punished in them? If you say that this is permissible, then permit that they be replaced with bodies and souls other than their bodies and souls that they had in this world, and be punished! And if you permit that, it would necessitate that those punished in the Hereafter by the Fire are other than those whom Allah promised punishment for their disbelief in Him and disobedience to Him, and that the disbelievers have been relieved of the punishment!!

* *

It is said: People differed regarding the meaning of that.

Some of them said: The punishment reaches only the human being who is other than the skin and flesh; the skin is burned so that the pain of the punishment reaches the human being. As for skin and flesh, they do not feel pain. They said: So it is no different whether the disbeliever's own skin that he had in this world is returned to him or another skin, since skins are not sensible or punished; rather, the sensible and punished one is the soul (nafs) that perceives pain, and the suffering reaches it. They said: And if that is so, it is not impossible that for every disbeliever in the Fire, at every moment and hour, skins that cannot be counted are created and burned upon him, so that the pain of the punishment may reach his soul, since skins do not feel pain.

* *

Others said: Rather, the skins feel pain, and the flesh and the rest of the parts of the human body do too. When his skin or another part of his body is burned, the pain of that reaches the whole. They said: The meaning of His saying: "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins" is: We will replace them with skins that are not burned. That is because they are restored new, while the first ones had been burned; so they are restored unburned, and therefore it is said: "other than them," because they are other than the skins they had in the world, with which they disobeyed Allah. They said: This is analogous to the Arabs' saying to the goldsmith, when one asks him to make a ring out of a ring already made — "istaṣāghahu khātaman" (he asked him to craft a ring for him): one transforms it from the form it has into another form: "Make for me from this ring another ring," and he breaks it and crafts for him from it another ring. The ring crafted with the second crafting is the first, yet when it was restored after being broken as a ring, it is said: "It is other than it." They said: Likewise is the meaning of His saying: "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins": when the skins are burned and then restored new after the burning, it is said: "They are other than them," in that sense.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that: "Every time their skins are roasted through" — their garments [sarābīl] — "We will replace them with other garments of tar." So the tar garments were made into skins for them, as one says of a thing particular to a person: "It is the skin between his eyes and his face," because of its being specific to him. They said: Likewise are the garments of tar that Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿Their garments will be of tar, and the Fire will cover their faces﴾ [Surah Ibrahim: 50]. When they became clothing for them that did not leave their bodies, they were made into skins for them, and so it is said: "Every time the tar ignites in their bodies and burns, they replace it with garments of other tar." They said: As for the skins of the people of disbelief among the people of the Fire, they are not burned, because in their being burned — up to the state of their restoration — is their annihilation, and in their annihilation is their relief. They said: Allah, mighty is His mention, has informed about them that they do not die and that their punishment is not lightened. They said: The skins of the disbelievers are one of their bodies; and if it were permissible for some of it to burn and perish and then be restored in the Fire after perishing, it would be permissible for all their parts. And if that were permissible, it would be necessary that annihilation, then restoration and death, then revival, be permissible for them, while Allah has informed about them that they do not die. They said: In His report about them that they do not die is clear evidence that no part of their bodies dies, and the skins are one of those parts.

* *

As for the meaning of His saying: "so that they may taste the punishment" — He says: We did that to them so that they may find the pain of the punishment, its distress and its severity, because of what they used to deny and reject the verses of Allah in the world.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Mighty and Wise﴾ (56)

Abu Ja'far said: He says: Indeed, Allah has always been "Mighty" in His vengeance upon whomever of His creation He takes vengeance against; no one who wills him harm is able to resist Him, and no one against whom He has brought down punishment can gain victory over Him; "Wise" in His management and decree. [[See the explanation of "ʿazīz" and "ḥakīm" in the language indices.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever; for them therein are purified spouses, and We will admit them to a shade, dense and deep﴾ (57)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying (mighty is His praise): "those who believed and did righteous deeds," He means those who believed in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, and affirmed what Allah sent down to Muhammad, confirming what was with them, from the Jews of the Children of Israel and all other nations; "and did righteous deeds" — meaning: they fulfilled what Allah commanded them of His obligations, and avoided what Allah forbade them of His disobediences; and that is the "righteous" [ṣāliḥ] of their deeds; ﴿We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ — meaning: Allah will admit them on the Day of Resurrection to "gardens," i.e., orchards [[See the explanation of "jannah" previously: 7:494, note 4, and the references there.]]; "beneath which rivers flow" — meaning: rivers flow beneath those gardens; ﴿abiding therein forever﴾ — meaning: remaining therein forever, without end or cessation, this being theirs permanently forever; ﴿for them therein are spouses﴾ — meaning: for them in those gardens whose attributes He described; ﴿purified spouses﴾ — meaning: free of impurities, doubts, menstruation, excrement, urine, pregnancy, spittle, and all else that occurs in the women of the people of the world. We have already mentioned the reports concerning that earlier, and that suffices instead of repeating them. [[See what has passed: 1:395–397 / 6:261, 262.]]

* *

As for His saying: "and We will admit them to a shade, dense and deep" — He says: We will admit them to a sheltering shade, as He, mighty is His praise, said: ﴿and a shade extended﴾ [Surah al-Waqi'ah: 30], and as:

9838 – Ibn Bashshār related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us = and Ibn al-Muthannā related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us = both of them said: Shuʿbah related to us, saying: I heard Abū al-Ḍaḥḥāk narrating, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels a hundred years without cutting it — the tree of eternity. [[The hadith 9838: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān is Ibn Mahdī. Abū al-Ḍaḥḥāk al-Baṣrī: a Successor, known only through this hadith, and no one narrated from him except Shuʿbah. Biographed in al-Tahdhīb and Ibn Abī Ḥātim 4/2/395. The hadith was narrated by Aḥmad in al-Musnad: 9870, from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ḥajjāj, and 9951, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Ibn Mahdī) — all three from Shuʿbah. Ibn Kathīr, 2:490, transmitted it from this place in al-Ṭabarī. The original hadith is established from Abū Hurayrah through many routes, in al-Musnad and the Two Ṣaḥīḥs and others, without the addition "the tree of eternity."]]

Commentary on the interpretation of His saying (Exalted is He): ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in Our verses — We will surely drive them into a Fire. Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins, so that they may taste the punishment.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a warning from Allah, mighty is His praise, to those who persisted in denying what Allah sent down to Muhammad ﷺ — among the Jews of the Children of Israel and others, and among all the rest of the disbelievers — and in denying His Messenger. Allah says to them: Indeed, those who denied what I sent down to My Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, of My verses — meaning: the verses of My revelation, the inspiration of His Book, which are its proofs and evidences for the truthfulness of Muhammad ﷺ — and did not believe in them, from the Jews of the Children of Israel and others among all the people of disbelief in it: ﴿We will surely drive them into a Fire﴾, meaning: We will surely roast them in a Fire in which they will be burned (yuṣallūna), i.e., they will be roasted in it [[See the explanation of "al-iṣlāʾ" (roasting/burning) previously: 27–29, 231.]]. ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through﴾, meaning: every time their skins are scorched by it and burned. ﴿We will replace them with other skins﴾, meaning: other than the skins that had been roasted and scorched.

As related:

9833 – Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Jarīr related to us, from al-A'mash, from Thuwayr, from Ibn ʿUmar: "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins," he said: When their skins are burned, We will replace them with white skins like sheets of paper. [[The report 9833: "Thuwayr" is Thuwayr ibn Abī Fākhitah Saʿīd ibn ʿAlāqah al-Hāshimī; his biography has passed under nos. 3212, 5414. In the printed edition: "Nuwayr," while in the manuscript it is undotted. In the printed edition: "jildan bayḍāʾ" (white skin), which is an error; the correct reading is in the manuscript. "al-qarāṭīs" is the plural of "qirṭās," the white sheet on which one writes.]]

9834 – Bishr ibn Muʿādh related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatādah, regarding His saying: "Indeed, those who disbelieved in Our verses — We will surely drive them into a Fire; every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins," he said: Every time their skins are burned, We will replace them with other skins.

9835 – Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Isḥāq related to us, saying: Ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ regarding His saying: "Every time their skins are roasted through," he said: We have heard that it is written in the earlier Book: the skin of one of them is forty cubits thick, [[In the printed edition: "anna jilda..."; I have kept the manuscript reading. He means by this the thickness of the skin, as will come in no. 9837.]] and his tooth is seventy cubits, and his belly, if a mountain were placed in it, would contain it. [[In the printed edition: "lawasaʿahu"; I have kept the manuscript reading.]] So when the Fire consumes their skins, they will be given other skins in their place.

9836 – Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Naṣr related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubārak informed us, saying: It reached me from al-Ḥasan: "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins," he said: We will roast them seventy thousand times a day.

9837 – Al-Qāsim related to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn related to us, saying: Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥaddād related to us, from Hishām ibn Ḥassān, from al-Ḥasan regarding His saying: "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins," he said: The Fire roasts seventy thousand skins every day. He said: The thickness of the skin of the disbeliever is forty cubits — and Allah knows best by which cubit! [[The report 9837: "Abū ʿUbaydah al-Ḥaddād" is ʿAbd al-Wāḥid ibn Wāṣil al-Sadūsī; his biography has passed under no. 8284. "Hishām ibn Ḥassān al-Qurdūsī" has passed under no. 2827.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone asks: What is the meaning of His saying (mighty is His praise): "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins"? And is it permissible that they be replaced with skins other than the skins they had in this world, and then be punished in them? If you say that this is permissible, then permit that they be replaced with bodies and souls other than their bodies and souls that they had in this world, and be punished! And if you permit that, it would necessitate that those punished in the Hereafter by the Fire are other than those whom Allah promised punishment for their disbelief in Him and disobedience to Him, and that the disbelievers have been relieved of the punishment!!

* *

It is said: People differed regarding the meaning of that.

Some of them said: The punishment reaches only the human being who is other than the skin and flesh; the skin is burned so that the pain of the punishment reaches the human being. As for skin and flesh, they do not feel pain. They said: So it is no different whether the disbeliever's own skin that he had in this world is returned to him or another skin, since skins are not sensible or punished; rather, the sensible and punished one is the soul (nafs) that perceives pain, and the suffering reaches it. They said: And if that is so, it is not impossible that for every disbeliever in the Fire, at every moment and hour, skins that cannot be counted are created and burned upon him, so that the pain of the punishment may reach his soul, since skins do not feel pain.

* *

Others said: Rather, the skins feel pain, and the flesh and the rest of the parts of the human body do too. When his skin or another part of his body is burned, the pain of that reaches the whole. They said: The meaning of His saying: "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins" is: We will replace them with skins that are not burned. That is because they are restored new, while the first ones had been burned; so they are restored unburned, and therefore it is said: "other than them," because they are other than the skins they had in the world, with which they disobeyed Allah. They said: This is analogous to the Arabs' saying to the goldsmith, when one asks him to make a ring out of a ring already made — "istaṣāghahu khātaman" (he asked him to craft a ring for him): one transforms it from the form it has into another form: "Make for me from this ring another ring," and he breaks it and crafts for him from it another ring. The ring crafted with the second crafting is the first, yet when it was restored after being broken as a ring, it is said: "It is other than it." They said: Likewise is the meaning of His saying: "Every time their skins are roasted through, We will replace them with other skins": when the skins are burned and then restored new after the burning, it is said: "They are other than them," in that sense.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that: "Every time their skins are roasted through" — their garments [sarābīl] — "We will replace them with other garments of tar." So the tar garments were made into skins for them, as one says of a thing particular to a person: "It is the skin between his eyes and his face," because of its being specific to him. They said: Likewise are the garments of tar that Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿Their garments will be of tar, and the Fire will cover their faces﴾ [Surah Ibrahim: 50]. When they became clothing for them that did not leave their bodies, they were made into skins for them, and so it is said: "Every time the tar ignites in their bodies and burns, they replace it with garments of other tar." They said: As for the skins of the people of disbelief among the people of the Fire, they are not burned, because in their being burned — up to the state of their restoration — is their annihilation, and in their annihilation is their relief. They said: Allah, mighty is His mention, has informed about them that they do not die and that their punishment is not lightened. They said: The skins of the disbelievers are one of their bodies; and if it were permissible for some of it to burn and perish and then be restored in the Fire after perishing, it would be permissible for all their parts. And if that were permissible, it would be necessary that annihilation, then restoration and death, then revival, be permissible for them, while Allah has informed about them that they do not die. They said: In His report about them that they do not die is clear evidence that no part of their bodies dies, and the skins are one of those parts.

* *

As for the meaning of His saying: "so that they may taste the punishment" — He says: We did that to them so that they may find the pain of the punishment, its distress and its severity, because of what they used to deny and reject the verses of Allah in the world.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Mighty and Wise﴾ (56)

Abu Ja'far said: He says: Indeed, Allah has always been "Mighty" in His vengeance upon whomever of His creation He takes vengeance against; no one who wills him harm is able to resist Him, and no one against whom He has brought down punishment can gain victory over Him; "Wise" in His management and decree. [[See the explanation of "ʿazīz" and "ḥakīm" in the language indices.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿As for those who believed and did righteous deeds, We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever; for them therein are purified spouses, and We will admit them to a shade, dense and deep﴾ (57)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying (mighty is His praise): "those who believed and did righteous deeds," He means those who believed in Allah and His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, and affirmed what Allah sent down to Muhammad, confirming what was with them, from the Jews of the Children of Israel and all other nations; "and did righteous deeds" — meaning: they fulfilled what Allah commanded them of His obligations, and avoided what Allah forbade them of His disobediences; and that is the "righteous" [ṣāliḥ] of their deeds; ﴿We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ — meaning: Allah will admit them on the Day of Resurrection to "gardens," i.e., orchards [[See the explanation of "jannah" previously: 7:494, note 4, and the references there.]]; "beneath which rivers flow" — meaning: rivers flow beneath those gardens; ﴿abiding therein forever﴾ — meaning: remaining therein forever, without end or cessation, this being theirs permanently forever; ﴿for them therein are spouses﴾ — meaning: for them in those gardens whose attributes He described; ﴿purified spouses﴾ — meaning: free of impurities, doubts, menstruation, excrement, urine, pregnancy, spittle, and all else that occurs in the women of the people of the world. We have already mentioned the reports concerning that earlier, and that suffices instead of repeating them. [[See what has passed: 1:395–397 / 6:261, 262.]]

* *

As for His saying: "and We will admit them to a shade, dense and deep" — He says: We will admit them to a sheltering shade, as He, mighty is His praise, said: ﴿and a shade extended﴾ [Surah al-Waqi'ah: 30], and as:

9838 – Ibn Bashshār related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān related to us = and Ibn al-Muthannā related to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar related to us = both of them said: Shuʿbah related to us, saying: I heard Abū al-Ḍaḥḥāk narrating, from Abū Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels a hundred years without cutting it — the tree of eternity. [[The hadith 9838: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān is Ibn Mahdī. Abū al-Ḍaḥḥāk al-Baṣrī: a Successor, known only through this hadith, and no one narrated from him except Shuʿbah. Biographed in al-Tahdhīb and Ibn Abī Ḥātim 4/2/395. The hadith was narrated by Aḥmad in al-Musnad: 9870, from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar and Ḥajjāj, and 9951, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Ibn Mahdī) — all three from Shuʿbah. Ibn Kathīr, 2:490, transmitted it from this place in al-Ṭabarī. The original hadith is established from Abū Hurayrah through many routes, in al-Musnad and the Two Ṣaḥīḥs and others, without the addition "the tree of eternity."]]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners, and when you judge between people, to judge with justice.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters of the Qur'an differed regarding who is meant by this verse.

Some of them said: It refers to the rulers of the Muslims.

Mention of those who said that:

9839 - Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi related to me, saying: Abu Usamah related to us, from Abu Makin, from Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: This verse, "Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners," was revealed concerning the rulers. [[The narration 9839: "Abu Usamah" is Hammad ibn Usamah ibn Zayd al-Qurashi, mentioned under no. 5265. And "Abu Makin" is Nuh ibn Rabi'ah, mentioned under no. 9742.]]

9840 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: Layth related to us, from Shahr, who said: It was revealed specifically concerning the commanders: "Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners, and when you judge between people, to judge with justice."

9841 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: Isma'il related to us, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, who said: Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) said words in which he was correct: "It is a right upon the imam to judge by what Allah has revealed and to render the trust. And when he does that, it is a right upon the people to listen, to obey, and to respond when called." [[The narration 9841: "Mus'ab ibn Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas al-Zuhri." He related from his father, Ali, Talhah, Ikrimah ibn Abi Jahl, and others. He was a trustworthy Successor; Ibn Sa'd said: "He was trustworthy and narrated much." Biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

9842 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Jabir ibn Nuh related to us, saying: Isma'il related to us, from Mus'ab ibn Sa'd, from Ali, with similar wording.

9843 - Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Muharibi related to me, saying: Musa ibn Umayr related to us, from Makhul, concerning Allah's saying: "And those in authority among you," he said: They are the people of the verse before it: "Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners," to the end of the verse.

9844 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd informed us, saying: My father said: They are the governors; He commanded them to render trusts to their owners.

Others said: The sultan was commanded by this: to admonish the women. [[In the printed edition: "that they give people," which differs from the manuscript, and which I have adopted; but in the manuscript it was undotted, so it was not read properly, and what has no meaning was written. The intended meaning is that the rulers should admonish women regarding disobedience (nushuz) and other matters, until they return them to their husbands. This is the view attributed to Ibn Abbas in the books of tafsir.]]

Mention of those who said that:

9845 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, concerning his saying: "Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners," he said: It means the sultan; they admonish the women. [[In the printed edition: "they admonish the people," which is an error; see the previous note.]]

* *

Others said: The one addressed by this was the Prophet ﷺ regarding the key of the Ka'bah; he was commanded to return it to Uthman ibn Talhah.

Mention of those who said that:

9846 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, concerning his saying: "Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners," he said: It was revealed concerning Uthman ibn Talhah ibn Abi Talhah. The Prophet ﷺ took from him the keys of the Ka'bah and entered the House with it on the day of the Conquest, [[In the printed edition: "the keys of the Ka'bah, and entered the House with them," whereas the manuscript reads: "the keys of the Ka'bah and entered the House with it," the word being singular "al-miftah" in this report and the one following, and Ibn Kathir in his tafsir (2:492) likewise has "miftah Ka'bah" in the singular, so I have corrected the text to match the manuscript, as in Ibn Kathir.]] and he went out reciting this verse. He called Uthman and handed him the key. He said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out reciting this verse: May my father and mother be ransomed for him! I had not heard him recite it before that!

9847 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Al-Zanji ibn Khalid related to us, from al-Zuhri, who said: He handed it to him and said: Help him. [[Narration 9847: "Al-Zanji ibn Khalid" is Muslim ibn Khalid ibn Farwah, Abu Khalid al-Zanji, the jurist of Mecca. They called him "al-Zanji" because he was very dark-skinned. Others said it was because he was reddish-fair like an onion, or that he was white tinged with redness; he was named "al-Zanji" for his love of dates, since his slave-girl said to him, "You are nothing but a Zanji," for eating dates, and this nickname remained on him.

From al-Zanji al-Shafi'i learned jurisprudence before he met Malik. But they spoke about his narrations; al-Bukhari said: "Munkar al-hadith; his hadith is written but not used as proof." They mentioned defects in the weakness of his narrations, though he was truthful. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views in my opinion is the view of the one who said: It is an address from Allah to the rulers of the Muslims, to render the trust to those whose affairs they have been entrusted with regarding their spoils (fay') and rights, and what they have been entrusted with of their affairs, judging justly between them in legal cases and dividing equally among them. What supports this is what He admonished the subjects in: "Obey Allah, and obey the Messenger, and those in authority among you," so He commanded them to obey, and enjoined the shepherd regarding the flock, and enjoined the flock to obey, as:

9848 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning his saying: "O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you," he said: My father said: They are the sultans. And Ibn Zayd recited: "You give sovereignty to whom You will and You take sovereignty from whom You will and You honor whom You will" [Surah Al 'Imran: 26]. And we only say: They are the scholars who surround the sultan [[The printed edition omitted this sentence because the publisher did not understand it, and arranged the text thus: "... of whom You will; do you not see that He commanded and said: Indeed, Allah commands you," which is a severe corruption, an abandonment of the trust, and a distortion of the words of the interpreters. The speaker of this statement is Ibn Zayd, after he mentioned the interpretation of his father Zayd ibn Aslam.

His saying "yutifun 'ala al-sultan" means those who draw near to him, whom he brings close in his assemblies and consults. From the phrase "tafa bi al-shay' wa tafa 'alayhi" and "atafa bihi wa atafa 'alayhi": he went around it.]]. Do you not see that He commanded them and began with them, the rulers, saying [[In the printed edition: "that He commanded and said ...", as noted in the earlier note. The sense of his statement is that He commanded the scholars regarding the rulers—He began with them, i.e., the scholars. The scholars are those who issue rulings to the rulers concerning the division of fay' and alms, since they are the people of knowledge concerning them. This is therefore an address to the scholars who have been entrusted with religion. Then He said to the rulers: "And when you judge between people," as you see in the context of the report.]]: "Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners"? And "the trusts" are the fay' which He entrusted them to collect and distribute, and the alms which He entrusted them to collect and distribute, "and when you judge between people, to judge with justice," the whole verse. So He commanded the rulers with this. Then He turned to us and said: "O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you."

* *

As for what Ibn Juraij said, that this verse was revealed concerning Uthman ibn Talhah, it is permissible that it was revealed concerning him, and that it is intended to cover every person entrusted with a trust, so the rulers of the Muslims enter into it, and every person entrusted with a trust in religion or worldly affairs. For this reason, those who said that it refers to the discharge of debts and the return of people's rights, as in:

9849 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, concerning his saying: "Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners," that He did not permit the wealthy or the poor to withhold them.

9850 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, concerning his saying: "Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners," from al-Hasan: that the Prophet of Allah ﷺ used to say: Render the trust to the one who entrusted you, and do not betray the one who betrayed you. [[Narration 9850: Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (2:490): "And in the hadith of al-Hasan, from Samurah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Render the trust to the one who entrusted you, and do not betray the one who betrayed you.' Related by Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan."]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: So the interpretation of the verse, since the matter is as we have described, is: Indeed Allah commands you, O assembly of the rulers of the Muslims, to render what your subjects have entrusted you with of their spoils, their rights, their wealth, and their alms to them, as Allah has commanded you to render each of these to the one to whom it belongs, after it has come into your hands, not wronging its people, not monopolizing any of it, not placing any of it in other than its place, and not taking it except from the one whom Allah has permitted you to take it from before it came into your hands. And He commands you, when you judge between your subjects, to judge between them with justice and equity, and that is the judgment of Allah which He revealed in His Book and explained through the tongue of His Messenger; do not transgress it, lest you oppress them.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah admonishes you with what is excellent. Indeed, Allah is ever Hearing and Seeing.﴾ (58)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: O assembly of the rulers of the Muslims, indeed Allah is an excellent thing with which He admonishes you, and an excellent admonition with which He admonishes you in His command to you to render trusts to their owners, and to judge between people with justice. [[See the explanation of "ni'imma" in what preceded, 5:582.]]

* *

"Indeed Allah is ever Hearing": He says, Allah has always been Hearing of what you say and utter, and He hears it from you when you judge between people and when you converse with them. "Seeing" of what you do regarding what you have been entrusted with of your subjects' rights and wealth, and what you decide between them of your judgments, whether with justice or oppression; nothing of that is hidden from Him. He preserves all of it, until He recompenses the good-doer among you with His goodness and the wrongdoer with his wrongdoing, or pardons by His bounty.

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying: ﴿O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His mention be exalted, He means: O you who believe, obey Allah, your Lord, in what He has commanded you and what He has forbidden you, and obey His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). Indeed, obeying him is obeying your Lord, because you obey him in obedience to Allah's command to you to obey him, as related:

9851 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever obeys my amir has obeyed me. Whoever disobeys me has disobeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys my amir has disobeyed me."

[[Hadith 9851: It is also narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad many times, through various chains, among them: 7330, 7428, 7643. It is narrated by the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others, as we detailed there. Ibn Kathir mentioned it (2:497), saying: "In the hadith agreed upon for its authenticity." And it is as he said.]]

* *

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of His saying: "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger."

Some of them said: This is a command from Allah to follow his sunnah (the Prophet's way and practice).

Those who said this:

9852 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata', regarding His saying: "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger." He said: The obedience to the Messenger is following his sunnah.

9853 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ya'la ibn 'Ubayd narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata': "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger." He said: The obedience to the Messenger is following the Book and the Sunnah.

9854 - And al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata', the like of it.

* *

Others said: This is a command from Allah to obey the Messenger during his lifetime.

Those who said this:

9855 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger": "If he is alive."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view on this matter is to say: It is a command from Allah to obey His Messenger during his lifetime in what he commands and forbids, and after his death to follow his sunnah. This is because Allah made the command to obey Him general and did not restrict it to one circumstance over another, so it remains general until what must be submitted to is specified.

* *

The interpreters differed regarding "those in authority" (ulu al-amr) whom Allah commanded His servants to obey in this verse.

Some of them said: They are the rulers (al-umara').

Those who said this:

9856 - Abu al-Sa'ib Salm ibn Janadah narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah regarding His saying: "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you," He said: They are the rulers.

[[Hadith 9856: This is a report halted at Abu Hurayrah (mawquf). Its isnad is sound and its meaning is sound. The Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) mentioned it in al-Fath (8:191) and said: "al-Tabari narrated it with a sound isnad."]]

9857 - al-Hasan ibn al-Sabbah al-Bazzar narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj ibn Muhammad narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ya'la ibn Muslim informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you": it was revealed concerning a man whom the Prophet (ﷺ) sent over a detachment (sariyyah).

[[Hadith 9857: Ya'la ibn Muslim ibn Hurmuz al-Basri al-Makki: trustworthy; the two Shaykhs narrated from him. Ibn Ma'in and Abu Zur'ah judged him trustworthy. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. See also al-Bukhari's al-Kabir 4/2/417 and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/302. He is the brother of "Abd Allah ibn Muslim," who appears in the isnad after him, as al-Bukhari and others favored.
The hadith is narrated by Ahmad in the Musnad (3124), from Hajjaj, who is Ibn Muhammad, with this isnad. In it the man is named as "Abd Allah ibn Hudhafah ibn Qays ibn 'Adi al-Sahmi."
Likewise al-Bukhari narrated it (8:190-191), from Sadaqah ibn al-Fadl, from Hajjaj ibn Muhammad, with the same.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it (2:494), citing al-Bukhari's narration, then said: "Thus it was narrated by the rest of the group except Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Hajjaj ibn Muhammad al-A'war, with the same. al-Tirmidhi said: a hadith hasan gharib, and we do not know it except from the hadith of Ibn Jurayj."
The story of 'Abd Allah ibn Hudhafah was narrated by Ahmad in the Musnad (11662; vol. 3, p. 67, Halabi edition), from a hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri. Its meaning was also narrated from a hadith of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (622).]]

9858 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Muslim ibn Hurmuz, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: that this verse was revealed concerning 'Abd Allah ibn Hudhafah ibn Qays al-Sahmi, when the Prophet (ﷺ) sent him in the detachment.

[[Hadith 9858: 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim ibn Hurmuz: according to the more likely view, he is the brother of Ya'la mentioned in the previous hadith. This 'Abd Allah has weakness, though al-Thawri narrates from him, and al-Thawri narrates only from the trustworthy. So it appears his weakness came from his memory. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/164-165.
In the manuscript and the printed edition here "Ubayd Allah" appears instead of "Abd Allah," which is an obvious error.
The hadith has the same meaning as the previous one.]]

9859 - Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from 'Anbasah, from Layth, who said: Maslamah asked Maymun ibn Mihran about His saying: "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you." He said: They are the commanders of the detachments in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ).

9860 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "O you who believe, obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you," he said: My father said: They are the sultans (rulers). He said, and Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "and those in authority among you," my father said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Obedience, obedience; and in obedience there is trial." And he said: "Had Allah willed, He would have placed the command in the prophets" - meaning: indeed, it was placed in their hands, with the prophets alongside them. Do you not see when they judged regarding the killing of Yahya ibn Zakariyya?

[[The manuscript reads here "had Allah willed He would have placed..." in the printed edition; I have followed the manuscript. In the printed edition: "meaning: indeed it was placed in their hands, with the prophets alongside them," which is sound, but the manuscript reads: "indeed it was placed in their hands and the prophets were with them," so I judged that "the command" was dropped and placed it between brackets.]]

9861 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you." He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a detachment under the command of Khalid ibn al-Walid, and in it was 'Ammar ibn Yasir. They marched toward the people they intended, and when they reached near them, they made 'arrasa (camped at the end of the night for a brief rest, then rose at dawn; a 'arrasa is when they stop in the last part of the night, rest, then move on as dawn breaks). A spy named Dhu al-'Uyaynatayn came and informed them, and in the morning they found that the people had fled, except for a man who ordered his family, and they gathered their goods. Then he walked in the darkness of the night until he came to Khalid's camp. He asked about 'Ammar ibn Yasir, and came to him and said: "O Abu al-Yaqzan, I have embraced Islam and testified that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. When my people heard of you they fled, but I remained. Will my Islam benefit me tomorrow, or else I will flee?" 'Ammar said: "Indeed it will benefit you, so remain." He remained. When they rose in the morning, Khalid attacked and found no one except the man, so he took him and took his property. The news reached 'Ammar, and he came to Khalid and said: "Release the man, for he has embraced Islam, and he is under my protection." Khalid said: "And by what right do you grant protection?" They quarreled and went to the Prophet (ﷺ). He upheld 'Ammar's protection and forbade granting protection a second time over a commander. They quarreled in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Khalid said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you leave this slave with the cut nose to insult me?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O Khalid, do not insult 'Ammar, for whoever insults 'Ammar, Allah insults him, and whoever hates 'Ammar, Allah hates him, and whoever curses 'Ammar, Allah curses him." 'Ammar became angry and stood up, and Khalid followed him until he took hold of his garment and apologized to him, and he was pleased with him. Then Allah the Exalted revealed His saying: "Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you."

[[Report 9861: Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir (2:497), then said: "Thus Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it through another chain, from al-Suddi, as a mursal (broken) report. Ibn Mardawayh narrated it from the narration of al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr, from al-Suddi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, mentioning it in similar form. And Allah knows best."]]

9868 - Ahmad ibn Hazim narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Husayn, from Mujahid: "and those in authority among you," he said: "The people of knowledge."

9870 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata': "and those in authority among you," he said: "The jurists and the scholars."

Do you not see that He says: ﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, those who seek to draw it out would have known it among them﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 83]?"

Abu Ja'far said: The most preferable of the views on this matter, as correct, is the view of those who said: They are the rulers and governors. This is because of the sound reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about the command to obey the imams and governors in what is an obedience to Allah and a benefit to the Muslims, such as what is related:

9876 - Ali ibn Muslim al-Tusi narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Urwah narrated to me, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from Abu Salih al-Samman, from Abu Hurayrah: that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "After me there will be governors over you; the pious among them will govern you with his piety and the wicked with his wickedness. So listen to them and obey them in all that accords with the truth, and pray behind them. If they do good, it is for you and for them; and if they do wrong, it is for you and against them."

[[Hadith 9876: Ibn Abi Fudayk: he is Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Muslim ibn Abi Fudayk al-Madani. He is a known trustworthy narrator, among the teachers of al-Shafi'i and Ahmad. The group narrated from him.
'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Urwah: he is 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr al-Madani. Abu Hatim said: "He is abandoned in hadith, very weak in hadith." Ibn Hibban said: "He narrates fabrications from trustworthy narrators." He is biographed in Lisan al-Mizan 3:331-332 and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/158.
This hadith is therefore very weak; we have not found it except in this place.
Ibn Kathir (2:495) and al-Suyuti (2:177) also quoted it, and they did not attribute it to anyone other than al-Tabari.]]

9877 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from 'Ubayd Allah, who said: Nafi' informed me, from 'Abd Allah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "The obligation upon the Muslim man is obedience in what he loves and dislikes, unless he is commanded to sin. For whoever is commanded to sin, there is no obedience."

Khalid in the second isnad is Ibn al-Harith al-Hujaymi al-Basri, whose biography has passed at no. 7818.
'Ubayd Allah in both isnads is Ibn 'Umar ibn Hafs ibn 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, al-'Umari.

9878 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Khalid narrated to me, from 'Ubayd Allah, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of it.

[[Hadiths 9877 and 9878: See the note above.]]
