]]

= Since it is known that there is no obligatory obedience owed to anyone other than God, His Messenger, or a just imam, and since God has commanded, saying, "Obey God and obey the Messenger and those in authority among you," by the obedience of those in authority over us, it is known that those whose obedience He, exalted is His remembrance, has commanded are those in authority over us, namely the imams and those whom they appoint over the Muslims. [In the printed edition it reads "and those whom the Muslims appoint," but I have kept what is in the manuscript. Abu Ja'far did not intend the meaning of the printed text; rather he meant: those whom the imams have appointed over the affairs of the Muslims.] Not others among people. Although it is an obligation to accept from anyone who commands abandoning disobedience to God and calls to obedience to God, there is no obedience owed to anyone in what they command or forbid, where the proof of its obligation has not been established, except to the imams whom God has bound His servants to obey in what they command their subjects, in matters that serve the general welfare of the subjects. For whoever they command with that must obey them. Likewise in everything that is not disobedience to God.

Since that is the case, it is known thereby that the interpretation (ta'wil, the explanation and return of a matter to its meaning) we have chosen is correct, to the exclusion of others.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Then if you dispute over anything, refer it to God and the Messenger, if you believe in God and the Last Day﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His praise, means by this: If you disagree, O believers, about anything in the matter of your religion, whether among yourselves or between you and your rulers, and you dispute over it [see the explanation of "tanazu'" (dispute) in what preceded, 7:289], then "refer it to God" means: seek knowledge of the ruling on that over which you have disputed, among yourselves or between you and those in authority over you, from God. That means from the Book of God, so follow what you find. As for His saying "and the Messenger," it means: if you do not find a way to knowledge of that in the Book of God, then seek knowledge of it also from the Messenger, if he is alive; and if he is dead, then from his sunnah. "If you believe in God and the Last Day" means: do this if you truly believe in God and "the Last Day," meaning the return (to God) in which there is reward and punishment. For if you do what you have been commanded in this, you will have from God great reward, and if you do not do it, you will have painful punishment.

* *

Those who held the same view as we have stated on this have been a group of the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil).

Mention of those who said that:

9879 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Ibn Idris related to us, saying: Layth informed us, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "If you dispute over anything, refer it to God and the Messenger." He said: If the scholars dispute, they should refer it to God and the Messenger. He said: that is, refer it to the Book of God and the sunnah of His Messenger.
Then Mujahid recited this verse: ﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, those who derive it among them would have known it﴾ [Surah an-Nisa: 83].

9880 - al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sufyan, from Layth, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "Refer it to God and the Messenger." He said: the Book of God and the sunnah of His Prophet (ﷺ).

9881 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Layth, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "Refer it to God and the Messenger." He said: "to God" means to His Book, and "to the Messenger" means to the sunnah of His Prophet.

9882 - Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from Anbasah, from Layth, who said: Maslamah asked Maymun ibn Mihran about His saying: "If you dispute over anything, refer it to God and the Messenger." He said: "God" is His Book, and "His Messenger" is his sunnah. So it was as if he had put a stone in his mouth.

9883 - Ahmad ibn Hazim related to us, saying: Abu Nu'aym related to us, saying: Ja'far ibn Marwan informed us, from Maymun ibn Mihran: "If you dispute over anything, refer it to God and the Messenger." He said: the referral to God is referral to His Book, and the referral to His Messenger, if he is alive; but if God has taken him to Himself, then referral is to the sunnah.

9884 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "If you dispute over anything, refer it to God and the Messenger." He says: refer it to the Book of God and the sunnah of His Messenger, "if you believe in God and the Last Day."

9885 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "If you dispute over anything, refer it to God and the Messenger." If the Messenger is alive, [refer to him]; and "to God" he said: to His Book.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿That is better and more excellent in outcome﴾ [59]

Abu Ja'far said: He, exalted is His praise, means by His saying "that": the referral of whatever you dispute to God and the Messenger is "better" for you with God in your return (to Him), and more beneficial for you in your worldly life, because that calls you to unity and to abandoning dispute and division. "And more excellent in outcome" means: more praiseworthy in end and consequence, and more beautiful in result.

* *

We have already shown earlier that "ta'wil" is the form "taf'il" from "ta'awwala," and that the saying of the speaker "ta'awwala" (is of the form "tafa"ala") from their saying "ala hadha al-amr ila kadha," meaning: it returned to such and such. This was sufficient, so there is no need to repeat it. [See what preceded, 6:204–206.]

* *

Those who held the same view as we have stated on this have been the people of interpretation.

Mention of those who said that:

9886 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, saying: Abu Asim related to us, saying: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And more excellent in outcome," he said: a good reward.

9887 - al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

9888 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: "That is better and more excellent in outcome." He says: that is more excellent in reward and better in consequence.

9889 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "And more excellent in outcome," he said: consequence.

9890 - Yunus related to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "That is better and more excellent in outcome," he said: and more excellent in consequence. He said: and "ta'wil" means confirmation (tasdiq).

**The interpretation of His saying:** ﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet they desire to take their disputes for judgment to the Taghut, though they were commanded to reject it? And Satan wishes to lead them far astray.﴾ (4:60)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "Have you not seen," O Muhammad, with your heart, so that you may know, about those who claim that they have believed in what has been revealed to you of the Book, and about those who claim that they have believed in what was revealed before you of the scriptures, that they desire to take their disputes for judgment to the *ṭāghūt*, meaning to one whom they revere, whose word they follow, and whose judgment they accept in place of the judgment of God. [[See the explanation of "*al-ṭāghūt*" in what has preceded, 5:416–419 and 8:461–465.]] ﴿And they were commanded to reject it﴾ means: God had commanded them to deny what the *ṭāghūt* to whom they resort had brought, but they abandoned the command of God and followed the command of Satan. ﴿And Satan wishes to lead them far astray﴾ means: Satan wishes to turn these people who seek judgment from the *ṭāghūt* away from the path of truth and guidance, so that he leads them far astray from it, meaning he diverts them from it with severe deviation. [[See the explanation of "*al-ḍalāl*" (error) in what has preceded, 8:428, note 4, and the references there.]]

* *

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a man of the hypocrites who called a Jewish man, in a dispute between them, to a certain soothsayer (*kāhin*) to judge between them, while the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was among them.

Those who said this:

9891 – Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from ʿAmir, concerning this verse: "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet desire to take their disputes for judgment to the *ṭāghūt*?" He said: There was a dispute between a Jewish man and a hypocrite. The hypocrite would call to the Jew, because he knew that they (the Jews) accepted bribes, and the Jew would call to the Muslims, because he knew that they did not accept bribes. So they agreed to submit their case to a soothsayer from Juhayna. Then God revealed this verse concerning it: "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you," until His saying: "and submit with complete submission."

9892 – Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from ʿAmir, concerning this verse: "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you," and he mentioned something similar, and added: God revealed: "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you," meaning the hypocrites, "and what was revealed before you," meaning the Jews, "they desire to take their disputes for judgment to the *ṭāghūt*," that is, to the soothsayer. "And they were commanded to reject it," meaning: this was commanded in His Book, and this was commanded in His Book, that they should reject the soothsayer.

9893 – Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from Dawud, from al-Shaʿbi, who said: There was a dispute between a man who claimed to be a Muslim and a Jewish man. The Jew said: "I will take you to judgment before the people of your religion" – or he said: "before the Prophet" – "because he knows that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) does not take bribes in judgment." They disagreed, so they agreed to go to a soothsayer in Juhayna. He said: Then it was revealed: "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you," meaning the one from the Ansar, "and what was revealed before you," meaning the Jew, "they desire to take their disputes for judgment to the *ṭāghūt*," to the soothsayer, "and they were commanded to reject it," meaning: this was commanded in His Book, and this was commanded in His Book. And he recited: "And Satan wishes to lead them far astray," and he recited: "But no, by your Lord, they will not [truly] believe until they make you judge concerning that over which they dispute among themselves," up to "and submit with complete submission."

9894 – Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, who said: A man from Hadramawt claimed that a Jewish man had become a Muslim, and there was a dispute between him and another Jewish man concerning a right. [[*al-mudāraʾa*: contention and dispute.]] The Jew said to him: "Go to the Prophet of God." He (the Muslim) knew that he (the Prophet) would rule against him, so he refused. They went to a soothsayer among the soothsayers and submitted to his judgment. God said: "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet desire to take their disputes for judgment to the *ṭāghūt*?"

9895 – Bishr ibn Muʿadh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you," the verse, until "far astray." It was mentioned to us that this verse was revealed concerning two men: a man from the Ansar called "Bishr," and a Jewish man, in a dispute between them concerning a right. They contended with one another and went to a soothsayer in Medina to judge between them, leaving the Prophet of God (ﷺ). God, mighty and majestic, rebuked that. It was also mentioned to us that the Jew used to call him to the Prophet (ﷺ) to judge between them, for he knew that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) would not be unjust to him. But the Ansari refused and, although he claimed to be a Muslim, called him to the soothsayer. So God, blessed and exalted, revealed what you hear, rebuking the one who claimed to be a Muslim and the Jew who was of the People of the Book. He said: "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you," until His saying: "turning away."

9896 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet desire to take their disputes for judgment to the *ṭāghūt*?" He said: Some Jews had become Muslims, and some of them were hypocrites. Qurayza and al-Nadir, in the pre-Islamic period, when a man from the Banu al-Nadir was killed, the Banu Qurayza would kill him in retaliation, [killing] one of their own. When a man from the Banu Qurayza was killed, the Nadir would kill him, and they gave his blood-money as sixty *wasq* of dates. [[*al-wasq* is a known measure in their time, equal to the load of a camel.]] When some people of the Banu Qurayza and al-Nadir became Muslims, a man from the Banu al-Nadir killed a man from the Banu Qurayza, and they submitted their dispute to the Prophet (ﷺ). The Nadiri said: "O Messenger of God, we used to give them the blood-money in the pre-Islamic period, so we will give them that today." But Qurayza said: "No, we are your brothers in lineage and religion, and our blood is like your blood. But you used to dominate us in the pre-Islamic period, and now God has brought Islam!" So God revealed, rebuking them for what they did, saying: "And We prescribed for them therein that a life is for a life" (5:45). He rebuked them, then he mentioned the Nadiri's statement: "We used to give them sixty *wasq* in the pre-Islamic period, and we would kill them but they would not kill us." So He said: "Then is it the judgment of ignorance they desire?" (5:50). The Nadiri took and killed [the Qurayzi] in retaliation for his companion. Then al-Nadir and Qurayza boasted to each other. Al-Nadir said: "We are more honorable than you!" Qurayza said: "We are more honorable than you!" They entered Medina to Abu Burda [[In the printed edition: "Abu Barza al-Aslami," which is a plain error. The correct reading is what was in the manuscript, for Abu Barza al-Aslami – Nadla ibn ʿUbayd – is a noble companion, and "Barza" is with a fatha on the *bāʾ*, followed by a silent *rāʾ*, then a *zāy*. As for "Abu Burda," it is with a *ḍamma* on the *bāʾ*, followed by a silent *rāʾ* and then a *dāl*.

Al-Thaʿlabi mentioned in his tafsir that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) invited Abu Burda al-Aslami to Islam, but he refused. Then his two sons spoke to him about it, and he responded and became a Muslim. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said: "In al-Tabarani, with a good chain, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: Abu Burda al-Aslami was a soothsayer who judged between the Jews," and he related the story concerning the revelation of God's saying: "Have you not seen those who claim…" (Al-Isaba, in his biography). Al-Haythami mentioned the report of Ibn ʿAbbas in Majmaʿ al-Zawaʾid 7:6, and in it also "Abu Barza al-Aslami," which is an error, and he said: "al-Tabarani narrated it, and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih." Likewise Ibn Kathir narrated it in his tafsir 2:500, and in it also "Abu Barza," which is an error.]] the Aslami soothsayer. The hypocrite from Qurayza and al-Nadir said: "Let us go to Abu Burda to decide between us by *tanfīr*!" [[In the printed edition here too: "Abu Barza," see the previous note. It is said: "The judge *nafara* one of the disputants against his companion, *tanfīr*": that is, he ruled against him by victory. It derives from *al-munāfara*, which is that two men boast, each against the other, and then they make a man judge between them, and one of them prevails over the other.]] The Muslims of Qurayza and al-Nadir said: "No, rather the Prophet (ﷺ) shall decide between us, so come to him!" The hypocrites refused and went to Abu Burda and asked him – [[In the printed edition here a third time: "Abu Barza."]] He said: "Make the morsel great" – meaning: make the stake great. [["*al-khaṭar*" is the wealth placed as a pledge between those who wager, and he meant by it the fee that each of the disputants gives to the judge. He called it "*al-luqma*" (morsel) metaphorically. All this the lexicographers did not record, and I have not found it in the reports of *munāfarāt*. From this report it is deduced that the judges in *munāfara* would set a fee for themselves which they took after hearing the dispute and after the judgment.]] They said: "For you, ten *awsāq*." He said: "No, rather a hundred *wasq*, as my blood-money, for I fear that if I rule against al-Nadir, Qurayza will kill me, or if I rule against Qurayza, al-Nadir will kill me!" They refused to give him more than ten *awsāq*, and he refused to judge between them. So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: "They desire to take their disputes for judgment to the *ṭāghūt*" – and he is Abu Burda [[In the printed edition here a fourth time: "Abu Barza."]] – "and they were commanded to reject it," up to His saying: "and submit with complete submission."

* *

Others said: "The *ṭāghūt*" in this context is Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf.

Those who said this:

9897 – Muhammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His saying: "They desire to take their disputes for judgment to the *ṭāghūt* while they were commanded to reject it." The *ṭāghūt* was a Jewish man called Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf. Whenever they were called to what God had revealed and to the Messenger to judge between them, they would say: "Rather we will judge before Kaʿb!" That is His saying: "They desire to take their disputes for judgment to the *ṭāghūt*," the verse.

9798 – Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from ʿIsa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's saying: "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you," he said: A hypocrite and a Jew disputed. The hypocrite said: "Come, let us go to Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf." The Jew said: "Come, let us go to the Prophet (ﷺ)." God, blessed and exalted, said: "Have you not seen those who claim…," the verse, and the verse that follows it also concerns them. [[In the manuscript: "the verse that follows it, from them, in both of them, also," which I do not understand, and what is in the printed edition is closer to correct.]]

9899 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you," and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: The Jew said: "Come, let us go to Muhammad."

9900 – al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Jaʿfar narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, regarding His saying: "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you," to His saying: "far astray." He said: There were two men of the companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) who had a dispute between them. One of them was a believer and the other a hypocrite. The believer called him to the Prophet (ﷺ), and the hypocrite called him to Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf. So God revealed: "And when it is said to them, 'Come to what God has revealed and to the Messenger,' you see the hypocrites turning away from you with aversion."

9901 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet desire to take their disputes for judgment to the *ṭāghūt*?" He said: A man of the believers and a Jewish man disputed. The Jew said: "Come, let us go to Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf." The believer said: "Come, let us go to the Prophet (ﷺ)." God said: "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you," up to His saying: "turning away." Ibn Jurayj said: "They claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you," he said: the Qur'an. "And what was revealed before you," he said: the Torah. He said: There would be a dispute between a Muslim and a hypocrite, and the Muslim would call him to the Prophet (ﷺ) to judge between them, but the hypocrite would refuse and call him to the *ṭāghūt*. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid said: "The *ṭāghūt*" is Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf.

9902 – It was narrated to me on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: "They desire to take their disputes for judgment to the *ṭāghūt*": it is Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "*al-ṭāghūt*" in another place, so we have disliked repeating it. [[See what has preceded, 5:507 and note 1, and the references there.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 61:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," you see the hypocrites turning away from you with aversion﴾ (4:61).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Have you not seen, O Muhammad, those hypocrites who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you, and those who claim that they believe in what was revealed before you, from the People of the Book, [who] want to seek judgment from the tyrant (taghut)? ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed"﴾, meaning by this: "And when it is said to them, 'Come' (ta'alaw)" — i.e., "Come (hallummu, i.e., hasten) to the judgment of Allah which He has sent down in His Book, and to the Messenger, that he may judge between us" [[See the explanation of "ta'alaw" in what has preceded, 6:474, 483, 485.]]. ﴿You see the hypocrites turning away from you﴾, meaning by this: they refrain from coming to you so that you may judge between them, and they also prevent others from coming to you. ﴿With aversion.﴾ [[See the explanation of "al-sadd" (turning away) in what has preceded, 4:300 / 7:53 / 8:482.]]

* *

Ibn Jurayj said regarding this:

9903 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger"﴾, he said: A Muslim invited a hypocrite to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to judge between them. He said: ﴿You see the hypocrites turning away from you with aversion.﴾

* *

As for the interpretation of those who made the one calling to the Prophet (ﷺ) a Jew and the one being called a hypocrite, according to what I mentioned of the statements of those who said that regarding His saying: "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you" — then it is as I explained earlier.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿So how will it be when a calamity strikes them because of what their hands have sent forth, and then they come to you swearing by Allah, "We intended nothing but good and conciliation"?﴾ (4:62)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: Almighty and Glorious is He means: So how will it be with these people who wish to take their disputes to the false deity (al-taghut), while they claim that they believe in what was revealed to you and what was revealed before you? ﴿When a calamity strikes them﴾ means: when a punishment (niqmah) from Allah descends upon them. ﴿Because of what their hands have sent forth﴾ means: because of their sins that they committed earlier. [See the explanation of "what their hands have sent forth" in earlier passages: 2:368 / 7:447.] ﴿Then they come to you swearing by Allah﴾ means: then they come to you swearing by Allah falsely and deceitfully ﴿"We intended nothing but good and conciliation"﴾.

This is a report from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, about these hypocrites: that admonitions (al-'ibar) and punishments (al-niqam) do not deter them from hypocrisy, and that if a punishment from Allah befalls them because of their taking their disputes to the false deity, they will not turn back in repentance or repent. Rather, they swear by Allah falsely and with audacity toward Allah: "We intended by our seeking judgment from him nothing but good from some of us toward others, and the correct outcome in what we sought judgment about from him."

[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "and that they, if there come to them" — the better reading is to omit the waw.]

**The Interpretation of His Words:** ﴿Those are the ones whom God knows what is in their hearts, so turn away from them, admonish them, and speak to them in their souls a far-reaching word.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "Those" (*ulaika*), may His praise be exalted, He means these hypocrites whose description I have given you, O Muhammad, that "God knows what is in their hearts" when they seek judgment from the *taghut* (false authority, idols, or anything worshipped or obeyed besides God) and abandon seeking judgment from you, turning away from you, of hypocrisy and deviation, [[السياق: "يعلم الله ما في قلوبهم ... من النفاق والزيغ".]] even if they swear by God, "We only intended goodness and reconciliation." ﴿So turn away from them and admonish them﴾ means: leave them, and do not punish them in their bodies and persons, but admonish them by warning them of God's might descending upon them and His punishment alighting in their abode, and warn them of the evil of what they are upon of doubt regarding the matter of God and the matter of His Messenger. ﴿And speak to them in their souls a far-reaching word﴾ means: command them to fear God and to affirm belief in Him, His Messenger, His promise and His threat.

* *

**The Interpretation of His Words:** ﴿We did not send any messenger except to be obeyed by God's leave.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted means: We did not send, O Muhammad, any messenger except that obedience to him was made obligatory upon those to whom We sent him. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So you, O Muhammad, are among the messengers whose obedience was made obligatory upon those to whom You sent them.

This is indeed a rebuke from God to the hypocrites who sought judgment, those who used to claim that they believed in what was sent down to the Prophet (ﷺ), when they disputed before the *taghut*, turning away from the Messenger of God (ﷺ). He, may His remembrance be exalted, says to them: We did not send any messenger except that obedience to him was made obligatory upon those to whom We sent him, and Muhammad (ﷺ) is among those messengers. So whoever abandons his obedience and his acceptance of his judgment and seeks judgment from the *taghut* has opposed My command and neglected My obligation.

* *

Then He, may His praise be exalted, informed that whoever obeys His messengers, obeys them only by His leave, meaning: by His decree of that, and His prior judgment in His knowledge and will, [[انظر تفسير"الإذن" فيما سلف ٨: ١٩٢ تعليق: ٢ والمراجع هناك.]] as related:

9904 – Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's words, "except to be obeyed by God's leave": it is obligatory for them that whoever God wills obeys them, and no one obeys them except by God's leave.

9905 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

9906 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Shibl, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This is only an allusion from God, may His remembrance be exalted, to these hypocrites, that their abandonment of obedience to God and obedience to His Messenger and their acceptance of His judgment is only due to what was previously decreed for them of abandonment by Him and the dominance of wretchedness over them. Were it not for that, they would have been among those granted permission to accept His judgment and to hasten to obey Him.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 64:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And if, when they had wronged themselves, they had come to you, [O Muhammad], and asked forgiveness of Allah, and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance and Merciful.﴾ (4:64)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: And if these hypocrites, whose description He has given in these two verses, those who, when they are called to the judgment of Allah and His Messenger, turn away with aversion, ﴿when they had wronged themselves﴾ by their acquiring for themselves the great sin of seeking judgment from the taghut (false judge) and turning away from the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger when they were called to it, ﴿had come to you﴾, O Muhammad, when they did what they did of going to the taghut, being content with his judgment over yours, had they come to you repentant and turning back in penitence, and asked Allah to pardon them, veiling their sin from punishment by covering it over, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) asked Allah for the same on their behalf. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿and asked forgiveness of Allah, and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them﴾.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance and Merciful﴾, He says: if they had done that and repented of their sin, ﴿they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance﴾, meaning, turning back to them from what they dislike to what they love (see the explanation of "istighfar" and "tawbah" in the earlier language indexes), ﴿Merciful﴾ to them, in His leaving off punishing them for the sin from which they repented.

* *

Mujahid said: By this is meant the Jew and the Muslim who went to judgment before Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf.

9907 - Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿wronged themselves﴾ up to His saying ﴿and submit in full submission﴾, he said: This refers to the Jewish man and the Muslim man who went to judgment before Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf.

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what is in dispute between them, and then find in themselves no discomfort at what you have decided, and submit with full submission﴾ (65).

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying "But no" (fa-la), the Exalted means: the matter is not as they claim, that they believe in what has been sent down to you while they seek judgment from the tyrant (al-taghut) and turn away from you when they are called to you, O Muhammad. Then He began an oath, may His remembrance be exalted, saying "by your Lord," O Muhammad, "they will not believe," meaning: they do not affirm Me, you, or what has been sent down to you, "until they make you judge (yuhakkimuka) in what is in dispute between them," meaning: until they make you an arbiter between them in what has become mixed up among them of their affairs, so that its ruling has become unclear to them. It is said: "shajara yashjuru shujuran wa shajran," and "tashājara al-qawm" when the people disagreed in speech or in a matter, "mushājaratan wa shijāran."

* *

"Then they find in themselves no discomfort (haraj) at what you have decided": it means they do not find in themselves any constriction at what you have decided. Its meaning is rather: their souls are not made to feel sin (lā taḥraj anfusuhum), that is, they do not commit a sin by denying what you have decided, or by doubting your obedience, or by holding that what you have decided between them is not a truth which they may not oppose, as related:

9908 – Related to me by al-Muthanna, who said: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, who said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "discomfort at what you have decided," he said: doubt.

9909 – Ibn Humayd related to us, who said: Hakkam related to us, from ʿAnbasah, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "discomfort at what you have decided," he says: doubt.

9910 – Related to me by Muhammad ibn ʿAmr, who said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, who said: ʿIsa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

9911 – Yahya ibn Abi Talib related to us, who said: Yazid informed us, who said: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak regarding His saying: "Then they find in themselves no discomfort at what you have decided," he said: sin. "And submit in full submission," he means: and submit to your judgment and ruling, in acknowledgment of obedience and of your prophethood, in full submission.

* *

The people of ta'wil (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about who is meant by this verse and about who it was revealed concerning.

Some of them said: It was revealed concerning al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam and a man from the Ansar, who disputed before the Prophet (ﷺ) about some matter.

Mention of the report to that effect:

9912 – Related to me by Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Yunus and al-Layth ibn Saʿd informed me, from Ibn Shihab, that ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr related to him that ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr related to him, from al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam: that he disputed with a man from the Ansar who had witnessed Badr with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), over some water channels (shirāj) from al-Harrah, which the two of them used to irrigate their palm trees with. [["al-Shirāj" (with a kasra on the shīn) is the plural of "sharj" (with a fatha and sukūn), which is the course of water from the lava field (al-ḥarrah) down to the plain. "Al-Harrah" is a well-known place in Medina, a land of black, porous stones, as if burnt by fire. "Al-Kalaʾ" is the herbage that livestock graze. In the printed edition it read "kalāhumā" without the hamza, which is an error that misleads.]] The Ansari said: Release the water to flow! [[His saying "sarrih al-māʾ" means let it loose, because the water used to pass over al-Zubayr's land before the Ansari's land, so he would hold it back until it had watered his land.]] But he refused him. So [the Prophet] said: O Messenger of God (ﷺ), the Ansari said: Water, O Zubayr, then release the water to your neighbour. The Ansari became angry and said: O Messenger of God, is it because he is the son of your aunt? [[His saying "an kāna..." — "an" (with a fatha on the alif and sukūn on the nūn) is causal: it means "is it because...?" The mother of al-Zubayr was Safiyyah bint ʿAbd al-Muttalib, the aunt of the Messenger of God (ﷺ).]] The face of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) changed color, then he said: Water, O Zubayr, then hold the water until it reaches the walls (al-jidr), then release the water to your neighbour. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) gave al-Zubayr his full right. Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct reading is "istawʿā" [[It is apparent that Abu Jaʿfar's statement "the correct reading is: istawʿab" refers only to the correct wording of the report in this narration with this chain. I do not think Abu Jaʿfar would deny that "istawʿā" may be correct, since "istawʿā" in the sense of "istawʿab" (took his right entirely and in full) is sound, undoubted Arabic.]] — "istawʿab" — and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had earlier given al-Zubayr an opinion, intending kindness toward him and toward the Ansari. When the Ansari angered the Messenger of God (ﷺ), he gave al-Zubayr his full right in the clear ruling. [["Ahfazahu" means he angered him.]] Al-Zubayr said: I do not think this verse was revealed except concerning that: "But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what is in dispute between them," to the end of the verse. [[Hadith 9912. The apparent sense of this chain is that it is from the hadith of "al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam," because of his saying: "that ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr related to him, from al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam." It may also be that it is from the hadith of "ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr," relating the story. The hadith has come with other chains, some of which apparently are from the hadith of ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, relating the story, so its apparent form is a mursal (a report omitting the companion). Others apparently are from the transmission of ʿUrwah from his father al-Zubayr, as will come:

Ibn Abi Hatim related it, as quoted by Ibn Kathir (2:503), with Tabari's chain: from Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla, from Ibn Wahb, the same.

Likewise Ibn al-Jarud related it in al-Muntaqa, p. 453, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAbd al-Hakam, from Ibn Wahb.

Likewise al-Isma'ili related it, as reported by al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) in al-Fath 5:26.

al-Nasaʾi related it (2:308–309) like this report of Tabari, but from two shaykhs: Yunus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla and al-Harith ibn Miskin, both from Ibn Wahb, with this chain, and in all of these — as here — "that ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr related to him from al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam."

Ahmad related it in al-Musnad (16185; 4:4–5 Halabi), in the Musnad of ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from Hashim ibn al-Qasim, from al-Layth, from Ibn Shihab, "from ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, who said: a man from the Ansar disputed with al-Zubayr," etc.

In a similar form, al-Bukhari related it (5:26–28), Muslim (2:221), Abu Dawud (3637), al-Tirmidhi (2:289–290), Ibn Majah (2480), Ibn Hibban in his Sahih (23, our edition) — all through al-Layth ibn Saʿd, from al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwah, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, relating the story. In some of their wordings: "from ʿUrwah: that ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr related to him." The apparent sense of these chains is that it is from the hadith of "ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr," relating the story, without explicit statement of his transmission from his father al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam.

Al-Bukhari said after this report: "No one mentions ʿUrwah from ʿAbd Allah except al-Layth alone."

Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar has responded to him with the narration of "al-Nasaʾi and others" — matching this report of Tabari, Ibn al-Jarud and Ibn Abi Hatim — that Yunus ibn Yazid al-Ayli mentioned in it "from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr," as al-Layth mentioned it. Indeed, Ibn Wahb added in this report from Yunus and al-Layth: that it is "from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam."

Ahmad related it in al-Musnad (1419), from Abu al-Yaman, from Shuʿayb, from al-Zuhri, who said: "ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that al-Zubayr used to narrate that he disputed with a man from the Ansar," etc.

Likewise al-Bukhari related it (5:227, Fath) from Abu al-Yaman, with this chain, like Ahmad's version.

So the apparent sense of this report is that ʿUrwah narrates the hadith in it directly from his father al-Zubayr ibn al-ʿAwwam.

Ibn Kathir (2:502–503) quoted this report from the Musnad, then said: "Thus Imam Ahmad related it, and it is discontinuous (munqaṭiʿ) between ʿUrwah and his father al-Zubayr, for he did not hear from him. What is definitively established is that he heard it from his brother ʿAbd Allah."

I have criticized him in my commentary on the Musnad (1419), saying: The hadith is the hadith of al-Zubayr, and it is not unlikely that his sons ʿAbd Allah and ʿUrwah heard it from him, and that ʿUrwah also heard it from his brother ʿAbd Allah, or that ʿAbd Allah confirmed it. As for the claim that ʿUrwah did not hear from his father, the evidence refutes it, for he was an adolescent or adult at the time of his father's death, at the age of 13. In Tahdhib (7:185): "Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj said in Kitab al-Tamyiz: ʿUrwah performed the Hajj with ʿUthman, and memorized from his father and from those after them among the Companions."

I add here that al-Bukhari stated in the biography of "ʿUrwah" in al-Tarikh al-Kabir (4/1/31) that he heard from his father, saying: "He heard from his father, ʿAʾishah, and ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar." And Imam Ahmad related another hadith before it (1418), through Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, "from ʿUrwah, who said: my father al-Zubayr informed me" — its chain is sound, and it explicitly states ʿUrwah's hearing from his father. Al-Hafiz in al-Fath (5:26) said: "Al-Bukhari authenticated it — despite this variation — relying on the soundness of ʿUrwah's hearing from his father."

ʿUrwah also related it on his own authority, relating the story without stating that it was from his brother or from his father, so its apparent form is a mursal hadith, as in the following report; the rest of the discussion will come there.]]

9913 – Related to me by Yaʿqub, who said: Ismaʿil ibn Ibrahim related to us, from ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwah, who said: al-Zubayr disputed with a man from the Ansar over a water channel from the channels of al-Harrah. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: O Zubayr, water (your land), then release the water. The Ansari, one of the Banu Umayyah, [[In the printed edition, the words "from Banu Umayyah" were omitted, apparently because the editor thought "Banu Umayyah" here meant the Quraysh! But "Banu Umayyah" here are the Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd ibn Qays ibn ʿAmir ibn Marrah ibn Malik ibn al-Aws.]] said: Be just, O Prophet of God, even if he is the son of your aunt! He said: The face of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) changed until it was known that what he said had grieved him. Then he said: O Zubayr, hold the water until it reaches the walls (al-jidr) — or: to the ankles (al-kaʿbayn) — then release the water. He said: And [this] was revealed: "But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what is in dispute between them." [[Hadith 9913. Ismaʿil ibn Ibrahim is Ibn ʿUlayyah.

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Harith ibn Kinanah: trustworthy (thiqah); Ibn Maʿin, al-Bukhari and others declared him trustworthy. Muslim included him in his Sahih. He is biographed in Tahdhib and in Ibn Abi Hatim (2/2/212–213).

This hadith has the form of a mursal, as we indicated in the hadith before it, because ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr — who is a Successor (tabiʿi) — relates the story without mentioning that he transmitted it from his father or his brother.

Likewise Yahya ibn Adam related it in Kitab al-Kharaj, no. 337 (our edition), from Ibn ʿUlayyah, like this report of Tabari.

In this form — the form of a mursal — al-Bukhari related it (5:29, Fath), through Maʿmar, from al-Zuhri, from ʿUrwah, who said: "al-Zubayr disputed with a man..." etc. Likewise he related it again (8:191) through Maʿmar.

Likewise he related it (5:30), through Ibn Jurayj, from al-Zuhri — in the form of a mursal.

Al-Hafiz in al-Fath (5:26) pointed to other reports from al-Zuhri that agree with the reports of Maʿmar and Ibn Jurayj in his narrating it in the form of a mursal hadith.

My view is that ʿUrwah heard the hadith from his father together with his brother ʿAbd Allah, and perhaps he was not fully certain of its memorization because of his young age, so he heard it again from his brother. He transmitted it in various ways: he mentions that it is from his brother, from his father; or he mentions that it is from his father directly; or he sends the story as a mursal without mentioning either of them, out of confidence in having heard it and assurance of it.

For this reason al-Bukhari included in his Sahih the report whose form is that of a mursal in two places, as authentication from him that it is established as a continuous chain (mawsul). Al-Hafiz in al-Fath (5:26) explained al-Bukhari's practice with his saying: "Then, the hadith came concerning something related to al-Zubayr, so the care of his sons for memorizing it was strong."

The hadith in its origin was mentioned by al-Suyuti (2:180), who added its attribution to ʿAbd al-Razzaq, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi.]]

9914 – Related to me by ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmayr al-Razi, who said: ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr related to us, who said: Sufyan related to us, who said: ʿAmr ibn Dinar related to us, from Salamah, a man from the descendants of Umm Salamah, from Umm Salamah: that al-Zubayr disputed a man before the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Prophet (ﷺ) ruled for al-Zubayr. The man said, when he ruled for al-Zubayr: "Is it because he is the son of your aunt?" So God revealed: "But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what is in dispute between them, then find in themselves no discomfort at what you have decided, and submit in full submission." [[Hadith 9914. ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmayr al-Razi, the shaykh of Tabari: I have found no biography of him nor mention of him in any of the sources.

ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr ibn ʿIsa al-Asadi: this is al-Humaydi, the trustworthy, well-known imam, one of al-Bukhari's teachers. Abu Hatim said: "He is the most reliable of people in (the narrations of) Ibn ʿUyaynah, and he is the leader of his companions; he is a trustworthy imam." He died in 219 AH.

Sufyan: this is Ibn ʿUyaynah.

"Salamah, a man from the descendants of Umm Salamah": this is "Salamah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar ibn Abi Salamah." His biography has passed at 8368, 8369.

This hadith contains the earlier story which ʿUrwah ibn al-Zubayr related.

Al-Hafiz referred to it in al-Fath (5:26), saying: "This story has come from another route, which al-Tabari and al-Tabarani related, from the hadith of Umm Salamah."

Al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id (vol. 7, p. 4) in similar form and said: "al-Tabarani related it, and in it is Yaʿqub ibn Humayd, whom Ibn Hibban declared trustworthy and others declared weak."

"Yaʿqub ibn Humayd" is not in this chain — Tabari's chain — so it is another route.

Ibn Kathir (2:503–504) mentioned it from the book of Ibn Mardawayh, through al-Fadl ibn Dukayn, from Ibn ʿUyaynah, with this chain. But in it: "from a man from the family of Abu Salamah, who said: al-Zubayr disputed a man," etc. In it there is no mention of "from Umm Salamah."

al-Suyuti mentioned it (2:180), and added its attribution to al-Humaydi — which is the route in Tabari here — and to Saʿid ibn Mansur, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, and Ibn al-Mundhir.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed concerning the hypocrite and the Jew described by God in His saying: "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you, desiring to seek judgment from the tyrant?"

Mention of those who said that:

9915 – Related to me by Muhammad ibn ʿAmr, who said: Abu ʿAsim related to us, from ʿIsa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what is in dispute between them, then find in themselves no discomfort at what you have decided, and submit in full submission," he said: This was the Jewish man and the Muslim man who were litigating before Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf.

9916 – Related to me by al-Muthanna, who said: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, who said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

9917 – Related to me by Yaʿqub, who said: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from Dawud, from al-Shaʿbi, similar to it — except that he said: to the soothsayer (al-kahin). [[There is another opinion that Tabari mentioned earlier, its evidence in the report no. 5819: that the verse was revealed concerning a man from the Ansar called Abu al-Husayn, who had two sons who became Christians. I have clarified earlier, at 5:410, note 4, that this is among the evidence of Abu Jaʿfar's abridgment of this tafsir.]]

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: This opinion — I mean the view of those who said: it refers to the two who went to the tyrant for judgment, whose situation God described in His saying: "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you?" — is more correct, because His saying: "But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what is in dispute between them" is in the context of the story of those whose report God began with His saying: "Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been sent down to you?" [[In the printed edition: "alladhīna asdā Allāh al-khabar ʿanhum" (those about whom God bestowed the report), which is a statement devoid of all meaning, caused by his not reading the manuscript well, and by not knowing the habits of its copyist, who writes "ibtada'" (began) as "ibtadā" without dots.]] And there is no indication showing that their story is cut off. So attaching part of this to part of it, where no indication of its being cut off has come, is more correct.

If someone supposes that the report transmitted about al-Zubayr and Ibn al-Zubayr concerning their case and the case of the Ansari regarding the watercourses of al-Harra, and the saying of those who said in their report, "So this was revealed: 'But no, by your Lord, they will not believe until they make you judge in what they dispute among themselves'," indicates that the ruling of this verse and its story is cut off from the story of the verses before it, then it is not impossible that the verse was revealed concerning the case of those who sought judgment from the false deity (al-Taghut), [[In the printed edition: "in the case of those who sought judgment (fi hissat al-muhtakimin)", which is a printing error.]] and that it contains a clarification of what al-Zubayr and his Ansari companion went to judgment over, since the verse is an indication that points to it. And since that is not impossible, attaching the meaning of part of this to part of that is more appropriate, so long as the meanings of the speech are coherent within a single context, unless there comes an indication that part of it is cut off from another part, in which case it is turned away from the meaning of what precedes it.
* *
As for His saying, "and submit," it is in the accusative as a conjunction (ma'tuf) on His saying, "then they find in themselves no discomfort." And His saying, "then they find in themselves no discomfort," is in the accusative as a conjunction on His saying, "until they make you judge in what they dispute among themselves."

القول في تأويل قوله: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّا كَتَبْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ أَنِ اقْتُلُوا أَنْفُسَكُمْ أَوِ اخْرُجُوا مِنْ دِيَارِكُمْ مَا فَعَلُوهُ إِلا قَلِيلٌ مِنْهُمْ﴾

(On the interpretation of His saying: "And if We had prescribed for them, 'Kill yourselves or leave your homes,' they would not have done it, except a few of them.")

قال أبو جعفر: يعني جل ثناؤه بقوله: "ولو أنا كتبنا عليهم أن اقتلوا أنفسكم"، ولو أنا فرضنا على هؤلاء الذين يزعمون أنهم آمنوا بما أنزل إليك، المحتكمين إلى الطاغوت، أن يقتلوا أنفسهم وأمرناهم بذلك = أو أن يخرجوا من ديارهم مهاجرين منها إلى دار أخرى سواها [[انظر تفسير "كتب" فيما سلف ص: ٨: ١٧٠، تعليق: ١، والمراجع هناك.]] = "ما فعلوه"، يقول: ما قتلوا أنفسهم بأيديهم، ولا هاجروا من ديارهم فيخرجوا عنها إلى الله ورسوله، طاعة لله ولرسوله = "إلا قليل منهم".

* *

وبنحو ما قلنا في ذلك قال أهل التأويل.

ذكر من قال ذلك:

٩٩١٨ - حدثني محمد بن عمرو قال، حدثنا أبو عاصم، عن عيسى، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد في قول الله: "ولو أنا كتبنا عليهم أن اقتلوا أنفسكم"، يهود يعني = أو كلمة تشبهها = والعربَ، [[في المطبوعة: "هم يهود يعني والعرب". ومثلها في الدر المنثور ٢: ١٨١، وهو تصرف من السيوطي، وتبعه الناشر الأول. وذلك أنه شك في معنى "أو كلمة تشبهها" فحذفها، وزاد في أول الكلام "هم". ولكن قوله: "أو كلمة تشبهها" أي: تشبه "يعني" في معناها، كقولك "يريد" أو "أراد".]] كما أمر أصحاب موسى عليه السلام.

٩٩١٩ - حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا أبو حذيفة قال، حدثنا شبل، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد: "ولو أنا كتبنا عليهم أن اقتلوا أنفسكم أو اخرجوا من دياركم"، كما أمر أصحاب موسى أن يقتل بعضهم بعضًا بالخناجر، لم يفعلوا إلا قليل منهم.

٩٩٢٠ - حدثنا محمد بن الحسين قال، حدثنا أحمد بن مفضل قال، حدثنا أسباط، عن السدي: "ولو أنا كتبنا عليهم أن اقتلوا أنفسكم أو اخرجوا من دياركم ما فعلوه إلا قليل منهم"، افتخر ثابت بن قيس بن شماس ورجل من يهود، فقال اليهودي: والله لقد كتب الله علينا أن اقتلوا أنفسكم، فقتلنا أنفسنا! فقال ثابت: والله لو كُتب علينا أن اقتلوا أنفسكم، لقتلنا أنفسنا! أنزل الله في هذا: "ولو أنهم فعلوا ما يوعظون به لكان خيرًا لهم وأشد تثبيتًا".

٩٩٢١ - حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا إسحاق قال، حدثنا أبو زهير، عن إسماعيل، عن أبي إسحاق السبيعي قال: لما نزلت: "ولو أنا كتبنا عليهم أن اقتلوا أنفسكم أو اخرجوا من دياركم ما فعلوه إلا قليل منهم"، قال رجل: لو أمرنا لفعلنا، والحمد لله الذي عافانا! فبلغ ذلك النبي (ﷺ) فقال: إنّ من أمتي لَرِجالا الإيمان أثبت في قلوبهم من الجبال الرَّواسي.

* *

واختلف أهل العربية (علماء العربية، أي: النحو واللغة) في وجه الرفع في قوله: "إلا قليل منهم".

فكان بعض نحويي البصرة يزعم أنه رفع "قليل"، لأنه جعل بدلا من الأسماء المضمرة في قوله: "ما فعلوه"، لأن الفعل لهم.

* *

وقال بعض نحويي الكوفة: إنما رفع على نية التكرير، كأن معناه: ما فعلوه، ما فعله إلا قليل منهم، كما قال عمرو بن معد يكرب: [[وأصح، نسبته إلى حضرمي بن عامر الأسدي، وينسب إلى سوار بن المضرب، وهو خطأ.]]

وَكُلُّ أَخٍ مُفَارِقُهُ أَخُوهُ، ... لَعمْرُ أَبِيك إلا الفَرْقَدَانِ

(Every brother is parted from by his brother, by your father's life, except the two Farqads.)

[[سيبويه ١: ٣٧١ / مجاز القرآن لأبي عبيدة ١: ١٣١ / البيان والتبيين ١: ٢٢٨ / حماسة البحتري: ١٥١ / الكامل ٢: ٢٩٨ / المؤتلف والمختلف: ٨٥ / الخزانة ٢: ٥٢= ٤: ٧٩ / شرح شواهد المغني: ٧٨. هذا ولم أجد أبيات عمرو بن معد يكرب، وأما شعر حضرمي، فقبل البيت، وهو شعر جيد:

وَذِي فَجْعٍ عَزَفتُ النَّفْسَ عَنْهُ ... حِذَارَ الشَّامتين، وَقَدْ شَجَانِي

(And one who was a source of grief, from whom I turned my soul away for fear of the gloaters, though he had grieved me.)

أَخِي ثِقَةٍ، إذَا مَا اللَّيْلُ أَفْضَى ... إلَيَّ بِمُؤْيِدٍ حُبْلَى كَفَانِي

(A trusted brother, who, when the night brought me a great calamity pregnant with evil, sufficed me.)

قَطَعْتُ قَرِينَتِي عَنْهُ فأغْنَى ... غناهُ، فَلَنْ أَراهُ وَلَنْ يَرَانِي

(I cut off my companion from him, and his sufficiency sufficed; I shall not see him, nor will he see me.)

وكُلُّ قَرِينَةٍ قُرِنَتْ بِأُخْرى، ... وَلَوْ ضَنَّتْ بِهَا، سَتَفَرَّقَانِ

(Every companion joined with another will part, even if it grudges that.)

وكُلُّ أَخٍ...................... ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .

(And every brother ......)

وَكُلُّ إِجَابَتي إِيَّاهُ أَنِّي ... عَطَفْتُ عَلَيْهِ خَوَّار الْعِنَانِ

(And my entire response to him is that I turned upon him a horse that yields to the rein.)

وقوله: "وذي فجع"، أي: صديق يورث فراقه الفجيعة، ويروى "وذى لطف"، ويروي "وذي فخم"، يعني: ذي كبرياء واستعلاء. و"عزف نفسه عن الشيء": صرفها. و"شجاني": أحزنني. و"المؤيد" الداهية العظيمة. "حبلى" تلد شرًا بعد شر. و"القرينة" النفس التي تقارن صاحبها لا تفارقه، حتى يموت. و"خوار العنان" صفة الفرس إذا كان سهل المعطف لينه كثير الجري، يعني، أنه ينصره في الحرب حين يستغيث به.]]

قال أبو جعفر: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك بالصواب، أن يقال: رفع "القليل" بالمعنى الذي دلَّ عليه قوله: "ما فعلوه إلا قليل منهم". وذلك أن معنى الكلام: ولو أنا كتبنا عليهم أن اقتلوا أنفسكم أو اخرجوا من دياركم ما فعله إلا قليل منهم = فقيل: "ما فعلوه" على الخبر عن الذين مضى ذكرهم في قوله: "ألم تر إلى الذين يزعمون أنهم آمنوا بما أنزل إليك وما أنزل من قبلك"، ثم استثنى "القليل"، فرفع بالمعنى الذي ذكرنا، إذ كان الفعل منفيًّا عنه.

* *

وهي في مصاحف أهل الشام: ﴿مَا فَعَلُوهُ إِلا قَلِيلا مِنْهُمْ﴾. وإذا قرئ كذلك، فلا مرْزِئَةَ على قارئه في إعرابه، [["المرزئة" (بفتح الميم، وسكون الراء، وكسر الزاي)، مثل الرزء، والرزيئة: وهو المصيبة والعناء والضرر والنقص، وكل ما يثقل عليك، عافاك الله. وكان في المطبوعة والمخطوطة: "فلا مرد به على قارئه"، وهو شيء لا يفهم ولا يقال!!]] لأنه المعروف في كلام العرب، إذ كان الفعل مشغولا بما فيه كنايةُ مَنْ قد جرى ذكره، [["الكناية" الضمير، كما سلف مرارًا كثيرة. ثم انظر مقالة أبي عبيدة في مجاز القرآن ١: ١٣١.]] ثم استثني منهم القليل.

* *

القول في تأويل قوله: ﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ فَعَلُوا مَا يُوعَظُونَ بِهِ لَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَهُمْ وَأَشَدَّ تَثْبِيتًا (٦٦)﴾

قال أبو جعفر: يعني جل ثناؤه بذلك: ولو أن هؤلاء المنافقين الذين يزعمون أنهم آمنوا بما أنزل إليك، وهم يتحاكمون إلى الطاغوت، ويصدُّون عنك صدودًا = "فعلوا ما يوعظون به"، يعني: ما يذكّرون به من طاعة الله والانتهاء إلى أمره [[انظر تفسير "الوعظ"، فيما سلف ص: ٢٩٩، تعليق: ٤، والمراجع هناك.]] = "لكان خيرًا لهم"، في عاجل دنياهم، وآجل معادهم = "وأشد تثبيتًا"، وأثبت لهم في أمورهم، وأقوم لهم عليها. [[انظر تفسير "التثبيت" فيما سلف ٥: ٣٥٤، ٥٣١ / ٧: ٢٧٢، ٢٧٣. ولو قال: "وأقوى لهم عليها"، لكان ذلك أرجح عندي، وكلتاهما صواب.]] وذلك أن المنافق يعمل على شك، فعمله يذهب باطلا وعناؤه يضمحلّ فيصير هباء، وهو بشكه يعمل على وناءٍ وضعف. [["الونا" و"الوناء": الفترة والكلال والإعياء والضعف.]]

ولو عمل على بصيرة، لاكتسب بعمله أجرًا، ولكان له عند الله ذخرًا، وكان على عمله الذي يعمل أقوى، ولنفسه أشدَّ تثبيتًا، لإيمانه بوعد الله على طاعته، وعمله الذي يعمله. ولذلك قال من قال: معنى قوله: "وأشد تثبيتًا"، تصديقًا، كما:

٩٩٢٢ - حدثني محمد بن الحسين قال، حدثنا أحمد بن مفضل قال، حدثنا أسباط، عن السدي: "لكان خيرًا لهم وأشد تثبيتًا"، قال: تصديقًا.

* *

= لأنه إذا كان مصدّقًا، كان لنفسه أشد تثبيتًا، ولعزمه فيه أشدّ تصحيحًا. وهو نظير قوله جل ثناؤه: ﴿وَمَثَلُ الَّذِينَ يُنْفِقُونَ أَمْوَالَهُمُ ابْتِغَاءَ مَرْضَاةِ اللَّهِ وَتَثْبِيتًا مِنْ أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ [سورة البقرة: ٢٦٥].

وقد أتينا على بيان ذلك في موضعه، بما فيه كفاية من إعادته، [[انظر تفسير الآية فيما سلف ٥: ٥٣٠ - ٥٣٤.]]

**The explanation of His saying:** ﴿And had We given them from Us a great reward﴾ (67) ﴿and guided them to a straight path﴾ (68)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Had they done what they were admonished to do, it would have been better for them, because We would have given them, for their compliance with what they were admonished to do, of obedience to Us and submission to Our command, ﴿a reward﴾, meaning recompense and ﴿a great reward﴾ [[See his explanation of "al-ajr" (reward) above, p. 365, note 3, and the references there.]], and firmer steadfastness for their resolve and opinions, and greater strength for them in their deeds, by Our guiding them to ﴿a straight path﴾, meaning a way free of crookedness, which is the upright religion of God that He chose for His servants and prescribed for them, and that is Islam. [[See his explanation of "al-sirat al-mustaqim" (the straight path) above, 1:170–177; 3:140–141; 6:441.]]

* *

The meaning of His saying "and guided them" is: and We would have granted them success (tawfiq) to the straight path. [[See his explanation of "al-hudā" (guidance) above, in the linguistic indices.]]

Then, may His praise be exalted, He mentioned what He promised to those who obey Him and obey His Messenger (peace be upon him), of lasting honour in His presence and high ranks with Him. He said: ﴿And whoever obeys God and the Messenger, those are with those whom God has blessed, of the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs, and the righteous﴾ — the verse.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verses 69–70:

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger—those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor of the prophets, the steadfast in truth (ṣiddīqīn), the martyrs, and the righteous. And excellent are those as companions﴾ [4:69], ﴿That is the bounty from Allah, and sufficient is Allah as Knower﴾ [4:70].

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger" by submitting to their command, sincerely accepting their judgment, adhering to their order, and refraining from what they have forbidden of disobedience to Allah. So he is with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, by guiding them and enabling them to obey Him, from among His prophets in this world, and in the Hereafter when he enters Paradise. "And the ṣiddīqīn," who are the plural of ṣiddīq.

* *

The meaning of "ṣiddīqīn" has been disputed.

Some said: "The ṣiddīqūn are the followers of the prophets who affirmed them and followed their way after them until they joined them." So, according to those who hold this view, ṣiddīq is on the pattern fiʿīl, from ṣidq (truthfulness), as one says rajul sikkīr (a drunkard) from sukr (intoxication), when he is addicted to it, and shirrīb (a habitual drinker), and khimmīr (one habitually given to khamr, wine).

* *

Others said: Rather, it is fiʿīl from ṣadaqah (charity). It has been related from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ something close to the interpretation of those who said this, namely what follows:

9923 – Sufyan ibn Wakī' related to us, saying: Khālid ibn Makhlad related to us, from Mūsā ibn Yaʿqūb, who said: My paternal aunt Qurayba bint ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb ibn Zamʿa informed me, from her mother Kurayma bint al-Miqdād, [In the manuscript it reads "Kurayma bint al-Miqdām," which is an error; the correct form is as in the printed edition.] from Ḍubāʿa bint al-Zubayr, [In the manuscript: "Matāʿa bint al-Zubayr," an error; its correct form is in the printed edition.] and she was married to al-Miqdād, from al-Miqdād, who said: I said to the Prophet ﷺ: "Something I heard from you, I have doubts about!" He said: "If one of you doubts a matter, let him ask me about it." He said: I said: "Your saying about your wives: 'Indeed I hope for them, after me, the ṣiddīqīn'." He said: "Whom do you count as the ṣiddīqīn?" I said: "Our children who die young." He said: "No, but the ṣiddīqīn are the ṣaddiqūn (those who affirm)." [In the manuscript and printed edition: "man taʿnūn al-ṣiddīqīn," which is an error with no meaning. The correct reading is what I have set down, from the abridged version of this report in Muntakhab Kanz al-ʿUmmāl (marginal to the Musnad) 5:113.]

[Note on the hadith 9923: Sufyan ibn Wakī' ibn al-Jarrāh, the teacher of al-Tabari, is weak, as we explained in 142–143. He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr of al-Bukhārī 4/1/298, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim 4/1/167, and neither mentions any criticism; Ibn Abī Ḥātim merely limited himself to Ibn Maʿīn's affirmation of him. Qurayba, diminutive, bint ʿAbd Allāh ibn Wahb ibn Zamʿa, aunt of Mūsā ibn Yaʿqūb: biographed in al-Tahdhīb, with no criticism of her. Her mother Kurayma bint al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad: a reliable Successor (tābiʿiyya). Ibn Ḥibbān mentioned her in al-Thiqāt. Ḍubāʿa bint al-Zubayr ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, daughter of the Prophet's paternal uncle: a well-known Companion. She was the wife of al-Miqdād ibn al-Aswad, and she has narrations from the Prophet ﷺ and from her husband al-Miqdād. This report was mentioned by al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr 2:183, in abridged form, and he did not attribute it to anyone other than Ibn Jarīr. But it was mentioned in the great compilation called Jamiʿ al-Jawāmiʿ, as is indicated by its mention in Muntakhab Kanz al-ʿUmmāl by al-Muttaqī al-Hindī, printed in the margin of Musnad Aḥmad (Ḥalabī edition), where it is given in abridged form (vol. 5, p. 113), and he attributed it to al-Ṭabarānī in al-Kabīr. I was unable to find it in Majmaʿ al-Zawāʾid, because it does not meet its conditions. I do not know whether al-Ṭabarānī's narration came through Sufyan ibn Wakī', or through another narrator. If it came through a narrator other than him, the chain would be good, since the criticism of Sufyan ibn Wakī' did not arise from any lack of truthfulness, as I explained in his biography.]

* *

This is a report which, if its chain were sound, we would not dare to go beyond. And even if there were some flaw in its chain.

Given that this is the case, the more fitting meaning of "ṣiddīq" is that it means one who affirms his speech by his deeds. Because the pattern fiʿīl in the speech of the Arabs, when derived from a verb, comes to express intensity, either in praise or in blame. From it is His saying, may His praise be exalted, concerning the description of Mary: ﴿And her mother was a ṣiddīqa﴾ [5:75].

And when the meaning is what we have described, then whoever is described by what we have stated is included among the ones who give charity (mutaṣaddiqīn) and the ones who affirm (muṣaddiqīn).

"And the martyrs (shuhadāʾ)," the plural of shahīd, who is one killed in the way of Allah. He was named so because he stood up for the testimony of truth in the cause of Allah until he was killed. [See the explanation of "shuhadāʾ" above, 368, note 3, and the references there.]

* *

"And the righteous (ṣāliḥīn)," the plural of ṣāliḥ, who is everyone whose inner and outer conduct is sound. [See the explanation of "ṣāliḥ" above, 293, note 1, and the references there.]

As for His saying, may His praise be exalted, "And excellent are those as companions (rafīqan)," it means: "And excellent are these whom He has described and characterized as companions in Paradise."

* *

"Rafīq" in form is singular but in meaning is plural, as the poet said: [The poet is Jarīr.]

"They called upon desire, then they shot our hearts
with arrows of enemies, and they are ṣadīq (friends)."

Meaning: "and they are ṣadāʾiq (friends)."

[The Dīwān: 398, and Ṭabaqāt Fuḥūl al-Shuʿarāʾ: 351, and al-Lisān (ṣ-d-q), and many others. From verses in which al-Ḥajjāj is mentioned; before it are verses of Ḥassān, to be memorized:
"I spent the night deceiving my two companions with patience, though your love had clung to me with its clinging.
So how with it? Neither does the house gather desire, nor are you, at the time of your youth, one who wakes from it.
Shall one heart in Iraq gather its companionship, and from it, in the shade of the arak trees, another group?
As though the fragrant ones had not pleased me one evening, and there had been no lover in the people of Iraq.
I struggle with a torment of your love, and a heart has worn me down, which throbs whenever you are mentioned.
Companions (ʾawānis), as for those who wanted my hardship, then he is a captive, and whoever they released, then he is free.
They called upon desire............."
In the printed edition it reads "nasabna al-hawā" [they set up desire], which is another transmission, different from what is in the manuscript and the Dīwān.]

* *

As for the accusative of "rafīq," the scholars of Arabic grammar differ about it.

One of the grammarians of Basra held that it is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl), and he said: It is like the saying of a man: "Zayd was generous as a man (karuma Zayd rajulan)," and he diverted it from the meaning of "niʿma al-rajul" (what an excellent man), and he said: "niʿma" only occurs with a noun that has "al-" (the definite article), or with an indefinite noun.

* *

One of the grammarians of Kufa held that it is in the accusative as a specification (tafsīr), [The "tafsīr" is the tamyīz, and the "mufassir" is the mumayyiz, as passed many times. See the index of terms.] and he denied that it is a circumstantial qualifier, and he cited as evidence that the Arabs say: "Karuma Zayd min rajul" and "Ḥasuna ulāʾika min rufaqāʾ," and that the entry of "min" is an indication that "rafīq" is its specification. He said: And it has been related of the Arabs: "Niʿimtum rijālan," which indicates that this is parallel to His saying: "Wa-ḥasuntum rufaqāʾ."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This view is closer to correctness, for the reason we mentioned for its proponents.

* *

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed because some people grieved over the loss of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, fearing that they would not see him in the Hereafter.

Mention of the narration to that effect:

9924 – Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Yaʿqūb al-Qummī related to us, from Jaʿfar ibn Abī al-Mughīra, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: A man from the Anṣār came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was grieved, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "O so-and-so, why do I see you grieved?" He said: "O Prophet of Allah, a matter I have been thinking about!" He said: "What is it?" He said: "We come to you in the morning and in the evening, we look at your face and sit with you, but tomorrow you will be raised with the prophets and we will not reach you!" The Prophet ﷺ did not reply with anything. Then Jibrīl (peace be upon him) came to him with this verse: "Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among the prophets, the ṣiddīqīn, the shuhadāʾ and the ṣāliḥīn, and excellent are those as companions." He said: Then the Prophet ﷺ sent for him and gave him good news.

9925 – Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Jarīr related to us, from Manṣūr, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, who said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Messenger of Allah, it is not fitting for us to be separated from you in this world, for if you were to die, you would be raised above us and we would not see you!" So Allah revealed: "Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger," the verse.

9926 – Bishr ibn Muʿādh related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatāda, regarding His saying: "Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among the prophets." It was mentioned to us that some men said: "This is the Prophet of Allah whom we see in this world, but in the Hereafter he will be raised and we will not see him!" So Allah revealed: "Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger," up to His saying: "companions."

9927 – Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn related to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal related to us, saying: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: "Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor," the verse. He said: Some of the Anṣār said: "O Messenger of Allah, when Allah admits you into Paradise and you are in its highest part, and we long for you, how shall we act?" So Allah revealed: "Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger."

9928 – Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Isḥāq related to us, saying: Ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ, regarding His saying: "Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger," the verse. He said: The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said: "We know that the Prophet ﷺ has his excellence over those who believed in him, in the ranks of Paradise, from among those who followed him and affirmed him. How will they be when they gather in Paradise, that some of them see others?" So Allah revealed concerning that. It is said: The two higher groups descend to those who are below them, and they gather in its gardens, mentioning what Allah has bestowed upon them and praising Him, and the people of the ranks descend to them, serving them with what they desire and what they call for, and they are in its meadow, rejoicing and enjoying its delights.

* *

As for His saying: "That is the bounty from Allah," He means: that those who obey Allah and the Messenger being with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among the prophets, the ṣiddīqīn, the shuhadāʾ and the ṣāliḥīn, is "the bounty from Allah." That is, it is Allah's gift to them and His favor upon them, not because they earned it through a prior merit that preceded them. [See the explanation of "faḍl" above, 2:344; 5:164, 571; 6:518; 7:299, 414; 8:268.]

* *

If someone says: Did they not reach what they reached of His favor through obedience?

It is said to him: They did not obey Him in this world except by His favor, which He bestowed upon them, guiding them by it to His obedience. So all of that is favor from Him, may His praise be exalted.

* *

As for His saying: "And sufficient is Allah as Knower," He means: sufficient for the servants is Allah who created them, as "Knower" of the obedience of the obedient among them and the disobedience of the disobedient, for nothing of that is hidden from Him. Rather, He counts it against them and preserves it, until He recompenses all of them: rewarding the good-doers among them with goodness, and the wrongdoers among them with wrongdoing, and He pardons whom He wills of the people of monotheism.
