* *

"And the righteous (ṣāliḥīn)," the plural of ṣāliḥ, who is everyone whose inner and outer conduct is sound. [See the explanation of "ṣāliḥ" above, 293, note 1, and the references there.]

As for His saying, may His praise be exalted, "And excellent are those as companions (rafīqan)," it means: "And excellent are these whom He has described and characterized as companions in Paradise."

* *

"Rafīq" in form is singular but in meaning is plural, as the poet said: [The poet is Jarīr.]

"They called upon desire, then they shot our hearts
with arrows of enemies, and they are ṣadīq (friends)."

Meaning: "and they are ṣadāʾiq (friends)."

[The Dīwān: 398, and Ṭabaqāt Fuḥūl al-Shuʿarāʾ: 351, and al-Lisān (ṣ-d-q), and many others. From verses in which al-Ḥajjāj is mentioned; before it are verses of Ḥassān, to be memorized:
"I spent the night deceiving my two companions with patience, though your love had clung to me with its clinging.
So how with it? Neither does the house gather desire, nor are you, at the time of your youth, one who wakes from it.
Shall one heart in Iraq gather its companionship, and from it, in the shade of the arak trees, another group?
As though the fragrant ones had not pleased me one evening, and there had been no lover in the people of Iraq.
I struggle with a torment of your love, and a heart has worn me down, which throbs whenever you are mentioned.
Companions (ʾawānis), as for those who wanted my hardship, then he is a captive, and whoever they released, then he is free.
They called upon desire............."
In the printed edition it reads "nasabna al-hawā" [they set up desire], which is another transmission, different from what is in the manuscript and the Dīwān.]

* *

As for the accusative of "rafīq," the scholars of Arabic grammar differ about it.

One of the grammarians of Basra held that it is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (ḥāl), and he said: It is like the saying of a man: "Zayd was generous as a man (karuma Zayd rajulan)," and he diverted it from the meaning of "niʿma al-rajul" (what an excellent man), and he said: "niʿma" only occurs with a noun that has "al-" (the definite article), or with an indefinite noun.

* *

One of the grammarians of Kufa held that it is in the accusative as a specification (tafsīr), [The "tafsīr" is the tamyīz, and the "mufassir" is the mumayyiz, as passed many times. See the index of terms.] and he denied that it is a circumstantial qualifier, and he cited as evidence that the Arabs say: "Karuma Zayd min rajul" and "Ḥasuna ulāʾika min rufaqāʾ," and that the entry of "min" is an indication that "rafīq" is its specification. He said: And it has been related of the Arabs: "Niʿimtum rijālan," which indicates that this is parallel to His saying: "Wa-ḥasuntum rufaqāʾ."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This view is closer to correctness, for the reason we mentioned for its proponents.

* *

It has been mentioned that this verse was revealed because some people grieved over the loss of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, fearing that they would not see him in the Hereafter.

Mention of the narration to that effect:

9924 – Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Yaʿqūb al-Qummī related to us, from Jaʿfar ibn Abī al-Mughīra, from Saʿīd ibn Jubayr, who said: A man from the Anṣār came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was grieved, and the Prophet ﷺ said to him: "O so-and-so, why do I see you grieved?" He said: "O Prophet of Allah, a matter I have been thinking about!" He said: "What is it?" He said: "We come to you in the morning and in the evening, we look at your face and sit with you, but tomorrow you will be raised with the prophets and we will not reach you!" The Prophet ﷺ did not reply with anything. Then Jibrīl (peace be upon him) came to him with this verse: "Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among the prophets, the ṣiddīqīn, the shuhadāʾ and the ṣāliḥīn, and excellent are those as companions." He said: Then the Prophet ﷺ sent for him and gave him good news.

9925 – Ibn Ḥumayd related to us, saying: Jarīr related to us, from Manṣūr, from Abū al-Ḍuḥā, from Masrūq, who said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O Messenger of Allah, it is not fitting for us to be separated from you in this world, for if you were to die, you would be raised above us and we would not see you!" So Allah revealed: "Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger," the verse.

9926 – Bishr ibn Muʿādh related to us, saying: Yazīd related to us, saying: Saʿīd related to us, from Qatāda, regarding His saying: "Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among the prophets." It was mentioned to us that some men said: "This is the Prophet of Allah whom we see in this world, but in the Hereafter he will be raised and we will not see him!" So Allah revealed: "Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger," up to His saying: "companions."

9927 – Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn related to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal related to us, saying: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī: "Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favor," the verse. He said: Some of the Anṣār said: "O Messenger of Allah, when Allah admits you into Paradise and you are in its highest part, and we long for you, how shall we act?" So Allah revealed: "Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger."

9928 – Al-Muthannā related to me, saying: Isḥāq related to us, saying: Ibn Abī Jaʿfar related to us, from his father, from al-Rabīʿ, regarding His saying: "Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger," the verse. He said: The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ said: "We know that the Prophet ﷺ has his excellence over those who believed in him, in the ranks of Paradise, from among those who followed him and affirmed him. How will they be when they gather in Paradise, that some of them see others?" So Allah revealed concerning that. It is said: The two higher groups descend to those who are below them, and they gather in its gardens, mentioning what Allah has bestowed upon them and praising Him, and the people of the ranks descend to them, serving them with what they desire and what they call for, and they are in its meadow, rejoicing and enjoying its delights.

* *

As for His saying: "That is the bounty from Allah," He means: that those who obey Allah and the Messenger being with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor from among the prophets, the ṣiddīqīn, the shuhadāʾ and the ṣāliḥīn, is "the bounty from Allah." That is, it is Allah's gift to them and His favor upon them, not because they earned it through a prior merit that preceded them. [See the explanation of "faḍl" above, 2:344; 5:164, 571; 6:518; 7:299, 414; 8:268.]

* *

If someone says: Did they not reach what they reached of His favor through obedience?

It is said to him: They did not obey Him in this world except by His favor, which He bestowed upon them, guiding them by it to His obedience. So all of that is favor from Him, may His praise be exalted.

* *

As for His saying: "And sufficient is Allah as Knower," He means: sufficient for the servants is Allah who created them, as "Knower" of the obedience of the obedient among them and the disobedience of the disobedient, for nothing of that is hidden from Him. Rather, He counts it against them and preserves it, until He recompenses all of them: rewarding the good-doers among them with goodness, and the wrongdoers among them with wrongdoing, and He pardons whom He wills of the people of monotheism.

The interpretation of His saying, exalted be His praise: ﴿O you who believe, take your precaution, then go forth in groups or go forth all together﴾ (4:71).

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted be His praise, "O you who believe" — [meaning] believe in God and His Messenger — "take your precaution" — take your armour and weapons with which you guard yourselves against your enemy for raiding and fighting them — "then go forth in groups."

* *

"Groups" is the plural of "thubah," and the "thubah" is a band of men.

The meaning of the words is: go forth against your enemy in group after group, armed.

From the use of "thubah" is the verse of Zuhayr:

"And we set out at dawn with a band of noble men... intoxicated, longing for what we desire."

["thubah" may be pluralized as "thubin." See Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah, 1:132.]

* *

"Or go forth all together," that is: or go forth all together with your Prophet ﷺ to fight them.

The interpreters of the Qur'an have said in agreement with what we have said.

Those who said so:

9929 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying, "take your precaution, then go forth in groups": he said: "groups" — bands, meaning separate detachments; "or go forth all together": meaning all of you.

9930 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding God's saying, "then go forth in groups": he said: "in companies, little by little."

9931 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His saying, "then go forth in groups": he said: "Thubat" means separate companies.

9932 - Al-Husayn ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, the like of it.

9933 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding "then go forth in groups": it is the band, and it is the "thubah"; "or go forth all together": with the Prophet ﷺ.

9934 - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying, "then go forth in groups": he said: "bands, dispersed."

The explanation of His words, ﴿And indeed among you is one who lingers behind, so if a disaster strikes you he says, "Allah has been gracious to me in that I was not a witness with them."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a description by Allah, may He be mentioned, of the hypocrites. He describes them to His Prophet ﷺ and his Companions, characterizing them by their attributes, and so He said: ﴿And indeed among you﴾, O believers, meaning: from your number and your people, and one who resembles you and appears to be from the people of your call and your religion, yet he is a hypocrite who holds back whoever among you obeys him from fighting your enemy and battling them when you go forth against them. ﴿So if a disaster strikes you﴾ [[See the discussion of "striking with a disaster" above: 514.]] means: if you suffer a defeat, or you are struck by killing or wounds from your enemy. ﴿He says, "Allah has been gracious to me in that I was not a witness with them,"﴾ meaning: "I was not struck by wounds, pain, or killing," and his being left behind from you pleases him, out of gloating over you, because he is among those who doubt the promise of Allah, which He promised the believers for what they suffer in His cause of reward and recompense, and in His threat. So he neither hopes for reward nor fears punishment.

* *

Those who held this same view as we have said about this matter are the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil).

Those who said this:

9935 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words: ﴿And indeed among you is one who lingers behind, so if a disaster strikes you﴾ up to His words ﴿then We shall give him a great reward﴾, that everything between them concerns the hypocrites.

9936 – al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

9937 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿And indeed among you is one who lingers behind﴾: from jihad and raiding in the way of Allah. ﴿So if a disaster strikes you, he says, "Allah has been gracious to me in that I was not a witness with them,"﴾ He said: This is the statement of one who denies.

9938 – al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: The hypocrite holds back the Muslims from jihad in the way of Allah. Allah said: ﴿So if a disaster strikes you﴾, he said: by the killing of Muslims by the enemy. ﴿He says, "Allah has been gracious to me in that I was not a witness with them,"﴾ he said: This is the statement of one who gloats.

9939 – Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿So if a disaster strikes you﴾: it is defeat.

* *

The lam in His words ﴿la-man﴾ entered and was given a fatha, because it is the lam that enters for emphasis of the predicate together with ﴿inna﴾, like the speaker's saying: "Indeed, in the house is one who will honor you." As for the second lam in ﴿la-yubaṭṭi'anna﴾, it entered as the answer to an oath, as if the meaning of the statement were: "And indeed among you, O people, is one who by Allah will surely linger behind." [[See the detailed treatment of this in al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 275, 276.]]

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And if a bounty from Allah reaches you, he will surely say, as if there had been no bond of affection between you and him, "Oh, I wish I had been with them so I could have attained a great success."﴾ (4:73)**

Abu Ja'far said: His, may His praise be exalted, meaning: "﴿And if a bounty from Allah reaches you﴾", that is, if Allah grants you victory over your enemy and you obtain spoils, ﴿he will surely say﴾, this one who holds back the Muslims from jihad alongside you in the cause of Allah, the hypocrite, ﴿as if there had been no bond of affection between you and him, "Oh, I wish I had been with them so I could attain"﴾ what is gained from the spoils obtained with them, ﴿a great success."﴾

* *

This is a report from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, about these hypocrites: that their presence in battle alongside the Muslims, if they are present, is for the sake of seeking spoils; and if they stay behind, it is because of the doubt in their hearts, and because they do not hope for reward for attending, nor fear punishment from Allah for staying behind.

* *

Qatadah and Ibn Juraij used to say: what the hypocrite says when victory belongs to the Muslims, "Oh, I wish I had been with them," is only out of envy of them.

9940. Bishr ibn Mu'adh told us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Sa'id told us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: ﴿And if a bounty from Allah reaches you, he will surely say, as if there had been no bond of affection between you and him, "Oh, I wish I had been with them so I could attain a great success."﴾ He said: It is the saying of one who envies.

9941. Al-Qasim told us, saying: Al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Juraij, regarding His saying: ﴿And if a bounty from Allah reaches you﴾, he said: It is the Muslims' victory over their enemy and their obtaining of spoils. ﴿He will surely say, "Oh, I wish I had been with them so I could attain a great success."﴾ He said: It is the saying of the envious one.

**The interpretation of His saying:** ﴿So let those fight in the way of Allah who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter. And whoever fights in the way of Allah and is killed or achieves victory, We will give him a great reward.﴾ (4:74)

Abu Ja'far said: This is an exhortation from Allah to the believers to fight His enemies from among the people of disbelief in Him, in every circumstance, whether they are victorious or defeated, and not to heed the words of the hypocrites concerning the fighting of those who fought against the polytheists, [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "and the disregard of the conditions of the polytheists." What the context of the commentary indicates is what I have confirmed. It means what the hypocrite says when the Muslims are defeated: "Allah has blessed me by not having been a martyr among them," and his saying when the dynasty and victory belong to the Muslims: "Would that I had been with them, so that I might achieve a great triumph."

His saying "and the disregard" is coordinated with his saying "This is an exhortation from Allah to the believers to fight His enemy."]] and that for them, in their fighting against them, whether defeated or victorious, there is an exalted station from Allah. [[In the place of what is between the brackets, the manuscript and the printed edition read: "occurred," which is a statement that does not stand at all. I have inferred that the correct wording of the context is what I have confirmed, or something similar in meaning.]]

* *

Allah, may His praise be exalted, says to them: "So let those fight in the way of Allah," meaning: in the religion of Allah and in calling to it, and in entering into what He has commanded concerning the people of disbelief in Him. "Who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter," meaning: those who sell their worldly life for the reward of the Hereafter and what Allah has promised to the people of His obedience therein. Their selling it for that consists of their spending their wealth seeking the pleasure of Allah, in fighting those whom He has commanded them to fight, from among His enemies and the enemies of His religion, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "as the fighting of those whom He has commanded to fight." The correct context is "for the fighting of..." as I have confirmed.]] and their giving up their souls for that purpose.

* *

Allah, may His praise be exalted, informs them of what awaits them in that when they do it, saying: "And whoever fights in the way of Allah and is killed or achieves victory, We will give him a great reward." That is, whoever fights, seeking to establish the religion of Allah and to raise the word of Allah, against the enemies of Allah, "and is killed," that is, the enemies of Allah kill him, "or achieves victory," that is, he overcomes them and gains the upper hand over them, "We will give him a great reward," that is, We will give him a great reward and recompense in the Hereafter. There is no measure of what He, may His praise be exalted, has called "great" that the servants of Allah can know the extent of. [[See the explanation of "reward" in what has preceded: 529, note 2, and the references there.]]

* *

We have already shown that the predominant meaning of "shara" (to buy/sell) in the speech of the Arabs is "sold," in a manner that suffices [without repeating it]. [[See the explanation of "shara" and "ishtara" in what has preceded: 1:312–315 / 2:340–342, 455 / 3:328 / 4:246 / 6:527 / 7:420, 459 / 8:428.

I have added what is between the brackets, following the pattern of his expression in hundreds of earlier places. It appears that the copyist forgot to write it, because "bima aghna" fell at the bottom of the page, then he turned the leaf to the next page and wrote "wa-qad."]]

And indeed:

9942 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "So let those fight in the way of Allah who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter": he said: They sell the life of this world for the Hereafter.

9943 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding "who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter": "yashri" means "yabi'" (sells), and "yashri" means "ya'khudh" (takes). And indeed the fools sold the Hereafter for this world.

**On the interpretation of His words:** ﴿And what is the matter with you that you do not fight in the way of God, and for the oppressed men, women, and children, who say: "Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers, and appoint for us from Yourself a protector, and appoint for us from Yourself a helper"﴾ (4:75).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may His praise be exalted, means by this: "And what is the matter with you," O believers, "that you do not fight in the way of God," and "for the oppressed" means: on behalf of the oppressed among you, "men, women, and children." As for the men, they had embraced Islam in Mecca, but their clans overpowered them by coercion, harmed them, and inflicted upon them torture and hardships on their bodies in order to turn them away from their religion. So God urged the believers to rescue them from the hands of the disbelievers who had overpowered them, and He said to them: "What is your situation that you do not fight in the way of God, and on behalf of the oppressed of your people and your community, whom the disbelievers have deemed weak, treated with contempt, and humiliated, seeking to tempt them and to divert them from their religion?" "Men, women, and children": "children" is the plural of "walad," and they are boys. "Who say: Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers." This means that these oppressed men, women, and children say in their supplication to their Lord that He should deliver them from the trial of those among the polytheists who had oppressed them: "O our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers."

* *

The Arabs call every city a "qaryah" (town), meaning: the one whose people have wronged us and themselves. In this place, according to what the people of ta'wil (interpretation) have explained, it is Mecca.

* *

The word "al-zalim" (wrongdoers) is in the genitive case because it is a qualifier of "ahl" (people). The pronoun "ha' and alif" (the suffix) in it refers back to "qaryah." Thus the Arabs do this: when a qualifier of a noun precedes it, and the qualifier bears a pronoun referring to a noun before it, they make its case match the case of the noun before it, as if it were its qualifier. So you say: "I passed by the noble man whose father (is noble)" ("marartu bi-l-rajuli al-karimi abuhu").

* *

"And appoint for us from Yourself a protector": this means that they also say in their supplication: "O our Lord, and appoint for us from Yourself a protector, who will take charge of our affairs with sufficiency against the trial we are in from the people of disbelief in You." "And appoint for us from Yourself a helper": they say: [[See the explanation of "al-wali" (protector) and "al-nasir" (helper) in the language indexes earlier.]] appoint for us from Yourself someone who will help us against those who have wronged us, the people of this town whose people are wrongdoers, by their barring us from Your path, until You grant us victory over them and exalt Your religion.

* *

The people of ta'wil have said what is similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

9944 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding God's words: "Of the men, women, and children, who say: Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers." He said: He commanded the believers to fight on behalf of the oppressed believers who were in Mecca.

9945 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And the oppressed men, women, and children" = the children, "who say: Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers," Mecca. He commanded the believers to fight on behalf of the oppressed believers who were in Mecca.

9946 - al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And what is the matter with you that you do not fight in the way of God and for the oppressed men, women, and children, who say: Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers." He says: What is the matter with you that you do not fight in the way of God and for the oppressed? As for "the town," it is Mecca.

9947 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Uthman ibn Ata, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words: "And what is the matter with you that you do not fight in the way of God and for the oppressed," he said: "and for the oppressed."

9948 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: al-Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abdullah ibn Kathir informed me that he heard Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Shihab say: "And what is the matter with you that you do not fight in the way of God and for the oppressed men, women, and children," he said: in the way of God and in the way of the oppressed.

9949 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Hasan and Qatada, regarding His words: "Bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers." Both said: A man went out from the wrongdoing town toward the righteous town, and death overtook him on the way. He leaned his chest toward the righteous town, [[His words "nai bi-sadrihi" mean he distanced himself with it. That is: he exerted himself while dying until his chest faced the righteous town, turning away from and avoiding the wrongdoing town. Similar is "nai bi-janbihi" (he turned his side away).]] and that alone saved him [[His words "fa-ma tala'fahu illa dhalik" mean: nothing rescued him from an evil end except this turning away he made from the wrongdoing town. This sentence was undotted in the manuscript, so the editor of the printed edition chose to omit it, since he could not read and understand it well.]]. So the angels of mercy and the angels of punishment disputed concerning him, [[His words "ihtajjat fihi" mean: the angels disputed over him, each party presenting its proof. This form with this meaning does not appear in the lexicons, but it is sound and ancient. They said "ihtajja bi-l-shay'" meaning he took it as a proof, and for disputing and contending they said "tahajja al-qawm." This is one of the sound additions beyond the restrictions of the language.]] and they were commanded to measure which of the two towns was nearer to him. They found him nearer to the righteous town by a span. Some of them said: God brought the righteous town near to him, so the angels of mercy took his soul.

9950 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding his words: "And the oppressed men, women, and children," they are Muslim people who were in Mecca and could not leave it to emigrate, so God excused them. They are those (referred to in) His words: "Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers." As for "the town," it is Mecca.

9950 (repeated as 9950a) - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: "And what is the matter with you that you do not fight in the way of God and for the oppressed men, women, and children who say: Our Lord, bring us out of this town whose people are wrongdoers": He said: What is the matter with you that you do not act? Fight for these weak, poor people who ask God to bring them out of this town whose people are wrongdoers. They have no strength, so what is the matter with you that you do not fight until God makes these and their religion victorious? He said: And "the town whose people are wrongdoers" is Mecca.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 76:

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Those who believe fight in the cause of Allah, and those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the Taghut (false deity). So fight against the friends of Satan. Indeed, the plot of Satan is ever weak.﴾ (4:76)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: He, may He be exalted and remembered, means: those who affirm Allah and His Messenger and are certain of Allah's promise to the people of faith in Him, "fight in the cause of Allah," that is, in obedience to Allah and in the path of His religion and His law which He has prescribed for His servants [see the explanation of "the cause of Allah" in the earlier indexes of language, root (s-b-l)]. "And those who disbelieve fight in the cause of the Taghut," that is, those who deny the oneness of Allah and disbelieve His Messenger and what he brought them from their Lord, "fight in the cause of the Taghut" [see the explanation of "Taghut" earlier, 3:416–420 / 8:461–465, 507–513], meaning: in the obedience of Satan, his way and his path which he has prescribed for his allies from among the people of disbelief in Allah. Allah says, strengthening the resolve of the believers among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and urging them against His enemies and the enemies of His religion from among the people of polytheism: "So fight," O believers, "the friends of Satan," meaning by this: those who take him as a protector and obey his command in opposition to the obedience of Allah and in denial of Him, and who support him [see the explanation of "wali" (protector, ally) earlier in the indexes of language]. "Indeed, the plot of Satan is ever weak," meaning by his plot: what he schemed against the believers, from his gathering of his allies among the disbelievers in Allah against His Messenger and his allies, the people of faith in Him [see the explanation of "al-kayd" (plotting) earlier, 7:156]. He means: do not fear the friends of Satan, for they are only his party and his helpers, and the party of Satan are people of weakness and frailty.

* *

He, may He be exalted and remembered, described them with weakness only because they do not fight hoping for reward, nor do they abandon fighting out of fear of punishment; rather, they fight out of zealotry or envy of the believers for what Allah has given them of His bounty. The believer who fights among them fights hoping for the great reward of Allah, and if he abandons fighting, he does so out of fear of the threat of Allah for abandoning it. Thus he fights with insight into what he has with Allah if he is killed, and into the spoils and victory if he survives. The disbeliever fights out of fear of being killed and despair of any return, so he is one of weakness and fear.

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 77:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands, establish prayer and give zakah"? But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a faction of them fear men as they fear Allah or with greater fear, and they say, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed for us fighting? If only You had delayed us to a near term."﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who had believed in him and affirmed him before jihad was prescribed for them. Prayer and zakah had already been prescribed for them, and they used to ask Allah to prescribe fighting for them. But when fighting was prescribed for them, it was hard for them, and they said what Allah related about them in His Book.

* *

As for the interpretation of His saying, "Have you not seen those who were told, 'Restrain your hands'": have you not seen with your heart, O Muhammad, [see the explanation of "Have you not seen" above: 426, note 5, and the references there] "those who were told" from among your Companions, when they asked you to ask your Lord to prescribe fighting for them; "Restrain your hands", that is, hold them back from fighting and warring against the polytheists; "and establish prayer", meaning: perform the prayer that Allah has prescribed for you within its limits [see the explanation of "establishing prayer" above in the index of language (qawm)]; "and give zakah", meaning: give zakah to its people, those whom Allah has designated for it from your wealth, as a purification for your bodies and your wealth [see the explanation of "giving zakah" above in the index of language: "atā" and "zakā"]. They disliked what they were commanded: restraining their hands from fighting the polytheists, and that was difficult for them. "But when fighting was prescribed for them", meaning: when the fighting that they had asked to be prescribed for them was prescribed [see the explanation of "kutiba" above 525, note 1, and the references there]; "behold, a faction of them", meaning: a group of them [see the explanation of "faction" above 2: 244, 245, 402 / 3: 549 / 6: 535]; "fear men", meaning: they fear that men will fight them; "as they fear Allah or with greater fear", or with greater dread [see the explanation of "khashya" above 1: 599, 560 / 2: 239, 243]. And they said, out of anxiety about the fighting that Allah had prescribed for them: "Why have You prescribed fighting for us?", why have You made fighting obligatory for us? Out of inclination to this world and preference for ease and comfort in it, [In the printed edition: "and preference for ease and guarding against what is disliked", and in the manuscript: "and guarding against what is disliked"; both are false and corrupt, and the correct reading is "and comfort", which is the softness of life. As for his saying "against the hardship of meeting the enemy", it is connected to his saying "and preference for ease ... against hardship ..."] against the hardship of meeting the enemy and the difficulty of warring and fighting them. "If only You had delayed us", that is, reporting about them, they said: why did You not delay us; "to a near term", meaning: until they die upon their beds and in their homes. [see the explanation of "term" above 5: 7 / 6: 43, 76].

* *

Scholars of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said, that this verse was revealed concerning it.

Mention of the reports on this, and the transmission from those who said it:

9951 - Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, saying: I heard my father say: al-Husayn ibn Waqid informed us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: that Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf and some companions of his came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, we were in honour while we were polytheists; when we believed, we became humiliated!" He said: "I have been commanded to pardon, so do not fight." When Allah moved him to Medina, He commanded fighting, and they held back. So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: "Have you not seen those who were told, 'Restrain your hands'", the verse. [The report 9951: "Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq" appeared under no. 1591, 2575, 2594. And his father "Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq ibn Dinar" appeared under no. 1909. In the printed edition it read "ibn al-Husayn ibn Shaqiq", which is an error. This report was narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 2: 307 with a difference in wording, and he said: "This is a sound hadith according to the condition of al-Bukhari, though they did not record it", and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. It was narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 9: 11, and Ibn Kathir in his tafsir 2: 514 narrated it through Ibn Abi Hatim; al-Suyuti took it out in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 184, attributing it to these and adding attribution to al-Nasa'i.]

9952 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrimah: "Have you not seen those who were told, 'Restrain your hands'", [from people]. "But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a faction of them", it was revealed concerning some people among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: Ibn Jurayj: And His saying, "They said, 'Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You had delayed us to a near term,'" he said: until we die a natural death; that is "the near term".

9953 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His saying: "Have you not seen those who were told, 'Restrain your hands and establish prayer'", and he recited until he reached: "to a near term." He said: Some people among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, while he was in Mecca before the Hijrah, were hasty about fighting, and they said to the Prophet of Allah ﷺ: "Let us make blades and fight the polytheists in Mecca with them!" The Prophet of Allah ﷺ forbade them from that, saying: "I have not been commanded to do that." When the Hijrah came and fighting was commanded, the people disliked it, and they did what you hear. Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: ﴿Say: The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, and you will not be wronged a whit.﴾

9954 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Have you not seen those who were told, 'Restrain your hands and establish prayer and give zakah'", he said: They were people who embraced Islam before fighting was prescribed for them, and there was nothing obligatory upon them except prayer and zakah, so they asked Allah to prescribe fighting for them. "But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a faction of them fear men as they fear Allah or with greater fear", the verse, to "to a near term [in the printed and manuscript editions: "the verse to to a near term", while the context requires the second "to"], which is death. Allah said: ﴿Say: The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah﴾.

* *

Others said: this and the verses after it were revealed concerning the Jews.

Mention of those who said that:

9955 - al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Have you not seen those who were told, 'Restrain your hands and establish prayer'", up to His saying: "you would have followed Satan, except a few", what lies between them concerns the Jews.

9956 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a faction of them", up to His saying: "Why have You prescribed fighting for us?", Allah, blessed and exalted, forbade this nation from doing as they did.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say: The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter is better for those who fear Allah, and you will not be wronged a whit (77)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "Say: The enjoyment of this world is little", say, O Muhammad, to these people who said, "Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? If only You had delayed us to a near term": your life in this world and your enjoyment of it is little, because it is perishing, and whatever is in it perishes [see the explanation of "enjoyment" above 1: 539, 540 / 3: 55 / 5: 262 / 6: 258]; "and the Hereafter is better", meaning: and the bliss of the Hereafter is better, because it is lasting and its bliss is lasting and everlasting. It was said, "and the Hereafter is better", and the meaning of the speech is what I described, that its bliss is intended, by the indication of the mention of "the Hereafter" with what was mentioned, on the meaning intended from it; "for those who fear Allah", meaning: for those who fear Allah by performing His obligations and avoiding His disobedience, obeying Him in all of that; "and you will not be wronged a whit", meaning: Allah will not diminish from the rewards of your deeds a whit.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "fatil" earlier, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary [see what preceded: 456 - 460].

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you were in towers built up high﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, is meant: wherever you may be, death will reach you and you will die. "Even if you were in towers built up high", that is: do not be anxious about death, and do not flee from fighting, and do not weaken in meeting your enemy out of fear for yourselves of killing and death, for death is before you wherever you are, and it will reach your souls wherever you are, even if you fortified yourselves against it with impregnable fortresses.

* *

The interpreters differed regarding the meaning of His saying: "even if you were in towers built up high."

Some of them said: it means: fortified palaces.

Mention of those who said that:

9957 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "even if you were in towers built up high", he says: in fortified palaces.

9958 - Ali ibn Sahl narrated to me, saying: Mu'ammal ibn Isma'il narrated to us, saying: Abu Hammam narrated to us, saying: Kathir Abu al-Fadl narrated to us, from Mujahid, who said: Among those who were before you there was a woman, and she had a hired servant, and she gave birth to a girl. She said to her hired servant: "Kindle a fire for us." He went out and found a man at the door, and the man said to him: "What did this woman give birth to?" He said: "A girl." He said: "Indeed this girl will not die until she fornicates with a hundred men, and her hired servant will marry her, and her death will be by a spider." He said: The servant said to himself: "Then I want her, after she has fornicated with a hundred!" So he took a blade, went in, and split the girl's belly. She was treated and recovered, grew up, and she was prostituting herself. She came to a shore of the seashores and stayed there prostituting. The man stayed as long as Allah willed, then came to that shore with much wealth, and said to a woman of the shore's people: "Find me a woman, the most beautiful woman in the village, that I may marry her!" She said: "Here is a woman among the most beautiful of people, but she prostitutes herself." He said: "Bring her to me." She went to her and said: "A man has come who has much wealth, and he said to me such-and-such." I said to him such-and-such. She said: "I have given up prostitution, but if he wants to marry her, I will marry him!" He said: So he married her, and she made an impression on him. One day while he was with her, he told her his story. She said: "I am that girl!" and she showed him the scar on her belly. "And I used to prostitute myself, and I do not know whether it was a hundred or fewer or more!" He said: "He told me that her death would be by a spider." He said: So he built her a tower in the desert and fortified it. One day while they were in that tower, a spider appeared on the ceiling. She said: "This will kill me? No one kills me but me!" She moved it and it fell; she went to it and placed the big toe of her foot upon it and crushed it, and its poison spread between her nail and the flesh, and her foot turned black, and she died. Then this verse was revealed: "Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you were in towers built up high." [The report 9958: "Kathir Abu al-Fadl" is Kathir ibn Yasar al-Tufawi, Abu al-Fadl al-Basri. He narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri, Thabit al-Bunani and others. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. This report was taken out by Ibn Kathir in his tafsir 2: 515 from the tafsir of Ibn Abi Hatim, and al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 184, attributing it also to Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu Nu'aym in al-Hilya. In the printed edition: "bi-l-'ankabut", and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]

9959 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "even if you were in towers built up high", he said: fortified palaces.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: palaces specifically in the sky.

Mention of those who said that:

9960 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you were in towers built up high", and they are white palaces built in the lowest heaven.

9961 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far informed us, from al-Rabi' regarding His saying: "Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you were in towers built up high", he says: even if you were in palaces in the sky. [The report 9961: "Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'd ibn Ammar ibn Sa'd al-Qaraz", appeared under no. 2929, and this same chain appeared earlier under no. 2919. In the manuscript and printed edition here it read "Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'id", as in no. 2929, but it will come correctly in the manuscript and printed edition shortly after as nos. 9962, 9972.]

* *

Scholars of Arabic differed regarding the meaning of "mushayyada".

Some Basran scholars said: "mushayyada" means lofty. He said: As for "mashid" with light stress, it means decorated.

* *

Another of them said something similar, except that he said: "al-mashid" with light stress means that which is worked with plaster, and "al-shayd" is gypsum.

* *

Some Kufan scholars said: "al-mashid" and "al-mushayyad" have one root; only that what is doubled is doubled for its own sake, and the verb in it is in plural, like their saying: "these are dyed garments" and "a flock of slaughtered sheep", so it is doubled, because it is a plural in which the action is distributed. Likewise, "palaces built up high", because palaces are many and building is distributed among them, and for this reason it was said: "towers built up high", and from it His saying: "and the doors were locked", and as one says: "he broke the stick", meaning he made it into pieces, piece after piece. The light form is also permitted in that; when it is singular, and the action is distributed in it and recurs much in a plural of it, doubling and light form are permitted by them, and one says: "this is a torn garment" and "a cut hide", because the action recurs in it through cutting and tearing. But if the action does not recur in it and is not distributed, they permit only the light form, like their saying: "I saw a slaughtered ram", and they do not permit "madhbahan" with doubling, because slaughter is not distributed in it as tearing is distributed in a garment.

* *

They said: For this reason it was said "qasr mashid", because it is singular, and it was placed in the position of their saying "slaughtered ram". They said: It is permissible for a palace to be said "mushayyad" with doubling, because building and plastering recur in it, and that is not permissible in "slaughtered ram", for the reason we mentioned. [This is the view of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 277.]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And if good befalls them, they say, "This is from Allah," and if evil befalls them, they say, "This is from you."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is His praise, "And if good befalls them, they say, 'This is from Allah,'" meaning: if ease, victory and triumph reach them and they gain booty [[See the explanation of "al-iṣābah" (striking/befalling) above: 514, 538.

And see the explanation of "al-ḥasanah" (good) above 4: 203-206.]] — "they say, 'This is from Allah'," meaning: from the side of Allah and by His decree [[See the explanation of "ʿind" (from/with) above: 2: 500 / 7: 490, 495.]] — "And if evil befalls them," meaning: if hardship of livelihood, defeat at the hands of an enemy, wounds and pain reach them [[See the explanation of "sayyi'ah" (evil) above: 2: 281, 282 / 7: 482, 490 / 8: 254.]] — "they say to you, O Muhammad: 'This is from you'," meaning: because of your faulty planning.

This is only a report from Allah, exalted is His mention, concerning those about whom He said to His Prophet: ﴿Have you not seen those who were told, "Restrain your hands"?﴾

And the people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said about this.

Those who said so:

9962 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Saʿd and Ibn Abi Jaʿfar related to us, both saying: Abu Jaʿfar related to us, from al-Rabiʿ, from Abu al-ʿAliyah, regarding His saying: "And if good befalls them, they say, 'This is from Allah,' and if evil befalls them, they say, 'This is from you'," he said: This is in ease and in adversity. [[The report: 9962 – see the comment on the previous report, no. 9961.]]

9963 - al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ, from Abu al-ʿAliyah, the same.

9964 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "And if good befalls them, they say, 'This is from Allah,' and if evil befalls them, they say, 'This is from you'," then he recited until he reached: "And We have sent you to mankind as a messenger," and said: These verses were revealed concerning the matter of war. Then he recited ﴿O you who have believed, take your precaution and go forth in small groups or go forth all together﴾, then he recited until he reached: "And if evil befalls them," they say: "This is from Muhammad, peace be upon him; he has erred in planning and erred in judgment! Neither is his planning good nor his judgment."

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Say, "All is from Allah."﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is His praise, "Say, all is from Allah," meaning: Say, O Muhammad, to these speakers who say, when good befalls them, "This is from Allah," and when evil befalls them, "This is from you": all of that is from Allah, apart from me and apart from others. From Him is ease and hardship, from Him is victory and triumph, and from Him is defeat and rout [[In the printed edition: "al-qatl wal-hazimah" (killing and defeat); in the manuscript: "al-ʿal wal-hazimah," unpointed. I judge the correct reading to be "al-fal," from the saying "falla al-qawm yafullahum falan": he defeated them and broke them.]], as:

9965 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzaq related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah: "Say, all is from Allah": the blessings and the calamities.

9966 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "All is from Allah": victory and defeat.

9967 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: ʿAbd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Muʿawiyah ibn Salih related to me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: "Say, all is from Allah. So what is the matter with these people that they hardly understand any statement?" He said: The good and the evil are from Allah. As for the good, He bestowed it upon you, and as for the evil, He tested you with it.

* *

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So what is the matter with these people that they hardly understand any statement? (78)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, exalted is His praise, "So what is the matter with these people," [[Al-Farra' said in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 278: "(Fa-mal), it has become so common in speech that they assumed the lam is attached to 'ma', and that it is a particle in some of its usage."]] what is the condition of these people who, if good befalls them, say, "This is from Allah," and if evil befalls them, say, "This is from you," "they hardly understand any statement," meaning: they hardly know the reality of what you tell them, that whatever befalls them of good or evil, harm or hardship, ease or prosperity, is from Allah, and none other than Him is able to do that. No one is struck by evil except by His decree, and no one attains ease and blessing except by His will.

This is an announcement from Allah to His servants that the keys of all things are in His hand, and none other than Him possesses any of them.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, "Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself," He means: whatever comfort, blessing, well-being and safety befalls you, O Muhammad, is from the bounty of Allah, which He bestows upon you as a kindness from Him to you. As for His words, "and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself," He means: whatever hardship, difficulty, harm and adversity befalls you, "is from yourself," meaning: because of a sin that you deserved it for, which your self has committed [[See the explanation of "good" (hasanah) above: 555, note 2, and the references there.

And see the explanation of "evil" (sayyi'ah) above: 555, note 4, and the references there.]] as:

9968 - Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself": as for "from yourself," he said: from your sin.

9969 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding "Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself": a punishment, O son of Adam, for your sin. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet ﷺ used to say: No man is struck by a scratch from a stick, nor a stumble of the foot, nor a twitch of a vein, except because of a sin, and what Allah pardons is more.

9970 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself," he said: "good" is what Allah granted him on the day of Badr, and the spoils and victory he obtained; and "evil" is what befell him on the day of Uhud, when his face was wounded and his front tooth was broken.

9971 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, regarding "Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself," he said: because of your sin. Then he said: All is from Allah, the blessings and the calamities.

9972 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Sa'd and Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, both saying: Abu Ja'far narrated to us, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah regarding His words: "Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself," he said: This applies to good deeds and evil deeds. [[See the commentary on the two preceding reports: 9961, 9962.]]

9973 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-Aliyah, the same.

9974 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding "and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself," he said: a punishment for your sin.

9975 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: "Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself," because of your sin, as He said to the people of Uhud: ﴿Why, when a disaster struck you, although you had struck [the enemy with] twice as much, did you say, "From where is this?" Say, "It is from yourselves."﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 165], because of your sins.

9977 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih regarding His words: "Whatever good befalls you is from Allah, and whatever evil befalls you is from yourself," and I am the One who decreed it for you.

9978 - Musa ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Masruqi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Bishr narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid narrated to me, from Abu Salih, with the like of it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: If someone says: What is the purpose of the particle "min" (from) in His words "Whatever good befalls you" and "from evil"?

* *

It is said: The grammarians differed on this.

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: "min" was introduced because "min" is good after a negation, as in: "No one from anyone came to me." He said: and the entry of the predicate with the "fa" (then) is because "ma" (whatever) holds the position of "man" (whoever). [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "and the entry of the predicate with the fa being obligatory, in the position of min," which is a statement with no meaning at all; the correct reading is what I have set down, and by the entry of the fa into the predicate he means His words "fa-min Allah" and "fa-min nafsika."]]

* *

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: "min" was introduced with "ma" just as it enters with "in" in the conditional, because both are conditional particles. Likewise it enters with "man" when it is conditional; the Arabs say: "Whoever visits you from anyone, you honor him," just as they say: "If anyone visits you, you honor him." He said: They introduced it with "ma" and "man" so that its entry with them would show that they are conditional. They said: When it enters with them it is not omitted, because if it were omitted the verb would govern two things, since "ma" in His words "whatever evil befalls you" is the subject of "befalls you" [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "whatever good befalls you," but the context requires mentioning the other, as I have set it down.]]; if "min" were omitted, "befalls you" would govern "evil" as its object, since its meaning would be: if evil befalls you. So "min" could not be omitted for this reason, because a verb in the form "fa'ala" or "yaf'alu" does not govern two things. [["fa'ala" or "yaf'alu" means the past and the present tense.] It was permissible with "man," because it resembles the prepositions, [["the prepositions" (al-sifat), meaning the particles of jarr, as mentioned many times before; refer to the glossary of terms.]] and it occupies the position of a noun. As for "in," "min" enters with it and leaves it, but it does not leave with "ayyin," because that is inflected and its inflection becomes manifest in it; and it entered with "ma" because the inflection does not appear in it.

* *

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿And We have sent you to mankind as a messenger, and sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾ (79)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, "And We have sent you to mankind as a messenger," He means: We have made you, O Muhammad, only a messenger between Us and the creation, conveying to them what We have sent you with of message, and there is nothing upon you but delivery and the discharge of the message to those to whom you were sent. If they accept what you were sent with, it is for their own benefit, and if they reject it, the loss is theirs. "And sufficient is Allah" as a witness over you and over them, "as a witness," meaning: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, is sufficient for you as a witness to your delivery of what He commanded you to deliver of His message and revelation, and over those to whom you were sent in their acceptance from you of what you were sent with to them. Nothing of your affair or theirs is hidden from Him; He will reward you for your delivery what He promised you, and He will reward them for the good or evil they did, as recompense to the doer of good for his goodness and to the doer of evil for his evil.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed Allah, and whoever turns away — We have not sent you as a guardian over them﴾ (80)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is a warning (i'dhar) from Allah to His creatures concerning His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, says to them: Whoever among you, O people, obeys Muhammad, has indeed obeyed Me by obeying him. So listen to his words and obey his command, for whatever he commands you to do is commanded by My command, and whatever he forbids you from is forbidden by My prohibition. Let none of you say: "Muhammad is only a human being like us, who wants to make himself superior over us!"

* *

Then He, may His praise be exalted, said to His Prophet: And whoever turns away from your obedience, O Muhammad, and turns his back on you [see the explanation of "tawalla" above, vol. 7, p. 326, note 3, and the references there], then We have not sent you over them as a "ḥafīẓ," meaning: a guardian of what they do and a reckoner. Rather, We have sent you only to make clear to them what has been sent down to them, and We suffice as Guardian of their deeds, and as Reckoner of them concerning them.

* *

This verse was revealed, as has been reported, before he was commanded to fight (jihad), as in the following report:

9979 — Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I asked Ibn Zayd about the words of Allah, "Then We have not sent you over them as a guardian." He said: "This was the first thing He sent him with." He said: "Then after this came His command to fight them and to be harsh with them until they submit." He recited: ﴿Your only duty is to convey (the message)﴾ [Surah ash-Shura: 48].

The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿They say, "Obedience." But when they leave your presence, a faction of them plots by night other than what you say. And Allah records what they plot by night.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "They say, 'Obedience'" — may His mention be exalted — He means the group whom Allah informed about, that when fighting was prescribed for them, they feared people as they would fear Allah or with a greater fear. They would say to the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), when he commanded them with a matter: "Your command is obedience, and from us is obedience in what you command us and forbid us." "And when they leave your presence" — he says: when they go out from you, O Muhammad [[See the explanation of "baraza" previously: 5: 354 / 7: 324.]] — "a faction of them plots by night other than what you say." By this, may His mention be exalted, He means: a group of them changed by night what you say to them.

Every deed done at night is "bayyata" (plotted by night). Among this is "bayyata" the enemy, which means to attack them by night. From this is the saying of 'Ubayda ibn Hammam:

[['Ubayda ibn Hammam, brother of the Banu al-'Adawiyya, of the Banu Malik ibn Hanzala, of the Banu Tamim. The publisher of Abu 'Ubayda's Majaz al-Qur'an supposed him to be "'Ubayda ibn Hammam al-Taghlabi", but no, that is Islamic, and this is pre-Islamic! I have deduced from the lineage of "Ya'la ibn Umayya" in Jamharat al-Ansab: 217, and elsewhere, that he is "'Ubayda ibn Hammam ibn al-Harith ibn Bakr ibn Zayd ibn Malik ibn Hanzala ibn Malik ibn Zayd Manat ibn Tamim. The report of this poetry indicates that he is pre-Islamic, for al-Jahiz mentioned in al-Hayawan 4: 376 the report of these verses, in a report about al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir and his faults, namely that his brother al-Mundhir ibn al-Mundhir proposed to 'Ubayda ibn Hammam, and he rejected him in the most abhorrent way, and he mentioned the verses.]]

They came to me, and I was not pleased with what they plotted, ... and they had come to me with a disgraceful thing.

[[Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda 1: 133; al-Hayawan 4: 376; al-Kamil 2: 35, 106; al-Azmina wa al-Amkina by al-Marzuqi 1: 263; Diwan al-Aswad ibn Ya'fur al-Nahshali, A'sha Banu Nahshal, in Diwan al-A'shayn: 298; al-Lisan (nakar). Another narration reads: "faqad taraquni bi-shay'".

"Taraquni": came to me at night. "Nukr" with two vowels, like "nukr" with a vowel and sukun: the disgraceful matter that you disapprove of. The verse is completed by the next one.]]

To marry their unmarried woman to Mundhir, ... and does a free man marry a slave to a free woman?!

[["Al-ayyim" among women is one who has no husband, whether virgin or previously married. "Rajul ayyim" is a man with no wife. "Mundhir" means al-Mundhir ibn al-Mundhir, brother of al-Nu'man ibn al-Mundhir. His saying "does a free man marry a slave to a free woman" means: does a free man, whose mother was a free woman, marry a slave from the slaves? That is a veiled insult to al-Mundhir and his brother al-Nu'man, who made his wife a wet-nurse for one of the sons of Kisra, and Kisra called him "slave". His saying "hurr li-hurr" means: a free man whose mother was a free woman, as you say, "he is noble to nobles, and free to free"; the lam here is for ascription, as if he said: noble, ascribed to noble fathers, and free, ascribed to free fathers. This that I have said you will not find in a book, so memorize it.

In the manuscript it was: "li-ankiha ilayhim Mundhiran", which is very corrupt as you see; and in it also: "hurr bi-hurr", and the correct reading is what I have set down.]]

By His words "I was not pleased with what they plotted" at night, he means: what they resolved upon and determined at night,

And from this is the saying of al-Namir ibn Tawlab al-'Uklî:

She rose to blame me at night, listen! ... Foolishly, blame keeps you awake, so sleep.

[[Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda 1: 133; al-Khizana 1: 153; al-'Ayni (in the margin of al-Khizana) 2: 536; Sharh Shawahid al-Mughni: 161; and others. In the printed edition it was "bi-layl isma'", which is an error, and similarly in the manuscript "bi-layl isma'", but I adopt the narration of Abu 'Ubayda, for it is the best of the narrations.

His saying "isma'" is the speech of his wife or his mother, who used to blame him for generosity and liberality, meaning that she would repeatedly say "listen, and listen to me". His saying "saf-han" means falsely and lightness of mind. His saying "tubayyitka al-malama" is not in the sense intended by al-Tabari, though the commentators have explained it so. To me it is from the saying "bata al-rajul" when he stayed awake, as in "bitt uraqi'u al-nujum", meaning I stayed up looking at them. So His saying "tubayyitka al-malama" means: my blame and reproach keep you awake; he says: this wearying vigil of yours is folly, so sleep and rest, for it is more restful for you!

Thus Abu 'Ubayda's citation of this verse, and al-Tabari after him, is not in its proper place, though the matter is close to one another.]] Allah, may His mention be exalted, says: "And Allah records what they plot by night", by which, may His mention be exalted, He means: and Allah records what they change of your words by night in the books of deeds that His guardian angels write.

* *

Those who expounded the interpretation said things similar to what we have said.

Mention of those who said that:

9980 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, he said: Yazid narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada regarding His words: "They say, 'Obedience,' but when they leave your presence, a faction of them plots by night other than what you say," he said: they change what the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) enjoined.

9981 - Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bazi' narrated to me, he said: Yusuf ibn Khalid narrated to us, he said: Nafi' ibn Malik narrated to us, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "a faction of them plots by night other than what you say," he said: those changed what the Prophet (ﷺ) said.

9982 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to me, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "They say, 'Obedience,' but when they leave your presence, a faction of them plots by night other than what you say," he said: those changed what the Prophet (ﷺ) said.

9983 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, he said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "They say, 'Obedience,' but when they leave your presence, a faction of them plots by night other than what you say, and Allah records what they plot by night," he said: These are the hypocrites who, when they attend the Prophet (ﷺ) and he commands them with a matter, say "Obedience," but when they leave his presence, a faction of them changes what the Prophet (ﷺ) says. "And Allah records what they plot by night," that is: what they say.

9984 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, he said: al-Husayn narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, he said: Ibn 'Abbas said regarding His words: "They say, 'Obedience,' but when they leave your presence, a faction of them plots by night other than what you say," he said: they change what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said.

9985 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, he said: my paternal uncle narrated to me, he said: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "They say, 'Obedience,' but when they leave your presence, a faction of them plots by night other than what you say," and they were people who used to say in the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "We believe in Allah and His Messenger," so that they would be safe for their blood and their wealth. And when they left the presence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), [[In the printed edition: "fa-idha barazu" with fa', and I adopt what is in the manuscript.]] they turned to what was other than what they had said in his presence, so Allah rebuked them, saying: "a faction of them plots by night other than what you say," that is: they change what the Prophet (ﷺ) said.

9986 - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, he said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, he said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: "a faction of them plots by night other than what you say," they are the people of hypocrisy.

* *

As for the nominative case of "ta'a" (obedience), it is by an omitted element indicated by the apparent sense of the speech, namely: your command is obedience, or: from us is obedience. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 378.]] As for His words "bayyata ta'ifa", the "ta'" of "bayyata" is vocalized with a fatha by the majority of the reciters of Madina, Iraq and the rest of the reciters, because it is the lam of "fa''ala".

* *

Some of the reciters of Iraq would vocalize it with sukun, then assimilate it into the "ta'", because they are close in place of articulation. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 379.]]

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in this is to leave off assimilation, because the two letters, "ta'" and "ta'" (the "ta'" and the "ta'") are from two different letters. When that is so, leaving off assimilation is the more eloquent of the two dialects among the Arabs, and the other dialect is permissible — I mean assimilation in this — and it is transmitted.

* *

The Interpretation of His Words: ﴿So turn away from them, and rely upon Allah, and Allah suffices as a Guardian﴾

Abu Ja'far said: Allah, may His mention be exalted, says to Muhammad (ﷺ): "So turn away", O Muhammad, from these hypocrites who say to you concerning what you command them: "Your command is obedience," [[See the explanation of "i'rad" previously: 2: 298, 299 / 6: 291 / 8: 88.]] but when they leave your presence, they oppose what you commanded them and change it to what you forbade them, so leave them and what they are upon of misguidance, and be content with Me as an avenger against them. "And rely", you, O Muhammad, "upon Allah", he says: and entrust your affair to Allah, trust in Him in your affairs, and place them with Him [[See the explanation of "tawakkul" previously: 7: 346.]]. "And Allah suffices as a Guardian", he says: and Allah suffices you, that is: sufficient for you is Allah, "as a Guardian", that is: in what He commands you, and a protector of it, and a defender of you and a helper. [[See the explanation of "wakil" previously: 7: 405.]]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an? Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy.﴾ (4:82)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, "Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?" — He, may His praise be exalted, means: Will those who plot by night, other than what you tell them, O Muhammad, of the Book of Allah, not reflect, so that they would know the proof of Allah against them in obeying you and following your command, and that what you have brought them of the revelation is from their Lord, because of the consistency of its meanings, the harmony of its rulings, and the way some of it confirms other parts through affirmation, and some of it bears witness to other parts through verification? For if it were from other than Allah, its rulings would differ, its meanings would contradict one another, and some of it would reveal the corruption of other parts, as:

9987 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying, "Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an? Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy": That is, the word of Allah does not differ; it is truth with no falsehood in it, whereas the word of people differs.

9988 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: The Qur'an does not contradict its own parts, nor does it invalidate one part by another. Whatever matter people fail to understand, it is only from the shortcoming of their intellects and their ignorance! And he recited: "Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much discrepancy." He said: It is therefore incumbent upon the believer to say, "All of it is from Allah," and to believe in the ambiguous (mutashabih) verses, and not to strike one part of it against another. And when he is ignorant of a matter and does not know it, he should say, "What Allah has said is true," and recognize that Allah, exalted is He, has not spoken a statement and then nullified it; he should believe in the reality of what has come from Allah.

9989 – Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak regarding His saying, "Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?" He said: "Tadabbur" (reflection) is looking into it.

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And when there comes to them a report of security or fear, they spread it﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, "And when there comes to them a report of security or fear, they spread it," may His majesty be exalted, He means: when there comes to this concealing group (al-tabyit) something other than what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ says, "a report of security," the ha' and the mim in His saying "when there comes to them" refer to the concealing group. He, may His majesty be exalted, says: when there comes to them news of a detachment (sariyya) of the Muslims that went out to raid, that they are secure from their enemy because they have overcome them, "or fear," meaning: or that they are fearful of their enemy because their enemy has struck them, "they spread it," meaning: they spread it and broadcast it among the people before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and before the arrival of the detachments of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. [[In the printed edition: "before the commanders of the detachments of the Messenger of Allah," and in the manuscript: "before amana," and the mim was joined with a letter resembling the ra', so the word became confused. I have preferred the correct reading which I have adopted.]] The ha' in His saying "they spread it" refers to "the report." Its interpretation is: they spread the matter of security or fear that came to them.

* *

It is said of this: "So-and-so spread this news, and spread it (adha'ahu)." And from it is the saying of Abu al-Aswad:

He spread it among the people until it was as if
on a high place a fire had been kindled with a fanned flame.

[[His Diwan (in Nafa'is al-Makhtutat: 2): 44; al-Aghani 12: 305; Majaz al-Qur'an by Abu 'Ubayda 1: 133; al-Lisan (dha'a). These are verses that Abu al-Aswad al-Du'ali said when he proposed to a woman of 'Abd al-Qays called Asma' bint Ziyad. He confided her matter to a friend of his, and the friend told a cousin of hers who had also been proposing to her. Her cousin went to her family and asked them to prevent her from marrying him, and they did so and harmed her until she married her cousin. Abu al-Aswad said:

I trusted a man in secret who was not prudent,
but he was not suspicious in counsel.
He spread it among the people until it was as if
on a high place a fire had been kindled with a fanned flame.
And whenever you do not guard your secret, its calamities will mix
between the mistaken and the correct.
Not every counselor will give you his counsel,
and not everyone who gives counsel is wise.
But when both qualities are gathered in one person,
he deserves a share of obedience.

These are verses of Hassan, as you see. "Al-thuqub" is that with which the fire is kindled, i.e., they kindled it.]]

Ahl al-ta'wil (the people of interpretation) said in agreement with what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

9990 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurai' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: "And when there comes to them a report of security or fear, they spread it." He says: they hastened with it and spread it.

9991 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And when there comes to them a report of security or fear, they spread it." He says: when there comes to them a report that they are secure from their enemy, or that they are fearful of them, they spread the talk until their matter reaches their enemy.

9992 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: "And when there comes to them a report of security or fear, they spread it." He says: they spread it and ran with it (sa'aw bihi). [[In the printed edition: "they denounced it (shanna'u bihi)," and the correct reading is from the manuscript. "Sa'a bi-fulan ila al-wali" means he informed on him to the governor, and this is from its metaphorical usage: i.e., he carried the news until it reached the enemy, as if he had informed on the detachments to their enemy. See the next note, no. 4.]]

9993 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "And when there comes to them a report of security or fear, they spread it." He said: this is said regarding news: when a detachment of the Muslims went out to raid, the people would inquire among themselves (takhabbara al-nas baynahum), so they said: "The Muslims struck their enemy with such-and-such, and the enemy struck the Muslims with such-and-such," and they spread it among themselves, without the Prophet ﷺ being the one who informed them. [[In the printed edition: "He is the one who informs them of it," I do not know why it was changed from the manuscript.]] Ibn Jurayj said: Ibn 'Abbas said regarding His saying "they spread it": they made it public and spread it.

9994 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying "they spread it": he said: they published it. He said: those who spread it are a people: either hypocrites, or others who were weak. [[In the printed edition: "and others who were weak (da'ifa')," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

9995 – It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: they made it public and ran with it, [[In the printed edition: "they denounced it," as previously in p. 569 note 1.]] and they were the people of hypocrisy.

* *
