The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them, those who seek to draw it out would have known it from them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, "And if they had referred it," He means the matter that befell them from their enemy [and the Muslims] to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and to their men of authority [[The phrase "and the Muslims" is so in both the manuscript and the printed edition, and I did not know what it is, so I left it as it is and placed it between brackets, and I fear that something may have dropped from the text. By deleting what is between the brackets, the text is correct.]] — meaning: and to their commanders — and they had remained silent and not spread what had come to them of the news, until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, or those of authority among them, are the ones who handle the report about it, [[In both the printed edition and the manuscript: "are the ones who say the report about it," which is a sickly statement; its correct form is what I have adopted, and it is a copyist's error.]] after its soundness or falsity has been established for them, so that they confirm it if it is sound, or nullify it if it is false. "Those who seek to draw it out would have known it from them": meaning: the truth of that report which came to them would have been known by those who investigate it and extract it "from them," meaning: from the men of authority. The ha' and the mim in His saying "from them" refer to the men of authority; meaning: from the men of authority, whoever deduces it.

* *

Everything drawn out which was hidden from the sight of the eyes or from the knowledge of the hearts is called "mustanbat" (drawn out). It is said: "istanbatta al-rakiyya" (I drew out the well), when one draws out its water, and "nabatatha, anbituha" (I dug it). And al-nabat is water drawn out from the earth, and from it is the saying of the poet:

Near is its wetness; the enemy cannot reach
its water-source, proud of humiliation, frowning.

[[The Asma'iyyat: 103, with its takhrij there. His saying "near is its wetness" means his generosity and goodness. "Al-thara" is moist soil, as if he were fertile in his surroundings. His saying "the enemy cannot reach its nabat" means no enemy can approach its water, because of his might and protection: when he protects a land, his enemy fears his valour. "Proud of humiliation" does not remain in disgrace. "Qatub" means frowning at evil.]]

He means by "al-nabat" the drawn-out water.

* *

Ahl al-ta'wil said in agreement with what we have said on this.

Those who said so:

9996 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them," he says: if they had kept silent and referred the report to the Prophet ﷺ and to their men of authority until he himself spoke about it, "those who seek to draw it out would have known it," meaning: about the reports; they are the ones who investigate the reports.

9997 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them," he says: to their scholars — "those who seek to draw it out would have known it from them," those who examine it and are concerned by it. [[In the manuscript: "yufsihuna 'anhu" (they make it clear), which is a copyist's error, transposed.]]

9998 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "And if they had referred it to the Messenger," until he himself informs them; "and to those of authority among them," the understanding of religion and reason. [[In the printed edition: "awla al-fiqh" (those most entitled to understanding), adding "awla," but what is in the manuscript is also correct, in the manner of the early exegetes in abbreviation, as occurred thousands of times before.]]

9999 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliya: "And if they had referred it to the Messenger and to those of authority among them," knowledge; [[In the printed edition: "li-'alimahu" in place of "al-'ilm," and what is in the manuscript is correct, as in the previous note, and it is their manner of abbreviation, meaning "awli al-'ilm" (those of knowledge).]] "those who seek to draw it out from them," they follow it up and search it out.

10000 – Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: Layth informed us, from Mujahid: "Those who seek to draw it out would have known it from them," he said: those who ask about it and investigate it.

10001 – Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "yastanbitunahu" (they draw it out). He said: their saying: "What was it?" "What did you hear?"

10002 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

10003 – Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliya: "Those who seek to draw it out": he said: they investigate it.

10004 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "would have known it from them," meaning: those who investigate it from them would have known it.

10005 – It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: "yastanbitunahu minhum" (draw it out from them): he said: they follow it up.

10006 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "And when there comes to them a report of security or fear, they spread it," until "and to those of authority among them." He said: the rulers who govern them in war, who reflect and consider the news that came to them: is it true or false? If it is false they nullify it, or if it is true they confirm it. He said: this is in war, and he recited: "they spread it." And if they had done other than this: "And if they had referred it to God and to the Messenger and to those of authority among them," etc. [[In the printed edition: "who are in war against them," which did not read the manuscript well, so it changed and substituted.]]

* *

The interpretation of His saying, ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except a few﴾ (83)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: were it not for Allah's favour upon you, O believers, with His bounty, His guidance and His mercy, [[See the explanation of "al-fadl" (grace) above: p. 535, note 4, and the references there.]] by which He saved you from what He tested these hypocrites with — those who say to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he commands them with a command, "obedience," but when they leave his presence, a group of them plot (bayyata) other than what he said — you would have been like them, and you would have followed Satan, except a few, as those whose attribute He described followed him.

* *

By His saying, may His mention be exalted, "And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan," He addressed those whom He addressed by His saying, may His praise be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, take your precaution, then go forth in parties or go forth all together﴾ [Surah an-Nisa': 71].

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed about "the few" whom He excepted in this verse: who are they, and from which quality did He except them?

Some of them said: they are those who draw out from among the men of authority; He excepted them from His saying: "those who seek to draw it out would have known it from them," and He negated from them that they would know, by deduction, what others among those who deduce would know of the report that came to them concerning security or fear. [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 279. He means that the exception is from "deduction" (istinbat), not from "spreading" (idhā'a).]]

Those who said so:

10007 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, who said: it is only: "those who seek to draw it out would have known it from them" — except a few of them — "and were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan."

10008 – al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada regarding His saying: "And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except a few," he says: you would all have followed Satan. As for His saying, "except a few," it is like His saying: "those who seek to draw it out would have known it from them," except a few.

10009 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us by reading, from Sa'id, from Qatada: "And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except a few," he said: he says: you would all have followed Satan. As for "except a few," it is like His saying: "those who seek to draw it out would have known it from them, except a few."

10010 – al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, the like of it — meaning the like of Qatada's saying — and he said: they would have known it, except a few.

Others said: rather, they are the group whom Allah described as saying to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ "obedience," but when they leave his presence, they plot other than what they said. The meaning of the speech is: "And when there comes to them a report of security or fear, they spread it" — except a few of them.

Those who said so:

10011 – al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: "And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except a few," it is at the beginning of the verse concerning the report of the hypocrites. He said: "And when there comes to them a report of security or fear, they spread it." He means by "the few" the believers, [as in His saying, may He be exalted: "Praise be to Allah, who has sent down the Book to His servant and has not made in it any crookedness, but upright" [Surah al-Kahf: 1-2]. He says: praise be to Allah who sent down the Book, just and upright, and did not make in it crookedness. [[The report 10011: the text of this report in the printed edition reads: "And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan," and then the speech breaks off. As for His saying, "except a few," it is at the beginning of the verse, informing about the hypocrites. He says: "And when there comes to them a report of security or fear, they spread it" — except a few. He means by "the few" the believers, like the saying "praise be to Allah..." until the end of the report, and it is taken from al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 187. As for the manuscript, it is like what I have recorded, except that at its end it says: "He says: praise be to Allah who sent down the Book, just and upright..." to the end of the speech.

I have preferred that what is in the manuscript from the beginning of the speech is correct, and that the end of the report has dropped out its mention of the text of the verse from Surah al-Kahf, so I have recorded it between the two statements.

His saying: "it is at the beginning of the verse concerning the report of the hypocrites," means that it is referred back to the beginning of the verse concerning their report. Then he followed this by mentioning the verse of Surah al-Kahf, and explaining what it contains of anteriority and posteriority. It seems that what I have preferred is correct.]]

10012 – Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: this verse is anterior and posterior; it is only: "they spread it, except a few of them. And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, not a few nor many would have been saved."

* *

Others said: rather, it is an exception from His saying "you would have followed Satan." They said: those excepted are people who had not intended what the others intended of following Satan. So Allah made known to those whom He saved from that the position of His favour toward them, and He excepted the others, among whom there was not what there was among the others.

Those who said so:

10013 – It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim say regarding His saying: "And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except a few," he said: they are the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, who had spoken to themselves of matters among the affairs of Satan, except a group of them.

* *

Others said the meaning of that is: And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy, you would all have followed Satan.

They said: His words, "except a few" (إلا قليلا), are phrased as an exception (istithna', exception) in wording, but they indicate the totality and comprehensiveness, and that without God's favour and mercy toward them, none would have been saved from misguidance. So His words "except a few" are taken as evidence of comprehensiveness. [[See what he said about the meaning of "few" in what has preceded: 2:331 / 8:439, and what I wrote in the first volume: 554, note 1.]] They cited in support of this the words of al-Tirimmah ibn Hakim, in praise of Yazid ibn al-Muhallab:

*A noble man (ashamm), abundant in giving of gifts, (...) few in blemishes and damaging defects.* [[Diwan: 139. "Al-ashamm": a lord of pride and grandeur, from "al-shamm," which is a elevation in the bridge of the nose, with its top level and the tip slightly raised. It is a quality of generosity and noble descent. His words "yudi" (with the yā' vowelled with a ḍamma and the dāl with a kasra, and the yā' doubled), or (with the yā' vowelled with a fatḥa, the dāl with a kasra, and the yā' doubled), are the plural of "yad." The first is pluralized on the pattern "fu'ūl," like fals and fulūs, and the second on the pattern "fa'īl," like 'abd and 'abīd. It is as if he said: abundant in hands of giving. In his Diwan it appears as "yadi" with a fatḥa on the yā' and dāl, and this is an error. In the manuscript it appears as "bara al-nawadi," which is an error with no meaning. "Al-mathalib" is the plural of "mathlaba," which are wounding defects. "Al-qadiha" means defects that damage his origin and character; he called them "damaging" (qādiha), and the word refers to the worm that eats teeth or trees, and he used it as a collective noun.]]

They said: The apparent sense of this statement describes the one praised as having blemishes and defects, while it is known that its meaning is that he has no blemishes and no defects. For whoever describes a man as having defects, even if he describes the defects he has as few, he has only dispraised him and not praised him. Rather, it is as we have described, the negation of all defects from him. They said: Likewise His words, "You would have followed Satan, except a few," mean only: all of you would have followed Satan.

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The most correct of these opinions in this matter, in my view, is the saying of the one who said: the exception of "a few" refers to "spreading (the news)" (al-idha'a), and he said: the meaning of the speech is: "And when there comes to them a matter of security or fear, they spread it, except a few; and if they had referred it to the Messenger..."

* *

We only said that this is more correct, because the statement on this must be one of the opinions we have mentioned, and it is impossible that it refers to His words, "You would have followed Satan," because whoever God has favoured with His grace and mercy cannot possibly be among the followers of Satan.

* *

It is also impossible to carry the meanings of the Book of God to other than what is most prevalent and understood from the apparent sense of the address in the speech of the Arabs. We have a way of carrying it to what is most prevalent in Arabic speech, so we direct it to the meaning toward which those who spoke directed it, "meaning: you would have followed Satan all together," and then he claimed that His words "except a few" are evidence for the totality of all. This is in addition to its departure from the interpretation of the people of interpretation. [[In the printed edition: "...from the interpretation of the people of interpretation, has no basis," so this word added by the editor was removed, in order for the reading of the speech to be correct. See the preceding note.]]

* *

Likewise there is no basis for directing this toward an exception from His words, "those among them who would know it from them" (4:83), because the knowledge of that, when it is referred to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, and the Messenger of God ﷺ and those in authority among them explain it after its clarity to them, then all who derive its reality (yastanbitūnahu) share equally in the knowledge of it, so there is no basis for excepting some of those who derive it from them, and singling out some of them with its knowledge, while all of them are equal in knowing it.

Since there is no statement on this except what we have said, and the flaws we have explained have affected these three opinions, it is clear that the correct view on this is the fourth, which is the opinion for which we have adjudged correctness, namely the exception from "spreading." [[See the meanings of the Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 279, 280.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 84:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿So fight in the way of Allah; you are not tasked except with yourself. And urge the believers. Perhaps Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve; and Allah is greater in might and greater in punishment﴾ [4:84].

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be majestic: [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "He means by that, may His praise be majestic," and the context confirms what has been established.]] "So fight in the way of Allah; you are not tasked except with yourself," meaning: fight, O Muhammad, the enemies of Allah from among the people of association with Him, "in the way of Allah," meaning: in His religion which He has prescribed for you, which is Islam, and fight them in it with your own self. [[See the explanation of "the way of Allah" above, 8:3470, 5:546, note 1, and the references there.]]

* *

As for His words, "you are not tasked except with yourself," it means: Allah does not burden you, regarding what He has obligated upon you of striving against His enemy and your enemy, except with what He has assigned to you of that, rather than what He has assigned to others; that is, you are only held accountable for what you have earned, not for what others have earned, and upon you is only what you have been charged with, not what others have been charged with. [[See the explanation of "taklif" (legal obligation) above, 5:45.]]

* *

Then He said to him: "And urge the believers," meaning: urge them to fight those whom You have commanded you to fight alongside you, "Perhaps Allah will restrain the might of those who disbelieve," meaning: perhaps Allah will restrain the fighting of those who disbelieved in Allah, denied His oneness and rejected your prophethood, away from you and from them, and their harm. [[The sense of the sentence is "that He restrain ... away from you and from them," then "and their harm" is joined by conjunction to "the fighting of those who disbelieved in Allah."]]

* *

We have explained earlier that "perhaps" (ʿasā) from Allah is binding, which makes it unnecessary to repeat it in this place. [[I have not found this place which al-Tabari refers to, and I fear that nothing of that has passed before, and that he has erred.]]

"And Allah is greater in might and greater in punishment," means: and Allah is more effective in harming His enemies, from among the people of disbelief in Him, than they are against you, O Muhammad, and your companions; so do not shrink back from fighting them, for I am watching them with might, harm, punishment and retribution, to weaken their plotting, diminish their power, and raise the truth over them.

And "tankil" (exemplary punishment) is a verbal noun from the saying of the speaker: "I made an example of so-and-so (nakkaltu bi-fulan), so I make an example of him, tankīlan," when one causes him pain by punishment, [[See the explanation of "nakal" and "tankil" above, 2:176, 177.]] as:

10014 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words "and greater in punishment," that it means chastisement.

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share of it, and whoever intercedes for an evil cause will bear a portion of it﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His saying, may His majesty be exalted, "Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share of it," He means: whoever becomes an intercessor (*shaf'*), O Muhammad, for the sake of your companions, by interceding for them in fighting their enemy and combating them in the way of God. This is "the good intercession." ([[See the explanation of "intercession" (*shafa'a*) above, 2:31-32 / 5:382-384, 395.]]) "Will have a share of it" means: will have a portion (*nasib*), that is, a lot (*hazz*) ([[See the explanation of "share" (*nasib*) above, p. 472, note 2, and the references there.]]), of it, from the same intercession, of God's reward and His abundant honour.

"And whoever intercedes for an evil cause": that is, whoever intercedes for the army of those who disbelieve in God against the believers in Him, by fighting alongside them. This is "the evil intercession." "Will bear a portion of it" (*yakun lahu kifl minha*).

He means by "*kifl*" the share and portion of burden and sin. It is derived from the "*kifl*" of a camel or mount, which is a cloth, or an object prepared for the animal, resembling a saddle on a beast. From it one says: "So-and-so came *mukta-fil*," when he came upon a mount that had been prepared for him, as we have explained, for riding. ([[See Abu 'Ubayda's *Majaz al-Qur'an* 1:135.]])

* *

It has been said that by His saying, "Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share of it," the verse means people's intercession for one another. It is not objectionable that the verse was revealed concerning what we have mentioned, and then it was generalised to include every intercessor for good or evil.

* *

We have chosen what we have said on this matter because it fits the context of the verse, in which God commanded His Prophet ﷺ to urge the believers to fight. The promise was for whoever responded to the Messenger of God ﷺ, and the threat for whoever refused to respond. This is more appropriate than an exhortation to people's intercession for one another, which had not been mentioned before and is not mentioned after.

**Mention of those who said this concerning people's intercession for one another:**

10015 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, he said: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying, "Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share of it, and whoever intercedes for an evil cause": he said: It is the intercession of some people on behalf of others.

10016 - al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, he said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

10017 - It was related to me from Ibn Mahdi, from Hammad ibn Salama, from Humayd, from al-Hasan, who said: "Whoever is interceded for in a good cause, he has two rewards for it," because God says, "Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share of it," and He did not say "is interceded for." ([[The report: 10016 - in the printed edition it read: "he has its reward even if he does not intercede, because God says..." This is the text of *al-Durr al-Manthur* 2:187, and I have kept what is in the manuscript. It seems to be an alteration by al-Suyuti, which the editor of the first printed edition followed. The correct reading is what is in the manuscript, except that the first "yushaffa'" in al-Hasan's statement should be read with a doubled *fa'* in the passive voice. What al-Hasan means is: the one who intercedes for his brother, if his intercession is granted, has two rewards: a reward for the good he brought to his brother, and another reward equal to that of the one interceded with, for doing the good he did.]])

10018 - Ibn Waki' told us, he said: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from al-Hasan, who said: "Whoever intercedes for a good cause," its reward is recorded for him for as long as its benefit continues.

10019 - Yunus told us, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd was asked about God's saying, "Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share of it." He said: It is the righteous intercession, in which he interceded and acted upon it; it is between you and him, the two of them are partners in it. "And whoever intercedes for an evil cause will bear a portion of it": the two of them are partners in it, just as its people were partners.

**Mention of those who said that "*kifl*" means "share":**

10020 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh told us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying, "Whoever intercedes for a good cause will have a share of it," i.e., a lot of it. "And whoever intercedes for an evil cause will bear a portion of it": "*kifl*" is sin.

10021 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, concerning His saying, "will bear a portion of it." As for "*kifl*," it is the lot.

10022 - al-Muthanna told me, he said: Ishaq related to us, he said: 'Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', concerning "will bear a portion of it": he said: a lot of it, an evil lot.

10023 - Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: "*Kifl*" and "*nasib*" are the same. And he recited: ﴿He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾ [Surah al-Hadid: 28].

* *

**The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And God is ever Muqit over all things﴾ (85)**

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation (*ahl al-ta'wil*) differed concerning the interpretation of His saying, "And God is ever *muqit* over all things."

Some of them said its interpretation is: And God is ever Watchful and a Witness over all things.

**Mention of those who said this:**

10024 - al-Muthanna told me, he said: 'Abdullah ibn Salih related to us, he said: Mu'awiya told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And God is ever *muqit* over all things," he says: watchful.

10025 - al-Muthanna told me, he said: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, he said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "*muqit*": a witness.

10026 - Ibn Waki' told us, he said: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from a man named Mujahid, from Mujahid, the same.

10027 - al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "*muqit*": he said: a witness, a reckoner, a watcher.

10028 - Ahmad ibn 'Uthman ibn Hakim told me, he said: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Shurayk related to us, he said: My father related to us, from Khusayf, from Mujahid Abu al-Hajjaj: "And God is ever *muqit* over all things," he said: "*al-muqit*" is the reckoner.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: the one who sustains (*al-qa'im*) over everything by management.

**Mention of those who said this:**

10029 - al-Qasim told us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Kathir said: "And God is ever *muqit* over all things," he said: "*al-muqit*" is the one who is constant (*al-wasib*). ([[It is said: "*wasiba al-rajulu 'ala malihi yasibu*" (like *wa'ada ya'idu*) when he persists with it and takes good care of it.]])

Others said: He is the Capable (*al-qadir*).

**Mention of those who said this:**

10030 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, he said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "And God is ever *muqit* over all things," as for "*al-muqit*," it is the Capable.

10031 - Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying, "And God is ever *muqit* over all things," he said: over all things Capable; "*al-muqit*" is the Capable.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view among these sayings is the view of those who said the meaning of "*muqit*" is the Capable. This is because, as is reported, it is so in the dialect of Quraysh, and there is a verse recited for al-Zubayr ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib, paternal uncle of the Messenger of God ﷺ: ([[I did not find it for al-Zubayr; rather I found it for Abu Qays ibn Rifa'a, with the rhyme in its nominative form, in *Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara'* of Ibn Sallam, p. 243, and its sources there. It is attributed in *al-Durr al-Manthur* 2:187-188 to Uhayha ibn al-Julah al-Ansari.]])

*And one with rancour whom I restrained myself from,*
*and I was, against his ill-will, capable (muqitan).*

That is: capable. ([[*Lisan al-'Arab* (*q-w-t*); see *Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara'* pp. 242-243 and the note there.]])

It has been said that among this usage is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ:

10032 - "It is sufficient sin for a man to neglect those whom he feeds (*man yuqit*)." ([[The hadith: 10032 - narrated by Ahmad in his *Musnad*, from the hadith of 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, nos. 6495, 6819, 6828, 6842, and by al-Hakim in *al-Mustadrak* 1:415. It is a sound hadith, and its wording is "*yaqut*."]]

In the narration of one who narrated it as "*yuqit*," it means: the one under his hands and in his authority from his family and dependants, so that he provides their sustenance (*quwt*). One says from it: "*aqata* so-and-so the thing, *yaqtihi, iqatatan*," and "*qatahu, yaqutuhu, qiyatatan, wa-qutan*," and "*al-qut*" is the noun. As for "*al-muqit*" in the verse of the Jew, in which he says: ([[He is al-Samaw'al ibn 'Adiya, the Jew.]])

*Would that I knew, and I would know, when*
*they bring it forth, spread out, and I am called!*
*Is the excellence (al-fadl) mine, or upon me, when I am reckoned?*
*Indeed I am muqit over the reckoning.*

([[His *Diwan*, pp. 13-14; *al-Asma'iyyat*, p. 85; *Majaz al-Qur'an* of Abu 'Ubayda 1:135; *Tabaqat Fuhul al-Shu'ara'* of al-Jumahi, pp. 236-237; *Lisan al-'Arab* (*q-w-t*), and others. His words "would that I knew" mean: would that I knew what will happen. "And would I know" is a question, meaning: and will I indeed know. "They bring it forth" means: the pages of his deeds on the day when people stand before the Lord of the worlds. The verse has other variant readings.]]) By "al-fadl" he means goodness, good reward, and blessing from God. "Or upon me" means: or upon me the sin that deserves punishment.

= Its meaning is: I am dependent upon the reckoning, and this is from a meaning other than this one. ([[This meaning that Abu Ja'far stated is the view of Abu 'Ubayda, and it is the best that has been said about the meaning of "*muqit*" in this verse. See the objections of those who objected to the verse, and their disagreement over its interpretation, under the root (*q-w-t*) in *Lisan al-'Arab*.]])

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan) on Surah 4, verse 86:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And when you are greeted with a greeting, then greet with one better than it, or return it.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, "And when you are greeted with a greeting," He means: when blessing is invoked upon you with long life, endurance and safety. [[For the meaning of "tahiyyah" (greeting) is: endurance and safety from afflictions.]] "Then greet with one better than it, or return it" means: then invoke upon whoever invoked that for you a blessing better than what he invoked for you. "Or return it" means: or return the greeting.

* *

Then the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the form of the "greeting" that is better than the one with which the greeter greeted, and the one that is equal to it.

Some of them said: The better one is that the one greeted, when it is said, "As-salamu 'alaykum," responds, "Wa 'alaykum as-salam wa rahmat Allah," adding to the supplication of the one who supplicated for him. And the return is that he says, "As-salamu 'alaykum," the same as it, as it was said to him, [[In the manuscript, in place of the words "as it was said to him" stands "qala qila lahu" ("he said, it was said to him"), which I do not understand; the first editor's alteration is acceptable.]] or he says, "Wa 'alaykum as-salam," supplicating for the one who greeted him with the like of what he supplicated for him. [[In the printed edition: "fa-yad'u al-da'i lahu" ("so he invokes for the supplicant"), and the correct reading is from the manuscript, but the scribe was led into error, since he wrote "fa-yad'u" with an alif after the waw.]]

Mention of those who said that:

1003 3 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And when you are greeted with a greeting, then greet with one better than it, or return it." He says: If someone greets you, say: "Wa 'alayka as-salam wa rahmat Allah," or limit yourself to "As-salamu 'alayka," as he said to you.

1003 4 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata', regarding His words: "And when you are greeted with a greeting, then greet with one better than it, or return it." He said: It is concerning the people of Islam.

1003 5 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding what was read to him, from 'Ata', who said: It is concerning the people of Islam.

1003 6 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Shurayh that he would return "As-salamu 'alaykum" as he was greeted.

1003 7 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn and Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Ibrahim that he would return "As-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmat Allah."

1003 8 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from 'Atiyyah, from Ibn 'Umar: that he would return, "Wa 'alaykum."

* *

And others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: greet with one better than it the people of Islam, or return it to the people of disbelief.

Mention of those who said that:

1003 9 - Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn Habib ibn al-Shahid narrated to me, saying: Humayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Salih, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Whoever greets you from among God's creation, return it to him, even if he is a Magian, for God says: "And when you are greeted with a greeting, then greet with one better than it, or return it."

1004 0 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Salim ibn Nuh narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "And when you are greeted with a greeting, then greet with one better than it," for the Muslims, "or return it," to the People of the Book.

1004 1 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "And when you are greeted with a greeting, then greet with one better than it," for the Muslims, "or return it," to the People of the Book.

1004 2 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "And when you are greeted with a greeting, then greet with one better than it," meaning: greet with something better than it, i.e., to the Muslims, "or return it," i.e., to the People of the Book.

1004 3 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd, regarding His words: "And when you are greeted with a greeting, then greet with one better than it, or return it," said: My father said: It is incumbent upon every Muslim who is greeted with a greeting to greet with one better than it; and if someone other than the People of Islam greets him, he should return to him the like of what he said.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two interpretations of the verse is the saying of those who said that it refers to the people of Islam, and that its meaning is directed to the fact that one returns the greeting to a Muslim when he greets him with a greeting better than his or like it. This is because the sound reports from the Messenger of God ﷺ state that it is obligatory upon every Muslim to return the greeting of every disbeliever with something lesser than his greeting. God has commanded the return of the better and the equal in this verse, without distinguishing between the one who deserves the return of the better of his greeting and the one to whom the like is returned, by any indication through which the correctness of the saying of those who said, "By returning the better is meant the Muslim, and by returning the like is meant the people of disbelief," could be known.

And the correct view, since there is no indication in the verse of the soundness of that, nor any binding report from the Messenger ﷺ [[In the printed edition: "wa la bi-sihhatihi athar lazim" and in the manuscript: "wa la sihhat athar lazim"; both are not sound, so I preferred what I have written as closer to the context.]] — is that the choice in that lies with the one greeted: between returning the better or the equal, except in the case where a Sunnah from the Messenger of God ﷺ has specified some of that, in which case he is bound by it. The Sunnah has specified for the people of disbelief the prohibition of returning to them the better of their greeting or its equal, except by saying, "Wa 'alaykum," and no one should exceed what the Messenger of God ﷺ has set as a limit in that. As for the people of Islam, the one greeted among them has in returning the choice that God has granted him in that.

A report has also been transmitted from the Messenger of God ﷺ regarding the interpretation of this in a manner similar to what we have said. It is this:

1004 4 - Musa ibn Sahl al-Ramli narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Sarri al-Antaki narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Lahiq narrated to us, from 'Asim al-Ahwal, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, from Salman al-Farisi who said: A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "As-salamu 'alayka ya Rasul Allah." He said: "Wa 'alayka wa rahmat Allah." Then another came and said: "As-salamu 'alayka ya Rasul Allah wa rahmat Allah." So the Messenger of God said to him: "Wa 'alayka wa rahmat Allah wa barakatuh." Then another came and said: "As-salamu 'alayka ya Rasul Allah wa rahmat Allah wa barakatuh." He said to him: "Wa 'alayka." The man said to him: "O Prophet of God, may my father and mother be your ransom, so-and-so and so-and-so came to you and greeted you, and you returned more to them than you returned to me!" He said: "You did not leave anything for us; God said: 'And when you are greeted with a greeting, then greet with one better than it, or return it,' so we returned it to you."

[[Hadith 1004 4: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Sarri al-Mada'ini al-Antaki: weak, though he was a righteous man, as they said. Abu Nu'aym said: "He narrates the strange reports, worthless." Ibn Hibban said in the Kitab al-Du'afa': "He narrated from Abu 'Imran wonderful reports about which there is no doubt they are fabricated." Recorded in al-Tahdhib and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/78. But he was not alone in narrating this hadith from Hisham ibn Lahiq, as will come.

Hisham ibn Lahiq, Abu 'Uthman al-Mada'ini: disputed concerning him. Ahmad said: "He narrates from 'Asim al-Ahwal, and we wrote from him hadiths; there was no harm in him, but he raised to 'Asim hadiths that were not raised, attributing them to Salman." Shababah denounced a hadith of his. This is the summary of what is in his biography in al-Bukhari's al-Kabir 4/2/200-201, and Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/69-70. In Lisan al-Mizan it is said that al-Nasa'i strengthened him, and that Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy and among the weak. Ibn 'Adi said: "His hadiths are good, and I hope there is no harm in him." It appears from all this that the criticism of him does not rest on doubt about his truthfulness, but on a wahm (error) or mistake on his part; the apparent judgment is that his hadith is good.

Ibn Kathir mentioned the hadith in 2: 526-527, from this place in al-Tabari. Then he quoted from Ibn Abi Hatim that he narrated it as a mu'allaq (suspended) report through 'Abd Allah ibn al-Sarri al-Antaki, with this chain, similarly.

Then Ibn Kathir said: "Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh narrated it: 'Abd al-Baqi ibn Qani' narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Ahmad ibn Hanbal narrated to us, my father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Lahiq Abu 'Uthman narrated to us — and mentioned the like. And I have not seen it in the Musnad."

It is as Ibn Kathir said: it is not in the Musnad.

But al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 188, and that Ahmad narrated it "in al-Zuhd" (Kitab al-Zuhd). He also attributed it to Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani, and said it is "with a good chain."

Al-Haythami also mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 8: 33, and said: "Al-Tabarani narrated it, and in its chain is Hisham ibn Lahiq, whom al-Nasa'i strengthened, and Ahmad abandoned his hadith; the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih."

His statement that Ahmad abandoned Hisham's hadith is not sound, for the established statement from Ahmad recorded by al-Bukhari and Ibn Abi Hatim does not indicate that.]]

* *

If someone says: Is returning the greeting obligatory according to what God commanded in His Book?

It is said: Yes, and a group of the earlier scholars held that.

Mention of those who said that:

1004 5 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibn Jurayj who said: Abu al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: "I have not seen him but making it obligatory" — the verse: "And when you are greeted with a greeting, then greet with one better than it, or return it." [[I.e., he makes returning the greeting obligatory.]]

1004 6 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Sufyan, from a man, from al-Hasan who said: The greeting is a voluntary act (tatawwu'), and the return is an obligation (fard).

* *

Commentary on His words: ﴿Indeed, God is ever Reckoner over all things (86).﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Indeed God is, over everything of what you do, O people, of deeds, of obedience and disobedience, Guardian over you, until He recompenses you for them with His recompense, as:

1004 7 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: 'Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Hasiban," he said: Guardian (hafiz).

1004 8 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like.

* *

The root of "al-hasib" in this place, in my view, is "fa'il" from "al-hisab," which has the sense of enumeration (al-ihsa'). It is said from it: "Hasabtu fulanan 'ala kadha wa kadha" (I reckoned with so-and-so over such-and-such), and "fulan hasibuhu 'ala kadha" (so-and-so is his reckoner over such-and-such), and "huwa hasibuhu" (he is his reckoner), when he is the owner of his reckoning.

* *

Some of the Basran lexicographers claimed that the meaning of "al-hasib" in this place is "sufficient" (al-kafi). It is said from it: "ahsabani al-shay'u yuhsibuni ihsaban," meaning it sufficed me, from their saying: "hasbi kadha wa kadha" (my sufficiency is such-and-such). [[This is Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 135; see also what preceded at 7: 596-597.]]

This is an erroneous and mistaken statement. For it is not said of "ahsabani al-shay'" (the thing sufficed me), "ahsaba 'ala al-shay', fahuwa hasib 'alayhi" (he reckoned over the thing, so he is its reckoner); rather one says: "huwa hasbuhu wa hasibuhu" (he is his sufficiency and his reckoner) — and God says: "Indeed God is ever over all things Reckoner."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 87:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Allah, there is no deity except Him. He will surely gather you for the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt. And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, "Allah, there is no deity except Him; He will surely gather you," He, may His praise be exalted, means: the Worshipped One, to whom alone worship is fitting,[[See what was written about "al-ubudah" (worship/servitude) earlier: 6:271, footnote 1; 404, footnote 2/549, footnote 2/565, footnote 2.]] the One to whom belongs the worship of everything and the obedience of every obedient one.[[See the explanation of "there is no deity except Him" earlier: 6:149.]]

* *

As for His words, "He will surely gather you for the Day of Resurrection," He says: He will surely resurrect you after your deaths, and gather you all together to the place of reckoning, where people will be recompensed for their deeds, and where He will judge between those who obey Him and those who disobey Him, and between those who believe in Him and those who disbelieve.[[See the explanation of "al-qiyamah" (the Resurrection) earlier: 2:518.]] "About which there is no doubt" [[See the explanation of "about which there is no doubt" earlier: 1:228, 378; 6:221, 294, 295.]] means: there is no doubt in the reality of what I tell you of that and inform you of my report: that I will surely gather you for the Day of Resurrection after your deaths.[[In the printed edition: "i.e., I gather you," a misreading of the manuscript.]] "And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?" means by this: know the reality of what I inform you of, for I will surely gather you for the Day of Resurrection, for recompense, presentation, reckoning, reward and punishment, with certainty. So do not doubt its truth nor dispute its reality,[[In the printed edition: "in its haqiyah (reality)," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] for my word is the truth in which there is no falsehood, and my promise is the truth which admits no failure. "And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?" means: and what speaker is more truthful in statement than Allah? That is because the liar only lies to bring to himself some benefit through his lie, or to repel some harm from himself by it. Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, is the Creator of harm and benefit, so it is impossible that lying could come from Him, for nothing calls Him to bring a benefit to Himself or to repel a harm from Himself [a caller. No one is free of a caller calling him to bring a benefit to himself or to repel a harm from himself], other than Him, may His remembrance be exalted,[[I added what is between the brackets to the printed text, because it is the correct meaning of the sentence. Abu Ja'far put forward the first proof in the preceding clause, to explain the impossibility of lying for Allah, glory be to Him. He then followed this with an explanation of the meaning of the comparative form in His words, "And who is more truthful than Allah in statement," and showed that Allah, glory be to Him, has no equal in this.

In the printed edition, apart from what is between the brackets, the text was as I have given it, and it is an incoherent sentence. As for the manuscript, it contained the following: "because it does not call him to bring a benefit or repel a harm from his self; other than Him, may His remembrance be exalted, so it would be permissible that ..." which is a garbled sentence indicating that the copyist omitted part of Abu Ja'far's words. I made an effort to supply this addition which I have included, so that the sentence is made correct in a valid way. I also added "fa-qala" (so he said) between brackets, because the sentence needs it.]] so it would be permissible for Him to have an equal in the impossibility of lying from Him, [fa-qala]: "And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?" and in report.

This is part 1 of 2 of the commentary. Translating the passage as given.

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿So what is wrong with you that you have become two factions concerning the hypocrites, while Allah has reverted them [to disbelief] for what they earned?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "So what is wrong with you concerning the hypocrites, two factions," He means: what is your state, O believers, regarding the people of hypocrisy, being two opposing factions? [See the explanation of "fi'ah" (faction) earlier, 5:352, 353 / 6:230.] "And Allah has reverted them for what they earned" means: Allah has returned them to the rulings applying to the people of polytheism, regarding the permissibility of shedding their blood and taking their offspring captive.

* *

"Al-ircas" (ارتكاس, al-irkās) means returning, and from it is the verse of Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt:

"They were reverted into the fiery hot water of the Fire, for they were rebellious, and they spoke falsehood and lies."

[Diwan: 36. This verse does not appear in exactly this form in the Diwan; rather it occurs in a poem in a different meter, which is: "They were reverted into Jahannam, for they were stubborn, speaking falsehood and lies." I have not found it in Abu Ja'far's version anywhere else.]

It is said from it: "arkasahum" and "rakasahum."

* *

It has been mentioned that in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy it is: ﴿wa-Allahu rakasahum﴾, without the alif. [See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:281. Then see the explanation of "arkasahum" below, pp. 15, 16.]

* *

The people of interpretation differed about those concerning whom this verse was revealed.

Some of them said: It was revealed concerning the disagreement among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about those who lagged behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of Uhud and turned back to Madinah, saying to the Messenger of Allah, peace be upon him, and to his Companions: ﴿If we had known there would be fighting, we would have followed you﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 167].

Those who said this:

10049 - Al-Fadl ibn Ziyad al-Wasiti narrated to me, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, who said: I heard 'Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Ansari narrating from Zayd ibn Thabit: When the Prophet ﷺ went out to Uhud, a group of those who were with him turned back, and the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ became two factions regarding them: one faction said, "Let us kill them," and another said, "No." Then this verse was revealed: "So what is wrong with you concerning the hypocrites, two factions? And Allah has reverted them for what they earned. Do you want to guide those whom Allah has sent astray?" ... the verse. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then said: Indeed it is good (Taybah), and it expels its impurity as the fire expels the impurity of silver.

[Hadith 10049: Al-Fadl ibn Ziyad al-Wasiti: I do not know who he is. The only biography I found under this name is "al-Fadl ibn Ziyad al-Tassas al-Baghdadi," who is of this same class, so perhaps he is him. He is mentioned in al-Jarh 3/2/62, Tarikh Baghdad 12:360, and has an unedited entry in Lisan al-Mizan 4:441.
Abu Dawud: this is al-Tayalisi.
Al-Tabari narrated this hadith by three chains, whose takhrij will come at the end of them, God willing.]

10050 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from 'Abdullah ibn Yazid, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out, and he mentioned something similar.

[Hadith 10050: Abu Usamah is Hammad ibn Usamah.]

10051 - Zurayq ibn al-Sakht narrated to me, saying: Shababah narrated to us, from 'Adi ibn Thabit, from 'Abdullah ibn Yazid, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: They mentioned the hypocrites in the presence of the Prophet ﷺ, so one group said, "Let us kill them," and a group said, "We will not kill them." Then Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: "So what is wrong with you concerning the hypocrites, two factions," until the end of the verse.

[Hadith 10051: Zurayq (with the zay first) ibn al-Sakht, the teacher of al-Tabari: I have not found a biography or mention of him except in al-Mushtabah of al-Dhahabi, p. 222, where he says: "Zurayq ibn al-Sakht, from Ishaq al-Azraq. That is correct, and it is said with the ra' first."
Shababah is Ibn Sawwar; his biography passed at 37.
There must be a gap in the isnad between Shababah and 'Adi ibn Thabit, since Shababah ibn Sawwar died in 204, 205 or 206, as al-Bukhari affirmed in al-Saghir, p. 228, while 'Adi ibn Thabit died in 116; the gap between them is about 90 years. It is apparent that a link [from Shu'bah] has dropped out of the isnad here.
'Adi ibn Thabit al-Ansari: a known reliable narrator; the group narrated from him. He is the son of the daughter of 'Abdullah ibn Yazid, his teacher in this isnad.
'Abdullah ibn Yazid al-Khatmi (with the kha' pointed and the ta' unpointed, sukun): a known Companion who witnessed al-Hudaybiyah as a youth.
This hadith is narrated by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad 5:184, from Bahz, from Shu'bah, like the first, longer narration here: 10049.
Likewise al-Bukhari narrated it, 4:83, 7:275 and 8:193, by way of Shu'bah. Muslim narrated it, 1:389-390, also by way of Shu'bah, but he narrated only the final part: "Indeed it is good..."
Ibn Kathir mentioned it, 2:529, from the narration of the Musnad, then said: "Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it in the Sahihayn by way of Shu'bah."
Al-Suyuti mentioned it, 2:189-190, and attributed it also to al-Tayalisi, Ibn Abi Shaybah, 'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il.
It is not in the printed Musnad of al-Tayalisi, since that is incomplete, as is well known.]

Others said: Rather, it was revealed concerning a disagreement among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about a people who had come to Madinah from Makkah, displaying to the Muslims that they were Muslims, then returned to Makkah and displayed polytheism to them.

Those who said this:

10052 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "So what is wrong with you concerning the hypocrites, two factions," he said: They were people who went out from Makkah until they came to Madinah, claiming that they were emigrants, then afterwards apostatized. They asked the Prophet ﷺ permission to go to Makkah to bring their goods with which they traded. The believers differed about them: one speaker said, "They are hypocrites," and another said, "They are believers." Then Allah made their hypocrisy clear and commanded fighting them. They came with their goods wanting Madinah, and 'Ali ibn 'Uwaymir, or Hilal ibn 'Uwaymir al-Aslami, met them, and between him and the Prophet ﷺ there was an alliance, and he was the one whose chest was constricted at fighting the believers or fighting his own people; so he defended them by [saying] they were heading to Hilal, and between him and the Prophet ﷺ there was a covenant.

10053 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly, in a similar wording, except that he said: "So Allah made their hypocrisy clear and commanded fighting them, but they were not fought that day; they came with their goods wanting Hilal ibn 'Uwaymir al-Aslami, and between him and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ there was an alliance."

[Reports 10052, 10053: see the following report, 10071.]

* *

Others said: Rather, their disagreement concerned people of polytheism who had displayed Islam in Makkah and who used to aid the polytheists against the Muslims.

Those who said this:

10054 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, his saying: "So what is wrong with you concerning the hypocrites, two factions." That was because there were people in Makkah who had spoken the words of Islam and who used to back the polytheists. They went out of Makkah seeking some need of theirs, and said: "If we meet the companions of Muhammad, peace be upon him, there is no harm to us from them!" When the believers were informed that they had gone out of Makkah, one faction of the believers said: "Ride out against the wicked ones and kill them, for they are backing your enemy against you!" Another faction of the believers said: "Glory be to Allah" (or as they said), "Will you kill a people who have spoken the same words you have spoken? Because they did not emigrate and leave their homes, will you make their blood and wealth lawful on that account?" Thus they became two factions, while the Messenger, peace be upon him, did not forbid either of the two groups from anything. Then it was revealed: "So what is wrong with you concerning the hypocrites, two factions, and Allah has reverted them for what they earned? Do you want to guide those whom Allah has sent astray?" ... the verse.

10055 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, his saying: "So what is wrong with you concerning the hypocrites, two factions," the verse. It was mentioned to us that they were two men from Quraysh who were with the polytheists in Makkah, who had spoken Islam but had not emigrated to the Prophet ﷺ. Some of the Companions of the Prophet of Allah met them as they were coming toward Makkah. Some of them said: "Their blood and wealth are lawful!" and some said: "It is not lawful for you!" So they disputed about them, and Allah revealed concerning that: "So what is wrong with you concerning the hypocrites, two factions, and Allah has reverted them for what they earned," until His saying, "And if Allah had willed, He would have given them power over you, and they would have fought you."

10056 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar ibn Rashid, who said: It reached me that some people of Makkah wrote to the Prophet ﷺ that they had embraced Islam, but that was a lie from them. Then they met them, and the Muslims differed about them: one group said, "Their blood is lawful!" and another group said, "Their blood is forbidden!" So Allah revealed: "So what is wrong with you concerning the hypocrites, two factions, and Allah has reverted them for what they earned."

* *

10057 - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: "So what is wrong with you concerning the hypocrites, two factions": They were people who lagged behind the Prophet of Allah ﷺ, stayed in Makkah, and openly professed faith without emigrating. The Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ differed about them: some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ befriended them, and others disavowed their friendship, saying: "They stayed behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and did not emigrate!" So Allah named them hypocrites, absolved the believers of their friendship, and commanded them not to take them as allies until they emigrate.

* *

Others said: Rather, their disagreement concerned people in Madinah who wanted to leave it in hypocrisy.

Those who said this:

10058 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "So what is wrong with you concerning the hypocrites, two factions, and Allah has reverted them for what they earned," he said: Some of the hypocrites wanted to leave Madinah, and they said to the believers: "We have been afflicted with ailments in Madinah, and it has made us ill" [ "ittakhamnaha" is the form "ifta'ala" from "al-wakhm" (unhealthiness). It is said: "a land is wakhimah and wakhimah and bi'ah," not suitable for a person to dwell in, so he finds it unpleasant. "Istawkhama al-qawm al-madinah" means they found Madinah heavy and its air did not agree with their bodies. What the lexicons mention is the form "istawkhama" as "istaf'ala," transitive from "al-wakhm," and they did not mention "ittakhama" as "iftaʻala," though it is sound by Arabic analogy. This is its witness.] So perhaps we will go out to the high ground until we recover, then return, ["al-zahr" is what is thick and raised of the land, and "al-batn" is what is soft, level, thin and low. Similar is "zahir al-ard," so they called what is far from the town and raised in the desert "zahr al-baldah wa-zahiruha."] for we were people of the desert. They set out, and the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ differed about them: one group said, "They are enemies of Allah and hypocrites! We wish the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had permitted us to fight them!" Another group said: "No, they are our brothers whom Madinah has distressed, so they found it unhealthy," and they went out to the high ground to take the air, [ "yatanazzahun" means they distance themselves from the land they found unhealthy, until they recover. "Al-tanazzuh" is distancing from the rural areas and waters, where there is no water, no dew, and no gathering of people, which is the open desert, and it is healthier for the bodies.] and when they recovered they returned. Then Allah said: "So what is wrong with you concerning the hypocrites, two factions," meaning: what is the matter with you that you have become two factions regarding them, "and Allah has reverted them for what they earned."

* *

Others said: Rather, this verse was revealed concerning the disagreement among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarding the people of the slander (al-ifk).

Those who said this:

10059 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "So what is wrong with you concerning the hypocrites, two factions, and Allah has reverted them for what they earned," until His saying, "So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate in the way of Allah," he said: This is concerning the matter of Ibn Ubayy when he spoke about 'A'ishah what he spoke.

10060 - And Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: When this verse was revealed: "So what is wrong with you concerning the hypocrites, two factions," and he recited until His saying, "So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate in the way of Allah," Sa'd ibn Mu'adh said: "I disavow to Allah and to His Messenger from his faction!" meaning 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings is the view of the one who said: This verse was revealed concerning the disagreement among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about a people from Makkah who had apostatized from Islam after their acceptance of it.

We said this is more correct because the difference among the people of interpretation is only in two views: one is that they were people from Makkah, as we have mentioned the reports from them; the other is that they were people from Madinah.

And in the words of Allah, may He be remembered: "So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate," there is clear evidence that they were not from the people of Madinah, because emigration in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was to his abode and city from all the lands of disbelief. As for those among the hypocrites and polytheists who remained resident in Madinah, the obligation of emigration did not fall upon them, since their homeland and residence was in the abode of emigration.

* *

The grammarians differed about the case of His saying "fi'atayn" (two factions).

Some of them said: It is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (hal), as you say, "What is with you standing?", meaning: what is your state while standing. This is the view of some Basran grammarians.

* *

Some of the Kufan grammarians said: It is in the accusative governed by the verb implied in "ma lak" (what is with you). He said: It does not matter whether the accusative after "ma lak" is definite or indefinite. He said: It is permissible in speech to say, "Ma laka al-sa'ira ma'anā" (what is with you walking with us), because it is like the verb that takes an accusative with "kāna" and "azunnu" and what resembles them. He said: Wherever a verb "fa'ala" or "yaf'alu" can fit with the accusative, it is permissible to put the definite or indefinite in the accusative, as "kāna" and "azunnu" take the accusative, because they are defective in meaning, even if you think they are complete.

This view is more correct, because what is sought in the saying "ma laka qā'iman" (what is with you standing) is "standing," so it falls under the category of "kāna" and its sisters, and "azunnu" and its companions.

* *

The interpretation of His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿And Allah has reverted them for what they earned﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed about the meaning of His saying "And Allah has reverted them."

Some of them said: Its meaning is: He returned them, as we have said.

Those who said this:

10061 - Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And Allah has reverted them for what they earned," He returned them.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: And Allah made them fall (awqa'ahum).

Those who said this:

10062 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullah narrated to me, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And Allah has reverted them for what they earned," he says: He made them fall.

Others said: The meaning of that is: He misguided them and destroyed them.

Those who said this:

10063 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "And Allah has reverted them," he said: He destroyed them.

10064 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah: "And Allah has reverted them for what they earned," He destroyed them for what they did.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 88 (part 2 of 2):

10065 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And Allah has overturned them for what they earned" – he destroyed them.

* *

We have already given an explanation of the meaning of this earlier, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. [See what has passed, p. 7]

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Do you want to guide those whom Allah has sent astray? And whomever Allah sends astray, you will not find for him a way﴾ (88)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, "Do you want to guide those whom Allah has sent astray," may He be exalted in praise, He means: Do you want, O believers, to guide to Islam, so that they are granted success in affirming it and entering it, those whom Allah has sent astray from it? He means by this: those whom Allah has forsaken, so that He has not granted them success in affirming it? [See the meaning of "guidance" (hudan) and the meaning of "misguidance" (dalal) in the linguistic indices of the earlier volumes.]

This is an address from Allah, may He be remembered, to the group that defended these hypocrites whose description Allah has given in this verse. He, may He be exalted in praise, says to them: Do you seek the guidance of these people whom Allah has sent astray and forsaken, away from the truth and from following Islam, by your defending them against fighting those among the believers who wish to fight them? "And whomever Allah sends astray, you will not find for him a way" – meaning: and whomever He forsakes in regard to his religion and in following what He has commanded him, namely affirming Him and His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he brought from Him, and sends him astray from it, "then you will not find for him" – O Muhammad – "a way," meaning: you will not find for him a path by which you can guide him to attain what Allah has forsaken him from [1], nor a course through which he can reach the matter which He has deprived him of reaching.

[1] This addition between the brackets is required by the context. See the explanation of "the way" (sabil) in the linguistic indices of the earlier volumes.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 89:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿They wish that you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved, and then you would be equal. So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate in the way of Allah﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "They wish that you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved," He means: these hypocrites wished [[See the explanation of "wadd" (to wish, love) above: 2:470 / 5:542 / 8:371.]] — you who are among them, O believers, as two groups — that you would disbelieve, denying the oneness of your Lord and the truthfulness of your Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), "as they disbelieved," meaning: as they themselves denied that. "Then you would be equal," meaning: you would become disbelievers like them, and you and they would be equal in associating partners with Allah [[See the explanation of "sawa'" (equal) above: 1:256 / 2:495–497 / 6:483, 486, 487 / 7:118]]. "So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate in the way of Allah," meaning [[See the explanation of "wali" and "awliya'" above: 8:430, note 1, and the references there.]]: until they leave the abode of polytheism and part from its people, who are polytheists in regard to Allah, for the abode of Islam and its people. "In the way of Allah," meaning: in seeking the religion of Allah, which is His way, so that at that point they become like you, and for them then will be your ruling, as:

10066 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "They wish that you would disbelieve as they have disbelieved, and then you would be equal. So do not take from among them allies until they emigrate," meaning: until they do as you have done, namely the emigration in the way of Allah.

* *

The explanation of His saying: ﴿But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them. And do not take from among them any ally or helper﴾ (89)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: if these hypocrites turn away from affirming Allah and His Messenger, and turn away from emigrating from the abode of polytheism to the abode of Islam, and from disbelief to Islam [[See the explanation of "tawalla" above: 8:562, note 1, and the references there.]], "then seize them," O believers, "and kill them wherever you find them," whether in their lands or outside their lands, wherever you reach them in the earth of Allah. "And do not take from among them an ally," meaning: do not take from among them a close friend who supports you in your affairs, nor a helper who aids you against your enemies, [[See the explanation of "wali" above: p. 17, note 3; and "nasir" above: 8:472, note 1, and the references there.]] for they are disbelievers who spare you no ruin and who love what distresses you.

* *

This report from Allah, may His praise be exalted, is a clarification of the genuineness of the hypocrisy of those about whom the believers differed, and a warning to whoever defends them against being defended in return.

* *

Those of the people of interpretation who said the like of what we have said in this matter include:

Those who said that:

10067 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas: "But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them," if they turn away from emigration, "then seize them and kill them."

10068 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "But if they turn away, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them," meaning: when they show their disbelief, then kill them wherever you find them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 90:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Except those who join a people between whom and you there is a covenant﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, "Except those who join a people between whom and you there is a covenant," [He means:] if these hypocrites about whom you disagreed turn away from faith in God and His Messenger, and refuse emigration, not emigrating in the way of God, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them, except for those among them who join a people between whom and you there is a truce, pact and covenant [[See the explanation of "covenant" above: 8:127, note 1, and the references there.]] and so enter among them, become one of them, and accept their judgment. For whoever among the polytheists joins them and enters among them, accepting their judgment, his blood is protected by his entering among them: he shall not be taken captive, nor his women and offspring, nor shall their property be seized, as in:

10069- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "Except those who join a people between whom and you there is a covenant": he says, if they reveal their disbelief, then kill them wherever you find them. But if any of them enters a people between whom and you there is a covenant, then treat him as you treat the people of dhimma (protected non-Muslims).

10070- Yunus related to me, from Ibn Wahb, who said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "Except those who join a people between whom and you there is a covenant": they join those people between whom and you there is a covenant, from among the people; they have the same security as those people have.

10071- al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrimah regarding His words: "Except those who join a people between whom and you there is a covenant." He said: It was revealed concerning Hilal ibn Uwaymir al-Aslami, Suraqa ibn Malik ibn Ju'shum, and Khuzayma ibn Amir ibn Abd Manaf. [[The report 10071: see the two preceding reports 10052, 10053.]]

* *

Some grammarians [[This is Abu Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:136; the printed Majaz al-Qur'an has a transposition and rearrangement that the editor did not correct, so it should be corrected in its place.]] claimed that the meaning of His words "Except those who join a people" is: except those who are connected by lineage to a people between whom and you there is a covenant, from their saying "the man connected himself" (ittasala al-rajul), meaning: he claimed kinship and affiliated himself, as al-A'sha said describing a woman who affiliated herself with a people:

When she claims kinship, she says: "Bakr ibn Wa'il!" ... and Bakr have taken her captive while the noses [of their men] are humiliated. [[His Diwan: 59; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu Ubayda 1:136; al-Nasikh wa'l-Mansukh: 109; Lisan (w-s-l); and others. In Lisan it is "for Bakr ibn Wa'il," and it explains "ittasalat" as "claimed kinship." The commentator on al-A'sha's poetry explains: "when she calls out," meaning she calls with the call of the Jahiliyya, which is boasting of kinship. This verse is the last verse of that ode of al-A'sha. He says: she is summoned to them and claims kinship with them, and she is one of their captive slave-women, whose noses were humiliated, and the noses of their men who used to defend them, then they fled from them and left them to be captured.]]

He means by "ittasalat": she claimed kinship.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: There is no basis for this interpretation in this context, because if claiming kinship with a people of truce or covenant were to bring to those claiming affiliation what they have, when they do not have the covenant and security that they have, then the Messenger of God ﷺ would not have fought the Quraysh, who were the kinsmen of the foremost early Muslims. And the rights of the believers by their faith are greater than the rights of the people of covenant by their covenant. And in the Messenger of God's ﷺ fighting the polytheists of Quraysh, by their refusing to enter what the believers among them had entered, despite the closeness of their lineage to the believers' lineage, is clear evidence that the claim of kinship by one without a covenant to one who has a covenant among them does not bring him the covenant that the one with the covenant has by his claim of kinship.

If one heedless should suppose that the Prophet's ﷺ fighting those among the polytheists of Quraysh who were kin to the believers occurred only after His words "Except those who join a people between whom and you there is a covenant" were abrogated, then the people of interpretation have unanimously agreed that the abrogating text is "Bara'a" (Repentance), and "Bara'a" was revealed after the conquest of Makkah and the entry of Quraysh into Islam. [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "the people of interpretation unanimously agreed that this is abrogation of a recitation revealed after the conquest of Makkah and the entry of Quraysh into Islam," which is an error with no meaning and a gross confusion. I have inferred that what I have written is correct and that he meant "Surat Bara'a," from al-Nasikh wa'l-Mansukh: 109, and from Tafsir Abi Hayyan 3:315, and Tafsir al-Qurtubi 5:308, all of which attribute it to al-Tabari as well.]]

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Or they come to you, their breasts constricted from fighting you or fighting their own people﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, "Or they come to you, their breasts constricted from fighting you or fighting their own people," "then if they turn away, seize them and kill them wherever you find them" = "except those who join a people between whom and you there is a covenant" = or: except those who come to you from among them, whose breasts are constricted from fighting you or fighting their own people, so they enter among you.

By His words "their breasts constricted" he means: their breasts were narrowed from fighting you or fighting their own people.
