The Arabs say of anyone whose soul is constrained from some act or speech: "he has been constricted" (qad hasira), and from this comes "al-hasar" in recitation. [[See the explanation of "al-hasr" above 6:376, 377, and see Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu Ubayda 1:136, and Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:282.]]

* *

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said.

Those who said so:

10072- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "Or they come to you, their breasts constricted," he says: they returned and entered among you. "Their breasts constricted," he says: their breasts were narrowed, "from fighting you or fighting their own people."

* *

In His words "Or they come to you, their breasts constricted from fighting you or fighting their own people," there is an omitted element, its mention left out because the context indicates it. Its meaning is: or they come to you, their breasts having been constricted, so "qad" is omitted, because it is the habit of the Arabs to do such a thing. They say: "So-and-so came to me, his mind gone," meaning: his mind has gone. And it is heard from them: "I woke up and looked at Dhat al-Tanannir," meaning: I had looked. [[This is the view of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:282. "Dhat al-Tanannir": a land between Kufa and the lands of Ghatafan; Yaqut said in his dictionary: "a pass opposite Zubala."] And because "qad" is implied with the past tense, it is permissible to place the past-tense verb in the position of a circumstantial clause (hal), since "qad," when it enters with it, brings it closer to the present and makes it resemble nouns. [[In the printed edition: "and resembled nouns," and what is in the manuscript is correct, meaning the past-tense verbs resembled nouns.]]

* *

This is the reading upon which the reciters in all the regions agree, "hasirat," and it is the reading by which the consensus of the authorities has been established.

* *

It has been reported from al-Hasan al-Basri that he used to read it: ﴿Or they come to you, their breasts [being] constricted﴾ in the accusative (haṣiratan), [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:282.]] and it is sound and eloquent in Arabic, but it is not permissible to recite it in that way in my view, because it is irregular and departs from the reading of the reciters of Islam.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And if God had willed, He would have given them power over you, so they would have fought you. But if they withdraw from you and do not fight you and offer you peace, then God has not made for you any way against them﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted: "And if God had willed, He would have given them power over you, so they would have fought you" — and if God had willed, He would have empowered these people who join a people between whom and you there is a covenant, so that they enter into their protection and dhimma, and those who come to you with breasts constricted from fighting you and fighting their own people — over you, O believers, and they would have fought you alongside your enemies among the polytheists. But God, exalted is His remembrance, restrained them from you. He, may His praise be exalted, says: So obey Him who has blessed you by restraining them from you, along with all the other blessings He has bestowed upon you, in what He commanded you concerning refraining from them when they join a people between whom and you there is a covenant, or come to you with breasts constricted from fighting you and fighting their own people. Then He, may His praise be exalted, said: "But if they withdraw from you," meaning: if these hypocrites whom I commanded you to refrain from fighting withdraw from you, by entering into the people of your covenant, or by coming to you with breasts constricted from fighting you and fighting their own people, "and do not fight you, and offer you peace," meaning: and make peace with you.

* *

"Salam" means submission. [[See the explanation of "Islam" also in the language indexes above under "s-l-m."] This is an image, as a man says to another: "I have given you my reins," and "I have cast my halter to you," when he submits to him and yields to his command. Likewise His words "and offer you peace" mean: they cast their leadership to you and submit to you, making peace and truce with you. And from "salam" is the verse of al-Tirimmah:

For Tamim left Salam to the lions, every chaste woman, heavy-buttocked... [[His Diwan: 145, from his ode in which he satirized al-Farazdaq and the houses of the Banu Darim and Banu Sa'd, saying before it: "And Darim—we cast a hundred of them into the blazing fire when they were thrown into the trenches..." ... He claims that Amr ibn al-Mundhir al-Lakhmi burned the Banu Darim, the kin of al-Farazdaq. Abu Ubayda said: al-Tirimmah had no knowledge of this event, meaning the event of the day of Awara, when Amr ibn al-Mundhir raided the Banu Darim and killed ninety-nine men of them. "The lions" means Amr ibn al-Mundhir and those with him. "Hassan" means a chaste woman. In the printed and manuscript editions it reads "kull mişşan" which is an error with no meaning. "Wa'tha" woman: abundant in flesh, as if the fingers sink into her from the abundance and softness of her flesh. "The buttocks" likewise. "Libad" is the plural of "libda" (with kasra then sukun): a woven cloth spread for sitting. He means by that she is heavy-buttocked, sitting upon the libad. So "libad" was named for buttocks. He says: Tamim surrendered its women to us and to the army of Amr ibn al-Mundhir, and fled from their honor, the fear of their weakness in defending themselves not turning them toward them, and terror made them forget their noble and luxurious women.] He means by "salaman": submission.

* *

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said.

Those who said so:

10073- al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': "But if they withdraw from you and do not fight you and offer you peace," he said: the reconciliation.

* *

As for His words "then God has not made for you any way against them," He says: when these hypocrites whose description has been given submit to you, making peace with you, "then God has not made for you any way against them," meaning: God has not made for you a path against their selves, their property, their offspring, and their women, to kill, capture, or plunder, by any permission from Him or any license, so do not expose them to that. Except for the good way.

* *

Then God abrogated the entire ruling of this verse and the one after it by His saying, may His praise be exalted: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾ to His saying: ﴿then let them go on their way, for God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [Surat al-Tawba: 5].

Those who said the same as what we have said:

10074- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, from al-Husayn, from Yazid, from Ikrimah and al-Hasan, who both said: ﴿So if they turn away, seize them and kill them wherever you find them, and do not take from among them any ally or helper, except those who join a people between whom and you there is a covenant﴾ to His saying: ﴿And those, We have given you clear authority over them﴾. And in "al-Mumtahana" He said: ﴿God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you over religion and do not expel you from your homes, from being righteous to them and dealing justly with them, for God loves the just﴾, and in it He said: ﴿God forbids you only from those who fight you over religion and expel you from your homes﴾ to ﴿it is those who are the wrongdoers﴾ [Surat al-Mumtahana: 8, 9]. Then these four verses concerning the polytheists were abrogated when He said: ﴿A declaration of immunity from God and His Messenger to those of the polytheists with whom you made a treaty. So travel freely in the land for four months, and know that you cannot escape God, and that God will disgrace the disbelievers﴾ [Surat al-Tawba: 1, 2]. So He gave them four months to travel in the land, and nullified what had been before that. And He said in the one that follows: ﴿So when the sacred months have passed, kill the polytheists wherever you find them, and seize them, besiege them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾, then He abrogated and made an exception, saying: ﴿But if they repent, establish prayer, and give zakat, then let them go their way﴾ to His saying: ﴿then deliver him to his place of safety﴾ [Surat al-Tawba: 5, 6].

10075- al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada regarding His words: "But if they withdraw from you": he said: it was abrogated by: ﴿then kill the polytheists wherever you find them﴾.

10076- al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal related to us, saying: Hammam ibn Yahya related to us, saying: I heard Qatada say regarding His words: "Except those who join a people between whom and you there is a covenant" to His words "then God has not made for you any way against them": then this was afterward abrogated in Bara'a, and He commanded His Prophet ﷺ to fight the polytheists by His words: ﴿So kill the polytheists wherever you find them, seize them, besiege them, and lie in wait for them at every place of ambush﴾.

10077- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "Except those who join a people between whom and you there is a covenant," the verse: this entire thing was abrogated altogether; it was abrogated by jihad. A term of four months was set for them: either they become Muslims, or there is jihad.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 91:

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿You will find others who wish to be secure from you and to be secure from their own people. Whenever they are returned to disorder, they are plunged back into it.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: These are another group of the hypocrites (munafiqun), who would show Islam to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his Companions, so that through it they would be safe from them regarding killing, captivity and the seizing of property, while they were unbelievers. Their own people knew this about them: when they met them, they were with them and worshipped what they worshipped apart from God, so that they would make them feel secure regarding their persons, their property, their women and their offspring. God says: ﴿Whenever they are returned to disorder, they are plunged back into it﴾, meaning: whenever [their people] call them to association with God [the addition in brackets is necessary for the context of the speech], they apostatise and become polytheists like them.

* *

The scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed about those intended by this verse.

Some of them said: They were people from among the people of Makkah who embraced Islam, as God described them, in a state of taqiyyah (dissimulation), while they were unbelievers, so that they might be secure for themselves, their property, their offspring and their women. God says: ﴿Whenever they are returned to disorder, they are plunged back into it﴾, meaning: whenever [their people] call them to associate others with God [the addition in brackets is necessary for the context of the speech], they apostatise and become polytheists like them, so that they may be secure among these and those.

Transmission of those who said this:

10078 – Muhammad ibn Amr related to me, saying: Abu Asim related to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿They wish to be secure from you and to be secure from their people﴾. He said: They were people who would come to the Prophet (ﷺ) and embrace Islam out of showing off, then return to Quraysh and relapse into idols, seeking by that to be safe here and there. So he commanded fighting them if they did not withdraw and make peace.

10079 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

10080 – Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿You will find others who wish to be secure from you and to be secure from their people; whenever they are returned to disorder, they are plunged back into it﴾. He says: Whenever they wish to come out of a trial, they are plunged back into it. That is because a man would be found who had spoken the words of Islam, and he would be brought near to a stick, a stone, a scorpion and a beetle, and the polytheists would say to that one who had spoken Islam: "Say: this is my lord", to the beetle and the scorpion.

* *

Others said: Rather, they were a people of polytheism who had sought safe-conduct from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), so that they might be secure with him, with his Companions and with the polytheists.

Transmission of those who said this:

10081 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: ﴿You will find others who wish to be secure from you and to be secure from their people﴾. He said: They were a tribe in Tihamah. They said: "O Prophet of God, we will not fight you nor fight our people", and they wished to make the Prophet of God secure and to be secure from their people. God refused that for them, and said: ﴿Whenever they are returned to disorder, they are plunged back into it﴾, meaning: whenever a trial comes upon them, they perish in it.

* *

Others said: This verse was revealed concerning Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud al-Ashja'i.

Transmission of those who said this:

10082 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, who said: Then he mentioned Nu'aym ibn Mas'ud al-Ashja'i, who was secure among the Muslims and the polytheists, carrying news between the Prophet (ﷺ) and the polytheists. So [God said]: ﴿You will find others who wish to be secure from you and to be secure from their people; whenever they are returned to disorder﴾, meaning: to polytheism.

* *

As for the interpretation of His words: ﴿whenever they are returned to disorder, they are plunged back into it﴾, it is as follows:

10083 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, regarding His words: ﴿whenever they are returned to disorder, they are plunged back into it﴾. He said: Whenever they are tested by it, they become blind within it.

10084 – Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: whenever a trial befalls them, they perish in it.

* *

The statement on this is what I have already explained earlier, namely that "fitnah" in the speech of the Arabs means testing, and "ikras" means returning. [See the explanation of "fitnah" earlier: 2:444; 3:565, 566, 570, 571; 4:301; 6:196, 197. And see the explanation of "ikras" earlier: pp. 7, 15, 16.]

* *

So the meaning of the speech is: whenever they are returned to testing in order to revert to disbelief and polytheism, they revert to it.

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿So if they do not withdraw from you and offer you peace and restrain their hands, then seize them and kill them wherever you find them. And those – We have made for you against them a clear authority﴾ (91).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, His mention (exalted is He) means: So if they do not withdraw from you, [in the printed and manuscript editions: "if they do not withdraw from you", and the context requires what is established here], O believers, these who wish to be secure from you and to be secure from their people, and who, whenever they are called to polytheism, respond to it; "and offer you peace", and do not submit to you, giving you compliance and making peace with you. [See the explanation of "offering peace" earlier: pp. 23, 24.] As:

10085 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far related to us, from his father, from al-Rabi': ﴿if they do not withdraw from you and offer you peace﴾, he said: reconciliation.

* *

"and restrain their hands", meaning: and restrain their hands from fighting you. [See the explanation of "restraint" earlier: 8:548.] "then seize them and kill them wherever you find them", His mention (exalted is He) says: if they do not do that, then seize them wherever you come upon them and encounter them on the earth, and kill them, for their blood is then lawful to you. "And those – We have made for you against them a clear authority", His mention (exalted is He) says: And these who wish to be secure from you and to be secure from their people, while they remain in their unbelief, and have not withdrawn from you, offered you peace or restrained their hands [in the printed and manuscript editions: "have not withdrawn from you", without the waw, and the correct reading includes it], We have made for you a proof for killing them wherever you encounter them, because of their remaining in their disbelief and their abandonment of emigration from the abode of polytheism. "clear" means: it makes clear their deserving that from you, and your being right in killing them. That is His saying: "a clear authority", and "authority" is proof. [See the explanation of "authority" earlier: 7:279, and the explanation of "clear" earlier: 8:124 note 1, and the references there.] As:

10086 – Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Qabisah related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from a man, from Ikrimah, who said: Whatever in the Qur'an is "sultan", it means: proof.

10087 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi regarding His words: "a clear authority". As for "clear authority", it is proof.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 92 (part 1 of 3):

The explanation of His words: ﴿It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake. And whoever kills a believer by mistake, [the penance is] the freeing of a believing slave and a compensation (diyah) delivered to his family, unless they give it up as charity.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, "It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake," may He be glorified, He means: Allah did not permit or allow a believer to kill a believer. That is, it was not his to do in any of the things his Lord granted him and permitted him, at all. As (narrated):

10088 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words, "It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake," he said: It was not his to do in what came to him from his Lord, from the covenant of Allah which was made with him.

* *

As for His words, "except by mistake," He is saying: However, a believer may kill a believer by mistake, and that is not something his Lord granted him or permitted him. This is from the exception that the grammarians call "the disconnected exception" (al-istithna' al-munqati'), as Jarir ibn 'Atiyyah said:

"Of the white women, she did not travel far, nor did she tread upon the ground except the fringe of a striped, embroidered garment."[[His Diwan: 457; al-Naqa'id: 706; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1: 137, from his poem in which he satirised al-Farazdaq and the family of al-Zibriqan ibn Badr; it is from the beginning of the poem, and before it is: "From the remnants of a covenant do my tears flow, as if the dust of my eyes were from the grain of fulful?..." "If Salma is seen by jinn who become familiar with her, and if Salma is seen by the monk of the mountain, he will descend." The reading in the Diwan and in Abu 'Ubaydah's al-Naqa'id is: "except the border of a striped mantle, embroidered." The "nir" (with a kasra on the nun) is the border ( 'alam) of the garment. The "mirt" is a silk wrap that has a border, and it may also be of wool. As for "al-rit", it is the plural of "rita", which is a sheet when it is a single piece and not made of two halves, and it is a fine, soft garment. The "murahhal" is the embroidered, a type of striped cloth, its pattern fixed like the fixed patterns of a saddle. In the manuscript and the printed edition it reads "murajjal" with a jim, which is an error.]]

That is: "and she did not tread upon the ground except that she trod upon the hem of a cloak, and the hem of a cloak is not from the ground." [[This is the view of Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an 1: 136-138.]]

Then He, may He be glorified, informed His servants of the ruling concerning one of the believers who is killed by mistake, saying: "And whoever kills a believer by mistake, [the penance is] the freeing of a believing slave," meaning: upon him is the freeing of "a believing slave" from his wealth, "and a compensation delivered to his family," which his 'aqilah (the paternal kin who pay blood-money for manslaughter by mistake; from 'aql, meaning blood-money) pay, "unless they give it up as charity," meaning: unless the family of the slain person by mistake gives up their claim against the one obligated to pay the blood-money for their slain, pardoning him and overlooking his offence, so that it is dropped from him.

* *

The position of "an" in His words "unless they give it up as charity" is in the accusative, because its meaning is: upon him is that, except that they give it up.

* *

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah al-Makhzumi, who had killed a Muslim man after his Islam, while he did not know of his Islam.

Mention of the reports on this:

10089 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah, "It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake," he said: 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah killed a believing man who had been torturing him along with Abu Jahl, and he was his maternal brother. He followed the Prophet (ﷺ) while he thought that man was still as he was. 'Ayyash had emigrated to the Prophet (ﷺ) as a believer. Then Abu Jahl, who was his maternal brother, came to him and said: Your mother beseeches you by her kinship and her right that you return to her, and she is Asma' bint Mukharribah. [[In the printed edition: "bint Makhramah"; the correct reading from the manuscript is "Mukharribah" with a heavy, kasra-marked ra and a ba. Asma' was of Banu Nahshal ibn Darim, of Tamim.]] So he went with him, and Abu Jahl bound him until he reached Mecca. When the disbelievers saw him, that increased them in disbelief and trial, and they said: Abu Jahl is indeed able to do with Muhammad what he wills, and to seize his companions.

10090 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly, except that in his report he said: [he] followed that man, while 'Ayyash supposed that he was a disbeliever as he was. 'Ayyash had emigrated to Medina as a believer, and Abu Jahl, who was his maternal brother, came to him and said: Your mother implores you by her kinship and her right to return to her. He also said: and he seizes his companions and binds them. [[In the printed edition: "fa-ya'khudhu" with a fa; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

10091 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, from Mujahid similarly. Ibn Juraij said, from 'Ikrimah, who said: al-Harith ibn Yazid ibn Unaysah, [[In the printed edition: "ibn Nabishah"; in the manuscript it is written without the alif at the beginning and unpointed. The correct form is from al-Isabah, Usd al-Ghabah and others.]] of Banu 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy, was torturing 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah along with Abu Jahl. Then al-Harith ibn Yazid went out as an emigrant to the Prophet (ﷺ), and 'Ayyash met him at al-Harrah, and struck him with the sword until he went silent, [["Sakata" means he became still and his movement ceased; this is among the usages that may be added to the dictionaries' entries.]] while thinking that he was a disbeliever. Then he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and informed him, and the verse was revealed: "It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake," the verse. He recited it to him, then said to him: Stand up and free [a slave].

10092 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake," he said: It was revealed concerning 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah al-Makhzumi, who was a brother of Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, through his mother, [[In the printed edition: "fa-kana akhan," a misreading of the manuscript.]] and he embraced Islam and emigrated among the early emigrants before the arrival of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Abu Jahl and al-Harith ibn Hisham sought him, and with them was a man from Banu 'Amir ibn Lu'ayy. They came to him in Medina, and 'Ayyash was the most beloved of his brothers to his mother. They spoke to him and said: "Your mother has sworn that no house will shade her until she sees you, and she is lying in the sun. Come to her so that she may look at you, then return!" They gave him a covenant from Allah that they would not harm him until he returned to Medina, [[In the printed edition: "la yahjizunahu," which is an error and a change from the manuscript. "Hajahu yahiju-hu" means he disturbed and drove him away; the intent is: they would not harm him with anything that would disturb or drive him away.]] so one of his companions gave him a noble camel and said: If you fear anything from them, sit upon the noble camel. When they took him out of Medina, they seized him and bound him, and the Amiri whipped him, and he swore that he would kill the Amiri. He remained imprisoned in Mecca until he went out on the day of the Conquest. The Amiri met him, having embraced Islam, and 'Ayyash did not know of his Islam, so he struck him and killed him. Then Allah revealed: "It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake," meaning: while he did not know that he was a believer. "And whoever kills a believer by mistake, [the penance is] the freeing of a believing slave and a compensation delivered to his family, unless they give it up as charity," meaning: they forgo the blood-money.

* *

Others said: This verse was revealed concerning Abu al-Darda'.

Mention of those who said that:

10093 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words, "It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake," the verse, he said: This was revealed concerning a man whom Abu al-Darda' killed; all of this was revealed about him. [[The printed edition omitted the phrase "all of this was revealed about him," and I do not know why it did that!]] They were in a military expedition, and Abu al-Darda' turned aside to a ravine to attend to a need of his, and he found a man of the people among his sheep. He charged at him with the sword, and the man said: There is no god but Allah! He said: So he struck him, then brought his sheep to the people. Then he felt something in himself, so he came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned that to him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: Why did you not split open his heart? He said: What could I have known! [["Ma 'asaytu ajid" comes from "'asa"; it is as if he said: what do I find by killing him while he is a polytheist?]] Is it, O Messenger of Allah, anything but blood or water? He said: He had told you with his tongue, yet you did not believe him? He said: How will it be with me, O Messenger of Allah? He said: How will it be with "There is no god but Allah"? He said: How will it be with me, O Messenger of Allah? He said: How will it be with "There is no god but Allah"? Until I wished that it had been the beginning of my Islam. He said: And the Qur'an was revealed: "It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake," until reaching "unless they give it up as charity." He said: Unless they waive it.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct statement on this matter is that it should be said: Allah, by this verse, made known to His servants what is owed by one who kills a believer by mistake, of expiation and blood-money. It is permissible that the verse was revealed concerning 'Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi'ah and his victim, and concerning Abu al-Darda' and his companion. Whichever of these it was, what Allah, exalted is He, meant by the verse is informing His servants of what we have mentioned, and whoever among His servants understood His revelation from Him has known that, and their ignorance of who it was revealed about does not harm them.

* *

As for "the believing slave," the scholars differ over its description.

Some of them said: A slave is not believing unless he has chosen faith after reaching maturity, and has prayed and fasted, and a child does not deserve this description.

Mention of those who said that:

10094 - Yaqub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Abu Hayyan, who said: I asked al-Sha'bi about His words, "[then] the freeing of a believing slave," and he said: She has prayed and knows faith.

10095 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words, "the freeing of a believing slave," he meant by "believing": one who understands faith and fasts and prays.

10096 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: Whatever in the Qur'an is "a believing slave," only one who fasts and prays suffices. And whatever in the Qur'an is "a slave" that is not "believing," a child suffices.

10097 - It was narrated from Yazid ibn Harun, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from al-Hasan, who said: Everything in the Book of Allah: "the freeing of a believing slave," is one who fasts, prays and understands. And when He says: "the freeing of a slave," whatever one wishes.

10098 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, who said: Everything in the Qur'an: "the freeing of a believing slave" is one who has prayed. And what is not "believing," the freeing of one who has not prayed suffices.

10099 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: "the freeing of a believing slave," and "the believing slave," according to Qatadah, is one who has prayed. And he disliked freeing in this matter a child who has not prayed and has not reached that.

10100 - Yahya ibn Talhah al-Yarbu'i related to me, saying: Fudayl ibn 'Iyad related to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim regarding His words, "the freeing of a believing slave," he said: When he understands his religion.

10101 - Al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq related to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said regarding "the freeing of a believing slave": a child does not suffice in it.

10102 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "the freeing of a believing slave," meaning by "believing": one who has understood faith and fasts and prays. And if he does not find a slave, then fasting two consecutive months, and upon him a compensation delivered to his family, unless they give it up as charity.

* *

Others said: If he was born between two Muslim parents, he is a believer, even if he is a child.

Mention of those who said that:

10103 - Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Juraij, from 'Ata', who said: Every slave born in Islam suffices.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two opinions on this matter is that of those who said: In killing by mistake, only slaves who have believed, and who understand faith, from adult men and women, suffice, provided that their parents were of some religion other than Islam, and the child was born to them while they were thus, and then neither of them embraced Islam until he was freed in expiation for the mistake. As for one born to two Muslim parents, the scholars unanimously agree that even if he has not reached the limit of choice and discernment, and has not attained puberty, he is judged by the ruling of believers regarding inheritance, the funeral prayer upon him if he dies, what is owed by him if he commits an offence, what is owed to him if an offence is committed against him, and marriage. Since this is the consensus of all of them, it is necessary that he have, in what suffices in the expiation for mistake if he is freed in it, the ruling of believers, like the ruling he has of belief in the other matters we have mentioned and others. Whoever refuses this, the matter is reversed for him, and he is then asked for the distinction between these from a principle or analogy. He will not state any opinion on any of these except that he is bound to the same in the others.

As for the "compensation delivered" to the family of the victim, it is what is handed to them, according to what is due to them, complete, without diminishing their rights from it. [[See the explanation of "muslimah" above, 2: 184, 213-215.]]

* *

It is mentioned from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to say: It is the complete one.

10104 - Al-Qasim related to us, saying: Al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said regarding His words, "and a compensation delivered to his family": it is complete.

* *

As for His words, "unless they give it up as charity," He means by it: unless they give the blood-money as charity to the slayer, or to his 'aqilah. The "ta'" in "yatasaddaqu" was assimilated into the "sad," so that the two became a single "sad."

* *

It is mentioned that this is in the reading of Ubayy: ﴿illa an yatasaddaqu﴾ (unless they give it as charity).

10105 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Bakr ibn al-Sharud related to us: the variant of Ubayy: ﴿illa an yatasaddaqu﴾.

* *

The explanation of His words: ﴿But if he was from a people hostile to you and he was a believer, then [the penance is] the freeing of a believing slave﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may He be glorified, "But if he was from a people hostile to you and he was a believer," if this slain person whom the believer killed by mistake was "from a people hostile to you," meaning: from among the enumerated people who are enemies to you in religion, polytheists who have declared war upon you in opposition to you on Islam, "and he was a believer, then [the penance is] the freeing of a believing slave," He says: if a Muslim kills by mistake a man from among the polytheists, and the slain is a believer while the slayer supposes that he is upon his disbelief, then upon him is the freeing of a believing slave.

* *

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of that.

Some of them said: Its meaning is: if the slain was from a people who are enemies to you, and he was a believer, meaning: among them and had not emigrated, and a believer killed him, then there is no blood-money upon him, but upon him is the freeing of a believing slave.

Mention of those who said that:

10106 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id related to us, from Sufyan, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah and al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim regarding His words, "And if he was from a people hostile to you and he was a believer," he said: It is the man who embraces Islam in the land of war and is killed. He said: There is no blood-money in it, and in it is the expiation.

10107 - Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah regarding His words, "And if he was from a people hostile to you and he was a believer," he said: meaning the slain is a believer while his people are disbelievers. He said: So there is no blood-money for him, but the freeing of a believing slave.

10108 - Al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Abu Ghassan related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words, "But if he was from a people hostile to you and he was a believer," he said: A man may be a believer while his people are disbelievers, so there is no blood-money for him, but the freeing of a believing slave.

10109 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "But if he was from a people hostile to you and he was a believer," in the land of disbelief, He says: "then [the penance is] the freeing of a believing slave," and there is no blood-money for him.

**Tafsir al-Tabari (Jami' al-Bayan), commentary on Surah 4, verse 92 (part 2 of 3)**

1010. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding "But if he came from a people hostile to you and he was a believer, then [the freeing of] a believing slave." And there is no blood money for his family, because they are disbelievers, and there is no covenant or protection (dhimmah) between them and Allah.

1011. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Hajjaj related to us, saying: Hammad related to us, saying: 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he said regarding the words of Allah, "And if he came from a people hostile to you and he was a believer," to the end of the verse: "A man would accept Islam, then go to his people and reside among them while they were polytheists. Then the army of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would pass by them, and he would be killed among those who were killed. His killer must free a slave, and he has no blood money."

1012. Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, regarding "But if he came from a people hostile to you and he was a believer, then [the freeing of] a believing slave." He said: This applies when a Muslim man from a people hostile to you, that is, with whom there is no covenant, is killed by mistake. Upon the one who killed him is the freeing of a believing slave.

1013. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding "But if he came from a people hostile to you and he was a believer": If he was among the people of war and he was a believer, and he was killed by mistake, then upon his killer is expiation by freeing a believing slave, or fasting two consecutive months, and there is no blood money upon him.

1014. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words, "And if he came from a people hostile to you and he was a believer": The slain person was a Muslim, and his people were disbelievers, so [the killer must free] a believing slave, and [blood money] is not to be paid to them lest they strengthen themselves against you with it.

* *

Others said: Rather, it refers to a man from the people of war who comes to the abode of Islam, accepts Islam, then returns to the abode of war. When the army of the Muslims passes by them, his people flee, but that Muslim remains among them there, and the Muslims kill him while thinking he is a disbeliever.

Mention of those who said this:

1015. Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding "But if he came from a people hostile to you and he was a believer, then [the freeing of] a believing slave": He is the believer who is among the enemy polytheists, who hear of a detachment (sariyyah) of the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), so they flee, while the believer remains and is killed, and for that there is the freeing of a believing slave.

* *

Commentary on His words: ﴿And if he came from a people between you and whom there is a covenant, then blood money must be paid to his family and [the freeing of] a believing slave﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, "And if he came from a people between you and between whom there is a covenant," Allah, may His praise be exalted, means: And if the slain person whom the believer killed by mistake came "from a people between you" (O believers) "and between whom there is a covenant," that is, a pact and protection, and they are not people of war against you, "then blood money must be paid to his family," meaning: upon his killer is blood money paid to his family, which his 'aqilah (the paternal kinsmen who bear the blood money) shoulder. "And [the freeing of] a believing slave" is an expiation for his killing.

* *

Then the people of interpretation differed regarding the description of this slain person who is from a people between us and them a covenant: is he a believer or a disbeliever? [[See the explanation of "covenant" (mithaq) above, p. 19, note 1, and the references there.]]

Some said: He is a disbeliever, but his killer is bound to pay his blood money, because he and his people have a covenant, so it is obligatory to pay his blood money to his people because of the covenant between them and the believers, and because it is a part of their property, and nothing of their property is lawful for the believers except with their goodwill.

Mention of those who said this:

1016. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding "And if he came from a people between you and between whom there is a covenant": He says: If he was a disbeliever under your protection and was killed, then upon his killer is blood money paid to his family, and [the freeing of] a believing slave, or fasting two consecutive months.

1017. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Ayyub, who said: I heard al-Zuhri say: The blood money of a dhimmi is the blood money of a Muslim. He said: And he used to interpret: "And if he came from a people between you and between whom there is a covenant, then blood money must be paid to his family."

1018. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Idris related to us, from 'Isa ibn Abi al-Mughirah, from al-Sha'bi regarding His words, "And if he came from a people between you and between whom there is a covenant, then blood money must be paid to his family": He said: He is from the people of the covenant, and is not a believer.

1019. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Mahdi related to us, from Hushaym, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, regarding "And if he came from a people between you and between whom there is a covenant": And he is not a believer.

1020. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding "And if he came from a people between you and between whom there is a covenant, then blood money must be paid to his family and [the freeing of] a believing slave": by his killing, that is, by what befell one of the people of his protection and covenant. "Then whoever does not find [the means], then fasting two consecutive months, as a repentance from Allah," to the end of the verse.

1021. Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words, "And if he came from a people between you and between whom there is a covenant, then blood money must be paid to his family": He says: Pay them the blood money, by virtue of the covenant. He said: The people of protection (ahl al-dhimmah) enter into this. "And [the freeing of] a believing slave. Then whoever does not find [the means], then fasting two consecutive months."

* *

Others said: Rather, he is a believer, and upon his killer is blood money which he pays to his people, who are polytheists, because they are people of protection.

Mention of those who said this:

1022. Ibn Humayd related to me, saying: Jarir related to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, regarding "And if he came from a people between you and between whom there is a covenant, then blood money must be paid to his family and [the freeing of] a believing slave": He said: This is a Muslim man whose people are polytheists with whom there is a pact, so his blood money is to his people, and his inheritance is to the Muslims, and his people bear the blood money (ya'qilu) for him, and the blood money is theirs.

1023. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Suwayd related to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Hushaym, from Abu Ishaq al-Kufi, from Jabir ibn Zayd regarding His words, "And if he came from a people between you and between whom there is a covenant": He said: And he is a believer.

1024. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ibn Mahdi related to us, from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Yunus, from al-Hasan regarding His words, "And if he came from a people between you and between whom there is a covenant": He said: All of them are believers. [[In the printed edition: "He said: He is a disbeliever," in place of "All of them are believers," and what is printed contradicts the translation. What I have adopted from the manuscript is also inconsistent with the translation, because of his statement "all of them are believers," meaning that he and his people are believers. Unless he meant by "all of them" every slain person mentioned in the preceding verses; and this is more probable in my view. He did not mean by "all of them" the people of the slain person.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two views regarding the interpretation of this verse is the view of those who said that it refers to the slain person from the people of the covenant. Because Allah left it vague, saying, "And if he came from a people between you and between them," and He did not say, "and he is a believer," as He said regarding the slain person from among the believers and the people of war, and He meant the slain person from among them who is a believer. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "or about the believer among them who is a believer," which has no meaning; the correct reading is what I have adopted.] So in His omission of describing him with the faith with which He described the two previously mentioned slain persons, there is clear evidence for the soundness of what we have said regarding this.

* *

If someone supposes that in His words, "then blood money must be paid to his family," there is evidence that he is of the people of faith, because in his view blood money is only for a believer, then he has erred. That is because the blood money of a dhimmi and of Muslims is equal, by the consensus of all of them that the blood money of their disbelieving slaves and of the slaves of the believers is equal. Likewise the ruling on the blood money of their free persons is equal. Moreover, if their blood money were as those who opposed us say, making it half the blood money of the believers or a third, that would not be evidence that the one meant by "And if he came from a people between you and between whom there is a covenant" is of the people of faith, because the blood money of a believing woman is not disputed by all (except those who are not counted as disputing) to be half the blood money of a believing man, and that does not remove it from being blood money. Likewise the ruling on the blood money of the people of protection: if it were less than the blood money of the people of faith, that would not remove it from being blood money. How then, when the matter is contrary to that, and their blood money and the blood money of the believers are equal?

* *

As for "covenant" (mithaq), it means a pact and protection. We have explained elsewhere that this is so, and the root from which it derives has been treated, so there is no need to repeat it here. [[See the explanation of "covenant" above, p. 19, and note 1, and p. 41, and note 1, and the references there.]]

Mention of those who said this:

1025. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to me, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi regarding His words, "And if he came from a people between you and between whom there is a covenant," he says: a pact.

1026. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri regarding His words, "And if he came from a people between you and between whom there is a covenant," he said: It is the treaty (mu'ahadah).

1027. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Ghassan related to us, saying: Isra'il related to us, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "And if he came from a people between you and between whom there is a covenant": a pact.

1028. Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from 'Ikrimah, the like of it.

* *

If someone says: What is the description of the mistake (khata') which, when a believer kills a believer or a treaty-bound person, makes binding upon him the blood money and the expiation? It is said: It is what al-Nakha'i said regarding it, and that is:

1029. Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: "The mistake" is that he intends a thing and hits other than it.

1030. Abu Kurayb and Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to us, both saying: Hushaym related to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: "The mistake" is that he throws at a thing and hits a person while not intending him; that is a mistake, and it falls upon the 'aqilah. [[The interpretation of "'aqilah" has passed many times: they are the paternal kinsmen (asabah) who pay the blood money on behalf of the killer from among them, from "al-'aql," which is the blood money.]]

* *

If he says: What is the blood money that is obligatory in that case?

It is said: As for the killing of a believer, it is one hundred camels, if he is from the people of camels, borne by the 'aqilah of his killer. There is no dispute among all of them about that, although there is a difference among the scholars regarding the ages of the camels. Some of them say: They are in quarters: twenty-five of them are hiqqah, and twenty-five are jadh'ah, and twenty-five are bint makhad, and twenty-five are bint labun. [[When a camel completes its third year and enters its fourth, it is then called "hiqq" (with a kasrah on the ha') and the female is "hiqqah." When it completes its fourth year and enters its fifth, it is then "jadh'" (with two fathas) and the female is "jadh'ah." Before that, the camel is called fasil. When the fasil completes a year and enters its second, it is then "ibn makhad," and the female "bint makhad." When it completes its second year and reaches its third, it is then "ibn labun," and the female "bint labun."]]

Mention of those who said this:

1031. Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding the mistake that resembles deliberate killing: thirty-three hiqqah, thirty-three jadh'ah, and thirty-four thaniyyah up to its bazil year. [[When a camel completes its fifth year and reaches its sixth, it is then "thaniyy," and the female "thaniyyah." When it completes its eighth year and reaches its ninth and its tooth has come out, it is then "bazil," and the female "bazil" without the ha'. Ibn al-A'rabi said: "There is no name called before the thaniyy, nor a name called after the bazil," meaning that a camel that has entered its seventh year and reached its eighth has no name by which it is called. That is perhaps because the bazil often splits its teeth in its eighth year. As for "bazil," it is the most advanced of the ages of the camel. Then they say "bazil of a year" and "bazil of two years," and so on for whatever exceeds that.]] And in the case of mistake: twenty-five hiqqah, twenty-five jadh'ah, twenty-five bint makhad, and twenty-five bint labun.

1032. Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Faras and al-Shaybani, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, the like of it.

1033. Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn Damrah, from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), similarly.

1034. Wasil ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from Ash'ath ibn Sawwar, from al-Sha'bi, from 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), that he said regarding the killing by mistake: The blood money is one hundred in quarters. Then he mentioned the like of it.

* *

Others said: It is in fifths: twenty hiqqah, twenty jadh'ah, twenty bint labun, twenty ibn labun, and twenty bint makhad.

Mention of those who said this:

1035. Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi related to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Abu Mijlaz, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from his father, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: In the case of mistake: twenty hiqqah, twenty jadh'ah, twenty bint labun, twenty ibn labun, and twenty bint makhad. [[The philologists denied that one may say "banu labun" as the plural of "ibn labun"; they said it is "banat labun" for both male and female. These sound reports indicate that it is correct in the Arabic language.]]

1036. Wasil ibn 'Abd al-A'la related to me, saying: Ibn Fudayl related to us, from Ash'ath, from 'Amir, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud regarding killing by mistake: one hundred camels in fifths: a fifth of jidha' (jadha'), and a fifth of hiqaq, [[The "haqaq" and "jidha'" are the plurals of "hiqqah" and "jadh'ah," and their explanation has been given previously in the notes.]] and a fifth of bint labun, and a fifth of bint makhad, and a fifth of banu makhad.

1037. Muhammad ibn Musa related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sulayman al-Taymi informed us, from Abu Mijlaz, from Abu 'Ubaydah, from 'Abd Allah, who said: The blood money is in fifths: the blood money for mistake: a fifth bint makhad, a fifth bint labun, a fifth hiqaq, a fifth jidha', and a fifth banu makhad. [[His saying "banu makhad" is among what the philologists denied; they do not say in the plural except "banat makhad" and "banat labun," and "banat awa" similarly. This report and what follows it indicate the soundness of their saying "banu makhad."]]

* *

Those who held this view argued with a ḥadīth:

1038. Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i related it to us, saying: Yahya ibn Abi Za'idah and Abu Khalid al-Ahmar related to us, from Hajjaj, from Zayd ibn Jubayr, from al-Khashf ibn Malik, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud: that the Prophet (ﷺ) decided the blood money for mistake in fifths. He said: Abu Hisham said: Ibn Abi Za'idah said: twenty hiqqah, twenty jadh'ah, twenty bint labun, twenty bint makhad, and twenty banu makhad. [[Report 1038: "al-Khashf ibn Malik al-Ta'i," who narrated from his father, from 'Umar, and from Ibn Mas'ud. Zayd ibn Jubayr al-Jushami narrated from him. Al-Nasa'i said: "Trustworthy (thiqah)"; al-Daraqutni said in al-Sunan: "Unknown (majhul)." Al-Azdi said: "He is not of that standing." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.

This report was transmitted by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (8: 75–76) by two routes: the route of Sa'dan ibn Nasr, from Abu Mu'awiyah Muhammad ibn Khazim, from al-Hajjaj, from Zayd ibn Jubayr, from Khashf ibn Malik, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) made the blood money for mistake to be in fifths. And he added nothing to this.

Then he narrated it from the route of Abu Dawud, from Musaddad, from 'Abd al-Wahid, from al-Hajjaj, from Zayd ibn Jubayr, from Khashf ibn Malik, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: For the blood money of mistake: twenty hiqqah, twenty jadh'ah, twenty bint makhad, twenty bint labun, and twenty ibn makhad, a male. Abu Dawud said: This is the saying of 'Abd Allah, meaning that it is only narrated as a saying of 'Abd Allah, stopped (mawquf), not raised (marfu').

Then al-Bayhaqi cited the critique of this ḥadīth from Abu al-Hasan al-Daraqutni, who said: "We do not know of anyone who narrated it except Khashf ibn Malik, who is an unknown man, from whom none narrated except Zayd ibn Jubayr ibn Harmal al-Jushami. And we do not know of anyone who narrated from Zayd ibn Jubayr except al-Hajjaj ibn Artah. Al-Hajjaj is a man known for tadlis (concealing defects in transmission), and for narrating from those he did not meet and did not hear from. He said: And a group of trustworthy transmitters narrated it from al-Hajjaj, and they differed about it on his authority." Then he mentioned the narrations from al-Hajjaj, and that in some of them he put "banu labun" in place of "hiqaq." Then he mentioned that they did not transmit in it an explanation of the fifths. Then he said: "It seems that al-Hajjaj may have explained the fifths by his own opinion after finishing the ḥadīth, so the listener supposes that this is part of the ḥadīth, and it is not so."]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 92 (part 3 of 3):

Al-Bayhaqi said: "However that may be, al-Hajjaj ibn Artah is not a reliable source for argument, Khashf ibn Malik is unknown, and the sound position is that it is a report from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud (a companion's statement, mawquf). The sound report from ʿAbd Allah is that he divided it into five parts, the bint al-makhad (a she-camel in her second year) being one of the fifths, in the chains of transmission that were mentioned earlier, and not as our shaykh Abu al-Hasan al-Daraqutni, may God have mercy on him and us, imagined. Those who turned away from the statement of ʿAbd Allah, may God be pleased with him, on this matter have offered two excuses. The first is the weakness of Khashf ibn Malik's transmission from Ibn Masʿud, as we have mentioned. The second is the disconnection (inqita') of the transmission of those who related it from him as a mawquf report." Then he set out its routes and explained their disconnection.

10139. Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Ishaq, from ʿAlqamah, from ʿAbd Allah: that he judged accordingly.

* *

Others said: they are quarters (arba'): thirty hiqqah (a she-camel in her fourth year), thirty bint labun (a she-camel in her third year), twenty bint makhad, and twenty ibn labun males.

Those who said this:

10140. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to me, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, from ʿAbd Rabbih, from Abu ʿIyad, from ʿUthman and Zayd ibn Thabit, who both said, concerning the quasi-intentional killing: forty jadhaʿah khalifah, [["al-khalifah" (with a fatha on the kha, a kasra on the lam, and a fatha on the fa): the pregnant she-camel. Its plural is makhad, as they say "imra'ah" and "niswah." As for its derivation, it is said "khalifat" and "khala'if." A hadith says: "Three verses one of you recites are better for him than three fat, large khalifat," and in the hadith of the demolition of the Kaʿbah: "When they demolished it, there appeared in it something like the khala'if of camels," meaning large rocks in its foundation like pregnant she-camels.]] and thirty hiqqah, and thirty bint makhad. And in unintentional killing: thirty hiqqah, thirty jadhaʿah, twenty bint makhad, and twenty ibn labun males.

10141. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from Saʿid, from Qatadah, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, from Zayd ibn Thabit: concerning the blood-money for unintentional killing: thirty hiqqah, thirty bint labun, twenty bint makhad, and twenty ibn labun males.

10142. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿUthmah narrated to us, saying: Saʿid ibn Bashir narrated to us, from Qatadah, from ʿAbd Rabbih, from Abu ʿIyad, from ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan, may God be pleased with him. He said: And Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, from Zayd ibn Thabit, the like of it. [[The report 10142: "Abu ʿUthmah" is Muhammad ibn Khalid ibn ʿUthmah, known as Ibn ʿUthmah. A similar isnad occurred under no. 5314, and his biography appeared under nos. 90, 91, 5483 and 9587. In the printed edition here it read "Ibn ʿUthmah," and I have restored what is in the manuscript, in accordance with what preceded at no. 5314; see the note there.
"ʿAbd Rabbih" is ʿAbd Rabbih ibn Abi Yazid. ʿAli ibn al-Madini said: "ʿAbd Rabbih, from whom Qatadah narrated, is unknown; no one narrated from him except Qatadah." Al-Bukhari said in al-Tarikh: "His lineage was (traced to) Hammam." ʿAli said: "Ibn ʿUyaynah knew him; he said: he used to sell garments." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.
"Abu ʿIyad" is al-Madani, whose name and narrations are disputed; see his biography in al-Tahdhib. He narrates from ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, and Qatadah narrates from him. This report indicates that he also narrates from ʿUthman ibn ʿAffan.]]

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct position on this matter is that all agree that in pure unintentional killing, for the people of camels, the obligation is one hundred camels.

Then they differed about the ages of these camels, and they agreed that the one entitled to them is not to be given less than the lowest of the ages we mentioned, those ages which the people whose disagreement we mentioned set, and that he is not to be given more than the highest of them. [[In the printed and manuscript texts: "and that he is not to exceed with them the one who is entitled above their highest," which is not correct. I have made it follow the structure of what precedes, adding "in" and "to him."]] Since this is a consensus from all of them, it is necessary that whoever is liable for the blood-money of unintentional killing may discharge it by delivering whichever of these ages the differing scholars disagreed about, to the one entitled to it. Because God, exalted is He, has not fixed this with a limit that may not be exceeded or fallen short of, nor has His Messenger, except what I have mentioned of their consensus on what they agreed upon. The ruler (imam) may not exceed or fall short of that in his judgment, and he has the choice among what lies between, according to what he sees as beneficial for both parties.

* *

If the paternal kin (ʿaqilah) of the killer are from the people of gold, then the heirs of the slain are owed, according to us, one thousand dinars. This is the position of the scholars of the regions (amsar).

* *

Some said: that was an assessment by ʿUmar, may God have mercy on him, of camels in terms of gold among the people of gold in his time. It is necessary that its value be assessed in every age, when the killer's kin lack camels. They argued with the following:

10143. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Musa, from Makhul, who said: The blood-money used to rise and fall. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, died, it was eight hundred dinars. Then ʿUmar, after him, feared (that it might change), so he made it twelve thousand dirhams and one thousand dinars. [[See al-Sunan al-Kubra of al-Bayhaqi 8: 76-80.]]

* *

As for those who made it obligatory in every age on the people of gold as one thousand dinars in gold, they said: that is an obligation which God imposed through the tongue of His Messenger, just as He imposed camels on the people of camels. They said: The consensus of the scholars of the regions in every era and time, except for whoever deviated from them, that it is neither increased above one thousand dinars nor decreased below it, is the clearest evidence that it is obligatory on the people of gold just as camels are obligatory on the people of camels. For if it were the value of one hundred camels, it would vary by increase and decrease, because camel prices change.

This position is the truth on this matter, due to the consensus of the authority (hujjah) on it that we have mentioned.

* *

As for silver among the people of silver, according to us, it is twelve thousand dirhams. [[Al-wariq (with fatha, then kasra) and "al-warq" (with fatha or kasra, then sukun) and "al-riqah" (with kasra, then fatha): these are the minted dirhams.]] We have explained the reasons for this in our book, "Kitab Latif al-Qawl fi Ahkam Shara'i' al-Islam."

* *

Others said: For the people of silver, it is only ten thousand dirhams of silver.

As for the blood-money of the mu'ahad (a person under a treaty) with whom there is a covenant between us and his people, the scholars differed about its amount.

Some of them said: his blood-money and the blood-money of a free Muslim are the same.

Those who said this:

10144. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Sari narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Saʿd, from al-Zuhri: that Abu Bakr and ʿUthman, may God be pleased with them both, used to make the blood-money of a Jew or Christian, when they were under treaty, the same as that of a Muslim.

10145. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Sari narrated to us, from al-Dastawa'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from al-Hakam ibn ʿUyaynah: that Ibn Masʿud used to make the blood-money of the People of the Book, when they were dhimmis, the same as the blood-money of Muslims.

10146. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿbah narrated to us, from Hammad, who said: ʿAbd al-Hamid asked me about the blood-money of the People of the Book, and I informed him that Ibrahim said: Their blood-money and ours are equal.

10147. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Hammad narrated to us, from Ibrahim and Dawud, from al-Shaʿbi, that both of them said: The blood-money of a Jew, a Christian, and a Magian is like the blood-money of a free Muslim.

10148. Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: It used to be said: The blood-money of a Jew, a Christian, and a Magian is like the blood-money of a Muslim, when he has a dhimmah (protected status).

10149. Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Najih narrated to us, from Mujahid and ʿAta', that both of them said: The blood-money of the mu'ahad is the blood-money of a Muslim.

10150. Sawwar ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: al-Masʿudi narrated to us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, that he said: The blood-money of a Muslim and of a mu'ahad is equal.

10151. Yaʿqub narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Ayyub, who said: I heard al-Zuhri say: The blood-money of a dhimmi is the blood-money of a Muslim.

10152. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from ʿAmir, who said: The blood-money of a dhimmi is like the blood-money of a Muslim.

10153. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Saʿid ibn Abi ʿArubah, from Abu Maʿshar, from Ibrahim, the like of it.

10154. Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, the like of it. [[Report 10154: In both the printed and manuscript texts this isnad was joined to the next one as follows: "from Ibrahim, who said: ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to us," which is an error. "Ibrahim" is al-Nakha'i, who appeared in the earlier reports. "ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Bayan" is al-Sukkari al-Qanna'd, the shaykh of Abu Jaʿfar. It seems to me that the copyist put "qal" (he said) in place of "mithlahu" (the like of it), and I have restored it to what is required.]]

10155. ʿAbd al-Hamid ibn Bayan narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yazid informed us, from Isma'il, from ʿAmir, who was informed that al-Hasan used to say: "The blood-money of a Magian is eight hundred, and the blood-money of a Jew and a Christian is four thousand." He said: Their blood-money is one.

10156. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from al-Shaʿbi, who said: The blood-money of a mu'ahad and of a Muslim are equal in their expiation.

10157. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, who said: The blood-money of a mu'ahad and of a Muslim is equal.

* *

Others said: Rather, his blood-money is half the blood-money of a Muslim.

Those who said this:

10158. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Dawud narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb, concerning the blood-money of a Jew and a Christian, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, made it half the blood-money of a Muslim, and the blood-money of a Magian eight hundred. I said to ʿAmr ibn Shuʿayb: "al-Hasan says: four thousand!" He said: That was before the "ghilmah" [[In the printed text it read "perhaps that was before," omitting "al-ghilmah" and adding "perhaps" at the beginning of the sentence, which is a poor practice. I have kept what is in the manuscript as it is, and I do not know what was intended, so I leave it to someone who knows.]] and said: He only made the blood-money of a Magian equal to that of a slave.

10159. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Zinad, from ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, who said: The blood-money of a mu'ahad is half the blood-money of a Muslim.

* *

Others said: Rather, his blood-money is one-third of the blood-money of a Muslim.

Those who said this:

10160. Wasil ibn ʿAbd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Mutarrif, from Abu ʿUthman, who said, and he was a judge for the people of Marw: ʿUmar, may God be pleased with him, made the blood-money of a Jew and a Christian four thousand, four thousand.

10161. ʿAmmar ibn Khalid al-Wasiti narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Saʿid narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Thabit, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, who said: ʿUmar said: The blood-money of a Christian is four thousand, and of a Magian eight hundred.

10162. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Thabit, who said: I heard Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab say: ʿUmar said: The blood-money of the People of the Book is four thousand, and the blood-money of a Magian eight hundred.

10163. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Thabit, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab: that ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said, and he mentioned the like of it.

10164. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from Saʿid, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Malih: that a man from his people shot a Jew or a Christian with an arrow and killed him, and the matter was brought to ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, and he obliged him to pay his blood-money, four thousand.

10165. And with it, from Qatadah, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, who said: ʿUmar said: The blood-money of a Jew and a Christian is four thousand, four thousand.

10166. Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Some of our companions informed us, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab, from ʿUmar, the like of it.

10167. He said: Hushaym narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from ʿAta', from ʿUmar, the like of it.

10168. He said: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Saʿid informed us, from Sulayman ibn Yasar, that he said: The blood-money of a Jew and a Christian is four thousand, and of a Magian eight hundred.

10169. Sawwar ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: Khalid ibn al-Harith narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, from ʿAta', the like of it.

10170. It was reported to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak concerning His words: "But whoever does not find, then fasting for two consecutive months," (he said): The fast is for one who does not find a slave, but as for the blood-money, it is an obligation that nothing cancels.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿So whoever does not find (the means), then fasting for two consecutive months as a repentance from God. And God is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ (4:92)

Abu Jaʿfar said: God, may His remembrance be exalted, by His saying, "So whoever does not find," means: whoever does not find a believing slave to free as an expiation for his error in killing someone, whether a believer or one under treaty, because of his straitened means to pay its price, "then fasting for two consecutive months." That is, then upon him is fasting for two consecutive months.

* *

The people of interpretation differed on the explanation of this.

Some of them said something similar to what we have said.

Those who said this:

10171. Muhammad ibn ʿAmr narrated to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, from ʿIsa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's saying: "So whoever does not find, then fasting for two consecutive months," he said: Whoever does not find emancipation, or ʿitaqah (Abu ʿAsim doubted which word), in the case of killing a believer by mistake. He said: It was revealed concerning ʿAyyash ibn Abi Rabiʿah, who killed a believer by mistake. [["al-ʿitaqah" (with fatha on the ʿayn) is the verbal noun of "ʿataqa al-ʿabd yaʿtiqu ʿitqan wa ʿitaqan wa ʿitaqah." See "al-ʿitaqah" in the commentary on the earlier report no. 9265.]]

* *

Others said: Fasting the two months is in place of both the blood-money and the slave. They said: The interpretation of the verse is: whoever does not find a believing slave, nor blood-money to deliver to its people, then upon him is fasting for two consecutive months.

Those who said this:

10172. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from al-Shaʿbi, from Masruq: that he was asked about the verse in "Surat al-Nisa'": "So whoever does not find, then fasting for two consecutive months." Is the fasting of the two months in place of the slave alone, or in place of both the blood-money and the slave? He said: Whoever does not find (the means), then it is in place of both the blood-money and the slave.

10173. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from ʿAmir, from Masruq, similarly.

* *

Abu Jaʿfar said: The correct position on this matter is that the fasting is in place of the slave, not the blood-money, because the blood-money for unintentional killing is upon the paternal kin (ʿaqilah) of the killer, while the expiation is upon the killer himself, by the consensus (ijma') of the authority (hujjah) on this, transmitted from their Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. [[In the printed text: "from our Prophet," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] So the fasting of one who fasts does not discharge what is obligatory on another in his property.

* *

"Al-Mutabaʿah" (consecutiveness) means fasting the two months and not breaking it by fasting only some of its days, except for an excuse that prevents him from his fast. [[In the printed text: "and not breaking it," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

* *

Then He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿as a repentance from God. And God is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ That is, a pardon from God for you, leading to ease for you, by His lightening for you what He lightened of the obligation to free a believing slave when you are unable to do so, by His imposing upon you fasting two consecutive months. "And God is ever Knowing": that is, God has never ceased to be knowing of what benefits His servants in what He imposes on them of His obligations and other things. "Wise": that is, in what He decides concerning them and wills. [[See the explanation of "al-tawbah" (repentance), "kana," "ʿalim" (knowing) and "hakim" (wise) under their roots in the lexical indices of the earlier volumes.]]

The interpretation of His words, exalted is He: ﴿Whoever kills a believer deliberately, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein; and Allah is angry with him, and curses him, and has prepared for him a great punishment﴾ [4:93].

Abu Ja'far said: Its meaning, may His praise be exalted: whoever kills a believer deliberately, intending to destroy his soul, ﴿his recompense is Hell﴾, meaning: his reward for having killed him is [[See the explanation of "recompense" (al-jaza') above: 2:27, 28, 314 / 6:576.]] ﴿Hell﴾, meaning: the punishment of Hell. ﴿Abiding therein﴾, meaning: remaining in it [[See the explanation of "abiding" (al-khulud) above: 6:577, note 2, and the references there.]]. The "hA'" and the "alif" in His words ﴿therein﴾ refer to "Hell." ﴿And Allah is angry with him﴾, meaning: Allah is angry with him for killing him deliberately [[See the explanation of "the anger of Allah" above: 1:188, 189 / 2:138, 347 / 7:116.]]. ﴿And curses him﴾, meaning: He removes him from His mercy and disgraces him [[See the explanation of "the curse" (al-la'nah) above: 2:328, 329 / 3:254, 261 / 6:577 / 8:439, 471.]]. ﴿And has prepared for him a great punishment﴾, and no one knows the measure of its extent except Allah, may His remembrance be exalted.

* *

The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the nature of the killing that makes its perpetrator deserve to be called "deliberate," after all of them agreed (ijma', scholarly consensus) that if a man strikes another with an iron implement that wounds with its edge, or that cuts and slices ["bada'a al-lahma yabda'uhu": he cut the flesh], and he does not desist from striking him with it until he destroys his soul, while he intends to strike him at the time of striking him with it, then he is a deliberate killer. Then they differed regarding what lies beyond that. Some of them said: there is no deliberate killing except what is of this description that we have described.

Those who said that:

10174. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: 'Ata' said: "al-'Amd" is the weapon [or he said: the iron]. He said: And Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab said: It is the weapon.

10175. Abu Kurayb and Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, both saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: The deliberate killing is what is done with an iron implement, and what is done with less than an iron implement is quasi-deliberate (shibh al-'amd), there is no qawad (retaliation) in it.

10176. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: The deliberate killing is what is done with an iron implement, and quasi-deliberate is what is done with a piece of wood. Quasi-deliberate does not occur except concerning the soul. [An omission in numbering: 10177.]

10178. Ahmad ibn Hammad al-Dulabi narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Tawus, who said: Whoever kills in a tribal dispute, by throwing stones among them, or by striking with whips, or by beating with a stick, it is a mistake (khata'), and its blood-money is the blood-money of a mistake.
