And whoever kills deliberately, there is qawad of his hand. [In the printed edition: "qawad yadayh" (retaliation of his hands); I have kept what is in the manuscript. His words "qawad yadihi" mean: retaliation for what his hand committed.]

10179. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir and Mughirah narrated to us, from al-Harith and his companions, concerning a man who strikes a man and he becomes ill until he dies. He said: I ask the witnesses whether he struck him, and he remained ill from his blow until he died. If it was with a weapon then it is qawad, and if it was by other than that then it is quasi-deliberate.

* *

Others said: every act by which the striker intends to destroy the soul of the one struck is deliberate, provided that what he struck him with is, for the most part, something that kills. [In the printed and manuscript texts: "idha kana alladhi darabahu al-aghlab" — the context requires the inclusion of "bihi" (with it), which I have included here.]

Those who said that:

10180. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yahya informed us, from Hibban ibn Abi Jabalah, from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, that he said: What deliberateness is more deliberate than striking a man with a stick and not desisting from him until he dies?

[Note on 10180: Hibban ibn Abi Jabalah al-Qurashi, their mawla (client), the Egyptian. He narrated from 'Amr ibn al-'As and the 'Abadilah except Ibn al-Zubayr; his biography passed under number 2195. As for "'Abd al-Rahman ibn Yahya," I do not know who he is, and I fear that the correct reading is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn An'am, who is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ziyad ibn An'am ibn Dhuri ibn Yahmad al-Ifriqi, whose biography passed under number 2195, and who also narrated from Hibban ibn Abi Jabalah.]

10181. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Abu Hashim, from Ibrahim, who said: If he strangles him with a rope until he dies, or strikes him with a piece of wood until he dies, then it is qawad.

* *

The reasoning of those who said "everything other than iron is a mistake" is what follows:

10182. Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Abu 'A'idh, from al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, who said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "Everything is a mistake except the sword, and for every mistake there is a compensation (arsh)." [Note on 10182: Sufyan is al-Thawri. Jabir is Ibn Yazid al-Ju'fi, who is very weak, accused of lying, as we explained at 2340. Abu 'A'idh is an unknown Kufan man. It was said his name is "Muslim ibn 'Amr," and it was said "Muslim ibn Arak." Only Jabir al-Ju'fi narrated from him, and al-Harith ibn Ziyad. As for al-Harith ibn Ziyad, he is unknown; Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned him, and narrated from his father that he said, "He is unknown." Al-Bukhari did not mention him. As for Abu 'A'idh, al-Bukhari mentioned him in al-Kabir, and Ibn Abi Hatim too, both under the name "Muslim ibn 'Amr." Despite this, he remains unknown, for no well-known trustworthy narrator narrated from him. The hadith was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (4:272, Halabi edition) from Wakf', with this chain, but with the wording "li-kull shay' khata'" (with the lam on "kull"). Then he narrated it (4:275, Halabi) from Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Malik, from Zuhayr, from Jabir (al-Ju'fi), with the wording "kull shay' khata' illa al-sayf, wa-fi kull khata' arsh." Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (8:42) through three chains, through Jabir al-Ju'fi; then he narrated it by another chain, through Qays ibn al-Rabi', from Abu Husayn, from Ibrahim ibn Bint al-Nu'man ibn Bashir, from al-Nu'man. Then he said: "The hadith revolves around Jabir al-Ju'fi and Qays ibn al-Rabi', and they are not used as proof." Al-Zayla'i mentioned it in Nasb al-Rayah (4:333), from the Musnad narration, and criticized it with what the author of al-Tanqih said: "In any case, Abu 'A'idh is not known." Then he quoted its criticism from al-Bayhaqi in al-Ma'rifah, similar to what he criticized it with in al-Sunan al-Kubra, and did not comment on either.]

* *

The reasoning of those who said "the ruling for whatever the struck person is killed by is the ruling of the sword, in that whoever is killed by it is a victim of deliberate killing" is what follows:

10183. Ibn Bashshar narrated it to us, saying: Abu al-Walid narrated to us, saying: Hammam narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik: that a Jew killed a girl for her ornaments (awda')  between two stones, so he was brought to the Prophet ﷺ, and he had him killed between two stones. [Note on 10183: This is an abridgement of a sound hadith agreed upon (muttafaq 'alayh). Al-Bukhari (12:174-175, 187-188) and Muslim (2:27) narrated it, both through Hammam, from Qatadah, from Anas. Al-Bukhari also narrated it (12:176, 180) and Muslim (2:26-27) from other routes from Anas. Ibn Taymiyyah al-Majd mentioned it in al-Muntaqa (3915) and said: "The group narrated it," meaning Imam Ahmad and the authors of the six books. "Al-awda'" is the plural of "wadh'" (with two fathahs), which is the sound dirham. Then ornaments were made from sound silver dirhams, and so they were called "awda'."]

* *

They said: So the Prophet ﷺ imposed retaliation on the killer with a stone, and that is not iron. They said: Likewise the ruling for everyone who kills a man with something that, for the most part, kills the like of the one killed by it, is the same as the ruling for the Jew who killed the girl between the two stones.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct position in this matter, in our view, is the statement of the one who said: Whoever strikes a person with something that for the most part destroys him, and does not desist from him until he destroys his soul with it, is a killer by deliberation, whatever the thing he was struck with, on account of the report we mentioned from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. [His words "whatever the thing he was struck with" mean: whatever thing it was that he was struck with.]

* *

As for His words: ﴿his recompense is Hell, abiding therein﴾, the interpreters differed regarding its meaning. Some of them said its meaning is: his recompense is Hell, if He recompenses him.

Those who said that:

10184. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Mijlaz, concerning His words, ﴿Whoever kills a believer deliberately, his recompense is Hell﴾, he said: That is his recompense, and if He wills, He may pardon him.

10185. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Nu'man al-Hakam ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Yasar, from Abu Salih: ﴿Whoever kills a believer deliberately, his recompense is Hell﴾, he said: His recompense is Hell, if He recompenses him.

* *

Others said: this refers to a particular man who had embraced Islam and then apostatized from his Islam, and killed a believing man. They said: So the meaning of the verse is: whoever kills a believer deliberately, considering his killing lawful, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein.

Those who said that:

10186. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ikrimah: that a man from the Ansar killed the brother of Miqyas ibn Subabah. The Prophet ﷺ gave him the blood-money, and he accepted it. Then he attacked the killer of his brother and killed him. [Ibn Jurayj said: Another said: The Prophet ﷺ fixed his blood-money upon the Banu al-Najjar. Then he sent Miqyas, and sent with him a man from the Banu Fihr on an errand for the Prophet ﷺ. Miqyas took the Fihri, and he was strong ["ayyidan" — strong, from "al-ayd," the firmness and power], and struck him against the ground, and crushed his head between two stones. Then he found himself chanting:

I took vengeance on Fihr through him, and I carried his blood-money
to the chiefs of the Banu al-Najjar, the lords of Fari'.

[Note: Sirah Ibn Hisham 3:305-306; Tarikh al-Tabari 3:66; Mu'jam al-Buldan (Fari'). These are the last of four verses, which are: "It soothed the soul that he spent the night at al-Qa' reclining, his two garments dyed with the blood of the nape-veins..." "And the cares of the soul before his killing used to trouble me, preventing me the comfort of the bed..." "I dissolved my debt through him, and attained my vengeance, and I was the first to return to the idols..." "I took vengeance on Fihr through him..." (The printed and manuscript texts had "qatalat bihi Fihran" — "I killed through him Fihr," which is not correct; the killer of his brother was Hisham ibn Subabah, whose name they say was "Aws," not "Fihr." As for "Fihr" in "tha'irtu bihi Fihran," it means the sons of Fihr, his kinsmen, whose vengeance he attained by killing the Ansari. In the Tarikh al-Tabari printed edition it is "Qahran" with a qaf, but the correct form is with the fa'. "Fari'" is a fortress in Medina of the Banu al-Najjar, which belonged to Hassan ibn Thabit, may Allah have mercy on him, and he mentioned it in his poetry.]

Then the Prophet ﷺ said: "I think he has committed a wrongdoing! By Allah, if he did it, I will not grant him safety, in sanctuary or outside it, in peace or in war!" So he was killed on the day of the Conquest. Ibn Jurayj said: It was concerning this that this verse was revealed: ﴿Whoever kills a believer deliberately﴾, the verse.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: except one who repents.

Those who said that:

10187. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to me, or: al-Hakam narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas about His words, ﴿Whoever kills a believer deliberately, his recompense is Hell﴾, and he said: If a man knows Islam and the laws of Islam, then kills a believer deliberately, his recompense is Hell, and there is no repentance for him. I mentioned that to Mujahid, and he said: "Except one who regrets."

* *

Others said: that is a decree from Allah of the threat for the killer of a believer deliberately, whoever the killer may be, as He described it in His Book, and He did not make repentance for his act possible. They said: So every believer who is deliberately killed by someone, for him is what Allah threatened of punishment and abiding in the Fire, and there is no repentance for him. They said: This verse was revealed after the one in "Surat al-Furqan."

Those who said that:

10188. Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Yahya al-Jabir, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, who said: We were with Ibn 'Abbas after his sight had gone. A man came to him and called out: "O 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas, what is your opinion of a man who killed a believer deliberately?" He said: ﴿His recompense is Hell, abiding therein, and Allah is angry with him, and curses him, and has prepared for him a great punishment﴾. The man said: "What do you think if he repents, believes, does righteous deeds, and then is guided?" Ibn 'Abbas said: "May his mother be bereaved of him! And how would he have repentance and guidance? By Him in whose hand is my soul, I heard your Prophet ﷺ say: 'May his mother be bereaved of him! A man who killed a man deliberately will come on the Day of Resurrection, taking hold of his killer with his right hand or his left, his veins gushing blood, at the front of the Throne of the Merciful, and the one who killed him will grasp him with his other hand, saying: Ask this one why he killed me!' By Him in whose hand is the soul of 'Abd Allah, this verse was revealed, and nothing abrogated it from any verse until your Prophet ﷺ passed away, and no proof came down after it."

[Note on 10188: "Yahya al-Jabir" is "Yahya ibn al-Mujabbir," who is Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith al-Mujabbir al-Taymi; my brother Sayyid Ahmad (Shakir) declared him trustworthy in the Musnad. Ahmad narrated it in the Musnad, number 2142, in full, and it is a sound hadith, through Muhammad ibn Ja'far from Shu'bah, from Yahya ibn al-Mujabbir al-Taymi. Then he narrated it under number 2683, and narrated it in abridged form under numbers 1941 and 3445. See Ibn Kathir 2:537-539. His words "tashkhabu awdajuhu dman" mean: his veins flow with blood that makes a sound as it comes out; "al-shakhb" is what comes out from under the hand of the milker at each squeeze of the ewe's udder, and its exit makes a sound during milking. "Al-awdaj" is the plural of "wadj" (two fathahs), which are the veins that surround the throat and the veins around the neck that the slaughterer cuts. His words "fi qubul 'arsh al-Rahman" — "qubul" (with a damma and sukun), or (two fathahs), or (two dammas), all of which are permissible, and it means the front, or what faces you of something, and by it is meant what is before the Throne where the observer faces it.]

10189. Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Qays, from Yahya ibn al-Harith al-Taymi, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Whoever kills a believer deliberately, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein, and Allah is angry with him, and curses him, and has prepared for him a great punishment." It was said to him: "And if he repents, believes, and does righteous deeds?" He said: "How could he have repentance?"

[Note on 10189: "Abu Khalid" is al-Ahmar, Sulayman ibn Hayyan al-Azdi, which passed under number 3956; Sufyan ibn Wakf's narration from him is under number 2472. "'Amr ibn Qays al-Mala'i" passed several times; see number 3956. "Yahya ibn al-Harith al-Taymi" is "Yahya al-Jabir," and "Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith" was ascribed to his grandfather, and passed in the earlier narration. This narration is an abridgement of the preceding one.]

10190. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Musa ibn Dawud narrated to us, saying: Hammam narrated to us, from Yahya, from a man, from Salim, who said: I was sitting with Ibn 'Abbas when a man asked him, saying: "What do you think of a man who killed a believer deliberately, where is his abode?" He said: "Hell, abiding therein, and Allah is angry with him, and curses him, and has prepared for him a great punishment." The man said: "What do you think if he repents, believes, does righteous deeds, and then is guided?" He said: "And how would he have guidance? May his mother be bereaved of him! By Him in whose hand is my soul, I heard him say—meaning the Prophet ﷺ—that he will come on the Day of Resurrection hanging his head by one of his hands, either his right or his left, taking his companion with the other hand, his veins gushing blood before the Throne of the Merciful, saying: 'O Lord, ask Your servant here why he killed me!' No prophet has come after your Prophet, and no book has been revealed after your Book."

[Note on 10190: "Musa ibn Dawud al-Dabbi al-Tarsusi," one of the teachers of Ahmad and 'Ali ibn al-Madini; trustworthy, a man of hadith, who held the judgeship of Tarsus until he died there. "Hammam" is Ibn Yahya ibn Dinar al-Azdi, who narrated from 'Ata', Qatadah, and Ibn Sirin, and narrated from al-Thawri, being of his contemporaries; trustworthy. This narration is another route for the preceding narration with the same meaning, and it places "a man" between Yahya al-Jabir and Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd; since Yahya did hear from Salim, it does no harm that he also heard it from a man who heard it from Salim.]

1019191- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Qabisah related to us, saying: Ammar ibn Ruzayq related to us, from Ammar al-Dahni, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ibn Abbas, with something similar, except that in his narration he said: "By God, it was revealed to your Prophet, and then nothing abrogated it. I heard him say: Woe to the killer of a believer; he will come on the Day of Resurrection holding his head in his hand." Then he mentioned the narration, similar to it. [[Report 10191: "Ammar ibn Ruzayq al-Dabbi," Abu al-Ahwas. He narrated from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i, al-A'mash, Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, and others. Ibn Ma'in said: thiqah (trustworthy). He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. In the printed edition, it was "Aman ibn Zurayq" with an "n" in "Ammar" and the "z" placed before the "r," which is an error.]]

1019192- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi related to us, from Sa'id, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza said to me: Ibn Abbas was asked about His saying: "And whoever kills a believer deliberately, his recompense is Hell," and he said: "Nothing has abrogated it." And regarding this verse he said: ﴿And those who do not invoke with God another deity, nor kill the soul which God has forbidden, except by right, nor commit adultery—and whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾ [Surah al-Furqan: 68]. He said: It was revealed concerning the people of polytheism.

1019193- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Mansur, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza commanded me to ask Ibn Abbas about these two verses, and he mentioned something similar. [[Reports 10192–10193: Related by Muslim (18:158) and al-Bukhari (Fath 8:380) through the chain of Muhammad ibn Bashshar and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, like the second isnad.]]

1019194- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Talq ibn Ghannam related to us, from Za'idah, from Mansur, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr related to me, or: I was told from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza commanded him to ask Ibn Abbas about these two verses in "al-Nisa'": "And whoever kills a believer deliberately, his recompense is Hell," to the end of the verse; and the one in "al-Furqan": ﴿And whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾, to ﴿and will abide in it humiliated﴾. Ibn Abbas said: If a man has entered Islam, learned its laws and its commands, and then kills a believer deliberately, there is no repentance for him. As for the one in "al-Furqan": when it was revealed, the polytheists of Mecca said: "We have associated others with God, we have killed the soul which God has forbidden except by right, and we have committed abominations, so what good is Islam to us?" He said: Then it was revealed: ﴿except for one who repents﴾, the verse. [[Report 10194: Related by al-Bukhari (Fath 8:379) and Muslim (18:159). Al-Bukhari related it through Sa'd ibn Hafs, from Shaybaan, from Mansur. Muslim related it through Harun ibn Abd Allah, from Abu al-Nadr Hashim ibn al-Qasim al-Laythi, from Abu Mu'awiyah Shaybaan. The manuscript omitted "and committed abominations," and it does not contain the word "the verse" at the end of the report.]]

1019195- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from al-Mughirah ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: "And whoever kills a believer deliberately, his recompense is Hell," he said: "Nothing has abrogated it."

1019196- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from al-Mughirah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "It is among the last things revealed; nothing has abrogated it."

1019197- Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from al-Mughirah ibn al-Nu'man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The people of Kufa disagreed about the killing of a believer, so I went to Ibn Abbas and asked him, and he said: "It was revealed among the last of what was revealed of the Qur'an, and nothing has abrogated it." [[Reports 10195–10197: Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (Fath 8/379) and Muslim (18:158). Ibn Hajar thoroughly discussed them in al-Fath. In the printed edition it read "It was revealed among the last of what was revealed," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]]

1019198- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Adam al-Asqalani related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, saying: Abu Iyas Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah related to us, saying: Shahr ibn Hawshab informed me, saying: I heard Ibn Abbas say: This verse, "And whoever kills a believer deliberately, his recompense is Hell," was revealed after His saying: ﴿except for one who repents and believes and does righteous work﴾, by a year.

1019199- Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Salm ibn Qutaybah related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, from Mu'awiyah ibn Qurrah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "And whoever kills a believer deliberately, his recompense is Hell": it was revealed after ﴿except for one who repents﴾, by a year.

1019200- Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Abd al-Samad ibn Abd al-Warith related to us, saying: Shu'bah related to us, saying: Abu Iyas related to us, saying: Someone who heard Ibn Abbas say about the killer of a believer informed me: "It was revealed a year after that." I said to Abu Iyas: Who informed you? He said: Shahr ibn Hawshab.

1019201- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "And whoever kills a believer deliberately," he said: "There is no repentance for the killer, except that he seek God's forgiveness."

1019202- Muhammad ibn Sa'd related to me, saying: My father related to me, saying: My paternal uncle related to me, saying: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, his saying: "And whoever kills a believer deliberately," the verse. Ata' said: Ibn Abbas was asked about it, and he asserted that it was revealed a full eight years after the verse in "Surat al-Furqan," which is His saying: ﴿And those who do not invoke with God another deity﴾, to His saying: ﴿Forgiving and merciful﴾.

1019203- Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Sufyan, from Mutarrif, from Abu al-Safar, from Najiyah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "They are the two mubhamatan: polytheism and killing." [[By "mubhamatan" he means the two verses from which there is no exit, as if they were a closed, locked door, that is, shut and not opened, with no way in. Polytheism and killing have as their penalty eternal abiding in the fire of Hell; may God protect us from it. Similar is the hadith: "Four are mubhamat: the vow, marriage, divorce, and emancipation," and another narration explained it as "four are muqfalat," meaning there is no exit from them, as if they were locked doors. The meaning of "mubham" was previously discussed in volume 8, page 143, note 2, with a different meaning, so refer to it.]]

1019204- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The greatest of the major sins are associating partners with God and killing a soul which God has forbidden, because God, glorified is He, says: "Its recompense is Hell, abiding therein, and God's wrath is upon him, and He has cursed him and prepared for him a great punishment."

1019205- Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Amr ibn Awn related to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from some of his Kufan teachers, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from Ibn Mas'ud regarding His saying: "And whoever kills a believer deliberately, his recompense is Hell," he said: "It is indeed definitive (muhkamah), and it only grows in severity."

1019206- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Uthman ibn Sa'id related to us, saying: Hayyaj ibn Bistam related to me, from Muhammad ibn Amr, from Musa ibn Uqbah, from Abu al-Zinad, from Kharijah ibn Zayd, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: "Surat al-Nisa'" was revealed six months after "Surat al-Furqan." [[Report 10206: "Hayyaj ibn Bistam al-Harawi"; his biography appeared under number 9603.]]

1019207- Ibn al-Barqi related to us, saying: Ibn Abi Maryam related to us, saying: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed us, saying: Abu Sakhr related to me, from Abu Mu'awiyah al-Bajali, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn Abbas said: "The one who was killed will come on the Day of Resurrection holding his head in his right hand, and his veins gushing blood, saying: 'O Lord, my blood is with so-and-so!' Then both will be seized and brought to the Throne, and I do not know what will be decided between them." Then he recited this verse: "And whoever kills a believer deliberately, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein," the verse. Ibn Abbas said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, God, mighty and majestic, has not abrogated it since He revealed it to your Prophet, peace be upon him." [[Report 10207: "Ibn al-Barqi" is Ahmad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi, mentioned earlier under number 22; the printed edition had "Ibn al-Raqi," which is an error. "Ibn Abi Maryam" is Sa'id ibn al-Hakam ibn Muhammad ibn Salim al-Jumahi, mentioned under number 22 and elsewhere. This report is missing from the manuscript.]]

1019208- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Adam related to us, from Ibn Uyaynah, from Abu al-Zinad, who said: I heard a man narrating to Kharijah ibn Zayd ibn Thabit, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: I heard your father say: "The severe was revealed after the lenient, by six months: His saying: 'And whoever kills a believer deliberately,' to the end of the verse, after His saying: ﴿And those who do not invoke with God another deity﴾, to the end of the verse [Surat al-Furqan, 68]."

1019209- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Abu al-Zinad, who said: I heard a man narrating to Kharijah ibn Zayd, saying: I heard your father in this place in Mina say: "The severe was revealed after the lenient." He said: I think: "by six months," meaning: "And whoever kills a believer deliberately" after: ﴿Indeed, God does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 48, 116].

1019210- Ibn Waki' related to us, saying: My father related to us, from Salamah ibn Nubayt, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, who said: "Nothing has abrogated it since it was revealed, and there is no repentance for him."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the opinions on this matter is the view of the one who said: its meaning is: "And whoever kills a believer deliberately, his recompense, if He recompenses him, is Hell, abiding therein. However, He pardons and graciously favors the people of faith in Him and His Messenger, so He does not punish them with eternal abiding in it. Rather, He, mighty is His remembrance, either pardons them by His grace and does not admit them to the Fire, or admits them to it and then brings them out of it by the grace of His mercy, in fulfillment of His promise to His believing servants in His saying: ﴿O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives all sins﴾ [Surat al-Zumar: 53].

* *

If someone supposes that if the killer must be included in this verse, then the polytheist must also be included in it, since polytheism is one of the sins, [the objection being that] God, mighty is His remembrance, has informed that He does not forgive polytheism for anyone, by His saying: ﴿Indeed, God does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 48, 116], and killing is less than polytheism. [[In the manuscript: "and we do not accept less than polytheism," which is a pure error; the printed text is the correct one.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 94 (part 1 of 3):**

**On the interpretation of His words:** ﴿O you who have believed, when you go forth [to fight] in the way of Allah, investigate carefully, and do not say to one who gives you [a greeting of] peace, "You are not a believer," seeking the goods of worldly life. For with Allah are abundant spoils. Thus were you before, and Allah conferred His favor upon you. So investigate carefully. Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted.﴾ (4:94)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari's kunya) said: By His saying, "O you who have believed," He, may His praise be exalted, means: O you who have affirmed Allah and affirmed His Messenger in what came to them from their Lord. "When you go forth in the way of Allah" means: when you set out on a journey for Allah, to fight your enemies [[See the explanation of "sabil Allah" (the way of Allah) earlier, p. 17, note 4, and the references there.]]. "Investigate carefully" means: be deliberate in killing the one whose situation is unclear to you, when you do not know the reality of his Islam or his disbelief, and do not hasten to kill one whose case is ambiguous to you. Do not proceed to kill anyone except one whom you know with certainty to be an enemy of you, of Allah and of His Messenger. [[In the manuscript it reads "فلما تعلموا" ("when you do not know"), which is an error.]] "And do not say to one who gives you [a greeting of] peace [*al-salam*]" [[In the printed edition here it read "al-salam", as in our Qur'an today. *Al-salam* means the greeting, and this is one of the two readings. But Abu Ja'far's subsequent explanation is of *al-salm*, meaning submission and compliance, which is the other reading that he chose. So writing it here as "al-salam" is an error, and the meaning does not stand by his explanation.]] He means: do not say to one who submits to you and does not fight you, showing you that he is of the people of your religion and your call, "You are not a believer," so that you kill him, seeking "the goods of worldly life." He means: seeking the enjoyment of the goods of this worldly life [[See the explanation of "al-ibtigha'" (seeking) earlier, vol. 8, p. 316, note 1, and the references there.]]. "For with Allah are abundant spoils" means: from His provision and the abundant bounties of His favors. These are better for you if you obey Allah in what He commanded you and forbade you, so that He rewards you for your obedience to Him. So seek that from Him. "Thus were you before" means: just as this man to whom you gave [a greeting of] peace, and to whom you said, "You are not a believer," and whom you then killed, so were you yourselves before. That is, before Allah strengthened His religion through His followers and helpers, you concealed your religion, just as this man you killed and whose property you took concealed his religion from his people, for fear of himself from them, lest he reveal it to them. It has also been said that the meaning of His saying, "Thus were you before," is: you were disbelievers like them. "Then Allah conferred His favor upon you" means: He bestowed His grace upon you by strengthening His religion through His helpers and the abundance of His followers. It has also been said: Allah conferred His favor upon you by granting you repentance for this killing of yours, of the man you killed and whose property you took after he had given you [a greeting of] peace [[In the printed edition it read "al-salam", and see the earlier note, p. 70, no. 4.]]. "So investigate carefully" means: do not hasten to kill the one you intend to kill, whose Islam is unclear to you, for perhaps Allah has already bestowed upon him Islam with the same favor He bestowed upon you, and guided him to the same faith to which He guided you. [[See the explanation of "min" (from/with) earlier, vol. 7, p. 369.]] "Indeed, Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted" means: indeed, Allah is aware of your killing of those you kill, and of your restraint from those you refrain from killing among the enemies of Allah and your enemies, and other of your affairs and the affairs of others. "Acquainted" means: possessing knowledge and awareness of it, preserving it for you and against you, until all of you are recompensed for it on the Day of Resurrection: the doer of good rewarded for his good, and the doer of evil for his evil. [[In the printed edition: "jaza' al-muhsin bi-ihsanihi.." ("the recompense of the doer of good for his goodness..."), which is not correct; the right reading is from the manuscript.]]

* * *

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a man killed by a detachment (*sariyyah*) sent by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, after he had said, "I am a Muslim," or after he had testified to the truth, or after he had greeted them with the salam, for a herd of livestock that he had with him, or some other property of his, which they took from him.

**The narrations and reports concerning this:** [[In the printed edition: "wa-al-athar bi-dhalika", and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]

**10211.** Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: The Prophet ﷺ sent Muhallim ibn Jaththamah on an expedition. He met them, and 'Amir ibn al-Adbat greeted them with the greeting of Islam. There had been a grudge (*hinnah*) between them in the Jahiliyyah [[In the printed edition: "ihnah fi al-jahiliyyah", which is correct; *al-ihnah* means rancor in the chest, from *ahinna*. As for *hinnah* as it is in the manuscript, it derives from *wahn*, and also means rancor. This word was annotated earlier, where it occurred in report no. 2195, vol. 3, pp. 152–153, note 2. There I mentioned al-Asma'i's denial of *hinnah*, and al-Azhari's claim that it is not from the speech of the Arabs. This is further evidence for the correctness of this word, and that what al-Azhari said is worthless.]]. So Muhallim shot him with an arrow and killed him. The news reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and 'Uyaynah and al-Aqra' spoke about it. Al-Aqra' said: O Messenger of Allah, establish a precedent today and change it tomorrow! [[In Ibn Kathir (2:546): "sir al-yawm wa-ghir ghadan" ("travel today and deceive tomorrow"), which is a plain error.]] 'Uyaynah said: No, by Allah, until his women taste the bereavement that my women have tasted. [[In the manuscript: "hatta tadhuqa bukaa'ahu" ("until his weeping tastes..."), which is a scribal distortion; the correct reading is from the context and from Ibn Kathir's tafsir.]] Then Muhallim came wearing two cloaks [[In the manuscript: "fi burd" ("in a cloak"), and the correct reading is from Ibn Kathir, as corrected in the printed edition from the context of the report.]], and sat before the Messenger of Allah to ask forgiveness for him. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: May Allah not forgive you! So he rose, weeping, wiping his tears with his two cloaks. Not seven days had passed before he died. They buried him, but the earth expelled him. They came to the Prophet ﷺ and informed him of that. He said: Indeed, the earth accepts one who is worse than your companion! But Allah, mighty and majestic, wished to admonish you. Then they cast him between two cliffs ("*sadfayn*" of a mountain) [["Al-sadf" (with two fathas) is the side of the mountain that faces you. *Al-sadf* is also every tall, great thing, like a wall or a mountain.]], and threw stones upon him. And there was revealed: "O you who have believed, when you go forth in the way of Allah, investigate carefully," to the end of the verse. [[Report 10211: in Ibn Kathir 2:546; also cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:200, abridged.]]

**10212.** Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Abd Allah ibn Qusayt [[In the printed edition: "'an Yazid 'an 'Abd Allah ibn Qusayt", which is an error; the correct reading is from the manuscript and all other sources.]], from Abu al-Qa'qa' ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad al-Aslami, from his father Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent us to Idam. [["Idam" is a valley that cuts through the Hijaz until it empties into the sea, from near Medina; it is a valley of the Ashja' and Juhaynah.]] I set out with a group of Muslims, among whom were Abu Qatadah al-Harith ibn Rib'i and Muhallim ibn Jaththamah ibn Qays al-Laythi. We set out until, when we were in the lowland of Idam, 'Amir ibn al-Adbat al-Ashja'i passed by us on a she-camel of his, with a little bundle of his goods [*muta'ya'*] and a waterskin of milk. [["Al-qa'ud" is a young camel, when its back can bear riding, from the time it is two years old until it enters its sixth year. "Muta'ya'" is the diminutive of "mata'" (goods): it means merchandise, household furnishings, and whatever a person enjoys of his needs or property. "Al-wat b" is a milk-skin.]] When he passed by us, he greeted us with the greeting of Islam, but we held back from him. Muhallim ibn Jaththamah al-Laythi attacked him, because of something that had been between them, and killed him, and took his camel and his bundle of goods. When we came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and informed him of the news [[In the printed edition: "wa-akhbarnahu" with a waw; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]], the Qur'an was revealed concerning us: "O you who have believed, when you go forth in the way of Allah, investigate carefully, and do not say to one who gives you [a greeting of] peace, 'You are not a believer,'" to the end of the verse. [[Report 10212: This report was transmitted by Ibn Ishaq in his Sirah (Ibn Hisham's Sirah 4:275); also by Ahmad in his Musnad 6:11; Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat 4/2/22 and 2/1/96 (without an isnad); al-Tabari in his History 3:106; Ibn Abd al-Barr in al-Isti'ab, p. 285; Ibn al-Athir in Usd al-Ghabah 3:77; Ibn Kathir in his tafsir 2:545; Ibn Hajar in the biography of "Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad"; and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:199, adding its attribution to Ibn Abi Shaybah, al-Tabarani, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Abu Nu'aym, and al-Bayhaqi, both of the last two in al-Dala'il.

There is great disorder (*idtirab*) in the chain of this report, which I hope to clarify in some of what I intend in this place.

1. The isnad of Muhammad ibn Ishaq in Ibn Hisham's Sirah: "Yazid ibn Abd Allah ibn Qusayt narrated to me, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad, from his father Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad."

2. The isnad of Ahmad in his Musnad: "Ya'qub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq (in the printed edition: "from Ishaq", an error; the correct reading is from Ibn Kathir's tafsir), Yazid ibn Abd Allah ibn Qusayt narrated to me, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad, from his father Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad."

3. The isnad of al-Tabari in his History: "Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, from Ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Abu al-Qa'qa' ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad (and some of them said: from Ibn al-Qa'qa'), from his father, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad."

4. The isnad of Ibn Sa'd in al-Tabaqat: "Muhammad ibn Umar informed us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Yazid ibn Qusayt narrated to us, from his father, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad al-Aslami, from his father."

The first three isnads, and the isnad of al-Tabari in the tafsir, all go through Muhammad ibn Ishaq, and the isnad of Ahmad and the isnad of Ibn Ishaq in Ibn Hisham's Sirah agree.

The isnads of al-Tabari differ from what Ahmad and Ibn Hisham agreed upon in the Sirah. Here in the tafsir it reads "from Abu al-Qa'qa'" rather than "from al-Qa'qa'." Then al-Tabari further complicated the matter in the History, saying "from Abu al-Qa'qa'... from his father, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad," adding "from his father," which is not mentioned in his tafsir or in the other isnads. The apparent view is that this is an error, and that the correct reading is as in the tafsir: "from his father Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad."

As for the isnad of Ibn Sa'd, it departs from all of this: in place of "al-Qa'qa'" or "Abu al-Qa'qa'" it has "Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad." I have found no mention of this Abd al-Rahman in the books of biographies of transmitters. Ibn Abd al-Barr in al-Isti'ab 2:452 mentions something even stranger than this, naming him "Abd Rabbih ibn Abi Hadrad al-Aslami," and he is not mentioned in any book. But I found in al-Jarh wa-al-Ta'dil of Ibn Abi Hatim 2/2/228: "Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hadrad al-Aslami," who heard Abu Hurayrah, and from whom Abu Mawdud Abd al-Aziz ibn Abi Sulayman al-Madani narrated. I do not think this is the one in Ibn Sa'd's isnad. (See also Tahdhib al-Tahdhib 6:160.)

As for "al-Qa'qa' ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad," al-Bukhari, in al-Kabir 4/1/187, included a biography of a Companion, "al-Qa'qa' ibn Abi Hadrad al-Aslami," and his wife "Buqayrah." As Ibn Hajar mentioned in al-Isabah, he was the brother of "Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad." Then al-Bukhari commented on this biography, saying: "It is said: al-Qa'qa' ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad, but this is not sound," meaning that this latter one has no valid claim to companionship, and that he is other than the first. Ibn Abi Hatim did likewise at 3/2/136, as in al-Tarikh al-Kabir.

As for al-Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) in Ta'jil al-Manfa'ah, p. 344, he included a biography of "al-Qa'qa' ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad al-Aslami," and erred in his quotation from al-Bukhari: he thought al-Bukhari had included a biography of him, and so he cited what al-Bukhari said in the biography of "al-Qa'qa' ibn Abi Hadrad." Yet he corrected this in the biography of "al-Qa'qa' ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad" in the third part of al-Isabah.

As for what al-Tabari mentioned, that it is "Abu al-Qa'qa' ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad" or "Ibn al-Qa'qa'," I have not found it elsewhere. However, I left what was in the isnad of the tafsir, "Abu al-Qa'qa'," even though he has no mention or biography in the books, because it agrees with what is in the History, and because what he transmitted, "It is said: Ibn al-Qa'qa'," makes any distortion or addition by a copyist or other person unlikely.

Furthermore, another isnad in the History 3:125 has come down, from Ibn Ishaq, from Ya'qub ibn Utbah ibn al-Mughirah ibn al-Akhnas ibn Shariq, from Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, from the son of Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad al-Aslami, "from his father Abd Allah ibn Abi Hadrad." Here his name is not mentioned as it was in the earlier isnad. Likewise in the following isnad as well: "from Ibn Abi Hadrad, from his father."

This is a strange disorder in its isnad, and I wished to gather it in this place, because I did not find anyone who had exhausted what is in it. Perhaps a researcher will have an opinion on it. [Written by Mahmud Muhammad Shakir.]]

**10213.** Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm narrated to me, saying: Al-Muharibi, Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad, narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Yazid ibn Abd Allah ibn Qusayt, from Ibn Abi Hadrad al-Aslami, from his father, with something similar. [[Report 10213: See the note on the preceding report. "Harun ibn Idris al-Asamm" was al-Tabari's teacher, and has been mentioned previously under no. 1455. "Al-Muharibi" is "Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Ziyad," mentioned previously under nos. 221, 875, and 1455.]]

**10214.** Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, who said: Some Muslims overtook a man with a small flock of his, and he said, "Peace be upon you!" They killed him and took that small flock, and this verse was revealed: "And do not say to one who gives you [a greeting of] peace, 'You are not a believer,' seeking the goods of worldly life," [referring to] that small flock. [["Al-ghunaymah" is the diminutive of "ghanam" (a flock of sheep), meaning a portion of sheep. The letter "ta'" was added to "ghunaymah" because what is intended is a piece of the flock. See what Abu Ja'far said about the addition of this ta' earlier, vol. 6, pp. 412–413.]]

**10215.** Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Uyaynah informed us, from Amr ibn Dinar, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, with something similar.

**10216.** Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata', from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Muslims overtook a man, and then he mentioned something similar. [[Report 10216: This report is omitted from the manuscript. "Sa'id ibn al-Rabi' al-Razi" was mentioned previously under nos. 3791 and 5312.]]

**10217.** Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A man from the Banu Sulaym passed by a group of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was with a flock of his. He greeted them with peace, and they said: He only greeted you so that he might seek refuge from you! So they went for him, killed him, and took his flock. They brought it to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: "O you who have believed, when you go forth in the way of Allah, investigate carefully," to the end of the verse.

This is part 2 of 3 of al-Tabari's commentary on Surah 4, verse 94. I have translated the passage as given.

10218 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: 'Ubaydullah narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of it.

[[The two reports 10217 and 10218: Ahmad narrated them in his Musnad through Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr, Husayn ibn Muhammad, Khalaf ibn al-Walid and Yahya ibn Adam, all from Isra'il. Their numbers in the Musnad are 2023, 2462, 2988, and the isnad is sound. Ibn Kathir said in his tafsir (2:544): "Ibn Jarir narrated it from the report of Ubaydullah ibn Musa and Abd al-Rahim ibn Sulayman, both from Isra'il with this chain. He said in some of his books other than the tafsir: 'And he narrated it through 'Abd al-Rahman alone' (thus in the original). This report, in our view, has a sound chain, but according to the others it may be defective, for reasons, among them: that no route for it from Simak is known except this one; and among them: that Ikrimah in their narration is subject to scrutiny; and among them: that the person about whom this verse was revealed is disputed among them, some saying it was revealed concerning Muhallam ibn Jaththama, others saying Usama ibn Zayd, and other things were said." I [the speaker, Ibn Kathir] say: This is a strange statement, and it is rejected on several grounds. First: it is established from Simak, narrated by more than one of the great imams. Second: Ikrimah is cited as a authority in the Sahih. Third: it is transmitted through another route from Ibn 'Abbas..."

This which Ibn Kathir quoted from some books of Abu Ja'far, I consider more likely, indeed I affirm, to be in his book Tahdhib al-Athar, and his explanation which Ibn Kathir quoted matches his method in Tahdhib al-Athar. I have quoted it here for benefit, and because it is, to my best judgment, the first quotation I have seen from Tahdhib al-Athar in Ibn Kathir's tafsir.]]

10219 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: A man would profess Islam, believing in Allah and the Messenger, and he would remain among his people. When the expedition of Muhammad (ﷺ) came, he informed his tribe, meaning his people, and they fled. The man remained, not fearing the believers because he was of their religion, until he met them and gave them the greeting of peace. The believers said, "You are not a believer," even though he had given the greeting, and they killed him. Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: "O you who believe, when you go forth in the way of Allah, verify..." up to "seeking the goods of the worldly life," meaning: you kill him desiring that his property, which you found with him, become lawful to you, and that is the goods of the worldly life. Yet with Allah are abundant spoils, so seek the bounty of Allah. He was a man named Mirdas, who caused his people to flee from a cavalry the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had sent, under the command of a man of Banu Layth named Qulayb. [[See the difference over his name, "Qulayb" with qaf and ba', or "Fulayt" with fa' and ta', in al-Isaba in its place.]] He did not flee with them, and when Mirdas met them and gave them the greeting, they killed him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered that his blood-money be paid to his family, returned his property to them, and forbade the believers from doing the like.

10220 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: "O you who believe, when you go forth in the way of Allah, verify," the verse, he said: This hadith concerns Mirdas, a man of Ghatafan. It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) sent an army under Ghalib al-Laythi against the people of Fadak, and among them were some people of Ghatafan, and Mirdas was one of them. His companions fled, and Mirdas said, "I am a believer, and I am not following you." The cavalry attacked them at dawn, [[Sabbahathum al-khayl (with two fathas): they came upon them in the morning, and most of their raids were in the morning. "Al-ghadwa" (with damma then sukun): the early part, what lies between the dawn prayer and sunrise.]] and when they reached him, Mirdas greeted them with peace, but the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) shot him and killed him, and took what he had of goods. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning him: "And do not say to one who gives you the greeting of peace, 'You are not a believer,'" because the greeting of the Muslims is peace, by which they recognize one another and greet one another. [[Report 10220: al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (1:200) and added its attribution to Abd ibn Humayd.]]

10221 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "O you who believe, when you go forth in the way of Allah, verify, and do not say to one who gives you the greeting of peace, 'You are not a believer,' seeking the goods of the worldly life; with Allah are abundant spoils. Thus were you before, then Allah bestowed favour upon you, so verify..." [[In the printed edition it read: "...the goods of the worldly life, the verse, he said: sent..." and I have kept what is in the manuscript, though the copyist omitted from the verse: "Thus were you before."]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent an expedition under Usama ibn Zayd against Banu Damrah, and they met a man from them called Mirdas ibn Nahik, who had a small flock and a red camel. When he saw them, he took refuge in a mountain cave, and Usama followed him. When Mirdas reached the cave, he placed his flock in it, then came out to them and said, "Peace be upon you, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." Usama charged at him and killed him, for the sake of his camel and his flock. The Prophet (ﷺ), whenever he sent Usama, loved that good be said of him, and he would ask his companions about him. When they returned, he did not ask them about him. The people began to speak to the Prophet (ﷺ), saying, "O Messenger of Allah, if you had seen Usama, and a man met him and said, 'There is no god but Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah,' and he charged at him and killed him!" And he was turned away from them. When they insisted, he raised his head to Usama and said, "How will you be when 'There is no god but Allah' comes?" He said, "O Messenger of Allah, he only said it seeking refuge, he sought refuge with it!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him, "Why did you not split open his heart and look at it?" He said, "O Messenger of Allah, his heart is only a piece of his body!" [["Al-bad'ah" (with fatha then sukun): a piece of flesh.]] Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed the account of this, and informed him that he killed him only for his camel and his flock, and that is when He says, "seeking the goods of the worldly life." When He reached "then Allah bestowed favour upon you," He says: Allah turned to you in forgiveness. Usama then swore that he would never fight a man who says, "There is no god but Allah," after that man, and what he had encountered from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning him.

10222 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His saying: "And do not say to one who gives you the greeting of peace, 'You are not a believer,'" he said: It reached me that a man from the Muslims raided a man from the polytheists and charged at him. The polytheist said to him, "I am a Muslim, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah," and the Muslim killed him after he had said it. This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), and he said to the one who killed him: "Did you kill him, when he had said there is no god but Allah?" He said, pleading: "O Prophet of Allah, he only said it seeking refuge, and it was not so!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Why did you not split open his heart?" Then the killer of the man died and was buried, but the earth expelled him. This was mentioned to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he ordered them to bury him, but the earth expelled him again, until this was done to him three times. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The earth has refused to receive him, so throw him into one of the ravines." Ma'mar said: Some of them said: "The earth receives one worse than him, but Allah made him a lesson for you."

10223 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Ahmad narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq: that some people from the Muslims met a man from the polytheists with a small flock of his, and he said, "Peace be upon you, I am a believer," and they assumed he sought refuge by that, so they killed him and took his small flock. He said: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And do not say to one who gives you the greeting of peace, 'You are not a believer,' seeking the goods of the worldly life," that small flock, "Thus were you before, then Allah bestowed favour upon you, so verify."

10224 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Amrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His saying: "O you who believe, when you go forth in the way of Allah, verify," he said: al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad went out in an expedition which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had sent. He said: They passed by a man with a small flock, and he said, "I am a Muslim," and al-Miqdad killed him. [[In the manuscript: "then al-Aswad killed him," and the correct reading is that of the printed edition, or it may be "then Ibn al-Aswad killed him."]] When they returned, they mentioned that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and this verse was revealed: "And do not say to one who gives you the greeting of peace, 'You are not a believer,' seeking the goods of the worldly life," he said: the spoils. [[Report 10224: Habib ibn Abi Amrah, the butcher, seller of reeds, also called "the butcher," Abu Abd Allah al-Hamani. He narrated from Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Umm al-Darda'. Al-Thawri and a group narrated from him. Ibn Sa'd said: "Trustworthy, narrates little." Biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

10225 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: That was revealed concerning a man whom Abu al-Darda' killed=
= Then he mentioned the story of Abu al-Darda', similar to the story mentioned concerning Usama ibn Zayd, and it has been mentioned in the interpretation of His saying: "It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake" [[See what preceded, number 10221.]], then he said in the report:
= And the Furqan was revealed: "It is not for a believer to kill a believer except by mistake," and he recited until he reached: "You are not a believer, seeking the goods of the worldly life," his flock which he had, the goods of the worldly life, "with Allah are abundant spoils," better than that flock, up to His saying: "Indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted."

10226 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "And do not say to one who gives you the greeting of peace, 'You are not a believer,'" he said: A shepherd, whom a group of believers met, and they killed him and took what he had, and they did not accept from him: "Peace be upon you, for I am a believer." [[In the manuscript: "sent a group of believers," which is an error; the correct reading is that of the printed edition.]]

10227 - al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: "And do not say to one who gives you the greeting of peace, 'You are not a believer,'" he said: Allah forbade the believers to say to one who testifies that there is no god but Allah, "You are not a believer," just as He forbade them carrion. He is secure in his property and his blood; do not reject his word.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying: "fatabayyanu."

The majority of the readers of Makkah and Madinah and some of the Kufans and Basrans recited: ﴿fatabayyanu﴾ with the ya' and the nun, from "al-tabayyun" (verification), meaning deliberation, looking, and uncovering it until it becomes clear. [[See the explanation of "al-tabayyun" above, p. 70.]]

The greater part of the Kufan readers recited: ﴿fatathabbatu﴾, meaning steadfast verification (tathabbut), which is the opposite of haste.

Abu Ja'far said: Our view on this is that both are well-known, widely transmitted recitations among the Muslims, with one meaning, though the wording differs. For "al-mutathabbit" is "al-mutabayyin," and "al-mutabayyin" is "al-mutathabbit." So whichever of the two recitations the reader recites, he is correct in the proper recitation.

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His saying: "wa-la taqulu li-man alqa ilaykumu al-salam."

The majority of the readers of Makkah, Madinah and Kufa recited: ﴿al-salama﴾ without an alif, meaning submission.

* *

Some of the Kufans and Basrans recited: ﴿al-salama﴾ with an alif, meaning greeting.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in our view is: ﴿li-man alqa ilaykumu al-salama﴾, meaning: whoever submitted to you, humbly acknowledging Allah's oneness, and affirming to you your religion.

We chose this because the reports differ concerning it. One narrator reported that he submitted by bearing witness to the truth and saying, "I am a Muslim." Another reported that he said, "Peace be upon you," greeting them with the greeting of Islam. Another reported that he was a Muslim by a previous Islam he had before they killed him. All these meanings are encompassed by "al-salam" (submission), for the Muslim is one who submits, the one who greets with the greeting of Islam submits, and the one who bears witness to the truth submits to the people of Islam. So the meaning "al-salam" comprehends all the meanings reported concerning the matter of the slain man about whom this verse was revealed, whereas "al-salam" (the greeting) does not fit this context except as a greeting. Therefore we have judged "al-salam" (submission) to be correct.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning His saying: "Thus were you before."

Some of them said: Its meaning is: just as this one whom you killed, after he had offered you submission, was hiding his religion among his people out of fear for himself from them, so you too were hiding your religions from your people out of caution for yourselves from them, and then Allah bestowed favour upon you.

Those who said this:

10228 - al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Kathir informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr concerning His saying: "Thus were you before," you were concealing your faith, just as this shepherd concealed his faith. [[In the manuscript: "concealing your faith," and the printed edition is better.]]

10229 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Amrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Thus were you before," you were concealing your faith among the polytheists.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: just as this one whom you killed, after he had offered you submission, was a disbeliever, you were disbelievers, and He guided him as He guided you.

Those who said this:

10230 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said concerning His saying: "Thus were you before, then Allah bestowed favour upon you," you were disbelievers like him, "so verify."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of these two views concerning the interpretation of the verse is the first, which is the view of those who said: Thus you were concealing your faith among your people from the polytheists while you were residing among them, just as this one whom you killed was residing among his people from the polytheists, concealing his religion from them.

We said "this interpretation is more correct" because Allah, mentioned, only rebuked those among the believers who killed him after he offered them submission, and his killers were not retaliated against, [[In the printed edition at this point and what follows, "al-salam" stands in place of "al-salam" ("submission"), but I have kept what is in the manuscript, since Abu Ja'far's exegesis follows "al-salam" and not "al-salam." The verb "lam yuqad" is passive from "al-qawd" (with fatha on the qaf and waw), meaning retaliation, killing the killer in place of the slain; one says "aqadtuhu bihi uqiduhu iqadah."]] because of the confusion that had entered his affair among his killers through his remaining among his people of polytheists, and their thinking that he offered submission to the believers out of seeking refuge from them. He did not rebuke them for killing him as a polytheist, so that it would be said, "Just as he was a disbeliever, you were disbelievers." Rather, there is no basis for that, since Allah, His praise be mentioned, did not rebuke any of His creatures for killing one who wars against Allah and His Messenger from among the people of polytheism, after His permission to kill him.

The people of interpretation also differed concerning His saying: "then Allah bestowed favour upon you."

Some of them said: Its meaning is: then Allah bestowed favour upon you by manifesting His religion and strengthening its people, until they manifested Islam after they had been concealing it from the people of polytheism. [[In the printed edition: "after they had been concealing it," but the manuscript's reading is better. "Yakhtatimun bihi" means concealing it.]]

Those who said this:

10231 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, from Sufyan, from Habib ibn Abi Amrah, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Then Allah bestowed favour upon you," so He made Islam manifest.

* *

Others said: Its meaning is: then Allah bestowed favour upon you, O you killers, who sought the goods of the worldly life from the one who offered you submission, by your repentance from killing him.

Those who said this:

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 94 (part 3 of 3):

10232 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿then Allah bestowed favour upon you﴾: he says, Allah turned to you in forgiveness.

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The more correct of the two interpretations in this matter is the interpretation you have mentioned from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, because of the indication we have mentioned that the meaning of His words ﴿thus were you before﴾ is what we have described earlier. It must therefore be that following this comes ﴿then Allah bestowed favour upon you﴾, meaning that He removed from you the fear of your enemies that you had been in, by making His religion manifest and strengthening its people, until He enabled you to openly display what you had been concealing of His oneness and worship, out of fear of the people of polytheism. [[In the printed edition: "ḥadharan" (حذرًا), but I have adopted what is in the manuscript; both are the same.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 95 (part 1 of 2):**

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Not equal are those believers who sit at home, other than those with a disability, and those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, "Not equal are those believers who sit at home, other than those with a disability, and those who strive," the Mighty and Majestic means: Those among the people of faith in Allah and His Messenger who hold back from striving in the way of Allah (jihad) are not equal to those who strive. The former prefer ease, comfort, and sitting in their homes over enduring the hardship of travel and journeying across the land, and the difficulty of confronting the enemies of Allah through striving for His sake and fighting in obedience to Allah. The exception is those among them who have a valid excuse, such as loss of sight or other ailments which prevent them, because of the harm they suffer, from fighting and striving in the way of Allah. "And those who strive in the way of Allah," that is, in His religion and path, [[See the explanation of "in the way of Allah" above, and the references there.]] so that the word of Allah may be the highest. They are those who exert their full capacity in fighting the enemies of Allah and the enemies of their religion, "with their wealth," by spending it in what weakens the schemes of the enemies of the people of faith in Allah, "and with their lives," by personally engaging in fighting with them, by which the word of Allah becomes exalted and the word of those who disbelieve becomes lowly.

* *

The reciters differed regarding the reading of His words, "other than those with a disability" (ghayru ulī al-ḍarar).

The majority of the reciters of Madinah, Makkah, and Syria read ﴿غَيْرَ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ﴾ with the accusative "ghayra," meaning: except those with a disability.

The majority of the reciters of Kufa and Basra [[In the printed edition: "the reciters of Iraq, Kufa and Basra," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]] read ﴿غَيْرُ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ﴾ with the nominative "ghayru," as an adjective (na't) modifying "those who sit."

Abu Ja'far said: The correct reading in our view is ﴿غَيْرَ أُولِي الضَّرَرِ﴾ with "ghayra" in the accusative, because the reports are consistent that the phrase "other than those with a disability" was revealed after "Not equal are those believers who sit at home and those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives," as an exception to "Not equal are those who sit at home and those who strive."

* *

Mention of some of the reports transmitted regarding this:

1. Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami narrated to us, saying: al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara': that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Bring me the shoulder-blade and the tablet," and he wrote, "Not equal are those believers who sit at home and those who strive," while Amr ibn Umm Maktum was behind him. He said: "Is there any concession for me, O Messenger of Allah?" So "other than those with a disability" was revealed.

[[The hadith: 1023 3. This is the hadith of al-Bara' ibn Azib concerning the occasion of revelation of His words, "other than those with a disability." Al-Tabari transmitted it here by seven chains. Five of them are consecutive: 10233 to 10237, then 10248 and 10249.
Abu Ishaq in all of them is Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i.
This hadith is the first of them, "from Nasr ibn Ali al-Jahdami." It was transmitted by al-Tirmidhi (3:19) from Nasr ibn Ali, with this same chain.
Likewise al-Nasa'i (2:54) transmitted it from Nasr ibn Ali.
Likewise Ibn Hibban in his Sahih, no. 40 (in our edition), transmitted it from Muhammad ibn Umar ibn Yusuf, from Nasr ibn Ali.
His words, "he wrote: not equal" etc., mean he ordered the writing. This is the established reading in the printed edition with "fa-kataba" (and he wrote) using the particle fa. It agrees with what is in al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Hibban. In the manuscript it is "wa-kataba" with waw. We have adopted the agreeing reading over the disagreeing one, though the meaning is the same.]]

2. Ibn Wakf narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: When "Not equal are those believers who sit at home" was revealed, Ibn Umm Maktum came, and he was blind, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, how (can I do this) when I am blind?" He had not moved away before "other than those with a disability" was revealed.

[[The hadith: 10234. It is a repetition of the hadith before it, as found with Sufyan ibn Wakf despite his weakness. But he heard from Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, and Abu Bakr heard from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i.
The hadith in itself is sound through this route: al-Nasa'i (2:54) transmitted it from Muhammad ibn Ubayd, from Abu Bakr ibn Ayyash, with the same chain.]]

3. Ibn Wakf narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, regarding His words, "Not equal are those believers who sit at home, other than those with a disability," who said: When it was revealed, Amr ibn Umm Maktum came to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he was blind. He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what do you command me, since I am blind?" So Allah revealed this verse, and he (ﷺ) said: "Bring me the shoulder-blade and the inkwell," or "the tablet and the inkwell."

[[The hadith: 10235. Sufyan ibn Wakf did not stand alone in narrating it from his father, from Sufyan al-Thawri. Ahmad transmitted it in his Musnad (4:290, 299, Halabi edition), from Waki', from al-Thawri, with this same chain. Likewise al-Tirmidhi (4:90-91) transmitted it from Mahmud ibn Ghaylan, from Wakf, and said: "This is a good sound hadith. It is said: Amr ibn Umm Maktum. It is also said: Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum. He is Abdullah ibn Za'ida. Umm Maktum was his mother."]]

4. Ismail ibn Isra'il al-Dalal al-Ramli narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mughira narrated to us, saying: Mis'ar narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara': that when "Not equal are those believers who sit at home" was revealed, Ibn Umm Maktum spoke to him, and then "other than those with a disability" was revealed.

[[The hadith: 10236. Ismail ibn Isra'il al-Dalal al-Ramli, Abu Muhammad: a trustworthy narrator among the teachers of Ibn Abi Hatim, who biographed him in 1/1/158 and said: "We wrote from him, and he is truthful." However, in Ibn Abi Hatim's work it reads "al-Sallal" instead of "al-Dalal." We did not find a preponderant reading, so we have kept what stands here in the manuscript and the printed edition. There is an error in the printed edition, "Muhammad ibn Isma'il," with an added "Muhammad ibn," which is not in the manuscript, so we have deleted it. What supports this is that al-Tabari himself transmitted from him in his History (2:273), with this same chain, from al-Bara' concerning the companions of Saul, and named him there "Ismail ibn Isra'il al-Ramli." The hadith of al-Bara' concerning the companions of Saul has passed with chains: 5724 to 5729, but among them there is not this chain found in the History.
Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mughira al-Kufi, who settled in Egypt: Ibn Abi Hatim biographed him in 2/2/158 and narrated from his father, saying: "He is not strong." He did not mention that he narrated from Mis'ar, but his narration from him is established in Tahdhib al-Kamal by al-Hafiz al-Mizzi, p. 1322 (photocopied manuscript), in the biography of Mis'ar, among those who narrated from him. Likewise it is established in his own biography in Lisan al-Mizan (3:332-333) that he narrates from Mis'ar. In that biography there is what indicates severe criticism of him which discards his narration.
The hadith through Mis'ar is established as sound apart from the narration of this Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn al-Mughira. Muslim transmitted it (2:101) from Abu Kurayb, from Ibn Bishr, who is Muhammad ibn Bishr ibn al-Farafisa al-Abdi the hafiz, from Mis'ar, with the same chain.]]

5. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, that he heard al-Bara' say concerning this verse, "Not equal are those believers who sit at home and those who strive in the way of Allah," that he said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered Zayd, and he brought a shoulder-blade and wrote it. He said: Ibn Umm Maktum complained to him of his blindness, and then "Not equal are those believers who sit at home, other than those with a disability" was revealed.

= Shu'ba said: Sa'd ibn Ibrahim informed me, from his father, from a man, from Zayd, concerning this verse, "Not equal are those who sit at home," similar to the hadith of al-Bara'.

[[The hadith: 10237. Abu Ishaq is al-Sabi'i, as we said just before. In the printed edition it appears as "Ibn Ishaq," which is certainly an error; the correct reading is in the manuscript.
The hadith was transmitted by Ahmad in his Musnad (4:282, Halabi edition), from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'ba, with the same chain. Muslim transmitted it (2:100-101) from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna (al-Tabari's teacher here) and from Muhammad ibn Bashshar, both from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, with the same chain.
Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi transmitted it (no. 705) from Shu'ba, with the same chain.
Ahmad also transmitted it (4:284) from Affan, and (4:299-300) from Abd al-Rahman (who is Ibn Mahdi), both from Shu'ba.
Al-Bukhari (6:34, Fath) and al-Darimi (2:209) both transmitted it from Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi, from Shu'ba.
Likewise Ibn Hibban transmitted it in his Sahih, no. 41 (in our edition), from Abu Khalifa, from Abu al-Walid al-Tayalisi, with the same chain.
Al-Bukhari also transmitted it (8:196, Fath) from Hafs ibn Umar, from Shu'ba.
Likewise al-Bayhaqi transmitted it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (9:23), by two chains, through Hafs ibn Umar. All of this concerns the original hadith, the hadith of al-Bara'. As for the other chain appended here, "Shu'ba, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from a man, from Zayd" (who is Ibn Thabit), it is in reality a different hadith with a different chain, containing an unnamed man. Its chain is therefore weak. The hadith of Zayd ibn Thabit in itself is sound, and will come: 10239 and 10240.
As for this weak route, Muslim also transmitted it, following the hadith of al-Bara' here, just as al-Tabari does here. Necessarily this chain does not meet Muslim's condition for soundness. He cited it only to complete the narration from Shu'ba as he heard it.
It is strange that al-Nawawi did not discuss it in his commentary (13:42), and did not mention its defect.
It is also strange that al-Hafiz al-Mizzi did not mention it in the chapter on the unnamed (al-Mubhamat) in Tahdhib al-Kamal, nor did any of its branches mention it, although it is in Sahih Muslim in two versions: "from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from a man, from Zayd," and "from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from a man, from Zayd."
Then we do not know this unnamed man.
Sa'd is Sa'd ibn Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf. His father was one of the senior Successors (tabi'un), so it is highly probable that the unnamed man who is his teacher here was a Companion. But we cannot establish that as preponderant.]]

6. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ishaq ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Abu Sinan al-Shaybani, from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd ibn Arqam, who said: When "Not equal are those believers who sit at home and those who strive in the way of Allah" was revealed, Ibn Umm Maktum came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, do I have no concession?" He said: "No!" Ibn Umm Maktum said: "O Allah, I am blind, so grant me a concession!" So Allah revealed: "other than those with a disability." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) ordered that it be written down, and it was written by the scribe.

[[The hadith: 10238. Ishaq ibn Sulayman al-Razi al-Abdi: his reliability has been established at 6456. Abu Sinan al-Shaybani: this is the younger, the Kufan, whose name is "Sa'id ibn Sinan al-Barjami." He is trustworthy, though he has been criticized on account of some of his errors. His biography has passed at 175.
The hafiz (Ibn Hajar) made a serious error in Fath (8:196), when he pointed to this hadith from the narration of al-Tabarani, as will come, and claimed that it was "Dirar ibn Murra." That is Abu Sinan al-Shaybani the elder. The one who narrates from Abu Ishaq al-Sabi'i and from whom Ishaq ibn Sulayman al-Razi narrates is "Abu Sinan al-Shaybani the younger, Sa'id ibn Sinan," as is clear from Tahdhib al-Kamal and its branches. The hafiz al-Mizzi did not mention in the biographies of the two of them anything beyond what we have said.
As for Abu Ishaq, he is al-Sabi'i, as we mentioned just before. In the printed edition it appears as "from Ibn Ishaq." This is an error; the correct reading is what we have adopted from the manuscript, and it is the established reading in the transmission.
The hadith was mentioned by al-Haythami in Majma' al-Zawa'id, vol. 7, p. 9, where he said: "al-Tabarani transmitted it, and its narrators are trustworthy."
The hafiz referred to it in Fath (8:196), as we said just before. He mentioned that it is in al-Tabarani, and gave as its defect that "the preserved version is from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara'. Thus the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) agreed on it through the route of Shu'ba..." Then he pointed to many of the reports that al-Tabari mentions here and in what follows.
We do not see this as a defect in that, nor that as a defect in this. The story is well known, and Zayd ibn Thabit also transmitted it, as will come: 10239 and 10240.
The Companion al-Faltan ibn Asim al-Jurmi also transmitted it, in a longer form. Al-Haythami mentioned it in Majma' al-Zawa'id, vol. 7, p. 9, and said: "Abu Ya'la and al-Bazzar transmitted it in similar terms, and al-Tabarani similarly... the narrators of Abu Ya'la are trustworthy."
The hafiz mentioned it in al-Isaba (5:213) in the biography of al-Faltan, from the narration of al-Hasan ibn Sufyan in his Musnad, then mentioned that Ibn Abi Shayba, Abu Ya'la and Ibn Hibban in his Sahih also transmitted it.
Al-Suyuti mentioned it (2:203-204), and added its attribution to Abd ibn Humayd.
It was also transmitted by Ibn Abbas, as will come: 10242.]]

7. Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Bazi' and Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, both saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from al-Zuhri, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: I saw Marwan ibn al-Hakam sitting, so I came and sat with him, and he narrated to us from Zayd ibn Thabit: that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had revealed to him, "Not equal are those believers who sit at home and those who strive in the way of Allah." He said: Ibn Umm Maktum came while he was dictating it to me, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if I were able to strive, I would strive!" He said: So it was revealed to him while his thigh was upon my thigh, and it grew heavy, and I thought my thigh would be crushed. Then the state of revelation passed from him, and he said: "other than those with a disability."

[[The hadith: 10239. al-Nasa'i (2:54) transmitted it from Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Bazi', one of al-Tabari's teachers here, with this same chain.
Ahmad transmitted it in his Musnad (5:184, Halabi edition), from Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Salih, from al-Zuhri, with the same chain, but he did not give its full wording, referring instead to the narration of Qubaysa ibn Dhu'ayb before it. That is the narration which will come here right after this one.
