Al-Bukhari (8:195-196, Fath) transmitted it through Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from Salih, with the same chain. Al-Tirmidhi (4:92), al-Nasa'i (2:54) and Ibn al-Jarud (p. 460) all transmitted it through Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Sa'd, from his father.
Al-Bayhaqi (9:23) transmitted it through Ibrahim ibn Sa'd.
Al-Suyuti mentioned it (2:202-203), and added its attribution to Ibn Sa'd, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Abu Nu'aym in al-Dala'il.
"Radda al-shay' yarudduhu radda": he broke it. "Suriya 'anhu" (in the passive form): that is, what he had been seized with of distress at the descent of revelation was lifted from him and made manifest.]]

8. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Qubaysa ibn Dhu'ayb, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: I used to write for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Write: 'Not equal are those believers who sit at home and those who strive in the way of Allah.'" Then Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum came and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I love striving in the way of Allah, but I have such disability as you see, for my sight has gone!" Zayd said: The thigh of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became heavy upon my thigh until I feared it would be crushed. Then he said: "Write: 'Not equal are those believers who sit at home, other than those with a disability, and those who strive in the way of Allah.'"

[[The hadith: 10240. It has the same meaning as the previous hadith from Zayd ibn Thabit, but it is from the narration of Qubaysa ibn Dhu'ayb from him.
Qubaysa ibn Dhu'ayb ibn Halhala: a great and trustworthy Successor, as passed at 5471. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and elsewhere, and in al-Isaba (5:271-272).
The hadith is in the Tafsir of Abd al-Razzaq, p. 48 (photocopied manuscript).
Ahmad transmitted it in his Musnad (5:184, Halabi edition), from Abd al-Razzaq.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it (2:549) from the Tafsir of Abd al-Razzaq, then said: "Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir transmitted it."
The hafiz referred to it in Fath (8:195), attributing it to Ahmad only.]]

9. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: Abd al-Karim informed me: that Miqsam, the freedman of Abdullah ibn al-Harith, informed him: that Ibn Abbas informed him, who said: "Not equal are those believers who sit at home," (referring to) Badr, and those who went out to Badr.

[[The hadith: 10241. This hadith is not in the Tafsir of Abd al-Razzaq, so it is perhaps in his Musannaf. Ahmad did not transmit it in his Musnad, as far as my search has reached.
Al-Bukhari transmitted it (8:196-197) in this abridged form, through Hisham, from Ibn Jurayj, and through Abd al-Razzaq, from Ibn Jurayj.
Ibn Kathir mentioned it (2:549) and said: "al-Bukhari alone transmitted it, apart from Muslim."
Al-Suyuti mentioned it (2:203), and added its attribution to Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim. A longer version of it will follow this one.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 95 (part 2 of 2):**

10242. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Karim informed me that he heard Miqsam narrate from Ibn Abbas that he heard him say: "Not equal are those who sit [at home] among the believers" [concerning] Badr, "and those who go forth to Badr," when the expedition of Badr was revealed. [[In the printed edition: "lamma nazalat ghazwat Badr" (when the expedition of Badr was revealed). I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]] Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum and Abu Ahmad ibn Jahsh ibn Qays al-Asadi said: "O Messenger of God, we are both blind. Is there any dispensation for us?" Then it was revealed: "Not equal are those who sit [at home] among the believers, other than those with a harm, and those who strive in the way of God with their wealth and their selves. God has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their selves over those who sit [at home] by a degree." [[Hadith 10242: This is the extended wording of the preceding hadith. It contains the story of Ibn Umm Maktum, which has passed several times through the hadith of al-Bara ibn Azib, the hadith of Zayd ibn Arqam, and the hadith of Zayd ibn Thabit, with some additional elements in the story.
This hadith, through this chain, was narrated by al-Tirmidhi (4:91), who said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith from this route, from the hadith of Ibn Abbas."
Al-Hafiz [Ibn Hajar] transmitted it in al-Fath (8:197) from the narration of al-Tirmidhi, and referred to the narration of al-Tabari here, as will come.
Ibn Kathir also transmitted it (2:549-550) from the narration of al-Tirmidhi.
Al-Suyuti transmitted it (2:203), and attributed it additionally to al-Nasa'i, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan.
In the narration of al-Tirmidhi and those who transmitted from him, the wording is: "wa-Abdullah ibn Jahsh" instead of "wa-Abu Ahmad ibn Jahsh." Al-Hafiz, in al-Fath, decided that the correct reading is what is in al-Tabari's narration, "Abu Ahmad ibn Jahsh," saying: "For Abdullah is his brother. As for him, his name is 'Abd,' without an addition, and he is well known by his kunya (teknonym)."
"Abdullah ibn Jahsh" was not blind, and he was martyred at the Battle of Uhud.
His brother Abu Ahmad is biographed in al-Isaba (7:3-4) and in Ibn Sa'd (7/1/76-77). Al-Hafiz decided in al-Isaba that his name is "Abd" without an addition, as he said in al-Fath. In Ibn Sa'd, his name is given as "Abdullah." I fear this is a printer's or copyist's error.
Al-Hafiz said in al-Isaba: "Abu Ahmad was blind; he would circumambulate Mecca, its upper and lower parts, without a guide. Al-Fari'a bint Abi Sufyan ibn Harb was his wife, and he was present at Badr and the battles."]]
10243. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas: "Not equal are those who sit [at home] among the believers and those who strive in the way of God with their wealth and their selves." Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum, the blind man, heard of this, so he came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of God, God has revealed about jihad what you know, and I am a man blind in sight and unable to strive. Is there a dispensation for me from God if I remain seated?" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to him: "I have not been commanded anything regarding your case, and I do not know whether there will be a dispensation for you and your companions!" Ibn Umm Maktum said: "O God, I beseech You by my sight!" Then God revealed to His Messenger (ﷺ) afterwards: "Not equal are those who sit [at home] among the believers, other than those with a harm, and those who strive in the way of God," up to His words: "by a degree."
10244. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata', from Sa'id, who said: It was revealed: "Not equal are those who sit [at home] among the believers and those who strive in the way of God." A blind man said: "O Prophet of God, I love jihad, but I cannot strive!" Then it was revealed: "other than those with a harm."
10245. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Abdullah ibn Shaddad, who said: When this verse on jihad was revealed: "Not equal are those who sit [at home] among the believers," Abdullah ibn Umm Maktum said: "O Messenger of God, I am blind, as you see!" Then it was revealed: "other than those with a harm." [[Hadith 10245: Husayn is Ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami.
This hadith is mursal (a report in which a successor omits the companion from whom he heard it), because Abdullah ibn Shaddad ibn al-Hadi al-Laythi is a successor, one of the great and trustworthy successors. However, he did not mention from whom he heard it. Although the core of the hadith is authentic in itself, as established by the preceding reports. Al-Suyuti mentioned the hadith (2:204) in this mursal form, and also attributed it to Sa'id ibn Mansur and Abd ibn Humayd.]]
10246. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "Not equal are those who sit [at home] among the believers, other than those with a harm." God excused the people of excuse by saying: "other than those with a harm." Ibn Umm Maktum was among them. "And those who strive in the way of God with their wealth and their selves."
10247. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Not equal are those who sit [at home] among the believers, other than those with a harm, and those who strive in the way of God," up to His words: "And God has promised each the best [reward]." When He mentioned the excellence of jihad, Ibn Umm Maktum said: "O Messenger of God, I am blind and cannot bear jihad!" So God revealed concerning him: "other than those with a harm."
10248. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah al-Nufayli narrated to us, saying: Zuhayr ibn Mu'awiya narrated to us, saying: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Bara', who said: I was with the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he said: "Call Zayd for me, and tell him to come with the shoulder-blade and the inkwell," or "the tablet and the inkwell" (the doubt is from Zuhayr), "and write: 'Not equal are those who sit [at home] among the believers and those who strive in the way of God.'" Ibn Umm Maktum said: "O Messenger of God, there is a harm in my eye!" So it was revealed before he had moved: "other than those with a harm." [[Hadith 10248: This and the following one are among the narrations of the hadith of al-Bara, which passed with its chains: 10233-10237, as we indicated there.
Through this route it was narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad (4:301, Halabi edition), from Hashim ibn al-Qasim, from Zuhayr, who is Ibn Mu'awiya, with this chain.]]
10249. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Raja al-Basri narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', with something similar, except that he said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Call Zayd for me, and let him come to me with a shoulder-blade and an inkwell," or "a tablet and an inkwell." [[Hadith 10249: Isra'il is Ibn Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq al-Sabi'i, who narrated from his grandfather Abu Ishaq.
The hadith was narrated by al-Bukhari (8:196), from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, from Isra'il.
Al-Bukhari also narrated it (9:19, Fath edition), from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, from Isra'il.
Likewise Ibn Hibban narrated it in his Sahih, no. 39 (edited by us), through the route of Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Ijli, from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa.]]
10250. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Ziyad ibn Fayyad, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, who said: When "Not equal are those who sit [at home]" was revealed, Amr ibn Umm Maktum said: "O Lord, You have tested me, so how should I act?" He said: Then it was revealed: "other than those with a harm." [[Hadith 10250: Ziyad ibn Fayyad al-Khuza'i al-Kufi: his biography and authentication have passed in (1382).
His teacher "Abu Abd al-Rahman": I have not known who he is, and I have not found an indication that identifies a specific teacher. "Abu Abd al-Rahman" is a very broad kunya with many bearers.
Whatever the case, he is for the most part a successor, because Ziyad ibn Fayyad does not go in his narration beyond the successors. So the hadith is mursal, not connected.
Al-Suyuti likewise mentioned it (2:204) in this form of irsal, and attributed it to Ibn Sa'd, Abd ibn Humayd, and al-Tabari.]]
Ibn Abbas used to say, regarding the meaning of "other than those with a harm," something similar to what we have said.
10251. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His words "other than those with a harm," that he said: "the people of harm."

* * *

**The discussion on the interpretation of His words: "God has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their selves over those who sit [at home] by a degree."**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, "God has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their selves over those who sit [at home] by a degree," He means: God has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their selves, over those who sit [at home] from among the people of harm, by one degree, that is, one excellence. This is due to the excellence of striving with one's own person. As for other than that, they are equal, as:
10252. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us that he heard Ibn Jurayj say regarding "God has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their selves over those who sit [at home] by a degree," that he said: "over the people of harm."

* * *

**The discussion on the interpretation of His words: "And God has promised each the best [reward], but God has preferred those who strive over those who sit [at home] with a great reward."**

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, "And God has promised each the best [reward]," He means: God has promised all of them, from the strivers with their wealth and their selves, and from the sitters who are people of harm, "the best" [[See what he said about "kull" (each/all) earlier: 3:195, 5:509, 6:210.]]. By "the best," may His praise be exalted, He means Paradise, as:
10253. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "And God has promised each the best [reward]," which is Paradise, "and God gives every possessor of excellence his excellence."
10254. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: "The best" is Paradise.

As for His words, "And God has preferred the strivers over the sitters with a great reward," He means: And God has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their selves over those who sit [at home], other than the people of harm, with a great reward, as:
10255. Al-Qasim narrated to me, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Abu Jurayj: "And God has preferred the strivers over the sitters with a great reward, [in] degrees from Him and forgiveness," he said: "over the sitters among the believers, other than the people of harm."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 96:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Degrees from Him, and forgiveness and mercy. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, means: "Degrees from Him," virtues from Him and stations of honour. [See the explanation of "degree" (daraja) above, 4:533, 536 / 7:368, and what has passed on p. 95, footnote 2.]

* *

The people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the meaning of the "degrees" of which He, may His praise be exalted, spoke: "Degrees from Him."

Some of them said:

10256 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding "Degrees from Him and forgiveness and mercy": It was said: Islam is a degree, emigration within Islam is a degree, jihad within emigration is a degree, and being killed in jihad is a degree.

* *

And others said:

10257 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I asked Ibn Zayd about the words of Allah, exalted is He: "And Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and their lives over those who sit back by a degree. To each Allah has promised good. But Allah has preferred those who strive over those who sit back with a great reward: degrees from Him," [saying]: "The 'degrees' are the seven which He mentioned in Surat Bara'ah: ﴿It was not fitting for the people of Medina and those of the Bedouins around them to remain behind from the Messenger of Allah, nor to prefer themselves over his own self. That is because they are not afflicted by thirst or fatigue﴾" and he recited until he reached: ﴿the best of what they used to do﴾ [Surat al-Tawbah: 120-121]. He said: "These are the seven degrees." He said: "At first, the degree of jihad was general, so the one who fought with his wealth had a name in this [category]. But when these degrees came in detail, he was excluded from them, and he had from them only the expenditure." He recited: ﴿They are not afflicted by thirst or fatigue﴾, and said: "This does not belong to the one who spends." Then he recited: ﴿And they spend no expenditure﴾, and said: "This is the expenditure of the one who sits back."

* *

And others said: He meant the degrees of Paradise.

Mention of those who said this:

10258 - Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Azdi narrated to us, saying: al-Ash'ja'i narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Hisham ibn Hassan, from Jabalah ibn Suhaym, from Ibn Muhayriz, regarding His words: "Allah has preferred those who strive over those who sit back," up to His words: "degrees": "The degrees are seventy degrees; between each two degrees is the distance a swift, well-trained horse runs in seventy years." [Note on this report: "Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Azdi," the teacher of al-Tabari, I have not found a biography for him, though he narrated from him in his History in several places, including 1:44, 49 / 6:73, 143. "al-Ash'ja'i" is Ubayd Allah ibn Ubayd al-Rahman al-Ash'ja'i, whose biography passed as no. 8622. "Sufyan" is al-Thawri. "Hisham ibn Hassan al-Qurdusi" passed as nos. 2827, 7287. "Jabalah ibn Suhaym" passed as no. 3003. "Ibn Muhayriz" is Abd Allah ibn Muhayriz, who passed as no. 8720. "Hudr al-faras" is its height in its running; "ahdar al-faras yuhdiru ihdaran" means it ran a severe run. "al-Faras al-mudammar" is the horse prepared through training for racing and galloping.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct interpretation of His words "Degrees from Him" is that they refer to the degrees of Paradise, as Ibn Muhayriz said. Because His words, exalted is He: "Degrees from Him" are an explanation and clarification of His words "a great reward," and it is known that "reward" (ajr) is nothing but recompense and requital. [See the explanation of "ajr" above, 8:542, footnote 1, and the references there.]

Since this is so, and since "degrees," "forgiveness," and "mercy" are an explanation of it, it is evident that there is no basis for the view of those who directed the meaning of His words "Degrees from Him" to the deeds and their increase over the deeds of those who stayed back from jihad, as Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said. Since this is so, and since the correct interpretation of this is what we have mentioned, it is clear that the meaning of the passage is: "Allah has preferred those who strive in the way of Allah over those who sit back, other than those with a valid excuse, with a great reward, and a generous recompense, which is degrees He has granted them in the Hereafter from the degrees of Paradise, elevating them thereby over those who sit back, for what they endured for the sake of Allah."

* *

"And forgiveness": he says: and pardon for them for their sins, so He graciously bestows upon them by abandoning their punishment for them.

"And mercy": he says: and compassion toward them.

"And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful": he says: Allah has never ceased to be Forgiving of the sins of His believing servants, pardoning them and not punishing them for them, "Merciful" toward them, bestowing favour upon them with His blessings, despite their opposition to His command and prohibition and their committing of His disobediences. [See the explanation of "forgiveness" (maghfirah), "mercy" (rahmah), "Forgiving" (ghafur) and "Merciful" (rahim) above in the language indices.]

**Commentary of al-Ṭabarī (Jāmiʿ al-Bayān) on Sūrah 4, verses 97–99 (part 1 of 2)**

**On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves, [the angels] will say, "In what [condition] were you?" They will say, "We were oppressed in the land." [The angels] will say, "Was not the earth of Allah spacious so you could emigrate therein?" For those, their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.﴾ (97) ﴿Except for the oppressed among men, women, and children who are unable to devise a plan and are not guided to a way.﴾ (98) ﴿For those, perhaps Allah will pardon them, and Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.﴾ (99)**

Abū Jaʿfar said: By His words, "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death" (inna alladhīna tawaffāhumu al-malāʾikah), He, may His praise be exalted, means: indeed, those whose souls the angels seize [see the explanation of *tawaffī* (taking in death) above, 6:455, 8:73]. "While they are wronging themselves" means: earning for themselves the anger and wrath of Allah.

* * *

We have already explained the meaning of *ẓulm* (wronging) earlier [see the explanation of *ẓulm* in the lexical indices of the preceding volumes].

* * *

"They will say, 'In what [condition] were you?'" means: the angels will say to them, "In what [condition] were you?" That is, in what matter of your religion were you? "They will say, 'We were oppressed in the land,'" meaning: those whom the angels took in death, while wronging themselves, will say, "We were oppressed in the land." The people of polytheism (*shirk*) against Allah oppressed us in our land and country by their great numbers and strength, and they prevented us from believing in Allah and following His Messenger ﷺ. This is a weak excuse and a feeble argument. "[The angels] will say, 'Was not the earth of Allah spacious so you could emigrate therein?'" means: "Would you not have gone out from your land and homes, and departed from those who prevented you therein from believing in Allah and following His Messenger ﷺ, to a land whose people do not prevent you from the authority of the people of polytheism against Allah, so that you could affirm the oneness of Allah there and worship Him, and follow His Prophet?" [see the explanation of *hijrah* (emigration) above, 4:317–318, 7:490].

Allah, may His praise be exalted, says: "For those, their refuge is Hell," meaning: those whom I have described to you are the ones whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves. "Their refuge is Hell" means: their destination in the Hereafter is Hell, and it is their dwelling [see the explanation of *maʾwā* (refuge) above, 7:279, 494]. "And wretched is the destination" means: and wretched is Hell as a dwelling for its people who have come to it [see the explanation of *sāʾa* (wretched) above, 8:138, 358], "destination," and abode and refuge [see the explanation of *maṣīr* (destination) above, 3:56, 6:128, 317, 7:366].

Then He, may His praise be exalted, made an exception for the oppressed (*al-mustaḍʿafīn*) whom the polytheists oppressed, "among men, women, and children," and they are those unable to emigrate, due to hardship, scarcity of means, poor sight, and lack of knowledge of the way, from their land, the land of polytheism, to the land of Islam, from the people whom He, may His remembrance be exalted, informed that their refuge is Hell. Hell is their refuge because of the excuse in which they are, as He, may His remembrance be exalted, has explained.¹

* * *

The word *al-mustaḍʿafīn* is in the accusative case as an exception from the *hāʾ* and *mīm* in His words, "For those, their refuge is Hell."² [See al-Farrāʾ, *Maʿānī al-Qurʾān*, 1:284. Abū Jaʿfar has departed from his method here and postponed discussion of His words "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death" until the end of the interpretation of the verse, p. ...]

* * *

Allah, may His praise be exalted, says: "For those, perhaps Allah will pardon them," meaning: these oppressed ones. He means: perhaps Allah will pardon them, because of the excuse in which they are, and they are believers. Thus He bestows favor upon them by overlooking their failure to emigrate, since they did not abandon it by choice or by preferring the abode of disbelief over the abode of Islam, but because of the inability in which they are to relocate from it. "And Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving." He means: Allah has never ceased to be *ʿAfuww*, that is, Possessor of pardon by His grace toward the sins of His servants, by not punishing them for them. "Forgiving" means: concealing their sins from them by His pardon for them.³ [see the explanation of *ʿafw* (pardon) and *ghafūr* (forgiving) in the lexical indices of the preceding volumes].

* * *

It is mentioned that these two verses and the one following them were revealed concerning groups of people from Makkah who had become Muslim and had believed in Allah and His Messenger, but who stayed behind and did not emigrate with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he emigrated. Some of them were subjected to trial (*fitnah*)⁴ and were seduced, and they fought alongside the polytheists against the Muslims. Allah refused to accept the excuse they offered, which He explained in His words, reporting about them: "They said, 'We were oppressed in the land.'"

* * *

Mention of the reports that confirm what we have mentioned: that the verse was revealed concerning those we have said it was revealed about.

**10259.** Abū Hishām al-Rifāʿī narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, saying: Ashʿath narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, regarding "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves": He said: Some people of Makkah had become Muslim, and whoever of them died there perished. Allah said: "For those, their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination, except for the oppressed among men, women, and children," up to His words "Pardoning and Forgiving." Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I am among them, and my mother is among them." ʿIkrimah said: "Al-ʿAbbās was among them."

**10260.** Aḥmad ibn Manṣūr al-Ramādī narrated to us, saying: Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Sharīk narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: A group of people from Makkah had become Muslim, and they were concealing their Islam. The polytheists took them out with them on the day of Badr. Some of them were struck down, and the Muslims said, "These companions of ours were Muslims, and they were coerced!" So they asked forgiveness for them. Then this was revealed: "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves, [the angels] said, 'In what [condition] were you?'" up to the end of the verse. He said: So a letter was written with this verse to those Muslims remaining in Makkah, [stating] that there was no excuse for them. [In the printed edition: "and that there was no excuse for them," with the addition of "and that," but I have kept what is in the manuscript, which agrees with Ibn Kathīr's *Tafsīr*.] He said: They went out, and the polytheists caught up with them and inflicted the *fitnah* upon them. So this was revealed concerning them: "And among people is he who says, 'We believe in Allah,' but when he is harmed for [the cause of] Allah, he considers the trial of people as the punishment of Allah" [Sūrah al-ʿAnkabūt: 10], up to the end of the verse. The Muslims wrote this to them, and they grieved and despaired of every good. Then this was revealed concerning them: "Indeed, your Lord, for those who emigrated after they were tried and then struggled and were patient, indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful" [Sūrah al-Naḥl: 110]. So they wrote to them with this: "Indeed, Allah has made for you a way out." So they went out, and the polytheists overtook them and fought them until whoever was saved was saved and whoever was killed was killed.

[Report 10260: Aḥmad ibn Manṣūr ibn Sayyār ibn al-Maʿārik al-Ramādī, the teacher of al-Ṭabarī, is trustworthy (*thiqah*). He is biographed in *al-Tahdhīb*. Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī has appeared many times previously. Muḥammad ibn Sharīk al-Makkī, Abū ʿUmārah, was described as "trustworthy" by Aḥmad and Ibn Maʿīn. He is biographed in *al-Tahdhīb*. This report was cited by Ibn Kathīr in his *Tafsīr* 2:552 from the *Tafsīr* of Ibn Abī Ḥātim, from Aḥmad ibn Manṣūr al-Ramādī. al-Suyūṭī cited it in *al-Durr al-Manthūr* 2:205 and attributed it additionally to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqī in his *Sunan*. It is in *al-Sunan al-Kubrā* 9:14, by way of Saʿdān ibn Naṣr, from Sufyān, from ʿAmr, from ʿIkrimah, with different wording. His words "*fa-aʿṭawhumu al-fitnah*" (they inflicted the *fitnah* upon them) appear thus in all the sources, except the *Tafsīr* of Ibn Kathīr, where it reads "*fa-aʿṭawhumu al-taqiyyah*" (they inflicted *taqiyyah* upon them), which is an error; the correct reading is that of the *Tafsīr* and the sources. Its meaning is: they disbelieved after their Islam. See the commentary on the following report, no. 10266.]

**10261.** Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ḥaywah informed me, or Ibn Lahīʿah (the doubt is from Yūnus), from Abū al-Aswad, that he heard a *mawlā* (freedman) of Ibn ʿAbbās say, from Ibn ʿAbbās: Some Muslims were with the polytheists, increasing the numbers of the polytheists against the Prophet ﷺ. An arrow would be shot and hit one of them and kill him, or he would be struck and killed. So Allah revealed concerning them: "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves," until "and emigrate therein."

**10262.** Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥakam narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥaywah informed us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Nawfal al-Asadī informed us, saying: A military expedition (*baʿth*) to Yemen was imposed upon the people of Madinah, and I was enrolled in it. I met ʿIkrimah, the freedman of Ibn ʿAbbās, and he forbade me from it most strongly. Then he said: Ibn ʿAbbās informed me that some Muslims were with the polytheists... and he mentioned a report similar to that of Yūnus, from Ibn Wahb.

[Reports 10261 and 10262: al-Bukhārī narrated it (*al-Fatḥ* 8:197–198) by the second chain, 10262, "from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-Muqriʾ, from Ḥaywah and others, who said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Abū al-Aswad, narrated to us." al-Bayhaqī narrated it in *al-Sunan* 9:12 by way of "Muḥammad ibn Maslamah al-Wāsiṭī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-Muqriʾ, Ḥaywah and a man narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Nawfal al-Asadī narrated to us," and he said: "Al-Bukhārī narrated it in the *Ṣaḥīḥ*."

It appears that the unnamed man in the chain of al-Bukhārī and al-Bayhaqī is "Ibn Lahīʿah," as appears in the first chain. The hāfiẓ (Ibn Ḥajar) in *al-Fatḥ* (8:198) reported that al-Ṭabarānī said: "None narrated it from Abū al-Aswad except al-Layth and Ibn Lahīʿah." The hāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar said: "The narration of al-Bukhārī by way of Ḥaywah refutes this, and the narration of Ibn Lahīʿah was also reported by Ibn Abī Ḥātim."

"Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ" is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-ʿAdawī, mentioned previously under nos. 318, 5451, 6743. "Abū al-Aswad" is Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Nawfal al-Asadī, the orphan of ʿUrwah, mentioned previously under no. 2891.

His words "A *baʿth* was imposed upon the people of Madinah": the hāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar said: "That is, an army. The meaning is that they were obliged to send out an army to fight the people of Syria. This was during the caliphate of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr over Makkah." As for "*ukttibtu*" (I was enrolled), it is in the passive voice.

Now, in the printed edition the words "to Yemen" were omitted, but they are present in the manuscript without doubt, though they are not found in all other versions of the report. They indicate that the hāfiẓ erred in his reasoning, since he claimed that the army went out to fight the people of Syria. It seems he derived that by inference in order to clear ʿIkrimah of the opinion of the Khawārij attributed to him. The hāfiẓ said in *al-Fatḥ* (8:198): "In this story is evidence of ʿIkrimah's innocence of the opinion attributed to him of the Khawārij, for he went to great lengths in forbidding fighting the Muslims and in declaring disbelievers the majority of those who fight them." This is a matter requiring further careful verification. Written by Maḥmūd Muḥammad Shākir.]

**10263.** Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves": They are people who stayed behind after the Prophet ﷺ and refused to go out with him. Whoever of them died before joining the Prophet ﷺ, the angels struck his face and his back.

**10264.** al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿIkrimah, regarding His words "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves, [the angels] said, 'In what [condition] were you?'" up to "and wretched is the destination": He said: It was revealed concerning Qays ibn al-Fākih ibn al-Mughīrah, al-Ḥārith ibn Zamʿah ibn al-Aswad, Qays ibn al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, Abū al-ʿĀṣ ibn Munabbih ibn al-Ḥajjāj, and ʿAlī ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf. [These names are as they appear in the manuscript and the printed edition, and the *al-Durr al-Manthūr* 2:295. Their unanimity made me hesitant to affirm what I know to be correct. These men who were killed at Badr are well known by their names in the biographies, and this is the correct form from the *Sīrah* of Ibn Hishām 2:295 and *Imtāʿ al-Asmāʿ* 1:20: "Abū Qays ibn al-Fākih ibn al-Mughīrah," "Abū Qays ibn al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah," "al-ʿĀṣ ibn Munabbih ibn al-Ḥajjāj." My strong belief is that this is an error of the copyists, not an error in the report. See the following report, no. 10266.] He said: When the polytheists of Quraysh and their followers went out to prevent Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb and the caravan of Quraysh from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions, and to seek retribution for what had been inflicted upon them at the Day of Nakhlah ["the Day of Nakhlah," meaning the expedition of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh ibn Ri'āb al-Asadī to Baṭn Nakhlah between Makkah and al-Ṭāʾif. ʿAbd Allāh and his companions went there until they stopped at Nakhlah, and a caravan of Quraysh passed by them, in which was ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥaḍramī. They killed ʿAmr and took some of the polytheists captive. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh and his companions came with the caravan and the two captives until they arrived before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Madinah. When they came to him, he said: "I did not command you to fight in the sacred month." See the *Sīrah* of Ibn Hishām 2:252–256 and *Imtāʿ al-Asmāʿ* 1:55–58.], they took with them young men who were unwilling. They had become Muslim, and they gathered at Badr without an appointment. They were killed at Badr as disbelievers, and they had turned back from Islam. They are those whom we have named. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujāhid said: This verse was revealed concerning those among the weak disbelievers of Quraysh who were killed on the Day of Badr. Ibn Jurayj said: ʿIkrimah said: When the Qur'an was revealed concerning these men, up to His words "and wretched is the destination, except for the oppressed among men, women, and children," He said: meaning the old man, the old woman, the small girls, and the boys.

**10265.** Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, regarding "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves," up to "and wretched is the destination": He said: When al-ʿAbbās, ʿAqīl, and Nawfal were taken captive, [i.e., al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, the uncle of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the two sons of his brothers: ʿAqīl ibn Abī Ṭālib ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, and Nawfal ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.] the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to al-ʿAbbās: "Ransom yourself and your two nephews." [In the printed edition and the manuscript it read "and your nephew" in the singular, but the correct form seems to be the dual, as I have written, though the singular "akhīka" is also correct, even though they are the sons of his two brothers, Abū Ṭālib and al-Ḥārith.] He said: "O Messenger of Allah, did we not pray toward your *qiblah* and bear witness to your testimony?" He said: "O al-ʿAbbās, you disputed and were defeated!" ["*Khuṣima*," in the passive voice: he was overcome in argument, and it means contention and reasoning.] Then he recited this verse: "Was not the earth of Allah spacious so you could emigrate therein? For those, their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination." So on the day this verse was revealed, whoever had become Muslim but had not emigrated was a disbeliever until he emigrated, except for the oppressed who are unable to devise a plan and are not guided to a way: a plan regarding wealth, and *al-sabīl* (the way) means the path. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I was among them, among the young boys."

**10266.** al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Ibn ʿUyaynah informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, who said: I heard ʿIkrimah say: Some people in Makkah had testified that there is no god but Allah. When the polytheists went out to Badr, they took them out with them, and they were killed. So this was revealed concerning them: "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves," up to "Those, perhaps Allah will pardon them, and Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving." The Muslims in Madinah wrote this to the Muslims in Makkah. He said: Some Muslims went out, until when they were on part of the road, the polytheists pursued them and overtook them. Some of them were subjected to the *fitnah* ["*Aʿṭawhu al-fitnah*," meaning they disbelieved after their Islam. See the commentary on the preceding report, no. 10260.], so Allah revealed concerning them: "And among people is he who says, 'We believe in Allah,' but when he is harmed for [the cause of] Allah, he considers the trial of people as the punishment of Allah" [Sūrah al-ʿAnkabūt: 10]. The Muslims in Madinah wrote this to the Muslims in Makkah. Allah revealed concerning those who were subjected to the *fitnah*: "Then indeed your Lord, for those who emigrated after they were tried and then struggled," up to "Forgiving and Merciful" [Sūrah al-Naḥl: 110]. [See the preceding report, no. 10260.]

1026​7 – Bishr ibn Muʿadh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words, "Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves" (to the end of the verse). It has been related to us that this verse was revealed concerning people from the people of Makkah who professed Islam, but then went out with the enemy of Allah, Abu Jahl, and were killed on the day of Badr. They offered excuses without valid reason, so Allah refused to accept them from them. And His words, "except the oppressed among men, women and children who cannot devise a plan nor are they guided to a way," are people from the people of Makkah whom Allah excused and excepted, saying: "Those - it is hoped that Allah will pardon them, and Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving." = He said: Ibn ʿAbbas used to say: "My mother and I were among those who could not devise a plan nor were guided to a way."
1026​8 – It was reported to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words, "Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves" (to the end of the verse): They are people from the hypocrites who stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and did not go out with him to Madinah, but went out with the polytheists of Quraysh to Badr, and were struck down that day among those who were struck down. So Allah revealed this verse concerning them.

He said: When the Prophet ﷺ was sent and prevailed, and faith sprang forth, hypocrisy sprang forth with it. [["Sprang forth" (nabaʿa), from the phrase "nabaʿa al-ma'" (water gushed forth), meaning it flowed and burst out from the depths of the earth.]] Some men came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, were it not that we fear these people will torture us and do this and that, we would have embraced Islam; but we testify that there is no god but Allah, and that you are the Messenger of Allah." And they would say this to him. When the day of Badr came, the polytheists stood up and said: "None of us will stay behind, but we will demolish his house and seize his wealth!" So those who used to say that statement to the Prophet ﷺ went out with them; a group of them was killed and a group was taken captive. He said: As for those who were killed, they are the ones concerning whom Allah said, "Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves," the whole verse, "Was not the earth of Allah spacious enough for you to emigrate therein?" and leave those who oppress you, "Those - their refuge is Hell, and evil is the destination." He said: Then Allah excused the people of sincerity, saying, "except the oppressed among men, women and children who cannot devise a plan nor are they guided to a way," who turn toward Him; had they gone out, they would have perished. "Then those - it is hoped that Allah will pardon them," for their remaining among the polytheists. And those who were taken captive said: "O Messenger of Allah, you know that we used to come to you and testify that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah, and that these people whom we went out with did so out of fear!" So Allah said: ﴿O Prophet, say to those in your hands of the captives: If Allah knows any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you and will forgive you﴾, your action which you did by going out with the polytheists against the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿And if they intend to betray you, then they have already betrayed Allah before, so He gave [you] power over them﴾, they went out with the polytheists. ﴿And Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 70, 71].

[[See the explanation of "al-Sabil" in what has passed, 1:497, and the other language indices in the previous volumes, root (s-b-l).]]

As for His words, "Indeed, those whom the angels take in death," there are two aspects to it: [[Al-Tabari, contrary to his usual practice, placed this section of his discourse out of its place, as I mentioned in another place.]]
One of them: that "tawaffahum" be in a position of nasb (accusative), meaning the past tense, because "fa'ala" is always in the nasb state. [[He means by "al-nasb" the fatha, i.e., that it is built on fatha because it is a past-tense verb. His words "fa'ala" mean the past-tense verb.]]
The other: that it be in a position of raf' (nominative), meaning the future tense, intending: "Indeed, those whom the angels will take in death," so one of the two "ta's" of "tawaffahum" is elided, yet intended within the word, because the Arabs do that: when two ta's come together at the beginning of a word, they sometimes drop one and keep the other, and sometimes keep both. [[See all of this in al-Farra's Maʿani al-Quran 1:284.]]

**Commentary of al-Ṭabarī (Jāmiʿ al-Bayān) on Sūrah 4, verses 97–99 (part 1 of 2)**

**On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves, [the angels] will say, "In what [condition] were you?" They will say, "We were oppressed in the land." [The angels] will say, "Was not the earth of Allah spacious so you could emigrate therein?" For those, their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.﴾ (97) ﴿Except for the oppressed among men, women, and children who are unable to devise a plan and are not guided to a way.﴾ (98) ﴿For those, perhaps Allah will pardon them, and Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.﴾ (99)**

Abū Jaʿfar said: By His words, "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death" (inna alladhīna tawaffāhumu al-malāʾikah), He, may His praise be exalted, means: indeed, those whose souls the angels seize [see the explanation of *tawaffī* (taking in death) above, 6:455, 8:73]. "While they are wronging themselves" means: earning for themselves the anger and wrath of Allah.

* * *

We have already explained the meaning of *ẓulm* (wronging) earlier [see the explanation of *ẓulm* in the lexical indices of the preceding volumes].

* * *

"They will say, 'In what [condition] were you?'" means: the angels will say to them, "In what [condition] were you?" That is, in what matter of your religion were you? "They will say, 'We were oppressed in the land,'" meaning: those whom the angels took in death, while wronging themselves, will say, "We were oppressed in the land." The people of polytheism (*shirk*) against Allah oppressed us in our land and country by their great numbers and strength, and they prevented us from believing in Allah and following His Messenger ﷺ. This is a weak excuse and a feeble argument. "[The angels] will say, 'Was not the earth of Allah spacious so you could emigrate therein?'" means: "Would you not have gone out from your land and homes, and departed from those who prevented you therein from believing in Allah and following His Messenger ﷺ, to a land whose people do not prevent you from the authority of the people of polytheism against Allah, so that you could affirm the oneness of Allah there and worship Him, and follow His Prophet?" [see the explanation of *hijrah* (emigration) above, 4:317–318, 7:490].

Allah, may His praise be exalted, says: "For those, their refuge is Hell," meaning: those whom I have described to you are the ones whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves. "Their refuge is Hell" means: their destination in the Hereafter is Hell, and it is their dwelling [see the explanation of *maʾwā* (refuge) above, 7:279, 494]. "And wretched is the destination" means: and wretched is Hell as a dwelling for its people who have come to it [see the explanation of *sāʾa* (wretched) above, 8:138, 358], "destination," and abode and refuge [see the explanation of *maṣīr* (destination) above, 3:56, 6:128, 317, 7:366].

Then He, may His praise be exalted, made an exception for the oppressed (*al-mustaḍʿafīn*) whom the polytheists oppressed, "among men, women, and children," and they are those unable to emigrate, due to hardship, scarcity of means, poor sight, and lack of knowledge of the way, from their land, the land of polytheism, to the land of Islam, from the people whom He, may His remembrance be exalted, informed that their refuge is Hell. Hell is their refuge because of the excuse in which they are, as He, may His remembrance be exalted, has explained.¹

* * *

The word *al-mustaḍʿafīn* is in the accusative case as an exception from the *hāʾ* and *mīm* in His words, "For those, their refuge is Hell."² [See al-Farrāʾ, *Maʿānī al-Qurʾān*, 1:284. Abū Jaʿfar has departed from his method here and postponed discussion of His words "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death" until the end of the interpretation of the verse, p. ...]

* * *

Allah, may His praise be exalted, says: "For those, perhaps Allah will pardon them," meaning: these oppressed ones. He means: perhaps Allah will pardon them, because of the excuse in which they are, and they are believers. Thus He bestows favor upon them by overlooking their failure to emigrate, since they did not abandon it by choice or by preferring the abode of disbelief over the abode of Islam, but because of the inability in which they are to relocate from it. "And Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving." He means: Allah has never ceased to be *ʿAfuww*, that is, Possessor of pardon by His grace toward the sins of His servants, by not punishing them for them. "Forgiving" means: concealing their sins from them by His pardon for them.³ [see the explanation of *ʿafw* (pardon) and *ghafūr* (forgiving) in the lexical indices of the preceding volumes].

* * *

It is mentioned that these two verses and the one following them were revealed concerning groups of people from Makkah who had become Muslim and had believed in Allah and His Messenger, but who stayed behind and did not emigrate with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he emigrated. Some of them were subjected to trial (*fitnah*)⁴ and were seduced, and they fought alongside the polytheists against the Muslims. Allah refused to accept the excuse they offered, which He explained in His words, reporting about them: "They said, 'We were oppressed in the land.'"

* * *

Mention of the reports that confirm what we have mentioned: that the verse was revealed concerning those we have said it was revealed about.

**10259.** Abū Hishām al-Rifāʿī narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, saying: Ashʿath narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, regarding "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves": He said: Some people of Makkah had become Muslim, and whoever of them died there perished. Allah said: "For those, their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination, except for the oppressed among men, women, and children," up to His words "Pardoning and Forgiving." Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I am among them, and my mother is among them." ʿIkrimah said: "Al-ʿAbbās was among them."

**10260.** Aḥmad ibn Manṣūr al-Ramādī narrated to us, saying: Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Sharīk narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: A group of people from Makkah had become Muslim, and they were concealing their Islam. The polytheists took them out with them on the day of Badr. Some of them were struck down, and the Muslims said, "These companions of ours were Muslims, and they were coerced!" So they asked forgiveness for them. Then this was revealed: "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves, [the angels] said, 'In what [condition] were you?'" up to the end of the verse. He said: So a letter was written with this verse to those Muslims remaining in Makkah, [stating] that there was no excuse for them. [In the printed edition: "and that there was no excuse for them," with the addition of "and that," but I have kept what is in the manuscript, which agrees with Ibn Kathīr's *Tafsīr*.] He said: They went out, and the polytheists caught up with them and inflicted the *fitnah* upon them. So this was revealed concerning them: "And among people is he who says, 'We believe in Allah,' but when he is harmed for [the cause of] Allah, he considers the trial of people as the punishment of Allah" [Sūrah al-ʿAnkabūt: 10], up to the end of the verse. The Muslims wrote this to them, and they grieved and despaired of every good. Then this was revealed concerning them: "Indeed, your Lord, for those who emigrated after they were tried and then struggled and were patient, indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful" [Sūrah al-Naḥl: 110]. So they wrote to them with this: "Indeed, Allah has made for you a way out." So they went out, and the polytheists overtook them and fought them until whoever was saved was saved and whoever was killed was killed.

[Report 10260: Aḥmad ibn Manṣūr ibn Sayyār ibn al-Maʿārik al-Ramādī, the teacher of al-Ṭabarī, is trustworthy (*thiqah*). He is biographed in *al-Tahdhīb*. Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī has appeared many times previously. Muḥammad ibn Sharīk al-Makkī, Abū ʿUmārah, was described as "trustworthy" by Aḥmad and Ibn Maʿīn. He is biographed in *al-Tahdhīb*. This report was cited by Ibn Kathīr in his *Tafsīr* 2:552 from the *Tafsīr* of Ibn Abī Ḥātim, from Aḥmad ibn Manṣūr al-Ramādī. al-Suyūṭī cited it in *al-Durr al-Manthūr* 2:205 and attributed it additionally to Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqī in his *Sunan*. It is in *al-Sunan al-Kubrā* 9:14, by way of Saʿdān ibn Naṣr, from Sufyān, from ʿAmr, from ʿIkrimah, with different wording. His words "*fa-aʿṭawhumu al-fitnah*" (they inflicted the *fitnah* upon them) appear thus in all the sources, except the *Tafsīr* of Ibn Kathīr, where it reads "*fa-aʿṭawhumu al-taqiyyah*" (they inflicted *taqiyyah* upon them), which is an error; the correct reading is that of the *Tafsīr* and the sources. Its meaning is: they disbelieved after their Islam. See the commentary on the following report, no. 10266.]

**10261.** Yūnus ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ḥaywah informed me, or Ibn Lahīʿah (the doubt is from Yūnus), from Abū al-Aswad, that he heard a *mawlā* (freedman) of Ibn ʿAbbās say, from Ibn ʿAbbās: Some Muslims were with the polytheists, increasing the numbers of the polytheists against the Prophet ﷺ. An arrow would be shot and hit one of them and kill him, or he would be struck and killed. So Allah revealed concerning them: "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves," until "and emigrate therein."

**10262.** Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥakam narrated to me, saying: Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ narrated to us, saying: Ḥaywah informed us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Nawfal al-Asadī informed us, saying: A military expedition (*baʿth*) to Yemen was imposed upon the people of Madinah, and I was enrolled in it. I met ʿIkrimah, the freedman of Ibn ʿAbbās, and he forbade me from it most strongly. Then he said: Ibn ʿAbbās informed me that some Muslims were with the polytheists... and he mentioned a report similar to that of Yūnus, from Ibn Wahb.

[Reports 10261 and 10262: al-Bukhārī narrated it (*al-Fatḥ* 8:197–198) by the second chain, 10262, "from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-Muqriʾ, from Ḥaywah and others, who said: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, Abū al-Aswad, narrated to us." al-Bayhaqī narrated it in *al-Sunan* 9:12 by way of "Muḥammad ibn Maslamah al-Wāsiṭī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-Muqriʾ, Ḥaywah and a man narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Nawfal al-Asadī narrated to us," and he said: "Al-Bukhārī narrated it in the *Ṣaḥīḥ*."

It appears that the unnamed man in the chain of al-Bukhārī and al-Bayhaqī is "Ibn Lahīʿah," as appears in the first chain. The hāfiẓ (Ibn Ḥajar) in *al-Fatḥ* (8:198) reported that al-Ṭabarānī said: "None narrated it from Abū al-Aswad except al-Layth and Ibn Lahīʿah." The hāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar said: "The narration of al-Bukhārī by way of Ḥaywah refutes this, and the narration of Ibn Lahīʿah was also reported by Ibn Abī Ḥātim."

"Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ" is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-ʿAdawī, mentioned previously under nos. 318, 5451, 6743. "Abū al-Aswad" is Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Nawfal al-Asadī, the orphan of ʿUrwah, mentioned previously under no. 2891.

His words "A *baʿth* was imposed upon the people of Madinah": the hāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar said: "That is, an army. The meaning is that they were obliged to send out an army to fight the people of Syria. This was during the caliphate of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr over Makkah." As for "*ukttibtu*" (I was enrolled), it is in the passive voice.

Now, in the printed edition the words "to Yemen" were omitted, but they are present in the manuscript without doubt, though they are not found in all other versions of the report. They indicate that the hāfiẓ erred in his reasoning, since he claimed that the army went out to fight the people of Syria. It seems he derived that by inference in order to clear ʿIkrimah of the opinion of the Khawārij attributed to him. The hāfiẓ said in *al-Fatḥ* (8:198): "In this story is evidence of ʿIkrimah's innocence of the opinion attributed to him of the Khawārij, for he went to great lengths in forbidding fighting the Muslims and in declaring disbelievers the majority of those who fight them." This is a matter requiring further careful verification. Written by Maḥmūd Muḥammad Shākir.]

**10263.** Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves": They are people who stayed behind after the Prophet ﷺ and refused to go out with him. Whoever of them died before joining the Prophet ﷺ, the angels struck his face and his back.

**10264.** al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿIkrimah, regarding His words "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves, [the angels] said, 'In what [condition] were you?'" up to "and wretched is the destination": He said: It was revealed concerning Qays ibn al-Fākih ibn al-Mughīrah, al-Ḥārith ibn Zamʿah ibn al-Aswad, Qays ibn al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, Abū al-ʿĀṣ ibn Munabbih ibn al-Ḥajjāj, and ʿAlī ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf. [These names are as they appear in the manuscript and the printed edition, and the *al-Durr al-Manthūr* 2:295. Their unanimity made me hesitant to affirm what I know to be correct. These men who were killed at Badr are well known by their names in the biographies, and this is the correct form from the *Sīrah* of Ibn Hishām 2:295 and *Imtāʿ al-Asmāʿ* 1:20: "Abū Qays ibn al-Fākih ibn al-Mughīrah," "Abū Qays ibn al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah," "al-ʿĀṣ ibn Munabbih ibn al-Ḥajjāj." My strong belief is that this is an error of the copyists, not an error in the report. See the following report, no. 10266.] He said: When the polytheists of Quraysh and their followers went out to prevent Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb and the caravan of Quraysh from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions, and to seek retribution for what had been inflicted upon them at the Day of Nakhlah ["the Day of Nakhlah," meaning the expedition of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh ibn Ri'āb al-Asadī to Baṭn Nakhlah between Makkah and al-Ṭāʾif. ʿAbd Allāh and his companions went there until they stopped at Nakhlah, and a caravan of Quraysh passed by them, in which was ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥaḍramī. They killed ʿAmr and took some of the polytheists captive. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh and his companions came with the caravan and the two captives until they arrived before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Madinah. When they came to him, he said: "I did not command you to fight in the sacred month." See the *Sīrah* of Ibn Hishām 2:252–256 and *Imtāʿ al-Asmāʿ* 1:55–58.], they took with them young men who were unwilling. They had become Muslim, and they gathered at Badr without an appointment. They were killed at Badr as disbelievers, and they had turned back from Islam. They are those whom we have named. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujāhid said: This verse was revealed concerning those among the weak disbelievers of Quraysh who were killed on the Day of Badr. As for His words, "Indeed, those whom the angels take in death," there are two aspects to it: [[Al-Tabari, contrary to his usual practice, placed this section of his discourse out of its place, as I mentioned in another place.]]
One of them: that "tawaffahum" be in a position of nasb (accusative), meaning the past tense, because "fa'ala" is always in the nasb state. [[He means by "al-nasb" the fatha, i.e., that it is built on fatha because it is a past-tense verb. His words "fa'ala" mean the past-tense verb.]]
The other: that it be in a position of raf' (nominative), meaning the future tense, intending: "Indeed, those whom the angels will take in death," so one of the two "ta's" of "tawaffahum" is elided, yet intended within the word, because the Arabs do that: when two ta's come together at the beginning of a word, they sometimes drop one and keep the other, and sometimes keep both. [[See all of this in al-Farra's Maʿani al-Quran 1:284.]]

**Commentary of al-Ṭabarī (Jāmiʿ al-Bayān) on Sūrah 4, verses 97–99 (part 1 of 2)**

**On the interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves, [the angels] will say, "In what [condition] were you?" They will say, "We were oppressed in the land." [The angels] will say, "Was not the earth of Allah spacious so you could emigrate therein?" For those, their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination.﴾ (97) ﴿Except for the oppressed among men, women, and children who are unable to devise a plan and are not guided to a way.﴾ (98) ﴿For those, perhaps Allah will pardon them, and Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving.﴾ (99)**

Abū Jaʿfar said: By His words, "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death" (inna alladhīna tawaffāhumu al-malāʾikah), He, may His praise be exalted, means: indeed, those whose souls the angels seize [see the explanation of *tawaffī* (taking in death) above, 6:455, 8:73]. "While they are wronging themselves" means: earning for themselves the anger and wrath of Allah.

* * *

We have already explained the meaning of *ẓulm* (wronging) earlier [see the explanation of *ẓulm* in the lexical indices of the preceding volumes].

* * *

"They will say, 'In what [condition] were you?'" means: the angels will say to them, "In what [condition] were you?" That is, in what matter of your religion were you? "They will say, 'We were oppressed in the land,'" meaning: those whom the angels took in death, while wronging themselves, will say, "We were oppressed in the land." The people of polytheism (*shirk*) against Allah oppressed us in our land and country by their great numbers and strength, and they prevented us from believing in Allah and following His Messenger ﷺ. This is a weak excuse and a feeble argument. "[The angels] will say, 'Was not the earth of Allah spacious so you could emigrate therein?'" means: "Would you not have gone out from your land and homes, and departed from those who prevented you therein from believing in Allah and following His Messenger ﷺ, to a land whose people do not prevent you from the authority of the people of polytheism against Allah, so that you could affirm the oneness of Allah there and worship Him, and follow His Prophet?" [see the explanation of *hijrah* (emigration) above, 4:317–318, 7:490].

Allah, may His praise be exalted, says: "For those, their refuge is Hell," meaning: those whom I have described to you are the ones whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves. "Their refuge is Hell" means: their destination in the Hereafter is Hell, and it is their dwelling [see the explanation of *maʾwā* (refuge) above, 7:279, 494]. "And wretched is the destination" means: and wretched is Hell as a dwelling for its people who have come to it [see the explanation of *sāʾa* (wretched) above, 8:138, 358], "destination," and abode and refuge [see the explanation of *maṣīr* (destination) above, 3:56, 6:128, 317, 7:366].

Then He, may His praise be exalted, made an exception for the oppressed (*al-mustaḍʿafīn*) whom the polytheists oppressed, "among men, women, and children," and they are those unable to emigrate, due to hardship, scarcity of means, poor sight, and lack of knowledge of the way, from their land, the land of polytheism, to the land of Islam, from the people whom He, may His remembrance be exalted, informed that their refuge is Hell. Hell is their refuge because of the excuse in which they are, as He, may His remembrance be exalted, has explained.¹

* * *

The word *al-mustaḍʿafīn* is in the accusative case as an exception from the *hāʾ* and *mīm* in His words, "For those, their refuge is Hell."² [See al-Farrāʾ, *Maʿānī al-Qurʾān*, 1:284. Abū Jaʿfar has departed from his method here and postponed discussion of His words "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death" until the end of the interpretation of the verse, p. ...]

* * *

Allah, may His praise be exalted, says: "For those, perhaps Allah will pardon them," meaning: these oppressed ones. He means: perhaps Allah will pardon them, because of the excuse in which they are, and they are believers. Thus He bestows favor upon them by overlooking their failure to emigrate, since they did not abandon it by choice or by preferring the abode of disbelief over the abode of Islam, but because of the inability in which they are to relocate from it. "And Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving." He means: Allah has never ceased to be *ʿAfuww*, that is, Possessor of pardon by His grace toward the sins of His servants, by not punishing them for them. "Forgiving" means: concealing their sins from them by His pardon for them.³ [see the explanation of *ʿafw* (pardon) and *ghafūr* (forgiving) in the lexical indices of the preceding volumes].

* * *

It is mentioned that these two verses and the one following them were revealed concerning groups of people from Makkah who had become Muslim and had believed in Allah and His Messenger, but who stayed behind and did not emigrate with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ when he emigrated. Some of them were subjected to trial (*fitnah*)⁴ and were seduced, and they fought alongside the polytheists against the Muslims. Allah refused to accept the excuse they offered, which He explained in His words, reporting about them: "They said, 'We were oppressed in the land.'"

* * *

Mention of the reports that confirm what we have mentioned: that the verse was revealed concerning those we have said it was revealed about.

**10259.** Abū Hishām al-Rifāʿī narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fuḍayl narrated to us, saying: Ashʿath narrated to us, from ʿIkrimah, regarding "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves": He said: Some people of Makkah had become Muslim, and whoever of them died there perished. Allah said: "For those, their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination, except for the oppressed among men, women, and children," up to His words "Pardoning and Forgiving." Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I am among them, and my mother is among them." ʿIkrimah said: "Al-ʿAbbās was among them."

**10260.** Aḥmad ibn Manṣūr al-Ramādī narrated to us, saying: Abū Aḥmad al-Zubayrī narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Sharīk narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: A group of people from Makkah had become Muslim, and they were concealing their Islam. The polytheists took them out with them on the day of Badr. Some of them were struck down, and the Muslims said, "These companions of ours were Muslims, and they were coerced!" So they asked forgiveness for them. Then this was revealed: "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves, [the angels] said, 'In what [condition] were you?'" up to the end of the verse. He said: So a letter was written with this verse to those Muslims remaining in Makkah, [stating] that there was no excuse for them. [In the printed edition: "and that there was no excuse for them," with the addition of "and that," but I have kept what is in the manuscript, which agrees with Ibn Kathīr's *Tafsīr*.] He said: They went out, and the polytheists caught up with them and inflicted the *fitnah* upon them. So this was revealed concerning them: "And among people is he who says, 'We believe in Allah,' but when he is harmed for [the cause of] Allah, he considers the trial of people as the punishment of Allah" [Sūrah al-ʿAnkabūt: 10], up to the end of the verse. The Muslims wrote this to them, and they grieved and despaired of every good. Then this was revealed concerning them: "Indeed, your Lord, for those who emigrated after they were tried and then struggled and were patient, indeed your Lord, after that, is Forgiving and Merciful" [Sūrah al-Naḥl: 110]. So they wrote to them with this: "Indeed, Allah has made for you a way out." So they went out, and the polytheists overtook them and fought them until whoever was saved was saved and whoever was killed was killed.

It appears that the unnamed man in the chain of al-Bukhārī and al-Bayhaqī is "Ibn Lahīʿah," as appears in the first chain. The hāfiẓ (Ibn Ḥajar) in *al-Fatḥ* (8:198) reported that al-Ṭabarānī said: "None narrated it from Abū al-Aswad except al-Layth and Ibn Lahīʿah." The hāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar said: "The narration of al-Bukhārī by way of Ḥaywah refutes this, and the narration of Ibn Lahīʿah was also reported by Ibn Abī Ḥātim."

"Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Muqriʾ" is ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd al-ʿAdawī, mentioned previously under nos. 318, 5451, 6743. "Abū al-Aswad" is Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Nawfal al-Asadī, the orphan of ʿUrwah, mentioned previously under no. 2891.

His words "A *baʿth* was imposed upon the people of Madinah": the hāfiẓ Ibn Ḥajar said: "That is, an army. The meaning is that they were obliged to send out an army to fight the people of Syria. This was during the caliphate of ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr over Makkah." As for "*ukttibtu*" (I was enrolled), it is in the passive voice.

Now, in the printed edition the words "to Yemen" were omitted, but they are present in the manuscript without doubt, though they are not found in all other versions of the report. They indicate that the hāfiẓ erred in his reasoning, since he claimed that the army went out to fight the people of Syria. It seems he derived that by inference in order to clear ʿIkrimah of the opinion of the Khawārij attributed to him. The hāfiẓ said in *al-Fatḥ* (8:198): "In this story is evidence of ʿIkrimah's innocence of the opinion attributed to him of the Khawārij, for he went to great lengths in forbidding fighting the Muslims and in declaring disbelievers the majority of those who fight them." This is a matter requiring further careful verification. Written by Maḥmūd Muḥammad Shākir.]

**10263.** Muḥammad ibn Saʿd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves": They are people who stayed behind after the Prophet ﷺ and refused to go out with him. Whoever of them died before joining the Prophet ﷺ, the angels struck his face and his back.

**10264.** al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿIkrimah, regarding His words "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves, [the angels] said, 'In what [condition] were you?'" up to "and wretched is the destination": He said: It was revealed concerning Qays ibn al-Fākih ibn al-Mughīrah, al-Ḥārith ibn Zamʿah ibn al-Aswad, Qays ibn al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, Abū al-ʿĀṣ ibn Munabbih ibn al-Ḥajjāj, and ʿAlī ibn Umayyah ibn Khalaf. [These names are as they appear in the manuscript and the printed edition, and the *al-Durr al-Manthūr* 2:295. Their unanimity made me hesitant to affirm what I know to be correct. These men who were killed at Badr are well known by their names in the biographies, and this is the correct form from the *Sīrah* of Ibn Hishām 2:295 and *Imtāʿ al-Asmāʿ* 1:20: "Abū Qays ibn al-Fākih ibn al-Mughīrah," "Abū Qays ibn al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah," "al-ʿĀṣ ibn Munabbih ibn al-Ḥajjāj." My strong belief is that this is an error of the copyists, not an error in the report. See the following report, no. 10266.] He said: When the polytheists of Quraysh and their followers went out to prevent Abū Sufyān ibn Ḥarb and the caravan of Quraysh from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and his Companions, and to seek retribution for what had been inflicted upon them at the Day of Nakhlah ["the Day of Nakhlah," meaning the expedition of ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh ibn Ri'āb al-Asadī to Baṭn Nakhlah between Makkah and al-Ṭāʾif. ʿAbd Allāh and his companions went there until they stopped at Nakhlah, and a caravan of Quraysh passed by them, in which was ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥaḍramī. They killed ʿAmr and took some of the polytheists captive. ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jaḥsh and his companions came with the caravan and the two captives until they arrived before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in Madinah. When they came to him, he said: "I did not command you to fight in the sacred month." See the *Sīrah* of Ibn Hishām 2:252–256 and *Imtāʿ al-Asmāʿ* 1:55–58.], they took with them young men who were unwilling. They had become Muslim, and they gathered at Badr without an appointment. They were killed at Badr as disbelievers, and they had turned back from Islam. They are those whom we have named. Ibn Jurayj said: Mujāhid said: This verse was revealed concerning those among the weak disbelievers of Quraysh who were killed on the Day of Badr. Ibn Jurayj said: ʿIkrimah said: When the Qur'an was revealed concerning these men, up to His words "and wretched is the destination, except for the oppressed among men, women, and children," He said: meaning the old man, the old woman, the small girls, and the boys.

**10265.** Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Aḥmad ibn Mufaḍḍal narrated to us, saying: Asbāṭ narrated to us, from al-Suddī, regarding "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves," up to "and wretched is the destination": He said: When al-ʿAbbās, ʿAqīl, and Nawfal were taken captive, [i.e., al-ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, the uncle of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the two sons of his brothers: ʿAqīl ibn Abī Ṭālib ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib, and Nawfal ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.] the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to al-ʿAbbās: "Ransom yourself and your two nephews." [In the printed edition and the manuscript it read "and your nephew" in the singular, but the correct form seems to be the dual, as I have written, though the singular "akhīka" is also correct, even though they are the sons of his two brothers, Abū Ṭālib and al-Ḥārith.] He said: "O Messenger of Allah, did we not pray toward your *qiblah* and bear witness to your testimony?" He said: "O al-ʿAbbās, you disputed and were defeated!" ["*Khuṣima*," in the passive voice: he was overcome in argument, and it means contention and reasoning.] Then he recited this verse: "Was not the earth of Allah spacious so you could emigrate therein? For those, their refuge is Hell, and wretched is the destination." So on the day this verse was revealed, whoever had become Muslim but had not emigrated was a disbeliever until he emigrated, except for the oppressed who are unable to devise a plan and are not guided to a way: a plan regarding wealth, and *al-sabīl* (the way) means the path. Ibn ʿAbbās said: "I was among them, among the young boys."

**10266.** al-Ḥasan ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Razzāq informed us, saying: Ibn ʿUyaynah informed us, from ʿAmr ibn Dīnār, who said: I heard ʿIkrimah say: Some people in Makkah had testified that there is no god but Allah. When the polytheists went out to Badr, they took them out with them, and they were killed. So this was revealed concerning them: "Indeed, those whom the angels took in death while they were wronging themselves," up to "Those, perhaps Allah will pardon them, and Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving." The Muslims in Madinah wrote this to the Muslims in Makkah. He said: Some Muslims went out, until when they were on part of the road, the polytheists pursued them and overtook them. Some of them were subjected to the *fitnah* ["*Aʿṭawhu al-fitnah*," meaning they disbelieved after their Islam. See the commentary on the preceding report, no. 10260.], so Allah revealed concerning them: "And among people is he who says, 'We believe in Allah,' but when he is harmed for [the cause of] Allah, he considers the trial of people as the punishment of Allah" [Sūrah al-ʿAnkabūt: 10]. The Muslims in Madinah wrote this to the Muslims in Makkah. Allah revealed concerning those who were subjected to the *fitnah*: "Then indeed your Lord, for those who emigrated after they were tried and then struggled," up to "Forgiving and Merciful" [Sūrah al-Naḥl: 110]. [See the preceding report, no. 10260.]
