1026​7 – Bishr ibn Muʿadh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, concerning His words, "Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves" (to the end of the verse). It has been related to us that this verse was revealed concerning people from the people of Makkah who professed Islam, but then went out with the enemy of Allah, Abu Jahl, and were killed on the day of Badr. They offered excuses without valid reason, so Allah refused to accept them from them. And His words, "except the oppressed among men, women and children who cannot devise a plan nor are they guided to a way," are people from the people of Makkah whom Allah excused and excepted, saying: "Those - it is hoped that Allah will pardon them, and Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving." = He said: Ibn ʿAbbas used to say: "My mother and I were among those who could not devise a plan nor were guided to a way."
1026​8 – It was reported to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Muʿadh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His words, "Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves" (to the end of the verse): They are people from the hypocrites who stayed behind from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and did not go out with him to Madinah, but went out with the polytheists of Quraysh to Badr, and were struck down that day among those who were struck down. So Allah revealed this verse concerning them.
1026​9 – Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I asked him - meaning Ibn Zayd - about the saying of Allah, "Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves," and he recited until he reached, "except the oppressed among men, women and children." He said: When the Prophet ﷺ was sent and prevailed, and faith sprang forth, hypocrisy sprang forth with it. [["Sprang forth" (nabaʿa), from the phrase "nabaʿa al-ma'" (water gushed forth), meaning it flowed and burst out from the depths of the earth.]] Some men came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, were it not that we fear these people will torture us and do this and that, we would have embraced Islam; but we testify that there is no god but Allah, and that you are the Messenger of Allah." And they would say this to him. When the day of Badr came, the polytheists stood up and said: "None of us will stay behind, but we will demolish his house and seize his wealth!" So those who used to say that statement to the Prophet ﷺ went out with them; a group of them was killed and a group was taken captive. He said: As for those who were killed, they are the ones concerning whom Allah said, "Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves," the whole verse, "Was not the earth of Allah spacious enough for you to emigrate therein?" and leave those who oppress you, "Those - their refuge is Hell, and evil is the destination." He said: Then Allah excused the people of sincerity, saying, "except the oppressed among men, women and children who cannot devise a plan nor are they guided to a way," who turn toward Him; had they gone out, they would have perished. "Then those - it is hoped that Allah will pardon them," for their remaining among the polytheists. And those who were taken captive said: "O Messenger of Allah, you know that we used to come to you and testify that there is no god but Allah and that you are the Messenger of Allah, and that these people whom we went out with did so out of fear!" So Allah said: ﴿O Prophet, say to those in your hands of the captives: If Allah knows any good in your hearts, He will give you better than what was taken from you and will forgive you﴾, your action which you did by going out with the polytheists against the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿And if they intend to betray you, then they have already betrayed Allah before, so He gave [you] power over them﴾, they went out with the polytheists. ﴿And Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 70, 71].

[[See the explanation of "al-Sabil" in what has passed, 1:497, and the other language indices in the previous volumes, root (s-b-l).]]

As for His words, "Indeed, those whom the angels take in death," there are two aspects to it: [[Al-Tabari, contrary to his usual practice, placed this section of his discourse out of its place, as I mentioned in another place.]]
One of them: that "tawaffahum" be in a position of nasb (accusative), meaning the past tense, because "fa'ala" is always in the nasb state. [[He means by "al-nasb" the fatha, i.e., that it is built on fatha because it is a past-tense verb. His words "fa'ala" mean the past-tense verb.]]
The other: that it be in a position of raf' (nominative), meaning the future tense, intending: "Indeed, those whom the angels will take in death," so one of the two "ta's" of "tawaffahum" is elided, yet intended within the word, because the Arabs do that: when two ta's come together at the beginning of a word, they sometimes drop one and keep the other, and sometimes keep both. [[See all of this in al-Farra's Maʿani al-Quran 1:284.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 100 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Whoever emigrates in the way of Allah will find on earth many a refuge and abundance. And whoever leaves his home emigrating to Allah and His Messenger and then death overtakes him, his reward has already become due from Allah. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ (4:100)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "Whoever emigrates in the way of Allah," He means: whoever departs from the land of polytheism and its people, fleeing with his religion from them and from it, to the land of Islam and its believing people [[See the explanation of "hijra" (emigration) above, p. 100, note 3, and the references there.]] = "in the way of Allah," meaning: in the path of the religion of Allah and His way, which He has prescribed for His creation, and that is the upright religion [[See the explanation of "sabil Allah" (the way of Allah) in the lexicographical sources.]] = "will find on earth many a refuge," meaning: this emigrant in the way of Allah will find = "many a refuge," and it is the place of movement and retreat in the lands.
* *
It is said of it: "Fulan opposed (rāgama) his people, opposition (muraghamah) and resistance (muraghamah)," as a verbal noun, and from it is the saying of the poet Nabigha of Banu Ja'da:

Like a mountain sheltered by its pillars,
Mighty in refuge and in escape.

[[From his diwan, p. 22; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubaydah 1:138; al-Lisan (r-gh-m). The verse is from his qasidah in the diwan, but it was cited alone, so its place is not known. "al-Tawd" means a great, lofty mountain. I do not know what the particle of comparison (kaf) governs.]]

As for His saying "abundance (sa'ah)," it may refer to the ease in the matter of their religion in Mecca, [[This phrase appears thus in the printed edition and in the manuscript, and it is not sound. I suspect that something from Abu Ja'far's speech has fallen out by the copyist, and perhaps it reads as follows: "As for His saying 'abundance,' it may refer to abundance in provision, and it may refer to abundance in the matter of their religion, from their being wronged in the land of the polytheists in Mecca, and that is their prevention...." Then His saying "and that is their prevention" is an explanation of "constraint (diq)," as is evident from Abu Ja'far's interpretation. See what will come later in the interpretation of the meaning of "sa'ah," p. 122.]] and that is their prevention of them from openly manifesting their religion and worshipping their Lord. [[In the printed edition, the word "kana" placed here between the two lines was dropped, the editor thinking it an error and an addition. It is sound Arabic speech; they use "kana" in this position to indicate the past, as if he said: "and that is what their prevention of them was," but the editor failed to know its meaning, so he omitted "kana," and did wrong.]]
* *
Then His praise, may He be exalted, informed about the one who went out emigrating from the land of polytheism, fleeing with his religion to Allah and His Messenger, that if his appointed death overtook him before he reached the land of Islam and the abode of emigration, He said: whoever is like that = "his reward has already become due from Allah," and that is the recompense for his deed and the payment for his emigration and his separation from his homeland and kin to the abode of Islam and the people of his religion. [[See the explanation of "ajr" (reward) above, p. 98, note 2, and the references there.]] His praise, may He be exalted, says: whoever goes out from his house emigrating to Allah and His Messenger, has deserved the reward of his emigration = if death cuts him off before he reaches the abode of his emigration [["akhramathu al-manayyah" means death took him from among his companions and cut him off from them, from "al-kharm," which is splitting and cutting; it is said: "I did not cut anything from it," meaning: I neither diminished nor severed it.]] = from his Lord. "And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful," meaning: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, has never ceased to be "Forgiving," that is, covering the sins of His believing servants by pardoning them from punishment for them, "Merciful," gentle with them. [[See the explanation of "kana," "ghafur," and "rahim" in their places in the lexical indexes in the preceding volumes.]]
* *
It is mentioned that this verse was revealed concerning a certain man who was residing in Mecca and was a Muslim, and he went out when he heard that Allah had revealed the two verses before it, namely His saying: "Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves" up to His saying: "And Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving," and he died on his way before reaching Medina.

Mention of the reports transmitted concerning that:

10282 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, concerning His saying: "And whoever leaves his house emigrating to Allah and His Messenger," he said: There was a man from Khuza'ah called Damrah ibn al-'Is, or al-'Is ibn Damrah ibn Zanbaa'. He said: When they were ordered to emigrate, he was sick, so he commanded his family to spread a bed for him on his litter and carry him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He said: They did so, and death came to him at al-Tan'im, and this verse was revealed. [[Report 10282, narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 9:14, 15. This story concerns one man whose name and his father's name differ in more than ten ways, as al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Isabah. Abu Ja'far here cites from 10282 to 10295 most of the variant forms of his name and his father's name, so I have omitted indicating this variance at its places in the following reports.
"al-Tan'im" is a place in the sacred territory (al-hill), between Marr and Sarif, two farsakhs from Mecca. From al-Tan'im, those of Mecca who wish to perform 'umrah enter the state of ihram.]]

10284 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, from al-'Awwam al-Taymi, similar to the report of Ya'qub, from Hushaym, he said: And he was a man from Khuza'ah. [[Report 10284: I have not found any mention of "al-'Awwam al-Taymi" in the biographical works, and I fear the correct reading is "al-'Awwam, from al-Taymi," meaning "al-'Awwam ibn Hawshab al-Shaybani," who narrates from "Ibrahim al-Taymi." And "Hushaym" narrates from "al-'Awwam ibn Hawshab."]]

10285 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "And whoever emigrates in the way of Allah will find on earth many a refuge and abundance," the verse. He said: When Allah revealed these verses, and a man from the believers called "Damrah" was in Mecca, he said: "By Allah, I have wealth that will bring me to Medina and further than it, and I am guided! Take me out!" He was sick at that time, and when he crossed the sacred territory (al-haram), Allah took him and he died. So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: "And whoever leaves his house emigrating to Allah," the verse.

10286 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, who said: When "Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves" was revealed, a man among the Muslims that day, who was sick, said: "By Allah, I have no excuse. I am a guide on the road, and I am well-off, so carry me," [[His saying "I am a guide (dalil) on the road," means one who knows it; it is said: "I knew this road well (dallaltu bihadha al-tariq dalalah)," meaning I knew it, so he is a guide with clear knowledge.]] so they carried him, and death overtook him on the road, and it was revealed concerning him: "And whoever leaves his house emigrating to Allah and His Messenger."

10287 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ibn 'Uyaynah informed us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, who said: I heard 'Ikrimah say: When Allah revealed "Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves," the two verses, a man of Banu Damrah, who was sick, said: "Take me out to al-Rawh," [[His saying "to al-Rawh" (with a fatha on the ra and a sukun on the waw) means: to spaciousness, rest, and the coolness of the breeze. This is its explanation. It will come in no. 10290, "Perhaps I will go out and the breeze (rawh) will reach me," meaning the coolness of the breeze, and he had been feeling the heat in Mecca until it distressed him, as will come in report 10294.
As for "al-Haslas," it is a place in the Hijaz; Yaqut said it is "a mountain overlooking Dhu Tuwa," meaning in the region of Mecca. It is also said "Dhu al-Haslas." A Hijazi poet said: Would that I knew whether after us the gazelles of Dhu al-Haslas have changed, their eyes large-lidded. And I have a wounded liver, in which the cracks of love have appeared; if only there were a smith to forge it!]] so they took him out, until when he was at al-Haslas he died, and it was revealed concerning him: "And whoever leaves his house emigrating to Allah and His Messenger," the verse.

10288 - Ibn Wakf' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from al-Mundhir ibn Tha'labah, from 'Alba' ibn Ahmar al-Yashkuri, concerning His saying: "And whoever leaves his house emigrating to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward has already become due from Allah," he said: It was revealed concerning a man from Khuza'ah. [[Report 10288: "Tha'labah ibn al-Mundhir ibn Harb al-Ta'i." And "'Alba' ibn Ahmar al-Yashkuri" were mentioned under no. 7190.]]

10289 - Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Qurrah narrated to us, from al-Dahhak, concerning the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: "And whoever leaves his house emigrating to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward has already become due from Allah," he said: When a man of the people of Mecca heard that the Banu Kinanah had been struck on their faces and backs by the angels, he said to his family: "Take me out," and he was near death. [[It is said: "the sun drew near to setting (dinfat al-shams lil-maghib)" (on the pattern of farih), and "adnafat," when it drew near to setting and became yellow; and likewise it is said of the sick: "the sick man became weak and near death (dinaf al-mari wa adnaf)," meaning he became heavy and drew near to death. And "al-danaf" (with two fathas) is a constant, persistent illness.]] He said: So he was carried until he reached a steep pass which he named, [["al-'aqabah" (with fathas) is a rough path in the mountain; or it is a long mountain that presents itself across the road, so one takes it.]] and he died, so Allah revealed: "And whoever leaves his house emigrating to Allah and His Messenger," the verse. [[Report 10289: This report is missing from the manuscript.]]

10290 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, who said: When Damrah ibn Jundab al-Dammari heard this = meaning, His saying: "Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves" up to His saying: "And Allah is ever Pardoning and Forgiving" = [in the printed edition: "when he heard of this"; the manuscript differs; the change is harmless, though the manuscript reading is also correct] he said to his family, and he was in pain: "Prepare my mount, for the two mountains have distressed me!" = meaning the two mountains of Mecca = "Perhaps I will go out and the breeze will reach me!" [[See the note above, p. 115, note 3.]] So he sat upon his mount, then headed toward Medina, and died on the road, so Allah revealed: "And whoever leaves his house emigrating to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward has already become due from Allah." As for when he set out toward Medina, he said: "O Allah, I am emigrating to You and to Your Messenger."

10291 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ikrimah, who said: When this verse was revealed = meaning His saying: "Indeed, those whom the angels take in death" = Jundub ibn Damrah al-Judda'i said: "O Allah, You have made the excuse and the proof complete, and I have no excuse and no proof!" He said: Then he went out, being an old man, and he died on part of the road. The companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: He died before he emigrated, and we do not know whether he is in authority or not! So it was revealed: "And whoever leaves his house emigrating to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward has already become due from Allah."

10292 - It was narrated to me on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say: When Allah revealed concerning those who were killed with the polytheists of Quraysh at Badr: "Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves," the verse, a man of Banu Layth, who was upon the religion of the Prophet ﷺ and residing in Mecca, and who was among those whom Allah excused, heard what Allah had revealed concerning them. He was an old man, afflicted with a lasting illness [[In the printed edition: "wada'an" (bright/pleasing), which has no acceptable meaning here; in the manuscript: "wasiyyan" with a ya, a corruption of what I have adopted. "Rajul wasib" means one whose illness persisted, clung to him and remained fixed upon him. "Al-wasab" (with two fathas) is a painful, lasting illness.]], and he said to his family: "I will not spend the night in Mecca tonight!" So he was taken out [[In the printed edition: "they took him out sick," which appears to be an alteration by a copyist or the first editor. In the Ad-Durr al-Manthur 2:208: "they took him out" without "sick." I have adopted the manuscript: "fakhruja bihi," in the passive.]], until when he reached al-Tan'im on the road to Medina, death overtook him, and it was revealed concerning him: "And whoever leaves his house emigrating to Allah," the verse.

10293 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His saying: "And whoever emigrates in the way of Allah will find on earth many a refuge and abundance," he said: A man from Banu Kinanah emigrated desiring the Prophet ﷺ and died on the road. His people mocked him and ridiculed him and said: "He has neither reached what he wanted, nor did he remain among his family, who would attend to him and bury him!" There was in Mecca a man called "Damrah," [[In the printed edition: "and there was in Mecca" with a waw; I have adopted the manuscript.]] from Banu Bakr, and he was sick, and he said to his family: "Take me out of Mecca, for I feel the heat." They said: "Where shall we take you?" He pointed with his hand toward Medina, so this verse was revealed: "And whoever leaves his house emigrating to Allah and His Messenger," to the end of the verse.

10295 - Al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn Aban narrated to us, saying: Qays narrated to us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: When this verse was revealed: "Those of the believers who sit at home, other than those with a disability, are not equal," [[Qur'an 4:95.]] some Muslims among those in Mecca, from those with disabilities, were granted concession in it, until the excellence of the strivers over those who sit at home was revealed. They said: "Allah has made clear the excellence of the strivers over those who sit, and has granted concession to those with disabilities!" until it was revealed: "Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they are wronging themselves," up to His saying: "and evil is their destination." They said: "This is binding!" until it was revealed: "except the weak among men and women and children, who are unable to devise a plan nor are they guided to a way" (4:98). Then Damrah ibn al-'Is al-Zuraqi, one of Banu Layth, who had lost his sight, said: "I have a plan, I have wealth, and I have slaves, so carry me." He went out while sick, and death overtook him at al-Tan'im, and he was buried near the Mosque of al-Tan'im. So this verse was revealed concerning him: "And whoever leaves his house emigrating to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him..." the verse. [[Report 10295: "al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah" is named after his grandfather; he is "al-Harith ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Usamah al-Tamimi," born in Shawwal 186 AH and died on the day of 'Arafah at mid-morning in 282 AH, at ninety-six years of age. Now, you have seen how they differed about the name of the man who went out emigrating to Allah and His Messenger, and I have left indicating this difference as I previously stated, for verifying any part of his name and his father's name nearly is impossible.]]

The interpreters differed concerning the interpretation of "muraghaman" (a refuge).
Some of them said: It is moving from one land to another land.
Mention of those who said that:

10296 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: "many a refuge," he said: "al-muraghbam" is moving from one land to another land.

10297 - It was narrated to me on the authority of al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say concerning His saying: "muraghaman kathiran" (many a refuge): he means: a place of transfer.

10298 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' concerning His saying: "finds on earth many a refuge," he said: a place of transfer.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 100 (part 2 of 2):

10299 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Abu Sufyan narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Hasan or Qatadah: "murāghaman kathīran" (much room to move and refuge), he said: "mutaḥawwilan" (one who changes place).

10300 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: "yajid fi'l-ardi murāghaman kathīran", he said: "mundūḥatan 'amma yukrah" (a way out from what is disliked).

* *

10301 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: "murāghaman kathīran", he said: "muzaḥzaḥan 'amma yukrah" (one who moves away from what is disliked).

10302 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "murāghaman kathīran", he said: "mutazaḥzaḥan 'amma yukrah" (one who moves away from what is disliked).

Others said: "mubtaghā ma'ishah" (a seeking of livelihood).

Those who said this:

10303 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "yajid fi'l-ardi murāghaman kathīran", he says: "mubtaghan lil-ma'ishah" (seeking livelihood).

Others said: "al-murāghamu" is the emigrant (al-muhājir).

Those who said this:

10304 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "murāghaman", "al-murāghamu" is "al-muhājaru" (the place of emigration).

Abu Ja'far said: We have already explained the most correct of these sayings earlier. [[See what has passed, pp. 112, 113.]]

They also differed regarding the meaning of "al-sa'ah" (abundance/ease) which Allah mentioned in this place, when He said: "wa-sa'ah" (and ease). Some of them said: it is abundance in provision.

Those who said this:

10305 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "murāghaman kathīran wa-sa'ah", he said: "al-sa'ah fi'l-rizq" (abundance in provision).

10306 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His saying: "murāghaman kathīran wa-sa'ah", he said: "al-sa'ah fi'l-rizq" (abundance in provision).

10307 - It was reported to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: "wa-sa'ah", he says: "sa'ah fi'l-rizq" (abundance in provision).

* *

Others said concerning this:

10308 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "yajid fi'l-ardi murāghaman kathīran wa-sa'ah", i.e., by Allah, from misguidance to guidance, and from poverty (al-'aylah) to wealth (al-ghina). [["al-'aylah": poverty.]]

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings is to say: Allah informed that whoever emigrates in His cause finds in the earth room to move (mudtarab) and breadth (mutta'sa'). "Al-sa'ah" includes abundance in provision and wealth after poverty, and it includes ease from the constriction of distress and grief in which the people of faith among the polytheists of Makkah were, and other meanings of "al-sa'ah" which carry the sense of relief and release (al-rawh wa-al-faraj) from the hardship Allah disliked for the believers by their remaining among the polytheists and under their authority. Allah did not indicate that by His saying "wa-sa'ah" He meant only some of the meanings of "al-sa'ah" we have described. So every meaning of "al-sa'ah" that is in the sense of relief and release from what they were in, namely the narrowness of living, the grief of dwelling among the people of polytheism, and the constriction of the breast from being unable to openly manifest faith in Allah, sincerely affirm His oneness, and abandon rivals and false gods, is included in it.

Some scholars have interpreted this verse, meaning His saying: "And whoever leaves his house emigrating to Allah and His Messenger, then death overtakes him, his reward has indeed fallen upon Allah" [as referring to the ruling on one who goes out to fight], that he is like the warrior who sets out for battle, then death overtakes him after he has departed from his dwelling, separated, and he dies; he has a share of the spoils even if he did not witness the engagement, as:

10309 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Yusuf ibn 'Adiy narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Ibn Lahi'ah, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib: that the people of Madinah used to say: "Whoever sets out separating (from home), his share becomes due," and they interpreted His saying, blessed and exalted is He: "And whoever leaves his house emigrating to Allah and His Messenger." [[The report 10309: Yusuf ibn 'Adi ibn Zurayq al-Taymi, a Kufan who settled in Egypt and died there in 232 AH. Trustworthy (thiqah). Biography in al-Tahdhib. "Yazid ibn Abi Habib al-Misri" has appeared earlier under nos. 4348, 5493.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 101 (part 1 of 3):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And when you travel through the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you. Indeed, the disbelievers are ever to you a clear enemy.﴾ (101)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "And when you travel through the land," He means: when you, O believers, journey through the land [[See the explanation of "travelling through the land" in what has preceded, 5: 593 / 7: 332.]] "then there is no blame upon you," meaning: there is no sin or wrongdoing upon you [[See the explanation of "janah" (blame) in what has preceded, 8: 180, footnote 1, and the references there.]] "in shortening the prayer," meaning: in reducing its number, so that you pray what was prescribed for you in number when resident, four, as two, according to some of them.

It has been said: its meaning is, there is no blame upon you in reducing the prayer to its least number while travelling through the land, indicating one rak'ah, according to others.

And others said: the meaning of that is, there is no blame upon you in shortening the prescribed limits of the prayer. "If you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you," meaning: if you apprehend that those who disbelieve may tempt you in your prayer. [[See the explanation of "fear" in what has preceded, 8: 298, 318, footnote 3, and the references there.]] Their temptation of them in it is: attacking them while they are prostrating, until they kill them or take them captive, thereby preventing them from establishing and performing it, and coming between them and the worship of God and sincere monotheism toward Him. [[See the explanation of "fitnah" (temptation) in what has preceded, 9: 28, footnote 1, and the references there.]]

= Then He, may His praise be exalted, informed them about what the people of disbelief are upon concerning them, saying: "Indeed, the disbelievers are ever to you a clear enemy," meaning: those who deny the oneness of God, "are ever to you a clear enemy," that is: an enemy who has made their enmity clear to you by their opposition to you in war because of your faith in God and His Messenger, and your abandoning the worship of what they worship of idols and images, and your opposing what they are upon of error. [[In the printed edition: "meaning: those who deny..." with the nominative, and what I have recorded from the manuscript is pure correctness, which is what Abu Ja'far followed in similar cases of tafsir.]]

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of "qasr" (shortening) by which God removed blame from its doer. Some of them said: it refers to travel, concerning the prayer which had been obligatory to complete when resident, four rak'ahs, and He permitted its shortening during travel to two.

Mention of those who said that:

10310- Ubayd ibn Isma'il al-Haba'ari narrated to me, saying: Abd Allah ibn Idris narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Ibn Abi Ammar, from Abd Allah ibn Babayah, from Ya'la ibn Munyah, who said: I said to Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him: "There is no blame upon you in shortening the prayer if you fear..." and the people are now secure! He said: I wondered at what you wondered at, until I asked the Prophet ﷺ about that, and he said: "It is a charity which Allah has bestowed upon you, so accept His charity." [[The report: 10310 - "Ubayd ibn Isma'il al-Haba'ari," and it is "Ubayd Allah ibn Isma'il al-Haba'ari," which has passed under numbers: 2890, 3185, 3325, 4888.
And "Ibn Idris" is "Abd Allah ibn Idris al-Awdi," which has passed under numbers: 438, 2030, 2890, and others.
And "Ibn Abi Ammar" is Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Ammar al-Qurashi, the one known as "al-Qass," owner of "Salamah," which is called "Salamat al-Qass." He is trustworthy.
And "Abd Allah ibn Babayah" is trustworthy. (It is with a bi, followed by an alif, followed by an open ta', followed by a sukun ya'.) It is also said "Abd Allah ibn Babaah."
And "Ya'la ibn Munyah" is "Ya'la ibn Umayyah al-Makki," and "Munyah" was his grandmother, to whom he is attributed. He was a Companion who narrated from the Prophet ﷺ. In the printed edition, in this report and the one following it, both read "Ya'la ibn Umayyah," but in the manuscript, in this report alone, what I have recorded is what was there.
This report was narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad, numbers 174, 244, 245; Muslim narrated it in his Sahih 5: 195, 196 through two chains; al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 3: 134, 140, 141; Abu Dawud in his Sunan 2: 4, number 1199; Ibn Majah narrated it, number 1065; and Ibn Kathir cited it in his Tafsir 2: 557, 558.
Another two chains will come after this, and it is a sahih hadith. Ali ibn al-Madini said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith from the narration of Umar, and it is not known except through this route, and its narrators are well known."]]

10311- Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Idris narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, from Ibn Abi Ammar, from Abd Allah ibn Babayah, from Ya'la ibn Umayyah, from Umar, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it.

10312- Sa'id ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Adiyy narrated to us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: I heard Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Ammar narrating, from Abd Allah ibn Babayah narrating, from Ya'la ibn Umayyah, who said: I said to Umar ibn al-Khattab: I wonder at people shortening the prayer when they are secure, while Allah, blessed and exalted, has said: "that you shorten the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you"! Umar said: I wondered at what you wondered at, so I mentioned that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said: "It is a charity which Allah has bestowed upon you, so accept His charity." [[The two reports 10311 and 10312 have sound chains and are repetitions of the preceding one.]]

10313- Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Hisham ibn Abd al-Malik narrated to us, saying: Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-'Aliyah, who said: I travelled to Makkah, and I used to pray two rak'ahs. Some readers from the people of this region met me and said: How do you pray? I said: Two rak'ahs. They said: Is it a sunnah or a Qur'an? I said: Both, a sunnah and a Qur'an. [[In the printed edition: "All of that is a sunnah and a Qur'an," and I have recorded what is in the manuscript and in al-Durr al-Manthur, which is correct. The addition is from the copyist or the editor.]] [Thus] the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed two rak'ahs. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "I said: The Messenger of Allah prayed..." and the word "I said" is not in al-Durr al-Manthur, so I have taken its reading as I recorded it between the brackets.]] They said: He was in a state of war! I said: Allah says: (Allah has certainly fulfilled for His Messenger the vision in truth: you will surely enter al-Masjid al-Haram, if Allah wills, in security, with your heads shaved and your hair shortened, not fearing) [Surah al-Fath: 27], and He said: "And when you travel through the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer," and he recited until he reached: "But when you are secure" [[The report: 10313 - Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 209, and attributed it only to Ibn Jarir.]]

10314- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Hashim narrated to us, saying: Sayf informed us, from Abu Rawq, from Abu Ayyub, from Ali, who said: A group of merchants asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: O Messenger of Allah, we travel through the land, so how should we pray? Then Allah revealed: "And when you travel through the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer," and then the revelation ceased. When a year had passed, the Prophet ﷺ went out to battle and prayed the Dhuhr, and the polytheists said: Muhammad and his Companions had an opportunity against them from their rear; why did you not press upon them? One of them said: Indeed, they have another prayer like it after it! So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed between the two prayers: "If you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you, indeed the disbelievers have ever been to you a clear enemy. And when you are among them and establish prayer for them, let a group of them stand with you" up to His saying: "Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment," and so the prayer of fear was revealed. [[The report: 10314 - This report was cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 209, and Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir 2: 565, and they did not attribute it to anyone other than Ibn Jarir.
In Ibn Kathir: "Ibn Jarir said: Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, Ishaq narrated to us..." differing from what is in the printed edition and the manuscript, making it "Ibn al-Muthanna," meaning "Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna," while al-Tabari narrates from both of them, from "al-Muthanna ibn Ibrahim," and from "Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna." But I incline to think the correct reading is what is in the printed edition, due to the frequency with which al-Muthanna narrates from Ishaq ibn al-Hajjaj al-Tahuni, as has passed hundreds of times.
In the manuscript and the printed edition it read: "Yusuf, from Abu Rawq," and the correct reading is "Sayf," as in the Tafsir of Ibn Kathir, and as will come in the words of Abu Ja'far. He is Sayf ibn Umar al-Tamimi, who is abandoned in hadith.
As for "Abd Allah ibn Hashim," I have not found a biography or mention of him.
Ibn Kathir said after citing this report: "This context is very strange, but some of it has a witness from the narration of Abu Ayyash al-Zuraqi, whose name is Zayd ibn al-Samit," then he cited the following report, number 10323, from the narration of Ahmad and Abu Dawud, as will come.
The rejection by Abu Ja'far that follows indicates his weakening of this hadith.]] Abu Ja'far said: This is a good interpretation of the verse, were it not for the word "idha" in the speech, and "idha" indicates the severance of what follows from the meaning of what precedes. [[He means by that the "idha" in His saying: "And when you are among them..."]] And had there not been "idha" in the speech, the meaning of the speech, according to this interpretation narrated by Sayf from Abu Rawq, would be: If you fear, O believers, that those who disbelieve may tempt you in your prayer, and you were among them, O Muhammad, and you established prayer for them, "then let a group of them stand with you," the verse.

* *

Furthermore, what has been mentioned concerning the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b is: [[In the manuscript: "wa-bi-add fa-inna," which is a rare slip of the copyist in his writing.]] ﴿And when you travel through the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, that those who disbelieve may tempt you﴾.

10315- Al-Harith narrated to me this, saying: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, saying: al-Thawri narrated to us, from Wasil ibn Hayyan, from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abza, from his father, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that he used to read: ﴿that you shorten the prayer, that those who disbelieve may tempt you﴾, and he did not read: "if you fear." [[The report: 10315 - "al-Harith" is "al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah," who is "al-Harith ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Usamah," mentioned shortly before under number 10295.
And "Abd al-Aziz" is "Abd al-Aziz ibn Aban al-Umawi," mentioned under number 10295.
And "Wasil ibn Hayyan al-Ahdab" has passed under number 10.]]

10316- Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Bakr ibn Sharud narrated to us, from al-Thawri, from Wasil al-Ahdab, from Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, that he read: ﴿that you shorten the prayer, that those who disbelieve may tempt you﴾. Bakr said: and in the "Imam," the codex of Uthman, may Allah have mercy on him: "If you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you." [[The report: 10316 - "Bakr ibn Sharud" has passed under number 8562.]]

This reading indicates that His saying: "If you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you" is connected to His saying: "there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer" [[In the manuscript: "and in the Imam, the codex of Uthman, may Allah have mercy on him: 'If you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you' from the origin of His saying: 'there is no blame upon you' ... and that the meaning of the speech...," which is a corrupt and disordered phrase, as if a copyist other than ours, or as if the editor, added one of them "and this reading..." etc., until the speech connected and became sound, so I left what is in the printed edition as it stands, except that it was written "indicates that His saying," so I made it "indicates that His saying ..." Its correction "from the origin" so that it reads "connected" is the correct reading, God willing.]] =, and that the meaning of the speech is: And when you travel through the land, then if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer= and that His saying: "And when you are among them" is a separate story, distinct from the story of this verse.

For the interpretation of Ubayy's reading that we have mentioned from him is: "And when you travel through the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, lest those who disbelieve tempt you," so "not" was omitted because the speech indicates it, as He, may His praise be exalted, said: ﴿Allah makes clear to you, lest you go astray﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 176], meaning: lest you go astray.

In what we have described there is clear evidence of the corruption of the interpretation narrated by Sayf from Abu Rawq.

* *

Others said: rather, it is the shortening during travel, except that He, may His praise be exalted, only permitted it for the traveller in a state of fear of an enemy whom he fears may tempt him in his prayer.

Mention of those who said that:

10317- Abu Asim Imran ibn Muhammad al-Ansari narrated to me, saying: Abd al-Kabir ibn Abd al-Majid narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq narrated to me, saying: I heard my father say: I heard Aisha say concerning travel: "Complete your prayer." They said: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed two rak'ahs during travel? She said: Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was in a state of war, and he used to fear; do you fear as well? [[The report: 10317 - "Abu Asim Imran ibn Muhammad al-Ansari," the teacher of al-Tabari, I have not found a biography for him. "Abd al-Kabir ibn Abd al-Majid, Abu Bakr al-Hanafi" has passed under number 6822.
As for "Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq," he is trustworthy, and is biographed in al-Tahdhib. In the printed edition, the manuscript, and al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 210, "Umar" stands in place of "Muhammad," which is an error, and the copyist often writes "Muhammad" as "Umar," as has passed in many places.
And his father is "Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq," known as Ibn Abi Atiq. He narrated from his paternal aunt Aisha, and two of his sons narrated from him, Abd al-Rahman and Muhammad (mentioned above).
I have not found this report in any of the collections of Sunnah available to me, and al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur and did not attribute it to anyone other than Ibn Jarir.]]

10318- Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Dhi'b narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Umayyah ibn Abd Allah ibn Khalid ibn Usayd: that he said to Abd Allah ibn Umar: We find in the Book of Allah the shortening of the prayer of fear, [[In the printed edition: "the shortening of the prayer in fear," and in the manuscript: "the shortening of the prayer the fear," and its correct form is from the Tafsir of Ibn Kathir.]] but we do not find the shortening of the prayer of the traveller? Abd Allah said: Indeed we found our Prophet ﷺ acting in a manner, and we acted upon it. [[The report: 10318 - Ibn Kathir cited it in his Tafsir 2: 561, and al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 210, and they did not attribute it to anyone other than Ibn Jarir. Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in his Sunan 3: 136 through the route of Ibn Wahb, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab. Al-Bayhaqi said: "al-Layth narrated it from Ibn Shihab, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, and a group traced it to Ibn Shihab but did not establish its chain."]]

10319- Ali ibn Sahl al-Ramli narrated to us, saying: Mu'ammal narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father: that Aisha used to pray two rak'ahs during travel.

10320- Sa'id ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Ibn Juraij narrated to us, saying: I said to Ata: Which of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to complete the prayer during travel? He said: Aisha and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas.

* *

Others said: rather, by this verse is meant the shortening of the prayer of fear, outside the state of close fighting. They said: and it was revealed concerning it.

Mention of those who said that:

10321- Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His saying: "There is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer," he said: On the day when the Prophet ﷺ and his Companions were at Usfan, and the polytheists at Dajnan, and they faced one another, [[To "face one another in combat" means to hold off from fighting for a time. In the printed edition: "tawafaqu," with the fa before the qaf, which is an error.]] the Prophet ﷺ prayed the Dhuhr with his Companions two rak'ahs — or four, Abu Asim was in doubt — their bowing, prostrating and standing together, all at once. The polytheists resolved to raid their goods and baggage, so Allah revealed to him: "Let a group of them stand with you," and he prayed the 'Asr. His Companions lined up in two rows, then he pronounced the takbir with them all together. Then the first row prostrated one prostration while the others stood, then the others prostrated when the Prophet ﷺ rose, then he pronounced the takbir with them, and they all bowed together; the rear row advanced and the front row withdrew, and they alternated the prostration as they had done the first time, and he shortened the 'Asr to two rak'ahs.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 101 (part 2 of 3):**

10322. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿there is no blame on you if you shorten the prayer﴾: He said: The Prophet ﷺ and his Companions were at ʿUsfan, and the polytheists were at Dajnan. They faced each other [[“tawaqafa al-fariqan fi al-qital” (the two parties confronted each other in battle), meaning they paused from fighting for an hour. In the printed edition it reads “tawafaqu,” with the fa placed before the qaf, and this is an error.]] and the Prophet ﷺ led his Companions in the midday prayer (ẓuhr) as two units (rakʿatayn), with their bowing, prostration and standing all together. The polytheists resolved to attack their goods and baggage. So Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿Let a party of them stand with you﴾. He then led them in the afternoon prayer (ʿaṣr). His Companions formed two rows, and he pronounced the takbir with them all. The first row then prostrated with his prostration, while the second row stood and did not prostrate, until the Prophet ﷺ stood up. He then pronounced the takbir with them, and they all bowed together. The rear row then advanced and the front row withdrew, and they took turns in prostration as they had entered the first time. The afternoon prayer was thus shortened to two units. [[In the printed edition it reads “bi-sujudihi” with a bāʾ, while I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is sound.]]

10323. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Abu ʿAyyash al-Zuraqi, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at ʿUsfan, and Khalid ibn al-Walid was in command of the polytheists. He said: We prayed the midday prayer, and the polytheists said: “They were in a state [in which] if we had wished we could have struck them unawares, [caught them] in heedlessness.” [[In the printed edition it reads “kanu ʿala hal” without “la-qad”; the copyist of the manuscript wrote “law kanu…”, and the correct reading is what I have kept.]] Then the verse of shortening (qasr) was revealed between the midday and afternoon prayers. The people took up their weapons and lined up behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, facing the qibla, while the polytheists faced them [[In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads “mustaqbalahum” (read with a damma on the mim, a sukun on the sin and a fatha on the ba), meaning: in front of them. The polytheists on that day were between them and the qibla.]]. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ pronounced the takbir and they all pronounced it. He then bowed and they all bowed; then he raised his head and they all raised theirs; then he prostrated and the row next to him prostrated, while the others stood guarding them. When these had finished their prostration, those prostrated. Then the row next to him drew back and the others advanced, taking their places. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ bowed and they all bowed; then he raised his head and they all raised theirs; then he prostrated and the row next to him prostrated, while the others stood guarding them. When these had finished their prostration, these others prostrated. Then they all rose together with him, sat down together, and he gave the salam to them all together. He prayed it at ʿUsfan, and he prayed it on the day of Banu Sulaym. [[Report 10323–10324: Abu Jaʿfar transmitted this report by three chains, and it will come with another chain, no. 10387, which is a sound hadith, narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad 4:59–60 by two routes: by way of ʿAbd al-Razzaq, from al-Thawri, from Mansur; and by way of Ghundar, from Shuʿba, from Mansur. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it in his Musnad 191–192 by way of Warqaʾ, from Mansur. al-Nasaʾi narrated it in his Sunan 3:176–177 by way of Shuʿba, from Mansur, and by way of ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn ʿAbd al-Samad, from Mansur. Abu Dawud narrated it in his Sunan 2:16, no. 1236, by way of Jarir ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid, from Mansur, with the same chain as Abu Jaʿfar’s first. al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 1:337 and said: “This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it.” al-Dhahabi said: “According to their conditions.” al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan in two places, 3:254 by way of Warqaʾ from Mansur, and then 3:256 by way of Jarir ibn ʿAbd al-Hamid from Mansur. al-Bayhaqi said: “This is a sound chain, and Qutaybah ibn Saʿid narrated it from Jarir, mentioning in it Mujahid’s hearing from Abu ʿAyyash Zayd ibn al-Samit al-Zuraqi.” Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir 2:566–567: “This is a sound chain and it has many corroborating reports.”]]

10324. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, from Shaybian al-Nahwi, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Abu ʿAyyash al-Zuraqi; and from Israʾil, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Abu ʿAyyash, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was at ʿUsfan, and then he mentioned something similar. [[Report 10323–10324: the same note as above, repeated in the printed text: Abu Jaʿfar transmitted this report by three chains, and it will come with another chain, no. 10387, a sound hadith narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad 4:59–60 by two routes… (the references of al-Nasaʾi, Abu Dawud, al-Hakim, al-Bayhaqi and Ibn Kathir are as given above).]]

10325. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muʿadh ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Sulayman al-Yashkuri: that he asked Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah about the shortening of the prayer: On which day was it revealed? Or: On which day was it? Jabir said: We set out to intercept a caravan of Quraysh coming from Syria, until when we were at Nakhl, a man from the people came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: “O Muhammad!” He said: “Yes.” He said: “Do you fear me?” He said: “No!” He said: “Then who will protect you from me?” He said: “Allah protects me from you!” He said: Then he drew the sword, and then he threatened and menaced him. Then he called for departure and taking up weapons. Then the prayer was called, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led a party of the people in prayer while another party guarded them. He prayed with those nearest to him two units, then those nearest to him withdrew backwards and stood in the ranks of their companions. Then the others came, and he prayed with them two units while the others guarded them, and then he gave the salam. So the Prophet ﷺ had four units, and the people had two units each. On that day Allah revealed the shortening of the prayer and commanded the believers to take up weapons. [[Report 10325: “Sulayman al-Yashkuri” is Sulayman ibn Qays al-Yashkuri. He narrated from Jabir and Abu Saʿid al-Khudri. Qatadah, ʿAmr ibn Dinar and Abu Bishr Jaʿfar ibn Abi Wahshiyyah narrated from him. al-Bukhari said: “It is said that he died in the lifetime of Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, and Qatadah did not hear from him, nor Abu Bishr, and we do not know of any hearing for any of them, except ʿAmr ibn Dinar, who heard from him in Jabir’s lifetime.” Abu Hatim said: “He sat with Jabir, heard from him and wrote a sheet from him; then he died and the sheet remained with his wife. Abu al-Zubayr, Abu Sufyan and al-Shaʿbi narrated from Jabir, and they had heard from Jabir, and most of it was from the sheet, and so was Qatadah.” He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/2/32, and Ibn Abi Hatim 2/1/136. This report was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad 3:364, 390, by way of Abu ʿAwanah from Abu Bishr, from Sulayman ibn Qays, with different wording but the same meaning. Abu Dawud in his Sunan 2:24, al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 3:259, and al-Tahawi in Maʿani al-Athar 1:187 also refer to the report of Sulayman ibn Qays. Ibn Kathir said in his Tafsir 2:568, after mentioning Ahmad’s report in the Musnad: “He is alone in narrating it by this route.”]]

* *

Others said: Rather, it refers to the shortening of the prayer of fear (ṣalat al-khawf) in circumstances other than severe danger, except that it refers to shortening in the journey prayer, not the prayer of residence. [[In the printed edition it reads “al-qasr fi salat al-safar, la fi salat al-iqamah”; I have kept what is in the manuscript.]] They said: The journey prayer in a state other than fear is two units, complete and not shortened, just as the prayer of residence is four units in a state of residence. They said: Thus it was shortened on a journey in a state of safety other than fear from the prayer of the resident, and it was made half, and it is complete on a journey. Then it was shortened on a journey in a state of fear from the prayer of safety on a journey, and it was made half, one unit.

Mention of those who said that:

10326. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And when you travel in the land, there is no blame on you if you shorten the prayer﴾, up to His words ﴿a manifest enemy﴾: The prayer, when it is prayed as two units on a journey, is complete. [[In the printed edition it reads “fa-hiya tamam” (and it is complete); I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is also correct.]] Shortening is not permissible except that you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you away from the prayer. The shortening is one unit: the imam stands and his troops stand in two groups, one party behind him and another party facing the enemy. He prays with those with him one unit, and they walk back on their heels until they stand in the position of their companions; that is the retreating walk. Then the other party comes and prays with the imam another unit, and then the imam sits and gives the salam. They then stand and pray for themselves one unit, and return to their row, and the others stand and add to their unit one unit. People say: No, rather it is one unit only; none of them prays anything beyond his unit, and the imam’s unit suffices for them. So the imam has two units and they have one. That is the statement of Allah: ﴿And when you are among them and establish the prayer for them﴾ up to His words ﴿and take your precaution﴾.

10327. Ahmad ibn al-Walid al-Qurashi narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Simak al-Hanafi, who said: I asked Ibn ʿUmar about the prayer on a journey, and he said: Two units, complete, not shortened; the shortening is only the prayer of fear. I said: And what is the prayer of fear? He said: The imam prays with one party one unit, then these come in place of those, and those come in place of these, and he prays with them one unit. So the imam has two units, and each party has one unit. [[Report 10327: al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan 3:263; al-Suyuti took it out in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:210 and added its attribution to ʿAbd ibn Humayd. Abu Dawud referred to it in al-Sunan 2:23.]]

10328. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said: How can it be a shortening when they pray two units? It is only one unit.

10329. Saʿid ibn ʿAmr al-Sakuni narrated to me, saying: Baqiyyah narrated to us, saying: al-Masʿudi narrated to us, saying: Yazid al-Faqir narrated to me, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah, who said: The prayer of fear is one unit. [[Report 10329: “Yazid al-Faqir” is Yazid ibn Suhayb. This report with this chain has already passed under no. 5563.]]

10330. Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to me, saying: ʿAmr ibn al-Harith informed me, saying: Bakr ibn Sawadah narrated to me: that Ziyad ibn Nafiʿ narrated to him from Kaʿb, and he was one of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, whose hand was cut off on the day of al-Yamamah, that the prayer of fear for each party is one unit and two prostrations. [[Report 10330: “Ahmad ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Wahb al-Misri” and “ʿAbd Allah ibn Wahb” have passed, under no. 2747. “ʿAmr ibn al-Harith ibn Yaʿqub al-Ansari” has passed, under nos. 1387 and 6889. “Bakr ibn Sawadah ibn Thumamah al-Judhami al-Misri,” a trustworthy Successor, biographed in al-Tahdhib. “Ziyad ibn Nafiʿ al-Tujibi al-Misri,” mentioned by Ibn Hibban in al-Thiqat, biographed in al-Tahdhib. “Kaʿb,” al-Aqtaʿ, biographed in al-Isabah and al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 4/1/222. Ibn Hajar, in his biography of “Kaʿb al-Aqtaʿ,” cited this report and said: “I think there is a break (inqitaʿ) in its chain, for al-Bukhari suspended it by way of Ziyad ibn Nafiʿ, from Abu Musa al-Ghafiqi, from Jabir ibn ʿAbd Allah. al-Bukhari said in al-Tarikh: Kaʿb, whose hand was cut off on the day of al-Yamamah, had companionship (ṣuhbah). Ziyad ibn Nafiʿ narrated from him.”]] Those who held this view argued from reports including:

10331. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Saʿid narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Ashʿath ibn Abi al-Shaʿthaʾ narrated to me, from al-Aswad ibn Hilal, from Thaʿlabah ibn Zahdam al-Yarbuʿi, who said: We were with Saʿid ibn al-ʿAs at Tabaristan, and he said: Which of you remembers the prayer of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the time of fear? Hudhayfah said: I do. So he had us stand behind him in one row, and another row facing the enemy. He prayed with those nearest him one unit; then these went to the position of those, and those came, and he prayed with them one unit. [[In the printed edition it reads “wa-saff muwazi al-ʿaduww” (in the singular); I have kept what is in the manuscript, which agrees with the wording of the hadith in its other transmissions.]] [[Report 10331: it will come with another chain, no. 10333. “Ashʿath ibn Abi al-Shaʿthaʾ” is Ashʿath ibn Sulaym ibn Aswad al-Muharibi, one of the trustworthy shaykhs of the Kufans, biographed in al-Tahdhib. “al-Aswad ibn Hilal al-Muharibi” was a pre-Islamic man who reached Islam; he narrated from Muʿadh ibn Jabal, ʿUmar and Ibn Masʿud, biographed in al-Tahdhib. “Thaʿlabah ibn Zahdam al-Hanzali,” whose companionship is disputed; he narrated from Hudhayfah and Abu Masʿud, and most of his reports are from the Companions, biographed in al-Tahdhib. This report was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad 5:385, 399, 404; Abu Dawud in his Sunan 2:23, no. 1246; al-Nasaʾi in his Sunan 3:167–168; al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan 3:261; al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 1:335, who said: “This is a hadith sound in its chain, though they did not record it,” and al-Dhahabi agreed; and al-Tahawi in Maʿani al-Athar 1:183. al-Suyuti took it out in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:212 and added its attribution to Ibn Abi Shaybah, ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Hibban.]]

10332. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya and ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, both saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Rukayn ibn al-Rabiʿ, from al-Qasim ibn Hassan, who said: I asked Zayd ibn Thabit about it, and he related to me something similar. [[Report 10332: “Rukayn ibn al-Rabiʿ ibn ʿUmaylah al-Fazari,” a trustworthy Kufan. “al-Qasim ibn Hassan al-ʿAmiri,” mentioned by Ibn Hibban in al-Thiqat. Ibn Hajar said: “He is among the followers of the Successors, which implies that he did not hear from Zayd ibn Thabit; but then I found that he (meaning Ibn Hibban) also mentioned him among the Successors.” al-Bayhaqi narrated the report in his Sunan 3:262, where there is an explicit statement of his hearing from Zayd ibn Thabit. He said: “From al-Qasim ibn Hassan who said: I came to so-and-so ibn Wadiʿah and asked him about the prayer of fear, and he said: Go to Zayd ibn Thabit and ask him. So I came to Zayd and asked him…” and he related the report. See also al-Tahawi’s Maʿani al-Athar 1:183.]]

10333. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-Ashʿath, from al-Aswad ibn Hilal, from Thaʿlabah ibn Zahdam al-Yarbuʿi, from Hudhayfah, similar. [[Report 10333: see the note on report 10331.]]

10334. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya narrated to me, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Jahm narrated to me, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Ibn ʿAbbas: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed at Dhu Qarad, and the people lined up behind him in two rows: one row behind him, and one row facing the enemy. He prayed with those behind him one unit; then those went to the position of these, and those came, and he prayed with them one unit. And they did not make up the missed unit. [[Report 10334: “Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Jahm” is Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi al-Jahm al-ʿAdawi, named after his grandfather, as in al-Tahdhib. In al-Kuna of al-Bukhari (p. 13) he is “Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Jahm ibn Sukhayr,” and in Ibn Abi Hatim 4/2/338 he is “Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi al-Jahm ibn Sukhayr.” Ibn Hajar said in al-Tahdhib: “The name of Abu al-Jahm is Sukhayr.” He was a jurist and trustworthy; Ibn Saʿd said: “He narrated little hadith.” He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. See what my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad wrote in his commentary on the Musnad of Ahmad. “ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah” is Ibn ʿUtbah ibn Masʿud al-Hudhali, a Successor, a scholar, trustworthy, abundant in hadith and knowledge, pious, a poet of good quality, one of the jurists of Medina, and the teacher of ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz. This report was narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad, nos. 2063 and 3364, with a sound chain. See my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad’s commentary there, and see al-Tahawi’s Maʿani al-Athar 1:182.]]

10335. Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Israʾil al-Azraq informed us, from Shurayk, from Abu Bakr ibn Sukhayr, from ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, similar. [[Report 10335: “Abu Bakr ibn Sukhayr” is “Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Jahm” in the preceding chain. In the printed edition and the manuscript it reads “Ibn Suhayr” with an unpointed ḥāʾ, which is an error.]]

10336 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Allah prescribed the prayer through the tongue of your Prophet ﷺ: four units in residence, two units while travelling, and one unit in fear."

10337 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Awanah narrated to us, from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it. [[The two reports 10336 and 10337. "Abu 'Awanah" is al-Wadah ibn 'Abd Allah al-Yashkuri, who was mentioned under number 4498. "Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas" is a Kufan and trustworthy (thiqah). This report is related by Ahmad in al-Musnad, numbers 2124 and 2293, and see the explanation of my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad there. Muslim also related it, 5:196.]]

10338 - Nasr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Azdi narrated to us, saying: al-Mihrabi narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn 'A'idh al-Ta'i, from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it. [[The two reports 10338 and 10339. "Nasr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Azdi" was mentioned under numbers 423, 875 and 2859. My brother al-Sayyid Ahmad has shown that the correct nisbah is "al-Azdi," not "al-Awdi" with a waw, and it was also "al-Awdi" in the printed edition here. This repetition makes me doubt this nisbah, and I fear that some confusion may have entered my brother's work on it, but I have not been able to verify this point from the sources available to me now. Nevertheless, I have followed him in correcting "al-Awdi" to "al-Azdi." "Al-Mihrabi" is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Mihrabi, mentioned under numbers 221 and 875. "Ayyub ibn 'A'idh ibn Mudlij al-Ta'i" is trustworthy, and is biographed in al-Kabir 1/1/420. This report with this isnad is related by Ahmad in al-Musnad, number 2177, through the route of al-Qasim ibn Malik mentioned below, and it is a sound isnad; see the explanation of my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad there. Muslim related it, 5:197. As for report 10339, it contains "Ya'qub ibn Mahan," who was mentioned under number 4901. As for "al-Qasim ibn Malik al-Muzani," he is one of Ahmad's teachers and is trustworthy, and is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

10339 - Ya'qub ibn Mahan narrated to us, saying: al-Qasim ibn Malik narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn 'A'idh al-Ta'i, from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas, the like of it. [[The footnote is the same as that of 10338 and 10339 above.]]

10340 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-Hakam, from Yazid al-Faqir, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led them in the prayer of fear. A row stood before him and a row behind him. He prayed with those behind him one unit and two prostrations. Then those [first] moved forward until they stood in the place of their companions, and those [others] came until they stood in the place of these. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then prayed with them one unit and two prostrations, then he gave the salam. So the Prophet ﷺ had two units, and they had one unit. [[The report 10340. "Yazid al-Faqir" is Yazid ibn Suhayb, mentioned under number 10329. This report was related by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan 3:174, and al-Nasa'i also related it through the route of al-Mas'udi, from Yazid al-Faqir, 3:175; and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 3:263. See al-Bayhaqi's discussion of it, where he pointed to the route of al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah from Yazid al-Faqir. And see Tafsir Ibn Kathir 2:569.]]

10341 - Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: my paternal uncle 'Abd Allah ibn Wahb narrated to me, saying: 'Amr ibn al-Harith informed me: that Bakr ibn Sawadah narrated to him, from Ziyad ibn Nafi' narrated to him, from Abu Musa: that Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to them: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led them in the prayer of fear on the day of Muharib and Tha'labah, one unit and two prostrations for each group. [[The report 10341. "Abu Musa" is 'Ali ibn Rabah. The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari 7:324 that he is "a well-known Successor (tabi'i) from whom Muslim related," and he also said that Abu Musa in this report: "it is said he is al-Ghafiqi: Malik ibn 'Ubadah, and he is also a well-known Companion." The mention of "'Ali ibn Rabah" has already passed under number 4747. This report was related by al-Bukhari (Fath al-Bari 7:324).]]

10342 - Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Tusi narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, saying: Sa'id ibn 'Ubayd al-Hunna'i narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, saying: Abu Hurayrah narrated to us: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ halted between Dajnan and 'Usfan. The polytheists said: "Indeed these people have a prayer that is dearer to them than their sons and their virgins, and it is the 'Asr. So gather your resolve and attack them in one charge." Then Jibril came to the Prophet ﷺ and ordered him to divide his companions into two halves: he would pray with one group while another group stood behind them, and they would take their precautions and their weapons. Then he would command the other group, and they would pray with him, while those [first] would take their precautions and weapons. So each group would have one unit with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would have two units. [[The report 10342. "Sa'id ibn 'Ubayd al-Hunna'i": Abu Hatim said, "a shaykh," and Ibn Hibban mentioned him among the trustworthy (al-Thiqat). He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. "'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq al-'Uqayli" has been mentioned under numbers 196 to 199. This report was related by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan 3:174, and al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, in the Book of Tafsir. Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:211, and limited its attribution to Ibn Jarir and al-Tirmidhi. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a sound, strange hadith from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Shaqiq, from Abu Hurayrah."]]

* *

Others said: it refers to shortening (qasr) while travelling, but it refers to shortening in the intensity of battle and at close combat (al-musayafah). So it is permitted, when the battle is joined, for the one praying to perform one unit by gesturing with his head, wherever he turns his face. They said: that is the meaning of His saying: "There is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve will harm you."

Mention of those who said that:

10343 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding "And when you travel in the land," the verse: the shortening of the prayer, if you meet the enemy and the prayer time has come: that you say "Allahu akbar" and lower your head by gesture, whether you are riding or walking.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these sayings that we have mentioned regarding the interpretation of the verse is the saying of the one who said: "What is meant by shortening in it is shortening of its limits (hudud). That means leaving off completing its bowing and prostrating, and permitting its performance however it is possible to perform it, facing the qiblah or turning away from it, and riding or walking. This is in the state of intense fighting (al-sallah), close combat, the clash of battle and the advancing of the ranks." [[In the printed edition: "in the state of the interlacing (al-shabakah) and close combat," which is an empty error; the correct reading is from the manuscript, and he did not read it well. "Al-sallah" is the drawing of swords; one says "we came upon them at the sallah," meaning at the drawing of swords in the battle, when the combatants come close.]] It is the state that Allah, blessed and exalted, mentioned when He said: ﴿So if you fear, then [pray] on foot or riding﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 239], and He permitted the obligatory prayer in it while riding, by gesture for the bowing and prostration, in the manner reported from Ibn 'Abbas in his interpretation of it.

We said this is the most correct interpretation of His saying: "And when you travel in the land, there is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer, if you fear that those who disbelieve will harm you," because of the evidence in the saying of Allah, exalted: ﴿And when you are secure, then establish the prayer﴾, that this is so. For establishing it is completing its limits of bowing, prostration and its other obligations, without increasing its number, which was not obligatory in the state of fear. If someone supposes that this is a command from Allah to complete its obligatory number in the state of safety after the fear has passed, then it would have to be that the traveller, in his shortened prayer, is not establishing his prayer the way the resident does, because the number of his prayer is reduced from the four that were obligatory on him in his state of residence to two. That is a saying which, if someone says it, contradicts what the community (ummah) unanimously agrees upon: that the traveller does not deserve to be told, when he performs his prayer with the complete limits obligatory on him and shortens its number from four to two, "he is not establishing his prayer." Since this is so, and since Allah, exalted, had commanded the one whom He permitted to shorten his prayer out of fear of his enemy harming him, to establish his prayer when he is secure and the fear has passed, it is clear that what was obligatory on him, establishing it in the state of security, is the very thing that was waived for him in the state of fear. And since what was obligatory on him in the state of security is establishing his prayer, then what was waived for him in other than the state of security is leaving off establishing it. We have shown that leaving off its establishment is only leaving off its limits, as we have explained.

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari), *Jami' al-Bayan*, on surah 4, verse 102 (part 1 of 4):

The exposition of His saying, may His majesty be exalted: ﴿And when you are among them and establish the prayer for them, let a group of them stand with you and let them take their arms. Then when they have prostrated, let them be behind you, and let another group who have not prayed come and pray with you, taking their precaution and their arms. Those who disbelieve wish that you would neglect your arms and your goods so they could attack you in one charge.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, He, may His majesty be exalted, means: And when you are, O Muhammad, among your companions who travel through the land, fearing their enemy that it may afflict them, ﴿and you establish the prayer for them﴾, meaning: and you establish the prayer for them with its limits, its bowing and its prostrations, and you do not shorten it with the shortening that I permitted them to shorten during their encounter with the enemy and the pressing of some of them upon others, by abandoning the establishing of its limits, its bowing, its prostrations, and its other obligations. ﴿Then let a group of them stand with you﴾, meaning: then let a company of your companions, among whom you are, stand with you in your prayer, ﴿and let the rest be in the face of the enemy﴾.

And the omission of mention of what the other groups, which did not pray with the Prophet ﷺ, should do is because the mentioned speech indicates its meaning, and because what is mentioned suffices for what its mention has been left out. ﴿And let them take their arms.﴾

The interpreters have differed concerning the group commanded to take up arms.

Some of them said: It is the group that was praying with the Prophet ﷺ. He said: The meaning of the speech, "and let them take," is: let the group praying with you from among them take ﴿their arms﴾. The weapon they were commanded to take is with them during their prayer, such as the sword that one of them wears on his shoulder, the dagger, or the knife that he fastens to his armour and the garments he is wearing, and similar of his weapons.

* *

Others said: Rather, the group commanded to take up arms from among them is the group that was facing the enemy, not the group praying with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. This is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas.

10344. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Then when they have prostrated﴾, he said: when the group that stood with you in your prayer prostrates, praying with your prayer, and finishes its prostration, ﴿let them be behind you﴾, he said: let them, after finishing their prostration, be behind you, facing the enemy, in the place where the other groups are that did not pray with you and did not enter into your prayer.

* *

Then the interpreters differed concerning the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Then when they have prostrated, let them be behind you.﴾

Some of them said: Its interpretation is: when they have prayed and finished their prayer, let them be behind you.

* *

Then the people of this view differed.

Some of them said: When this group prays with the imam one rak'ah, it gives the salam and departs from its prayer, until it reaches the position of its companions in the face of the enemy, and there is no making up for it. They said: They are the ones whom Allah meant by His saying: ﴿There is no blame upon you to shorten the prayer﴾, that you make it, when you fear that those who disbelieve will afflict you, one rak'ah. And they narrated from the Prophet ﷺ that he prayed the prayer of fear with one group one rak'ah, and they did not make it up, and with another group one rak'ah, and they did not make it up.

We have mentioned some of this earlier, and what we have mentioned is sufficient rather than exhaustively mentioning all that is in it.

* *

Others among them said: Rather, the obligation upon this group, which Allah commanded to stand with its Prophet when he intended to establish the prayer with them in a time of fear of the enemy, and when it finishes its rak'ah which Allah commanded it to pray with the Prophet ﷺ as He commanded it in His Book, is to stand in its place where it prayed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and pray the remainder of its prayer for itself and give the salam, and come to the line of its companions. And the Prophet ﷺ had to remain standing in his place until the group that prayed with him the first rak'ah finishes the rest of its prayer, if its prayer that it prayed with him is of a kind whose number may be shortened below what is obligatory upon the residents in security; then it goes to the line of its companions, and the other group that was facing its enemy comes, and he prays another rak'ah of his prayer with them.

* *

Then they differ concerning the ruling for this second group.
