A faction among the people of this view said: When the Prophet ﷺ finished his two rak'ahs and raised his head from his prostration of the second rak'ah, he had to sit for the tashahhud, and the group that prayed with him the second rak'ah but did not catch the first rak'ah with him, because it was occupied with its enemy, had to stand and make up its missed rak'ah with the Prophet ﷺ. And the Prophet ﷺ had to wait for it, sitting in his tashahhud, until this group finishes its missed rak'ah and makes its tashahhud, then he gives the salam with them.

* *

Another faction among them said: Rather, the obligation upon the group that did not catch the first rak'ah with him, when the Prophet ﷺ sat for the tashahhud, was to sit with him for the tashahhud and make its tashahhud with his tashahhud. When the Prophet ﷺ finishes his tashahhud, he gives the salam. Then the group that prayed the second rak'ah with him then stands and makes up its missed rak'ah. [In the manuscript: "Rather, the obligation upon the group that did not catch the first rak'ah with him, when the Prophet ﷺ sat from his tashahhud, gave the salam, then the group that prayed the second rak'ah with him stood..." — a part that is established in the printed edition was dropped by the copyist, and that is the correct reading, God willing.] Each speaker of those whose sayings we have mentioned narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reports that he did what he said.

* *

Mention of the one who said: The Prophet ﷺ waited for both groups until each group [finished] its prayer, and he did not come out of his prayer except after the two groups finished their prayers. [In the manuscript: "until it finished its prayer"; in the printed edition: "until they both finished their prayer" in the dual, which tried to correct the manuscript's wording and erred; I have placed what is between the brackets by judgment so that the speech is sound.]

10345. Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Malik informed me, from Yazid ibn Ruman, from Salih ibn Khawwat, from one who prayed with the Prophet ﷺ the prayer of fear on the day of Dhat al-Riqa': that a group lined up with him, and a group was facing the enemy. [In the printed edition: "that a group lined up with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ", and I have kept what is in the manuscript.] So he prayed with those who were with him one rak'ah, then he remained standing and they completed for themselves. Then the other group came and he prayed with them, then he remained sitting and they completed for themselves, then he gave the salam with them. [Report 10345: Yazid ibn Ruman al-Asadi, Abu Ruh al-Madani, one of the shaykhs of Malik, was a learned man of much hadith, trustworthy. And Salih ibn Khawwat ibn Jubayr ibn al-Nu'man al-Ansari, narrated from his father and his maternal uncle Sahl ibn Abi Hathma; he was a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i) of little narration. The group narrated from him the hadith of the prayer of fear. He is biographed in al-Kabir 2/2/277. And Sahl ibn Abi Hathma al-Ansari, who had companionship, the Messenger of Allah died when he was eight years old, and he memorized from him. The Hafiz said in al-Tahdhib: "Ibn Abi Hatim said, from his father: he pledged under the tree and attended all the battles except Badr, and he was the guide of the Prophet ﷺ on the night of Uhud. Ibn Abi Hatim said: I heard a man from his descendants whom my father asked about that, and he informed him of it." I say: I did not find in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil a biography of "Sahl," nor the saying of Ibn Abi Hatim. Then the Hafiz said: "Ibn al-Qattan said: Abu Hatim's saying is not sound with them at all, and the error in it is from this man who is not known who he is. Rather the one whom the Prophet ﷺ sent as a estimator (kharis) was his father Abu Hathma, and he was the guide of the Prophet ﷺ to Uhud, as Ibn Jarir and others mentioned." And Sahl ibn Abi Hathma is biographed in al-Tahdhib and in al-Kabir 2/2/98, and his mention has passed under number 9179. This is a sound hadith, narrated by Malik in the Muwatta' 183, al-Shafi'i in al-Risala no. 509, 677, and in al-Umm 1:186, al-Bukhari (Fath 7:325), al-Bukhari in al-Tarikh al-Kabir 2/2/277, Muslim 6:128, Abu Dawud in his Sunan 2:18 no. 1238, al-Nasa'i 3:171, al-Tirmidhi 2:456 (with the commentary of my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad), al-Tahawi in Ma'ani al-Athar 1:184, al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan 3:252, and see what my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad wrote in the commentary on al-Tirmidhi and the commentary on al-Shafi'i's Risala. And al-Jassas in Ahkam al-Qur'an 2:259, 260. The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Fath 7:326: "His saying: 'from one who witnessed with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the prayer of fear on the day of Dhat al-Riqa'' — it is said: the name of this unnamed person is Sahl ibn Abi Hathma, because al-Qasim ibn Muhammad narrated the hadith of the prayer of fear from Salih ibn Khawwat, from Sahl ibn Abi Hathma. This is the apparent reading of al-Bukhari's narration, but the more probable is that it is his father Khawwat ibn Jubayr, because Abu Uwais narrated this hadith from Yazid ibn Ruman, the shaykh of Malik in it, and said: from Salih ibn Khawwat, from his father; Ibn Mandah cited it in Ma'rifat al-Sahaba by his route. Likewise al-Bayhaqi cited it (3:253) by the route of Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Khawwat, from his father. And al-Nawawi in his Tahdhib affirmed that it is Khawwat ibn Jubayr, and said: it is verified from the narration of Muslim and others." And the Hafiz excelled in clarifying this afterward in al-Fath (7:329), and indicated that Sahl ibn Abi Hathma was young in the time of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and that the Messenger of Allah died when he was eight years old, and so this confirms that the intended one in His saying "from one who prayed with the Prophet ﷺ" is Khawwat ibn Jubayr, not Sahl ibn Abi Hathma.]

10346. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Mu'adh narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from Salih ibn Khawwat, from Sahl ibn Abi Hathma, who said: The Prophet ﷺ prayed with his companions in fear, and he placed them behind him in two rows. He prayed with those who were adjacent to him one rak'ah, then he stood, and he did not cease standing until those behind him prayed one rak'ah. Then they advanced, and those who had been in front of them fell back, and he prayed with them one rak'ah, then he sat until those who had fallen back prayed one rak'ah, then he gave the salam. [Report 10346: the hadith of Sahl ibn Abi Hathma, through the route of Shu'ba from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim. This and the one following it were narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 4:448, al-Bukhari in al-Fath (7:329), Muslim 6:128, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 3:253, 254. See the comment on the preceding report, and the following report no. 10351.]

10347. Sufyan ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Rawh narrated to us, saying: Shu'ba narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from Salih ibn Khawwat, from Sahl ibn Abi Hathma, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said concerning the prayer of fear: A group stands before the imam and a group behind him, and he prays with those behind him one rak'ah and two prostrations, then he sits in his place until they make up one rak'ah and two prostrations, then they move to the place of their companions, then those move to the place of these, and he prays with them one rak'ah and two prostrations, then he sits in his place until they pray one rak'ah and two prostrations, then he gives the salam. [Report 10347: a repetition of the preceding one. Narrated by Ahmad in al-Musnad 4:448, and al-Bukhari in al-Tarikh al-Kabir 2/2/277. This is the marfu' hadith to which he will refer in no. 10351.]

* *

Mention of the one who said: "The second group would sit with the Prophet ﷺ until the Prophet ﷺ finished his prayer, then it would make up what remained for it, and he would give the salam over them afterwards."

10348. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: I heard Yahya ibn Sa'id say: I heard al-Qasim say: Salih ibn Khawwat ibn Jubayr narrated to me: that Sahl ibn Abi Hathma narrated to him: that the prayer of fear is: the imam stands facing the qiblah and prays, and with him is a group of his companions, and another group facing the enemy, and he prays. The imam bows with those with him and prostrates, then he stands; when he is standing upright, those behind him bow for themselves one rak'ah and two prostrations, then they give the salam and depart while the imam is standing, and they stand in the face of the enemy. The others come and say takbir behind the imam, and the imam bows with them and prostrates, then gives the salam; then they stand and bow for themselves one rak'ah and two prostrations, then they give the salam. [Reports 10348 and 10349: narrated by Malik in al-Muwatta' 183, al-Bukhari (al-Fath 7:328), and Abu Dawud in his Sunan 2:18 no. 1239.]

10349. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id informed us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad: that Salih ibn Khawwat informed him, from Sahl ibn Abi Hathma, concerning the prayer of fear, then he mentioned something similar. [Reports 10348 and 10349: narrated by Malik in al-Muwatta' 183, al-Bukhari (al-Fath 7:328), and Abu Dawud in his Sunan 2:18 no. 1239.]

10350. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, and he asked, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Salih, from Sahl ibn Abi Hathma, concerning the prayer of fear, he said: The imam stands facing the qiblah, and a group stands with him, and a group from the direction of the enemy with their faces toward the enemy. He prays with them one rak'ah, then they bow for themselves and prostrate twice in their place, and they go to the place of those, and those come, and he prays with them one rak'ah and prostrates twice. So he has two rak'ahs and they have one. Then they bow one rak'ah and prostrate twice. [Report 10350: "Yahya ibn Sa'id" is al-Qattan. This report was narrated by al-Bukhari (al-Fath 7:328), al-Tirmidhi 2:455 (with the commentary of my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad), al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan 3:253, and al-Nasa'i in his Sunan 3:178.]

10351. Bundar said: I asked Yahya ibn Sa'id about this hadith, and he narrated to me from Shu'ba, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, from his father, from Salih ibn Khawwat, from Sahl ibn Abi Hathma, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of the hadith of Yahya ibn Sa'id, and he said to me: Write it beside it, for I do not memorize it, but it is like the hadith of Yahya ibn Sa'id. [Report 10351: this report is a reference to the preceding report no. 10347, as a marfu'. It was narrated by al-Tirmidhi 2:456 and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 3:253. al-Tirmidhi said: "Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari did not raise it from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, and thus the companions of Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Ansari narrated it as mawquf. And Shu'ba raised it from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim ibn Muhammad."]

10352. Nasr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, from Salih ibn Khawwat: that the imam stands and forms two rows, a group facing the enemy and a group behind the imam. The imam prays with those behind him one rak'ah, then they stand and pray one rak'ah for themselves, then they give the salam, then they depart and form rows. The others come and he prays with them one rak'ah and gives the salam, then they stand and pray one rak'ah for themselves. [Reports 10352 and 10353: I did not find a source for these two reports. As for the hadith of Ubayd Allah (that is Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar) from al-Qasim, al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan 3:253 from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, from his brother Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Khawwat, from his father, who said: "The Prophet ﷺ prayed the prayer of fear..." In it he explicitly stated that he narrated it from his father, and did not say "from a man of the companions of the Prophet," and it differs from it entirely in its wording. See the comment on report no. 10346. In the printed edition here it read: "Of what we mention concerning the prayer of fear, I have heard nothing that is better in my view than this," with "shay'an" in the accusative, but in the manuscript it reads "shay'," and I considered reading it as "bi-shay'."]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 4, Verse 102 (Part 2 of 4):**

10353. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard ʿUbayd Allah, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Khawwat, from a man among the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "The prayer of fear (ṣalat al-khawf): a group stands behind the imam (imam, the leader of prayer) and another group faces the enemy. The imam prays with those behind him one rak'ah (rak'ah, a unit of prayer), and he remains standing, and the people pray the second rak'ah by themselves. Then they give the salam (salam, the closing greeting) and go off to their companions. Their companions come while the imam is still standing, and he prays with them one rak'ah and gives the salam. Then they stand and pray one more rak'ah by themselves, and then they depart." ʿUbayd Allah said: "Of what we mention regarding the prayer of fear, I have heard nothing that I find better than this."

[[The report: 10352, 10353 – I have not found a source for these two reports. The narration of ʿUbayd Allah (namely ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿUmar) from al-Qasim was transmitted by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 3: 253, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar, from his brother ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿUmar, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Salih ibn Khawwat, from his father, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) prayed the prayer of fear…" In that version he explicitly states that he narrated it from his father, and he does not say "from a man among the Companions of the Prophet," and it differs from this wording entirely. See the note on report no. 10346.
In the printed edition here it reads: "Of what we mention regarding the prayer of fear, I have heard nothing (shay'an) that I find better than this," with "shay'an" in the accusative, whereas in the manuscript it reads "shay'" (nominative). I preferred to read it as "bi-shay'" (with a thing).]]

10354. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding his saying: ﴿And when you are among them and establish the prayer for them, let a group of them stand with you﴾. This refers to the prayer during fear: the imam stands, and a group stands with him, and another group takes their weapons and stands facing the enemy. The imam prays with those who are with him one rak'ah, then he remains seated in his position, and the people stand and pray the second rak'ah for themselves while the imam is seated. Then they depart until they reach their companions and take up their positions. Then the others come, and the imam prays the second rak'ah with them, then gives the salam, and the people stand and pray the second rak'ah for themselves. Thus the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed on the day of Batn Nakhlah.

* * *

Others said: Rather, the interpretation of His saying: ﴿So when they have prostrated, let them be behind you﴾ is this: when the group that stood with the Prophet (ﷺ), upon his entering into his prayer, prostrates the second prostration of its first rak'ah, joining him in his prayer, [[Context: "When the group prostrates… the second prostration."]] "let them be behind you," meaning: behind you, O Muhammad, and behind your companions who did not pray, facing the enemy. They said: This group would not give the salam at the end of its rak'ah when it had finished the two prostrations of the rak'ah it prayed with the Prophet (ﷺ); rather, it would proceed to the position of its companions facing the enemy, while the remainder of its prayer was still upon it. They said: The other group, which had been facing the enemy, would come to join the Prophet (ﷺ) in the remainder of his prayer, and the Prophet (ﷺ) would pray with them the rak'ah that remained for him. They said: This is the meaning of the saying of Allah, mighty is His mention: ﴿And let another group that has not prayed come and pray with you, and let them take their precaution and their weapons﴾.

* * *

Then the proponents of this view differed regarding the manner of making up what remained for each of these two groups of their prayer, after the Prophet (ﷺ) finished his prayer and gave his salam, according to the statement of the adherents of this view and the interpreters of this interpretation.

Some of them said: The second group, which had prayed the second rak'ah with the Prophet (ﷺ), when the Prophet (ﷺ) gave the salam from his prayer, would stand and make up what had been missed of its prayer with the Prophet (ﷺ) in its place, after the Prophet (ﷺ) had finished his prayer. As for the group that prayed the first rak'ah with the Prophet (ﷺ) while facing the enemy, it had not yet completed. [[In the printed edition: "lam tatimm ṣalatuhā" (added "ṣalatuhā"); I have kept the manuscript reading, which is a sound one.]] When it had finished the remainder of its prayer that it had missed with the Prophet (ﷺ), it went to the line of its companions facing the enemy, and the first group, which had prayed the first rak'ah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), came to its place where it had prayed behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and made up the rest of its prayer.

Mention of the narration to that effect:

1035 5. Muhammad ibn ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Abi al-Shawarib narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad narrated to us, saying: Khusayf narrated to us, saying: Abu ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd Allah narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd Allah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed with us the prayer of fear. A group of us stood behind him, and a group stood facing the enemy [[or: "facing"]]. The Prophet (ﷺ) prayed with those behind him one rak'ah, then they withdrew and went to the position of their companions. The others came and stood behind the Prophet (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed with them one rak'ah. Then the Messenger of Allah gave the salam. Then these stood and prayed one rak'ah for themselves, then they went and took the position of their companions facing the enemy, and the others returned to their position and prayed one rak'ah for themselves.

[[The report: 10355. ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad al-ʿAbdi is one of the reliable leading scholars; he was mentioned under no. 2616.
Khusayf is Khusayf ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Jazari, mentioned under no. 8136. Scholars have spoken about him. Ibn Hibban said: "Some of our imams abandoned him, and others relied on him. He was a righteous, learned, and devout shaykh, except that he would often err in what he narrated, and would report alone from well-known transmitters what was not corroborated. He is truthful in his narration, but justice regarding him is to accept what agrees with the reliable transmitters in narrations and to leave what is not corroborated. As for him, I seek Allah's guidance concerning him."
Abu ʿUbaydah is Abu ʿUbaydah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud, mentioned under nos. 4570 and 4694. ʿAbd Allah is ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud.
This report was transmitted by Abu Dawud 2: 22, no. 1224, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan 3: 261, via ʿAbd al-Salam ibn Harb from Khusayf, and via al-Thawri from Khusayf, and via Sharik from Khusayf. This last is no. 10357. Its wording differs from the wording of the narration of ʿAbd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad from Khusayf. Al-Bayhaqi said: "This hadith is mursal (mursal, a report with a missing link); Abu ʿUbaydah did not meet his father, and Khusayf al-Jazari is not strong."]]

1035 6. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, saying: Khusayf narrated to us, from Abu ʿUbaydah, from ʿAbd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) prayed with us the prayer of fear, and he mentioned something similar.

[[The two reports 10356 and 10357 are repetitions of the preceding one. See Abu Dawud's narration in al-Sunan 2: 22, no. 1224.]]

1035 7. Tamim ibn al-Muntasir narrated to us, saying: Ishaq informed us, saying: Sharik informed us, from Khusayf, from Abu ʿUbaydah, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar.

[[The two reports 10356 and 10357 are repetitions of the preceding one. See Abu Dawud's narration in al-Sunan 2: 22, no. 1224.]]

Others said: Rather, the second group, which had prayed the second rak'ah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), would not make up the remainder of its prayer after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave the salam from his prayer; rather, it would depart before making up the rest of its prayer, and would stand in the position of its companions who had prayed the first rak'ah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The first group would come to its position where it had prayed its first rak'ah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and would make up its remaining rak'ah. Some of them said: It would make up that rak'ah without recitation. Others said: Rather, it would make it up with recitation. When it had made up its remaining rak'ah there and given the salam, it would proceed to the line of its companions facing the enemy. The group that had prayed the second rak'ah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would come to its position where it had prayed the second rak'ah with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), from the prayer of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and would make up the second rak'ah of its prayer with recitation. When it had finished and given the salam, it would depart to its companions.

Mention of those who said that:

1035 8. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, regarding the prayer of fear, he said: The imam forms a row behind him, and a row facing the enemy in a place other than the prayer place. He prays with the row behind him one rak'ah, then they go to the line of those, and those facing the enemy come, and he prays with them one rak'ah, then gives the salam to them. He has prayed two rak'ahs, and each row has prayed one rak'ah. Then those to whom he gave the salam stand in the line of those facing the enemy, and take their positions, and come and make up the rak'ah, then they go and stand in the position of those facing the enemy, and those come and pray one rak'ah. [[In the printed edition: "fa-yuṣalli bihim rak'ah thumma yusallim ʿalayhim," with the verbs in the present tense; the sound reading is what I have taken from the manuscript.]] Sufyan said: Thus each person has two rak'ahs, two rak'ahs.

[[The report: 10358. "al-Harith" is al-Harith ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Usamah, and "ʿAbd al-ʿAziz" is ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Aban al-Umawi; both were mentioned under nos. 10295 and 10315, among others, and will come under no. 10360.]]

1035 9. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Mihran narrated to us, and ʿAli narrated to me, saying: Zayd narrated to us, all of them from Sufyan, who said: Ibrahim used to say regarding the prayer of fear, and he mentioned something similar.

1036 0. Al-Harith narrated to me, saying: ʿAbd al-ʿAziz narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah have mercy on him, something similar.

[[The report: 10360. "al-Harith ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Usamah" and "ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Aban al-Umawi"; see the note on report 10358. I added "may Allah have mercy on him" from the manuscript.]]

* * *

Others said: Rather, each of the two groups makes up its prayer as far as it is able, without either group neglecting any part of it.

Mention of those who said that:

1036 1. Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Yunus ibn ʿUbayd, from al-Hasan: that Abu Musa al-Ashʿari prayed the prayer of fear with his companions in Isfahan when he campaigned there. He said: He prayed with one group of the people one rak'ah, and the other group stood guard. Those with whom he had prayed one rak'ah withdrew, and the others took their place and stood in their position. He prayed with them one rak'ah and then gave the salam. Then each group stood and prayed one rak'ah.

1036 2. ʿImran ibn Musa al-Qazzaz narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Warith narrated to us, saying: Yunus narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Abu Musa, something similar.

1036 3. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muʿadh ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-ʿAliyah and Yunus ibn Jubayr, who both said: Abu Musa al-Ashʿari prayed with his companions at the monastery (al-Dayr) of Isfahan, [[In the printed edition: "Abu Musa prayed with his companions at Isfahan," which differs from the manuscript; in al-Durr al-Manthur it reads "bi-l-dar min Isfahan." I was unable to identify a place called "al-Dayr" or "al-Dar" in the lands of Isfahan. Nevertheless, many places in these regions have been omitted from the geographical dictionaries, and one rarely finds them except in scattered reports in historical and conquest books.]] and there was no fear upon them at that time, [[In al-Durr al-Manthur: "wa-ma bihim yawma'idhin kabir khawf."]] but he wished to teach them their prayer. He arranged them in two rows: a row behind him and a row facing the enemy, confronting them. He prayed with those next to him one rak'ah, then they went to the line of their companions. Those others came, and he arranged them behind him, and prayed with them one rak'ah, then gave the salam. These made up one rak'ah, and those made up one rak'ah, then some of them gave the salam to others. So the imam had two rak'ahs in congregation, and they had one rak'ah each. [[In the printed edition: "rak'atayn" (two rak'ahs); I have kept the manuscript.]]

[[The report: 10363 and 10364. Al-Suyuti transmitted it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 213, attributing it to Ibn Abi Shaybah and others, with wording other than this. Al-Bayhaqi also referred to it in al-Sunan 3: 252.]]

1036 4. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to us, from Saʿid, from Qatadah, from Abu al-ʿAliyah, from Abu Musa, something similar.

1036 5. Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: that he said regarding the prayer of fear: He prays one rak'ah with one group of the people, and another group stands guard. Then those with whom he prayed one rak'ah depart until they stand in the position of their companions. Then those others come, and he prays one rak'ah with them, then gives the salam. Then each group stands and prays one rak'ah. [[In the printed edition: "yuṣalli ṭāʾifah," which is corrected from the manuscript.]]

[[The report: 10365. The reports that follow it, 10366, 10367, then 10370 and 10371, are five chains for the hadith of Nafiʿ from Ibn ʿUmar. It is a sound hadith, transmitted by Ahmad in his Musnad, no. 6159; this is the chain of al-Tabari no. 10371. He transmitted it again under no. 6431, via Musa ibn ʿUqbah, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar. See the commentary of my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad in the Musnad on the report 6159.]]

1036 6. Nasr ibn ʿAli narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allah narrated to us, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, something similar.

1036 7. ʿImran ibn Bakkar al-Kalaʿi narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿAyyash narrated to us, saying: ʿUbayd Allah narrated to us, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): that he prayed the prayer of fear, and he mentioned something similar.

[[The report: 10367. ʿImran ibn Bakkar al-Kalaʿi, mentioned under no. 2071.]]

1036 8. Saʿid ibn Yahya al-Umawi narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us, saying: Al-Zuhri informed me, from Salim, from Ibn ʿUmar: that he used to narrate that he prayed with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then he mentioned something similar.

[[The two reports 10368 and 10369: the report of Salim from Ibn ʿUmar is a sound hadith, transmitted by Ahmad in his Musnad, no. 6351. See my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad's commentary there.]]

1036 9. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla narrated to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn ʿUmar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar.

[[The two reports 10368 and 10369: the report of Salim from Ibn ʿUmar is a sound hadith, transmitted by Ahmad in his Musnad, no. 6351. See my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad's commentary there.]]

1037 0. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Nafiʿ, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) said regarding the prayer of fear: "The commander and a group of the people stand and prostrate one prostration together, and a group of them remains between them and the enemy." Then he mentioned something similar.

[[The two reports 10370 and 10371: see the note on no. 10365.
Muhammad ibn Harun al-Harbi, known as Abu Nashit, is from Baghdad. His nisbah in the Tahdhib is "al-Rabʿi," a nisbah to a tribe; as for "al-Harbi," it is a nisbah to "al-Harbiyyah," a large quarter in Baghdad near "Bab Harb," the cemetery of Bishr al-Hafi and Ahmad ibn Hanbal. It is named after one of the commanders of Abu Jaʿfar al-Mansur, who held the police command of Baghdad; he is "Harb ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Balkhi." A large group of scholars of Baghdad are ascribed to it. I have not found this nisbah for Muhammad ibn Harun except in the tafsir.
Abu al-Mughirah al-Himsi is ʿAbd al-Quddus ibn al-Hajjaj al-Khawlani, reliable (thiqah), one of the shaykhs of Ahmad. Al-Bukhari narrated from him, and he and the rest narrated from him through Ishaq ibn al-Kawsaj, Ahmad ibn Hanbal and others. He died in the year 212, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal led the funeral prayer over him.]]

1037 1. Muhammad ibn Harun al-Harbi narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Mughirah al-Himsi narrated to us, saying: Al-Awza'i narrated to us, from Ayyub ibn Musa, from Nafiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar: that the Prophet (ﷺ) prayed the prayer of fear with one of the two groups one rak'ah, then he mentioned something similar.

[[The two reports 10370 and 10371: see the note on no. 10365, which is the same note given above for the preceding report.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 102 (part 3 of 4):

10372. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, saying: my paternal uncle narrated to me, saying: my father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: ﴿And when you are among them and establish prayer for them﴾ up to His words: ﴿let them pray with you﴾. He said: a group of them would take up their weapons and face the enemy, while the other group prayed with the Imam one rak'ah. Then they would take their weapons and face the enemy, and their companions would come back and pray with the Imam one rak'ah. Thus the Imam would have two rak'ahs, and the rest of the people one rak'ah each, and then they would complete one more rak'ah each. This is the complete prayer.

* *

Others said: rather, this verse was revealed concerning the prayer of fear, when the enemy was on that day in the direction of the qiblah between the Muslims and the qiblah. So the prayer which the Prophet ﷺ performed with them that day was the prayer of fear, since the enemy was between the Imam and the qiblah.

Mention of the reports transmitted regarding this:

10373. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to me, from al-Nadr Abu 'Umar, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out on a campaign and met the polytheists at 'Usfan. When he prayed the noon prayer, they saw him bowing and prostrating, he and his companions. Some of them said to others that day: "This was an opportunity for you! Had you attacked them, they would not have known about you until you engaged them!" A speaker among them said: "Indeed they have another prayer which is dearer to them than their families and their wealth, so prepare yourselves until you raid them during it." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And when you are among them and establish prayer for them﴾ to the end of the verse, and informed him of what the polytheists had plotted. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed the afternoon prayer, they were facing him in the qiblah, so he arranged the Muslims behind him in two rows. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said takbir, and they all said takbir. Then he bowed and they all bowed with him. When he prostrated, the row nearest to him prostrated with him, and the row behind them stood facing the enemy. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his prostration and stood up, the second row prostrated, then they stood up, and those nearest the Messenger of Allah ﷺ moved back and the others advanced, so that they were now nearest to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When he bowed, they all bowed with him; then he raised his head and they raised theirs with him; then he prostrated and those nearest to him prostrated with him, and the second row stood facing the enemy. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his prostration and sat, those nearest to him sat, and the rear row prostrated; then they all sat and recited the tashahhud with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave the salam, he gave salam to them all. When the polytheists saw some of them prostrating while others stood looking at them, they said: "They have been informed of what we intended!"

[[Report 10373: "Al-Nadr Abu 'Umar" is "Nadr ibn 'Abd al-Rahman al-Khazzaz", previously mentioned under no. 718, and he is weak in hadith. Abu Nu'aym was asked about him and said: "This is not worth anything... he would come and sit with al-Hammani, and whenever anything was asked of him he would say: 'Ikrimah from Ibn 'Abbas'."
This report was transmitted by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 3:30, and he said: "This hadith is sound according to the conditions of al-Bukhari, though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. This is strange, for al-Bukhari said in the biography of "al-Nadr": "munkar al-hadith" (rejected in hadith)! How then can this report be according to his conditions?! Because of such things the scholars did not care for al-Hakim's authentication, may Allah forgive him. Al-Suyuti also cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 1:213, and attributed it additionally to al-Bazzar.]]

10374. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Bashir narrated to us, saying: 'Umar ibn Dharr narrated to us, saying: Mujahid narrated to me, saying: The Prophet ﷺ was at 'Usfan, and the polytheists were at Dajnan, at the water that is near Mecca. When the Prophet ﷺ prayed the noon prayer and they saw him, he prostrated and the people prostrated. They said: "If he performs a prayer after this, we will raid him!" So Allah warned him of that. The Prophet ﷺ stood in prayer, said takbir, and the people said takbir with him, and he mentioned something similar.

10375. 'Imran ibn Bakkar narrated to me, saying: Yahya ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, saying: 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Amr informed me, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: I was with the Prophet ﷺ, and we met the polytheists at Nakhl, and they were between us and the qiblah. When the time of the noon prayer came, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed with us while we were all present. When we finished, the polytheists were filled with regret [[tadhammara: they blamed one another for losing the opportunity; some said it may mean they urged one another to fight. But the better meaning, in my view, is the first, since "tadhammar" carries the sense of mutual blame and urging the seizing of an opportunity against the enemy. In al-Durr al-Manthur it reads "ta'ammara al-mushrikun", but the correct reading is what is in the manuscript and the printed edition. Ibn al-Athir mentioned it with this wording, and the author of al-Lisan quoted "tadhammara al-mushrikun" in the hadith of the prayer of fear, meaning this very hadith without doubt.]] and said: "If only we had charged them while they were praying!" Some of them said: "Indeed they have a prayer which they are waiting for, which is coming now, and it is dearer to them than their sons, so when they pray, descend upon them." He said: Then Gabriel came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with the news, and taught him how to pray. When the afternoon prayer came, the Prophet of Allah ﷺ stood facing the enemy, and we stood behind him in two rows. The Prophet of Allah said takbir and we said takbir with him all together, then he mentioned something similar. [[Report 10375: 'Imran ibn Bakkar al-Kala'i, previously mentioned shortly before under no. 10367. Yahya ibn Salih al-Wuhadhi was trustworthy, from the people of Syria; he died in 222 AH, and he narrated from 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Amr al-Raqqi and Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash and others. "Ibn 'Ayyash" is Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash ibn Salim al-'Ansi, trustworthy and retentive, though some have spoken about him; he is biographed in al-Tahdhib. "'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Amr al-Raqqi al-Jazari" Abu Wahb, previously mentioned under nos. 1566 and 4964; the printed and manuscript editions here read "'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Umar", which is an undoubted error, since it is he who narrates from Abu al-Zubayr. "Abu al-Zubayr" is Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Tadrus, previously mentioned under nos. 2029 and 8025. This report was transmitted by Ibn Jarir through three chains; this and the two following chains. The hadith of Abu al-Zubayr from Jabir was transmitted by Muslim 5:127 through Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Yunus, from Zuhayr, from Abu al-Zubayr. al-Nasa'i transmitted it in al-Sunan 3:176 through 'Amr ibn 'Ali, from 'Abd al-Rahman, from Sufyan, from Abu al-Zubayr. al-Bukhari alluded to it (al-Fath 7:326). Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar elaborated on the hadith of Abu al-Zubayr from Jabir in several places. al-Bukhari transmitted it through Hisham ibn Abi 'Abd Allah al-Dastuwa'i; these are the two chains of Abu Ja'far, nos. 10377 and 10378. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi in his Musnad: 240 also through Hisham. al-Bayhaqi transmitted it in al-Sunan 3:258; all of them abridged it. al-Suyuti was brief in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:214, attributing it only to Ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Jarir; Ibn Jarir's version is extended.]]

10376. Muhammad ibn Mu'ammar narrated to me, saying: Hammad ibn Mas'adah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Abi 'Abd Allah, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, similarly.

10377. Mu'ammal ibn Hisham narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Hisham, from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he mentioned something similar.

10378. 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd al-Samad narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from Abu 'Ayyash al-Zuraqi, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at 'Usfan, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in the noon prayer, and over the polytheists was Khalid ibn al-Walid. The polytheists said: "We have caught them off guard, we have caught them in heedlessness!" So Allah revealed the prayer of fear between the noon and afternoon prayers. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ led us in the afternoon prayer, [and divided us] — meaning into two groups — [[In the printed edition: "the afternoon prayer, meaning two groups", which hardly makes sense, so I added the bracketed words from al-Nasa'i, whose text there reads "and divided us into two groups" without "meaning".]] one group prayed with the Prophet ﷺ, and another group prayed behind them, guarding them. Then he said takbir and they all said takbir, and they all bowed. Then those nearest to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ prostrated; then he stood, and the others advanced and prostrated; then he stood and bowed with them all; then he prostrated with those nearest him, until these drew back and stood in the ranks of their companions, then the others advanced and prostrated, then he gave salam to them. So each of them had two rak'ahs with their imam. And he prayed again in the land of Banu Sulaym. [[Report 10378: 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Amuli, the teacher of al-Tabari, previously mentioned under no. 3759, where my brother said: "I do not know who he is, and I have found no biography of him; perhaps he is a distortion of something I do not know." What he said is not correct, for 'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid also appears here, and Abu Ja'far narrated from him in the History in one place, 1:184, saying: "'Amr ibn 'Abd al-Hamid al-Amuli narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us," so it is established that it is not a distortion. The report of Abu 'Ayyash al-Zuraqi was previously transmitted through Mansur, from Mujahid, from Abu 'Ayyash, through three chains, nos. 10323 and 10324; the chain of 'Abd al-'Aziz ibn 'Abd al-Samad is the one transmitted by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan 3:177. This report is not present in the manuscript.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse, according to those who held this view and transmitted this report: ﴿And when you are among them﴾, meaning among your companions, fearful, ﴿and establish prayer for them, let a party of them stand with you﴾, meaning from those who enter with you into your prayer. ﴿Then when they have prostrated﴾ means: when this party has prostrated with your prostration and raised their heads from their prostration, ﴿let them be behind you﴾, meaning: let those behind you move behind the party that guarded you, and them, when you prostrate with them and they prostrate with you. ﴿And let another party come who have not prayed﴾, meaning the guarding party that prayed with him, except that they did not prostrate with his prostration. So the meaning of His words ﴿have not prayed﴾, according to the view of these people, is: have not prostrated with your prostration. ﴿Then let them pray with you﴾, meaning: let them prostrate with your prostration when you prostrate, and let those who prostrated with your prostration in the first rak'ah guard you and them; ﴿and let them take their precaution and their weapons﴾, meaning the guarding party.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse most preferred among the views we have mentioned is the view of him who said: the meaning is: when the party that stood with you in their prayer prostrates, ﴿then let them be behind you﴾, meaning: behind you and behind those who enter your prayer who did not pray the first rak'ah with you, facing the enemy, and after they finish the rest of their prayer. ﴿And let another party come﴾, and they are the party that was facing the enemy, ﴿who have not prayed﴾, meaning: who did not pray the first rak'ah with you, ﴿then let them pray with you﴾, meaning: let them pray with you the rak'ah that remains for you, ﴿and let them take their precaution and their weapons﴾, for fighting their enemy, after they finish their prayer.

This is like the report transmitted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he did this on the day of Dhat al-Riqa', and the report transmitted by Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah. [[That is, the report no. 10345, then the report of Sahl ibn Abi Hathmah from 10346 to 10353.]]

We only said that this is more fitting for the interpretation of the verse because Allah, Mighty is His remembrance, said: ﴿And when you are among them and establish prayer for them﴾, and we have shown that "establishing" it means completing it with its bowing and prostration, and we have also shown, along with that, that His words ﴿there is no blame upon you if you shorten the prayer if you fear that those who disbelieve may tempt you﴾ are only a permission to shorten from its bowing and prostration in a state of severe fear.

Since that is established, it is clear that there is no basis for the interpretation of one who interprets it as: the first party, when it prostrates with the Imam, has concluded its prayer, based on His words ﴿then when they have prostrated, let them be behind you﴾, because these meanings have the possibilities I mentioned before; and because there is no indication in the verse that the shortening mentioned in the verse before it refers to shortening the number of rak'ahs.

Since there is no basis for that, the view of one who said: "It is meant by that the advancing and retreating within the prayer, in the manner of the Prophet's prayer at 'Usfan," is far-fetched. [[The word "abd" (far-fetched) is the predicate of "fa-qawl man qal" (the view of him who said); the construction is: the view of him who said ... is far-fetched.]] That is because Allah, may His praise be exalted, says: ﴿Let another party come who have not prayed, then let them pray with you﴾, and both parties had prayed with the Prophet ﷺ his first rak'ah in his prayer at 'Usfan. It is impossible that the party that prayed with the Prophet ﷺ be the party that did not pray with him.

If someone supposes that by "have not prayed" is meant "have not prostrated", that is not the apparent meaning of "prayer", and the meanings of the words of Allah, may His praise be exalted, are directed to the most apparent and well-known of their senses, unless something prevents that which must be accepted.

Since that is so, and there was no command from Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, to the first party to delay the completion of what remained of their prayer until the Imam finished the rest of his prayer, and there was no harm upon the Muslims who were facing the enemy from their occupation with completing that, so that the command for them to delay it and to withdraw from their position before completing the rest of their prayer had no purpose.

However, even if the matter is so, we hold that whoever among the Imams prayed it in a manner that matched some of the aspects we have mentioned from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he prayed it, his prayer is valid and complete for him, because the reports of all of that from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are sound, and it is among the matters which the Messenger of Allah ﷺ taught his community, then permitted them to act according to whichever of these they wished.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for His words ﴿The disbelievers wish that you would be negligent of your weapons and your belongings, and they would swoop down upon you in one attack﴾, He means: the disbelievers who disbelieved in Allah wished ﴿that you would be negligent of your weapons and your belongings﴾, meaning: that you would be occupied with your prayer, away from your weapons with which you fight them, and away from your belongings by which you travel on your journeys, so you would be heedless of them. ﴿And they would swoop down upon you in one attack﴾, meaning: they would charge upon you in one assault while you are occupied with your prayer and away from your weapons and belongings, so they would strike you by surprise, kill you, and plunder your camp.

He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: So do not do that after this, so that you all occupy yourselves with your prayer when your prayer time comes while you are facing the enemy, so that you give your enemy an opportunity over yourselves, your weapons, and your belongings. Rather, establish the prayer as I have explained it to you, and take your precaution and your weapons against your enemy.

* *

The explanation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And there is no blame upon you if you have a hardship from rain or if you are ill that you put down your weapons; but take your precaution. Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.﴾ (102)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, "there is no blame upon you" (wa la junah 'alaykum), He, great is His praise, means: there is no sin or fault upon you [see the explanation of "junah" above, p. 123, note 2, and the references there] "if you suffer any hurt from rain" — meaning: if you are harmed by rain that falls on you while you are facing your enemy — "or if you are ill" — meaning: if you are wounded or sick [a'la', the plural of 'alil; the printed edition had "wounded" only, and I have restored the addition from the manuscript] — "to lay down your weapons," meaning: if you are too weak to carry them. But if you lay down your weapons because of harm from rain or sickness, then "take your precaution" (khudhu hidhrakum), meaning: be on your guard against them, lest they incline upon you while you are heedless of them and off your guard — "Indeed, Allah has prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment." By this He means: He has prepared for them a degrading punishment in which they will remain forever, never coming out of it. That is the punishment of Hell. [See the explanation of "muhin" above, 8:355, note 3, and the references there.]

* *

It has been mentioned that His words, "or if you are ill," were revealed concerning 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, who was wounded.

Those who said this:

10379. Al-Abbas ibn Muhammad related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to us, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: Ya'la ibn Muslim informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding "If you suffer any hurt from rain or are ill": 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, who was wounded.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 103:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿So when you have completed the prayer, remember Allah standing and sitting and on your sides. And when you are secure, establish the prayer.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: when you, O believers, have finished your prayer while facing your enemy, [[See the explanation of "qada" (completed) above: 2:542-543 / 4:195.

His words "which We have explained to you" describe His words "your prayer."

In the printed edition here also appears "muwafiqu 'aduwwikum" (those who agree with your enemy), which is an error. See the note above, p. 163, note 2.]] then remember Allah in all your conditions, standing, sitting, and lying on your sides, by magnifying Him and by asking Him for victory over your enemy for yourselves, so that Allah may grant you victory and help you against them. This is similar to His words: ﴿O you who believe, when you meet a force, stand firm and remember Allah much, that you may succeed﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 45]. And as follows:

10380 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "and remember Allah much" [[In the printed edition: "fadhkuru Allaha qiyaman" in place of His words "wadhkuru Allaha kathiran." In my view this is an alteration by the publisher; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] – he said: Allah does not impose upon His servants any obligation without setting for it a known limit, [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "illa ja'ala laha jaza'an ma'lumans," which is an error; the correct reading is "haddan," as the context of the speech and the meaning indicate.]] then He excuses its performers in a condition of excuse, except for remembrance, for Allah has not set a limit to it at which it ends, and He has excused no one from abandoning it except one overcome in his intellect. So He said: "remember Allah standing and sitting and on your sides," by night and by day, on land and at sea, while traveling and at home, in wealth and in poverty, in sickness and in health, in secret and in public, and in every condition.

* *

As for His words: "And when you are secure, establish the prayer," the people of interpretation differed concerning its explanation.

Some of them said: The meaning of His words, "and when you are secure," is: when you settle in your homelands and reside in your cities, "then establish," meaning: complete the prayer that He permitted you to shorten in a state of fear during your journey and your striking upon the earth. [[In the manuscript: "fa-aqimu al-salah allati adhina lakum..." without "yaʻni: fa-atimmu."]]

Those who said this:

10381 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Mujahid regarding His words: "and when you are secure," he said: leaving the abode of travel for the abode of residence.

10382 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "and when you are secure," he said: "when you are secure in your cities, then complete the prayer."

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "when you are settled," "then establish the prayer," meaning: complete its limits with its bowing and prostration.

Those who said this:

10383 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "and when you are secure," he said: when you are secure after fear.

10384 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "and when you are secure, establish the prayer," he said: when you are secure, then perform the prayer; do not pray it riding, nor walking, nor sitting. [[See the explanation of "iqamat al-salah" above: 1:241, and the language indexes in the earlier volumes.]]

10385 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "and when you are secure, establish the prayer," he said: complete it.

10386 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more preferable of the two interpretations of the verse is the interpretation of those who interpreted it as: when your fear of your enemy has ceased and you are secure, O believers, and your souls are at rest in safety, "then establish the prayer," that is, complete its prescribed limits upon you, [[In the printed edition: "fa-atimmuha bi-hududiha," which differs from the manuscript, having been wrongly altered by the editor.]] not falling short of any of its limits.

We said that this is the more preferable interpretation of the verse because Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, made known to His believing servants the obligation upon them of their prayer through these two verses in two states:

The first: the state of severe fear, in which He permitted them to shorten the prayer, as I have explained, by shortening its limits from completeness.

The second: the state other than severe fear, in which He commanded them to establish its limits and complete them, as He described to them, may His praise be exalted, regarding one group of them standing guard for another during prayer behind their imams and guarding one another from their enemy. This is a state in which there is no shortening, for He, may His praise be exalted, says to His Prophet ﷺ in this state: "And when you are among them and lead them in prayer..." Thus it is known from this that His words "So when you are secure, establish the prayer" mean only: when you are secure from the state in which you were not establishing your prayer, then establish it. And that state is the state of severe fear, since He has commanded them to establish it in a state other than severe fear by His words: "And when you are among them and lead them in prayer," the verse.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers a decree of specified times﴾ (103)

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed concerning the explanation of this.

Some of them said: Its meaning: indeed, prayer was an obligation prescribed upon the believers. [[See the explanation of "kitab" above: 3:364, 365, 409 / 4:295, 297 / 5:300, and other places in the language indexes.]]

Those who said this:

10387 - Abu al-Sa'ib narrated to me, saying: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Fudayl ibn Marzuq, from 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi regarding His words: "Indeed, the prayer was upon the believers a decree of specified times," he said: prescribed.

10388 - Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "Indeed, the prayer was upon the believers a decree of specified times," he said: prescribed, "al-mawquut" is the prescribed.

10389 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi who said: As for "kitaban mawquutan," it is prescribed.

10390 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Layth, from Mujahid: "kitaban mawquutan," he said: prescribed.

* *

Others said: Its meaning: indeed, the prayer was upon the believers an obligation, binding.

Those who said this:

10391 - Yaʻqub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan regarding His words: "Indeed, the prayer was upon the believers a decree of specified times," he said: a binding decree.

10392 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "a decree of specified times," he said: obligatory.

10393 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

10394 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Ma'mar ibn Sam, from Abu Ja'far regarding His words: "a decree of specified times," he said: required.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 104:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And do not falter in pursuing the people. If you are suffering, then indeed they suffer just as you suffer, and you hope from Allah for what they do not hope for.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, "and do not falter" — may His praise be majestic — He means: do not weaken.

* *

From their saying: "Wahana fulan fi hadha al-amr yahinu wahnan wa wuhunan" (a man weakened in this matter, he weakens, weakness and feebleness). [[See the explanation of "wahn" above, 7: 234, 269, and "al-wuhun" is a verbal noun which most lexicographical books do not mention, and which Abu Ja'far did not mention above, 7: 234.]]

* *

As for His saying, "in pursuing the people," it means: in seeking out the people and pursuing them. [[See the explanation of "al-ibtigha'" above, p. 71, note 2, and the references there.]] "The people" are the enemies of Allah and the enemies of the believers, from among the people of polytheism toward Allah. "If you are suffering" — He says: if you, O believers, are in pain from the wounds that befall you from them in this world. [[It is said: "waja'a al-rajul yujau wa yay'ju wa yaja'u waj'an," all of which are good and correct.]] "Then indeed they suffer just as you suffer" — He says: then indeed the polytheists are in pain from what befalls them from you of wounds and harm, just as you are in pain from their wounds and harm to you. "And you hope" — you, O believers — "from Allah" — for reward for what befalls you from them — "for what they do not hope." He says: since you are certain of Allah's reward for you for what afflicts you from them, [[In the printed edition: "if you are certain," which is an error; the correct reading is what is in the manuscript. This clause sits between the two parentheses, interposed between subject and predicate. The context is: "so you are more worthy and more fitting to be patient."]] with what they are deniers of, you are more worthy and more fitting to be patient in fighting them and warring against them than they are in fighting and warring against you, and to exert yourselves in seeking them out and pursuing them for battle, where they falter and do not exert themselves. How much more so, then, in what they have exerted themselves in and not faltered? [[In the printed edition: "So if you find [the strength] to seek them out and pursue them for battle over what you falter in and do not find, how much more over what they have found and not faltered," which is a statement with no meaning; the first-edition editor placed the number (3) on it as a sign of confusion in the wording.

In the manuscript: "And if you find [the strength] to seek them out and pursue them for battle over what you falter and do not ... how much more over what ... and did not falter"! Which is even more confused and corrupt because it is unpointed. The correct reading is what I have established.

The context of this whole phrase: "So you are ... more worthy and more fitting to be patient in their war and fighting ... and to exert yourselves in seeking them out and pursuing them, for battle with them over what they falter in ..." That is: so that they might fight them over a matter in which they do not exert themselves with any resolve that would accompany weakness.]]

* *

Those who interpreted the verse said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

10400- Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "And do not falter in pursuing the people. If you are suffering, then indeed they suffer just as you suffer," he says: do not weaken in seeking the people, for indeed if you are suffering, they suffer as you suffer, and you hope from Allah for the reward and recompense that they do not hope for.

10401- Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And do not falter in pursuing the people. If you are suffering, then indeed they suffer just as you suffer," he said: he says: do not weaken in seeking the people; if you are suffering from wounds, [[In the printed edition: "suffering from the wounds," with an added "min"; what is in the manuscript is correct.]] then indeed they suffer as you suffer.

* *

10402- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And do not falter in pursuing the people," do not weaken.

10403- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi' regarding His saying: "And do not falter," he says: do not weaken. [[This report is incomplete in the manuscript: the page ends at the words "so do not falter," then the reverse side is written "in pursuing the people ...", and it carries the rest of the following report but omits its chain. I have left the printed edition as it stands, which is undoubtedly correct.]]

10404- Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "And do not falter in pursuing the people," he said: he says: do not weaken in seeking them, "if you are suffering" from fighting, "then indeed they suffer just as you suffer." This is before the wounds reach them — if you dislike fighting and so you suffer from it, "then indeed they suffer just as you suffer, and you hope from Allah what they do not hope," he says: so do not weaken in seeking them in the place of fighting. [[In the printed edition: "in the place of fighting," and in the manuscript: "for the place of fighting," which is the correct reading; meaning: their exertion in seeking the people in the battle.]]

10405- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: "If you are suffering," — in pain.

10406- al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Juraij regarding "If you are suffering," he said: in pain from what befalls you from them; then indeed they are in pain as you are in pain, and you hope for reward for what befalls you, which they do not hope for.

10407- al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Hafs ibn Umar narrated to us, saying: al-Hakam ibn Aban narrated to us, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: When the battle of Uhud took place, and what befell the Muslims befell them, the Prophet (ﷺ) went up the mountain. Abu Sufyan came and said: "O Muhammad, will you not come out? Will you not come out? War is a series of turns: a day for us and a day for you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions: "Answer him." They said: "Not equal, not equal. Our slain are in Paradise and your slain are in Hell." Abu Sufyan said: "We have al-Uzza and you have no al-Uzza." [["al-Uzza" was an idol of the Quraysh and Banu Kinanah.]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Say to him: Allah is our Protector and you have no protector." Abu Sufyan said: "Exalt Hubal, exalt Hubal!" [["Hubal" was an idol in the Ka'bah belonging to the Quraysh. The explanation of "a'la Hubal" has passed, 7: 310, and the one who vocalized "a'la" with a hamzah on the alif, a sukun on the 'ayn and a kasrah on the lam was mistaken; the correct form is from "ala ya'lu."]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Say to him: Allah is higher and more majestic!" Abu Sufyan said: "Our appointment with you is at Badr al-Sughra," and the Muslims slept with their wounds. ["al-Kulum" is the plural of "kalm" (with a fatha and sukun): a wound. And "al-kulaym": the wounded.]

Ikrimah said: And in this were revealed: ﴿If a wound touches you, a similar wound has touched the people; and these days We alternate among people﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 140], and concerning them was revealed: "If you are suffering, then indeed they suffer just as you suffer, and you hope from Allah what they do not hope. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise." [[Report 10407 has passed as number 7098, and it appears there correctly; from it and from the manuscript I have corrected what came before.]]

10408- Yahya ibn Abi Talib narrated to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak regarding His saying: "If you are suffering, then indeed they suffer just as you suffer," he said: they are in pain as you are in pain.

It has been reported from some of them that he interpreted His saying: "and you hope from Allah what they do not hope" as: and you fear from Allah what they do not fear, from the saying of Allah: ﴿Say to those who believe: forgive those who do not hope for the Days of Allah﴾ [Surah al-Jathiyah: 14], meaning: those who do not fear the Days of Allah.

It is not known in the speech of the Arabs that "al-raja'" (hope) is turned to the meaning of "al-khawf" (fear), except with a preceding negation, as His praise says: ﴿What is the matter with you that you do not hope for dignity from Allah?﴾ [Surah Nuh: 13], meaning: you do not fear greatness from Allah; and as the poet said: [[In the printed edition: "the Hudhalī poet," which is an error that transferred the attribution of Abu Dhu'ayb in the following verse to this place. I do not know who this rajiz was, though I fear the rajaz may belong to Abu Muhammad al-Fuq'asi.]]

*lā tartajī ḥīna tulāqī al-dhā'idā ... ʾasabʿatan laqat maʿan ʾam wāḥidā*

And as Abu Dhu'ayb al-Hudhali said:

*idhā lasaʿat-hu al-naḥlu lam yarju lasʿahā ... wa khālafahā fī bayti nawbin ʿawāmilī*

[[His Diwan: 143; Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1: 286; al-Addad of Ibn al-Anbari: 9; and Lisan (raja). The verse comes from a poem of his describing one who gathers honey from beehives. It is narrated with "idha lasa'tahu al-dabr" and its version appears in the exegesis as "nawb 'awasil" as well. Before this verse he said: he who descends upon them with ropes, firmly tied, strong in his instructions, a skilled son of a skilled father... The meaning: he is not afraid of the sting of the bees when he enters upon them and they rage at him to sting him. "Fa-khalafahā" means he entered their hive to take their honey, and they came out to him when they heard his stir, and he went against them to the honeycombs without fearing their stings. It is also narrated as "ḥālafahā" with a ḥā', meaning he stayed with them and did not fear their stings. "Al-nawb" is the plural of "nā'ib," an attribute of the bees, meaning they graze and then return to their hive to deposit their honey, coming and going. "Al-'awāmil" are those that work the honey; "al-'awāsil" are the bees that make honey, or those that possess honey.]] And it has reached us that it is a dialect of the people of the Hijaz, who say it meaning: I am not concerned, and I do not care.

* *

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And Allah has ever been Knowing and Wise﴾ (104)

By this He means, may His praise be majestic: Allah has never ceased to be "Knowing" of the interests of His creation, "Wise" in His management and decree. [[See the explanation of "kana," "alim" and "hakim" above in the indices of language.]] And from His knowledge, O believers, of your interests, He informed you — when your prayers are present and the obligation of the duty God has imposed on you, while you face your enemy — of what would lead to your attaining the performance of God's obligation upon you and your safety from your enemy. And from His wisdom He made you see what supports you and weakens the plot of your enemy. [[In the printed edition: "made you see by what supports you," with an added bāʾ; I have kept the manuscript reading, which is correct.]]

* *

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you, and do not be a advocate for the deceivers﴾ (105)

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 4, verses 105–106 (part 1 of 2):**

The exegesis of His words: ﴿And ask forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (106).

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His remembrance be exalted, ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, "Indeed, We have sent down to you," O Muhammad, "the Book," meaning the Qur'an, "so that you may judge between the people," so that you may decide between the people and separate them, "by what Allah has shown you," meaning by what Allah has revealed to you of His Book. "And do not be a disputer for the treacherous," he says: do not be a defender for one who betrays a Muslim or a covenant-partner in his person or his property, "a disputer," who argues on his behalf and repels from him the one who demands from him his right which he betrayed. "And ask forgiveness of Allah," O Muhammad, and ask Him to pardon you for the punishment of your sin in disputing on behalf of the traitor who betrayed another's property. "Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful," he says: Indeed Allah has never ceased to pardon the sins of His believing servants, by abandoning their punishment for them when they ask Him for forgiveness from them, "Merciful" towards them. [[See the explanation of "seeking forgiveness" (al-istighfar), and "kana" (was), "ghafur" (Forgiving) and "rahim" (Merciful) in what has preceded in the lexical indices.]]

So do that, O Muhammad, and Allah will forgive you what preceded of your disputing on behalf of this traitor.

* *

It has been said that the Prophet (ﷺ) had not disputed on behalf of the traitor, but he had intended to do so, so Allah commanded him to seek forgiveness for what he had intended of that.

* *

It is mentioned that the traitors whom Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, reproached His Prophet (ﷺ) for disputing on behalf of were the Banu Ubayriq.

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the betrayal that was committed by them, for which Allah described him.

Some of them said: It was a theft that he committed.

Those who said this:

10409. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, up to His words: ﴿And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾, in between that, concerning Ibn Ubayriq, [[In the printed edition: "Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq," and the mention of "Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq" will come in no. 10412, but here in the manuscript it is "Ibn Ubayriq," and you will see the variation in the reports about these Banu Ubayriq.]] and his coat of mail, of iron, from the Jews, which he stole. And his companions from among the believers said to the Prophet: "Excuse him among the people with your tongue," and they accused a innocent man of the Jews of the coat of mail. [[The phrase "from the Jews" I have affirmed from the manuscript.]]

10410. Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly. [[Report 10410: this report is not established in the manuscript.]]

10411. Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Shu'ayb, Abu Muslim al-Harrani, narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah, from his father, from his grandfather Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man, who said: There was a household among us called the Banu Ubayriq: Bishr, Bashir, and Mubashshir. Bashir was a hypocrite, and he would compose poetry satirizing the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then attribute it to some of the Arabs, saying: "So-and-so said this," and "So-and-so said that." When the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard that poetry, they said: "By Allah, none composes this poetry except the wicked one!" So he said:

*Do the men compose a poem and then they harbor resentment and say: "It is the son of Ubayriq who composed it!"*

[[In the printed edition: "Except this wicked one," and I have affirmed what is in the manuscript. In the manuscript: "They attributed it and said," and I left what is in the printed edition as it is. This verse has come in al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim erroneously: "... they gathered against the son of Ubayriq, he composed it." What is here is its correct form, and after it there he recited: "Arrogant, as if I feared them, may God cut off their noses and sever them." Thus it came with the iqwa' (the variation of the rhyme), due to the difference between the rhyme in "qalaha" and "abanaha," a defect that occurs similarly in poetry, due to the closeness of the articulation points of the lam and the nun, and the presence of the ha' and alif as an extension of the rhyme helped with that. And his saying "adammu" means they became angry at him and held rancor. And his saying "mutakhammitin" means they became enraged, roared, rose up and shouted. A man who is mutakhammit is one with intense anger, having a surge and clamor. In al-Mustadrak it is "mutakhatmin" with the ta' preceding the mim, which is an error; its correct form is what I have affirmed.]]

He said: They were a household of poverty and need in the pre-Islamic period and in Islam. The people of Medina ate only dates and barley. When a man had means, a caravan (dafitah) would come from Syria with fine flour (darmak), and the man would buy some of it and reserve it for himself. [[The "dafitah": they were a people of the Nabateans who carried flour, oil and other goods to Medina. Then they called the one who brings provisions and goods to cities, and the muleteer who hires out loads, "dafitah" and "daffat." And "darmak" is pure, fine, white flour.]] As for their dependents, their food was only dates and barley. Then a caravan came from Syria, and my uncle Rifa'ah ibn Zayd bought a load of darmak, and placed it in a storeroom (mashraba) of his. [[The "mashraba" (with the mim fathah, the shin sakin and the ra' fathah or damma): it is the upper room, or the loft, or the veranda before the upper room. And "al-masharib" are the upper rooms.]] In the storeroom there was his weaponry: two coats of mail, two swords and what suits them. Then he was attacked during the night, [[In other sources: "from under the house," and it seems that what is in al-Tabari is the correct version of the report.]] the storeroom was broken into, and the food and the weapons were taken. When he awoke in the morning, my uncle Rifa'ah came to me and said: "O son of my brother, you know that we were attacked during this night, our storeroom was broken into, and our weapons and food were taken!" He said: We searched in the dwelling [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "fa-tajassasna" with the jim, which is correct, and better than with the ha', as in all other sources. "Tahassasa al-khabar": to seek and investigate the news. And in the revelation: "O my sons, go and seek out (tahassasu) news of Joseph and his brother." And "al-dar" here: the quarter that a tribe or a clan of it settles in, and by it is meant the tribe or clan, as in the hadith: "Shall I inform you of the best dwellings of the Ansar? The dwellings of the Banu al-Najjar, then the dwellings of the Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal, and in every dwelling of the Ansar there is good." Meaning the tribe gathered in a quarter it inhabits.]] and we asked, and it was said to us: "We saw the Banu Ubayriq kindle a fire this night, and we do not see, in what we see, except that it is on some of your food."

= He said: The Banu Ubayriq had said, while we were asking in the dwelling: "By Allah, we do not see your companion except Labid ibn Sahl!" — a man from among us who had righteousness and Islam. [[In the printed edition: "rajul" with the nominative, as if he disapproved of the accusative! And it is pure and excellent correctness.]] When Labid heard of this, he unsheathed his sword, then came to the Banu Ubayriq and said: "By Allah, this sword will mingle with you, or you will clarify this theft!" They said: "Away from us, O man! By Allah, you are not its perpetrator!" We asked in the dwelling until we did not doubt that they were its perpetrators. My uncle said: "O son of my brother, if only you would go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mention that to him!"

= Qatadah said: So I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), mentioned that to him, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, a household among us of harshness, [[Al-jafa': coarseness of temperament.]] went to my uncle Rifa'ah, broke into his storeroom, and took his weapons and his food. Let them return our weapons to us; as for the food, we have no need of it." [[In the manuscript: "fa-la hajata lana bihi," and both are the same.]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will consider that." [[In the printed edition: "I will consider that," and in al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Kathir: "I will consult about that," and I have affirmed what is in the manuscript.]] When the Banu Ubayriq heard of that, they went to a man among them called Usayr ibn 'Urwah, and spoke to him about it. A number of people from the dwelling gathered to him, and they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man and his uncle went to a household among us, a household of Islam and righteousness, accusing them of theft without evidence or proof." [[Al-thabt (with two fathahs): proof, evidence and argument.]]

= Qatadah said: So I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and spoke to him, and he said: "You went to a household described as having Islam and righteousness, accusing them of theft without evidence or proof!!" He said: So I returned, and I wished that I had come out of some of my wealth and had not spoken to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about that. Then I came to my uncle Rifa'ah, and he said: "O son of my brother, what have you done?" So I informed him of what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said to me, and he said: "Allah is the One sought for help!"
