= Then we had not waited long before the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you. And do not be a disputer for the treacherous﴾, meaning: the Banu Ubayriq, ﴿and ask forgiveness of Allah﴾, that is: for what you said to Qatadah, ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾, that is: the Banu Ubayriq, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is a habitual traitor and sinner. They hide from the people﴾ up to His words: ﴿Then he asks forgiveness of Allah; he will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾, that is: if they ask forgiveness of Allah, He will forgive them, ﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself. And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise. And whoever earns an error or a sin and then throws it onto an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a clear sin﴾, meaning their saying about Labid, ﴿And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, a faction of them would have resolved to mislead you﴾, meaning: Usayr and his companions, ﴿but they mislead none except themselves, and they cannot harm you at all. And Allah has revealed to you the Book and wisdom﴾ up to His words: ﴿We will give him a great reward﴾.

Then when the Qur'an was revealed, the weapons were brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he returned them to Rifa'ah. = Qatadah said: When I brought the weapons to my uncle, and he was an elder who had grown old in the pre-Islamic period, [[ "'asa fi al-jahiliyyah": he grew old and aged, from the saying "'asa al-'ud," meaning it dried, hardened and became stiff.]] and I had seen his Islam as being corrupted, [[ "Al-madkhul," from "al-dakhl" (with two fathahs), which is a defect, corruption or deceit, meaning that his faith had hypocrisy in it. And "rajul madkhul": that is, there is a flaw and corruption in his intellect.]] when I brought him the weapons, he said: "O son of my brother, it is in the way of Allah." He said: So I knew that his Islam was sound.

When the Qur'an was revealed, Bishr joined the polytheists, and he stayed with Sullafah, daughter of Sa'd ibn Shuhayd. [[In the printed edition: "Sullafah daughter of Sa'd ibn Sahl," and in the manuscript: "... daughter of Sa'd ibn Suhayl," and in al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Kathir: "daughter of Sa'd ibn Sumayyah," and in al-Mustadrak: "Salamah daughter of Sa'd ibn Sahl, sister of the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, and she was married to Talhah ibn Abi Talhah in Mecca." The correct form beyond doubt is what I have affirmed, and it has come correctly in al-Durr al-Manthur, and then similarly in the Diwan of Hassan ibn Thabit. "Sullafah bint Sa'd ibn Shuhayd" was an Ansari woman from the Banu 'Awf ibn 'Amr ibn Malik ibn al-Aws, whose lineage I have verified: "Sullafah daughter of Sa'd ibn Shuhayd ibn 'Amr ibn Zayd ibn Umayyah ibn Zayd ibn Malik ibn 'Awf ibn 'Amr ibn 'Awf ibn Malik ibn al-Aws." This is from Jamharat al-Ansab of Ibn Hazm, p. 314, where he mentioned "'Uwaymir ibn Sa'd ibn Shuhayd ibn 'Amr ... " and said: "He had companionship (suhbah); 'Umar appointed him over Palestine." I did not find in the biographies of the Companions and other sources "'Uwaymir ibn Sa'd ibn Shuhayd." However, Ibn Hazm's transmission is undoubtedly correct. If that is so, then this 'Uwaymir is the brother of this Sullafah. And "Sullafah bint Sa'd ibn Shuhayd al-Ansariyyah" is well known and unquestioned; she was the wife of Talhah ibn Abi Talhah, and she was the mother of Musafi', al-Jullas and Kilab, the sons of Talhah ibn Abi Talhah (Ibn Hisham 3:66). They and their father were killed at the Battle of Uhud. Musafi' and al-Jullas were killed by 'Asim ibn Thabit ibn Abi al-Aqlah, the protector of the hornets. So Sullafah vowed: "If I am able to get the head of 'Asim, I will drink wine from his skull!" But the hornets (the bees) protected him when the Hudhayl wanted to take his head to sell it to Sullafah (Ibn Hisham 3:180). This is the verification of her name, if Allah wills, by which what is in al-Tirmidhi, al-Mustadrak and those who transmitted from them is corrected.]] So Allah revealed concerning him: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers﴾ up to His words: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly strayed far astray﴾. When it was revealed concerning Sullafah, Hassan ibn Thabit hurled at her verses of poetry, [[The poetry of Hassan in his Diwan, p. 271, in which at its beginning he mentions Sullafah with evil speech. He said:

*"And the thief of the two coats of mail, if you mention him, is not among the noble men whom I would shelter.*
*The daughter of Sa'd has indeed sheltered him, so she became one who contends with his skin, and he contends with her."*]]

So she took his saddlebag, placed it on her head, went out, and threw it into al-Abtah, [[In the printed edition: "she threw it at al-Abtah," and I have affirmed what is in the manuscript, which agrees with what is in al-Tirmidhi. "Al-Abtah" is the Abtah of Mecca, or the Batha' of Mecca, and it is the channel of its valley.]] then she said: "You have sent me the poetry of Hassan! You never brought me anything good!"

[[Report 10411: "Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Shu'ayb 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim al-Umawi," Abu Muslim al-Harrani. From the people of Harran, he settled in Baghdad. Al-Khatib said: "Reliable, trustworthy." Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat and said: "He is strange." He narrated from Muhammad ibn Salamah. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/2, and Tarikh Baghdad 7:266.

This report was narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, in the explanation of this verse, with the same chain as al-Tabari, namely from al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Shu'ayb. It was narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 4:385, Ibn Kathir cited it in his Tafsir 2:574–576, and al-Suyuti in al-Durr 2:214, 215, and he added its attribution to Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh.

The chain of al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: "Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me ..." and he gave its chain raised (marfu') to Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man, as in the tafsir and al-Tirmidhi.

Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi pointed to this report with his chain: "'Uthman ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Allaf informed us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Shafi'i informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Shu'ayb (and he is Abu Shu'ayb) narrated to us, my grandfather and my father together narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us," and he cited it as the chain of Abu Ja'far.

The Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned in al-Tahdhib that Abu Muslim al-Harrani (al-Hasan ibn Ahmad) narrated from his father and grandfather, and I fear that this is an error, and the error came from this chain because of his saying "my grandfather and my father together narrated to me," whereas the one who says that is 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad, not al-Hasan ibn Ahmad.

Then al-Khatib al-Baghdadi said: "Abu Shu'ayb said: 'My father (meaning al-Hasan ibn Ahmad) said: Yahya ibn Ma'in heard it from me in Baghdad in the Friday mosque, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, 'Ali ibn al-Madini, and Ishaq ibn Abi Isra'il.'" As for Ibn Kathir, the speaker of this is "Muhammad ibn Salamah," and this is the correct form.

Al-Hakim said in al-Mustadrak (and his wording differs from the wording of al-Tabari): "This is a hadith sound according to the condition of Muslim, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it."

As for al-Tirmidhi, he said: "This is a strange hadith; we do not know anyone who transmitted it with a chain other than Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Harrani. Yunus ibn Bukayr and more than one narrated this hadith from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah, as a mursal report, not mentioning in it 'from his father, from his grandfather.'"

However, al-Hakim narrated it, as you see, through the route of Yunus ibn Bukayr, raised to Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man.]]

10412. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, he says: by what Allah has revealed to you and made clear to you. ﴿And do not be a disputer for the treacherous﴾, then he recited up to His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is a habitual traitor and sinner.﴾ It was mentioned to us that these verses were revealed concerning Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq, and concerning what the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) intended in excusing him. Allah made clear the matter of Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq and admonished His Prophet and warned him not to be a disputer for the treacherous.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verses 105–106 (part 2 of 2):

Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq was a man from the Helpers (al-Anṣār), from the clan of Ẓafar. He stole a coat of mail belonging to his paternal uncle, which had been deposited with him as a trust. Then he planted it with a Jew who used to frequent them, called Zayd ibn al-Samīn. [Editor's note: In the manuscript and al-Durr al-Manthur it reads "faqaddamahā" (he presented it), but the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.] [Editor's note: In al-Wāḥidī's Asbāb al-Nuzūl, p. 134, it reads "Zayd ibn al-Samīr" with a rāʾ, while the other sources, as here in the printed edition and manuscript, read "al-Samīn".] The Jew then came to the Prophet of God (ﷺ) crying out (yuhnif), [Editor's note: The printed edition and manuscript read "yahtif" with a tāʾ, as if he meant he was shouting and calling on the Messenger of God and appealing to him. But I have preferred the reading with nūn, from the expression "ahnafa al-ṣabiyy ihnāfan," meaning the child prepared to cry and sobbed. It is also said of men, "ahnafa al-rajul," when he wept like children from extreme humility. This, in my judgment, fits the context of the story better.] When his people, the Banū Ẓafar, saw this, they came to the Prophet of God (ﷺ) to clear their companion, and the Prophet of God, peace be upon him, had resolved to excuse him, until God revealed concerning his case what He revealed, saying: ﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾, up to His words: ﴿There you are, those who argued on their behalf in the life of this world; but who will argue with God on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection?﴾, meaning by this his people. ﴿And whoever earns a sin or an offense and then throws it upon an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a clear sin.﴾ Ṭu'ma had cast the theft upon an innocent man. When God made clear the matter of Ṭu'ma, he became a hypocrite and joined the polytheists in Mecca. So God revealed concerning him:
﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers – We will leave him in what he has turned to and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination.﴾

10413 – Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what God has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾. He said: That was because a group of the Helpers went out with the Prophet (ﷺ) on one of his campaigns, and a coat of mail belonging to one of them was stolen. So they suspected a man from the Helpers (ẓanna bihi rajulan min al-Anṣār). [Editor's note: "ẓanantu al-rajul" and "aẓnantuhu" mean I accused him. And "al-ẓunna" (with a kasra) means accusation.] The owner of the coat of mail came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq has stolen my coat of mail." The man was brought to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). When the thief saw that, he went to it and threw it into the house of an innocent man, and said to some men of his tribe: "I have hidden the coat of mail and thrown it into the house of so-and-so, and it will be found with him." So they went to the Prophet of God (ﷺ) by night [Editor's note: "laylan" (by night) is not in the manuscript, but a few lines later there is something that indicates the correctness of including it.] and said: "O Prophet of God, our companion is innocent, and the thief of the coat of mail is so-and-so, and we have full knowledge of that. So excuse our companion before the people and argue on his behalf, for if God does not protect him through you, he will perish!" [Editor's note: The printed edition reads "in lam yaʿṣimhu Allāh" (if God does not protect him), but what is in the manuscript is the ancient, correct reading.] The Messenger of God (ﷺ) stood up, declared him innocent, and excused him before the people. So God revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what God has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾, meaning: judge between them by what God has sent down to you in the Book. ﴿And seek forgiveness of God; indeed God is ever Forgiving and Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾, to the end of the verse. Then He said to those who came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) by night: ﴿They hide from the people, but they cannot hide from God, and He is with them when they plot by night what He does not approve of of speech﴾, up to His words: ﴿Or who will be a guardian over them?﴾, meaning: those who came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in secret, arguing on behalf of the traitor. Then He said: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness of God will find God Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: those who came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in secret with the lie. [Editor's note: In the printed edition, the phrase from "arguing on behalf of the traitor" to "with the lie" was dropped by the publisher; I have restored it from the manuscript.] Then He said: ﴿And whoever earns a sin or an offense and then throws it upon an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a clear sin﴾, meaning: the thief and those who argue on behalf of the thief.

10414 – Yūnus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what God has shown you﴾, to the end of the verse: A man stole an iron coat of mail in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) and threw it upon a Jew. The Jew said: "By God, I did not steal it, O Abu al-Qāsim, but it was thrown upon me!" The man who had stolen it had neighbors who would clear him and cast the blame on the Jew, saying: "O Messenger of God, this wicked Jew disbelieves in God and in what you have brought!" So the Prophet (ﷺ) leaned toward them with some words, and God, the Mighty and Majestic, rebuked him for that, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what God has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous, and seek forgiveness of God﴾, for what you said to this Jew, ﴿indeed God is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ Then He turned to his neighbors and said: ﴿There you are, those who argued on their behalf in the life of this world﴾, and he recited until he reached: ﴿Or who will be a guardian over them?﴾ He said: Then He offered repentance, saying: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness of God will find God Forgiving and Merciful. And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself﴾. "So what has brought you, O people, to argue on behalf of this one, concerning his sin?" ﴿And God is ever Knowing and Wise. And whoever earns a sin or an offense and then throws it upon an innocent person﴾, even if he is a polytheist, ﴿has certainly borne a slander and a clear sin﴾. Then he recited until he reached: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret conversation﴾, [Editor's note: The printed edition omits "then he recited until he reached: There is no good in much of their secret conversation," and adds in the following phrase "until he reached His words." I have restored the manuscript text.] and he recited until he reached: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him﴾. He said: He refused to accept the repentance that God had offered him, and went out to the polytheists in Mecca, and broke into a house to steal it, [Editor's note: The printed edition has "li-yasriqahu" (in order to steal it), but the manuscript reading is the correct, well-established one.] and God caused it to collapse on him and killed him. That is the saying of God, blessed and exalted: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him﴾, and he recited until he reached: ﴿and evil it is as a destination.﴾ [Editor's note: The printed edition has "fa-dhālika qawluhu" (that is His saying), and I have retained the manuscript text.] It is said: he was Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq, and he was residing among the Banū Ẓafar.

* *

Others said: Rather, the treachery by which God described the one mentioned in His words, "and do not be an advocate for the treacherous," was his denying a deposit that had been entrusted to him.

Those who said this:

10415 – Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn related to us, he said: Aḥmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal related to us, he said: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, regarding: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what God has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾. He said: As for "what God has shown you," it is what God revealed to you. He said: It was revealed concerning Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq. A man from the Jews had entrusted him with a coat of mail, so he took it to his house. The Jew dug a hole for it and buried it. Then Ṭu'ma went secretly to it, dug it up, and took it. When the Jew came seeking his coat of mail, he denied it to him [Editor's note: "kāfarahu ḥaqqahu" means he denied his right, and "kāfarahu ʿanhu" is clear Arabic.] So the Jew went to some Jews from his tribe and said: "Come with me, for I know where the coat of mail is." When Ṭu'ma learned of them, he took the coat of mail and threw it into the house of Abū Mulayl al-Anṣārī. When the Jews came seeking the coat of mail and could not find it, Ṭu'ma and some men of his people attacked them and reviled them, saying: "Do you accuse me of betrayal?" So they went searching for it in his house, and they looked over the house of Abū Mulayl, and there they found the coat of mail. Then Ṭu'ma said: "Abū Mulayl took it!" The Helpers argued on behalf of Ṭu'ma, and he said to them: "Go with me to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and tell him to defend me and refute the Jew's argument, for if I am accused, the Jew will lie against the people of Medina!" Some Helpers came to him and said: "O Messenger of God, argue on behalf of Ṭu'ma and refute the Jew." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was about to do so, when God revealed to him: ﴿And do not be an advocate for the treacherous, and seek forgiveness of God﴾, for what you intended, ﴿indeed God is ever Forgiving and Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves; indeed God does not love one who is a habitual traitor and sinner.﴾ Then He mentioned the Helpers and their arguing on his behalf, and said: ﴿They hide from the people, but they cannot hide from God, and He is with them when they plot by night what He does not approve of of speech﴾, meaning: they say what He does not approve of in speech. ﴿There you are, those who argued on their behalf in the life of this world; but who will argue with God on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ Then He called to repentance, saying: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness of God will find God Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ Then He mentioned his saying when he said: "Abū Mulayl took it," and said: ﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself﴾. ﴿And whoever earns a sin or an offense and then throws it upon an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a clear sin.﴾ Then He mentioned the Helpers and their coming to him, to defend their companion and argue on his behalf, and said: ﴿A faction of them had intended to mislead you, but they do not mislead except themselves, and they cannot harm you in the least. And God has sent down to you the Book and wisdom﴾, meaning: prophethood. Then He mentioned their secret talk about what they wanted to do to exonerate Ṭu'ma, and said: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret conversation, except for one who orders charity or what is right or reconciliation between people.﴾ When God exposed Ṭu'ma in Medina through the Qur'an, he fled until he came to Mecca, and disbelieved after his Islam, and stayed with al-Ḥajjāj ibn ʿIlāṭ al-Sulamī. He broke into al-Ḥajjāj's house intending to steal it, but al-Ḥajjāj heard a rustling in his house and a clattering of hides that were there. [Editor's note: "al-khashkhasha" is the sound of movement, which comes from weapons when they rub together, or from a new garment, or from dry plants. "Al-qaʿqaʿa" is stronger than al-khashkhasha, the sound that comes from dry hide and from weapons when they strike one another.] He looked, and there was Ṭu'ma. He said: "My guest and my cousin, and you wanted to steal from me!" So he expelled him, and he died in the lava field of the Banū Sulaym, a disbeliever. [Editor's note: "Ḥarrat Banī Sulaym" is in the upper Najd. "Al-ḥarra" is land with black, crumbling stones, as if burned by fire.] And God revealed concerning him: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers – We will leave him in what he has turned to﴾, up to ﴿and evil it is as a destination.﴾

10416 – al-Qāsim related to us, he said: al-Ḥusayn related to us, he said: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿIkrima, who said: A man from the Helpers had entrusted to Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq a room of his in which was a coat of mail. [Editor's note: "al-mashruba" is the upper room, as I have noted in the commentary.] He went out and was absent. When the Helper returned, he opened his room and did not find the coat of mail, so he asked Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq about it. Ṭu'ma threw it upon a Jewish man called Zayd ibn al-Samīn. The owner of the coat of mail then accused Ṭu'ma about his coat of mail. When his people saw that, they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and spoke to him so that he would ward off the accusation from him. He was about to do so, when God, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what God has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous. * And seek forgiveness of God; indeed God is ever Forgiving and Merciful. * And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾, meaning: Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq and his people. ﴿There you are, those who argued on their behalf in the life of this world; but who will argue with God on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be a guardian over them?﴾, Muḥammad (ﷺ) and the people of Ṭu'ma. ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness of God will find God Forgiving and Merciful﴾, Muḥammad and Ṭu'ma and his people. He said: ﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself﴾, the verse; Ṭu'ma. ﴿And whoever earns a sin or an offense and then throws it upon an innocent person﴾, meaning Zayd ibn al-Samīn. ﴿Has certainly borne a slander and a clear sin﴾, Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq. ﴿And were it not for the bounty of God upon you and His mercy﴾, O Muḥammad, ﴿a faction of them had intended to mislead you, but they do not mislead except themselves, and they cannot harm you in the least﴾, the people of Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq. ﴿And God has sent down to you the Book and wisdom and taught you what you did not know; and ever has the bounty of God been great upon you﴾, O Muḥammad. ﴿There is no good in much of their secret conversation, except for one who orders charity or what is right﴾, until the verse concludes with reference to people in general: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers﴾, the verse. He said: When the Qur'an was revealed concerning Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq, he joined the Quraysh and reverted from his religion. Then he attacked a room belonging to al-Ḥajjāj ibn ʿIlāṭ al-Bahzī, then al-Sulamī. [Editor's note: In the printed edition and manuscript it reads "al-Bahrī," which is a scribal error. I do not accept this; rather, the correct form is to say "al-Sulamī, then al-Bahzī," with the order reversed, for Bahz is the son of Imru' al-Qays ibn Bahtha ibn Sulaym ibn Manṣūr, and Bahz is a clan of Sulaym ibn Manṣūr.] who was an ally of the Banū ʿAbd al-Dār. He broke into it, and a stone fell upon him and he was trapped. [Editor's note: "Laḥija bi-l-makān" means he became stuck in it and was bound to it, and it became too narrow for him to leave. "Laḥij al-sayf" means the sword became stuck in its sheath and would not come out.] When morning came, they expelled him from Mecca. He went out and encountered a caravan from Bahrāʾ of Quḍāʿa. He presented himself to them and said: "A traveler cut off from his way!" So they carried him, until when night fell he attacked them and robbed them, then departed. They went in pursuit of him and caught up with him, and pelted him with stones until he died. Ibn Jurayj said: All these verses were revealed concerning him, up to His words: ﴿Indeed, God does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾, and these were revealed concerning Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq. And they say: He threw the coat of mail into the house of Abū Mulayl ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Khazrajī. When the Qur'an was revealed, he joined the Quraysh, and what happened to him happened.

10417 – I was told on the authority of al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulaymān related to us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say, regarding His words: ﴿that you may judge between the people by what God has shown you﴾, he says: by what He has sent down to you and shown you in His Book. This verse was revealed concerning a man from the Helpers who was entrusted with a coat of mail, and its owner denied it, and men among the companions of the Prophet of God (ﷺ) accused him of treachery. His people became angry on his behalf and came to the Prophet of God (ﷺ) and said: "They have accused our companion of betrayal, and he is a trustworthy Muslim. So excuse him, O Prophet of God, and restrain them from him!" The Prophet of God rose and excused him, and refuted the charge on his behalf, while he believed that he was innocent and that it was falsely attributed to him. So God revealed the clarification of that, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what God has shown you﴾, up to His words: ﴿Or who will be a guardian over them?﴾ Then God made his treachery clear, so he joined the polytheists of Mecca and apostatized from Islam. So there was revealed concerning him: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him﴾, up to His words: ﴿and evil it is as a destination.﴾

* *

Abū Jaʿfar (al-Ṭabarī) said: The most preferable of the two interpretations in this matter, in accordance with what the apparent meaning of the verse indicates, is the view of those who said: His treachery by which God described him in this verse was his denial of what had been entrusted to him, because this is the well-known meaning of "khiyānāt" (treacheries) in the speech of the Arabs. And directing the interpretation (ta'wīl) of the Qur'an toward the most famous meanings of Arabic speech, where that path can be found, is preferable to other approaches.

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 4, verses 105–106 (part 1 of 2):**

The exegesis of His words: ﴿And ask forgiveness of Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (106).

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His remembrance be exalted, ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, "Indeed, We have sent down to you," O Muhammad, "the Book," meaning the Qur'an, "so that you may judge between the people," so that you may decide between the people and separate them, "by what Allah has shown you," meaning by what Allah has revealed to you of His Book. "And do not be a disputer for the treacherous," he says: do not be a defender for one who betrays a Muslim or a covenant-partner in his person or his property, "a disputer," who argues on his behalf and repels from him the one who demands from him his right which he betrayed. "And ask forgiveness of Allah," O Muhammad, and ask Him to pardon you for the punishment of your sin in disputing on behalf of the traitor who betrayed another's property. "Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful," he says: Indeed Allah has never ceased to pardon the sins of His believing servants, by abandoning their punishment for them when they ask Him for forgiveness from them, "Merciful" towards them. [[See the explanation of "seeking forgiveness" (al-istighfar), and "kana" (was), "ghafur" (Forgiving) and "rahim" (Merciful) in what has preceded in the lexical indices.]]

So do that, O Muhammad, and Allah will forgive you what preceded of your disputing on behalf of this traitor.

* *

It has been said that the Prophet (ﷺ) had not disputed on behalf of the traitor, but he had intended to do so, so Allah commanded him to seek forgiveness for what he had intended of that.

* *

It is mentioned that the traitors whom Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, reproached His Prophet (ﷺ) for disputing on behalf of were the Banu Ubayriq.

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning the betrayal that was committed by them, for which Allah described him.

Some of them said: It was a theft that he committed.

Those who said this:

10409. Muhammad ibn 'Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of Allah: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, up to His words: ﴿And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah﴾, in between that, concerning Ibn Ubayriq, [[In the printed edition: "Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq," and the mention of "Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq" will come in no. 10412, but here in the manuscript it is "Ibn Ubayriq," and you will see the variation in the reports about these Banu Ubayriq.]] and his coat of mail, of iron, from the Jews, which he stole. And his companions from among the believers said to the Prophet: "Excuse him among the people with your tongue," and they accused a innocent man of the Jews of the coat of mail. [[The phrase "from the Jews" I have affirmed from the manuscript.]]

10410. Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, similarly. [[Report 10410: this report is not established in the manuscript.]]

10411. Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Shu'ayb, Abu Muslim al-Harrani, narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah, from his father, from his grandfather Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man, who said: There was a household among us called the Banu Ubayriq: Bishr, Bashir, and Mubashshir. Bashir was a hypocrite, and he would compose poetry satirizing the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), then attribute it to some of the Arabs, saying: "So-and-so said this," and "So-and-so said that." When the companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard that poetry, they said: "By Allah, none composes this poetry except the wicked one!" So he said:

*Do the men compose a poem and then they harbor resentment and say: "It is the son of Ubayriq who composed it!"*

[[In the printed edition: "Except this wicked one," and I have affirmed what is in the manuscript. In the manuscript: "They attributed it and said," and I left what is in the printed edition as it is. This verse has come in al-Mustadrak of al-Hakim erroneously: "... they gathered against the son of Ubayriq, he composed it." What is here is its correct form, and after it there he recited: "Arrogant, as if I feared them, may God cut off their noses and sever them." Thus it came with the iqwa' (the variation of the rhyme), due to the difference between the rhyme in "qalaha" and "abanaha," a defect that occurs similarly in poetry, due to the closeness of the articulation points of the lam and the nun, and the presence of the ha' and alif as an extension of the rhyme helped with that. And his saying "adammu" means they became angry at him and held rancor. And his saying "mutakhammitin" means they became enraged, roared, rose up and shouted. A man who is mutakhammit is one with intense anger, having a surge and clamor. In al-Mustadrak it is "mutakhatmin" with the ta' preceding the mim, which is an error; its correct form is what I have affirmed.]]

He said: They were a household of poverty and need in the pre-Islamic period and in Islam. The people of Medina ate only dates and barley. When a man had means, a caravan (dafitah) would come from Syria with fine flour (darmak), and the man would buy some of it and reserve it for himself. [[The "dafitah": they were a people of the Nabateans who carried flour, oil and other goods to Medina. Then they called the one who brings provisions and goods to cities, and the muleteer who hires out loads, "dafitah" and "daffat." And "darmak" is pure, fine, white flour.]] As for their dependents, their food was only dates and barley. Then a caravan came from Syria, and my uncle Rifa'ah ibn Zayd bought a load of darmak, and placed it in a storeroom (mashraba) of his. [[The "mashraba" (with the mim fathah, the shin sakin and the ra' fathah or damma): it is the upper room, or the loft, or the veranda before the upper room. And "al-masharib" are the upper rooms.]] In the storeroom there was his weaponry: two coats of mail, two swords and what suits them. Then he was attacked during the night, [[In other sources: "from under the house," and it seems that what is in al-Tabari is the correct version of the report.]] the storeroom was broken into, and the food and the weapons were taken. When he awoke in the morning, my uncle Rifa'ah came to me and said: "O son of my brother, you know that we were attacked during this night, our storeroom was broken into, and our weapons and food were taken!" He said: We searched in the dwelling [[In the printed and manuscript editions: "fa-tajassasna" with the jim, which is correct, and better than with the ha', as in all other sources. "Tahassasa al-khabar": to seek and investigate the news. And in the revelation: "O my sons, go and seek out (tahassasu) news of Joseph and his brother." And "al-dar" here: the quarter that a tribe or a clan of it settles in, and by it is meant the tribe or clan, as in the hadith: "Shall I inform you of the best dwellings of the Ansar? The dwellings of the Banu al-Najjar, then the dwellings of the Banu 'Abd al-Ashhal, and in every dwelling of the Ansar there is good." Meaning the tribe gathered in a quarter it inhabits.]] and we asked, and it was said to us: "We saw the Banu Ubayriq kindle a fire this night, and we do not see, in what we see, except that it is on some of your food."

= He said: The Banu Ubayriq had said, while we were asking in the dwelling: "By Allah, we do not see your companion except Labid ibn Sahl!" — a man from among us who had righteousness and Islam. [[In the printed edition: "rajul" with the nominative, as if he disapproved of the accusative! And it is pure and excellent correctness.]] When Labid heard of this, he unsheathed his sword, then came to the Banu Ubayriq and said: "By Allah, this sword will mingle with you, or you will clarify this theft!" They said: "Away from us, O man! By Allah, you are not its perpetrator!" We asked in the dwelling until we did not doubt that they were its perpetrators. My uncle said: "O son of my brother, if only you would go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and mention that to him!"

= Qatadah said: So I went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), mentioned that to him, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, a household among us of harshness, [[Al-jafa': coarseness of temperament.]] went to my uncle Rifa'ah, broke into his storeroom, and took his weapons and his food. Let them return our weapons to us; as for the food, we have no need of it." [[In the manuscript: "fa-la hajata lana bihi," and both are the same.]] The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I will consider that." [[In the printed edition: "I will consider that," and in al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Kathir: "I will consult about that," and I have affirmed what is in the manuscript.]] When the Banu Ubayriq heard of that, they went to a man among them called Usayr ibn 'Urwah, and spoke to him about it. A number of people from the dwelling gathered to him, and they came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man and his uncle went to a household among us, a household of Islam and righteousness, accusing them of theft without evidence or proof." [[Al-thabt (with two fathahs): proof, evidence and argument.]]

= Qatadah said: So I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and spoke to him, and he said: "You went to a household described as having Islam and righteousness, accusing them of theft without evidence or proof!!" He said: So I returned, and I wished that I had come out of some of my wealth and had not spoken to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about that. Then I came to my uncle Rifa'ah, and he said: "O son of my brother, what have you done?" So I informed him of what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had said to me, and he said: "Allah is the One sought for help!"

= Then we had not waited long before the Qur'an was revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you. And do not be a disputer for the treacherous﴾, meaning: the Banu Ubayriq, ﴿and ask forgiveness of Allah﴾, that is: for what you said to Qatadah, ﴿Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾, that is: the Banu Ubayriq, ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is a habitual traitor and sinner. They hide from the people﴾ up to His words: ﴿Then he asks forgiveness of Allah; he will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾, that is: if they ask forgiveness of Allah, He will forgive them, ﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself. And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise. And whoever earns an error or a sin and then throws it onto an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a clear sin﴾, meaning their saying about Labid, ﴿And if not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy, a faction of them would have resolved to mislead you﴾, meaning: Usayr and his companions, ﴿but they mislead none except themselves, and they cannot harm you at all. And Allah has revealed to you the Book and wisdom﴾ up to His words: ﴿We will give him a great reward﴾.

Then when the Qur'an was revealed, the weapons were brought to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he returned them to Rifa'ah. = Qatadah said: When I brought the weapons to my uncle, and he was an elder who had grown old in the pre-Islamic period, [[ "'asa fi al-jahiliyyah": he grew old and aged, from the saying "'asa al-'ud," meaning it dried, hardened and became stiff.]] and I had seen his Islam as being corrupted, [[ "Al-madkhul," from "al-dakhl" (with two fathahs), which is a defect, corruption or deceit, meaning that his faith had hypocrisy in it. And "rajul madkhul": that is, there is a flaw and corruption in his intellect.]] when I brought him the weapons, he said: "O son of my brother, it is in the way of Allah." He said: So I knew that his Islam was sound.

When the Qur'an was revealed, Bishr joined the polytheists, and he stayed with Sullafah, daughter of Sa'd ibn Shuhayd. [[In the printed edition: "Sullafah daughter of Sa'd ibn Sahl," and in the manuscript: "... daughter of Sa'd ibn Suhayl," and in al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Kathir: "daughter of Sa'd ibn Sumayyah," and in al-Mustadrak: "Salamah daughter of Sa'd ibn Sahl, sister of the Banu 'Amr ibn 'Awf, and she was married to Talhah ibn Abi Talhah in Mecca." The correct form beyond doubt is what I have affirmed, and it has come correctly in al-Durr al-Manthur, and then similarly in the Diwan of Hassan ibn Thabit. "Sullafah bint Sa'd ibn Shuhayd" was an Ansari woman from the Banu 'Awf ibn 'Amr ibn Malik ibn al-Aws, whose lineage I have verified: "Sullafah daughter of Sa'd ibn Shuhayd ibn 'Amr ibn Zayd ibn Umayyah ibn Zayd ibn Malik ibn 'Awf ibn 'Amr ibn 'Awf ibn Malik ibn al-Aws." This is from Jamharat al-Ansab of Ibn Hazm, p. 314, where he mentioned "'Uwaymir ibn Sa'd ibn Shuhayd ibn 'Amr ... " and said: "He had companionship (suhbah); 'Umar appointed him over Palestine." I did not find in the biographies of the Companions and other sources "'Uwaymir ibn Sa'd ibn Shuhayd." However, Ibn Hazm's transmission is undoubtedly correct. If that is so, then this 'Uwaymir is the brother of this Sullafah. And "Sullafah bint Sa'd ibn Shuhayd al-Ansariyyah" is well known and unquestioned; she was the wife of Talhah ibn Abi Talhah, and she was the mother of Musafi', al-Jullas and Kilab, the sons of Talhah ibn Abi Talhah (Ibn Hisham 3:66). They and their father were killed at the Battle of Uhud. Musafi' and al-Jullas were killed by 'Asim ibn Thabit ibn Abi al-Aqlah, the protector of the hornets. So Sullafah vowed: "If I am able to get the head of 'Asim, I will drink wine from his skull!" But the hornets (the bees) protected him when the Hudhayl wanted to take his head to sell it to Sullafah (Ibn Hisham 3:180). This is the verification of her name, if Allah wills, by which what is in al-Tirmidhi, al-Mustadrak and those who transmitted from them is corrected.]] So Allah revealed concerning him: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers﴾ up to His words: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly strayed far astray﴾. When it was revealed concerning Sullafah, Hassan ibn Thabit hurled at her verses of poetry, [[The poetry of Hassan in his Diwan, p. 271, in which at its beginning he mentions Sullafah with evil speech. He said:

*"And the thief of the two coats of mail, if you mention him, is not among the noble men whom I would shelter.*
*The daughter of Sa'd has indeed sheltered him, so she became one who contends with his skin, and he contends with her."*]]

So she took his saddlebag, placed it on her head, went out, and threw it into al-Abtah, [[In the printed edition: "she threw it at al-Abtah," and I have affirmed what is in the manuscript, which agrees with what is in al-Tirmidhi. "Al-Abtah" is the Abtah of Mecca, or the Batha' of Mecca, and it is the channel of its valley.]] then she said: "You have sent me the poetry of Hassan! You never brought me anything good!"

[[Report 10411: "Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Shu'ayb 'Abd Allah ibn Muslim al-Umawi," Abu Muslim al-Harrani. From the people of Harran, he settled in Baghdad. Al-Khatib said: "Reliable, trustworthy." Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat and said: "He is strange." He narrated from Muhammad ibn Salamah. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/2, and Tarikh Baghdad 7:266.

This report was narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Sunan, in the explanation of this verse, with the same chain as al-Tabari, namely from al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Shu'ayb. It was narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak 4:385, Ibn Kathir cited it in his Tafsir 2:574–576, and al-Suyuti in al-Durr 2:214, 215, and he added its attribution to Ibn Abi Hatim and Abu al-Shaykh.

The chain of al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: "Abu al-'Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar narrated to us, Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me ..." and he gave its chain raised (marfu') to Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man, as in the tafsir and al-Tirmidhi.

Al-Khatib al-Baghdadi pointed to this report with his chain: "'Uthman ibn Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Allaf informed us, Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Shafi'i informed us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Shu'ayb (and he is Abu Shu'ayb) narrated to us, my grandfather and my father together narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Salamah narrated to us," and he cited it as the chain of Abu Ja'far.

The Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned in al-Tahdhib that Abu Muslim al-Harrani (al-Hasan ibn Ahmad) narrated from his father and grandfather, and I fear that this is an error, and the error came from this chain because of his saying "my grandfather and my father together narrated to me," whereas the one who says that is 'Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad, not al-Hasan ibn Ahmad.

Then al-Khatib al-Baghdadi said: "Abu Shu'ayb said: 'My father (meaning al-Hasan ibn Ahmad) said: Yahya ibn Ma'in heard it from me in Baghdad in the Friday mosque, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal, 'Ali ibn al-Madini, and Ishaq ibn Abi Isra'il.'" As for Ibn Kathir, the speaker of this is "Muhammad ibn Salamah," and this is the correct form.

Al-Hakim said in al-Mustadrak (and his wording differs from the wording of al-Tabari): "This is a hadith sound according to the condition of Muslim, though they (al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it."

As for al-Tirmidhi, he said: "This is a strange hadith; we do not know anyone who transmitted it with a chain other than Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Harrani. Yunus ibn Bukayr and more than one narrated this hadith from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from 'Asim ibn 'Umar ibn Qatadah, as a mursal report, not mentioning in it 'from his father, from his grandfather.'"

However, al-Hakim narrated it, as you see, through the route of Yunus ibn Bukayr, raised to Qatadah ibn al-Nu'man.]]

10412. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth so that you may judge between the people by what Allah has shown you﴾, he says: by what Allah has revealed to you and made clear to you. ﴿And do not be a disputer for the treacherous﴾, then he recited up to His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love one who is a habitual traitor and sinner.﴾ It was mentioned to us that these verses were revealed concerning Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq, and concerning what the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) intended in excusing him. Allah made clear the matter of Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq and admonished His Prophet and warned him not to be a disputer for the treacherous.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verses 105–106 (part 2 of 2):

Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq was a man from the Helpers (al-Anṣār), from the clan of Ẓafar. He stole a coat of mail belonging to his paternal uncle, which had been deposited with him as a trust. Then he planted it with a Jew who used to frequent them, called Zayd ibn al-Samīn. [Editor's note: In the manuscript and al-Durr al-Manthur it reads "faqaddamahā" (he presented it), but the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.] [Editor's note: In al-Wāḥidī's Asbāb al-Nuzūl, p. 134, it reads "Zayd ibn al-Samīr" with a rāʾ, while the other sources, as here in the printed edition and manuscript, read "al-Samīn".] The Jew then came to the Prophet of God (ﷺ) crying out (yuhnif), [Editor's note: The printed edition and manuscript read "yahtif" with a tāʾ, as if he meant he was shouting and calling on the Messenger of God and appealing to him. But I have preferred the reading with nūn, from the expression "ahnafa al-ṣabiyy ihnāfan," meaning the child prepared to cry and sobbed. It is also said of men, "ahnafa al-rajul," when he wept like children from extreme humility. This, in my judgment, fits the context of the story better.] When his people, the Banū Ẓafar, saw this, they came to the Prophet of God (ﷺ) to clear their companion, and the Prophet of God, peace be upon him, had resolved to excuse him, until God revealed concerning his case what He revealed, saying: ﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾, up to His words: ﴿There you are, those who argued on their behalf in the life of this world; but who will argue with God on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection?﴾, meaning by this his people. ﴿And whoever earns a sin or an offense and then throws it upon an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a clear sin.﴾ Ṭu'ma had cast the theft upon an innocent man. When God made clear the matter of Ṭu'ma, he became a hypocrite and joined the polytheists in Mecca. So God revealed concerning him:
﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers – We will leave him in what he has turned to and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination.﴾

10413 – Muḥammad ibn Saʿd related to me, he said: my father related to me, he said: my paternal uncle related to me, he said: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what God has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾. He said: That was because a group of the Helpers went out with the Prophet (ﷺ) on one of his campaigns, and a coat of mail belonging to one of them was stolen. So they suspected a man from the Helpers (ẓanna bihi rajulan min al-Anṣār). [Editor's note: "ẓanantu al-rajul" and "aẓnantuhu" mean I accused him. And "al-ẓunna" (with a kasra) means accusation.] The owner of the coat of mail came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and said: "Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq has stolen my coat of mail." The man was brought to the Messenger of God (ﷺ). When the thief saw that, he went to it and threw it into the house of an innocent man, and said to some men of his tribe: "I have hidden the coat of mail and thrown it into the house of so-and-so, and it will be found with him." So they went to the Prophet of God (ﷺ) by night [Editor's note: "laylan" (by night) is not in the manuscript, but a few lines later there is something that indicates the correctness of including it.] and said: "O Prophet of God, our companion is innocent, and the thief of the coat of mail is so-and-so, and we have full knowledge of that. So excuse our companion before the people and argue on his behalf, for if God does not protect him through you, he will perish!" [Editor's note: The printed edition reads "in lam yaʿṣimhu Allāh" (if God does not protect him), but what is in the manuscript is the ancient, correct reading.] The Messenger of God (ﷺ) stood up, declared him innocent, and excused him before the people. So God revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what God has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾, meaning: judge between them by what God has sent down to you in the Book. ﴿And seek forgiveness of God; indeed God is ever Forgiving and Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾, to the end of the verse. Then He said to those who came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) by night: ﴿They hide from the people, but they cannot hide from God, and He is with them when they plot by night what He does not approve of of speech﴾, up to His words: ﴿Or who will be a guardian over them?﴾, meaning: those who came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in secret, arguing on behalf of the traitor. Then He said: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness of God will find God Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: those who came to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) in secret with the lie. [Editor's note: In the printed edition, the phrase from "arguing on behalf of the traitor" to "with the lie" was dropped by the publisher; I have restored it from the manuscript.] Then He said: ﴿And whoever earns a sin or an offense and then throws it upon an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a clear sin﴾, meaning: the thief and those who argue on behalf of the thief.

10414 – Yūnus related to me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what God has shown you﴾, to the end of the verse: A man stole an iron coat of mail in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ) and threw it upon a Jew. The Jew said: "By God, I did not steal it, O Abu al-Qāsim, but it was thrown upon me!" The man who had stolen it had neighbors who would clear him and cast the blame on the Jew, saying: "O Messenger of God, this wicked Jew disbelieves in God and in what you have brought!" So the Prophet (ﷺ) leaned toward them with some words, and God, the Mighty and Majestic, rebuked him for that, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what God has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous, and seek forgiveness of God﴾, for what you said to this Jew, ﴿indeed God is ever Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ Then He turned to his neighbors and said: ﴿There you are, those who argued on their behalf in the life of this world﴾, and he recited until he reached: ﴿Or who will be a guardian over them?﴾ He said: Then He offered repentance, saying: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness of God will find God Forgiving and Merciful. And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself﴾. "So what has brought you, O people, to argue on behalf of this one, concerning his sin?" ﴿And God is ever Knowing and Wise. And whoever earns a sin or an offense and then throws it upon an innocent person﴾, even if he is a polytheist, ﴿has certainly borne a slander and a clear sin﴾. Then he recited until he reached: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret conversation﴾, [Editor's note: The printed edition omits "then he recited until he reached: There is no good in much of their secret conversation," and adds in the following phrase "until he reached His words." I have restored the manuscript text.] and he recited until he reached: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him﴾. He said: He refused to accept the repentance that God had offered him, and went out to the polytheists in Mecca, and broke into a house to steal it, [Editor's note: The printed edition has "li-yasriqahu" (in order to steal it), but the manuscript reading is the correct, well-established one.] and God caused it to collapse on him and killed him. That is the saying of God, blessed and exalted: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him﴾, and he recited until he reached: ﴿and evil it is as a destination.﴾ [Editor's note: The printed edition has "fa-dhālika qawluhu" (that is His saying), and I have retained the manuscript text.] It is said: he was Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq, and he was residing among the Banū Ẓafar.

* *

Others said: Rather, the treachery by which God described the one mentioned in His words, "and do not be an advocate for the treacherous," was his denying a deposit that had been entrusted to him.

Those who said this:

10415 – Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn related to us, he said: Aḥmad ibn al-Mufaḍḍal related to us, he said: Asbāṭ related to us, from al-Suddī, regarding: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what God has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾. He said: As for "what God has shown you," it is what God revealed to you. He said: It was revealed concerning Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq. A man from the Jews had entrusted him with a coat of mail, so he took it to his house. The Jew dug a hole for it and buried it. Then Ṭu'ma went secretly to it, dug it up, and took it. When the Jew came seeking his coat of mail, he denied it to him [Editor's note: "kāfarahu ḥaqqahu" means he denied his right, and "kāfarahu ʿanhu" is clear Arabic.] So the Jew went to some Jews from his tribe and said: "Come with me, for I know where the coat of mail is." When Ṭu'ma learned of them, he took the coat of mail and threw it into the house of Abū Mulayl al-Anṣārī. When the Jews came seeking the coat of mail and could not find it, Ṭu'ma and some men of his people attacked them and reviled them, saying: "Do you accuse me of betrayal?" So they went searching for it in his house, and they looked over the house of Abū Mulayl, and there they found the coat of mail. Then Ṭu'ma said: "Abū Mulayl took it!" The Helpers argued on behalf of Ṭu'ma, and he said to them: "Go with me to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and tell him to defend me and refute the Jew's argument, for if I am accused, the Jew will lie against the people of Medina!" Some Helpers came to him and said: "O Messenger of God, argue on behalf of Ṭu'ma and refute the Jew." The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was about to do so, when God revealed to him: ﴿And do not be an advocate for the treacherous, and seek forgiveness of God﴾, for what you intended, ﴿indeed God is ever Forgiving and Merciful. And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves; indeed God does not love one who is a habitual traitor and sinner.﴾ Then He mentioned the Helpers and their arguing on his behalf, and said: ﴿They hide from the people, but they cannot hide from God, and He is with them when they plot by night what He does not approve of of speech﴾, meaning: they say what He does not approve of in speech. ﴿There you are, those who argued on their behalf in the life of this world; but who will argue with God on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ Then He called to repentance, saying: ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness of God will find God Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ Then He mentioned his saying when he said: "Abū Mulayl took it," and said: ﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself﴾. ﴿And whoever earns a sin or an offense and then throws it upon an innocent person has certainly borne a slander and a clear sin.﴾ Then He mentioned the Helpers and their coming to him, to defend their companion and argue on his behalf, and said: ﴿A faction of them had intended to mislead you, but they do not mislead except themselves, and they cannot harm you in the least. And God has sent down to you the Book and wisdom﴾, meaning: prophethood. Then He mentioned their secret talk about what they wanted to do to exonerate Ṭu'ma, and said: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret conversation, except for one who orders charity or what is right or reconciliation between people.﴾ When God exposed Ṭu'ma in Medina through the Qur'an, he fled until he came to Mecca, and disbelieved after his Islam, and stayed with al-Ḥajjāj ibn ʿIlāṭ al-Sulamī. He broke into al-Ḥajjāj's house intending to steal it, but al-Ḥajjāj heard a rustling in his house and a clattering of hides that were there. [Editor's note: "al-khashkhasha" is the sound of movement, which comes from weapons when they rub together, or from a new garment, or from dry plants. "Al-qaʿqaʿa" is stronger than al-khashkhasha, the sound that comes from dry hide and from weapons when they strike one another.] He looked, and there was Ṭu'ma. He said: "My guest and my cousin, and you wanted to steal from me!" So he expelled him, and he died in the lava field of the Banū Sulaym, a disbeliever. [Editor's note: "Ḥarrat Banī Sulaym" is in the upper Najd. "Al-ḥarra" is land with black, crumbling stones, as if burned by fire.] And God revealed concerning him: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers – We will leave him in what he has turned to﴾, up to ﴿and evil it is as a destination.﴾

10416 – al-Qāsim related to us, he said: al-Ḥusayn related to us, he said: Ḥajjāj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from ʿIkrima, who said: A man from the Helpers had entrusted to Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq a room of his in which was a coat of mail. [Editor's note: "al-mashruba" is the upper room, as I have noted in the commentary.] He went out and was absent. When the Helper returned, he opened his room and did not find the coat of mail, so he asked Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq about it. Ṭu'ma threw it upon a Jewish man called Zayd ibn al-Samīn. The owner of the coat of mail then accused Ṭu'ma about his coat of mail. When his people saw that, they came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and spoke to him so that he would ward off the accusation from him. He was about to do so, when God, blessed and exalted, revealed: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what God has shown you, and do not be an advocate for the treacherous. * And seek forgiveness of God; indeed God is ever Forgiving and Merciful. * And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves﴾, meaning: Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq and his people. ﴿There you are, those who argued on their behalf in the life of this world; but who will argue with God on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be a guardian over them?﴾, Muḥammad (ﷺ) and the people of Ṭu'ma. ﴿And whoever does evil or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness of God will find God Forgiving and Merciful﴾, Muḥammad and Ṭu'ma and his people. He said: ﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself﴾, the verse; Ṭu'ma. ﴿And whoever earns a sin or an offense and then throws it upon an innocent person﴾, meaning Zayd ibn al-Samīn. ﴿Has certainly borne a slander and a clear sin﴾, Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq. ﴿And were it not for the bounty of God upon you and His mercy﴾, O Muḥammad, ﴿a faction of them had intended to mislead you, but they do not mislead except themselves, and they cannot harm you in the least﴾, the people of Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq. ﴿And God has sent down to you the Book and wisdom and taught you what you did not know; and ever has the bounty of God been great upon you﴾, O Muḥammad. ﴿There is no good in much of their secret conversation, except for one who orders charity or what is right﴾, until the verse concludes with reference to people in general: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers﴾, the verse. He said: When the Qur'an was revealed concerning Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq, he joined the Quraysh and reverted from his religion. Then he attacked a room belonging to al-Ḥajjāj ibn ʿIlāṭ al-Bahzī, then al-Sulamī. [Editor's note: In the printed edition and manuscript it reads "al-Bahrī," which is a scribal error. I do not accept this; rather, the correct form is to say "al-Sulamī, then al-Bahzī," with the order reversed, for Bahz is the son of Imru' al-Qays ibn Bahtha ibn Sulaym ibn Manṣūr, and Bahz is a clan of Sulaym ibn Manṣūr.] who was an ally of the Banū ʿAbd al-Dār. He broke into it, and a stone fell upon him and he was trapped. [Editor's note: "Laḥija bi-l-makān" means he became stuck in it and was bound to it, and it became too narrow for him to leave. "Laḥij al-sayf" means the sword became stuck in its sheath and would not come out.] When morning came, they expelled him from Mecca. He went out and encountered a caravan from Bahrāʾ of Quḍāʿa. He presented himself to them and said: "A traveler cut off from his way!" So they carried him, until when night fell he attacked them and robbed them, then departed. They went in pursuit of him and caught up with him, and pelted him with stones until he died. Ibn Jurayj said: All these verses were revealed concerning him, up to His words: ﴿Indeed, God does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾, and these were revealed concerning Ṭu'ma ibn Ubayriq. And they say: He threw the coat of mail into the house of Abū Mulayl ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Khazrajī. When the Qur'an was revealed, he joined the Quraysh, and what happened to him happened.

10417 – I was told on the authority of al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say: ʿUbayd ibn Sulaymān related to us, he said: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say, regarding His words: ﴿that you may judge between the people by what God has shown you﴾, he says: by what He has sent down to you and shown you in His Book. This verse was revealed concerning a man from the Helpers who was entrusted with a coat of mail, and its owner denied it, and men among the companions of the Prophet of God (ﷺ) accused him of treachery. His people became angry on his behalf and came to the Prophet of God (ﷺ) and said: "They have accused our companion of betrayal, and he is a trustworthy Muslim. So excuse him, O Prophet of God, and restrain them from him!" The Prophet of God rose and excused him, and refuted the charge on his behalf, while he believed that he was innocent and that it was falsely attributed to him. So God revealed the clarification of that, saying: ﴿Indeed, We have sent down to you the Book in truth, that you may judge between the people by what God has shown you﴾, up to His words: ﴿Or who will be a guardian over them?﴾ Then God made his treachery clear, so he joined the polytheists of Mecca and apostatized from Islam. So there was revealed concerning him: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him﴾, up to His words: ﴿and evil it is as a destination.﴾

* *

Abū Jaʿfar (al-Ṭabarī) said: The most preferable of the two interpretations in this matter, in accordance with what the apparent meaning of the verse indicates, is the view of those who said: His treachery by which God described him in this verse was his denial of what had been entrusted to him, because this is the well-known meaning of "khiyānāt" (treacheries) in the speech of the Arabs. And directing the interpretation (ta'wīl) of the Qur'an toward the most famous meanings of Arabic speech, where that path can be found, is preferable to other approaches.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 107:

The explanation of His words: ﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not love one who is a habitual betrayer, sinful.﴾ (4:107)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "And do not argue," O Muhammad, "on behalf of those who betray themselves," meaning: those who act treacherously toward themselves, making themselves traitors through their betrayal of what they took from those they betrayed, namely the wealth of others that they wronged. They are the Banu Ubayriq. He says: Do not dispute on their behalf with one who demands their rights and what they wronged him of in their wealth. "Indeed, Allah does not love one who is a habitual betrayer, sinful," meaning: Allah does not love one whose characteristic is betraying people in their wealth and committing sin in that and in other things that Allah has forbidden him.

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said the same as what we have said on this matter, and the narrations from them have already been mentioned.

10418- Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: "And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves," he said: A man stole a coat of mail from his paternal uncle, then threw it to a Jew who used to visit them. The uncle of the man then argued on behalf of his people, and it was as if the Prophet (ﷺ) excused him. Then he joined the land of polytheism, and this verse was revealed concerning him: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him...﴾ (4:115).

The commentary on His saying, ﴿They hide from the people, but they cannot hide from Allah, for He is with them when they plot by night in speech that He does not approve. And Allah is ever encompassing of what they do﴾ [4:108]:

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, "They hide from the people," He, great is His praise, means: these people who betray themselves hide from "the people" the wrongdoing they have committed and the shame and disobedience they have incurred, because they cannot be held to account for anything except by being reminded of the ugliness of what they did and the grievousness of the crime they committed, should it become known. They do this out of shame before them and fear of the bad reputation (al-uhdutha).

"But they cannot hide from Allah," who sees them, nothing of their deeds is hidden from Him, and in His hand are punishment, retribution and the hastening of torment. He is more deserving to be shamed before than anyone else, and more fitting to be magnified by not seeing them where they dislike any of His creatures to see them.

"And He is with them," meaning: Allah is witnessing them.

"When they plot by night in speech that He does not approve," meaning: when they arrange by night what He does not approve of in speech, altering it from its proper form and lying in it.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "tabyit" (plotting by night) in another place: it is any speech or matter that is arranged at night.

It has been related from some of the Tayy tribe that "tabyit" in their language means "tabdil" (alteration), and he recited the verse of al-Aswad ibn 'Amir ibn Juwayn al-Ta'i, rebuking a man: [The name in the printed and manuscript editions reads "ibn Jarir," but the correct form is what has been given here: al-Aswad ibn 'Amir ibn Juwayn al-Ta'i, Abu 'Amir ibn Juwayn al-Ta'i, with whom Imru' al-Qays stayed (al-Aghani 8: 90, 95). Ibn Duraid mentioned both in al-Ishtiqaq (233) and said, "They were two chieftain leaders." Ibn Hazm also mentioned both in al-Jamharah (379), and said of al-Aswad ibn 'Amir: "a poet." Then he said: "From this al-Aswad was born Qabisah ibn al-Aswad, who came as a delegation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)."]

"And you have altered my word to 'Abd al-Malik, may Allah fight you, O stubborn slave!" [I have not found this verse in any source. I knew it but its location escaped me. I hope to locate it and add its explanation in another edition or another book.]

Meaning: you have changed my word.

* *

It is related from Abu Razin that he used to say, regarding the meaning of His saying "yubayyitun," that it means "yu'allifun" (they compose/fabricate).

10419: Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Razin: "when they plot by night in speech that He does not approve," he said: they fabricate speech that He does not approve.

10420: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti narrated to us, saying: Abu Yahya al-Himmani narrated to us, from Sufyan, from al-A'mash, from Abu Razin, with something similar.

10421: al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Razin, the like of it. [The reports 10419–10421: "Abu Razin" is Abu Razin al-Asadi, Mas'ud ibn Malik, mentioned under numbers 4291–4294 and then 4791–4793.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This view is close in meaning to what we have stated. That is because "ta'lif" (fabrication) is the arranging and altering of a matter from what it truly is, and turning it from its meaning to something else.

* *

It has also been said that by His saying, "They hide from the people but they cannot hide from Allah," He meant the group who came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning the matter of defending Ibn Ubayriq and disputing on his behalf, as we mentioned earlier, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas and others.

* *

"And Allah is ever encompassing of what they do": He, great is His praise, means: Allah is encompassing of what these people who hide from the people do, regarding the wrongdoing they committed out of shame before them, including their plotting by night in speech He does not approve and their other deeds, "encompassing," counting it all, nothing of it hidden from Him, guarding it against them, until He recompenses them for it with their due recompense. [See the explanation of "al-ihatah" and "muhit" above: 2: 284; 5: 396; 7: 158.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 109:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Here you are, those who argued on their behalf in the life of this world, but who will argue with Allah on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection, or who will be their guardian?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His majesty be exalted, ﴿Here you are, those who argued on their behalf in the life of this world﴾, He means: you are the ones who argued [[See what has been said regarding "ha antum ula'i" and "ha antum ha'ula'" earlier, 7:150, 151.]] O company of those who argued on behalf of the Banu Ubayriq, "in the life of this world." The "ha'" and the "mim" in His saying "on their behalf" refer to the traitors.

﴿Then who will argue with Allah on their behalf﴾, meaning: who then will dispute with Allah on their behalf ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾, that is, the Day when people rise from their graves to their gathering, [[See the explanation of "the Day of Resurrection" earlier, 2:518 / 8:592.]] so as to defend them against what Allah will do to them and the punishment with which He will punish them. What is meant by this is: you, who defend these traitors, even if you defend them in the immediate life of this world, they will in the deferred life of the Hereafter come to One before whom no one can defend them against the painful torment and the retribution of punishment that will befall them.

As for His saying ﴿or who will be their guardian?﴾, it means: and who then will be a guardian (wakil) for these traitors on the Day of Resurrection, that is, who will take up their cause in the dispute with their Lord on their behalf on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "wakalah" (agency) earlier, and that it is undertaking the affair of the one who has entrusted it to you. [[See the explanation of "al-Wakil" earlier, 7:405 / 8:566.]]

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 110:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And whoever does wrong or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (4:110).

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: whoever commits a sin, which is "evil" [[See the explanation of "al-su'" (evil) in the earlier indexes of language.]], "or wrongs himself," by earning for himself that which makes him deserving of Allah's punishment; "then seeks forgiveness from Allah," that is, then repents to Allah, turning back from the evil and the wronging of himself that he committed, and returning to what Allah loves of righteous deeds that erase his sin and remove his offence; "will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful," that is, he will find his Lord covering his sin, pardoning him from the punishment of his crime, and merciful toward him. [[See the explanation of "istaghfar" (seeking forgiveness), "ghafur" (Forgiving) and "rahim" (Merciful) in the earlier indexes of language.]]

* *

The scholars of interpretation differed concerning who is meant by this verse.

Some of them said: It refers to those whom Allah described as betrayers in His words: "And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves."

* *

Others said: Rather, it refers to those who used to argue on behalf of the betrayers, [[In the printed edition: "those who argue on behalf of the betrayers," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]] those to whom Allah said: "There you are, those who argued on their behalf in the life of this world," and we have already mentioned the proponents of both views earlier.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The correct view in this matter, in our opinion, is that by it is meant everyone who does evil or wrongs himself, even though it was revealed concerning the matter of the betrayers and those who argued on their behalf, whose affair Allah mentioned in the verses before it.

* *

A group of the scholars of interpretation also said in accordance with what we have said.

Those who said that:

10422. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from 'Asim, from Abu Wa'il, who said: 'Abdullah (ibn Mas'ud) said: When one of the Children of Israel committed a sin, by morning it would be written as expiation for that sin on his door. And if urine struck any part of him, he would cut it off with scissors. A man said: Allah gave the Children of Israel good! 'Abdullah said: What Allah has given you is better than what He gave them. Allah made water a purifier for you, and He said: ﴿And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves, remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins﴾ (3:135), and He said: "And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful."

10423. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Ibn 'Awn narrated to us, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, who said: A woman came to 'Abdullah ibn Mughaffal and asked him about a woman who committed fornication and became pregnant, and when she gave birth she killed her child. Ibn Mughaffal said: What about her? For her is the Fire! So she left weeping. He called her back and said: I see your matter as only one of two: "Whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful." He said: She wiped her eyes and went on her way.

10424. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: 'Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: "And whoever does evil or wrongs himself, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful." He said: Allah informed His servants of His forbearance, His pardon, His generosity, the vastness of His mercy and His forgiveness. Whoever commits a sin, whether small or great, then seeks forgiveness from Allah, will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful, even if his sins were greater than the heavens, the earth and the mountains.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 111:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And whoever earns a sin, he earns it only against himself. And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise.﴾ (111)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Whoever commits a sin, deliberately and knowingly, he bears the burden, the harm, the disgrace and the shame of that sin upon himself alone, and not upon anyone else among the rest of Allah's creation. [[See the explanation of "kasb" (earning) above, 8:267, footnote 1, and the references there; and the explanation of "ithm" (sin) above, 4:328, footnote 1, and the references there.]] He says: So do not argue, O you who argue, on behalf of these traitors, for even if they are your kinsfolk, tribe and neighbours, they are innocent of the sin they committed and of the liability for which they are held accountable; and if you defend them or dispute on their behalf, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "fa-innakum matā dāfa'tum ..." but the context requires "wa-innakum".]] you will be just like them. So do not defend them, nor dispute on their behalf.

As for His saying: ﴿And Allah is ever Knowing and Wise﴾, it means: Allah is ever Knowing of what you do, O you who argue on behalf of those who betray themselves, in your argument on their behalf and in your other actions and the actions of others; He keeps account of them against you and against them, until He recompenses all of you for them.
