"Wise" means: He is Wise in His governance and His management of you and of the management of all His creation. [[See the explanation of "'alim" (knowing) and "hakim" (wise) above in the language indexes.]]

* *

It has also been said: This verse was revealed concerning the Banu Ubayriq. We have already mentioned, earlier, those who said so. [[Meaning the earlier reports from 10409 to 10418.]]

**The interpretation of His words:** ﴿And whoever commits a sin or a misdeed, then throws it onto an innocent person, has certainly taken on a slander and a manifest sin﴾ [4:112]

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: whoever does a wrong, which is an offence, ﴿or a misdeed﴾, which is what is unlawful of disobedience. [[See the explanation of "khati'ah" (wrongdoing) above, 2:110, 284, 285.]]

* *

The reason He distinguished between "khati'ah" and "ithm" is that "khati'ah" may arise from intention or from unintentional error, whereas "ithm" arises only from intention. So He, may His praise be exalted, distinguished between them, saying: whoever commits a "khati'ah" without intending it, or an "ithm" with intent.

* *

﴿Then throws it onto an innocent person﴾ [[The printed edition contained an addition which I have removed; the text read: "then throws it onto an innocent person, meaning by what he intentionally did, an innocent person, meaning..." which is a corruption in the interpretation, so I removed it and followed the manuscript.]] means: then he attributes to an innocent person, who is free of it, the wrong or sin he committed, which he attributes to him and falsely imputes to him. ﴿Has certainly taken on a slander and a manifest sin﴾, meaning: by that act he has burdened himself with a fabrication, a lie, and a great sin, a great crime, knowingly and deliberately, for what he committed of disobedience and sin. [[See the explanation of "buhtan" (slander) above, 5:432 / 8:124.]]

* *

The people of interpretation differed concerning whom God meant by His words "innocent," after all had agreed that the one who threw the sin he himself had committed onto an innocent person was Ibn Ubayriq, whose case we described earlier.

Some said: God, mighty and majestic, meant by the innocent a man from among the Muslims called Labid ibn Sahl. [[See report no. 10411.]]

* *

Others said: rather, He meant a man from among the Jews called Zayd ibn al-Samin, and we have already mentioned the narration from those who said so. [[See nos. 10412, 10416.]]

* *

Among those who said "he was a Jew" was Ibn Sirin.

10425: Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Ghundar narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Khalid al-Hadhdha', from Ibn Sirin: ﴿Then throws it onto an innocent person﴾, he said: a Jew.

10426: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Badal ibn al-Muhabbar narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Khalid, from Ibn Sirin, the like of it. [[Report 10426: "Badal ibn al-Muhabbar ibn al-Munabbih al-Tamimi al-Yarbu'i" narrated from Shu'bah and al-Khalil ibn Ahmad, author of the science of prosody ('arud), and others. Al-Bukhari and the four (compilers of the Sunan) narrated from him through Muhammad ibn Bashshar. He is trustworthy (thiqah). "Badal" is pronounced with two fathahs.]]

* *

It was also said: ﴿throws it onto an innocent person﴾ means: then he throws the sin which this traitor committed onto one who is innocent of what he accused him of. In this case, the pronoun in "bihi" (onto it) refers to "ithm" (sin). Had it been taken as a reference to both "ithm" and "khati'ah," that would also be permissible, since acts, though their expressions differ, return to one meaning, namely that they are an act. [[This is an abridgement of the view of al-Farra' in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, 1:286–287.]]

* *

As for His words ﴿has certainly taken on a slander and a manifest sin﴾, their meaning is: the one who accuses another of what he himself has done of disobedience and committed of sin as a wrongdoing has burdened himself with ﴿a slander﴾, which is a fabrication and a lie, against the innocent person who is free of what he accused him of, ﴿and a manifest sin﴾, meaning a grave burden, ﴿manifest﴾, meaning that it makes evident the state of the one who bears it and his audacity towards his Lord, [[See the explanation of "mubin" (manifest) above, p. 3, note 1, and the references there. In the printed edition it read "makes evident the matter of his action," the correct reading being from the manuscript.]] and his advancing against what He forbade him, to anyone who knows his situation.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 113:

﴿Had it not been for Allah's bounty upon you and His mercy, a party of them would have resolved to lead you astray, but they lead astray none except themselves, and they cannot harm you in any way. And Allah has sent down to you the Book and the wisdom, and taught you what you did not know. And the bounty of Allah upon you has been immense.﴾ (4:113)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be great, "Had it not been for Allah's bounty upon you and His mercy," [He means]: had it not been that Allah showed you favour, O Muhammad, [[See the explanation of "al-fadl" in the earlier indexes of language.]] and so protected you by His guidance and made clear to you the matter of this traitor, so that you refrained from arguing on his behalf and from defending him against the people of truth regarding their rights from him, "a party of them would have resolved", meaning: a group of them would have resolved, [[See the explanation of "ta'ifah" above, 1:141, note 1, and the references there.]] that is, of those who betray themselves, "to lead you astray", meaning: to make you slip from the path of truth, [[See the explanation of "al-idlal" above, 8:507, note 1, and the references there.]] and this would have been through their confusing the matter of the traitor for him, ﷺ, and through their testifying to the traitor's innocence of what was claimed against him, and their asking him to excuse him and to speak in his defence before his companions. Then Allah, blessed and exalted, said: and these people who resolved to lead you astray from what is obligatory in the judgment concerning this traitor, who stole the shield of his neighbour, "lead astray none except themselves."

* *

If someone says: What was the manner of their leading themselves astray?

It is said: The manner of their leading themselves astray is their taking themselves toward what Allah did not permit them to take themselves in, from among His ways. That is because Allah, may His praise be great, had already commanded them, in what He had prescribed in His Book through His Messenger to His creatures, to refrain from cooperating in sin and transgression, and to command cooperation in righteousness. Thus it was obligatory before Allah, for whoever strove on behalf of the traitors whose matter Allah described in His words, "And do not be a disputant for the treacherous," to assist those who had been wronged, rather than those who sued them before the Messenger of Allah, ﷺ, seeking their right from them. So their effort in assisting them, rather than assisting those who had been wronged, was a taking of themselves away from the path of Allah. This is their leading themselves astray, which Allah described when He said: "and they lead astray none except themselves."

* *

"And they cannot harm you in any way," meaning: these people who resolved to make you slip from the truth in the matter of this traitor from his people and his clan cannot harm you "in any way", because Allah is the one who makes you firm and guides you in your affairs, and makes clear to you the matter of those who strove to lead you astray from the truth concerning him and their own matter, so He exposes him and them.

His words: "And Allah has sent down to you the Book and the wisdom," mean: and among the bounties of Allah upon you, O Muhammad, along with the rest of His favours which He has bestowed upon you, is that He has sent down to you "the Book", which is the Qur'an, containing the clarification of everything, guidance and admonition, "and the wisdom", meaning: and He has sent down to you along with the Book the wisdom, which is what was summarised in the Book, its lawful and unlawful matters, its commands and prohibitions, its rulings, its promise and its warning. [[See the explanation of "al-hikmah" above, 3:87, 88, 211, and 5:15, and other places in the indexes of language.]] "And He taught you what you did not know", concerning the news of the former and the latter peoples, and what was and what will be. All of that is from the bounty of Allah upon you, O Muhammad, from the time He created you. [[In the printed and manuscript texts: "and what was and what will be before that of the bounty of Allah upon you", which is not correct; the right reading is what I have set down, with "fa-kull" in place of "qabl".]] So thank Him for what He has granted you of His kindness to you, by holding fast to His obedience, hastening to His pleasure and love, persisting in acting by what He has sent down to you in His Book and wisdom, and opposing whoever tries to lead you astray from His path and the way of His religion. For Allah is the one who takes you under His protection by His bounty, and suffices you against the calamity of whoever intends you harm and tries to turn you away from His way, just as He sufficed you in the matter of the party that resolved to lead you astray from His way concerning this traitor. No one other than Him can rescue you from evil if He intends it for you, should you oppose Him in any of His commands or prohibitions and follow the desires of whoever tries to turn you from His way.

* *

This verse is an admonition from Allah to His Prophet Muhammad, ﷺ, concerning the place of his error, [[In the printed edition: "the place of his share", whereas in the manuscript it is undotted, and this is the correct reading in agreement with the context of the story.]] and a reminder from Him to him of what is obligatory upon him in respect of His right.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 114:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿There is no good in much of their secret talk, except for one who enjoins charity or what is right or reconciliation between people. And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah – We will give him a great reward.﴾ (4:114)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, "There is no good in much of their secret talk," may He be exalted in praise, He means: there is no good in much of the secret talk of people in general. "Except for one who enjoins charity or what is right" – "what is right" (al-ma'ruf) is everything that Allah has commanded or recommended of the works of righteousness and goodness. [See the explanation of "al-ma'ruf" above, 3:371 / 7:105, and other places in the indexes of language.] "Or reconciliation between people" – this is reconciliation between those who are estranged or in dispute, by that which Allah has permitted of reconciling between them, so that they return to that which brings harmony and unity of word, in accordance with what Allah has permitted and commanded.

Then He, may He be exalted in praise, informed of what He promised to the one who does that, saying: "And whoever does that seeking the pleasure of Allah – We will give him a great reward." He says: whoever enjoins charity or what is right, or reconciles between people, "seeking the pleasure of Allah," meaning: seeking the approval of Allah by doing that, "We will give him a great reward," meaning: We will give him a great recompense for what he has done of that. [See the explanation of "al-ibtigha'" (seeking) above, p. 170, note 3, and the references there.] "A great reward" – [See the explanation of "ajr" (reward) above, p. 113, note 3, and the references there.] and there is no limit to the extent of what Allah has named "great," which none but Him knows. [See the explanation of "azim" (great) above, 6:518.]

* *

The people of Arabic grammar differed regarding the meaning of His saying: "There is no good in much of their secret talk, except for one who enjoins charity."

Some of the grammarians of Basra said: the meaning is: there is no good in much of their secret talk, except in the secret talk of one who enjoins charity – as if "man" (who) were conjoined to the "hā' and mīm" in "najwāhum" (their secret talk). [In the printed edition: "ka-annahu ʿaṭaf min" without the bāʾ, and I have affirmed what is in the manuscript, which is correct.] This is an error according to the grammarians, because "illa" (except) is not conjoined to the "hā' and mīm" in such a position, since the negation did not reach it.

* *

Some of the grammarians of Kufa said: "man" may be in a position of genitive (khafd) or accusative (nasb). As for the genitive, it is according to your saying: "There is no good in much of their secret talk except in one who enjoins charity." Then "najwa" (secret talk), under this interpretation, means the men who converse secretly, as He, may He be exalted in praise, said: ﴿There is not a secret conversation of three but He is their fourth﴾ (58:7), and as He said: ﴿when they are in secret conversation﴾ (17:47).

As for the accusative, it is according to making "najwa" a verbal noun [His saying "fi'lan" means "maṣdaran," i.e. a verbal noun], so that it is in the accusative, because then it is an exceptive of disconnection (istithna' munqati'), since "man" is other than "najwa." This is like the saying of the poet. [He is al-Nabigha al-Dhubyani.]

...... "And there is nothing in the enclosure of anyone
except the traces, dim, which I make clear..." ......

[The poem, its takhrij and completion were mentioned above, 1:183, 523, and it is in Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:288.]

It is also possible, under this interpretation, that "man" be in the nominative, as the poet said: [He is Jiran al-Ud al-Numayri.]

"And a land in which there is no companion
except the yu'afir (gazelles) and except the 'is (white camels)..."

[His Diwan: 52; Sibawayh 1:133, 365; Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:288; Majalis Tha'lab: 316, 452; al-Khizana 4:197; al-'Ayni (margin of al-Khizana) 3:107; it will come in the tafsir at 12:28 / 27:39 (Bulaq), then in hundreds of books of grammar and Arabic. The version of this poem in his Diwan is: "We have left the dwelling, O Lamis, where the fierce beast prowls, the wolf, or the maned one, the bold one, [...] in a waste where there is no companion except the yu'afir and the 'is, and a spotted cow with white markings..." – "ya'tasu": seeks what to eat; "al-jurus" here means one who eats fiercely, and the owner of al-Khizana erred when he said "from al-jars, which is the faint sound," and this is not among the attributes of the wolf, its howling when hungry being enough, as a denial of describing it with faint sound! And he has clarified in the third verse that he means the "wolf." "Dhu labad" is the lion, and "al-labda" is the hair between its shoulders. "Hamus" is an attribute of the lion; it is said at times: one who walks with a walk that conceals it, so that the sound of its stepping is not heard; and it is said at other times: one who bites hard with his molars when eating. This is what is meant here, for he intended to mention the emptiness of these abodes and the dangers in them. "Bisabis" are deserts, empty. As for the variant "wa-baldatin," "al-baldah" here is the barren land to which animals resort. "Al-yu'afir" is the plural of "ya'fur," which is the gazelle in the color of dust. "Al-'is" is the plural of "a'is," which is the white gazelle with a tinge. "Kunus" is the plural of "kanis," which is the gazelle or cow when it enters its resting place, its den in the trees where it hides. "Al-mis" is the plural of "maisa'," which is she who sways and struts like a bride in her gait.

Then see al-Khizana and Majalis Tha'lab. And see all that has preceded in Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:287, 288.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these opinions regarding this is to make "man" in the genitive position, by way of returning to "najwa," and "najwa" meaning the collective of those who converse secretly, coming out in the form of "sukra," "jarha," and "marda" (drunken, wounded, sick). This is because that is the most evident of its meanings.

So the interpretation of the statement is: there is no good in much of those who converse secretly, O Muhammad, from among the people, except in one who enjoins charity or what is right or reconciliation between people, for those have good in them.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 115:

The explanation of His words: ﴿And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers - We will give him what he has turned to and drive him into Hell, and evil it is as a destination.﴾ (4:115)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, "And whoever opposes the Messenger" (wa-man yushaqiq al-rasul), He, may His praise be exalted, means: whoever separates himself from the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), taking a hostile position toward him and parting from him in enmity towards him [[See the explanation of "shiqaq" (opposition) above, 3:115, 116, 336; 8:319.]]. "After guidance has become clear to him" means: after it has become clear to him that he is the Messenger of God, and that what he has brought from God guides to the truth and to a straight path. "And follows other than the way of the believers" means: he follows a path other than the path of those who affirm the truth, and takes a course other than their course. This is disbelief in God, because disbelief in God and His Messenger is other than the way and course of the believers. "We will give him what he has turned to" means: We will make his helper that which he sought help from and relied upon, namely the idols and images, [[See the explanation of "wala" above, p. 17, note 3, and the references there.]] which cannot benefit him, nor avert from him anything of God's punishment, nor profit him, as:

10427. Narrated to me by Muhammad ibn Amr, who said: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, "We will give him what he has turned to," he said: "From the false gods."

10428. Narrated to me by Ibn al-Muthanna, who said: Abu Huthayfa narrated to us, who said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

"And drive him into Hell" means: We will make him fuel for the fire of Hell [[In the printed edition: "sila" with a shadda on the ya; the correct reading is from the manuscript. "Al-sila'" (with a kasra on the sad) means roasted meat, because it is roasted by fire.]], meaning: We will burn him with it.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "al-sila" (burning) earlier, in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary [[See what has passed in the explanation of "al-isla'" (burning), 8:27-29, 231, 484.]].

* *

"And evil it is as a destination" means: and Hell is evil [[See the explanation of "sa'a" above, p. 101, note 2, and the references there.]] as a "destination" (masira), a place to which whoever arrives will go [[See the explanation of "masir" above, p. 101, note 3, and the references there.]].

* *

This verse was revealed concerning the treacherous people whom God mentioned in His words, "And do not be an advocate for the treacherous" (4:105), when those among them who refused repentance refused it. He is Ta'mah ibn Ubayriq, who joined the polytheists among the idol worshippers in Mecca as an apostate, separated from the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and his religion.

The Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on Surah 4, Verse 116:

Discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with; but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly gone far astray.﴾ (4:116)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, He, may His praise be exalted, means: Indeed, Allah does not forgive Ta'mah when he associated others with Him and died in his polytheism toward Allah, nor does He forgive any other of His creatures for their associating and disbelieving in Him. "But He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills" means: He forgives sins other than associating others with Allah, for whomever He wills. By this, He, may His praise be exalted, means: Had Ta'mah not associated others with Allah and died in his polytheism, he would have been subject to Allah's will regarding his past betrayal and disobedience, and his matter would have been left to Allah regarding His punishment of him and His pardon of him. And this is the ruling for everyone who commits a crime: his matter is left to Allah, except that if his crime is associating others with Allah and disbelief, then he is one upon whom it is decreed that he is among the people of the Fire if he dies in his polytheism. [[This phrase that I have placed between the two lines is an interruption within the sentence, and its context is: Ta'mah, had he not died in his polytheism, would have been subject to Allah's will regarding his past betrayal and disobedience, and his matter would have been left to Allah regarding His punishment of him and His pardon of him... But when he dies in his polytheism... The first printed edition's publisher misread this phrase, and wrote it thus: "it is decreed upon him that he is among the people of the Fire if he dies in his polytheism, so when he dies in his polytheism..." and the whole statement became meaningless and confused.]] — But when he dies in his polytheism, then Allah has forbidden Paradise to him, and his abode is the Fire.

* *

And al-Suddi said concerning this:

10429. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with; but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ — he said: those among the Muslims who avoid the major sins (al-kaba'ir).

* *

As for His words: ﴿And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly gone far astray﴾, it means: whoever makes for Allah a partner in His worship has departed from the path of truth and deviated from the straight way, a far departure and a severe deviation. This is because by associating others with Allah in His worship, he has obeyed Satan and followed his path, [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "then he has obeyed Satan," with the fa' added, and it has no meaning here.]] and abandoned obedience to Allah and the course of His religion. That is the far error and the manifest loss.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 117:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿They invoke besides Him only females﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: The meaning is: They invoke besides Him only al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat, and God named them "females" by the naming of the polytheists who called them by the name of females.

Those who said this:

10430 - Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Husayn informed us, from Abu Malik, concerning His words: "They invoke besides Him only females," he said: al-Lat, al-'Uzza and Manat, all of them feminine.

10431 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Husayn, from Abu Malik, with something similar, except that he said: all of them feminine.

10432 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal related to us, saying: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi, concerning "They invoke besides Him only females," he says: They named them "females": Lat, Manat and 'Uzza.

10433 - Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words: "They invoke besides Him only females," he said: Their gods: al-Lat, al-'Uzza, Yasaf and Na'ila, [["Isaf" (with kasra and with fatha on the hamza) and "Yasaf" (with kasra and with fatha on the ya') are the same. They claim that Isaf ibn 'Amr and Na'ila bint Sahl, from Jurhum, found a private place in the Ka'bah, and committed fornication therein, so God transformed them into two stones, which Quraysh afterwards worshipped. It is said: they were two idols that 'Amr ibn Luhayy placed on al-Safa and al-Marwa, and he would slaughter upon them opposite the Ka'bah.]] females, they invoke them besides God. And he recited: "They invoke besides Him only a rebellious devil."

* *

Others said: The meaning is: They invoke besides Him only lifeless things with no spirit in them.

Those who said this:

10434 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His words: "They invoke besides Him only females," he says: a dead thing.

10435 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: "They invoke besides Him only females," i.e., only a dead thing with no spirit in it. [[In the manuscript: "la arwah fihi" in the plural.]]

10436 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Hajjaj related to us, saying: Mubarak ibn Fadalah related to us, from al-Hasan: "They invoke besides Him only females," he said: And "females" is every thing that is dead with no spirit in it: a dry piece of wood or a dry stone. God, may He be exalted, said: "They invoke only a rebellious devil," up to His words: "and they will surely cut off the ears of the cattle."

* *

Others said: He meant by this that the polytheists used to say: "The angels are the daughters of God." [[In the printed edition: "Inna al-mala'ikah..." and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

Those who said this:

10437 - Yahya ibn Abi Talib related to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, concerning His words: "They invoke besides Him only females," he said: The angels, whom they claim are the daughters of God.

* *

Others said: The meaning is: The people of idols used to name their idols "females," so God revealed that thus.

Those who said this: [[From the beginning of the report no. 10437 up to this place is missing from the manuscript.]]

10438 - Sufyan ibn Waki' related to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun related to us, from Nuh ibn Qays, from Abu Raja', from al-Hasan who said: Every tribe of the Arab tribes had an idol, which they named: "The female of the Banu so-and-so," [[In the book al-Muhtasib by Ibn Jinni, in question no. 143 (which is in manuscript with me), from al-Hasan: "It is the name of an idol for a tribe of the Arabs, whom they worshipped and named: the female of the Banu so-and-so." I fear that the copyist omitted here [they used to worship it].]] so God revealed: "They invoke besides Him only females."

10439 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Nuh ibn Qays related to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sayf Abu Raja' al-Hudani related to us, saying: I heard al-Hasan say: Every tribe of the Arabs..., and he mentioned something similar. [[The two reports 10438 and 10439: "Abu Raja'", "Muhammad ibn Sayf al-Hudani", who met Anas, and narrated from al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Mutar al-Warraq, 'Ikrimah and others. Trustworthy. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.

In the printed edition it was "al-Harrani" with a ra', and the correct reading from the manuscript is with a ha' vowelled with damma and a dal doubled.]]

* *

Others said: "Females" in this place means idols.

Those who said this:

10440 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: "females," he said: idols.

10441 - al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Huthayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

10442 - Sufyan related to us, saying: Abu Usamah related to us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, from his father, who said: In the codex of 'A'ishah was: "They invoke besides Him only idols."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to read it: "Uthunan" (plural of "wathan"), meaning the plural of "wathan," as if he pluralised "wathan" into "wuthun," [["Uthun" (with damma on the hamza and the tha') and "wuthn" (plural of "wathan," with damma then sukun) and "wuthun" (with two dammas), and "awthan".]] then he changed the waw into a hamza with damma, as it is said: "How beautiful are these ajuh," meaning wujuh; and as it is said: "And when the messengers are brought to a time (uqqitat)" [Surah al-Mursalat: 11], meaning: wuqqitat. [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 288.]]

* *

It is also mentioned from some of them that he used to read it: "Unuthan," as if he meant the plural of "al-inath" (females), so he pluralised it as "anth," just as "al-thimar" is pluralised as "thumuran." [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1: 289. "Al-thamar" with damma on the tha' and the mim.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The reading which we do not permit reading other than, is the reading of the one who reads: "Inna yad'una min dunihi illa inathan," meaning the plural of "untha," because it is so in the codices of the Muslims, and because of the consensus of the authorities upon reading it so.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most preferred of the interpretations I have mentioned for its interpretation, given that the correct reading according to us is what I have described, is the interpretation of the one who said: It refers to the deities which the polytheists of the Arabs used to worship besides God, and called "females" by name, such as al-Lat, al-'Uzza, Na'ila and Manat, and what resembles them.

We only said that this is more preferred as the interpretation of the verse, because the most apparent of the meanings of "females" in the speech of the Arabs is what is defined by the feminine and nothing else. Since this is so, it is obligatory to direct its interpretation to the most well-known of its meanings.

* *

Since this is so, the interpretation of the verse is: "And whoever opposes the Messenger after guidance has become clear to him and follows other than the way of the believers, We will leave him in what he has turned to and burn him in Hell, and evil is it as a destination." * "They invoke besides Him only females," meaning: those who oppose the Messenger and follow other than the way of the believers invoke nothing "besides God," after God and other than Him, "except females," meaning: except what they named with the names of females, such as al-Lat, al-'Uzza and what resembles them. He, may His praise be exalted, says: Sufficient as proof against those who associated others with God, and worshipped what they worshipped besides Him of idols and rivals, in their misguidance, their disbelief and their turning away from the right path, is that they worship females and call them gods and lords. And the females of every thing are its lowest, so they acknowledge servitude to the lowly among things, with knowledge of its lowliness, and refrain from sincerely devoting servitude to the One to whom belongs the dominion of everything, and in whose hand are creation and command. [[In the printed edition: "bil-ubudiyyah" and "al-ubudiyyah" in both places, and I have kept what is in the manuscript. "Al-ubudah" is worship, and al-Tabari's use of this form has been used before, and the editor changed it each time. See 3: 347 n.1, 6: 271 n.1, 404 n.2, 549 n.2, 564 n.3, 8: 592 n.2.]]

* *

The discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿And they invoke only a rebellious devil﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, means by His words: "And they invoke only a rebellious devil," that what these people who invoke these female idols besides God invoke by their invocation of them = "only a rebellious devil," meaning: one who rebels against God in opposing Him in what He commanded him and what He forbade him, as:

10443 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah: "And they invoke only a rebellious devil," he rebelled against the disobedience of God.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 118:

The discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿Allah cursed him, and he said, "I will surely take of Your servants a specified portion"﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "Allah cursed him" (la'anahu Allah), He, may His praise be exalted, means: He humiliated him, removed him far away, and distanced him.

* *

The meaning of the statement: "And they invoke none but a rebellious devil" — Allah has cursed him and distanced him from every good.

* *

"And he said, 'I will surely take...'" means: the rebellious devil said to his Lord when He cursed him: "I will surely take of Your servants a specified portion."

By "mafrud" (specified), he means known. [[See the explanation of "nasib" (portion) earlier, 4: 206, and again 8: 58, note 4, and the references there; and the explanation of "al-fard" (obligation) earlier, 4: 121, 5: 120, 7: 597-599, 8: 50.]] As related:

* *

1044 - Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Na'im related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak, regarding "a specified portion," he said: "known."

* *

If someone says: How can Satan take a specified portion from the servants of Allah?

It is said: He takes that portion by leading them astray from the right path, calling them to his obedience, and adorning for them error and disbelief until he turns them away from the straight way. Whoever answers his call and follows what he has made attractive to them, is from his known portion and his apportioned share.

* *

Allah, may His praise be exalted, informed in this verse of what He reported of Satan's saying: "I will surely take of Your servants a specified portion," so that those who opposed the Messenger after guidance had become clear to them would know that they are from the portion of Satan, whom Allah cursed, the specified one [["al-mafrud" is an attribute of "nasib al-shaytan"]], and that they are among those upon whom his assumption proved true. [[In the printed and manuscript texts: "wa-annahu min" ..., but the context requires "wa-annahum."]]

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "al-la'na" (curse) earlier, so we dislike repeating it. [[See the explanation of "al-la'na" earlier, p. 57, note 4, and the references there.]]

**Commentary on the words of God: ﴿And I will surely mislead them, and I will surely arouse their desires, and I will surely command them, so they will surely slit the ears of the cattle﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, may His majesty be exalted, reporting the speech of the rebellious Satan whose description is given in this verse, ﴿and I will surely mislead them﴾: I will surely divert the allotted portion that I take from Your servants from the clear path of guidance to error, and from Islam to disbelief. ﴿And I will surely arouse their desires﴾: he says, I will surely turn them aside, by the desires I place in their souls, from obedience to You and from the affirmation of Your oneness, toward obedience to me and associating others with You. ﴿And I will surely command them, so they will surely slit the ears of the cattle﴾: he says, I will surely command the portion allotted to me from Your servants to worship other than You, the idols and rivals, until they sacrifice for it [[The verb "nasaka yansuku," when one slaughters a nasikah, meaning a sacrificial animal. See the earlier discussions of this in 3:75–80, 4:86, and 4:195.]] and forbid and permit on its behalf, and legislate other than what You have legislated for them, so that they follow me and oppose You.

* * *

"Al-batk" means cutting. In this place it means cutting the ear of the baheerah, so that it is known to be a baheerah. [[The "baheerah" is one of the cattle that was part of the beliefs of the people of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era). Islam abolished it. It is a she-camel or a sheep whose ear is split, and then it is left alone so that no one touches it.]]

By this, the wicked one only meant that he calls them to the baheerah, and they respond to him and practise it in obedience to him.

* * *

The people of ta'wil (interpretation) said things similar to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

10445. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah, concerning His words, ﴿so they will surely slit the ears of the cattle﴾, he said: The slitting is for the baheerah and the saa'ibah. They used to slit their ears for their idols (tawaghit).

10446. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, concerning His words, ﴿and I will surely command them, so they will surely slit the ears of the cattle﴾: as for "they will surely slit the ears of the cattle," they split them, and make them baheerah.

10447. Al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hajjaj told me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah informed me, from Ikrimah, concerning ﴿so they will surely slit the ears of the cattle﴾, he said: It is a religion that Iblis legislated for them, in the form of the baheer and the sawaib. [[The "saa'ibah" or the "baheerah": this is because a man would make a vow: if he returned from a long journey, or recovered from an illness, or was saved from some hardship or war, he would say, "This she-camel of mine is saa'ibah," meaning that she is let loose, so her back is not used, she is not kept away from water, she is not prevented from pasture, and she is not ridden. The plural of "saa'ibah" is "sayb" (with the sin vowelled with a damma, and the shadda on the yaa' with a fatha), like "na'im" and "nawm," and "na'ihah" and "nawh." This is how it came in the manuscript, correctly, but the publisher of the printed edition made it "sawa'ib," as if he disapproved of this plural, and he committed the utmost error in changing the correct reading, although "sawa'ib" is also correct, and these reports are evidence in the language.]]

* * *

Concerning His words: ﴿and I will surely command them, so they will surely alter the creation of God﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of ta'wil differed regarding the meaning of His words, "so they will surely alter the creation of God."

Some of them said: The meaning is: "and I will surely command them, so they will surely alter the creation of God among the animals, by castrating them." [[The phrase "khasa al-fahl yakhsihi khasa'" (with a kasra on the kha') means to remove his testicles. The early jurists used to say "al-ikhsa'" (the castration), but the lexicographical books did not mention it. Al-Mutarrizi said in al-Maghrib (1:159): "Khasa' is on the pattern of fi'al, and al-ikhsa' is in its meaning, which is an error." This is a point of difficulty, for you will find it widespread in the reports that follow, and they are a sound text permitting "al-ikhsa'." It is by such reports that the authors of the lexicons argued, and how could it not be argued by them, when it has come in the words of Ibn Abbas, as you see in report 10451.]]

Those who said that:

10448. Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah told us, from Ammar ibn Abi Ammar, from Ibn Abbas, that he disliked castration and said: It was about this that it was revealed: "and I will surely command them, so they will surely alter the creation of God."

10449. Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Dawud told us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi told us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Anas, that he disliked castration and said: It was about this that it was revealed: "and I will surely command them, so they will surely alter the creation of God."

10450. Ibn Wakee' told us, saying: My father told us, from Abu Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: It is castration, meaning God's words: "and I will surely command them, so they will surely alter the creation of God."

10451. Ibn Wakee' told us, saying: Ibn Fudayl told us, from Mutarrif, who said: A man told me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The castration of animals is mutilation! Then he recited: "and I will surely command them, so they will surely alter the creation of God."

10452. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi informed us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: From the alteration of God's creation is castration.

10453. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ja'far ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: Shubayl informed me, that he heard Shahr ibn Hawshab recite this verse: "so they will surely alter the creation of God," and he said: "al-khisa'" (castration). He said: I ordered Abu al-Tayyah, and he asked al-Hasan about the castration of sheep, and he said: There is no harm in it. [[Report 10453: "Ja'far ibn Sulayman al-Dab'i" has passed under numbers 2905 and 6461. "Shubayl" is "Shubayl ibn Azrah ibn Umayr al-Dab'i," who narrates from Shahr ibn Hawshab, and Ja'far ibn Sulayman narrated from him. He is trustworthy (thiqah). Abu Dawud narrated one hadith from him. Shubayl was one of the leading authorities in Arabic, and he was the son-in-law of Qatadah. Al-Jahiz mentioned him in al-Bayan (1:343), saying: "Among the scholars of the Kharijites is Shubayl ibn Azrah al-Dab'i, the author of al-Gharib, and he was a transmitter, an orator, a poet, and a genealogist. For seventy years he was a Rafidi, then he moved on to become a Kharijite of the Safriyyah sect." Al-Baladhuri said: "He was not a Kharijite, but he used to recite poems expressing that out of dissimulation (taqiyyah)." He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.
In the printed edition it was "Shibl," which is an error, because the one who edited it did not read the manuscript well, as it has no dots.
"Abu al-Tayyah" is "Yazid ibn Humayd al-Dab'i," who narrated from Anas and al-Hasan al-Basri. He is a reliable, trustworthy and well-known transmitter. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

10454. Al-Hasan told us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: My paternal uncle Wahb ibn Nafi' told us, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, who said: Mujahid ordered me to ask Ikrimah about His words, "so they will surely alter the creation of God." So I asked him, and he said: It is castration.

10455. Ibn Wakee' told us, saying: My father told me, from Abd al-Jabbar ibn Ward, from al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, who said: Mujahid said to me: Ask Ikrimah about it: "and I will surely command them, so they will surely alter the creation of God." So I asked him, and he said: The castration. Mujahid said: What is wrong with him? May God curse him! By God, he knew that it is other than castration. Then he said: Ask him again. So I asked him, and Ikrimah said: Did you not hear the words of God, blessed and exalted: ﴿the nature of God upon which He created mankind; there is no altering of the creation of God﴾ [Surat al-Rum: 30]? He said: It means the religion of God. Then I related that to Mujahid, and he said: What is wrong with him? May God disgrace him! [[Report 10455: "Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-Ward ibn Aghar ibn al-Ward al-Makhzumi" is trustworthy, there is no harm in him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. He has passed in the chain under number 4631, but he was not biographed there.
Mujahid's words about Ikrimah, "What is wrong with him, may God curse him," and "What is wrong with him, may God disgrace him," mean that Mujahid meant Ikrimah's inconsistency in his narration. Mujahid held a poor opinion of him, just as Malik ibn Anas held a poor opinion of him, saying: "I do not think anyone should accept his hadith." It has been said that he was inconsistent in his hadith, and that he was of little intelligence! The Hafiz (Ibn Hajar) related in al-Tahdhib (7:269): "al-A'mash said, from Ibrahim: I met Ikrimah and asked him about al-batshah al-kubra [the greatest assault]. He said: It is the Day of Resurrection. I said: But Abd Allah used to say it is the Day of Badr. Then the one who asked him after that informed me that he said: It is the Day of Badr." This is similar to this report before us. See also the following report, number 10469.
See also the biography of Ikrimah al-Barbari in al-Tahdhib, where the Hafiz has fully discussed his reliability (adalah), his authentication (tawthiq), and the narration of the leading scholars from him.]]

10456. Ibn Wakee' told us, saying: Hafs told us, from Layth, who said: Ikrimah said: "so they will surely alter the creation of God," he said: It is castration.

10457. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, saying: Harun al-Nahwi told us, saying: Mutar al-Warraq told us, who said: Ikrimah was asked about His words, "and I will surely command them, so they will surely alter the creation of God," and he said: It is castration.

10458. Ibn Wakee' told us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman told us, from Sufyan, from Isma'il ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Salih, who said: It is castration.

10459. Amr ibn Ali told us, saying: Wakee' told us, saying: Abu Ja'far al-Razi told us, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say concerning His words, "and I will surely command them, so they will surely alter the creation of God": Among it is castration.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verses 119–120 (part 2 of 2):

The route of Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah (10489), narrated by Ahmad: 4434, and its wording is "Allah has cursed the women who tattoo (al-mutawashimat) and the women who pluck their facial hair (al-mutanammisat) ...". I fear that "al-mutawashimat" has dropped out from the copyist's text.

"Al-mutafallijah" (the woman who makes a gap, al-falj, between her teeth) is one who, when her teeth are close together, creates a gap by filing between them with a file (al-mibrad) until the space between her teeth widens.

"Al-mutanammisah" and "al-namisah" are the women who remove the hair of their eyebrows with tweezers (al-minqash) until they thin them, raise them, and make them even. "Al-mustawshimah" and "al-washimah", and "al-washm," refer to pricking a needle into the skin until blood flows, then filling the wound with kohl or something else so that it turns green. It is also said: "It is making a beauty mark on the face with kohl." They also do this on the lips and gums, and all of that falls within what Allah has forbidden and cursed.

= "Al-washarah" is the woman who files her teeth and thins them with a saw (al-minshar), which is the file (al-mibrad).

All of what Allah has cursed the doer of, our Muslim women do today: they display their adornment (mutabarrijat) by it, they go to excess in it, and they imitate those who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger. Because of their disobedience and their disregard, and indeed because of the disobedience of all of us, Allah has brought upon us the punishment with which the Messenger of Allah warned us, may my father and mother be his ransom (ﷺ). So Allah has made His might (ba's) fall between us, has given power over us to our worst, and has gathered the nations against us to devour us. O Allah, guide our lost ones, seize the foreheads of our disobedient ones, forgive us and have mercy on us. In You we trust, by You we seek refuge, and to You we turn.

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The most correct of the opinions regarding the interpretation of this is the statement of the one who said: its meaning is "I will command them, so they will change the creation of Allah," he said: the religion of Allah. This is because of the evidence of another verse that this is its meaning, which is His saying: ﴿The nature of Allah upon which He created mankind. There is no alteration to the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion﴾ [Surah al-Rum: 30].

If that is its meaning, then included in it is the doing of everything Allah has forbidden: such as castrating what is not permissible to castrate, tattooing and filing the teeth which He has forbidden, and other acts of disobedience. It also includes abandoning everything Allah has commanded. This is because Satan, without doubt, calls to all the disobedience of Allah and forbids all His obedience. That is the meaning of his saying that he will take "his appointed share" from the servants of Allah, by changing the creation of Allah in His religion.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: There is no sense in the interpretation of the one who understood His saying, "and I will command them, so they will change the creation of Allah," to mean a promise by the one commanding to change some of what Allah has forbidden but not all of it, or some of what He has commanded but not all of it. If the one who gave this interpretation understood it to refer only to castration and tattooing and nothing else, [[In the printed edition: "If the one who interpreted ... " and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] he did so because he believed its meaning was that it refers to changing bodies, [[In the printed edition: "meant by it," with the addition of "by it," which is a corruption; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] but in His saying, may His praise be exalted, reporting the words of Satan, "and I will command them, so they will cut the ears of the cattle," there is an indication that the meaning is other than what he took it to be. This is because cutting the ears of cattle is among the changing of the creation of Allah, which is bodies. The report about it has already passed that it is a promise by the one commanding to change the creation of Allah among bodies, explained in detail, so there is no reason to repeat the report about it in summary form, [[A line dropped from the manuscript, so it read: "The report about it has already passed in summary, since the eloquent usage," which is garbled. What is in the printed edition is correct, God willing. I do not know whether this is the initiative of a copyist or editor, or whether it is Abu Ja'far's own wording as written.]] since the eloquent usage in the speech of the Arabs is to explain what is summary with what is detailed, and to render the general with the specific, not to render the detailed with the summary or the specific with the general. Directing the Book of Allah toward the most eloquent speech is better than directing it toward anything else, wherever that is possible.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And whoever takes Satan as a protector instead of Allah has certainly suffered a manifest loss. He promises them and arouses desires in them, but Satan does not promise them except delusion﴾ [Surah al-Nisa: 119–120].

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from Allah, may His praise be exalted, about the state of the appointed share of Satan, those who opposed Allah and His Messenger after the guidance had become clear to them. [[In the printed edition: "from those who opposed ..." with the addition of "from," and the correct reading omits it, as in the manuscript.]] Allah says: whoever follows Satan, obeying him in disobedience to Allah and opposing His command, and befriends him, taking him as a protector for himself and a helper instead of Allah, [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "and a helper instead of Allah" with "from" omitted, which is a slip by the copyist in haste. I have added it because the verse indicates its place.]] ="then he has suffered a manifest loss," meaning: he has perished with a perishing, and has defrauded himself of its share, so he has ruined it with defrauding. "Manifest" = it shows his destruction and ruin. [[See the explanation of "khasir" (suffered loss) earlier: 1:417 / 2:166, 572 / 6:570 / 7:276. And the explanation of "mubin" (manifest) earlier, p. 199, note 2, and the references there.]] This is because Satan cannot grant him any help from Allah if He punishes him for his disobedience in opposing His command. Rather, he forsakes him at the time of his need for him. His relationship with him lasts only while he is alive and is given respite from punishment, as Allah, may His praise be exalted, described it in His saying: "He promises them and arouses desires in them, but Satan does not promise them except delusion." By this, Allah, may His praise be exalted, means: Satan, the rebellious one, promises his protégés, who are his appointed share, that they will have a helper against whoever intends them harm and a supporter for them against him, who will protect them from him and defend them, and he arouses in them the hope of victory over those who seek to harm them and of prevailing over them. ["Al-falaj" (with two fatha vowels) means victory, triumph, and dominance over an opponent.]

= Then He said: "but Satan does not promise them except delusion," meaning: Satan does not promise his protégés, those who took him as a protector instead of Allah, "except delusion," meaning: except falsehood. [[See the explanation of "al-ghurur" (delusion) earlier: 7:453.]]

Allah, may His praise be exalted, made His promise to them "delusion" because they used to think that by taking him as a protector they were on the truth regarding his promises, which were lies, and his desires, which were false. [[In the printed edition: "on its truth," and the correct reading is from the manuscript. The printed edition also has "his false promises," and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is entirely correct.]] Then, when the truth became manifest and they came to need him, the enemy of Allah said to them: ﴿Indeed, Allah promised you a true promise, and I promised you, but I failed you. I had no authority over you except that I invited you and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I disbelieve in your associating me with Allah before﴾ [Surah Ibrahim: 22]. As He said to the polytheists at Badr, when he had made their deeds appear fair to them: ﴿No one among mankind can overcome you today, and I am your protector. But when the two hosts came in sight of each other﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 48]. The truth became manifest, and he witnessed the severity of the matter and the descent of Allah's punishment upon His party [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "hadd al-amr" with a ḥāʾ: that is, its severity and might. Reading it as "jadd" would also be correct, and indeed it is the more likely, which is why I have adopted it.]] =: ﴿He turned back on his heels and said, "Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see. Indeed, I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment"﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 48]. Thus the promises of the enemy of Allah to them became delusion when they needed him, ﴿like a mirage in a level desert, which the thirsty one thinks is water until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds Allah with him, and He pays him in full his account﴾ [Surah al-Nur: 39]. [["Qawluhu: 'adw Allah' is in the accusative of censure, and it separates the verbal noun from its object."]]

**Commentary on the words of God: ﴿And I will surely mislead them, and I will surely arouse their desires, and I will surely command them, so they will surely slit the ears of the cattle﴾**

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, may His majesty be exalted, reporting the speech of the rebellious Satan whose description is given in this verse, ﴿and I will surely mislead them﴾: I will surely divert the allotted portion that I take from Your servants from the clear path of guidance to error, and from Islam to disbelief. ﴿And I will surely arouse their desires﴾: he says, I will surely turn them aside, by the desires I place in their souls, from obedience to You and from the affirmation of Your oneness, toward obedience to me and associating others with You. ﴿And I will surely command them, so they will surely slit the ears of the cattle﴾: he says, I will surely command the portion allotted to me from Your servants to worship other than You, the idols and rivals, until they sacrifice for it [[The verb "nasaka yansuku," when one slaughters a nasikah, meaning a sacrificial animal. See the earlier discussions of this in 3:75–80, 4:86, and 4:195.]] and forbid and permit on its behalf, and legislate other than what You have legislated for them, so that they follow me and oppose You.

* * *

"Al-batk" means cutting. In this place it means cutting the ear of the baheerah, so that it is known to be a baheerah. [[The "baheerah" is one of the cattle that was part of the beliefs of the people of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era). Islam abolished it. It is a she-camel or a sheep whose ear is split, and then it is left alone so that no one touches it.]]

By this, the wicked one only meant that he calls them to the baheerah, and they respond to him and practise it in obedience to him.

They used to slit their ears for their idols (tawaghit).

[[The "saa'ibah" or the "baheerah": this is because a man would make a vow: if he returned from a long journey, or recovered from an illness, or was saved from some hardship or war, he would say, "This she-camel of mine is saa'ibah," meaning that she is let loose, so her back is not used, she is not kept away from water, she is not prevented from pasture, and she is not ridden. The plural of "saa'ibah" is "sayb" (with the sin vowelled with a damma, and the shadda on the yaa' with a fatha), like "na'im" and "nawm," and "na'ihah" and "nawh." This is how it came in the manuscript, correctly, but the publisher of the printed edition made it "sawa'ib," as if he disapproved of this plural, and he committed the utmost error in changing the correct reading, although "sawa'ib" is also correct, and these reports are evidence in the language.]]

* * *

Concerning His words: ﴿and I will surely command them, so they will surely alter the creation of God﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The people of ta'wil differed regarding the meaning of His words, "so they will surely alter the creation of God."

Some of them said: The meaning is: "and I will surely command them, so they will surely alter the creation of God among the animals, by castrating them." [[The phrase "khasa al-fahl yakhsihi khasa'" (with a kasra on the kha') means to remove his testicles. The early jurists used to say "al-ikhsa'" (the castration), but the lexicographical books did not mention it. Al-Mutarrizi said in al-Maghrib (1:159): "Khasa' is on the pattern of fi'al, and al-ikhsa' is in its meaning, which is an error." This is a point of difficulty, for you will find it widespread in the reports that follow, and they are a sound text permitting "al-ikhsa'." It is by such reports that the authors of the lexicons argued, and how could it not be argued by them, when it has come in the words of Ibn Abbas, as you see in report 10451.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verses 119–120 (part 2 of 2):

The route of Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah (10489), narrated by Ahmad: 4434, and its wording is "Allah has cursed the women who tattoo (al-mutawashimat) and the women who pluck their facial hair (al-mutanammisat) ...". I fear that "al-mutawashimat" has dropped out from the copyist's text.

"Al-mutafallijah" (the woman who makes a gap, al-falj, between her teeth) is one who, when her teeth are close together, creates a gap by filing between them with a file (al-mibrad) until the space between her teeth widens.

"Al-mutanammisah" and "al-namisah" are the women who remove the hair of their eyebrows with tweezers (al-minqash) until they thin them, raise them, and make them even. "Al-mustawshimah" and "al-washimah", and "al-washm," refer to pricking a needle into the skin until blood flows, then filling the wound with kohl or something else so that it turns green. It is also said: "It is making a beauty mark on the face with kohl." They also do this on the lips and gums, and all of that falls within what Allah has forbidden and cursed.

= "Al-washarah" is the woman who files her teeth and thins them with a saw (al-minshar), which is the file (al-mibrad).

All of what Allah has cursed the doer of, our Muslim women do today: they display their adornment (mutabarrijat) by it, they go to excess in it, and they imitate those who disbelieve in Allah and His Messenger. Because of their disobedience and their disregard, and indeed because of the disobedience of all of us, Allah has brought upon us the punishment with which the Messenger of Allah warned us, may my father and mother be his ransom (ﷺ). So Allah has made His might (ba's) fall between us, has given power over us to our worst, and has gathered the nations against us to devour us. O Allah, guide our lost ones, seize the foreheads of our disobedient ones, forgive us and have mercy on us. In You we trust, by You we seek refuge, and to You we turn.

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: The most correct of the opinions regarding the interpretation of this is the statement of the one who said: its meaning is "I will command them, so they will change the creation of Allah," he said: the religion of Allah. This is because of the evidence of another verse that this is its meaning, which is His saying: ﴿The nature of Allah upon which He created mankind. There is no alteration to the creation of Allah. That is the correct religion﴾ [Surah al-Rum: 30].

If that is its meaning, then included in it is the doing of everything Allah has forbidden: such as castrating what is not permissible to castrate, tattooing and filing the teeth which He has forbidden, and other acts of disobedience. It also includes abandoning everything Allah has commanded. This is because Satan, without doubt, calls to all the disobedience of Allah and forbids all His obedience. That is the meaning of his saying that he will take "his appointed share" from the servants of Allah, by changing the creation of Allah in His religion.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: There is no sense in the interpretation of the one who understood His saying, "and I will command them, so they will change the creation of Allah," to mean a promise by the one commanding to change some of what Allah has forbidden but not all of it, or some of what He has commanded but not all of it. If the one who gave this interpretation understood it to refer only to castration and tattooing and nothing else, [[In the printed edition: "If the one who interpreted ... " and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] he did so because he believed its meaning was that it refers to changing bodies, [[In the printed edition: "meant by it," with the addition of "by it," which is a corruption; the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] but in His saying, may His praise be exalted, reporting the words of Satan, "and I will command them, so they will cut the ears of the cattle," there is an indication that the meaning is other than what he took it to be. This is because cutting the ears of cattle is among the changing of the creation of Allah, which is bodies. The report about it has already passed that it is a promise by the one commanding to change the creation of Allah among bodies, explained in detail, so there is no reason to repeat the report about it in summary form, [[A line dropped from the manuscript, so it read: "The report about it has already passed in summary, since the eloquent usage," which is garbled. What is in the printed edition is correct, God willing. I do not know whether this is the initiative of a copyist or editor, or whether it is Abu Ja'far's own wording as written.]] since the eloquent usage in the speech of the Arabs is to explain what is summary with what is detailed, and to render the general with the specific, not to render the detailed with the summary or the specific with the general. Directing the Book of Allah toward the most eloquent speech is better than directing it toward anything else, wherever that is possible.

* *

On the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And whoever takes Satan as a protector instead of Allah has certainly suffered a manifest loss. He promises them and arouses desires in them, but Satan does not promise them except delusion﴾ [Surah al-Nisa: 119–120].

Abu Ja'far said: This is a report from Allah, may His praise be exalted, about the state of the appointed share of Satan, those who opposed Allah and His Messenger after the guidance had become clear to them. [[In the printed edition: "from those who opposed ..." with the addition of "from," and the correct reading omits it, as in the manuscript.]] Allah says: whoever follows Satan, obeying him in disobedience to Allah and opposing His command, and befriends him, taking him as a protector for himself and a helper instead of Allah, [[In the manuscript and the printed edition: "and a helper instead of Allah" with "from" omitted, which is a slip by the copyist in haste. I have added it because the verse indicates its place.]] ="then he has suffered a manifest loss," meaning: he has perished with a perishing, and has defrauded himself of its share, so he has ruined it with defrauding. "Manifest" = it shows his destruction and ruin. [[See the explanation of "khasir" (suffered loss) earlier: 1:417 / 2:166, 572 / 6:570 / 7:276. And the explanation of "mubin" (manifest) earlier, p. 199, note 2, and the references there.]] This is because Satan cannot grant him any help from Allah if He punishes him for his disobedience in opposing His command. Rather, he forsakes him at the time of his need for him. His relationship with him lasts only while he is alive and is given respite from punishment, as Allah, may His praise be exalted, described it in His saying: "He promises them and arouses desires in them, but Satan does not promise them except delusion." By this, Allah, may His praise be exalted, means: Satan, the rebellious one, promises his protégés, who are his appointed share, that they will have a helper against whoever intends them harm and a supporter for them against him, who will protect them from him and defend them, and he arouses in them the hope of victory over those who seek to harm them and of prevailing over them. ["Al-falaj" (with two fatha vowels) means victory, triumph, and dominance over an opponent.]

= Then He said: "but Satan does not promise them except delusion," meaning: Satan does not promise his protégés, those who took him as a protector instead of Allah, "except delusion," meaning: except falsehood. [[See the explanation of "al-ghurur" (delusion) earlier: 7:453.]]

Allah, may His praise be exalted, made His promise to them "delusion" because they used to think that by taking him as a protector they were on the truth regarding his promises, which were lies, and his desires, which were false. [[In the printed edition: "on its truth," and the correct reading is from the manuscript. The printed edition also has "his false promises," and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is entirely correct.]] Then, when the truth became manifest and they came to need him, the enemy of Allah said to them: ﴿Indeed, Allah promised you a true promise, and I promised you, but I failed you. I had no authority over you except that I invited you and you responded to me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. I cannot help you, nor can you help me. Indeed, I disbelieve in your associating me with Allah before﴾ [Surah Ibrahim: 22]. As He said to the polytheists at Badr, when he had made their deeds appear fair to them: ﴿No one among mankind can overcome you today, and I am your protector. But when the two hosts came in sight of each other﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 48]. The truth became manifest, and he witnessed the severity of the matter and the descent of Allah's punishment upon His party [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "hadd al-amr" with a ḥāʾ: that is, its severity and might. Reading it as "jadd" would also be correct, and indeed it is the more likely, which is why I have adopted it.]] =: ﴿He turned back on his heels and said, "Indeed, I am free of you. Indeed, I see what you do not see. Indeed, I fear Allah, and Allah is severe in punishment"﴾ [Surah al-Anfal: 48]. Thus the promises of the enemy of Allah to them became delusion when they needed him, ﴿like a mirage in a level desert, which the thirsty one thinks is water until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing, and finds Allah with him, and He pays him in full his account﴾ [Surah al-Nur: 39]. [["Qawluhu: 'adw Allah' is in the accusative of censure, and it separates the verbal noun from its object."]]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Those, their refuge is Hell, and they will find no escape from it﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying "Those" (ulā'ika), He, may His praise be exalted, means those who took Satan as a guardian besides Allah. "Their refuge is Hell" means their destination, the place to which they will return, is Hell. [See the explanation of "al-ma'wā" (refuge) above, 7:279, 494.] "And they will find no escape from it" means: they will not find, when Allah brings them to it on the Day of Resurrection, any way of turning away from Hell (ma'dil) that they can take.

* *

It is said of this: "ḥāṣa fulān 'an hādhā al-amr yaḥīṣu ḥaysan wa ḥuyūṣan" (حاص فلان عن هذا الأمر يحيص حيصًا وحيوصًا), meaning that he turned away from the matter.

From this is the report of Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent a detachment (sariyya) in which I was, and we met the polytheists, and we "ḥiṣnā ḥayṣa" (حصنا حيصة), meaning we turned away in flight. [In the printed edition: "bi'athanā rasūl Allāh" (we were sent by the Messenger of Allah), but the correct reading is from the manuscript. I was not able to locate the rest of Ibn 'Umar's report, although I think it is well known.] Some of them said: "fajāḍū jayḍa" (فجاضوا جيضة). The words "ḥayṣ" (حيص) and "jayḍ" (جيض) are close in meaning. [In the printed and manuscript editions, the diacritical points on "jāḍa" and "ḥāṣa" were misplaced; I have restored them to their correct form.]

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And those who believe and do righteous deeds – We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. The promise of Allah is true, and who is more truthful than Allah in statement?﴾ (4:122)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, "And those who believe and do righteous deeds," the Exalted means: those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger as true, and acknowledged to Him the oneness (tawhid), and to His Messenger (ﷺ) the prophethood, "and do righteous deeds," meaning: they performed the obligations of Allah which He had enjoined upon them [[See the explanation of "doing righteous deeds" in what has preceded: 8:488.]]. "We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow," meaning: We will surely admit them on the Day of Resurrection, when they come to Allah, as a recompense for what they did of righteous deeds in this world. "Gardens" means orchards [[See the explanation of "gardens" under the root (j-n-n) in the earlier language indexes.]]. "Beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever," meaning: remaining in these gardens which He has described. [[See the explanation of "abiding" (khulud) in the earlier language indexes.]] "Forever," meaning: perpetually.

And His saying, "The promise of Allah is true," means: a promise from Allah to them of this in the world, "true," meaning: a sure and truthful certainty, unlike the false promise of Satan, which is a delusion to whoever is promised it from among his allies. Rather, it is a promise from One who does not lie, and from whom falsehood does not come, [[In the printed edition: "But the promise ..."; I have retained what is in the manuscript.]] and who does not break His promise.

The Exalted described His promise as true and certain in this verse only because of what preceded of the report of the Exalted concerning the words of Satan, which He related in His saying: "And he said, 'I will surely take from among Your servants a specified portion. And I will mislead them, and I will arouse in them desires, and I will command them so they will slit the ears of cattle'" (4:118–119). Then the Exalted said: "He promises them and arouses desires in them, but Satan does not promise them except delusion" (4:120). But Allah promises those who believe and do righteous deeds that He will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever, a promise from Him that is true, unlike the promise of Satan whose attribute He described.

Thus the Exalted described the two promises and the two promisers, and informed of the ruling for the people of each promise, as a reminder from Him to His creation of what contains their benefit and their deliverance from destruction and ruin [[In the printed edition: "wal-'atab," which is correct; in the manuscript: "wal-'atbah," and I preferred to write it as I judged its reading to be. The plural of al-ma'tab and al-ma'tabah is ma'athib.]], so that they would refrain from disobeying Him and act in obedience to Him, and thereby attain what He has prepared for them of His reward in His gardens.

Then the Exalted said to them: "And who is more truthful than Allah in statement?" That is: O people, who is more truthful in statement than Allah? No one is more truthful in statement than Him! So how can you abandon acting upon what your Lord has promised you for acting upon it – gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever – while you disbelieve in it, oppose His command, and you know that no one is more truthful in statement than He, yet you act upon what Satan commands you, hoping to attain what he promises you of his false enticements and vain desires, while you know that his enticements are delusion, having neither soundness nor reality? And you take him as a protector besides Allah, and you refrain from obeying Allah in what He commands you and forbids you, so that you become His allies?

* *

The meaning of "al-qiyl" (statement) and "al-qawl" (saying) is one and the same.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 123 (part 1 of 3):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed concerning those who were meant by His saying: "It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book."

Some of them said: By His saying "It is not by your wishful thinking" is meant the people of Islam.

Mention of those who said that:

10490 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: The Christians and the people of Islam boasted, and these said: "We are better than you!" and those said: "We are better than you!" He said: So Allah revealed: "It is not by your wishful thinking nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book."
