10506 - Ibn WakI' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say: "It is not by your wishful thinking nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book," the verse, he said: It was revealed concerning the People of the Book when they opposed the Prophet (ﷺ). [[Report 10506: in the printed edition: "My father narrated to us, from Abu Usayd," and I do not know where this came from! In the manuscript: "My father Sufyan narrated to us," and the correct reading is "from Sufyan," who is al-Thawri. This is a chain that has passed similarly.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of the two interpretations is what Mujahid said: that by His saying "It is not by your wishful thinking" is meant the polytheists of Quraysh.

We say this is more correct because the Muslims were not mentioned in regard to their wishful thinking in the verses preceding His saying "It is not by your wishful thinking." Rather, mention had passed of the wishful thinking of the portion of Satan that is prescribed, in His saying: "And I will surely mislead them and I will surely arouse in them desires, and I will surely order them so they will slit the ears of cattle" and His saying: "He promises them and arouses in them desires." So linking the meaning of His saying, "It is not by your wishful thinking," to what has been mentioned before is more right and more fitting than claiming an interpretation for it for which there is no indication in the apparent meaning of the revelation, nor any report from the Messenger (ﷺ), nor a consensus of the interpreters.

Since this is so, the interpretation of the verse is therefore: The matter is not by your wishful thinking, O company of the allies of Satan and his party, which your protector, the enemy of Allah, arouses in you, of rescuing you from those who want evil for you, and of your being victorious over them and prevailing against them; nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book, who said, through deception regarding Allah and His forbearance toward them: "The Fire will not touch us except for a number of days" and "None will enter Paradise except he who was a Jew or a Christian." Indeed, Allah will recompense every doer among you, and among others, according to his deed: whoever of you does evil, will be recompensed for it, and he will not find for himself, besides Allah, any protector or helper. And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer, those will enter Paradise.

What also indicates the correctness of what we have said concerning its interpretation, and that by His saying "It is not by your wishful thinking" is meant the polytheists of the Arabs, as Mujahid said, is that Allah described the promise of Satan to his allies and reported the state of his promise, then He followed that with the description of His true promise by His saying: "And those who believed and did righteous deeds, We will surely admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever; the promise of Allah is true." He, may His praise be exalted, mentioned along with His description of Satan's promise to his allies, his arousing of desires in them by His saying: [[In the printed edition: "and his arousing" with a waw, and the correct reading omits it as in the manuscript, because the meaning of the statement is the mention of their arousal of desires along with the description of Satan's promise.]] "He promises them and arouses in them desires," just as He mentioned his promise to them. So the more fitting is that his arousing of desires in them be followed by a description similar to that which followed his promise to them.

Since this is so, it is established that His saying: "It is not by your wishful thinking nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book; whoever does evil will be recompensed for it," the verse, is only a report from Allah concerning the desires of the allies of Satan, and what their desires lead to, together with their evil deeds, of evil recompense, and what the deeds of the allies of Allah lead to, of good recompense. Allah, may His praise be exalted, joined the People of the Book with the polytheists in His saying "It is not by your wishful thinking nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book" because the desires of both groups are from the arousing of Satan, whom He promised to arouse in them by His saying: "And I will surely mislead them and I will surely arouse in them desires and I will surely order them."

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters differed concerning the interpretation of that.

Some of them said: By "evil" (al-su') is meant every disobedience to Allah. They said: The meaning of the verse is: whoever commits a minor or major sin, from a believer or an unbeliever, of the acts of disobedience to Allah, Allah will recompense him for it.

Mention of those who said that:

10507 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: that al-Rabi' ibn Ziyad asked Ubayy ibn Ka'b about this verse: "Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it," and he said: "I did not think you were more learned in understanding than I see! [It is] the stumbling, the return, and the scratch." [[Report 10507: "Al-Rabi' ibn Ziyad ibn Anas al-Harithi" narrated from Ubayy ibn Ka'b and Ka'b al-Ahbar. Abu Mijlaz, Mutarrif ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir, and Hafsah bint Sirin narrated from him. Neither Ibn Abi Hatim nor al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar mentioned Qatadah's narration from him. Al-Bukhari mentioned it, saying: "Rabi' ibn Ziyad heard Ubayy ibn Ka'b ('Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it'). Mu'adh ibn Fudalah narrated from Hisham, from Qatadah, that al-Rabi'... and Hafsah said from al-Rabi' ibn Ziyad: he heard Ka'b."
Al-Bukhari mentioned no criticism of him. Al-Rabi' was the agent of Mu'awiyah over Khurasan. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib, al-Kabir of al-Bukhari 2/1/245, and Ibn Abi Hatim 1/2/460.
In the printed edition and the manuscript, and in al-Durr al-Manthur, it was "Ziyad ibn al-Rabi'," which is an error; the correct form will come in the following report, and this is shown by what al-Bukhari also narrated in al-Kabir. I have therefore corrected it.
This report was indicated by al-Bukhari as you have seen, and al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:227, and added its attribution to Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Abi al-Dunya, and al-Bayhaqi.
"Al-Nakbah" is what befalls a man when he is struck by a stone he collided with. In the hadith: "his finger was struck (nakabat)," meaning the stones reached it and hit it.]]

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 123 (part 2 of 3):**

10508. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Ghundar narrated to us, from Hisham al-Dastuwā'ī, who said: Qatādah narrated to us, from al-Rabī' ibn Ziyād, who said: I said to Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "The saying of Allah, blessed and exalted is He: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾. By Allah, if we were recompensed for everything we did, we would be destroyed!" He said: "By Allah, I used to think you were more discerning than what I see! No man is struck by a scratch or a stumble except for a sin, and what Allah pardons is far more numerous, even the sting and the kick." [[The report: 10508. "Al-Rabī' ibn Ziyād": see the note on the earlier report. This report is the one al-Bukhārī referred to in al-Tārīkh al-Kabīr, as I mentioned in the earlier note.
"Al-nafḥah" with an unpointed ḥā', as if it derives from "nafakhat al-dābbah bi-rijlihā," when the animal kicks with its leg. In the ḥadīth of Shurayḥ: "He nullified the nafḥ," meaning the kick of an animal with its leg, which is the rafs (kick).]]

10509. Al-Qāsim ibn Bishr ibn Ma'rūf narrated to us, saying: Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb narrated to us, saying: Ḥammād ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ḥajjāj al-Ṣawwāf, from Ayyūb, from Abū Qilābah, from Abū al-Muhallab, who said: I entered upon 'Ā'ishah, wishing to ask her about this verse: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor the wishful thinking of the People of the Book; whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾. She said: "That is what befalls you in this world." [[The report: 10509. "Al-Qāsim ibn Bishr ibn Ma'rūf" is a teacher of al-Ṭabarī, and his narration from him will come under no. 10531. He is narrated from many times in al-Tārīkh 1: 12, 23, 28, 29, 32, 106 / 2: 19, and in this place in al-Tārīkh he said: "Al-Qāsim ibn Bishr ibn Ma'rūf narrated to me, from Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb."
I have not found a biography of him except in Tārīkh Baghdād 12: 427: "Al-Qāsim ibn Bishr ibn Aḥmad ibn Ma'rūf, Abū Muḥammad al-Baghdādī," who heard Yaḥyā ibn Sulaym al-Ṭā'ifī, Sufyān ibn 'Uyaynah, and Abū Dāwūd al-Ṭayālisī. I fear that he is al-Ṭabarī's teacher, and I hope that something will come later that indicates the correct reading.
In the printed and manuscript copies here it reads "al-Qāsim ibn Bishr ibn Ma'rūr," and al-Ṭabarī's chain in the manuscript of the Tafsīr, in what will come under no. 10531, and in the Tārīkh, shows the correct form.
"Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb ibn Bujayl al-Azdī" settled in Mecca and was its judge. He narrated from Shu'bah, Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥah ibn Muṣarrif, the two Ḥammāds, and Jarīr ibn Ḥāzim. al-Bukhārī and Abū Dāwūd narrated from him, and the rest narrated from him through Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah, 'Alī ibn Naṣr al-Jahḍamī, 'Amr ibn 'Alī al-Fallās, and others. He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb.
"Abū al-Muhallab" is "Mu'āwiyah ibn 'Amr" or "'Amr ibn Mu'āwiyah," his name being disputed; he was the paternal uncle of Abū Qilābah al-Jarmī. He narrated from 'Umar, 'Uthmān, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and others among the Companions. He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb.
al-Ḥākim recorded it in al-Mustadrak 2: 308 by way of Sulaymān ibn Ḥarb, and al-Dhahabī put the sign (kh, m), meaning that it meets the conditions of Muslim and al-Bukhārī.]]

10510. Al-Qāsim narrated to us, saying: al-Ḥusayn narrated to us, saying: Ḥajjāj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Khālid informed me that he heard Mujāhid say about His saying: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾: "He will be recompensed for it in this world." I said: "And what do calamities reach?" He said: "What you dislike."

Yaḥyā ibn Abī Ṭālib narrated to me, saying: Yazīd informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, meaning by that: the Jews, the Christians, the Magians, and the disbelievers of the Arabs. ﴿And they will not find for themselves besides Allah any protector or helper.﴾

Others said: The meaning of "evil" (al-sū') in this place is: polytheism. They said: The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ is: whoever associates partners with Allah will be recompensed for his association. ﴿And he will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper.﴾

Those who said that:

10518. al-Muthannā narrated to me, saying: 'Abd Allāh ibn Ṣāliḥ narrated to us, saying: Mu'āwiyah narrated to me, from 'Alī, from Ibn 'Abbās, his statement: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, he says: "Whoever associates partners will be recompensed for it"—and this is "evil." ﴿And he will not find for himself besides Allah any protector or helper﴾, except that he repents before his death, and then Allah relents toward him.

10519. Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Ḥakkām narrated to us, from 'Anbasah, from Ibn Abī Laylā, from al-Minhāl ibn 'Amr, from Sa'īd ibn Jubayr: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, he said: "Polytheism."

* *

Abū Ja'far [al-Ṭabarī] said: The most preferable of the interpretations we have mentioned regarding the explanation of the verse is the interpretation we have mentioned from Ubayy ibn Ka'b and 'Ā'ishah: that everyone who does evil, small or great, whether a believer or a disbeliever, will be recompensed for it.

We said that this is more preferable as the interpretation of the verse, because of the generality of the verse, "every doer of evil," without specifying or excepting any one of them. It stands in its generality, since there is no indication in the verse that it is specific, nor has any proof been established for that from a report from the Messenger (ﷺ).

* *

If someone says: What about the saying of Allah: ﴿If you avoid the major sins which you are forbidden, We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾? [Sūrat al-Nisā': 31] How is it permissible that He would recompense for what He has promised to expiate? It is said: He did not promise, by His saying "We will remove from you your misdeeds," to abandon the recompense for them. He only promised expiation by refraining from disgracing their owners on the Day of Return, just as He disgraces the people of polytheism and hypocrisy. As for when He recompenses them for these in this world with calamities in order to expiate them for them, so that they meet Him with no sin deserving recompense, He has indeed fulfilled His promise to them in His saying "We will remove from you your misdeeds," and carried out for them what He guaranteed them in His saying: ﴿And those who believed and did righteous deeds—We will admit them to gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾. [Sūrat al-Nisā': 122]

* *

In a manner similar to what we have said regarding this, the reports from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) have come in agreement.

The reports related concerning that:

10520. Abū Kurayb, Sufyān ibn Wakī', Naṣr ibn 'Alī, and 'Abd Allāh ibn Abī Ziyād al-Qaṭawānī narrated to us, saying: Sufyān ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Muḥayṣin, from Muḥammad ibn Qays ibn Makhramah, from Abū Hurayrah, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, it weighed heavily upon the Muslims and affected them as much as Allah willed. They complained of that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he said: "Draw near and be steadfast. For every affliction that a Muslim is struck with there is an expiation, even the thorn-prick he is pricked by, or the thorn that pricks him." [[The report: 10520. "Naṣr ibn 'Alī" is al-Jahḍamī, passed under nos. 2861 and 2376. "'Abd Allāh ibn Abī Ziyād al-Qaṭawānī" passed under no. 5796.
"Ibn Muḥayṣin" is 'Umar ibn 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn Muḥayṣin al-Sahmī al-Qurashī, from the people of Mecca. See the rest of his biography and its sources in the commentary on Musnad Aḥmad.
"Muḥammad ibn Qays ibn Makhramah ibn al-Muṭṭalib ibn 'Abd Manāf," a reliable Successor (tābi'ī). See the commentary on the Musnad. In the manuscript and the printed edition it read "Muḥammad ibn Qays 'an Makhramah," which is a clear error.
This report was narrated with this chain by Aḥmad in his Musnad: 7380, and my brother al-Sayyid Aḥmad fully completed the commentary on it. I add that al-Bayhaqī recorded it in al-Sunan 3: 373.
"Al-nakbah": it is a stone striking the finger when a man stumbles a stumble, or whatever it may be.]]

10521. 'Abd Allāh ibn Abī Ziyād and Aḥmad ibn Manṣūr al-Ramādī narrated to me, both saying: Zayd ibn Ḥabbāb narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ḥārithī narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn Zayd ibn Qunfudh narrated to us, from 'Ā'ishah, from Abū Bakr, who said: When this was revealed: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, Abū Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we be held to account for everything we do?" He said: "O Abū Bakr, does not what befalls you such-and-such? That is its expiation." [[The report: 10521. "'Abd Allāh ibn Abī Ziyād al-Qaṭawānī" passed in no. 10520.
"Aḥmad ibn Manṣūr al-Ramādī," his biography passed under no. 10260.
"Zayd ibn Ḥabbāb al-'Ukalī" passed under nos. 2185, 5350, 8165. In the printed edition it read "Yazīd ibn Ḥayyān," which is a clear error; the correct form is from the manuscript.
"'Abd al-Malik ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abī Ḥakīm al-Ḥārithī," also said to be "al-Jārī," "Abū Marwān al-Aḥwal." Aḥmad said: "There is no harm in him," and Ibn Ma'īn said: "Reliable." He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb. "Muḥammad ibn Zayd ibn Qunfudh" is "Muḥammad ibn Zayd ibn al-Muhājir ibn Qunfudh al-Taymī al-Jadʿānī al-Qurashī," who saw Ibn 'Umar once. Ibn 'Umar died in the year 73, and 'Ā'ishah, Mother of the Believers, died in the year 58, so he certainly did not meet her, and his narration from her is discontinuous (munqaṭi'). He is biographed in al-Tahdhīb, al-Kabīr 1/1/84, and Ibn Abī Ḥātim 3/2/255.
This report was mentioned by Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr 2: 587, and by al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr 2: 266, and they did not attribute it to anyone other than Ibn Jarīr.]]

10522. Ibrāhīm ibn Sa'īd al-Jawharī narrated to me, saying: 'Abd al-Wahhāb ibn 'Aṭā' narrated to us, from Ziyād al-Jaṣṣāṣ, from 'Alī ibn Zayd, from Mujāhid, who said: 'Abd Allāh ibn 'Umar narrated to me, that he heard Abū Bakr say: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it" in this world. [[The report: 10522. "Ibrāhīm ibn Sa'īd al-Jawharī al-Ṭabarī" passed under nos. 3355, 3959.
"'Abd al-Wahhāb ibn 'Aṭā' al-Khaffāf" passed under nos. 5429, 5432.
"Ziyād ibn Abī Ziyād al-Jaṣṣāṣ" is very weak, of no value.
"'Alī ibn Zayd" is Ibn Jud'ān: reliable, but poor in memory. Passed under nos. 40, 4897, 6495.
This report was narrated by Aḥmad in al-Musnad: 23, and my brother al-Sayyid Aḥmad said: "Its chain is weak." Ibn Kathīr took it out in his Tafsīr 2: 587, in extended form, from Abū Bakr ibn Mardawayh, from Muḥammad ibn Hishām ibn Juhaymah, from Yaḥyā ibn Abī Ṭālib, from 'Abd al-Wahhāb ibn 'Aṭā'; then he said: "Abū Bakr al-Bazzār also narrated it in his Musnad from al-Faḍl ibn Sahl, from 'Abd al-Wahhāb ibn 'Aṭā', in abridged form."
al-Suyūṭī took it out in al-Durr al-Manthūr 2: 266, and added its attribution to al-Khaṭīb in al-Muttafiq wa-al-Muftariq.]]

10523. Ibn Ḥumayd narrated to us, saying: Ḥakkām narrated to us, from Ismā'īl, from Abū Bakr ibn Abī Zuhayr, from Abū Bakr al-Ṣiddīq, that he said: "O Prophet of Allah, what is the remedy after this verse?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Which verse?" He said: Allah says: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor the wishful thinking of the People of the Book; whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾. "So, what we do, are we recompensed for it?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May Allah forgive you, O Abū Bakr! Do you not fall ill? Do you not grieve? Does not hardship (al-la'ā') befall you?" He said: "That is what you are recompensed for!" [[The report: 10523. This report and what follows it up to no. 10528 are six chains for a single report, and their discussion will come at the end.
"Al-la'ā'": hardship, straitness of livelihood, and difficulty.]]

10524. Yūnus narrated to us, saying: Sufyān narrated to us, from Ismā'īl ibn Abī Khālid—he said: "I think it is from Abū Bakr al-Thaqafī, from Abū Bakr," who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, Abū Bakr said: "What is the remedy?"—then he mentioned something similar, except that he added in it: "Are you not stricken (tunkab)?" [[The report: 10524. This report is missing from the manuscript.
"Nakaba al-rajul yunkabu," in the passive voice: a stone struck him and cut his finger or nail.]]

10525. Ya'qūb ibn Ibrāhīm narrated to me, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Ismā'īl ibn Abī Khālid narrated to us, from Abū Bakr ibn Abī Zuhayr, that Abū Bakr said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "What is the remedy?" Then he mentioned the like of it. [[In the printed edition: "fa-dhakara naḥwahu," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]]

10526. Muḥammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Muḥāribī narrated to me, saying: Abū Mālik al-Janbī narrated to us, from Ismā'īl ibn Abī Khālid, from Abū Bakr ibn Abī Zuhayr al-Thaqafī, who said: Abū Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah," then he mentioned something similar—except that he said: "So every evil we have done, are we recompensed for it?" And he also said: "Do you not fall ill? Do you not become weary?" ["Naṣiba al-rajul yanṣabu naṣban" (the verbal noun with vowels): he was exhausted and became tired.] "Do you not grieve? Does hardship not befall you?" He said: "Yes." He said: "That is what you are recompensed for!"

10527. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Ibn Abī Khālid, from Abū Bakr ibn Abī Zuhayr al-Thaqafī, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿It is not by your wishful thinking, nor the wishful thinking of the People of the Book; whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, Abū Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we really be recompensed for everything we do?" He said: "O Abū Bakr, do you not become weary? Do you not grieve? Does hardship not befall you? That is among what you are recompensed for."

10528. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Sa'īd narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abī Khālid narrated to us, saying: Abū Bakr ibn Abī Zuhayr al-Thaqafī narrated to me, from Abū Bakr, [[In the printed edition: "fa-dhakara mithla dhālika"; I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]] then he mentioned the like of it. [[The reports 10523–10528: a single report. "Abū Bakr ibn Abī Zuhayr al-Thaqafī" is one of the junior Successors; he is unknown (mastūr), not mentioned for either criticism or praise. For this reason my brother al-Sayyid Aḥmad said in the Musnad, no. 68: "Its chain is weak because of its discontinuity." Then he said: "al-Ḥākim authenticated it, and al-Dhahabī agreed with him, and that is strange from both of them, for its chain is clearly discontinuous."
It was narrated by Aḥmad in the Musnad: 68–71, al-Bayhaqī in al-Sunan 3: 373, and al-Ḥākim in al-Mustadrak 3: 74, 75. Ibn Kathīr took it out in his Tafsīr 2: 587, and al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr 2: 266, and he attributed it additionally to Hannād, 'Abd ibn Ḥumayd, al-Ḥakīm al-Tirmidhī, Abū Ya'lā, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Ḥibbān, Ibn al-Sunnī in 'Amal al-Yawm wa-al-Laylah, and al-Bayhaqī in Shu'ab al-Īmān.]]

10529. Abū al-Sā'ib and Sufyān ibn Wakī' narrated to us, both saying: Abū Mu'āwiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim, who said: Abū Bakr said: "O Messenger of Allah, how severe is this verse: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾?" He said: "O Abū Bakr, indeed the affliction in this world is a recompense." [[The report: 10529. "Abū Mu'āwiyah" is "Muḥammad ibn Khāzim al-Tamīmī," Abū Mu'āwiyah al-Ḍarīr, passed under no. 2783.
"Al-A'mash" is "Sulaymān ibn Mihrān," passed under nos. 2918, 3295, 8207, 8208. "Muslim" is "Muslim ibn Ṣubayḥ al-Hamdānī," passed under nos. 5424, 7216, 8206.
This report was taken out by Ibn Kathīr in his Tafsīr 2: 588, from Ibn Mardawayh: "Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Isḥāq al-'Askarī narrated to us, saying: Muḥammad ibn 'Āmir al-Sa'dī narrated to us, saying: Yaḥyā ibn Yaḥyā narrated to us, saying: Faḍḍīl ibn 'Iyāḍ narrated to us, from Sulaymān ibn Mihrān, from Muslim ibn Ṣubayḥ, from Masrūq, who said: Abū Bakr said," and he related the report at greater length than here, and with a different wording.
al-Suyūṭī took it out in al-Durr al-Manthūr 2: 226, 227, with Ibn Mardawayh's wording, from Masrūq from Abū Bakr, and attributed it to Ibn Jarīr, Abū Nu'aym in al-Ḥilyah, Hannād, and Sa'īd ibn Manṣūr.]]

But the report of al-Tabari does not mention "Masruq." He is Masruq ibn al-Ajda' al-Wada'i al-Hamdani, and he passed earlier under numbers 242 and 7216. I fear that the name "Masruq" fell out of this chain through the copyists.

10530. Ibn WakI' related to us, saying: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah related to us, saying: Abu 'Amir al-Khazzaz related to us, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah, who said: I said: "Indeed I know which verse in the Book of God is the most severe." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to me: "Which verse?" I said: "﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾." He said: "Indeed the believer is recompensed for the worst of his deeds in this world." Then he mentioned other things, including illness and fatigue, and the last of them was that he mentioned the *nakbah* [[In the printed edition: "an dhikr al-nakbah," and I have preferred what is in the manuscript. "Al-nakbah," as I have already explained, is when a stone strikes a person's finger or nail.]], and he said: "Everyone is recompensed for his deed, O 'A'ishah. Indeed, no one will be called to account on the Day of Resurrection without being punished." I said: "Does not God say: ﴿He will be called to a light reckoning﴾ [Surah al-Inshiqaq: 8]?" He said: "That is at the presentation. Whoever is subjected to a close reckoning (*munaqashah*) will be punished." [["Naqasahu al-hisab munaqashah" means he thoroughly investigated his reckoning until nothing of it was left, from the expression "naqsh al-shawkah," when one thoroughly extracts a thorn from the body.]] He [the Prophet] said this and gestured with his hand on his finger, as if he were pricking it [[The phrase "qala bi-yadihi" means he pointed with it and gestured. The word "qal" is used in several meanings. In the printed edition it reads "ka'annahu yanktuhu," without the final ha', and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which agrees with what comes later in the tafsir, 30:84 (Bulaq), where this report is related in abridged form.]], as if he were pricking it.

[[Report 10530: "Rawh ibn 'Ubadah al-Qaysi" is trustworthy; his biography has passed under numbers 3015, 3355, 3912. "Abu 'Amir al-Khazzaz" is Salih ibn Rustum al-Muzani, who passed under numbers 5458, 6371, 6383, 6384, 6387, 6614. "Al-Khazzaz" is written with dotted letters; in the printed edition it appeared as "al-Kharraz," and in the manuscript it is undotted. "Ibn Abi Mulaykah" is 'Abd Allah ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah, who heard 'A'ishah and other Companions. He passed under numbers 6605 and 6610. All the men in this report are trustworthy. It will come under number 10532, through the route of Hushaym from Abu 'Amir al-Khazzaz, with a different wording in abridged form.

Al-Bukhari related it with a different wording through the route of Sa'id ibn Abi Maryam, from Nafi' ibn 'Umar, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah (Fath al-Bari 1:176).

He then related it (Fath 8:535) with a different wording through three routes: through Yahya al-Qattan, from 'Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah; then through Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ayyub, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah; then through Yahya, from Abu Yunus Hatim ibn Abi Saghirah, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'A'ishah. Then he returned and related it (Fath 11:347, 348) through seven routes. The hafiz Ibn Hajar fully discussed it in these three places of the Sahih of al-Bukhari.

Muslim related it in his Sahih (17:208) through four routes: through Ibn 'Ulayyah, from Ayyub, from 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah; and through Hammad ibn Zayd, from Ayyub, with this isnad, in similar wording; and through Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, from Abu Yunus al-Qushayri, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from al-Qasim, from 'A'ishah; and through Yahya al-Qattan, from 'Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah, with the same wording as the report of Abu Yunus.

Abu Dawud related it in his Sunan (3:250, no. 3093), with a different wording, through the route of 'Uthman ibn 'Umar, from Abu 'Amir al-Khazzaz, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah.

Al-Tirmidhi related it in abridged form in the chapter "What has come concerning the presentation" and in the chapter "Tafsir of Surah al-Inshiqaq," through the route of 'Uthman ibn al-Aswad, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from 'A'ishah, and he said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith."

It will come in the tafsir of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari), through several routes in the tafsir of Surah al-Inshiqaq (30:74, Bulaq), and we will discuss its chains there.

Ibn Kathir abridged it in his tafsir (2:589), and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (2:227), and both shortened its attribution, but al-Suyuti added its attribution to Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi.

His saying "yanktuhu" comes from the expression "nakata al-ard bi-qadib aw bi-isba'": that is, he struck the ground with the tip of it until it left an impression. It is a sign of *munaqashah* (close reckoning), which, as we have already noted, is a thorough reckoning, as if the reckoner were digging out a thorn that has lodged beneath the skin, so he extracts it from within the flesh. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "This is how a person is treated when he is subjected to close reckoning and his sins are thoroughly examined."]]

10531. al-Qasim ibn Bishr ibn Ma'ruf related to me, saying: Sulayman ibn Harb related to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Umayyah, who said: I asked 'A'ishah about this verse: ﴿Whether you show what is in your souls or conceal it, God will call you to account for it﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 284], and "not by your wishful thinking nor the wishful thinking of the People of the Book; whoever does evil will be recompensed for it." She said: No one has asked me about it since I asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about it [[In the Musnad of Ahmad (6:218) it reads "'anhuma" (about them both), which is better, but "'anha" (about it) in the singular is what is found in the manuscript, and there is no harm in that in Arabic.]], and he said: "O 'A'ishah, that is the *mathabah* of God toward His servant for what befalls him of fever and grief, [[In the printed edition it reads "mathabat Allah al-'abd" without the lam before "al-'abd," and I have kept what is in the manuscript. In the manuscript "mathabah" is clearly dotted. It has already appeared in report 6495 as "mutabi'ah Allah al-'abd," and similarly in the Musnad (6:218), and in al-Tayalisi (221) as "mu'atabah" (reproach).
If what is in the manuscript is correct, it seems a good reading. "Al-mathabah" comes from "thaba ilayhi yathubu," meaning he returned. He says: that is God's return to the servant with forgiveness. This is the meaning of "al-thawab," which also means recompense. That is, this is God's recompense to His servant.
The explanation of "al-mutabi'ah" and "al-mu'atabah" has already been given under number 6495, so refer to it.]] and the one who puts his money in his sleeve and then loses it, and then grieves for it and finds it in his sleeve, [[Here it reads "fa-yajiduha fi kummihi" (he finds it in his sleeve). In report 6495 it reads "fi dabnihi" (in his side-pocket), and in al-Tayalisi (221) "fi jaybihi" (in his pocket), and these are close to one another. The rest of the report differs somewhat in wording.]] until the believer emerges from his sins as red gold emerges from the furnace. [[This report was related above under number 6495, through the route of al-Rabi', from Asad ibn Musa, from Hammad ibn Salamah, in similar wording, with slight variation in its wording. My brother al-Sayyid Ahmad has already fully traced it there, and I explained its words and rare vocabulary there.]]

10532. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Hushaym related to us, saying: Abu 'Amir al-Khazzaz informed us, saying: Ibn Abi Mulaykah related to us, from 'A'ishah, who said: I said: "O Messenger of God, indeed I know the most severe verse in the Qur'an!" He said: "What is it, O 'A'ishah?" I said: "It is this verse, O Messenger of God: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾." He said: "It is what befalls the believing servant, even the *nakbah* that strikes him." [[This report's chain was traced under number 10530. Here too in the printed edition it read "al-Kharraz" with a *ra'*, and the correct form is what I have given.]]

10533. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from al-Rabi' ibn Subayh, from 'Ata', who said: When it was revealed, "Not by your wishful thinking nor the wishful thinking of the People of the Book; whoever does evil will be recompensed for it," Abu Bakr said: "O Messenger of God, how severe is this verse!" He said: "O Abu Bakr, you fall ill, you grieve, and harm befalls you; that is its recompense." [[This report is *mursal*: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah did not hear Abu Bakr. "Al-Rabi' ibn Subayh al-Sa'di," whose biography has passed under numbers 6403, 6404, 7482, 7603, and he is weak. Al-Bukhari included him in al-Kabir (2/1/254).
In the printed edition and the manuscript it read "ibn Subh," which is a pure error.]]

10534. al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah informed me, who said: When it was revealed, Abu Bakr said: "The back-breaking calamity has come!" The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "It is only the calamities of this world." [[This report is *mursal*. I have not found it elsewhere.]]

* *

The explanation of His saying: ﴿And he will not find for himself, besides God, any protector or helper﴾ [Surah al-Nisa': 123]

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: and the one who does evil, by disobeying God and contravening what He commanded him, will not find "besides God" — that is, apart from God and other than Him — "a protector" who takes charge of his affair and shields him from the punishment of God that befalls him, "nor a helper," that is, a helper who supports him against what descends upon him of God's punishment and His painful retribution. [[For the explanation of "min dun" (besides), see what has passed earlier, p. 211, note 1, and the references there. For the explanation of "wali" (protector), see what has passed earlier, p. 205, note 1, and the references there. For the explanation of "nasir" (helper), see what has passed earlier, p. 18, note 2, and the references there.]]

Discussion of the words of Allah: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer – those will enter Paradise and will not be wronged, [even] as much as a speck (naqir).﴾ (4:124)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means those to whom He said: "It is not by your wishful thinking, nor by the wishful thinking of the People of the Book" [Qur'an 4:123]. Allah says to them: Only he who does righteous deeds from among your males and females, and the males and females of My servants, while he is a believer in Me and in My Messenger Muhammad, affirming My oneness and the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he brought from Me, will enter Paradise and be blessed therein in the Hereafter – not you, O polytheists, who associate others with Me and deny My Messenger. So do not hope to be granted the status of the believers in Me, and enter their dwellings on the Day of Resurrection, while you are disbelievers and deniers of My Messenger. As:

10535 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words: "And whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer," he said: He refused to accept faith except with righteous deeds, and He refused to accept Islam except with excellence (ihsan).

* *

As for His words: "and they will not be wronged [even] as much as a speck (naqir)," it means: Allah will not wrong those who do righteous deeds in the reward of their deeds by the amount of the naqir, which is the small pit that is in the back of a date stone, in its smallness; so how much less than that or more? Allah, may His praise be exalted, only informs His servants that He will not diminish from the recompense of their deeds anything, little or much, but will pay them in full as He promised them. [See the explanation of "naqir" above: 8:472–475.]

* *

And according to what we have said regarding the meaning of "naqir," the people of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) have said.

Mention of those who said that:

10536 – Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Mujahid: "and they will not be wronged [even] as much as a speck (naqir)," he said: The naqir is that which is in the back of the date stone.

10537 – Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, saying: Qurrah narrated to us, from 'Atiyyah, who said: The naqir is that which is in the middle of the date stone. [From his words "And according to what we have said regarding the meaning of naqir" to the end of this report is missing from the manuscript. These two reports, 10536 and 10537, were not mentioned there (8:472–475) among the reports in which the explanation of "naqir" appeared. This is one of the forms of Abu Ja'far's abridgment of his tafsir.]

* *

If someone asks us: What is the purpose of the particle "min" (from) in His words "And whoever does [min] righteous deeds," when He did not say "And whoever does righteous deeds"?

It is said: Its inclusion has two aspects:

The first: That Allah knew that His believing servants would not be able to perform all the righteous deeds, so He made His promise binding for whoever does what he is able to of them, and does not deprive him of His bounty because of what his strength failed to perform of them. [In the manuscript: "minha qawlahu" (منها قوله), and above "qawlahu" is written "kadha" (كذا), as evidence that it was so in the original from which the copyist transcribed. The correct reading is what is given here. In the printed edition: "qawāhu" (قواه) in the plural, which is also good.]

The other of the two: That He, exalted is His remembrance, made His promise binding for whoever avoids the major sins and performs the obligatory duties, even if he falls short in some of what is obligatory upon him, as a bounty from Him to His believing servants, since bounty is more fitting from Him and pardon toward the people of faith is more deserving.

* *

Some people of Arabic grammar have claimed [in the manuscript the word "qawm" (people) is absent; its inclusion is acceptable, and this is the view some Basran scholars held, as he indicated repeatedly earlier] that it was inserted in this place with the meaning of omission (al-hadhf), and they interpret it as: "And whoever does the righteous deeds, whether male or female, while he is a believer." [See the insertion of "min" in negation and affirmation earlier: 2:126, 127, 442, 470 / 5:586 / 6:551 / 7:489.]

This, in my view, is not permissible, because its insertion carries a meaning, so it is not permissible that its meaning be omission.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth?﴾

Abu Ja'far said: This is a judgment from Allah, may His praise be exalted, in favor of Islam and its adherents, preferring them over all other religions and their adherents. Allah says: "And who is better in religion" O people, "and more correct in path, and more rightly guided in way," "than one who submits his face to Allah" — that is, than one who surrenders his face to Allah, submitting to Him in obedience, affirming His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) in what he brought from his Lord [[See the explanation of "submits his face" above, 2:510-512 / 6:280.]], "while being a doer of good" — meaning: while acting in accordance with what his Lord has commanded him, making lawful what He has made lawful and unlawful what He has made unlawful [[See the explanation of "ihsan" in the index of linguistic terms above.]], "and follows the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth" — meaning by this: and follows the religion that Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, held, and that he commanded his descendants after him and enjoined upon them [[See the explanation of "millah" above, 2:563 / 3:104.]], "inclining toward truth" — meaning: upright upon his method and way.

* *

We have already explained the disagreement of those who differ concerning the meaning of "hanif" earlier, and the evidence for the correct view on that, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. [[See the explanation of "hanif" above, 3:104-108 / 6:494.]]

* *

Those from the People of Interpretation who said the same as what we have said include:

Among those who also said this was al-Dahhak.

10538- Yahya ibn Abi Talib related to me, saying: Yazid informed us, saying: Juwaybir informed us, from al-Dahhak, who said: Allah preferred Islam over every religion, saying: "And who is better in religion than one who submits his face to Allah while being a doer of good" up to His words "and Allah took Abraham as a friend," and no deed other than Islam is accepted, and it is the hanifiyyah.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And Allah took Abraham as a friend﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, is meant: Allah took Abraham as a close ally (wali).

* *

If someone says: What is the meaning of the "khullah" (friendship) that was given to Abraham?

It is said: From Abraham, peace be upon him, it is enmity for the sake of Allah and hatred for His sake, and loyalty for the sake of Allah and love for His sake, as is known from the meanings of "khullah." As for from Allah to Abraham, it is His support against whoever plots evil against him, like what He did when Nimrod intended to harm him by burning him with fire, and He rescued him from it; or His proof over the one who argued with him, when he argued with him; and as He did with the king of Egypt when he intended (harm) to his wife [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "malik Misr" without the preposition; the context requires what is adopted here.]]; and His enabling him in what he loved; and His making him an imam for those after him among His servants, and an exemplar for those who follow him in obedience and worship. This is the meaning of His befriending him.

It has also been said: Allah named him "khalil" because a drought struck the people of his region, so he traveled to a friend of his from the people of Mosul [some say: from the people of Egypt] seeking provisions of food for his family from that friend, but he did not find what he needed with him. When he drew near to his family, he passed through a desert with sand, and he said: "If I filled my sacks with this sand, so that I would not grieve my family by returning to them without provisions, and so that they would think I had brought them what they love!" He did so, and the sand in his sacks turned into flour. When he reached his home, he slept. His family got up, opened the sacks, found flour, kneaded it and baked bread. He woke up and asked them about the flour from which they had baked, and they said: From the flour you brought from your friend's place! He understood, and said: Yes! It is from my friend, Allah! They said: So Allah named him "khalil" by this.

[[This is another example of Abu Ja'far's abridgment of his tafsir in various places, as was said in his biography. Had it not been for abridgment, he would have related the accounts of Abraham, upon him and upon our Prophet be peace. The accounts of Abraham have already passed in various places of the tafsir.]]

Commentary on the interpretation of His words, may He be exalted: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and Allah is ever, of all things, Encompassing﴾ (4:126).

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "And Allah took Abraham as a close friend" (khalil), for his obedience to his Lord, his sincerity in worship to Him, and his hastening toward His good pleasure and love, not out of any need on His part for him or for his friendship. How could He need him or his friendship, when to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, both little and much, as possession? And the owner, to whom the possessed thing is in need, is not the one who is in need of it. He says: [[The word "yaqul" ("he says") is not in the printed edition, but it is present in the manuscript.]] Likewise, Abraham's need is not for Him such that He would take him as a friend because of a need of His for him; rather, He took him as a friend because of his hastening toward His good pleasure and love. He says: "Likewise, hasten toward My good pleasure and My love, so that I may take you as My allies." ﴿And Allah is ever, of all things, Encompassing﴾: Allah has always been counting all that His servants do, good and evil, knowing it, nothing of it hidden from Him, and not even the weight of an atom escaping Him. [[See the explanation of "kana" in the sense of "lam yazal" (he has always been) in the indexes of language under (k-w-n), and the explanation of "al-ihatah" (encompassing) and "muhit" (encompassing) earlier, p. 193, note 1, and the references there.]]

**The interpretation of His words:** ﴿They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, "Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and [also concerning] what is recited to you in the Book regarding the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them, yet you desire to marry them."﴾

Abu Ja'far [al-Tabari] said: By His words, "They ask you for a ruling concerning women," glorified be His praise, He means: your companions ask you, O Muhammad, to give them a ruling concerning the matter of women and what is due to them and from them. He suffices with mentioning "women" in place of mentioning "their affairs," because what appears of the speech indicates its intended meaning.

"Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning them'": Say to them, O Muhammad, "Allah gives you a ruling concerning them," meaning: concerning women. "And what is recited to you in the Book regarding the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them."

\* \*

The people of ta'wil (interpretation, i.e., tafsir) differed concerning the interpretation of His words, "and what is recited to you in the Book."

Some of them said: By His words, "and what is recited to you," [the meaning is]: "Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and concerning what is recited to you.'" They said: What is recited to them is the verses of the inheritance shares that are at the beginning of this surah.

Mention of those who said this:

10539. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, who said: Hakkam ibn Salm narrated to us, from Amr ibn Abi Qays, from Ata, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and [also concerning] what is recited to you in the Book'": He said: The people of the Jahiliyyah (the time of ignorance before Islam) would not give inheritance to a newborn child until he grew up, nor would they give inheritance to a woman. When Islam came, [Allah] said: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and [also concerning] what is recited to you in the Book'" at the beginning of the surah, concerning the shares of inheritance, "regarding the orphan women to whom you do not give what Allah has prescribed for them."

[Note on the report 10539: Amr ibn Abi Qays al-Razi, al-Azraq, has passed as no. 6887, and in the chains as nos. 8611 and 9346. "Ata" is Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, who has passed many times. This report will come through another route, no. 10541.]

10540. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, who said: My father narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, from Aisha: "And what is recited to you in the Book regarding the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them, yet you desire to marry them." She said: This refers to the orphan girl who is in a man's care. Perhaps she is his partner in his wealth, and he has more right to her than anyone else, so he turns away from her, not wanting to marry her, and he withholds her from marriage for the sake of her wealth, not letting anyone else marry her, out of dislike that anyone should share her wealth with him.

[Note on report 10540: This is the hadith of Hisham ibn Urwa, from his father, from Aisha, which is transmitted through several routes. Al-Bukhari narrated it (al-Fath 8: 179, 199). A similar report passed in the tafsir as no. 8457.]

10541. Ibn Wakī' and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: In the Jahiliyyah they did not give inheritance to women or to the young boy until he reached puberty. So Allah revealed: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and [also concerning] what is recited to you in the Book regarding the orphan women,'" at the beginning of "Surat al-Nisa'," concerning the inheritance shares.

[Note on report 10541: Al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak 2: 308, traced to Ibn Abbas (raised as a hadith) with a different wording, and said: "This hadith has a sound chain, but the two [Bukhari and Muslim] did not narrate it." In the printed edition it read "the women and the child," and I have restored what is in the manuscript. The next report has "the small man," who is the young boy (fata).]

10542. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, who said: Jarir narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from Ja'far, from Shu'ba, who said: In the Jahiliyyah they did not give inheritance to the orphan girl, and they would not marry her off, and they would withhold her [from marriage], so Allah revealed: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning them'," until the end of the verse.

10543. Al-Qasim narrated to us, who said: Al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Al-Hajjaj informed me, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Abd Allah ibn Kathir informed me that he heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr say concerning His words, "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and [also concerning] what is recited to you in the Book regarding the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them, yet you desire to marry them'," the verse, he said: Only a man who had reached maturity would inherit; a small boy would not inherit, nor would a woman. When the verses of inheritance in "Surat al-Nisa'" were revealed, it weighed heavily on the people, and they said: The small child who does not work with the wealth nor manage it, and the woman who is likewise, will inherit just as the man who works with the wealth inherits! They hoped that some new matter would come from heaven about this. They waited, but when they saw that no new matter came, they said: If this is established, it is truly obligatory and there is no escaping it! Then they said: Ask! So they asked the Prophet (ﷺ), and Allah revealed: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and [also concerning] what is recited to you in the Book'" at the beginning of the surah, "regarding the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them, yet you desire to marry them." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When the guardian (wali) had a woman who was beautiful and wealthy, he desired her, married her, and kept her to himself; and when she was not beautiful and wealthy, he married her off [to another] and did not marry her himself.

[Note on report 10543: Al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2: 231, and attributed it further to Ibn al-Mundhir.]

10544. Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim [al-Nakha'i], regarding: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and [also concerning] what is recited to you in the Book regarding the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them, yet you desire to marry them'," he said: When a girl was an orphan and ugly, they would not give her inheritance, and they would prevent her from marriage until she died, and then they would inherit from her. So Allah revealed this.

10545. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, who said: Hushaym narrated to us, who said: Mughira informed us, from Ibrahim, regarding His words, "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning them'," he said: A man among them would have an orphan girl in his care who had ugliness and a defect that made one averse to her, and she had wealth. He would neither marry her nor let her marry, until she died and he inherited from her. He said: So Allah forbade them from that.

10546. Sufyan ibn Wakī' narrated to us, who said: Abd Allah narrated to us, from Isra'il, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, regarding: "And what is recited to you in the Book regarding the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them, yet you desire to marry them," he said: When a woman was in the care of a guardian who was averse to her, he would withhold her if he did not marry her, and he would not let anyone else marry her.

10547. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, who said: Abu Asim narrated to us, who said: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words, "regarding the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them": He said: The people of the Jahiliyyah would not give inheritance to women or to children anything. They used to say: They do not fight, nor do they take booty of any good! So Allah prescribed for them the inheritance as a binding right, so that the man would be eager (yatanafasu) concerning the wealth of his orphan ward, if she were not beautiful. [Or, another reading: "so that the man would be stingy" (liyanfus) concerning the wealth of his orphan ward.]

[Note on report 10547: In the printed edition it read "if she is beautiful," dropping the "not" (lam), which corrupted the meaning; it is present in the manuscript. The phrase "liyatanafasa al-rajulu fi mal yatimatihi" appears to use "yatanafasu" intransitively in the singular form, which is correct Arabic. Al-munafasa and al-tanafus mean desire for a thing in order to have it exclusively, in a manner of contest. As for "li-yanfus al-rajul fi mal yatimatihi," it derives from the expression "nafasa bi-l-shay'," meaning he was miserly with it and kept it for himself, and "nafasa fihi," meaning he desired to keep it for himself. It is also said: "This is an item that is nafus fihi," meaning desirable.]

10548. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, who said: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, with similar wording.

10549. Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, who said: My father narrated to us, who said: My paternal uncle narrated to us, who said: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and [also concerning] what is recited to you in the Book'," meaning: the shares that were made obligatory concerning the matter of women, "regarding the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them, yet you desire to marry them." He said: The orphan girl would be in the care of a man, and he would desire to marry her or to have intercourse with her, and he would not give her her wealth, hoping that she would die so that he could inherit from her. If a close relative of hers died, she would not be given any part of the inheritance. [The word "hamim" means a near relative.] This was in the Jahiliyyah, and Allah explained that to them.

[Note on report 10549: The phrase "yarghab an yankihaha" is elliptical for "yarghab 'an an yankihaha," meaning: he turns away from marrying her. "Raghiba 'an al-shay'" means he abandoned it deliberately, lost interest in it, disliked it, and did not want it. Omitting the preposition here is permissible, since the context indicates it.]

10550. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, who said: Yazid narrated to us, who said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words, "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning them'," until "and you desire to marry them": A man would have an orphan girl in his care who had an ugliness, and she had wealth. He would turn away from marrying her, and he would withhold her for the sake of her wealth. So Allah revealed concerning him what you hear.

10551. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, who said: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, who said: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatada, regarding His words, "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning them'," he said: The orphan girl would be in a man's care, and she had ugliness, so he turned away from marrying her, and he would not let her marry, out of desire for her wealth.

10552. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, who said: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, who said: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His words, "And what is recited to you in the Book regarding the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them, yet you desire to marry them," up to His words, "with justice": He said: Jabir ibn Abd Allah al-Ansari, then al-Sulami, had a paternal cousin who was blind and ugly. She had inherited wealth from her father. Jabir was averse to marrying her, and he would not let her marry, out of fear that the husband would take away her wealth. So he asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about that. There were also people who had girls in their care in the same situation. Jabir kept asking the Prophet (ﷺ): "Does the girl inherit if she is ugly and blind?" The Prophet (ﷺ) kept saying: "Yes!!" So Allah revealed this concerning them.

[Note on report 10552: Refer to the report of Jabir ibn Abd Allah and his paternal cousin, in a different form, earlier, as no. 4939.]

\* \*

Others said: The meaning is: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and [also concerning] what is recited to you in the Book'," at the end of "Surat al-Nisa'," which is His words: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say, "Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalalah"﴾, until the end of the surah [Surat al-Nisa': 176].

Mention of those who said this:

10553. Al-Harith narrated to me, who said: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, who said: Salam ibn Sulaym narrated to us, from Ata ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: The people of the Jahiliyyah would not give inheritance to young children until they reached puberty. So Allah revealed: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women," until His words, "Indeed Allah is ever Knowing of it." He said: And this verse was revealed: ﴿If a man dies leaving no children﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 176], the whole verse.

[Note on report 10553: "Al-Harith" is al-Harith ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Usama, who has passed as no. 10295 and following. "Abd al-Aziz" is Abd al-Aziz ibn Aban al-Umawi, who has also passed as no. 10295 and following. In the manuscript it read "the people of the Jahiliyyah, the young children," and in its margin "(t)," indicating an error. The first printed edition correctly added what it added.]

\* \*

Others said: Rather, the meaning is: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and [also concerning] what is recited to you in the Book'," meaning: at the beginning of this surah, which is His words: ﴿And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry what seems good to you of [other] women﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 3].

Mention of those who said this:

10554. Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to me, who said: Ibn Wahb informed us, who said: Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Urwa ibn al-Zubayr informed me that he asked Aisha, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), about the words of Allah: ﴿And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry what seems good to you of [other] women﴾. She said: O son of my sister, she is the orphan girl who is in the care of her guardian (waliyyuha), who shares his wealth with her. He is attracted to her wealth and beauty, so her guardian wants to marry her without being just in her dowry, giving her what he would give another. So they were forbidden to marry them unless they would deal justly with them, and give them the highest standard of dowry customary for them. They were commanded to marry whatever women seemed good to them other than these. Urwa said: Aisha said: Then the people asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for a ruling concerning them after this verse, so Allah revealed: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and [also concerning] what is recited to you in the Book regarding the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them, yet you desire to marry them'." She said: What Allah mentioned as being recited in the Book is the first verse in which He said: ﴿And if you fear that you will not deal justly with the orphan girls, then marry what seems good to you of [other] women﴾.

[Note on report 10554: Abu Ja'far narrated it in abridged form earlier as no. 8457, and my brother, Sayyid Ahmad, takes it out there.]

10555. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, who said: Abu Salih narrated to us, who said: Al-Layth narrated to me, who said: Yunus narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab, from Urwa, from Aisha, the like of it.

[Note on report 10555: It passed as no. 8459, as a reference to the earlier report.]

\* \*

Others said: This verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) concerning a group of his companions who asked him about some matters concerning women, and left off asking about other things they had been doing. So Allah gave them a ruling concerning what they asked about and what they left off asking about.

Mention of those who said this:

10556. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Sufyan ibn Wakī' narrated to us, Sufyan said: Abd al-A'la narrated to us; and Ibn al-Muthanna said: Abd al-A'la narrated to me, who said: Dawud narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, concerning this verse: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women," he said: They asked the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) about women, and they were silent about something they used to do. So Allah revealed: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and [also concerning] what is recited to you in the Book'," and [He would] give a ruling concerning what you did not ask about. He said: They would not marry the orphan girl if she was ugly, and they would not give her her wealth so that she could spend it. So it was revealed: "Say, 'Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and [also concerning] what is recited to you in the Book regarding the orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them, yet you desire to marry them'," and: "and [concerning] the oppressed among the children." He said: They used to give inheritance to the adults and not to the young. Then He gave them a ruling on what they had been silent about, saying: "And if a woman fears cruelty or aversion from her husband, there is no blame upon them if they make terms of settlement between themselves, and settlement is best"; and the wording of the hadith is that of Ibn al-Muthanna.

[Note on report 10556: Muhammad ibn Abi Musa was mentioned by al-Bukhari in al-Kabir 1/1/236, as a man bearing this name, and it is evident that Dawud ibn Abi Hind narrated from him. He said: "Al-Humaydi narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, from Ibn Abbas." And in al-Tahdhib it says: "Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, from Ibn Abbas, his statement... and Abu Sa'id al-Baqqal narrated from him." I (the one who said this, Ibn Hajar) say: In his tabaqah (generation) [is]: Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, who narrated from Ziyad al-Ansari, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, and from him Dawud ibn Abi Hind." It seems to him that they are two men.]

Abu Ja'far said: According to this view, "what is recited to us in the Book" is what Allah, glorified be His praise, referred to when He said: "Allah gives you a ruling concerning them, and [also concerning] what is recited to you": "And if a woman fears cruelty or aversion from her husband," the verse. And the question the people asked, about which they were answered, concerns the orphan women who were not given what Allah had prescribed for them of inheritance from the one they inherited from.

\* \*

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct of these views that we have mentioned, from those we have cited, and the one most consistent with the apparent sense of the revelation, is the view of the one who said: The meaning of His words, "and what is recited to you in the Book," is the verses of the inheritance shares at the beginning and the end of this surah.

This is the continuation of al-Tabari's commentary on Surah an-Nisa', verse 127.

We said that this is the more correct interpretation because the bridal gift (ṣadāq) belongs to women only through marriage. So if a woman has not married, she has no bridal gift due from anyone. If that is not due to her from anyone, it is not among what has been prescribed for her. If it is not among what has been prescribed for her, then the statement of the speaker [[The manuscript omits this passage, which appeared between two statements and read: "So if she has not married, she has no bridal gift from anyone, and if that is not hers, there is no statement of a speaker ... "; I have therefore kept the wording of the printed edition as it stands.]] cannot mean, by His words "and what is recited to you in the Book," the regulation of bridal gifts for orphan women. [[The construction of the sentence: "there is no ... of a speaker ... a basis (wajh)."]] Because God said, in the context of the verse, explaining the ruling He promised to give us: ﴿Concerning orphan women, to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them﴾. So He informed us that part of what He instructs us about concerning women is the matter of the orphan girl who is prevented from receiving what God has prescribed for her. [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "al-muhawwalah baynahā" (the one prevented from); the correct reading is what I have adopted, meaning: the one between whom and what God has prescribed for her a barrier has been placed.]] A bridal gift before the marriage contract is not something God has prescribed for her from anyone. Thus it became clear that the one intended by this verse is the one who has been prevented from what was prescribed for her, of what is recited to us in the Book of God. If that is so, it becomes clear that this is the inheritance which God has made obligatory for them in His Book.

* *

As for what was reported from Muhammad ibn Abi Musa, [[That is, the earlier report numbered 10556.]] it is, apart from departing from the view of the exegetes (ahl al-ta'wil, the scholars of interpretation), far from what the apparent meaning of the revelation indicates. He claimed that what God meant by His words "and what is recited to you in the Book" is: "and if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion." When the speech is directed toward the meaning he interpreted, the speech becomes detached from His words "concerning orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them," as an explanatory restatement (tarjamah) of His words "concerning them" [[Tarjamah here means badal, bayan and tafsir (substitution, clarification and explanation).]], and the meaning of the speech becomes: "Say: God gives you a ruling concerning them, concerning orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them." There is no indication in the verse for what he said, and no report from anyone whose statement is known to be sound supports that. Since this is so, connecting the meanings of the speech to one another is preferable wherever that is possible. Given that the matter is as we have described, His words "concerning orphan women" being a complement (ṣilah) to His words "and what is recited to you" is more appropriate than its being an explanatory restatement of His words "God gives you a ruling concerning them," because it is closer to His words "and what is recited to you in the Book," and separated from His words "gives you a ruling concerning them."

* *

Since that is so, the interpretation of the verse is: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say: God gives you a ruling concerning them and concerning what is recited to you in the Book of God which He revealed to His Prophet regarding orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them." That is, what God has ordained for them of inheritance from those whom they inherit from, [[See the explanation of "kutiba" in what has preceded, vol. 8, p. 548, note 4, and the references there.]] as:

10557. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding "you do not give them what has been prescribed for them": You do not give them inheritance.

10558. al-Muthanna told me, saying: 'Amr ibn 'Awn told us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, regarding His words "you do not give them what has been prescribed for them": It is of the inheritance. He said: They used not to give women inheritance.

"and you desire to marry them."

* *

The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of His words "and you desire to marry them."

Some said: The meaning of that is: "and you are averse to marrying them." The mention of a group who said this has already passed, and we will mention the views of others whom we have not mentioned.

10559. Humayd ibn Mas'adah al-Sami told us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Awn told us, from al-Hasan, regarding "and you desire to marry them": He said: You are averse to them. [[Report 10559: Humayd ibn Mas'adah al-Sami, his nisbah traced to Sammah ibn Lu'ayy with a sin; it has passed as nos. 196 and 5842. In the printed edition it was "al-Shami" with a shin, which is an error; this nisbah is not in the manuscript. "'Abd Allah ibn 'Awn ibn Arṭaban" has passed as nos. 4003 and 7776; the printed edition had "'Ubayd Allah," and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]

10560. Ya'qub and Ibn Wakī' told us, both saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah told us, from Ibn 'Awn, from al-Hasan, the like of it.

10561. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Yunus ibn Yazid informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Urwah, who said: 'A'ishah said regarding God's words "and you desire to marry them": [it is] the aversion of one of you toward his orphan ward who is in his guardianship when she is of little wealth and beauty. So they were forbidden to marry those orphan women whose wealth and beauty they desired except with equity, because of their aversion to them. [[Report 10561 is the continuation of the earlier report, no. 8457, then its counterpart no. 10554, and al-Bukhari transmitted it immediately after with its chain (Fath 8: 179, 180).]]

10562. al-Muthanna told me, saying: 'Abd Allah, meaning Ibn Salih, told us, saying: al-Layth told me, saying: Yunus told me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: 'Urwah said: 'A'ishah said, and he mentioned the like of it. [[Report 10562 is the report that passed as no. 8459, then its counterpart no. 10555.]]

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "and you desire to marry them." The mention of a group who said this has already passed, and we will mention the views of those among them whom we have not mentioned.

10563. Humayd ibn Mas'adah told us, saying: Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Ibn 'Awn told us, from Muhammad, from 'Ubaydah, regarding "and you desire to marry them": He said: and you desire them.

10564. Yahya ibn Ibrahim and Ibn Wakī' told me, both saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah told us, from Ibn 'Awn, from Muhammad, who said: I said to 'Ubaydah, "and you desire to marry them," and he said: You desire them.

10565. al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words "concerning orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them and you desire to marry them": A man in the Jahiliyyah would have an orphan girl in his care and would throw his garment over her. When he did that to her, no one could marry her ever. If she was beautiful and he loved her, he would marry her and consume her wealth. If she was ugly, the man would prevent her from marrying indefinitely until she died, and then he would inherit from her. God forbade that and prohibited it. [[Report 10565: see the report of Ibn 'Abbas earlier, with this same chain, no. 8882.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two views regarding the interpretation of the verse is the view of the one who said: The meaning of that is "and you are averse to marrying them." Because their withholding of their wealth from them, together with their restraining them (called 'adl, preventing a woman from remarrying), was only so that they might inherit their wealth, without a husband if they married. If those who withheld their wealth from them had withheld it only out of desire to marry them, there would be no recognized reason for withholding from them, because they were their guardians, and nothing prevented them from marrying them, so there would be no need to withhold her wealth from her in order to make withholding it a means to forcing her to marry him.

* *

The discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿And concerning the oppressed among the children and that you establish justice for orphans﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say: God gives you a ruling concerning them, and concerning what is recited to you in the Book, and concerning the oppressed among the children, and that you establish justice for orphans."

The report of this from those who said it among the Companions and the Successors has been mentioned previously. Those whom He ruled for concerning the matter of the oppressed among the children, that they should give them their rights of inheritance, [[In the printed edition: "wa-alladhī afta-hum" (the one He ruled for); the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] because they used not to give inheritance to the young children of the deceased, and He commanded them to act justly toward them, that they should be fair, and give them their shares as God had apportioned them in His Book, as:

10566. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi regarding His words "and the oppressed among the children": They used not to give inheritance to a girl or a young boy, so God commanded them to establish justice for orphans. "Justice" means that each person with a right among them is given his right, male or female, the young among them being in the same position as the grown.

10567. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "They ask you for a ruling concerning women. Say: God gives you a ruling concerning them, and what is recited to you in the Book concerning orphan women to whom you do not give what has been prescribed for them": He said: You do not give them inheritance of property. "And that you establish justice for orphans": He said: So women and the young and the old entered into inheritance, and the earlier ruling was abrogated (naskh, the cancellation of an earlier ruling by a later one) by inheritance.

10568. Muhammad ibn 'Amr told me, saying: Abu 'Asim told us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding "and that you establish justice for orphans": They were commanded to be just toward orphans, to be fair.

10569. al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

10570. Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: 'Abd Allah told us, from Isra'il, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik regarding "and the oppressed among the children and that you establish justice for orphans": He said: They used not to give inheritance except to the eldest, then the eldest.

10571. al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiyah told me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words "and the oppressed among the children": In the Jahiliyyah they used not to give inheritance to young children or to daughters. That is the meaning of His words "you do not give them what has been prescribed for them." God forbade that and made clear to every holder of a share his share, saying: ﴿For the male is the equal of the portion of two females﴾ [Surah an-Nisa': 11, 176], whether young or old.

10572. Muhammad ibn Sa'd told me, saying: My father told me, saying: My paternal uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "And the oppressed among the children and that you establish justice for orphans": That is because they used not to give the young and weak anything of inheritance, so God commanded that his share of the inheritance be given.

10573. al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim, that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, when a guardian of an orphan girl came to him, if she was good-looking and wealthy, 'Umar would say to him: Marry her to someone other than yourself, and seek for her one better than you. If she was plain and had no wealth, he would say: Marry her, for you have the better right to her!

10574. al-Qasim told us, saying: al-Husayn told us, saying: Hushaym told us, saying: Yunus ibn 'Ubayd informed us, from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: A man came to 'Ali ibn Abi Talib and said: O Commander of the Faithful, what is my affair and the affair of my orphan ward? He said: In what state are you both? [["al-bal": the matter, affair and condition; from it the hadith: "every matter of importance not begun with praise of God is cut off," and "a matter of importance" means one of significance, worthy of attention and concern.]] Then 'Ali said: Would you marry her, rich and beautiful? He said: Yes, by God! He said: Then marry her when she is plain and has no wealth! Then 'Ali said: Choose for her [[In the printed edition: "Then 'Ali said: Marry her if you are better for her." The printer did not understand what is in the manuscript and changed it, and how wrong that was! "Khir lahā" is from the expression "khāra lahu," meaning he chose the better of the two options for him; from it the saying "khāra Allāh laka," meaning God gave you what is better for you.]] for her. If someone other than you is better for her, then join her with the better. [[Report 10574: Yunus ibn 'Ubayd ibn Dinar al-'Abdi has passed as nos. 2616, 4931, 8047. As for "al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj," I have not found among the transmitters of his generation anyone called "al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj." In the printed edition it stood as "al-Hasan," meaning al-Hasan al-Basri, and I suspect this is an alteration by a copyist or publisher. Yes, Yunus ibn 'Ubayd transmits from al-Hasan al-Basri, but I incline to think that there is a corruption in his name, and I fear it may be: "al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Hurr," or "al-Husayn ibn Malik ibn al-Khashkhash al-'Anbari," who transmitted from him, Yunus ibn 'Ubayd. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib. We hope that the commentary will contain what shows the correct reading.]] Abu Ja'far said: So their standing up for orphans with justice was the fairness in what God commanded concerning them.

* *

The discussion of the interpretation of His words: ﴿And whatever good you do, indeed God is ever Knowing of it﴾ (127)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "Whatever it is that you do, O believers, of justice regarding the wealth of orphans, concerning which God commanded you to stand with equity regarding them, and to abide by God's command in that and in other matters, and to obey Him" — "indeed God is ever Knowing of it." He has never ceased to know what will occur from you. He records all of it against you and preserves it until He repays you for it on the Day of Resurrection. [[See the explanation of "kāna" and "ʿalīm" in what has preceded, in the language indexes.]]
