**The interpretation of His words:** ﴿And if a woman fears ill-treatment (nushuz) or aversion from her husband﴾

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, means: "And if a woman fears from her husband," that is, knows from her husband,[[See the explanation of "fear" above, 4:550, and its explanation as "knowledge" above, 8:298-299. See also the explanation of "baʿl" (husband) above, 4:526.]] "nushuzan" (ill-treatment), meaning: his exalting himself over her toward another, showing preference for someone other than her, and holding himself aloof from her, whether out of hatred, or out of his dislike of some of her "asbab" (circumstances).[[In the printed edition: "some things about her," which is a weak reading; the editor did not properly understand what is in the manuscript. "Asbab" is the plural of "sabab," originally meaning a rope, then borrowed for anything by which one reaches something. Later writers of the second and third centuries AH and after used it to mean anything connected with or attached to a thing. Some instances of this usage occurred earlier in Abu Ja'far's discourse, which I fear I may have pointed out in a note, but which have now escaped my memory.]] Or [it is from] her ugliness, or her age and advanced years, or other matters concerning her. [[See the explanation of "nushuz" above, 3:475-476, and 8:299.]] "Or aversion" (i'radan), meaning: his turning away from her with his face, or with some of the benefits he had provided to her. [[See the explanation of "i'rad" above, 2:298-299, 6:291, and 8:88, 566.]] "There is no blame upon them both if they make a settlement between themselves, a settlement," meaning: there is no sin on them both, that is, on the woman who fears her husband's ill-treatment or his aversion from her, "that they make a settlement between themselves, a settlement," which is that she give up her day to him, or waive some of what is owed to her as a right from him, seeking to win him over by this and to continue in remaining in his bond and holding fast to the contract of marriage between her and him. He says: "And settlement is better," meaning: settlement by giving up some of the right, to maintain the sanctity [of the marriage] and to hold fast to the marriage contract, is better than seeking separation and divorce.

* *

Those who engage in ta'wil (interpretation of the Qur'an) have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

10575. Hannad ibn al-Sarri narrated to us, saying: Abu al-Ahwas narrated to us, from Simak, from Khalid ibn ʿArʿara: that a man came to ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, asking him for a ruling concerning a woman who feared ill-treatment or aversion from her husband. He said: "A woman may be with a man, and his eyes turn away from her because of her ugliness, her old age, her bad character, or her poverty, and she dislikes his leaving her. So if she gives him something of her dowry, it is permitted to him, and if she gives him some of her days, there is no blame."

10576. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Jaʿfar narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Khalid ibn ʿArʿara, who said: ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, was asked about: "And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband, there is no blame upon them both if they make a settlement between themselves, a settlement." He said: "A woman who is old, or ugly, or whom her husband does not love, so they reconcile."

10577. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abu Dawud narrated to us, saying: Shuʿba, Hammad ibn Salama, and Abu al-Ahwas, all of them, narrated to us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Khalid ibn ʿArʿara, from ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, in a similar report.

10578. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Israʾil, from Simak, from Khalid ibn ʿArʿara: that a man asked ʿAli, may Allah be pleased with him, about His words: "There is no blame upon them both if they make a settlement between themselves, a settlement." He said: "A woman may be with a man who finds her ugly, and his eye turns away from her because of her ugliness or her age. If she gives him some of her days or some of her wealth, there is no blame upon him." [[In the printed edition: "then there is no blame upon him," and both are the same. I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

10579. Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Ashʿath, from Ibn Sirin, who said: A man came to ʿUmar and asked him about a verse. He disliked that and struck him with the durra (a whip). Then another asked him about this verse: "And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband," and he said: "Ask about the like of this!" Then he said: "This is a woman who is with a man who has passed beyond her age, and he marries a young woman seeking to have children by her. Whatever the two of them agree upon is permissible." [[In the manuscript: "hadhihi al-imra'a," which is the original form of putting the definite article on "imra'a," but it is rare in their speech. Abu ʿAli al-Farisi reported it, and this is its witness. I have not adopted it, and I have left what is in the printed edition, lest I confuse the reader!! "Khala min sinnihā" means: she grew old and most of her life had passed. From their saying: "khala qarn wa-zaman," i.e., it passed.]]

10580. ʿAmr ibn ʿAli narrated to us, saying: ʿImran ibn ʿUyayna narrated to us, saying: ʿAta ibn al-Sa'ib narrated to us, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding His words: "And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband," he said: "It is the woman who is with a man until she grows old. He wants to marry another woman over her, so they reconcile between themselves with a settlement, on the basis that she has one day and this one [the new wife] has two or three days." [[In the printed edition: "fa-yataṣāliḥā," and the correct form is from the manuscript.]] [[Report 10580: "ʿImran ibn ʿUyayna ibn Abi ʿImran al-Hilali," the brother of "Sufyan ibn ʿUyayna." Ibn Maʿin and Abu Zurʿa said: "Ṣāliḥ al-ḥadīth" (his narrations are acceptable). Ibn Hibban mentioned him in al-Thiqat, and he is truthful (ṣadūq). Abu Hatim said: "His hadith is not used as proof, because he brings unusual reports." He is biographied in al-Tahdhib. It has passed under no. 4189 with a similar chain.]]

10581. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: ʿImran narrated to us, from ʿAta, from Saʿid, from Ibn ʿAbbas, in a similar report, except that he said: "until she gives birth or grows old." And he also said: "There is no blame upon them both if they reconcile over one night, and the other [the new wife] over two nights."

10582. Ibn Wakiʿ and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from ʿAta, from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, who said: "It is the woman who is with a man whose companionship with her has been long and who has grown old. He wants to replace her, but she dislikes to be separated from him, and he marries another over her, and so he makes peace with her on the basis that he gives her days, and the other [wife] has days and a month." [[In the printed edition: "fa-yatazawwaju ʿalayhā fa-yuṣālaḥuhā ʿalā an yajʿal lahā ayyāman," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

10583. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Hakkam narrated to us, from ʿAmr ibn Abi Qays, from ʿAta, from Saʿid, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband." He said: "It is the woman who is with a man, and he wants to separate from her, but she dislikes that he separate from her. He wants to marry and says: 'I cannot be equal to you in dividing my time as I divide it for her.' So she makes peace with him on the basis that she has one day among the days, and they agree on that, and they remain on what they have settled upon."

10584. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿAʾisha: "And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband, there is no blame upon them both if they make a settlement between themselves, a settlement, and settlement is better." She said: "This applies to a woman who is with a man, and perhaps he feels she is too old for him, and she has no child, and she has companionship [with him]. So she says: 'Do not divorce me, and you are free regarding my affairs.'" [[In the printed edition: "fa-la'allahu lā yakūnu tastakthiru minhā, wa-lā yakūnu lahā walad wa-lahā ṣuḥba," which differs from the manuscript. I have kept what is in the manuscript, because it is correct in meaning. Her saying "yastakbir minhā" means: he sees that she has reached an age and advanced years that prompt him to seek a replacement. Her saying "wa-lā yakūnu lahā walad yakūnu lahā ṣuḥba" means: a child who calls him to her companionship and to not leaving her. What led the editor to correct it is that ʿAʾisha's hadith in other transmissions says: "A man has a woman with him, he is not desirous of her, and he wants to separate from her," which is the wording of al-Bukhari, and as will come in the following report: 10585. But that is not a reason for such a change, for the meaning you mentioned has come from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿAʾisha in reports 10585 and 10588, which is: "concerning a woman who has entered old age." So there is no sense in altering a report unless the error of its meaning or the correctness of its wording elsewhere has been verified. See the takhrij (sourcing) of this report in the following notes.]] [[Report 10584: The report of Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿAʾisha, which Abu Ja'far narrated through three consecutive chains, and through a single chain, no. 10588.
al-Bukhari narrated it with a different wording (al-Fath 9:266) through Ibn Salam, from Abu Muʿawiya, from Hisham. Then he narrated it with another wording (al-Fath 8:199).
al-Bukhari narrated it with a different wording (al-Fath 8:199) through Muhammad ibn Muqatil, from ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, from Hisham, from ʿAʾisha, and this is Abu Ja'far's chain, no. 10586. Then he narrated it with another wording (al-Fath 9:266) through Ibn Salam, from Abu Muʿawiya, from Hisham.
Muslim narrated it (18:157) through Abu Kurayb, from Abu Usama, from Hisham, and its wording is closer to the wording that the editor of the first printed edition adopted, which is: "It was revealed concerning a woman who is with a man, so perhaps he does not desire her, and she has companionship and a child, so she dislikes that he separate from her," the hadith. And al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan (7:296) with a different wording.]]

10585. Narrated to me al-Muthanna, saying: Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salama narrated to us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from ʿUrwa, from ʿAʾisha, concerning His words: "And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband," she said: "This is a man who has two wives: one of them has become incapable, or is ugly, and he does not desire her much. So she says: 'Do not divorce me, and you are free regarding my affairs.'"

10586. Narrated to me al-Muthanna, saying: Hibban ibn Musa narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿAʾisha, in a similar report, except that he said: "So she says: 'I make you free of my affairs!' So this verse was revealed concerning that." [[The two reports, 10585 and 10586, are repetitions of the earlier report through two chains.]]

10587. Narrated to me al-Muthanna, saying: Abu Salih narrated to us, saying: Muʿawiya narrated to me, from ʿAli ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words: "And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband," he said: "That woman is with a man who does not see in her what he loves in abundance, and he has another woman, dearer to him than her, and he prefers her over her. So when that happens, Allah commands him to say to her: 'O you! If you wish to remain with what you see of preference [for another], I will provide for you and spend on you, so remain. And if you dislike that, I will release you!' If she agrees to remain after he gives her the choice, there is no blame upon him. This is His words: 'And settlement is better,' and that is the choice." [["Al-muwasah" is from "al-usra" (solace/companionship), whose root is the hamza, which changed to a waw for ease. It means sharing and participation in livelihood and sustenance.]]

10588. al-Rabiʿ ibn Sulayman and Bahr ibn Nasr narrated to us, both saying: Ibn Wahb narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi al-Zinad narrated to me, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwa, from his father, from ʿAʾisha, who said: "Allah revealed this verse concerning the woman who has entered old age," [her saying: "dakhalat fi al-sinn," means: she grew old and her age rose.] "so she gives her day to another woman." She said: "Concerning that was revealed: 'There is no blame upon them both if they make a settlement between themselves, a settlement.'" [[Report 10588: "Bahr ibn Nasr ibn Sabiq al-Khawlani," of Egypt, reliable and truthful (thiqa ṣadūq). He narrated from Ibn Wahb, al-Shafiʿi, and Asad ibn Musa. Abu Jaʿfar al-Tahawi narrated from him. He is biographied in al-Tahdhib. However, in the manuscript the chain does not include "Bahr ibn Nasr," but is limited to al-Rabiʿ. I have not found this report from this route anywhere else.]]

10589. Narrated to me Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Hisham informed us, from Ibn Sirin, from ʿUbayda, who said: I asked him about Allah's words: "And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband," and he said: "She is a woman who is with her husband, and he wants to marry another over her, so she makes peace with him from her day by a settlement." He said: "They are both upon what they have agreed upon. But if he breaks it, [in the printed edition: "intaqaṣat bihi," with ṣād, and I am in firm doubt about it, while in the manuscript it is undotted, so I have preferred to read it as I have written, from their saying: "naqaḍa al-amr baʿda ibramihi" (he undid the matter after its ratification), "wa-intaqaḍa wa-tanāqaḍa." And the use of "bihi" with "intaqaḍat" is good Arabic, as if it carries the sense of "specific to it," i.e., he undid it.] then it is incumbent upon him to be just to her, or to separate from her."

10590. Narrated to me Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Mughira informed us, from Ibrahim, that he used to say that.

10591. Narrated to me Yaʿqub, saying: Hushaym narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj informed us, from Mujahid, that he used to say that.

10592. Narrated to me Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, from ʿUbayda, concerning His words: "And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband," to the end of the verse, he said: "He makes a settlement with her on what she accepts, below her right, so that is permitted to him as long as she accepts. But if she rejects it, or says: 'You have been unjust!' then he has the choice to be just to her, or to satisfy her, or to divorce her."

10593. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Wahhab narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Muhammad, who said: I asked ʿUbayda about the words of Allah: "And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband," and he said: "It is the man who has a wife who has passed beyond her age," [i.e., she has grown old and her best years have passed] "so she makes peace with him, on account of her right, for something, and that is his as long as she accepts. But if she dislikes it, then he has the choice to be just to her, or to satisfy her with her right, or to divorce her."

10594. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Hisham, from Ibn Sirin, who said: I asked ʿUbayda about His words: "And if a woman fears ill-treatment," and he mentioned something similar, except that he said: "If she is displeased, then he has the choice to satisfy her, or to give her all her right, or to divorce her."

10595. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughira, who said: Ibrahim said: "If she wishes, she remains upon her right; and if she wishes, she refuses and rejects the settlement, and it is in her hand. If he wishes, he divorces her, and if he wishes, he keeps her upon her right." [[Report 10595: This report is missing from the manuscript.]]

10596. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughira, from Ibrahim: "And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband, there is no blame upon them both," he said: ʿAli said: "A woman may be with a man for a long time, and she fears that he will divorce her, so she makes a settlement with him for whatever settlement they both wish: that he stays with her for such-and-such nights, and with another [wife] for what they agree upon; and that her maintenance be less than what it was. Whatever settlement she makes with him is permissible."

10597. Ibn Wakiʿ narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn ʿAbd al-Malik narrated to us, from his father, from al-Hakam: "And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband," he said: "It is the woman who is with a man, and he wants to release her. So if she fears that from him, there is no blame upon them both if they make peace between themselves, a settlement, she giving up some of her days when he marries." [[Report 10597: "Yahya ibn ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Humayd ibn Abi Ghaniya al-Khuzaʿi," Abu Zakariyya: reliable (thiqa). He is biographied in al-Tahdhib.
And his father: "ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Humayd ibn Abi Ghaniya," who is "Ibn Abi Ghaniya," passed under no. 8535.]]

10598. Narrated to me Muhammad ibn Saʿd, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His words: "And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband," to His words: "And settlement is better," it is about a man who has under him an older woman, and he marries a young woman over her. He dislikes to separate from the mother of his child, so he makes peace with her by giving her a gift of his wealth and himself, and that settlement is good for him.

10599. Narrated to us Bishr ibn Muʿadh, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Saʿid narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His words: "And if a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband," he recited until he reached: "Indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted." He said: "This concerns a man who has a woman with him who has passed beyond her age, and some of her affairs have become less important to him, so he says: 'If you are content with [a lesser share of] myself and my wealth, less than what you were content with before today!' [The answer to the condition is omitted, because the speech indicates it, i.e., if you are content with that, then that is so; otherwise, I will separate from you.] So if they reach a settlement on some matter, Allah has made that permissible for them both. But if she refuses, then it is not right for him to hold her in humiliation." [["ʿAla al-khasf" means: in degradation, and making her bear what she dislikes.]]

10600. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya told me, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Sulayman ibn Yasar, that Rafi' ibn Khadij had a wife who was past her prime. He married a young woman in addition to her and favoured the young woman over her. His first wife refused to remain content with this, so he divorced her once. When only a short time of her waiting period remained, he said: "If you wish, I will take you back and you may bear the favouritism, and if you wish, I will leave you until your waiting period ends!" She said: "Rather, take me back, and I will bear the favouritism." So he took her back, then favoured the other over her again, and she did not bear the favouritism, so he divorced her a second time and favoured the young woman. He said: "That is the reconciliation which, we have been told, Allah revealed concerning it: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion, there is no blame upon them if they make terms of settlement between themselves, and settlement is best﴾."

Al-Hasan said: Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed me, and Ayyub informed me, from Ibn Sirin, from Ubayda, with the like of the report of al-Zuhri, and he added in it: "If he harms her with the third divorce, then he must give her her right or divorce her."

[[Note on report 10600: al-Hakim narrated this report in al-Mustadrak (2:308) with this wording, through Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, from Abd al-Razzaq, traced back to Rafi' ibn Khadij. Al-Hakim said: "A sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not narrate it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him.
Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan (7:296) at greater length, through another chain: through Abu al-Yaman, from Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamza, from al-Zuhri.
Malik narrated it in al-Muwatta' (p. 548): "From Ibn Shihab, from Rafi' ibn Khadij: that he married the daughter of Muhammad ibn Maslama al-Ansari," the hadith, which is close to the wording of Ma'mar from al-Zuhri.
Al-Shafi'i narrated the report of Rafi' ibn Khadij in abridged form through Sufyan ibn Uyayna, from al-Zuhri (al-Umm 5:171).]]

10601. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, saying: Abu Asim told us, saying: Isa told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿ill-treatment or aversion﴾: it is a man's saying to his wife: "You are old, and I want to replace you with a young, beautiful woman. So be content for your son's sake, and I will not give you any of my time." That is the reconciliation between them. He was Abu al-Sanabil ibn Ba'kak.

[[Note on report 10601: "Abu al-Sanabil ibn Ba'kak ibn al-Harith ibn Umayla ibn al-Sabbaq ibn Abd al-Dar al-Qurashi" was a Companion from among those who converted at the Conquest (of Makkah). al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah narrated from him.
"Ba'kak" (with a fatha, then a sukun, then a fatha) is of the pattern of "Ja'far."]]

10602. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa told us, saying: Shibl told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, regarding ﴿ill-treatment or aversion﴾, then he mentioned something similar. Shibl said: I said to him: "If a man has a wife and he gives her time, but does not give time to this one?" He said: "If she agrees to that, then there is nothing upon him."

[[In the printed edition: "If she reconciles with him," but I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

10603. Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: My father told us, from Isra'il, from Jabir, who said: I asked Amir about a man who has a wife and wants to divorce her, but she says: "Do not divorce me, and give me one day and give the newly married one two days." He said: "There is no harm in it; it is a reconciliation."

10604. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi, regarding ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion, there is no blame upon them if they make terms of settlement between themselves, and settlement is best﴾: He said: A woman sees some decline (al-hatt) from her husband, and she has grown old, or does not bear children, so her husband wants to marry another. He comes to her and says: "I want to marry a young woman, more youthful than you, so that she may bear me children, and I will favour her in days and provision." If she agrees to that, well and good; otherwise he divorces her, and they reconcile on what both of them love.

[[In the printed edition: "some harshness" (al-jafa'), which differs from the manuscript. "Al-hatt" means lowering and dropping. It means: some diminishing of her right and coolness in her affection.
In the printed edition and the manuscript: "more fitting (ansab) than you," which is a misreading; the correct reading is what I have given.]]

10605. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words ﴿ill-treatment or aversion﴾: ill-treatment toward her, he became displeased with her. ﴿A man who has two wives﴾ ﴿or aversion﴾, by abandoning her, ﴿there is no blame upon them if they make terms of settlement between themselves, settlement﴾: either he pleases her so she releases him, or she pleases him so he inclines towards her.

[[In the manuscript and printed edition: "ghurida bi-ha" with the letter 'ayn, which is an error; the correct reading is what I have given ("ghurida," with a fatha on the ghayn and a kasra on the ra', meaning he was bored with her and tired of her). Then his later words "the man who has two wives" mean that this applies to a man who has two wives. It is a new statement, not connected to the verb before it.]]

10606. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih told me, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words ﴿ill-treatment or aversion﴾, meaning: hatred.

10607. Al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj told me: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words ﴿ill-treatment or aversion﴾: It is the man who has an older wife under him, and he marries a young woman in addition to her, and he inclines towards her, and she is more beloved to him than the older one. So he makes terms with the older one, that he will give her from his wealth and give her a known portion of his time.

10608. Amr ibn Ali and Zayd ibn Akhzam told us, both saying: Abu Dawud told us, saying: Sulayman ibn Mu'adh told us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Ikrima, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Sawda feared that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would divorce her, so she said: "Do not divorce me, and do not give me my turn." He did so, and this was revealed: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾.

[[Note on report 10608: "Zayd ibn Akhzam al-Ta'i al-Nabhani" was a hafiz who narrated from Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, Yahya al-Qattan, Ibn Mahdi and Abu Amir al-Aqadi. All the compilers narrated from him except Muslim. al-Nasa'i said: "Trustworthy." The Zanj killed him during the upheaval in the year 257 AH. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.
"Akhzam" has a khā' with a dot and a zāy. In the printed edition it was "Akhram," which is an error. This report is missing from the manuscript.
The report is in the Musnad of Abu Dawud (p. 349, no. 2683), and in al-Tirmidhi in the Book of Tafsir, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan (3:297). Their narrations all agree:
"... She said: 'Do not divorce me, keep me, and let my day be for Aisha.' He did so, and this verse was revealed: ﴿And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion﴾, the verse, ﴿...whatever they agree upon between them is permissible.﴾"
I do not know where this variation in the wording of the report came from, and I hope it is not an alteration by an earlier copyist.
al-Tirmidhi said after narrating it: "This is a hasan sahih gharib hadith."]]

* *

The readers differed regarding the recitation of His words ﴿that they make terms of settlement between themselves﴾ [[In the manuscript and printed edition: "an yuṣālaḥā" with an alif, but the correct writing is what I have given, following the script of the Qur'an, so that the script allows both readings.]].

The majority of the readers of Madina and some of the people of Basra recited it with a fatha on the "ya'" and a shadda on the "sad," meaning: "an yatasālaḥā baynahumā ṣulḥan," and then the "ta'" was assimilated into the "ṣad," so both became a shadda-ed "ṣad." [[This recitation is written thus: (أَنْ يَصَّالَحَا بَيْنَهُمَا صُلْحًا).]]

* *

The majority of the readers of Kufa recited it: ﴿an yuṣliḥā baynahumā ṣulḥan﴾, with a damma on the "ya'" and a light "sad," meaning: the husband and the wife made peace between them.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most preferable of the two readings to me is the reading of the one who recited ﴿an yuṣālaḥā baynahumā ṣulḥan﴾ [[In the manuscript and printed edition together: "illā an yuṣālaḥā" with an added "illā," which a copyist inserted by mistake, and the editor followed him.]], with a fatha on the "ya'" and a shadda on the "sad," meaning: "yatasālaḥā." Because "al-tasāluḥ" in this context is more well known, clearer in meaning, more eloquent, and more common on the tongues of the Arabs than "al-iṣlāh." And "al-iṣlāh," in the sense of the opposite of "corruption," is more well known than it in the sense of "al-tasāluḥ."

If someone supposes that His word "ṣulḥan" indicates that the reading of the one who recited ﴿yuṣliḥā﴾ with a damma on the "ya'" is more correct, then the matter is contrary to what he supposes. That is because "al-ṣulḥ" is a noun and not a verb, so it cannot be used as evidence to decide which of the two readings is more correct in His words "yuṣliḥā baynahumā ṣulḥan."

* *

On the interpretation of His words: ﴿And the souls are made present with stinginess, but if you do good and fear Allah, then indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾ (4:128).

Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed regarding the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: Its meaning: the souls of the women were made present with stinginess regarding their shares from the souls and wealth of their husbands. [[In the printed edition: "and their wealth," but the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]

Those who said this:

10609. Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: Imran ibn Uyayna told us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas: "And the souls are made present with stinginess," he said: their share of it.

10610. Muhammad ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Abu Ahmad told us. And Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us. Both said together: Sufyan told us, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "And the souls are made present with stinginess," he said: regarding the days.

10611. Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Abd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata': "And the souls are made present with stinginess," he said: regarding the days and provision.

10612. Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: Ibn Mahdi and Ibn Yaman told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', who said: regarding provision.

10613. Ibn Wakī'... told us, saying: Rawh told us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', who said: regarding provision. [[Report 10613: I fear that the correct chain of this is "Ibn Wakī' said: my father told us, Rawh told us," and "my father told us" has dropped out.]]

10614. And Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: My father told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata': "And the souls are made present with stinginess," he said: regarding the days. [[Report 10614: This report is missing from the manuscript.]]

10615. Ibn Bashshar told us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far told us, saying: Shu'ba told us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding this verse: "And the souls are made present with stinginess," he said: the woman's soul is attached to her share from her husband, from his self and his wealth.

10616. Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: My father told us, from Shu'ba, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, with the like of it.

10617. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Hibban ibn Musa told us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, saying: Shu'ba told us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, the like of it.

10618. Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: Ibn Yaman told us, from Sufyan, from a man, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: regarding provision.

10619. Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: Ibn Mahdi told us, from Sufyan, from al-Shaybani, from Bukayr ibn al-Akhnas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: regarding the days and provision.

10620. Ibn Wakī' told us, saying: Ibn Mahdi told us, from Sufyan, from al-Shaybani, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: regarding the days and provision.

10621. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Muslim ibn Ibrahim told us, saying: Shu'ba told us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr regarding His words: "And the souls are made present with stinginess," he said: the woman is stingy with her husband's wealth and self.

10622. Al-Muthanna told us, saying: Hibban ibn Musa informed us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Shurayk, from Salim, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: When this verse was revealed, "And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion," a woman came and said: "I want you to give me a share of yourself!" She had been content for him to leave her without divorcing her and without coming to her. So Allah revealed: "And the souls are made present with stinginess."

10623. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn told us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal told us, saying: Asbat told us, from al-Suddi: "And the souls are made present with stinginess," he said: her soul looks forward to her husband and to his provision. He said: And he claimed that it was revealed concerning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Sawda bint Zam'a. She had grown old, so the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wanted to divorce her, and they agreed that he would keep her and give her day to Aisha, so she was stingy about her place with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

* *

Others said: The meaning of that: the soul of each one of the man and the woman was made present with stinginess regarding his or her right with respect to the other.

Those who said this:

10624. Yunus told me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: I heard Ibn Zayd say regarding His words: "And the souls are made present with stinginess," he said: his soul is not content to give her anything, so that she releases him; and her soul is not content to give him anything of her wealth, so that he inclines towards her.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two sayings regarding this is the saying of the one who said: it means: the souls of the women were made present with stinginess regarding their shares from their husbands, in the days and provision.

* *

"Al-shuhh" (stinginess) is excessive greed for a thing, and in this place it means: the woman's excessive greed for her share of her husband's days and provision.

* *

So the meaning of the speech: the souls of the women were made present with their desires, from the excess of greed for their rights from their husbands, and stinginess with that regarding their co-wives.

* *

In agreement with what we have said about the meaning of "al-shuhh," it is reported from Ibn Abbas that he used to say:

10625. Al-Muthanna told me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Mu'awiya told me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas regarding His words: "And the souls are made present with stinginess," and "al-shuhh" is his desire for a thing, that he is greedy for it.

* *

We only said this to be the more correct view, rather than the view of the one who said: "What is meant by that: the souls of men and women were made present with stinginess," as Ibn Zayd said. That is because a man reconciling with his wife by giving her from his wealth as a payment (ju'l) on condition that she overlook his division of time for her is not permissible. That is because he receives no return for the payment he has offered her. A ju'l is valid only upon a return, either a specific thing or a benefit. When a man makes a payment to a woman on condition that she overlook his day and night, he has acquired from her no specific thing and no benefit. Since that is so, it is one of the meanings of consuming wealth falsely. Since that is so, it is known that there is no basis for the view of the one who said: "What is meant by that is the man and the woman."

If someone supposes that, since it is a right of the woman, and she has the claim to it, the man may ransom himself from her with a payment, just as the one claiming pre-emption (shuf'a) in a share of a house that a man bought from a partner who has a right in it has the claim to it, so it should be that the one claimed against may ransom it with a payment: then the consensus of all on the invalidity of making reconciliation on this in return for a consideration, since the one claimed against in pre-emption does not receive from it a specific thing or a benefit, is evidence against the reconciliation of a man with his wife for a consideration, on condition that she overlook her claim against him regarding division of time.

When that is invalid, it is correct that the interpretation of the verse is what we have said. The report we mentioned from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab and Sulayman ibn Yasar [[This is the report numbered 10600.]] has made clear that His words: "And if a woman fears from her husband ill-treatment or aversion," the verse, were revealed concerning the matter of Rafi' ibn Khadij and his wife, when he married a young woman in addition to her and favoured the young woman over her, and the older one refused to remain content with the favouritism, so he divorced her once and left her. When her waiting period was nearly over, he gave her the choice between separation, taking her back, and bearing the favouritism, and she chose taking back and bearing the favouritism. He took her back and favoured the other over her, and she did not bear it, so he divorced her. In that is clear evidence that His words "And the souls are made present with stinginess" mean only: the souls of the women were made present with stinginess regarding their rights from their husbands, as we have described.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: As for His words "And if you do good and fear Allah," it means: and if you do good, O men, in your dealings with your wives, [[See the explanation of "al-ihsan" (good doing) in the indexes of language earlier.]] when you dislike in them ugliness or character or some of what you dislike in them, by being patient with them, fulfilling their rights to them, and treating them kindly. "And fear Allah," he says: and fear Allah regarding them by abandoning oppression of them by you in what is owed to whoever you dislike among them, of division of time for her, provision, and good companionship. ﴿Then indeed Allah is ever, of what you do, Acquainted﴾: he says: indeed Allah is ever, of what you know in the matters of your wives, O men, of good to them and good companionship, and of oppression of them in what is obligatory for you towards them and due. ﴿Acquainted﴾ means: knowing, aware, nothing of it is hidden from Him, but He knows it, and He is the Reckoner over you, until He pays you the recompense for that: the good-doer among you for his good, and the evil-doer for his evil. [[See the explanation of "khabir" (acquainted) in the indexes of language earlier.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 129 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And you will never be able to be just between wives, even if you should strive [to do so]; so do not incline completely [to one] and leave her [as it were] suspended﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, "And you will never be able to be just between wives," may His mention be exalted, He means: you men will never be able to make equal between your wives in love of their hearts, such that you are just between them in that matter, so that in your hearts there is no love for any of them except like what there is for her co-wives, because that is something you do not control, and it is not in your hands. "Even if you should strive" means: even if you should strive to make them equal in that matter, as [in the report]:

10626 - Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words: "And you will never be able to be just between wives, even if you should strive," he said: It is obligatory that you will not be able to be just between them.

* *

"So do not incline completely," means: do not incline with your desires toward the one whose love you do not control, completely inclining, so that this leads you to act unjustly toward her co-wives by neglecting the duty owed to them from your side, namely: the turn allotted to them, the maintenance provided for them, and living with them in kindness [[See the explanation of "al-mayl" above, 8: 212.]]. "And leave her as it were suspended" means: and leave the one other than the one you have inclined to by your desires, "as it were suspended," meaning: like one who is neither a married woman nor a widow.

* *

Those who interpreted it said what we have said regarding this.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His mention be exalted, only commanded, by His words, "So do not incline completely and leave her as it were suspended," men to be just between their wives in what they are able to be just between them: the division among them, the maintenance, and refraining from injustice in that by favoring one over the other in what He has obligated them to be just between them, since He has excused them from what they cannot be just about between them, namely what is in the hearts of love and inclination.

* *

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And if you amend [your conduct] and fear Allah, then indeed Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ (129)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His mention be exalted, He means: "And if you amend" your deeds, O people, by being just in your division among your wives, and in what Allah has made obligatory for them upon you of maintenance and kind treatment (al-'ushra bil-ma'ruf), and do not act unjustly in that, "and fear Allah" — He says: and fear Allah regarding the inclination that He has forbidden you, by inclining toward one of them over the other, so that you wrong her of her right which Allah has made incumbent upon you for her. "Then indeed Allah is ever Forgiving" — He says: then indeed Allah covers over for you what has passed from you of inclination and injustice toward them before that, by leaving off punishing you for it, and veils that from you by His pardon for what has passed from you in that before. "Merciful" — He says: and He has been Merciful to you, since He has turned to you in repentance, accepting your repentance for what has passed from you of injustice toward them in that, and in His permitting you reconciliation between yourselves and them, by their forgoing their rights to division from you on condition that they not be divorced.

[Refer to the explanation of "taqwa" (God-consciousness), "Ghafur" (Forgiving), and "Rahim" (Merciful) in the earlier lexical indexes.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 130:

The explanation of His words: ﴿And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance. And Allah is ever All-Encompassing and Wise.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: If the wife, whose husband has turned away from her (nushuz), when he has turned aside from her out of inclination toward her co-wife because of her beauty or youth, or other things to which souls are inclined toward that one [[In the printed edition: "or he turns away from her ... with which souls incline to her." The text without "to" and with "him" is the wording of the manuscript, and it is correct. The meaning: because of which souls incline toward this woman described.]] refuses reconciliation by her forgoing her day and night for her husband, and she seeks her right from him regarding equal division (qasm), maintenance (nafaqah), and what Allah has made obligatory for her upon him, and the husband refuses to deal with her with the kindness that Allah has urged upon him by His saying: ﴿And if you do good and fear Allah, then indeed Allah is ever Acquainted with what you do﴾, and [he refuses] to keep her in the equal division due to her, in maintenance, and in companionship, while he inclines toward the other, so they separate by the husband's divorce of her, ﴿Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance﴾, meaning: Allah will enrich the husband and the divorced wife from the abundance of His bounty. As for her, He will provide her with a husband who is better for her than the first divorcer, or with wider provision and chastity. As for him, He will provide him with wide provision and a wife who is better for him than the divorced one [[See the explanation of "abundance" (si'ah) earlier, p. 121. And His saying "or chastity" means: with wide provision ... or with chastity.]] or chastity. ﴿And Allah is ever All-Encompassing﴾, meaning: Allah is All-Encompassing for both of them, in His provision to them and to others of His creation, ﴿Wise﴾ in what He decreed between him and her of separation and divorce, and the other meanings we have explained of the judgment between them in these verses and others, and in His other rulings, His management, and His decrees concerning His creation. [[See the explanation of "Wise" earlier in the language indices.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 131:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And We have certainly instructed those who were given the Scripture before you and [now] you, to fear Allah. But if you disbelieve - then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth; and ever is Allah Free of need and Praiseworthy.﴾ (131)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His mention be exalted, He means: To Allah belongs the entire dominion of everything that the seven heavens and the seven earths contain, of all things without exception. Allah, may His mention be exalted, mentioned this immediately after His words, "And if they separate, Allah will enrich each of them from His abundance," as an admonition from Him to His creation about where to turn in desire when one of them parts from his wife, so that they may turn to Him in distress over need, poverty, and loneliness caused by parting from one's dwelling and wife; and as a reminder from Him to them that He is the One to whom all things belong, and that whoever has dominion over all things is not incapable of enriching him, and everyone in poverty and need, and comforting everyone in loneliness.

* *

Then Allah, may His mention be exalted, returned to rebuking those who had worked to defend the Banu Ubayriq and to reproaching them, and to threatening whoever among them had done what the apostate had done. So He said [see the explanation of the preceding verses, from verse 105 to verse 116]: ﴿And We have certainly instructed those who were given the Scripture before you and [now] you﴾, meaning: We have certainly commanded the People of the Scripture, who are the people of the Torah and the Gospel, and "[now] you" meaning: We have commanded you and said to you and to them: ﴿to fear Allah﴾, meaning: beware of Allah lest you disobey Him and oppose His command and prohibition [see the explanation of "wasiyyah" (instruction) in what preceded, 3:93-96; 405/8:30, 68; and see his discussion of "an" (that) with "wasiyyah" in what preceded, 3:94, 95]. ﴿But if you disbelieve﴾, meaning: if you, believers, deny His instruction to you and oppose it, ﴿then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, meaning: by your opposition to His instruction you harm no one but yourselves, and by your disbelief in that you will not escape becoming like the Jews and Christians in the descent of His punishment upon you and the alighting of His wrath upon you, just as it alighted upon them when they altered His covenant and broke His pact, so He changed for them the ease of living and the security of their homes [in the printed edition it reads "wa amn al-shurb" with a shin, which is a clear error; it is correct in the manuscript. "Al-sarb" (with a kasra on the sin and a sukun on the ra') means self, wealth, family, and children. It is said: "Asbaha fulan aminan fi sarbihi," meaning secure in his self, family, wealth, and children. The sin may also be vowelled with a fatha, so it is said: "asbaha aminan fi sarbihi," meaning in his course and his direction wherever he travelled and headed; and "khafd al-'aysh" means its softness and abundance], and made some of them apes and swine. That is because to Him belongs the entire dominion of everything the heavens and the earth contain; nothing He wills with regard to all of it or any part of it is beyond His power, whether honouring whom He wills to honour, or humbling whom He wills to humble, or any other matters at all, because the creation is His creation; to Him they turn in need and want, by Him are their strength and their survival, and their destruction and their annihilation; and He is "the Free of need," who is not touched by any need for anything, nor does any poverty befall Him that would compel Him to you, O people, nor to anyone else [see the explanation of "al-Ghani" in what preceded, 5:521, 570]; and "the Praiseworthy," who has deserved praise from you, O creation, through His good favours toward you and His beautiful bounties upon you. So maintain that, O people, by fearing Him and hastening to obey Him in what He commands you and forbids you, as:

10674 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd Allah ibn Hashim narrated to us, saying: Sayf informed us, from Abu Rawq, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him), regarding "And ever is Allah Free of need and Praiseworthy," he said: "Free of need from His creation," and "Praiseworthy," he said: "One whom they praise."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 132:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾ (4:132).

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: To Allah belongs the dominion over all that the heavens and the earth contain. He is the Sustainer of all of it in its entirety and the Guardian of all of that; no knowledge of any part of it escapes Him, and its preservation and management do not burden Him, as related:

10675 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, regarding ﴿and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾, he said: "Guardian." [[See the explanation of "al-Wakil" in what has preceded: 7:405 / 8:566 / 9:193.]]

* *

If someone says: What is the purpose of repeating His saying ﴿to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ in two verses, one immediately after the other?

It is said: It was repeated because the two statements about what is in the heavens and the earth differ in meaning across the two verses. The statement in one of the two verses mentions the creation's need for its Originator and the Originator's independence from it; in the other, it mentions the Originator's preservation of it, His knowledge of it, and His management of it.

If someone says: Why not say ﴿and Allah is Ever Rich and Praiseworthy﴾ and ﴿sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾?

It is said: What is in the verse in which He said ﴿and Allah is Ever Rich and Praiseworthy﴾ is suitable to conclude with the description of Allah as self-sufficient and praiseworthy, but it does not mention anything suitable to conclude with a description of Him alongside preservation and management. Therefore He repeated His saying ﴿to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 133:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿If He wills, He can remove you, O people, and bring others; and Allah is ever capable of that﴾ (4:133).

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His mention be glorified, He means: If Allah wills, O people, to "remove you" — that is, to remove you by destroying and annihilating you — "and bring others," meaning: and bring other people besides you to support and aid His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and to assist him. "And Allah is ever capable of that," meaning: Allah is capable of destroying and annihilating you and of replacing you with others besides you. "Capable" means: having power over that. [[See the explanation of "al-Qadir" (the Capable) earlier: 1: 361 / 2: 484, 504.]]

* *

Almighty Allah rebuked, through these verses, the traitors who betrayed the coat of mail whose matter we have described, those whom Allah mentioned in His saying: ﴿And do not be an advocate for the treacherous﴾ (4:105). He warned the Companions of Muhammad ﷺ against being like them, or doing what the apostate among them did in his apostasy and his joining the polytheists. He made them know that whoever among them does his deed will harm only himself, and will not bring ruin by his apostasy upon anyone other than himself, because he is the one in need — along with everything in the heavens and on the earth — of Allah, while Allah is free of need of them. Then He threatened them in His saying: "If He wills, He can remove you, O people, and bring others," with destruction and extermination, if they do the deed of Ibn Ubayriq, Ṭu'mah the apostate [["Ṭu'mah" is the name of "Ibn Ubayriq", as mentioned earlier in the report no. 10416.]], and with replacing them with others besides them, to support His Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, accompany him, and aid him in his religion, as He said in another verse: ﴿And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people, then they will not be like you﴾ (47:38).

It has been related from the Prophet ﷺ that when this verse was revealed, he struck Salman on the back with his hand and said: "They are the people of this one," meaning the non-Arabs of Persia. Thus:

10676 — I was told, from ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Muhammad, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet ﷺ.

[[The report no. 10676: "ʿAbd al-ʿAziz ibn Muhammad ibn ʿUbayd ibn Abi ʿUbayd al-Darawardi" — spoken of (criticised). Biographed in al-Tahdhib.

And "Suhayl ibn Abi Salih" — spoken of. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.

And his father: "Dhakwan al-Samman," "Abu Salih," a trustworthy, firm narrator in his transmissions from Abu Hurayrah. Biographed in al-Tahdhib; passed as nos. 304, 3226, 5387.

This report was cited by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 6: 67, attributing it to Ibn Jarir, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Mardawayh.

It will come with other chains in the commentary on Surat Muhammad, at its end, 26: 42 (Bulaq); we will discuss them there.]]

* *

Qatadah said regarding this:

10677 — Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His saying: "If He wills, He can remove you, O people, and bring others; and Allah is ever capable of that": "Capable, by Allah, is our Lord of that: to destroy whomever He wills of His creation, and to bring others after them."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 134:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world — with Allah is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. And ever is Allah Hearing and Seeing.﴾ (4:134)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, He, great is His praise, means: "Whoever desires," from among the hypocrites (munafiqun) who showed faith in Muhammad (ﷺ), those who conceal disbelief while at the same time displaying faith, "the reward of this world," meaning: the goods of this world (ʿaraḍ al-dunya), [[See the explanation of "thawab" above: 2:458 / 7:262, 304, 490.]] by his displaying what he showed of faith with his tongue. "Then with Allah is the reward of this world," meaning: his recompense in this world, from it, and his reward therein, which is what he obtains of the spoils when he witnesses a battle with the Prophet, and his security for himself, his offspring and his wealth, and what is similar to that. As for his reward in the Hereafter, it is the Fire of Hell.

* *

So the meaning of the verse is: whoever among the doers from the hypocrites intends by his deed the reward of this world and its recompense for his deed, then Allah will repay him for it: his recompense in this world from this world, and his recompense in the Hereafter from the Hereafter, of punishment and retribution. This is because Allah is able to do all of that, and He owns all of it, as He said in the other verse: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein, and they will not be deprived therein. Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire, and what they did therein will be voided, and worthless is what they used to do.﴾ [Surah Hud: 15–16].

* *

What is meant by this, great is His praise, is those who hastened in the matter of the Banu Ubayriq, [[In the printed edition: "those who strove in the matter of the Banu Ubayriq"; in the manuscript, as I have written it, the letters are undotted. It is said "tatayya'a fulan fi al-amr wa-tatayya'a": when one hastens to it and rushes into it without thought or deliberation. This is used only for evil, not for good. What is in the printed edition is correct in meaning, context and report, but I followed the manuscript's orthography, which also agrees with the context of their story.]] and those whom He described in His saying: ﴿And do not argue on behalf of those who betray themselves. Indeed, Allah does not like one who is a betrayer, sinful. They conceal themselves from the people but cannot conceal themselves from Allah, and He is with them when they plot by night what He does not approve of in speech.﴾ [Surah An-Nisa: 107–108], and whoever was of their likeness in their actions and hypocrisy.

* *

As for His saying: "And ever is Allah Hearing and Seeing," it means: Allah was Hearing of what these hypocrites say, who desire the reward of this world by their deeds, and their display to the believers of what they show them when they meet the believers, and their saying to them, "We believe" [[See the explanation of "Hearing" above: 6:363, and the references there.]] — "Seeing," meaning: He was Seeing of them and of what they harbour toward the believers, folding it within themselves, of deceit and the rancour that is in their breasts toward them, which they conceal and do not reveal to them. [[In the printed edition, "lahum" has been dropped from the end of this sentence.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 135 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So do not follow [your] desires, lest you not be just﴾

This is an admonition from Allah, exalted is His mention, to His believing servants, who believe in Him and in His Messenger [[It is said: "taqaddama ilayhi fi kadha," meaning he commanded him with a command or a prohibition; here it means a prohibition.]] that they do as those did who approached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ regarding the matter of the Banu Ubayriq, [asking him] to make excuses for them before his companions, to defend them, and to make their matter appear good by saying that they were people of want and poverty. Allah says to them: "O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice," meaning: let standing firm in justice be among your characteristics and qualities, [[See the explanation of "al-qist" above, 6:77, 270 / 7:541.]] that is, in justice, "witnesses for Allah."
* *
"Shuhada'" (witnesses) is the plural of "shahid" (witness).
* *
"Shuhada'" is put in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (qat') referring to the subject of "qawwamin" in the phrase "alladhina amanu" [["Qat'," a category of ḥāl (circumstantial accusative); see what has passed in the index of technical terms.]]. Its meaning: stand firm in justice for Allah when you bear witness, or: at the time of your witnessing.
"Even if it be against yourselves," meaning: even if your testimony is against yourselves, or against your parents or relatives, [[In the printed edition: "or against your parents (wald-ikum)," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]] then stand firm in it with justice and fairness, and establish it in its correctness by saying in it the truth, and do not lean in it toward the rich because of his wealth against the poor, nor toward the poor because of his poverty against the rich, lest you act unjustly. For Allah, who made equal the judgment concerning the rich and the poor in what He obligated you, O people, of establishing testimony for each of them with justice, is "more worthy of both," and more entitled than you, because He is the owner of both and more worthy of them than you. He knows what is in the interest of each of them in that and in all other matters more than you do. Therefore He commanded you to equalize between them in testimony for them and against them. "So do not follow [your] desires, lest you be just," meaning: do not follow the desires of your souls to incline in your testimony when you establish it, toward the rich against the poor, or toward the poor against the rich, so that you say other than the truth. Rather, stand firm in it with justice, and render the testimony as Allah has commanded you to render it, with fairness toward the one for whom or against whom you testify.
* *
If someone says: How can a witness who testifies with justice stand firm in testimony against himself? Does a witness testify against himself?
[[In the printed edition: "wa-hal yashhadu al-shahid," and in the manuscript: "wa-bima yashhadu." I consider what is in the printed edition to be correct, because of his answer "yes," and I almost read it: "wa-bima yashhadu al-shahid," had the answer of Abu Ja'far not indicated otherwise.]]
It is said: Yes, and that is when a right belonging to another is upon him, so he acknowledges it for him; that is his standing firm for him in testimony against himself.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: This verse, in my view, is a disciplining by Allah, exalted is His praise, of His believing servants, that they do what those did who excused the Banu Ubayriq, in their theft of what they stole and their betrayal of what they betrayed, from among those we mentioned earlier [[In the printed edition: "wa-khiyanatihim ma khanu min dhikr ma qila 'inda rasul Allah...", which is corrupt speech, different from the manuscript. The manuscript reads as I have adopted, except that it wrote "min dhakarna qabl" and placed a fatha on the mim of "min," which is an error in the copyist's writing and transmission; that fatha is really another mim in "mimman" which he misread, so he misreported it. Similar things have occurred in such letters many times before, and I have pointed them out.]] = with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and their testimony for them with him as to their righteousness. So He said to them: when you stand to testify for or against a person, speak in it with justice, [[In the printed edition: "fa-qawwamu fiha bil-'adl," and what is in the manuscript is pure correctness.]] even if your testimony is against yourselves, your fathers, your mothers, and your relatives, and let not the wealth or poverty of the one for whom you testify, or his kinship and near relation to you, lead you to testify falsely for him, or to refrain from testifying against him with the truth and concealing it.
* *
It has been said that it was revealed as a disciplining of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
Those who said this:
10678 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding His saying: "O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah," he said: It was revealed concerning the Prophet ﷺ, when two men, one rich and one poor, brought a dispute before him, and he was inclined toward the poor man, thinking that the poor man would not wrong the rich man. But Allah refused except that he should stand firm in justice regarding the rich and the poor, so He said: "Whether he be rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So do not follow [your] desires, lest you be just," the verse.
* *
Others said: Regarding this, it is similar to our statement: it was revealed concerning testimony, a command from Allah to the believers that they make equal, in their standing firm with their testimonies, for whomever they stand with them, [[In the printed edition: "li-man qamu lahu biha," adding "lahu," which corrupts the speech. The context is: "amran min Allah al-mu'minin ... li-man qamu biha," i.e., for whoever among the believers stood with testimony, and mentioning it is an interjection in another statement, namely his saying: "in their standing firm with their testimonies."]] between the rich and the poor.
Those who said this:
10679 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: "Be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives," he said: Allah commanded the believers to speak the truth even against themselves, their fathers, or their sons, and not to show favor to a rich man because of his wealth, nor to have mercy on a poor man because of his poverty. This is His saying: "Whether he be rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So do not follow [your] desires, lest you be just," lest you abandon the truth and act unjustly.
10680 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, saying: Ibn al-Mubarak informed us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, regarding the testimony of a father for his son and of a close relative. He said: That was the custom of the past among the early Muslims, and they would interpret in it the saying of Allah: "O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether he be rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both," the verse. So the righteous early Muslims were not accused regarding the testimony of a father for his son, nor a son for his father, nor a brother for his brother, nor a man for his wife. Then people became corrupt after that [["Dakhala" (on the pattern of "fariḥa") is said: "dakhala amruhu dakhalan" (both vowels fatha), meaning it became corrupt, and "al-dakhal" (both fatha) is deceit and corruption. "Fulan madkhul al-Islam" is said when there is deceit and corruption in him, which is hypocrisy.]], and there appeared among them matters that led the rulers to accuse them, so the testimony of whoever was accused was rejected when it came from their relatives. This became so of the son and the father, and the brother and the husband and the wife; only these were accused at the end of time. [[Would that I knew what Ibn Shihab would have said had he lived in our time, in which we are! We ask for safety, and we seek guidance from him in standing by what we were commanded in His Book.]]
10681 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: "O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah," to the end of the verse: The poverty of this man should not move you to have mercy on him so that you do not establish testimony against him. He said: This is said to the witness.
10682 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Zuray' narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah," the verse: This is regarding testimony. So establish testimony, O son of Adam, even against yourself, or your parents, or your close relatives, or the nobility of your people [[In the printed edition: "aw ashraf qawmik," as if he thought "sharafan" was an error; it is entirely correct, since "sharif" has plurals "ashraf," "shurafa'," and "sharaf" (with fatha on the shin and ra'). As they said "rajul karim" and "qawm karam." Had it been said that it is a description by the verbal noun like "'adl," it would have been correct.]]. For testimony belongs to Allah and is not for people. Allah is pleased with justice for Himself, and equity and justice are the balance of Allah on earth; by it Allah turns back the strong from the weak, the liar from the truthful, and the falsifier from the righteous. By justice He confirms the truthful, refutes the liar, repels the transgressor and humbles him, [[In the printed edition: "wa-yuwabbikhu" (rebukes), which has no meaning here. In the manuscript it is unpointed, and the correct reading is what I have adopted. It is said: "rankhu al-rajul," meaning he humiliated him. Had it been read "yuрikhu" with a ya', it would be correct; it is said: "they beat so-and-so until they made him weak," meaning they weakened and humiliated him. Qatadah al-Sadusi often used rare words of language in his speech.]] exalted is our Lord and blessed. By justice people are set right, O son of Adam. "Whether he be rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both," meaning: more worthy of your rich and your poor. He said: It has been mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah Moses, peace be upon him, said: "O Lord, what is the least thing You have placed on earth?" He said: "Justice is the least thing I have placed on earth." So let neither the wealth of the rich nor the poverty of the poor prevent you from testifying against him with what you know, for that is a right upon you. And He, exalted is His praise, said: "Allah is more worthy of both."
* *
It has been said: "Whether he be rich or poor," the verse, meaning: Allah is more worthy of the richness of the rich and the poverty of the poor, because that belongs to Him and not to anyone else. Therefore He said "bihima" (of both) and did not say "bihi" (of it).
* *
Others said: It was only said "bihima" because He said "in yakun ghaniyyan aw faqiran," without intending a specific poor man or a specific rich man, and he is unknown. When he is unknown, the reference to him may be made in singular, dual, or plural. [[In the printed edition: "al-radd 'alayhi bil-tawhid..." and what I have adopted from the manuscript is pure correctness.]]
* *
Those who held this view mentioned that in the reading of Ubayy: ﴿fa-llahu awla bihim﴾ (Allah is more worthy of them).
* *
Others said: "aw" in this place means "wa" (and).
* *
Others said: The dual "bihima" was permitted because both had been mentioned, as it was said: ﴿wa-lahu akhun aw ukhtun fa-li-kulli wahidin minhuma﴾ [Surat al-Nisa': 12].
* *
It has been said: it was permitted, because "man" is implied in it, as if it were said: "in yakun man khasama ghaniyyan aw faqiran" = meaning: two rich men or two poor men, "fa-llahu awla bihima" (Allah is more worthy of both).
* *
As for His saying: "So do not follow [your] desires, lest you be just," meaning: away from the truth, so that you deviate by abandoning the establishment of testimony in truth. And if it were directed to the meaning: "So do not follow the desires of your souls, fleeing from deviating from the truth in establishing testimony with justice," it would have been a valid interpretation. [[In the printed edition: "kana wajhan," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]]
* *
It has been said: the meaning of that is: "So do not follow desire so that you may be just" = as one says: "Do not follow your desire so that you may please your Lord," meaning: I forbid you from it, just as you please your Lord by abandoning it. [[See the Ma'ani al-Qur'an of al-Farra' 1:291.]]
* *
The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And if you distort [testimony] or refuse to give it, then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted﴾ [4:135]
Abu Ja'far said: The people of interpretation differed regarding its interpretation.
Some of them said: It means: "And if you distort," O judges, in judging for one of the two adversaries over the other, "or refuse, then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted."
They directed the meaning of the verse to refer to the judges, in the manner of the statement we mentioned from al-Suddi, that the verse was revealed concerning the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, as we mentioned earlier. [[This is the narration above, number 10678.]]
Those who said this:
10683 - Ibn Humayd and Ibn Wakic narrated to us, both saying: Jarir narrated to us, from Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan, from his father, from Ibn Abbas, regarding the saying of Allah: "And if you distort or refuse," he said: They are the two men who sit before the judge, and the judge's distortion and his turning away is toward one of them over the other. [[Narration 10683: "Qabus ibn Abi Zabyan al-Janbi," who narrated from his father "Husayn ibn Jundub" and others. Ibn Ma'in said: "Trustworthy, weak in narration." Ibn Hibban said: "He is alone in narrating from his father what has no basis, so he sometimes raises the mursal and makes the mawquf into a musnad. His father is trustworthy." See what has passed, number 9745.
His father "Abu Zabyan" is "Husayn ibn Jundub." He narrated from Umar, Ali, and Ibn Mas'ud. Trustworthy; see what has passed, number 9745.]]
* *
Others said: The meaning of that is: "And if you distort, O witnesses, in your testimonies, by altering them and not establishing them, or refuse them, by abandoning them."
Those who said this:
10684 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn Abbas regarding his saying: "And if you distort or refuse," he said: If you distort with your tongues in testimony, or refuse it.
10685 - Muhammad ibn Sa'd narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: My uncle narrated to me, saying: My father narrated to me, from his father, from Ibn Abbas regarding his saying: "O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah," to His saying: "And if you distort or refuse," he said: You twist your tongue away from the truth, and that is stammering, so you do not establish testimony as it should be. And "i'rad" is abandonment.
10686 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, saying: Isa narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying: "And if you distort," meaning you alter the testimony, "or refuse," he said: you conceal it.
10687 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfa narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And if you distort," he said: by altering the testimony, and "i'rad" is concealing it.
10688 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And if you distort or refuse," he said: If you distort or abandon.
10689 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "And if you distort or refuse," he said: You stammer or conceal. And this is regarding testimony.
10690 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "And if you distort or refuse," as for "distort," you twist the testimony so that you do not establish it; and as for "refuse," you turn away from it and conceal it, and say: I have no testimony!
10691 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said: "And if you distort," meaning you conceal the testimony, twisting some of it [[In the printed edition: "talwi tanqusu minha" (twists, diminishes some of it), and I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which is good and sound, from the saying "lawa 'anhu al-khabar," meaning he folded it up or told it not in its proper form.
The context in the printed edition was with the ta' in the sense of address: "talwi," "tu'rid," etc. So I have adopted what is in the manuscript, dotted accordingly.]] = or he turns away from it and conceals it, refusing to testify against him. He says: I conceal it from him because he is a poor man whom I have mercy on! So he says: I will not establish testimony against him. And he says: This is a rich man whom I keep and hope for what he has, so I will not testify against him! That is His saying: "Whether he be rich or poor."
10692 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "And if you distort," meaning you alter, "or refuse," meaning you abandon. [[In the manuscript: "tahrifu aw tahrifu," repeated, which I do not think is a mistake.]]
10693 - Muhammad ibn Amara narrated to us, saying: Hasan ibn Atiyya narrated to us, saying: Fudayl ibn Marzuq narrated to us, from Atiyya regarding His saying: "And if you distort," he said: If you stammer in testimony and corrupt it, "or refuse," he said: you abandon it. [[In the printed edition: "fa-tatrukuha," and what is in the manuscript is good.]]
10694 - Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Awn narrated to us, saying: Hushaym informed us, from Juwaybir, from al-Dahhak regarding His saying: "And if you distort or refuse," he said: If you distort in testimony, by not establishing it as it should be, "or refuse," he said: you conceal the testimony. [[In the printed edition: "an la tuqimuhuma" in the plural, and what is in the manuscript is good and fine.]]
10695 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hammad narrated to us, saying: Shayban narrated to us, from Qatadah: that he used to say: "And if you distort or refuse," meaning: stammer, "or refuse," he said: you leave it and do not testify.
10696 - It was narrated to me from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj, who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: Ubayd ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His saying: "And if you distort or refuse," as for "distort," it is that a man twists his tongue away from the truth, meaning in testimony.
* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two interpretations in this matter is the interpretation of the one who interprets it as meaning that the witness twists (layy) his testimony for the one he testifies for or against, which is his distorting it with his tongue [[In the printed edition: "لسانه" without the ba' (bi-lisanihi), and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]] and his abandoning its establishment, so that by this his testimony is nullified for the one he testifies for and against the one he testifies against. [[See the explanation of "al-layy" above, 6: 535-537 / 8: 435.]]

As for his turning away from it (i'rad), it is his leaving off its delivery and standing by it, so he does not bear witness to it. [[See the explanation of "al-i'rad" above, p. 268, note 4, and the references there.]]

We said that this interpretation is more correct because God, exalted is His praise, said: "Be persistent in justice, witnesses for God," so He commanded them to stand firmly by justice as witnesses. The most evident meaning of "witnesses" is what we have mentioned of describing them as bearing testimony.

* *

The readers differed concerning the recitation of His words: "wa-in talwu" (and if you distort).

The majority of the readers of the regional centres, apart from Kufa, recited it: ﴿وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا﴾ with two waws, from "lawaani al-rajul haqqi, wa-l-qawm yalwunani dayni" (the man postponed my right, and the people postponed my debt to me), which is when they delay it, "layy" (delay).

* *

A group of the readers of Kufa recited it: ﴿وإن تلوا﴾ with a single waw.

* *

For the reading of the one who recited it thus there are two aspects:
The first: that its reciter intended to hamza the waw because it is damma-vowelled, then dropped the hamza, so that the case-ending of the hamza transferred to the lam when he dropped it, and one waw remained. As if he meant "talu'u" and then deleted the hamza.
