If this aspect is intended, its meaning is the meaning of the one who recited "wa-in talwu" with two waws, except that it contradicts the familiar usage of the Arabs. That is because the second waw in "talwu" is the waw of the plural, and it is a marker of a meaning, so it is not valid to hamza it and then delete it after hamzing, which would nullify the marker of the meaning for which the deleted waw was introduced. [[This is a strange error from someone like Abu Ja'far, for the hamza in "talu'u" falls on the waw of the verb, which is the middle radical of the verb "lawa", and the deletion after dropping the hamza falls on the verb's waw, not the waw of the plural, which is original and was not introduced for a meaning. How then did Abu Ja'far err and think it was the waw of the plural!! See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 291.]]

The other aspect: that its reciter recited it thus, intending that "talu" derives from "al-wilaya" (guardianship), so its meaning would be: and if you take charge of people's affairs and abandon them. This meaning, when the reciter directs his recitation to it as we have described, is outside the meanings of the people of interpretation, and what the Companions of the Messenger of God ﷺ and the Successors directed the interpretation of the verse toward.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: Since the corruption of that is clear from both its aspects, the correct recitation which no other may be read with, in our view, is: ﴿وَإِنْ تَلْوُوا أَوْ تُعْرِضُوا﴾, with the meaning of "layy", which is delay.

* *

So the sense of the statement becomes: and if you push back from establishing the testimony in its proper form to the one to whom you are obligated to stand by it, so you alter it and substitute, or you turn away from it so you abandon standing by it for him, just as a man postpones another man's debt, repelling him by not paying him what is due to him, delaying him, as al-A'sha said:

يَلْوِينَني دَيْنِي النَّهارَ، وأَقْتَضِي ... دَيْنِي إذَا وَقَذَ النُّعَاسُ الرُّقَّدَا [[Diwan: 151, and Lisan (lawa) and (waqadha), from verses, the good ones of which, the first of which precedes it: "And I see the beauties, when I grew white-haired, deserting me, that I am not like them, a beardless youth. Indeed the beauties do not keep company with a man who has lost youth, though they may keep company with a beardless one. Would that I knew! Could I return as a youth like me, a fleeting time, to alight at Burqat Anqad, when my hair was black, following its shadow, playing in idle error, running hither and thither." "They postpone my debt to me by day, and I demand my debt when sleep overwhelms the sleepers." Note: the Diwan's version reads "wa-ajtazi dayni" (and I demand my debt), it is said "ijtaza daynahu", i.e. he demanded it from him, and similarly "tajaza daynahu". "Waqadhahu": he struck him until he went limp and approached death. "Waqadhahu al-nu'as" is a metaphor, meaning they became like drunkards who have gone limp and dazed from sleep.]]

* *

As for the interpretation of His words: "Indeed God is ever, of what you do, Aware," He meant: "Indeed God is ever, of what you do," in your establishing the testimony and your distorting it, and your turning away from it by concealing it, "Aware", meaning one who has knowledge of it and is informed of it, who preserves that record of you against you, until He requites you for it in the Hereafter, rewarding the good among you for their good and the evil for their evil. He says: so fear your Lord regarding that. [[See the explanation of "al-khabir" above in the language indices.]]

The interpretation of His saying, exalted be His praise: ﴿O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger and the Book which He revealed before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day has certainly strayed far astray﴾ [4:136].

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, is meant: "O you who have believed," [addressing] those who came before Muhammad from among the prophets and messengers, and who affirmed what they had been brought from Allah. "Believe in Allah and His Messenger," meaning: affirm Allah and Muhammad His Messenger, that he is Allah's Messenger, sent to you and to all the other nations before you. "And the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger," meaning: and affirm what Muhammad has brought you of the Book which Allah sent down to him, and that is the Qur'an. "And the Book which He revealed before," meaning: and believe in the Book which Allah revealed before the Book He sent down to Muhammad ﷺ, and that is the Torah and the Gospel.

* *

If someone says: What is the purpose of calling these people to believe in Allah, His Messenger, and His books, when He has already named them "believers"?

It is said: He, exalted be His praise, did not name them "believers"; rather, He described them as having "believed," and that is a description of them with a particular kind of affirmation. For they were of two groups: the People of the Torah, who affirmed it and the one who brought it, but who denied the Gospel, the Qur'an, Jesus and Muhammad, may Allah's blessings be upon them both; and the People of the Gospel, who affirmed it and the Torah and the rest of the books, but denied Muhammad ﷺ and the Furqan (the Criterion, i.e., the Qur'an). So He, exalted be His praise, said to them: "O you who have believed," meaning: by what you already profess of the books and messengers, "believe in Allah and His Messenger" Muhammad ﷺ, "and the Book which He sent down upon His Messenger," for you know that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and you find his description in your books; and [believe in] the Book which was revealed before, which you claim you believe in, for you will not be believers in it while you deny Muhammad, because your Book commands you to affirm him and what he has brought you. So believe in your Book by following Muhammad; otherwise you are disbelievers in it. This is the meaning of His command to them to believe in what He commanded them to believe in, after describing them with the words He used: "O you who have believed."

[[Abu Ja'far should have mentioned here the disagreement of the readers regarding the recitations of "anzala" and "unzila," and "nazzala" and "nuzzila." It is evident that he forgot to mention them here, so he deferred them to the place that follows on p. 323, footnote 1.]]

* *

As for His saying: "And whoever disbelieves in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day," its meaning is: whoever disbelieves in Muhammad ﷺ, denying his prophethood, has certainly strayed far astray.

Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, only said "and whoever disbelieves in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day" — its meaning being: whoever disbelieves in Muhammad and what he brought from Allah, [[In the printed edition it read: "Whoever disbelieves in Muhammad ﷺ, denying his prophethood, then he disbelieves in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day, because denial of any part of that is denial of all of it." The text printed above omits what I have restored, because the manuscript contains an error that confused the sentence, which the editor did not correct well; he deleted so that some phrases join others, and did so very poorly.

The error in the manuscript is that it presented the sentence as I have written it, except that it wrote: "Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, only said: whoever disbelieves in Allah, then he disbelieves in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers," and it became clear that "then he disbelieves" was a slip of the copyist's pen; the correct reading is to drop it, so the sentence stands as I have given it.

The structure of the sentence is: "Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, only said such-and-such ... its meaning ... such-and-such, because denial of any part of that is denial of all of it."]] = because denial of any part of that is denial of all of it, and because no one among creation's faith is valid except by believing in what Allah commanded them to believe in. [[When the first editor made that deletion in the sentence, he was compelled at this point to make the phrase: "That is because no one among creation's faith is valid..." and so he added "that" to the sentence.]] Disbelief in any part of it is disbelief in all of it. Therefore He said: "And whoever disbelieves in Allah and His angels and His books and His messengers and the Last Day," following His address to the People of the Book and His command to them to believe in Muhammad ﷺ, as a warning to them, while they affirm the oneness of Allah, the angels, the books, the messengers, and the Last Day, apart from Muhammad ﷺ and what he brought of the Furqan.

* *

As for His saying: "has certainly strayed far astray," it means: he has departed from the right path and deviated from the clear road to ruin, going astray far away. Because the disbelief of whoever disbelieves in these is a departure from the religion of Allah which He prescribed for His servants. Departure from the religion of Allah is the ruin in which is destruction, and straying from guidance is misguidance. [[See the explanation of "far astray" earlier, pp. 206–207, and the meaning of "al-dalal" (straying) in vol. 1: 195 / vol. 2: 495–496, and elsewhere in the language indices.]]

The interpretation (ta'wil) of His words: ﴿Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief - Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a path﴾ [4:137]

Abu Ja'far [al-Tabari] said: The scholars of interpretation (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the interpretation of this.

Some of them said: Its interpretation is: "Indeed, those who believed in Musa, then disbelieved in him, then believed" - meaning the Christians - "in Isa, then disbelieved in him, then increased in disbelief in Muhammad (ﷺ)": "Allah would not forgive them, nor would He guide them to a path."

Mention of those who said this:

10697. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief," and they are the Jews and the Christians. The Jews believed in the Torah, then disbelieved; the Christians believed in the Gospel, then disbelieved. Their disbelief in it was their abandoning it. "Then increased in disbelief" - in the Criterion (al-Furqan) and in Muhammad (ﷺ). So Allah said: "Allah would not forgive them, nor would He guide them to a path," meaning: Allah would not forgive them, nor would He guide them to the way of guidance, and they had disbelieved in the Book of Allah and in His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).

10698. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah regarding His words: "Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved," he said: These are the Jews; they believed in the Torah, then disbelieved. Then he mentioned the Christians, then said: "Then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief," meaning: they believed in the Gospel, then disbelieved in it, then increased in disbelief in Muhammad (ﷺ).

* * *

Others said: Rather, it refers to the hypocrites (ahl al-nifaq), that they believed, then apostatized, then believed, then apostatized, then increased in disbelief by dying upon disbelief. [Editor's note: In the printed edition: "upon their disbelief", and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]

Mention of those who said this:

10699. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid regarding His words: "Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief," he said: We used to think they were the hypocrites, and whoever was like them is included in that. "Then increased in disbelief": they persisted (tammu) upon their disbelief until they died. [Editor's note: In the printed edition it reads "nammu" with a nun, and the correct reading is what I have adopted. "Tamma 'ala al-shay'" means: he remained upon it and adhered to it.]

10700. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Then increased in disbelief," he said: They died. [Editor's note: By his words "they died", he means they died upon it; this is an abbreviation in the narration.]

10701. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "Then increased in disbelief," he said: Until they died. [Editor's note: In the manuscript it reads "when they died", meaning when they died upon it, and this too is correct.]

10702. Yunus narrated to us, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His words: "Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved," the verse, he said: These are the hypocrites; they believed twice and disbelieved twice, then increased in disbelief after that. [Editor's note: See the explanation of "then increased in disbelief" in what preceded, vol. 6, pp. 579-582.]

* * *

Others said: Rather, they are the People of the Two Scriptures, the Torah and the Gospel, who committed sins in their disbelief and then repented, but their repentance was not accepted, along with their persistence in their disbelief.

Mention of those who said this:

10703. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Abu Khalid narrated to us, from Dawud ibn Abi Hind, from Abu al-Aliyah: "Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief," he said: They are the Jews and the Christians; they sinned in their polytheism, then repented, but their repentance was not accepted. Had they repented from polytheism, it would have been accepted from them.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The most preferable of these statements for the interpretation of this verse is the statement of the one who said: It refers to the People of the Book who acknowledged the ruling of the Torah, then denied it by opposing it, then some of them acknowledged Isa and the Gospel, then denied it by opposing it, then denied Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Criterion, so they increased in disbelief upon their disbelief through their denial of him.

We only said that this is more correct in the interpretation of this verse because the verse before it concerns the narratives of the two groups of the People of the Book - I mean His words: "O you who believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger" - and there is no indication showing that His words "Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved" are cut off in meaning from what precedes it. So attaching it to what precedes is more preferable, until there comes an indication showing it is separate from it.

* * *

As for His words "Allah would not forgive them," it means: Allah would not conceal their disbelief and sins by pardoning them from punishment for it, but rather He would expose them before the witnesses. "Nor would He guide them to a path": that is, He would not guide them to the right path so as to grant them success in reaching it; rather He would forsake them from it, as a punishment for them for their great crime and their audacity against their Lord.

* * *

Some people held that the apostate is asked to repent three times, deriving this from this verse (yantazi'u, "one derives the meaning of a verse from the Book of Allah" when he infers and extracts it). Others disagreed with them on this.

Mention of those who said: He is asked to repent three times.

10704. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Hafs narrated to us, from Ash'ath, from al-Sha'bi, from Ali (peace be upon him), who said: Indeed, I used to ask the apostate to repent three times. Then he recited this verse: "Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved."

10705. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from Amir, from Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): The apostate is asked to repent three times. Then he recited: "Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed, then disbelieved, then increased in disbelief."

10706. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Abd al-Karim, from a man, from Ibn Umar who said: The apostate is asked to repent three times.

* * *

Others said: He is asked to repent each time he apostatizes.

Mention of those who said this:

10707. Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Amr ibn Qays, from one who heard Ibrahim, who said: The apostate is asked to repent each time he apostatizes.

* * *

Abu Ja'far said: The establishment of proof that the apostate is asked to repent the first time provides clear evidence that the ruling for each time he apostatizes from Islam is the ruling of the first time, in that his repentance is accepted and his Islam protects his blood. Because the cause that protected his blood the first time is his Islam, it is not permissible for the cause for which his blood was protected in the first instance to exist, and then his blood to be made lawful while it exists, unless one distinguishes between the ruling of the first time and the other times, by something that must be accepted from a firm principle, and then it would leave the domain of analogy (qiyas) at that point.

Commentary on the interpretation of His words: ﴿Give good tidings to the hypocrites that for them is a painful punishment (138)﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, "Give good tidings to the hypocrites," He means: inform the hypocrites. [In the manuscript and the printed edition: "He means by that," and the correct reading is what I have established.]

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "tabshir" (giving good tidings) earlier, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. [See what has passed: 1:383 / 2:393 / 3:221 / 6:287, 369, 370, 411.]

* *

"That for them is a painful punishment" means: that for them, on the Day of Resurrection, from Allah, because of their hypocrisy, is a "painful punishment," which is the painful one, and that is the punishment of Hell. [See the explanation of "alim" (painful) in the linguistic indexes of what has passed.]

**The interpretation of His saying:** ﴿Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek honour with them? Indeed, honour belongs entirely to Allah﴾ [4:139]

Abu Ja'far said: As for His saying, exalted is His praise, "Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers," it describes the hypocrites. Allah says to His Prophet: O Muhammad, give good tidings to the hypocrites who take the people of disbelief in Me and of opposition to My religion as "allies" (meaning: helpers and intimate friends) [[See the explanation of "al-wali" (ally) above, p. 247, note 5, and the references there.]] "instead of the believers," meaning: other than the believers [[See the explanation of "min dun" (instead of) above, p. 247, note 3, and the references there.]]. "Do they seek honour with them?" meaning: do they seek protection and strength from them, [[See the explanation of "al-ibtigha'" (seeking) above, p. 202, note 1, and the references there.]] by taking them as allies instead of the people of faith in Me? "Indeed, honour belongs entirely to Allah," meaning: those who take the disbelievers as allies, seeking honour with them, are the humiliated and the few. Why did they not take allies from among the believers, so that they might seek honour, protection and support from Allah, to whom belongs honour and protection, who bestows honour on whom He wills and humiliates whom He wills, so that He would give them honour and protect them?

* *

The root of "al-'izza" (honour) is hardness. From it comes the term for hard, firm ground, "'azaz." It is also said: "qad usti'uzza 'ala al-mari" (the sick man has been overcome), [["Usti'azza" is in the passive form. In a hadith: "that he was overcome (ista'azza) by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in his illness in which he died," meaning: the illness became severe for him, overwhelmed him, and he approached death.

And His saying, "and he was about to recover" (wa kada yashfi), means: he was about to perish. (Ashfa, yashfi, ishfa'.)]] when his illness becomes severe and he is near recovery. It is also said: "ta'azzaza al-lahmu" (the flesh became firm), when it grew firm. From the same root comes: "'azza 'alayya an yakuna kadha wa kadha" (it was hard for me that such-and-such should be), meaning: it was difficult for me. [[See the explanation of "al-'izza" and "'aziz" above at 3:88, 4:244, 6:168, 6:271, 6:476. Moreover, Abu Ja'far did not explain the meaning of "al-'izza" at length except in this place, and this is further evidence of his method of abbreviating this tafsir.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 140:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of God being disbelieved in and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in another topic. Indeed, you would then be like them. Indeed, God will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hell all together﴾ [4:140].

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: "Give the hypocrites good tidings" [4:138], those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers, "and it has already been revealed to you in the Book", meaning: He informs that whoever among these hypocrites has taken the disbelievers as helpers and allies, after the Qur'an was revealed to them, "that when you hear the verses of God being disbelieved in and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in another topic", meaning: after they have known God's prohibition against sitting with the disbelievers who disbelieve in the proofs of God and the verses of His Book and mock them, "until they engage in another topic", meaning by "engage" (yakhudu, "to plunge into") — they speak about a topic other than it, "that for them there is a painful punishment." [[Abu Ja'far intended by this passage to clarify that His saying in the first verse, "that for them there is a painful punishment", is placed earlier, and its meaning is delayed. Therefore he began the discourse with "Give the hypocrites good tidings", then digressed to mention the two verses following it, then concluded with the conclusion of the first.]]

As for His saying, "Indeed, you would then be like them", meaning: it has already been revealed to you that if you sit with those who disbelieve in the verses of God and mock them while you are hearing, then you are like them. That is, if you do not rise from them in that state, you are like them in their action, because you have disobeyed God by sitting with them while you hear the verses of God being disbelieved in and mocked, just as they disobeyed Him by mocking the verses of God. So you have committed a disobedience of God similar to what they committed, and so you are like them in committing disobedience to God and doing what God has forbidden you.

* *

In this verse there is clear evidence for the prohibition of sitting with the people of falsehood of every kind, from innovators and sinners, when they plunge into their falsehood.

* *

In this manner a group of the earlier imams used to say, [[In the printed edition: "a group of the past nation", and the correct reading from the manuscript.]] interpreting this verse as meaning the prohibition of witnessing every falsehood when its people engage in it.

Mention of those who said that:

10708 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from al-Awwam ibn Hawshab, from Ibrahim al-Taymi, from Abu Wa'il, who said: Indeed a man speaks a word of falsehood in a gathering to make his companions laugh, and so God becomes displeased with them. He said: I mentioned that to Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and he said: Abu Wa'il has spoken the truth. Is it not in the Book of God: "that when you hear the verses of God being disbelieved in and mocked, do not sit with them until they engage in another topic. Indeed, you would then be like them"?

10709 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Idris narrated to us, from al-'Ala' ibn al-Munhal, from Hisham ibn 'Urwah, who said: Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz seized a group of people over drinking and flogged them, and among them was a fasting man. They said: "Indeed this man is fasting!" So he recited: "Do not sit with them until they engage in another topic. Indeed, you would then be like them."

10710 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiyah narrated to me, from Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His words: "that when you hear the verses of God being disbelieved in and mocked", and His words: ﴿And do not follow the ways, lest they separate you from His way﴾ [6:153], and His words: ﴿Establish the religion and do not be divided therein﴾ [42:13], and similar verses of the Qur'an. He said: God commanded the believers to unity, and forbade them from disagreement and division, and informed them: Those who were before you were destroyed only through disputation and contention about the religion of God.

* *

As for His saying, "Indeed, God will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers in Hell all together", He says: Indeed God will gather both groups, the people of disbelief and hypocrisy, on the Day of Resurrection into the Fire, uniting them in His punishment in Hell and in His painful torment, just as they agreed in the world, gathering together in enmity against the believers and cooperating in discouraging from the religion of God, and from that which He approved and commanded, and from its people. [[His saying "and its people" is in the genitive, conjoined to His saying "from the religion of God"; the context is: "from the religion of God ... and from its people".]]

* *

The reciters differed regarding the recitation of His saying: "And it has already been revealed to you in the Book."

The majority of reciters read it with a dammah on the "nun" and with a shaddah (emphasis) on the "zay", in the form of the passive (what has not been named as subject).

* *

Some Kufan reciters read it with a fathah on the "nun" and a shaddah on the "zay", meaning: "And God has already revealed to you."

* *

Some Meccan reciters read: ﴿wa-qad nazzala 'alaykum﴾ with a fathah on the "nun" and a lightened "zay", meaning: "And there has already come to you from God that when you hear..."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: None of these three recitations has a meaning far from what the wording allows. However, the one I choose is the recitation of those who read ﴿wa-qad nuzzila﴾ with a dammah on the "nun" and a shaddah on the "zay", in the passive form. This is because the meaning of the discourse in it is the placing-earlier that I described before [[See what has preceded, p. 320, and note 1.]], meaning: "Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers" = "And it has already been revealed to you in the Book that when you hear the verses of God being disbelieved in..." up to His saying "another topic" = "Do they seek honor with them?" Then His saying, "Indeed, honor belongs to God entirely", refers to the delay. Therefore the dammah on the "nun" of "nuzzila" is more correct in our view in this place.

* *

Likewise they differed regarding the recitation of His saying: "the Book which has been revealed to His Messenger and the Book which was revealed before."

Most reciters read "nazzala" and "anzala" with a fathah, meaning: "the Book which God revealed to His Messenger, and the Book which was revealed before."

* *

Some reciters of Basra read both words with a dammah, in the passive form.

* *

Both are close in meaning. However, the fathah in this is more pleasing to me than the dammah, because the mention of God has already occurred before it in His saying: "Believe in God and His Messenger."

The Discourse on the Interpretation of His Words: "Those who wait [in suspense] about you: if there is a victory for you from Allah, they say, 'Were we not with you?' And if the disbelievers have a share, they say, 'Did we not gain mastery over you and protect you from the believers?' Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers." (4:141)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His words, "Those who wait [in suspense] about you," He, mighty is His praise, means: those who wait, O believers, regarding you [see the explanation of "tarabbus" above, 4:456, 515 / 5:79]. "If there is a victory for you from Allah," meaning: if Allah grants you a conquest over your enemy, and bestows upon you spoils of war, "they say," to you, "Were we not with you?", i.e., we fought your enemy and raided them alongside you, so give us a share of the booty, for we have witnessed the fighting with you. "And if the disbelievers have a share," meaning: if your enemies among the disbelievers have a portion from you, by striking you, [see the explanation of "nasib" above, p. 212, note 1, and the references there]. "They say" [in the printed edition alone: "and they say, 'Were we not with you?'", which is an error by the first editor], meaning: these hypocrites say to the disbelievers, "Did we not gain mastery over you," i.e., did we not prevail over you until you overcame the believers, "and protect you" from them, by discouraging them for your sake, until they refrained from you and withdrew. "Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection," meaning: Allah will judge between the believers and the hypocrites on the Day of Resurrection, separating you by a decisive judgment [see the explanation of "al-hukm" above, p. 175], by admitting the people of faith into His Paradise and the people of hypocrisy, together with their allies among the disbelievers, into His Fire. "And Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers," meaning: a proof on the Day of Resurrection [see the explanation of "al-sabil" in the indices of language above].

This is a promise from Allah to the believers that He will not cause the hypocrites to enter the place they occupy in Paradise, nor the believers to enter the place of the hypocrites, lest the disbelievers thereby have a proof against the believers, by saying to them, if they were made to enter the hypocrites' place: "Behold, you were our enemies in the world, and the hypocrites were our allies, and now you have gathered together in the Fire; He has joined you with our allies! Where are those whom you claimed you were fighting us for in the world?" That is the "way" which Allah promised the believers He would not grant the disbelievers over them.

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an have said what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said this:

10711 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words, "If there is a victory for you from Allah": He said: The hypocrites wait in suspense regarding the Muslims. "If there is a victory for you," [he said]: If the Muslims obtain booty from their enemy, the hypocrites say, "Were we not with you?", we were with you, so give us booty like what you take. "And if the disbelievers have a share," they strike the Muslims. The hypocrites say to the disbelievers, "Did we not gain mastery over you and protect you from the believers?", we used to discourage them from you.

* *

The interpreters differed regarding the interpretation of His words, "Did we not gain mastery over you?"

Some of them said: its meaning is: did we not overcome you.

Mention of those who said this:

10712 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding His words, "Did we not gain mastery over you?", he said: we overcame you.

* *

Others said: the meaning of that is: did we not make clear to you that we are with you in what you are upon.

Mention of those who said this:

10713 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "Did we not gain mastery over you?", did we not make clear to you that we are with you in what you are upon.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: These two sayings are close in meaning. For whoever interprets it as "did we not make clear to you," he intends, if Allah wills: did we not overcome you by what came from us of making clear to you that we are with you.

* *

The root of "istihwadh" in the speech of the Arabs, as has reached us, is domination (al-ghalaba), and from it is the saying of Allah, mighty is His praise: "Satan has gained mastery over them and caused them to forget the remembrance of Allah" [Surat al-Mujadila: 19], meaning: he dominated them. It is said from it: "hadha 'alayhi wa-istahadha," "yahidhu" and "yastahidhu," and "ahadha yahidhu" (the form "ahadha yahidhu" is not found in lexicons, though it is correct in Arabic; they used instead "ahwadha thawbahu," meaning he gathered his garment, and they brought the verse of Labid cited below as evidence for it). And from the dialect of those who said "hadha," is the verse of al-Ajjaj describing a bull and a dog:

It drives them, while it is for them a driver ... fearing mixing, it is a stranger
As the gatherer drives the troop

They interpreted "yahudhuha" as: drives them with a strong drive, and similar to it is "yahuzzuha" in the narration that follows. Some of them recited: "yahuzzuhunna wa-lahu huzziyy" (a driver for them). The two meanings are close. And from the dialect of those who said "ahadha," is the verse of Labid describing a wild ass and its jennies:

When they gather, and he gathers both their flanks ... and brings them on crooked long legs

Meaning by his words "wa-ahwadha janibayha," he overpowered and subdued them until he had gathered both their sides, so that not one of them strayed.

Analogically, in His words, "Satan has gained mastery over them," it should have been "istaha'a 'alayhim" (with the form of "ahad" not "ahwadha"), because when the "waw" is the middle radical of the verb, and is vowelled with fatha, and what precedes it is quiescent, the Arabs transfer its vowel to the first radical before it and convert it into an alif, following the vowel of what precedes it, as in their saying "istahala hadha al-shay' 'amma kana 'alayhi" (from "hala yahulu"), "istanara fulan bi-nur Allah" (from "nur"), and "ista'adha bi-Allah" (from "'adha ya'udhu"). Sometimes they leave it in its original form, as Labid said "wa-ahwadha," and did not say "wa-ahada"; and in this dialect the Qur'an came in His words, "Satan has gained mastery over them."

* *

As for His words, "Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers," there is no disagreement among them that its meaning is: Allah will never grant the disbelievers, on that day, a way over the believers.

Mention of the report from those who said this:

10714 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Dharr, from Yusay' al-Hadrami who said: I was with Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, when a man said: O Commander of the Faithful, what do you say about the words of Allah, "And Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers," when they fight us and prevail and kill us? Ali said to him: Come closer, come closer! Then he said: "Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers", on the Day of Resurrection.

10715 - Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Thawri informed us, from al-A'mash, from Dharr, from Yusay' al-Kindi regarding His words, "And Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers", he said: A man came to Ali ibn Abi Talib and said: How is this verse, "And Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers"? Ali said: Come closer. "Allah will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah will never grant [the disbelievers] a way over the believers" [on the Day of Resurrection].

10716 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Dharr, from Yusay' al-Hadrami, from Ali, similarly.

10717 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ghundar narrated to us, from Shu'bah who said: I heard Sulayman narrate, from Dharr, from a man, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said regarding this verse, "And Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers", that it refers to the Hereafter.

10718 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Isra'il, from al-Suddi, from Abu Malik: "And Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers", on the Day of Resurrection.

* *

10719 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata' al-Khurasani, from Ibn Abbas: "And Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers", he said: That is the Day of Resurrection.

As for "al-sabil" in this place, it means the proof, as:

10720 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi regarding His words, "And Allah will never grant the disbelievers a way over the believers", he said: a proof.

The commentary of Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) on the verse, "Indeed, the hypocrites [seek to] deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them. And when they stand up to prayer, they stand lazily, showing [themselves] to the people and not remembering Allah except a little" (4:142).

Abu Ja'far said: We have already explained earlier the meaning of "the hypocrite's deception of his Lord" and the manner of "Allah's deception of them," with sufficient detail that there is no need to repeat it here, despite the differences of opinion on this matter. [[See what preceded: 1:272–277, then 301–306, as an inclusion.]]

* *

So the interpretation of that is: Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah by securing, through their hypocrisy, their blood and their property; and Allah is deceiving them by ruling that their blood be protected because of what they displayed with their tongues of faith, while He knows the hidden state of their inner consciences and their belief in disbelief, as a gradual leading on (istidraj) from Him for them in this world, until they meet Him in the Hereafter, when He will bring them, because of what they concealed of disbelief, into the Fire of Hell. As:

10721 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: "Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, and He is deceiving them." He said: On the Day of Resurrection He will give them a light by which they walk with the believers as they walked with them in this world; then He will strip them of that light and extinguish it, so they will stand in their darkness, and a wall will be struck between them.

10722 - al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said: "Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, and He is deceiving them." He said: It was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Ubayy and Abu Amir ibn al-Nu'man, [["Abu Amir ibn al-Nu'man," thus it is in the manuscript and the printed edition; I suspect the copyist dropped part of his name, which I have restored, for the one mentioned among the hypocrites with Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul is: "Abu Amir Abd Amr ibn Sayfi ibn al-Nu'man, of the clan of Dubay'a ibn Zayd, who is called 'Abu Amir the Monk,' and he is the father of Hanzala al-Ghasil on the day of Uhud. Abu Amir had become a monk in the pre-Islamic period and wore woolen garments, and he was a noble and obeyed leader among his people, the Aws. When Allah brought Islam, he refused except disbelief and separation from his people, the Aws, so he left, departing from Islam and from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah said: 'Do not call him the monk, but call him the wicked.' See Ibn Hisham's Sirah 2:234, 235.

Furthermore, I have not found anyone other than him among the hypocrites or others called 'Abu Amir ibn al-Nu'man,' so what I have said is established as correct in my view.]] and concerning the hypocrites, "they deceive Allah, and He is deceiving them": it is like His saying in "al-Baqarah": (They deceive Allah and those who believe, but they deceive none except themselves) [Surat al-Baqarah: 9]. [[In the printed edition: "and they deceive none except themselves," which is one of two readings; our reading is in our mushaf, and it is also the reading which Abu Ja'far has deemed authentic earlier, 1:277.]] He said: As for His saying "and He is deceiving them," it means: in the light given to the hypocrites with the believers; they are given light, but when they reach the wall, it is taken away, and what Allah mentioned of their saying [[In the manuscript: "and what was mentioned of it: 'Wait for us that we may borrow from your light'," which is incomplete; what is in the printed edition is close to the correct.]] "Wait for us that we may borrow from your light" [Surat al-Hadid: 13]. He said: "and He is deceiving them."

10723 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Sufyan ibn Husayn, from al-Hasan: that when he recited "Indeed, the hypocrites deceive Allah, and He is deceiving them," he said: A light is cast upon every believer and hypocrite by which they walk, until when they reach the Sirat, the light of the hypocrites is extinguished, and the believers proceed with their light, while they call out to them: "Wait for us that we may borrow from your light," until His saying: "but you tempted yourselves" [Surat al-Hadid: 13, 14]. Al-Hasan said: [[In the printed edition: "then that is Allah's deception of them," and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which is correct.]] so that is Allah's deception of them. [[Report 10723: "Sufyan ibn Husayn ibn al-Hasan al-Wasiti," passed as nos. 3471, 3879, 6462.]]

* *

As for His saying: "And when they stand up to prayer, they stand lazily, showing [themselves] to the people," it means: the hypocrites do not perform any of the deeds which Allah has obligated upon the believers in order to draw near to Allah through them, because they are not certain of a return, nor of reward or punishment; they only perform the outward deeds they perform to preserve themselves, [[In the printed edition: "bqa' 'ala anfusihim," and the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]] and out of fear of the believers, lest they be killed or have their property seized. So when they stand up to the prayer, which is among the obligations that are outwardly apparent, they stand to it lazily, showing off to the believers so that they reckon them among themselves while they are not of them, because they do not believe in its obligation and its being required of them; so in their standing to it they are lazy. [[See the explanation of "riya'" (showing off) earlier, 5:521, 522 / 8:356.]] As:

10724 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada, regarding His saying: "And when they stand up to prayer, they stand lazily," he said: By Allah, were it not for the people, the hypocrite would not pray, and he prays only out of showing off and reputation.

10725 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said regarding His saying: "And when they stand up to prayer, they stand lazily, showing [themselves] to the people," he said: They are the hypocrites; were it not for showing off, they would not pray.

* *

As for His saying: "and they do not remember Allah except a little," one might say: Is there anything little in the remembrance of Allah?

It is said to him: The meaning of that, contrary to what you have supposed, is: and they do not remember Allah except as a remembrance of showing off, [[In the printed edition: "The meaning of that, contrary to what you have supposed, is: and they do not remember Allah except as a showing-off remembrance," and I have kept what is in the manuscript, for it is correct; the phrase "contrary to what you have supposed" is an interjection in the text, which I have placed between two lines.]] so that they may thereby ward off from themselves killing, captivity, and the seizure of property, not as the remembrance of one who is certain and affirms the Oneness of Allah, sincerely devoting lordship to Him. For this reason Allah called it "little," because it is not intended for Allah, nor sought thereby to draw near to Allah, nor desired thereby is Allah's reward and what is with Him. So it, though abundant, is, in one respect, toil for its doer and its remembrer, [["al-nasab" (with two fatha vowels): fatigue.]] in the sense of the mirage which has an outward appearance without the reality of water.

* *

Those of interpretation have said similarly to what we have said on this matter.

Those who said that:

10726 - Ibn Wakic narrated to us, saying: Abu Usama narrated to us, from Abu al-Ashhab who said: al-Hasan recited "and they do not remember Allah except a little," and said: It is only little because it was for other than Allah.

10727 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatada: "and they do not remember Allah except a little," he said: The remembrance of the hypocrite is only little, because Allah did not accept it. And everything Allah rejects is little, and everything Allah accepts is abundant.

Commentary on the words of God: ﴿Wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those. And whomever Allah leaves astray, you will not find for him a way﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "mudhabdhabin" (wavering), may His praise be exalted, He means: vacillating, going back and forth.

* *

The root meaning of "al-tadhabdhub" (wavering) is movement and agitation, as al-Nabigha said:

Did you not see that God has given you a sovereignty, whereby every king below it is tossed about? [[The verse has already passed, with its sourcing and explanation, in 1:105.]]

* *

God only means by this that the hypocrites are bewildered in their religion, not inclining to hold to any belief with certainty. They are neither with the believers in insight, nor with the polytheists in ignorance, but they are perplexed between the two. Their likeness is the parable that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) struck for them, which is:

10728 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The likeness of the hypocrite is like the lone sheep wandering between two flocks: it goes to this one at one time, and to that one at another time, not knowing which of them to follow."

10729 - Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated it to us again, from Abd al-Wahhab, but he halted it at Ibn Umar and did not raise it. He said: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us twice in this same manner. [[The two reports 10728 and 10729 have a sound chain. Abd al-Wahhab ibn Abd al-Majid al-Thaqafi is trustworthy and has passed many times. Ubayd Allah ibn Umar ibn Hafs ibn Asim is trustworthy and has passed many times. This report is also transmitted by Muslim (17:128) through Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna from Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi in the same wording, except that he did not mention "not knowing which of them to follow." Muslim also transmits it through Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Numayr from his father from Ubayd Allah, and through Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah from Abu Usamah from Ubayd Allah. Ahmad in his Musnad (5079) transmits it through Ishaq ibn Yusuf from Ubayd Allah with slight variation in wording, and again (5790) through Muhammad ibn Ubayd from Ubayd Allah with wording like that of Abu Ja'far. He also transmits its meaning in the Musnad under reports nos. 472, 5359, 5546, 5610. My brother al-Sayyid Ahmad fully traced its sources in his commentary on the Musnad, and the hafiz Ibn Kathir added to its sourcing in his Tafsir (2:611), so refer to them there. In the printed edition it read "lā tadrī ayyatuhumā tattabi'" and I have restored what is in the manuscript, which agrees with Ahmad's transmission in the Musnad. "Al-shah al-a'irah" is the sheep that wanders between two flocks, not knowing which to follow; from the saying "ara al-faras wa al-kalb wa ghayruhuma ya'iru 'iyaran," meaning it has bolted away from its owner, so it wanders here and there. His words "ta'ir ila hadhihi marratan" mean that in its wandering it goes to this one at one time and to that one at another time.]]

10730 - Imran ibn Bakkar narrated to me, saying: Abu Rawh narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ayyash narrated to us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Umar narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), the same. [[This report repeats the two preceding ones. Imran ibn Bakkar al-Kala'i is Ibn Jarir's shaykh, trustworthy, passed as no. 2071, and al-Tabari narrates from him in many places. Abu Rawh is al-Rabi' ibn Rawh al-Hims, trustworthy, passed as no. 8164. Ibn Ayyash is Isma'il ibn Ayyash al-Himsi, passed as nos. 5445, 8164. The printed editions read "Ibn Abbas," which is an error. The route of Ibn Ayyash from Ubayd Allah, traced to the Prophet, is noted by Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir (2:611).]]

* *

Those of the exegetes who said the like of what we have said about its interpretation include:

10731 - Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those": he says, they are not polytheists who would openly display polytheism, nor are they believers.

10732 - Bishr narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding "wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those": he says, they are not sincere believers, nor are they polytheists who declare polytheism. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (peace be upon him) used to strike a parable for the believer, the hypocrite and the disbeliever, as the likeness of three men who were pushed toward a river. The believer fell in and crossed over. Then the hypocrite fell in, and when he nearly reached the believer, the disbeliever called out to him: "Come to me, for I fear for you!" The believer called out to him: "Come to me, for with me is this and this!" enumerating for him what he had. The hypocrite kept wavering between the two until a wave came upon him and drowned him. [[In the printed edition: "until the water came upon him and drowned him"; in the manuscript: "until a wave came upon him that drowned him." The correct reading is what has been adopted here. "Al-adhi" means the strong surging wave. Ibn Shumayl said: "Adha al-ma'," refers to the layers of foam that the wind lifts from the surface, below the waves.] He remained in doubt and suspicion until death overtook him in that state. He said: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) used to say: The likeness of the hypocrite is like a bleating ewe between two flocks, [["Al-thaghiyah" means the sheep; "tha'at al-shah yatha'u tha'a'an" means it cried out.] who saw a flock on a raised ground and went to them but did not recognize them, then saw another flock on a raised ground and went to them and sniffed them but did not recognize them. [["Al-nashz" is the elevated ground of a valley, like a hillock. "Shammatha" means she approached them and sniffed them to know whether they were her sisters or others. From it is said "shamamtu fulanan" when one draws close to someone seeking to know what he has through testing and probing; it is a form of "mufa'alah" from "al-shamm".]]

10733 - Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu Asim narrated to us, from Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His words "wavering": he said, the hypocrites.

10734 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding "wavering between that, belonging neither to these nor to those": he says, neither to the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), nor to these Jews.

10735 - Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: Al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His words "wavering between that": he said, they did not purify their faith so as to be with the believers, and they are not with the people of polytheism.

10736 - Yunus narrated to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His words "wavering between that", between Islam and disbelief, "belonging neither to these nor to those".

* *

As for His words "And whomever Allah leaves astray, you will not find for him a way," He means: whomever Allah forsakes from the path of guidance, which is Islam, to which God has called His servants. He says: whomever Allah forsakes from it and does not grant him success in it, "then you will not find for him," O Muhammad, "a way," meaning a path by which he may proceed to the truth other than it. And what way could there be for him to the truth other than Islam? God, may His praise be exalted, has informed us that whoever seeks a religion other than it, it will not be accepted from him, and whomever God leaves astray from it has gone astray, and there is no guide for him besides it. [[Refer to the entries on "al-dalal" (straying) and "al-sabil" (the way) in the lexical indices of what has passed before.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 144:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿O you who have believed, do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers. Do you wish to give Allah a clear case against yourselves?﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: This is a prohibition from Allah to His believing servants that they adopt the characteristics of the hypocrites, who take disbelievers as allies instead of believers, so that they become like them in committing what He has forbidden them, namely allying with His enemies.

He, may His praise be exalted, says to them: O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger, do not ally with the disbelievers, supporting them instead of the people of your religion and faith among the believers, lest you become like those among the hypocrites for whom the Fire has been made obligatory. Then He, may His praise be exalted, said, threatening whoever among them takes disbelievers as allies instead of believers, if he does not refrain from allying with them and desist from befriending them, that He will join him to the people of their allegiance among the hypocrites, to whom His Prophet ﷺ was commanded to give the good news that there is a painful punishment for them: "Do you wish", O you who take disbelievers as allies instead of believers, those who have believed in Me and My Messenger, "to give Allah a clear case against yourselves", meaning: a proof, [[See the explanation of "sultan" above, 7: 279.]] by your taking disbelievers as allies instead of believers, so that you deserve from Him what the people of hypocrisy deserve, whose description He has told you and whose station with Him He has informed you of, "clear", meaning: it makes clear its validity and its reality. [[In the printed edition: "its validity and its truthfulness (ḥaqqiyyatuhā)", and the correct reading is from the manuscript. It seems the editor found it objectionable that "ḥaqīqa" should mean that it is true!! But it is undoubtedly correct, and for this reason the editor replaced "ḥaqīqatuhā" with "ḥaqqiyyatuhā" in many places, which I have pointed out in earlier notes. See also what will come below, p. 360, note 4.]] He says: Do not expose yourselves to the anger of Allah, by providing a proof against yourselves in advancing toward what your Lord has forbidden you, namely allying with His enemies and the people of disbelief in Him.

* *

The people of interpretation have said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

10737. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "O you who have believed, do not take disbelievers as allies instead of believers. Do you wish to give Allah a clear case against yourselves?" He said: Indeed Allah has authority over His creation, but He says: a clear excuse.

10738. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Qabisah ibn Uqbah narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from a man, from Ikrimah, who said: Whatever in the Qur'an is "sultan", it is a proof.

10739. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to me, saying: Abu 'Asim narrated to us, from 'Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding His saying: "a clear case", he said: A proof.

10740. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it. [[These reports explaining the meaning of "sultan" here indicate that al-Tabari was abridging his tafsir, for the explanation of "sultan" as "proof" has already occurred at 7: 279, and he did not, as is his custom, bring the reports showing that interpretation there as well.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 145:

The interpretation of His, may He be glorified, words ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire, and you will not find for them a helper﴾ (4:145)

Abu Ja'far said: By His, may His majesty be exalted, words "Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire," He means: indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest level of the levels of Hell.

* *

Every level of the levels of Hell is called "darak" (darak, a level or stratum). It has two readings: "darak," with the letter "ra" vocalized with a fatha, and "dark," with the "ra" unvocalized (sukun). Whoever vocalizes the "ra" with a fatha makes its plural of paucity "adrak," and if he wishes he makes its plural of multiplicity "durub" (dorook). Whoever vocalizes the "ra" with a sukun says "thalatha adruk" (three levels), and for the plural of multiplicity "durook."

* *

The reciters have differed concerning the recitation of this:

The common reciters of Madina and Basra recited ﴿fi al-darak﴾ with a fatha on the "ra."

* *

The common reciters of Kufa recited it with a sukun on the "ra."

Abu Ja'far said: These are two well-known recitations, and whichever of them the reciter reads is correct, since the meaning is the same and both recitations are widely transmitted among the Muslims. However, I have seen people of knowledge of Arabic mention that the fatha on the "ra" in this word is more widespread among the Arabs than the sukun. They related from them by hearing: "Give me a darak (rope-end) with which I may reach my rope," [this is the statement of Abu 'Ubayda in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:142. It is strange that Abu Ja'far should cite this as evidence and make it more common in Arabic speech. For "darak" here means the rope, because one reaches with it the bottom of the well, and that is far removed from the meaning of "darak," which is the level!!] and that is when someone asks for what will let his rope reach the well-shaft he has failed to reach. ["al-rakiyya": the well.]

* *

People of interpretation have said things similar to what we have said about its interpretation.

Mention of those who said that:

1074. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: my father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Khaythama, from Abdullah: "Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire," he said: in coffins of iron, sealed over them. ["mubhama": closed and shut tight, with no way to know where it opens or any exit from it.]

1074. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Wahb ibn Jarir narrated to us, from Shu'ba, from Salama, from Khaythama, from Abdullah, who said: Indeed the hypocrites are in coffins of iron, locked over them in the Fire.

1074. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Yaman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Asim, from Dhakwan, from Abu Hurayra: "Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire," he said: in coffins that are bolted shut over them. ["arjata al-bab yarjuhu": he closed it firmly.]

1074. Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, saying: Mu'awiya ibn Salih narrated to us, from Ali ibn Abi Talha, from Ibn Abbas, his words: "Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire," meaning: at the bottom of the Fire.

1074. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Abdullah ibn Kathir said to me concerning his words: "in the lowest depth of the Fire," he said: We have heard that Jahannam has adrak (levels), stations. [His words "stations" are an explanation of "adrak," the plural of "darak."]

1074. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, saying: Sufyan narrated to us, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Khaythama, from Abdullah: "Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth of the Fire," he said: coffins of fire, closed down over them.

* *

As for His words "and you will not find for them a helper," He means: and you, O Muhammad, will not find for these hypocrites, from Allah, if He places them in the lowest depth of the Fire, a helper who will help them against Him, rescuing them from His punishment and warding off from them His painful retribution. [See the explanation of "nasir" above, p. 247, note 6, and the references there.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 146:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying: ﴿Except for those who repent, amend, hold fast to God, and make their religion sincerely for God. Those will be with the believers, and God will give the believers a great reward﴾ (4:146).

Abu Ja'far said: This is an exception made by God, great is His praise, exempting those who repent of their hypocrisy when they amend their conduct, make their religion sincerely for God alone, disavow the deities and rivals, and affirm His Messenger, from being with those who persist in their hypocrisy until their appointed deaths come upon them — in the Hereafter [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "until He fulfils for them their appointed deaths" (حتى يوفيهم مناياهم), which is meaningless. "Wafatahu maniyyatuhu" means: his death came to him, reached him and overtook him; the context of this sentence is: "that they be with those who persist ... in the Hereafter."]] — and that they enter the gates of Hell. Rather, God, great is His praise, promised them that He would settle them with the believers in a station of honour and let them dwell with them in their dwellings in Paradise. [[In the printed edition: "yuskinahum" without the waw, which is an error by a copyist or typesetter.]] And He promised them, as a reward for their repentance, abundant bounty, saying: "And God will give the believers a great reward."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse, "Except those who repent" — that is, they return to the truth [[See the explanation of "repentance" (tawbah) above, 1:547 / 2:72, 73, and other places in the linguistic indices.]] and turn back from their hypocrisy, to nothing but the affirmation of God's oneness, the confirmation of His Messenger, and what he brought from his Lord — "and amend" — meaning: they amend their deeds, act by what God commanded them, perform His obligations, desist from what He forbade them, and refrain from His disobedience [[See the explanation of "amendment" (islah) above, 8:88, and the linguistic indices above.]] — "and hold fast to God" — he says: they grasp the covenant of God firmly.

* *

We have already shown earlier that "i'tisam" (holding fast) means clinging and attaching oneself. [[See the explanation of "i'tisam" above, 8:62, 63, 70.]] So holding fast to God is clinging to His covenant and His pact, which He established in His Book with His creatures, of obedience to Him and abandonment of disobedience to Him.

* *

"And make their religion sincerely for God" — he says: they make their obedience and their deeds, which they perform, sincerely for God, intending Him by them, and do not perform them for the show of people, nor out of doubt about their religion, nor out of hesitation about whether God counts for them what they do, so that He rewards the good-doer for his goodness and the evil-doer for his evil — but they perform them with certainty regarding the reward of the good-doer for his goodness and the requital of the evil-doer for his evil, or that his Lord may show him grace and pardon him — seeking nearness to God through them, desiring thereby the Face of God. That is the meaning of "their sincerely making their religion for God." [[In the printed edition: "fa-yujazi" (then he rewards); I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]

Then He, great is His praise, said: "Those will be with the believers," — he says: those whom He has described, from among the hypocrites, after their repentance, their amendment, their holding fast to God and their making their religion sincerely His — that is, with the believers in Paradise, not with the hypocrites who died in their hypocrisy, whom He threatened with the lowest level of the Fire. [[In the printed edition: "wa-ikhlasuhum lahu ma'a al-mu'minin..." — I have kept the correct reading from the manuscript, as changing it makes no sense.]]

Then He said: "And God will give the believers a great reward" — he says: God will give those whose description this is, for their repentance, their amendment, their holding fast to God, their making their religion sincerely His, and for their faith [[In the printed edition and the manuscript: "for their faith" without the waw; the correct reading includes it.]] — a great reward, which is [[See the explanation of "reward" (ajr) above, p. 202, note 2, and the references there.]] degrees in Paradise, just as He gave those who died in hypocrisy dwellings in the Fire, the lowest of them. For God, great is His praise, promised His believing servants that He would give them that for their faith, just as He threatened the hypocrites for their hypocrisy with what He mentioned in His Book.

* *

This is the meaning of the saying of Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman, who said:

10747 — It was narrated to us by Ibn Humayd and Ibn Waki', who both said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Ibrahim, who said: Hudhayfah said: "Certainly people who were hypocrites will enter Paradise!" Abdullah said: "And what knowledge do you have of that?" Hudhayfah became angry, then stood up and withdrew. When they dispersed, Alqamah passed by him and called him, saying: "Indeed, your companion knows what you said!" Then he recited: "Except those who repent, amend, hold fast to God, and make their religion sincerely for God. Those will be with the believers, and God will give the believers a great reward."

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 147:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And Allah is ever Appreciative and Knowing.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe?" He means: What would Allah do, O hypocrites, with your punishment if you repent to Allah and return to the truth that is owed to Him by you, thanking Him for the blessings He has bestowed upon you in your selves, your families, and your children, by turning back to His Oneness, holding fast to Him, making your deeds sincerely for His sake, abandoning showing off to people through them, and believing in His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), affirming him, acknowledging what he brought to you from Him, and acting upon it?

He says: Allah has no need to place you in the lowest level of the Fire if you return to His obedience, and turn back to acting upon what He has commanded you and abandoning what He has forbidden you. This is because He does not gain any benefit for Himself through your punishment, nor does He repel any harm from Himself by it. His punishment of whoever He punishes among His creation is only a recompense from Him to them for their audacity against Him, their opposition to His command and prohibition, and their ingratitude for the thanks due for His blessings upon them. So if you thank Him for His blessings and obey Him in His command and prohibition, then He has no need to punish you. Rather, He will show appreciation to you for what comes from you of obedience and gratitude to Him, by recompensing you for that with what your wishes fall short of and your hopes do not reach [[In the printed edition: "فلم تبلغه" with the fa', but the correct reading is what is in the manuscript.]] "And Allah is ever Appreciative" toward you and His servants for their obedience to Him, by granting them abundant reward for it and magnifying for them the compensation for it, "Knowing" of what you do, O hypocrites, and others, of good and evil, righteous and wicked, counting all of that against you and encompassing all of it, until He recompenses you with your due on the Day of Resurrection: the good-doer with his goodness, and the wrongdoer with his wrongdoing. And it has been narrated:

10748 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: "What would Allah do with your punishment if you are grateful and believe? And Allah is ever Appreciative and Knowing." He said: Indeed Allah, may His praise be exalted, does not punish one who is grateful, nor one who is a believer.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 148:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged. And Allah is ever Hearing and Knowing.﴾ (4:148)

Abu Ja'far said: The reciters differed in their reading of this.

The majority of the reciters of the great cities read it with a ḍammah on the "ẓā'" (ẓulima).

* *

Others read it: ﴿illā man ẓalama﴾, with a fatḥah on the "ẓā'".

* *

Then those who read it with a ḍammah on the "ẓā'" differed in its interpretation.

Some said: The meaning is: Allah, exalted is His remembrance, does not like that any one of us should publicly invoke curses against another. That, in their view, is "the public mention of evil speech except by one who has been wronged": that is, except one who has been wronged, who may invoke curses against his wrongdoer, for Allah, majestic is His praise, does not dislike that for him, since He has permitted it to him.

Mention of those who said this:

10749. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Salih related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah ibn Salih related to me, from 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: "Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech," he said: Allah does not like that anyone should invoke curses against anyone, except one who has been wronged, for He has permitted him to invoke curses against the one who wronged him. That is His words: "except one who has been wronged." But if he is patient, it is better for him.

10750. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: 'Abd Allah related to us, saying: Mu'awiyah related to me, from 'Ali, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His words: "Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech except by one who has been wronged," that He does like the public mention of evil speech.

10751. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech except by one who has been wronged. And Allah is ever Hearing and Knowing," that Allah excused the wronged one, as you hear, that he should supplicate.

10752. Al-Harith related to me, saying: Abu 'Ubayd related to us, saying: Hushaym related to us, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, who said: It refers to a man who is wronged by another man, so he does not invoke curses against him, but says: "O Allah, help me against him; O Allah, extract my right for me; O Allah, come between him and what he desires," [[In the manuscript: "O Allah, come between me and what he desires," and what is in the printed edition is closer to the correct reading.]] and similar supplications.

* *

= Thus, "man" according to this statement of Ibn 'Abbas is in the nominative position, because he directed the public mention of evil to mean supplication, and excepted the wronged one from it. So the meaning of the speech, according to his statement, would be: Allah does not like that evil speech be publicly uttered, except by the wronged one, for there is no blame on him for uttering it.

This is an opinion which the grammarians regard as an error in Arabic. That is because "man" cannot, in their view, be nominative with respect to "al-jahr," since it is in the complement of "an" and was not preceded by a negation, so it is not permissible to make it coordinate with it. [[In the printed edition: "because it is in the complement of 'an,' and 'an' was not preceded by a negation," with an added "an," and what is in the manuscript is purely correct.]] Among the errors in their view is to say: [[In the printed edition: "Among the errors in their view," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]] "It does not please me that anyone stand up except Zayd."

It is possible that "man" is in the accusative, according to the interpretation of Ibn 'Abbas's statement, and his words "Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech" are a complete statement, then it is said: "except one who has been wronged, there is no blame on him," so that "man" is an exception from the act, even though there is no apparent noun before the exception from which it is excepted, as He, majestic is His praise, said: ﴿You are not over them a controller. Except one who turns away and disbelieves﴾ [Surah al-Ghashiyah: 22-23], and as they say: "I dislike disputation and contention, except—O Allah—a man who seeks Allah by it," though nothing of the nouns was mentioned before it. [[See al-Farra's Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1: 293, 294.]]

* *

And "man," according to this statement of al-Hasan, is in the accusative, as an exception from the meaning of the speech and not from the noun, as we mentioned before in the interpretation of Ibn 'Abbas's statement when "man" is directed to the accusative, and like the saying of one who says: "Such-and-such a matter occurred, except that so-and-so, may Allah reward him well, did such-and-such."

* *

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech, except by one who has been wronged, who informs others of what was inflicted upon him.

Mention of those who said this:

10753. Ibn Wakf'i related to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: It refers to a man who arrives at a man's house and he does not treat him well as a guest, so he leaves his presence and says: "He treated my hospitality badly and did not do it well!"

10754. Al-Qasim related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, saying: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: "except one who has been wronged," he said: except one who narrates what was said to him. [[In the printed edition: "ātha" with a lengthened hamza, which is an error. "Athara al-hadith yathuruhu": he related it and transmitted it and spoke of it. From it: "a transmitted saying" (qawl ma'thur), meaning people inform one another of it, one transmitting it from predecessor to successor.]]

10755. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal related to us, saying: Hammad related to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from Abd Allah ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: "Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech except by one who has been wronged," he said: It is the guest whose baggage is moved, for he publicly speaks evil of his host.

* *

Others said: It means the man who arrives at a man's house and he does not host him, and so he is harmed by the one who did not host him.

Mention of those who said this:

10756. Muhammad ibn 'Amr related to me, saying: Abu 'Asim related to us, saying: 'Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His words: "except one who has been wronged," he said: except one who has been wronged and takes his revenge, publicly speaking evil.

10757. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah related to us, saying: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, the like of it.

10758. Ibn Wakf'i related to us, saying: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr, from Mujahid = and from Humayd al-A'raj, from Mujahid: "Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech except by one who has been wronged," he said: It is the man who arrives at a man's house and he is not treated well, so Allah has permitted him to speak about him. [[Report 10758: "Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr al-Makki al-Akhnasi," who heard Tawus and Mujahid. Ibn Abi Najih and Ibn Jurayj related from him; he is biographed in al-Tahdhib.

In the manuscript it was: "Ibrahim from Abu Bakayr," and in the following chain, 10759: "Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakayr." This is a problematic discrepancy.

In the first chain, as in the manuscript, I do not know who "Ibrahim" would be.

As for "Abu Bakayr," among them is "Abu Bakayr Marzuq al-Taymi al-Kufi," who narrates from Mujahid, mentioned earlier under no. 4305, though this is not, in my judgment, the one.

As for "Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakayr" in the second chain, among them is "Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakayr," mentioned by al-Bukhari in al-Kabir 1/1/277 in the biography of "Ibrahim Abu Bakayr," and it seems to be an error by a copyist who dropped "ibn" = and "Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakayr ibn Ibrahim" is biographed in Ibn Abi Hatim 1/1/90, and neither of them is recorded as narrating from Mujahid.

For this reason, it is established to me that what is in the printed edition is correct, God willing; due to the narration of "Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr" from Mujahid, and Ibn Najih's narration from him.]]

10759. And Ahmad ibn Hammad al-Dulabi related to me, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakr, from Mujahid: "Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech except by one who has been wronged," he said: It concerns hospitality: a man comes to a people, lodges with them, and they do not host him. Allah has permitted him to speak about them. [[Report 10759: In the manuscript: "Ibrahim ibn Abi Bakayr." See the note on the earlier report.]]

10760. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: al-Muthanna ibn al-Sabbah informed us, from Mujahid regarding His words: "Allah does not like the public mention of evil speech," the verse, he said: A man was a guest of another man, but he did not give him his due right of hospitality. When he left, he informed the people, saying: "I was a guest of so-and-so, and he did not give me my right of hospitality!"
