Others said: The meaning of that is: "And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in Muhammad (ﷺ) before the death of the People of the Book."

Mention of those who said this:

10829. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal related to us, saying: Hammad related to us, from Humayd who said: 'Ikrima said: No Christian or Jew dies until he believes in Muhammad (ﷺ), meaning in His words: "And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him before his death."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct and sound of the sayings is the view of the one who said that the interpretation of this is: "And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in Jesus before the death of Jesus."

We only said that this is more correct than the other sayings because God, may His praise be exalted, has ruled for every believer in Muhammad (ﷺ) by the ruling of the people of faith, in inheritance and in the funeral prayer over him, and in attaching his young children to his ruling in the religion. So if every People of the Book believed in Jesus before his death, it would follow that a People of the Book who dies upon his religion should not inherit, except his young children, or those of them who are adult Muslims, if he has a young or adult Muslim child. And if he has no young child nor adult Muslim child, his estate would be disbursed where the property of a Muslim who dies with no heir is disbursed, and his ruling would be the ruling of the Muslims regarding the funeral prayer over him, washing him, and burying him (taqbiruhu). [[His words "taqbiruhu" mean his burial where burial takes place; it seems to be one of the terms of the jurists in the time of Abu Ja'far. In the language, "qabara yaqburuhu" means he buried him, and "aqbara" means he made a grave for him. As for "qabbara yuqabbiru taqbiran" in this sense, I have not found it in the lexicons.]] Because whoever dies believing in Jesus, has died believing in Muhammad and all the messengers. For Jesus (may God's blessings be upon him) came confirming Muhammad and all the messengers (may God's blessings be upon them), so whoever affirms and believes in Jesus, also affirms Muhammad and all the prophets and messengers of God. Just as whoever believes in Muhammad, believes in Jesus and all the prophets and messengers of God. It is impermissible that one who denies Muhammad be a believer in Jesus.

* *

If someone supposes that the meaning of the Jew's belief in Jesus, which God mentioned in His words: "And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him before his death," is merely his acknowledgment that he is a prophet sent by God, apart from his affirmation of everything he brought from God, then he has erred.

That is because it is not permissible for someone to be credited with affirming the prophethood of a prophet while denying some part of what that prophet brought as revelation from God. Indeed, it is not permissible for anyone to be credited with affirming the prophethood of any one of God's prophets, because the nations were commanded to affirm all of God's prophets and messengers. Whoever denies some of God's prophets regarding what they brought to their nation from God is, in effect, denying all of God's prophets regarding what they called God's servants to, of God's religion. Since this is so, and since all the people of Islam agree that every People of the Book who died before affirming Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he brought from God is judged by the religion he followed during his lifetime, and that none of his rulings concerning his person, property, or children, young and old, are transferred from what he was upon during his life after his death, the evidence shows that the meaning of God's statement, "And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in him before his death" [Q 4:159], is only: "they will surely believe in Jesus before Jesus's death." This applies to a specific group of the People of the Book, referring to a particular era among them and not to all the eras that came after Jesus, and it will occur at his descent, as in the following report:

10830. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Adam, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: "The prophets are half-brothers; their mothers are different, but their religion is one. I am the closest of people to Jesus son of Mary, because there was no prophet between me and him. He will descend, so when you see him, recognize him. He is a man of medium build, inclining to redness and whiteness, with straight hair, as if his head were dripping though no water has touched it, and he will wear two garments dyed with saffron. He will break the cross, kill the swine, abolish the jizyah, and money will overflow. He will fight people for Islam until God destroys in his time all religions except Islam, and God will destroy in his time the Antichrist, the great liar, the Dajjal. Security will prevail on earth in his time, so that lions will graze with camels, panthers with cattle, wolves with sheep, and boys or children will play with snakes without harming one another. He will remain on earth as long as God wills," and perhaps he said, "forty years," "then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him and bury him."

[Note on the report 10830: this hadith has already passed as no. 7145, through Ibn Humayd, from Salamah, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar, from Qatadah, with the same meaning but with very slight variation in wording. It is a sound hadith; my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad traced its sources (takhrij) in its place there, and he pointed to this chain of al-Tabari here, so refer to it there.]

* *

As for the one who said that the intended meaning of his words "will surely believe in him before his death" is "will surely believe in Muhammad (ﷺ) before the death of the People of the Book," this has no comprehensible basis. Because, along with its corruption on the ground that we have shown the corruption of the view of the one who said, "He meant: will surely believe in Jesus before the death of the People of the Book," it is further corrupted by the fact that no mention of Muhammad (peace be upon him) has preceded in the verses before this, so that the pronoun in "will surely believe in him" could be directed toward his mention. Rather, "will surely believe in him" occurs in the context of discussing Jesus, his mother, and the Jews. It is not permissible to turn speech away from its context toward something else, except with a proof that must be accepted, either from the clear indication of the revelation or from a report from the Messenger which constitutes a binding proof. As for mere claims, they are not difficult for anyone to make.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse, since the matter is as we have described, is: "And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in Jesus before Jesus's death." The word "man" (مَن) after "illa" (except) has been omitted, since the sense of the speech indicates it, so the indication of the sense makes its explicit mention unnecessary, like the rest of what has preceded of similar examples, which we have already explained.

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His statement: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾ [Q 4:159]

Abu Ja'far said: By this, the Almighty means: "And on the Day of Resurrection, Jesus will be a witness against the People of the Book," meaning a witness against them of the denial of those among them who denied him, and the affirmation of those among them who affirmed him, regarding what he brought them from God, and of his conveying the message of his Lord. [See the explanation of "shahid" (witness) in the earlier language indexes.] As in the following report:

10831. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, regarding "And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them," that he had conveyed to them what he was sent with to them.

10832. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding "And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them": he says, "He will be a witness against them on the Day of Resurrection that he had conveyed the message of his Lord, and acknowledged servitude for himself."

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His statement: ﴿For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We made unlawful for them good things which had been lawful for them, and because of their hindering from the way of God many times over, and their taking of usury though they had been forbidden from it, and their consuming of the wealth of people unjustly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment﴾ [Q 4:160–161]

Abu Ja'far said: By this, the Almighty means: "We made unlawful for the Jews who broke their covenant which they pledged to their Lord, disbelieved in the signs of God, killed their prophets, spoke a great slander against Mary, and did what God described them as doing in His Book, good things of food and other things, which had been lawful to them, as a punishment for their wrongdoing, which God reported about them in His Book." [See the explanation of "hadu" (Jews) in the earlier volumes, 2:143, 507, 508. And the explanation of "al-tayyibat" (good things) in the earlier volumes, 3:301 / 5:555 / 6:361 / 7:424 / 8:409.] As in the following report:

10833. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding "For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We made unlawful for them good things which had been lawful for them," to the end of the verse: the people were punished for a wrong they committed and a transgression they perpetrated; things were made unlawful for them because of their transgression and wrongdoing.

* *

As for His statement, "and because of their hindering from the way of God many times over," it means: and because of their hindering the servants of God from His religion and from the paths He prescribed for His servants, a great hindering. [In the printed edition: "the paths He explained to His servant," which is an obvious error.] Their hindering from the way of God was by their saying false things about God, claiming that this was from God, their altering the Book of God, and their distorting its meanings from their proper aspects. Among the greatest of this was their denial of the prophethood of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and their withholding the clarification of what they knew of his matter from people who were ignorant of his matter. [See the explanation of "al-sadd" (hindering) in the earlier volumes, 4:300 / 7:53 / 8:482, 513, and the explanation of "al-sabil" (the way) in the earlier language indexes.]

* *

In a similar sense Mujahid used to say:

10834. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to me, saying: Isa narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God, "and because of their hindering from the way of God many times over," he said: "[They were hindering] themselves and others from the truth."

10835. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

As for His statement, "and their taking of usury," it refers to their taking what they added to their capital, in exchange for an extension of the term after its due date. I have already explained the meaning of "usury" (riba) earlier, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. [See the explanation of "riba" in the earlier volumes, 6:7, 8, 13, 15, 22.]

* *

As for "though they had been forbidden from it," it means: forbidden from taking usury.

* *

As for His statement, "and their consuming of the wealth of people unjustly," it means what they used to take as bribes for judgment, as God described them in His saying: ﴿And you see many of them hastening toward sin and aggression and consuming of unlawful gain. Wretched is what they used to do﴾ [Q 5:62]. Among their consuming of people's wealth unjustly was what they used to take as payment for the books they wrote with their own hands, then they would say, "This is from God," and similar base and corrupt foods. God punished them for all of that by forbidding them the good things that had been lawful to them before.

God described them as having consumed the wealth of people in this unjust manner because they consumed it without right, and they took their property from them without entitlement.

* *

As for His statement, "And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment," [in the printed edition: "So His statement..." — the manuscript reading is correct] it means: We have made ready for the disbelievers in God and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) from these Jews [See the explanation of "a'tada" (prepared) in the earlier volumes, 8:103, 355 / 9:353], the painful punishment, which is the agonizing one [See the explanation of "al-alim" (painful) in the earlier language indexes], from the punishment of Hell, with Him, which they will burn in the Hereafter when they come before their Lord, and He will punish them with it. [In the printed edition: "from the punishment of Hell, a fire they will burn..." — the manuscript reading is correct.]

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of this.

Some of them said: The meaning of it, "And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him," meaning in Jesus, "before his death," meaning before the death of Jesus, points to the fact that all of them will affirm him when he descends to kill the Dajjal (the Antichrist). Thus all the religions will become one, which is the religion of Islam, the upright (hanifiyya) faith, the religion of Abraham (ﷺ).

He said: Before the death of Jesus, son of Mary.

Then a man from among his companions said to him: How, when a man drowns, or burns, or a wall falls on him, or a predator eats him? He said: His spirit does not leave his body until faith in Jesus is cast into him.

It was reported from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: "And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him before his death," He said: None of the Jews dies until he testifies that Jesus is the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

10828. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ya'la related to us, from Juwaybir regarding His words: "Surely he will believe in him before his death," He said: In the recitation of Ubayy: "before their death." [[The report 10828: See the earlier report No. 10814.]]

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in Muhammad (ﷺ) before the death of the People of the Book."

Mention of those who said this:

10829. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal related to us, saying: Hammad related to us, from Humayd who said: 'Ikrima said: No Christian or Jew dies until he believes in Muhammad (ﷺ), meaning in His words: "And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him before his death."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct and sound of the sayings is the view of the one who said that the interpretation of this is: "And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in Jesus before the death of Jesus."

We only said that this is more correct than the other sayings because God, may His praise be exalted, has ruled for every believer in Muhammad (ﷺ) by the ruling of the people of faith, in inheritance and in the funeral prayer over him, and in attaching his young children to his ruling in the religion. So if every People of the Book believed in Jesus before his death, it would follow that a People of the Book who dies upon his religion should not inherit, except his young children, or those of them who are adult Muslims, if he has a young or adult Muslim child. And if he has no young child nor adult Muslim child, his estate would be disbursed where the property of a Muslim who dies with no heir is disbursed, and his ruling would be the ruling of the Muslims regarding the funeral prayer over him, washing him, and burying him (taqbiruhu). [[His words "taqbiruhu" mean his burial where burial takes place; it seems to be one of the terms of the jurists in the time of Abu Ja'far. In the language, "qabara yaqburuhu" means he buried him, and "aqbara" means he made a grave for him. As for "qabbara yuqabbiru taqbiran" in this sense, I have not found it in the lexicons.]] Because whoever dies believing in Jesus, has died believing in Muhammad and all the messengers. For Jesus (may God's blessings be upon him) came confirming Muhammad and all the messengers (may God's blessings be upon them), so whoever affirms and believes in Jesus, also affirms Muhammad and all the prophets and messengers of God. Just as whoever believes in Muhammad, believes in Jesus and all the prophets and messengers of God. It is impermissible that one who denies Muhammad be a believer in Jesus.

* *

If someone supposes that the meaning of the Jew's belief in Jesus, which God mentioned in His words: "And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him before his death," is merely his acknowledgment that he is a prophet sent by God, apart from his affirmation of everything he brought from God, then he has erred.

That is because it is not permissible for someone to be credited with affirming the prophethood of a prophet while denying some part of what that prophet brought as revelation from God. Indeed, it is not permissible for anyone to be credited with affirming the prophethood of any one of God's prophets, because the nations were commanded to affirm all of God's prophets and messengers. Whoever denies some of God's prophets regarding what they brought to their nation from God is, in effect, denying all of God's prophets regarding what they called God's servants to, of God's religion. Since this is so, and since all the people of Islam agree that every People of the Book who died before affirming Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he brought from God is judged by the religion he followed during his lifetime, and that none of his rulings concerning his person, property, or children, young and old, are transferred from what he was upon during his life after his death, the evidence shows that the meaning of God's statement, "And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in him before his death" [Q 4:159], is only: "they will surely believe in Jesus before Jesus's death." This applies to a specific group of the People of the Book, referring to a particular era among them and not to all the eras that came after Jesus, and it will occur at his descent, as in the following report:

10830. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Adam, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: "The prophets are half-brothers; their mothers are different, but their religion is one. I am the closest of people to Jesus son of Mary, because there was no prophet between me and him. He will descend, so when you see him, recognize him. He is a man of medium build, inclining to redness and whiteness, with straight hair, as if his head were dripping though no water has touched it, and he will wear two garments dyed with saffron. He will break the cross, kill the swine, abolish the jizyah, and money will overflow. He will fight people for Islam until God destroys in his time all religions except Islam, and God will destroy in his time the Antichrist, the great liar, the Dajjal. Security will prevail on earth in his time, so that lions will graze with camels, panthers with cattle, wolves with sheep, and boys or children will play with snakes without harming one another. He will remain on earth as long as God wills," and perhaps he said, "forty years," "then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him and bury him."

[Note on the report 10830: this hadith has already passed as no. 7145, through Ibn Humayd, from Salamah, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar, from Qatadah, with the same meaning but with very slight variation in wording. It is a sound hadith; my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad traced its sources (takhrij) in its place there, and he pointed to this chain of al-Tabari here, so refer to it there.]

* *

As for the one who said that the intended meaning of his words "will surely believe in him before his death" is "will surely believe in Muhammad (ﷺ) before the death of the People of the Book," this has no comprehensible basis. Because, along with its corruption on the ground that we have shown the corruption of the view of the one who said, "He meant: will surely believe in Jesus before the death of the People of the Book," it is further corrupted by the fact that no mention of Muhammad (peace be upon him) has preceded in the verses before this, so that the pronoun in "will surely believe in him" could be directed toward his mention. Rather, "will surely believe in him" occurs in the context of discussing Jesus, his mother, and the Jews. It is not permissible to turn speech away from its context toward something else, except with a proof that must be accepted, either from the clear indication of the revelation or from a report from the Messenger which constitutes a binding proof. As for mere claims, they are not difficult for anyone to make.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse, since the matter is as we have described, is: "And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in Jesus before Jesus's death." The word "man" (مَن) after "illa" (except) has been omitted, since the sense of the speech indicates it, so the indication of the sense makes its explicit mention unnecessary, like the rest of what has preceded of similar examples, which we have already explained.

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His statement: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾ [Q 4:159]

Abu Ja'far said: By this, the Almighty means: "And on the Day of Resurrection, Jesus will be a witness against the People of the Book," meaning a witness against them of the denial of those among them who denied him, and the affirmation of those among them who affirmed him, regarding what he brought them from God, and of his conveying the message of his Lord. [See the explanation of "shahid" (witness) in the earlier language indexes.] As in the following report:

10831. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, regarding "And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them," that he had conveyed to them what he was sent with to them.

10832. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding "And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them": he says, "He will be a witness against them on the Day of Resurrection that he had conveyed the message of his Lord, and acknowledged servitude for himself."

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His statement: ﴿For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We made unlawful for them good things which had been lawful for them, and because of their hindering from the way of God many times over, and their taking of usury though they had been forbidden from it, and their consuming of the wealth of people unjustly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment﴾ [Q 4:160–161]

Abu Ja'far said: By this, the Almighty means: "We made unlawful for the Jews who broke their covenant which they pledged to their Lord, disbelieved in the signs of God, killed their prophets, spoke a great slander against Mary, and did what God described them as doing in His Book, good things of food and other things, which had been lawful to them, as a punishment for their wrongdoing, which God reported about them in His Book." [See the explanation of "hadu" (Jews) in the earlier volumes, 2:143, 507, 508. And the explanation of "al-tayyibat" (good things) in the earlier volumes, 3:301 / 5:555 / 6:361 / 7:424 / 8:409.] As in the following report:

10833. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding "For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We made unlawful for them good things which had been lawful for them," to the end of the verse: the people were punished for a wrong they committed and a transgression they perpetrated; things were made unlawful for them because of their transgression and wrongdoing.

* *

As for His statement, "and because of their hindering from the way of God many times over," it means: and because of their hindering the servants of God from His religion and from the paths He prescribed for His servants, a great hindering. [In the printed edition: "the paths He explained to His servant," which is an obvious error.] Their hindering from the way of God was by their saying false things about God, claiming that this was from God, their altering the Book of God, and their distorting its meanings from their proper aspects. Among the greatest of this was their denial of the prophethood of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and their withholding the clarification of what they knew of his matter from people who were ignorant of his matter. [See the explanation of "al-sadd" (hindering) in the earlier volumes, 4:300 / 7:53 / 8:482, 513, and the explanation of "al-sabil" (the way) in the earlier language indexes.]

* *

In a similar sense Mujahid used to say:

10834. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to me, saying: Isa narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God, "and because of their hindering from the way of God many times over," he said: "[They were hindering] themselves and others from the truth."

10835. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

As for His statement, "and their taking of usury," it refers to their taking what they added to their capital, in exchange for an extension of the term after its due date. I have already explained the meaning of "usury" (riba) earlier, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. [See the explanation of "riba" in the earlier volumes, 6:7, 8, 13, 15, 22.]

* *

As for "though they had been forbidden from it," it means: forbidden from taking usury.

* *

As for His statement, "and their consuming of the wealth of people unjustly," it means what they used to take as bribes for judgment, as God described them in His saying: ﴿And you see many of them hastening toward sin and aggression and consuming of unlawful gain. Wretched is what they used to do﴾ [Q 5:62]. Among their consuming of people's wealth unjustly was what they used to take as payment for the books they wrote with their own hands, then they would say, "This is from God," and similar base and corrupt foods. God punished them for all of that by forbidding them the good things that had been lawful to them before.

God described them as having consumed the wealth of people in this unjust manner because they consumed it without right, and they took their property from them without entitlement.

* *

As for His statement, "And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment," [in the printed edition: "So His statement..." — the manuscript reading is correct] it means: We have made ready for the disbelievers in God and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) from these Jews [See the explanation of "a'tada" (prepared) in the earlier volumes, 8:103, 355 / 9:353], the painful punishment, which is the agonizing one [See the explanation of "al-alim" (painful) in the earlier language indexes], from the punishment of Hell, with Him, which they will burn in the Hereafter when they come before their Lord, and He will punish them with it. [In the printed edition: "from the punishment of Hell, a fire they will burn..." — the manuscript reading is correct.]

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾**

Abu Ja'far said: The interpreters (ahl al-ta'wil) differed regarding the meaning of this.

Some of them said: The meaning of it, "And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him," meaning in Jesus, "before his death," meaning before the death of Jesus, points to the fact that all of them will affirm him when he descends to kill the Dajjal (the Antichrist). Thus all the religions will become one, which is the religion of Islam, the upright (hanifiyya) faith, the religion of Abraham (ﷺ).

He said: Before the death of Jesus, son of Mary.

Then a man from among his companions said to him: How, when a man drowns, or burns, or a wall falls on him, or a predator eats him? He said: His spirit does not leave his body until faith in Jesus is cast into him.

It was reported from al-Husayn ibn al-Faraj who said: I heard Abu Mu'adh say: 'Ubayd ibn Sulayman informed us, who said: I heard al-Dahhak say regarding His words: "And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him before his death," He said: None of the Jews dies until he testifies that Jesus is the Messenger of God (ﷺ).

10828. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: Ishaq related to us, saying: Ya'la related to us, from Juwaybir regarding His words: "Surely he will believe in him before his death," He said: In the recitation of Ubayy: "before their death." [[The report 10828: See the earlier report No. 10814.]]

* *

Others said: The meaning of that is: "And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in Muhammad (ﷺ) before the death of the People of the Book."

Mention of those who said this:

10829. Al-Muthanna related to me, saying: al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal related to us, saying: Hammad related to us, from Humayd who said: 'Ikrima said: No Christian or Jew dies until he believes in Muhammad (ﷺ), meaning in His words: "And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him before his death."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The most correct and sound of the sayings is the view of the one who said that the interpretation of this is: "And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in Jesus before the death of Jesus."

We only said that this is more correct than the other sayings because God, may His praise be exalted, has ruled for every believer in Muhammad (ﷺ) by the ruling of the people of faith, in inheritance and in the funeral prayer over him, and in attaching his young children to his ruling in the religion. So if every People of the Book believed in Jesus before his death, it would follow that a People of the Book who dies upon his religion should not inherit, except his young children, or those of them who are adult Muslims, if he has a young or adult Muslim child. And if he has no young child nor adult Muslim child, his estate would be disbursed where the property of a Muslim who dies with no heir is disbursed, and his ruling would be the ruling of the Muslims regarding the funeral prayer over him, washing him, and burying him (taqbiruhu). [[His words "taqbiruhu" mean his burial where burial takes place; it seems to be one of the terms of the jurists in the time of Abu Ja'far. In the language, "qabara yaqburuhu" means he buried him, and "aqbara" means he made a grave for him. As for "qabbara yuqabbiru taqbiran" in this sense, I have not found it in the lexicons.]] Because whoever dies believing in Jesus, has died believing in Muhammad and all the messengers. For Jesus (may God's blessings be upon him) came confirming Muhammad and all the messengers (may God's blessings be upon them), so whoever affirms and believes in Jesus, also affirms Muhammad and all the prophets and messengers of God. Just as whoever believes in Muhammad, believes in Jesus and all the prophets and messengers of God. It is impermissible that one who denies Muhammad be a believer in Jesus.

* *

If someone supposes that the meaning of the Jew's belief in Jesus, which God mentioned in His words: "And there is none of the People of the Book but that he will surely believe in him before his death," is merely his acknowledgment that he is a prophet sent by God, apart from his affirmation of everything he brought from God, then he has erred.

That is because it is not permissible for someone to be credited with affirming the prophethood of a prophet while denying some part of what that prophet brought as revelation from God. Indeed, it is not permissible for anyone to be credited with affirming the prophethood of any one of God's prophets, because the nations were commanded to affirm all of God's prophets and messengers. Whoever denies some of God's prophets regarding what they brought to their nation from God is, in effect, denying all of God's prophets regarding what they called God's servants to, of God's religion. Since this is so, and since all the people of Islam agree that every People of the Book who died before affirming Muhammad (ﷺ) and what he brought from God is judged by the religion he followed during his lifetime, and that none of his rulings concerning his person, property, or children, young and old, are transferred from what he was upon during his life after his death, the evidence shows that the meaning of God's statement, "And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in him before his death" [Q 4:159], is only: "they will surely believe in Jesus before Jesus's death." This applies to a specific group of the People of the Book, referring to a particular era among them and not to all the eras that came after Jesus, and it will occur at his descent, as in the following report:

10830. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to me, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Adam, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Prophet of God (ﷺ) said: "The prophets are half-brothers; their mothers are different, but their religion is one. I am the closest of people to Jesus son of Mary, because there was no prophet between me and him. He will descend, so when you see him, recognize him. He is a man of medium build, inclining to redness and whiteness, with straight hair, as if his head were dripping though no water has touched it, and he will wear two garments dyed with saffron. He will break the cross, kill the swine, abolish the jizyah, and money will overflow. He will fight people for Islam until God destroys in his time all religions except Islam, and God will destroy in his time the Antichrist, the great liar, the Dajjal. Security will prevail on earth in his time, so that lions will graze with camels, panthers with cattle, wolves with sheep, and boys or children will play with snakes without harming one another. He will remain on earth as long as God wills," and perhaps he said, "forty years," "then he will die, and the Muslims will pray over him and bury him."

[Note on the report 10830: this hadith has already passed as no. 7145, through Ibn Humayd, from Salamah, from Ibn Ishaq, from al-Hasan ibn Dinar, from Qatadah, with the same meaning but with very slight variation in wording. It is a sound hadith; my brother al-Sayyid Ahmad traced its sources (takhrij) in its place there, and he pointed to this chain of al-Tabari here, so refer to it there.]

* *

As for the one who said that the intended meaning of his words "will surely believe in him before his death" is "will surely believe in Muhammad (ﷺ) before the death of the People of the Book," this has no comprehensible basis. Because, along with its corruption on the ground that we have shown the corruption of the view of the one who said, "He meant: will surely believe in Jesus before the death of the People of the Book," it is further corrupted by the fact that no mention of Muhammad (peace be upon him) has preceded in the verses before this, so that the pronoun in "will surely believe in him" could be directed toward his mention. Rather, "will surely believe in him" occurs in the context of discussing Jesus, his mother, and the Jews. It is not permissible to turn speech away from its context toward something else, except with a proof that must be accepted, either from the clear indication of the revelation or from a report from the Messenger which constitutes a binding proof. As for mere claims, they are not difficult for anyone to make.

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The interpretation of the verse, since the matter is as we have described, is: "And there is none of the People of the Book but will surely believe in Jesus before Jesus's death." The word "man" (مَن) after "illa" (except) has been omitted, since the sense of the speech indicates it, so the indication of the sense makes its explicit mention unnecessary, like the rest of what has preceded of similar examples, which we have already explained.

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His statement: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them﴾ [Q 4:159]

Abu Ja'far said: By this, the Almighty means: "And on the Day of Resurrection, Jesus will be a witness against the People of the Book," meaning a witness against them of the denial of those among them who denied him, and the affirmation of those among them who affirmed him, regarding what he brought them from God, and of his conveying the message of his Lord. [See the explanation of "shahid" (witness) in the earlier language indexes.] As in the following report:

10831. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, saying: Ibn Jurayj said, regarding "And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them," that he had conveyed to them what he was sent with to them.

10832. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding "And on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them": he says, "He will be a witness against them on the Day of Resurrection that he had conveyed the message of his Lord, and acknowledged servitude for himself."

* *

Concerning the interpretation of His statement: ﴿For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We made unlawful for them good things which had been lawful for them, and because of their hindering from the way of God many times over, and their taking of usury though they had been forbidden from it, and their consuming of the wealth of people unjustly. And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment﴾ [Q 4:160–161]

Abu Ja'far said: By this, the Almighty means: "We made unlawful for the Jews who broke their covenant which they pledged to their Lord, disbelieved in the signs of God, killed their prophets, spoke a great slander against Mary, and did what God described them as doing in His Book, good things of food and other things, which had been lawful to them, as a punishment for their wrongdoing, which God reported about them in His Book." [See the explanation of "hadu" (Jews) in the earlier volumes, 2:143, 507, 508. And the explanation of "al-tayyibat" (good things) in the earlier volumes, 3:301 / 5:555 / 6:361 / 7:424 / 8:409.] As in the following report:

10833. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding "For the wrongdoing of those who were Jews, We made unlawful for them good things which had been lawful for them," to the end of the verse: the people were punished for a wrong they committed and a transgression they perpetrated; things were made unlawful for them because of their transgression and wrongdoing.

* *

As for His statement, "and because of their hindering from the way of God many times over," it means: and because of their hindering the servants of God from His religion and from the paths He prescribed for His servants, a great hindering. [In the printed edition: "the paths He explained to His servant," which is an obvious error.] Their hindering from the way of God was by their saying false things about God, claiming that this was from God, their altering the Book of God, and their distorting its meanings from their proper aspects. Among the greatest of this was their denial of the prophethood of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), and their withholding the clarification of what they knew of his matter from people who were ignorant of his matter. [See the explanation of "al-sadd" (hindering) in the earlier volumes, 4:300 / 7:53 / 8:482, 513, and the explanation of "al-sabil" (the way) in the earlier language indexes.]

* *

In a similar sense Mujahid used to say:

10834. Muhammad ibn Amr narrated to us, saying: Abu Asim narrated to me, saying: Isa narrated to me, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding the words of God, "and because of their hindering from the way of God many times over," he said: "[They were hindering] themselves and others from the truth."

10835. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Abu Hudhayfah narrated to us, saying: Shibl narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.

* *

As for His statement, "and their taking of usury," it refers to their taking what they added to their capital, in exchange for an extension of the term after its due date. I have already explained the meaning of "usury" (riba) earlier, in a way that makes repeating it unnecessary. [See the explanation of "riba" in the earlier volumes, 6:7, 8, 13, 15, 22.]

* *

As for "though they had been forbidden from it," it means: forbidden from taking usury.

* *

As for His statement, "and their consuming of the wealth of people unjustly," it means what they used to take as bribes for judgment, as God described them in His saying: ﴿And you see many of them hastening toward sin and aggression and consuming of unlawful gain. Wretched is what they used to do﴾ [Q 5:62]. Among their consuming of people's wealth unjustly was what they used to take as payment for the books they wrote with their own hands, then they would say, "This is from God," and similar base and corrupt foods. God punished them for all of that by forbidding them the good things that had been lawful to them before.

God described them as having consumed the wealth of people in this unjust manner because they consumed it without right, and they took their property from them without entitlement.

* *

As for His statement, "And We have prepared for the disbelievers among them a painful punishment," [in the printed edition: "So His statement..." — the manuscript reading is correct] it means: We have made ready for the disbelievers in God and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) from these Jews [See the explanation of "a'tada" (prepared) in the earlier volumes, 8:103, 355 / 9:353], the painful punishment, which is the agonizing one [See the explanation of "al-alim" (painful) in the earlier language indexes], from the punishment of Hell, with Him, which they will burn in the Hereafter when they come before their Lord, and He will punish them with it. [In the printed edition: "from the punishment of Hell, a fire they will burn..." — the manuscript reading is correct.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 162:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿But those firm in knowledge among them and the believers believe in what has been sent down to you, and what was sent down before you, and those who establish prayer and give zakah and believe in Allah and the Last Day — those We will give a great reward﴾ [4:162].

Abu Ja'far said: This is an exception from Allah, exalted is His praise, exempting from the People of the Book, the Jews, whose description He had given in the verses that preceded, from His words: ﴿The People of the Book ask you to bring down to them a book from heaven﴾ [4:153].

Then He, exalted is His praise, said to His servants, explaining to them the ruling concerning those among them whom He had guided to His religion and granted success in right guidance: Not all the People of the Book have the description that I have described to you, ﴿but those firm in knowledge among them﴾ — those who have become firmly rooted in knowledge of the rulings of Allah which His prophets brought, who have perfected that and known its reality.

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "being firm in knowledge" sufficiently to dispense with repeating it in this place. [See the explanation of "those firm in knowledge" earlier: vol. 6, pp. 201–208.]

* *

"And the believers" means: the believers in Allah and His messengers. They believe in the Qur'an that Allah has sent down to you, O Muhammad, and in the books He sent down to those before you of the prophets and messengers. They do not ask you, as those ignorant ones among them asked you [in the printed edition: "as these asked", and I have retained what is in the manuscript]: to bring down to them a book from heaven. This is because they have known, from what they have read of the books of Allah and what their prophets brought them, that you are the messenger of Allah, and that it is obligatory for them to follow you, and nothing else suffices them. So there is no need for them to ask you for a miraculous sign or any proof other than what they already know of your affair through the firmly rooted knowledge in their hearts, from the information their prophets gave them about that, and from the proofs of your prophethood that I have given you. Thus, through their knowledge and their firmness in it, they believe in you and in what has been sent down to you of the Book, and in what was sent down before you of all the other books, as:

10836 — Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding His words: "But those firm in knowledge among them and the believers believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you." Allah excepted a group (uthbiyyah) of the People of the Book, and there were among them those who believed in Allah and in what was sent down to them and what was sent down to the Prophet of Allah; they believed in it and affirmed it, and knew it to be the truth from their Lord.

* *

Then they differed concerning "those who establish prayer" — are they the ones firm in knowledge, or are they others?

Some of them said: They are the same.

* *

Then those who said that differed concerning the reason why their i'rab (grammatical case) differs from the i'rab of "those firm in knowledge," although both are descriptions of one category of people.

Some of them said: That is an error by the scribe [see Abu Ja'far's refutation of this view below, pp. 397–398; it is among the soundest refutations, in which he appealed to sound discernment], and the original reading is: "But those firm in knowledge among them and those who establish prayer."

Those who said this:

10837 — Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Al-Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal narrated to us, saying: Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from al-Zubayr, who said: I said to Aban ibn Uthman ibn Affan: What is the matter with it, that it is written: "But those firm in knowledge among them and the believers believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you, and those who establish prayer"? He said: When the scribe wrote "But those firm in knowledge among them," and then reached [the point], he said: What shall I write? It was said to him: Write "and those who establish prayer," and he wrote what he was told.

10838 — Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from Hisham ibn Urwah, from his father: that he asked A'ishah about His words "and those who establish prayer," and about His words: ﴿Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews and the Sabians﴾ [5:69], and about His words: ﴿Indeed, these two are certainly magicians﴾ [20:63]. She said: O son of my sister, this is the work of the scribe; they made errors in the writing. [In the printed edition: "the work of the scribes", and I have retained what is in the manuscript, which is purely correct.]

* *

It is also mentioned that this is in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: ﴿and those who establish prayer﴾.

* *

Others said, and this is the view of some grammarians of Kufa and Basra: "and those who establish prayer" is a description of "those firm in knowledge," but when the speech became lengthy, and what intervened between "those firm in knowledge" and "those who establish prayer" was long, "those who establish prayer" was put in the accusative by way of praise. They said: The Arabs do this with the description and attribute of one thing: when it is extended with praise or blame, they sometimes vary the i'rab of its beginning and middle, then return the end to the i'rab of the beginning. Sometimes they make the i'rab of the end follow that of the middle, and sometimes they make it all one kind of i'rab. They cited as evidence for their view the verses I mentioned in His words: ﴿And those who fulfil their covenant when they make it, and the patient in misfortune and hardship﴾ [2:177]. [In the printed edition: "the verses I mentioned", which is a plain error; the correct reading is from the manuscript and from consulting the source referred to.]

Others said: Rather, "those who establish prayer" is a description of someone other than "those firm in knowledge" in this place, although "those firm in knowledge" are among "those who establish prayer."

* *

All those who held this view said: The position of "those who establish prayer" in the i'rab is genitive (khafd).

Some of them said: Its position is genitive by coordination with "ma" in His words: "believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you," meaning: and [they believe] in those who establish prayer.

* *

Then those who interpreted it this way differed about the meaning of the speech.

Some of them said: The meaning is: "and the believers believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you," and in establishing prayer. They said: Then "and those who give zakah" is put in the nominative, as a coordination with the reference to "the believers" in "believe," as if it were said: "and the believers believe in what has been sent down to you, they and those who give zakah."

* *

Others said: Rather, "those who establish prayer" are the angels. They said: Their establishing prayer is their glorifying their Lord and their seeking forgiveness for those on earth. They said: The meaning of the speech is: "and the believers believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you," and in the angels.

* *

Others among them said: Rather, the meaning is: "and the believers believe in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you," and they believe in those who establish prayer, they and those who give zakah, as He, exalted is His praise, said: ﴿He believes in Allah and believes the believers﴾ [9:61].

* *

Those who held this view denied that "those who establish prayer" is in the accusative by way of praise. They said: The Arabs put into the accusative by way of praise only the description of one whom they mention after the completion of his predicate. They said: The predicate of "those firm in knowledge" is His words: "those — We will give them a great reward." He said: It is not permissible to put "those who establish prayer" in the accusative by way of praise while it is in the middle of the speech and the predicate of the subject has not yet been completed.

* *

Others said: The meaning is: "But those firm in knowledge among them, and among those who establish prayer." They said: The position of "those who establish prayer" is genitive.

* *

Others said: Its meaning is: "and the believers believe in what has been sent down to you, and in those who establish prayer."

* *

Abu Ja'far said: This view and the one before it are rejected by the Arabs, who hardly ever coordinate an apparent noun with a pronoun in the genitive case, although that has occurred in some of their poetry. [In the printed edition: "li-zahir" with a lam, and the correct reading is from the manuscript.] [See what has passed, vol. 7, pp. 519–520.]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The view I hold most correct is that "those who establish prayer" is in the genitive position, as a coordination with "ma" in His words: "in what has been sent down to you and what was sent down before you" — and that the meaning of "those who establish prayer" be directed to the angels.

So the interpretation of the speech becomes: "and the believers among them believe in what has been sent down to you," O Muhammad, of the Book, "and in what was sent down before you," of My books, "and in the angels who establish prayer." Then it returns to the description of "those firm in knowledge," saying: But those firm in knowledge among them, and the believers in the books, and those who give zakah, and the believers in Allah and the Last Day.

* *

We chose this over other views because it is mentioned that this is in the reading of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: ﴿and those who establish prayer﴾, and so it is in his codex, as they report. If it were an error by the scribe, it would have been required that it be so in all the codices other than our codex, which the scribe who erred wrote for us. But it is in agreement with the codex of Ubayy and in differing from what is in our codex, and the agreement of our codex and the codex of Ubayy on this shows that what is in our codex is correct and not an error. Moreover, if that were an error in the writing, the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from whom the Qur'an was taken would not have taught those who learned it among the Muslims with a grammatical error; they would have corrected it with their tongues and taught the Ummah the correct form. [In the printed edition: "wa-laqqanuhu lil-ummah," with a lam, which is a bad and ugly change.]

And the transmission of all Muslims of that as a recitation, in the form it is written in the script, is the strongest proof of its correctness and soundness, and that the scribe had no hand in it. [This argument put forward by our imam Abu Ja'far, may Allah be pleased with him, is the argument of a jurist versed in the meanings of speech and the directions of opinion. It is the argument of a man of learning, comprehensive in the methods of knowledge, aware of what the evidence of transmission and the proofs of reason require. Many of our imams have dealt with this, but Abu Ja'far's argument remains the most upright in refuting this report attributed to A'ishah, Mother of the Believers.]

* *

As for those who directed it to the accusative by way of praise for "those firm in knowledge" — although that may be possible, though remote from the speech of the Arabs, for the reason I mentioned earlier, namely that the Arabs do not depart from the i'rab of the described noun in its description except after the completion of its predicate — the speech of Allah, exalted is His praise, is the most eloquent speech, so it is impermissible to direct it except to what is [more] fitting for it in eloquence. [The addition between the brackets is required by the context.]

* *

As for those who directed it to coordination with the "ha" and "mim" in His words: "But those firm in knowledge among them," or to coordination with the "kaf" in "what has been sent down to you," or to the "kaf" in "what was sent down before you," that is further from eloquence than putting it in the accusative by way of praise, because of the ugliness, which I mentioned earlier, of returning an apparent noun to a pronoun in the genitive.

* *

As for those who directed "those who establish prayer" to "establishment" [of prayer], that is a claim without proof from the apparent indication of the revelation, nor a report whose authority is established. It is impermissible to transfer the apparent meaning of the revelation to a hidden meaning without proof.

* *

As for His words: "and those who give zakah," it is coordinated with His words "and the believers believe," and it is part of their description.

* *

Its interpretation: those who give the zakah of their wealth to whom Allah has made it lawful and directed it to — "and the believers in Allah and the Last Day," meaning: those who affirm the oneness and divinity of Allah, and the resurrection after death, and reward and punishment — "those — We will give them a great reward," meaning: those who have this description — "We will give them," meaning: We will bestow upon them — "a great reward," meaning: recompense for what was theirs of obedience to Allah and following His command, and a great reward, which is Paradise. [See the explanation of "giving" (al-iytha') and "reward" (al-ajr) in the indexes of language earlier.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 163:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you, [O Muhammad], as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him. And We revealed to Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, the Descendants, Jesus, Job, Jonah, Aaron, and Solomon, and to David We gave the Psalms.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah," He means: Indeed, We have sent to you, O Muhammad, with prophethood, just as We sent to Noah and to the rest of the prophets whom I have named to you after him, and those whom I have not named to you [[See the explanation of "awha" (revealed) in what has preceded, 6:405, 406.]], as:

10839 - Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Mundhir al-Thawri, from al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, regarding His saying: "Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him," he said: He revealed to him as He revealed to all the prophets before him. [[The report 10839: "Mundhir al-Thawri" is "Mundhir ibn Ya'la al-Thawri," Abu Ya'la. He narrated from Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and others. Narrated from him his son al-Rabi' ibn al-Mundhir, al-A'mash, Fitr ibn Khalifa, and others. Trustworthy, few narrations. Biographed in al-Tahdhib.]]

* *

It is mentioned that this verse was revealed to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ because some of the Jews, when Allah exposed them with the verses He sent down to His Messenger ﷺ— this being His saying: ﴿The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from heaven﴾— the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited that to them, and they said: "Allah has not sent down anything to a human after Moses!" So Allah revealed these verses, refuting them, and informed His Prophet and the believers in him that He had indeed revealed to him after Moses, and to those He named in this verse, and to others He did not name, as:

10840 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Yunus ibn Bukayr narrated to us— and Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Salamah narrated to us— from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, he said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, narrated to me, he said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to me— or Ikrimah— from Ibn Abbas, he said: Sukayn and Adi ibn Zayd said: "O Muhammad, we do not know that Allah has sent down anything to a human after Moses!" So Allah revealed in response to their words: "Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him," through to the end of the verses. [[The report 10840: Ibn Hisham's Sira 2:211, which continues the reports whose last previously was 9792. In the printed and manuscript editions it read "Adi ibn Thabit," which is certainly an error, for in Ibn Hisham's Sira and elsewhere it is "Adi ibn Zayd." I did not find "Adi ibn Thabit" among the enemies from among the Jews.

"Sukayn ibn Abi Sukayn" and "Adi ibn Zayd" were from Banu Qaynuqa', mentioned by Ibn Hisham in the Sira among the enemies from among the Jews, 2:161.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, they said, when Allah revealed the verses before this one concerning them: "Allah has not sent down anything to a human, nor to Moses, nor to Jesus!" So Allah, may His praise be exalted, revealed: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure when they said, "Allah has not sent down anything to a human"﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 91], nor to Moses nor to Jesus.

Those who said that:

10841 - Al-Harith narrated to me, he said: Abd al-Aziz narrated to us, he said: Abu Ma'shar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, he said: Allah revealed: "The People of the Scripture ask you to bring down to them a book from heaven," through to His saying: "and their saying against Mary a great slander." When he recited it to them— meaning to the Jews— and informed them of their evil deeds, they denied everything Allah had sent down and said: "Allah has not sent down anything to a human, nor to Moses nor to Jesus!! Nor has Allah sent down anything to any prophet!" He said: So he [Muhammad ibn Ka'b] loosened his hold on his cloak [["Al-hibwa" (with a fatha or damma on the ha', and sukun on the ba'): the garment with which one sits in iḥtibā'. "Al-iḥtibā'": that a person draws his legs up to his belly with a garment that gathers them together with his back and ties them there. Iḥtibā' may also be done with the hands in place of a garment.]] and said: "Nor to anyone!" So Allah, may His praise be exalted, revealed: ﴿They did not measure Allah with His true measure when they said, "Allah has not sent down anything to a human"﴾ [Surah al-An'am: 91].

* *

As for His saying: "And to David We gave the Psalms" (Zabur), the reciters differed in its recitation.

The majority of the reciters of the Muslim cities, except a group of the reciters of Kufa, recited it: ﴿wa-ātaynā Dāwūda zabūran﴾, with a fatha on the "z" in the singular, meaning: We gave David the book named "Zabur."

* *

Some of the Kufan reciters recited it: ﴿wa-ātaynā Dāwūda zubūran﴾, with a damma on the "z," as the plural of "zabr" (ẓabr).

It is as if they interpreted its meaning: We gave David books and written scriptures.

* *

This is from their saying: "I wrote the book" (zabartu al-kitāb, azburuhu zabran) and "I wrote it" (dhabartuhu adhburuhu dhabran), when I wrote it. [[See the explanation of "al-Zabur" in what has preceded, 7:450, 451; here he clarifies what was summarized there, and this is one of the forms of his abridgment of the tafsir.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The more correct of the two readings in our view is the reading of the one who recites: ﴿wa-ātaynā Dāwūda zabūran﴾, with a fatha on the "z," as the name of the book given to David, just as the book given to Moses was named "al-Tawrat" (Torah), the book given to Jesus "al-Injil" (Gospel), and the book given to Muhammad "al-Furqan" (the Criterion), because that is the name by which what was given to David is known. The Arabs say: "Zabur of David," by which all nations know his book.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 164:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿And messengers We have related to you before, and messengers We have not related to you; and Allah spoke to Moses with direct speech﴾ (4:164).

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His mention be exalted, He means: "We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and to the messengers We have related to you, and messengers We have not related to you."

* *

Someone may say: "If that is its meaning, why is His saying 'wa-rusulan' (and messengers) in the accusative and not in the genitive?" It is said: It was put in the accusative because the preposition "ila" (to), which governed the nouns before it, was not repeated over it. Although the nouns before it were in the genitive, they carry the sense of the accusative, because the meaning of the speech is: "We have sent you as a messenger just as We sent Noah and the prophets after him." So "the messengers" is coordinated with the case of the nouns before it, since it is separated from them in wording only, and the particle that governed it in the genitive was not repeated over it, as the poet said [[I do not know who said it.]]:

"Even if you brought him bread crumbled, and eggs cooked together with sugar, it would not satisfy him until he became drunk."

[[In the manuscript: "lau jita lana bil-khairi mubashshiran", which is very corrupt; the correct reading is what is in the printed edition. His saying "munashshiran" means spread out flat, as a cloth is spread, as if he meant thin layers piled on one another.]]

* *

It may also be that "the messengers" is in the accusative because the conjunction "wa" is connected to the verb, meaning: "and We have related messengers to you before," just as He, may His mention be exalted, said: ﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy, and the wrongdoers—He has prepared for them a painful punishment﴾ (76:31). [[Abu Ja'far has clarified this in his tafsir of Surat al-Insan, 29:140 (Bulaq edition), saying: "The accusative of (the wrongdoers) is because the 'wa' is an adverbial element of 'a'adda' (prepared). The meaning is: 'and He has prepared for the wrongdoers a painful punishment.'"]]

* *

It has been reported that in the reading of Ubayy it is: ﴿wa-rusulun qad qasasnahum alayka min qablu wa-rusulun lam naqsusshum alayka﴾, with the nominative case; since it is read so, the case is due to the returning pronoun in "qasasnahum alayka". [[See Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra' 1:295.]]

* *

As for His saying: "and Allah spoke to Moses with direct speech," by this, may His mention be exalted, He means: God addressed Moses with His speech, an address. And:

10842 – Ibn Humayd related to us, he said: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, he said: Nuh ibn Abi Maryam related to us, and he was asked: "How did Allah speak to Moses with direct speech?" He said: "Face to face."

* *

And:

10843 – Ibn WakI' related to us, he said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Ibn Mubarak, from Ma'mar and Yunus, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, who said: Juz ibn Jabir al-Khath'ami informed me, he said: I heard Ka'b say: "When Allah, may His mention be exalted, spoke to Moses, He spoke to him in all the languages before His speech"—meaning: the speech of Moses—"so he began to say: 'O Lord, I do not understand!' until He spoke to him in his own language, the last of the languages, and he said: 'O Lord, is this Your speech?' He said: 'No, and if you heard My speech—i.e., in its true form—you would be nothing!'"

= Ibn Wakī' said: Abu Usamah said: Abu Bakr al-Saghani added to me in this report that Moses said: "O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that resembles Your speech?" He said: "No, and the closest of My creation in resemblance to My speech is the most intense of thunderbolts that people hear."

[[Report 10843: "Abu Usamah" is Hammad ibn Zayd ibn Usamah, mentioned under no. 5265, and there is difference over his name. "Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham," his biography is given under nos. 2351, 7820.

"Juz ibn Jabir al-Khath'ami": al-Bukhari recorded him in al-Kabir under the name "Jarz ibn Jabir al-Khath'ami," and said: "Abu al-Yaman related it from Shu'ayb, from Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman." Then he said: "Abd al-Razzaq related from Ma'mar: Jariz ibn Jabir al-Khath'ami" [I say: the correct form is "Juz," as in the manuscript of al-Tabari, and as Ibn Abi Hatim stated, as will follow]. Then al-Bukhari said: "Yunus, Ibn Akhi al-Zuhri and al-Zubaydi said: Juz'." Then he also said: "Isma'il related from his brother Sulayman, from Ibn Abi Atiq: Jaru ibn Jabir" [I say: this is the chain that follows as no. 10846].

As for Ibn Abi Hatim in al-Jarh wa-al-Ta'dil, he recorded him under the name "Juz' ibn Jabir al-Khath'ami," and said: "In the transmission of Shu'ayb ibn Abi Hamzah, from al-Zuhri." This shows that al-Bukhari's entry may be under the name "Juz' ibn Jabir," indeed I incline that this is the correct form, God willing.

Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: "In the transmission of Ma'mar: Juz ibn Jabir, and it is a mistake, al-Zubaydi followed him in it." So he agreed with al-Bukhari regarding Ma'mar's transmission and differed with him regarding al-Zubaydi's following, for al-Bukhari said of him in his transmission "Juz'." Then he also said: "It is said: Hazn ibn Jabir"—I heard my father say that—and I fear there is distortion in the copy of Ibn Abi Hatim, and that its correct form, as in al-Bukhari, is "Jaru" with a ra, or "Jazu" with a zayn. All of this is problematic and the truth cannot be determined in it; it is only transmission. See also reports 10845–10847.

In the printed edition it read "Juz' min Jabir," and I have adopted the manuscript reading, which is the correct one indicated by the words of al-Bukhari and Ibn Abi Hatim, since this is Ma'mar's transmission.

Then another problem arises: in the manuscript: "Qala Ibn Ka'b, qala Abu Usamah, wa-zadani Abu Bakr al-Saghani..."

As for "Ibn Ka'b," it is an obvious error with no doubt; it is in fact, as in the printed edition, "Ibn Wakī'," and the copyist slipped, because of the mention of "Ka'b al-Ahbar" in the report, so the similarity between "Wakī'" and "Ka'b" misled him until he forgot and wrote "Ibn Ka'b."

As for the problem: "Abu Bakr al-Saghani" is Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Ja'far, the hafiz and traveller, and he is the teacher of al-Tabari; his transmission from him has passed in several places, see no. 4074, where his biography is given, and no. 4330. He related from him in al-Muntakhab min Dhayl al-Mudhayyal (appended to his history), p. 104, as I pointed out. There is no doubt that "Abu Usamah Hammad ibn Zayd" never related from him at all. It is clear that the speaker "wa-zadani Abu Bakr al-Saghani" is Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Jarir himself.

So what is his saying "Ibn Wakī' said, Abu Usamah said"? I do not know with certainty; either something fell from the copyist, or the dictator (Abu Ja'far or another) wished to move to the following chain, no. 10844, dictated the opening of the chain, then returned to what he had missed of the rest of Abu Ja'far's words in report 10843, namely "wa-zadani Abu Bakr al-Saghani," and the writer did not notice it because of the hesitation the dictator had. This is the furthest I can find in explaining it. The manuscript is not to be relied upon fully at this point, because it has a gap or omission, as you will see in the chains 10845–10847. And God alone knows. Written by Mahmud Muhammad Shakir.

The printed edition had "ashaddu ma tasma'u" (the most intense of what people hear), and I have adopted the manuscript reading.]]

10844 – Ibn Wakī' related to us, he said: Abu Usamah related to us, from Umar ibn Hamzah ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar, who said: I heard Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi say: Moses was asked: "What have you likened the speech of your Lord to among what He created?" Moses said: "The pouring thunder."

[[Report 10844: "Umar ibn Hamzah ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar ibn al-Khattab," passed under no. 7819. In the manuscript it was "...Abd Allah ibn Amr," which is a clear error.

His saying "al-ra'd al-sakib": so I read it, while in the manuscript and printed edition it is "al-ra'd al-sakin" with a nun at the end, and I find no intelligible meaning for it. As for "al-sakib," it is the apt description of the intensity of the sound of thunder, namely its successiveness and spreading out. In a hadith: "When the muezzin pours out (sakaba) the first call of the dawn prayer, he rises and prays two light rak'ahs," and that describes the muezzin when he calls, extending his call and repeating and returning it. Its origin is from "sakb al-ma'" (pouring water), then "sakb" was borrowed for pouring forth speech or other sounds, as one says: "Pour a story into my ear," meaning: cast and pour it.]]

10845 – Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la related to me, he said: Abd Allah ibn Wahb related to us, he said: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, who said: Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me that Juz ibn Jabir al-Khath'ami informed him, who said: When Allah spoke to Moses in all the languages before his tongue, he began to say: "By Allah, O Lord, I do not understand this!" until He spoke to him in the last of the languages, in a voice like his own, and Moses said: "O Lord, is this Your speech?" He said: "No." He said: "Is there anything in Your creation that resembles Your speech?" He said: "No, and the closest of My creation in resemblance to My speech is the most intense of what people hear of thunderbolts."

[[Report 10845: "Juz ibn Jabir al-Khath'ami": this is the correct form, because it is the transmission of Yunus from Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, which al-Bukhari pointed to, as I stated in the note on report 10843.]]

10846 – Abu Yunus al-Makki related to me, he said: Ibn Abi Uways related to us, he said: My brother informed me, from Sulayman, from Muhammad ibn Abi Atiq, from Ibn Shihab, from Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham: that Juz ibn Jabir al-Khath'ami informed him that he heard [Ka'b] al-Ahbar say: When Allah spoke to Moses in all the languages before his tongue, Moses began to say: "O Lord, by Allah, I do not understand this!" until He spoke to him in the last of the languages, in his tongue, in a voice like his own, and Moses said: "O Lord, is Your speech like this?" He said: "If I spoke to you with My speech you would be nothing!" He said: "O Lord, is there anything in Your creation that resembles Your speech?" He said: "No, and the closest of My creation in resemblance to My speech is the most intense of thunderbolts."

[[Report 10846: "Abu Yunus al-Makki," the teacher of al-Tabari, I have not identified him, nor found him, and no earlier transmission from him has passed before me.

"Ibn Abi Uways" is Isma'il ibn Abd Allah ibn Uways al-Asbahi, whose biography passed under no. 45.

"His brother" is Abu Bakr Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Uways, also passed under no. 45.

"Sulayman" is Sulayman ibn Bilal al-Taymi al-Qurashi, passed under nos. 4333, 4923.

"Ibn Abi Atiq," or "Muhammad ibn Abi Atiq," is Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr al-Siddiq, whose biography passed under nos. 4923, 10317.

This is the chain which al-Bukhari pointed to, as I mentioned in the note on report 10843, where his transmission has "Jaru ibn Jabir," and Ibn Abi Hatim also mentioned it, so see what I said there.

In the printed edition here it read "anahu sami'a al-Ahbar taqulu," but the earlier and following reports, and what al-Bukhari and Ibn Abi Hatim pointed to, show that the correct form is "Ka'b al-Ahbar," so I added "Ka'b" between brackets, which is the pure correctness, God willing.]]

10847 – Ibn Abd al-Rahim related to us, he said: Amr related to us, he said: Zuhayr related to us, from Yahya, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Harith ibn Hisham, from Juz ibn Jabir: that he heard Ka'b say: When Allah spoke to Moses in the languages before his tongue, Moses began to say: "O Lord, I do not understand this!" until Allah spoke to him in the last of the languages, like his tongue, and Moses said: "O Lord, is this Your speech?" Allah said: "If I spoke to you with My speech you would be nothing!" He said: "O Lord, is there anything of Your creation that resembles Your speech?" He said: "No, and the closest of My creation in resemblance to My speech is the most intense of thunderbolts."

[[Report 10847: this is a chain which al-Bukhari did not point to, nor Ibn Abi Hatim. Moreover, the last three reports, 10845–10847, are not in the manuscript, so it seems the copyist abridged in his copy.

Whatever the case of this report, the attributes of our Lord, exalted is He and sanctified are His names, are not taken from Ka'b al-Ahbar and his like; rather the matter concerning them belongs to Allah alone, as He praises Himself, and as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ conveyed from Him, not Ka'b al-Ahbar and whoever follows his way.]]

**On the interpretation of His words:** ﴿Messengers as bearers of good news and as warners, so that people will have no argument against God after the messengers. God is ever Mighty and Wise.﴾ (4:165)

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: We revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him, and among the messengers We mentioned, ﴿messengers﴾ ("rusulan") is in the accusative as a *qat'* (grammatical detachment, meaning the word is taken out of the preceding noun group and put in the accusative) relative to the names of the prophets He mentioned, ﴿bearers of good news﴾ ("mubashshirin"). He says: I sent them as messengers to My creation and My servants, bearing good news of My reward to those who obey Me, follow My command, and believe My messengers, and warning of My punishment to those who disobey Me, oppose My command, and deny My messengers. ﴿So that people will have no argument against God after the messengers﴾: He says: I sent My messengers to My servants as bearers of good news and as warners, so that no one who disbelieves in Me, worships rivals besides Me, or strays from My path can argue, if I punish him, by saying: ﴿Had You sent us a messenger, we would have followed Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced﴾ (20:134). Thus He cut off the argument of every false claimant who denied His oneness and opposed His command, by all the meanings of decisive proofs that remove their excuse, as a warning from Him to them, so that the conclusive proof of God may be against them and against all His creatures.

* *

Those who interpret the Qur'an (ahl al-ta'wil) said things similar to what we have said.

Those who said that:

10849 – Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi: ﴿so that people will have no argument against God after the messengers﴾, meaning they would say: You did not send messengers to us.

* *

﴿God is ever Mighty and Wise﴾: He says: God has always been Mighty in His retribution against those of His creatures whom He punished [for] their disbelief in Him and their disobedience to Him, after establishing His proof against them through His messengers and His evidences. ﴿Wise﴾: in His management of their affairs in what He has ordained.

[Editor's note: The addition between the brackets is necessary for the context of the speech.]

[Editor's note: On the explanation of "Mighty" see earlier, p. 408, note 2, and its references there; and on the explanation of "Wise" see the earlier language indexes.]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 166:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness. And Allah is sufficient as a witness﴾ (4:166).

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: If those Jews who asked you to cause a book to descend to them from heaven disbelieve in what We have revealed to you, O Muhammad, and who said to you, "Allah has not sent down anything upon a human being" (6:91), and so they denied you, then they have indeed denied.
