The matter is not as they claim. Rather, "Allah bears witness" to His sending down to you what He has revealed of His Book and His inspiration. He sent that down to you with knowledge from Him that you are His chosen one among His creation and His selected one among His servants. His angels also bear witness to that for you. So do not let the denial of those who deny you, or the opposition of those who oppose you, grieve you. "And Allah is sufficient as a witness": that is, your Lord is sufficient as a witness to your truthfulness, apart from anything else of His creation. For when your Lord bears witness to your truthfulness, the denial of those who deny you will not harm you.

It has also been said that this verse was revealed concerning a group of Jews whom the Prophet ﷺ invited to follow him, and he informed them that they know the reality of his prophethood, but they denied his prophethood and rejected acknowledging it.

Mention of the report to that effect:

10850. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad, client of Zayd ibn Thabit, told me, who said: Sa'id ibn Jubayr, or Ikrimah, told me, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A group of Jews entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said to them: "By Allah, I know that you certainly know that I am the Messenger of Allah!" They said: "We do not know that!" So Allah revealed: "But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness. And Allah is sufficient as a witness."

10851. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Ishaq told me, saying: Muhammad ibn Abi Muhammad told me, from Ikrimah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: A band of Jews entered upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then he mentioned something similar. [[The two reports: 10850, 10851 — Sirat Ibn Hisham 2: 211, with variation in wording; it follows the preceding report no. 10840.]]

10852. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding "But Allah bears witness to what He has sent down to you; He has sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels bear witness. And Allah is sufficient as a witness": they are witnesses, and by Allah, witnesses who are not accused of partiality.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 167:

The explanation of His words: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve and avert [others] from the way of Allah have certainly strayed far astray﴾ (4:167).

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Indeed, those who denied, O Muhammad, your prophethood after they had knowledge of it, from among the People of the Book whose story I have related to you, and who denied that Allah, may His praise be exalted, had revealed His Book to you, "and averted [others] from the way of Allah," meaning: from the religion with which Allah sent you to His creation, which is Islam. Their averting [people] from it was by their saying to the people who asked them about Muhammad from among the polytheists, "We do not find the description of Muhammad in our Book!", and their claim that it had been enjoined upon them that prophethood would not be except among the progeny of Aaron and among the descendants of David, and other such matters by which they would discourage people from following the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and believing in him and in what he had brought from Allah.

* *

As for His words, "have certainly strayed far astray," meaning: they have deviated greatly from the straight path and turned away from the clear course.

Allah, may His praise be exalted, only means by their deviation from the course and their straying from it, their erring from the religion of Allah which He has approved for His servants and with which He sent His messengers. He says: whoever denies the message of Muhammad (ﷺ) and averts [others] from the community with which he was sent, [and] whoever accepts that from him, has indeed strayed and departed from the religion, which is the religion of Allah with which He sent His prophets, [into] far astray.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verses 168–169:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged—Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a way, except the way of Hell, to abide therein forever. And that is ever easy for Allah.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Indeed, those who denied the message of Muhammad (ﷺ), disbelieving in Allah by denying that, and who wronged by persisting in disbelief knowingly, wronging the servants of Allah, envying the Arabs, and transgressing against His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿Allah would not forgive them﴾, meaning: Allah would not pardon their sins by abandoning their punishment for them; rather He will disgrace them through it, by punishing them for it [[In the printed edition: "إياهم عليهم" (punishing them upon them), and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]. ﴿Nor would He guide them to a way﴾, meaning: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, would not guide these who disbelieved and wronged, whose description we have mentioned, so as to grant them success in any of the paths by which they would attain Allah's reward and, by adhering to it, reach Paradise. Rather, He forsakes them from that until they take the path of Hell. Mentioning "the way" is a figurative reference to the religion. The meaning of the statement is: Allah would not grant them success in Islam; rather He forsakes them from it toward ﴿the path of Hell﴾, which is disbelief, meaning: until they disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and so enter Hell, ﴿abiding therein forever﴾, meaning: remaining therein forever. ﴿And that is ever easy for Allah﴾, meaning: the eternal abiding of those whose description I have given you in Hell is easy for Allah, because whoever He wills to do that to cannot prevent it, and no one can stop Him from it, and what He intends to do to them is not difficult for Him. And that is ever easy for Allah, because the creation is His creation and the command is His command.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verses 168–169:

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved and wronged—Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to a way, except the way of Hell, to abide therein forever. And that is ever easy for Allah.﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: Indeed, those who denied the message of Muhammad (ﷺ), disbelieving in Allah by denying that, and who wronged by persisting in disbelief knowingly, wronging the servants of Allah, envying the Arabs, and transgressing against His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿Allah would not forgive them﴾, meaning: Allah would not pardon their sins by abandoning their punishment for them; rather He will disgrace them through it, by punishing them for it [[In the printed edition: "إياهم عليهم" (punishing them upon them), and the correct reading is from the manuscript.]]. ﴿Nor would He guide them to a way﴾, meaning: Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, would not guide these who disbelieved and wronged, whose description we have mentioned, so as to grant them success in any of the paths by which they would attain Allah's reward and, by adhering to it, reach Paradise. Rather, He forsakes them from that until they take the path of Hell. Mentioning "the way" is a figurative reference to the religion. The meaning of the statement is: Allah would not grant them success in Islam; rather He forsakes them from it toward ﴿the path of Hell﴾, which is disbelief, meaning: until they disbelieve in Allah and His messengers and so enter Hell, ﴿abiding therein forever﴾, meaning: remaining therein forever. ﴿And that is ever easy for Allah﴾, meaning: the eternal abiding of those whose description I have given you in Hell is easy for Allah, because whoever He wills to do that to cannot prevent it, and no one can stop Him from it, and what He intends to do to them is not difficult for Him. And that is ever easy for Allah, because the creation is His creation and the command is His command.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 170:

The interpretation of His saying: ﴿O mankind, the Messenger has certainly come to you with the truth from your Lord, so believe; it is better for you. But if you disbelieve, then indeed, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth, and ever is Allah Knowing and Wise.﴾ (4:170)

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, glorious is His praise, "O mankind," He means the polytheists of the Arabs and all categories of disbelief. "The Messenger has certainly come to you" means Muhammad (ﷺ), he has certainly come to you. "With the truth from your Lord" means with Islam, the religion which Allah has approved for His servants as a religion; that is, "from your Lord," meaning from the presence of your Lord. [[See the explanation of "from your Lord" with the same wording, previously, 6:440.]] "So believe; it is better for you" means: so confirm him and confirm what has come to you from your Lord of religion, for belief in that is better for you than disbelief in it. "But if you disbelieve" means: but if you deny his message and deny him and what has come to you from your Lord, then your denial of that and your rejection of it will not harm anyone but yourselves; the detriment of that returns only upon you, not upon Him who commanded you through what He sent to you by His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). [[In the printed edition: "other than Allah who commanded you ...", and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]] That is because to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and earth, in dominion and creation; your disbelief in what you have disbelieved of His command, and your disobedience to Him in what you have disobeyed, does not diminish from His dominion and sovereignty anything. [[The context: "your disbelief does not diminish ... anything from His dominion and sovereignty."]] "And ever is Allah Knowing and Wise" means: "And ever is Allah Knowing," of what you are going to of obedience to Him in what He commanded you and what He forbade you, and disobedience in that, with His knowledge of that from you, He commanded you and forbade you. [[In the printed edition: "and with knowledge" with an added waw; I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]] "Wise" means: wise in His command to you with what He commanded you, and in His prohibition to you of what He forbade you, and in other than that, of His management concerning you and concerning others of His creation.

* *

The scholars of Arabic grammar differed regarding the reason for which His saying "khayran lakum" ("better for you") is in the accusative case.

One of the grammarians of Kufa said: "khayran" is in the accusative by way of departure (al-khuruj) from what precedes it (see "al-khuruj" previously in the index of terms), because what precedes it is complete, namely His saying "fa-aminu" (so believe). He said: The Arabs have indeed been heard to do this in every complete statement to which speech is joined after its completion, in the manner of the joining of "khayr" with what precedes it. So one says: "Lata qumanna khayran laka" (you will surely stand, it being better for you), "law fa'alta dhalika khayran laka" (if you did that, it would be better for you), and "ittaqi Allah khayran laka" (fear Allah, it being better for you). He said: But when the speech is incomplete, it is only in the nominative, as in your saying: "In tattaqi Allah khayrun laka" (if you fear Allah, it is better for you), and ﴿And that you be patient is better for you﴾ (Surah an-Nisa: 25).

* *

Another of them said: The accusative of "khayran" came about because the original sentence is: "fa-aminu huwa khayrun lakum" (so believe; it is better for you). When "huwa" (it), which is a pronoun referring back and a verbal noun (masdar), was dropped, the speech was joined to what precedes it, and what precedes it is definite while "khayr" is indefinite, so it took the accusative because of its connection to the definite. The implied form is from the verb: "qum fa-al-qiyamu khayrun laka" (stand, for standing is better for you) and "la taqum fa-tarku al-qiyami khayrun laka" (do not stand, for abandoning standing is better for you). When it was dropped, it joined the first. He said: Do you not see that you find the pronoun referring to the command placed before the predicate, so you say to a man: "ittaqi Allah huwa khayrun laka" (fear Allah; it is better for you), meaning: the fearing is better for you. He said: Its accusative is not by way of implying "yakun" (let it be), because that leads by analogy to something that refutes this. Do you not see that you say: "ittaqi Allah takun muhsinan" (fear Allah, you will be a good-doer), and it is not permitted to say: "ittaqi Allah muhsinan" (fear Allah, a good-doer), while you imply "kana"? And is it not correct to say: "unsurna akhana" (help us, our brother), while you mean: "takun akhana" (be our brother)? [[From his words "Do you not see that you find the pronoun ..." up to this point, is the text of al-Farra's words in Ma'ani al-Qur'an 1:295, 296. It is evident, then, that this is al-Farra's statement, both what precedes and what follows it. However, I did not find it at this place in Ma'ani al-Qur'an, so perhaps Abu Ja'far compiled it from his book in other places, and I hope to find them and refer to them later.]] The proponent of this view claimed that he does not permit this except specifically with the "af'al" form (comparative/imperative form), so one says: "if'al hadha khayran laka" (do this, it being better for you) and "la taf'al hadha khayran laka" (do not do this, it being better for you), and "afdal laka" (better for you), but one does not say "salahan laka". He claimed that it was said only with "af'al" because "af'al" indicates that this is more fitting than that.

* *

One of the grammarians of Basra said: "khayran" is in the accusative because, when He said to them "aminu" (believe), He commanded them with what is better for them; it is as if He said: "i'malu khayran lakum" (do good, it being better for you). Likewise: ﴿Desist, it is better for you﴾ (Surah an-Nisa: 171). He said: This occurs only in command and prohibition specifically, and does not occur in statement. You do not say: "An anta'i khayran li?" (that I desist is better for me?). Rather it is put in the nominative as two clauses, because command and prohibition have an implied element in them; it is as if you removed him from one thing to another, for when you said to him "intahi" (desist), it is as if you said to him: "Leave this, and enter another." [[In the printed edition and manuscript: "ittaqihi" with a qaf, but the correct reading is "intahi", since the example before it is "an antahi khayran li".]] This statement he mentioned is the statement of Sibawayh in al-Kitab 1:143, and Abu Ja'far expanded upon it and abridged it.

He cited the verse of the poet 'Umar ibn Abi Rabi'ah:

*Fa-wa'idihi sarhatay Malikin / aw al-Ruba baynahuma aslahā*

[[His Diwan: 131; Sibawayh 1:143; al-Khizanah 1:280, and many others. After the verse: "Wa-l-ya'ti in ja'a 'ala baghlatin / inni akhafu al-mahra an yasylaha!" Here "aslaha" means: come by the easier of the two matters for you. This is its explanation according to Sibawayh's view.]]

just as you say: "wa'idihi khayran laka" (promise her, it being better for you). He said: And this accusative has been heard in statement too: the Arabs say: "ati al-bayta khayran li, wa atrukuhu khayran li" (I come to the house, it being better for me, and I leave it, it being better for me), and it is according to what I explained to you in command and prohibition. [[This is the completion of Sibawayh's statement, but I was unable to find its place in al-Kitab.]]

Another of them said: "khayran" is in the accusative by an implied verb, and he sufficed with that implied element by his saying "la taf'al hadha" (do not do this) or "if'al al-khayr" (do the good), and he permitted it in other than "af'al", so he said: "la taf'al dhaka salahan laka" (do not do that, it being good for you).

* *

Another of them said: "khayran" is in the accusative as the response to the implied condition "yakun khayran lakum" (let it be better for you). He said: Likewise every command and prohibition. [[This is the statement of Abu 'Ubaydah in Majaz al-Qur'an 1:143.]]

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 171 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His words: ﴿O People of the Scripture, do not commit excess in your religion, and do not say about Allah except the truth﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "O People of the Scripture," He, may His praise be exalted, means: O People of the Gospel, the Christians. "Do not commit excess in your religion" means: do not go beyond the truth in your religion so that you fall short of it [or: neglect it]. "And do not say about Jesus other than the truth," for your saying about Jesus that he is the son of Allah is a saying about Allah other than the truth, because Allah has not taken a son, so that Jesus or anyone else of His creation could be a son to Him. "And do not say about Allah except the truth."
* *
The root of "ghuluww" (excess) in everything is going beyond its limit, which is its boundary. It is said of it in regard to religion: "He has exceeded (qad ghalā), so he exceeds (yaghlū) with an excess (ghuluwwan)." And "ghalā bi-l-jāriya" means her size and flesh grew, when a girl hastens into youth and surpasses her peers: "he exceeds with her, excess (ghuluwwan) and abundance (ghalā'an)." Among examples of this is the verse of al-Harith ibn Khalid al-Makhzumi:

Slender of waist, with her girdle loose, in the bloom of youth, the bulk of her bones has grown with her [[al-Aghani 9: 226; Majaz al-Qur'an of Abu 'Ubayda 1: 143; Lisan (ghala). In al-Aghani it reads "ʿalā" with the unpointed ʿayn, which is an error that needs correcting.
A verse of this same qasida has already passed at 1: 116, note 3, and I mentioned its story there. It is among verses in which he describes his beloved and what has passed of his days and hers:
When her affection was pure and seeing her was a wish, and her speech was spoils,
Fair-cheeked, her anklets full, large-hipped, with no bulk to her bones,
Slender of waist............................
And as if ghaliya, a perfume, were touching her beneath her garments when the star sets.
It is good poetry and a fine description of a woman. "Laffa" means one whose thighs are close together, with firm flesh; this is good in women and ugly in men. "Mamlu' mukhalkhaluhā" means the place of her anklet is full: her bones were hidden under flesh, which is a fine quality, so her bones did not show, as if they had been struck with nails. "ʿAjzā'" means well-proportioned in the hips. "Khumsāna" (with fatha or damma on the kha') means slim in the belly. "Qalaq mushawwahuhā" means her form is even, so the girdle slides over her because of her slenderness, not filled with flesh that would make her one mass. "Ruwd al-shabāb" means a young woman who sways from delicacy and radiance of complexion. "Al-ghāliya" is a kind of perfume. "Ṣaghā al-najm" means the star inclines toward setting, and this is at the beginning of dawn, when people's breath and bodies change and an unpleasant smell appears. Few people are of this description!!]]
* *
And:
10853 – Al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from al-Rabi', who said: They became two groups: a group that committed excess in the religion, so their excess in it was doubt about it and turning away from it; and a group among them who fell short of it, and so they transgressed against the command of their Lord.
* *
The interpretation of His words: ﴿The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, is only the Messenger of Allah and His word which He directed to Mary and a spirit from Him﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary is only," He means: the Messiah is not, O you who commit excess in your religion among the People of the Scripture, the son of Allah, as you claim, but he is Jesus son of Mary, and has no lineage other than that, beyond other creatures. Then Allah, may His praise be exalted, described him with his description and characterized him with his attribute, saying: He is the Messenger of Allah, whom Allah sent with the truth to those among His creatures to whom He sent him.
* *
The root of "al-Masih" is "al-mamsūḥ" (the one wiped), transferred from the form "maf'ūl" to "fa'īl." Allah named him by this because He purified him from sins. It was said: he was wiped of sins and defilements that occur in human beings, just as a thing is wiped of the harm that is in it, so that it is purified of it. For this reason Mujahid and whoever said the same as him said: "al-Masih" means the truthful (al-siddiq). [[See what has passed at 6: 414, where you will find this statement of Mujahid. I annotated it there and pointed to Abu Ja'far's abridgment, and I favored that there is a deficiency in the text. This place in his speech indicates that Abu Ja'far himself was the one who abridged the discussion there, from forgetfulness in my estimation, or because he composed his tafsir at intervals that were far apart for him. Had it not been so, he would have referred here—as is his habit—to the earlier passage where he explained the meaning of "al-Masih."]]
* *
Some people have claimed that the origin of this word is Hebrew or Syriac "Mashiha," which was Arabized and became "al-Masih," just as all the names of prophets in the Qur'an were Arabized, such as "Isma'il," "Ishaq," "Musa," and "'Isa."
* *
Abu Ja'far said: The example they cite for "al-Masih" is not comparable. For "Isma'il," "Ishaq," and what is similar to them are names, not attributes, whereas "al-Masih" is an attribute. It is not permissible that the Arabs, or other kinds of creation, be addressed about the attribute of a thing except by means of what they understand from the one who addresses them. If "al-Masih" were not from the speech of the Arabs, and the Arabs did not comprehend its meaning, it would not have been addressed to them. We have already given sufficient explanation of similar cases earlier, so there is no need to repeat it here. [[See what has passed at 1: 13–24.]]
* *
As for "al-Masih al-Dajjal," it also means "the one whose eye is wiped," transferred from "maf'ūl" to "fa'īl." So the meaning of "al-Masih" applied to Jesus, peace be upon him, is: the one whose body is wiped of defilements and sins; and the meaning of "al-Masih" applied to the Dajjal is: the one whose right or left eye is wiped, as is narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning that. [[This is what came in the sound hadiths from a group of the Companions describing al-Masih al-Dajjal, may Allah protect us from his trial. Among them is the hadith of Hudhayfah (Muslim 18: 60), who said:
(The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: The Dajjal is blind in the left eye, with bushy hair, with him is a garden and a fire; his fire is a garden and his garden is a fire.)
And the hadith of Ibn 'Umar:
(The Messenger of Allah ﷺ mentioned the Dajjal among the people and said: Indeed Allah is not one-eyed. Beware, al-Masih al-Dajjal is blind in the right eye, as if his eye were a floating grape.)
The hadiths about the Dajjal are numerous, varying in wording, brief and extended. O Allah, I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Hell, from the punishment of the grave, from the trial of life and death, and from the trial of al-Masih al-Dajjal.]]
* *
As for His words "and His word which He directed to Mary," He means by "the word" the message which Allah commanded His angels to bring to Mary as good news from Allah to her, which Allah, may His praise be exalted, mentioned in His words: ﴿When the angels said: O Mary, indeed Allah gives you good news of a word from Him﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 45], meaning: with a message from Him and good news from Him.
* *
Qatadah said about this:
10854 – Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Qatadah: "and His word which He directed to Mary," he said: it is His saying "Be," and it was.
* *
We have already explained the disagreement of those who differed among the people of Islam on this matter earlier, sufficiently so that there is no need to repeat it here. [[See the explanation of "al-kalima" at 6: 411, 412.]]
* *
His words "directed to Mary" mean: He informed her of it and told her, as one says: "I threw a good word to you" (alqaytu ilayka kalima hasana), meaning: I informed you of it and spoke it to you. [[This meaning is recorded in the lexicons, though you rarely find it there, and it is very clear.]]
* *
As for His words "and a spirit from Him," the people of knowledge differed in its interpretation.

Some of them said: the meaning of His words "and a spirit from Him" is also a breath from Him, because it refers to the breathing of Gabriel, peace be upon him, into the shift of Mary by Allah's command to him to do so, [["Shift of the woman" (dir'u al-mar'a): her shirt which protects her from the eyes of the wicked, as a coat of mail protects its wearer. It is far-fetched that anything of women's clothing today be called "dir'," for it protects from nothing, and a man does not refrain from anything!! And Allah is the one sought for help.]] so it was attributed to Him as "a spirit from Allah," because it came by His command. He said: The breath is called "spirit" only because it is a wind that comes out of the spirit (al-rūḥ). They cited as evidence for this from the saying of Dhu al-Rummah in describing a fire he described:

When it appeared I shrouded it, while it was a little child, in a dirty cloth that did not reach a cubit nor a span [[His Diwan: 176; Lisan (rawh); al-Muzhir 1: 556; and others. Note: the manuscript contains only the first three verses; the printed edition added a fourth verse, but there is a verse before it in Dhu al-Rummah's poetry, which I added from his Diwan and placed between parentheses, because it completes the meaning of the verses.
Before these verses are verses describing the extraction of a spark of fire from the tinder by striking, and when he struck it he shrouded it as is mentioned in the rest of the poetry. His words "when it appeared" mean: when the spark of fire appeared from the upper tinder upon striking; "I shrouded it" means he wrapped it in a dirty rag which did not reach a cubit or a span, which he called "ṭalsā'" because of its blackness from its dirt. It was "a little child" because it had fallen from its mother at that moment, so he received it in the rag he made as its shroud. He made it a shroud for it because the spark falls from the tinder shining and living, but when it falls into the cotton wick, one does not see its light, as if the spark had died. Yet he returns, following the spark until he revives it again, and he said to his companion: "lift it up to you," meaning take it in your hand and raise it to your mouth; then "revive it with your breath," meaning blow on it a gentle breath; "and feed it a measured feeding," commanding him to be gentle and to blow lightly little by little, as if he made the breath its food for this child, measured out for it, bit by bit, until it is complete.
Then when he finished that and the fire grew somewhat, he said to him: "Spread for it some of the dry crushed wood," meaning place finely broken dry firewood piled upon one another, and feed this child; "al-shakht" is the fine powder of anything, so that the fire may spread more quickly in it. Then he says to him: face it toward the east wind so that this may be growth for it; "and make your hands a screen for it," meaning to shield it from the other directions so that the east wind strikes it and it does not die again.
Then he returns to describe its growth, saying: "and when it grew up and rose," "it eats the dry branches," it eats what has dried of tree stems, leaving neither dry nor green of what they had been gathering for it, and that was when it became strong and reached its maturity. When they saw the fire then running through the "jazl" — which is the thick, dried firewood — as if its light were the flash of lightning, they raised their hands in gratitude to the One who created them and created the fire.
This is good poetry, sound and on the right path.
And of what clarifies this here: al-Suyuti related in al-Muzhir from Abu 'Ubayd in al-Gharib al-Musannaf that al-Asma'i said: 'Isa ibn 'Umar informed me, he said: Dhu al-Rummah recited to me: "wazahhir lahā min yābis al-shakht" (and fuel it with dry fine wood). Then he recited after this: "min bā'is al-shakht" (from wretched fine wood). Abu 'Ubayd said: I said to him: You recited to me "min yābis al-shakht"? He said: "al-yabs" is from "al-bu's" (misery). Al-Suyuti said: That is a connected, sound chain, for Abu 'Ubayd heard it from al-Asma'i.
In the printed edition there was "jarat lil-jazl" and "li-khāliqihā," and I have adopted the wording of the Diwan.]]
I said to him: lift it up to you, and revive it
with your spirit, and feed it a measured feeding.
Kindle for it from dry fine wood, and seek help
against it from the east wind, and make your hands a screen for it.
[And when it grew and began to eat the thin dry branches, it left nothing of what they gathered, neither dry nor green.]
Then when it ran through the jazl like a running
flash of lightning, we gave thanks to its Creator.

And they said: by His words "revive it with your spirit," He means: revive it with your breath.
* *
Some others said, by His words "and a spirit from Him," that he was a human being by Allah's reviving him with His word "Be." They said: the meaning of "and a spirit from Him" is life from Him, meaning Allah's giving him life through His creating.
* *
Others said: [[In the printed edition: "Some of them said," and I have restored what is in the manuscript.]] the meaning of "and a spirit from Him" is mercy from Him, just as He, may His praise be exalted, said in another place: ﴿And He strengthened them with a spirit from Him﴾ [Surah al-Mujadila: 22]. They said: its meaning in this place is: mercy from Him. [[In the printed edition: "He said," in the singular; I have restored what is in the manuscript.]] They said: So Allah made Jesus a mercy from Him to those who followed him, believed in him and affirmed him, because he guided them to the path of rectitude.
* *
Others said: the meaning is: and a spirit from Allah, which He created and fashioned, then sent to Mary, and it entered into her mouth, and Allah, exalted is He, made it the spirit of Jesus, peace be upon him.
* *
Mention of those who said that:
10855 – Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Sa'd narrated to us, saying: Abu Ja'far informed me, from al-Rabi', from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, concerning His words: ﴿And when your Lord took from the children of Adam, from their loins, their descendants﴾ [Surah al-A'raf: 172], he said: He took them and made them spirits, then He fashioned them, then He questioned them, and the spirit of Jesus was among those spirits over which the covenant and the pledge were taken; then He sent that spirit to Mary, and it entered into her mouth, so she conceived the one who addressed her, and he is the spirit of Jesus, peace be upon him. [[In the printed edition: "So she conceived, and the one who addressed her is the spirit of Jesus ..." with the waw dropped at the end of the sentence; I have restored it at its beginning, returning it to its original form in the manuscript, which is correct. It refers to His words in Surah Maryam 24: "Then he called to her from beneath her: Do not grieve, your Lord has placed beneath you a stream."
This report does not occur in the explanation of the verse of al-A'raf in its proper place there, and it is one of the evidences of Abu Ja'far's abridgment of his tafsir and one of the aspects of his method of abridgment.]]
* *
Others said: the meaning of "the spirit" here is Gabriel, peace be upon him. They said: the meaning of the speech is: "His word which He directed to Mary, and He also directed to her a spirit from Allah." They said: so "the spirit" is conjoined to the mention of Allah in His words "directed," meaning: the throwing of the word to Mary was from Allah, and then from Gabriel, peace be upon him.
* *
Abu Ja'far said: For all these sayings there is an aspect and a view not far from the truth.
* *
The interpretation of His words: ﴿So believe in Allah and His messengers, and do not say "Three." Desist; it is better for you﴾

Abu Ja'far said: By His words, may His praise be exalted, "So believe in Allah and His messengers," He means: affirm, O People of the Scripture, the oneness and lordship of Allah, and that He has no son; affirm His messengers in what they brought you from Allah, and in what they told you, that Allah is one, without partner, without consort, without son. "And do not say 'Three'," meaning: do not say: the lords are three.
* *
"Three" is in the nominative by an omitted word indicated by the context, which is "they." The meaning of the speech: do not say: they are three. This is permissible because "saying" is a quotation, and the Arabs do this in quotation; from it is Allah's word: ﴿They will say: they are three, their fourth is their dog﴾ [Surah al-Kahf: 22]. Likewise, every nominative that occurs after "saying" with no raising element before it has an implied raising element for that noun.
* *
Then He, may His praise be exalted, said to them, threatening them for their monstrous saying that they said about Allah: "Desist," O you who say: Allah is the third of three, from what you say of falsehood and polytheism with Allah, for desisting from that is better for you than your saying it, because of the swift punishment you have from Allah for your saying that if you persist in it and do not turn back to the truth which I have commanded you to turn to, and the deferred punishment in your return. [[His words "and the deferred punishment in your return" are conjoined to his words "from the swift punishment you have ..."]]
* *
The interpretation of His words: ﴿Allah is only one God. Glory be to Him that He should have a son. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾ (171)

Abu Ja'far said: By His words "Allah is only one God," He means: Allah is not, O you who say: Allah is the third of three, as you say, because whoever has a son is not a god. Likewise whoever has a consort, it is not permissible that he be a god worshipped. But Allah, to whom belong divinity and worship, is one God, worshipped, having no son, no father, no consort, no partner.
Then He, may His praise be exalted, declared Himself far above and exalted Himself and raised Himself above what His enemies, the disbelievers in Him, said about Him, saying: "Glory be to Him that He should have a son," meaning: Allah is exalted, majestic, mighty, and far above having a son or a consort. [[See the explanation of "subhan" at 1: 474–476, 495 / 2: 537.]]

Then Allah, His praise be exalted, informed His servants that ʿIsa and his mother, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, are His servants, His bondsmen and His creation, and that He is their Provider and their Creator, and that they are in need of Him and dependent upon Him. This was an argument from Him against those who claimed that the Messiah is His son: that if he were His son as they say, he would not be in need of Him, nor would he be a servant owned by Him. So He said: ﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾, meaning: to Allah belongs everything in the heavens and everything on the earth, in ownership and in creation, and He provides for them, sustains them and manages their affairs. How then could the Messiah be a son of Allah, when he is either on the earth or in the heavens, and is not beyond being in one of these places?

And His saying: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Disposer of affairs﴾ means: sufficient for what is in the heavens and what is on the earth, with Allah as their Guardian, their Manager and their Provider, so that there is no need for anything besides Him. [[See the explanation of "al-Wakil" above: p. 297, note 2, and the references there.]]

The commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 172:

The exposition of His saying: ﴿The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels brought near﴾

By His saying, may His praise be exalted, "The Messiah will never disdain," it means: the Messiah will not be too proud or too arrogant "to be a servant of Allah," meaning: to be a servant of Allah, as in:

10856 - Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah: ﴿The Messiah will never disdain to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels brought near﴾, meaning: the Messiah will not be ashamed to be a servant of Allah, nor will the angels.

* *

As for His saying, "nor will the angels brought near," it means: and they will also not disdain to acknowledge, before Allah, their servanthood and to submit to Him in that, His messengers, "the brought near," those whom Allah has brought near and whose ranks He has elevated above others of His creation.

* *

It is related from al-Dahhak that he used to say regarding this:

10857 - Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Buzuri narrated to me, saying: Ya'la ibn Ubayd narrated to us, from al-Ajlah, who said: I said to al-Dahhak: "What are 'the brought near'?" He said: "The nearest of them to the second heaven."

[Editor's note on the report 10857: I have not found "Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Buzuri" with this nisba. What I found in Tahdhib al-Tahdhib, among those who narrate from Ya'la ibn Ubayd, is "Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Wasiti al-Warraq," resident of Baghdad, who died in the year 265, and he is the one most fitting for Abu Ja'far to narrate from. Then review Tarikh Baghdad, where there are many named "Ja'far ibn Muhammad," but I did not find "al-Buzuri" among them. Perhaps the following chains will reveal who Abu Ja'far means.

"Al-Ajlah" is "al-Ajlah ibn Abd Allah ibn Hujayyah al-Kindi," Abu Hujayyah, whose name is said to be "Yahya," and "al-Ajlah" is a laqab (epithet). He heard from Abd Allah ibn al-Hudhayl, Ibn Buraydah, al-Sha'bi, and Ikrimah. Al-Thawri and Ibn al-Mubarak narrated from him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib and al-Kabir 1/2/68.]

* *

The exposition of His saying: ﴿And whoever disdains His worship and is arrogant, He will gather them to Himself all together﴾ (172)

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: whoever magnifies himself above the worship of his Lord, and disdains humility and submission to Him in obedience, from all of creation, and is arrogant toward that, "He will gather them to Himself all together," meaning: He will resurrect them all on the Day of Resurrection and assemble them for their appointed meeting with Him. [See the explanation of "al-hashr" (gathering) earlier, 4:228 / 6:229.]

The interpretation of His words: ﴿Then as for those who believed and did righteous deeds, He will pay them their rewards in full and give them more from His bounty. But as for those who disdained and were arrogant, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will not find for themselves, besides Allah, any ally or helper.﴾

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: As for the believers who affirm the oneness of Allah, who submit to Him in obedience, who humble themselves to Him in servitude, and who do righteous deeds, that is, who come before their Lord having believed in Him and in His messengers, and having acted upon what His messengers brought them from their Lord, by doing what He commanded them and avoiding what He forbade them, ﴿He will pay them their rewards﴾, meaning: He will give them the full and complete recompense for their righteous deeds [[See the explanation of "He will pay them their rewards" in what has preceded, 6:465 / 7:364.]] ﴿and give them more from His bounty﴾, meaning, may His praise be exalted: He will give them, beyond what He promised them as recompense and reward for their righteous deeds, additional bounty and increase whose extent He has not made them know and whose limit He has not defined. This is because Allah promised His believing servants who come with one good deed ten times its like in reward and recompense. This is the wage of every worker for his righteous deed among the people of faith, whose extent is limited, and the increase beyond that is a favor from Allah upon them, though all of it is from His bounty to His servants. Only, what He promised His believing servants, that He would pay them in full without diminishing from the reward of their righteous deeds, is what is fixed in extent as ten-fold; the increase beyond that has no fixed limit, so He increases for whomever He wills of His creatures beyond that by whatever amount He wills, with no bound to its measure that can be stopped at.

* *

Some of them said: the increase is up to seven hundred-fold.

Others said: up to two thousand-fold.

I have already mentioned the disagreement of those who differ on this matter earlier, in a way that makes repeating it in this place unnecessary. [[See what has preceded, 5:512-516.]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿And as for those who disdained and were arrogant﴾, He means: As for those who exalted themselves against acknowledging Allah's lordship in servitude, and submitting to Him in obedience, and were arrogant against humbling themselves to His divinity and worship, and against surrendering lordship and oneness to Him, ﴿He will punish them with a painful punishment﴾, meaning: a punishment that causes pain. ﴿And they will not find for themselves, besides Allah, any ally or helper﴾, meaning: those who disdain His worship and are arrogant toward it will not find, when Allah punishes them with His painful punishment, anyone besides Allah for themselves as an ally who will save them from His punishment and rescue them from it. ﴿Nor any helper﴾, meaning: nor a helper who will aid them, rescuing them from their Lord, and repelling by his strength the vengeance of Allah that has befallen them, as those who used to do for them when others of the people of the world wished them ill in this world, by helping them and defending them. [[See the explanation of "ally" (wali) and "helper" (nasir) in what has preceded in the language indexes.]]

The Interpretation of His saying: ﴿O mankind, there has certainly come to you a proof from your Lord, and We have sent down to you a manifest light﴾ [4:174]

Abu Ja'far said: By His saying, "O mankind, there has certainly come to you a proof from your Lord," may He be glorified and exalted, He means: O mankind, of all categories of religions, its Jews, its Christians and its polytheists, whose accounts God, may He be glorified and exalted, relates in this sura: "there has certainly come to you a proof from your Lord"; that is, there has come to you a argument from God that makes clear to you the falsehood of what you are persisting in of your religions and creeds, [[See the explanation of "proof" (burhan) above, 2:509.]] and it is Muhammad ﷺ, whom God has made a proof against you, by which He has cut off your excuse, and He has fully conveyed to you the evidence through sending him to you, along with his making you aware of the truth of his prophethood and the verification of his mission. "And We have sent down to you a manifest light": that is, We have sent down to you along with him "a manifest light," meaning: it makes clear to you the clear path and the guiding ways to what holds for you salvation from the punishment of God and His painful retribution, if you follow them and are illuminated by its radiance. [[See the explanation of "manifest" (mubin) above, p. 360, note 5, and the references there.]]

And that "manifest light" is the Qur'an which God sent down upon Muhammad ﷺ.

* *

Those of the people of interpretation said the same as what we have said on this matter.

Mention of those who said that:

10858. Muhammad ibn Amr related to us, he said: Abu Asim related to us, he said: Isa related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning God's saying: "a proof from your Lord," he said: a proof.

10859. al-Muthanna related to me, he said: Abu Hudhayfa related to us, he said: Shibl related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

10860. Bishr ibn Mu'adh related to us, he said: Yazid related to us, he said: Sa'id related to us, from Qatada, concerning His saying: "O mankind, there has certainly come to you a proof from your Lord," that is, a clear evidence from your Lord; "And We have sent down to you a manifest light," and it is this Qur'an.

10861. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn related to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Mufaddal related to us, he said: Asbat related to us, from al-Suddi: "there has certainly come to you a proof from your Lord," he says: a proof.

10862. al-Qasim related to us, he said: al-Husayn related to us, he said: Hajjaj related to me, from Ibn Juraij: "a proof," he said: evidence. "And We have sent down to you a manifest light," he said: the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 175:

The explanation of His saying: ﴿As for those who believed in Allah and held fast to Him, He will admit them to mercy from Him and bounty, and guide them to Himself on a straight path﴾.

Abu Ja'far said: By this, may His praise be exalted, He means: As for those who affirmed Allah and acknowledged His oneness, and [affirmed] what Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent with from among the people of the faiths, "and held fast to Him," meaning: and held firmly to the clear light that He sent down to His Prophet. [See the explanation of "i'tisam" (holding fast) in what has preceded: 7:62, 70 / 9:341.] As related:

10863. Al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj: "and held fast to Him," he said: "to the Qur'an."

* *

"He will admit them to mercy from Him and bounty," meaning: His mercy will reach them, which will save them from His punishment and make His reward, His mercy and His Garden obligatory for them, [His saying "and His Garden" is not in the manuscript.] and there will reach them from His bounty what reached the people of faith in Him and in the affirmation of His messengers. [In the printed edition: "what reached the people of faith," and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.] "And guide them to Himself on a straight path," meaning: He will grant them success in attaining His bounty, which He has bestowed upon His friends, and will make them firm in following the way of those upon whom He has bestowed favour from among the people of His obedience, and in following their footsteps and their religion. That is the "straight path," and it is the religion of Allah that He has approved for His servants, and it is Islam. [See the explanation of "the straight path" in what has preceded: 1:170–177 / 3:140, 141 / 6:441 / 8:529.]

* *

The "straight path" is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (qat') from the pronoun "hu" (him) in His saying "ilayhi" (to Himself). [The "qat'" is the circumstantial accusative (hal), or a section of it; see the index of technical terms above.]

**The interpretation of His words: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: "Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalala (one who dies without a father or child). If a man dies leaving no child but has a sister, she receives half of what he leaves."﴾**

By His words "They ask you for a ruling" (yastaftunaka), He means: they ask you, O Muhammad, to give them a ruling concerning the kalala.[[See the explanation of "yastafti" in what preceded, p. 253.]]

* *

We have already explained the meaning of "kalala" earlier, with the evidence that supports it, and we mentioned the differences of opinion about it, so there is no need to repeat it. We stated that, in our view, "kalala" refers to anyone other than a child or a parent.[[See what preceded regarding "kalala," 8:53–61.]]

* *

As for His words "If a man dies leaving no child but has a sister, she receives half of what he leaves," by "If a man dies" He means that a person among people has died,[[See the explanation of "al-mar'" (a man) in what preceded, 2:446.]] as related:

10864. Muhammad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn al-Mufaddal narrated to us, saying: Asbat narrated to us, from al-Suddi, regarding "If a man dies," that he said: "He died."

* *

"Leaving no child," whether male or female. "But has a sister": that is, the deceased has a sister through the same father and mother, or through the same father. "Then she receives half of what he leaves": that is, his sister who survives him, in the manner we have described, receives half of his estate as an inheritance from him, to the exclusion of the rest of his male agnatic relatives. What remains goes to his agnates.

* *

It is mentioned that the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) were troubled by the matter of the kalala, so Allah, blessed and exalted, revealed this verse concerning it.

Those who related this:

10865. Bishr ibn Mu'adh narrated to us, saying: Yazid narrated to us, saying: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, regarding "They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalala": they asked the Prophet of Allah about it, so Allah revealed in that regard the Qur'an: "If a man dies leaving no child," and he recited until he reached "And Allah is Knowing of all things." He said: It has been mentioned to us that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) said in his sermon: "Verily, the verse that Allah revealed at the beginning of Surat al-Nisa' concerning the obligatory shares was revealed concerning the child and the parent. The second verse He revealed concerning the spouse and the wife and the brothers through the mother. The verse with which Surat al-Nisa' ends He revealed concerning the brothers and sisters through the father and mother. The verse with which Surat al-Anfal ends He revealed concerning those of kinship (ulu al-arham), some of whom have more right than others in the Book of Allah than the agnates whom the womb has drawn [in inheritance]." [[The report 10865: Al-Bayhaqi related this report in al-Sunan 6:31, and Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his Tafsir 2:42, and al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:251.]]

10866. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Jarir narrated to us, from al-Shaybani, from Amr ibn Murrah, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the kalala, and he said: "Has Allah not already made that clear?" He said: Then "They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalala" was revealed. [[The report 10866: Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir 2:42, and he did not attribute it to anyone other than Ibn Jarir.]]

10867. Mu'ammal ibn Hisham Abu Hisham narrated to us, saying: Isma'il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from Hisham al-Dastawa'i, who said: Abu al-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: "I fell ill, and I had nine sisters" or "seven"—I am uncertain [[In the printed edition: "Abu Ja'far who is uncertain," and I have kept what is in the manuscript.]]—"so the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon me and blew upon my face, and I regained consciousness and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, should I not bequeath two-thirds to my sisters?'" [[In the printed edition: "one-third," and I have kept what is in the manuscript, which agrees with the narration of al-Bayhaqi. As for the narration of Abu Dawud in his Sunan, it is what is found in the printed edition.]] He said: "Excellent!" I said: "Half?" He said: "Excellent!" Then he left and left me, then he returned to me and said: "O Jabir, I do not think you will die from this illness of yours, and Allah has revealed concerning what is due to your sisters that He has given them two-thirds." Jabir used to say: "This verse was revealed concerning me: 'They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalala.'" [[The report 10867: "Mu'ammal ibn Hisham al-Yashkuri" is Abu Hisham. He narrated from Isma'il ibn Ulayyah, who was his son-in-law. Al-Bukhari, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa'i and others narrated from him. He is biographed in al-Tahdhib.
"Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Miqsam al-Asadi" is Ibn Ulayyah, mentioned many times before. "Abu al-Zubayr" al-Makki is Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Tadrus al-Asadi, mentioned under numbers 2029, 3581, 8205.
This report was related by Abu Dawud in his Sunan 3:164 through the chain of Kathir ibn Hisham, from Hisham al-Dastawa'i, in the same wording.
Al-Bayhaqi related it in his Sunan 6:231 through several chains, in longer and shorter forms.
Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi related it in his Musnad, p. 240, in shorter form, and in it is "two-thirds," as in the manuscript of al-Tabari.
Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:250, and added its attribution to Ibn Sa'd and al-Nasa'i.]]

10868. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Hisham—that is, al-Dastawa'i—from Abu al-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Prophet (ﷺ), the like of it. [[The report 10868: It is a repetition of the preceding report, through the chain of Ibn Abi Adi, from Hisham.
This report was related by al-Wahidi in Asbab al-Nuzul, p. 139, who gave its wording with slight differences from the preceding report.]]

10869. Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, who said: "I fell ill, and the Prophet (ﷺ) came to visit me, he and Abu Bakr, both walking, and they found me unconscious" [[His words "they found me" (fawajadūnī) are thus in the printed edition and the manuscript, while in other wordings it is "found me" (fawajadanī). What is in the manuscript and the printed edition is correct, because it refers to Abu Bakr and the Messenger of Allah and whoever was with them, or whoever was in the house. Had he taken it as the plural while it is the dual, there would be a basis for it in Arabic.]] "so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) performed ablution, then poured some of his ablution water on me, and I regained consciousness and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how should I dispose of my property?' or 'How should I act regarding my property?' He had nine sisters, and he had no father or child." 
He said: "He did not answer me anything until the verse of inheritance was revealed: 'They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalala,' to the end of the surah." Ibn al-Munkadir said: Jabir said: "This verse was only revealed concerning me." [[The report 10869: The report of "Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir ibn Abdullah" is transmitted through many chains. It passed through the chain of Shu'bah from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, abridged, under number 8730, and then through the chain of Ibn Jurayj from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, under number 8731, with other wording, abridged. See their takhrij there. As for this one, al-Bukhari related it (Fath 12:2) with the same content, with slight difference in wording, and al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar in his commentary explained the differences in it.
Muslim related it through many chains, including the chain of Sufyan, in his Sahih 11:54–56.
Abu Dawud related it in his Sunan 3:164 through the chain of Ahmad ibn Hanbal, from Sufyan.
al-Tirmidhi related it in his Sunan (in the book of tafsir), and said: "This is a hasan sahih hadith, related by more than one, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir." Then he cited it through the chain of "al-Fadl ibn Sabah al-Baghdadi, from Sufyan ibn Uyaynah, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir," then he said: "In the hadith of al-Fadl ibn Sabah there is more discussion than this." The hadith of al-Fadl ibn Sabah, al-Tirmidhi related before that in the book of inheritance (al-faraid) in full, and said: "This is a sahih hadith."
al-Bayhaqi related it in his Sunan 6:223, 224, then al-Bayhaqi said: "Jabir ibn Abdullah, concerning whom the verse of the kalala was revealed, had neither child nor parent, because his father was killed on the day of Uhud. And this verse was revealed after him."
Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir 2:41, and al-Suyuti in al-Durr 2:249, adding its attribution to Ibn Sa'd, and Ibn Majah, and Ibn al-Mundhir.]]

* *

Some of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: This verse is the last verse revealed of the Qur'an.

Those who related this:

10870. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara' ibn Azib, who said: "I heard him say: 'Verily, the last verse revealed of the Qur'an was: "They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalala."'" [[The report 10870: It will come under numbers 10871 and 10873, through the chain of Abu Ishaq from al-Bara'.]]

10871. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Khalid, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: "The last verse revealed of the Qur'an was: 'They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalala.'" [[The report 10871: Muslim related it in his Sahih 11:58, from Ali ibn Khashram, from Waki', in the same wording. Then he cited it through other chains from Abu Ishaq from al-Bara'.
And al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan 6:224.]]

10872. Muhammad ibn Khalaf narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Samad ibn al-Nu'man narrated to us, saying: Malik ibn Mighwal narrated to us, from Abu al-Safar, from al-Bara', who said: "The last verse revealed of the Qur'an was: 'They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalala.'" [[The report 10872: Muhammad ibn Khalaf ibn Ammar al-Asqalani, the teacher of al-Tabari, passed under numbers 126 and 6534.
Abd al-Samad ibn al-Nu'man al-Bazzaz. Ibn Abi Hatim biographed him, 3/1/51, 52, and said: "My father was asked about him and said: he is salih al-hadith, truthful."
Malik ibn Mighwal is trustworthy, passed under number 5431.
Abu al-Safar is Sa'id ibn Yahmad al-Thawri, or Sa'id ibn Ahmad, passed under number 3010. The report was related by Muslim 11:59 through the chain of Amr al-Naqid, from Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri, from Malik ibn Mighwal.
al-Tirmidhi related it in the book of tafsir, through the chain of Abd ibn Humayd, from Abu Nu'aym, from Malik ibn Mighwal, and said: "This is a hasan hadith."]]

10873. Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamdani narrated to us, saying: Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam narrated to us, saying: Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Bara', who said: "The last surah revealed in its entirety was Bara'ah, and the last verse revealed, the conclusion of Surat al-Nisa', was: 'They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalala.'" [[The report 10873: It is a repetition of the two preceding reports, 10870 and 10871.
"Harun ibn Ishaq al-Hamdani" is a teacher of al-Tabari, passed under number 3001.
"Mus'ab ibn al-Miqdam al-Khath'ami," passed under numbers 1291, 3001.
This report, through the chain of Isra'il from Abu Ishaq, was related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih (Fath 12:22). In the manuscript here it reads "the end of Surat al-Baqarah," and the correct reading is what is in the printed edition.]]

* *

Scholars differed about the place where the verse was revealed.

Jabir ibn Abdullah said: It was revealed in Medina. The report has been transmitted from him to that effect earlier, some of it at the beginning of the surah at the opening of the verse of inheritance, and some of it at the start of the reports about the occasion of revelation of this verse. [[That is, what preceded under numbers 8730, 8731, and then what preceded shortly, 10867–10869.]]

* *

Others said: Rather, it was revealed during a journey in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and his Companions were traveling.

Those who related this:

10874. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayd narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, who said: "'They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalala' was revealed while the Prophet was on a journey, and beside him was Hudhayfah ibn al-Yaman. The Prophet (ﷺ) conveyed it to Hudhayfah, and Hudhayfah conveyed it to Umar ibn al-Khattab, who was traveling behind him. When Umar was appointed caliph, he asked Hudhayfah about it, hoping that he would have its explanation. Hudhayfah said to him: 'By Allah, you are incapable if you think that your authority obliges me to tell you what I did not tell you that day!' Umar said: 'I did not intend this, may Allah have mercy on you!'"

10875. Al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, similar to it—except that in his narration [Hudhayfah] said: "By Allah, you are a fool if you think..."

10876. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Ibn Awn narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, who said: "They were on a journey, and the head of Hudhayfah's mount was beside the rear of the Messenger of Allah's mount, and the head of Umar's mount was beside the rear of Hudhayfah's mount." He said: "The verse 'They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalala' was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah conveyed it to Hudhayfah, and Hudhayfah conveyed it to Umar. When some time had passed, Umar asked Hudhayfah about it, and he said: 'By Allah, you are a fool if you think the Messenger of Allah conveyed it to me and I conveyed it to you as he conveyed it to me! By Allah, I will never add anything to it ever!'" He said: Umar used to say: "O Allah, whomever You made it clear to, [[In the printed edition and in Ibn Kathir it is "if You," and I have kept what is in the manuscript and in al-Durr al-Manthur, which is pure correctness; see it likewise in the following report, number 10892.]] for it has not been made clear to me." [[The reports 10874–10876: Ibn Kathir mentioned the last of them in his tafsir 3:44, then said: "Thus Ibn Jarir related it, and he also related it from al-Hasan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Razzaq, from Ma'mar, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, likewise, similar. And it is disconnected (munqati') between Ibn Sirin and Hudhayfah. The Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Amr al-Bazzar said in his Musnad: 'Yusuf ibn Hammad al-Ma'nī and Muhammad ibn Marzuq narrated to us, both saying: Abd al-A'la ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Hisham ibn Hassan narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Abu Ubaydah ibn Hudhayfah, from his father, who said: The verse of the kalala was revealed...'" and he mentioned the report, then said: "Al-Bazzar said: We do not know anyone who related this hadith except Hudhayfah, and we do not know a chain for it from Hudhayfah except this one, and no one related it from Hisham except Abd al-A'la." Ibn Kathir said: "Likewise Ibn Mardawayh related it."
Al-Haythami takhrraj it in Majma' al-Zawa'id 7:13, and said: "al-Bazzar related it, and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih, except Abu Ubaydah ibn Hudhayfah, whom Ibn Hibban declared trustworthy."
Al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:250, saying: "al-Adani and al-Bazzar related it in their Musnads, and Abu al-Shaykh in al-Fara'id, with a sahih chain from Hudhayfah," then he mentioned the report. He returned to it in 2:251 and attributed it to Ibn Jarir, Abd al-Razzaq, and Ibn al-Mundhir, from Ibn Sirin, disconnected.]]

* *

Narrations from Umar concerning the kalala differ. It is related from him that he said about it at the time of his death: "It is one who has neither child nor parent." We mentioned the report from him to that effect earlier, at the beginning of this surah, in the verse of inheritance. [[See numbers 8745–8748, 8767.]]

* *

It is also related from him that he said before his death: "It is what is left after the father." [[See numbers 8745–8748, 8767.]]

Those who related this:

10877. Al-Hasan ibn Arafah narrated to us, saying: Shababah narrated to us, saying: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah al-Ya'muri, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) never made me more stern—or: I never disputed with the Messenger of Allah about anything as I disputed about the verse of the kalala—until he struck my chest and said: 'The verse of summer, which was revealed at the end of Surat al-Nisa', is enough for you: "They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning the kalala," and I will decide regarding it with a judgment that whoever reads and whoever does not read will know: it is what is left after the father.'" [[Ibn Arafah said: I think so. Shababah said: The uncertainty is from Shu'bah.]] [[His words "which was revealed at the end of Surat al-Nisa'" are not established in the manuscript, but they are established in the reports of the hadith that will come in the takhrij.]] [[The report 10877: The report of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan, from Umar, Abu Ja'far will narrate it from four other chains, in what will come, from numbers 10884–10887.
Muslim related this report from the chain of Shababah ibn Sawwar, from Shu'bah, from Qatadah, in his Sahih 11:57, by allusion.
al-Bayhaqi related it in his Sunan 6:224 in the same wording, and said: "Muslim related it from Zuhayr ibn Harb." Al-Suyuti takhrraj it in al-Durr al-Manthur 2:251, and did not attribute it to anyone other than Ibn Jarir, thereby falling short in its attribution. See the takhrij of the following reports that I pointed to.]]

* *

It is also related from him that he said: "Indeed I am too shy to oppose Abu Bakr in it," and Abu Bakr used to say: "It is what is left after the child and the parent." We mentioned the report to that effect from him earlier at the beginning of the surah. [[See what preceded, numbers 8745–8749.]]

* *

It is also related from him that he said at his death: "I had written a letter concerning the kalala, and I was seeking Allah's guidance regarding it, and I have decided to leave you upon what you were upon," and that he used to wish during his lifetime that he had knowledge of it.

Those who related this:

**Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 4, verse 176 (part 2 of 3):**

10878. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayd al-Ma'mari narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab: that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab wrote a document concerning the *jadd* (grandfather) and the *kalala* (the heirless person whose heirs are collateral relatives). He remained seeking guidance from God (*istikhara*) regarding it, saying: "O God, if You know good in it, then carry it out." Then, when he was stabbed, he called for the document and it was erased[[In the printed edition: "bi-l-kitab fa-muhiya" (with the definite article); this is also how it appears in al-Durr al-Manthur. I have adopted what is in the manuscript, which agrees with the narration of Ibn Kathir in his tafsir.]] so that no one knew what had been written in it. He said: "I had written a document concerning the *jadd* and the *kalala*, and I was seeking God's guidance regarding it, and I decided to leave you as you were upon it."[[Narration 10878: Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir (3:45) citing this passage of the tafsir. al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (2:250), attributing it to 'Abd al-Razzaq and not attributing it to Ibn Jarir. al-Tabari narrated it in a similar form in the following narration: 10879.]]

10879. al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, saying: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from 'Umar, in a similar form.[[Narration 10879: see the note on 10878.]]

10880. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, who said: 'Amr ibn Murrah narrated to us, from Murrah al-Hamdani, who said: 'Umar said: "Three matters, if the Prophet (ﷺ) had explained them to us, would be dearer to me than the world and whatever is in it: the *kalala*, the caliphate, and the *abwab al-riba* (the aspects/forms of usury)."[[Narration 10880: Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi narrated it through Shu'bah, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, with slight variation in wording, in a longer form. al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan through Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi (6:225). al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (2:304) through Sufyan, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, with the wording of al-Tabari, and said: "This is a sound hadith according to the conditions of the two Shaykhs (al-Bukhari and Muslim), though they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir (3:45), attributing it only to al-Hakim. al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr (2:251-252) and additionally attributed it to 'Abd al-Razzaq, al-'Adani, Ibn Majah and al-Saji. As for his saying "abwab al-riba", meaning the aspects and ways of usury: this wording is not in any of the sources I consulted; in all of them it is "wa-l-riba" (and usury). See the following narration 10883 and the comment on it.]]

10881. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthām narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, saying: "I heard them mentioning, and I do not think Ibrahim (al-Nakha'i) was not among them, from 'Umar, who said: 'That I should know the *kalala* is dearer to me than that I should have the like of the tribute of the palaces of the Romans.'"[[Narration 10881: al-Suyuti cited it in al-Durr al-Manthur (2:251), attributing it only to Ibn Jarir, and his text has "qusur al-Sham" (the palaces of Syria) instead of "qusur al-Rum" (the palaces of the Romans). The two are the same in meaning, but it is strange that he transmitted it from this place of the tafsir and wrote "al-Sham" in place of "al-Rum".]]

10882. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: 'Uthām narrated to us, saying: al-A'mash narrated to us, from Qays ibn Muslim, from Tariq ibn Shihab, who said: 'Umar took a shoulder blade (for divination) and gathered the companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), then said: "I will certainly issue a judgment concerning the *kalala*, a judgment that the women will speak of in their chambers!" Then a snake came out of the house, and they dispersed. He said: "If God had willed to complete this matter, He would have completed it."[[Narration 10882: al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan (6:245) through Jarir from al-A'mash, with some difference in wording. Ibn Kathir mentioned it in his tafsir (3:44-45), then said: "This chain is sound." al-Suyuti cited it (2:250) and attributed it only to Ibn Jarir. In the manuscript: "al-nisa' fi khudurha" (the women in her chambers), and the two are the same.]]

10883. Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, saying: Abu Hayyan narrated to us, saying: al-Sha'bi narrated to me, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "I heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab delivering a sermon on the pulpit of Madinah, and he said: 'O people, I wished that the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had not parted from us until he had given us a clear commitment regarding three matters: the *jadd*, the *kalala*, and the *abwab al-riba*.'"[[Narration 10883: "Abu Hayyan" is Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Taymi, who has passed with the numbers 5382, 5383, 6318, 8155. This report was narrated by al-Bukhari in full (Fath al-Bari 10:39-43) through Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan, from Abu Hayyan al-Taymi. Muslim narrated it in his Sahih (18:165) through four routes: through 'Ali ibn Mushir from Abu Hayyan; through Ibn Idris from Abu Hayyan; through Ibn 'Ulayyah from Abu Hayyan; and through 'Isa ibn Yunus from Abu Hayyan. al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan (6:245; 8:289). al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur (2:249), attributing it additionally to 'Abd al-Razzaq and Ibn al-Mundhir. In all the sources the wording is "wa-abwab min abwab al-riba" (and aspects of the aspects of usury). For an explanation of this, see the comment on narration 10880.]]

10884. Ya'qub narrated to me, saying: Ibn 'Ulayyah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah: that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: "I did not ask the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about anything more than I asked him about the *kalala*, until he poked his finger into my chest and said: 'The verse of summer at the end of *Surat al-Nisa'* suffices you.'"[[Narration 10884: The report of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd from Ma'dan has passed with the number 10877, through the route of Shu'bah from Qatadah. Muslim indicated it in his Sahih (11:57) through the route of Ibn 'Ulayyah from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah. Ahmad narrated it in al-Musnad, number 341, through the route of Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, in a longer form. He also narrated it in a longer form, number 89, through the route of 'Affan, from Hammam ibn Yahya, from Qatadah. He narrated it in an abbreviated form, number 179, through the route of Isma'il, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah. Ibn Kathir cited the last of these from the Musnad of Ahmad in his tafsir (2:241), and mentioned nothing of the other routes, but said: "Thus he narrated it in abbreviated form, and Muslim narrated it in a longer form than this," although Ahmad narrated it in longer form in several places, as you see, and as will come in the comment on number 10887.]]

10885. Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari narrated to us, saying: 'Abd Allah ibn Bakr al-Sahmi narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan, from 'Umar, who said: "I will never leave anything more important to me than the matter of the *kalala*. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) was never as harsh with me about anything as he was about it, until he poked his finger into my chest, or he said: into my side, and said: 'The verse that was revealed at the end of *al-Nisa'* suffices you.'"[[Narration 10885: Ibrahim ibn Sa'id al-Jawhari, the teacher of al-Tabari, is trustworthy; he has passed with the numbers 3355, 3959. 'Abd Allah ibn Bakr ibn Habib al-Sahmi is trustworthy, truthful and reliable, one of the teachers of Ahmad; he is biographed in al-Tahdhib. He has passed in the chain with the number 8284, and this is another route of the earlier report. In the printed edition: "lam adda'" (I did not leave), and I have adopted what is in the manuscript.]]

10886. Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah: that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab addressed the people on Friday, saying: "Indeed, by God, I will not leave after me anything more important to me than the matter of the *kalala*. I have asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about it, and he was never as harsh with me about anything as he was about it, until he struck me in my chest and said: 'The verse of summer that was revealed at the end of *Surat al-Nisa'* suffices you.' And if I live, I will judge in it with a ruling about which no one who has recited the Qur'an will differ."[[Narration 10886: This is another route for the two preceding reports, the route of Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah.]]

10887. Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Hisham narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Salim ibn Abi al-Ja'd, from Ma'dan ibn Abi Talhah, from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, in a similar form.[[Narration 10887: Muslim narrated it through this route in his Sahih (11:56). Ahmad narrated it in a longer form in al-Musnad, number 186. See the comment on the preceding reports.]]

10888. Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq narrated to us, saying: I heard my father say: Abu Hamzah informed us, from Jabir, from al-Hasan ibn Masruq, from his father, who said: "I asked 'Umar, while he was addressing the people, about a relative of mine who inherited as a *kalala*. He said: 'The *kalala*, the *kalala*, the *kalala*!!' and he took hold of his beard, then said: 'By God, that I should know it is dearer to me than that I should have whatever is on the earth. I asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) about it, and he said: "Did you not hear the verse that was revealed about summer?"' and he repeated it three times."[[Narration 10888: Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq is trustworthy; he has passed with the numbers 1591, 2575. His father, 'Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Shaqiq, is trustworthy; he has also passed, with the numbers 1591, 1909. Abu Hamzah is al-Sukkari, Muhammad ibn Maymun, a trustworthy imam; he has passed with the number 1591. Jabir is Jabir al-Ju'fi, Jabir ibn Yazid ibn al-Harith al-Ju'fi, who has passed with the numbers 764, 858, 2340, and many other places. He is extremely weak and was accused of lying. As for "al-Hasan ibn Masruq", I have not found among the narrators anyone by this name. As for his father, he appears to mean Masruq ibn al-Ajda' al-Hamdani al-Wada'i, one of the reciters and jurists, who narrated from Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman and many of the Companions. Among the narrators from Masruq there is no one named "al-Hasan", and I have not found anyone with a son called "al-Hasan ibn Masruq". So this chain has in it what it has of affliction. This report was mentioned by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (2:251), from al-Hasan ibn Masruq, from his father, as here, and he attributed it to al-Tabari alone.]]

10889. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Zakariyya, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Salamah, who said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and asked him about the *kalala*, and he said: "Did you not hear the verse that was revealed about summer: *'And if a man is inherited from as a kalala...'* to the end of the verse?"[[Narration 10889: Abu Usamah is Hammad ibn Usamah ibn Zayd al-Kufi, who has passed with the numbers 29, 51, 223, 2995, 5265. Zakariyya is Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah, who has passed with the numbers 112, 1219. Abu Ishaq is al-Sab'i. Abu Salamah is Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf al-Zuhri, who has passed with the numbers 8, 67, 3015, 8394. This report was narrated by al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan (6:224), through Yahya ibn Adam, from 'Ammar ibn Ruzayq, from Abu Ishaq, from Abu Salamah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, and he said: "The report of Abu Ishaq from Abu Salamah is discontinuous (munqati') and not well known."]]

10890. Muhammad ibn Khalaf narrated to me, saying: Ishaq ibn 'Isa narrated to us, saying: Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr: that a man asked 'Uqbah about the *kalala*, and he said: "Are you not amazed at this? He asks me about the *kalala*, and nothing has baffled the Companions of the Messenger of God (ﷺ) as much as the *kalala* baffled them!"[[Narration 10890: Ishaq ibn 'Isa ibn Najih is Abu Ya'qub, Ibn al-Tabbaq, who has passed with the number 2836. Ibn Lahi'ah has passed many times. Yazid ibn Abi Habib al-Misri is trustworthy; he has passed with the numbers 4348, 5493. Abu al-Khayr is Murthid ibn 'Abd Allah al-Yazani, the Egyptian jurist, who narrated from 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir al-Juhani, with whom he was constantly, and 'Amr ibn al-'As, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, and others of the Companions. He is a trustworthy Successor (tabi'i), biographed in al-Tahdhib. This report was narrated by al-Darimi in his Sunan (2:366), through the route of 'Abd Allah ibn Yazid, from Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib.
