In the printed edition of al-Darimi there is an error which says "from Yazid ibn 'Abd Allah al-Yazani", and the correct form is "Murthid ibn 'Abd Allah", who is Abu al-Khayr, as already noted. al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur (2:250), and additionally attributed it to Ibn Abi Shaybah. "a'dala al-amr" and "a'dala bihi al-amr" mean: it became constricted and unclear; he was at a loss because of its obscurity.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far (al-Tabari) said: If someone says: What is the meaning of His saying, may His praise be exalted: *"And if a man dies leaving no child and he has a sister, then for her is half of what he left"*, when you know the agreement of all the people of the qibla (the Muslims)[[Ahl al-qibla: the Muslims as a whole.]] (apart from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr, may God have mercy on them both) that if the deceased left a daughter and a sister, the daughter has half, and what remains goes to the sister, if she is a full or consanguine sister? And where is that in His saying: *"If a man dies leaving no child and he has a sister, then for her is half of what he left"*, when they gave her half alongside a child?

It is said: The matter in that is contrary to what you have suggested. God, may His praise be exalted, only made, by His saying: *"If a man dies leaving no child and he has a sister, then for her is half of what he left"*, when the deceased has neither male nor female child, and he is inherited from as a kalala, half of his estate a fixed portion (fard) for her, specified. As for when the deceased has a female child, she is then a residuary heir (*'asabah*) along with her, and what would go to any other residuary heir, had she not existed, goes to her. That is not limited by a fixed limit, nor is it a fixed portion (fard) of the shares of the heirs by their inheritance from their deceased. God did not say in His Book: "If he has a child, then nothing is for his sister with him," so that there would be for what was related from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr in this a direction to which it could be guided. Rather, God, may His praise be exalted, explained the extent of her right when the deceased is inherited from as a kalala, and left the explanation of what right she has when he is not inherited from as a kalala in His Book; and He explained it through His revelation, by the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ), making her a residuary heir alongside the female children of the deceased. That is a meaning other than the meaning of her inheriting from the deceased when he is inherited from as a kalala.

* *

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying: *"And he (the male) inherits her if she has no child"*

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His praise be exalted, means by this: and the brother of the woman inherits from her if she dies before him, when she is inherited from as a kalala,[[In the printed edition: "idha wurith kalala" (when he is inherited from as a kalala); the correct form is what I have adopted from the manuscript.]] and she has no child or father.

* *

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying: *"And if there are two (female siblings), then for them two-thirds of what he left; and if there are siblings, men and women, then for the male is the like of the share of two females"*

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His praise be exalted, by His saying: *"If there are two"*, means: if the deceased females left behind are two sisters of the full or consanguine type, or two consanguine sisters, then for them are two-thirds of what their brother left behind, the deceased, if he has no child and he is inherited from as a kalala. *"And if there are siblings"*, meaning: if the ones he left behind of his siblings are *"men and women, then for the male"* among them, by their inheritance from him from his estate, *"is the like of the share of two females"*, meaning: the like of the portion of two of his sisters.[[See the explanation of "the like of the share of two females" above: 8:30-34.]] This applies when he is inherited from as a kalala, and the siblings are his brothers and sisters, full or consanguine.

* *

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying: *"God makes clear to you lest you go astray"*

Abu Ja'far said: God, may His praise be exalted, means by this: God makes clear to you the division of your inheritances, and the ruling of the kalala, and how their shares are (to be divided), *"lest you go astray"*, meaning: lest you go astray in the matter of inheritances and their division; that is, lest you deviate from the truth in that and err in the ruling concerning it, and so stray from the straight path,[[See the explanation of "al-dalal" (going astray) above in the indices of vocabulary.]] as follows:

10891. al-Qasim narrated to us, saying: al-Husayn narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to me, from Ibn Jurayj, regarding His saying: *"God makes clear to you lest you go astray"*, he said: "In the matter of inheritances."

10892. Ibn Wakī' narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Humayd al-Ma'mari narrated to us, and al-Hasan ibn Yahya narrated to us, saying: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, both of them saying: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, who said: "When 'Umar recited *'God makes clear to you lest you go astray'*, he would say: 'O God, whomever You have made the kalala clear to, while it has not been made clear to me...'"[[Narration 10892: see the preceding report, number 10876.]]

* *

Abu Ja'far said: The position of "an" (lest) in His saying *"God makes clear to you lest you go astray"* is in the accusative case, according to some grammarians, because it is joined to the verb.

* *

According to another opinion: it is in the genitive case, meaning: God makes clear to you so that you do not go astray, and in order that you not go astray. The "la" (not) was dropped from the wording, though it is required in meaning, because the sense of the speech indicates it. The Arabs do this; they say: "I came to you that you blame me," meaning: I came to you that you not blame me, as al-Qutami said describing a she-camel:

*"We saw what the discerning see in her, so we swore an oath over her that she not be sold."*[[Diwan 43. Lines from this poem have passed in 1:116 and 7:557, describing his she-camel when she reached her full maturity and became as he described; he says: when we saw her nobility and beauty, we swore an oath upon her that she should not be sold, because of her preciousness to us.]]

meaning: that she not be sold.

* *

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying: *"And God is Knower of all things" (176)*

Abu Ja'far said: He, may His praise be exalted, means by this: "And Allah is, of all things," including the interests of His servants in the division of their inheritances and otherwise, and of all things, "Knowing" (ʿalīm), meaning: He possesses knowledge of all of that. [[See the explanation of "ʿalīm" in the earlier indexes of linguistic terms.]]

* *

﴿End of the commentary on Surah an-Nisa'﴾ And praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah bless Muhammad (ﷺ), his family, and his companions.
